title: landmod.f90 has a dropped continuation marker and the model does not compile
description:
The merged tip does not build. gfortran on landmod.f90:

  landmod.f90:256:7:
    256 |      &                ,snowcovz
        |       1
  Error: Invalid character in name at (1)

The line before it, ',newsurf,rinifor,nwatcini,dwatcini,dgroundalb', has lost its trailing '&', so the continuation chain that lists the namelist ends there and ',snowcovz' starts a new statement.

Reproduce: python exoplasim/scripts/build_model.py --res T21 --ranks 4 --no-publish. Every other object in the T21 L10 p4 production configuration compiles; landmod is the only failure and it stops the link.

Found from a worktree branched at d09dba4c while building to compile-check an unrelated aerocore.f90 change (world-2lsg). landmod.f90 was last touched by aaeaed55 'Merge batch H (cross-cutting model), resolving against batch G's deletions', so this is very likely a continuation marker lost in that merge resolution rather than a defect either batch wrote.

Do: restore the trailing '&' on the dgroundalb line. Then rebuild every binary and --verify, per CLAUDE.md rule 4.

Not fixed here because landmod.f90 is outside this batch's file ownership and a parallel batch editing the same line would conflict.
notes:
FIXED on branch fanout-AK at 743c67a9, which is the base of every gate result that batch reports. The line adding snowcovz to landmod_nl was appended below a line with no trailing &, so gfortran read the ampersand at column 6 of the snowcovz line as an invalid character in a name. Restoring the continuation on the dgroundalb line is the whole change; the namelist's contents and order are untouched. Left OPEN because it is another batch's issue and a second fix may exist to merge against; the coordinator should keep whichever lands and close this.

Confirmed by building: with it, T21 l10 p16 compiles and links from the merged tip and runs a timestep.
close_reason: Duplicate of world-33ba, filed by a sibling batch for the same landmod.f90 continuation break. Both were fixed identically and independently; the merge kept one. world-33ba carries the better framing -- that smoke_test passes on a tree that does not compile, because nothing in the gate set compiles the model, which is why the break survived a merge and five batches. Keeping world-33ba as the live record.

title: continue_exoplasim never writes the hyperdiffusion namelist, so every segment after the first runs the model compiled defaults
description:
run_exoplasim.py writes TDISSQ, TDISST, TDISSZ, TDISSD, NHDIFF and NDEL into plasim_namelist (six references). continue_exoplasim.py writes NONE of them (zero references). The model reads them from the namelist on every invocation and they are not restart records, so a continued segment silently falls back to the values compiled into plasimmod and plasim.f90.

CONFIRMED ON THE PRODUCTION BASELINE. run_2b20e3324bb0 -- the T21 run the project climatology and every downstream component rests on -- has FIVE segments and its plasim_namelist contains no hyperdiffusion keys at all. So four of its five segments, and 84 of its 85 orbits, ran with the model defaults rather than the derived values.

WHAT THAT CHANGES AT T21. plasim.f90:1443 branches only on NTRU==42, so T21 falls through to plasimmod defaults: ndel 2, nhdiff 15, tdissd 0.20 d, tdissz 1.10 d, tdisst 5.60 d, tdissq 0.1 d. The configured values are ndel 4, nhdiff 16, divergence 0.4457, vorticity 2.2285, temperature 5.6449, humidity 0.7421.

  ndel 2 against 4 is the ORDER of the operator -- grad^4 instead of grad^8
  humidity   0.1  against 0.7421  -- 7.4x stronger damping
  divergence 0.20 against 0.4457  -- 2.2x
  vorticity  1.10 against 2.2285  -- 2.0x
  temperature 5.60 against 5.6449 -- negligible

A different operator order is not a tuning difference. The hyperdiffusion derivation in config/planet.yaml, the alpha=4 choice and the n*/N=0.381 confinement target all describe a model the continued segments were not running.

ALSO AFFECTS the T42 cold arm built for the ladder work (run_8102b89a08ac): one orbit at the configured values and 86 on defaults, so it is not usable as a resolution reference until re-run.

HOW IT SURFACED. A converted T21-to-T42 state crashes with SIGFPE in the radiation (world-bhs). Arm A does not crash in its own directory but DOES crash on the identical restart when run under a namelist that carries the hyperdiffusion keys -- which is what exposed that the two namelists differ.

check_consistency has a hyperdiffusion check but it validates config/planet.yaml against its own rule, not a run namelist against the config. That is the gap: nothing compares what a run INTEGRATED with against what was declared.

Source: exoplasim/scripts/continue_exoplasim.py, exoplasim/scripts/run_exoplasim.py, exoplasim/runs/run_2b20e3324bb0/plasim_namelist, vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/plasim.f90:1443, plasimmod.f90:201,444,877-880
close_reason:
Fixed by world-8bs in this fan-out (batch H). continue_exoplasim.py:587 now calls declare_hyperdiffusion(model, config), the same function the prepare path uses, so a continuation writes NDEL, NHDIFF and the four TDISS* into plasim_namelist instead of falling through to the compiled defaults. They are written as replicated '<layers>*<value>' text rather than as scalars, which also closes world-720's failure mode -- a Fortran namelist assignment of a scalar to an array sets element 1 only and leaves the rest at the compiled default, giving a mixed-unit array. expected_namelist_keys covers all six plus FILTERKAPPA and NFILTEREXP, and verify_staged_namelists compares the five replicated ones as text so a scalar cannot pass.

The CODE defect is closed. The consequence for the existing baseline -- run_2b20e3324bb0 having run 84 of its 85 orbits on compiled hyperdiffusion -- is a separate issue and stays open as world-hxm.

title: Every cold start builds an Earth Arctic sea-ice field and starts the ocean at freezing
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 1.

configure()'s `rm *.sra` correctly removes the shipped Earth boundary fields --
the diag confirms codes 169, 210, 211, 709 and 903 all print `Init ...
internally`. The model does not then fall back to anything neutral.

With code 169 absent, xclsst stays at its -999 sentinel (icemod.f90:119) and
icemod.f90:230 does `where (xclsst <= TFREEZE) xclicec = 1.0`, putting full ice
cover on every ocean cell. make_ice_thickness (icemod.f90:1929-1982) then shapes
it with hmaxn=3.0, hmaxs=0.50, cminn=0.1, cmins=0.25 and a fourteen-element
monthly modulation table credited in its own comment to "CCM3 report pp
127-129".

Separately oceanmod.f90:96 declares `real :: yclsst(NHOR,0:13)` with no
initialiser while its neighbours at :95, :97, :99 and :100 all have one.
oceanmod.f90:285 does `yclsst = MAX(yclsst,TFREEZE)` and :291-293 copies it into
the ocean temperature, so whatever was in memory is clipped up to freezing.
Note -finit-real=snan in the checked profile does NOT cover this: it covers
locals, not module-scope SAVE arrays.

Measured 2026-08-24, first output bin of run_2b20e3324bb0:
  ts   ocean: min=214.832  max=271.900  mean=258.860
  sic  ocean: min=0.000    max=0.000    mean=0.000
  sit  ocean: NH mean=2.533   SH mean=0.139
The ocean starts globally at TFREEZE, every ocean cell carries ice in an 18:1
north-south ratio -- Earth's Arctic-Antarctic contrast on a world with 32 deg
obliquity and unrelated geography -- and ice COVER is identically zero because
xicecc initialises to 0 (icemod.f90:97) and mkicec can only grow it. Thick ice
carrying no albedo is not a physical state, and neither is the field it
replaced.

Both are written to the restart (icemod.f90:995-997, oceanmod.f90:615) and read
back, so this persists through every continuation. yclsst is also emitted as
ocean code 990 "clim. sst", which is meaningless.

The exposure is sweep_flux_earth, which has not run: each arm would cold-start
from a fully iced ocean, so the warm branch is only approached from below and
the hysteresis is never probed from the ice-free side. An arm at 0.90 that fails
to melt out would read as a snowball bifurcation when it is an initial-condition
artifact.

Do: give the ice and ocean a declared cold-start state for this world rather
than a constructed Earth one. Blocks the flux sweep.
acceptance_criteria: A cold start produces a declared initial ice and SST state with no CCM3 field and no uninitialised read; sic and sit are mutually consistent in the first bin; the flux sweep can start from a defensible state.
close_reason: A cold start with no codes 169/210/211 now begins from a DECLARED profile or refuses to begin. read_ice_surface no longer constructs ice cover from the SST sentinel; make_ice_thickness's CCM3 relation is reachable only when a real cover was read, and warns that it is Earth-fitted and hemispherically asymmetric. ice_cold_start takes either the read climatology or icemod_nl's tsst_eq/tsst_pol/hice_ini profile, tsst_pol + (tsst_eq-tsst_pol)*cos(lat)**2, symmetric by construction, and aborts if neither exists. oceanmod's yclsst gains its -999 initialiser (module-scope SAVE, which -finit-real does not reach) and the ocean starts from the declared profile rather than from memory clipped to freezing. xicecc is set from the initial cover on BOTH paths, which is the fix for sic being identically zero beside a non-zero sit: mkicec only grows it and icestep copies it into xicec every step. config/planet.yaml declares ocean.cold_start and run_exoplasim writes TSST_EQ/TSST_POL/HICE_INI on a prepare and on every resume; expected_namelist_keys checks them. The declared cold start is ice-free, which is the side of the hysteresis the flux sweep could not reach; an arm that wants the iced side declares a sub-freezing pole or a non-zero thickness. WHAT DEPENDED ON THE OLD BEHAVIOUR: all 9 runs in exoplasim/runs cold-started from the constructed field and the ocean at freezing, and every restart carries it forward; per rule 7 the canonical climatology lineage does not exist, so all of it is disposable. NO RESTART RECORD ADDED OR CHANGED. Commit b5918b94.

title: pyburn cannot read raw output: pyfft extensions are built for CPython 3.12, venv is 3.14
description:
Every new climate run dies at postprocessing and ExoPlaSim reports 'crashed or begun producing garbage', which is false: the model integrates fine (T42 arm, 95 s/orbit, sensible MOST_DIAG fields, no NaN, complete MOST_REST). Only the postprocessor fails.

ROOT CAUSE, reproduced on the surviving raw file: pyburn.readfile imports exoplasim.pyfft (pyburn.py:662), an f2py extension. The only built copies are pyfft.cpython-312-*.so and pyfft991.cpython-312-*.so; the venv is Python 3.14.7 since a1d37bf7. A cpython-312 extension is not importable from 3.14, so pyburn cannot read ANY raw output. The .so files are untracked build artifacts (git tracks only the .f90), so the interpreter upgrade silently invalidated them and no new run has been postprocessed since.

FIX: rebuild both extensions for 3.14. exoplasim.compile_pyfft() exists but wants meson, ninja, gfortran, gcc -- ninja/gfortran/gcc are present, MESON IS NOT, and numpy 2.5 f2py refuses the distutils backend on Python>=3.12.

DO NOT call compile_pyfft() blindly: it runs sysconfigure() when most_compiler/firstrun are absent, which is the pre-CMake build path replaced in 137c55a2. Drive numpy.f2py directly.

The error message is its own defect: __init__.py:1150 turns any postprocessing exception into _crash(), which moves the run to <run>_crashed/ and blames the model.

BLOCKS every run, so SPAT-11 and the physics-filter arms both wait on it.
close_reason:
Fixed and verified 2026-08-23. Every acceptance criterion met.

Both extensions rebuilt for the running interpreter and import: pyfft.cpython-314 and pyfft991.cpython-314. Verified against an identity that can fail rather than by the import alone -- inigau's Gaussian weights are the measure of [-1,1] and must sum to 2, and both give 2.0000000000 exactly.

A raw MOST file postprocesses: run_9d4f4a3ad847's MOST.00000 went to NetCDF, and four subsequent two-orbit runs completed with their postprocessing.

smoke_test carries the check and it was verified BY BREAKING IT: both .so deleted, the check reports the ModuleNotFoundError and exits non-zero, the build restores them, and it goes green. 19 checks 0 failed.

environment.md records that a new interpreter means a pyfft rebuild, with the two commands.

BEYOND THE ROW, because compile_pyfft() could not be the answer: it swallowed failure (the raise was commented out), it called sysconfigure() which calls back into it behind marker files this fork stopped writing -- constructing a Model creates firstrun, which disabled the rebuild permanently -- and it verified nothing. Rewritten to build through sys.executable so the ABI tag cannot disagree with the interpreter that will import the result, to raise with f2py's output on failure, and to verify what it produced. exoplasim/scripts/build_pyfft.py is the registered entry point with a --check arm. Commits 5bb81bb7 and be4e41b3.

Needs meson on the host, which is now installed.

title: Field capacity can only be staged at T21, so the escalation route runs the uniform bucket at every rung above it
description:
exoplasim/notes/route-step-criteria.md, "Above T21 the route CANNOT take a cold
start", measured 2026-08-31 pre-flight on the T42 arms world-90y6 bought.

Staged surface code 229, field capacity, and its split 2290 exist at T21 and
nowhere else, and no step in config/pipeline.yaml can produce them at another
rung. Every other field in the staged family takes a --grid and is cut at any
exported rung; exoplasim/inputs/t42 carries all thirteen of those.

WHY. build_surface_soil_water.py takes no --grid. It reads the grid and the
boundary land mask off a climatology and calls require_configured_grid on it,
so with model.resolution set to T42 it refuses every climatology this project
has, T21 being the only rung any run has reached a climatology at.

THE DEPENDENCY IS ON THE GRID, NOT ON THE CLIMATE, and the builder says so at
the point of read: what it takes from the climatology "is the grid and the
boundary land mask, and nothing else: the water capacity itself comes from the
land column states, which pedology weathered under a climate of their own." The
mask is a pure function of the terrain and build_boundary_conditions.py already
writes it at every rung as code 172. So the field's CONTENT is rung-independent
and only its CARRIER pins it to T21.

The pipeline edge surface_soil_water -> bootstrap_climatology is about
DETERMINATION and is right: a staged surface field is an input to the run whose
output would otherwise build it, and the bootstrap satisfies that. What is
wrong is that a grid coupling rides on the same argument.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY, and it is the whole escalation route above T21.
model.soil_water_source is `pedology`, which makes 229 a refusal in
run_exoplasim.py. So:

  * a COLD arm above T21 cannot start at all, because it reads dwmax from the
    .sra;
  * a CONVERTED arm above T21 cannot carry the field either, because
    restart_schema.py gives dwmax the policy STATIC_GRID, TARGET -- the
    capacity comes from the TARGET TEMPLATE, never from the donor, which is
    correct because a donor's capacity belongs to another soil column.

So every rung above T21 runs the uniform 0.5 m bucket whichever initial
condition it starts from. config/planet.yaml argues at that key that the
uniform bucket is materially wrong here: the land-mean capacity is well under
it, which changes evaporation, which changes P - E, which is the numerator of
the carve criterion.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Give build_surface_soil_water.py a --grid and take the
land mask from the export at that rung -- code 172, which every other builder
in the family already reads -- keeping the climatology edge for determination
and dropping it as the grid carrier. Then add the 2290 split on the same terms.
Check the alternative first, per the standing agreement about whether a thing
should exist: if a remap of the T21 field is defensible, lib/remap.py is the
one door for it and the answer is a pipeline step rather than a flag. Either
way the artifact needs a row in config/pipeline.yaml before it exists.

BLOCKS: world-j1po, which is "build the T85 staged surface family" and cannot
produce a complete one until this lands. Bears on world-3y2v, whose T85
endurance arm would otherwise be bought on a soil water capacity the project
has declared wrong for this world.

title: The water closure omits soil evaporation and interception, and has never run
description:
The water closure subtracts transpiration and calls it AET, so it omits soil
evaporation and canopy interception entirely, and it has never actually been
measured on a run.

`biosphere/config/lpj_acceptance.yaml` closes water as precipitation minus
`aaet.out` Total minus `tot_runoff.out` Total over ten complete forcing cycles.
`aaet.out` Total is TRANSPIRATION: `commonoutput.cpp` builds it from
`indiv.aaet` summed over individuals and patches. The model's own annual water
record adds three terms, `patch.aaet + patch.aevap + patch.aintercep`
(`somdynam.cpp`). `patch.aevap`, bare soil evaporation, and `patch.aintercep`,
canopy interception evaporation, reach no output table: `commonoutput.cpp`
accumulates both and sends them only to the interactive `plot()`. The monthly
tables that would carry them, `mevap.out` and `mintercep.out`, are commented
out in every `.ins` the port ships.

The residual is therefore not the implied storage change the contract's own
interpretation calls it. It is soil evaporation plus interception plus the
storage change, and the first two are ordinary-sized annual fluxes.

THE CHECK HAS NEVER RUN. Before the current tree the closure loop raised on the
first failing element, and water sat after carbon and nitrogen, so every
assessment that refused on nitrogen returned before reaching it. The refusal
recorded on `lpj_de8a0c8bd4324639b4bd62b66867d23f` names nitrogen alone for
that reason and is not a statement that water closed.

MEASURED on that run with the contract's own window and limits: 1578 of 1617
gridcells fail, the largest ten-cycle residual is 3416.7 mm against a 79.5 mm
limit, and only 3.34 per cent of gridcell-cycles sit inside the 2.0 mm floor.
The residual GROWS LINEARLY with window length -- +3417 mm at ten cycles,
+30715 at a hundred, +330709 at 1252 on the worst gridcell -- which is what
separates a missing flux from a storage change, since a storage term telescopes
to an endpoint difference and cannot grow. The steady 264 mm per cycle on a
gridcell receiving 1591 mm is 17 per cent of precipitation, the size the two
omitted fluxes should be.

Evidence and method in notes/audits/closure-stocks-are-incomplete.md.

WHAT TO DO. Enable `file_mevap` and `file_mintercep` in the port's `.ins`,
retain both tables, and have the water rule subtract their twelve monthly
columns alongside AET and runoff. That is a config change and needs no model
source change: both tables are mainline LPJ-GUESS and both are already written
by the compiled binary the moment the `.ins` names them. At three written
decimals over twenty-four columns and ten cycles they add 0.12 mm to the
water resolution bound, which keeps the 2.0 mm floor above the contract's
required tenfold margin.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. A short diagnostic run with the two tables retained,
checking that precipitation minus transpiration, soil evaporation, interception
and runoff closes to the storage change rather than to 264 mm per cycle. Until
it does, the acceptance run refuses on water in 98 per cent of gridcells.

title: The nitrogen closure differences a pool snapshot against a flux integral, and the mineral pool's jitter exceeds the floor
description:
The nitrogen closure differences an end-of-cycle POOL SNAPSHOT against a
CYCLE-INTEGRATED FLUX, and the fast soil mineral pool's cycle-to-cycle jitter
lands entirely in the residual. That jitter is larger than the declared
2.0 kgN/ha floor in a handful of gridcells, so it is what the next acceptance
run will refuse on now that world-e1cl has removed the write-out quantisation
that was masking it.

MEASURED on run lpj_de8a0c8bd4324639b4bd62b66867d23f, 1617 gridcells, 1253
retained cycles. Evidence and method in
notes/audits/closure-tolerance-under-written-precision.md.

WHAT IS TRUE. Over the 2,024,484 gridcell-cycles the per-cycle residual
`(npool Total[y] - npool Total[y-1]) * 1e4 + nflux NEE[y]` stays within
1.0 kgN/ha for 99.885 per cent of them, which is the endpoint-quantisation
bound of the old output precision. The 2329 that exceed it are not spread
evenly: in those gridcell-cycles the cycle-to-cycle change in the soil mineral
nitrogen snapshot, soil_npool.out NH4+NO3, averages 5.70 kgN/ha against 0.29
elsewhere -- a factor of nineteen. They also associate with fire, 71.7 per cent
carrying a fire gas emission against a 44.4 per cent base rate.

IT DOES NOT ACCUMULATE, which is why this is not a conservation defect in the
model. The worst gridcell's mean per-cycle residual is -0.0046 kgN/ha; over the
whole 1252-cycle record that reaches -5.75 kgN/ha, which is 0.035 per cent of
that gridcell's nitrogen throughput and inside the contract's own
`relative_throughput_limit` of 0.001 by a factor of three. What does not average
out is a TEN-cycle window, which is short enough to cut through the jitter: the
same gridcell reads -4.95 over the contract's window.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. Two of world-e1cl's four refused gridcells were write-out
quantisation and will drop out. Two carried a residual near -5 and near -3.6
that is flat in window length from ten cycles to twelve hundred, so it is real
and it will still exceed the 2.0 kgN/ha floor. A re-run therefore still refuses
on nitrogen closure unless this is settled first, and it refuses honestly
rather than on rounding.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Establish whether the pool snapshot and the flux integral
are the same accounting -- that is, whether every mineral pool inside
npool.out Total has its change carried by a term inside nflux.out NEE, or
whether some of it is an internal transfer the annual output cadence cannot
see. That is a source question in vendor/lpj-guess, answerable without a run,
and it decides between two dispositions: a defect in the model's annual
nitrogen bookkeeping, or a closure rule whose window is shorter than the
variability of the pools it differences. THE SECOND DISPOSITION MAY NOT BE
TAKEN BY LENGTHENING THE WINDOW UNTIL THE RUN PASSES -- the window is a
declared threshold and a criterion chosen after the run it judges is not a
criterion. It would have to be derived from the fast pools' own timescale.

Do not weigh this against the cost of the run it invalidates: nothing is
commissioned, so there is no price (CLAUDE.md rule 7).
close_reason: The stock was incomplete, not the tolerance: npool.out Total omits four of the six soil mineral pools ntransform.cpp conserves over. Pairing it with soil_npool.out NO2+NO+N2O+N2 closes every one of 2,024,484 gridcell-cycles inside the written-precision bound and all four refused gridcells inside the declared 2.0 kgN/ha floor. Fixed in ea1212e42; carbon is clean, water is world-24xd.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTRATION, world-w89k, written before any measurement of the correction
term. Source finding first, then the falsifiable test.

SOURCE FINDING (commonoutput.cpp, ntransform.cpp, guess.h; no run involved).

The soil nitrogen operator's own conservation identity, enforced in
vendor/lpj-guess/modules/ntransform.cpp:ntransform, is over SIX soil pools:

    n_total = NH4_mass + NO3_mass + NO2_mass + NO_mass + N2O_mass + N2_mass

npool.out Total counts TWO of them. commonoutput.cpp:1550 builds availn as

    availn += (NH4_mass + NO3_mass + snowpack_NH4_mass + snowpack_NO3_mass)
              * to_gridcell_average

and Total is nmass_gridcell + nlitter_gridcell + surfsoillittern + cwdn +
centuryn + availn (commonoutput.cpp:2011). NO2_mass, NO_mass, N2O_mass and
N2_mass appear in NO pool column of npool.out. They are persistent state:
soil.cpp serialises them across the restart, and n_gas_emission removes only
the fraction ftemp * (1 - wcont) of each per day, so a remainder carries to
the next day and across the cycle boundary.

nflux.out NEE reports the gas only when it LEAVES those pools:
report_flux(NO_SOIL/N2O_SOIL/N2_SOIL) is called on the emitted increment, not
on the production. So nitrogen nitrified or denitrified out of NH4/NO3 and
still resident in NO2/NO/N2O/N2 at the cycle boundary has left npool.out Total
and has not yet entered nflux.out NEE.

commonoutput.cpp:1481-1486 accumulates the same four pools with the same
to_gridcell_average weight, in the same stand/patch loop, and soil_npool.out
writes them in kgN/ha at four decimals.

HYPOTHESIS H. The nitrogen closure residual is exactly the change in the
omitted pools. With

    X[y] = soil_npool.out (NO2 + NO + N2O + N2)[y]            kgN/ha
    R[y] = (npool.out Total[y] - Total[y-1]) * 1e4 + nflux.out NEE[y]
    C[y] = R[y] + (X[y] - X[y-1])

H says C is zero to within the written quantisation of the three columns. On
this run npool.out Total was written at four decimals in kgN/m2, so the
audit's endpoint bound is 1.045 kgN/ha; X contributes 2e-4 and is negligible.
The bound is therefore 1.045 kgN/ha, and it is the audit's number, not a new
one.

FALSIFICATION CRITERIA, fixed now, before the numbers are seen.

F1. The two gridcells the audit found to carry a real flat residual,
    (-135.00, -19.38) and (0.00, -13.84), must have their TEN-CYCLE window
    residual fall below the declared absolute_floor_kg_n_ha of 2.0 after
    correction. If either does not, H is refused.
F2. The share of gridcell-cycles with |C| <= 1.045 must EXCEED the 99.885 per
    cent that |R| achieves. If it does not exceed it, H explains nothing and
    is refused.
F3. The correction must create no new failures: no gridcell whose ten-cycle
    window residual was inside the 2.0 floor may fall outside it after
    correction.
F4. Sign. H predicts R tracks -(X[y] - X[y-1]). The least-squares slope of R
    on -(X[y] - X[y-1]) over the gridcell-cycles that exceed the quantisation
    bound must be within 0.1 of 1.0. A slope near zero refuses H even if F1-F3
    pass by accident.

If H holds this is outcome ONE of the three: the two columns are not
differenceable as written, and the pairing that closes is
Total + (NO2+NO+N2O+N2)/1e4 differenced against NEE.

If H is refused, the omitted pools are not the mechanism and the disposition
returns to outcome two or three.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESULT. Outcome one of the three: the two columns are not differenceable as
written, and the pairing that closes is npool.out Total plus soil_npool.out
(NO2 + NO + N2O + N2) against nflux.out NEE.

The mechanism is not a snapshot against an integral. npool.out Total is not the
complete nitrogen stock. ntransform.cpp's own conservation identity, enforced
every simulated day, is over six soil mineral pools; commonoutput.cpp builds
Total's mineral term from two of them. The other four are persistent state,
serialised across the restart and drained only fractionally per day, and
nflux.out NEE reports their gas when it LEAVES them rather than when it enters,
so nitrogen resident in them at a cycle boundary is on neither side of the
check. The residual is therefore the change in those four pools, which
telescopes over any window to their endpoint difference. Flat in window length
is the signature of that and of nothing else.

The pre-registered criteria, measured on lpj_de8a0c8bd4324639b4bd62b66867d23f:

F1 PASS. All four refused gridcells fall inside the 2.0 kgN/ha floor. The two
   that carried a real flat residual go from -4.95 to -0.03 and from -2.43 to
   +0.24; the other two from +2.43 to -0.21 and +2.03 to +0.35.
F2 PASS. The share of gridcell-cycles inside the 1.045 kgN/ha quantisation
   bound goes from 99.913 to 100.000 per cent of 2,024,484. The largest
   corrected per-cycle residual is 1.0019 kgN/ha and the largest corrected
   ten-cycle window residual is 1.0000, both one endpoint quantum.
F3 PASS. No gridcell inside the floor before is outside it after.
F4 FAILED AS WRITTEN, and the criterion was the defect. It asked for the slope
   of the residual on -(X[y]-X[y-1]) over the gridcell-cycles selected by
   |R| > 1.045, which conditions on the dependent variable and inflates the
   slope by construction; it read 1.203 against a required 1.0 +/- 0.1.
   Without that selection the slope is 1.0021 over all gridcell-cycles, 1.0102
   selecting on the independent variable at |dX| > 1.045, and 1.0082 at
   |dX| > 5.0, with the correlation rising to 0.998. The registration is
   reported as it stood; the unbiased forms are the ones the conclusion rests
   on, and F2's 100.000 per cent is stronger than any slope.

NOT A TOLERANCE CHANGE. No floor moved and no window lengthened. The floor is
the declared 2.0 kgN/ha it always was, and it now discriminates on the
simulation because both sides of the difference account for the same nitrogen.

CARBON DOES NOT SHARE THE DEFECT. cpool.out Total is VegC + LitterC + SoilC and
cflux.out NEE is built from the same budget; there is no carbon analogue of the
four soil mineral pools, and labile_carbon is assigned from the day's
decomposition rather than accumulated, so it is a rate and not a store.
Measured on the same run, the carbon residual's largest per-cycle value is
0.001000 kgC/m2, exactly one written quantum, and every one of the 2,024,484
gridcell-cycles is inside the quantisation bound.

WATER SHARES THE CLASS AND IN A STRONGER FORM, and it is world-24xd. aaet.out
Total is transpiration, not evapotranspiration: soil evaporation and canopy
interception reach no output table at all. That is an omitted FLUX rather than
an omitted stock, so it does not telescope, and the water check had never
actually run because the closure loop raised on nitrogen before reaching it.

Evidence and method: notes/audits/closure-stocks-are-incomplete.md.
Fixed in ea1212e42.

title: Nitrogen conservation fails in four cells on the first run to reach equilibrium
description:
THE EQUILIBRIUM PROBLEM IS SOLVED AND THIS IS WHAT IS BEHIND IT. Run lpj_de8a0c8bd4324639b4bd62b66867d23f -- the derived 8600-cycle spin-up with a 1253-cycle retained record, npatch 5, 1617 cells -- is the first LPJ run this project has made that passes every equilibrium check under vesper-lpj-equilibrium-window/5. assess_lpj_run.py evaluates stability before closure, so reaching a closure refusal means every assessed quantity settled. It then refuses on conservation.

MEASURED, on the acceptance contract's own nitrogen rule (npool.out Total against nflux.out NEE, pool_to_flux_units 1e4, absolute_floor_kg_n_ha 2.0, relative_throughput_limit 0.001, over the contract's 10-cycle window):

  lon  -135.00  lat -19.38   residual -4.95  throughput 127.05  limit 2  x2.47
  lon     0.00  lat -13.84   residual -2.43  throughput  72.41  limit 2  x1.22
  lon  -174.38  lat -13.84   residual +2.43  throughput  39.73  limit 2  x1.21
  lon   -28.12  lat   8.31   residual +2.03  throughput  70.03  limit 2  x1.02

Four of 1617 cells. The ABSOLUTE FLOOR binds everywhere, not the relative limit: throughputs are 40 to 127 kgN/ha so 0.001 x throughput is 0.04 to 0.13, two orders below the 2.0 floor. So this is a violation against a declared absolute tolerance and the tolerance is not obviously the wrong instrument -- but check it before believing the four, because a floor that binds everywhere is a floor doing all the discriminating.

TWO FEATURES THAT LOOK STRUCTURED RATHER THAN RANDOM, and either could be the whole story:
  * two cells carry residuals of EXACTLY +2.43 and -2.43 at the SAME latitude, -13.84, at longitudes 0.00 and -174.38. Equal magnitude, opposite sign, on a shared parallel is not what an accumulating numerical drift looks like.
  * lon 0.00 is a coordinate a longitude convention can produce by construction, and CLAUDE.md rule 3 exists because this project has silently matched zero cells three times across the export/ExoPlaSim boundary. A cell at exactly 0.00 in a refusal list earns a check that it is a real cell and not an artifact of how the table is keyed.

WHY THIS ROW IS A P1 AND WHO SHOULD READ IT FIRST. bd memories carries a standing instruction to watch the nitrogen gas terms specifically on the first LPJ run, because this project has changed five soil-N constants in vendor/lpj-guess/modules/ntransform.cpp against Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) and Weier et al. (1993) -- world-nga2, nga3, nga4, nga6, nga7 -- on a file otherwise byte-identical to mainline 4.1.1, and NONE of them has ever been execution-verified. The largest removed nh3_max entirely, raising NH3 volatilisation by 1e3 above pH 6 and 1e5 below; the nitrification gas share moved 0.33 to 0.022; the denitrification temperature response was unclamped. This is the first run that has ever exercised them, and it fails nitrogen conservation. That may be coincidence and it may not, and the comparison is CHEAP because the stock-4.1.1 arm already exists as a runnable profile.

NOTE WHAT THE RUN IS AND IS NOT. It was integrated on the binary built BEFORE world-2aij, world-xfif and world-pidx landed, so its physics is one merge behind the tree and it can never itself become the accepted run -- world-w62x's gate refuses a binary that does not match its source. Its value is diagnostic: it establishes that the derived spin-up settles the equilibrium half, and it localises a conservation defect to four cells.
acceptance_criteria: The four cells' nitrogen residual is explained -- as a real conservation defect with its mechanism named, as an instrument defect in the closure rule, or as a coordinate/keying artifact -- and the explanation is checked against something that could have failed. If it is a real defect, the term responsible is named in vendor/lpj-guess and the fix is registered as a divergence with its gate.
notes: Filed 2026-08-31 immediately after the run landed. Diagnostic reproduced by reading npool.out and nflux.out directly through lib/lpj_table.py; the closure code at assess_lpj_run.py:290-304 raises before writing its per-cell report, so acceptance.json carries only the count -- that is itself worth fixing, since a refusal that names four cells without saying which is a refusal nobody can act on.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS, written before any of the three tests was run.

Two facts established first, from the artifact and from source, that the predictions are framed against.

FACT A. npool.out Total is written with FOUR decimal places in kgN/m2 (commonoutput.cpp:336, ColumnDescriptor width 10+bm_extra_prec, precision 4+bm_extra_prec, and bm_extra_prec is 0 unless RUN_BENCHMARKS is defined at compile time). The closure rule multiplies that column by pool_to_flux_units 1e4. So ONE LEAST-SIGNIFICANT DIGIT OF THE POOL COLUMN IS 1.0 kgN/ha. The residual is a difference of two such written values, so it carries up to +/-1.0 kgN/ha of pure write-out quantisation before any physics. nflux.out NEE is written to two decimals in kgN/ha (commonoutput.cpp:370), so the nine summed flux terms contribute at most +/-0.045.

FACT B. At full precision every one of the 1617 residuals is an exact multiple of 0.01, and the population is: median 0.26, q0.90 0.70, q0.99 0.96, q0.999 2.43, max 4.95; 12 cells above 1.0, 4 above the 2.0 floor. The shoulder sits at 1.0, which is exactly the endpoint-quantisation bound of Fact A.

H1 -- COORDINATE OR KEYING ARTIFACT. Predicts the two cells at lat -13.84 are not two independent cells: either their npool/nflux series are identical row for row, or one of them is absent from the manifest-pinned driver, or lon 0.00 is a value the table keying manufactures. FALSIFIED IF both cells appear in the driver with different precipitation AND their pool and flux series differ over the retained record.

H2 -- INSTRUMENT DEFECT. Predicts the residual is dominated by the pool endpoints' write-out quantisation, which is an ENDPOINT error and not an accumulating one. FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION: the residual must NOT grow with the closure window length. Recomputing the same cells over 50, 100, 500 and 1252 cycles instead of 10 must leave the magnitudes O(1) rather than scaling by the window ratio. H2 is falsified if any of the four grows roughly linearly with window length.

H3 -- REAL CONSERVATION DEFECT IN THE MODEL. Predicts a persistent per-cycle nitrogen leak, so the residual grows LINEARLY with window length: the -4.95 cell would carry about -0.5 kgN/ha per cycle and therefore about -500 kgN/ha over the full 1252-cycle record. Also predicts the leaking term is identifiable as a flux the model emits that nflux.out NEE does not account for, which is where the five unverified ntransform divergences would enter. FALSIFIED IF the residual is flat in window length.

The window-length test discriminates H2 from H3 with a right answer rather than a difference, and it costs no run: it re-reads the record already on disk. Ranking before testing: H2 first on Fact A alone, H3 second, H1 third -- but H1 is tested first because it is cheapest.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESULTS AGAINST THE PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS. Two of the three predictions held; the third split the four cells and its failing half is reported as a result.

H1 -- COORDINATE OR KEYING ARTIFACT: DEAD, and it was tested first as registered. The two cells at lat -13.84 are distinct simulated gridcells. Their npool.out Total series differ in all 1253 retained cycles and their nflux.out NEE series differ in all 1253; npool.out holds 1617 distinct (lon, lat) keys for 1617 simulated cells; longitude 0.00 sits in the regular T21 sequence beside -5.62 and 5.62. The +2.43/-2.43 tie is arithmetic, not structural: residuals are written to hundredths, so the 1617 cells take only 110 distinct magnitudes and share 25,685 tied pairs, and the tie does not survive a change of window -- at 25 cycles the same two cells read -0.21 and -3.29. A structural symmetry would have survived that.

H2 -- INSTRUMENT DEFECT: HELD, and it is the answer. The registered falsifiable prediction was that the residual must not grow with the closure window. It does not.

  lon/lat            L=10    L=25   L=100   L=500  L=1252
  -174.38,-13.84    +2.43   -0.21   -0.39   -0.09   -0.43
  -135.00,-19.38    -4.95   -4.61   -5.98   -5.50   -5.75
   -28.12,  8.31    +2.03   +0.42   -0.54   -0.05   +0.32
     0.00,-13.84    -2.43   -3.29   -3.42   -3.57   -3.62

Two of the four collapse to well under the 1.0 kgN/ha quantisation bound at every window except the one the contract happened to choose. The other two carry a flat offset of a few kgN/ha that is likewise independent of window length, so it is not a leak either. Population-wide: the per-cell-year residual (pool[y]-pool[y-1])*1e4 + NEE[y] falls within 1.0 kgN/ha for 99.885% of all 2,024,484 cell-years, which is exactly the endpoint-quantisation bound; the ten-cycle |residual| distribution has its shoulder at q0.99 = 0.96 with 12 of 1617 cells over 1.0. The worst cell's mean per-cycle residual is -0.0046 kgN/ha, accumulating to -5.75 over the entire 1252-cycle record, which is 0.035% of that cell's nitrogen throughput and inside the contract's own relative_throughput_limit of 0.001 by a factor of three.

H3 -- REAL CONSERVATION DEFECT: FAILED, on the registered test. It predicted the -4.95 cell would carry about -500 kgN/ha over the full record. It carries -5.75. There is no accumulating leak in any cell.

THE FIVE NTRANSFORM DIVERGENCES ARE EXONERATED OF THIS REFUSAL, on two independent grounds, neither of which needed a stock arm.

BY CONSTRUCTION: commonoutput.cpp:1464 accumulates flux_ntot from all four soil gas terms the operator produces -- NH3_SOIL, NO_SOIL, N2O_SOIL, N2_SOIL -- alongside the four fire terms, and nflux.out NEE is built from flux_ntot. Every term the divergences act on is already inside the budget the closure differences, so whatever they do to its magnitude they move nitrogen from a pool to a flux the check counts. They cannot open a hole in it.

BY SIZE: the four soil gas terms average 0.105 kgN/ha per cycle over the last hundred cycles, against 0.874 for the fire terms and a total nitrogen input of 2.199. Producing -4.95 kgN/ha over ten cycles from an unbudgeted soil gas would need about 0.5 kgN/ha per cycle, five times the entire soil gas flux. A term omitted from the budget outright could not reach it.

Consistent with that, the cell-years that do exceed the quantisation bound associate with FIRE and not with the soil operator: 71.7% of them carry a fire gas emission against a 44.4% base rate, and their mean fire gas nitrogen is 2.51 kgN/ha against 0.87 over all cell-years.

This exonerates the divergences of the CONSERVATION refusal only. Whether their calibration is right for Vesper is a different question and stays with world-9f1v and world-qcse, whose stock_4_1_1_matched arm already measured them and whose re-take on a pair that passes acceptance is still owed.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
CLOSED. The four cells are explained: the closure tolerance was finer than the column it differenced, and what survives that is a snapshot-versus-integral mismatch that world-w89k now holds.

THE FIX, and it is checked against something that could have failed. `assess_lpj_run.py:written_quantum` measures each closure column's decimal step from the output table it read; `closure_resolution` forms the residual an exactly conserving model would report from those quanta; the gate refuses a tolerance under `minimum_resolution_margin` (10.0, declared in lpj_acceptance.yaml) times it BEFORE evaluating a single cell. On the diagnostic run the measured margins are nitrogen 1.91, water 3.64, carbon 9.57 -- all three under ten, so the margin spares nothing and was not chosen to.

`commonoutput.cpp` now writes the six columns the closure differences at a precision that can resolve their tolerances: npool Total 7 dp, nflux NEE 5, cpool Total 6, cflux NEE 5, aaet Total 4, tot_runoff Total 4. A change to the written representation only; no simulated quantity moves. CONFIRMED against the rebuilt binary's own output rather than against the source -- measured quanta 1e-7, 1e-5, 1e-6, 1e-5, 1e-4, 1e-4, giving margins nitrogen 1914, carbon 217, water 2000.

The gate reads the quantum off the artifact and never off the model source, so raising a column's precision and forgetting to record it still gives the honest margin, and dropping one back refuses the next run. A self-test fixture coarsens npool.out to the released precision and requires THAT refusal by its wording, not merely any refusal.

ALSO FIXED, both found on the way and both in the same class -- an instrument reporting a difference that carries no information:

- Closure evaluated carbon and then raised, leaving nitrogen and water unmeasured. It now evaluates all three before any of them raises, so a run is fixed once rather than once per element.
- A refusal carried a count and not the cells. `ClosureError` now carries the per-element report with the failing cells named, largest residual first, and `write_failure` records it in acceptance.json.
- `vesper.h` carried its generation time, and that file's hash is what `build_lpj_guess.py --verify` uses to condemn a binary. Regenerating it invalidated a correct binary and cost a rebuild to reach a byte-identical model. The date moved to the provenance JSON; two regenerations now produce the same file.
- The self-test's fpc.out fixture had drifted behind the equilibrium contract, so the whole self-test was failing at HEAD on a column-name refusal. Fixture columns now come from the contract, so adding a quantity there needs no edit here.

IS A RE-RUN WORTH BUYING? NOT YET, and this is the one place the answer is negative. Two of the four cells were quantisation and will drop out. The other two carry a residual near -5.0 and near -3.6 that is FLAT in window length from ten cycles to twelve hundred, so it is real and it will still exceed the 2.0 kgN/ha floor. Buying 2.5 hours to receive a refusal that is already predictable from this run's own record is not worth it. world-w89k names what would settle it, and it is answerable from source without a run.

ONE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MAIN CHECKOUT. `vendor/lpj-guess/framework/vesper.h` is a link into the main checkout, so regenerating it there wrote through. It now holds the reproducible, timestamp-free header, which is the correct forward state, but the main checkout's LPJ binary was built against the previous one and its `--verify` will refuse until it is rebuilt once.
