title: An LPJ run cannot be extended from a saved state, so every refusal re-buys the whole spin-up
description:
An LPJ run cannot be extended, so every refusal re-buys the whole spin-up.

WHAT IS TRUE. `vendor/lpj-guess/framework/framework.cpp` supports both halves of
a state file -- `save_state` writes one through `GuessSerializer` and `restart`
reads one through `GuessDeserializer`, keyed on the last simulated day the state
covers. `biosphere/scripts/run_lpj_guess.py` sets neither, and
`biosphere/generated/vesper_pfts.ins` names neither. So a run that the
acceptance contract refuses can only be answered by a new run from bare ground.

WHAT IT COSTS, and the derivation that made it worth filing. The spin-up floor
is now the minimax over the unmeasured relaxation time, 6.86325 times the
retained record (`lib/run_lengths.py:ecological_spinup_multiple`), so a run at
today's floors is 8600 cycles of spin-up in front of 1253 retained: the spin-up
is 87 per cent of the wall clock. With a state file the marginal cost of more
retained record, or of a second seed, or of an npatch arm, is the record alone.
Without one every such question re-buys the spin-up.

WHAT IT WOULD ALSO SETTLE, and this is the part that is not just throughput. The
one thing standing between this tree and its first accepted LPJ run is
`cpool.out` total carbon bounding at 0.0503 against 0.05 on
`lpj_7d3c576ee4e342acb097b46fece976e0` -- a drift, not a resolution failure,
living in vegetation carbon, which is what an under-spun run leaves behind. A
state file makes "spin up further and re-take the record" a 1253-cycle question
rather than a 9853-cycle one.

WHAT TO DO. Add `save_state` and `restart` to the instruction file
`run_lpj_guess.py` derives, put the state directory in the run manifest, and
make the acceptance artifact record which state a run started from so a chain of
extensions has provenance. The run identity rule still holds: an extended run is
a new run with a new UUID whose manifest names its parent.

WHAT TO CHECK BEFORE BUILDING IT. Whether the vendored serializer covers the
CNP fork's own state -- the C-N-P pools and the ntransform state are this
project's additions and a serializer that predates them writes a state file that
silently restores less than it should. That is the failure this row must not
create, and it is a right answer to test against: serialize, restore, run one
cycle, and require bitwise equality with the unbroken run.

CITES: biosphere/notes/equilibrium-trend-null.md (the two floors and the
throughput), vendor/lpj-guess/framework/framework.cpp:202-211,
biosphere/scripts/run_lpj_guess.py.

title: The spin-up floor has no derivation: this model's relaxation time is measured on no record it has
description:
The spin-up floor has no derivation, because this model's relaxation time is measured on no record it has.

WHAT HAPPENED. `lib/lpj_output.py:relaxation_time` reads an e-folding time from the contraction `r` of successive equal-block differences, `tau = -Q / ln(r)`, which diverges as `r` approaches one. Its declared admissibility conditions covered the sign, `r` being in (0, 1), each difference exceeding twice its own memory-corrected standard error, and the two ratios agreeing inside a factor of two. None asked whether the contraction was RESOLVED. It now requires `r + 2 se(r) < 1`, which is the same class of check as every other in this contract: compare the instrument with the size of the effect before believing it.

WHAT THAT CHANGED. Over 192 field-records across the three diagnostic runs, every one is now declined: 97 for block differences that change sign, 82 for a difference inside its own standard error, five for a ratio that is not a contraction, and every one of the eight that reached a contraction has an uncertainty reaching one. The best of them is 0.584 +/- 0.331 -- an interval of essentially (0, 1.25). The worst read out as an e-folding time of 37647 cycles from 0.992 +/- 0.344, and a spin-up sized from it would have been about 74000 cycles.

WHAT IT COSTS. The 59.7 to 846.8 cycle relaxation bracket that world-r9nz's 2318-cycle spin-up came from was not supported, so `nyear_spinup` stands on the rescaled Earth convention again -- with the wire from measurement to value built and tested, and the module's own reason recorded in the emitted provenance. `ecological_run_cycles` returns no spin-up and names the estimator and the count; the gate checks that absence the same way it checks a derivation, so a default fails where a number would.

WHAT WOULD LIFT IT, and it is the same currency the record floor is bought in: a record long enough that a block difference is several times its own memory-corrected standard error, with four blocks each long against the memory time. On the runs on record a block of 250 to 313 cycles carries a memory time of 60 to 320, so the blocks are barely longer than the thing they are averaging over. A record that resolves a contraction is at least a few times that. THIS IS NOT A SEPARATE PURCHASE from world-qcse's: the retained record it needs is already tens of thousands of cycles, and the question is only whether the spin-up that precedes it can be sized before it is bought or has to be bounded after.

A SECOND DISPOSITION IS WORTH WEIGHING FIRST, because deleting is a fix. The spin-up exists to leave a retained record clean, and the acceptance contract already refuses a record that is not. If the record is long enough for the contract to bound the drift, an under-spun run is REFUSED rather than silently accepted, and what the spin-up derivation buys is not correctness but the cost of a wasted run. That is a real thing to buy at eight hours a run, and it may be cheaper to buy it as a lower bound on the relaxation time -- which the declined estimates DO carry, since `r - 2 se(r)` bounds `tau` from below -- than as a measured value.

CITES: biosphere/notes/equilibrium-trend-null.md, lib/lpj_output.py:relaxation_time, lib/run_lengths.py:ecological_run_cycles.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTRATION: the spin-up has a derivation that needs no relaxation time.

THE FOUR DISPOSITIONS ARE NOT ALL OPEN HERE, because one of them can be taken
without any measurement at all, and it is DERIVE.

`lib/run_lengths.py:ecological_spinup_cycles` returns the smallest S with

    exp(-S / tau) * (1 - exp(-L / tau)) <= tolerance

for a relaxation time tau this project has never measured. That S is a function
of tau, and IT IS BOUNDED OVER ALL tau. Substituting u = L / tau,

    S(tau) = L * ln((1 - exp(-u)) / tolerance) / u

which goes to minus infinity as u goes to zero -- a relaxation so slow it
barely moves across the record puts almost no drift into it -- and to zero as u
grows. So it has a finite maximum, and because S is decreasing in the
inequality's left-hand side, ANY S at or above that maximum satisfies the
inequality at EVERY tau. The supremum is therefore the smallest spin-up that
works whatever the relaxation time is, and it is the minimax answer rather than
a guess at a length.

It is exactly proportional to the retained record and depends on nothing else:

    S* = C(tolerance) * L,   C(t) = max over u of ln((1 - exp(-u)) / t) / u

C(0.05) = 6.86325, attained at tau = 7.3519 L. C(0.02) = 17.896, C(0.10) =
3.190. Verified scale-invariant against `ecological_spinup_cycles` itself by
sweeping tau at L = 100, 1253 and 5000, which returns S*/L = 6.86325 at all
three.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE ROW. The relaxation time does not have to be measured
for the spin-up to be derived, so the record that would measure it is not owed
and the thread closes as unnecessary rather than blocked. A measured relaxation
time would only ever SHORTEN the spin-up below S*, so `ecological_run_cycles`
should return the measured value where one is admissible and the minimax where
none is -- never a convention, and never None.

WHAT IT COSTS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY. S* is 6.86 times the retained record,
so it dominates a run. It is not a correctness requirement: a residual
transient enters the very statistic the acceptance contract gates on, so an
under-spun run is REFUSED rather than silently accepted. What S* buys is that
the run is not refused FOR THAT REASON, and that is the thing being priced.

WHAT I AM ABOUT TO MEASURE: nothing. C(t) is a maximum of a closed-form
function of the declared tolerance and is computed, not measured. What is
checked is that the returned S satisfies the inequality at the argmax tau and
at a sweep around it, which is a check with a right answer.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESOLVED, by DERIVE, and the relaxation time never has to be measured.

WHAT THE DERIVATION IS. `ecological_spinup_cycles` inverts

    exp(-S / tau) * (1 - exp(-L / tau)) <= tolerance

at a relaxation time no record this project has can resolve. That requirement is
BOUNDED OVER ALL tau. Substituting u = L / tau,

    S(tau) = L * ln((1 - exp(-u)) / tolerance) / u

falls away at both ends -- an approach far slower than the record puts almost
none of itself into the record, and one far faster has finished -- so it has a
finite maximum. The left-hand side is decreasing in S, so any S at or above that
maximum satisfies the requirement at EVERY tau, and the maximum is the smallest
that does. It is the minimax answer, not a guess at a length.

`lib/run_lengths.py:ecological_spinup_multiple` returns it. It is exactly
proportional to the retained record with a constant fixed by the tolerance alone:

    C(0.05) = 6.86325 records, attained at tau = 7.3519 records
    C(0.02) = 17.896        C(0.10) = 3.1901

So `ecological_run_cycles` now ALWAYS returns a spin-up -- at a measured
relaxation time where one is admissible, at the minimax where none is -- and
`spinup_basis` names which. A measured relaxation time can only ask for LESS, so
the minimax is a ceiling on the floor. `build_vesper_pfts.py` reaches the rescaled
Earth convention only where there is no acceptance artifact at all, and
`vesper_pfts.ins` now carries nyear_spinup 8600 with its basis recorded.

THE CHECK HAS A RIGHT ANSWER AND IS NOT A REPORT. The gate requires the returned
spin-up to hold the residual drift inside the tolerance across eight relaxation
times spanning five decades around the worst case, and requires one per cent
shorter to FAIL at the worst case. It also requires the returned number to be
exactly the multiple times the record. Both would fail on a loose derivation.

WHAT THIS RETIRES. The record that would measure a contraction is no longer owed
for this purpose, so the thread closes as UNNECESSARY rather than blocked. The
192 declined field-records stand as the finding they were; they simply no longer
block a number.

WHAT IT COSTS AND WHAT IT BUYS. 6.86 records is most of a run's wall clock, so on
today's floors a run is 8600 spin-up in front of 1253 retained. That is worth
saying plainly: the spin-up is NOT a correctness requirement, because a residual
transient enters the very statistic the acceptance contract gates on and an
under-spun run is REFUSED rather than silently accepted. What the minimax buys is
that the run is not refused for that reason. Which is exactly the state
lpj_7d3c576ee4e342acb097b46fece976e0 is in: it carried 2318 cycles of spin-up and
is refused by cpool.out total carbon at 0.0503 against 0.05, on a drift living in
vegetation carbon.

That the spin-up dominates is what makes world-gqyp worth having -- LPJ-GUESS
supports save_state and restart and this project uses neither, so every refusal
re-buys the whole 8600.

title: The equilibrium tolerance is derived through one consumer quantity and applied to 64 fields, and it sizes the run
description:
`relative_end_to_end_limit` is derived through ONE consumer-facing quantity and applied to every assessed field, and for the per-PFT columns it sits below the model's own internal variability.

THE DERIVATION, in biosphere/notes/equilibrium-trend-null.md, runs through `exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_albedo.py --mode modelled`: it reads `fpc.out`, mixes tree and grass cover into the surface albedo, and a 5 per cent drift there is worth about +0.064 K of surface temperature. That chain is about AGGREGATE cover. The contract then applies the same 0.05 to all 64 assessed fields of the seven stability tables, including each plant functional type's own column in anpp, lai, fpc and aaet.

WHAT THAT COSTS, measured on lpj_7d3c576e's 1253-cycle record at fixed forcing. The relative scatter of a PFT's spatial-mean cycle series, about its own linear fit, runs to 0.12; the aggregates run 0.002 to 0.007. Under vesper-lpj-equilibrium-window/4's drift bound the record at which a settled field resolves 0.05 is:

  every Total column, every soil pool, the grasses     inside the 1253 on disk
  the woody PFT columns                                1400 to 16500 cycles
  binding field, aaet.out IBS                          16532 cycles

So the record the contract demands is set by a per-PFT quantity no consumer reads, at a tolerance derived for one that is. Ten of the assessed fields have a marginal scatter ABOVE 0.05 outright, which means their spatial mean wanders further than the tolerance at equilibrium: no record makes such a field's ten-cycle value stable to 5 per cent, and lengthening the record only makes the RECORD mean precise.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not an argument for a looser number, and it must not be settled by looking at what the current run needs -- that is choosing a criterion after the run it judges. The question is which quantities the acceptance claim is ABOUT, and it is answerable from the consumers: `build_surface_albedo.py` reads fpc tree and grass cover, `score_prediction.py` reads anpp, `build_soil.py` reads the soil carbon pool. A per-PFT column that no consumer reads and that no aggregate hides is a different claim from the one the tolerance was derived for, and it wants either its own derivation or removal from the assessed set.

DECIDE BEFORE the next long run is bought, because the assessed set is what sizes it: on the current set the record floor is about 16500 cycles, roughly four and a half hours at npatch 5 on 16 ranks, against about 1300 for the aggregates alone.

CITES: biosphere/notes/equilibrium-trend-null.md, biosphere/config/equilibrium_window.yaml, biosphere/config/lpj_acceptance.yaml (stability_outputs). Blocks nothing by itself; it changes what world-qcse's next run costs.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTRATION of the rule, and the order the work was done in.

THE RULE, derived from the consumer list and not from any measurement. The
acceptance claim is about the QUANTITIES A CONSUMER READS, so:

  1. The assessed set is the set of consumer quantities. A quantity is a table
     plus the columns a consumer sums, and a consumer forms it by summing --
     `build_surface_albedo.py` sums every non-grass column into tree cover and
     C3G+C4G into grass cover; `build_soil.py` reads the SoilC column;
     `score_prediction.py` reads anpp Total, lai Total, and fpc's tree, grass,
     C4G and boreal sums.
  2. A COLUMN THAT ENTERS A CONSUMER QUANTITY ONLY THROUGH A SUM OWES NOTHING
     BEYOND WHAT THE SUM OWES. The sum's own series carries that column's drift
     at its own share, with every cancellation and every reinforcement already
     in it, and the drift bound applied to the sum bounds the sum exactly.
     Bounding each column separately at the sum's tolerance is a strictly
     stronger claim than any consumer makes, and it is what the 27x buys.
  3. A quantity's tolerance is the TIGHTEST tolerance among the consumers that
     read it, each derived through that consumer's own chain.
  4. A column no consumer reads is not assessed. It keeps a reported drift
     bound as a diagnostic, so nothing is hidden, and the acceptance artifact
     stops claiming the biosphere has settled and claims what it measured.

THE TOLERANCES, one derivation each:

  build_surface_albedo.py --mode modelled -- fpc tree sum, fpc grass sum.
  0.05, and this is the derivation that already exists: a 5 per cent drift in
  both covers is worth about +0.064 K of surface temperature, bracketed +0.032
  to +0.128 K. It was always ABOUT these two quantities.

  build_soil.py -- cpool SoilC. 0.05, the tightest derived tolerance in the
  tree, applied to a quantity whose own chain (SoilC to organic fraction to
  volumetric water capacity to dwmax) has not been priced. Conservative and
  stated; it does not bind.

  score_prediction.py -- anpp Total, lai Total, fpc tree/grass/C4G/boreal sums.
  0.2727, DERIVED from the ten bands pre-registered in
  notes/productivity-prediction.md before the model ran a Vesper gridcell. A
  drift must not carry a value at the band centre out of the band, so the
  tolerance is the band's half-width over its centre; the tightest of the ten
  is 0.2727, set by line 3 (1.6 to 2.8) and line 5 (0.40 to 0.70). The loosest
  is 1.0. Reading the drift against the record MEAN rather than against any
  point in the record would double it; the stricter reading is taken.

WHAT IS NO LONGER ASSESSED, and it is the whole 27x: every per-PFT column of
anpp, lai, fpc and aaet; aaet and tot_runoff's Totals; cpool VegC and LitterC
and Total; npool's columns. The binding field was anpp.out TrBR at 33846
cycles and no consumer reads it.

THE ORDER THIS WAS DONE IN, because it decides whether the rule is a criterion
or a rationalisation. The consumer list was enumerated from the tree
(`require_lpj_acceptance` has exactly three callers) and the four rules above
were fixed BEFORE any aggregate was measured. The measurement then answered a
separate question -- whether the record on disk suffices -- and it did not
choose the rule. What the rule does NOT get to choose after the fact is
membership: cpool.out Total is the one field whose disposition the measurement
could have flipped, and it is settled on consumer grounds alone below.

CPOOL.OUT TOTAL. Its only reader is the carbon closure in
biosphere/config/lpj_acceptance.yaml, which compares the pool's change against
cflux NEE throughput. That is a CONSERVATION test and it holds whether or not
the pool is drifting, so it does not make Total a quantity read as a level.
Loop B's exit predicate is land-mean soil organic carbon, which is SoilC and is
assessed. So Total is not in the assessed set, and its drift bound is reported
as a diagnostic rather than removed.

WHAT I AM ABOUT TO MEASURE, and what would settle it: whether every assessed
quantity's drift bound falls inside its own tolerance on the 1253-cycle record
lpj_7d3c576ee4e342acb097b46fece976e0 already carries, and what
`cycles_for_bound` asks of the assessed set. That is what decides whether the
33846-cycle run is owed.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESOLVED. The tolerance is now per consumer quantity, derived, and the 33846-cycle
run is not owed.

WHAT SHIPPED, `vesper-lpj-equilibrium-window/5`. The contract declares an
`assessed` block of eleven CONSUMER QUANTITIES -- a table plus the columns a
consumer sums -- each with its own tolerance, its readers, and where that
tolerance came from. `trend.relative_end_to_end_limit` is the tightest of them
and `read_policy` refuses when it is not, because the spin-up floor is derived at
it. Both halves of the contract, the whole-record drift bound and the per-cell
slope, run on the quantities; every column keeps a bound as a diagnostic and the
artifact stops claiming the biosphere has settled.

THE DERIVATION, taken from the consumer list before anything was measured. A
column that enters a consumer quantity only through a sum owes nothing beyond
what the sum owes: the sum's own series carries that column's drift at its own
share, with every cancellation and every reinforcement in it, so the bound on the
sum bounds the sum exactly. Bounding each column separately at the sum's
tolerance is a strictly stronger claim than any consumer makes.

| consumer | quantity | tolerance | derivation |
| build_surface_albedo.py --mode modelled | fpc tree cover, grass cover | 0.05 | the albedo-to-temperature chain, which is ABOUT these two |
| build_soil.py | cpool SoilC | 0.05 | tightest in the tree, conservative on an unpriced chain |
| lpj_acceptance.yaml closure | cpool, npool, aaet, tot_runoff Totals | 0.05 | the same; the closure is a conservation test and imposes none |
| score_prediction.py | anpp Total, lai Total, fpc tree, grass, C4G, boreal | 0.2727 | tightest half-width over centre of the ten pre-registered bands |

WHAT IT MEASURED. Re-assessed under contract 5, lpj_7d3c576ee4e342acb097b46fece976e0
settles ten of the eleven on the 1253 cycles already on disk -- fpc tree cover at
0.0186 and grass cover at 0.0420 against 0.05, cpool SoilC at 0.0153, the closure
totals 0.0031 to 0.0194, the scoring quantities 0.0107 to 0.0744 against 0.2727.
The eleventh, cpool.out total carbon, bounds at 0.0503 against 0.05: a DRIFT
refusal and not a resolution failure, since a settled series of its scatter closes
inside the record it has. The drift lives in vegetation carbon (0.1495) while the
cover those woody types present has settled, which is what an under-spun run
leaves behind.

THE MECHANISM IS MEASURED AND NOT ASSUMED. fpc tree cover's relative scatter about
its own fit is 0.00807 against 0.0220 to 0.0290 for the woody columns it sums; the
boreal sum is 0.0167 against 0.0220 to 0.0267 for its three. The sum is quieter
than any of its parts, which is what a competitive shift looks like from outside.

THE TEST THAT CAN FAIL. `equilibrium_window_gate.py` builds two fixtures whose
columns drift at the same size, one cancelling in the sum and one not. Judged on
the sum a consumer forms the first is accepted and the second refused; judged
column by column both are refused. Plus: an exclusion that no longer describes its
table, a quantity with no reader, a declared limit that is not the tightest, and a
quantity naming its columns both ways -- all refusals. 46 checks, 0 failed.

THE RUN. 33846 retained cycles is not owed. The record floor is 1253, the record
on disk; with world-nhhm's spin-up that prices the next run at 9853 cycles, about
two and a half hours at npatch 5 on 16 ranks, against the seventy hours the old
assessed set implied. That purchase is world-qcse's and was not made here.

FILED: world-gqyp (no LPJ restart, so a refusal re-buys the whole spin-up),
world-cqoc (five quantities carry the tightest-in-tree tolerance rather than a
derived one).

title: build_groundwater.py prefers the baseline climatology while surface_water.py is pinned to the bootstrap, so the groundwater step refuses on any build that has a baseline
description:
On canonical-10m-carve2, `python hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater.py` with no arguments exits without solving:

  hydrography/data/canonical-10m-carve2/surface_water.nc was forced by
  exoplasim/analysis/climatology/bootstrap_regular_climatology.nc and this run
  resolved .../baseline_regular_climatology.nc as the baseline climatology.

build_groundwater.py:385 calls `best_available_climatology`, which returns the baseline once config/planet.yaml names one; surface_water.py:525 calls `bootstrap_climatology_path`, which cannot return anything else. The coupling guard at build_groundwater.py:390-409 then refuses, correctly, because the lakes and the water table are the surface and subsurface halves of one water balance. So the step is unrunnable with its own defaults from the moment a baseline exists, which it now does (run_67323a923013, vesper_source_build canonical-10m-carve2).

The guard names two routes and only one is reachable. `re-run surface_water on this climatology` cannot be done: surface_water.py takes no --climatology and hardcodes the bootstrap resolver. `pass --climatology` is the only route, and it forces the water table onto the bootstrap.

WHICH SIDE IS WRONG IS THE DECISION, and it is not obvious from the tree.

config/planet.yaml says the bootstrap 'exists to produce the climate the derived fields -- lakes, soil, soil water, dust, sea salt, the biosphere calendar -- are built FROM'. That names lakes as a bootstrap consumer by design, which says surface_water.py's pin is deliberate and build_groundwater.py's preference is the defect: the subsurface half of a balance whose surface half is declared bootstrap-derived cannot prefer a different climate.

Against that, build_groundwater.py's own comment argues recharge is a function of the climate STATE and the bootstrap is the best answer only on the pass where it is the only one, which is CLAUDE.md's loop agreement stated exactly.

Both cannot hold. Whichever way it goes, the two scripts must resolve through ONE rule, and scripts/smoke_test.py's check of each step's declared need against the resolver its script calls does not catch this because each script is individually consistent with its own step's `needs`; the inconsistency is BETWEEN two steps that the guard, and only the guard, knows are one balance.

Evidence: reproduced 2026-08-30 on canonical-10m-carve2. config/pipeline.yaml declares `surface_water needs bootstrap_climatology` and `groundwater needs bootstrap_climatology`, so the GRAPH says bootstrap for both and only build_groundwater.py's resolver disagrees with the graph.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESOLVED 2026-08-30. THE PIN WAS THE DEFECT, and the tree already carried the decision procedure that says so.

lib/paths.py:best_available_climatology states the test in its own docstring: a step reads the best available where its answer depends on the climate STATE, and bootstrap_climatology_path where it depends only on the model calendar or the grid. A lake extent is solved from P-E, routed runoff and open-water evaporation and from nothing else, so it is a climate-state quantity and the resolver contract already required the best available. scripts/smoke_test.py carries the same rule in check 'each step resolves a climatology its needs permit', which permits BOTH resolvers for a bootstrap_climatology step precisely because only a reader can say which of the two a given answer depends on. That is why the disagreement was invisible to the gate.

WHAT SETTLED IT RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. config/planet.yaml names six derived surface fields the bootstrap exists to produce: lakes, soil, soil water, dust, sea salt, the biosphere calendar. Three of them already read the best available -- aeolian/scripts/build_dust.py, build_sea_salt.py and build_volcanic_sulfate.py -- so membership of that list was never a pin. surface_water.py was the last of the group still hardcoded, and its comment argued a circularity that applies identically to the three that had already moved.

THE CIRCULARITY IS THE LOOP. On a later pass the lakes are forced by a climate their own extent helped produce. That is true of every derived surface field and is what makes loop A a loop; a step pinned to the bootstrap forever is right on the first pass and holds the loop back on every pass after, which is CLAUDE.md's agreement stated exactly.

WHAT CHANGED. surface_water.py resolves through best_available_climatology, unpacks the stage, and stamps climatology_stage on both surface_water.nc and its report, which smoke_test requires of anything built through that resolver. The needs: bootstrap_climatology edge is UNCHANGED, because the edge says which artifact must exist for a first pass and that is still the bootstrap. 73 checks, 0 failed; the seven basin-to-region identity checks in --selftest still pass.

CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE LOOP ASKING TO TURN RATHER THAN A REGRESSION. The surface_water.nc on canonical-10m-carve2 was forced by the bootstrap and now carries a stage the resolver would not choose, so the coupling guard will refuse a default groundwater run until the lakes are re-solved on the baseline. That refusal is correct and is the guard doing its job: it says the lakes are from the earlier climate. Re-running surface_water is a loop-A step with downstream consequences and was not taken here.

A SECOND DEFECT FOUND ALONGSIDE AND FIXED IN BOTH SCRIPTS. Each resolved the climatology before naming it. A worktree links the climatology payload in from the main checkout, so resolve() follows the link out of the project root, rel() can only return an absolute path, and the guard compared that against a repo-relative forcing stamp. It never matched: the groundwater step refused in EVERY worktree even when both halves named the same file, and would have stamped water_table.nc with a path no other tree has. hydrography/analysis/groundwater_report.json on disk carries such an absolute forcing, which is the defect's own fingerprint. Both scripts now name by the declared path and read by the resolved one, and the identity compares the two forcings as FILES rather than as spellings.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
CONFIRMED AFTER THE FIX, 2026-08-30. Running build_groundwater.py with no arguments on canonical-10m-carve2 now refuses like this:

  hydrography/data/canonical-10m-carve2/surface_water.nc was forced by exoplasim/analysis/climatology/bootstrap_regular_climatology.nc and this run resolved exoplasim/analysis/climatology/baseline_regular_climatology.nc as the baseline climatology.

Two things changed and both matter. Both paths are now repo-relative, where before the fix the second was an absolute path into the main checkout and the comparison could never match in a worktree whatever the two forcings were. And the remedy the message offers -- re-run surface_water on this climatology -- is now a thing a reader can actually do: surface_water.py resolves through the same resolver, so re-running it lands on the baseline and the two halves agree. Before the fix that sentence named an action the script it pointed at could not perform, since surface_water.py took no --climatology default other than the bootstrap.

The refusal that remains is the loop asking to be turned rather than the defect: the lakes on disk are from the earlier climate and say so.

title: A worktree loses every untracked artifact it creates in a mixed-tracking directory
description:
scripts/link_worktree.py links ignored payloads into a worktree. For a directory holding ONLY untracked content it makes a DIRECTORY SYMLINK -- biosphere/runs is one -- so a write from the worktree reaches the main checkout. For a directory holding tracked content BESIDE untracked payloads it cannot do that, so it makes a real directory containing one symlink PER EXISTING FILE.

The consequence is silent and one-signed: a NEW untracked file created in such a directory from inside a worktree is a real file in the worktree and nowhere else. It is untracked, so it is never committed. When the worktree is removed the file is gone, while any TRACKED record referring to it survives and outlives its own artifact.

MEASURED. references/ has this shape. Thirteen rows in references/INDEX.md cite a pdf by filename that is not on disk, eleven of them marked read and several carrying extracted numbers; two are load-bearing on live model constants, jackson_1996 for the cumulative root-depth equation and beta values LPJ-GUESS uses, and pilegaard_2013 for the aerobic/anaerobic split and NO share ntransform.cpp cites. The papers were fetched by agents inside worktrees, the INDEX rows were committed, and the pdfs died with the worktrees.

THE SAME SHAPE EXISTS IN TWO MORE PLACES and neither is bookkeeping:
  exoplasim/runs/   1 tracked file (INDEX.json) beside untracked run payloads
  source/          35 tracked READMEs beside the export payloads

A model run or an Orogen export payload generated inside a worktree is lost the same way, which is a rule 7 hazard: what the world is reconstructed from would vanish while the record saying it exists is committed.

TWO DISPOSITIONS, and they are complementary rather than alternatives.

STRUCTURAL, where it is cheap: move the untracked bulk into a subdirectory that holds nothing else, so link_worktree.py can give it a directory symlink. For references/ that is references/pdf/, and the change is a path prefix on INDEX.md's filename column plus its consumers. world-26d0 removes four tracked trees from the same directory and should land first or together.

DETECTION, everywhere: link_worktree.py --check should report untracked files sitting in a per-file-linked directory, because those are files that will die with the worktree. This is what covers source/ and exoplasim/runs/, where moving the payload is invasive and the guard is not.
acceptance_criteria: A pdf, a run payload or an export payload created inside a worktree either reaches the main checkout or is reported by link_worktree.py --check before the worktree is removed. The check names the file and says why it is about to be lost.
notes: Established 2026-08-30 by inspecting the link shape directly: biosphere/runs is a directory symlink, references/, source/ and exoplasim/runs are real directories of per-file symlinks. The user proposed the same explanation independently. A sweep of all 84 worktrees found 21 real pdfs, all of whose basenames already exist in the main checkout, so nothing is orphaned right now. Do the structural half with no agent holding a worktree.
close_reason: Both halves are in. Detection shipped with the recovery pass: link_worktree.py:258 stranded() reports ignored payload living only in the worktree, covering source/ and exoplasim/runs/ where the payload cannot be separated from the tracked index. Structural repair for references/: the papers are under references/pdf/, a directory of pure payload that a worktree links as one symlink. Verified by probe -- a pdf written inside a worktree IS in the main checkout, and a loose file at references/ top level is still named by --check. INDEX.md untouched; it cites by bare filename, so the resolver moved instead, which also stops a pdf inside an external source tree standing in for a paper of the same name.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
DETECTION HALF DONE, in scripts/link_worktree.py itself. Commit 5de7826e6.

link_worktree.py now reports ignored payload that exists only in the worktree, and --check exits 1 on it. It walks the worktree skipping symlinked directories, .git, .claude, __pycache__ and the three held-back classes (a worktree building its own vendor/exoplasim is the arrangement, not the failure), keeps every real path the main checkout has nothing at, and passes the candidates through one `git check-ignore --stdin` call -- because a candidate git would happily commit is ordinary new work and not this failure. A directory the main checkout does not have at all is reported whole and not descended, so a stranded run is one line rather than thousands.

It fails --check for the same reason a misdirected link does: nothing is absent, so every existing count comes out complete while the worktree holds artifacts that die with it, and --check is where a caller asks whether a worktree can be thrown away. Reported and never moved -- whether a file belongs in the main checkout is a judgement this script does not make.

EXERCISED BOTH WAYS. A clean worktree passes. A probe pdf under references/ and a probe run directory under exoplasim/runs/ are both caught, the run directory as one line. verify_entry_points.py and smoke_test.py pass.

THE STRUCTURAL HALF IS NOT DONE and is still world-26d0's to unblock.

THE THIRTEEN PAPERS ARE ALL HELD AGAIN, under the filenames INDEX.md asserts: eight through paperfetch from open-access routes, five supplied by hand after every automated route refused them. Every quoted number in every recovered row was re-checked against its file. One did not verify: 13.8 is not in Reich and Oleksyn (2004) -- it is Yuan et al. (2011)'s summary statistic OF that compilation, and the row now says so. Eight of the thirteen are read by code or config rather than prose alone.

Evidence, with the per-directory link shapes, the recovery table and what refused each of the five: notes/audits/worktree-stranded-payload.md.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 THE DETECTION HALF IS ALREADY SHIPPED. scripts/link_worktree.py:258 stranded() reports ignored payload that exists only in the worktree, wired into --check at :391, and it covers source/ and exoplasim/runs/ as well as references/ -- which is the half that matters where moving the payload is invasive. It was exercised both ways: a probe PDF and a probe run directory are both caught, and it cleared six dangling links on the way.

So what remains on this row is the STRUCTURAL half for references/ only.

SCOPE, measured rather than estimated:
- references/INDEX.md cites 381 pdfs BY BARE FILENAME, not by path, so the index itself needs no edit. Only the resolver in scripts/check_reference_index.py changes directory.
- 38 citations elsewhere write the path references/<file>.pdf, across 15 files. The heaviest are biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml (10) and notes/audits/cryosphere-material-properties.md (9); the rest are ones and twos.
- .gitignore's references/*.pdf becomes a directory rule, which is what lets link_worktree.py make a DIRECTORY symlink instead of a per-file one.
- CLAUDE.md's layout line for references/ states the current shape and has to state the new one.

ALSO PERTINENT, from the recovery pass: all 13 stranded papers are back, every quoted number was re-checked against its file, and one citation was wrong -- 13.8 was attributed to Reich and Oleksyn (2004), which prints no grand mean N:P; it is Yuan et al. (2011)'s statistic of that compilation. scripts/smoke_test.py now checks per commit that every filename the index asserts is on disk.

ONE THING THE MOVE WILL CARRY ALONG, flagged rather than fixed: references/ holds 7 short-name duplicates of long-named rows. Four are byte-equivalent (goll2012, reich2004, yang2011, yuan2011); romps2014.pdf is a legitimate article beside its supplement; parton2010.pdf is the PUBLISHED JGR version where the long name holds the manuscript, and the row's claim that it contains no phosphorus was verified against BOTH; and yang2013.pdf is a mis-fetch holding a Spanish-language review of primary-school attainment. None but romps is cited. They are untracked with no history, so nothing is deleted without the author saying so.

title: Nothing gates the LPJ-GUESS binary against the source it was built from
description:
The derived-spin-up run refused to start: the built binary at vendor/lpj-guess/build/guess dated 2026-08-28 09:26 did not know frac_labile_carbon_humus, which framework/parameters.cpp declares and data/ins/global_soiln.ins sets. Source files dated 2026-08-30 14:36 and 14:55 had never been compiled. The failure was loud only because the parameter reaches the model through an instruction file, so the parser refused an undefined identifier. A change confined to C++ -- a constant, a rate law, one of the five ntransform divergences -- would have run silently on a binary that did not contain it, and every number out of it would have been attributed to source the run never executed.

CLAUDE.md rule 4 states exactly this hazard for ExoPlaSim and exoplasim/scripts/verify_model_compiles.py --verify compares each executable against the sha of the source it was built from. The biosphere has no equivalent: no gate, no recorded source hash on the binary, and run_lpj_guess.py records the BINARY's hash in the manifest, which pins what ran but cannot say whether it matches the tree.

Do: give the LPJ-GUESS binary the same treatment ExoPlaSim's has. Record the source sha at build time and check it before a run starts, so a stale binary refuses rather than runs.
acceptance_criteria: A stale vendor/lpj-guess build refuses a run or fails a gate, naming the source files that are newer than the binary. The check runs where the ExoPlaSim equivalent runs.
notes: Found 2026-08-30 launching the world-qcse derived-spin-up run. Rebuild took under two minutes with cmake --build vendor/lpj-guess/build --parallel 16, so the cost of the guard is the cost of noticing, not the cost of the build.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Guard built and exercised on branch worktree-agent-a4f2143f6384fdad1 (commits 2a5b261d4, 3822cb542, 6410e9c5b, abffa8641).

DESIGN: content shas recorded at build time, checked statically before every run.

vendor/lpj-guess/build/guess.provenance.json: the executable's sha256 beside the
sha of each of the 124 files it was compiled from -- the four subdirectory
CMakeLists' declared headers/source lists, the closure over quoted #include from
them (which is what reaches the generated, gitignored framework/vesper.h), the
build files themselves, and the compiler and cmake cache entries. --verify
compares that record against the tree and builds nothing.

REJECTED: mtimes ('refuse on a binary older than its newest source'), because a
git checkout or link_worktree.py rewrites the mtime of a file whose bytes did not
move, so it refuses correct builds, and a binary copied in carries the mtime of
the copy and passes against any source. Content shas subsume it; mtimes survive
only as the human aid in the refusal text. Also REJECTED: rebuild-as-the-check,
on two grounds -- a rule 8 tier violation for a check that must sit in front of
every run, and a rebuild replaces the executable whose sha a concurrent run's
manifest has already hashed, so the gate would mutate the artifact it judges.

RECORD LOCATION: beside the binary, untracked, on the .provenance.json convention
prepare_stock_ntransform_arm.py already established in this component, rather
than a tracked manifest. The binary is untracked and per-worktree (build/ is
deliberately not linked by link_worktree.py) and this build is not known to be
path-reproducible, so ExoPlaSim's reason for tracking its manifest does not carry
over.

TIER: both, at the two points ExoPlaSim splits after world-anl.
- scripts/check_consistency.py (expensive tier) asks build_lpj_guess.verify().
  It reads artifacts -- an untracked binary and the generated header -- so it is
  a check_consistency question and not a smoke_test one; a fresh checkout has no
  binary and a per-commit gate over it would be red on a coherent tree.
  Reports WARN 'not built', FAIL when stale.
- run_lpj_guess.py and verify_lpj_restart_continuity.py both REFUSE at launch,
  because the gate is not run before every run and the binary can move between
  the two. Those two are the whole set of scripts that spawn the model.

The build-file restatement (SUBDIRS/ENTRY/INCLUDE_DIRS) is checked INSIDE
verify(), so a CMakeLists that grew a fifth source directory fails rather than
letting a short source set pass a stale binary.

title: Gate biosphere/config/fire.yaml: the fire divergence is declared but not enforced
description:
biosphere/config/fire.yaml registers one declared divergence from mainline LPJ-GUESS 4.1.1 -- the deletion of GlobFIRM's 0.001 burn-probability floor in modules/vegdynam.cpp under world-v5j1 -- and nothing reads it. The other three registers in biosphere/config/ each have a gate: ntransform_gate.py, somdynam_gate.py and snow_thermal_gate.py. Until this one does, the divergence can be silently reverted by an upstream pull or an editor and no check fires, which is the exact failure vendored-upstreams.md says the gates exist to prevent.

The register was written gate-ready. The entry declares mainline_form: deleted_line, which is a shape none of the existing gates handle: a deletion has no live line to look for. The check is the mainline half plus an absence.

What a biosphere/scripts/fire_gate.py has to assert, per entry:
  1. every string in mainline appears in the source file verbatim, so the record cannot go missing;
  2. every string in mainline is ABSENT from the source once // comments are stripped, so a silent revert fails;
  3. for mainline_form: deleted_line, every string in absent_from_stripped is also absent from the stripped source, so a reformatted revert fails too;
  4. for a normal entry, live appears in the stripped source.
All four hold on the tree as it stands, checked by hand against vegdynam.cpp.

It also belongs in scripts/smoke_test.py beside the other three gates, since every check in it is a static read.

Not done under world-v5j1 because biosphere/scripts/ was outside that task's declared file scope.

Evidence: biosphere/config/fire.yaml, docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md section 'GlobFIRM's burn probability diverges from the RELEASE'.
