title: The equilibrium trend test needs a statistic valid at this model's memory time
description:
vesper-lpj-equilibrium-window/3's memory-adequacy guard fails closed on every run this project has, which is correct and is why the trend test beneath it is currently unreachable. That test is not valid at any window this model supports and needs replacing, not rethresholding.

WHAT IS MEASURED AND SETTLED (biosphere/notes/equilibrium-trend-null.md):
- The integrated autocorrelation time of the assessed spatial-mean series is 9.3 to 125.3 complete forcing cycles; the window is 10. A slope fitted inside one memory time sees one smooth excursion, its residuals are small because the process is smooth on that scale, and the measured per-cell flag rate is 0.47 to 0.86 against a nominal 0.081.
- Inflating the ordinary least-squares standard error by the square root of tau recovers only 0.19 to 0.46. The correction is for a MEAN over a span and cannot make a span shorter than its memory carry a trend.
- Contract 2's empirical per-field null cannot control the family rate: it measured 0.34 against a declared 0.05, and an empirical null would need about 710 windows and 7100 retained cycles to express 0.05.

THE SHAPE OF THE REPLACEMENT, and it must be analytic rather than empirical. A candidate was built and validated far enough to be promising and not far enough to ship: compare two half-record means of each field's spatial-mean series against the standard error lib/autocorrelation.py gives for a mean over a series with memory, with the per-field significance derived from a declared FAMILY rate by a Sidak correction over a family size counted from lpj_acceptance.yaml:stability_outputs rather than declared. Measured family refusal rate 0.040 against a declared 0.05, power 0.31 at the contract's own drift limit and 0.92 at twice it.

THREE SUBTLETIES ALREADY FOUND, so they are not rediscovered:
1. The difference of two half-means is HALF the end-to-end change for a steady drift. Left unscaled it silently doubles relative_end_to_end_limit. Scale by two; the significance ratio is unaffected because the standard error scales with it.
2. lib/autocorrelation.py's RELIABLE_SPAN_MULTIPLE belongs on the span whose mean is being taken -- the half -- not on the whole record. Applied to the record, a half carries five effective samples at the bar and the measured family rate was 0.23 against a declared 0.05.
3. Guarding on an estimated tau and then using that same estimate for the standard error selects for underestimates and is anti-conservative near the bar. A conservative upper bound on tau, or a guard estimated independently of the series used for the test, is needed.

DO NOT re-derive the timescales; they are measured and reproducible with biosphere/scripts/derive_trend_null.py --timescales. What is owed is a statistic whose size is validated against a known answer across the measured tau range, and whose power is stated at the contract's own drift limit.

Blocks world-qcse's acceptance criterion and, through it, world-cp27.
close_reason: Resolved. The equilibrium test is an upper confidence bound on each field's end-to-end relative drift over the whole retained record, passed when the bound is inside the tolerance (vesper-lpj-equilibrium-window/4, lib/lpj_output.py:drift_bound). Reversing the direction from 'fail to reject no drift' to 'bound the drift' removes the multiplicity correction by intersection-union, removes the separate span guard because the test fails closed on its own, and gives a record floor that converges where the span multiple twice did not. Size validated on 2000 AR(1) trials per cell against the registered bar of 0.075: the registered form missed it from a memory time of 213 upward, rule 2 fired, and at the upper end of the memory time's own sampling interval it holds 0.000 to 0.033 across 1 to 400 against a declared 0.05. Power at the contract's own drift limit is reported and the significance form this row proposed is measured beside it, passing a drifting run about 93 times in 100 on this model's slowest fields. One registered check misses and is recorded as a miss. Follow-ons filed: world-4hlw, world-mxmr.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 DECLINED FOR NOW, WITH THE CONDITION THAT LIFTS IT, and the reason is not
caution about the design. It is that the statistic's validation covers a regime this
model is not in.

WHAT WAS VALIDATED. The candidate -- two half-record means compared against
`lib/autocorrelation.py`'s memory-corrected standard error, with the per-field
significance DERIVED from a declared family rate by a Sidak correction over a family
size counted from lpj_acceptance.yaml rather than declared -- measured a family
refusal rate of 0.040 against a declared 0.05, with power 0.31 at the contract's own
drift limit and 0.92 at twice it. That was on synthetic AR(1) fields with memory times
drawn from 2 to 40 cycles on a 1000-cycle record.

WHY THAT IS NOT ENOUGH. The measured memory times of the fields it would judge are 9.3
to 125.3 cycles. Above 40 the same validation returns a family refusal rate of 0.23
against the declared 0.05, and the cause is subtlety 3 already on this row: guarding on
an estimated tau and then using that same estimate for the standard error selects for
underestimates, which understate the error. So the validated domain stops well below the
range the statistic would be used in, and the gap is not a margin -- it is a factor of
five in the false-refusal rate.

WHAT LIFTS IT, and it is now a derived number rather than a wish. world-r9nz's spin-up
derivation asks for a 2318-cycle spin-up and a 1253-cycle retained record, 3571 cycles
in all, about 55 minutes at npatch 5. On a record that long every measured memory time
up to 125 has at least 14 effective samples per half, which is inside the bar the
validation held at, and the regime the statistic was validated in is the regime the
model would be in. Subtlety 3 is also cheaper to fix there: a record that long can
estimate tau on one half and test on the other, which removes the selection entirely
rather than bounding it.

SO THE ORDER IS: buy the run, then validate the statistic on the record it produces,
then ship it. Shipping it first would mean validating on a regime the model is not in,
which is the same class of error as the instrument this row exists to replace -- and I
would rather not repair a class-34 defect by committing another one.

This is a judgement about evidence, not about the delegator's ask; the design is on this
row in full, with all three subtleties, so whoever takes it after the long run does not
start from nothing.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 PRE-REGISTERED, BEFORE ANY OF IT IS MEASURED: THE FORM OF THE
REPLACEMENT, ITS VALIDATION, AND THE RULE THAT PICKS BETWEEN TWO CANDIDATES.

WHY THE FORM ON THIS ROW IS NOT THE ONE I AM SHIPPING FIRST. The candidate
here is a SIGNIFICANCE test: reject the null of no drift, with the per-field
level set from a declared family rate by Sidak. That controls the rate at
which a SETTLED run is refused. An acceptance gate's job is the other error:
it must not let a DRIFTING run through. The correct instrument for "prove
this has settled" is an EQUIVALENCE test -- an upper confidence bound on the
drift, passed when that bound falls below the tolerance -- and switching the
direction removes three of this row's four difficulties at once:

* MULTIPLICITY DISAPPEARS. A run passes only if every assessed field passes,
  so by the intersection-union principle the run-level false-ACCEPTANCE rate
  is bounded by the per-field level with NO correction. The Sidak factor, the
  counted family size and the 0.34 family rate that killed contract /2 are all
  gone, and they are gone by a derivation rather than by a longer record.
* THE GUARD DISAPPEARS. A record too short to resolve the tolerance gives a
  wide bound, the bound exceeds the limit, and the field is refused. Failing
  closed is the test's own behaviour rather than a separate memory-adequacy
  gate ahead of it, so there is no second span rule to be self-referential.
* THE RECORD FLOOR CONVERGES. The length that answers a refused field is the n
  at which its bound falls below the limit, and the bound falls as 1/sqrt(n)
  while tau grows sublinearly with n. "n >= 10 tau(n)" does not converge and
  has now failed twice; this does.

Subtleties 1 and 2 on this row are load-bearing in both forms and are carried:
the half-to-half difference is doubled so it estimates the END-TO-END change,
and the span bar belongs on the half whose mean is taken. Subtlety 3 is
answered differently: there is no tau-based guard to select on, tau is taken as
the LARGER of the two halves' estimates (selection toward overestimates, which
is conservative here), and sigma and tau are estimated on the RAW half rather
than a detrended one, so a real drift inflates the error rather than shrinking
it.

THE STATISTIC, per assessed field, on the spatial-mean cycle series x[0..n-1]:

  m = n // 2;  H1 = x[0:m], H2 = x[n-m:n]
  tau  = max(integrated_time(H1).tau, integrated_time(H2).tau)
  v_i  = var(H_i, ddof=1) * tau / m                     (lib/autocorrelation.py)
  D    = 2 * (mean(H2) - mean(H1))          end-to-end change, subtlety 1
  seD  = 2 * sqrt(v1 + v2)
  scale = max(|mean(x)|, absolute_scale_floor)
  R, seR = |D| / scale, seD / scale
  df   = Welch on v1, v2 at m/tau - 1 degrees of freedom each, floored at 1
  U    = R + t.isf(alpha, df) * seR          one-sided upper bound on the drift
  PASS the field iff U <= relative_end_to_end_limit.

alpha is DECLARED as `maximum_false_acceptance_rate: 0.05` and is what the
contract controls, per field and, by intersection-union, per run.

VALIDATION, all on synthetic AR(1) of length 1253 -- this run's own record --
with tau swept over 1, 10, 20, 40, 80, 125, 175, 213, 300, 400, covering and
exceeding the measured 11.1 to 212.7. 2000 trials per point.

  A. SIZE, the controlled quantity: inject a true end-to-end relative drift of
     exactly relative_end_to_end_limit and measure the share of trials the
     field PASSES. PASS BAR, FIXED NOW: at most 0.075 at every swept tau. The
     Monte-Carlo standard error at 0.05 on 2000 trials is 0.0049, so 0.075 is
     five standard errors and is a failure rather than noise.
  B. COST, reported and not barred: zero drift, the share refused. This is what
     sizes the record and it is the number that decides whether a longer run is
     owed.
  C. KNOWN ANSWER, so the harness can fail: at tau = 1 the construction must
     reproduce the textbook two-sample t, size 0.05 within Monte-Carlo error;
     and the estimated tau must recover the AR(1) truth (1+r)/(1-r) inside the
     estimator's own reliable regime. A harness that cannot reproduce an answer
     it already knows is not a validation.
  D. THIS MODEL'S NUMBERS: A and B repeated with the per-field sigma and tau
     measured on lpj_7d3c576e's own 1253-cycle record, so the reported cost is
     this model's and not a synthetic's.
  E. The row's SIGNIFICANCE candidate is measured on the SAME trials for size
     and for power at 1x and 2x the limit, and reported whatever happens.

DECISION RULE, FIXED NOW.

  1. Arm A passes at every swept tau -> the equivalence form ships as
     vesper-lpj-equilibrium-window/4.
  2. Arm A fails -> tau is replaced by the upper end of its own sampling
     interval and A is re-measured ONCE under the same bar. Passing ships;
     failing means no analytic form is validated on this record, and the
     finding is reported with no contract change.
  3. The significance form ships only if the equivalence form fails and the
     significance form holds a family false-refusal rate at or below 0.08 at
     every swept tau.
  4. THE RECORD FLOOR replaces `lib/run_lengths.py:ecological_record_cycles`'s
     span multiple: it is the smallest n at which every assessed field's bound
     falls below the limit at its own measured sigma and tau, computed by the
     same code that runs the test. If any field needs more than the record on
     disk, the length is REPORTED and no run is launched.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and why the scope line is here. The PER-CELL half stays
exactly as contract /3 has it: a 10-cycle window, a slope fit, and a per-field
limit measured from the run's own detrended windows. It answers a different
question -- spatially incoherent drift that leaves the spatial mean flat -- and
its empirical-null construction needs many windows, which the whole-record
statistic above cannot supply, so the two are not interchangeable and the
replacement is a second piece of design. What is stated with it is what it is:
its slope fit still sits inside one memory time, its size is absorbed into a
per-run limit rather than derived, and its family false-refusal rate is about
0.24 on a 1253-cycle record. It errs toward REFUSING, so a pass through it is
evidence and a refusal through it is not, and its verdict on this run is
reported whatever it is. A row is filed for its analytic replacement.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-31 PRE-REGISTERED ADDENDUM, BEFORE THE ARITHMETIC IS TAKEN: THE
REPORTED WINDOW IS THE SAME DEFECT AS THE TEST SPAN AND GETS THE SAME TEST.

Building /4 exposed a span I had scoped out and should not have. The contract
now certifies the WHOLE RETAINED RECORD and reports a mean over the LAST TEN
CYCLES, and it is the reported mean that `build_surface_albedo.py`,
`score_prediction.py` and `build_soil.py` actually consume. A ten-cycle mean of
a series whose memory time is tens to hundreds of cycles is one effective
sample, so its own sampling error may be larger than the drift the contract
refuses -- in which case the gate certifies a state to 5 per cent and hands the
consumer a number that is not known to 5 per cent. That is failure-modes class
34 pointed at the value rather than at the test.

THE TEST, and it uses no threshold that was not already declared. For each
assessed field, the relative standard error of the REPORTED window mean is
sigma_rel * sqrt(max(tau, window) / window) at the field's own scatter and
memory time -- the max because a window shorter than one memory time carries
one effective sample and cannot do better than the marginal scatter. Compare it
with `relative_end_to_end_limit`, which is 0.05 and was declared long before
any of this.

DECISION RULE, FIXED NOW.

* If NO assessed field's reported-window standard error exceeds the limit, the
  reported window stays at `complete_forcing_cycles` and nothing changes.
* If ANY field's does, the reported window is the same defect as the test span
  was, and the reported mean and temporal spread move to the whole retained
  record -- the span the contract certifies. The per-cell half keeps
  `complete_forcing_cycles`, because its empirical null is built from windows
  and needs many of them.

THE INPUTS ARE ALREADY ON THIS ROW and were measured before this rule was
written: the per-field scatter and memory time are what `--timescales` reports
and what the validation harness reads off the record. What is new here is only
the comparison and what it decides, and both are stated before either is taken.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-31 THE JUDGEMENT THE ROW ASKED FOR, SETTLED ON THE MEASUREMENT AND
INDEPENDENT OF THE VALIDATION STILL RUNNING: THE PER-FIELD WINDOW IS NOT THE
REPAIR, AND NEITHER IS ANY OTHER SPAN MULTIPLE.

The three options were the statistic alone, the statistic plus a per-field
window of ten times that field's own memory time, or something else. It is the
third, and the per-field window is specifically wrong for three reasons.

1. IT PUTS ONE TABLE'S FIELDS ON DIFFERENT TEMPORAL SUPPORTS. A window of ten
times each field's own memory time gives anpp.out's TrBR column 1698 cycles and
its C3G column 120, so the Total column stops being the sum of its parts over
the same span. `lib/spatial_support.py` exists because a support is an identity.

2. IT DOES NOT CONVERGE, AND MAKING IT PER FIELD MAKES 64 OF THAT. The span
multiple asks for a span ten times a memory time read off the record itself, and
the memory time this model reports grows with the window it is read on: 9.3 to
125.3 cycles on the 1000-cycle diagnostic implied 1253, and the 1253-cycle
record it bought reads 11.1 to 212.7 and implies 2127. Six of the seven fields
above the bar are marked NOT reliable by the estimator, so 212.7 is a floor too.

3. IT ANSWERS THE WRONG QUESTION. `RELIABLE_SPAN_MULTIPLE` asks whether the
MEMORY TIME can be ESTABLISHED. What an acceptance gate needs to know is whether
the TOLERANCE can be RESOLVED. Ask the second question and the window, the
guard and the multiplicity correction all dissolve into the statistic:

  * The test is an upper confidence bound on the end-to-end relative drift over
    the whole record, and a field passes when the bound is inside the tolerance.
  * A record too short to resolve the tolerance gives a wide bound and is
    refused BY THE TEST. There is no guard in front of it to be self-referential.
  * A run passes only when every field passes, so by intersection-union the
    run-level rate of accepting a field that truly drifts at the tolerance is
    the per-field rate with NO correction. The Sidak factor, the counted family
    size and contract 2's measured 0.34 family rate are gone by a derivation.
  * The length that answers a refusal is the record at which the bound closes,
    which falls as one over the root of the record while the memory time grows
    sublinearly with it. That converges where the span multiple did not.

AND THE 57-OF-64 SPLIT IS NOT THE OPERATIVE ONE. Under a valid statistic the
split is about SCATTER, not about memory time. What a record has to see through
is a field's own standard error on the drift, which is its relative scatter
times the root of its memory time over the half length -- so cpool.out Total, at
a memory time of 212.7 and a relative scatter of 0.0055, is resolved on the
1253-cycle record already on disk, while aaet.out IBS, at a memory time of 95.1
and a relative scatter of 0.0672, is not resolved until about 16500. The fields
that cannot be judged are the woody plant functional types' own columns, whose
spatial means wander further than the tolerance; every aggregate and every slow
pool is inside the record on disk.

SO THE ANSWER TO "DO SEVEN FIELDS NEED A LONGER RUN" IS NO, AND IT IS WORSE
THAN THAT: on the assessed set as it stands, about twenty-six do, and the
binding one needs roughly thirteen times the record rather than 1.7 times it.
That is about four and a half hours of retained record at npatch 5 on 16 ranks,
plus a spin-up. NO RUN HAS BEEN LAUNCHED.

WHAT DECIDES WHETHER THAT RUN IS THE RIGHT PURCHASE is world-mxmr, filed for it:
the tolerance is derived through ONE consumer-facing quantity, aggregate tree
and grass cover feeding the surface albedo, and the contract applies its number
to all 64 assessed fields including every per-PFT column. The assessed set is
what sizes the run, so it is decided before the run is bought and not after.
Ten of the assessed fields have a marginal scatter above the tolerance outright,
which means their spatial mean wanders further than the tolerance AT
equilibrium: no record makes such a field's value stable to 5 per cent, and a
longer record only makes the RECORD mean precise.

Shipped as `vesper-lpj-equilibrium-window/4`. The validation of the statistic's
size and cost against series whose answer is known by construction is running
under the host lock and its numbers follow.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-31 MEASURED, AGAINST THE BAR REGISTERED BEFORE IT WAS RUN. SHIPPED AS
`vesper-lpj-equilibrium-window/4`.

ARM A, THE RATE THE CONTRACT DECLARES: the share of trials that ACCEPT a field
whose true end-to-end drift is exactly the tolerance. 2000 AR(1) trials per
cell, 1253 cycles, relative scatter 0.02, declared 0.05, registered bar 0.075.

  memory time      1     10     20     40     80    125    175    213    300    400
  as registered  .000   .012   .020   .037   .051   .053   .068   .080   .099   .109
  after rule 2   .000   .004   .005   .011   .018   .020   .027   .028   .031   .033

THE REGISTERED FORM MISSED THE BAR at 213, 300 and 400 -- and 213 is the top of
the range this model is actually in, so the miss is inside the domain and not
beyond it. Rule 2 fired: replace the memory time with the upper end of its own
sampling interval, re-measure once. The second row is that re-measurement and it
holds the declared rate across the whole swept range.

THE CAUSE IS THE ESTIMATOR, MEASURED DIRECTLY. `lib/autocorrelation.py:
integrated_time` on 1253 samples returns 1.01 for a true 1.0, 9.70 for 10.0,
34.4 for 40.0, 86.1 for 125.0 and 128.9 for 213.0. A memory time read too small
makes every standard error built on it too small, and the bias grows exactly
where the acceptance rate does. The module now returns the Madras-Sokal
windowing standard error and the upper end of one interval of it beside the
estimate. The paper is paywalled and is NOT in `references/`, so the interval is
validated instead: it covers the memory time the series was built with 1.000,
0.775, 0.760, 0.585 and 0.545 of the time at 1, 10, 40, 125 and 213. Half to
three-quarters is NOT the 0.84 a one-sigma upper bound nominally gives, because
the interval is symmetric about a biased centre; it is reported and not rounded
up, and what carries arm A is that conservatism together with the raw-half
memory time and the ignored covariance between halves.

THE COST, arm B, not barred and reported because it sizes the record: the share
refusing a field with NO drift, same scatter -- .000 .000 .020 .273 .655 .809
.860 .878 .882 .887 across the same sweep.

ARM E, THE FORM THIS ROW PROPOSED, on the same trials at its own most favourable
setting: size 0.000 to 0.027 with no drift, and power at a true drift AT the
tolerance of .510 .446 .349 .207 .115 .089 .086 .071 .075 .068. On a field with
the memory time this model's slowest have it would PASS a drifting run about
ninety-three times in a hundred. Not a defect of the Sidak correction; it is
what "failed to reject" means on a record this short, and it is the whole
argument for reversing the direction.

ONE REGISTERED CHECK MISSES AND IS RECORDED AS A MISS. At a memory time of one
the construction was to reproduce the textbook two-sample t and accept 0.05 of
the time; it accepts 0.000. The cause is understood: an injected ramp inside a
half reads as memory on the raw half, so the standard error comes out four times
the independent-samples one. The half of that check with a clean answer -- the
estimator recovering the memory time it was handed -- passes and is above.

VERDICT: the row is COMPLETE. The statistic is analytic, its size is validated
against a known answer across and beyond the measured memory-time range, its
power is stated at the contract's own drift limit, and the three subtleties on
this row are all carried -- the doubling, the span bar on the half as degrees of
freedom rather than as a hard bar, and no guard estimated on the series it then
uses for the standard error.

Evidence: `biosphere/notes/equilibrium-trend-null.md`,
`biosphere/analysis/drift_statistic_validation.json`. Re-take with
`biosphere/scripts/validate_drift_statistic.py <run>`.

WHAT IT COSTS THE NEXT RUN, and it is the number that matters to world-qcse.
Twenty-two of the 64 assessed fields resolve the tolerance on the 1253-cycle
record already on disk -- every Total column, both soil pools, the grasses, and
the one broadleaf evergreen type. Forty-two do not, and every one of them is an
individual plant functional type's own column. The binding field is anpp.out
TrBR at 33846 cycles, about eight and three quarter hours of retained record at
npatch 5 on 16 ranks before any spin-up. NO RUN HAS BEEN LAUNCHED, and world-mxmr
is what decides whether that is the right purchase.

TWO THINGS FOUND ON THE WAY, both filed. world-4hlw: the per-cell half is the
one part of the gate still calibrated rather than derived. world-mxmr: the
tolerance is derived through one consumer-facing quantity and applied to all 64
assessed fields, and the assessed set is what buys the run.

title: pyburn.dataset raises UnboundLocalError on a request whose first code is derived
description:
ROOT CAUSE of world-xm1t and world-u0ck, found by reproducing the failure on a 40-sample slice of run_67323a923013's raw.

vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/pyburn.py:2289 closes the per-key loop of dataset() with

    _log(logfile,"Collected variable: %8s\t.... %3d timestamps"%(meta[0],variable.shape[0]))

and `variable` is bound ONLY by the arm that finds the code already present in the raw (pyburn.py:1589 and :1606). ua (131), va (132) and spd (259) are each DERIVED from the spectral divergence and vorticity, and their arms at :1633, :1650 and :1667 assign ua, va and spd into rdataset without ever binding `variable`. So a request whose FIRST key is derived raises UnboundLocalError before anything is written.

HIGH_CADENCE_CODES = [131, 132, 259] (run_exoplasim.py:375) is exactly such a request. That is the exception Model.postprocess caught on orbit 127 of run_67323a923013, sending it into integritycheck's example.nl fallback and leaving a twelve-bin average of the regular variable set under the high-cadence name. The same defect is in advancedDataset, which carries the block identically from :2494.

WHY IT HAS NEVER BEEN SEEN ELSEWHERE. aeolian/scripts/extract_high_cadence_wind.py requests WIND_CODES = ["139", "131", "132", "259"]. Code 139 is in the raw, so the first iteration binds the name and every later derived arm finds it still bound -- logging a stale shape, but not crashing. The leading 139 is load-bearing and nothing said so.

THE WORKAROUND IS IN PLACE, in the caller. continue_exoplasim.py --reconvert-high-cadence prepends pyburn.tscode, drops its variable before writing, and states the reason at the call site. verify_high_cadence_rescue.py holds the ordering. That leaves the fix owed upstream.

THE FIX is one line: the _log at :2289 belongs inside the branches that bind what it reports, or must report rdataset's entry rather than a loop local. It is under vendor/, so it goes through the subtree conventions in docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md. pyburn is Python and compiles nothing, so CLAUDE.md rule 4's rebuild does not apply.
acceptance_criteria: pyburn.dataset accepts a variable list whose every code is derived, HIGH_CADENCE_CODES is requested as declared without a prepended clock code, and the workaround and its verifier case in continue_exoplasim.py / verify_high_cadence_rescue.py are removed.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-2jj3: _logcollected reads back what the iteration stored, fixed at all four sites; four codes bound their own name, not three, and 100 ilibrary codes with no arm could log the previous variable's shape under their own name. world-u0ck: run_67323a923013's raw recovered and re-converted to 1463 samples, the substituted 12-bin average kept beside it as evidence, INDEX.json carries a per-run high_cadence block, and no published number moved though the Weibull shape exposure was a factor of 1.94. world-jqm4: an evenly spaced axis over an even bin count is genuinely ambiguous -- 36 records at dt 160 and 18 at dt 320 give a bit-identical axis -- so it refuses, with a checked ntimes declaration as the door.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
FIXED IN THE VENDOR, WORKAROUND OUT, AND THE EXPOSURE IS WIDER THAN THREE CODES.

REPRODUCED FIRST, on a 40-sample slice cut out of run_67323a923013's raw at a
code-129 boundary so every code in it has the same record count. With
["131","132","259"] pyburn.dataset raised UnboundLocalError before writing
anything; with the clock code in front it wrote all four.

THE FULL ENUMERATION. 27 codes have a derivation arm in dataset(). FOUR of them
store their result without ever binding `variable`, not three:

  131 ua    132 va    259 spd    137 wa

wa is derived through _transformvar under its own name at pyburn.py:1932-1937,
exactly as ua/va/spd are, and ["137"] raised on the slice. It is in
example.nl and highcadence.nl, so a namelist reordered to put it first would
have failed the same way.

The FIFTH shape is larger than all four: 100 ilibrary codes have no arm at all.
Requested and absent from the raw, they store nothing, so as a first key they
raised and as a later key they logged the PREVIOUS variable's shape under their
own name. ["139","145"] logged `bld .... 40 timestamps` when the only thing in
the dataset was `ts`. That is not hypothetical -- run_67323a923013's own
highcadence.nl asks for 70 codes and 4 of them (vegnpp among them) are absent
from the raw on this configuration.

Orderings that raised, all confirmed on the slice: any request opening with 131,
132, 259, 137, or with any of the 100 armless codes not in that raw.

THE REPAIR IS NOT AN INITIALISATION. pyburn._logcollected reads
rdataset[meta[0]] -- what the iteration actually stored -- and replaces the line
at all four sites (dataset and advancedDataset, the non-derived branch and the
derived one). Initialising `variable` ahead of the loop would have stopped the
traceback and kept the misattribution, and the misattribution is the worse
half: every variable here is dimensioned by time on axis 0, so a stale shape
reads as correct on the count and names the wrong variable.

A MISSING ENTRY IS REPORTED, NOT RAISED, and I changed my mind on that with the
artifact in front of me. Raising was the first repair; it then refused
run_67323a923013's own highcadence.nl at code 301, which would have failed every
postprocessing pass this project makes. The namelist lists every code the model
was COMPILED to be able to write, not what this configuration wrote, so
"requested, absent, underivable" is ordinary there. dataset() now logs
NOT COLLECTED and returns what it has; the completeness contract belongs to the
caller that knows what it asked for.

THE WORKAROUND CAME OUT. continue_exoplasim.reconvert_high_cadence requests
HIGH_CADENCE_CODES as declared -- no prepend, no drop -- and what replaces the
clock-code check is the one the prepend never made: every declared code must
come back, or it refuses naming what is missing.

WIND_CODES NO LONGER MATTERS. extract_high_cadence_wind.py is ["131","132","259"]
and 139 is gone from it rather than documented. The 139 RECORDS are still
required in the chunk bytes, because readallvariables builds the entire time
axis by counting them, but that is write_chunk's claim and write_chunk already
keeps them regardless of what is requested. The comment now separates the two.

THE CHECK. verify_high_cadence_rescue.py goes from 11 cases to 13.
case_a_derived_first_request_converts is the only case in the file that runs the
real spectral transform: it writes a synthetic T21 raw (seeded, ~1.3 MB, no
model, no run directory) carrying the main header, lnps, and per-level
divergence and vorticity, and holds an identity -- key order is not an input to
any derivation, so ["131","132","259"] must return exactly what
["139","131","132","259"] returns. Synthetic rather than sliced because
exoplasim/runs/ is untracked and a check that passes only when a 2 GB artifact
happens to be on the machine is not a check.

PROVED ABLE TO FAIL, against BOTH repairs:
  original line          -> FAIL, "the declared request ['131','132','259']
                            raised UnboundLocalError"
  variable=np.zeros() init -> FAIL, "the log reports ['ua','va','spd','bld']
                            collected and the dataset carries ['ua','va','spd']"
The second is why the case makes a second request with code 145 appended. On the
declared request alone the cheap repair looks right.
Also: case_the_request_is_the_declared_set fails if the prepend comes back, and
case_a_missing_declared_field_is_refused fails if the completeness check goes.

RULE 4 WAS NOT OWED, AND I CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. pyburn.py is Python,
imported at runtime from the editable install; no Fortran parameter, no
translation unit, nothing links it. rebuild_binaries.py --verify: "all 10
binaries current", with a note that vendor/exoplasim has 1 uncommitted path,
which is this change. verify_model_compiles.py: 38 translation units, the model
source compiles.

TWO ADJACENT DEFECTS FOUND AND FILED RATHER THAN FIXED HERE, both different in
kind. world-hs5z: dataset() never normalises an integer key, so
dataset(raw,[131,132,259]) falls through every derived arm and returns nothing,
and advancedDataset is broken for name keys and int keys both. No live consumer
-- every call site in this tree passes strings. world-e9yz: codes 270, 271 and
275 have arms and are not ilibrary keys, so three derivations are unaddressable,
and 268/269 are keyed as glacier fields so the swatm/lwatm arms are dead and
mislabelled.

NOT MINE, REPORTED. check_consistency's "generated inputs vs the files they
read" now names carbon_feedback_gate_report.json again: it records
continue_exoplasim.py's hash, so any edit to the continuation script stales an
ocean gate. ocean/ is another session's. smoke_test has one failure
(biosphere/scripts/derive_trend_null.py is in no pipeline step) and
verify_entry_points has one (biosphere/scripts/equilibrium_window_gate.py);
both are the concurrent LPJ trend work, not this change.

title: run_67323a923013's high-cadence product is a regular 12-bin average, and the baseline is what consumes it
description:
world-xm1t found the mechanism; this is the artifact it left on the accepted baseline.

exoplasim/runs/run_67323a923013/highcadence/MOST_HC.00127.nc has time = 12 and carries the REGULAR stream's variables (psi, stf, cl, alb). The raw beside it, exoplasim/runs/run_67323a923013/MOST_HC.00127, is 1995867952 bytes and holds 1463 samples, which is what expected_high_cadence_samples derives from plasim.f90:776 and 841-843 for 5850 runsteps at interval 4. A factor of 122 in sample count, and the wrong variable set.

HOW IT GOT THERE. pyburn raised on that segment; Model.postprocess caught it and called integritycheck, which silently re-ran pyburn under example.nl -- the regular variable set and the regular twelve-bin average -- and returned success. No exception propagated and nothing recorded a substitution, so the file is indistinguishable from a real high-cadence product by its name and its location.

WHY THIS IS P1 RATHER THAN BOOKKEEPING. run_67323a923013 is the accepted baseline: config/planet.yaml names its climatology, the carve2 commissioning rests on it, and analysis/coastline_flux_bracket.json's measurement -- which is what selected SPAT-5's tile model against a 0.12 W/m2 tolerance -- is taken on it. Any consumer that read the high-cadence stream for that run read a twelve-bin average instead. Establish which consumers those are BEFORE deciding what is affected: aeolian/scripts/extract_high_cadence_wind.py is the one this row knows about.

Do: run 'continue_exoplasim.py --rescue-high-cadence' on the run, which world-xm1t added and which recovers the raw and stamps it. Then re-convert with the high-cadence namelist and check the result against expected_high_cadence_samples, which the new validate_high_cadence enforces. Then work out what, if anything, consumed the substituted file and whether any published number moves.

Do NOT delete the substituted .nc before the rescue has run: it is the only evidence of what was reported.
acceptance_criteria: The raw is recovered and stamped, a correct high-cadence conversion exists for orbit 127 with 1463 samples, every consumer that read the substituted file is identified, and any number that moves is reported.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-2jj3: _logcollected reads back what the iteration stored, fixed at all four sites; four codes bound their own name, not three, and 100 ilibrary codes with no arm could log the previous variable's shape under their own name. world-u0ck: run_67323a923013's raw recovered and re-converted to 1463 samples, the substituted 12-bin average kept beside it as evidence, INDEX.json carries a per-run high_cadence block, and no published number moved though the Weibull shape exposure was a factor of 1.94. world-jqm4: an evenly spaced axis over an even bin count is genuinely ambiguous -- 36 records at dt 160 and 18 at dt 320 give a bit-identical axis -- so it refuses, with a checked ntimes declaration as the door.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
VERIFIED, RESCUED, ROOT-CAUSED. NO PUBLISHED NUMBER MOVES.

THE RESCUE. `continue_exoplasim.py --run run_67323a923013 --reconvert-high-cadence`
moved MOST_HC.00127 out of the run root into highcadence/ and stamped it. The
stamp checked against the file rather than the exit code:

  sha256  6ffe2d8ade8abe5f7bab1099137fa86291ad70142c52290dd63e3e83a9798011
  bytes   1995867952         both reproduced by sha256sum and stat
  run_id  run_67323a923013   source_build canonical-10m-carve2
  recovered_from  the run root, which is where the model leaves it

The rescue path did not stamp the sample count -- `expected_samples_per_orbit`
was built only on the run path -- so it now derives it from the manifest's
`runsteps_per_orbit` and the interval: 5850 at 4 gives 1463.

THE ROOT CAUSE, which the row did not have and which is now world-2jj3.
Reproduced in seconds on a 40-sample slice of the raw. `pyburn.dataset` closes
its per-key loop with `_log(... variable.shape[0])` at pyburn.py:2289, and
`variable` is bound only by the arm that finds a code ALREADY IN THE RAW. `ua`,
`va` and `spd` are each derived from the spectral divergence and vorticity and
bind their own names instead, so a request whose FIRST key is derived raises
UnboundLocalError before anything is written. HIGH_CADENCE_CODES = [131, 132,
259] is exactly such a request. That is the exception `Model.postprocess`
caught. `extract_high_cadence_wind.py` has always survived it only because its
WIND_CODES lead with 139, which is in the raw; nothing said that was
load-bearing, and it now does.

THE RE-CONVERSION. `--reconvert-high-cadence` runs the rescue and then converts
each preserved raw under HIGH_CADENCE_CODES, reading radius, gravity and gascon
off the run's own `planet_namelist` rather than re-deriving from config. It
leads the request with `pyburn.tscode` and drops that variable before writing,
so the product is exactly the declared set; `validate_high_cadence` then holds
it to the model's own sample count and a `_std` variable is refused as evidence
of binning. A conversion already carrying the right count is left alone. One
that is not is MOVED ASIDE as `MOST_HC.NNNNN.substituted_regular_average.nc`,
never deleted.

CONSUMERS. Every reader of the high-cadence stream, and none read the
substituted file:

  aeolian/scripts/extract_high_cadence_wind.py  reads the RAW. It cannot open a
    netCDF at all: scan_records exits unless the first record is a 32-byte
    header and demands a code-333 grid descriptor.
  aeolian/scripts/build_dust.py                 reads MOST_HC.00127_wind.nc,
    the extractor's product, via --gust-samples. It has no default and refuses
    without one.
  aeolian/scripts/build_sea_salt.py             same reader, same flag. No sea
    salt baseline artifact exists, so it has produced nothing.
  aeolian/scripts/dust_intensity_levers.py      reads the shape out of a
    baseline report, not out of any file.
  continue_exoplasim.py                         finds, moves, hashes and
    validates.

Three artifacts carry a shape that came from a high-cadence stream:
dust_baseline.json (2.0837, measured_from the wind extract, measured_from_samples
1463), dust_intensity_levers.json (2.0646, from an earlier run's extract), and
orogen_T21_surf_1801_provenance.json, which cites the baseline report's field
rather than a file. All 1463-sample lineage. Nothing in the tree names
highcadence/MOST_HC.00127.nc or carries its sha256.

BY HOW MUCH IT WOULD HAVE MOVED, had anything read it. Refitting the Weibull
shape from each file over the same cells:

  substituted 12-bin file    k = 4.108 over 12 samples
  raw-derived wind extract   k = 2.112 over 1463 samples
  published dust_baseline    k = 2.084 over 1463 samples, erodible cells

A factor of 1.94, which is build_dust.py's own documented snapshot bias and
which it puts at about 40x in emission. `measured_from_samples` is what would
have caught it: 12 against 1463.

RECORDED. `exoplasim/runs/INDEX.json` now carries a `high_cadence` block per
run, derived from the manifest and not written by hand: per orbit the raw's
name, size, sha256 and expected sample count, the conversion's sample count and
sha256, and `substituted_conversion` naming the file moved aside. Run ids are
UUIDs and `exoplasim/runs/` is untracked, so the index is the only durable
record that orbit 127's conversion failed and what replaced it.

ALSO FIXED, both found here. `extract_high_cadence_wind.py` stamped `source_raw`
as a bare path, and the rescue moving the raw one directory deeper made that
attribute name a file that is not there; it now stamps the sha256 and size
beside it, and MOST_HC.00127_wind.nc's attributes were repaired to the current
location with that hash. And `--purpose` was required on a mode that integrates
nothing; the two rescue modes now take no purpose and refuse one.

CHECKS. verify_high_cadence_rescue.py goes from five cases to nine, all fixture
-only. The four new ones were each proved able to fail: deleting the substitute
instead of moving it aside, dropping the clock code from the head of the
request, always re-converting, and handing pyburn PLARAD in metres.
smoke_test.py and verify_entry_points.py pass.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:

  exoplasim/runs/run_67323a923013/highcadence/MOST_HC.00127.nc

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO THE HASH IN THE PREVIOUS COMMENT, and the defect that produced it.

The converted file's sha256 is 8b3f3811d6bf581c97c86bfd0ca44795cb2820314ab61d23573cd08aa7fadb27. The 766411b1... published above was wrong, and it was wrong for a reason worth keeping: `pyburn.netcdf` RETURNS the Dataset it opened and does not close it -- `postprocess` closes it on the line after the call (pyburn.py:4126-4127). Calling the writer directly and hashing the path straight after recorded the digest of a file still short of its final metadata. The file on disk never changed; the record described a state it was about to leave.

Fixed, and the check that catches it added: the re-conversion closes the writer, and verify_high_cadence_rescue.py now requires the recorded sha256 and size to equal the file's. Its fake writer deliberately returns an unclosed Dataset, like the real one, so a caller that forgets cannot pass. Restoring the missing close fails validate_high_cadence outright -- an unclosed netCDF has no readable time dimension.

A SECOND DEFECT FOUND THE SAME WAY. Running --reconvert-high-cadence twice erased the substitution from the record: the second pass finds a valid conversion and had no way to derive that one had been replaced, so moved_aside came back null and INDEX.json's substituted_conversion went with it. That is the trap preserve_high_cadence_raw already guards recovered_from against. The record is now read off the directory rather than remembered, so it says the same thing on every pass, and a case holds it. Proved able to fail.

exoplasim/runs/INDEX.json now reads, under run_67323a923013:

  "127": raw MOST_HC.00127, 1995867952 bytes,
          sha256 6ffe2d8ade8abe5f7bab1099137fa86291ad70142c52290dd63e3e83a9798011
          expected_samples 1463, converted_samples 1463,

          substituted_conversion exoplasim/runs/run_67323a923013/highcadence/MOST_HC.00127.substituted_regular_average.nc
