title: The production span is priced through a statistic that has already converged
description:
lib/run_lengths.py buys PRODUCTION_SPAN_TAU_MULTIPLE = 20 tau, on a coverage criterion measured against synthetic series whose answer is known in closed form. That derivation is sound and it assumes what a synthetic AR series has and this world's does not: a tau that is a property of the PROCESS rather than of the window.

Measured on 140 clean orbits of run_893e276ee029 (exoplasim/notes/memory-time-and-the-production-span.md): tau is 1.00 at 20 orbits, 1.35 at 40, 1.90 at 60 and 6.30 at 140, every one of them a supported estimate. So the rule does not close. At 60 orbits it reads 1.90 and asks for 38; at 140 it reads 6.30 and asks for 126. Every span bought raises the tau that prices the next one, and there is no fixed point in the table.

WHAT THE CRITERIA ACTUALLY NEED IS MET LONG BEFORE EITHER. The offset criterion discriminates at 0.15 K and wants the statistic's standard error at a third of that, 0.05 K. The mean's interval is 0.019 K at 40 orbits and never rises above 0.026 at any length measured. The margin is a factor of two at the worst reading and it is there by 20 orbits.

So the span on this world is not set by the mean's interval at all. It is set by the SLOPE's, which assess_convergence.py sizes separately through orbits_for_slope_standard_error and which does keep tightening with the window. Pricing the span through tau prices it through the one statistic that has already converged.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE, and it is a decision as much as a derivation: either the span is sized directly on the standard error the criterion needs, measured by batch means on the run's own series so it is self-limiting -- buy orbits until the interval is under tolerance over factor, then stop -- or PRODUCTION_SPAN_TAU_MULTIPLE keeps its coverage argument and the note records why it overbuys here. It is not a free choice: the span multiplies every rung of the ladder, and at T85 the difference between 44 orbits and 126 is the difference between an afternoon and a day.

DO NOT resolve this by lowering the multiple. The coverage criterion behind 20 is measured and the batch-length half of it -- BATCH_LENGTH_TAU_MULTIPLE = 5, because batches of two tau miss coverage however many there are -- is independently supported by the batch-means table in the note, where the inflation factor plateaus only once the batches reach about three tau. What is wrong is the input, not the multiple.
close_reason: Verified the operative self-limiting production-span rule is already implemented in lib/run_lengths.py via production_span_from_report, using each convergence report's binding required-window statistic and preserving lower-bound status. Synthetic right-answer fixtures are wired into smoke_test and the full 56-check smoke suite passes. The twenty-tau rule remains only for pre-run pricing and is documented as overbuying on this world.

title: A worktree's surface build writes through the linked .sra into the main checkout
description:
scripts/link_worktree.py holds back docs/book/, maps/build/ and biosphere/generated/ under SKIP_REGENERABLE, 'because they are regenerable output, and a link makes the worktree write over the main checkout's copy'. exoplasim/inputs/<rung>/*.sra is regenerable output too and it IS linked, entry by entry, because a worktree also has to READ it to stage a run. So the same hazard applies and nothing holds it back.

The consequence is concrete: exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_albedo.py without --output resolves its output to INPUTS/<rung>, every .sra there is a symlink into the main checkout, and write_sra opens the path and writes through it. build_surface_soil_water.py, build_boundary_conditions.py and build_surface_roughness.py write the same directory. A worktree agent running any of them replaces the staged fields a commissioning run in the main checkout is reading, and check_consistency's 'runs vs the surface fields they staged' would then report the run as being on a surface the tree no longer holds -- with nothing saying which worktree did it.

A skip is the wrong repair, because a worktree legitimately reads these. The repair is a refusal at the point of writing, which link_worktree.py already implements for ITSELF: its _caught_by_symlinked_ancestor refuses to write a path whose ancestor is a symlink into the main checkout. The same guard belongs where the generators write, plausibly as one helper beside lib/paths.py's existing clean-I/O and configured-grid guards, so a worktree build without --output refuses instead of silently clobbering.

Found while running the surface_albedo step from a worktree during PHYS-15; the build was cancelled before it took the host lock, so nothing was overwritten.

Source: scripts/link_worktree.py SKIP_REGENERABLE and _caught_by_symlinked_ancestor; docs/src/reference/environment.md, the 'Two things are held back' paragraph; exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_albedo.py:617
close_reason:
Fixed rather than tracked, and fixed at the point the row names. sra.py:write_sra gains refuse_a_write_through_a_symlink, which refuses a path that IS a symlink or that has one as an ancestor, and says to pass --output inside the worktree or to run the generator in the main checkout. write_sra is the single door all four builders go through, so one guard covers build_surface_albedo.py, build_surface_soil_water.py, build_boundary_conditions.py and build_surface_roughness.py at once.

A skip in link_worktree.py stays the wrong repair for the reason the row gives: the READ is legitimate and a worktree that cannot stage a run cannot do anything.

smoke_test.py check_no_write_through_a_symlink drives it: an ordinary path still writes, a symlinked file is refused, a path under a symlinked directory is refused, and the donor is asserted untouched and un-created-in after both refusals. In the main checkout nothing on these paths is a link, so the guard never fires there.

This was live rather than hypothetical: an agent working phys-15 in a worktree queued a build_surface_albedo rebuild that would have replaced the staged fields the vegetated baseline commissioning run is reading, and cancelled it before it took the host lock. Nothing was overwritten.

title: A lake-bearing baseline may have three times the memory of its lake-free bootstrap, and 44 orbits cannot measure it
description:
Measured 2026-08-27 on canonical-10m-base at T21, both arms cold-started, both assessed over 41 clean-I/O orbits of one instrument, same flux and same model:

  run_e0c431cf67e2, the BARE-ROCK BOOTSTRAP, terrain-only surface fields
     lag1 +0.170 +/- 0.152   tau 1.82   ess 22.6   reliable TRUE
  run_58f467b0872d, the BARE-ROCK BASELINE, its own lakes and pedology soil water
     lag1 +0.549 +/- 0.109   tau 5.49   ess  7.5   reliable FALSE

The direction is a real signal: the lag-1 difference is 0.38 against a combined standard error of about 0.18, so roughly 2.2 sigma. The MAGNITUDE is not measured and the estimator says so -- tau_span_supports_the_estimate is false and the effective sample size is 7.5, which is the regime where Geyer's estimator returns a number of the ordinary size without support. lib/run_lengths.py:report_is_settled_production already filters it out of the bound test, which is why the gate is green and why this is a task rather than a failure.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIGMA. The production span is 20 x tau at every rung. At the declared bracket top of 2.22 that is 44 orbits; at 5.49 it is 110. The whole accepted run structure -- 70 orbits at T21, then about 10 at each higher rung -- is priced on tau, so this is the one measurement that can make the ladder unaffordable.

THE MECHANISM IS NOT IDENTIFIED and the obvious candidate is wrong. The baseline's land bucket is SMALLER than the bootstrap's, not larger: pedology gives a land-mean dwmax of 0.117 m against ExoPlaSim's uniform 0.5, and lake_dwmax_m is only 0.2 m on the lake fraction. So this is not a bigger reservoir integrating longer. What else differs is the albedo, which now carries the solved lakes and the derived evaporite split. Do not write down a mechanism until one is measured.

WHAT SETTLES IT: clean-I/O orbits on a lake-bearing baseline. At tau near 5.5 an effective sample of 25, which is what made the bootstrap's estimate reliable, needs about 140 orbits. At T21 dt 45 that is roughly 35 minutes of model time, so the measurement is cheap even though the consequence is not. Take it on the vegetated baseline rather than the bare-rock arm, since that is the lineage the world's numbers rest on.

Related: world-k8vv, which asks the next bootstrap for at least 24 clean orbits; if this holds, the number it asks for is wrong by a factor of three.
close_reason:
Measured on 140 clean-I/O orbits of run_893e276ee029, the vegetated baseline. exoplasim/notes/memory-time-and-the-production-span.md carries the tables.

THE HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED AT MATCHED WINDOW LENGTH. Over 41 orbits, the length the bare-rock arms were judged on, the vegetated baseline reads tau 1.46 against the bare-rock bootstrap's 1.82 -- the lake-bearing arm is the LESS autocorrelated of the two. The 5.49 that raised the question was the unsupported reading this row warned about in its own text, at an effective sample of 7.5.

WHAT IS TRUE INSTEAD is more useful and is why this closes rather than being re-scoped. Tau grows monotonically with the window it is measured on -- 1.00 at 20 orbits, 1.35 at 40, 1.90 at 60, 6.30 at 140 -- while the lag-1 correlation does not, sitting between 0.27 and 0.52 throughout. An AR(1) at the measured lag-1 would give 2.88 against the 6.30 measured on the same orbits, so the autocorrelation does not decay geometrically and tau is a property of the window rather than of the process. Batch means, which compute no tau at all, agree independently: the inflation over the independent expectation reaches 2.5 at a batch length of 20 and holds, which is tau 6.3 by an instrument that never estimates one.

AND THE QUANTITY TAU EXISTS TO CORRECT HAS ALREADY CONVERGED. The standard error of the mean is 0.0201 K at 20 orbits and 0.0255 at 140, while the independent expectation falls from 0.0201 to 0.0102. Seven times the orbits buy no better a mean. This model's per-orbit global mean surface temperature can be determined to about 0.025 K and no better, whatever is spent.

The follow-on is world-vd6a: PRODUCTION_SPAN_TAU_MULTIPLE prices the span through the one statistic that has already converged, and the rule does not close on a series whose tau depends on the window -- at 60 orbits it asks for 38 and at 140 for 126.

title: Tier 2 of the frozen-quantities audit: the values that reach the namelist
description:
Tier 2 of `notes/audits/frozen-derived-quantities.md`: every value that reaches the model's namelist or a staged surface field, so an error is in the physics from the first timestep.

Each row took one of the project's two dispositions. Disposition one, state no number at all: `model.ozone_height_m`, `model.ozone_spread_m`, `model.cold_start_profile.lapse_rate_k_per_m`, `model.cold_start_profile.tropopause_height_m` and `surface.land_water_column.layer_capacity_fraction` are removed from `config/planet.yaml` and derived at use; `lib/lapse.py:SIGMA_LOWEST`'s copy in `hydrography/scripts/carve_verdict.py` is deleted; `corrk_cross_check.py`'s three path constants come from `shortwave_band_weights.py`. Disposition two, declare and refuse on disagreement: the table in `check_consistency.py` grows from four rows to fourteen and gains element-wise comparison and a build stamp, and four further checks re-derive what no artifact emits.

The five config removals are declared in `lib/provenance.py:REMOVED_CONFIG_KEYS` with the values the keys held, so the resume guard can tell a removal from a value that moved.

This row is the OWNER cited by those five declarations. It closes with the tier-2 table in the audit.
close_reason: Every tier-2 row dispositioned; the table in notes/audits/frozen-derived-quantities.md records which disposition each took and what moved. The one blocked row, the shortwave water path, is world-wtt3.

title: Re-derive the shortwave water path and the three weights quoted at it, once a baseline climatology exists
description:
The shortwave water path is frozen on a baseline that no longer exists, and the gate above it cannot see that.

`exoplasim/scripts/shortwave_band_weights.py` declares `CORRK_PATH_CM = 2.7891`, the model's own effective water path magnified by zbetta, and `CORRK_RATIO_TO_EQ21 = 1.127592`, which is `corrk_cross_check.py`'s absorptance at that path over Lacis and Hansen Eq. 21 at the same amount. `config/planet.yaml`'s `h2o_sw_level` is that ratio times one plus the water vapour continuum fraction.

WHAT IS FROZEN. `column_water_cm` derives the path from the BASELINE climatology and falls back to Earth's global mean when none is named. `baseline_climatology` is null, and the baseline the 2.7891 was measured on was on `precarve-craton` under a model that has since moved. So the path cannot be re-derived through its own producer.

WHY THE EXISTING GATE DOES NOT CATCH IT. `check_consistency.py` holds `model.h2o_sw_level` against `exoplasim/analysis/h2o_sw_level.json`, which `--level` writes from `CORRK_RATIO_TO_EQ21` and `H2O_CONTINUUM_FRACTION` and from nothing else. The gate regenerates its own reference from the frozen value, so it catches a retyping error into config and cannot catch the climatology moving under the path. That row stays: it does catch the retyping.

WHAT IS MEASURED NOW. `check_consistency.py:check_water_path_currency` re-derives the path from the best available climatology and reports the distance. On `bootstrap_regular_climatology.nc` (run_432e5e46adef, canonical-10m-base) it is 2.0017 cm against the declared 2.7891, 28 per cent lower, which is what a global mean 9 K colder does to the column. It is a WARN and not a refusal, for the reason below.

WHY THE NUMBER IS NOT MOVED NOW. `h2o_sw_weight` and `co2_sw_weight` are quoted at the SAME path, and `shortwave_band_weights.py`'s full report cannot be written while `baseline_climatology` is null because its prediction blocks open a climatology and have no Earth fallback by design. Moving `CORRK_PATH_CM` alone would leave the three config keys quoted at two different paths, which is worse than one stale path.

WHAT THE MOVE IS WORTH, measured rather than assumed. `corrk_cross_check.py --water-cm` at both paths gives an Eq. 21 ratio of 1.127590 at 2.7891 and 1.125937 at 2.0017: 0.15 per cent, which is `h2o_sw_level` 1.163 against 1.161, two units in the last place `config/planet.yaml` writes. So the whole plausible range of the path is worth about two units in the last written place of the number that reaches the model.

WHAT SETTLES IT. A baseline climatology on the configured build. Name it in `config/planet.yaml`, re-run `exoplasim/scripts/shortwave_band_weights.py` for the full report, read the new `column_water_cm` into `CORRK_PATH_CM`, re-run `exoplasim/scripts/corrk_cross_check.py` at that path for `CORRK_RATIO_TO_EQ21`, and retype `h2o_sw_weight`, `co2_sw_weight` and `h2o_sw_level` together. The four-row table in `check_consistency.py` then holds all three.

Evidence: notes/audits/frozen-derived-quantities.md, tier 2.
close_reason:
Settled by the thing it named: a baseline climatology on the configured build. run_893e276ee029's 140 clean orbits gave one, and all three constants moved together as the row required.

  CORRK_PATH_CM        2.7891 -> 2.1128 cm, radmod's own effective path magnified by 1.66
  CORRK_RATIO_TO_EQ21  1.127592 -> 1.126163, re-evaluated with corrk_cross_check at the new path
  h2o_sw_weight        1.346 -> 1.351
  h2o_sw_level         1.163 -> 1.161, bracket [1.129, 1.206] -> [1.128, 1.205]
  co2_sw_weight        1.510 -> 1.510, unchanged at the precision config writes

WHAT IT IS WORTH, and it is the reason no run is bought: +0.070 K on the global mean. shortwave_band_weights.py prints a prediction of +2.16 K, but that is quoted from the BLACKBODY weight of 1.2025 and the baseline did not run there -- its radmod_namelist carries H2OSWW = 1.346. The move actually on the table is 3.2 per cent of that span. Against a materiality threshold of 1.0 K the baseline stands and does not need re-running, which is what A2 needed answering before the stellar cycle run could be bought.

The check's OK branch was also printing the failure's prose -- the reason a stale path is not moved alone, on a row that had passed. The two branches say different things now.

Note for whoever reads shortwave_band_weights.py next: its  node is misnamed. The model is not using the blackbody weight and has not been since the config carried 1.346.

title: The next bootstrap buys at least 24 clean-I/O orbits, not 12
description:
run_432e5e46adef, the bootstrap of canonical-10m-base, ran 70 orbits of low-I/O spinup and 12 clean-I/O orbits. A verdict window may no longer span the change of I/O regime at orbit 70 (segments.py:refuse_a_window_spanning_an_io_regime_change), so the whole verdict is taken on those 12.

At 12 orbits the report resolves four of six criteria. abs_surface_slope and extrapolated_offset do NOT resolve: the offset statistic's standard error is 0.1436 K against a 0.15 K threshold, so the criterion cannot discriminate at the factor of three the report requires. The report prices the offset criterion at 23.4 orbits ON THIS RUN'S OWN STATISTICS, which is lower than the 37-orbit nominal default because this run's memory time reads 1.0 rather than the bracket's 2.22.

THIS RUN CANNOT BE EXTENDED TO FIX IT. config/planet.yaml has moved since it was made: surface.soil_albedo_moisture.saturation_at_full_layer 0.7877 -> 0.7642 is a change to the surface albedo, so orbits added now would be a different model in the same series. continue_exoplasim.py refuses the resume for exactly this reason.

So this is a requirement on the NEXT bootstrap, which is needed anyway for model.soil_water_source: pedology and the corrected land_longwave_emissivity: run at least 24 clean-I/O orbits after the equilibrium cutoff, not 12. At T21 dt45 that is cheap.

SECOND EFFECT, and the reason the priority is not lower: the memory-time bracket in lib/run_lengths.py, (1.89, 2.22), was swept on a window that spanned the join and is therefore inflated by the step. The clean block reads a lag-1 of 0.076 against the mixed window's 0.43, but at 12 samples the standard error on a lag-1 is about 0.29 and cannot tell those apart. About 30 clean orbits would resolve the memory time on one instrument and could collapse the bracket, which prices the production span at every rung.

Evidence: notes/audits/frozen-derived-quantities.md; exoplasim/analysis/convergence/run_432e5e46adef_convergence.json resolving_power block.
close_reason: Completed the next bootstrap on canonical-10m-carve2 as run_5994d1f9624e: 70 low-I/O approach orbits, then 53 clean post-equilibrium orbits priced by the run's own resolving-power report (52.50, offset criterion binding, not a lower bound). The final 46-orbit clean window passes all six convergence criteria, and bootstrap regular/snapshot climatologies were built from years 70-122 and named in config.

title: Re-measure the eddy wind on the bootstrap run and judge it against its declared bracket
description:
world-9y07 replaced eddy_wind_m_s with 10.09 m/s measured on runs that were themselves damped with the OLD value of 5.94, so the number is a FIRST ITERATE rather than a converged one. The measurement's own two criteria were met with room to spare -- sampling standard error 0.13 to 0.25 per cent against a 5 per cent bar, eddy variance above 0.7 of the truncation at 0.42 per cent against a 5 per cent bar -- but neither of those bounds the feedback, which is that changing the hyperdiffusion changes the eddies the hyperdiffusion is derived from.

The bound that does exist: the arm pair in exoplasim/notes/resolution-tuned-parameters.md moved the hyperdiffusion by far more than the 1.699x this change makes and moved eddy kinetic energy at 1.3 sigma. So the feedback is expected to be small, and expected is not measured.

THE SWEEP IS THE BOOTSTRAP RUN ITSELF, AT ZERO MARGINAL COST. exoplasim/scripts/measure_eddy_wind.py runs on any completed run's snapshot stream, so the first run taken under the new damping re-measures the quantity for free.

THE CRITERION IS FIXED BEFORE THE RESULT IS SEEN, which is why this row exists rather than a note to look later: the declared bracket is +/- 5 per cent. Within it the value STANDS and this row closes. Outside it the value is REPLACED with the new measurement and the run is REPEATED under the corrected damping, and this row reopens against that run. A second iterate landing outside the bracket again would mean the fixed point is not being approached and the bracket itself is the thing to re-derive.

Blocks nothing before the bootstrap run. Must be evaluated on it before any climatology from it is read.
notes: SUCCEEDS world-9y07, which replaced eddy_wind_m_s with 10.09 m/s and closed. The instrument is exoplasim/scripts/measure_eddy_wind.py and the five existing per-run verdicts under exoplasim/analysis/eddy-wind/ are what a bootstrap measurement is compared against.
close_reason:
The iterate converged and the feedback is bounded at 2.5 per cent.

10.09 m/s was measured on runs damped with the OLD 5.94, which is what made it a first iterate rather than a number: changing the hyperdiffusion changes the eddies the hyperdiffusion is derived from, and neither of that measurement's two criteria bounded the feedback.

run_893e276ee029 was damped with 10.09, so measuring on it is the second iterate. Over its 140 clean orbits and 4480 instantaneous snapshots it reads 9.838 m/s +/- 0.006, which is 0.06 per cent of itself, tau 1.00 orbits and an effective sample of 140. Eddy variance above zonal wavenumber 15 is 0.30 per cent against a 5 per cent transferability criterion.

So the fixed point is 9.838 against a first iterate of 10.09: the feedback moved the answer by 2.5 per cent, inside the +/-5 per cent bracket the declaration already carried. The declaration and the five timescale rows derived from it are moved to it, every timescale scaling by 1.025615.

THE BASELINE STANDS. The damping changes by 2.6 per cent, and the arm pair in exoplasim/notes/resolution-tuned-parameters.md moved the hyperdiffusion by 1.699x -- twenty-seven times as far -- and moved eddy kinetic energy at 1.3 sigma. A change this size is far under what that pair could see, so nothing is re-run.

check_eddy_wind's note was also asserting that every measurement is on a superseded build, and kept asserting it after one was taken on the configured one. It counts them now and says whether the declaration is a first iterate or a closed loop, which is the distinction that matters here.

title: The soil heat solver's conductivity is a seventh live batch-2 term with no namelist route
description:
Commit 3aecf4ec changed the soil heat solver's thermal conductivity in vendor/exoplasim. The bisect of the batch-2 forcing bundle (world-sjja's arm) measured the conductivity spanning a factor of 6.9 across the land cells it applies to, on every land cell, and the commit is inside the batch-2 window.

IT IS NOT IN ANY REGISTERED PREDICTION. exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md registered five terms; vdiff_lamm was the sixth, found unregistered by world-sjja, and this is the seventh. A3's sum-against-sum check has now been run twice against a total that omitted a live term.

IT IS ALSO UNMEASURED, and the reason is one missing line rather than anything hard. All six keys the solver reads are already declared in landmod_nl, so the model will take them from a namelist; what is missing is the exoplasim/scripts/run_exoplasim.py route that writes them. Without it the run integrates the compiled value and no artifact records which value that was, so an A3 arm cannot be built as one binary and one namelist key -- exactly the shape world-sjja fixed for vdiff_lamm, in the same file, with a one-row change to configure_otherargs and expected_namelist_keys.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE: the six keys routed from config, a prediction registered before the arm, and a paired 25-orbit measurement against the same control the rest of the bundle was measured against, with its resolution bar fixed in advance.
close_reason: Six keys routed at efe927a9 and measured on a 50-orbit paired arm, run_ae5aaf479f57 against run_8f75d23c0730, one binary and one restart, four landmod_nl keys apart. Land seasonal ts range +2.838 +/- 0.103 K over orbits 25-49, a rise of 7.3 per cent against a registered +13 to +55; top-of-atmosphere forcing -0.044 +/- 0.085 W/m2, not resolved, so the bundle entry is 0.00 W/m2 measured rather than argued. tas +0.240 +/- 0.034 K, resolved and WARMING against a registered cooling, and a quarter of the 1.0 K materiality threshold, so the term is not material. exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md carries the prediction, the bar, and the measurement.

title: Ct and Dt do not reproduce: zcnow is read while mpsyncsp advances sd
description:
Across three IDENTICAL runs -- same binary, same restart, same namelist -- 7 of 9 CONVDECOMP columns are bit-identical and Cimp - Ct takes +0.00026, +0.00400 and -0.00373. It CHANGES SIGN.

That quantity is world-0ov's own control. The row's acceptance criteria are stated in terms of Cimp - Ct and denergy26 - denergy27, so an instrument that cannot reproduce its own reading cannot answer the question it was built for, and any future arm taken through it inherits the instability.

LOCALISED, not merely observed: it is zcnow, the only array feeding terms 3 and 4 of the decomposition. zcnow is copied from sd INSIDE the parallel region while mpsyncsp advances sd later in the same routine, so which value a thread copies depends on where it is when the sync lands. nconvtime reads it too.

NOT IN THE WAY OF THE BUNDLE, checked rather than assumed: no bundle arm sets NENERGY at all, so zcnow is never allocated in them and none of the bundle's numbers inherit this. It bites only at nenergy = 2, which is the decomposition control.

T21 CANNOT DIAGNOSE IT. The displacement there is 2e-4 against a scatter of 1.5e-4, so the rung cannot resolve the quantity being examined -- failure-modes class 34. A T42 nenergy = 2 arm is what would separate them, and that is runnable for the first time now that the epilog use-after-free is fixed.

DO: order the copy against the sync so zcnow is read from a settled sd, then demonstrate reproducibility the way it was broken -- three identical runs, and Cimp - Ct agreeing to better than the displacement being measured.

Found by world-0ov's arms. Source: exoplasim/notes/resolution-tuned-parameters.md.
close_reason:
FIXED, and the row's mechanism was half wrong. It was right about zcnow and wrong about what advances sd: plasimmod.f90:assoc_spectral points each thread's sdp at a disjoint slice sd(mypid*NSPP+1 : +NSPP), and what carries sd from t to t+dt is step 4.b of spectrala writing THROUGH that pointer. mpsyncsp is an omp barrier and nothing else (mpimod_omp.f90:830); it publishes a write that has already happened. The old comment at plasim.f90:3776 attributed the advance to mpsyncsp and both notes repeated it; all three are corrected.

zcnow(:,:) = sd(:,:) at the head of the routine copies the WHOLE array into a thread-local allocatable while each thread owns one slice, and between that copy and 4.b there is no barrier. A thread held up in the copy reads slices other threads have already advanced, so its zcnow is a mixture of t and t+dt slice by slice. Terms 3 and 4 are the only ones reading it; terms 1, 2 and 5 come through mpgallsp and term 6 reads sd after mpsyncsp, which is exactly the seven-versus-two split observed.

THE FIX is one !$omp barrier immediately after the copy, inside the existing nenergy>1 .or. nconvtime>0 branch. Conditional is safe because both switches are broadcast by mpbci before this runs. No array added, so the 32 MB per-die target is untouched.

REPRODUCTION, criterion fixed before measuring: three runs of one configuration must give byte-identical CONVDECOMP lines across every print and all nine columns; the pre-fix binary must fail it and fail on ct/dt alone; plasim_status must be one hash across every run of both binaries. The race is intermittent -- three 200-step arms caught it 3/3 while three 600-step arms over the same trajectory caught it 0/3 -- so the arms oversubscribe the thread team onto a fraction of the cores and alternate the two binaries.

T21, 5 repeats each: pre-fix Ct 2.19992, 2.21728, 2.17264, 2.21490, 2.23887, with ct and dt the only columns moving; post-fix 2.19130 five times, byte-identical over 7 prints and 9 columns; plasim_status one hash over all ten runs. 2.19130 is also what the pre-fix binary printed where the race did not fire, so the barrier makes the intended number the only obtainable one rather than inventing one.

T42, 3 repeats each: pre-fix Cimp - Ct at -0.0818, +0.0710, +1.0365; post-fix -0.1828 three times. On that bed the pre-fix scatter is the same size as the -0.96 W/m2 displacement world-0ov's diagnosis rests on, so a pre-fix T42 reading could have returned any sign. It is a cold-start bed, so those magnitudes are not the spun-up arm's.

nconvtime NOT AFFECTED, tested rather than argued: it indexes zcnow(jsg,jlev2) with jsg = jsp + mypid*NSPP, exactly the thread's own slice, and three runs of each binary write one plasim_status.

NOT IN THE WAY OF THE BUNDLE, checked at the root: config/planet.yaml declares energy_diagnostics level 1 and no conversion_time_level, so a configured run never allocates zcnow at all.

All 10 binaries rebuilt and verified against f029a2e0. Side finding filed separately: at T21 the term traps at dt 15 while the timestep alone completes there.

title: vdiff_lamm shipped as a live forcing change with no registered prediction
description:
Commit 44050c1e changed vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/fluxmod.f90's asymptotic mixing length from a hard-coded

    real :: vdiff_lamm = 160.

to a rotation-derived default

    real :: vdiff_lamm = -1.    ! <0: derive from rotation rate
    if (vdiff_lamm < 0.) vdiff_lamm = VDLAMM_REF * (OMEGA_EARTH / ww)

At this world's 30-hour rotation that is 160 * 1.2534 = 200.5 m, a +25.3 per cent change in a first-order boundary-layer parameter that sets turbulent exchange over land and ocean alike. It is LIVE BY DEFAULT: run_exoplasim.py writes no VDIFF_LAMM key, so the derived value is what every run since that commit has integrated.

IT APPEARS IN NO REGISTERED PREDICTION. exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md carries five -- world-trs3, world-o12h, OCN-22, world-jgen with world-f9ig, and world-2esd -- and `grep vdiff_lamm` over that file returns nothing. So the batch-2 bundle had a SIXTH term that A3's sum-against-sum check could not see, and the check was run against a total that omitted it.

HOW IT SLIPPED THROUGH, which is the part worth fixing beyond the number. WORLD-AWM5 closed as "no numeric and no form change: irreducible with the argument". That verdict is CORRECT and is about vdiff_c, the constant the row was filed about. The mixing-length half -- delivered in the same commit from the newly fetched Blackadar (1962) -- moved a DIFFERENT constant, and the close reason says so plainly while the headline does not. One row, two constants, one verdict, and the verdict covered one of them.

THE SCALING IS SOUND AND IS NOT WHAT IS IN QUESTION. Blackadar's eq. 25 makes the asymptotic length proportional to the geostrophic wind over the Coriolis parameter, so lambda goes as 1/Omega and that is the only part of him that transfers to another rotator; the coefficient does not, being matched to one observed wind deflection at one site. What is in question is that a live change of this size arrived unpredicted and unpriced.

DO:
1. Register a prediction for it retrospectively AND mark it as retrospective -- a prediction written after the arm is not the same object as one written before, and pretending otherwise is worse than having none.
2. Measure it. vdiff_lamm is in fluxmod_nl, so `vdiff_lamm = 160` reverts it on the SAME BINARY -- an A3-clean pair needing no control build. This is the cheapest discriminating measurement available on the batch-2 bundle and it should be the first one taken.
3. Decide whether the derived value should be live by default at all, or should be declared in config/planet.yaml like every other value of its kind. A first-order forcing parameter that reaches the model without appearing in config is not inspectable from config.

Found while bisecting the bundle's unattributed -10.8 K. Source: notes/audits/tuned-values.md row 10, world-awm5's close reason, exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md.
close_reason: Items 1 and 2 done. VDIFF_LAMM now has a route from model.asymptotic_mixing_length_m, written unconditionally by configure_otherargs and checked by expected_namelist_keys, so a control is a namelist key rather than a code fork; the model prints which branch it took (160.0000 against 200.5476). Measured A3-clean on one binary and one restart: run_5373310a7b9f against run_c9c24d438a94, 25 orbits each, orbits 15-24, -0.153 +/- 0.062 K. The criterion fixed before the run was 2*sqrt(2)*SEM = 0.176 K, so the term is NOT RESOLVED FROM ZERO and is recorded that way; forcing is -0.05 W/m2 at the top of the atmosphere. The prediction is marked retrospective in exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md. It was not the bundle's missing term: that is world-f9ig at -10.01 +/- 0.07 K. Item 3, whether the derived value should be declared in config/planet.yaml rather than defaulting from the compiled sentinel, moves to world-et25, which carries it together with gamma and rcritwidth because it is one decision for all three.

title: derive_design_flux's candidate range and comfort thresholds were declared under the superseded cloud optics
description:
exoplasim/scripts/derive_design_flux.py declares its search over flux ratio 0.850 to 1.000 in steps of 0.0025, and scores land area against a comfort band of warmest-bin mean <= 33.0 C and coldest-bin mean >= -25.0 C, with harsh and extreme bands beyond. All of those numbers were fixed when the shortwave cloud reflectance came from PlaSim's tuned tswr1/tswr2/tswr3 fits.

Those fits are gone. WORLD-F9IG replaced them with the Stephens, Ackerman and Smith (1984) tables and WORLD-JGEN split the cloud optical depth into its two band-resolved Stephens fits. The bound on the change is -25.4 to -6.5 W/m2, which is -20.6 to -5.3 K. Offsetting it moves the design flux ratio by +0.026 to +0.102 from 0.945, so the winning candidate may sit ABOVE the declared range's ceiling of 1.000 -- and a search that cannot reach its own answer returns the edge of its range rather than a result.

THE COMFORT BAND IS THE SHARPER HALF. Its width is 58 K and the physics moved by up to 20.6 K, which is a third of it. A threshold whose justification rests on where the old physics put the tropics is not obviously still the threshold, and the script's own docstring says the warm ceiling is 'the recorded anchor' from a prose derivation while 'every other number is declared here, sourced to nothing, and that label is the point'.

WHY THIS IS URGENT RATHER THAN MERELY OPEN: thresholds are fixed before results are seen, and a criterion chosen after the run it judges is not a criterion. The next commissioning cycle produces the runs this script reads. So the range and the thresholds have to be re-examined BEFORE those runs exist, or the re-examination is contaminated by them. That window is open now and closes when commissioning starts.

Do: re-derive the candidate range from where the corrected physics can plausibly put the balance, and re-examine each comfort threshold against what it was resting on. Where a threshold is genuinely a declared design preference rather than a derived number, say so and keep it -- but say it, rather than leaving it inherited. Needs no model run.
notes:
Raised after an attempt to run two T21 flux arms ad hoc was stopped: the flux derivation is a commissioning step and happens during commissioning, so running arms outside it is not a task. What IS a task is making sure the criteria those runs will be judged against were not chosen under physics that no longer exists.
RESOLVED, no run needed. THE RANGE: 0.850-1.000 could not reach its own answer, because 0.945 plus the full offset bound of +0.102 is 1.047. Re-derived to 0.790-1.100 at the same 0.0025 step, both bounds argued in the docstring from where the winner can be (the superseded-physics winners, 0.8725 uncapped and 0.945 capped, moved by the offset bound) plus a margin sized on the harsh-band widths. An edge winner now REFUSES instead of being reported as an interior_optimum flag; so do an undeclared cold-extreme cap, a cap that admits no candidate, and an anchor or equivalent-temperature pin that is not interior to the range. All five refusals exercised on synthetic seasonal fields. THE COMFORT BAND: no threshold changed value. The reason is a mechanism, not a judgement call -- the band is stated in degrees and a radiation change moves which flux delivers a temperature field, not which temperature is comfortable, which is what trace-gas-absorbers.md section 4 already recorded from the greenhouse side. cold_floor_c, warm_extreme_c and cold_extreme_c are DECLARED DESIGN PREFERENCES, kept and now stated as such. warm_ceiling_c was REVERSE-ENGINEERED -- its recorded justification was where the superseded optics put the tropics at the anchor flux, and the corrected optics delete that justification rather than shift it -- so it is re-declared at the same value under the third of the four dispositions: declared WITH A BRACKET THAT GETS SWEPT, THRESHOLD_BRACKET, with the design flux each bracket point returns carried in the artifact. Also fixed while in there: equivalent_ceiling_c subtracted 273.15 from a bisection result already in Celsius, so the artifact reported a ceiling near -211 C. Verdicts recorded in notes/audits/tuned-values.md finding 1; the maintenance rule in docs/src/pipeline/state.md 5b.
close_reason: Candidate range re-derived to 0.790-1.100 under the corrected cloud optics with an edge-winner refusal; comfort thresholds audited one at a time, three kept as declared design preferences and warm_ceiling_c re-declared with a swept bracket. The cold-extreme cap stays clim-30 and the script now refuses without it.

title: frac_labile_carbon is one of DNDC's two path coefficients applied to both paths
description:
vendor/lpj-guess/data/ins/global_soiln.ins:6 sets frac_labile_carbon 0.5 with NO COMMENT. It is consumed at vendor/lpj-guess/modules/somdynam.cpp:1347 as

    soil.labile_carbon = respsum * frac_labile_carbon;

that pool is split by water-filled pore space, and it becomes the Michaelis-Menten substrate term at vendor/lpj-guess/modules/ntransform.cpp:412, where d_N_max multiplies BOTH denitrification steps (415 and 436). It is the only substrate control on denitrification in the model. vendor/lpj-guess/framework/parameters.cpp:55 defaults it to 1.0, with declareitem and its [0.0, 1.0] bound at 510, and the instruction file halves that.

REGISTERED AND SOURCED, 2026-08-25 in commit 865de8aa. Li et al. (1992), 'A model of nitrous oxide evolution from soil driven by rainfall events: 1. Model structure and sensitivity', JGR 97(D9) 9759-9776, doi 10.1029/92JD00509, is held at references/li1992-a-model-of-nitrous-oxide-evolution-from-soil.pdf and has been read. So the two steps this row was opened for are done.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG IS THE SCOPE, and that is what remains. DNDC's decomposition submodel has TWO paths with different recycled fractions:

    microbial biomass   20 per cent CO2, 60 recycled, 20 to humads   -> 3.0
    humads              40 to stable humus, 40 CO2, 20 recycled      -> 0.5

0.5 is the humads-path ratio 0.2/0.4 exactly. It is NOT a fit residual, so it is not tuned, and the derivation is reachable and has been read, so it is not opaque. One of two path coefficients is applied to both paths: exact on the path it came from and a factor of six low on the other.

DO: separate the microbial-biomass and humus respiration paths at somdynam.cpp:1347 so each carries its own coefficient. Under ifcentury 1 that means mapping DNDC's biomass/humads pair onto the CENTURY pools, which is a judgement rather than a transcription, and it is a live divergence from mainline LPJ-GUESS in a file this project has already changed five constants in -- see world-8vqn.

Magnitude: dimensionless on [0,1]. Sitting inside a saturation, a factor of six on one of two paths is worth between one and six times on d_N_max, hence on the mineral nitrogen the simulated plants can reach.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md section 11, biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml.
notes:
Li et al. (1992) fetched, filed and READ 2026-08-25. Half of this issue is done and the other half changed shape.

DONE, and it did not wait on the paper: frac_labile_carbon is registered in biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml -- instruction_parameters.values, parser_bounds [0.0, 1.0] matching parameters.cpp:510's declareitem, and calibration.entries with verdict unsourced and this issue as owner. ntransform_gate.py --strict now refuses on it. Commit 865de8aa.

THE PAPER DOES NOT SUPPLY THE NUMBER, and cannot, because DNDC never forms this ratio. Its soluble carbon pool is per-path: 60 per cent of the carbon leaving microbial biomass plus 20 per cent of the carbon leaving humads, in both cases the share recycled into biomass, and the paper says it 'is not actually a carbon pool but rather an indicator of the daily rate of decomposition'. The CO2 shares on those same two paths are 20 and 40 per cent. So the soluble-to-respired ratio DNDC implies is 3.0 on the biomass path and 0.5 on the humads path, and the declared 0.5 is the humads path applied to ALL respiration: exact on one path, six times low on the other.

WHAT IS LEFT. The sourced object is a form with two coefficients, and somdynam.cpp:1316 sets soil.labile_carbon = respsum * frac_labile_carbon from a single summed respsum. Implementing it means separating the microbial-biomass and humus respiration paths at that point and giving each its own coefficient. Under ifcentury 1 the CENTURY pools are what would have to be split, and the mapping from DNDC's biomass/humads pair onto CENTURY's is itself a judgement, not a transcription -- so this is not a one-line change and it is what remains open here.

Also settled in passing: Li's table 7 attributes Kc and Kn to Shah and Coulman (1978) rather than measuring them, so world-nga5 is one paper further along than recorded. See world-80ia.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. The row said two paths; the paper has three decomposing pools and residue carbon reaches the soluble pool only through microbial biomass, which inverts the repair's direction: the paired form gives 0.70 of mainline's substrate on a leaf-and-root mix, 0.26 on coarse woody debris. The ratio form was rejected because a recycled-to-respired ratio does not cross between models that respire different shares -- it exceeds the parameter's own [0,1] bound. One bracket where the correspondence genuinely disagrees (SLOWSOM's return share, [0.2, 0.447] one-sided), registered as the twelfth declared divergence with invariants pinning the pool assignment.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Re-verified 2026-08-30 against the files, and three source lines in this issue are wrong.

CORRECTIONS. somdynam.cpp is 1347, not 1316, in both the description and the notes (stock 4.1.1 has it at 1347 too, so 1316 was never right). parameters.cpp is framework/parameters.cpp, not modules/; line 55 for the 1.0 default and 510 for the declareitem are both correct. ntransform.cpp:412 and global_soiln.ins:6 are correct. The description's 'ntransform.yaml:743 records it as not held' is obsolete: the paper is held and read.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE PDF, not the note. references/li1992-a-model-of-nitrous-oxide-evolution-from-soil.pdf title page is JGR 97(D9) 9759-9776, Li, Frolking and Frolking, DNDC. The decomposition submodel says in as many words that the soluble carbon pool 'consists of the carbon from microbial biomass decomposition (60%) and humads decomposition (20%) that is recycled into microbial biomass' and 'Thus it is not actually a carbon pool but rather an indicator of the daily rate of decomposition'. The two paths: microbial biomass gives 20 per cent to CO2, 60 per cent recycled, 20 per cent to resistant humads; humads gives 40 per cent to stable humus, 40 per cent to CO2, 20 per cent recycled. So 3.0 and 0.5, and the declared 0.5 is the humads path. Every claim in the notes holds.

WHAT I FIXED, all outside vendor/.

ntransform.yaml. The li1992 source entry cited references/li1992-parameterization-of-cloud-optical-properties.pdf with a paragraph explaining that the filename was wrong and the file right. The file has since been renamed, so the citation pointed at nothing and the paragraph asserted the opposite of the truth. Both rewritten to the real path.

ntransform.yaml gains instruction_parameters.not_constants, and ntransform_gate.py gains the check that closes the hole this issue is about. The drift check only ever walked from the register to the instruction file, so a constant in the file that nobody declared was invisible: absence from the register looked exactly like absence of a constant. It now walks back as well, and refuses on any numeric key in global_soiln.ins that is in neither values nor not_constants (ifntransform is the only exemption, with its reason). Two fixtures: dropping frac_labile_carbon from values, and withdrawing the ifntransform exemption. This is the check that would have caught the original finding.

ntransform_gate.py also gains a 'source' check: every paper in calibration.sources must cite a file under references/ that references/INDEX.md records. The PDFs are untracked so on-disk existence is not the test; the index is. Two fixtures. This is what would have caught the dead li1992 slug. 24 of 24 fixtures pass, 0 findings, --strict still refuses on the same 7 plus 5 preconditions.

references/INDEX.md. The li1992 row still asserted the magnitude argument for the per-m3-of-SOIL reading of the Michaelis-Menten divisor, which the shah1978 row and ntransform.yaml both record as withdrawn. Withdrawn there too. The slug narration is compressed to the verification claim, which is still load-bearing since a different Li et al. (1992) answers to the same author and year.

notes/audits/tuned-values.md. Section 11's heading still read 'in no register at all' and its body still stated the absence in the present tense; both now read for the registered state, with the line number corrected. The magnitude argument is withdrawn there too. Section 17 cited seven line numbers into ntransform.yaml that were all stale by 40 to 140 lines; replaced with the entry keys, which do not move.

THE CLASS, stated because the repair follows from it. It is NOT tuned: 0.5 is not the residual of a fit, it is DNDC's humads-path ratio 0.2/0.4 exactly. Not opaque: the derivation is reachable and has been read. It is Earth-calibrated like everything in DNDC, but implicit-Earth is not the defect that bites first, and that class's repair -- find this world's number -- is neither available nor to the point. The defect is SCOPE: one of two path coefficients applied to both paths, exact on the path it came from and six times low on the other. The register's verdict stays unsourced, which is the honest one for a single fraction the primary does not form.

STILL OPEN, unchanged: separating the microbial-biomass and humus respiration paths where somdynam.cpp:1347 sets labile_carbon. Under ifcentury 1 that means mapping DNDC's biomass/humads pair onto the CENTURY pools, which is a judgement. Not touched here: an LPJ-GUESS run holds the host and vendor/lpj-guess was off limits.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
THE REMAINING HALF IS TAKEN. The paths are separated and both coefficients are
the paper's.

VERIFIED FIRST, against the source and the PDF rather than against this row.
Every line number in the 2026-08-30 comment holds: global_soiln.ins:6,
somdynam.cpp:1347, ntransform.cpp:412, framework/parameters.cpp:55 and :510.
`git show b368b893:modules/somdynam.cpp` confirms the CNP fork runs the same
line at its own 1084, so the form is the fork's as well as 4.1.1's.
`pdftotext` on the held PDF gives p. 9765 verbatim: microbial biomass 20 per
cent CO2, 60 recycled, 20 to resistant humads; humads 40 to stable humus, 40
CO2, 20 recycled; soluble carbon "consists of the carbon from microbial biomass
decomposition (60%) and humads decomposition (20%) that is recycled into
microbial biomass".

ONE CORRECTION TO THE ROW, and it changes the repair. The row says DNDC has TWO
paths. It has FOUR pools and THREE that decompose: residues, microbial biomass
and humads, with passive humus assumed not to interact with the other three.
Residue decomposition contributes NOTHING to soluble carbon; residue carbon
reaches it one step later, after passing through microbial biomass. That third
path is what the row's magnitude estimate was missing, and it inverts the sign.

WHAT WAS IMPLEMENTED, and why not the obvious thing.

The ratio form is wrong and I did not use it. 3.0 and 0.5 are recycled carbon
over respired carbon, and the two models respire different shares of the same
pool: DNDC respires 20 per cent of the carbon leaving microbial biomass where
CENTURY respires 0.6 on every SURFMICRO call and 0.85 - 0.68*(clay + silt) on
SOILMICRO. `3.0 * respfrac` is 1.8 for every surface microbial transfer and
above 1 for every soil texture with clay plus silt below 0.76, so the ratio form
makes the substrate larger than the carbon that produced it. It is also outside
`declareitem`'s [0, 1] parser bound. What crosses between two models that state
the same process differently is the FRACTION, not the ratio between two of them.

So `somfluxes` now applies one coefficient per pool class to that class's
DECOMPOSITION, which is bounded by cdec by construction and is the number the
paper states:

    frac_labile_carbon       0.6   SURFMICRO, SOILMICRO
    frac_labile_carbon_humus 0.2   SURFHUMUS, SLOWSOM, PASSIVESOM
    (nothing)                      the six litter pools

THE CENTURY CORRESPONDENCE rests on position in the flow network, not on
turnover time, since the two models' rates are not on a common reduction factor.
SURFMICRO and SOILMICRO are the pools every litter transfer feeds and which feed
the humified pools: CENTURY splits DNDC's one microbial pool by horizon, not by
function. SURFHUMUS and SLOWSOM both receive from a microbial pool and hand on
to a more humified one, which is humads' position in DNDC fig. 3, and the CNP
fork's own nitrogen ramp already gives SURFHUMUS SLOWSOM's C:N pair off
SLOWSOM's driver. The litter pools get nothing because that is DNDC's structure.

IT NEEDED A BRACKET IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE.
- SLOWSOM returns csa = 1 - csp - 0.55 of its decomposition to SOILMICRO, 0.447
  to 0.450 over the whole clay range, where DNDC's humads returns 0.2. That is a
  real disagreement between two models about one quantity, factor 2.2. BRACKET
  [0.2, 0.447], one-sided, DNDC's number declared, on
  `instruction:frac_labile_carbon_humus`. Filed as world-gfut.
- PASSIVESOM has NO DNDC counterpart, since DNDC's stable humus does not
  decompose. Loose, and it needs no bracket because the quantity is immaterial:
  it carries 0.03 to 0.35 per cent of decomposition, so its coefficient moves
  the labile carbon by 0.16 to 1.61 per cent over the whole of [0, 1].
- SOILMICRO's cdec includes organic leaching, which DNDC has no path for. Worth
  under 0.05 across orgleachfrac's range.

QUANTIFIED, and it goes the OTHER WAY from what this row expected. The steady
state of somfluxes fixes each pool class's share of decomposition from the
transfer coefficients alone -- every unit of litter carbon leaves as CO2 or DOC,
so the shares are a property of the network and not of the decay rates -- so it
solves exactly for unit input. Against mainline's 0.5 * respsum the paired form
gives 0.70 of the labile carbon on a leaf and root litter mix, 0.62 to 0.74
across the texture simplex, 0.49 on a woody mix, 0.26 on coarse woody debris
alone; lignin moves it by under 0.01 and organic leaching by under 0.05. The
repair LOWERS the substrate, because the litter pools carry 48 to 76 per cent of
respiration and DNDC gives them nothing. d_N_max sits on the roughly linear limb
(k_C * water is of order 0.0026 kgC/m2 against a labile pool of the same order
or below), so 0.7 to 1.0 of that reaches both denitrification steps.

AGAINST THE ARM COMPARISON: the stock-versus-Vesper arms put gross
denitrification 209 times apart, so a factor between 0.26 and 0.88 on the
substrate term is a small share of the span two Earth calibrations of the same
operator already cover, and it moves denitrification down. Plant mineral-N
uptake moved 0.343 per cent over that 209-fold span, so nothing visible is
expected in what the simulated plants take up.

DECLARED IN TWO REGISTERS, one per source file.
- `labile_carbon_paths` in biosphere/config/somdynam.yaml, source half, with two
  new `invariants` entries pinning which pools carry which coefficient (the
  divergence's own `live` line is the sum and would survive a pool moving).
  Header widened: that register is keyed on modules/somdynam.cpp, not on
  phosphorus, and says so.
- `labile_carbon_microbial_share` in ntransform.yaml, instruction half, with
  mainline's `frac_labile_carbon 0.5` recorded in global_soiln.ins beside the
  changed lines. Both keys are in instruction_parameters.values and
  parser_bounds; both calibration entries now read `agrees` with the paper's
  value, where the single one read `unsourced`. --strict refuses on six where it
  refused on seven.
- ntransform.yaml gains `execution_scope`: the arms cover eleven of the now
  twelve entries and this one is not among them. Nothing enforces that block --
  biosphere/scripts/ was another agent's this batch -- so world-h3qg carries the
  exact gate code and two fixtures.

COMPILES. `c++ -fsyntax-only` on modules/somdynam.cpp and
framework/parameters.cpp with the build's own flags and includes, clean, 0.9 s.
A full link was not taken: the host lock is held by world-yyx8 for about three
hours of paired T42 ladder arms, and nothing outside those two translation units
sees the change beyond an added extern.

NOT RUN, deliberately. world-qcse: no LPJ-GUESS run reaches acceptance, the
trend statistic is fitted inside one memory time and the spin-up is short of
this world's relaxation time, so a run could not tell whether this is right. The
verification owed is the world-9f1v construction on an ACCEPTED pair, with the
bracket as a second axis; world-gfut carries it, blocked by world-qcse.

Also updated: notes/audits/tuned-values.md section 11 rewritten for the resolved
state and section 17's list dropped from seven to six, references/INDEX.md's
li1992 row, and docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md's two divergence
sections. smoke_test 69/69, both gates clean with all fixtures, mdBook builds.

title: Derive the regolith production-to-erosion ratio instead of calibrating it
description:
pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml:557 `erosion_weight: 1.5` is calibrated
against a declared Earth-analogue depth target and the file says so:
"the one free scale parameter in the depth model. There is no measurement of
this world's soils to fit, so it is calibrated against a declared
Earth-analogue target."

TWO KEYS CARRY ONE DEGREE OF FREEDOM AND ONLY ONE IS WATCHED.
`erosion_reference_relief_m: 200.0` at :560 enters build_soil.py:313-318 only
through the ratio `erosion_weight / erosion_reference_relief_m`, so halving 200
is identical to doubling 1.5. Its only comment describes a different quantity
("Normalised so Earth-like mean land conditions give E near 1"), with no source,
no bracket and no note anywhere in the tree. `maximum_depth_m: 5.0` at :543 is
the third: a pure prefactor whose whole comment is "Asymptote, not a clip", with
no derivation.

WHAT RIDES ON IT: regolith depth times volumetric_capacity_by_texture is the
land-mean plant-available water capacity, and that field IS the model's `dwmax`
bucket whose overflow is the runoff that drives the weathering law that produced
the depth (pedology/README.md:686). A 10 per cent move in the ratio moves
land-mean depth and land-mean PAWC by 7.9 per cent; a 10 per cent move in
maximum_depth_m moves both by exactly 10 per cent.

Do: construct an absolute production-to-erosion ratio rather than fitting one.
Heimsath et al. (1997), 10.1038/41056, gives the production function and is
read. Portenga and Bierman (2011), GSA Today 21(8), 4-10, 10.1130/G111A.1, gives
global cosmogenic denudation by lithology and is HELD, which by
references/INDEX.md's own rule is an exposure rather than a resource -- reading
it is the first step. If the derivation does not close, collapse the two
degenerate keys into one and ship the bracket the rest of the same file already
ships on every other declared value.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md
close_reason:
Portenga and Bierman (2011) read 2026-08-25. It does NOT publish a relief-to-erosion relation -- mean basin slope is the regressor, relief is secondary, and no equation is given -- so this issue's premise was half wrong and the audit row now says so. What it did give: the FORM (erosion rising with cell relief is its slope result at fixed mesh spacing) and an absolute standardised denudation scale.

Both halves of the Do: line are done. The degenerate pair is collapsed: erosion_weight and erosion_reference_relief_m are replaced by erosion_coefficient_per_relief_m = 1.5/200 = 0.0075, with the law and every number unchanged. And the bracket the rest of pedogenesis.yaml ships on every other declared value is now shipped here, sourced rather than declared: Heimsath's production function inverted against Portenga and Bierman's rates gives 0.15 m at their basin median, 0.81 and 1.16 m at their outcrop mean and median, 1.30 m at their slowest subpopulation, and NO SOLUTION at their basin mean and their arid-basin mean, both of which exceed Heimsath's maximum production rate. Bracket 0.15 to 1.30 m, declared as regolith_depth_bracket_m; the current value's 1.04 m land mean is inside it, upper third.

maximum_depth_m is split out to world-34n2: neither paper bears on it and the audit's expectation that they would was wrong.

Remaining: converting the depth bracket into a coefficient bracket is one re-run of build_soil.py per endpoint on a build with a climatology. Not filed separately; it is what the sweep on the declared bracket is.

Commit 1ede2347.

title: Re-measure eddy_wind_m_s: the run its value was measured on was deleted
description:
config/planet.yaml:731 carries `eddy_wind_m_s: 5.94` under the comment
"Measured, not assumed: eddy RMS wind (departure from the zonal mean, which is
what cascades -- the jet does not), area-weighted over the column, from
run_4182235e9781 orbit 39."

THAT RUN IS NOT ON THIS TREE. It survives as a `restart_from_run` string in
seven other manifests and as one INDEX row in
archive/runs/_bulk_2026-08-24/INDEX_AT_DELETION.json:1552. That archive's README
records the cause: the directories were removed by an `rm -rf` whose argument
came from an unguarded command substitution that expanded to nothing, and this
bulk archive carries only the INDEX row -- no manifest, no climate series, no
NetCDF. So the derivation cannot be inspected, checked or re-run.

It is the single free quantity in `tau_vorticity = pi * radius /
(NTRU * eddy_wind)` and divides into every entry of the `timescales_days` table
at config/planet.yaml:747-752, five rungs by four fields, which reach the model
as TDISSD, TDISSZ, TDISST and TDISSQ. Linear: a factor of two in the value
halves every damping timescale.

The block's own corroboration is on the RULE and not on the value. ECHAM5's
empirically tuned table implies a constant eddy wind of 12.6 to 17.5 m/s; 5.94
is a factor of two to three below that band, and nothing has explained the gap.

Do: re-measure on a converged climatology, by the recipe the config block
already states (eddy RMS departure from the zonal mean, area-weighted over the
column), and record the run it came from in a form that survives. No paper is
needed. Until then the value stands with the deletion recorded beside it, so
that nobody reads the comment as a live citation.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md
notes: CORRECTION to the close reason above: the follow-up row is WORLD-TSBZ, not the id written there. world-tsbz carries the bootstrap run's re-measurement with the +/- 5 per cent criterion fixed in advance.
close_reason:
RESOLVED by re-measurement, and the old number turned out to be a different quantity. eddy_wind_m_s is now 10.09 m/s with a declared +/- 5 per cent bracket. The recipe is stated in the instrument: departure from the zonal mean at the same instant, level and row, on the INSTANTANEOUS snapshot stream, vector magnitude, area-weighted by the model's own Gaussian row weights and mass-weighted by dsigma, reduced as the root of the mean variance.

WHAT 5.94 WAS. The run it was measured on is deleted and cannot be re-read, but the value is identifiable: reducing the TIME-MEAN output stream by the same recipe returns 5.82 to 5.97 across five runs on disk, and run_57cecaa8391b's verdict records stationary_eddies_only.eddy_wind_m_s = 5.966 against measured.eddy_wind_m_s = 10.087. The ratio is 0.58 on every run. A time mean carries the stationary eddies and drops the transients, and nothing is advected by a time average, so an advective time built from a time-mean field is not an advective time. It also closes a gap the config block could not explain: 5.94 sat a factor of 2.1 to 2.9 below ECHAM5's implied 12.6 to 17.5 m/s, and 10.09 sits 1.25 to 1.7 below.

INSTRUMENT: exoplasim/scripts/measure_eddy_wind.py, registered under one_offs, writing per-run JSON verdicts to exoplasim/analysis/eddy-wind/ that outlive the run directories. Two criteria fixed before any result was seen: sampling standard error under 5 per cent of the mean, measured 0.13 to 0.25 per cent via lib/autocorrelation.py; and eddy variance above 0.7 of the truncation under 5 per cent, measured 0.42 to 0.43 per cent, which is what licenses one wind measured at T21 being applied at five rungs.

CONSEQUENCE: every hyperdiffusion timescale shortens by 1.699x at every rung. check_consistency reports 5 rungs derive from pi*a/(NTRU*10.09 m/s). No binary rebuild: these are namelist keys read after the compiled defaults. No stability ceiling moves, and lib/rungs.py records why beside STABILITY_GRID_TAU_SCALE -- the operator is implicit in the damped variable and the change is more damping.

NOT RESOLVED AND NAMED AS SUCH: the runs measured were damped with the old value, so 10.09 is a first iterate. The sweep is the bootstrap run's own re-measurement at zero marginal cost, and world-mkxc carries it with the criterion fixed in advance.

title: smoke_test.py is no longer a smoke test: split the per-unit subprocess passes out of the per-commit gate
description:
`scripts/smoke_test.py` is the gate every agent runs before every commit, so its cost is multiplied by every commit in the project. Two of its 42 checks are process-per-unit sweeps and they dominate it:

- `check_help` spawns a fresh interpreter per script with a `__main__` -- about 136 of the 166 .py files under SCRIPT_DIRS -- each importing numpy, netCDF4 and whatever else the module pulls at import time. Serial. Its own --skip-help help text says it 'dominates runtime', which is the file admitting the problem rather than fixing it.
- `check_model_source_compiles` shells out to `exoplasim/scripts/verify_model_compiles.py`, which runs `gfortran -fsyntax-only` over about 36 translation units. Serial.

Neither is a static read and neither answers in seconds. A smoke test answers 'is this tree coherent' from static reads; a per-script interpreter sweep and a front-end compile are real checks with real value, but they are pre-build / pre-push checks, not per-commit ones.

Do: split. The fast static gate keeps the name `smoke_test.py` and the per-commit role. `check_help` moves to its own entry point; the compile pass is already a registered standalone gate (`verify_model_compiles`) so smoke_test simply stops calling it. Every caller moves with the split: `config/pipeline.yaml`, CLAUDE.md rule 8, `docs/src/pipeline/sequencing.md`, `exoplasim/README.md`. Do not change what any check asserts, only where and how it runs. Prove the surviving gates still fail on what they are meant to fail on by injecting a fault.
close_reason:
Split done and every caller moved. The fast gate keeps the name and the per-commit role: 40 checks, all static reads, 2 subprocesses (both single-threaded text-parse lints), one thread. The two per-unit passes moved to scripts/verify_entry_points.py (new, 137 fresh interpreters, parallel and bounded by machine.workers()) and exoplasim/scripts/verify_model_compiles.py (already a registered standalone gate; smoke_test just stops calling it). No assertion changed.

A third cause of the same complaint, independent of both: numpy's OpenBLAS opened a 32-thread SPINNING pool inside the gate, observed at 1129 per cent CPU. Both gates now pin it to 1 before numpy loads. Shape: 176 child processes and 32 spinning threads -> 2 child processes and 1 thread.

Fault injection, each shown red on the fault and green off it: an argparse default that raises while constructed and an unresolvable import -> verify_entry_points exit 1, fast gate still 0 failed (the class is genuinely invisible to a static pass, which is why it moved rather than being reimplemented cheaply); the world-adts dropped continuation in landmod.f90 -> fast gate's check_no_dropped_continuation FAIL and verify_model_compiles exit 1 with the original diagnostic; a syntax error and an unbound name in lib/lapse.py -> the parse and pyflakes passes FAIL.

title: COMMISSIONING_EVIDENCE says the T21 dt-45 rung met all six criteria; under the upper-bound form it does not
description:
lib/rungs.py COMMISSIONING_EVIDENCE[('T21', 45.0)] carries detail "The route's first rung. All six criteria met, first passing at 47." That was true under the point-estimate form of the criteria. world-s8n3 made every criterion an upper bound, |statistic| + its standard error < threshold, and run_ec32946bec89 now FAILS the storage criterion: 0.0961 W/m2 with a standard error of 0.0303, so 0.1264 against a 0.1200 allowance. What is wrong is the sentence claiming the criteria were met, and the 'first passing at 47', which came from a --through sweep under the old form and has no counterpart under the new one -- the run does not pass at any truncation on that criterion unless its storage falls.
