title: Build the third surface-flux path: an EMBM-free driven configuration for the offline ocean host
description:
genie.F calls a surface-flux routine in exactly two places and each is behind an atmosphere flag: flag_ebatmos calls EMBM's surflux, and flag_plasimatmos calls surflux_goldstein_seaice. With both false no flux routine runs, no wind stress is produced, and istep_ocn is never incremented, because both of its increments sit inside those same two gates. So an EMBM-free configuration needs a THIRD path in genie.F, not a switch.

Less of one than that suggests. The routine the third path should call already exists and carries no EMBM dependency: surflux_goldstein_seaice lives in genie-goldsteinseaice, and its arguments are fluxes and the atmosphere's own transfer coefficients rather than a state to recompute them from, which is the contract the offline exchange needs. It also carries the sea-ice surface solve, which is why the host's sea ice cannot be switched off on this path.

Do: add a flag_fluxatmos of type atmosphere to genie_control.f90, initialise_genie.F's namelist and src/xml-config/xml/definition.xml; in genie.F increment istep_ocn under it as the plasim block does, and call surflux_goldstein_seaice under it inside the sea-ice block; and supply the coupling fields from OCN-10's forcing set rather than computing them. The fields are enumerated in section 1d of notes/audits/cgenie-embm-free-path-and-threading.md.

Do NOT use surf_ocn_sic. It is compiled, it has a wrapper in genie_loop_wrappers.f90, nothing calls it, and its name makes it look like the answer -- but it takes atmospheric STATE and computes the turbulent fluxes from bulk formulae on the OCEAN grid, which is the coarse-grid flux evaluation the offline architecture exists to avoid.

The wind stress rows carry OCN-17's declared scf bracket: goldstein.F:199-205 sets dztau = scf*stressxu_ocn, so the ocean's stability ceiling inherits that 1-to-3 bracket linearly and any sweep on this path returns a bracket rather than a number.

BLOCKED on OCN-10 for the supply half only. The gate, the flag and the registry entry do not depend on the file format; what the forcing set IS does.

Source: notes/audits/cgenie-embm-free-path-and-threading.md section 1
notes:
2026-08-26. THE GATE, THE FLAG AND THE REGISTRY ARE LANDED; the SUPPLY half is
what remains and it is OCN-10's. Merged to main as part of the batch-2 fan-out.

flag_fluxatmos is declared in genie_control.f90, read from GENIE_CONTROL_NML in
initialise_genie.F at .FALSE., and registered in definition.xml as a model of
type atmosphere. That registry entry is load-bearing rather than decorative:
build_job.xsl writes one control-namelist param per model in /definition/config,
so a flag with no entry there cannot be set from any configuration at all.
genie.F advances istep_ocn under it on the PLASIM gate's phase and calls
surflux_goldstein_seaice through the wrapper that gate already used, renamed
surflux_goldstein_seaice_wrapper after the routine rather than after either
caller -- a second copy for the second caller is what section 2 deleted
tstepo_flux_t for. surf_ocn_sic is untouched and still uncalled.

TWO GUARDS, and the second one IS the seam. The permanent guard refuses
flag_fluxatmos beside flag_ebatmos or flag_plasimatmos, since all three are the
atmosphere slot and istep_ocn would advance once per true gate. The temporary
guard refuses flag_fluxatmos alone, because nothing in this tree fills
insolar_sic, netheat_sic, the transfer coefficients or the four wind-stress
fields with no atmosphere running: the run would integrate an ocean forced by
.bss zeros and write output shaped like a result. DELETING THAT ONE BLOCK IS
WHAT TURNING THE PATH ON CONSISTS OF, and it is what OCN-10 earns.

ACCEPTANCE BIT-FOR-BIT AND PASSING: 28 GOLDSTEIN year-20 variables identical at
1 and 16 threads with worst_relative 0.0, and 88 BIOGEM 3-D fields identical.
Against shipped genie-knowngood, the same two pre-existing differences the audit
already recorded and no others.

WORLD-U9KG DISCHARGED FOR THIS PATH, before wiring rather than after: it reaches
only genie-goldstein and genie-goldsteinseaice, grep calibrate over both returns
nothing, and genie-rokgem is not reachable from it. Two things it does carry are
declared in audit section 1f -- scf shipped at 2.00 against definition.xml's own
"plausible range 1 to 3" with three fitted values beside it, entering linearly at
goldstein.F:199-205 so any sweep on this path returns OCN-17's bracket and not a
number; and delta_flux, the residual by which the surface solve fails to
conserve, which a driven path computes and drops because it has no atmosphere to
hand it back to. That is a diagnostic the forcing contract may read and never a
correction.

title: The escalation route's reconvergence steps are specified as commissioning verdicts, not settling tests
description:
docs/src/pipeline/sequencing.md specifies route steps 2 and 4 -- the reconvergences at the target rung's timestep -- as 'one convergence window, then three-orbit increments until the criteria are met'. That is the COMMISSIONING standard, and it is the wrong instrument for these steps.

WHY IT IS WRONG. The convergence window is priced so the slope's standard error can resolve its threshold; it exists to support the claim that a run is equilibrated for worldbuilding, which is a claim about the WORLD'S CLIMATE. Nothing reads the climate of T21 at dt 30 or T42 at dt 22.5. Those states exist to hand the next conversion a restart that is not mid-transient, and the chapter says as much elsewhere: the coarse rungs are a ROUTE to T85, not a measurement. Any residual drift a reconvergence leaves is absorbed by the CONVERGENCE that follows the next conversion.

THE COST IS NOT SMALL AND IT GROWS UP THE LADDER. The commissioning window is 35 orbits against a settling time of about 10, so each reconvergence is priced at roughly 4.5x what its purpose needs. At step 2 that is T21 orbits. At step 4 it is T42 orbits at dt 22.5, where an orbit costs many times more.

WHAT IS WANTED. A SETTLING test for steps 2 and 4, distinct from the commissioning verdict and named separately so the two cannot be confused: has the step change's perturbation decayed, not has this world reached equilibrium. Derive its length from the relaxation time the same way the commissioning window is derived from the slope error, and state what it does NOT establish.

WHAT THE FIRST RUN OF STEP 2 ACTUALLY SHOWED, as the evidence this is the right split: run_14906cb7b914 passed all four slope criteria and the storage criterion at 35 orbits and failed only the extrapolated offset, on its UNCERTAINTY rather than its magnitude (offset 0.1375 K, half-width 0.1443 K). A settling test would have returned a verdict at roughly 10 orbits on the same state.
notes:
DONE, alongside world-cikl: the two are one derivation from two timescales and were taken together.

Route steps 2 and 4 are now SETTLING blocks, named apart from commissioning verdicts. A settling block is a LENGTH and not a verdict on a mean, which is why it escapes the slope-error pricing: n = tau_relaxation * ln(A / 0.15 K), where A is the step change's perturbation and the residual is the offset criterion's own allowance, deliberately the same number because a residual smaller than what the instrument judging the NEXT state can see is one that state cannot be held responsible for. scripts/smoke_test.py checks the two are one number.

tau_relaxation is bracketed 6.27 to 13.68 by the three fits that are evidence, NOT taken from the derived 10.1: world-gknw found the derived value is not established as a bound on the fitted ones. A half-kelvin step therefore settles in 8 to 17 orbits, which is where the ten to twenty this project has repeatedly seen comes from -- the derivation reproduces the experience rather than replacing it, and smoke_test fails if it stops doing so.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH is stated in three places (lib/run_lengths.py, sequencing.md, the pipeline loop D exit): not equilibrium, not the rung's climate, not an interval on any mean taken over it.

STEPS 1, 3 AND 5 KEEP THE COMMISSIONING STANDARD, and the reason is the same one that removes it from 2 and 4: loop A is replayed on those rungs and the carve verdict is taken on their climatologies, so something does read their climate.

The evidence the issue cites stands: run_14906cb7b914 passed the four slope criteria and the storage criterion at 35 orbits and failed only the extrapolated offset on its uncertainty. Its 0.5 K step from dt 45 settles in 8 to 17 orbits by the derivation.
close_reason: Steps 2 and 4 are settling blocks with their own derived length, tau_relaxation * ln(A / 0.15 K), named apart from the commissioning verdict and stating what they do not establish. A half-kelvin step settles in 8 to 17 orbits against the 35 the commissioning window costs, and the bracket reproduces the ten to twenty this project has seen. Steps 1, 3 and 5 keep the commissioning standard because loop A is replayed on those rungs. lib/run_lengths.py carries it, sequencing.md section D decides it, pipeline.yaml loop D cites it. Commit e73f1f4a.

title: A degenerate exponential fit reports a finite relaxation time instead of refusing
description:
assess_convergence.py fits T(n) = T_inf - A exp(-n/tau) and reports `relaxation_orbits_fitted`. On run_14906cb7b914 (T21 at dt 30, 35 orbits) that fit returned tau = 44017.9 orbits against a derived expectation of 10.10 -- four orders of magnitude apart. A tau that large is the fit finding NO CURVATURE and settling on a straight line; the number is not a relaxation time and nothing should read it as one.

The gate itself behaved correctly: the criterion tests abs(offset) + half_width < 0.15 and FAILED CLOSED on the half-width (offset 0.1375, half-width 0.1443, sum 0.2818), which is exactly the documented 'a fit that will not converge is not evidence of equilibrium'. So the verdict is right and the REPORTED METRIC is wrong, which is the dangerous combination: the artifact carries a plausible-looking field that any later consumer would take at face value.

WHAT IS WANTED. The fit declares its own degeneracy rather than emitting a number. A tau far beyond the series length is unidentifiable from that series -- the exponential is indistinguishable from a line over the fitted range -- so the honest output is a refusal plus the bound the data can support, not a point estimate.

THIS BEARS DIRECTLY ON WORLD-GKNW, which asks whether the derived relaxation time is a ceiling and has never been checked against a fitted one. Taken at face value this run REFUTES the ceiling (fitted 44018 >> expected 10.10); recognised as degenerate it is simply no evidence either way. Which of those it is has to be settled before world-gknw can use any fitted tau, and the two rows should be answered together.
notes:
FIXED. The rule is a property of the data: tau is identifiable only when finite, positive and no longer than the span the fit saw. Otherwise relaxation_orbits_fitted is null, relaxation_fit_identifiable is false, relaxation_fit_verdict says why, relaxation_orbits_fitted_lower_bound_orbits carries the span (the only bound the data supports), and relaxation_fit_raw_tau_orbits keeps the optimiser's number so a degenerate fit is visible rather than silent.

BEHAVIOUR PRESERVED. approach_to_equilibrium still returns the raw tau and still widens the asymptote's interval by the overshoot it implies, which is how such a fit refuses through the criterion. Re-assessed run_14906cb7b914 and run_ec32946bec89: every pre-existing metric bit-identical apart from the nulled tau, both verdicts stand (False, True).

FOR WORLD-GKNW. run_14906cb7b914 is excluded twice over and neither exclusion depends on the size of the number: the assessment took the drift fallback on that run (temperature_remaining_offset_k equals remaining_offset_implied_by_drift_k exactly, and the half width is hypot(offset, tau_expected*slope_se) to sixteen digits), so the tau is from a fit it had already discarded; and the fit is degenerate by the rule above, 44018 orbits over 23 orbits of data. So it is not evidence in either direction. The fitted-tau record stays the three rows it was.

Five of the eight reports on disk carry a degenerate tau; they are STALE, not worthless -- no verdict in any of them moves -- and re-running assess_convergence on any run still on disk will null the field.
close_reason: A fit whose tau is not identifiable from its own series now reports null plus the reason plus the span, with the optimiser's number kept under relaxation_fit_raw_tau_orbits. No verdict moves: the raw tau still widens the asymptote's interval, which is how such a fit refuses through the criterion. run_14906cb7b914's 44018 is excluded from world-gknw twice over, by the drift fallback and by degeneracy, so it is no evidence either way and the fitted-tau record is unchanged. Commit 937804cd.

title: Delete the array-section temporaries tstepo_flux creates for eosd: a tenth of the ocean's instructions
description:
tstepo_flux.F:82 calls eosd with two STRIDED sections of a four-dimensional array, `ts1(1,i,j,k:k+1)` and `ts1(2,i,j,k:k+1)`, against a dummy declared `real t(2)`. gfortran packs each into a contiguous temporary before the call and frees it after; disassembling the built executable shows two `call malloc@plt` and three `call free@plt` in the basic block around the one `call eosd_`. It happens once per wet cell per level per ocean timestep.

Measured 2026-08-25 at 100 model years: 9.26 per cent of retired instructions at 36 x 36 x 16 and 7.87 per cent at 72 x 72 x 16.

Do: pass the two levels as scalars, or copy into a two-element local, so no temporary is created. The same pass should delete tstepo.F's six dead array copies (ts_t1, ts1_t1, rho_t1, ts_t2, ts1_t2, rho_t2), which serve only the commented-out OpenMP sections and cost a further 0.56 per cent at 36 x 36 x 16 and 0.38 at 72 x 72 x 16.

Both are correctness-preserving, so the acceptance test is bit-for-bit or a declared ULP count against genie-knowngood/ through genie-main/src/c/compare.cpp built as nccompare, with the tolerance declared in the same commit as the change. Take this BEFORE any parallelisation is designed: it removes an allocator call from the middle of what would become the innermost parallel loop, and it moves the sixteen-thread Amdahl bound from 6.0 to 12.5.

Source: notes/audits/cgenie-parallelism-and-coupling-support.md sections 2d and 2e
notes: MEASURED IN THE BIOGEM CONFIGURATION TOO, 2026-08-25: the heap share is 11.17 per cent of the shipped regression case at 36 x 36 x 8 with fourteen tracers, against 9.26 at 36 x 36 x 16 physics-only and 7.87 at 72 x 72 x 16. So it does not shrink when the model does more work. Removing it moves the sixteen-thread Amdahl bound from 4.74 to 9.42 in that configuration.
close_reason:
FIXED. eosd now takes t1,t2,s1,s2 as scalars and tstepo_flux passes four element references, so no array-section temporary is created. objdump over the built executable shows zero malloc@plt and zero free@plt in tstepo_flux_, against the two and three the audit disassembled, with the one call eosd_ still there. tstepo.F's six dead copies and their fill loop are deleted, and tstepo_flux_t -- the unreachable second copy of the whole routine those commented-out OpenMP sections called -- went with them.

MEASURED, worjh2 36 x 36 x 16 over 100 model years, retired instructions counted with perf stat: the unedited tree at 4038c12e retires 302.68 G and this branch's serial build 246.64 G, a saving of 18.5 per cent. That figure is the whole of this branch rather than this issue alone: it also carries -frecursive and the threading restructuring, and the three cannot be separated cleanly because the storage class changes what the source change costs. What is attributable here without ambiguity is the disassembly.

Acceptance, against a bar fixed before any arm was built: every float variable in both shipped regression cases BIT-FOR-BIT against the tree at 4038c12e -- 28 variables of eb_go_gs's GOLDSTEIN year-20 average and 88 of eb_go_gs_ac_bg's BIOGEM 3-D fields. analysis/cgenie_omp.py is the driver and analysis/cgenie_omp.json the record.

title: A physical basin depth floor makes the model terrain gravity-dependent, and the generator declares it must not be
description:
WORLD-YRIL changed selectBasins to compare BASIN_MIN_DEPTH_KM against b.depthKm rather than against dimensionless model elevation. That is a units correction and the constant's own name asks for it: the declared 0.05 was demanding between 0.000 and 0.492 km depending where a basin sat, and 22.1 per cent of the preserved catalogue was shallower than its own declared floor.

IT ALSO BROKE A STATED GENERATOR INVARIANT, and vendor/orogen/tools/test-integration.mjs catches it: 'gravity scales PHYSICAL relief as 1/g, leaving the model terrain alone' now fails, r_elevation hashing 4a0df352 at double gravity against 09c8786 at Earth's. Bisected to 7a798274; every commit before it passes.

THE PATH IS REAL, not an artefact of the test. js/pipeline.js:148 runs selectBasins unconditionally during generation; :154 inciseOutlets notches the rims of the SELECTED set; :157 buildBasinProtection constrains erosion over them. So which basins are selected reaches r_elevation. A depth floor in kilometres selects a different set at a different gravity, because relief scales as 1/g while the floor does not, and the terrain moves with it.

THE TWO POSITIONS ARE BOTH DEFENSIBLE AND THEY CONFLICT. The test states the design intent in its own comment: the model's dimensionless terrain must be untouched because erosion constants are calibrated in model units and pushing a scaled parameter through the nonlinear height curve damps the effect instead of delivering it. Gravity is meant to enter at export. Against that, a depth floor named _KM is a claim about a real depth, and comparing it in model units means the catalogue's binding criterion has the wrong units -- which WORLD-YRIL measured as the floor that actually decides the catalogue at the settled region count, admitting 2,521 basins against area's 1,105 and cells' 8.

Note the contrast with PHYS-13, where the glacial altitude gate turned out to be gravity-INVARIANT because two factors of 1/g cancel -- the relief ceiling from sigma/(rho g) and a dry-adiabatic freezing height from Gamma = g/cp. There is no such cancellation here.

Do: decide whether the floor is a physical depth or a fraction of relief, and make the name, the comparison and the invariant agree. If physical, the test's invariant is too strong and must be rewritten to state what IS invariant, the way WORLD-YRIL already rewrote test-basins' gravity assertion (higher gravity may only drop basins, never add one; enumeration order of survivors does not move). If dimensionless, BASIN_MIN_DEPTH_KM is misnamed and the units correction should be reverted with that reasoning recorded. Do not leave the gate red. Evidence: vendor/orogen/tools/test-integration.mjs:76, js/pipeline.js:148-162, js/basins.js selectBasins, notes/audits/basin-catalogue-floor.md
notes:
SETTLED: the floor is a length, and the length is in REFERENCE-GRAVITY kilometres. The two positions in the description were both partly right and the conflict dissolves, as the PHYS-13 contrast suggested it might: reliefScale multiplies the whole land relief distribution, so a floor stated against that distribution carries the same factor as the depths it judges and the two cancel. Same argument computeScarpPotential already makes for the escarpment relief gate from the sigma/(rho g) ceiling. Corroborated by calibration: the L2 detail-noise pass digs pits to 0.05 km through the UNSCALED curve, which is BASIN_MIN_DEPTH_KM's value in BASIN_MIN_DEPTH_KM's currency, so read on Vesper the floor would demand 1.31 noise amplitudes instead of one.

WHAT CHANGED. measureDepression publishes selectionDepthKm beside orderingVolumeKm3, by the same construction and for the same reason; qualifies() compares against it. Equals depthKm at Earth gravity. WORLD-YRIL's units correction is NOT reverted -- the model-unit comparison and its 22.1-per-cent-below-its-own-floor state stay fixed.

MEASURED on both pre-carve builds (LIMITS, not states), via catalogue_floor.py, which now knows three currencies and reconstructs selectionDepthKm from the published spill/sink heights and planet.reliefScale. At 10M: 9,419 as built (model units), 8,024 in reference-gravity km (-1,610/+215), 7,471 in this-planet km (-2,077/+129). The reference-gravity set strictly contains the this-planet set. At 2.5M: 3,621 / 3,065 / 2,879. Cost stated: 553 of the 8,024 are shallower than 50 m as depths on Vesper, the shallowest 38 m = 0.766 x the floor, and none has zero depth (min depthKm 0.0383 against 0.0007 as built).

FOR WHOEVER RUNS THE NEXT GENERATION: the preserved set at 10M drops by about 15 per cent on this terrain, so the carve list drawn from it moves. Nothing in source/ changes until then.

selectionDepthKm is deliberately NOT in the manifest: a field added to basins.catalogue moves hashes.basinCatalogue, which is the signal that a carve verdict still refers to the same basins. basins.resolution declares minDepthComparedIn = 'km at reference gravity' and minDepthReferenceGravityMS2, and the number is exactly reconstructible from published fields.

GATE: test-integration.mjs and test-basins.mjs both pass (127 tests across tools/), smoke_test 38/0. Three assertions pin the currency and each was verified to FAIL against the reading it forbids -- comparing b.depthKm fails 3 tests across the two files, comparing b.depth fails 3.
close_reason: Depth floor compared in reference-gravity km: selectionDepthKm beside orderingVolumeKm3, name/comparison/invariant agree, both gravity tests green and each assertion verified to fail against the readings it forbids. Reasoning in notes/audits/basin-catalogue-floor.md and selectBasins.

title: Reconvergence needs its own criterion: the cold-start test costs 35 orbits to decide something that settles in 10 to 20
description:
WORLD-OMN derived the convergence window from the declared bar and got 35 orbits, bracketed 21 to 43.9, because on a settled run the fit has nothing to grip and the fallback statistic's standard error at a 10-orbit window exceeds its own 0.15 K threshold. That derivation is sound and it is now what assess_convergence.py computes. It was then applied to RECONVERGENCE, and docs/src/pipeline/sequencing.md now says a reconvergence is one convergence window then three-orbit increments, while admitting in the next paragraph that the first block is longer than the reconvergence itself, which settles in ten to twenty orbits.

THAT IS THE WRONG CRITERION FOR THE QUESTION, not a window that needs widening. The cold-start criterion asks whether a state is trendless, established from scratch against the model's own variability. Reconvergence asks whether the transient introduced by a conversion has decayed -- and there the pre-conversion state is KNOWN, so there is a reference point the cold-start test does not have and does not use. Testing for absence of trend when the target is already known discards that information and then charges 35 orbits for it. The user's operational experience, recorded in exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md, is that reconvergence after a timestep change or a conversion settles in 10 to 20 orbits; a criterion that cannot decide inside that is measuring the wrong thing rather than measuring the right thing carefully.

THE TWO CONVERSION KINDS ARE NOT THE SAME PROBLEM and may want different tests. A timestep change at constant resolution (T21 at 45 to T21 at 30) returns to essentially the climate it left, so it is a return-to-known-state test and should be the cheapest of all. A resolution conversion (T21 at 30 to T42 at 30) has a genuinely different target, but starts near it, so what is under test is the decay of a BOUNDED DEPARTURE rather than the discovery of an unknown equilibrium.

Do: design the reconvergence criterion, argue it, and implement it in assess_convergence.py beside the cold-start one rather than replacing it. Constraints: thresholds fixed before any result is seen; the criterion needs a right answer, so build a check that can fail on a synthetic series whose true relaxation and true departure you set; and it must be consistent with 10 to 20 orbits or explain why the operational experience is wrong. The escalation in sequencing.md section D and config/pipeline.yaml loop D are updated in the same commit. Evidence: exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md, world-omn, lib/autocorrelation.py
notes:
2026-08-25, coordinator, clarifying the constraint. An earlier framing said the criterion must not loosen its threshold to make ten orbits pass. That is too broad and could push the work away from the right answer.

DERIVE THE TEST AGNOSTIC TO THE ORBIT COUNT, then read the number it needs as a DIAGNOSTIC of whether the test is right. A new criterion that settles in eight or ten or fifteen orbits is a fine and expected outcome -- a cheap test that is a real test is the whole point of asking a different question. A correct test needing significantly more than ten to twenty orbits is the signal to go back to the drawing board, because it probably means the reference point is still unused and the statistic is measuring absence-of-trend in disguise.

What is forbidden is narrower: taking the EXISTING cold-start statistic and moving its threshold until a short window passes. That changes the bar rather than the question and is choosing a criterion after seeing what it judges. Designing a different statistic whose bar is set on its own grounds before any result is seen is what this row asks for, whatever orbit count falls out.

The operational 10 to 20 orbits is the sanity check on the derivation, not a target to fit. Concluding it is wrong remains acceptable, with an argument.
close_reason: Designed, argued and implemented beside the cold-start criterion. The statistic is the remaining departure from a two-parameter decay fitted at the DERIVED relaxation time over the whole post-conversion record, held to the SAME 0.15 K allowance and the same resolving factor of three as the offset criterion: nothing was loosened, the estimator is different. The record length is max(14, relaxation * ln(departure / tolerance)); the 14 is derived from the same nominal scatter, autocorrelation and relaxation the 35 is derived from, and the second term is why ONE criterion covers both conversion kinds -- the fit measures the departure, so a timestep change costs fewer orbits than a resolution conversion without a second test. Fixing the relaxation time is conservative because every large correction to it shortens it; the regime where that fails is a state whose sea ice is reorganising, so the verdict carries the sea-ice criterion rather than assuming it (world-gknw tracks checking the ceiling against fitted values). Synthetic control in scripts/smoke_test.py, with a set relaxation, departure and noise: it fires inside the allowance, refuses outside it, bounds the truth at the coverage a one-sided one-standard-error bound has, survives a faster relaxation, costs less for a smaller departure, and the cold-start statistic refuses the same series at the same length. Measured on those series: a 1.0 K departure decides at 22 orbits against 50 for the cold-start criterion, 0.5 K at 16 against 40, 0.3 K at 14 against 35. The 10-to-20 operational experience is CORROBORATED, not revised: that band is departures of about 0.4 to 1.1 K, and notes/audits/resolution-ladder.md's converted T42 arm met every criterion at 19. sequencing.md section D and pipeline.yaml loop D updated together, with no length carried as a literal.

title: Re-take the T42 ladder comparison with the corrected equilibrium instrument
description:
notes/audits/resolution-ladder.md concludes that the cold-start T42 arm run_1d39fef9bfc2 and the converted arm run_42aaf441b10b are not at the same equilibrium. Every bound in that table came from compare_equilibria.py before world-yj9o was fixed: the standard error was the orbit-to-orbit scatter over the root of the count, which understates it by about a factor of two and by more where the span is not stationary.

Do: run compare_equilibria.py on both arms again now that it takes sigma and tau over the longest stationary tail and refuses a metric whose error it cannot bound. Neither arm is on this machine's runs directory, so this needs them restored or re-run. If they carry fewer orbits at equilibrium than ten times tau, the honest outcome is that the surface rows come back indeterminate, and that is the result rather than a failure to get one.

Blocked on: the two arms existing. Nothing else.
notes:

2026-08-25, user correction. NOT BLOCKED ON MISSING ARMS. The row was read as needing two T42 runs that no longer exist and whose identity was never preserved, and therefore as unrunnable at any effort. That is the wrong frame: the escalation route WALKS THROUGH T42. docs/src/pipeline/sequencing.md section D is T21 at dt 45, converge, reconverge at dt 30 if the conversion needs it, convert to T42 at dt 30, converge. title: compare_equilibria.py understates its own SEM: orbits within a window are not independent
description:
exoplasim/scripts/compare_equilibria.py takes the standard error of a window mean from the ORBIT-TO-ORBIT SCATTER WITHIN that window, which assumes the orbits are independent samples. They are not, and the size of the error is measurable.

MEASURED 2026-08-25 on a pair of 85-orbit T21 runs, run_4769c35837df (eight-byte) and run_073d3e108760 (four-byte arm), identical configuration and cold_start_seed, differing only in compiled precision. The two runs reproduce their own 40-orbit predecessors bit for bit over orbits 0-39, so nothing here is a different draw.

  The difference series has lag-1 autocorrelation 0.615. Eighty-five orbits
  therefore carry about 20 independent samples, not 85, and the SEM is
  understated by roughly a factor of two.

  compare_equilibria --window 20 on orbits 65-84 reports the four-byte arm
  0.1875 K warmer at 7.24 sigma and fails four of six metrics.

  The whole-run mean difference over all 85 orbits, with the SEM taken on the
  effective sample size, is +0.0139 +- 0.0352 K. Four tenths of a sigma.

  And the eight-byte arm's OWN non-overlapping 20-orbit means, one run with no
  precision involved at all, are 291.355, 291.835, 291.757 and 291.651 K:
  spread 0.210 K, range 0.480 K. Every FP32-vs-FP64 window difference measured
  -- -0.068, -0.105, +0.062, +0.187 -- is SMALLER than that.

So the test rejects pairs that differ by less than the model's own low-frequency variability, and it does so with a sigma figure that looks decisive. This is the project's declared instrument for 'are two runs at the same equilibrium' and the failure is not specific to a precision comparison: it applies to every conversion arm SPAT-8 was meant to judge and to any A/B the ladder work produces.

Do: take the SEM on an effective sample size rather than on the raw count. The lag-1 estimate n_eff = n (1-r1)/(1+r1) is the cheap form and is what the numbers above use; a block or a spectral estimate is better and the script already has the whole series in hand. Report the autocorrelation beside the verdict, because a reader cannot otherwise tell a real difference from a window that happened to land on a swing. The criterion's SHAPE -- two sigma on a difference of two means, fixed before the arms are compared -- is right and does not need changing.
close_reason:
FIXED. lib/autocorrelation.py is the one place the arithmetic lives and compare_equilibria.py takes sigma and tau from the longest stationary tail of each run's production series rather than from inside the window, because tau estimated from a 20-orbit span comes back at about half its true value: measured on synthetic AR(1) with a known answer, true tau 4.195 recovers as 1.46 at n=10, 2.28 at n=20, 3.54 at n=85. The script now reads every production orbit, reports tau, the effective sample size and the smallest resolvable difference beside the verdict, and reports a metric INDETERMINATE with the verdict refused where no tail supports a tau. The criterion's shape is unchanged. smoke_test runs the estimator against AR(1) series whose tau is known in closed form and against the empirical spread of window means, with the count-based form as the control it must beat.

Same defect found and fixed in assess_convergence.py: curve_fit scales its covariance as though residuals were independent, so the asymptote half width is widened by the root of the residual tau.

The ladder audit's verdict was re-read against the correction: the two TOA rows survive at about 16 and 13 sigma and the cloud-state conclusion stands, but the surface rows land near 2 to 3.5 sigma and the +0.106 K offset is smaller than the 0.21 K the model's own 20-orbit means move by, so they are not established. Re-taking that comparison is world-yyx8.

title: convert_restart --self-test dies on NLSOILWX, a dimension restart_schema was never taught
description:
`python exoplasim/scripts/convert_restart.py --self-test` does not run. Its 'schema' section raises

  KeyError: "'NLSOILWX' is a dimension no geometry here knows. It came out of a call site, so the model has grown a symbol this module has not been taught."

from `restart_schema.py:818` `Geometry.resolve`, reached through `candidate_counts` -> `Geometry.elements`. `resolve`'s table knows NLEV, NLEP, NLSOIL and the rest; `NLSOILWX` is not in it.

WHERE IT CAME FROM. `landcolumn.f90:44` declares `integer, parameter :: NLSOILWX = 8` and uses it as the shape of the land column's per-layer water and ice arrays. It arrived with the land-column work (dacee645 lshy-5, 4f87bffd lshy-3) and `restart_schema` was not extended with it.

WHY IT SURVIVED. `scripts/smoke_test.py`'s 'the restart schema covers every record the model writes' passes, so the gap is not in POLICY coverage but in dimension resolution, which only `candidate_counts` reaches. And nothing runs `--self-test`: it is not in smoke_test's check list and no script calls it.

A SECOND DEFECT IN THE HARNESS, visible because of the first. `restart_convert_selftest.run()` catches only `Failed`, so a KeyError out of a section aborts the whole self-test with a traceback instead of reporting that section as failed and running the rest. A harness that cannot report its own section failures hides every later section.

Do: teach `Geometry.resolve` NLSOILWX from the model source rather than as a literal (the module already reads shapes out of call sites, so the parameter should come from the same place); make `run()` catch any exception per section; and decide whether `--self-test` belongs in smoke_test, since a self-test nothing runs is the same shape as `rungs.check_restatements` having had no caller.

Found while adding the timestep-contract section under world-fl9c. That section passes; this one has never been reachable since the land-column work landed.
close_reason:
FIXED. restart_schema.parameter_dimensions_from_source() reads the model's integer parameters out of the compiled sources and describe() puts NLSOILWX on the Geometry, so no number is restated here; the source table is consulted only for symbols Geometry.resolve does not already own, so a helper module's local NLAT cannot shadow a file's header. restart_convert_selftest.run() now catches Exception per section, names the type, resolves the donor inside the same guard, and still exits non-zero. All seven sections pass.

On whether --self-test belongs in smoke_test: NO, and the gap it exposed got a better caller instead. --self-test needs a real plasim_restart, which a fresh checkout does not have, so it would have to skip silently on the very tree where a check matters most. The thing that actually broke is dimension RESOLUTION, and restart_schema.check_every_shape_resolves() tests that from the source alone, with no restart file and no run output. It is wired into smoke_test's existing restart-schema check and fails on a shape written in a symbol no Geometry knows, which check_policy_covers_source cannot see because it compares names. Verified it fails in that direction. exoplasim/README.md's 'If you add or remove a restart record' now says a new dimension is a second thing to add.

title: The filter confinement gate computes its crossover from a rate law two timestep pairs refute
description:
scripts/check_consistency.py's 'filter confinement' check solves 2*kappa*x^gamma/dt against the cascade rate x/tau_vorticity and reports x = (dt/(2*kappa*tau))**(1/(gamma-1)), failing below a 0.60 floor. It currently reports 'T21 damps from 0.625 of the truncation' and passes.

THE RATE LAW IS REFUTED. legmod.f90 folds the filter into every per-mode transform WEIGHT, and what passes through those weights is the nonlinear TENDENCY: no filtered value is ever stored back into the prognostic spectral state. So the filter attenuates the source by a fixed factor rather than damping the state at a rate, and its spectral effect carries no timestep. Measured on two pairs differing in MPSTEP alone, same binary by sha, same cold start, same seed:

  T21 gamma 16, dt 45 -> 22.5: depth at 0.8N moves +0.009 dex, 0.1 sigma, where the rate law predicts -0.296 against a three-sigma bar of 0.15.
  T42 gamma 16, dt 45 -> 30:   depth moves -0.007 dex, 0.2 sigma, predicted -0.169 against a bar of 0.08.

The bite point does not move either, at either rung. exoplasim/notes/filter-spectral-price.md carries the measurement and exoplasim/analysis/filter_dt_pair*.json the arms.

AND THE GATE'S NUMBER DISAGREES WITH THE SPECTRUM, in both directions. The gate says 0.625 at T21 where spectral_tail.py's bite point measures 0.561 +/- 0.020 over 22 two-orbit windows, and it says 0.655 at T42 where the bite measures 0.714 +/- 0.000. So a gate meant to catch resolution being damped away passes a rung whose measured spectrum is below its own floor.

The surviving law is spec/law = exp(-2 kappa x^gamma), which puts the half-power crossover at (ln2/(2 kappa))**(1/gamma) -- scale-free, timestep-free, 0.822 at kappa 8 and gamma 16. At gamma 8 the two laws differ by nearly a factor of two, 0.675 against 0.381, and the measured bite is 0.688.

NOT CHANGED HERE ON PURPOSE. Swapping the formula makes the gate pass more comfortably, but the thing it exists to catch -- the measured spectrum departing below 0.60 of the truncation -- is now known to be caused mostly by the HYPERDIFFUSION rather than the filter, so what the gate should confine is a decision and not a substitution. Deciding it needs an answer to 'is a bite point of 0.56 at T21 acceptable', which is a criterion question.
close_reason: Gate fixed and the criterion decided. DECIDED: the gate confines the FILTER and not the measured spectrum. It now asserts the surviving law's half-attenuation point (ln2/(2 kappa))**(1/gamma) -- no dt, no rung -- against the UNCHANGED 0.60 floor; the quantity moved and the bar did not, because re-choosing a bar to suit a corrected quantity is choosing a criterion after seeing the result it judges. It no longer claims to predict a run's bite point: that carries the hyperdiffusion, which is the larger lever, and a config gate has no spectrum to read. spectral_tail.py already fails a run whose bite sits below 0.6 of the truncation and keeps that half. The gate reports the kappa the floor holds to at the declared gamma (1229 at gamma 16), so it is honest about being in practice a guard on gamma; it reports the filter's own depletion at 0.8N beside it, which IS linear in kappa. filter_spectral_cost.py carried the same refuted law and is fixed; --restate recomputed sensitivity and verdict in the five affected result files from their own recorded namelists, measured mean and sd untouched. config/planet.yaml's filter block described the replaced gate and is corrected; no value changed. Commits 67154ee3, d2e2bd00, 50d1e843.

title: mpgetgp scatters an uninitialised buffer when the record is absent
description:
mpimod_omp.f90's mpgetgp declares 'real :: z(NUGP,klev)' as a local with no initialiser, calls get_restart_array into it on the root thread only, and then unconditionally scatters z. get_restart_array (restartmod.f90) RETURNS WITHOUT TOUCHING its argument when the named record is absent and nexcheck is 0. So a mpgetgp under a lowered nexcheck scatters whatever was on the stack, and pre-zeroing the caller's array does not help: the scatter overwrites it.

plasim.f90 already states this correctly in the comment above the ecological stream's version marker, and that block avoids mpgetgp for exactly this reason. landmod's restart read does NOT: it sets dwatcl(:,:) = -1.0, dsoili(:,:) = 0. and adrain(:) = 0. and then calls mpgetgp for each under nexcheck = 0. A restart lacking any of those four records therefore scatters garbage rather than leaving the pre-set value, and the 'if (ALL(dwatcl(:,:) < 0.0))' rebuild test that follows is deciding on garbage. WORLD-P9QQ's adrain and the layered soil store are the affected records.

Do: give the caller a way to know. Either return a found flag from get_restart_array and have mpgetgp zero or leave z accordingly, or zero z inside mpgetgp before the call and change landmod's dwatcl sentinel from -1.0 to a test that reads correctly against zero. The first is the one that does not put a second trap where the first was.

Evidence: vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/mpimod_omp.f90 subroutine mpgetgp; vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/restartmod.f90 subroutine get_restart_array; vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/landmod.f90 restart read block; vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/plasim.f90 comment above the ecovers marker.
close_reason:
restartmod gained has_restart_array (a name lookup that reads nothing) and mpimod_omp gained mpgetgp_found, which asks on NROOT where yresnam and nresnum live, broadcasts the answer with mpbci exactly as mpsurfgp broadcasts its iread, skips mpscgp when the record is absent, and returns the answer in kfound. Not an optional argument: these are external subroutines with no explicit interface, where OPTIONAL is not conforming and PRESENT cannot be relied on, so a separate entry point is the conforming shape. The presence answer therefore reaches every thread the way every other root-only fact does, which mpscgp's omp barriers require.

landmod's four may-be-absent reads (dwatcl, dsoili, ddrain, adrain) go through mpgetgp_found and the rebuild branches on kfound rather than on ALL(dwatcl < 0.0). landini no longer lowers nexcheck at all, because mpgetgp_found never asks for a name the file does not carry. ddrain was the one of the four with no pre-set value at all and is pre-set to zero with the others. Plain mpgetgp now zeroes its buffer, which is determinism rather than safety; what keeps it from being misused is the pair.

Behaviour preserved: a restart carrying dwatcl restores all four records unchanged, and one without it rebuilds the layered store from dwatc on the declared layer shape exactly as before. What changes is that the rebuild now happens when it should, and adrain starts its output window at zero rather than from stack contents.

SWEEP, recorded in notes/audits/absent-restart-records.md. Four sites lower nexcheck: read_atmos_restart's stamped geometry, the ecovers block and the accuvers block in plasim.f90, and landini. The three in plasim.f90 are sound and for the same reason -- what each reads under the lowered nexcheck is a SCALAR on NROOT, or an array behind a version marker epilog writes AFTER the whole set, so none goes through mpgetgp and none is exposed to the scatter. landini's was the only member of the silent class. The loud class -- a record read under the default nexcheck that the file lacks, which stops the model with the record named -- is persistt, assolu and asthru, and is a decision rather than a defect: filed as world-t16e.

VERIFIED. exoplasim/scripts/verify_absent_restart_record.sh compiles the real restartmod.f90 at -Og -fdefault-real-8 -finit-real=snan, writes a restart carrying one record and asks for one that is not in it. Four criteria fixed before the run, all met: an absent name leaves get_restart_array's argument alone; has_restart_array answers 1 and 0 and moves no read position; THE CONTROL, the pre-fix mpgetgp shape, delivers a NaN into the caller's array and makes ALL(p < 0.0) come back false; and the mpgetgp_found shape leaves the array at its pre-set value and reports 0, and delivers the record and reports 1 when it is there. The control armed, so the gate has been seen to catch the defect. mpscgp is transcribed rather than linked because it needs the whole of pumamod; what that cannot cover, that every thread takes the same branch, rests structurally on mpbci. verify_model_compiles.py --profile poisoned passes and a full T21 l10 p4 poisoned build with --no-publish links, which is where the two new external subroutines are shown to resolve. smoke_test 28/28, including the restart schema's coverage check (unaffected: the schema scans WRITE sites, and no put_* call changed).

RULE 4: every published binary is now stale. Nothing was published and nothing under exoplasim/runs/ or source/ was touched.

Commits 434a961d, 496e2742 on fanout-BV.

title: The Howard-band water vapour reconstruction is 8-10 percent above every published determination
description:
world-zvk2 declared a bound for exoplasim/scripts/shortwave_band_weights.py's
reconstruction of the Lacis and Hansen Eq. 21 quantity, sourced from the paper
rather than from the run: the envelope of the three published absorptivity
determinations Lacis and Hansen plot together in their Fig. 11 (Eq. 21
Yamamoto, Eq. 22 Fowle, Eq. 23 Korb), widened by the +/-3 per cent Howard,
Burch and Williams (1956) state for the band absorptions the reconstruction is
built from. The grounds are LH74 p. 127: "the uncertainty in their absolute
value is as great as the differences among the three curves."

THE RECONSTRUCTION MISSES IT. Measured 2026-08-25 on the BT-Settl 5772 K solar
reference: inside only at w = 0.01 cm, and above the top of the widened
envelope at every larger amount, by 1.2 per cent at 0.03 cm rising to 10.3 per
cent at 5 cm. The excess is nearly flat above 0.3 cm. The script now raises.

WHY THIS NEEDS A DECISION RATHER THAN MORE MEASUREMENT. Every stated accuracy
in the chain is smaller than the miss, so the miss lives in the step that has
none: Yamamoto's flux weighting, his pressure scaling and his small-w Elsasser
extrapolation, and the 0.72 and 0.81 um bands, which Howard never measured and
which this file carries at the 0.94 um band's shape under WEAK_BLUE_SCALE, a
factor no source supplies. Howard's +/-3 per cent is also an AVERAGE and
excludes the 0.94 um band, fitted on twelve runs and called approximate, which
is a band carrying real solar flux.

WHAT IS ALREADY HANDLED, so this is not an unpriced defect. The file's product
is a RATIO of the star's absorptance to the Sun's, and a flat level offset
divides out of it. The file already prices the extreme attribution: the
`weight_without_2.7_3.2_6.3um_complex` arm charges the whole excess to one band
complex and drops it, which is Yamamoto's own curve 1 and is the low end of the
reported bracket.

DO, and it is one decision with three possible answers:
1. Establish that the offset is a LEVEL offset and not a shape one, by testing
   whether the excess is flat in the band-flux-fraction space the weight ratio
   actually integrates over, rather than flat in w. If it is, the envelope
   check should test the SHAPE the product depends on and the level miss is
   recorded rather than gating.
2. Or find the term that makes it 10 per cent high. WEAK_BLUE_SCALE and the
   band-interval choice are the two candidates with no source behind them:
   Yamamoto's own intervals are wider than Howard's for the 0.94, 1.1, 1.38,
   1.87 and 6.3 um bands, and this file uses Howard's.
3. Or accept that a Howard reconstruction cannot reproduce the quantity to
   better than a flat 10 per cent, declare that, and widen the bound to it with
   the reason stated -- which is only legitimate if the flatness in (1) is
   established first, otherwise it is a criterion chosen after the run.

Do NOT widen the bound on its own. The bound was fixed before the run and the
miss is information.

Evidence: exoplasim/scripts/shortwave_band_weights.py, the block beside
`korb_h2o` and `reconstruction_vs_published_absorptivity_envelope`.

BLOCKED ON NOTHING, but note the script cannot currently run end to end:
config/planet.yaml names no `baseline_climatology` and the prediction blocks
have no fallback by design. The envelope check is climatology-free.
notes:
2026-08-25, coordinator. THE BLOCKING REFERENCE IS NOW HELD, and the shape of the decision is narrower than the title suggests.

WHAT IS ALREADY SETTLED, so it is not re-litigated here. The level error DIVIDES OUT of this file's product. h2o_sw_weight is a star-over-Sun ratio and config/planet.yaml:905 says so; the level correction is already carried as a separate key at 1.127, derived by correlated-k against Eq. 21 in exoplasim/notes/corrk-cross-check.md, which runs 1.10 to 1.15 across the range. WORLD-ZVK2's envelope miss -- 1.012 at w = 0.03 cm rising to 1.103 at 5 cm -- is the same sign and the same magnitude reached by band integration instead of correlated-k, so it corroborates 1.127 rather than contradicting it. Two methods, one answer.

AND THE CHECK IS CORRECTLY SUN-AGAINST-SUN. absorptance_solar is absorptance(sun, ...), so this is not the star's spectrum meeting an Earth-fitted curve. Worth stating because the suspicion is natural: this star puts 58.2 per cent of its flux above 0.75 um against the Sun's 48.3 per cent, a factor of 1.204 more in the near infrared where water vapour absorbs, and Lacis and Hansen's own 'approximately 35 per cent of the solar flux is in the regions of significant water vapor absorption' is a SOLAR constant. That matters for h2o_sw_weight and it does not matter for this check.

SO WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN is one thing: 1.127 is declared ONE-SIGNED AND A LOWER BOUND, because the correlated-k side carries no water vapour continuum. Five sources are now held under references/INDEX.md's radiation section and each answers a different half:
mlawer2012 -- the MT_CKD continuum formulation itself, the missing term. User-supplied; every automated route was closed.
shine2012 -- how large the continuum is and how well it is known, including where the self- and foreign-broadened components are least constrained.
oreopoulos2012 -- CIRC Phase I line-by-line reference cases AND the spread across the codes scored on them, which is an envelope with a right answer.
ramaswamy1992 -- near-infrared reference solutions against which broadband parameterizations of exactly the Lacis-Hansen kind are scored.
freidenreich1999 -- the successor scheme, which reports the error of the broadband parameterizations it replaces.

Do: read them, turn 1.127 into a two-sided number with the continuum included, and decide whether the level correction moves. Then say whether shortwave_band_weights.py's envelope check is measuring the same thing as corrk-cross-check.md and should cite it, or a different thing and should say which. Note that WORLD-ZVK2 left the script raising on the envelope miss, so anything invoking it exits 1 until this is settled.


2026-08-25, SETTLED. Four bars were fixed and committed in 63175256 BEFORE any of the five papers was opened; all four are answered in exoplasim/notes/corrk-cross-check.md.

BAR 1, the key moves. mlawer2012 does not ship an evaluable continuum -- the coefficients follow from summing the line shape over every water vapour line and travel with LBLRTM -- so the term is bounded from shine2012 p. 548: the CAVIAR laboratory continuum adds 1.25 W/m2, about 1.5 per cent, to global-mean clear-sky shortwave absorption relative to MT_CKD, which is 2.1 to 2.5 per cent of water vapour's own shortwave absorption. The total is f/(f-1) times that increment for f the near-infrared window factor by which the laboratory determination exceeds MT_CKD, and over shine2012's and mlawer2012's f of 2 to 12 that runs 2.3 to 5.0 per cent, estimate 3.1. With the transfer to this defined path bracketed at 0.8 to 1.4, the missing term is 0.15 to 7.0 per cent of the correlated-k absorptance. h2o_sw_level goes from 1.127 to 1.163, bracket 1.129 to 1.206, and stops being one-signed. 0.036 is 0.35 K against the 0.02 the bar was set at.

BAR 2, carried as a bracket. Half-width 0.039, which is 0.38 K, so h2o_sw_level_bracket is a new config key and its ends are arms to run: world-u9hq.

BAR 3, the envelope gate is FALSIFIED and stops raising. HITRAN2020 correlated-k, computing the same quantity on the same path, falls outside the same widened envelope at every amount from 0.1 to 10 cm, by 6.1 to 9.8 per cent, inside only at 0.01 cm -- exactly the reconstruction's own pattern. That is a floor because it has no continuum either. A bar a modern line list misses is not a bar on the reconstruction. The comparison is recorded, NOT widened.

BAR 4, they are ONE QUANTITY. Same numerator definition, same denominator, only the absorption data differs. They agree to 0.26 per cent at the operating path against the 3 per cent the bar was set at, and to 0.2-1.5 per cent everywhere from 0.1 to 10 cm. The 1.012-to-1.103 envelope miss and the 1.10-to-1.15 correlated-k figure were never two answers to one question: the first has the widened three-curve envelope top as its denominator and the second has Eq. 21, and between 0.3 and 5 cm those differ by exactly Howard's 1.03. shortwave_band_weights.py now carries CORRK_RATIO_TO_EQ21, H2O_SW_LEVEL and H2O_SW_LEVEL_BRACKET as declared constants and raises if its reconstruction disagrees with the correlated-k ratio by more than 3 per cent.

UNASKED-FOR FOURTH METHOD. ramaswamy1992 Table I p. 11,491 scores Lacis and Hansen (1974) itself against a line-by-line reference with no continuum, and finds them under-absorbing by 8 to 11 per cent, ratio 1.091 to 1.123. Not folded into the bound -- a real slant column is a different quantity from a homogeneous 760 mm Hg path -- but it corroborates the base. oreopoulos2012 shows all 13 CIRC shortwave codes under-absorbing against an MT_CKD-2.0 line-by-line reference; freidenreich1999's successor scheme is still -1 to -2 per cent on clear-sky column absorption with the sign never flipping.

FILED, not fixed: world-o3t1 (h2o_sw_level has no artifact-vs-config check because its generator cannot run), world-njlb (the two methods part by 14 per cent at 0.01 cm), world-u9hq (run the bracket arms), world-4m7r (the held CIRC PDF has only its odd pages).
close_reason: Both halves done. (1) h2o_sw_level is two-sided and MOVES: 1.163 over a bracket of 1.129 to 1.206, from 1.127. The continuum adds absorption to the line-by-line side, so 1.127 was a floor as declared; the missing term is 0.15 to 7.0 per cent of the correlated-k absorptance, estimate 3.1 per cent, bounded from shine2012's 1.25 W/m2 CAVIAR-minus-MT_CKD increment and mlawer2012's per-window laboratory factors of 2 to 12. mlawer2012 supplies no evaluable coefficients, so the term is bounded from Shine as the constraint required. h2o_sw_weight untouched at 1.346: the continuum moves it 0.004, worth 0.03 K. (2) shortwave_band_weights.py's envelope check and corrk-cross-check.md measure the SAME quantity through different denominators -- the ratio_to_eq21 arm is Eq. 21 and is identical in definition to the correlated-k ratio, agreeing to 0.26 per cent at the operating path; the 1.012-to-1.103 envelope excess is that same ratio divided by the widened three-curve envelope top, which between 0.3 and 5 cm is exactly Howard's 1.03. The script now carries the correlated-k ratio and the level as declared constants and raises if its reconstruction disagrees by more than 3 per cent. The envelope gate stops raising because HITRAN2020 correlated-k misses the same envelope by 6 to 10 per cent at every amount from 0.1 to 10 cm: falsified as a gate, not widened. All four bars were fixed and committed in 63175256 before any paper was opened. Five papers marked read in references/INDEX.md. Follow-ups filed: world-o3t1, world-njlb, world-u9hq, world-4m7r.

title: The ocean surface has been absorbing longwave it reflected, and every run in the tree carries it
description:
notes/audits/surface-longwave.md finding 1.

radmod.f90:lwr applied its non-black-surface correction over jlev = 1,NLEV. ztausf is dimensioned (NHOR,NLEV), so the surface level NLEP never received the term and the reflected part of the downward longwave was propagated up through the atmosphere without ever being debited from the surface.

dlwfl(:,NLEP) is what landmod and seamod settle the surface energy budget with and what output code 177 reports, so the modelled surface absorbed (1-eps)*LWdown that it had just reflected while the lowest atmospheric layer paid for it. Identically zero while eps is 1, and never zero over water: ELWSEA is 0.98, so every ocean and sea-ice cell in every run in the tree carries a spurious 0.02 of the downward longwave as absorbed energy.

The solver is fixed. This issue is the CONSEQUENCE: the surface energy budget of every existing run and climatology was integrated with the defect, and the land side moves too now that the land emissivity is no longer a blackbody.

Do: nothing until the canonical climatology lineage is being declared, and then make sure nothing seeds from a run that predates the fix. Named here so the fix is not mistaken for a change that only affects runs made after it.
acceptance_criteria: No run or climatology that predates the lwr surface reflection fix is in the canonical lineage or is seeded from.
close_reason: Discharged by the run purge. The solver defect is FIXED -- radmod.f90's lwr now applies the non-black-surface reflection at NLEP, so the surface is debited for the longwave it reflects, verified against the merged tree. This row was left open to carry the CONSEQUENCE: every run in the tree had integrated the surface energy budget with the defect, worth about 7.5 W/m2 over water against a surface net longwave of 52.9, and nothing must seed from one. Every run in exoplasim/runs/ has since been deleted -- 247 GB, 54 directories, only the tracked INDEX.json remains -- and every staged surface artifact with them. There is no run left to seed from and no climatology carrying the defect, so the consequence has no referent. Nothing is left to do.

title: The pedology/Cosby capacity gap is regolith depth, not texture: the two consumers disagree about how deep the column is
description: LSHY-1's comparison reports the pedology-vs-LPJ-GUESS capacity ratio as a median 1.585 with a p10-p90 of 0.81 to 2.40, and land-column-property-contract.md attributes the gap to the declared endmember capacities and the Cosby inversion being different numbers for the same texture. That is true at fixed depth and it is the smaller part. Binned on the configured build's T21 map (1019 cells) with the report's own lpj_capacity_mm, which reproduces 1.585/0.81/2.40 exactly, the ratio is a monotone function of regolith depth: 2.033 below 0.5 m (n=325), 1.642 at 0.5-1.0 m (n=249), 1.464 at 1.0-1.5 m (n=176), 1.030 at 1.5-2.5 m (n=187), 0.627 above 2.5 m (n=82). A factor of 3.2 across the range, crossing unity near 1.7 m. So the quoted spread is structure and not scatter, and reporting it as a p10-p90 invites reading it as uncertainty. The mechanism is that the two consumers use different column extents. build_soil.py line 584 sets awc as volumetric*depth*1000 clipped only at the declared minimum and maximum, so it follows regolith to the 3.9 m p99. vesperinput.cpp's apply_regolith_scaling, transcribed at land_column_properties.py:134, fills fifteen 100 mm layers to the contract's 1.5 m physical base and gives layers below the regolith contact only the bedrock fraction. Shallow cells therefore favour LPJ because bedrock still contributes below the contact where pedology has almost nothing; deep cells favour pedology because it keeps multiplying past 1.5 m. 269 of 1019 cells already exceed the column base. CONSEQUENCE FOR WORLD-OF6N: all three unification candidates settle the volumetric states and none of them touches column extent, so adopting any of them leaves the two consumers still disagreeing about how much soil there is. of6n as scoped cannot unify them. This decision is worth more than the gravity suction question it is bracketed with: that one moves capacity 7 per cent with a p10-p90 of 0.924-0.932, this one moves it by a factor of 3.2 across the map. Do: decide whether the physical column follows regolith depth or pedology's capacity stops at the declared column base, and settle it in the contract before or with of6n. Evidence: pedology/notes/land-column-property-contract.md, pedology/analysis/land_column_properties_report.json consumer_comparison, pedology/scripts/build_soil.py:584, pedology/scripts/land_column_properties.py:134
notes:
2026-08-25, coordinator. FOUR OPTIONS COSTED, ONE RECOMMENDED.

A. Stretch fifteen layers to fit the regolith. Dissolves the disagreement rather than resolving it, since pedology's theta*depth and LPJ's sum of theta_i*Dz_i become the same integral, and Dz[] is already a per-patch serialized array. DEAD ON MEASUREMENT: per-layer thickness would run 5.5 mm at p1 and 14.1 mm at p10, and 431 of 1019 cells fall outside a 50-260 mm band, so clamping leaves the disagreement on 42 per cent of the map.

B. Pedology's capacity stops at the declared column base. One line at build_soil.py:584. Drops a median 33 per cent of the water on the 321 cells whose regolith exceeds 1.5 m after WORLD-UYFB's 11.8 per cent rise.

C. Deepen the declared base. Keeps 100 mm resolution; 26 layers to cover p90, 43 for p99. NSOILLAYER appears 155 times across six modules and rootdist in the instruction file must carry NSOILLAYER components.

D. Deep regolith becomes aquifer storage. The architecturally right home, since the contract already declares the 1.5 m base as where soil_liquid stops and the aquifer begins. No home today: transient_saturated_storage is a DECLARED UNREPRESENTABLE in hydrography/config/land_water_ledger.yaml because the groundwater solver is steady-state and carries no storage change. Owner plhy-4.

RECOMMENDED: B, and it is a correction rather than a compromise. LPJ's root distribution spans exactly NSOILLAYER = 15 layers = 1.5 m and the contract declares the rootable column shallower still at 1.0 m, so nothing in the model can draw water from below 1.5 m. awc is a PLANT-AVAILABLE capacity, so multiplying it by the full regolith depth puts non-rootable water into a plant-available number. Capping at the column base is the definition, and it makes both consumers agree on extent by construction. The dropped 33 per cent is not lost physics: it is water that belongs to the aquifer term D would need, so C and D become worth doing when the groundwater solver gains storage and not before.
close_reason: FIXED, option B. pedology/scripts/build_soil.py now multiplies the volumetric capacity by min(regolith depth, column_base_m), with the base READ from pedology/config/land_column_properties.yaml rather than written as a literal, and the same cut applied to both ends of the declared bracket. This is a correction and not a truncation: awc is a PLANT-AVAILABLE capacity, the contract's physical column is fifteen 100 mm layers to the base, LPJ-GUESS's root distribution spans exactly those fifteen layers and the contract's rootable base is shallower still at 1.0 m, so nothing in this pipeline can draw water from below the base. Measured on the configured build's T21 soil map, 1019 cells: 269 carry regolith below the base and on those a median 29.8 per cent of the cell's water was below it; pedology's land-mean capacity falls from 142.0 to 113.8 mm and its median is unchanged at 112.8 because the median cell is shallower than the base. After WORLD-UYFB's 11.8 per cent regolith rise the same map gives 321 cells and a median 32.5 per cent, which is what the next build_soil run will produce. The dropped water is not lost physics: it belongs to the aquifer term the contract already declares this column stops at, and hydrography/config/land_water_ledger.yaml registers transient_saturated_storage as an UNREPRESENTABLE owned by PLHY-4 because the groundwater solver is steady-state. SUCCESSOR, recorded and not done: deepening the declared column, 26 layers of 100 mm to cover the regolith p90 and 43 for the p99 against NSOILLAYER across six LPJ-GUESS modules and a rootdist that must carry one component per layer, becomes worth doing when that solver gains storage and not before. soil_report.json now records the column base, the count of land cells with regolith below it and the median share below it. Commit a33b61bf.

title: Apply the expectation operator to erodibility in the regolith depth law
description:
SPAT-7 measured this as the largest nonlinear reduction in the pipeline. pedology/scripts/build_soil.py area-mixes every rock class's erodibility inside a cell and then applies depth = maximum_depth * P / (P + erosion_weight * E), which is convex in the erodibility. Erodibility spans 0.25 to 3.5 across the export's lithology table, a factor of fourteen, so the mean of the depths is well above the depth at the mean.

Measured on precarve-craton-10m at every ladder rung, notes/audits/nonlinear-spatial-reductions.md section 1: the land-mean gap is 0.19 to 0.28 m of regolith against a 0.02 m bar (regolith.minimum_depth_m), on 63 to 87 percent of land area, at the middle of the sweep of the law's one free ratio. It is ONE-SIGNED across the whole sweep and every rung: mixing first always makes the soil thinner. Refinement reduces it and does not remove it -- T170 still carries 9.4 times the bar.

Do: replace the mix-then-apply order with lib/gridding.py:cell_expectation, which evaluates the law per mesh region and area-averages the result. The operator takes the law as a callable precisely so the order cannot be got wrong at the call site. This CHANGES the soil map and everything downstream of it; the depth moves deeper, never shallower.

Not done in the SPAT-7 batch because pedology/ was owned by another batch while this was measured.
close_reason: build_soil.py now reduces the regolith depth law through lib/gridding.py:cell_expectation: the law is evaluated on each mesh region's own erodibility and the depths are area-averaged over the cell's land. Measured on precarve-craton-10m at T21 against the bootstrap climatology: land-mean regolith 1.4601 -> 1.7449 m, plant-available capacity 139.0 -> 153.8 mm, gap 0.283 m at the land mean on 87.6% of land area, which is the audit's own T21 prediction. The operator's mean arm reproduces the pre-change field to all digits, so the difference is the operator's alone. The one-signed invariant is a check that raises. Commit 0cfdc167.

title: The ntransform constants we changed are mainline LPJ-GUESS 4.1.1, on by default: re-examine as a declared divergence
description:
Established 2026-08-24 by fetching LPJ-GUESS 4.1.1 from Zenodo record 8065737 (SVN r10118, MPL-2.0) and comparing.

WHAT IS TRUE:
- vendor/lpj-guess/modules/ntransform.cpp is BYTE-IDENTICAL to guess_4.1/modules/ntransform.cpp apart from the stripped MPL-2.0 licence header. The CNP fork never touched this file.
- Its own header: '\author Xu-Ri and modified for LPJ-guess by Peter Eliasson, David Warlind and Stefan Olin', $Date 2013-10-14.
- nh3_max (0.001 above pH 6, 0.00001 below) is mainline, verbatim.
- nit_act (min of a*exp(wcont*b) and max(0, 4-5*wcont)) is mainline, verbatim.
- The crossed gas constant is mainline: official line 160 is 'double ngas_inc = f_denitri_gas_max * no3_inc;' inside the NITRIFICATION function.
- It is ON BY DEFAULT for global runs: data/ins/global.ins line 9 is 'import "global_soiln.ins"', and global_soiln.ins line 1 is 'ifntransform 1'. parameters.cpp badins() if it is not declared, so every run declares it.

SO: these are not fork quirks. They are long-standing, default-on code in a very widely used model, and this project changed them under world-nga2/3/4/6/7 on the strength of reading Xu-Ri and Weier.

The arithmetic behind those changes is not in doubt -- exp(2*(pH-10)) alone returns 3.4e-4 at pH 6 and 1.0 at pH 10, which is what the paper's text states the NH3/NH4 ratio is, and nh3_max multiplies a second pH-keyed factor on top. What IS in doubt is whether a project like this should silently diverge from mainline behaviour in a community model, or record the divergence as a declared one.

Do: re-examine world-nga2, nga3, nga4, nga6, nga7 as a SET, with the mainline value recorded beside each changed value and the divergence declared where it stands. Decide per constant whether to keep the change, revert to mainline, or gate it. Consider whether a comparison against a stock-4.1.1 arm is worth building, since the port already exists.

DO NOT treat 'it is mainline' as proof the code is right, and do not treat 'the paper says otherwise' as licence to change it silently. Both are evidence.

RELATED, SETTLED HERE: there is nothing upstream to integrate. Comparing SVN $Date headers across modules/ and framework/, our fork is OLDER than 4.1.1 on ZERO files, identical on 26 and NEWER on 8 (2022 against 2021). The fork is at or ahead of 4.1.1 everywhere.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the five changed constants carries its mainline value and the divergence is declared, or is reverted. The decision per constant is recorded with its reasoning. references/INDEX.md or vendored-upstreams.md records that ntransform.cpp is stock 4.1.1.
notes:
2026-08-24, world-nga9 settled as a DECLARED DIVERGENCE, and the machinery to
declare one now exists. nit_act's falling limb, max(0.0, 4.0 - 5.0*wcont), is
removed on Greaves and Carter (1920), the primary measurement behind Linn and
Doran fig. 1: their mean at 80 per cent of water-holding capacity is 9.6 per
cent of the optimum rather than zero, their only zero is at saturation, and no
single linear map from their axis to WFPS gives mainline both its peak at 0.6
and its zero at 0.8. The rising limb is kept unchanged.

How it is declared, which is the pattern the other four can use:
- vendor/lpj-guess/modules/ntransform.cpp records mainline's line verbatim in a
  comment beside the changed code, under a DECLARED DIVERGENCE FROM MAINLINE
  heading naming this issue as owner.
- biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml carries `divergence: {mainline, owner}` on
  the response function.
- biosphere/scripts/ntransform_gate.py checks BOTH halves: the mainline string
  is in the operator source, so the record cannot go missing, and it is NOT in
  the source with comments stripped, so a silent revert fails. Two fixtures
  cover it. The failure kind is `divergence`.
close_reason:
Re-examined as a set. All five KEEP AS DECLARED DIVERGENCE; none reverted, and the six older divergences in the same file are registered on the same terms, eleven in total.

nh3_max (nga7): forced by arithmetic. exp(2*(pH-10)) alone is 3.4e-4 at pH 6 and 1.0 at pH 10, which is the ratio the paper's text states, mainline's nh3_max is 0.001/0.00001 keyed on the same pH 6, and mainline's own comment calls it the 'maximum conversion ratio from NH4_mass to NH3 gas', which is what fpH is. The mass-transfer-coefficient reading fails on the factor-100 step at pH 6.

The nitrification gas share (nga3): forced. Table 11 brackets RNON+RN2ON at 0.2-4.2 per cent and the code applies the constant as a straight multiplier with no min() between it and the flux, so mainline's 0.33 is the share on every day of every gridcell, 7.9x the top of the bracket.

The crossed reads (nga4): kept, and the weakest and smallest of the five. Four declarations against two uses; the values corroborate the names (0.33 and 0.33 for the two steps of the reduction sequence). Its whole behavioural content once nga3 is settled is the denitrification NO2-to-gas ceiling, 0.25 to 0.33, on a constant unsourced either way. The cheaper option -- leave the reads crossed and move the value on f_denitri_gas_max -- is named in the note and refused, because it puts a denitrification-named constant on a nitrification quantity.

The temperature clamp (nga6): looked like typography and is not. The paper states the response has a Q10 of about 2; unclamped it is 0.594 at 15 C and 1.211 at 25 C, Q10 2.04, and clamped the same interval gives 1.68. The clamp contradicts a number the paper states about the function it is applied to.

The gas partition (nga2): kept, and the one that costs something. It repairs a hard zero N2 below 0.7 WFPS that Weier refutes directly, an N2O:NO regression attributed to a paper that never measured NO, and a logistic in temperature from a single-temperature study; but at 0.90 WFPS mainline's N2 share of 0.846 is inside Weier's interquartile range and the replacement's 0.978 is above all of it. No table 11 constant reconciles the two papers. That cost stays refused as form:denitrification_n2_share.

The machinery: each divergence records mainline's line verbatim at its own site under a DECLARED DIVERGENCE FROM MAINLINE heading, ntransform.yaml carries mainline_divergences with verdict/settles/worth, and the gate checks THREE halves -- mainline recorded, mainline not live, changed line live -- so reverting by deleting both fails too. An instruction-file divergence is checked the same way against global_soiln.ins, where mainline's f_nitri_gas_max 0.25 is now recorded. Six fixtures cover it and all three real-source failure modes were verified to fail.

NOTHING IS EXECUTION-VERIFIED and both arms of the gate say so. The stock-4.1.1 comparison arm is specified and filed as world-9f1v; it can bound what the divergences are worth and cannot settle which Earth calibration is right. docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md now records that ntransform.cpp is stock 4.1.1 with declared divergences, and that there is nothing upstream to integrate.

No behaviour changed by this issue: every constant and every form the model runs is what it was before.

title: Repair the four wetland hydrology defects in the vendored CNP fork
description:
The four source changes biosphere/notes/wetland-activation-contract.md section 2 specifies, all in vendor/lpj-guess, none of them made yet. biosphere/scripts/wetland_gate.py probes for each and refuses activation while the probe still matches, so this row is what makes the gate's WET-SOURCE-* refusals go away.

1. modules/soilwater.cpp, the is_true_wetland_stand() block: bound the infiltration by the water that arrived. It clamps soil.rain_melt to zero when it is smaller than total_potential and then adds the full per-layer deficit anyway, so the simulated wetland creates water. ifsaturatewetlands controls only whether patch.wetland_water_added_today records it, and it records the whole total_potential rather than the created part. Saturation must be an outcome of the ledger, never a source term.

2. modules/soil.cpp: replace soiltype.runon = wetland_runon. A namelist scalar in mm/day applied to every wetland stand carries no catchment. The groundwater solver's recharge and discharge on the native mesh is the seam, through PLHY-4's single exchange.

3. modules/soil.cpp: the annual water-table average is guarded on date.day == Date::MAX_YEAR_LENGTH. Date::next() in framework/guess.h resets day to 0 on the last day of the last month, so day never exceeds MAX_YEAR_LENGTH - 1 and the block is unreachable on the Earth and the Vesper calendar alike. awtp therefore holds the 0.0 it is initialised to, for the whole run and across restarts because it IS serialized, and update_acrotelm_co2 interpolates linearly in awtp, so the simulated acrotelm CO2 is pinned to the pore-water value everywhere and always.

4. modules/soil.cpp, Soil::serialize: it does not carry Wtot, wtd, stand_water, mwtp, Frac_ice or rootfrac. Frac_ice is the current ice fraction and is distinct from the serialized Frac_ice_yesterday; rootfrac is initialised on day zero only. Serialize all six and add the exact-continuity fixture: a run stopped and resumed mid-year reproduces the uninterrupted run bit for bit, which is a check with a wrong answer rather than a different one.

Then declare hydrology.free_water_repair, runon_source, annual_water_table_update and restart_continuity_fixture in biosphere/config/wetlands.yaml. The gate reports a declaration made while its probe still matches as WET-DECLARATION-CONTRADICTED, so the declaration cannot run ahead of the repair.

Source: biosphere/notes/wetlands-peat-methane-audit.md finding 3, biosphere/notes/wetland-activation-contract.md section 2. Split out of WET-3 because the audit, the contract, the declaration and the refusal landed 2026-08-24 while the batch that wrote them was barred from vendor/lpj-guess.
close_reason: All four repaired in vendor/lpj-guess and declared in biosphere/config/wetlands.yaml; gate refusals 32 -> 24 with every WET-3 hydrology refusal gone except water_ledger (PLHY-4's). Commit c201af6d. Two findings filed: world-fuj4 (LPJ-GUESS has no mid-year save point, so the zero-step round trip is not expressible and the fixture is a year-boundary split-run comparison).

title: The dust intensity bracket is playa_clastic's roughness alone, and neither end of it is a measurement of a clastic playa
description:
notes/audits/dust-intensity-levers.md section 4, measured 2026-08-24.

WHAT IS NOW SETTLED. The factor of 10.6 the aeolian roughness bracket puts on
emission is entirely playa_clastic's. Holding playa_clastic at its centre and
sweeping evaporite across its whole declared range moves the emission by 0.6
percent; doing the reverse reproduces 10.415 of the full 10.501. That follows
from the erodible weights, 1.0 against 0.1. So revisiting evaporite's roughness
cannot narrow the intensity and revisiting playa_clastic's is the only thing
that can.

WHY THAT BRACKET IS SOFT. aeolian/config/dust.yaml gives playa_clastic
1.0e-5 to 1.0e-4 m, and neither end is a measurement of a clastic playa.
The smooth end is a MODELLING CONVENTION quoted by Prigent et al. (2005):
'a low surface roughness on the order of 0.001 cm is used to describe active
dust sources'. The rough end is that paper's sand-desert boundary, 'z0 below
~0.02 cm', stepped down one order on the argument that a clay plain is smoother
than a sand sheet. The smoothest MEASURED entries in its Table 1 are 2.3e-3 cm
and 4.0e-3 cm, which sit at and just above the declared centre.

WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN IT WAS. The bracket now reaches past emission into a
cryosphere albedo term through the deposition field (dust-14, itself blocked on
clim-63), so a factor of 10 on deposition is a factor of 10 on that term.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. A measured aerodynamic roughness for a clastic playa
surface, of the kind MacKinnon et al. (2004) supplies for the salt crust and
this project already uses for evaporite. Candidates already held and not read:
references/greeley1997.pdf, the in-situ measurements behind Prigent Table 1's
G97 rows, whose Death Valley set includes playa surfaces; references/laurent2008.pdf,
the later Saharan surface database; and the Callot et al. (2000) geomorphologic
paper filed under its title. Menut et al. (2013) records that the in-situ LISA
roughness for arid North Africa spans 1e-4 to 10 cm, so a per-surface-type
breakdown of that data set would also do it.

DO NOT reach for the export's geometry. Section 5 of the note measures why it
