cannot help: the mesh edge is 7.60 km against centimetre-scale roughness
elements, and erodible connected components are basin-fill provinces up to
4.3e6 km2 rather than playas.
notes:
FROM BATCH AY (lith-27), measured 2026-08-24 on the raw mesh of both builds. This narrows the bracket by changing what the class IS, without touching aeolian/.

playa_clastic IS NOT A CLAY PLAIN, and both ends of the declared z0 bracket were chosen as if it were. It is a RESIDUAL of two geometric conditions in vendor/orogen/js/lithology.js: inside a preserved closed basin (COVER_SEQUENCE basin_fill fires on !!c.endorheic and on nothing else), and NOT within LITHO_SALT_CRUST_DEPTH_FRAC = 0.25 of the sink, which saltCrustMask takes for evaporite. No grain size and no depositional process enters anywhere. Orogen's own class name is 'Playa mud / alluvial fan fill' and the second half is the part that has been dropped.

MEASURED, area-weighted over surface_class, normalised height above the sink: p25 0.633 / 0.544, p50 0.840 / 0.827, p75 0.930 / 0.928 (2.5M / 10M). HALF THE CLASS SITS ABOVE 83 PER CENT OF ITS BASIN'S RELIEF. It is dominated by the basin MARGIN, not the floor.

Steepest descent on elevation_km, bands fixed before the measurement -- below 1e-3 the playa and mud-flat band, 1e-3 to 1e-2 sand flat and distal fan, above 1e-2 alluvial fan and bajada:

  playa_clastic  2.5M  0.6379 | 0.3058 | 0.0563
  playa_clastic  10M   0.5328 | 0.3731 | 0.0940
  evaporite      2.5M  0.7312 | 0.2485 | 0.0203
  evaporite      10M   0.5929 | 0.3735 | 0.0335

The two rows per class ARE the bracket: a gradient measured over a mesh edge is scale-dependent on a self-affine surface, so the finer mesh reports steeper everywhere. What survives it is the shape -- between a third and a half of playa_clastic lies on gradients a mud flat does not have.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE ROUGHNESS BRACKET. It does not supply a z0 and does not reach for the mesh to do so: roughness elements are centimetric and the mesh edge is kilometric, which section 5 of dust-intensity-levers.md already establishes. What it does is say the class is a MIXTURE of two landforms with two different measured roughnesses, so the question is not 'what is a clastic playa's z0' but 'what weights the mud-flat value against the fan value'. Stepping the sand-desert boundary DOWN one order on the argument that a clay plain is smoother than a sand sheet is the assumption this contradicts: a third to a half of the class is a gravel apron, which is rougher than a sand sheet rather than smoother. The rough end is likely too LOW, and the honest narrowing is a two-endmember mix rather than a single value.

ALSO NOTE the class fraction itself moves: playa_clastic is 0.238693 of land on precarve-craton and 0.279782 on precarve-craton-10m (the CONFIGURED build), a sixth more, because the preserved-basin catalogue gains small basins as minCells stops binding. Both are pre-carve LIMITS. If the emission lever is proportional to playa area, the support choice is worth a sixth of it before any z0 is argued about.

Full evidence and the derivation chain: notes/audits/orogen-lithology.md, section 'What playa_clastic is derived from'.

THE CLASS EXTENT THIS ISSUE'S LEVERAGE RESTS ON IS A PRE-CARVE LIMIT, NOT A
STATE. Added by the coordinator 2026-08-24, because two batches each saw half of
it and neither drew the consequence.

The dust side measured that playa_clastic alone reproduces 10.415 of the dust
bracket's 10.501, which is what makes narrowing its z0 the item that matters.
The lithology side measured the class fraction at 0.238693 of land on
precarve-craton and 0.279782 on precarve-craton-10m, and recorded correctly that
both columns are LIMITS governed by failure-modes class 9: the cover rule fires
on the endorheic flag, so opening a basin removes the flag and the floor reverts
to parent material.

Put together: the fraction drops substantially once the carve list is applied,
and it is the fraction that carries the leverage. So

  - 10.415 of 10.501 is an upper bound on this class's share of the dust
    bracket, not its share in the carved world;
  - a narrowing effort sized against the pre-carve number is sized against the
    limit, and the effort may be worth materially less after the carve;
  - and the two builds already differ by a sixth of the class on region count
    alone, because the preserved-basin catalogue gains small basins as minCells
    stops binding, so there is a support dependence stacked on the carve
    dependence.

None of that says do not narrow the bracket -- the roughness is still the
component's largest single uncertainty and the endmember question stands on its
own. It says the ORDER matters: this is worth doing after a carve, or worth
doing with the post-carve fraction estimated first, rather than sized on a
number that is by construction the largest it will ever be.

What does NOT change with the carve is the finding that reopened this: the class
is basin MARGIN rather than clay plain -- half of it above 83 per cent of its
basin's relief, 31-37 per cent in the sand-flat/distal-fan band -- so the rough
end of the bracket is likely too low rather than too high. That is a statement
about the class's composition and it survives the extent shrinking.
close_reason: Bracket re-sourced from measurement. Criteria fixed in 91d5e04 and the derivation script in 495f7a1, both before any value was read. playa_clastic z0 3.0e-5 -> 3.9e-4 m and bracket [1.0e-5,1.0e-4] -> [1.0e-4,8.0e-4] m, from Greeley et al. (1997) Table 2 wind-profile determinations mixed geometrically over the landform bands orogen-lithology.md measures. The declared prediction held: the mix-derived high end is 8.0e-4 m against the 1.0e-4 m threshold, and the smoothest aerodynamically measured playa already sits above the whole old bracket. Class ordering flips, playa_clastic now rougher than evaporite. Emission bracket WIDENS 10.50 -> 1142.6 because the class moved into a steeper part of the drag partition; criterion 5 governs and it is adopted. Instrument checked: feff 0.238 at the rough end against the scheme's stated validity floor of 0.2. Second fix from the same transcription error: within_class_z0 sigma_g 2.736 -> 2.523. dust_baseline.{json,nc} and the old dust_intensity_levers.json are worthless, not purged.

title: f_denitri_gas_max routes a third of gross nitrification to N gas where Xu-Ri gives 0.2 to 4.2 percent
description: global_soiln.ins sets f_denitri_gas_max 0.33, and modules/ntransform.cpp nitrification reads it as the share of gross nitrification leaving as NO plus N2O. Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 11 gives RNON as 0.1 to 4 per cent with a mean of 2 per cent and RN2ON as under 0.1 to 0.2 per cent, so the sum is 0.2 to 4.2 per cent, about 2.2 per cent at the means. 0.33 is 7.9 times the top of that range and 15 times its mean: of every kilogram nitrified the operator routes 330 grams to gas where the paper routes 2 to 42 grams. This is the largest single constant disagreement in the operator and it lands directly on NET_NITRIF, NO_SOIL and N2O_SOIL. Do: decide whether the port intends a different quantity or the constant is wrong, and either way state which. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md
close_reason: f_nitri_gas_max is 0.022 in global_soiln.ins, from Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 11's RNON (0.1-4 per cent, stated mean 2 per cent) plus RN2ON (under 0.1-0.2 per cent, no mean stated), applied by table 8 eqns 3 and 4. Bracket 0.002-0.042; the rule, stated once in the note and used for all three gas fractions, is the paper's stated mean where it states one and the top of the stated bound where it does not. The constant that carried this quantity was f_denitri_gas_max only because the two reads were crossed; world-nga4 moved the reads first. Of every kg nitrified the operator now returns 978 g to NO3 where it returned 670. Calibration entry instruction:f_nitri_gas_max is now 'agrees' and out of the --strict refusal. Not execution-verified: LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree.

title: The model's state does not reproduce across a restart, and the divergence is immediate
description:
MEASURED, not reasoned. T21 L10 p4, cold start, six timesteps taken whole against the same six taken as 3 + 3 with the first segment's plasim_status as the second's plasim_restart.

The first three timesteps are bit-identical. The FOURTH, the first timestep after the restart, already differs by 1.19 K in near-surface air temperature and 1341 Pa in surface pressure. So this is not accumulated round-off: something in the state is not restored. After 24 steps split 12 + 12 the two restarts differ in 60 of 222 records, worst relative difference 1.0 on dcc, with the leapfrog previous-level arrays sdm and spm differing in 4830 of 5060 and 483 of 506 elements.

NOT A RACE. Each arm reproduces itself exactly when repeated. NOT CAUSED BY THE NEW ECOLOGICAL STREAM: the same pair of restart hashes comes out with NECO = 0 and with NECO = 1.

WHAT IT COSTS. Every segmented run is a different experiment from the same run taken whole, from its first step after each model call. Every climatology assembled from more than one segment carries a discontinuity at each boundary. The stellar-cycle runs, the convergence ladder and EFOR-6's replay-seam test all assume the opposite.

WHERE TO LOOK FIRST. sdm and spm are the leapfrog minus-level spectral arrays. A restart that saves the n level and reconstructs n-1, or saves the two at points in the timestep that are not a consistent pair, would produce exactly this signature: a self-consistent state that is not the state the uninterrupted run was in.

Evidence and the exact run recipe: notes/audits/ecological-stream-restart-continuity.md. The comparison tool is exoplasim/scripts/compare_eco_streams.py (structure, bounds, payload, headers, separately) and exoplasim/scripts/diff_restarts.py.

Three obstacles found on the way and worth knowing before reproducing: no restart in exoplasim/runs/ can be resumed by the current model (glaciermod reads persistt and none carries it); exoplasim/bench/bed_check and run_2b20e3324bb0 both carry namelist keys the current sources do not declare (NGUIDBG, ZETA); and a cold start now needs tsst_eq and tsst_pol declared in icemod_nl.
close_reason: glacierini ended both branches with an unguarded call mpscsp(sp,spm,1), overwriting the leapfrog minus level that read_atmos_restart had just restored; surfini runs below the restart read in prolog. Guarded with nrestart == 0 in 97c05751. With the guard a run split in two is bit-identical to the same run taken whole in all 222 restart records at 2=1+1, 6=3+3 and 24=12+12, and a zero-step restart round trip loses nothing; without it the round trip loses spm alone and it comes back as sp element for element. NOT a regression from worktree-world-wt-1: main loses spm the same way and the same guard fixes it there. exoplasim/scripts/verify_restart_continuity.py is the measurement as a gate. Every binary under vendor/exoplasim must be rebuilt (rule 4).

title: Nothing in the gate set compiles the model, so a tree that cannot build passes every check
description:
world-33ba/world-6dcz: landmod.f90 lost a continuation marker, so the namelist statement ended early and `,snowcovz` began a statement with a comma. gfortran rejects it and landmod is the only object that fails, which stops the link -- no binary could be built from the tip. It survived a merge and five parallel batches, and smoke_test reported 24/24 the whole time.

The reason is structural: smoke_test and check_consistency read the model SOURCE as text and never invoke a compiler. Every existing check of the Fortran is a grep or a parse. So the one property that makes model source usable at all -- that it compiles -- is checked by nothing until somebody runs rebuild_binaries by hand, and rule 4 means that is exactly when it is most expensive to discover.

Two levels are wanted and they are not alternatives:

1. A CHEAP LINT in smoke_test, for this class specifically. A continued statement whose continuation is dropped shows up as a source line whose first non-blank character after the fixed-form marker is a comma, or as a continuation chain that ends where the next line clearly continues it. That is a fast text check and it would have caught this instance in the commit that made it.

2. A REAL COMPILE, somewhere it is affordable. `gfortran -fsyntax-only` over the compiled source set in build order, against the flags config declares, including -fdefault-real-8. Note the trap: without -fdefault-real-8 the selectors world-ako added report a spurious REAL(4)-to-REAL(8) mismatch, so a syntax gate run on the wrong flags invents defects. The module dependency order is already known to CMakeLists' _sources list, and restart_schema.compiled_modules() already parses it.

Do: build 1 and 2. Each must be PROVEN to fail on the broken tree -- 81dcba5e is the commit that does not compile, so a check that passes on it is not the check. Say what 2 costs and where it belongs; if it is too slow for smoke_test, it belongs in check_consistency or its own verify_ step with a pipeline row, not nowhere.

Do NOT satisfy this by rebuilding binaries in the gate. The question is whether the source compiles, not whether an executable is current; rule 4 already owns the second.
acceptance_criteria: Both checks exist and both are demonstrated to fail on 81dcba5e's landmod.f90 and pass on the current tip. The compile gate runs under the flags config/planet.yaml declares, -fdefault-real-8 included, and its cost and location are stated.
close_reason: Both levels built and both demonstrated to fail on 81dcba5e's landmod.f90. Level 1: smoke_test's check_no_dropped_continuation, a text check over every .f90 in plasim/src and exoplasim/scripts, reports landmod.f90:256 and is clean on the tip. Level 2: exoplasim/scripts/verify_model_compiles.py, gfortran -fsyntax-only over the 36 translation units CMakeLists names in use order under the declared flag line including -fdefault-real-8, reports gfortran's Invalid character in name at landmod.f90:256 and passes on the tip. Cost is 36 front-end invocations, no codegen and no link; it lives in its own script, is run by smoke_test with --skip-compile to opt out, and is registered under checks: in config/pipeline.yaml and in exoplasim/README.md. The passive rule 4 half is world-wkci.

title: No gate can get a bed: make_profile_bed's cold beds are refused by icemod and its namelists carry keys the model has dropped
description:
Found 2026-08-24 while getting world-5rs, world-klr and world-knr a bed to run on. Every transform gate in exoplasim/scripts takes a bed as its first argument, and nothing in the tree can currently produce one that runs.

TWO FAILURES, IN ORDER.

1. THE NAMELIST CARRIES KEYS THE MODEL NO LONGER DECLARES. make_profile_bed.py copies the source run's namelist files verbatim and edits a handful of keys. Every run on disk predates wave 1, so the copied plasim_namelist still carries NGUIDBG and carbonmod_namelist still carries ZETA, both of which wave 1 removed. The model dies in readnl with 'Cannot match namelist object name nguidbg' before it reaches a timestep. A bed made from any existing run has this.

2. A COLD BED IS THEN REFUSED BY icemod. icemod.f90:641 aborts with 'a cold start with no sea surface temperature climatology' unless either an SST climatology was read (surface code 169) or TSST_EQ and TSST_POL are declared in icemod_nl. The refusal is right -- the model must be told which case it is in rather than guessing -- but make_profile_bed's --cold path declares neither, and no run directory or exoplasim/inputs/t21 or t42 carries an N???_surf_0169.sra. So --cold produces a bed that cannot start. exoplasim/bench/bed_check, the only bed on disk, is cold with TSST_EQ = -999 and is in this state too.

3. AND THE WARM PATH IS NO BETTER, for a third reason: the restarts on disk predate wave 1's restart layout change, so a warm bed from run_2b20e3324bb0 dies in get_restart_array with 'Requested array {persistt} was not found'. That one is rule 7 working as designed -- the runs are disposable -- but it means the warm route is not available either until a run exists on the current model.

WHAT WAS DONE TO GET PAST IT, so the gate results of 2026-08-24 are attributable: a cold T21 bed from run_2b20e3324bb0 with the two unknown keys stripped and TSST_EQ = 300.0, TSST_POL = 273.0 written into icemod_namelist by hand. Those two numbers are a bed initial condition and nothing read them into a world value.

Do: make_profile_bed.py should produce a bed that runs. That means dropping from each copied namelist any key the model's own namelist statements do not declare, and reporting which it dropped in the manifest the way it already reports the keys it changed; and declaring the cold-start sea surface temperature profile rather than inheriting -999. The second half is a DECISION about what a cold verification bed starts from and belongs with config/planet.yaml's other declared initial conditions rather than being invented per bed.
notes:
TWO CORRECTIONS to the description, found after filing.

1. THE COLD-START PROFILE IS ALREADY DECLARED. config/planet.yaml:301 carries ocean.cold_start with sst_equator_k 300.0, sst_pole_k 273.0 and sea_ice_thickness_m 0.0, and run_exoplasim.py:286-288 stages all three into icemod_namelist as TSST_EQ, TSST_POL and HICE_INI. So the second half of the Do is NOT a decision -- it is make_profile_bed.py failing to force keys the config declares, which it already has a mechanism for: CONFIG_FORCED at line 69 does exactly this for NENERGY and NENER3D and needs three more rows. The source runs predate that staging, so a bed inherits an icemod_namelist that has none of the three.

2. THE HAND-EDITED BED THEREFORE CARRIED THE DECLARED VALUES. The 300.0 and 273.0 written by hand for the 2026-08-24 gate runs are ocean.cold_start's own numbers, so the gate results of that day are on the project's declared cold-start profile and not on an invented one.

The first half of the description is unchanged: nothing prunes namelist keys the model has dropped, and NGUIDBG and ZETA both kill a bed made from any run on disk before it reaches a timestep.
close_reason: make_profile_bed.py now prunes every namelist key the model's own namelist statements do not declare (derived from plasim/src, with the file-to-group binding taken from each module's open/read pair) and forces TSST_EQ, TSST_POL and HICE_INI from ocean.cold_start alongside NENERGY/NENER3D, keyed by namelist file. --seed defaults to model.cold_start_seed instead of restating it, and require_settled_bed refuses to WRITE a cold bed with KICK and no fixed SEED. Proved by running: a cold T21 bed from run_2b20e3324bb0 on a T21 binary built from this tree integrates 60 steps and writes plasim_status, with plasim_diag recording the cold start from the declared SST profile. Two negative controls: NGUIDBG restored kills it in readnl, TSST_EQ/TSST_POL removed kills it in ice_cold_start.

title: Declare the PROPAGATING uninitialised-read gate; nothing checks that class at production's optimisation level
description:
world-5rs measured the positive control and it settles the -O question against the trapping form: a deliberate uninitialised read at the head of gridpointd faults with SIGFPE at -Og and exits 0 at -O2 and at -O3, and the -O2 and -O3 binaries carry the compiler-folded quiet NaN in .rodata beside the signalling one -finit-real=snan stores. So -finit-real=snan is a trap only at -Og, which production does not run, and it now lives in the poisoned profile rather than in checked.

That leaves production with no zeroing and no check of this class at its own optimisation level. -finit-real=zero was removed on the argument that a check which can FAIL beats a tax that hides what it protects against, and it was worth 26.03% of T170. Re-adding it is NOT an option: exoplasim/notes/the-zeroing-is-an-init-flag.md measured the restart bit identical without it, so it hides the defect rather than catching it.

The one check that does work at production's optimisation level is the PROPAGATING form, because it does not need the trap to arm. Build with -finit-real=snan and FE_INVALID MASKED, run a bed, and compare the restart bit for bit against production's on the same bed. If anything uninitialised reached a stored value, the poisoned initialisation changes that value; the fold to a quiet NaN does not defeat that, because a quiet NaN in a stored record is just as visible as a signalling one. That gate produced the evidence the 26.03% trade rests on, taken once on 2026-08-22 at e1733979 at T170, 60 steps, NSHTNS=1, NLOWIO=1.

It has not been run since. Wave 1 changed the model heavily and world-qml changed surfmod.f90.

Do: declare it. A driver beside the other exoplasim/scripts/verify_*.sh, a row in config/pipeline.yaml so it is part of the graph, and a fixed criterion -- the two restarts must be bit identical, with the advisory-record policy of verify_shtns_model.sh if any record needs one. It needs one extra binary per rung it runs at and one bed run per check. The masking is the part to get right: -ffpe-trap=invalid is in f90_opts, so the arm has to drop it rather than add anything.

Source: notes/audits/uninitialised-reads-and-implicit-save.md finding 1, and exoplasim/notes/the-zeroing-is-an-init-flag.md.
close_reason: exoplasim/scripts/verify_uninitialised_reads.sh: shipped flag line against the same line with -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow dropped, -ffpe-trap=zero,overflow added back and -finit-real=snan added; plasim_status compared bit for bit, no tolerance. Two verdict arms, NSHTNS=1 (production) and NSHTNS=0 (model isolated from SHTns's own scratch over-read). Declared as a checks row in config/pipeline.yaml with its cost, and a row in exoplasim/README.md. Run at T21/16/60 steps on a cold bed from run_2b20e3324bb0: both arms bit identical, and the control -- an external subroutine with one never-written local folded into the temperature tendency through a run-time zero -- is rejected, its shipped arm staying bit identical to the unpatched shipped arm. the-zeroing-is-an-init-flag.md and notes/audits/uninitialised-reads-and-implicit-save.md finding 1 both rewritten.

title: No gate compiles the model source, so a Fortran syntax error reaches the merged tip
description:
world-khn added snowcovz to landmod_nl without extending the continuation on the line above, and the whole model stopped compiling: gfortran rejects landmod.f90 with 'Invalid character in name' and nothing downstream of landmod builds. Every wave-2 worktree carried it. scripts/smoke_test.py passed on that tree, because nothing in it compiles the model source, and check_consistency.py did not object, because the binaries in vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/run were built from an older source than the tip, so a run would have picked up a stale executable rather than failing.

The defect itself is fixed. What is not is that a syntax error in the model source is invisible to every gate the project runs before a commit.

Do: add a check that the model source COMPILES. The cheapest form is a syntax-only pass -- gfortran -fsyntax-only over plasim/src with the same -cpp and -fdefault-real-8 the real build uses, which needs no linking and no resolution -- run from smoke_test.py. It must not build a binary and must not touch the resolution ladder or the registry. A second, separate question is whether check_consistency.py should refuse a binary whose recorded model_source does not match the tree, which is rule 4's failure mode reached passively.
notes:
EVIDENCE from batch AK, 2026-08-24. This is not hypothetical any more. The merged tip d09dba4c did not compile at all: landmod.f90's namelist had lost a continuation marker (world-6dcz), and every build of every configuration failed at that file. Six batches' worth of static review had passed over it. The first thing batch AK did with a compiler was hit it, and nothing in that batch -- four gates, all of which build the model -- could have run until it was fixed.

Two further defects in the same class, both invisible to any static check and both found by running:

- verify_threaded_numerics.sh's model half had NEVER executed. build_arm asked build_model.py to publish, and the wrongband control writes a control-patch marker that build_model.py refuses to put under the registry's tag, so the control arm exited 'build failed or stale' every time it was asked. Fixed under world-knr.
- No bed in the tree can start the model: make_profile_bed's namelists carry keys wave 1 removed, and its cold path leaves TSST_EQ at -999, which icemod now refuses. Filed as world-99hq.

So the cost of no compile gate in this wave was one broken tip, one gate that had never run, and one class of input that no longer works, and every one of them was found in the first hour of having a compiler.
close_reason: Settled by world-adts: smoke_test now runs a dropped-continuation lint and gfortran -fsyntax-only over the compiled source set, both demonstrated failing on 81dcba5e's landmod.f90. The second, separate question it raises -- whether check_consistency should refuse a binary whose recorded model source has moved -- is world-wkci.

title: The in-model dust emission quadrature is a rule world-494 replaced offline, and the boundary-field mirror still matches the old one
description:
build_dust_source_fields.py --self-test is RED and exits 1: max relative error 6.619e-03 against a declared 1e-10. It is failing honestly, and what it is reporting is a divergence between the offline chain and the model, not a defect in the check.

build_dust.emission_over_weibull integrates over [0, S_t] in SURVIVAL space and scales by S_t/n (world-494, commit cd8c2dab, 2026-08-24). build_dust_source_fields.py:190-207 and the Fortran it mirrors, exoplasim/patches/exoplasim-3.4.2-dust-emission.patch, integrate over [0,1] in PROBABILITY space and scale by 1/n. The two coincide only at u_t = 0. At k = 2.012 and n = 96: at u_t/c = 1.5 the q-rule puts 10 of 96 nodes above threshold and the survival rule puts 96; at u_t/c = 3.0 the q-rule puts ZERO, so the mirror returns exactly 0 where the reference returns a finite flux. world-494 measured the old rule as biasing every arm low, -10% at 15% active and -100% below 0.01% active.

So whatever a rebuilt binary emits is not what the offline chain computes, and the identity is currently unsatisfiable.

Do: port the survival-space rule into the patch -- compute zst = EXP(-(zut/zscale)**dustwk), set zq(n) = (-LOG(MAX(zst*(REAL(n)-0.5)/REAL(dustnq), tiny)))**(1.0/dustwk), and scale the accumulated total by zst/dustnq rather than 1/dustnq -- then mirror the same two changes at build_dust_source_fields.py:190-191 and :207. CLAUDE.md rule 4 then applies: rebuild every binary and --verify.

SECOND DEFECT, same file, world-60x0's class and to be fixed in the same pass. build_dust.py:952 broadcasts a PER-CELL z0_aeolian from the erodible lithology mosaic into drag_efficiency; build_dust_source_fields.py:226 and :270 both build drage from a SCALAR -- np.full_like(srcw, z0_aeolian) in build_fields and np.full(n, drag_efficiency([DUSTZ0])[0]) in self_test. Because the self-test's fixture is a constant drage, the identity passes on that axis whatever the boundary field carries, so the mosaic world-c8m added reached only the offline arm. Take the per-cell z0 plane out of bd.source_fractions for the requested bracket end and pass the array; draw the self-test's drage from a randomised z0 array rather than np.full. DUSTZ0 stays scalar only for the ln(zref/z0) term, and if the mosaic is to be honoured in-model that term needs its own field.

THIRD, smaller: build_fields folds erodible * f_clay into dsrcw while production run_one uses bare, which --variant arid_bare_ground raises above erodible. The three fields cannot express that variant and the self-test's synthetic srcw never exercises it.

Not done under world-60x0 because the wave was under a no-compile, no-model-run constraint and the fix requires rebuilding every binary.
close_reason:
The derivation names the in-model half as the wrong one and that is the half that changed. Both rules are quadratures of E = integral_0^1 flux(u(q)) dq, but the probability-space rule's highest node sits at u = c(-ln(1/2N))^(1/k), a ceiling independent of the threshold, so it returns exactly zero wherever u*t clears it; the survival-space rule places every node inside [0, S_t] with its coarsest at S_t/2N, above u*t by construction. aerocore.f90 dustsrc now integrates in survival space, with zstln taken in log space because config/planet.yaml compiles with -ffpe-trap=overflow. build_dust.emission_over_weibull is untouched.

Verified against the shipped subroutine, not a transcription: aerocore.f90 lines 1247-1468 extracted verbatim, compiled with the production flag line including -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow, run on the self-test fixture. Reproduces build_dust.emission_over_weibull to 8.1e-16 relative. The pre-change subroutine on the same harness returns EXACTLY ZERO on 2479 of the 3440 fixture cells that emit.

Second defect fixed in the same pass: build_fields unpacked five values from source_fractions, which has returned six since world-c8m, so it raised before writing anything; and it built ddrage from a scalar. It now takes the bracket-end plane of the roughness stack, and the self-test's drage fixture is drawn log-uniformly across the declared bracket rather than np.full. Verified end to end: the drag partition now spans a range across source cells instead of being one number.

Third defect declared rather than fixed, as world-4qem: --variant arid_bare_ground's dry mask is per time bin and is not a static boundary condition. The residual scalar DUSTZ0 in the ln(zref/z0) term is world-h24h.

CLAUDE.md rule 4 is NOT discharged: no binary was rebuilt. Every binary must be rebuilt and rebuild_binaries.py --verify run before any ldustemit = 1 run. That is blocked on world-6dcz, a dropped continuation marker in landmod.f90 that stops the model compiling at all on this base.

title: verify_weight_factorisation compares two restatements of the same product, not legini against the model
description:
world-60x0's sweep found this and it is the fixture-self-agreement shape at full strength.

verify_weight_factorisation.py's compare() builds a dict it calls `legini` from zpli, zpld, a, b, znn1, mm, nn, zgwd and zgwdcsq, and a `got` from the same nine quantities. legini is a PYTHON TRANSCRIPTION of legmod.f90 and is never read from it, so for qi the comparison is zpli*a against zpli*a*1.0, and for qm it is (zpli*zgwdcsq*mm)*b against zpli*(b*mm)*zgwdcsq. Every one of the eight is the identical product reassociated, which the docstring itself concedes at about one ulp for six of them.

It therefore proves float reassociation, not that legini builds those eight matrices that way. The negative control break_qm fails only because it perturbs the per_mode restatement while leaving the legini restatement alone; a transcription error in either, or in legini_recurrence which feeds BOTH sides, cancels exactly. CLIM-48 rests on this.

verify_legendre_parity.py carries a SECOND independent hand-transcription of the same recurrence; neither is checked against legmod.f90.

Do: the correct pattern is already in the tree. verify_inverse_transform.py's extract(text, name) lifts the loops verbatim out of legmod.f90 and compiles them. Do the same for legini, or at minimum read legmod.f90 and assert each of the eight assignment lines textually before trusting the legini dict. Then re-derive CLIM-48's verdict from the strengthened check and say in its note which version measured it.

Not done in world-60x0's sweep because verifying such a fix requires compiling the extracted driver, and that wave was under a no-compile constraint.
close_reason:
verify_weight_factorisation.py now compiles legini verbatim out of legmod.f90 against a stub, and checks pmat, qmat and the six per-mode factors against scipy's sph_legendre_p_all through banded_transform_reference plus the filter's declared formula. Two sides that share no code, so a transcription error no longer cancels. Which table pairs with which factor is extracted from fc2sp, sp2fc, sp2fcdmu, dv2uv and mktend rather than assumed, which is the issue's fallback done as well as the extraction. Five negative controls perturb the extracted Fortran and each must apply exactly once and be caught.

Run at every rung on the ladder, passes at all eight: worst weight 1.6e-14 at T21 and 3.4e-13 at T170 against 8*NTRU^2*eps declared before the arms ran, which the bottom rung clears by 50 times and the top by 153.

CLIM-48's verdict, re-derived in exoplasim/notes/rank-imbalance-and-weight-traffic.md: the correctness sentence there was measured by verify_weight_factorisation_model.sh, which runs the model, so it never rested on the script that proved nothing. What rested on this script was the separability half, and that had no evidence until now. The 1.56% regression verdict is a timing measurement and is untouched.

One mistake stays undetectable and is named in the header rather than papered over: crossing skgpsp and skspgp cannot be caught by anything while nfilter selects one shape for both directions, since the two arrays are then identical element for element. The control in that slot checks the filter is read at the total wavenumber instead, which is the indexing mistake the same block invites, and it is caught on qc and qe.

verify_legendre_parity.py, the second hand-transcription the issue names, is NOT fixed here: its subject is the deleted paired decomposition and the fix is a deletion that needs a design decision first. Filed as world-x3zd.

title: Re-determine the stability grid: every cell was measured on damping the runs do not use
description:
exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md carries the grid the ladder's timestep choices rest on -- which rung refuses at which step, at kappa 8 and with the filter off, and the per-rung cost that follows. Every cell of it is contaminated, in two independent ways, and both are now fixed in the writers rather than in the note.

FIRST, the damping reached one level in ten. ndel and the four tdiss are (NLEV) arrays and a Fortran namelist scalar assigns element one, so nine levels kept readnl's presets: at T21 NDEL=4 with 9*2 behind it, and at T42 the top level in SECONDS where days were meant, damped 86400 times too hard. That is world-td3's blow-up.

SECOND, the probe did not declare hyperdiffusion at all. stability_probe.py only writes the TDISS keys when --tau-scale is given, and the grid was taken without it, so every probe cell ran the model's own built-in damping rather than the values config/planet.yaml derives. A refusal boundary measured on different damping is a boundary for a different model.

So T170's stable step is UNKNOWN. The 22.5 the ladder is using came from this grid, and dt 22.5 costs twice what dt 45 does at every rung -- at T170 that is the difference between roughly 21 and 42 hours for fifty orbits.

A third correction is about the instrument rather than the inputs. The grid's cells are 600-step probes and, in two places, a single orbit. T42 at dt 45 passed a two-orbit arm and blew up in its forty-seventh, so a probe qualifies a step against REFUSAL and nothing else. The re-determination has to separate the two verdicts and say which one each cell carries.
acceptance_criteria: A grid re-measured with --tau-scale 1 on the fixed writers, reporting refusal separately from endurance, with each endurance cell stating how many orbits it actually survived; the note's tables rewritten; and the ladder's per-rung step chosen from it.
notes:
Raised after finding the per-level namelist defect (committed daff50f4). The first clean data point is run_3e1e116f99ee, T42 from cold at dt 45 with 10*-valued damping, where the previous attempt at that step died in orbit 47. The probe must be run alone: it prices steps from wall time and any concurrent run corrupts that.

WORKED 2026-08-25. VERDICT: NOT DONE, blocked on a rebuilt and manifest-named
binary set. The writers are fixed and the procedure is recorded; the grid is
not re-taken, and re-taking it now would produce a cell as unattributable as
the ones it replaces.

WHAT IS FIXED IN THE WRITERS (commit d35a996e):
- stability_probe.py's --tau-scale now DEFAULTS to 1.0, so every probe writes
  the derived NHDIFF, NDEL and TDISS* over all NLEV levels. It wrote them only
  when --tau-scale was given, and the 2026-08-23 grid was taken without it.
  --inherited-damping is the explicit arm for the old behaviour.
- --refusal-only runs one probe and reports the refusal verdict with NO cost
  field at all. The issue's two verdicts are now two code paths, and the half
  that does not need a quiet machine can be taken on a contended one. A cost
  differenced against a shared wall clock is worse than no cost.
- Every cell carries a `declared` block naming the gamma and the damping it was
  measured on, which is what the old grid omitted and what made it unreadable
  three months later.

A THIRD CONTAMINATION, from world-qnue and larger than the two in the issue.
The 22 entries in analysis/stability_probe.json name no executable, no sha and
no template; the file's single `generated` field is rewritten on every write so
there are no per-entry timestamps; find_template selected by mtime; and run
directories are untracked. So a cell is not merely measured under the wrong
damping and the wrong gamma -- it is measured under an unknown build. That is
why the grid is re-taken from scratch rather than patched: there is no cell in
it a new cell could be compared against.

THE BLOCKER, and it is not the host. Rule 7: the grid rests on the model, the
fan-out is still landing changes under vendor/exoplasim, and a boundary measured
against a moving source is worthless on arrival rather than stale. Two things
have to be true first: every binary rebuilt, and binary_manifest.json
describing the tree -- it currently predates the parmode-axis removal, so
--verify reports all five MATRIX rows missing and the registry is empty. That is
a stale registry and is not evidence about the damping.

The cost half is separately blocked on a quiet host and stays blocked here: the
probe prices a step by differencing two lengths, so a concurrent run biases it
in one direction rather than adding noise.

THE COMMAND, recorded in exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md under
"What it would take to re-take this grid", refusal half first:

  python exoplasim/scripts/stability_probe.py --rung T170 \
      --sweep 45,30,22.5,15,10 --kappa 8,off --refusal-only --steps 600

once per rung in T21, T42, T85, T127, T170, then the same sweep without
--refusal-only. --tau-scale and --gamma default to config/planet.yaml.

WHAT THIS GRID ALSO OWES, folded in from world-6on rather than duplicated:
model.resolution_timestep_minutes' measured-ceiling column is unread against the
filter the model runs. Every entry was taken at gamma 8 and the model runs
gamma 16, and T42 at dt 90 is measured to refuse at the first and run at the
second. config/planet.yaml's table now says so at the table.

NOT AFFECTED BY ANY OF THIS: the spectral work under world-6on, which is taken
from run directories whose manifests name an executable sha, and which
calibrates against nothing in stability_probe.json.

2026-08-25, coordinator, ON MERGING MAIN. MAIN RE-TOOK THE GRID AND THE RE-TAKE IS ALSO SUPERSEDED. It stays open.

Main found two instrument defects this branch had not, and both are kept:
  THE PROBE RAN SIXTEEN MODELS AT ONCE. find_template preferred an MPI binary and fell through to the threaded one when none existed -- which is every rung, since rebuild_binaries' MATRIX is five omp rows -- then launched it under mpiexec -np 16. That does not run one model on sixteen threads; it runs sixteen independent models in one directory over each other's output. Every cell of the old grid was measured that way.
  NOTHING ABOVE T42 WAS REFUSING. The master thread runs on the PROCESS stack, no OMP variable moves it, and the threaded build is -frecursive so the model's large locals are stack-allocated. Above T42 the master overruns a 16 MB limit and takes SIGSEGV before writing a record; the probe read that as a refusal and reported the rung impossible at every timestep. That is the shape the grid had for T85 and above. Fixed with ulimit -s unlimited through a shell.
  Main also split refused_only_at_length from refused as its own verdict, which is WORLD-TD3: collapsing them is what let T42 at dt 45 read as usable when it dies in its forty-seventh orbit.

WHY THE RE-TAKE DOES NOT CLOSE THIS. Main's tree did not carry this branch's work, so its grid was measured before all of the following, each of which reaches the cells:
  WORLD-6ON refuted the rate law the timestep ceilings were reasoned from. The filter folds into per-mode transform weights and what passes through them is the nonlinear TENDENCY, so its spectral effect carries no timestep at all. Two timestep pairs measure 0.1 to 0.2 sigma where the rate law predicts several times the bar.
  WORLD-BA0's null is withdrawn: the derived damping moves the T21 spectrum by 6.4 sigma, more than the whole of filter_kappa is worth. Hyperdiffusion is the larger lever, not the filter.
  Three batches changed vendor/exoplasim Fortran after main's grid was taken -- WORLD-3QFZ's band-resolved solar accumulators and accuvers 2.0, CONS-15's namelist rewrite, GRAV-8's snow density coupling, and WORLD-ONW8's absent-record fix in restartmod, mpimod_omp and landmod. Rule 4: every published binary is stale against them, so no cell of main's grid names a model this tree can build.
  WORLD-ANL and WORLD-QNUE: entries written before the manifest check name no executable at all.

SO THE ORDER IS FIXED. Rebuild the binaries first, then re-take, and take the refusal half with --refusal-only on a contended host since it carries no cost field. The probe now records executable name, sha256 and build profile per cell, and every cell records the damping it was measured on, so the next grid is the first one that can be attributed at all. Nothing in exoplasim/analysis/stability_probe.json written before 2026-08-25 should be used as an anchor, including main's.
2026-08-25, batch fanout-W1. VERDICT: NOT DONE, and the blocker is NEW. The two
this issue was waiting on are gone -- every binary was rebuilt and the manifest
describes the tree -- and the run purge that discharged them removed the thing
the probe stages from.

THE PROBE HAS NOTHING TO STAGE A BED FROM. stability_probe.py copies staging; it
does not build it. A bed needs a namelist and the rung's surface .sra family,
and both come from a run directory that already exists. exoplasim/runs/ holds
INDEX.json and nothing else, so find_template refuses at every rung. Verified by
running it: `--rung T21 --dt 45 --refusal-only` exits on "no run directory
carries N032_surf_*.sra and a T21 binary".

AND THERE IS NO STAGING TO REBUILD ONE FROM EITHER. pipeline.py --status reports
boundary_conditions, surface_albedo, surface_roughness, surface_soil_water,
surface_dust and dust_source_fields all MISSING, so exoplasim/inputs/<rung>/ is
empty at every rung and run_exoplasim.py has no surface family to stage. Getting
back to a probeable tree is the whole surface chain and then one arm at the rung,
a failing one being enough.

WHY THIS BATCH DID NOT JUST DO THAT. Three reasons and each alone is sufficient.
The surface builders are another batch's files and were being edited while this
ran, so a grid measured on staging they are still changing is rule 7's
worthless-on-arrival rather than stale. run_exoplasim.py stages into
exoplasim/runs/, which this batch was told not to write. And the binaries exist
in the main checkout's build directories, which are deliberately not linked into
a worktree, so this worktree would have to build the five MATRIX rows first --
cheap, and not the binding constraint.

THE ORDER, unchanged from before and now with its first step named:
  1. Build the surface family for each rung to be probed.
  2. Stage one arm per rung; a crashed one serves.
  3. Rebuild the binaries in whatever tree the probe runs in, and --verify.
  4. Refusal half, --refusal-only, then the cost half on a quiet machine.

WHAT THIS BATCH DID FIX, before any measurement rather than after (commit
b591b397):
  * Every cell now records the sha256 of its namelist and of each surface .sra
    in its bed. A cell that named its executable and not its surface fields was
    half attributable: the same probe on the same binary over a different land
    mask is a different boundary, and `template` is a path into an untracked
    UUID-named directory nobody can resolve later.
  * --template names the run directory outright. Selection was still by
    modification time and silent about it; the default still takes the newest
    candidate and now says how many it chose from.
  * find_template's refusal names the real precondition instead of "run one arm
    first", which is not actionable in a tree with no surface family to run an
    arm with.

NOT RE-DERIVED HERE, and it reaches the grid: world-6on's refutation of the rate
law is now in the gate and in config/planet.yaml (world-ugxo, closed). The
timestep ceilings this grid exists to replace were reasoned from that law, so
the re-take is measuring a boundary that no longer has an arithmetic prediction
to be compared against -- which makes it the only evidence there will be.

2026-08-26, THE AUTHOR RESTATES WHAT THIS ROW IS FOR, and it is narrower and
more valuable than "re-take the grid": THE GOAL IS THE MAXIMAL-dt ROUTE -- the
largest step each rung can actually carry, so the escalation's TOTAL run time is
as short as it can be. The refusal grid is an input to that and not the answer.

THREE CONSEQUENCES.

REFUSAL IS NOT ENDURANCE, and this project already owns the counterexample. A
900-step probe is about a seventh of an orbit at dt 45. T42 is probe-clean at
EVERY column the grid measured, 45 and 60 included, and it blew up in its
forty-seventh orbit at dt 45. So a refusal ceiling systematically overstates what
a rung carries, and a route set from refusal cells buys a blow-up at hour twenty.

THE STEPS ARE COUPLED. convert_restart refuses a conversion across a change of dt
(WORLD-FL9C), so every rung change happens at constant dt and the step converted
AT is the step the TARGET rung commissions at, with the DONOR settling to it
first. The free variables are three, not five: T21's commissioning step, the step
T42 commissions at, and the step T85 commissions at. They cannot be maximised
per rung independently.

AND THE BIG LEVER IS T85, WHICH LOOKS LIKE IT WAS LEFT BEHIND BY THE BUG THIS ROW
IS ABOUT. The route runs T85 at 22.5. lib/rungs.py's CORRECTED
STABILITY_CEILING_MINUTES puts T85's refusal ceiling at 45, and
COMMISSIONING_EVIDENCE has NO T85 row at all -- so 22.5 rests on nothing about
T85. It is very likely a leftover from the contaminated grid, the one where
nothing above T42 appeared to refuse anywhere because the master thread overran a
16 MB stack and took SIGSEGV before writing a record, which the probe read as a
refusal at every timestep. That artifact is fixed and the ceiling moved with it;
the route's number did not.

WHAT IT IS WORTH: steps go as 1/dt, so T85 at 30 rather than 22.5 is 25 per cent
fewer steps at the most expensive rung on the route, and it shortens T42's
settling block by the same factor. At 45 it is 50 per cent. That is the largest
single saving available in the escalation.

WHAT CAPS IT: the T42-to-T85 conversion is at constant dt, so the step is bounded
by T42's endurance as well as T85's. T42 endured 30 for 84 orbits and blew up at
45 in orbit 46 -- and WORLD-TD3, which owns that mechanism, is DEFERRED, so 45
cannot be assumed safe at T42. On the evidence that exists, 30 is the defensible
target for that conversion, and it is already the 25 per cent.

SO THE DELIVERABLE IS: the three route steps, each backed by an ENDURANCE verdict
naming the orbits it survived rather than by a refusal cell; the attributed
refusal grid beneath them; and the route's TOTAL cost under the candidate step
sets, so the saving is a number rather than an argument.

2026-08-26, CORRECTION TO THE NOTE ABOVE. It said T42 at dt 45 "cannot be
assumed safe" while WORLD-TD3 is deferred, and treated 30 as the cap on the
T42-to-T85 conversion. THAT IS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN.

THE 46-ORBIT BLOW-UP WAS OBSERVED ON SUPERSEDED SOURCE and is not evidence about
the model being run. Batch 2 changed rainmod, fluxmod, radmod, seamod, landmod,
plasim and outmod, and every binary was rebuilt from that source. So T42 at dt 45
is UNMEASURED on the current model rather than known-bad, and the deferral of
td3 caps nothing.

TEST 45 AT T42 ON ITS MERITS. Both outcomes are useful. If it endures, the
conversion can happen at 45 and T85 runs at 45 instead of 22.5 -- 50 per cent
fewer steps at the most expensive rung on the route, double the saving the note
above quoted, and td3 is very likely retired by whatever batch 2 fixed. If it
blows up, that IS the reproducer td3 has lacked since its run was deleted without
an archive stub, and the ladder blocks on the mechanism at that point with a
fresh crashed directory to work from -- which is exactly the condition the
deferral was written against.

IF IT BLOWS UP, PRESERVE THE RUN DIRECTORY AND ITS RESTARTS FIRST AND INDEX IT.
That is what was lost last time, it is WORLD-WW6Z's failure mode, and it is what
turned a ninety-second diagnosis into an unrecoverable one.

AND CARRY THE QUESTION UP: T85's corrected refusal ceiling is 45 as well, so if
45 holds at T42 the conversion step may be able to go there rather than stopping
at 30.

title: Tissue C:N and C:P proportions are applied to window endpoints, so the model uses 12.36 and 15.30 where its sources measured 6.9
description:
Pft::init_cton_limits and Pft::init_ctop_limits set cton_sap_max = cton_leaf_max * frac_leaftosap and ctop_sap_max = ctop_leaf_max * PFRAC_LEAFTOSAP, and the same for the fine-root pair. The constants are therefore ratios of window ENDPOINTS. But what reaches the simulated plant is a ratio of window MEANS: canexch.cpp:1406 computes sapwood N demand against cton_leaf_opt * cton_sap_avr / cton_leaf_avr and canexch.cpp:1578 computes sapwood P demand against ctop_leaf_opt * ctop_sap_avr / ctop_leaf_avr, with the root pair alongside at 1573.

avg_cton and avg_ctop are harmonic means, and the leaf and sapwood windows have very different widths, so the applied proportion is 0.94737 * frac * (1 + frac_mintomax) / 2, not frac:

  sapwood, phosphorus: 0.94737 * 6.9 * (1 + 3.68) / 2 = 15.30
  sapwood, nitrogen:   0.94737 * 6.9 * (1 + 2.78) / 2 = 12.36
  fine root, phosphorus: 0.94737 * 1.16 * 2.34 = 2.57
  fine root, nitrogen:   0.94737 * 1.16 * 1.89 = 2.08

The sources measure the tissue mean, not the endpoint. Friend, Stevens, Knox and Cannell (1997) Table 4 p. 254 and text p. 274 give X_C:N(f/p) = 0.145, reciprocal 6.897, as a mean across nine species of measured tissue C:N ratios, used in Hybrid v3.0 Eqs. 42-44 to hold relative TISSUE ratios fixed. Heineman, Turner and Dalling (2016) Table 3 gives a species-mean tissue proportion of 7.44 for nitrogen at their sample mean. Two independent datasets agree at 6.9 to 7.4 and the model applies 12.36.

Two consequences.

(1) The check that fails: after init_cton_limits() / init_ctop_limits(), cton_sap_avr / cton_leaf_avr should equal the tissue proportion the constant is sourced from, and it is 1.79 times it on the nitrogen side and 2.22 times it on the phosphorus side.

(2) A side effect of widening PFRAC_MINTOMAX from 2.78 to 3.68 under BIO-34 that was not intended by that change: the phosphorus and nitrogen window factors are now 2.34 and 1.89, so the effective sapwood and fine-root P-against-N proportions moved by 1.238. That silently breaks the PFRAC_LEAFTOROOT derivation, which rests on Yuan et al. (2011) finding root N:P not separable from leaf N:P and therefore a contrast of exactly 1.0; the model now applies 1.238.

Do: decide whether the constants stay at the window endpoint or move to the tissue mean, on BOTH elements together. It cannot be settled for phosphorus alone, and moving the nitrogen side changes the established C-N configuration's results, so this is a decision and not a repair. If they move to the tissue mean the divisor is 0.94737 * (1 + frac_mintomax) / 2 in each place. If they stay at the endpoint, the guess.h comments must stop attributing them to sources that measured something else, and PFRAC_LEAFTOROOT's derivation has to be redone against the applied 1.238 rather than the intended 1.0.

Nothing here is execution-verified; LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree. Evidence and the full arithmetic are in biosphere/notes/phosphorus-cycle-parameterisation.md, section 'Sapwood: the constant is nitrogen's, and it is not the quantity the model applies'.
notes:
Full extent established, both elements, static source and literature only. No
build, no run: LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree. Nothing below is
execution-verified. No value was changed.

THE COMPLETE TABLE. applied/declared = [2m/(1+m)] * (1+f)/2 with m = frac_maxtomin
= 0.9 and f = frac_mintomax.

  N sapwood  non-crop  frac_leaftosap  guess.h:2371   6.9  f=2.78  applied 12.355  source 6.897  x1.791
  N root     non-crop  frac_leaftoroot guess.h:2368   1.16 f=2.78  applied  2.077  source 1.163  x1.786
  P sapwood  non-crop  PFRAC_LEAFTOSAP guess.h:289    6.9  f=3.68  applied 15.296  no source
  P root     non-crop  PFRAC_LEAFTOROOT guess.h:250   1.16 f=3.68  applied  2.571  contrast 1.238 vs derived 1.0
  N sapwood  CROPGREEN f=5.0                          6.9          applied 19.611  source 6.897  x2.843
  N root     CROPGREEN f=5.0                          1.16         applied  3.297  source 1.163  x2.835
  P sapwood  CROPGREEN f=7.77                         6.9          applied 28.664  no source
  P root     CROPGREEN f=7.77                         1.16         applied  4.819  contrast 1.238

That is all of it. The crop stem pair is the only other tissue in the same demand
construction and is NOT affected: cton_stem_avr / ctop_stem_avr are set directly
as means at guess.h:2405-2406 and :2452-2453, and guess.cpp:2034/:2045 read them
in exactly the form the four constants above are read in. That is also internal
corroboration of which quantity the construction wants.

WHICH IS RIGHT: the applied number, verified against the papers rather than
assumed. Friend Eqs. 42-44 hold relative TISSUE C:N fixed with no window at all;
d/c = X_C:N(f/p) * Cp/Cf gives C:N_sap / C:N_leaf = 1/X = 6.897 at every nitrogen
status, and X is a mean over nine species. cton_leaf_opt * cton_sap_avr /
cton_leaf_avr is that same fixed relative ratio applied to an individual's own
current leaf ratio. Heineman regresses species-mean tissue concentrations, so its
proportion is also between means. Friend Table 8 p.280 ranks X_C:N(f/r) ninth of
76 parameters (0.665) and X_C:N(f/p) twenty-sixth (0.337), so 1.79 on them is not
a detail.

ROOT CAUSE is not the constants. It is that the tight root/sapwood window is
anchored on cton_leaf_max while frac_maxtomin sets its width independently.
Anchoring it on the MEAN instead makes applied == declared for any f and any m,
keeps both sourced values, preserves the tighter-window property m encodes, keeps
the respcoeff normalising sum at 1.95x the mean, and makes PFRAC_LEAFTOROOT's
contrast exactly 1.0 independent of both leaf window widths. Same inversion
init_ctop_min() already performs on the leaf window.

COST TO THE ESTABLISHED C-N CONFIGURATION, hand arithmetic:
- fine-root and sapwood N demand per unit tissue carbon both x1.7905.
- whole-plant structural N requirement x1.256 (no sapwood) to x1.535 (6 kgC/m2
  sapwood), at leaf C:N 30 and 0.3 kgC/m2 each of leaf and fine root. Illustrative
  composition, not a prediction.
- maintenance respiration: guess.h:2399-2403 renormalises respcoeff so that path
  is invariant, BUT global.ins sets acclimated_respiration 1 and
  respiration_acclimated() never reads respcoeff, so on the CONFIGURED path
  sapwood and fine-root maintenance respiration scale as 1/cton directly, up to
  x1.7905 in the N-replete limit and less when N-starved (the cton_sap() floor
  moves by the same factor).
- NPP = 0.75 (A - Rm), so at Rm/A of 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.40 NPP falls to 0.80 / 0.66 /
  0.47 of present in that limit. Rm/A is BRACKETED, not measured: no accepted
  respiration diagnostic exists (physiology audit finding 10).
Phosphorus side moves nothing that limits growth: ifplim 0, and refused anyway.

CROSS-EFFECT ON PFRAC_LEAFTOROOT: the derivation is sound and is not delivered.
Applied contrast = (1+3.68)/(1+2.78) = 1.238; Yuan's point estimates support
0.879 to 1.164 (the 1.02-1.35 constant bracket / 1.16). 1.238 is outside it. The
mean anchor returns it to exactly 1.0 and keeps 1.16; the endpoint anchor needs
0.937 and would need redoing whenever either leaf window moves.

LEFT OPEN, and the question is: take the mean-anchored repair now, which divides
every fine-root and sapwood C:N by 1.79 and makes every established C-N number
worthless, or gate it behind a declared re-commissioning? The alternative of
keeping the endpoint anchor is not a live option: it leaves all four constants as
free parameters attributable to no measurement and still needs
PFRAC_LEAFTOROOT = 0.937.

Documented without changing any value in commit 28b36e6f: finding 11 of
biosphere/notes/plant-physiology-carbon-allocation-audit.md carries the table,
the paper reading and the repair; guess.h says at each constant what is applied
and what is sourced; the phosphorus note answers the Yuan question in place.
close_reason: Mean-anchored the fine-root and sapwood C:N and C:P windows in Pft::init_cton_limits and Pft::init_ctop_limits, on both elements and both phenology arms, per the user's decision. <tissue>_avr = <leaf>_avr * frac, <tissue>_max = <tissue>_avr * (1+m)/(2m), <tissue>_min = m * <tissue>_max, the same inversion init_ctop_min() performs on the leaf window. Applied/declared is 1.000 for all four pairs in both arms: 6.9 sapwood and 1.16 fine root on both elements, against 12.355/2.077 (N non-crop), 15.296/2.571 (P non-crop), 19.611/3.297 (N CROPGREEN) and 28.664/4.819 (P CROPGREEN) before. The Yuan et al. (2011) fine-root N:P contrast returns from 1.238 to exactly 1.0 and PFRAC_LEAFTOROOT is decoupled from PFRAC_MINTOMAX permanently. The respcoeff normalising sum stays 1.95 times the tissue mean, so respiration() is invariant. The crop stem pair is untouched. Constants keep their sourced Friend et al. (1997) values and frac_maxtomin/PFRAC_MAXTOMIN stays 0.9, now setting the window WIDTH only. Every fine-root and sapwood C:N divides by 1.7905 and every C:P by 2.2168, so every C-N number the model has produced is worthless; world-zbeq carries the re-measurement and world-vnbc the acclimated/respcoeff instruction-file decision. The ifplim refusal is narrowed: PFRAC_LEAFTOSAP stays refused on the element, the form Heineman et al. (2016) rejects, and the level, the applied 6.9 now sitting below the 10.1 to 15.5 bracket rather than at the top of it by cancellation. guess.h, parameters.cpp, the physiology audit finding 11, the phosphorus note and biosphere/README.md all describe what is now the case. Nothing is execution-verified: LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree. Commits 65d259c5 and 0a052ffe.

title: notes/external-model-survey.md lost sections 12 to 59 in commit 39d3d5b0; 4149 lines, recoverable
description:
Commit 39d3d5b0 ("radmod's surface albedo quotient now covers one interval") appended sections 11f and 11g to notes/external-model-survey.md and, in the same write, deleted everything after them: the file went from 5486 lines to 1388 and its body now stops at section 11g. The commit's diffstat records 4192 changed lines in that file against 303 insertions across the whole commit, so the loss is a whole-file rewrite from a partial copy rather than an edit.

The document's own index table lists 59 sections and states the invariant that every section is either cited by a bd issue or named there as opening nothing. 48 of those 59 sections no longer exist in the body, so every citation to them dangles. Confirmed dangling from this batch alone: BVOC-6's notes cite sections 42a, 46a and 48; notes/external-tree-checklist.md cites 40a, 40b, 40c, 42e, 43c, 45b, 46b, 46c, 47d, 48c, 48d, 48e, 51a, 51c, 52b, 53b, 53e and 54b; notes/external-source-inventory.md cites 46c; clim-62's notes cite 45c-d. The truncated file's own section 4 index row is what earlier work read for BIG-MITgcm.

RECOVERY, and it is clean: the pre-truncation content is `git show bc8525d8:notes/external-model-survey.md`, 5486 lines. Sections 11f and 11g are the only content added by 39d3d5b0 and they must be kept, so the restore is that file with 11f and 11g re-inserted after 11e, not a plain checkout.

Not done in batch W: the file is outside that batch's owned set and other wave-2 batches may be editing it, so restoring 4100 lines there would have been a merge conflict rather than a fix. Whoever takes it should hold the restore in one commit that touches nothing else.

Not a revert: 39d3d5b0's 47 insertions were real work -- 11f and 11g on the repaired albedo quotient and on a stale binary in a run directory -- and they are the only content postdating bc8525d8, so the restore is bc8525d8's text with that block spliced back at its place after 11e.
