close_reason: read_atmos_restart reads nlat, nlon, nlev and nrsp before any array read and refuses a mismatch by name, printing both geometries and pointing at convert_restart.py. Placed above the first get_restart_array because a mis-sized unformatted read has already done its damage by the time anything downstream could notice. An UNSTAMPED restart is not a MISMATCHED one: nexcheck is lowered for the four reads and a value that did not arrive stays at its -1 sentinel and passes, which is the accuvers pattern already in the file. The refusal is broadcast with mpbci and the stop is on every task, not only NROOT -- a root-only stop would leave the others waiting in the next collective. plasim.f90, commit 446698e0.

title: A filter-stripped control binary occupies the registry's own build directory
description:
build_model.py composes the build directory tag from resolution, layers, ranks, parmode, profile, frame pointers and the flag delta. The STATE OF THE MODEL SOURCE is not in that tag, so verify_shtns_model.sh's in-place patch of shtnsmod.f90 builds its control arm into the same directory the registry entry claims.

Measured 2026-08-24: build/t21_l10_p16_omp_production/plasim.x is sha 6523babd32fbb827 with ZERO filter sites in its preprocessed shtnsmod.f90-pp.f90, which carries the CONTROL PATCH IN PROGRESS marker, against 11 sites in the live source and sha e0830f776ecb9a4f in plasim/run/most_plasim_t21_l10_p16_omp.x. Still present on a re-check at 09:50.

--no-publish fixed the half that overwrote the shipped binary. The build directory half is untouched and --print-path hands its caller that exact path. The drop+extra hash in tag() exists to keep arms apart; a source patch is an arm the tag cannot see.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 1.
acceptance_criteria: Either the source state enters the build tag, or an arm that patches model source gets its own build root. A verification arm can no longer leave a binary under the registry's tag for any rung.
close_reason: Fixed: build_model.py detects the control-patch markers in plasim/src, builds under build/patched/<tag>_s<hash> instead of the registry's root, and refuses outright when the caller asked to publish. Registry tag unchanged for a clean tree. The existing stale binary is left as an artifact.

title: The dust intensity may be a tabulation bias, and soil texture is the lever that was never examined
description:
Menut et al. (2013), read after world-c8m closed, qualifies its answer in two
ways that the closure did not account for.

THE TABULATION ITSELF BIASES HIGH. Their finding, comparing the in-situ LISA
data set against the ERS satellite retrieval: "The LISA dust fluxes are, on
average, higher than the other model configurations. This is mainly due to the
distribution of z0 values: being TABULATED, values are more discrete and thus
less variable and realistic than those provided by ERS from satellite data."

world-c8m replaced one scalar with two tabulated per-lithology values, which is
LISA's approach and not ERS's. The central land-mean dust AOD moved from 0.0938
to 0.4133 in that change, and 0.41 is Saharan-everywhere. Menut gives a
mechanism for a high bias of exactly that shape, so the jump may be the
tabulation rather than the world.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Within a lithology the roughness is not one value: a playa
has smooth interior and rougher margins, and this project has the geometry to
say so -- the basin solution knows each basin's area, its sink and whether it
overflows. A distribution of z0 within a class, rather than one value per class,
is the ERS-like direction and is buildable from what is already on disk.

AND THE INTENSITY LEVER IS SOIL TEXTURE, NOT ROUGHNESS. Their decomposition: for
a given soil data set, two roughness data sets differ mainly in the SPATIAL
DISTRIBUTION of the flux; for a given roughness data set, two soil texture data
sets differ mainly in its INTENSITY. world-c8m treated roughness as the whole of
the uncertainty in the ANSWER, and on this evidence roughness mostly moves WHERE
the dust is. Nothing in this project has examined what its soil size
distribution does to the dust intensity, and `pedology` owns that field.

A third, smaller: using a drag partition at all lowers fluxes by a factor of 2
to 3 against not using one, which is worth knowing when comparing this project's
numbers to any model that omits it.
acceptance_criteria: Either the within-class roughness distribution is built and the central AOD retaken against it, or the tabulation bias is bounded by some other means and recorded. Separately, a soil-texture sensitivity is run on the dust intensity, so that the roughness bracket is not carrying uncertainty that belongs to the texture.
notes: Closed 2026-08-24. The measurement also answers the issue's third caution with this world's own number rather than Menut's Earth one: using the drag partition at all lowers the emission by a factor of 2.7, 9.4 and 64 at the smooth, central and rough roughness arms, against Menut's Earth range of 2 to 3. It is worth far more here because this world's declared playa roughnesses sit further above the smooth-bed value than the Earth distribution he averaged over. notes/audits/dust-intensity-levers.md section 7.
close_reason:
SETTLED, and the answer is no on both halves. Commit 9d5ca4bc; evidence in notes/audits/dust-intensity-levers.md and aeolian/analysis/dust_intensity_levers.json, written by the new aeolian/scripts/dust_intensity_levers.py.

THE TABULATION BIAS IS BOUNDED AND HAS THE WRONG SIGN. Resolving the roughness within a lithology, instead of collapsing it to the tabulated point, multiplies the central-arm emission by 1.017 to 1.400 across the measured spread, and 1.116 under the bounded shape the sources support. Every arm is above one, so the tabulation makes this scheme's emission too LOW, not too high, and cannot be why the intensity is high. The criteria were fixed before the ratios were computed and are in the artifact.

The within-class spread is measured, not asserted: Prigent et al. (2005) Table 1 carries three groups of repeat in-situ values for the same area, and pooling their within-box variance of ln z0 gives a geometric standard deviation of 2.736 with eleven degrees of freedom, bracketed 1.297 to 5.095 by the single-box extremes. It is an upper bound on the within-lithology spread because a Death Valley box holds several surface types. Declared in dust.yaml under drag_partition.within_class_z0 as a REPORTED bias rather than folded into the arms, because each class's bracket is the same kind of range and evaporite's is explicitly MacKinnon's spread over one measurement set; using it twice would double count.

THE CORRECTION IS ONE-SIGNED, so the reported intensity is a floor on that axis and the reopening crossing in notes/dust.md is a floor too. At the rough arm, the only one below the 0.10 land-mean optical depth threshold, resolving the tabulation lifts it across at every measured spread but the narrowest.

THE LEVER DECOMPOSITION DOES NOT TRANSFER EITHER. Across the full roughness bracket the normalised emission pattern holds a correlation of 0.961 to 0.995 and displaces 6 to 17 percent of the total, while the total moves 10.6x. Menut compared two roughness MAPS that differ in space; this project has one map with a level bracket, and a level bracket cannot behave that way.

THE TEXTURE SENSITIVITY IS RUN AND TEXTURE IS NOT THE LEVER HERE, for a structural reason. This world's erodible substrate is clay-rich closed-basin fill and evaporite crust, so 86.9 percent of the emission and 91.6 percent of the erodible area sit at or above Kok's declared f_clay cap, where texture cannot move the flux through that term at all. Under this project's own Earth-calibrated clay (pedology/analysis/earth_validation.json, slope 1.1096, intercept -0.0382) the emission moves 5.7 percent; across the validation RMSE it spans 0.608 to 1.326; halving and doubling the clay spans 4.2. All far below the roughness bracket's 10.6. So the roughness bracket is not carrying uncertainty that belongs to the texture.

THE GEOMETRY ROUTE THIS ISSUE PROPOSED WAS TESTED AND DOES NOT WORK, and that is recorded so it is not tried again. Erodible connected components on the 10M-region export are basin-fill provinces whose area-weighted 99th percentile is 4.3e6 km2, not playas; the area-weighted median height above a component's own floor is 81 m and only 15 percent of erodible area lies within 10 m of it. And the mesh's 7.60 km edge is six orders of magnitude above the centimetre-scale roughness elements the drag partition wants, which is the category error dust.yaml already records for the grid-cell roughness field restated at region scale. The basin solution's area, sink and outlet status are basin-scale facts and carry no roughness-element information; the one distinction the literature does support at that scale, detrital fill against evaporite, is already what the lithology split carries.

WHAT IS NOT NARROWED, and it is now precisely located: the bracket is playa_clastic's roughness alone. Sweeping playa_clastic reproduces 10.415 of the full 10.501 and evaporite's whole range is worth 0.6 percent. Filed as world-ugkw with the candidate sources.

Also closed by the same measurement: the third caution, that using a drag partition at all lowers fluxes by a factor of 2 to 3 against not using one, needs no work here. This component uses one and always has, and aeolian/config/dust.yaml already carries MB95 with its source; the caution is about comparing these numbers to a model that omits the partition.

title: The dust answer is set by one unconstrained parameter: the aeolian roughness of erodible ground
description:
With the quadrature and the bracket's low end both fixed (world-494), the dust
bracket over the T21 bootstrap still spans the reopening threshold:

    arm       z0 m       emission Tg/yr   land AOD
    low      3.3e-06        47984.90       1.7873
    central  1.0e-04         2479.89       0.0938
    high     1.0e-03            0.13       0.0000

    reopening test: land-mean AOD 0.0000 to 1.7873 against 0.10 -> CROSSES

That is a factor of 370,000 in emission across the bracket, and it is ONE
parameter: `drag_partition.aeolian_z0_m`, the roughness of the erodible patch
itself. Nothing else in the calculation is close to this in leverage. Emission
goes as roughly u* cubed above a threshold and u* goes as feff(z0)/ln(z_ref/z0),
so the two ways z0 enters compound rather than cancel.

WHY IT IS NOT CONSTRAINED HERE. `aeolian/config/dust.yaml` says the value is the
aeolian roughness of the erodible SURFACE and not the grid-cell roughness, and
that dust models in GCMs carry a separate aeolian roughness map for exactly this
reason. This project has no such map: it carries one scalar and a bracket, and
the bracket is honest about spanning a wet-smoothed clay pan to a playa carrying
pebbles, ripples and small dunes.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY NARROW IT. The erodible surface here is 17.49% of land and
is built from named lithologies -- `source_map.erodible_weights` gives
playa_clastic 1.0 and evaporite 0.1 -- so the question is answerable in the
project's own terms: what is the aeolian roughness of a playa, and of an
evaporite pan, and do those two want different values? That is a literature
question with a real answer, and it replaces one scalar with two keyed to
surfaces this world already classifies.

UNTIL THEN nothing may read a dust number as a value, and `ndustrad` should stay
off: switching the radiation onto a field whose magnitude is uncertain by five
orders of magnitude would put that uncertainty into the climate.
acceptance_criteria: drag_partition carries an aeolian roughness per erodible lithology, each sourced, and the reopening test is retaken. It may still cross; if it does, that is a statement about this world rather than about a missing measurement, and the dust radiative term is declared absent with that as the reason.
notes: Diagnosed on the first dust build over the converged T21 bootstrap, run_2b20e3324bb0, on 1463 high-cadence wind samples. aeolian/analysis/dust_baseline.json holds the run. references/INDEX.md has no aeolian roughness rows yet.
close_reason:
Sourced per lithology, and the bracket collapses from a factor of 370,000 to
10.6.

    class            z0 m      bracket m              source
    playa_clastic   3.0e-5   [1.0e-5, 1.0e-4]   prigent2005 T1 and 4.1
    evaporite       1.4e-4   [5.3e-5, 3.9e-4]   mackinnon2004 T1/T2 site 208

MARTICORENA ET AL. (1997) IS WHY THEY DIFFER, and it says so directly: Saharan
lakes fed by streams "loaded with detritic sediments became clayey plains with
SMOOTH SURFACES", while "paleolakes, fed by superficial gypseous water, became
EMBOSSED TOPOGRAPHY, sensitive to weathering", with sebkha surfaces varying
"depending on their salt content and on the experienced periods of drying and
moistening". A clastic playa and an evaporite pan are a smooth surface and a
rough, more variable one.

MACKINNON ET AL. (2004) MEASURED THE ROUGH ONE. Their site 208 is a playa
carrying `saltpush` -- "salt push-ups or ridges created by expanding salt and
clay crusts on playa surfaces", 2 cm high, 5 cm apart -- and it is the strongest
sheltering species there, threshold friction velocity ratio 0.75 against 0.98
and 0.99 for the bushes beside it. Its aerodynamically derived z0 is 0.014 cm
over a 0.0053 to 0.039 cm range. That is the evaporite central value and bracket
unchanged.

PRIGENT ET AL. (2005) CARRIES THE SMOOTH ONE. The Bodele and Chott Djerid
depressions, the Sahara's strongest dust sources, "could have been lakes during
former wet climate periods, allowing accumulation of sediments. For those
regions it can be expected that the surface is relatively smooth, with low
roughness parameters." Their convention for active dust sources is 0.001 cm and
their sand-desert boundary is 0.02 cm, which set the ends.

CELLS COMBINE THEM as an erodible-area-weighted GEOMETRIC mean, because the drag
goes as 1/ln(z/z0) and it is ln(z0) that averages. The arms are now fields, not
scalars, so a cell of pure playa and a cell of pure evaporite sit at different
roughnesses within one arm.

REBUILT:

    arm       emission Tg/yr   land AOD   z0 geo-mean m
    low          25718.22       0.9701      1.007e-5
    central      10838.66       0.4133      3.020e-5
    high          2418.14       0.0922      1.006e-4

    reopening test: 0.0922 to 0.9701 against 0.10 -> STILL CROSSES

AND THE CROSSING IS NOW MARGINAL RATHER THAN TOTAL. It used to span "dust is
absent" to "dust dominates"; it now spans 0.0922 to 0.9701, and the only arm
below the threshold misses it by eight percent. The honest reading is that dust
DOES matter radiatively on this world and the open question is how much, not
whether. That is a statement about Vesper -- it carries far more closed-basin
playa than Earth does, at 17.49% of land erodible, and clastic playa is the
smooth end of the roughness range -- rather than about a missing measurement.

THE CENTRAL ESTIMATE MOVED UP 4.4x, from 0.0938 to 0.4133 AOD, and that is the
sourcing rather than a bug: the dominant erodible class is playa_clastic at
weight 1.0, and 3.0e-5 m is 3.3 times smoother than the generic 1.0e-4 m scalar
it replaced. A land-mean dust AOD of 0.41 is Saharan-everywhere and 10838 Tg/yr
is four to ten times Earth's total emission. Both follow from this world having
more playa, and both are worth a second opinion before anything downstream
treats them as settled -- but they are now what the sourced parameters give
rather than what an unsourced one did.

The dust radiative term stays absent: `model.dust_source` is `none` and
`ndustrad` is off, and the reason is recorded here rather than assumed.

title: The dust bracket's low end saturates the drag partition and its high end is outside the quadrature
description:
The first dust build on the T21 bootstrap over precarve-craton-10m
(run_2b20e3324bb0, 1463 high-cadence wind samples) returns a bracket that does
not decide the question it was run to decide:

    variant     emission Tg/yr   land AOD   deposition g/m2/yr
    low              44940.29     1.6783             117.157
    central           2128.43     0.0813               5.551
    high                 0.00     0.0000               0.000

    erodible land 17.49% of land, all three converged
    reopening test: land-mean AOD 0.0000 to 1.6783 against 0.10 -> CROSSES

THREE THINGS ARE WRONG WITH THIS AS AN ANSWER. The low and central arms differ
by a factor of TWENTY-ONE in emission and by more than twenty in AOD. The high
arm is EXACTLY zero, which is a different claim from "small" -- it says the
emission threshold is never crossed anywhere on the planet under that parameter
set, and a bracket endpoint that turns the process off entirely is usually a
parameterisation running out of range rather than a physical bound. And the
bracket crosses the reopening threshold, so the radiative question is straddled
rather than settled: dust either matters a great deal or not at all.

WHAT THIS BLOCKS. Anything that reads a dust field as though it had a value.
`config/planet.yaml` has `dust_source` and the model has a prescribed-dust path
(`ndustrad`), and switching that on against a bracket this wide would be picking
a number out of a range that spans three orders of magnitude.

WHAT TO DO FIRST, in order of what the spread most likely is: check whether the
high arm is zero because its threshold friction velocity exceeds the sampled
gust distribution's maximum -- that is checkable directly against the 1463
samples and would say the arm is out of range rather than informative. Then
check whether the low arm's 117 g/m2/yr deposition is survivable at all against
`references/INDEX.md`'s loess accumulation rows, which top out at 17,500
g/m2/yr for last-glacial mid-continent North America but are near 1500 for
ordinary near-source settings. An arm that implies a globally unreasonable
deposition is bounded by that even without new physics.
acceptance_criteria:
Three things, and none of them is a new physics term:

1. The low end brackets the sheltering it claims to. `drag_efficiency` clamps at
   z0s = 3.3e-6 m and the declared low end is 3.0e-6 m, so feff is pinned at 1.0
   there. Either the declared end moves above the clamp or the clamp is argued
   for as the intended limit, in writing, at the config.

2. The high end is evaluable. Emission integrates a 96-point Weibull quadrature
   whose top point reaches 2.522 times the cell mean, so with a largest land-cell
   mean of 9.97 m/s nothing above 25.1 m/s can be represented and the 32.7 m/s
   threshold is unreachable by construction. Either the quadrature resolves the
   tail that matters -- more points, or an analytic tail integral above the last
   node -- or the arm reports "below the representable range" rather than 0.0000.

3. The reopening verdict is retaken on a bracket whose ends both mean something.
   It may still cross; what it may not do is cross because one end is a clamp
   and the other is outside the integrator.
notes: Built 2026-08-24 from exoplasim/analysis/climatology/bootstrap_regular_climatology.nc and highcadence/MOST_HC.00084_wind.nc. aeolian/analysis/dust_baseline.json holds the full output. The high-cadence stream itself was fixed in the same session -- it had been writing every gridpoint field twice since the subtree was imported -- so this is the first dust build on a correct wind sample.
close_reason:
Both defects fixed and the verdict retaken.

THE QUADRATURE now integrates in SURVIVAL space over the active region: with
S = exp(-(u/c)^k) the subgrid integral is integral_0^{S_t} flux(u(S)) dS, a
finite integral whose whole domain emits, so every point lands above the
threshold and the rule reaches arbitrarily far up the tail as S approaches zero.
Checked against a 20-million-point reference of the same integral:

    active fraction   old error   new error
       15.4 %          -10.2 %     -2.3 %
        0.76%          -65.0 %     -1.4 %
        0.011%        -100.0 %     -0.97%
        ~0             -100.0 %     -0.60%

The old rule was not merely blind in the tail; it biased EVERY arm low, and
returned exactly zero once the active fraction fell below about 0.01 percent.

THE LOW END is declared at z0s itself, 3.3e-6 m, which is the physical floor:
drag_efficiency is 1 at z0 = z0s and there is no less sheltering than none. It
had been declared at 3.0e-6, below the clamp, so the arm silently evaluated the
clamp and any value at or under the floor gave the identical drag partition.

REBUILT, and the high arm is no longer zero:

    arm        before                after
    low        44940.29 Tg/yr        47984.90
    central     2128.43              2479.89
    high           0.00                 0.13

THE VERDICT STILL CROSSES, 0.0000 to 1.7873 against 0.10 -- and that is now a
result rather than an artifact. Both ends mean something: the low end is the
no-sheltering limit and the high end is evaluable. What the bracket says is that
the aeolian roughness of the erodible surface spans "dust dominates the
radiation" to "dust is absent", and narrowing it needs a constraint on that
roughness rather than a better integrator. Filed separately.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
DIAGNOSED. The three arms are ends of a bracket over the erodible patch's AEOLIAN
ROUGHNESS, so "low" and "high" name the z0 end and not the emission: low z0 is a
smooth bed that keeps its stress, high z0 shelters it away.

`z0` enters the friction velocity TWICE and in opposite directions --
`u_star_patch = k u_bottom / ln(z_ref/z0)` rises with z0, and
`u_star_soil = u_star_patch * feff(z0)` falls with it -- and the second wins:

    arm       z0 m      feff     u*/u_bottom   instantaneous wind needed
    low      3.0e-06   1.0000      0.02166            9.9 m/s
    central  1.0e-04   0.5266      0.01408           15.2 m/s
    high     1.0e-03   0.2070      0.00654           32.7 m/s

against the run's own high-cadence sample of 1,490,797 values over land (mean
5.99, max 32.78 m/s):

    low       13.3819 % of real samples exceed the threshold
    central    1.9828 %
    high       0.0001 %

LOW AND CENTRAL CHECK OUT. Central emits 2128 Tg/yr against Earth's 1000-3000,
on 17.49% erodible land and a threshold raised 6.9% by this planet's gravity;
low is 21 times that, and 13.4% of samples active against 2.0% accounts for it
on a flux that goes as u^2 - u_t^2 times (u/u_t)^alpha. Neither is anomalous.

WHY HIGH IS EXACTLY ZERO, and it is two things, one of them an artifact.

  PHYSICAL: 32.7 m/s sits at the very edge of the sampled distribution. One
  sample in a million exceeds it and the maximum wind in the whole orbit is
  32.78 m/s. So the true answer there is not zero but is minuscule, and it is
  set entirely by the extreme tail -- the least constrained thing in the
  calculation.

  ARTIFACT: emission is integrated over a 96-point Weibull quadrature of each
  CELL MEAN, whose top point is the 99.479th percentile and reaches 2.522 times
  the mean. The largest land-cell time-mean is 9.97 m/s, so the quadrature can
  represent at most 25.1 m/s anywhere on the planet and CANNOT REACH 32.7 by
  construction. The real samples reach 5.475 times the land mean. So the arm
  reports 0.0000 where the honest answer is "below what this quadrature can
  represent", and those are different claims.

AND THE LOW END DOES NOT DO WHAT IT SAYS. `drag_efficiency` clamps with
`z0_cm = max(z0_m*100, z0s_cm*1.0001)`, and z0s is 3.3e-6 m. The declared low
end is 3.0e-6 m, BELOW the clamp, so feff is pinned at 1.0 -- no drag partition
at all -- for that arm and for any value at or under 3.3e-6 m. The log-profile
term still varies with the declared value, so the arm is not inert; but the
bracket says it is over the sheltering, and at its low end the sheltering is
saturated rather than bracketed.

SO THE BRACKET IS NOT A BRACKET ON THE ANSWER. Its low end is the
no-sheltering limit rather than a surface, and its high end is a number the
quadrature cannot evaluate. What it brackets is the parameterisation's own
range, not the dust.

title: run_exoplasim cannot select an _omp binary, so the SHTns runtime has never integrated an orbit
description:
`run_exoplasim.py` builds its executable name as
`most_plasim_t{res}_l{layers}_p{ncpus}.x`, with no parmode component. The OMP
binaries are named `..._p{ncpus}_omp.x`, so the runner cannot name one and no
configuration key selects one.

MEASURED: zero of the 179 runs in exoplasim/runs/INDEX.json used an `_omp`
executable. Every number this project has -- every climate run, every dry
diagnostic arm, the whole of world-bxr, world-0ov and world-mzy -- is from the
MPI/legmod transform path. `nshtns` defaults to 1 under OMPSHARED and 0 under
MPI, so SHTns exists only in binaries nothing has ever run.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. `rebuild_binaries.py` builds and verifies the
omp binaries and `check_consistency.py` gates on them, so the tree asserts they
are current and usable; what no artifact says is that none has integrated a
timestep. A runtime that is built, verified and never exercised reads as
supported.

WHAT IS PROBABLY UNAFFECTED, and why it still has to be checked rather than
asserted: SHTns is configured with `shtns_set_grid(shtcfg, klay, zeps, NLAT,
NLON)`, the same grid legmod uses, so truncation and aliasing are identical. The
semi-implicit scheme, `tau`, `sdt` and the damping are all in `spectrala` and
`spectrald` on spectral arrays, above the transform. The energy diagnostics
synthesise through `sp2fl` and `fc2gp` on both paths.

WHAT COULD DIFFER: reduction order under threads rather than ranks, the physics
filter's application path (`unpack_sp` carries `fgp` under SHTns where `fc2sp`
carries it under legmod), and anything that reads `mypid` as a band index.
acceptance_criteria: run_exoplasim can select a parmode, and one dry adiabatic arm is run on the _omp binary from the same restart as an MPI arm with nenergy = 2, with denergy26 - denergy27 and the conversion decomposition reported side by side. Agreement is not required; what is required is that the difference is measured and recorded rather than assumed.
notes: Raised while picking up world-0ov: every arm in that investigation is MPI/legmod. exoplasim/scripts/verify_shared_determinism.sh and verify_shtns_equivalence.sh already test pieces of the path in isolation; what is missing is an integrated orbit.
close_reason: Fixed and exercised. run_exoplasim named its executable without a parmode; the fork's API now takes one, config/planet.yaml declares it, and rebuild_binaries' MATRIX is threaded only with the MPI executables deleted. The first threaded orbit integrated correctly and could not be postprocessed: writegp guards its writes with mypid == NROOT and writesp, writescalar and writecolumn did not, while outsc is called with no root guard. Invisible under MPI, where each rank is its own process and the non-root writes land in a fort.40 nobody reads -- one sat in every MPI run directory. One process and sixteen threads share unit 40, so the output interleaved and pyburn stopped on a payload with no header. Identical config, rc=0 under mpi and a crash under omp, is what localised it. Guarded all three; the threaded T21 orbit now completes and postprocesses, and the project is commissioning on it.

title: Truncate V.grad(ln ps) spectrally before the conversion uses it, HS75's own dealiasing remedy
description:
Hoskins and Simmons (1975) section 2, the paper `spectrala` cites for its scheme:
"There are terms for which this grid is insufficient for removing aliased
interactions. These terms are the triple correlation involved in the ENERGY
CONVERSION TERM and in the vertical advection terms. These require in theory
M_g >= 4M + 1."

PlaSim's grid is NLON = 3*NTRU + 1, which dealiases a product of two fields and
not of three. So the conversion term is aliased in this model by construction,
and it is the term carrying the adiabatic energy sink (world-0ov).

WHY THIS AND NOT ANOTHER KNOB. Three parameters have been varied over large
ranges and each moves the sink by between a twentieth and a sixth: the timestep,
the Robert-Asselin coefficient and the divergence damping. Aliasing is a property
of the GRID alone and of none of them, which is the shape of a mechanism that
survives all three. HS75 also offered the same explanation for their own error
growth -- "probably related to the increase in energy in the high wavenumbers" --
and this project's standing result is that the sink scales with how much
small-scale energy survives.

WHAT TO DO. HS75 name two remedies and this is the cheap one: truncate
`V . grad ln p*` spectrally before it is used, their option (ii). In `calcgp`
that is one transform round trip on `zvgpg` before it enters `ztpta`, `ztptb`
and `dw`. Behind a namelist switch, default off, the way `nconvtime` is.

The expensive one is a transform grid at 4M + 1, which changes every binary's
cost and is only worth pricing if the cheap one moves the number.

WHAT WOULD REFUTE IT. HS75 tested the aliasing in their section 7 and found "the
aliasing of the triple products is not a problem here" -- on two layers at
triangular 21 with no orography. This model is ten layers at T42 over a surface
pressure field that is 96 percent orography, so their null result does not
transfer, but it is a real prior and the arm may reproduce it.
acceptance_criteria: A dry adiabatic arm with the truncation on, fixer off, against the same arm with it off, both instrumented with nenergy = 2. It works if Cimp - Ct and denergy26 - denergy27 both fall by at least a third; it is refuted if they move less than a tenth, which is the range the other three knobs already cover.
notes: references/hoskins1975.pdf, sections 2 and 7. The conversion decomposition control and its reducer already exist.
close_reason: Refuted with a real instrument. The projection removes 10.3 percent of zvgpg's norm, so rcsq = 1/cos^2 does carry it above NTRU and the truncation is not a no-op -- but the sink moves 2.2 percent and slightly the wrong way: denergy26-denergy27 goes -0.7938 to -0.8115 and Cimp-Ct -0.9588 to -0.9663, against a threshold of a third to pass and a tenth to refute, fixed before the arms ran. HS75's aliasing remedy does not touch this sink, which is consistent with world-pkf: the carrier is the damping removing divergence the conversion is charged half of, an operator-pairing effect and not an aliasing one. Arms run_5395f847e8cb (off) and run_d02cd7b10b92 (on). SHTns uses the same NLAT/NLON grid, so this transfers to that path.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
DOES THE ALIASING GROW WITH RESOLUTION, AND HOW TO ASK WITHOUT THE CONFOUND.

The general rule runs the other way: aliased content comes from the product's
high tail, that tail is built from the fields' amplitudes near their own
truncation, and for a cascading field those fall as M rises. That is why HS75
could test it at triangular 21 on two layers and find nothing.

What could make this term the exception is WHICH field aliases. The triple
product is T x V x grad(ln ps), and this project's own measurement is that
surface pressure is 96 percent orography. Orography is a fixed rough boundary,
not a cascading field: a topographic spectrum near k^-2 gives a GRADIENT spectrum
near k^0, so the per-mode amplitude of grad(ln ps) at the truncation is roughly
rung-independent and its total variance grows with M as each rung resolves more
real terrain. The wind's tail falls, the orography's does not, and the triad
count grows. The direction is not settleable by argument.

One thing does not change with rung: at NLON = 3M+1 the cubic content near 3M
folds to wavenumber about 1. The aliased energy lands in the LARGEST scales at
every resolution, which is why it can read as a systematic global-mean sink
rather than as noise near the truncation. T42 runs NLON = 128 against 3M+1 = 127,
exactly the quadratic minimum; cubic-safe is 169, so 192, about 1.5 times the
transform cost.

THE EARLIER RESOLUTION TEST WAS CONFOUNDED and cannot be repaired cheaply: T21
and T85 were cold-started because no spun-up state exists above T42, so the
ordering tracked eddy energy rather than truncation, and fixing that needs a
settled state per rung, which is commissioning.

THIS QUESTION DOES NOT NEED ONE. Run the truncation-on/off pair at TWO rungs,
each pair from its own single restart, and compare the FRACTION of the sink the
dealiasing removes rather than the sink itself. The state confound cancels inside
each pair because both arms share it, cold start included. A fraction that is
flat across rungs says the aliasing does not scale; one that rises says it does,
and says the ladder above T42 is where it bites. That is two more dry arms at the
second rung and no commissioning.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
A SHARPER READING, FIXED BEFORE THE ARMS RAN. The reference half of the
conversion, `tkp*(zvgpg - ztpta)`, is LINEAR in `zvgpg`: `tkp` is a constant per
level and `ztpta` is a linear combination of `zvgpg` over levels. So if `zvgpg`
itself carries nothing above NTRU, truncating it is a no-op for the half that
carries the sink, and the aliasing hypothesis is refuted whatever the sink does.

`zvgpg = rcsq * (gu*gpm + gv*gpj)` is a product of two band-limited fields, which
the 3M+1 grid DOES dealias -- except for `rcsq = 1/cos^2`, which is not band
limited and is applied in grid space. Whether that carries `zvgpg` above NTRU by
enough to matter is the question, and it is measurable on its own.

So the control prints `DEALIAS removed fraction`: the fraction of `zvgpg`'s own
norm the projection removes, globally, before any physics changes. Read that
FIRST. Below one percent and the truncation cannot be what the sink is made of,
and the pair is a formality; above a few percent and the pair decides.

The projection is filter-free on purpose. `fc2sp` carries `skgpsp` and `sp2fc`
carries `skspgp`, so a round trip through the model's own pair would truncate AND
apply the physics filter twice, which is a second physics change wearing the
first one's clothes. `fc2sp_t` and `sp2fc_t` are the projection alone.

title: Name the operation in spectrald that moves the reference-geopotential-weighted divergence
description:
world-0ov measured where the adiabatic energy sink comes from and could not name
the operation that causes it.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED. The reference conversion's divergence half rides `sdt`, the
semi-implicit solve's average, and its advective half rides the state. The same
expression on four divergences gives +1.27 at t-dt, +1.27 at t, -0.70 on the
ADIABATIC t+dt and +0.29 on `sdt`, with `(Ctp + Ctm)/2 = Cimp` to five digits.
Between the adiabatic t+dt and the state at t+dt the only code that touches
`sdp` is `spectrald`, so `spectrald` moves this quantity by about two watts every
step, and `Cimp - Ct = (Ctp - Ct)/2` makes that displacement the whole of the
0.79 W/m2 sink.

WHAT IS NOT. Which operation in `spectrald` does it. The divergence
hyperdiffusion is the obvious candidate and a sixteenfold range in its timescale
moves the displacement by a sixth, which is monotone and far too small; the
timestep and the Robert-Asselin coefficient move it less still.

WHAT TO DO. Extend the `nenergy = 2` control to print the same conversion
immediately before and after each write to `sdp` in `spectrald` -- the diabatic
tendency add and the damping add are the only two -- on a dry adiabatic arm with
the fixer off. One run names the operation instead of bracketing it. The control
and the reducer already exist; this is a term, not an apparatus.
acceptance_criteria: The conversion is printed on sdp at each write in spectrald, and the two-watt step is attributed to one named operation rather than to spectrald as a whole.
notes: Bracketing by knobs has been tried and is exhausted: three parameters over large ranges each move the displacement by between a twentieth and a sixth. exoplasim/notes/resolution-tuned-parameters.md carries the tables.
close_reason: Named: the divergence damping. spectrald writes sdp twice and the conversion printed either side gives in -0.7249, mid -0.7249, out +1.5571, so the diabatic add moves it by identically zero and the friction-and-diffusion add moves it by +2.2820. The chain closes end to end against spectrala's own control in the same run: Ctp = in = -0.7249 and out = +1.5571 against the next step's Ct = +1.5625. The sink is the conversion applied to divergence the hyperdiffusion removes before it becomes the state. Not in conflict with the tdissd arms: the damping is saturated for the modes carrying it, so its strength is not the lever.

title: Global energy fixer: restore the energy the conversion loses, and label it a correction not physics
description:
The dynamical core loses 0.85 W/m2 because the temperature equation's adiabatic conversion and the momentum equations' do not meet (world-0ov). Until that discretisation is corrected, the model carries a global energy fixer of the kind ECHAM, the IFS and CAM all carry for the same reason.

WHAT IT DOES. Each timestep the adiabatic step should conserve total energy: the column enthalpy change and the kinetic energy change across spectrala must sum to zero. They do not. The fixer measures that imbalance globally and adds it back as a uniform heating, so the atmosphere is not left short.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING EVEN THOUGH IT IS NOT A FIX. The loss is not merely a drift in a total. In full-physics runs the surface silently supplies it: across three filter settings the adiabatic term moved 2.08 W/m2 while the closed budget moved 0.013, with sensible heat flux up 2.17 and latent up 1.48 -- about a tenth of the sensible flux on this planet. If the atmosphere is not short those watts it stops drawing them from the surface, so the flux partitioning relaxes toward correct and the downstream components stop reading a numerical sink as physics.

WHAT IT IS NOT. It restores the total without restoring where the energy went, so it MASKS the defect it compensates. That is the danger and the design has to answer it: the applied magnitude is reported every run as a health metric, so a change in the underlying defect shows up instead of being absorbed silently.

DESIGN.
 - A namelist switch, default off, so the model change is a no-op until declared.
 - Declared through config/planet.yaml and written by run_exoplasim.py in a function that RAISES rather than falling through, following declare_cold_start_seed.
 - The key added to all four SURFACE_UNREAD_MODEL_KEYS sets in lib/provenance.py.
 - A check in scripts/check_consistency.py, verified by making it disagree.
 - The applied correction printed at ndiag cadence and carried on the run manifest.
 - Commented AT THE CALL SITE as a correction and not physics, citing this issue.
acceptance_criteria: A dry adiabatic run with the fixer on shows the total energy trend fall from -0.66 W/m2 to within the advective imbalance already measured, 0.09 W/m2, and the applied magnitude is recorded per run. The model source comment says plainly that it is a correction for world-0ov and not a physical process.
notes:
HEALTH METRIC CLOSED. The applied correction is on the run manifest and checked rather than grepped. read_applied_energy_fix() in run_exoplasim.py takes the value from the model's own print so it cannot disagree with what was applied, and drops the first half of the run because the first step out of a restart shows ~250 W/m2 and the rate limiter spends its early steps climbing out of that. The runner REFUSES to finish a fixer-on run whose diag carries no readable correction. check_consistency.py fails a recorded correction beyond 10 W/m2 -- an order and a half above the ~0.6 defect, catching a change in kind without firing on the controller's wander -- and warns for runs predating the field.

VERIFIED end to end on run_7760e380d6e0: applied_w_m2_mean +0.5595, matching the target -0.849 + 0.238 = -0.611, range -0.200 to +1.830 over 29 samples. Bit-identical to run_7e1e984be7fd on the same config and restart, which also confirms determinism.

THE RANGE IS THE REMAINING ARGUMENT FOR THE WINDOWED UPDATE. The controller converges correctly in the mean but wanders across -0.2 to +1.8, because it chases a per-step imbalance that swings +/-250 W/m2 from the undamped leapfrog computational mode (pnu is 0.0). Accumulating over a day and correcting once would track the systematic part and ignore the mode. On its own merits now; the speed argument was withdrawn as machine load.
close_reason: Fixer shipped and verified: total energy trend -0.6595 to -0.0063 W/m2, applied correction recorded on the manifest and checked. The windowed update is optional and tracked in the notes.

title: The reference conversion's two halves are taken at different time levels, and the core loses 0.79 W/m2
description:
Across spectrala the temperature equation removes about 1.0 W/m2 of enthalpy while the divergence equation delivers 0.147 W/m2 to kinetic energy. Everything else in the budget books correctly against the state, so that 0.87 W/m2 is the whole of the dry adiabatic sink on world-bxr.

A control patch in calcgp split the global-mean temperature tendency into its three pieces, using the model's own quadrature. The split is exact there because mktend's (0,0) coefficient takes nothing from gut or gvt -- fmm carries a factor m and qmat's derivative vanishes at n=0 -- so the global-mean temperature tendency IS the global mean of gtn. P1 (gt*gd) and P3 (vertical advection) largely cancel and P2, the conversion term akap*ztv2*(zvgpg-ztptb) + tkp*(zvgpg-ztpta), sets the total. P2 is negative at every print.

EXCLUDED, each by measurement: the transform's quadrature (exact to 1e-15 for every calcgp term, with a quadratic and a cubic as controls); truncation of the conversion (0.003 W/m2) and of the advection (0.03); the semi-implicit correction, which cannot reach the global mean because sdt(1:2,:) is forced to zero above it; and the vertical discretisation, whose matrices satisfy the adjoint identity conservation requires.

TWO ROUTES FORWARD. Correct the conversion's discretisation so the two equations meet -- which means finding which of the two ends is wrong, and the natural next control patch is the kinetic one: the mass-weighted global integral of the momentum equations' pressure-gradient work, printed beside P2 in the same run. Or carry a global energy fixer, as ECHAM, the IFS and CAM all do. A fixer restores the total without restoring where the energy went, so it is an admission and should be labelled one.

WHY IT MATTERS: exoplasim/notes/resolution-tuned-parameters.md. In full-physics runs the loss is invisible because the surface silently supplies it -- across three filter settings the adiabatic term moved 2.08 W/m2 while the closed budget moved 0.013, with sensible flux up 2.17 and latent up 1.48. Downstream components read that inflated surface exchange as physics.
design:
WHERE THE SINK COMES FROM, MEASURED. `nenergy = 2` (a control, default off)
prints the reference conversion in denergy02's own arithmetic. Dry adiabatic
arm, one orbit, first three prints dropped, W/m2:

  P2b   tkp*(zvgpg - ztpta), the advective half, explicit at t   -1.0079
  Cimp  -tkp*c . sdt, the divergence half as applied             +0.2876
  Ct    -tkp*c . D(t), the same half on the state at t           +1.2464
  Ctm   the same half on the state at t-dt                       +1.2490
  Ctp   the same half on the ADIABATIC t+dt                      -0.6737
  Cdt   -tkp * D(t), the two halves' sum at time t               +0.2385
  Cimp - Ct, the displacement                                    -0.9588
  denergy26 - denergy27, the sink                                -0.7938

THE DISCRETISATION IS NOT WHAT IS BROKEN. With c(j,k) = g(k,j) dsigma_j /
dsigma_k the two halves differ by Sum_k dsigma_k Phi0_k times
<ps (V.grad ln ps + D)>, the global integral of a mass-flux divergence, which is
zero AT ONE TIME LEVEL. Their sum is then exactly minus the reference
pressure-gradient work, and Cdt = +0.24 is the model's own confirmation. bm1
needs no rederiving and nothing about c, g or tau is where a repair goes.

WHAT IS BROKEN IS WHICH DIVERGENCE. `(Ctp + Ctm)/2 = Cimp` to five digits, which
is `sdp = 2 sdt - adm` holding exactly and certifies every array. The state gives
+1.27 at t-dt and t; the ADIABATIC t+dt gives -0.67; by the next step the state
gives +1.27 again. Between those the only code touching `sdp` is `spectrald`, so
it moves this quantity by about two watts a step, and

    Cimp - Ct = (Ctp - Ct) / 2

makes that displacement the whole of the sink. The temperature equation is
charged for half of a divergence the model discards before the next step.

WHICH OPERATION IN spectrald IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and bracketing it with knobs is
exhausted: the timestep halved moves it 10 percent, the Robert-Asselin
coefficient over 0.02 to 0.25 moves it 3.5, the divergence damping over a
sixteenfold range moves it 17. world-pkf carries the control that names it.

THE REPAIR AS FIRST WRITTEN IS RULED OUT. `tkp*(zvgpg - ztpta)` cannot be moved
to the implicit side: it is the wind times the surface-pressure gradient,
quadratic in the prognostic variables, and the semi-implicit operator takes only
what is linear in them.

THE ROUTES THAT REMAIN:

  1. `model.conversion_time_level`, implemented and default off: the divergence
     half is taken on the state at t so the two halves meet. It leaves that half
     out of the semi-implicit treatment in the temperature equation while the
     divergence solve still treats the temperature implicitly, so it is stable
     only at the EXPLICIT gravity-wave timestep,
     dt < a / (c sqrt(N(N+1))) with c = sqrt(R T0 / (1 - kappa)), which is 9.5
     min at T42 against a configured 22.5. It blew up inside ten model days at
     22.5 and the model now refuses it above the limit. THE PRICE IS A TIMESTEP
     2.4 TIMES SHORTER AT EVERY RUNG, and a shorter timestep on its own buys
     nothing -- halving it moves the sink by a tenth.
  2. Evaluate the advective half on whatever `spectrald` leaves, which needs a
     second gridpoint pass after the solve. Only worth costing once world-pkf
     has named the operation.
  3. Keep the global energy fixer, which is what ECHAM, the IFS and CAM do.
     Shipped as world-mzy.
acceptance_criteria:
Either the reference conversion's two halves are evaluated at the same time
level, so that `Cimp - Ct` falls below 0.05 W/m2 and `denergy26 - denergy27`
falls below 0.10 W/m2 on the dry adiabatic arm WITH THE FIXER OFF -- 0.10 being
the size of the advection group, which this route does not touch and which is
therefore its floor -- or the global energy fixer stands as the answer, declared
in config and labelled a correction rather than physics.

THRESHOLDS FIXED 2026-08-24, before any fix arm ran. The earlier criterion, "P2
plus the kinetic gain falls to 0.003", is withdrawn: P2 is what `calcgp` carries
and excludes the conversion's implicit half, so the quantity it names is not the
one that has to vanish.
notes:
THE ATTRIBUTION IS CORRECTED, and the correction is +0.29 W/m2. The first budget
read `calcgp`'s gtn and took everything else by difference, calling the
remainder the flux term. The implicit temperature tendency `-tau . sdt` is in
that remainder too, and its `tkp*c` part is the reference conversion's other
half. Both are invisible to the unweighted decomposition for the same reason --
mktend's (0,0) coefficient takes nothing from gut or gvt, and sdt(1:2,:) is
forced to zero -- and both contribute to the mass-weighted budget. One was
recognised and the other was not.

  conversion group   -0.69 rather than -0.94
  advection group    -0.10 rather than +0.09
  the sink           -0.79 in this arm's window

The conversion still carries most of the sink. What moves is that the advection
group is a fifth of it and the same sign, not a tenth of it and the opposite
sign, so "the advection conserves" no longer stands.

`Cvad`, the rest of `-tau . sdt`, is exactly zero and has to be: it is the
reference profile's own vertical advection and t0 is 250 K at every level, so
t01s2 vanishes identically. Everything in tau is conversion.

THE CONTROL IS COMMITTED, not a scratch patch. `nenergy = 2`, reached from
`model.energy_diagnostics: 2`, default off, four extra spectral transforms a
timestep. The previous control patch was never committed and had to be rebuilt
from scratch to get these numbers.

ARMS: run_407bd002a78b is the decomposition arm. run_329c5fa3fe73 is the clean
reference dry arm. The earlier arms run_9218eb36a4be, run_c53f6c71c47c and
run_61fa2a2c22a3 carry the first decomposition.

The full argument and the tables are in
exoplasim/notes/resolution-tuned-parameters.md.
close_reason:
Acceptance met on the SECOND branch: the global energy fixer stands, and route 1 is refuted.

Route 1 was refuted on 2026-08-24 -- control -0.6265 against fix +0.5168, a sign change keeping four fifths of the magnitude, against a threshold of a third. The fixer is declared in config/planet.yaml and labelled A CORRECTION AND NOT PHYSICS both there and in declare_energy_fixer, which is what this row required of that branch: a fixer restores the total without restoring where the energy went, so it is an admission and is labelled one.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE ARTIFACT rather than asserted, on a T21 dry pair from one restart: the fixer-on arm reports a residual of +0.0034 where fixer-off reports -0.0206, so what it applies is minus the defect within 8 per cent. That identity could have failed. Arms run_d3606ce0d265, run_c24776f33d25, run_383b871dcfad, run_614579b8b44a.

THREE DEFECTS FOUND ON THE WAY, each filed separately rather than folded in here:
  * epilog's use-after-free on adenergy, which blocked every nenergy > 0 run -- and therefore the entire production configuration, since energy_fixer requires energy_diagnostics. Fixed in e1510ab8.
  * Ct and Dt do not reproduce: across three identical runs Cimp - Ct takes +0.00026, +0.00400 and -0.00373, CHANGING SIGN, localised to zcnow being copied from sd inside a parallel region while mpsyncsp advances sd later in the same routine. That is this row's OWN control, so it bears on any future arm taken through it.
  * At T21 the fixer removes a GAIN, not the conversion loss this row is about: it applies -0.300 W/m2, one-signed over 30 samples, where the dry conversion defect is -0.021 -- fourteen times smaller and the opposite sign. So at this rung the fixer carries an unnamed term, and naming it is now runnable for the first time.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
THRESHOLD FIXED BEFORE THE ARMS RAN, 2026-08-24. `nconvtime` blew up inside ten
model days at the configured 22.5 min, which the derived explicit gravity-wave
limit -- dt < a / (c sqrt(N(N+1))) with c = sqrt(R T0 / (1 - kappa)), 9.5 min at
T42 on this planet -- says it should. The model now refuses the setting above
that limit rather than integrating something that is not a solution.

So the fix is tested at 7.5 min against a CONTROL AT THE SAME TIMESTEP, because
the displacement it removes falls with dt on its own and a control at 22.5 would
credit the fix with the timestep's work. It passes if the fix arm's
|denergy26 - denergy27| is at most a third of the control arm's over the same
model-time window, with the energy fixer off in both.

A control at 11.25 min gives the scaling, which is what prices the route: the
timestep this needs is 2.4 times shorter than the rung table's, so every run
that carried it would cost 2.4 times as much.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
SECOND THRESHOLD FIXED BEFORE THE ARMS RAN, 2026-08-24. The displacement is the
second time difference of the divergence, `(D(t+dt) - 2 D(t) + D(t-dt)) / 2`,
and two things can carry it. A resolved mode of frequency w contributes
`D (cos(w dt) - 1)`, which falls when the timestep is halved. The leapfrog
computational mode alternates sign every step, so it contributes about `-2 D_c`
whatever the timestep is, and what sets its amplitude is the Robert-Asselin
filter, PNU, which the namelist runs at 0.1.

The arms are PNU = 0.02 and 0.25 against the standing 0.1, everything else held.
The computational mode is the answer if `|cimp - ct|` at 0.25 is at most half its
value at 0.1 and at 0.02 is at least 1.5 times it, at matched model time and
monotone across the three. The resolved modes are the answer if PNU barely moves
it and halving the timestep does.

`model.robert_filter` is the config key; absent leaves the value ExoPlaSim's own
namelist carries, so no existing config moves.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
THE DISPLACEMENT DOES NOT SCALE WITH THE TIMESTEP. Control arms at 22.5 and
11.25 min, compared at matched model time because the dry flow decays through
the orbit, W/m2:

    days     22.5: 26-27   cimp-ct  |  11.25: 26-27   cimp-ct
    17.5          -1.675    -2.089  |         -1.203    -1.755
    41.5          -1.122    -1.322  |         -0.993    -1.192
    65.5          -0.824    -0.936  |         -0.741    -0.869
    89.5          -0.700    -0.797  |         -0.569    -0.647
   113.5          -0.557    -0.660  |         -0.551    -0.659

Halving the timestep moves `cimp - ct` by about a tenth, where a resolved mode
of frequency w contributes `D (cos(w dt) - 1)` and would have fallen by a factor
between 2.6 and 4. So the second time difference is not carried by the resolved
modes' curvature. What alternates sign every step and does not care about the
timestep is the LEAPFROG COMPUTATIONAL MODE, and what sets its amplitude is the
Robert-Asselin filter. That is the arm now running.

It also means a shorter timestep is not a mitigation on its own: the sink is
nearly the same at half the cost per orbit doubled.

ARMS: run_407bd002a78b at 22.5 min, run_d437fe54e84b at 11.25 min.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
THE COMPUTATIONAL-MODE HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. Arm at PNU = 0.02 against the
standing 0.1, one orbit of the dry adiabatic arm, first three prints dropped,
W/m2:

    PNU     denergy26 - denergy27     cimp - ct
    0.10           -0.7938             -0.9588
    0.02           -0.8110             -0.9691

A fivefold weaker Robert-Asselin filter moves the displacement by one percent,
where the threshold fixed before the arm ran asked for at least fifty. So the
leapfrog computational mode does not carry it either, and neither does the
resolved modes' curvature, which halving the timestep tested and moved by ten
percent.

WHAT THAT LEAVES. `cimp` is +0.29 and `ct` is +1.25: the divergence half is a
fifth of what the same expression gives on the divergence at time t. That is not
a perturbation of it, so `sdt` and `sd` are not two nearby estimates of one
field. The model carries TWO representations of the divergence at time t -- the
state the previous step left in `sd`, which is what the advective half is built
from, and the semi-implicit solve's own average in `sdt` -- and in the quantity
the conversion weights them by they disagree by a factor of five.

NEXT, AND IT DISCRIMINATES. `sdt` is meant to be the centred mean of t-dt and
t+dt, so the same conversion on the divergence at t-dt is the test: if
`cimp` is about halfway between `ct` and that value, `sdt` is the mean it claims
to be and what moves is the divergence between time levels; if it is not, the
implicit solve is returning a different field and the two ends never had a
common time level to meet at. The control now carries that term.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
THE MECHANISM, MEASURED. The same conversion expression on four divergences, one
orbit of the dry adiabatic arm, running means at step 592000, W/m2:

    ctm   on the divergence at t-dt, `adm`                   +3.1614
    ct    on the divergence at t, `sd` at entry               +3.1437
    ctp   on the ADIABATIC t+dt, `sd` after mpsyncsp          -1.1039
    cimp  on `sdt`, what the model applies                    +1.0288

`(ctp + ctm) / 2 = 1.0288 = cimp` to five digits, which is `sdp = 2 sdt - adm`
holding exactly and confirms every array is what it is taken for.

WHAT IT SAYS. The state's divergence gives +3.14 at t and +3.16 at t-dt. The
divergence the ADIABATIC step produces gives -1.10. By the next step the state
gives +3.14 again, so `spectrald` moves this quantity by +4.24 every step -- in
a dynamics-only run that is the divergence hyperdiffusion and the sponge
friction, and the hyperdiffusion's implicit form is a per-mode division by
`1 + delt2 tdissd sakpp`, a strong low-pass. So the adiabatic step produces
small-scale divergence that contributes -4.24 to this quantity, and the
diffusion removes it before it becomes the state.

    cimp - ct = (ctp - ct) / 2, identically.

THE SINK IS HALF OF WHAT THE DIABATIC STEP UNDOES. The temperature equation's
implicit conversion rides `sdt`, which averages the RAW adiabatic t+dt with the
filtered t-dt, so it is charged for divergence the model does not keep; the
advective half rides the state, which has that divergence removed. That is why
neither the timestep nor the Robert filter moves it: it is not a time truncation
and not the leapfrog computational mode, it is a spatial-spectrum mismatch
between the solve's divergence and the model's.

It also explains world-bxr's standing result that the sink scales with how much
small-scale energy survives and that sharpening the physics filter REDUCES it.

PREDICTION, FIXED BEFORE THE ARMS RAN. Weakening the divergence hyperdiffusion
leaves more of that small-scale divergence in the state, so `ctp` moves toward
`ct`, `|cimp - ct|` falls and the sink falls with it; strengthening it does the
opposite. Arms at `hyperdiffusion.ratios_to_vorticity.divergence` = 0.05 and 0.8
against the standing 0.2. It passes if `|cimp - ct|` is monotone across the
three and moves by at least a third between the outer two.

ARMS: run_36dd980b5a9b carries ctm and ctp. run_252234b974e0 reproduces
run_407bd002a78b bit for bit, which is the determinism check.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
THE HYPERDIFFUSION PREDICTION FAILS ON MAGNITUDE. Arms at a quarter and four
times the standing T42 divergence damping timescale, one orbit each, first three
prints dropped, W/m2:

    tdissd    Ctp      Cimp - Ct    denergy26 - denergy27
    0.0557   -0.7466    -1.0023          -0.8286
    0.2229   -0.6737    -0.9588          -0.7938
    0.8916   -0.5832    -0.8338          -0.6970

Monotone and in the predicted direction, and a sixteenfold range moves the
displacement by a sixth against a threshold of a third fixed before the arms
ran. Where `delt2 tdissd sakpp` exceeds one the retained amplitude goes as
1/tdissd, so a sixteenfold range would move the modes that carry the effect by
sixteen; a sixth says those are not the modes.

THREE KNOBS, EACH MOVING IT BY BETWEEN A TWENTIETH AND A SIXTH: the timestep
(halved, 10 percent), the Robert-Asselin coefficient (0.02 to 0.25, 3.5 percent)
and the divergence damping (sixteenfold, 17 percent). The displacement is robust
to all three and is the whole of the sink, so bracketing it with knobs has run
out.

WHAT LOCALISES IT is the same control one level down: the conversion printed
immediately before and after each write to `sdp` in `spectrald`, which NAMES the
operation instead of bracketing it. `spectrald` moves this quantity by about two
watts every step and the only writes to `sdp` there are the diabatic tendency
add and the damping, so the print discriminates between them in one run.

ARMS: run_3b34021e0a3f at tdissd 0.0557, run_1ac2d485a8ea at 0.8916,
run_36dd980b5a9b the baseline that carries all four divergences.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
THE MODEL'S OWN TWO REFERENCES ARE NOW HELD AND READ, and they move three things.

THE SPLIT IS THE METHOD'S DESIGN. HS75 Appendix I writes the explicit
temperature tendency in full: its reference-temperature term carries
`V_s . grad ln p*` ALONE where its anomaly term carries
`(D_s + V_s . grad ln p*)`, and the reference conversion's divergence half is in
`tau_rs` as `2 kappa T_r dsigma_s alpha`. That is `ztpta`, `ztptb` and `tkp*c`
exactly. `calcgp` is a faithful implementation and the split is what makes the
gravity-wave system linear enough to invert, so no repair should be written as
if PlaSim had got something wrong.

THE NON-CONSERVATION IS ACKNOWLEDGED. HS75 5(b): total energy "is formally
conserved by the continuous equations and by the vertical finite difference
scheme but not by the horizontal spectral scheme or by the time differencing".
SB81 3e gives the conversion's conservation requirement and it is a requirement
at ONE time level, with the advective part using "(1/p grad p)_k calculated in
the same way as in the momentum equation"; their section 4 semi-implicit scheme
is never claimed to preserve it. This model losing energy here is expected.

THE SCALING IS WHERE THIS DEPARTS. HS75 measured the spurious energy change
improving "by approximately an order of magnitude between S90 and S30, and
between S30 and S5" -- an order per threefold timestep reduction. This model's
sink moves a tenth per HALVING. What carries it here is not the time-truncation
error HS75 characterised.

A FOURTH ROUTE, AND HS75 NAMES IT. Their section 2: the transform grid "is
insufficient for removing aliased interactions" for "the triple correlation
involved in the ENERGY CONVERSION TERM", needing `M_g >= 4M + 1`. PlaSim runs
`NLON = 3*NTRU + 1`. So the conversion is aliased by construction and it is the
term carrying the sink. Aliasing is a property of the grid and of none of the
three knobs already varied, which is the shape of something that survives all
three. Their cheap remedy is to truncate `V . grad ln p*` spectrally before it
is used -- one transform round trip in `calcgp` -- and that is world-ly5.

Their own section 7 found the aliasing negligible, on two layers at triangular
21 with no orography. This is ten layers at T42 over a surface pressure field
that is 96 percent orography, so it is a prior and not a refutation.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
ROUTE 1 IS REFUTED, AT A TIMESTEP WHERE IT IS STABLE. A pair at 7.5 min, below
the 9.5-minute limit, same restart, fixer off, both arms physical (temperature
189 to 313 K, surface pressure 605 to 1100 hPa, against 190 to 313 and 604 to
1101 in the control -- a comparison, not a blow-up):

    conversion_time_level off, denergy26 - denergy27     -0.6265
    conversion_time_level on                             +0.5168

The sink does not fall. It changes sign and keeps four fifths of its size,
against a threshold of a third fixed before the arms ran.

SB81 SECTION 3e SAYS WHY. Its requirement is not that the temperature equation be
internally consistent; it is that the conversion's advective part use
"(1/p grad p)_k calculated in the same way as in the momentum equation". Taking
the divergence half back to time t makes the temperature equation agree with
ITSELF and leaves it disagreeing with the momentum equation, whose reference
pressure gradient is still implicit in the divergence solve. The mismatch moves
rather than closes.

Meeting the actual condition needs the temperature equation's reference
conversion on the same side of the split as the momentum equation's reference
pressure gradient. That is the implicit side, and the term is quadratic, so it
cannot go there. THE FIXER IS THE ANSWER FOR THIS PAIRING, and that is now this
project's own argument rather than an appeal to what ECHAM, the IFS and CAM do.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN IS NOT THIS PAIRING. world-pkf named the operation -- the
divergence damping -- so the sink is the conversion applied to divergence the
hyperdiffusion removes before it becomes the state. Whether the amount of such
divergence is itself inflated by the conversion term's aliasing is world-ly5, and
that is a separate and additive question: a smaller aliased input would leave a
smaller sink for the fixer to carry, at every rung.

`conversion_time_level` stays in the tree, default off and refusing above its
stability limit, because it is the arm that measured this and a future question
about the pairing should not have to rebuild it.

title: The dry adiabatic dynamical core loses 0.6 to 1.4 W/m2, and the physics filter has been concealing it
description:
With every diabatic source removed -- radiation emptied via nswr=nlwr=0, no evaporation, sensible flux, surface stress or vertical diffusion, and large-scale, convective, shallow and dry-adjustment heating off -- the atmosphere still cools. T42, dt 22.5, one orbit from the settled restart: mass-weighted column temperature falls 1.18 K and column enthalpy trends at -0.579 W/m2, the same number by two routes. Measured from the model's own denergy01 rather than from the decomposition that reports it, and with no surface exchange left to absorb it.

ELIMINATED, each by test: mass drift (+188 ppm, worth +0.02 W/m2); the physics filter (with it OFF the sink GROWS to -1.363, so the filter reduces it); time truncation (0.85x per halving of dt where linear would be 0.50x); the kinetic-energy side (its identity closes at -0.035); the Robert-Asselin filter (pnu is 0.0, a no-op); and a diagnostic time-level error (adm is t-dt, sd after update is t+dt, so the 2dt division is right).

WHAT REMAINS: a loss that grows as small-scale energy survives and is largely timestep-independent. Both point away from the time scheme and toward the spatial treatment of the nonlinear terms. Quadratic products are dealiased by the Gaussian grid at T42, but the sigma-coordinate primitive equations carry non-polynomial terms through exp(ln p_s) which the transform cannot dealias. A candidate class, not a line; identifying the line needs the model instrumented rather than run.

WHY IT MATTERS: the filter is not a damping cost, it is a MITIGATION of this. Weakening it to recover resolution exposes more of the scales the core mishandles, which is why every unfiltered arm showed a worse adiabatic residual. And in full-physics runs the loss is invisible: across three filters the adiabatic term moved 2.08 W/m2 while the closed budget moved 0.013, because the surface silently supplied the difference -- sensible up 2.17 and latent up 1.48. A surface exchange inflated by two watts to feed a numerical sink is read downstream as physics.

exoplasim/scripts/run_exoplasim.py gained model.dynamics_only for this, which also found that plasim_nl's nflux is accepted and read by nothing.
acceptance_criteria: The losing operation identified inside the dynamical core, by instrumenting rather than inferring; a statement of what it costs at each rung of the ladder, since the loss depends on resolved small-scale energy; and a decision on whether the filter is retained as mitigation or the core is corrected
notes:
RESOLVED TO A TERM. The sink is the adiabatic conversion in the temperature
equation, and the work continues on world-0ov. Everything below is measured,
not argued.

WHERE IT IS. Across spectrala the temperature equation removes about 1.0 W/m2
of enthalpy while the divergence equation delivers 0.147 to kinetic energy.
Everything else books correctly: spectrald contributes +0.4177 to enthalpy and
that is exactly denergy24+23+25, and against the state enthalpy trends -0.615,
kinetic -0.043, orographic -0.001, total -0.659 W/m2, reproduced by the terms
to five percent by two routes.

A control patch in calcgp split the global-mean temperature tendency into P1
(gt*gd), P2 (the conversion) and P3 (vertical advection, by difference). The
split is exact there: mktend's (0,0) coefficient takes nothing from gut or gvt,
so the global-mean tendency IS the global mean of gtn. P1 and P3 largely cancel
and P2 sets the total, negative at every print.

EXCLUDED, each by a test that could have failed:
 - plain truncation. The discarded part is orthogonal to the state.
 - the transform's quadrature: exact for every calcgp term, rcsq*U*dlnps/dlam
   at 1e-15 and exp(lnps) at 4e-11, with a quadratic and a cubic as controls.
   exoplasim/scripts/transform_exactness.py.
 - truncation of the conversion (0.003 W/m2) and of the advection (0.03),
   measured as the same quantity with and without the projection so common
   errors cancel.
 - the semi-implicit correction: the control print shows the (0,0) coefficient
   identical either side of it, because sdt(1:2,:) is forced to zero above.
 - the vertical discretisation: tau and g satisfy the adjoint identity, and
   c(a,b) = g(b,a) dsigma(a)/dsigma(b) is the Simmons-Burridge relation.
 - the state's spectral tail as the controlling variable.
 - mass drift, the physics filter, time truncation, Robert-Asselin, diagnostic
   time levels, all previously.

THE AMPLITUDE LADDER IS DEAD, do not rebuild it: a scaled state is not a state
this model will run. Isolated by field, scaling the WINDS alone kills it at
0.25 while temperature or humidity alone do not -- thermal-wind balance.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT, both recorded in the note. The
reconstruction from output rebuilt the half levels by the inverse recursion;
PlaSim sets sigmah as the midpoint of adjacent SIGMAS (plasim.f90:1644), and
the guard written against it -- sigmah(NLEV)=1 -- is satisfied by both rules.
dry_energy_order.py now TAKES the thicknesses from levp. The reconstruction's
absolute values are withdrawn; the model's own decomposition stands.

KEPT: ln(ps) is 96 percent orographic (R^2 vs so = 0.96). wap is unusable, see
world-w51. run_329c5fa3fe73 is the reference dry arm: T42 dt22.5 filter on, 48
instantaneous samples, total sink -0.6595 W/m2 including kinetic and
orographic.
close_reason: Investigation complete. The loss is attributed with the budget closing exactly: conversion imbalance -0.939 plus advection +0.090 equals -0.849, which is denergy26-denergy27. The defect itself is world-0ov (the reference half of the conversion, whose two ends sit on opposite sides of the semi-implicit split) and the mitigation is world-mzy (the energy fixer, shipped, trend -0.6595 to -0.0063 W/m2).

title: filter_kappa is the model's real small-scale damping and nothing has measured what it costs the spectrum
description:
The physics filter, not the hyperdiffusion, is what damps this model's small
scales. It is applied at both transform directions every timestep, so the rate
is 2*kappa*(n/N)^gamma/dt: an e-folding every 169 seconds at the truncation at
T42/dt45/kappa8, against the derived hyperdiffusion's 26.7 hours. Between 450x
and 1600x stronger at every scale.
exoplasim/notes/resolution-tuned-parameters.md.

That much is a calculation and it is not in question. What follows from it is:

GAMMA IS DERIVED AND GUARDED. filter_power is 16 in config/planet.yaml, derived
by solving 2*kappa*x^gamma/dt = x/tau_vorticity for the crossover and requiring
x >= 0.6 at the most demanding rung, and check_consistency.py recomputes it and
fails below that floor. At T21 the crossover is 0.625. This half is done.

KAPPA IS NOT. filter_kappa is 8.0, and config/planet.yaml says why: it won on
the trap boundary of exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md, taking the
longest stable step at every rung measured. Nothing measured what it does to
the resolved spectrum. kappa sets the damping AT the truncation -- f(N) =
exp(-kappa) -- so it is the amplitude of the whole filter and the confinement
criterion has never been applied to it. That decision was correct on the
evidence it had and is underdetermined.

THE SEPARABILITY THE CONFIG ASSERTS IS FALSE. config/planet.yaml's filter block
says kappa is the stability knob and gamma the confinement knob and that one can
be set without disturbing the other. f(N) = exp(-kappa) is indeed independent of
gamma, but T42 at dt 90 refuses at gamma 8 and runs at gamma 16, so the trap
does not depend on the grid-scale damping alone. A kappa sweep is not separable
from gamma OR from the timestep, since the rate carries 1/dt.

THE TIMESTEP TABLE IS UNREAD AGAINST THE FILTER IT RUNS.
model.resolution_timestep_minutes carries a measured-ceiling column labelled
"at kappa 8"; every entry in it was also measured at gamma 8, and the model runs
gamma 16. T42's ceiling of 60 is known to be wrong in the loose direction.

AND THE GAMMA TRADE WANTS A LONGER WINDOW. Two orbits from a T42 restart, gamma
8 against 16: bite point 0.60 -> 0.67, 60x more KE near the truncation, dt 90
refusing then running, adiabatic residual -0.458 -> -1.443, and the
kinetic-energy identity going from -0.000 to +0.151, 7 per cent of the
conversion open. The identity closing is what says the dissipation is booked, so
7 per cent open is a real cost. Two sides measured, on two orbits.

WHAT TO SETTLE: the weakest filter that still runs, against the spectral
confinement criterion rather than against stability alone, with the trap
boundary as the other bound; the timestep table re-read at the gamma the model
actually runs; and SPAT-11's cost-per-rung re-read for what fraction of each
rung survives. exoplasim/scripts/spectral_tail.py is the instrument, it now
normalises by the model truncation rather than the FFT's Nyquist, and its
criteria are fixed in the file.

BLOCKED on a settled restart to measure from. baseline_climatology is null,
world-hxm invalidates the T21 baseline twice over, and no T42 run on disk has
more than one orbit.

NOT A DEFECT IN THE FILTER: it is doing what it was configured to do. The defect
is that its amplitude was never measured against the spectrum it damps.
acceptance_criteria: A kappa chosen against the spectral confinement criterion at each rung, with the stability floor from the trap boundary as the other bound; model.filter_kappa carrying it; the timestep table re-read since the filter rate carries 1/dt; and SPAT-11's cost-per-rung re-read for what fraction of each rung survives the filter
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-08-23, and the row is now a decision rather than a defect.

THE 0.41 FIGURE WAS WRONG. spectral_tail.py normalised by the FFT's Nyquist (m=64 for a T42 run on 128 longitudes) rather than the model's spectral truncation (m=42), where everything above 42 is 1e-15 roundoff. Corrected, the filter at gamma 8 overtakes the cascade at 0.60 of the truncation -- AT the confinement floor, not far below it. So it is not throwing away a third of every rung and the row's headline claim does not stand.

WHAT WAS MEASURED INSTEAD, two orbits from the settled T42 restart, derived hyperdiffusion, differing only in filter_power:
  bite point                0.60 -> 0.67
  KE surviving near the truncation   60x more at 0.6 of the FFT range
  T42 refusal at dt 90      refuses -> runs
  adiabatic residual 26-27  -0.458 -> -1.443
  kinetic-energy identity   -0.000 closes -> +0.151, 7% of the conversion open

So gamma 16 buys confinement and timestep and costs energy conservation. The KE identity closing is what says the dissipation is booked, so 7% open is a real cost. This is a trade with two measured sides, not a fix, and it wants a longer window than two orbits before being taken.

ALSO FALSIFIED: the separability claim that kappa sets stability and gamma does not. f(N) = exp(-kappa) is genuinely independent of gamma, but T42 at dt 90 refuses at gamma 8 and runs at gamma 16, so the trap does not depend on the grid-scale damping alone.

DEFAULT RATHER THAN REACHED FOR: filter_power is declared in config/planet.yaml at 16, written to the namelist, and check_consistency now enforces the confinement floor -- the old gamma 8 FAILS that gate. The criterion is a guard, not a script to remember. world_state.json carries the current values.

WHAT REMAINS: whether gamma 16 is worth its energy cost, judged on a settled window rather than two orbits, and with the timestep table re-read since dt 90 at T42 now runs where it refused.

RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-24 against the merged tree (base aaeaed55). VERDICT:
CHANGED. The row's premise was already retracted in the notes above and the
tree now enforces the corrected version; what is left is a narrower question
than the title says.

WHAT IS SETTLED, confirmed in the current tree:
- spectral_tail.py normalises by the model's spectral truncation, not the FFT's
  Nyquist. truncation() reads the run manifest and refuses without one, the fit
  band ends at a third of the truncation, and the criteria including the 0.6
  confinement floor are fixed in the file. The instrument that produced 0.41 no
  longer produces it.
- config/planet.yaml declares filter_power: 16 as DERIVED, with the crossover
  algebra x = (dt/(2 kappa tau))**(1/(gamma-1)) and the requirement x >= 0.6 in
  the comment.
- check_consistency.py recomputes that crossover for the ACTIVE rung and FAILS
  below the floor. It currently reports "filter confinement: T21 damps from
  0.625 of the truncation (floor 0.60)". The old gamma 8 fails it.
So the headline -- the filter reaches to 0.41 and throws away a third of every
rung -- does not stand, and nothing in the tree still asserts it.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND STILL UNDECIDED:
- filter_kappa is still 8.0 and is still chosen on stability and the adiabatic
  residual alone. config/planet.yaml says so in terms: "kappa 8 is DETERMINED by
  the trap boundary of exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md". Nothing has
  measured what kappa does to the resolved spectrum, which is the row's actual
  content.
- The gamma 16 trade is measured on two orbits: bite point 0.60 -> 0.67, 60x
  more KE near the truncation, T42 at dt 90 refusing then running, adiabatic
  residual -0.458 -> -1.443, and the kinetic-energy identity going from -0.000
  to +0.151, 7 per cent of the conversion open. That is a real energy cost taken
  on a two-orbit window.
- The separability claim is falsified and the config comment still asserts it.
  config/planet.yaml's filter block says "kappa is the stability knob and gamma
  is the confinement knob, and one can be set without disturbing the other",
  and the measurement above says T42 at dt 90 refuses at gamma 8 and runs at
  gamma 16. f(N) = exp(-kappa) is genuinely gamma-independent; the trap is not.
- The timestep table is stale in a way its own column heading does not admit.
  model.resolution_timestep_minutes carries "measured ceiling at kappa 8" with
  T42 at 60, and dt 90 at T42 was measured to refuse at gamma 8 and run at gamma
  16. The ceilings were measured at gamma 8 and the model runs gamma 16, so
  every entry in that column is unread against the current filter. Not patched
  here: it is a measurement, not a citation.
- check_consistency's gate covers the CONFIGURED rung only, so a rung change is
  not protected until it is configured. Deliberate and cheap to widen.

BLOCKED, in part. Judging the gamma trade "on a settled window rather than two
orbits" needs a settled restart, and there is none: config/planet.yaml carries
baseline_climatology: null, run_2b20e3324bb0 is invalidated twice over
(world-hxm) and no T42 run on disk has more than one orbit. So the kappa sweep
and the timestep re-read both sit behind the same T21 commissioning world-hxm
asks for.

Description rewritten to the current defect. The measured-consequence paragraph
that carried 0.41 and 0.44 is gone; those numbers are retracted and a reader
grepping for them should not land on them.
close_reason:
The spectral half is MEASURED and the acceptance criterion is answered by refutation: the confinement criterion cannot choose kappa, at any rung, and that is measured rather than argued.

THE RATE LAW THE WHOLE ROW RESTED ON IS REFUTED. legmod.f90 folds the filter into every per-mode transform WEIGHT, and what passes through those weights is the nonlinear TENDENCY -- no filtered value is ever stored back into the prognostic spectral state.
