So the filter attenuates the source that fills a wavenumber by a fixed factor rather than damping the state at a rate, and its spectral effect carries no timestep. Two pairs differing in MPSTEP alone, same binary by sha, same cold start, same seed:

  T21 gamma 16, dt 45 -> 22.5: depth at 0.8N moves +0.009 dex, 0.1 sigma; rate law predicts -0.296 against a three-sigma bar of 0.15
  T42 gamma 16, dt 45 -> 30:   depth moves -0.007 dex, 0.2 sigma; predicted -0.169 against a bar of 0.08

The bite point does not move at either rung. So '2*kappa*(n/N)^gamma/dt, an e-folding every 169 seconds at the truncation, 450x to 1600x the hyperdiffusion' is not a rate the spectrum obeys, and the comparison it licensed is between a rate on the state and a thing that is not one.

THE SURVIVING LAW, exp(-2 kappa x^gamma), is confirmed on the gamma pair: T42 dt 30, gamma 8 vs 16, differing in NFILTEREXP alone, 12 two-orbit windows each. Depth at 0.8N moves +0.789 +/- 0.036 dex at 22 sigma where f^2 predicts +0.970 and the rate law +0.763; the sharper test is the gamma 8 bite point, where the two laws disagree by nearly a factor of two -- f^2 says 0.675, the rate law says 0.381, it measures 0.688.

WHAT KAPPA COSTS, measured. The whole of kappa 8 is worth 0.196 dex of depletion at 0.8 of the truncation, against a total measured depletion of 0.602 dex at T42 and 0.969 to 1.418 at T21. So the filter is a third of it at T42 and a fifth at T21; the hyperdiffusion and the spectrum's own steepening carry the rest, and world-ba0 measures the hyperdiffusion's share at 0.449 dex.

WHY NO KAPPA SWEEP WAS RUN. The confinement criterion goes as kappa^(-1/gamma) = kappa^(-1/16), so a factor of two in kappa moves the bite point by 0.030 of the truncation -- below the instrument's quantisation at T21 (1/21 = 0.048) and at it at T42 (1/42 = 0.024) against a measured three-sigma bar of 0.000 to 0.021. The acceptance criterion 'a kappa chosen against the spectral confinement criterion at each rung' is not achievable at the gamma the model runs. The depth at 0.8N can see a factor of two, at about 1.5 bars at T42 and below the bar at T21 -- so a sweep would price kappa, not choose it, and the price is already known analytically from a law now checked on two independent contrasts.

SPAT-11's cost-per-rung, re-read: the eddy KE the damping removes is 1.9% +/- 0.2% at T42 and 12.2 to 14.5% at T21, and the last wavenumber standing clear of roundoff is 0.95N at T21 and 0.976N at T42. The top of every rung is empty and it is mostly the mode count rather than the damping; filed as world-77a9.

filter_kappa STAYS 8.0 and filter_power stays 16. config/planet.yaml now records what determines each, with the retracted 0.41 and 0.44 bite figures and the falsified separability claim removed rather than marked.

WHAT DOES NOT CLOSE HERE, each already owned elsewhere:
  - the timestep table re-read at gamma 16 -- world-37tn, whose acceptance already includes choosing the ladder's per-rung step from the re-taken grid
  - check_consistency.py's confinement gate, which computes the refuted crossover and disagrees with the measured bite in both directions -- world-ugxo
  - kappa 8's own standing: it comes from a trap boundary taken at gamma 8, on damping that reached one level in ten, from probe entries that name no executable (world-qnue). kappa 8 is recorded as UNSETTLED rather than determined, and the re-measurement is world-37tn. What this row removes is the possibility that the spectrum could settle it instead.

Instrument: exoplasim/scripts/filter_spectral_cost.py, thresholds committed at b27d5afd before any arm was read. Its first version read the depth at m=NTRU and returned the roundoff floor; the repair at the second commit is the instrument failing its own validity check, not a threshold moved after a result. Evidence: exoplasim/notes/filter-spectral-price.md and exoplasim/analysis/filter_*.json.

title: The jtune radiation tuning is unreachable at every resolution, because the block runs before the namelist read
description:
radmod.f90:968-1035 sets the shortwave transmissivities and the water-vapour
continuum per resolution -- tswr1, tswr2, tswr3, th2oc -- through a variable
named jtune, with branches for T21/T1, T31 and T42. Every branch is guarded by
`if(NDCYCLE==1) then jtune=0`, ndcycle's compiled default is 1 at
radmod.f90:205, and `read(11,radmod_nl)` is at radmod.f90:1056, eighty-eight
lines after the block. So ndcycle is always its compiled default when the test
is made, whatever the namelist says, and jtune is ALWAYS 0.

The model announces it: "No radiation setup for this resolution (NTRU,NLEV) /
using default setup. You may need to tune the radiation", at radmod.f90:1035.
Every run directory this project has produced prints it, including the T42 ones
where a branch exists and cannot fire. No ExoPlaSim user at any resolution has
ever had the tuned shortwave coefficients applied unless they disabled the
diurnal cycle.

So the warning has always been correct and always been unactionable. It is an
ordering defect, not a tuning question: the block reads a namelist value before
the namelist is read.

Do: report it upstream, or move the block after the namelist read in the fork,
and record which. Moving it CHANGES RESULTS for anyone running ndcycle 0 and
NEQSIG other than 1, and this project runs ndcycle 1, so nothing here moves
either way; say so in the commit.

exoplasim/notes/resolution-tuned-parameters.md section 2 has the reading.

THE HYPERDIFFUSION HALF OF THIS ROW IS SETTLED and has been split off. The
upstream `if(NTRU==42)` branch at plasim.f90:1544 is still the whole of
ExoPlaSim's resolution dependence and every finer rung still falls through to
T21's defaults at plasimmod.f90:206,447,874-877 -- but this project overrides
it: config/planet.yaml carries a derived model.hyperdiffusion table for all
five rungs, declare_hyperdiffusion writes it from both drivers as
layer-count-replicated lists and refuses an unlisted rung, verify_staged_
namelists compares the arrays as text, and check_consistency compares the table
against the rule. The prediction that T21's damping explained the ladder's
late failures is refuted in the note: the physics filter supplies two to three
orders of magnitude more damping at the same scales. What survives of the

title: The physics filter is unbooked, and it biases the identity that found the adiabatic energy source
description:
TWO FINDINGS, and the second is the one that matters.

ONE: NO TERM BOOKS THE PHYSICS FILTER. mkdheat (plasim.f90:4337-4603) recomputes the wind field before and after Rayleigh friction and biharmonic diffusion, converts the kinetic-energy difference to a temperature tendency and books it as denergy23 and denergy25; fluxmod books surface friction and vertical-diffusion frictional heating as 21 and 22. Nothing does this for the physics filter. The filter preserves n=0 exactly -- f(0)=exp(0)=1 -- so it cannot change the global MEAN of a linear field, and global-mean enthalpy is safe. Kinetic energy is QUADRATIC in the winds, so damping high-n modes removes KE, and that removal is returned as heat nowhere.

TWO: THE 26-27 IDENTITY IS NOT FILTER-NEUTRAL. exoplasim/notes/water-and-energy-closure.md finds denergy26 - denergy27 = +0.3446 +/- 0.0129 W/m2 where it must be zero, calls the spectral core a net energy source worth 15.6% of the conversion it performs, and concludes the atmosphere is radiating away energy the numerics create. That identity is built at plasim.f90:3275-3325 from GRIDPOINT fields, and both are filtered:

  denergy27 takes winds from dv2uv(zsd,zsz,zugp,zvgp), and dv2uv applies fmu = znn1*m*skspgp and fmv = znn1*skspgp. KE is 0.5*(u^2+v^2), so it carries the filter SQUARED.
  denergy26 takes temperature from sp2fl -> sp2fc, which applies fsp = skspgp. Enthalpy is linear in T, so it carries the filter to the FIRST power.

The note already reasons that the Robert-Asselin time filter enters both terms the same way and so cannot be read out of their difference. The physics filter does NOT enter both the same way. f against f^2 does not cancel, so 26 - 27 cannot vanish under a nontrivial filter even for a dynamical core that conserves exactly. The difference is largest where f is near 0.5, which is n/NTRU = 0.737 by construction.

THE DECISIVE TEST, and it has a right answer: measure denergy26 - denergy27 on a short NENERGY=1, NLOWIO=0 window with NFILTER=0 and with NFILTER=2, identical otherwise. If the source collapses toward zero with the filter off, the +0.3446 is the filter -- either as diagnostic bias or as real unbooked dissipation, which the KE identity -denergy27 = denergy(21+22+23+25) then separates. If it is unchanged, the filter is innocent and the note's attribution to the semi-implicit scheme stands.

WHAT IS AT STAKE. If confirmed, a headline finding in the water-and-energy-closure note is wrong: the spectral core is not creating 0.3446 W/m2, the instrument is reporting it. NENERGY is 0 in the active configuration, so this costs a short diagnostic segment rather than a production run. It also bears on the physics-filter row, since it changes what turning the filter off would COST.

NOT A CANDIDATE FOR THE PLANETARY RESIDUAL: that closed as measurement under CLIM-11.
acceptance_criteria: denergy26-27 measured at NFILTER=0 and NFILTER=2 on one bed, both arms reported with their scatter; the water-and-energy-closure note updated to whichever answer the arms give; if the filter carries it, the KE identity re-read to say how much is diagnostic bias and how much is unbooked dissipation
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-23 by a five-arm grid; exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md has it. THE BIAS HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, and by the arm that makes the bias identically zero.

denergy26-27, two orbits each, common restart, same binary and surface:
  kappa 8, dt 45     0.3147 +/- 0.0150
  kappa 2, dt 45     0.4020 +/- 0.0528
  kappa 8, dt 22.5   0.1204 +/- 0.0114
  kappa 2, dt 22.5   0.1637 +/- 0.0153
  filter off, dt 22.5  0.5575 +/- 0.0503

With the filter off, f = 1 everywhere, denergy26 and denergy27 carry the same weight by construction, and the f-against-f^2 bias term is exactly nothing. The residual is then the LARGEST of the five -- 0.5575 against 0.1204 for kappa 8 at the same step. If bias were the cause, removing it would drive the residual toward zero; it raises it 4.6x.

Both dependences are the time-scheme signature instead. It SCALES WITH THE TIMESTEP: halving dt gives ratios of 0.38 at kappa 8 and 0.41 at kappa 2, between first and second order, which is truncation-error behaviour and not what a spatial weighting artifact does. And it GROWS AS THE FILTER WEAKENS, monotone at fixed dt -- 0.1204, 0.1637, 0.5575 for kappa 8, kappa 2, off -- because less filtering leaves more small-scale structure for the semi-implicit step to mishandle.

So water-and-energy-closure.md's attribution stands and its number is not a constant of the model: the spectral core genuinely fails to conserve enthalpy plus kinetic energy, and the size is set by the timestep and by how much spectrum survives the filter. At the configuration this project runs it is 0.31 W/m2.

The kinetic-energy identity closes in all five arms against a ~2.1 W/m2 conversion, so the pairing holds throughout. The short-dt arms were checked per orbit against the dt-45 control for a leapfrog transient off a dt-45 restart and show none: 0.1284/0.1123 against the control's 0.3253/0.3042.

STILL OPEN, and the row stays open only for this: no term books what the filter removes. mkdheat covers Rayleigh friction and biharmonic diffusion alone.
close_reason:
Both halves resolved 2026-08-23; exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md carries the evidence.

THE BIAS HALF IS REFUTED, by the arm built to test it. The claim was that denergy26 carries the filter to the first power and denergy27 carries it squared, so 26-27 could not vanish under a nontrivial filter however well the core conserves. With the filter OFF, f = 1, both terms carry the same weight by construction and the bias term is exactly zero -- and the residual is the LARGEST of the whole grid, 0.5575 against 0.1204 for kappa 8 at the same step. Removing the bias raises the residual 4.6x where the hypothesis needs it to fall to zero. Confirmed across nine further cells: the residual grows monotonically as the filter weakens at every timestep.

What the dependences say instead is truncation error. It scales with the timestep, ratios of 0.60 at dt 30 and 0.38-0.41 at dt 22.5 against linear's 0.667 and 0.500, consistent across kappa 8, 4 and 2. So water-and-energy-closure.md's attribution to the semi-implicit step stands, and its number is not a constant of the model: 0.31 W/m2 is what this timestep and this filter cost. Eight-orbit arms confirm the short windows to within 2%.

THE UNBOOKED HALF IS BOUNDED, by an identity that runs the wrong way for it. Nothing books the filter's KE removal -- mkdheat covers Rayleigh friction and biharmonic diffusion, fluxmod the surface and vertical-diffusion terms, neither knows the filter exists -- and the filter preserves n=0 exactly so only the quadratic quantity is exposed. The kinetic-energy steady-state identity is what would find it, and a stronger filter removes more, so the gap must WIDEN with kappa if the filter is the missing term. It NARROWS: -0.013 to -0.000 at kappa 8, rising through +0.007 at kappa 2 to +0.039 with the filter OFF, where the filter's dissipation is identically zero and there is nothing to book.

At the adopted kappa 8 the identity closes to within 0.013 W/m2 against a conversion of about 2.1, six tenths of a percent. The term is real in principle and below what this instrument can see at production settings, so the row closes on the bound rather than on an mkdheat implementation.

REOPEN IF: the identity stops closing at the adopted kappa, or a rung's KE conversion grows enough that six tenths of a percent is worth chasing.

title: Settle the physics filter before the timestep ladder: gp|exp|sp came from the tidally-locked presets
description:
config/planet.yaml declares physics_filter: "gp|exp|sp", which run_exoplasim.py, continue_exoplasim.py and run_stellar_cycle.py pass to ExoPlaSim's configure(). Confirmed in an actual run namelist rather than inferred from config: NFILTER=2, NGPTFILTER=1, NSPVFILTER=1, FILTERKAPPA=8.0, NFILTEREXP=8, MPSTEP=45.0.

WHERE IT CAME FROM, and this is the reason the row exists. The base Model.configure defaults physicsfilter="" -- OFF. Earthlike sets a 45-minute timestep and NO filter. The three tidally-locked classes, TLaquaplanet, TLlandplanet and TLmodel, set physicsfilter="gp|exp|sp" AND a 30-minute timestep. This project's config carries the timestep from one preset and the filter from the other, and Vesper is not tidally locked. It has been in config/planet.yaml since the initial commit 67ff46ba with no decision commit behind it, and exoplasim/notes/parameter-decisions.md records only "We enable the filter but tune nothing".

UPSTREAM'S OWN GUIDANCE is that Earth-like models typically do not require filtering, that tidally-locked models do, and that filtering MAY be beneficial for Earth-like models at very high resolution or with sharp topography. Vesper is Earth-like in composition and unlike Earth in its star; it also has deliberately sharp topography, since preserving carved closed-basin floor below sea level is the entire point of the Orogen fork. So the setting is not obviously wrong -- it is UNDECIDED, and it is currently decided by inheritance.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, computed from legmod.f90:167-235. f(n) = exp(-8 (n/NTRU)^8), applied to skgpsp at gp->sp and skspgp at sp->gp, then folded into the per-mode factors fsp, fgp, fmu and fmv. The fork's own comment is explicit: every SP->GP weight carries skspgp and every GP->SP weight carries skgpsp, NO WEIGHT IS EVER USED UNFILTERED. So it reaches fc2sp, sp2fc, sp2fcdmu, dv2uv, uv2dv, qtend and mktend -- the nonlinear dynamical tendency transforms as well as the physics coupling -- and shtnsmod.f90 imports fsp from legmod so the SHTns path carries the identical filter.

IT IS SCALE-FREE IN n/N, which is what the vague "use at higher resolutions" guidance does not capture. The half-power point is n/N = 0.737 at EVERY rung: n=15.5 at T21, 30.9 at T42, 62.6 at T85, 93.5 at T127, 125.2 at T170. Per application f is 0.63 at n/N=0.7, 0.45 at 0.75, 0.26 at 0.8, 0.03 at 0.9; with both directions on, the round-trip transfer is 0.40, 0.20, 0.068 and 0.001. Every rung loses the same FRACTION of its spectrum, so the filter does not distort the ladder's relative comparison -- but the effective resolution of every rung is well under nominal, and T170's half-power wavenumber of 125 sits essentially at T127's truncation.

WHY IT GATES SPAT-11. The filter damps exactly the smallest scales that set the stability limit, so the largest scientifically acceptable timestep is a function of the filter setting. Measuring the ladder under one filter configuration and running production under another gives a number for a model nobody runs. Upstream pairs gp|exp|sp with 30 minutes and no filter with 45; this project runs the filter with 45.

DECIDE IT PER RUNG, because the reason upstream gives is resolution-dependent even though the filter is not: higher resolution resolves sharper gradients off the same topography, so Gibbs ringing gets worse while the filter cuts the same fraction. The decision procedure is arms with and without the filter at a rung, judged on the ringing signature near steep orography rather than on preference -- spectral overshoot around the carved basin rims, negative specific humidity, oscillatory precipitation downstream of sharp relief.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded per-rung decision with its evidence, in exoplasim/notes/parameter-decisions.md; config/planet.yaml carries the chosen setting per rung rather than one global string; SPAT-11's timestep ladder runs at the chosen setting and says which one
notes:
THE FILTER BUYS TIMESTEP. Measured 2026-08-23; exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md.

The filter-off arm TRAPS at dt 45 and integrates two clean orbits at dt 22.5. So the earlier reading here -- that the filter is load-bearing full stop -- is too strong. It is load-bearing AT A 45-MINUTE STEP. Upstream pairs gp|exp|sp with 30 minutes; this configuration pairs it with 45 and would need roughly 22.5 without it.

That makes the filter and the timestep one decision rather than two, and it is the finding that reaches SPAT-11: the largest scientifically acceptable step is a FUNCTION of filter strength, so a ladder that fixes one and sweeps the other measures one arbitrary point on a trade.

There is a second axis to the trade, from the same grid. Weakening the filter raises the spectral core's non-conservation monotonically at fixed timestep -- 0.1204, 0.1637, 0.5575 W/m2 for kappa 8, kappa 2, off at dt 22.5 -- so a weaker filter costs spurious energy creation as well as timestep. A stronger filter costs spectrum: f is scale-free in n/NTRU with its half-power point at 0.737 for kappa 8 and 0.876 for kappa 2.

So the row's question is now three-cornered and per rung: kappa, timestep, and how much of the top of the spectrum each rung can afford to lose. The trap gives a hard floor to measure against at each rung -- the weakest filter that still runs at a given step.
close_reason:
Settled 2026-08-23. The provenance finding stood and its conclusion did not: gp|exp|sp did come from the tidally-locked presets while the 45-minute step came from Earthlike, and the setting is load-bearing rather than inherited cargo. exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md has the arms, exoplasim/notes/parameter-decisions.md the argument.

THE FILTER BUYS TIMESTEP, so a filter strength and a timestep are one decision. Without the filter the model traps in the shortwave on the first radiation call at 45 minutes and runs at 22.5, and the requirement STRENGTHENS up the ladder: unfiltered, T42 runs at dt 30 and T170 needs dt 10. That is upstream's stated reason for filtering, measured rather than quoted -- a finer grid resolves sharper gradients off the same orography while a scale-free filter keeps cutting the same fraction.

KAPPA 8 AT EVERY RUNG, and it is not a compromise because it wins on both axes. Against kappa 4, 2, 1 and off it takes the longest stable step at every rung tested AND gives the smallest adiabatic non-conservation -- 0.3147 W/m2 at dt 45 against 0.3460, 0.4020, 0.6574 and a trap. What it costs is spectrum, which is the only reason not to go stronger: f is scale-free in n/NTRU with its half-power point at 0.737, so a stronger filter takes more of every rung's spectrum for a benefit nothing has measured. Nothing above kappa 8 was tested.

THE STEP IS THE PER-RUNG PART, and config/planet.yaml now carries it as model.resolution_timestep_minutes with check_consistency.py refusing a timestep_minutes that disagrees -- verified by making it disagree. Adopted: T21 45, T42 45, T85 45, T127 30, T170 22.5. Measured ceilings: T21 90+, T42 60, T85 45 untested above, T127 30 with dt 45 refusing outright, T170 22.5 with dt 30 blowing up after 3.8 minutes.

THE ADOPTED STEP IS BELOW THE CEILING AT T42 DELIBERATELY. A step that does not blow up is a stability floor and not a licence. T42 at 60 would be a third off every T42 run and is not adopted, because the roadmap's timestep experiment -- cold-start stability with traps armed, warm-start closure, climatological differences after settling, wall time per orbit -- has not been run. That is SPAT-11's, and this table is what it starts from rather than what it concludes.

CARRIED FORWARD to SPAT-11, which is the acceptance criterion this row cannot discharge itself: the ladder must run at the adopted setting and say which one. Two cells carry more risk and are labelled: T85 at 45 and T127 at 30 are at their tested ceiling on a single orbit, and T170 at 22.5 sits one step below a cell that fails LATE, which a short check cannot see.

title: Register the threaded build: parmode is a fourth dimension of the binary registry
description:
rebuild_binaries.py hardcodes "mpi" at its build call and its MATRIX is (resolution, layers, ranks), so no OpenMP/SHTns binary can enter binary_manifest.json. most_plasim_t42_l10_p16_omp.x is in vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/run/ and absent from the manifest, so scripts/check_consistency.py FAILS on main today and rebuild_binaries.py --verify exits 1.

The threaded build is what exoplasim/notes/non-mpi-performance-roadmap.md's measurement order calls the new baseline, and CLIM-74, CLIM-59, CLIM-84 and SPAT-11 all measure on it. Rule 4 counts binaries over the triple; parmode makes it a quadruple, and every threaded binary is currently outside the registry with unknown provenance.

Register parmode: carry it in MATRIX, in expected(), and in each manifest entry. Record the effective flag line PER BINARY, because -fopenmp -DOMPSHARED means one global effective_f90_opts would repeat the exact defect toolchain() documents -- a threaded binary carrying a provenance record of flags it was not built with. Register 16 threads at each rung on exoplasim/notes/thread-count-by-resolution.md: sixteen wins at every resolution measured, below it is monotonically worse, above it is refused on two grounds, and NPRO must divide NLAT.
acceptance_criteria: rebuild_binaries.py --verify exits 0; check_consistency.py binaries check passes; binary_manifest.json carries an omp entry per rung with its own effective flag line; CLAUDE.md rule 4 and exoplasim/README.md name the fourth dimension
close_reason:
Done. rebuild_binaries.py MATRIX now carries parmode as a fourth dimension and the build loop passes it instead of the literal "mpi"; expected() carries the _omp suffix and stays a SECOND statement of build_model.executable_name's rule so the cross-check can still fail. Five threaded rungs registered at 16 threads each (T21/T42/T85/T127/T170) on thread-count-by-resolution.md.

Per-binary provenance: each entry records parmode and its own effective_f90_opts, and the top-level toolchain records effective_f90_opts_by_parmode instead of one line, because -fopenmp -DOMPSHARED means a single global line would have repeated the exact defect toolchain() documents. assert_parmode_flags_agree() reads the flags back out of build_model.py and fails the run if the restatement drifts -- verified to fire.

VERIFIED: 17 binaries built, --verify 'all 17 binaries current' exit 0, check_consistency.py 29 checks 0 failed (was FAILing on most_plasim_t42_l10_p16_omp.x not in manifest), smoke_test.py 17 checks 0 failed. The twelve MPI shas reproduced bit-for-bit from the previous manifest, which independently re-confirms the bit-reproducible build claim in notes/audits/aocl-and-model-build-flags.md.

Docs: CLAUDE.md rule 4, exoplasim/README.md, failure-modes.md class 11, check_consistency.py, reproducibility_matrix.py and run_exoplasim.py all name the quadruple. notes/ left alone as dated records.

title: Verify the prescribed ocean heat-transport channel end to end with a field whose answer
description:
Verify the prescribed ocean heat-transport channel end to end with a field whose answer is known, BEFORE anything computes a real one. `nfluko = 1` makes `oceanmod.f90` read surface code 903 as a monthly W/m2 field and `addfc` apply it under the header comment "prescribed advection"; `close_ocean_energy.py` already reads the same code out of the `ocean_output` stream and records it as identically zero today. Use a zero-global-integral ocean dipole; bind grid, calendar, interval, units, source hash and land/sea/ice mask; require the reported accumulation to reproduce the written field and its area-weighted global integral to remain zero

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` finding 2 and section 8a
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and instrumentation rather than physics, so it is a diagnostic segment and not an orbit. Cheapest row here and it is what makes OCN-3 legible: without it, an offline model's first field would arrive with no way to separate a wrong field from a wrong channel. It also converts the error budget's no-q-flux item from STRUCTURAL with "no cheap version exists" into something with a route, which `nhdiff` bounded but did not supply [step: bootstrap_run]. WHY THIS IS FIRST, made explicit 2026-08-22: the channel this row verifies is what makes OCN-5's loop possible at all. The atmosphere-ocean poleward transport partition cannot be got right in one pass, because a slab-forced climatology has the atmosphere carrying the entire load with no coefficient to reduce -- unlike cGENIE, which tunes `betaz`, `betam` and `diffamp` to make room for its ocean. The correction has to return to the NEXT atmospheric run, and code 903 under `nfluko = 1` is the only path for it. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 28c CRITICAL PATH, 2026-08-24. Section 59 decides the coupling architecture as offline full-flux, which has exactly one structural weakness: the atmosphere-ocean transport partition is iterated rather than solved, because a slab-forced climatology hands the ocean a flux field computed on the assumption that the ocean does nothing. Surface code 903 under nfluko = 1 is the only channel that returns the correction to the next atmospheric run. So this row is no longer merely the cheapest ocean row -- it is the one the adopted architecture depends on, and raised to P1 to say so. Nothing else in the ocean set should be started ahead of it. SCOPE UNCHANGED BY THE SEA-ICE DECISION, 2026-08-24, recorded so it is not widened by mistake. Section 7b adds an ocean surface velocity to the return set, but that field has no channel in ExoPlaSim to verify: icemod has no advection at all, so the consumer does not exist until world-pt8 writes it. This row remains the heat channel alone, surface code 903 under oceanmod's nfluko = 1. Note that icemod carries its OWN nfluko in icemod_nl, a separate variable with a different meaning -- a flux correction toward a prescribed ice climatology -- so setting the ocean's does not activate the ice one, and neither is exposed by ExoPlaSim's Python API. The route is a namelist patch or a fork change either way.

DONE 2026-08-24. `exoplasim/scripts/verify_ocean_flux_channel.py` stages the field and the prediction and answers each criterion against the stream; criteria and tolerances are module constants declared in that file before any run existed. Verified on a T42 diagnostic segment on the current model source, cold start, nfluko = 1, 512 steps, 16 ocean-stream records, ice-free by construction, in a scratch directory outside the run registry. Reported field equals the written field to 1.90e-6 W/m2 over every record and cell against a bar of 1e-4, which is the float32 resolution of the stream and nothing else; the nearest wrong field (a one-cell zonal roll) differs by 0.51 W/m2 and a sign reversal by 72.67, so the orientation is discriminated by five to seven orders. Area-weighted global integral 2.05e-8 W/m2 at worst against 1e-4. The field is carried over land as well, on 4116 land cells, which confirms that getflxco does not mask and only addfc does. Delivery: 61,140 samples over 4076 ice-free ocean cells and 15 record pairs fit ONE proportionality with a maximum residual of 3.05e-5 K against a 0.469 K largest change, and the fitted record interval is 86,400.027 s against a declared 86,400. WHAT IT CAUGHT: the fitted interval missed by 4.75 per cent until the sea water pair came from the model. close_ocean_energy.py and close_state_energy.py carried CRHOS = 1030.0 and CPS = 4180.0 as literals attributed to oceanmod.f90, which does not own them; icemod.f90 declares both as icemod_nl keys and its CPS is 3990.34, sea water at S = 34.7 and its freezing point. assess_convergence.py imports those names to build the slab capacity its convergence verdict rests on. lib/sea_water.py now reads all four of the salinity quartet from the model and the run's namelist. close_ocean_energy.py's D4 and D6 carry yfsst, and yfsst left MUST_BE_ZERO; behaviour on every run made so far is unchanged. FOR OCN-10: a globally zero-integral field integrates to -0.919 W/m2 over this build's ocean, so the contract's zero-integral condition holds on the OCEAN. NOT VERIFIED, and world-coqw carries them: the monthly interpolation and addfc's ice branches. notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md section 11.
close_reason: Channel verified end to end on a field whose answer was stated before the run: reproduction to 1.90e-6 W/m2, global integral held, carried over land, and delivered to the slab at the declared heat capacity and interval, the last recovered to 3.2e-7 from the SST response. Instrument is exoplasim/scripts/verify_ocean_flux_channel.py; finding is notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md section 11. The monthly interpolation and addfc's ice branches were deliberately out of scope and are world-coqw.

title: Register the worktree link check in smoke_test.py and verify_entry_points.py
description:
scripts/check_worktree_links.py exists and is exercised, but nothing runs it automatically. It has two registration points and world-ov4u's agent was scoped out of both files.

PER COMMIT, in scripts/smoke_test.py: call check_worktree_links() from scripts/check_worktree_links.py. It returns a list of failure strings in smoke_test's own vocabulary and is EMPTY outside a worktree and in a worktree with no ledger, so it is a no-op in the main checkout and does not punish worktrees that stood before the ledger existed. It costs 0.13 s on the standing payload -- a JSON read plus a hash of the link targets under the ledger's budget, 74 MB of the 11.6 GB -- so it is a static read and belongs in the fast tier.

BEFORE A BUILD, in scripts/verify_entry_points.py: run 'python scripts/check_worktree_links.py --self-test', the way that file already runs 'scripts/lock_and_run --self-test'. It builds a throwaway repository and a REAL git worktree in a temporary directory, which is why it is not a per-commit cost.

Until the first is registered, a worktree that writes through a link is told only by the next 'link_worktree.py --check', which is the half of the acceptance that does not reach the agent that made the write.

## Context
notes/audits/worktree-write-through.md
acceptance_criteria: smoke_test.py runs check_worktree_links() and verify_entry_points.py runs its --self-test. Both were exercised against a worktree that had written through a link.

title: A worktree writing a linked generated file invalidates the main checkout's binary
description:
scripts/link_worktree.py links ignored payload into a worktree, and where a directory holds tracked content beside untracked payload it links PER FILE. world-bga1 closed the direction where that loses a worktree's own new file. THE OTHER DIRECTION IS OPEN AND IT IS SHARPER: an existing linked file is a symlink INTO THE MAIN CHECKOUT, so a worktree that REGENERATES one writes through, and the main checkout's artifacts built from it are silently invalidated.

MEASURED 2026-08-31. vendor/lpj-guess/framework/vesper.h is generated, gitignored, and lives beside tracked source, so a worktree gets a per-file symlink to the main checkout's copy:

  .claude/worktrees/<agent>/vendor/lpj-guess/framework/vesper.h
      -> /home/cfutro/docs/world/vendor/lpj-guess/framework/vesper.h

An agent regenerated it in its worktree -- correctly, to move a generation timestamp out of a header whose hash gates the binary -- and that write landed in the main checkout. The main checkout's LPJ-GUESS binary had been built against the previous bytes, so build_lpj_guess.py --verify began refusing it. Recovered by one rebuild, and the agent reported it, which is the only reason it was not discovered by a later refusal.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE DIRECTION ALREADY CLOSED. A file that dies with its worktree costs the work that made it. A file that writes THROUGH mutates a tree other agents are using, at a moment nobody chose, and the damage lands on an artifact -- a compiled binary, a staged field -- rather than on the file itself. This session had five agents live at once; the same write during another agent's build would have produced a binary whose provenance record named source that had already moved.

WHAT ALREADY PROTECTS AND WHAT DOES NOT. world-w62x's binary gate CAUGHT it: --verify named vesper.h as changed since the build. That is the backstop working, and it is why this is a P2 rather than a P1. link_worktree.py --check does NOT catch it -- it reports payload living only in the worktree, which is the other direction. Nothing warns at the moment of the write.

vesper.h is not the only file of this shape: exoplasim/inputs' .sra fields are the same, and an agent this session correctly declined to restage from a worktree for exactly this reason, having reasoned it out rather than been told. The convention is currently carried by agents remembering it.

Do: decide whether a worktree should be able to write a linked generated file at all. The dispositions worth weighing are a read-only link, a copy-on-write local shadow, and a --check arm that compares each linked file's target against the mtime or hash the worktree was linked at. Ask which of them keeps a worktree honest without making a legitimate regeneration impossible.
acceptance_criteria: A worktree either cannot silently write through a linked generated file, or the write is reported to the agent that made it and to the next --check. The decision names which of the three dispositions was taken and why the other two were not.
notes: Found 2026-08-31 when an agent regenerating vesper.h in its worktree invalidated the main checkout's LPJ binary. Related to world-bga1, which closed the losing-a-file direction; this is the writing-through direction and nothing covers it. The agent that hit it reported it unprompted, which is what made the recovery one rebuild instead of a confusing refusal later.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
TAKEN: the link ledger, plus the write-door refusal where one already exists. Rejected the other three.

A READ-ONLY LINK CANNOT BE BUILT. A symlink carries no permissions of its own on Linux; the only mode that decides whether a write lands is the TARGET's, in the main checkout. Setting it is a change to shared state -- it refuses the main checkout's own legitimate regeneration and every other worktree at once -- and it is per-file rather than per-worktree, so no worktree can hold it without holding it for all of them. The enforceable equivalent is a refusal at the write door, which the project already does once: sra.py:write_sra covers exoplasim/inputs/<rung>/ for all four staged-field builders (world-4o59). That form is adopted, and world-pkt5 carries the remaining doors.

A COPY-ON-WRITE SHADOW COSTS ABOUT A TERABYTE. 11.6 GB of per-file payload against 84 standing worktrees. It is also wrong twice on its own terms: a copy pins the worktree to the moment it was taken, so a step reads the earliest available input rather than the best; and it converts a write-through into world-bga1's direction, silently, with the worktree's correct regeneration dying at removal having looked right.

DOING NOTHING IS NOT ENOUGH, though the backstop did work. build_lpj_guess.py --verify covers ONE of the eight groups a worktree can regenerate through a per-file link, and it reports the symptom to whoever builds next rather than the cause to whoever wrote. notes/audits/worktree-write-through.md enumerates the eight.

WHAT LANDED. link_worktree.py records size, mtime and a content digest below a 4 MB hash budget for every per-file link, into the worktree's own .git/worktrees/<name>/link-ledger.json -- which no ignore rule has to cover and git worktree remove deletes with the tree. Any target whose bytes moved is reported on every run and fails --check. check_worktree_links.py asks the same question at commit time, which is the half of the acceptance that reaches the agent that made the write; 0.13 s on the standing payload. It names the fact and not the culprit, because from inside a worktree a write from here and a regeneration in the main checkout are indistinguishable and both matter.

ALSO FOUND: vendor/cgenie was linked and should never have been -- 234 .o, 81 .dep, 74 .mod, 16 .a, no ignored directory at all, so a worktree that built the ocean model wrote its objects over the main checkout's. It is in SKIP_COMPILED now.

EXERCISED BOTH WAYS against a real git worktree of a throwaway repo (check_worktree_links.py --self-test): a genuine write-through caught by both doors, and the regeneration that caused it still possible and accepted by re-linking. Two mutations of the implementation confirmed to fail it. On the real tree, falsifying the ledger's record of vesper.h and a climatology named exactly those two out of 590 entries.

FOLLOW-ON: world-o2ig (register the check in smoke_test.py and verify_entry_points.py -- this agent was scoped out of both files), world-pkt5 (the remaining write doors), world-h9hs (vendored-upstreams.md's cgenie reason is now stale).

title: The leaf-to-wood phosphorus ratio varies with temperature and plant functional type, and the model applies one scalar to every type
description:
PFRAC_LEAFTOSAP is one number applied to every simulated plant type, and Yan et
al. (2016) shows the quantity it stands for is not one number.

335 woody species in 198 genera at 12 forest sites across eastern China, 18.7 to
50.9 degrees north, mean annual temperature -5.7 to 25.3 C:

  - The leaf P over twig stem P ratio, which is what PFRAC_LEAFTOSAP is, runs
    0.77 at 18.7 N to 2.63 at 50.9 N. A factor of 3.4, for one tissue, with
    r2 = 0.31 against latitude and 0.30 against MAT, both p < 0.001 (their
    Fig. 4).
  - The stem-P-on-leaf-P scaling exponent runs 1.58 tropical, 0.97 temperate,
    0.80 boreal, and by functional group 1.26 evergreen broad-leaved, 0.96
    deciduous broad-leaved, 0.70 coniferous. It correlates with MAT and not with
    precipitation or soil total N or P.

Both axes -- evergreen against deciduous against needleleaf, and warm against
cold -- are ones this model already distinguishes. Its woody plant types span
exactly that range, and Pft::init_ctop_limits gives every one of them the same
PFRAC_LEAFTOSAP.

WHAT IT IS WORTH. Across simulated plant types leaf C:P varies only through sla,
as sla^-0.80936, and the woody types' calculated sla runs 9.300 to 26.03, so leaf
C:P spans 2.30 and under a fixed scalar sapwood C:P spans the same 2.30. Yan's
own ratio spread of 3.4 between its warmest and coldest sites is larger than
that, so the per-type dependence this constant ignores is bigger than the
variation it does carry.

THIS IS NOT BIO-34. That row is the LEVEL of the single scalar and is blocked on
a measurement of paired leaf and whole-sapwood phosphorus over more than one
region. This row is the SHAPE of the dependence, and it stays open even if that
measurement arrives, because a single global mean would still be applied to
every type.

Do NOT read this as a licence to fit per-type values off Yan. The tissue is
terminal twig stems, whose mass share of a simulated individual's sapwood pool
is small, so its ratios are not substitutable for this model's -- the tissue
gradient between twigs and bole wood is a factor of twenty, larger than the
climate gradient. What Yan licenses is the statement that the dependence exists
and which way it goes; what it does not licence is a number.

Evidence: biosphere/notes/phosphorus-cycle-parameterisation.md, section 'Yan et
al. (2016) runs the same test across 32 degrees of latitude';
references/pdf/yan_2016_nutrient-allocation-strategies-of-woody-plants-an-approach-from-the-sc.pdf

title: The surface microbial pool's C:P is a fixed 80 taken from Fig. 3's active soil line, for a pool that paper does not have
description:
With the litter-concentration C:P ramp removed under WORLD-PIDX, the surface
microbial pool holds the P:C that vendor/lpj-guess/modules/soil.cpp initialises
it to for the whole of a run:

    sompool[SURFMICRO].ptoc = 1.0 / 80.0;

That 80 is Parton, Stewart and Cole (1988) Fig. 3 p. 115's ACTIVE SOIL line at
its ctop_max end. The paper has no surface microbial pool, so the value is a
soil pool's endpoint applied to a surface pool, exactly as the deleted ramp's
80-to-30 pair was. Removing the ramp did not create that defect and does not
repair it; it makes it load-bearing, where before the dead ramp overwrote 80
with 78.1 to 79.2.

WHY THE OBVIOUS REPLACEMENT IS WRONG. Measured decomposer microbial biomass C:P
is about 66.5 by MOLE, which is 25.8 by mass (Mooshammer et al. 2014 Table 2,
from Xu et al. 2013, n = 405), and the model's ratios are mass ratios. So the
model's 80 is about three times measured microbial biomass C:P. That is not by
itself an error: CENTURY's microbial pools are conceptual SOM pools rather than
measured biomass, and the same offset is in the nitrogen side, where the pool's
sourced C:N of 10 to 20 sits against a measured microbial biomass C:N of about
7 by mass. Substituting a biomass measurement for one element and not the other
would break that consistency, so the number cannot be repaired one pool at a
time.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT is the same thing that would settle the other three C:P
initialisers and the three unsourced C:N ramp pairs: what CENTURY's pool
endpoints are measured against, which is not in any paper this project holds.
Parton, Schimel, Cole and Ojima (1987),
10.2136/sssaj1987.03615995005100050015x, is the candidate and could not be
fetched.

WHAT IT IS WORTH. sompool[SURFMICRO].ptoc is the P:C at which the surface
microbial pool receives carbon from all four surface litter pools, so it sets
the phosphorus immobilised out of litter decomposition. It is inert under
ifplim 0, which is what this project runs.

Evidence: notes/audits/lpj-soil-cn-ratios.md for the shared standing of the
CENTURY pool endpoints; biosphere/notes/phosphorus-cycle-parameterisation.md;
WORLD-PIDX

title: The soil C:N ramps are driven by NH4 alone where Parton et al. (1993) Fig. 4(a) drives them by NO3 + NH4
description:
vendor/lpj-guess/modules/somdynam.cpp line 857:

    const double nmin_mass = soil.nmass_avail(NH4);// + soil.NO3_mass;

nmin_mass is the driver of every setntoc() call in somfluxes(): the slow, soil
microbial, surface humus and (under WORLD-XFIF) passive pools' C:N ratios.

Parton et al. (1993) Fig. 4(a), which that block cites and which NMASS_SAT is
taken from, plots those C:N ratios against an abscissa labelled SOIL NO3 + NH4
(gm-2). So the figure's driver is the whole mineral N pool and the code's is one
of its two components, with the other explicitly commented out on the same line.

IT DEPENDS ON A SWITCH, AND THIS PROJECT IS ON THE WRONG SIDE OF IT.
Soil::nmass_avail in modules/soil.cpp begins

    if (!ifntransform) {
        pref = NH4;
        if (NO3_mass > 0.0) { NH4_mass += NO3_mass; NO3_mass = 0.0; }
    }

so under ifntransform 0 the NO3 pool is folded into NH4 and nmass_avail(NH4)
does return NO3 + NH4, which is the figure's quantity. Under ifntransform 1 the
two pools are kept apart and it returns NH4 alone. data/ins/global.ins imports
global_soiln.ins, which sets ifntransform 1, so the configuration this project
runs is the one in which the driver is not the figure's.

This is the same class as WORLD-Z01O on the phosphorus side, where PMASS_SAT
reads a Hedley-labile pool and its source measured resin-extractable
orthophosphate. Here the mismatch is one-signed and its size is the NO3 share of
the mineral N pool, which the nitrogen transformation operator makes prognostic.

Do: either restore the figure's driver by summing the two pools at line 857, or
establish that the surface-litter-independent argument for NH4 alone is a real
one and record it. There IS a candidate argument -- nitrate is mobile and
leaches where ammonium is held on exchange sites, so a microbial pool's
stoichiometric target might reasonably track the immobile fraction -- but
nothing in this tree makes it and Fig. 4(a) does not.

Not settled by this row, and not settleable without a run: how large the NO3
share actually is in this model's simulated soils. That is one reported quantity
off any run that reaches output.

Blocked-adjacent: WORLD-LNZN, which owns the SATURATION POINT the same ramps
use. The two are separate defects on one line of the same figure -- one is what
the abscissa MEASURES and the other is where it SATURATES -- and they can be
repaired independently.

Evidence: notes/audits/lpj-soil-cn-ratios.md; references/pdf/parton1993-century-soil-organic-matter.pdf Fig. 4(a)

title: The climatology's soil water exceeds the staged bucket capacity on 55 land cells
description:
A bucket cannot hold more than its capacity, and on this build it does.

MEASURED 2026-08-31 while pricing LSHY-6's mosaic crossing, by hydrography/scripts/lake_mosaic_cost.py, and published in its controls block in hydrography/analysis/lake_mosaic_cost.json.

THE FACT. On 55 of the 1,639 land cells of canonical-10m-carve2 at T21, the maximum over climatology bins of mrso from baseline_regular_climatology.nc exceeds the value of the staged surface code 0229 field in the same cell, matched BY INDEX. The worst is an excess of 0.0678 m on a cell whose staged capacity is 0.0490 m, a ratio of 2.38. The staged field was verified against its own orogen_T21_surf_0229_provenance.json sha256 and that record names source_build canonical-10m-carve2, the configured build, so this is not a cross-build read.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A ROUNDING. landmod.f90 computes saturation-excess runoff as the overflow of this bucket and the evaporation wetness factor as min(1, w / (0.4 C)). If the staged 0229 is not the capacity the run used, then every offline calculation that reads the pair together is computing on two different worlds, and the wetness factor saturates on cells where the run did not saturate. LSHY-6's flux numbers are reported both with and without this population for that reason, and the verdict happened to be the same on both -- which is luck, not a reason to leave it.

THE DISPOSITION SPACE, and exactly one of these is true. Either (a) the staged 0229 field is not what run_67323a923013 was actually run with, in which case the run's own namelist or input copy says so and the staged field has been rewritten since; or (b) mrso is not the quantity 0229 caps -- the land water column is multi-layer under LSHY-3 and 0229 may be a per-layer or partition capacity rather than the column total, in which case the comparison needs the split rather than the total and every consumer making the same comparison needs to know; or (c) the model permits a transient overshoot above dwmax within a timestep that the bin mean retains.

DO. Decide which, from the run record and landcolumn.f90 rather than from the documentation. If (b), name the quantity 0229 caps where a reader lands on it, because the comparison is natural and wrong. If (a), the staged field and the accepted baseline disagree and rule 5's pairing check did not catch it.

NOT FIXED HERE: exoplasim/ and the staging path were outside the file scope of the session that found it.

Evidence: hydrography/analysis/lake_mosaic_cost.json controls block; notes/audits/land-mosaic-support-reductions.md section 3.
close_reason:
Disposition (a): the staged code 229 field was rewritten on 2026-08-30, after run_67323a923013 finished on 2026-08-28, and the two differ on 1598 of 2048 cells. (b) and (c) are refuted rather than untested -- mrso is code 140 in metres, the column total dwmax caps, and it fits the run's own bucket to a maximum fill fraction of 0.99997 with zero cells above it.

Nothing is corrupt. A restage is ordinary; what was missing was a door that read the pairing run_manifest.json had recorded all along. lib/provenance.py gains run_surface_field, and staged_surface_field gains paired_with_run which refuses the cross-iteration read by name. hydrography/scripts/lake_mosaic_cost.py now stands its flux arms on the field the climatology's own run integrated and keeps the staged field for the arm that asks about the next staging; the overshoot is a refusal rather than a declared population.

No restage and no rebuild: the run directory was the evidence and it was already on disk. Nothing to fold into world-6nri.

317cf8774, f2f3c29ba, 5ae436b7f. Filed world-hl06.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTERED 2026-08-31, before the measurement, by the session taking the row.

WHAT IS ALREADY ESTABLISHED WITHOUT A MEASUREMENT, from the artifacts rather than the documentation:

- exoplasim/inputs/t21/orogen_T21_surf_0229.sra has mtime 2026-08-30 10:43 and sha256 3e3af79356...; the run's own copy exoplasim/runs/run_67323a923013/N032_surf_0229.sra has mtime 2026-08-28 07:15 and sha256 0fd07c1c3f.... They are two different fields, not two copies of one: 1598 of 2048 cells differ, the largest difference is 0.483 m, and the whole-grid means are 0.1915 m staged against 0.2962 m run. Code 2290 differs likewise. So the staged field IS NOT what run_67323a923013 was run with, and the question is only whether that accounts for the whole overflow.
- The bucket clips exactly. landcolumn.f90:75-89 bucket_step sets pwnew = max(min(pwmax, zw), 0), and the layered path landmod.f90:2114-2155 clips each layer at dwmax*dsoilwfc and sums, with dsoilwfc renormalised per cell in landwfrac. dwatc is therefore <= dwmax at every timestep, and a bin mean of clipped values is <= the clip. Zero tolerance is the right tolerance.
- mrso is code 140, units m, lwe_of_soil_moisture_content: the same quantity dwmax caps, and the column total rather than a layer. That is disposition (b) answered in the negative before it is tested.
- build_surface_soil_water.py builds its field on the climatology's own lat array north-first and writes it straight through write_sra, so .sra element order and mrso[t].ravel() order are one order and matching by index is exact.

INVARIANT A, the test with a right answer. For every one of the 1,639 matched land cells, max over the 12 climatology bins of mrso from baseline_regular_climatology.nc is <= the value at the same index in the RUN'S OWN N032_surf_0229.sra. Tolerance zero, on the clip argument above; the .sra text carries 5 decimals, so an excess below 1e-5 m is the format and not a violation.

PREDICTIONS, written before the numbers are seen.
- A holds on all 1,639 cells and the 55-cell population goes to zero. Then disposition (a) is the whole answer, the repair is about staging and provenance rather than about the model, and every offline consumer that reads the accepted baseline's climatology against exoplasim/inputs/t21/ is reading two different worlds.
- A fails on a residual. Then (c) contributes and I report the residual count and worst ratio separately from the 55.
- The residual is exactly the same 55 cells. Then the file difference is NOT the cause and (a) is refuted despite the sha mismatch.

I also expect, and will report either way, that run_manifest.json hashes only landmap and topomap and carries no hash for surface codes 229 or 2290. If so, rule 5's pairing check could not have caught this, and that is a defect in the manifest rather than in the run.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESULT, and the pre-registered test's verdict. Measured 2026-08-31.

INVARIANT A HOLDS EXACTLY. Against the run's own N032_surf_0229.sra: zero violations on all 1,019 binary-land cells, at a tolerance of 1e-5 m. Against the staged field, on the same instrument in the same pass: 55 violations, worst excess 0.06776 m on a 0.04902 m bucket, ratio 2.3823 -- which reproduces the filing measurement exactly, so the two instruments agree and the difference is the field and not the reader. The intersection of the two violating sets is empty.

The clip is visible in the data rather than merely argued: the maximum fill fraction max_bins(mrso) / dwmax over land is 0.999968, the fifth-percentile headroom is 0.0023 m and the minimum is 7e-6 m. The bucket touches its capacity and never passes it.

DISPOSITION (a), and (b) and (c) are refuted rather than untested. (b) is refuted because mrso is code 140, units m, lwe_of_soil_moisture_content -- the column total dwmax caps, not a layer -- and it fits the run's own dwmax to 3e-5 of it. (c) is refuted because a transient overshoot would show against the run's own field too, and nothing does.

WHAT (a) IS, precisely. exoplasim/inputs/t21/orogen_T21_surf_0229.sra was rewritten on 2026-08-30 10:43, after the run finished on 2026-08-28 07:15. The two fields differ on 1598 of 2048 cells, the largest difference is 0.483 m, and the whole-grid means are 0.1915 m staged against 0.2962 m run. Code 2290 differs likewise. Nothing is corrupt and nothing is a rounding: a restage happened, which is ordinary, and every offline calculation pairing this run's climatology with exoplasim/inputs/ has been computing on two worlds since.

MY OWN PRE-REGISTERED EXPECTATION ABOUT THE MANIFEST IS REFUTED, and the refutation is the good news. I expected run_manifest.json to hash only landmap and topomap. It does not: it carries surface_field_sha256 for all twelve staged codes, and its entry for 229 is the run's own field. The evidence for the pairing was already written down. What was missing was a door that reads it, so the repair is a reader and not a new record.

REPAIR TAKEN, at 317cf8774. lib/provenance.py gains run_surface_field(code, run), which resolves the field a run consumed from its manifest and its own directory copy and returns both hashes with matches_staged; and staged_surface_field gains paired_with_run, which refuses the cross-iteration pairing by name. No restage and no rebuild: the run directory is the evidence and it is already on disk.

NOT A CONSEQUENCE OF THIS ROW: that the staged field is the better one. It is the more determined artifact and the next run should read it. The defect was pairing it with a climatology from before it existed.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTERED, before re-running the instrument on the corrected pairing.

hydrography/scripts/lake_mosaic_cost.py's flux arms need one (w, C) state, and the only self-consistent one that exists is the run's. Re-pointing them at run_surface_field(229, run) changes published numbers in notes/audits/land-mosaic-support-reductions.md, so what I expect is written here first.

1. The overshoot control goes to zero, and 'all_land_cells' and 'excluding_the_overshoot_population' become the same numbers in every arm. That is the invariant above restated as an output.
2. THE DIRECTION REVERSES on the run's field. lake_dwmax_m is 0.2 m. The staged field's land mean capacity is 0.1915 m, so lake_dwmax_m exceeds it on much of the map and blending RAISES the capacity -- section 5's inversion. The run's field has a land mean of 0.2962 m, so on the run's field lake_dwmax_m is mostly BELOW the soil capacity, blending LOWERS the capacity, and that is the direction config/planet.yaml argues for. I expect the lake-bearing-land-area share where lake_dwmax_m exceeds the soil capacity to fall well below the 55.8 per cent measured on the staged field, and the absent-tile flux gap to change SIGN from negative to positive.
3. If 2 holds, then the inversion world-kvr owns is a property of the field that WILL be staged and not of the world that ran, and the audit's section 5 has to say which field it is about in every sentence.
4. The curvature finding does not depend on which field is read: the knee is at C = w/0.4 and both fields straddle it. I expect the straddling share to move but to stay far from zero and far from one.

A result outside these is reported as such rather than reconciled.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESULT of the pre-registered re-run, at f2f3c29ba and 5ae436b7f. Measured 2026-08-31.

PREDICTION 1 HOLDS. Overshoot against the run's own field is zero on all 1,639 land cells, minimum headroom 6.6e-6 m, maximum fill fraction 0.9999684. The 'excluding the overshoot population' arm is gone: there is nothing to exclude, and the control is now a REFUSAL rather than a declared caveat.

PREDICTION 2 IS REFUTED, and the error was mine rather than the world's. I predicted the direction would reverse on the run's field because I compared WHOLE-GRID means -- 0.2962 m against 0.1915 m -- most of which is ExoPlaSim's uniform 0.5 m sitting on cells with no soil. Weighted by land area the two fields are close: 0.1588 m for the field that ran against 0.1522 m staged. The direction does not reverse; it gets WORSE. lake_dwmax_m exceeds the soil capacity over 76.1 per cent of lake-bearing land area on the field that ran, against 55.8 per cent staged. That is a check on my own instrument failing before the measurement did: a mean over a grid whose ocean cells carry a default is not a mean over land.

PREDICTION 3 falls with 2. The inversion world-kvr owns is a property of lake_dwmax_m against a pedology capacity, not of which iteration is read, and it is the field that RAN that is worse.

PREDICTION 4 HOLDS. The straddling share moves from 16.4 to 13.1 per cent and both-tiles-unsaturated from 71.7 to 74.9. Far from zero and far from one, so the curvature finding and its consequence for the repair are unaffected by the pairing.

UNPREDICTED, and reported because it was not registered: both flux terms GREW. The absent lake tile goes from 0.40-0.68 to 0.63-0.80 times the bar and the mixing term from 0.14-0.23 to 0.44-0.50. Neither reaches the bar at either end of the bracket, so the audit's verdict is unchanged. What changes is the ORDERING: the absent tile was two to three times the mixing term and is now about one and a half, so a repair that stages the blend and stops leaves nearly as much on the table as it recovers. The worst cell falls from -16.0 to -6.9 W m-2, because the staged field's thin tail of cells whose capacity the blend would multiply -- max perturbation 435 per cent, 2.6 per cent of lake-bearing area above 100 per cent -- does not exist on the field that ran, where the perturbation reaches 50 per cent and nothing exceeds 100.

FILED: world-hl06 (P3). A run keeps the .sra bytes it staged and their sha256 but not the per-code provenance record, so whether the lake blend was applied is recoverable for the staged field and not for the field that ran. The report says so by name rather than assuming they agree.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
CORRECTION, found while running the artifact gate after the repair. Recorded here because a reader of this row would otherwise believe something false.

RULE 5's PAIRING CHECK DID CATCH IT. The row's disposition (a) says 'the staged field and the accepted baseline disagree and rule 5's pairing check did not catch it'. scripts/check_consistency.py's 'runs vs the surface fields they staged' arm reports run_67323a923013 with exactly two orphaned codes, 229 0fd07c1c -> 3e3af793 and 2290 3b52a278 -> df5cf8b1, and it is a FAIL in the report right now. The gate is not blind and the manifest was not the missing piece.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING, and it is two things.

First, a door at the point of read. The gate answers a question about the TREE, once, when someone runs it; an offline consumer pairing a climatology with a staged field asks the question at the moment it matters and had nowhere to ask it. That is what run_surface_field and paired_with_run are, and it is why the repair is a reader rather than a record.

Second, the gate's verdict is framed for one consumer. It says 'the run is on a surface the tree no longer holds and nothing can be seeded from it', which is about restart seeding. Seeding is not the only thing that breaks: every offline calculation reading that run's climatology against exoplasim/inputs/ is computing on two worlds, and this row is what that cost. Filed as world-3n89.

This does not change the disposition or the repair. It changes who was at fault: the tree said so and nobody was listening at the point it mattered.

title: NMASS_SAT is Parton et al. (1993) Fig. 4(a)'s saturation point times an undocumented 0.05, so the soil C:N ramps are degenerate
description:
vendor/lpj-guess/modules/somdynam.cpp declares

    // Corresponds to the amount of soil available nitrogen where SOM C:N ratio reach
    // their minimum (nitrogen saturation) (Parton et al 1993, Fig. 4)
    // Comment: NMASS_SAT is too high when considering BNF - Zaehle
    static const double NMASS_SAT = 0.002 * 0.05;

and it is the fmax of every setntoc() call in the file. The 0.002 is the cited
figure's own saturation point in the model's units and the 0.05 has no
derivation anywhere in the tree.

THE FIGURE, READ. Parton et al. (1993) Fig. 4(a) plots the C:N ratio of the
active, slow and passive SOM pools against SOIL NO3 + NH4 in gN/m2 over an axis
running 0 to 2.5. Measured at 600 dpi against ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20: all
three lines break at 2.0 gN/m2 and are flat beyond it, at slow 12.06, passive
3.17 and active 2.14. So the saturation point the constant's own comment names
is 2.0 gN/m2 = 0.002 kgN/m2, which is the first factor written into the line.

LPJ-GUESS'S OWN PAPER SAYS THE SAME NUMBER FOR THE SAME REASON. Smith et al.
(2014) Appendix C: the soil mineral N pool Navail 'is capped at a saturation
level of 2 g N m-2 following Parton et al. (1993)'. So the model's mineral N
pool is capped at exactly the driver value at which the figure's ramps
saturate, and NMASS_SAT should be that cap.

WHAT THE 0.05 DOES. NH4_mass and NO3_mass are kgN/m2 (framework/guess.h), so
NMASS_SAT is 1.0e-4 kgN/m2 = 0.1 gN/m2, a twentieth of the cap. Every setntoc
ramp therefore reaches its cton_min at 5 per cent of the driver's attainable
range and the four pools sit at their minimum C:N over the other 95 per cent:
SLOWSOM at 15 rather than ramping 30 to 15, SOILMICRO at 6 rather than 15 to 6,
SURFHUMUS at 15 rather than 30 to 15, and PASSIVESOM at 7 rather than 10 to 7.
The ramps are declared, evaluated and effectively inert. The recorded
justification is one attributed opinion, 'NMASS_SAT is too high when
considering BNF - Zaehle', with no argument and no number behind it, which is a
tuned value in this project's sense: the constant IS the residual of a
judgement nobody can inspect.

DISPOSITION SPACE. Removing the 0.05 gives 0.002 with a source, and it is what
the model's own documentation says the cap is. Against that: LPJ-GUESS's
simulated Navail may not reach CENTURY's grassland NO3+NH4 range at all, which
is presumably what the Zaehle comment means, and if so the honest form is a
bracket 1.0e-4 to 2.0e-3 swept rather than a point. Deciding needs one number
this project does not have: the distribution of simulated nmin_mass over a run.
That is cheap to get from any run that reaches output -- NH4_mass is already a
reported quantity -- and it is what should settle this rather than a preference.

WHAT ELSE IS ON THIS BLOCK. Two discrepancies between the model and its own
paper, found in the same reading and NOT covered here:
  - The driver. Fig. 4(a)'s abscissa is NO3 + NH4. somdynam.cpp line 857 reads
    'soil.nmass_avail(NH4);// + soil.NO3_mass;' and under ifntransform 1, which
    is what this project runs, nmass_avail(NH4) returns NH4 alone. Under
    ifntransform 0 it folds NO3 in, so the driver matches the figure only in the
    configuration this project does not use. Same class as WORLD-Z01O.
  - The passive pool's base decay rate. Smith et al. (2014) Table C1 gives
    3.9e-6/day; somdynam.cpp's K_MAX array gives 1.9e-6. A factor of two on the
    turnover time of the slowest pool in the model.
Each wants its own row.

Evidence: references/pdf/parton1993-century-soil-organic-matter.pdf Fig. 4(a) and
p. 791; references/pdf/smith_2014_implications-of-incorporating-n-cycling-and-n-limitations-on-primary-p.pdf Appendix C and Table C1; notes/audits/lpj-soil-cn-ratios.md

title: The two columns' modelled snow uses two specific heats of ice: a fixed 2090 and Fukusako's linear relation
description:
The two components now build the modelled snowpack's volumetric heat capacity the same way -- the pack's own density times the specific heat of ice Ih -- but they do not use the same specific heat.

vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/landmod.f90 declares
    real, parameter :: CPSNOW = 2090. ! specific heat of snow (J/kg/K)
and landini derives snowcap = rhosnow * CPSNOW.

vendor/lpj-guess/modules/soil.cpp's update_snow_properties evaluates Fukusako's
linear relation in absolute temperature,
    Csnow = (0.185 + 0.689 * (K2degC + dailyairtemp) * 0.01) * J_PER_KJ;
which gives 2067.0 J/kg/K at 273.15 K and 1791.4 at 233.15 K.

So the two agree to 1.1 per cent at the melting point and are 16.7 per cent
apart at -40 degC, and only one of them varies with the simulated air
temperature at all. This is the same class as WORLD-GJOV -- one material
property with two values inside one project -- with two differences that make
it smaller and separable: the constructions now agree, and the spread is 17 per
cent rather than a factor of two.

What is missing is a source. Neither number is sourced where it stands. 2090 is
the textbook value for ice Ih at 0 degC and carries no citation in landmod;
soil.cpp cites 'Fukusako, Eq. 2', which is Fukusako (1990), Thermophysical
properties of ice, snow, and sea ice, Int. J. Thermophys. 11, 353-372,
10.1007/BF01133567, and PAPERFETCH COULD NOT OBTAIN IT (Springer landing pages
return no PDF; sci-hub 403). The linear form c_p = 185 + 6.89 T J/kg/K is a
standard one and evaluates correctly at 0 degC, but this project holds no copy
of the source, so it is OPAQUE in the project's sense: the derivation exists
somewhere a reader cannot reach.

Do: obtain Fukusako (1990) or an equivalent primary source for the specific
heat of ice Ih as a function of temperature -- IAPWS R10-06(2009) already
reaches this project through analysis/ice_properties.py and gives c_p(T)
exactly, which is the route most likely to settle it without a fetch -- then
declare the one relation where both columns can restate it, on the lib/snow.py
arrangement the conductivity already has. IAPWS-06 would replace both numbers
rather than pick between them.

WORTH, before anyone runs it: the modelled snowpack's thermal mass and its
diffusivity both scale with the specific heat, so 17 per cent at the cold end is
17 per cent on the pack's thermal mass there. That is smaller than the
vapour-kinetics bracket the conductivity already carries and it is not a factor
of two, which is why this is its own row and not part of WORLD-2AIJ.

Evidence: notes/audits/cryosphere-material-properties.md, section 'The third
instance: the vegetation model's snow carried ice heat capacity'; the check that
could have failed and did not is in biosphere/config/snow_thermal.yaml under
snow_heat_capacity_density.

title: build_surface_albedo.py should record each override class's share of the staged land mean
description:
scripts/error_budget.py prices its playa_clastic item as a class-albedo step
times that class's share of the STAGED land-mean albedo. That share was an
opaque literal 0.147 with no derivation anywhere in the tree, and it is
measured at 0.0851423, so the item was overstated by 1.727 and ranked one
place too high. Fixed in 58bed5424 by declaring the measured share beside its
recipe, with verify_land_mean_shares waiting to refuse a disagreement.

THE DECLARATION IS OUTSIDE ANY LOOP AND THAT IS THE DEFECT LEFT. Nothing
re-runs when the share changes: the albedo report records the override that
was APPLIED and not the sensitivity to it, so the check is silent and the
number will drift from the terrain it describes with nothing objecting. That
is the field-update rule in CLAUDE.md, and the disposition it names is the
second one: the declaration sits inside a loop that re-derives it and a check
fires when the two disagree.

WHAT TO DO. Have build_surface_albedo.py record, per entry in
lithology_albedo_overrides, land_mean_share: how far land_mean_written moves
per unit of that class's albedo. It is exact and linear -- three runs put it at
0.08514230 to eight figures across a factor of five in step size -- so it can
be computed rather than finite-differenced, from the same gridded field and
weights the land mean already uses, provided the class indicator is carried
through the same vegetated repaint, derived evaporite split, lake compositing
and gridding the albedo is. The repaints are what make it not an area
fraction, and threading the indicator through them is the work.

error_budget.py:verify_land_mean_shares reads
lithology_albedo_overrides.<class>.land_mean_share and refuses at 1e-6. It is
written and it will start checking the moment the key exists; no change is
needed there.

WORTH ASKING FIRST whether the salt crust item has the same defect. It is
priced as 0.10 times a literal 0.019 and the salt crust level is not settable
by an override at all -- it comes from the derived evaporite split, which the
staged report records as null. That item cannot be measured by this recipe and
needs its own answer.

Source: scripts/error_budget.py LAND_MEAN_SHARES; notes/audits/albedo-attenuation.md.

title: The wet-soil albedo mixing crosses the storage tolerance and has no builder fix
description:
`build_surface_albedo.py` stages a DRY band pair and a SATURATED band pair, each an area-weighted mean over the cell's own lithology, and `landmod.f90:wetalb` mixes them per cell through `wet_soil_albedo`, which is Sadeghi, Jones and Philpot (2015): linear in the Kubelka-Munk transform and therefore NOT in the albedo. The model computes the mixing of the cell's mean rock where what the cell owes the atmosphere is the area mean of the mixings of its own rocks.

MEASURED AND MATERIAL. `analysis/spatial_reduction_gap.py`'s `wet_albedo_mixing` arm, on canonical-10m-carve2 at every rung with the watts taken on the accepted baseline. The gap reaches 0.147 W m-2 of global-mean absorbed shortwave against the accepted baseline's 0.12 W m-2 state-storage tolerance -- the same bar `config/partial_surface.yaml` selected the tile operator against -- and stays past it from about 0.10 to about 0.47 of the model's declared 0 to 0.7609 saturation range. The land-mean albedo gap is -1.97e-03 in band 1 at T21 falling to -1.25e-03 at T170; the worst cell carries 1.68e-02 at every rung. The sign is negative, so the modelled wet ground is brighter than its own mixture of rocks and the surface absorbs less than it should.

THE MATERIALITY DOES NOT REST ON A GUESS ABOUT HOW WET THIS WORLD IS. `landmod.f90:181` puts `drhsfull` at 0.4 of capacity, the fraction above which the wetness factor reaches one, and `config/planet.yaml` maps a full surface layer to a saturation of 0.7609. The knee is therefore at a saturation of 0.304 and the gap peaks at 0.285. The modelled soil crosses that point every time it wets or dries through the limiter's ceiling.

THERE IS NO BUILDER FIX, AND THIS IS THE PART TO READ BEFORE PROPOSING ONE. Staging the albedo whose Kubelka-Munk transform is the cell's area mean of the per-region transforms was pre-registered as the exact repair. It is wrong at first order: on a two-class cell it is off by 1.1e-01 where the defect is 1.0e-03, and it fails hardest at zero saturation. The reason is that the two staged fields are not free parameters. Code 174 IS the dry albedo -- `sadeghi_mix` returns it unchanged at zero saturation and the radiation reads the same field on dry ground -- so it is pinned to the cell's area-mean dry albedo by a boundary condition that has nothing to do with wetting, and the saturated pair is pinned at the other end by the same argument. The mixing is linear in the transform of its ARGUMENT and the inverse transform is applied afterwards; reducing in the transform makes the argument exact and leaves the inverse's own Jensen term, which is convex where the measured one is concave. The two available stagings bracket the truth from opposite sides and neither reaches it.

TWO DISPOSITIONS, AND THE CHOICE IS THE WORK.
1. A model change: `wetalb` reads a third staged field carrying the cell's own curvature, so that the mixing is exact at a declared saturation rather than at the two ends only. That is a surface code, a namelist key and a rebuild of every binary (CLAUDE.md rule 4), and the declared saturation is a decision that needs stating.
2. A declared bracket: the measured table is carried as model-form error in the surface energy budget, in the manner `config/partial_surface.yaml` carries its flux bracket, and nothing is staged.

Do not offer "leave it" as a third: the gap exceeds the accepted run's own storage tolerance over the range the soil actually occupies, so it is not inside anything the model already declares.

WHAT WOULD SHARPEN THE CHOICE. The arm sweeps saturation because the surface layer's own saturation is not recoverable from the accepted climatology: `mrso` is the whole column and `wetalb` reads `dwatcl(:,1)`. Retaining the surface layer's water in the output would collapse the sweep to one number and turn the range above into a single verdict.

Evidence: notes/audits/nonlinear-spatial-reductions.md section 7; analysis/spatial_reduction_gap.json under `by_rung.<rung>.wet_albedo_mixing`.
Source: spat-7
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTRATION, world-yxor, before any edit or measurement. Nothing below was written after seeing a result.

THE CHOICE IS THE WORK, AND IT IS NOT TAKEABLE UNTIL ONE THING IS MEASURED. The row offers a model change or a declared bracket. Disposition 1 is specified as 'wetalb reads a third staged field carrying the cell's own curvature, so that the mixing is exact at a declared saturation rather than at the two ends only'. NOBODY HAS MEASURED WHETHER THAT WORKS. The pre-registered builder repair was measured wrong by two orders, so the standard this row already set is that a proposed repair is priced before it is adopted, not after. Choosing disposition 1 without that number would be choosing the repair the audit refused, one layer up.

THE CANDIDATE FORMS, priced in the same terms as the defect, in analysis/spatial_reduction_gap.py's wet_albedo_mixing arm:

  as_built            the two staged fields and landmod's current mixing. The measured defect.
  staged_in_transform the refuted repair, priced so the artifact carries why it fails rather than only the note.
  three_point_knee    a THIRD staged field, the exact area mean of the per-region mixed albedo at the declared knee, with the model mixing piecewise: dry to knee below it and knee to saturated above it, on the saturation rescaled inside each segment. Exact at three points by construction, because each of the three staged fields is an exact area mean of a per-region quantity.

THE DECLARED SATURATION IS DERIVED AND NOT CHOSEN. landmod.f90's drhsfull is the fill fraction above which the wetness factor reaches one, and wetalb maps a fill fraction onto saturation through config/planet.yaml's saturation_at_empty_layer and saturation_at_full_layer. The knee is the image of drhsfull under that map. Both numbers are READ from their files rather than written into the measurement, and both predate this row. The gap peaking near the knee is a result, not the reason for the choice.

THE CRITERION, fixed here. Disposition 1 is VIABLE if and only if three_point_knee's global-mean absorbed-shortwave gap is at or under 0.12 W m-2 -- config/partial_surface.yaml's accepted-baseline state-storage tolerance, the same bar the defect is measured against -- at EVERY point of the declared saturation range. The defect fails that from about 0.10 to about 0.47 of the range. If the three-point form fails it anywhere in the range, disposition 1 in its one-extra-field shape is REFUTED and disposition 2 is the answer with that as its reason.

PREDICTION. three_point_knee's peak comes in at or under 0.05 W m-2, a fall of at least a factor of three from the defect's 0.147, because splitting a smooth one-signed hump at its peak leaves two humps of a shorter interval each pinned at both ends. If it lands between 0.05 and 0.12 the criterion still passes and I report the prediction as missed. staged_in_transform is predicted to be worse than as_built at every saturation including zero, reproducing the note's 1.1e-01 on the two-class case.

SECONDARY AND NOT DECISIVE: the land-mean albedo gap against the defect's -1.97e-03 in band 1 at T21, and the worst cell against 1.68e-02.

WHERE IT IS TAKEN. On canonical-10m-carve2 at T21, because the watts are available on the accepted baseline's own rung and on no other, and the criterion is in watts. The albedo-side rows are taken at every rung the run covers.

NO CLIMATE RUN, and none is needed for this: every candidate's correctness is arithmetic on the mesh, which is what the arm already does for the defect.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, declared before the measurement. The gap is swept over saturation because the surface layer's own saturation is not recoverable from the accepted climatology: mrso is the whole column and wetalb reads dwatcl(:,1). So every number here is a SUPREMUM over a coordinate the output does not carry, and that is true of the defect and of every candidate equally. It does not affect the comparison between them, which is what the criterion is on.
