comments.text:
RESULT, against the pre-registration above. Measured 2026-08-30 on canonical-10m-carve2 at T21, on the accepted baseline's own downward shortwave.

GLOBAL-MEAN ABSORBED-SHORTWAVE GAP, W m-2, against the 0.12 W m-2 bar:

  saturation | as_built | staged_in_transform | three_point_knee
  -----------|----------|---------------------|------------------
  0.0000     |  0.0000  |       0.8567        |      0.0000
  0.0951     | -0.1051  |       0.8722        |     -0.0289
  0.1902     | -0.1418  |       0.8756        |     -0.0234

  peak                    0.1471       0.8756          0.0421
  past the bar at          3 of 9      9 of 9          0 of 9

THE CRITERION IS MET AND DISPOSITION 1 IS SELECTED. three_point_knee is inside the 0.12 W m-2 storage tolerance at every saturation the modelled column reaches. as_built reproduces the audit's 0.147 peak exactly, so the arm is measuring what it measured before.

PREDICTION HELD ON BOTH CLAUSES. I said at or under 0.05 W m-2 and a fall of at least a factor of three. The peak is 0.0421 and the fall is 3.49x. The albedo side falls with it: the band 1 land-mean gap goes from -1.97e-03 to -5.58e-04 at its worst and the worst cell from 1.55e-02 to 4.26e-03, both about a factor of 3.6.

THE REFUTED REPAIR IS NOW PRICED IN WATTS AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE NOTE SAID. staged_in_transform is 0.83 to 0.88 W m-2 across the whole range, SIX times the defect and seven times the bar, and it is 0.857 at ZERO saturation where the defect is exactly zero. The note measured it on a two-class synthetic; on the real mesh it is past the bar at every point of the sweep including the one the defect gets exactly right. That is now in the artifact rather than only in prose, which is what stops it being proposed again.

WHY THREE POINTS AND NOT A BETTER TWO. Each of the three staged fields is an exact area mean of a per-region quantity -- the dry albedo, the saturated albedo, and the cell's own mixed albedo at the knee -- so the composition is exact at three saturations by construction where the current form is exact at two. Verified directly: the form returns the staged dry field at zero, the staged knee field at the knee and the staged saturated field at one, to the last bit. The only choice in it is WHERE the third point sits, and that is landmod.f90's drhsfull mapped through config/planet.yaml's declared saturation endpoints -- read from both files by the measurement, not written into it. Nothing is fitted.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is construction rather than a question: build_surface_albedo.py stages the third band pair, wet_soil_albedo gains the three-point form, wetalb reads it behind a namelist key, and every binary is rebuilt (CLAUDE.md rule 4). The form is verifiable without a climate run -- analysis/soil_albedo_wetting.py already compiles a driver against landcolumn.f90 and requires the Fortran to agree with the Python -- so the implementation has a gate that can fail.

STILL A SUPREMUM, as declared before the measurement. Every number here is over a saturation the accepted output does not carry, because mrso is the whole column and wetalb reads dwatcl(:,1). That is true of the defect and of every candidate equally, so it does not affect the comparison the criterion is on; it does mean the defect's 0.147 is an upper bound on what the model actually suffers, and the repair's 0.042 likewise.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
DISPOSITION TAKEN: 1, the model change. Implemented, gated as far as anything offline can gate it, and the two steps that must happen where the payloads live are filed as world-6nri.

WHAT IS IN THE TREE.

landcolumn.f90:wet_soil_albedo_3pt runs the same Sadeghi mixing in two segments through a third staged albedo. landmod gains dalbknee/dalbknee1/dalbknee2 and nwetsoil = 2; surfmod registers codes 1743, 1751 and 1761; wetalb computes the knee saturation as skinsrad + drhsfull*(skinsrfc - skinsrad) from its own module constants, so the saturation the field is staged at and the one it is mixed at are one expression rather than two declarations. build_surface_albedo.py forms the field by applying the mixing per REGION and reducing afterwards. run_exoplasim.py routes surface.soil_albedo_moisture.three_point to NWETSOIL, restart_surface.py records the three codes as boundary conditions and not states, and config/planet.yaml turns it on with the measurement as the reason.

THE GATES THAT CAN FAIL, and did not.

The compiled wet_soil_albedo_3pt agrees with the Python bitwise over 400 samples, with the knee swept across the whole open unit interval rather than held at the staged value, and with four samples placed ON the knee: all three staged points come back exactly, worst disagreement 0.0. The builder refuses a staged knee outside the bracket its two ends set, because the mixing darkens monotonically and a knee outside it is a reduction taken in the wrong order. The broadband member is recombined from the band pair, so z1*1751 + z2*1761 == 1743 holds at the third point the way it already did at the other two. verify_model_compiles passes and one T21 l10 p8 binary LINKED under --no-publish, which is the check a syntax-only pass cannot reach. smoke_test and verify_entry_points pass.

TWO MODES REFUSE RATHER THAN APPROXIMATE. --mode scaled does not stage the third point: it multiplies already-reduced endmembers by a per-cell factor, and the mixing of two scaled endmembers is not the scaling of their mixing, so a knee carried through it would still be called exact and would not be. landini then stops on the sentinel. --flat-bands has no pair for a third point to sit inside. Both say which in the report.

WHY A PER-CELL SIGMA WAS REFUSED. It would have cost the same one extra field per band and kept a single Sadeghi curve, but a shape parameter chosen so the two-field curve passes through the truth at one saturation IS the residual of a fit, with no derivation to carry to another planet. The third albedo is an exact area mean of a per-region quantity, the same reduction the other two staged fields are.

WHAT IS OUTSTANDING AND WHY IT IS NOT HERE. The staged .sra inputs and the ten compiled binaries both live in the main checkout; link_worktree.py deliberately does not link vendor/exoplasim or the build directory, and exoplasim/inputs' .sra files are symlinks into it, so re-staging or rebuilding from a worktree would either write across the isolation boundary or produce executables that die with the tree. world-6nri carries both with the commands. Until then run_exoplasim.py refuses by naming the builder and the setting, and scripts/pipeline.py --status reports surface_albedo missing exactly those three files, which is the tree telling the truth rather than a broken state.

NO CLIMATE RUN WAS LAUNCHED and none was needed for any of the above. What no offline check reaches is the climate response to a 0.1 W m-2 change in absorbed shortwave, and that belongs to the next run rather than to this row.

title: The 0.5 wet-mask verdict prices its land side and not its ocean side
description:
`config/partial_surface.yaml` records `threshold_verdict: retain` for ExoPlaSim's 0.5 binarisation of `yls`, and the cost it is retained against is priced on the LAND side only. `analysis/coastline_threshold_cost.json` carries `land_dropped_of_mesh_land`, `water_promoted_of_model_land`, `model_land_area_relative` and `land_volume_closure_relative`, and four candidate rules beside them. There is no ocean-side row anywhere.

MEASURED 2026-08-30, on canonical-10m-carve2, as a by-product of sizing the ocean support crossing. At a zero depth horizon there is no threshold on depth at all, so the whole difference between the binarised ocean area and the mesh's own is the 0.5 cut and nothing else:

| support | ocean-side area error, in multiples of 0.001 of planetary area |
| --- | ---: |
| T21 | 5.0 |
| T42 | 4.3 |
| T85 | 4.3 |
| T127 | 4.2 |
| T170 | 3.3 |
| GOLDSTEIN 36 x 36 | 12.3 |

The bar is `ocean/config/transport_loop.yaml`'s `sea_ice_area` criterion, which is this project's one declared bar on a planetary area fraction. The numbers are in `analysis/ocean_support_reduction.json` under each support's `horizon_area` at `horizon_km: 0.0`, as `binarised_gap_km2`.

WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A NOTE. The mask error barely falls along the ladder -- 5.0 to 3.3 across a factor of eight in linear resolution -- because it is a coastline-length quantity and a coastline does not get shorter. So it does not go away by refining, and the decision record that retains the threshold does not state what it costs the ocean. A decision that names its price on one side of a boundary and not the other cannot be re-taken by a reader.

DO. Add the ocean-side rows to `analysis/coastline_threshold_cost.py`'s ledger, in the same terms as the land side and against the same four candidate rules, so the retain verdict carries both halves of its cost. Nothing here reopens the verdict: the flux bracket that selected the tile model is a separate measurement and this does not bear on it.

NOT A BATHYMETRY QUESTION, which is why it is not in the ocean audit's own follow-ups. It is the same mask on the same coastline that SPAT-5 already owns, seen from the wet side.

Evidence: notes/audits/ocean-support-nonlinear-reductions.md section 2, last paragraph; analysis/ocean_support_reduction.json.
Source: spat-7
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTRATION, world-3w1m, before any edit or measurement.

WHAT I WILL ADD, in coastline_ledger's own terms and against the same candidate rules the land side is priced against.

Per candidate rule, beside the five land-side rows in cost():
  model_ocean_area_relative        model ocean area over mesh ocean area, minus one
  ocean_promoted_of_mesh_ocean     mesh OCEAN area landing in a model land cell, over mesh ocean area
  land_added_of_model_ocean        mesh LAND area landing in a model ocean cell, over model ocean area
  ocean_area_gap_km2               |model ocean area - mesh ocean area|
  ocean_area_gap_of_planet         that gap over the planetary area
  ocean_area_gap_over_bar          that fraction over the bar

THE BAR is ocean/config/transport_loop.yaml criterion sea_ice_area, threshold 0.001, units fraction_of_planet -- this project's one declared bar on a planetary area fraction, and the same one notes/audits/ocean-support-nonlinear-reductions.md uses. It is READ from that file rather than written into the script. The denominator is the analytic planetary area 4*pi*r^2 from the mesh manifest's own radius, which is the denominator the audit's fraction_of_planet uses; the mesh's summed cell area exceeds it by about 7e-4 of the planet, so the denominator choice is stated rather than defaulted.

THE CHECK, and it is the point of doing this rather than a restatement. The ocean-side gap at a zero depth horizon is computable two ways by two scripts that share no code path: analysis/ocean_support_reduction.py bins the mesh onto each support and differences binarised against fine ocean area, and analysis/coastline_threshold_cost.py differences the land ledger's two one-signed halves. PREDICTION, fixed here: for as_configured, the new ocean_area_gap_km2 equals ocean_support_reduction.json's binarised_gap_km2 at horizon_km 0.0 on every one of T21/T42/T85/T127/T170, to relative 1e-9. If they disagree one of the two is wrong and I report which rather than adjusting either.

SECOND PREDICTION. The area_conserving rule is defined by zeroing the net land area error, and mesh ocean is the exact complement of mesh land in this build (INLAND_WATER is measured at exactly zero area), so that rule must put the ocean-side gap at or under 1e-3 of the bar while every other rule leaves it above the bar. If any rule other than area_conserving comes in under the bar, or if area_conserving does not, the complement identity does not hold on this build and that is the result.

SCOPE. The GOLDSTEIN 36 x 36 figure the row quotes at 12.3 times the bar is not this builder's mask: coastline_threshold_cost.py prices the Gaussian ladder ExoPlaSim binarises, and the ocean grid's own mask is OCN-11's. It stays in the ocean audit and I say so in the artifact rather than importing it.

NOT REOPENING THE VERDICT. config/partial_surface.yaml's threshold_verdict stays retain. What changes is that the record carries both halves of the cost.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESULT, against the pre-registration above. Commit ab09d266e. Measured 2026-08-30 on canonical-10m-carve2, terrain hash f496ae9f, 10,000,005 regions.

THE OCEAN SIDE, in multiples of the 0.001-of-planetary-area bar (ocean/config/transport_loop.yaml, sea_ice_area), by candidate rule and rung:

  rule                            | T21    | T42   | T85   | T127  | T170
  --------------------------------|--------|-------|-------|-------|------
  as_configured (0.5, RETAINED)   |   4.95 |  4.28 |  4.33 |  4.18 | 3.29
  area_conserving                 |   0.06 |  0.09 |  0.03 |  0.00 | 0.01
  exempt_below_datum_share_any    | 202.63 | 93.24 | 27.66 | 10.70 | 3.88
  exempt_below_datum_share_0.10   |   3.88 |  4.06 |  4.19 |  4.00 | 3.20
  exempt_below_datum_share_0.25   |   4.95 |  4.28 |  4.33 |  4.17 | 3.29

PREDICTION 1 HELD, EXACTLY. The ocean-side gap for as_configured equals analysis/ocean_support_reduction.json's binarised_gap_km2 at horizon_km 0.0 on every rung to a relative difference of 0.000e+00, against a 1e-9 bar. T21 3637389.596971, T42 3140350.638367, T85 3180219.701074, T127 3066875.146819, T170 2419640.109210. The two routes are the ocean audit binning the mesh onto each support and differencing binarised against fine ocean area, and this builder differencing the land ledger's two one-signed halves; they agree bit for bit, which is the identity that the ocean is the exact complement of the land on a build whose INLAND_WATER area is measured at exactly zero.

PREDICTION 2 HELD ON ITS STATED FALSIFICATION CONDITION AND FAILED ON AN INCIDENTAL FIGURE. I named the falsifier as 'any rule other than area_conserving under the bar, or area_conserving not under it'. Neither happened: area_conserving is under at every rung and the other four are over at every rung. But I also wrote 'at or under 1e-3 of the bar' and it lands at 0.003 to 0.09 of the bar, up to ninety times that figure. The reason is that the mask is a STEP FUNCTION of the threshold, so the bisection's 60 iterations do not set the residual -- the smallest cell-area increment near the crossing does. The residual floor is one cell's worth of area, not a bisection tolerance, and the figure I wrote was a tolerance mistaken for a floor.

THE FINDING THE ROW WAS ASKING FOR, and it is not the arithmetic. The land side selects the retained rule -- the alternatives worsen the below-datum land-volume closure -- and the ocean side selects area_conserving by a factor of fifty to a thousand on the only bar this project declares on a planetary area fraction. The two sides of the coastline do not agree, and a record that priced one of them could not show that. config/partial_surface.yaml now carries cost_land_side, cost_ocean_side and the reason the ocean side does not reopen the verdict: the tile model is selected, so the binary mask's remaining job is topology and the atmosphere reads the fractional area. What the ocean-side error still bears on is TOPOLOGY, which is OCN-11's and is what the ocean audit's connectivity arm measures.

WHERE THE BAR COMES FROM. build_boundary_conditions.py READS transport_loop.yaml's sea_ice_area criterion and refuses if it is not declared in fraction_of_planet, rather than restating 0.001. The denominator is 4*pi*r^2 from the mesh manifest's own radius, stated in the artifact, because the mesh's summed polygon area exceeds the sphere by about 7e-4 of the planet, which is the same order as the bar.

SCOPE HELD. The GOLDSTEIN 36 x 36 figure at 12.3 times the bar stays in the ocean audit; it is that grid's own binarisation and is OCN-11's mask, and the artifact says so where a reader would otherwise look for it.

title: error_budget.py dies on a missing carve list instead of taking its own unavailable path
description:
scripts/error_budget.py cannot run at all on the configured build. basin_response
opens hydrography/data/canonical-10m-carve2/carve_list.json and raises
FileNotFoundError, so the whole budget dies before it prints anything, including
the albedo half that needs no hydrography artifact whatsoever.

The file already has the right disposition for this exact question and does not
apply it here. verify_hydrological_response returns a list of problems, main
prints "CARVE CURRENCY UNAVAILABLE, so every runoff and basin column below reads
--", and carve_columns renders a null as "--". That path exists because the
carve conversion was measured on a build that is no longer configured. A carve
list that is simply absent is the same class of thing and should reach the same
report, not a traceback.

What stops it being a two-line guard is that basin_response returns three values
and the tail of main reads basins["overflowing_basins"],
basins["reconstruction_check"] and basins["change_in_overflowing_basins"]
unconditionally, and CARVE_ITEMS is priced through the `overflowing` closure it
returns. So the fix is a decision about what the budget PRINTS and WRITES when
its carve half is absent, across five places, and that is worth doing
deliberately rather than as a drive-by.

Found while measuring the attenuation for world-ckbt, which is why it matters
now: the albedo half of the budget was just repriced onto a measured constant
and nothing can run the generator to see the new table.

Source: scripts/error_budget.py:basin_response, and the CARVE CURRENCY
UNAVAILABLE block in main.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Fixed in 8f99abed2.

THE DECISION. The carve half of the budget has THREE outputs and they read
different things, so unavailability is per-currency rather than one flag:

  runoff percent   the configured build's water balance and
                   HYDROLOGICAL_RESPONSE_PER_KELVIN. Null iff the response
                   fails to verify.
  basin count      those, AND a carve list on the configured build. Null iff
                   either fails.
  the CARVE_ITEMS table and the basin-verdict table
                   the carve list ALONE. The file's own note already says these
                   have no kelvin anywhere in their path, so the response cannot
                   reach them. Null iff the carve list cannot be read.

The albedo and forcing halves read no hydrography artifact and neither
unavailability touches them. Folding the two together would print -- for a
runoff column that is fully determined; folding them the other way is what made
a build with no carve list a traceback.

basin_response now returns a summary carrying an  list instead of
raising, for all THREE ways the list can fail to answer, not just the one filed:
absent; every basin carried from a previous pass (rows[0] was an unguarded
IndexError); and the pre-BUDG-5 format that records no water terms, which was a
SystemExit and is the same class. Two banners, CARVE CURRENCY UNAVAILABLE and
BASIN CRITERION UNAVAILABLE, print separately with their reasons, and the
artifact carries carve_currency.unavailability_is_per_currency plus the reason
under carve_currency.basin_response.

SECOND DEFECT ON THE SAME PATH, found by fixing the first: the generator got
one line further and died on sensitivity._index_entries, which no longer
exists. The live index and the archived identities were deliberately split so a
bracket measured on two deleted runs could not go on reproducing its constant,
and error_budget.py's comment still claimed sensitivity merged them. Both are

returns 416 overflowing, reproduces the recorded overflow count, and gives the
Penman carve item +181 to +348. Unchanged.

WHAT THE BUDGET NOW PRINTS on canonical-10m-carve2: the full albedo table on the
measured 0.38 attenuation, the full forcing table, the land water balance, and
-- for every basin column and both basin tables, with the two reasons stated.
The biosphere endmember item is +3.17 K attenuated against +8.33 K naive.

title: The spatial-support vocabulary has no term for the DISTRIBUTION reduction
description:
`lib/gridding.py` carries a DISTRIBUTION reduction -- `cell_quantiles`, the area-weighted quantile table a sub-grid hypsometry IS, with `area_fraction_above` reading a share back out of it -- and CLAUDE.md's `lib/` list names it as one of the operators by field semantics. `config/spatial_support.yaml`'s `aggregation_operators` vocabulary has no term for it:

    identity, conservative_source_area, conservative_destination_area,
    covered_area_mean, area_weighted_fraction, categorical_majority,
    categorical_histogram, vector_rotation_and_component_remap,
    stochastic_demographic_sampling

`lib/spatial_support.py:validate_contract` refuses any `aggregation.operator` outside that list, so a spatial artifact carrying a per-cell hypsometry has two options and both are wrong: declare `covered_area_mean`, which says the field is a cell mean when it is a quantile table, or fail validation. There is no third.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDINESS. The whole point of SPAT-1's contract is that a reader can tell what a number is a reduction OF without reading the generator, and the whole point of SPAT-7 is that the reduction ORDER changes answers by amounts that move decisions. A contract that cannot name the one operator that preserves a within-cell distribution can only describe artifacts that have already thrown it away. The two SPAT rows point in opposite directions at this seam.

IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND IT IS ABOUT TO BIND. `hydrography/scripts/build_spatial_support.py` already builds a hypsometry with `cell_quantiles` and states in its own prose that the hypsometry is the DISTRIBUTION operator; it does not route that through a SPAT-1 contract, so nothing has refused yet. `notes/audits/ocean-support-nonlinear-reductions.md` measures that the ocean support cannot use a cell-mean depth, so OCN-11's artifact will carry a per-cell depth distribution, and OCN-11 is required to emit a SPAT-1 contract. That is where the missing term stops being an omission and becomes a refusal.

DO. Add a distribution term to `aggregation_operators` in `config/spatial_support.yaml`, named for what it is rather than for the function that computes it, and give it the same treatment the categorical pair already has in `validate_contract`: a field whose semantics say it is a distribution may only carry that operator, and a field carrying that operator must declare the probability vector its quantiles are at, because a quantile table without its probabilities is not readable. `lib/gridding.py:cell_quantiles` requires `probs` from the caller for exactly that reason and declines to default it.

Check the vocabulary against the operators `lib/gridding.py` actually exposes while there. The two lists have drifted once and nothing compares them.

Evidence: config/spatial_support.yaml aggregation_operators; lib/spatial_support.py:213; lib/gridding.py:454 and :541; notes/audits/ocean-support-nonlinear-reductions.md.
Source: spat-7
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTRATION, world-erln, before any edit.

WHAT I AM ADDING, and the names, fixed here so the report cannot rename them after the fact.

config/spatial_support.yaml gains one field semantics, `distribution_quantiles`, and three aggregation operators, `area_weighted_distribution`, `covered_area_expectation` and `covered_area_moments`. The distribution term is named for the reduction and not for cell_quantiles; the other two close the drift the row asks me to check, because lib/gridding.py's SPAT-4 block exposes six cell_* reductions and the vocabulary named four of them.

The mapping I claim, and it is falsifiable by reading either file:

  conservative_source_area      cell_sum        (and remap EXTENSIVE_TOTAL)
  conservative_destination_area (remap FLUX_DENSITY only)
  covered_area_mean             cell_mean       (and remap INTENSIVE)
  area_weighted_fraction        cell_fraction
  categorical_histogram         cell_fraction
  covered_area_moments          cell_moments
  covered_area_expectation      cell_expectation
  area_weighted_distribution    cell_quantiles
  identity, categorical_majority, vector_rotation_and_component_remap,
  stochastic_demographic_sampling                (no lib.gridding reduction)

THE RULES validate_contract will enforce, each of which is a case that can fail rather than a case that can only differ:

  R1 semantics distribution_quantiles admits only operator identity or area_weighted_distribution.
  R2 operator area_weighted_distribution admits only semantics distribution_quantiles. Bidirectional, unlike the categorical pair, because a quantile table is not a value of anything else.
  R3 a field carrying area_weighted_distribution must declare quantile_probabilities.
  R4 quantile_probabilities must be a non-empty, strictly increasing vector inside [0, 1] -- cell_quantiles' own precondition, restated where a reader of the artifact can check it.

THE DRIFT CHECK, and its criterion is fixed before I run it: every module-level callable in lib.gridding whose name begins with cell_ must be claimed by exactly one aggregation operator term, and every lib.gridding name a term claims must exist. The check derives the gridding side by introspection rather than from a hand-kept list, so adding a seventh reduction fires it without anyone remembering to. It runs in scripts/spatial_support_gate.py, which is already the pipeline's spatial_support_gate step. PREDICTION: run against the vocabulary as it stands today it FAILS on cell_moments, cell_expectation and cell_quantiles, and on nothing else. If it fires on a fourth name my mapping above is wrong and I report that rather than adjusting the mapping.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING. Not changing schema_version or contract_version: every addition is additive, no contract valid today becomes invalid, and R1-R4 can only refuse a field that could not be expressed at all before. If that turns out false -- if any existing contract in the tree fails after the change -- it is a version bump and I report it as a failed pre-registration.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESULT, against the pre-registration above. Commit d1a2d32da.

WHAT HELD.

The three rules R1-R3 and the probability precondition R4 are in lib/spatial_support.py and each has a negative case in scripts/spatial_support_gate.py that refuses: a distribution declaring covered_area_mean, the distribution operator on an intensive_state field, a missing quantile_probabilities, an unordered vector, and a vector leaving [0, 1]. Positive case is a five-point elevation hypsometry on the reference contract. The gate runs 27 checks and passes.

The additive claim held and is checked rather than asserted. Every contract stored in the tree -- analysis/ocean_remap.json's source and destination contracts and biosphere/data/canonical-10m-carve2/rootable_fraction_T21_report.json's spatial_contract -- revalidates unchanged, and lib.spatial_support.grid_support_contract still builds and validates. No schema_version or contract_version bump.

The mapping I claimed held: lib.gridding exposes exactly six module-level cell_* reductions -- cell_sum, cell_mean, cell_fraction, cell_moments, cell_expectation, cell_quantiles -- and no seventh. The three the old vocabulary could not name were cell_moments, cell_expectation and cell_quantiles, exactly as predicted, so the drift is closed by covered_area_moments, covered_area_expectation and area_weighted_distribution and by nothing else.

WHAT FAILED IN THE PRE-REGISTRATION, reported rather than re-registered.

I fixed the drift criterion as 'claimed by exactly one term'. That is wrong and the mapping in the same comment contradicts it: cell_fraction implements BOTH area_weighted_fraction and categorical_histogram, because one class share and a partition of them are the same computation under two declared semantics. The criterion as implemented is COVERAGE -- every exposed cell_* claimed by at least one term, and every claimed name resolving -- which is the direction that actually drifted. The many-to-one relation is stated in lib/gridding.py's block and in the check's own docstring so the next reader does not have to rediscover it. Nothing about the prediction's substance changes; the defect was in the uniqueness clause, not in the mapping.

ALSO DONE, and outside the DO as written. config/pipeline.yaml's ocean_support gate stated the distribution requirement in prose the contract could not express; it now names the field semantics and the operator, so the gate is expressible rather than special-cased. docs/src/pipeline/steps.md's spatial_support_gate paragraph gains the operator and the reason a mean is not a reduction of a distribution.

NOT DONE, and it is not this row. hydrography/scripts/build_spatial_support.py still does not route its land hypsometry through a SPAT-1 contract. It now CAN, and applying the contract to every production artifact is SPAT-10's, not this row's.

title: The groundwater solve refactorises every pass, and the file already names the 27x lever it cannot reach
description:
hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater.py takes minutes on the active build and is on the critical path of the hydrology loop, so its cost shapes how often anyone re-solves a water table.

THE DIAGNOSIS IS ALREADY IN THE FILE AND IS MEASURED, which is why this row is specific rather than an invitation to profile. hydrography/scripts/groundwater.py around line 1240 records a solver comparison that survives testing:

  SuperLU spsolve, the line in use      1.39 s
  UMFPACK via scikit-umfpack           1.93 s   0.72x
  pyamg smoothed aggregation + CG      7.05 s   0.20x
  CG, diagonal preconditioner           20 s    DID NOT CONVERGE

and it draws the right conclusion: THE LINEAR SOLVE IS NOT THE COST. At 1.39 s against the roughly 20 outer passes a linear run takes -- the reports on disk record 17 and 18 -- that is about 30 s inside a multi-minute run. What is expensive is the NUMBER of passes.

THE ONE LEVER THE FILE NAMES AND CANNOT CURRENTLY REACH: splu re-solves in 0.049 s against 1.3 s to refactorise, 27x, on any pass where the matrix repeats. Reaching it needs the evapotranspiration iteration RESTRUCTURED so the diagonal is held fixed across inner steps. It is not a faster library and it is not an ordering change -- the same comment records ordering as a measured NEGATIVE at this size: MMD_AT_PLUS_A halves fill and is about 3x faster at 2M unknowns on a synthetic, and at this problem's 55,977 free cells the fill is IDENTICAL either way, because SuperLU's partial pivoting undoes the symmetric ordering unless SymmetricMode is on with diag_pivot_thresh 0, which spsolve cannot pass.

SO THE WORK IS: establish which passes actually repeat the matrix, restructure the ET iteration to hold the diagonal fixed across inner steps so those passes reuse a factorisation, and measure. If the matrix turns out to repeat on few passes, the lever is smaller than 27x and the honest answer is to say so and to attack the PASS COUNT instead -- the active set churning is what sets it.

DO NOT re-derive the solver comparison; it is measured and recorded. Do not swap libraries.

MEASURE BEFORE AND AFTER ON THE SAME BUILD, and record the load beside the timing. The verdict must be bit-identical: an active-set method on a box-constrained linear complementarity problem terminates exactly, and the convergence criterion is DECLARED BEFORE THE FIRST RUN in that file's own words -- water balance residual on free cells over total land recharge AND a still active set, both not either. A restructuring that changes which cells are found dry has changed the answer, not the speed.

RELATED AND NOT THIS ROW: world-v3ur's reverse uniqueness trajectory starts with every land cell free, 834 M entries against 400 M, about 10 GB against 4.8 GB, and the file names splu with SymmetricMode as the untried lever against that memory blocker. That is world-v3ur's, and this row should not consume it.
acceptance_criteria: A groundwater solve on the active build is materially faster with a bit-identical water table and an identical converged active set, the before and after are recorded with the load they were measured under, and the share of passes that actually reuse a factorisation is stated rather than assumed.
notes: Filed 2026-08-31 at the author's request after a run queued behind it for 12 minutes. The lesson from world-l11x applies and is why this row leads with the file's own measurement: there, the first structural guess at the hot spot was wrong and the profile put the cost somewhere else entirely. If the recorded reasoning here turns out not to hold on the current build, say so and profile before changing anything.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
MEASURED, AND THE ROW IS NOW ABOUT REACHABILITY RATHER THAN EFFICIENCY. Corrects my earlier comment on this row, which reported the solve as still running at 39 minutes.

It never finished. One CONFINED constant-thickness solve on canonical-10m-carve2 -- 10,000,005 regions, 4,328,732 land regions, bootstrap regular climatology, alone on the host under scripts/lock_and_run at 2,600% CPU and about 16 GB peak RSS -- ran for over 40 minutes, wrote no water_table.nc, and was then killed. Because the run's stdout was block-buffered to a file with no tty, the kill lost every line of it: the log is zero bytes, so there is not even a pass trace to say how far it got. That is a second, cheap thing this row could fix -- a solve whose progress is only knowable if it exits normally cannot be diagnosed when it does not.

THE DECLARED COST IS WRONG. config/pipeline.yaml declares the groundwater step at cost: minutes. On the active build it is not minutes, and the row's own call-site comment describes 'about 30 s inside a multi-minute run', which was sized on a smaller build.

GW-18 needs a sixth. At 40+ minutes each and a single-holder host lock that had SIX other agents queued on it at the time -- world-rnns three times, spat-7, clim-34, and this one -- that is not a scheduling inconvenience, it is the reason those rows have now failed to be run on three separate occasions. So the lever this row already names -- splu factorisation reuse across passes that repeat the matrix, 0.049 s against 1.3 s -- is not an optimisation. It is what makes GW-18 and GW-24 answerable on a shared host at all.

title: config-rationale.md restates config values, and five of them are wrong
description:
docs/src/reference/config-rationale.md restates config/planet.yaml's current values inside fenced blocks, once per key, in about forty-five sections. A restated value is a derived quantity written down with nothing re-deriving it, so it drifts, and it drifts silently: a reader grepping for the state of a key lands on the restatement rather than on the key. That is what CLAUDE.md's field-update rule refuses and what its "do not write current values into prose" convention already forbids.

MEASURED 2026-08-30 by parsing every fenced block in the file and comparing each `key: value` line against config/planet.yaml. Ten disagreed. Four are fixed and the fixes are in the tree; five need a disposition this row cannot source; one is a false positive.

FIXED, because the correct content was verifiable end to end:
- `source_build` named precarve-craton against a configured canonical-10m-carve2, two builds back.
- `baseline_climatology` was documented as null. It names run_67323a923013's regular climatology on canonical-10m-carve2. This one was load-bearing: SPAT-7's ocean, land-water and albedo arms and world-bjpg were all deferred on the null.
- `h2o_sw_weight` quoted 1.346 against 1.351 and `h2o_sw_level` 1.163 against 1.161 with a bracket of [1.129, 1.206] against [1.128, 1.205]. Their prose does not depend on the digits, so the value fences are gone and nothing else moved.

STILL WRONG, and each needs a disposition rather than an edit:
- `resolution` quotes T42 and argues at length for T42 over T21 for the iteration-1 baseline. Config carries T21, the last indexed run is T21, and the baseline climatology is 32x64. The section's whole argument is inverted and rewriting it means knowing why the project moved back, which this row does not.
- `energy_diagnostics` quotes false while the prose says "ON, because energy_fixer is driven by denergy26 and denergy27". Config carries true. One of the two is what is meant.
- `conversion_time_level` and `robert_filter` are quoted with values while neither key is in config/planet.yaml at all; both are optional `model.*` keys that run_exoplasim reads with `.get`. `robert_filter`'s prose says "Present because ...", which is the statement that is false. A fenced `key: value` for an undeclared key reads as a declaration.
- `land_longwave_emissivity` quotes `<the lithology-weighted land mean>`, which is a description of where the value comes from and not a value. It is correct as written and the checker flags it only because it does not parse as a number.

DO, and the second half is what keeps it fixed. First, settle the four dispositions above with whoever owns the resolution and diagnostics decisions. Second, give the file a check: parse every fenced `key: value` in it and compare against config/planet.yaml, refusing a disagreement. That is a static read over two tracked files and belongs in scripts/smoke_test.py. Without it this row is a snapshot and the next config move re-opens it.

The alternative to a check is to carry no values in the file at all, which is what the convention actually asks for: the heading names the key, config/planet.yaml holds the value and its comment, and the section carries the argument. That is the larger edit and it makes the check unnecessary rather than complementary.

Evidence: the measurement is fifteen lines and is reproducible from the description above; the four fixes are in the tree.
Source: spat-7

title: Size the marine-productivity reduction once OCN-13 and OCN-14 give it a law
description:
SPAT-7 names marine productivity among the reductions to size. The GEOMETRY half of the ocean crossing is now measured -- notes/audits/ocean-support-nonlinear-reductions.md sizes bathymetry, the area on either side of a depth horizon, and connectivity, on terrain alone -- and the BIOLOGY half cannot be, because the law it would be a reduction of does not exist.

WHAT IS ABSENT. notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md section 8d says "reached the ocean" is a boundary condition and not marine nutrition: ANUT-6 routes terrestrial export to the coast and OCN-13 begins there, and neither is built. OCN-14 has not declared the trait space a marine productivity law would be evaluated over. Sizing the nonlinearity of a law nobody has written would be sizing a preference, and that is why this arm reports the geometry and stops.

WHAT IS ALREADY DECIDED, AND WHAT IT COSTS THIS ARM. The geometry measurement establishes that the ocean support's cell-mean depth does not carry the area on either side of a depth horizon, at a size far above the loop's own declared area bar. Every marine productivity law reads exactly such a threshold at least twice: a euphotic depth, and a shelf-versus-open partition for benthic supply and burial. So this arm inherits a support defect rather than starting from a clean one, and a productivity map built on a cell-mean bathymetry would carry it silently.

PRE-REGISTERED INVARIANTS, written before any such measurement.
1. The one-class control. A cell whose wet population is uniform in depth and irradiance has no spread, so both orders agree exactly. Falsifiable, and it is checked before any gap is quoted.
2. Light limitation is CONVEX in depth over the attenuating column and saturating in irradiance, so the two curvatures act in opposite directions and the sign of the combined gap is an outcome. NO SIGN IS PRE-REGISTERED.
3. Nutrient limitation through a Michaelis-Menten form is concave, so its own gap is one-signed for a fixed cell; the combined gap is not, because the two limitations multiply.
4. Refinement shrinks every gap, because in the limit of one mesh region per wet cell both orders are the same computation. A gap that does not is a support artifact.

THE INSTRUMENT, declared now. `ocean/config/transport_loop.yaml`'s `heat_transport_change`, 0.12 W m-2 over ocean area, is not the right bar for a productivity field and this row does not borrow it. The bar is OCN-15's accepted marine artifact reporting its own spread on export production; a reduction gap smaller than the spread the accepted artifact already carries is inside the model's own scatter. That bar is declared here and cannot be chosen after the result.

DO. Once OCN-13's ledger and OCN-14's trait space exist and OCN-15 accepts an artifact, evaluate the limitation terms per sub-cell depth and irradiance bin -- `lib/gridding.py:cell_quantiles` is the operator that supplies the bins, and it is the same hypsometry the geometry arm found the support is missing -- and area-average, against the same terms on the cell mean. Report each gap against OCN-15's own spread.

Evidence: notes/audits/ocean-support-nonlinear-reductions.md; notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md sections 8b and 8d.
Source: spat-7

title: Size the fire and terrestrial-productivity reductions on SPAT-6's response units
description:
SPAT-7 names fire and terrestrial productivity among the reductions to size, and neither can be sized today for a reason that is structural rather than a matter of effort. This row carries the pre-registered invariants and the decision procedure so that the measurement is one comparison when the input exists.

WHAT IS MISSING IS NOT A CLIMATOLOGY, IT IS A SUB-GRID POPULATION. The land audit's section 4 established the constraint that decides every arm in this class: a cell-scale parameter may consume a statistic of a distribution the CELL CONTAINS, and where the input is solved at the grid there is no such distribution and no operator is warranted however curved the law is. Fire's ignition, spread and combustion-completeness laws and the productivity laws' light, water and nutrient limitations are all evaluated on quantities LPJ solves per column, and this project has one column per cell. There is no mesh-resolved fuel load, fuel moisture, leaf area or soil nitrogen anywhere in the tree, so the two orders of the reduction are not both defined and there is nothing to difference.

SPAT-6 IS WHAT CREATES THE POPULATION. The co-located ecological response-unit mosaic is exactly a within-cell distribution of terrain, lithology, soil profile, lake and playa state and groundwater access, with conserved area weights and LPJ columns evaluated on each environment before aggregation. The moment that exists, aggregate-then-process and process-then-aggregate are both computable for fire and for productivity, and this row's measurement becomes a difference of two runs of the same code on the same mosaic. Until then the arm has one order and not two.

PRE-REGISTERED INVARIANTS, written before any such measurement.
1. The one-unit control. A cell whose mosaic holds a single response unit has no spread, so both orders return the same number exactly. This is the falsifiable half and it must be checked before any gap is quoted.
2. The gap vanishes as the unit count rises to one unit per mesh region, because in that limit both orders are the same computation. A gap that does not shrink with unit count is carrying a support artifact rather than a Jensen term, which is the mechanism the land audit's section 6 separated for `subgrid_slope`.
3. NO SIGN IS PRE-REGISTERED, for either arm, and the reason is specific rather than caution. Fire area is convex in fuel load below the ignition threshold and concave above it, so a cell straddling the threshold can gain or lose burnt area by the order of its reduction. Productivity saturates in light and in nutrient supply while being convex in water stress over part of its range, so the sign depends on where the cell's own distribution sits relative to each knee. A universal sign for refinement would be a prediction the mechanism does not support.

THE INSTRUMENTS, declared now.
Fire: the burnt-area fraction the fire component reports itself against, taken from FIRE-8's accepted artifact once it exists; a gap smaller than the seed and patch ensemble spread `lib/lpj_output.py` already reports is inside the model's own scatter and is not material by definition.
Terrestrial productivity: the same ensemble spread on net primary production, for the same reason, and BIO-2's `nfix_a` bracket of 0.102 to 0.367 carried through rather than a central value, because a reduction gap smaller than a declared input bracket cannot move a decision the bracket does not already move.

DO. Once SPAT-6's mosaic and an accepted LPJ run both exist, evaluate the fire and productivity laws on each response unit and area-average, against the same laws evaluated on the mosaic's area-mean environment, and report each gap against the instrument above. `lib/gridding.py:cell_expectation` is the operator if a gap exceeds it. A gap inside it is a reason NOT to carry an expectation, and saying so is a result.

Evidence: notes/audits/nonlinear-spatial-reductions.md section 4 for the constraint; biosphere/notes/spatial-support-ecological-aggregation-audit.md finding 4.
Source: spat-7

title: Size the land-water capacity reduction once the lake blend stages a lake fraction
description:
SPAT-7 names land and soil water and runoff among the reductions to size. The chain was traced on 2026-08-30 and it is one reduction, not several, and it is currently inert. This row carries the pre-registered invariant and the instrument so that the measurement is a comparison rather than a re-derivation when the reduction becomes live.

WHERE THE REDUCTION IS. `build_surface_soil_water.py` makes exactly one mesh-to-grid reduction: `land_fraction_of_class` on the per-region lake indicator, which is `gridding.cell_fraction`, the categorical operator. The result blends the bucket capacity as `(1 - f_lake) * C_soil + f_lake * lake_dwmax_m` and writes surface code 0229.

THE REDUCTION IS AFFINE AND THAT IS THE PRECONDITION FOR THE GAP, NOT ITS ABSENCE. The blend is literally the area-weighted mean of a two-point capacity distribution, so it adds no curvature of its own. The curvature is entirely in the consumers, and both are convex and non-increasing in the capacity: saturation-excess runoff is `max(0, w + F*dt - C)/dt` at `landcolumn.f90:84-86`, and the evaporation wetness factor is `min(1, w/(0.4*C))` at `landcolumn.f90:370`. So `E[g(C)] >= g(E[C])` for both, and mixing the capacity first UNDER-predicts runoff and UNDER-predicts evaporative efficiency on every cell holding lake.

PRE-REGISTERED INVARIANTS, written before the measurement.
1. The gap is EXACTLY ZERO wherever the cell's store-plus-flux lies outside the interval between the two capacities, because both terms are then zero or the law is linear across the interval. It is therefore confined to cells with a positive lake fraction whose water lands strictly between `lake_dwmax_m` and `C_soil`, and it is bounded above by `f_lake * |C_soil - lake_dwmax_m|`. A measured gap outside that bound indicts the binning.
2. The gap vanishes at `f_lake = 0` and at `f_lake = 1` and is one-signed in between, because a two-point distribution has one sign of curvature.
3. Refinement shrinks it, because a cell fine enough to hold one surface has no spread.
No sign is pre-registered for the SIZE across the ladder: `f_lake` is a fraction whose spread depends on how many cells straddle a shoreline, and that is what is being measured.

THE INSTRUMENT. `exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md` carries a measured runoff-versus-capacity chord of `d ln R / d ln C = -0.0416` over a factor 3.75 in capacity, taken on an offline bucket validated against the model's own soil water. That converts a fractional capacity gap into a fractional land-runoff gap directly, and it is the instrument this arm reports against rather than a percentage invented for it. The note states its own magnitude as "well under one per cent" rather than three digits, because the local slope at the operating point is unmeasured, and that qualification travels with any result taken through it.

WHY IT IS NOT MEASURED NOW. The staged field is inert: `exoplasim/inputs/t21/orogen_T21_surf_0229_provenance.json` carries `"lakes": null`, so nothing the model runs today performs this reduction at all. Sizing a reduction no artifact carries would price the `--lakes` path rather than the world. The measurement becomes worth taking the moment a lake fraction is staged.

DO. When surface code 0229 is next staged with `--lakes`, take the per-cell `f_lake`, `C_soil` and `lake_dwmax_m`, evaluate both consumers in both orders over the cell's two-point capacity distribution, and report the runoff gap against the chord above and the wetness-factor gap against the accepted baseline's own latent heat flux. `lib/gridding.py:cell_expectation` is the operator if the gap exceeds the instrument, and a gap inside it is a reason NOT to carry one.

Evidence: notes/audits/nonlinear-spatial-reductions.md; exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_soil_water.py; vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/landcolumn.f90:84-86 and :370.
Source: spat-7
close_reason:
Settled rather than deferred, and the row's deferral premise was wrong. A staged field with no lake blend is not a reduction that is absent; it is the reduction with the tile dropped, and that is what the world runs and what the capacity is read as on every land cell. Both consumers are now answered without waiting for a --lakes staging.

ENERGY: the absent tile is 0.63 to 0.80 times the bar and the mixing term 0.44 to 0.50, both under it at the upper end, so the DO's own criterion says do NOT carry a correction. MASS: the absent tile is under 0.1 per cent of land runoff through the chord the row names; the mixing term cannot go through that chord at all, because the blend moves no mean capacity, and no substitute exists in this tree.

INVARIANTS. 1 holds where tested. 2 is FALSE for the wetness factor -- it is concave at the saturation knee and 13.1 per cent of solved lake area straddles it -- and TRUE for runoff, which is convex throughout; selftest identities 2 to 5 hold each half. 3 is untested and nothing turns on it: refinement only shrinks a gap already under the bar.

CONSEQUENCE, which is the part that outlives the row: a tile operator for this crossing has to carry the DISTRIBUTION and not a corrected mean, because a correction with one sign cannot track a gap with two. lib/gridding.py:cell_quantiles is the operator, as it is for the ocean crossing that reached the same place by a different mechanism. cell_expectation, which this row named, is the wrong one.

The live question moved to world-kvr: the term that IS staged has the wrong direction, on both capacity fields, and worse on the one that ran.

Evidence: notes/audits/land-mosaic-support-reductions.md sections 3, 4 and 5. 826042bf4.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
INVARIANT 2 IS FALSE FOR THE WETNESS FACTOR, found 2026-08-31 while pricing LSHY-6's mosaic crossing. Reported here rather than acted on, because this row is not mine and the correction is to its pre-registration rather than to its plan.

WHAT THIS ROW REGISTERED: 'The gap vanishes at f_lake = 0 and at f_lake = 1 and is one-signed in between, because a two-point distribution has one sign of curvature.' The endpoints hold exactly. The one sign does not.

THE MECHANISM. The wetness factor min(1, w / (0.4 C)) is NOT convex in the capacity. It is FLAT for C below the saturation knee at C = w / 0.4 and convex above it, so the derivative jumps from zero down to -1/C at the knee and the function is CONCAVE there. A two-point distribution is one-signed only when the law it is pushed through has one sign of curvature, and this one does not. A cell whose soil tile is saturated while its lake tile is not straddles the knee and carries the opposite sign; the sign reverses within a SINGLE cell as f_lake is varied. Worked case, w = 0.05 m, C_soil = 0.09 m, C_lake = 0.2 m: the gap is -0.0375 at f_lake 0.1, -0.0938 at 0.25, -0.0059 at 0.75, and +0.0011 at 0.9.

THE ROW'S OTHER CONSUMER IS UNAFFECTED. Saturation-excess runoff max(0, w + F dt - C) / dt is a maximum of zero and a decreasing affine function of the capacity, so it is convex throughout and a two-point distribution through it IS one-signed. This row's statement 'both are convex and non-increasing in the capacity' holds for runoff and fails for the wetness factor, so the two consumers need separating rather than the sentence weakening.

HOW OFTEN IT BITES, measured on canonical-10m-carve2 at T21 over the solved lake area, bin by bin: 71.7 per cent has both tiles on the unsaturated branch where the registered sign holds, and 16.4 per cent straddles the knee where it does not.

INVARIANT 1 AND 3 ARE UNTOUCHED. The gap is still exactly zero outside the interval between the two capacities and still bounded above by f_lake * |C_soil - lake_dwmax_m|, and refinement still shrinks it.

WHAT IT CHANGES FOR THIS ROW'S PLAN. The stated disposition -- 'lib/gridding.py:cell_expectation is the operator if the gap exceeds the instrument' -- now needs an argument it did not need before: a correction term carrying one sign cannot track a gap carrying two, so on the straddling cells an expectation operator has to carry the DISTRIBUTION rather than a corrected mean. That is the same conclusion notes/audits/ocean-support-nonlinear-reductions.md reached from a different mechanism.

THE SIZE THIS ROW DEFERRED HAS BEEN TAKEN, under LSHY-6 and against a different bar, so it does not pre-empt this row's own measurement. Against config/partial_surface.yaml's 0.12 W m-2, on the planet mean: the mixing term is 0.14 to 0.23 times the bar and the whole absent tile is 0.40 to 0.68. This row's sign prediction for the mixing term -- that blending under-predicts evaporative efficiency -- is CONFIRMED in the aggregate: the gap is +0.016 to +0.028 W m-2, positive, tiled above blended.

Evidence: notes/audits/land-mosaic-support-reductions.md section 4; hydrography/scripts/lake_mosaic_cost.py --selftest, which is where it was caught, identities 3 to 6.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RE-TAKEN 2026-08-31 on what is now known, and the row's OWN DEFERRAL PREMISE IS REFUTED before anything is measured.

THE PREMISE. 'WHY IT IS NOT MEASURED NOW: the staged field is inert; nothing the model runs today performs this reduction at all. Sizing a reduction no artifact carries would price the --lakes path rather than the world.'

WHY IT IS WRONG. A reduction with f_lake = 0 is not a reduction that is absent; it is the reduction with the lake tile DROPPED, and that is what the world runs. The capacity is read on every land cell whose dwmax is positive -- landmod.f90:1155-1156 calls land_wetness there unconditionally -- so the consequence of the missing tile is live on every land cell, not waiting on a staging. notes/audits/land-mosaic-support-reductions.md measured it without --lakes, from f_lake in the support file and the two-point distribution: the absent tile is worth 0.63 to 0.80 times the bar and the mixing term 0.44 to 0.50, and the absent tile is the LARGER of the two. So the thing the row deferred as unpriceable is the bigger term and was priceable all along.

INVARIANT 1 HOLDS where it has been tested. A cell saturated in both tiles is insensitive to the capacity in both orders and the gap is exactly zero: selftest identity 6.

INVARIANT 2 IS FALSE FOR THE ENERGY CONSUMER AND TRUE FOR THE MASS ONE, and the split is the whole finding. min(1, w/(0.4 C)) is flat below the saturation knee at C = w/0.4 and convex above it, so its curvature changes sign AT the knee and a two-point distribution through it is not one-signed: 13.1 per cent of solved lake area has tiles that straddle it. max(0, w + F dt - C)/dt is a maximum of zero and a decreasing affine function of the capacity, convex throughout, and the invariant holds for it exactly. Selftest identities 2, 3, 4 and 5 hold each half.

INVARIANT 3 IS UNTESTED and needs a support file at a finer rung. It is a claim about second-order Jensen behaviour under refinement and nothing turns on it: the verdict at T21 is already under the bar and refinement only shrinks the gap.

PRE-REGISTERED, before the remaining arm is taken. The row's DO names one instrument for the runoff consumer: the chord d ln R / d ln C = -0.0416 from exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md, which converts a fractional MEAN capacity change into a fractional land-runoff change.

- I expect that instrument to be INAPPLICABLE to the mixing term, because the blend is the area-weighted mean of the two-point capacity distribution and therefore changes no mean capacity at all. A chord in the mean cannot measure a Jensen gap at fixed mean. If that is right, the row's named instrument does not measure the row's named gap, and no substitute is available: the runoff law needs the per-timestep water flux and a climatology carries bin means.
- I expect it to be APPLICABLE to the absent-tile term, which IS a mean capacity change: from the blend to the soil capacity alone. I predict the land-area-weighted fractional capacity change to be small enough that 0.0416 times it lands well under one per cent of land runoff, which is the magnitude the note already states without digits, and I will report it as a bracket rather than three digits because the local slope at the operating point is unmeasured.
- A result outside these is reported as such.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESULT of the pre-registered runoff arm, at 826042bf4. Measured 2026-08-31.

BOTH PREDICTIONS HOLD.

The mixing term cannot go through the chord, and the reason is exact rather than approximate: the blend IS the area-weighted mean of the two-point capacity distribution, so the residual between the blend and that mean is 0.000e+00 m on every land cell. A chord in the mean has nothing to act on. No substitute exists in this tree either -- max(0, w + F dt - C)/dt needs the per-timestep water flux, and a climatology carries bin means. So the row's own named instrument does not measure the row's own named gap for this half, and that is a property of the law.

The absent tile does go through it. Land-area-weighted, dropping the lake tile lowers the mean log capacity by 0.019815 on the field the run integrated and 0.023259 on the staged field, 0.021865 and 0.024807 with the signs not allowed to cancel. Times 0.0416 that is 0.082 to 0.091 per cent of land runoff on the field that ran and a shade more on the staged one: under 0.1 per cent either way, which is the 'well under one per cent' the note states without digits.

INSTRUMENT CHECK. The chord spans a factor 3.75, |d ln C| = 1.3218, and is asked here about 0.0219 -- a factor of sixty INSIDE its own range, so this is interpolation. What stops it being three digits is not extrapolation but that the local slope at the operating point is unmeasured and the chord carries no scatter. The sign is not in doubt.

The two log-capacity changes are emitted by hydrography/scripts/lake_mosaic_cost.py rather than written down, so they re-derive when either field changes; the conversion and its instrument check live in the audit, because the arm's conclusion is that the instrument cannot resolve the effect and a number that re-derived every run would be one nobody should read.

title: The equilibrium contract's per-cell half is still calibrated, and its family refusal rate is five times what it declares
description:
The equilibrium contract's PER-CELL half is the one part still calibrated rather than derived, and it is the only part of the gate whose declared rate is not the rate it achieves.

WHAT IT IS FOR, and it is a real job no other half can do: opposed regional drifts that cancel in the spatial mean. Measured on the 1000-cycle diagnostic, a cancelling dipole at twice the contract's drift limit is caught by the cell half in 42 of 64 fields and by the global half in 0 of 64.

WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT.

* Its slope is fitted over `complete_forcing_cycles` = 10, which is inside one memory time for 61 of 64 assessed fields. The bare flag rate that produces is 0.47 to 0.86 against a nominal 0.081, and the contract absorbs that by measuring each field's limit from the run's own detrended windows rather than repairing it.
* Because the limit is the largest of N null windows, its declared rate is exact PER FIELD and wrong per run: 1-(1-1/(N+1))^F_eff, measured 0.34 at N=99 and about 0.24 at the N=124 a 1253-cycle record leaves. Raising N cannot fix it -- the finest probability an N-window null can express is 1/(N+1), so 0.05 over about 35 effective fields needs about 710 windows and 7100 retained cycles.
* Its empirical-null construction needs many windows and therefore cannot adopt the whole-record statistic the global half now uses. The two are not interchangeable and this is a second piece of design.

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT AND IS ALSO NOT FINE. The error is in the REFUSING direction: this half refuses a settled run about a quarter of the time, so a PASS through it is sound evidence and a REFUSAL through it establishes nothing. The gate is therefore usable today and its refusals are not trustworthy, which is exactly the state a row should hold rather than a comment.

WHAT THE REPLACEMENT HAS TO DO. Bound the spatially incoherent drift from above, in the same direction the global half now works in, without a per-window null. The natural quantity is the excess of the cells' mean square relative drift over what their own memory-corrected standard errors predict, since the null term is computable per cell and falls with the patch count while a real dipole does not -- which also repairs the finding that the current ratio test is invariant to both patch count and record length. What it needs and does not have is the effective number of independent cells, because 1617 gridcells of one field are not 1617 independent samples.

CITES: biosphere/notes/equilibrium-trend-null.md, biosphere/config/equilibrium_window.yaml (trend.cell_fraction).

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
world-mxmr's assessed set shrank this row's family, and the numbers in it are now over a different count.

The per-cell half runs on the eleven CONSUMER QUANTITIES rather than on the 64 columns of the seven stability tables, at each quantity's own tolerance. Its empirical-null construction is unchanged and still calibrated rather than derived, but the family it refuses over is eleven and not 64, so the 0.34 measured on 100 windows and the 0.24 on the 124 a 1253-cycle record leaves are both upper bounds on what it now costs. The analytic replacement this row holds is unaffected -- what makes the per-window null wrong is that 1/(N+1) is the finest probability it can express, and that does not depend on the family size.

title: verify_entry_points reports a deliberate refusal as an entry point that does not start
description:
scripts/verify_entry_points.py exists to prove the import graph resolves: it starts every entry point and reports the ones that do not. It decides 'does not start' by exit status, so a script that STARTS PERFECTLY WELL and then refuses on purpose is reported as a broken import.

Measured on a clean tree at 212 entry points, 2 reported as not starting, and both are deliberate refusals:

  aeolian/scripts/playa_roughness_mix.py -- refuses because the band shares are a property of one build's terrain and it will not mix another build's landform composition into a roughness a dust run will consume. That refusal is the whole point of the script and it prints its reason.
  analysis/partial_surface_decision_gate.py -- exits non-zero because the SPAT-5 seam is open, which is the gate reporting the state it exists to report.

Both became visible when world-6247 widened SCRIPT_DIRS to reach aeolian/ and analysis/, so this is that row's findings continuing to arrive rather than a new regression.

WHY IT MATTERS. A checker that cannot tell 'your imports are broken' from 'this gate correctly refused' teaches its readers to ignore its output, and the failure it is meant to catch -- an import graph that no longer resolves, invisible to every static pass -- is the one CLAUDE.md rule 8 promoted it to a gate for. Two non-zero exits it should never have equated.

THE DISTINCTION IS AVAILABLE. An import failure dies before main with a traceback naming ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError; a refusal reaches its own code and prints its own reason. Separating on that, rather than on exit status alone, is the repair. Deciding it by a per-script allowlist is the wrong shape: it would need maintaining per gate and would go stale silently, which is the defect class this checker belongs to.
acceptance_criteria: verify_entry_points distinguishes an import that does not resolve from a script that started and refused, reports them separately, and fails only on the first. Both current cases are reported as refusals and the run is green on a clean tree.
notes: Found 2026-08-30 running the gate after the references/pdf move. Related to world-ujcj, which is about the same script RUNNING what it only needs to START; that row is the mutation half and this is the exit-status half.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 SETTLED. The row's argument held: the distinction is available, and a per-script allowlist is the wrong shape. What it did not anticipate is that the classifier is not where the two current cases get fixed.

WHERE THE DISTINCTION LIVES. Not in stderr, which is a guess, and not in a list of names, which goes stale. Inside the child it is an exception type. scripts/_entry_probe.py runs the script under except clauses that name it and reports a CLASS: import (ImportError/ModuleNotFoundError), refusal (SystemExit with a non-zero code), start (anything else). The first two fail the gate; a refusal is printed beside them under 'started and refused, which is not this gate's business' and the run stays green.

THE TWO CURRENT CASES ARE NOT CLASSIFIED, THEY ARE NOT REACHED. world-ujcj's half of the repair picks the probe per script, and neither playa_roughness_mix.py nor partial_surface_decision_gate.py builds an ArgumentParser, so both are probed by importing the module body and never enter main(). They report ok. The acceptance criterion said they would be 'reported as refusals'; they are better than that -- a gate that never runs them never has an opinion about their verdict, which is the correct scope for a start check. Both are green on a clean tree.

SO THE CLASSIFIER IS NOT DEAD CODE. It still decides for the 185 help-mode entry points (a script refusing before its parser is reached) and for any module-level refusal, and it is what makes the failure message true: '[import] ModuleNotFoundError' and '[start] FileNotFoundError' are different repairs. --self-test builds one script of each class and checks it, and runs as part of a full pass, so it cannot rot unexercised. Each arm was confirmed to fail when its expectation is flipped.

PROVEN ON REAL TREE SCRIPTS, not only synthetic ones. A ModuleNotFoundError inserted into minerals/scripts/build_prospectivity.py: '[import] ModuleNotFoundError: No module named ...', exit 1. The same script made to refuse at module level: 'said no', reported separately, exit 0. And the two real refusers probed in help mode both come back kind=refusal rather than kind=import.

ALSO FIXED HERE: the gate's own self-checks fired for any directory named 'scripts', so verify_entry_points.py minerals/scripts ran the lock wrapper's self-test. They now compare against the repository's own scripts/.

91d9892e7, 06b48e91a. The class is docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md 38.

title: assess_lpj_run.py parses 89 million rows in Python, and the gate is slow enough to shape behaviour
description:
biosphere/scripts/assess_lpj_run.py is the gate every coupled consumer waits on (BIO-14: exit code zero is necessary and insufficient). On the first run long enough to matter -- lpj_7d3c576ee4e342acb097b46fece976e0, 1617 cells, 1253 retained cycles, 19 outputs, 16 ranks -- it takes long enough that a person notices, and a gate people notice is a gate people route around.

MEASURED, not inferred; the profile is on this row. read_table at :62 is 198 s of tottime and 349 s cumulative out of 575.8 s, so about 60 per cent of the run. It is a pure-Python line parser doing, per data row, one str.split, two round(float(...), 2), a list comprehension of float() into np.asarray, and np.isfinite(values).all(). The call counts fix the volume exactly: 89.1M str.split and 178.3M round, so 89.1 million data rows parsed.

The assessment reads the data about seventeen times over BY DESIGN -- read_table is called for the merged table at :286 and once per rank at :292, and BIO-14 exists to check every rank -- and then verifies the merge ROW BY ROW, which is the 36.5M numpy.array_equal calls, each allocating two arrays and running a reduce.

Nothing here is algorithmically wrong. It is the right work done through the slowest available access path.

DO, in this order:
1. Parse column-wise. np.loadtxt or a pandas whitespace read, then round, the finiteness guard and the duplicate-key check vectorised over columns rather than per row. This is the 198 s.
2. Verify the merge wholesale. Sort merged and per-rank tables once by (lon, lat, year) and compare value blocks as arrays.
3. ONLY THEN consider parallelism. The 19 outputs are independent and a pool is clean, but it multiplies a constant that 1 and 2 reduce by a large factor, and it pays to pickle what it distributes. Re-measure first.

WHAT THIS ROW IS NOT ABOUT, recorded because it was the first guess and it was wrong: field_series' per-year dict lookup does not appear in the profile's top ten. The cost is upstream of it, in getting the tables into memory at all.

CONSTRAINT THAT DECIDES THE DESIGN: this script's verdict gates real work, so it must produce a bit-identical report before and after. The existing --selftest and its fixtures are the check, and any change that cannot keep the fixtures passing is the wrong change.
acceptance_criteria: Assessment of a 1617-cell, 1253-cycle run is materially faster with a bit-identical acceptance.json, --selftest still passes, and the measured before and after are recorded with the run they were measured on.
notes: Filed 2026-08-30 at the author's request after the derived-spin-up assessment. A cProfile run over the same run is in flight and its hot spots go on this row when it lands; until then the ordering of causes here is read off the source and is explicitly not measured.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 PROFILED, and the ordering I inferred from structure was WRONG. cProfile over lpj_7d3c576ee4e342acb097b46fece976e0, 1617 cells, 1253 cycles, 19 outputs, 16 ranks:

  575.8 s profiled, 1,252,504,778 function calls.

  ncalls        tottime  cumtime  what
       306      198.2    348.9    assess_lpj_run.py:62 read_table
         8       53.1     88.0    lib/lpj_output.py:157 _read_rows
 125619674       44.6     44.6    numpy.ufunc.reduce
 178296888       40.1     40.1    builtins.round
 162088960       38.1     38.1    numpy.asarray
  36469818       27.2     54.4    numpy.array_equal
       306       26.5     26.5    assess_lpj_run.py:100 coverage
 125618341       22.3     81.9    ndarray.all
  89149559       19.6     19.6    str.split

field_series DOES NOT APPEAR IN THE TOP TEN. The per-year dict lookup this row was filed about is not the cost, and the row's description is rewritten rather than annotated.

WHERE THE TIME ACTUALLY GOES. read_table is a pure-Python line parser and it is 60 per cent of the run. Per data row it does one str.split, two round(float(...), 2), a list comprehension of float() into np.asarray, and np.isfinite(values).all(). The counts say the volume exactly: 89.1M str.split and 178.3M round is 89.1M data rows parsed, two rounds each. The 125.6M reduce and .all are the per-row isfinite guard. Nothing here is algorithmically wrong; it is 89 million Python-level iterations doing what a column-wise parse does in a few C passes.

THE 36.5M array_equal IS THE MERGE VERIFICATION, and it is legitimate work done the slowest way. read_table is called at :286 for the merged table and at :292 per rank, 19 outputs x 16 ranks, so the assessment reads the data about seventeen times over by design -- BIO-14 checks every rank -- and then compares merged against per-rank ROW BY ROW, each comparison allocating two arrays and running a reduce.

DISPOSITION, in this order, and the first two are where the run time is:
1. Parse column-wise. np.loadtxt or a pandas whitespace read, then round, isfinite and the duplicate-key check vectorised over columns. This is the 198 s.
2. Verify the merge wholesale. Sort both tables once by (lon, lat, year) and compare the value blocks as arrays instead of 36.5M array_equal calls on single rows.
3. ONLY THEN consider parallelism. The 19 outputs are independent and a process pool is clean, but it multiplies a constant that items 1 and 2 reduce by a large factor, and it pays to pickle what it distributes. Measure again before reaching for it.

CAVEAT ON THE NUMBER: 575.8 s is under cProfile, which is heavy on code making 1.25 billion calls. The unprofiled assessment of the same run was faster; the RATIO between rows is what this table is good for, not the absolute.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-31 DONE, and parallelism is DECLINED on a measurement.

MEASURED on lpj_7d3c576ee4e342acb097b46fece976e0 (1617 cells, 1253 cycles, 19
outputs, 16 ranks), unprofiled, same host, same warm run directory:

  before  356.94 s   load 1.36 before / 1.52 after
  after    41.66 s   load 1.74 before / 1.80 after
  after    41.81 s   load 3.50 before / 4.12 after (rebased tree, busier host)

8.6x. The acceptance.json is BIT-IDENTICAL: sha256 of the report with only
`generated` removed is 6ca3b7dbdcd9d9d85b1444053abb01a86c92fb66189847f0536f821112857815
before and after. --selftest passes, its 210-year fixture retained.

WHAT CHANGED. lib/lpj_table.py parses each column in one pass and states every
check as a vectorised test. It CERTIFIES OR DECLINES: anything it cannot
certify -- a header that is not Lon Lat Year, a ragged row, a nonnumeric or
nonfinite field, a nonintegral year, a duplicated cell-year, a coordinate near
a half-cent tie -- raises RowParseRequired, and the caller's own row-at-a-time
parser diagnoses it. That is what keeps every refusal message identical: the
fast path never diagnoses a defect, it only declines to certify one. Sixteen
malformed-table cases were compared parser against parser; every one either
agrees exactly or declines to the original wording.

A table arrives sorted on ONE int64 cell-year key, which turns the coverage
check into a row count against a product, the merge check into two array
comparisons (was 36.5M numpy.array_equal on single rows), and a closure series
into a read out of a reshaped grid. lib/lpj_output.py:_read_rows takes the same
fast path and builds its cube by reshape rather than scatter; on the run's real
tables it is 5.7-11.5x faster and returns a cube identical element for element.

WHERE THE TIME GOES NOW. cProfile, 34.3 s: numpy's C tokenizer
_load_from_filelike is 25.8 s of it, 75 per cent, reading about 7 GB of decimal
text at 245 MB/s. Everything else is small: hashing 1.4 s, np.unique in years()
1.1 s, the whole merge verification 0.8 s, the coordinate checks 0.6 s, argsort
0.4 s. read_table and _read_rows no longer appear as costs of their own.

PARALLELISM, MEASURED AND DECLINED. A ProcessPoolExecutor over six merged
outputs (1.31 GB): serial 5.34 s, pool returning a scalar 1.31 s (4.1x), pool
returning the parsed table 1.46 s (3.7x, 0.96 GB moved). Transport is cheap, so
Amdahl on a 75-per-cent-parallel gate puts a pool at roughly 19 s against 41.8.
That 2.2x is real and is not worth its price: it turns a gate every coupled
consumer calls into a nineteen-process job on a host where CPU use is
lock-mediated, it raises the memory peak, and at 41.8 s the gate is a step in a
script rather than a wait anyone routes around. The remaining time is the shape
of the data -- seven gigabytes of decimal text -- and not a defect in the gate.
Reopen this only if the run size grows enough that 41.8 s becomes a wait again;
the numbers above are what the decision would be re-taken against.
