title: The ANUT-8 multiplier is one scalar over four elements whose true values differ by an order of magnitude
description:
biosphere/scripts/abiotic_nutrient_ledger.py:standing_pool_g_per_m2 reads one scalar, `belowground_and_exchangeable_multiplier`, and applies it to K, Ca, Mg and S alike. Now that pedology emits an exchange complex the four are separately computable and they are not close.

The scalar has to cover the worst element, so it is the maximum over the four and every other element is screened far more strictly than any mechanism supports. Sulfur is the largest gap and it is a mechanism gap rather than a measurement one: SULFATE IS AN ANION and the cation exchange complex holds none of it, so sulfur's entire below-ground term is roots. Its true multiplier is 1 + the root-to-shoot ratio; the scalar it currently gets is set by whichever cation binds.

biosphere/config/abiotic_nutrients.yaml now carries `belowground_and_exchangeable_by_element` beside the scalar with the per-element bound, and pedology/scripts/build_soil.py refuses when any entry falls below what the emitted field implies, so the map is inside a loop rather than frozen. What is missing is the read.

Do: have abiotic_nutrient_ledger.py:standing_pool_g_per_m2 take the per-element entry where one exists and keep the scalar as the fallback, and carry the per-element value into the report's adequacy block so the critical runoff per element is computed on its own bound. The scalar stays declared and stays conservative until it does.

biosphere/scripts/ was another session's directory when this was found, which is why the config half is done and the read half is not.

Source: biosphere/config/abiotic_nutrients.yaml adequacy block, pedology/analysis/soil_report.json exchange_complex.

title: Source allophane content against a LEACHING measure, which is the axis that controls it
description:
REPLACES world-9loh's bar, which asked for the wrong axis. Parfitt (2009), `10.1180/claymin.2009.044.1.135`, now read, states on the controls of allophane formation in tephra and Andisols that 'the effect of time is subordinate to these factors' -- the factors being silicic-acid activity in the soil solution, Al availability, the opportunity for co-precipitation, leaching regime, soil organic matter and pH. So allophane content against a DEVELOPMENT measure is content against the weakest control, and a transfer built on it would carry the residual variance of all the others.

The axis that does control it is one this pipeline has. Parfitt reports the New Zealand aeolian case in the exact form the andisol model already runs on: halloysite and no allophane at 1000 mm of rainfall, only allophane at 1600 mm, the switch turning on soil-solution silicon crossing about 10 mg/l. pedogenesis.yaml's andisol block already gates andic development on a precipitation threshold. What is missing is the CONTENT above the threshold, not the threshold.

THE BAR: allophane content over allophanic soils against a leaching measure -- rainfall, a water balance, or soil-solution silicon activity. Not a development measure, and not a review's extremes.

TWO CANDIDATES, both sought on 2026-08-30 and neither reachable from this host (publisher, Google Scholar and Sci-Hub all 403):
  Parfitt, Russell, Orbell (1983). Weathering sequence of soils from volcanic ash involving allophane and halloysite, New Zealand. Geoderma 29(1), 41-57. `10.1016/0016-7061(83)90029-0`
  Singleton, March, Otsuka, Parfitt (1989). Allophane and halloysite content and soil solution silicon in soils from rhyolitic volcanic material, New Zealand. Aust. J. Soil Res. 27(1), 67-77. `10.1071/SR9890067`
Both are rows in references/INDEX.md as sought and not reached. Either would supply a distribution; neither supplies a transfer, because soil-solution silicon is not a quantity this pipeline emits.

WHAT IS NO LONGER MISSING: Parfitt (2009) supplies the distribution-shaped statements Parfitt (1990) Table 3's named maxima could not -- 2 to 22 per cent allophane across Icelandic field soils at 11 to 42 per cent C (Sigfusson et al. 2008), and under 6 per cent in Atlantic volcanic island mineral horizons. Both are unconditional ranges over real populations, so the factor of several that substituting maxima would have put into a protection coefficient is off the table. They still cannot place a CELL, which is why this row is open.

THE SECOND GATE STANDS AND THIS ROW DOES NOT TOUCH IT: even with all four proxies the mineral-aware arm cannot be written, because no read source supplies a parameterised transfer from a proxy to a protection coefficient. Do not read closing this as unblocking the arm.

Source: pedology/notes/mineral-reactivity-supply.md section 2.

title: Wire the emitted cation exchange capacity into the mineral-aware arm's polyvalent-cation proxy
description:
pedology/notes/mineral-reactivity-supply.md section 4's verdict has moved from not derivable to derivable. Both halves of the polyvalent cation saturation proxy now exist:

  the CAPACITY is emitted -- pedogenesis.yaml's `exchange` block and build_soil.py:exchange_properties derive cation exchange capacity from the clay and organic-matter fractions on the two slopes of Sahrawat (1983), `10.1080/00103628309367409`, and the soil map carries it as the `cec` column;
  the SHARE is measured against pH, which this component emits -- Solly et al. (2020), `10.3389/ffgc.2020.00098`, put exchangeable calcium on 59 to 83 per cent of effective CEC at pH at or above 5.5 and exchangeable aluminium on 21 to 44 per cent below pH 5, both polyvalent, with iron under 1 per cent.

biosphere/config/mineral_reactivity.yaml still carries `undeclared` for the proxy and mineral_reactivity_gate.py still refuses on it.

Do: emit polyvalent cation saturation in cmol(+)/kg from the emitted capacity and the pH-indexed share, declare it in the contract's carried_state, and take the sentinel out.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, and the row should not be read as doing it: the mineral-aware arm stays refused whatever this closes. mineral-reactivity-supply.md's last section records the second gate -- Cotrufo et al. (2013) and Lehmann and Kleber (2015) name the associating surfaces and neither supplies a parameterised transfer from any proxy to a protection coefficient. The proxies are the first of two gates and the second is on the consuming model's side. Three of the four proxies also stay undeclared.

Carries the LEVEL exposure of world-n4i0: the capacity's absolute magnitude rests on one region's fit.

Source: pedology/notes/mineral-reactivity-supply.md section 4.

title: Register check_reference_index.py in the fast gate
description:
scripts/check_reference_index.py exists and passes. It reads references/INDEX.md's first column and fails on a backticked filename that is not on disk, which is a static read over a tracked file and therefore the fast gate's own criterion (CLAUDE.md rule 8). It is not yet wired into scripts/smoke_test.py, so nothing runs it.

It was written as its own script rather than as a smoke_test function because another agent held scripts/smoke_test.py at the time.

Do: add the import and one row to the checks list in scripts/smoke_test.py:main(), beside the other registry checks --

    ("every filename references/INDEX.md asserts is on disk",
     lambda: check_reference_index()),

The function already returns list[str] in smoke_test's own vocabulary and prints its own skip line when the untracked library is absent from the checkout, so no adaptation is needed. Alternatively fold the body into smoke_test.py and delete the standalone script; the standalone form is only worth keeping if a reader wants to run this one check on its own.

Evidence and what it caught: notes/audits/worktree-stranded-payload.md.

title: Four external source trees in references/ are tracked only by omission from an enumerated ignore list
description:
scripts/link_worktree.py cannot give references/ a directory symlink because the directory holds tracked content beside untracked payloads, and that is what loses a pdf fetched inside a worktree. Part of the reason references/ is mixed is an inconsistency that stands on its own.

.gitignore carries an ENUMERATED policy for external model source consulted as reference, with its rule stated in the file: exclude the bulk, keep the record, because what such a tree grounds is written into references/INDEX.md and that is what makes the extraction reproducible. It names twenty-odd trees one at a time -- climber-x, big-mitgcm, socrates, speedy, marbl, exort, exocam, isca, muffingen, climaland, arcsdm, caaba-mecca, cama-flood, esmf, fates, landlab, pysdm, aus_groundwater, ecospeclib, poseidon_surface_albedo, splib07.

Four siblings of exactly that class are tracked because no row was ever added for them:

  references/cloudmicrophysics/    263 files  2.6M
  references/pyrcel/               135 files  2.8M
  references/ESurf ..._files/       84 files  3.2M   saved webpage assets
  references/wrf-lightning/          2 files   16K

About 8.6 MB of external source in this project's history that the stated rule says does not belong there. The tell that it is an oversight rather than a decision is .gitignore's own line references/pyrcel/pyrcel/data: a SUBdirectory of pyrcel is ignored while the tree containing it is not, so pyrcel was being treated under the rule and the top-level row was simply missed.

Nothing in the tree reads any of them. cloudmicrophysics is named once in notes/audits/ocean-tier-implicit-earth.md as prose; the pyrcel matches are self-matches inside its own tree; wrf-lightning has no consumer.

WHAT STAYS TRACKED, by the same rule and for the opposite reason: INDEX.md, penndorf-1/2/3.png and hartmannmoosdorf2012-glim-lithological-map.txt are EXTRACTIONS from sources not otherwise held. They are the record the rule exists to keep, not the bulk it exists to exclude, and the Penndorf figures are the only copy of that evidence in the project.
acceptance_criteria: The four trees are ignored and untracked, the ignore rows sit with their twenty siblings and carry the same stated reason, and the four extraction artifacts remain tracked. references/INDEX.md still records what each untracked tree grounds.
notes: Found 2026-08-30 while establishing why a pdf fetched inside a worktree never reaches the main checkout. Do this with no agent holding a worktree: an untrack rewrites index state under every live checkout.
close_reason: The four trees carry ignore rows beside the twenty their rule already named and are out of the index: cloudmicrophysics, pyrcel, wrf-lightning and the saved ESurf webpage assets, 484 files and about 8.6 MB. The subsumed references/pyrcel/pyrcel/data line is gone. What stays tracked is the record rather than the bulk: INDEX.md, the three Penndorf figures and the Hartmann-Moosdorf lithological table, all extractions from sources not otherwise held. Working-tree files are untouched.

title: The CEC relation's LEVEL rests on one region's fit and is a live exposure
description:
pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml's `exchange` block emits a cation exchange capacity field from clay and organic matter with the two slopes of Sahrawat (1983), `10.1080/00103628309367409`: 38 cmol(+)/kg of clay and 300 cmol(+)/kg of organic matter, the paper's 7.98 intercept dropped as a regional artifact.

The SHAPE is checked and holds: at Sahrawat's own mean composition the pair puts the organic share of CEC at 37.9 per cent, inside the 35 to 50 per cent Solly et al. (2020), `10.3389/ffgc.2020.00098`, measured by partial regression over 1204 Swiss forest profiles. Two continents, two methods, and the check could have failed.

The LEVEL is not checked. It is one region's multiple regression, n = 40 surface soils, R2 = 0.60, and the dropped intercept is 25 per cent of that fit's own mean CEC. Under this project's vocabulary that is an exposure and not a source: the emitted field's absolute magnitude has an inspectable derivation only as far as forty Philippine rice soils carry it.

Two sources close it and neither is reachable from this host, both behind the same Wiley/ACSESS 403:
  Helling, Chesters, Corey (1964). Contribution of Organic Matter and Clay to Soil Cation-Exchange Capacity as Affected by the pH of the Saturating Solution. SSSAJ 28(4), 517-520. `10.2136/sssaj1964.03615995002800040020x`
  Manrique, Jones, Dyke (1991). Predicting Cation-Exchange Capacity from Soil Physical and Chemical Properties. SSSAJ 55(3), 787-794. `10.2136/sssaj1991.03615995005500030026x`

Helling is the one that matters most, because it separates the clay and organic-matter contributions AS A FUNCTION OF pH and is therefore the only candidate whose independent variables are the three columns build_soil.py already emits. Manrique is what supplies a bracket on the LEVEL across soil orders, which no single-region fit can.

Do: acquire either, read it, and replace the level. Source: pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml exchange block, pedology/notes/mineral-reactivity-supply.md section 4.

title: references/INDEX.md rows claim held PDFs that are not on disk
description:
`references/INDEX.md`'s header says the read/held distinction IS the point of the file: a number taken from a citation rather than from the paper is failure-modes class 9, and it has cost this project twice. A row naming a PDF that is not in `references/` breaks that guarantee silently -- the row still reads as evidence, and every decision resting on it is OPAQUE by this project's vocabulary, its derivation existing somewhere a reader cannot reach.

FOUND BY GOING TO READ ONE. world-znr7 needed nolet2014-surface-moisture-beach-sand-reflectance.pdf, whose row is marked read with section-level detail. The file was not there, in the worktree or in the main checkout. It was refetched (PLoS ONE, open access, one paperfetch call) and every claim in the row checked out against the PDF, so the row was right and only the payload was gone.

A sweep of the same shape found 13 more rows whose first cell names a `.pdf` that is absent:

  mcgroddy2004-forest-cnp-stoichiometry.pdf            10.1890/03-0351
  yuan2011-fine-root-nitrogen-phosphorus.pdf           10.1038/ncomms1346
  yang2013-global-soil-phosphorus-distribution.pdf     10.5194/bg-10-2525-2013
  yang2011-hedley-phosphorus-pedogenesis.pdf           10.5194/bg-8-2907-2011
  reich2004-leaf-nitrogen-phosphorus-latitude.pdf      10.1073/pnas.0403588101
  parton2010-forcent.pdf                               10.1029/2009JG001193
  goll2012-nutrient-limitation-carbon-uptake.pdf       10.5194/bg-9-3547-2012
  pilegaard_2013_processes-regulating-nitric-oxide-emissions-from-soils.pdf  10.1098/rstb.2013.0126
  jackson_1996_a-global-analysis-of-root-distributions-for-terrestrial-biomes.pdf  10.1007/BF00333714
  papastefanou_2024_simulated-sensitivity-of-the-amazon-rainforest-to-extreme-drought.pdf  10.1088/1748-9326/ad8f48
  mcmahon_1973_size-and-shape-in-biology.pdf           10.1126/science.179.4079.1201
  king_2005_linking-tree-form-allocation-and-growth-with-an-allometrically-explici.pdf  10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2004.11.017
  blackadar1962-the-vertical-distribution-of-wind-and-turbulent-exchange.pdf  10.1029/JZ067i008p03095

Eleven of the thirteen are biosphere phosphorus, allometry and root-distribution sources, so the exposure is concentrated in the component whose numbers are least checkable elsewhere.

THE CHECK IS ARMED. `scripts/check_consistency.py:check_held_references_are_on_disk` reads every table row whose first cell is a single backticked `.pdf` and fails on any whose file is absent. It sits in check_consistency and not smoke_test because `references/` is untracked payload, which is that gate's own line. A source sought and not reached is written as a bullet without a filename and is deliberately NOT checked: that shape is the honest record of a paper this host cannot get, and the check must not push anyone toward inventing a filename for one.

Do: refetch what is fetchable. Where a paper cannot be reached, the row moves to the bullet form the file already uses for Lobell (2002) -- title, DOI, what it would settle, and that supplying the file directly is the route -- and any claim in the tree that reads it secondhand is downgraded to held, or to the citation it actually rests on.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESOLVED IN THE TREE, and the finding is different from the row's first framing. Nothing was lost: every one of the fourteen was a filename that had drifted from its row, not a paper nobody has.

references/INDEX.md's convention is <firstauthor><year><suffix>-<slug>.pdf. Eleven of the fourteen sat on disk under an earlier short form -- mcgroddy2004.pdf, blackadar1962.pdf, mcmahon1973.pdf, jackson1996.pdf, pilegaard2013.pdf and the rest -- so the rows were renamed to the convention and the files were not. nolet2014 was the exception and was genuinely absent; it refetched from PLoS in one call.

ONE OF THEM WAS THE WRONG PAPER, and only opening it said so. yang2013.pdf held 'Factores que Afectan el Rendimiento Academico en la Educacion Primaria', a Spanish-language education review, under a row for Yang, Post, Thornton and Jain (2013) on global soil phosphorus. That is exactly the failure the file's own header warns about: a wrong paper resolves, and nothing about the result says so. The correct Biogeosciences 10, 2525-2537 paper is now in place, verified by its own first page.

VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Every file whose row had drifted was opened and matched against its row's title before being accepted -- mcmahon_1973 needed the full extract rather than page 1, whose two-column scan carries a neighbouring article's references and reads as a different paper.

All 375 rows that name a PDF now resolve and check_held_references_are_on_disk passes. What the check buys going forward is that a rename without its file, and a row whose file was never fetched, both fail loudly instead of surfacing when someone goes to read one.

Left alone deliberately: eight paperfetch-named files under references/ that no row names (fan_2007, iverson_2012, jiang_2010, pacala_1993, price_1992, ugelvig_2016, wong_2013, zhao_2022). They are another session's, references/ is untracked payload with no history to fall back on, and garbage-collecting it is not this row.

title: Seventeen documents cite runs no record can identify and do not say so
description:
Forty run ids this tree cites are in no record at all: not in
exoplasim/runs/INDEX.json, not an INDEX_ENTRY.json stub, not an
INDEX_AT_DELETION.json batch, not a RECONSTRUCTED.json. The finding and the
mechanism that closed the leak are in notes/audits/run-identity.md; the
enumeration is archive/runs/RECORDLESS.json and regenerates with
`python exoplasim/scripts/index_runs.py --recordless`.

Eighteen documents cite at least one of them. notes/audits/resolution-ladder.md
is done: it now carries a table splitting its conclusions by whether they can be
re-read, and each affected section states the consequence, because a row nothing
can check reads exactly like a row that has been checked. The other seventeen do
not, and this is the sweep for them (counts measured 2026-08-30):

  10  exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md
   6  exoplasim/notes/energy-diagnostic-restart-defect.md
   6  exoplasim/notes/resolution-tuned-parameters.md
   5  exoplasim/notes/cloud-water-reference.md
   4  exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md
   4  exoplasim/notes/restart-resolution-precision-converter.md
   3  notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md
   2  exoplasim/notes/shtns-viability.md
   2  exoplasim/notes/soil-albedo-moisture.md
   2  notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md
   2  notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
   1  exoplasim/notes/filter-spectral-price.md
   1  exoplasim/notes/the-zeroing-is-an-init-flag.md
   1  hydrography/notes/retain-fraction.md
   1  notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md
   1  notes/audits/ecological-stream-restart-continuity.md
   1  notes/external-model-survey.md

THE DECISION PROCEDURE PER CITATION, and it is not "add a warning". Ask what the
document's claim rests on, then take one of three dispositions:

  RE-DERIVABLE   a surviving analysis artifact carries the measurement. Say
                 which artifact, and say that the run's build and executable sha
                 are not recoverable, so the claim cannot be attributed to a
                 source state or paired with a controlled arm.
  RECONSTRUCTIBLE  enough survives across several artifacts to piece the
                 identity back together. Write a RECONSTRUCTED.json under
                 archive/runs/ citing the artifact behind every field and
                 listing what is unrecoverable, as the three existing ones do.
                 This is worth doing where a claim is load-bearing: it is how
                 the two T42 ladder arms were found to differ in NFILTEREXP,
                 which falsified the audit that cited them.
  NEITHER        no artifact carries the quantity. The claim rests on a number
                 the document is the sole copy of. Say so, and file what would
                 replace it.

Rewrite in place; do not mark. A reader grepping for a number must land on the
number with its standing beside it.

title: Re-measure the T42 endpoint of the resolution comparison, which no artifact carries
description:
notes/audits/resolution-ladder.md's timestep-against-resolution table has three
rows and one of them cannot be checked. run_4fe5e6050df5 is T42 at dt 22.5, and
its 294.567 K appears in that note and nowhere else: the run is recordless

run_aaa95662e21a, keep convergence reports and are re-readable -- and the

title: T85 is the last rung on the route with no endurance row, and dt 45 now rests on it alone
description:
exoplasim/notes/route-step-criteria.md, section C.

C-ROUTE-1 adopts a step for a rung's commissioning block only where the refusal
cell is clean on the CURRENT model source AND lib/rungs.py:COMMISSIONING_EVIDENCE
carries an endured row for that exact pair. The route runs dt 45 at every rung.

T21 dt 45   endured, converged, 108 orbits, run_0d41aa82c287
T42 dt 45   endured, converged, 144 orbits, run_88ed6f9d34ae
T85 dt 45   endurance row EMPTY

So the route's most expensive block is the only one still running at a step no
commissioning-length run has held. A refusal-clean cell is necessary and never
sufficient, because T42 at dt 45 was refusal-clean at every column any probe
measured and blew up in its forty-seventh orbit on an earlier source.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one T85 commissioning-length arm at dt 45. Nothing cheaper
substitutes, and it is also the last endurance row the route needs.

BLOCKED ON THREE ABSENT INPUTS, not on the arm's price.

1. The T85 staged surface family does not exist: no exoplasim/inputs/t85, no run
   directory carrying an N128_surf_*.sra. The T85 probe cells were staged from
   run_2a50670d8f2b, which is in archive/runs/RECORDLESS.json. That is world-j1po.
2. The T85 restart template does not exist: only its provenance survives, and it
   records the template as cut from precarve-craton-10m, the pre-carve build.
   convert_restart.py needs a target template. Also world-j1po.
3. T85's refusal cell at dt 45 names executable 6722f7280e09, which is not what
   exoplasim/binary_manifest.json registers for most_plasim_t85_l10_p8.x now, so
   C-ROUTE-1 part 1 is unmet. Re-taking it needs (1).

The T42 state to convert from does exist: run_88ed6f9d34ae.

COST, and it is a bracket rather than a number because a T85 orbit has never been
timed on this host. lib/run_lengths.commissioning_bracket(15) gives a converted
commissioning span of 53 to 92 orbits. The T85-to-T42 orbit ratio is between 4,
the gridpoint count, and 8, what the Legendre transform scales by, against T42's
measured 94 s an orbit on eight pinned threads at loads of 11 to 28: so 6.3 to
12.5 minutes an orbit, and 5.6 to 19.2 hours of held host lock at p8. A single
arm is not a pair and may take sixteen threads, which is unmeasured too.

WHAT CLOSES THE BRACKET, once (1) exists: stability_probe.py at T85 and dt 45
over 600 and 1200 steps, differenced per C-ROUTE-5, at p8 and at p16. Minutes,
and it also re-takes the refusal cell (3). Until that number exists the arm is
priced across a factor of three and C-ROUTE-4 cannot say what raising C is worth.

THE WET-SOIL MERGE DOES NOT SPOIL THIS ROW. An endurance row establishes a new
fact about a (rung, step) pair rather than comparing to an old one, so it wants
the current source and gets it.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-31. VERDICT: BLOCKED, and not on the arm's price. This row says "BLOCKED ON NOTHING: the T85 surface family exists, its refusal cell was measured on the grid built for it, and the T42 state to convert from is run_88ed6f9d34ae". Three of those four clauses are now false. exoplasim/notes/route-step-criteria.md section C carries the evidence.

WHAT IS ABSENT

1. The T85 staged surface family. There is no exoplasim/inputs/t85 and no run directory carrying an N128_surf_*.sra. The T85 cells in exoplasim/analysis/stability_probe.json were staged from run_2a50670d8f2b, which is in archive/runs/RECORDLESS.json: no record, no payload, no build. source/canonical-10m-carve2/exoplasim-T85 exists, so the family can be built; nothing has. It must also carry codes 1743, 1751 and 1761, because config/planet.yaml declares surface.soil_albedo_moisture.three_point and landini REFUSES at NWETSOIL 2 without them. That is world-j1po, filed and set blocking this row.

2. The T85 restart template. exoplasim/inputs/templates holds T85_l10_p16_omp.rest.provenance.json and no .rest beside it, and that provenance records the template as cut from precarve-craton-10m -- the pre-carve build. convert_restart.py needs a target template, so the hop this row is about has no target. Also world-j1po.

3. The refusal cell on the current source. Every T85 probe cell names executable 6722f7280e09, and exoplasim/binary_manifest.json registers eac3a529... for most_plasim_t85_l10_p8.x now. C-ROUTE-1 part 1 asks for the cell in the grid re-taken on the current model source, so it has to be re-taken, and it cannot be until (1).

4. The T42 state to convert from does exist: run_88ed6f9d34ae. lib/rungs.py:evidence_source_currency now reads it as `superseded`, which under C-ROUTE-6 supports keeping dt 45 and does not condemn it.

THE PRICE, honestly. lib/run_lengths.commissioning_bracket(15) puts a converted commissioning span at 53 to 92 orbits, not the 35 to 40 this row's cost line assumed. A T85 orbit has never been timed on this host: the ratio to a T42 orbit is between 4 (the gridpoint count) and 8 (what the Legendre transform scales by), so 6.3 to 12.5 minutes an orbit against T42's measured 94 s on eight pinned threads. That is 5.6 to 19.2 HOURS of held host lock at p8, not three to four. A single arm is not a pair, so it may take all sixteen threads, and that speedup is unmeasured too.

WHAT CLOSES THE BRACKET, and it costs minutes once (1) exists. C-ROUTE-5's cost half differences two wall times on one bed: stability_probe.py at T85 and dt 45 over 600 and 1200 steps, differenced, gives seconds per step, and 5850 steps is one orbit at this step. The same two passes at p8 and p16 settle the thread question with it. Until that number exists the arm is priced across a factor of three and C-ROUTE-4 cannot say what raising C is worth in wall clock.

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: the model change does NOT spoil this row, and the delegating brief was right about why. An endurance row establishes a new fact about a (rung, step) pair rather than comparing to an old one, so it wants the CURRENT source and gets it. The block is entirely the three absent inputs.

ORDER OF PURCHASE: world-j1po (the staging and the template), then the T85 refusal cell and the two differenced timing passes, then the arm at a price that is by then a number.

title: A converted T42 arm settles with 22.5 per cent more sea ice than a cold one, and the mechanism is not established
description:
notes/audits/resolution-ladder.md, measured 2026-08-30 on run_88ed6f9d34ae (T42
dt 45 cold, 144 orbits, converged) against run_8d0ae7e2d02c (the same rung and
step converted from run_0d41aa82c287, 89 orbits, converged). Both arms read one
arm config, so they differ in their initial state and in nothing else.

Five of six metrics agree. Sea ice fraction does not: 0.0767 against 0.0626,
+0.0141 on a bound of 0.0018, sixteen sigma. It is polar and in both hemispheres
-- +0.076 in fraction north of 60 degrees, +0.042 south of -60, +0.037 and +0.019
in the mid-latitude bands, identically zero equatorward of 40 -- and 292 of 8192
cells differ by more than 0.05. Both ice series are stationary over their tails.
Neither arm shows any radiative or thermal consequence of it.

WHAT THE 2026-08-31 RE-READ ADDED, with no run cut. The converted arm settles on
its DONOR RUNG's ice fraction: the T21 donor settles at 0.07586 with an orbit
scatter of 0.00203, the converted arm at 0.07665, the cold arm at 0.06257. B is
its donor's value to 0.00080, under half the bound; B - A is eighteen times that.
And it is not a frozen field: the remap put 0.08933 on the target grid and the
arm relaxed 0.0127 out of it over about fifteen orbits before stopping. Two
settled ice states at one rung explain the pair equally well, so this does not
settle it -- but that reading leaves the coincidence unexplained and the donor's
imprint does not.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is the whole of this row: whether the offset is
the DONOR'S IMPRINT or a second margin the target rung reaches on its own; and
whether it shrinks as the jump shrinks, which is what the ladder's next hop,
T42 to T85, needs to know.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the only row on which a converted state and a cold state
differ, and the escalation route exists to avoid paying for a cold start at every
rung. An ice offset that is the donor's imprint accumulates up the ladder; one
the target rung would reach anyway does not.

THE MODEL CHANGE DOES NOT BLOCK IT. The efcbfba2d wet-soil diff is entirely
gated on nwetsoil == 2, so at NWETSOIL 1 the new executable is the old model;
what differs is that config/planet.yaml now declares
surface.soil_albedo_moisture.three_point. That configuration change is worth at
most 0.105 W/m2 of global-mean absorbed shortwave, 0.072 K, and 0.00050 to
0.00064 in sea ice fraction -- a quarter to a third of this comparison's bound.
The instrument does not resolve it.

THE EXPERIMENT, and it is not the one this row first named. There is no second
donor at (T21, dt 45) whose settled ice differs from run_0d41aa82c287's by more
than the bound: a second cold T21 arm settles in the same place, and
convert_restart refuses a conversion across a change of step. The lever is the
INITIAL ice, and every per-orbit restart of the donor survives
(MOST_REST.00000 to MOST_REST.00107), so it can be taken anywhere between 0.0022
and 0.080. Three T42 arms at dt 45 on the current configuration, FORTY orbits
each:
  A'  cold, initial ice ~0
  B'  converted from run_0d41aa82c287's final restart, initial remapped ice ~0.089
  C'  converted from run_0d41aa82c287/MOST_REST.00005, whose orbit-mean ice is 0.0409

THRESHOLD, declared before the arms: with L the linear interpolation of f_A' and
f_B' at C's initial remapped ice, GRADED (the imprint accumulates) if
|f_C' - L| <= 0.0018; BIMODAL (two attractors, no accumulation) if f_C' is within
0.0018 of f_A' or f_B' AND |f_C' - L| > 0.0054; NEITHER otherwise, reported as
neither.

FORTY ORBITS IS ENOUGH, and the arms are what shows it: over orbits 20-40 both
ice series carry slopes of 4.7e-5 and 3.6e-5 an orbit against a 0.001 criterion,
and B - A read there is +0.01444 against +0.01408 over the tails.
compare_equilibria.py already reads a twenty-orbit window. The 144 and 89 orbits
were bought for the TEMPERATURE's memory time, which this row does not need.

COST: two p8 arms pinned one per die under one lock, then the third, at 94 s an
orbit measured at loads of 11 to 28. About 2.1 hours of held host lock plus
staging, and it settles the row with no bias to report because all three arms sit
on one configuration.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-31. VERDICT: not blocked by the wet-soil merge, and the row's own question moved without a run being cut. notes/audits/resolution-ladder.md carries all of it.

1. THE MODEL CHANGE DOES NOT SPOIL THE COMPARISON, and this is measured rather than argued. The efcbfba2d diff to landmod.f90, landcolumn.f90 and surfmod.f90 is entirely inside `nwetsoil == 2` branches, a new staged-field read and a new pure function; the one ungated edit is `nwetsoil == 1` widened to `nwetsoil >= 1`, which is the same test at 1. At NWETSOIL 1 the new executable IS the old model. What differs is the configuration: config/planet.yaml now declares surface.soil_albedo_moisture.three_point, so a run today sets NWETSOIL 2 where the arms ran 1.

That configuration change has a size. notes/audits/nonlinear-spatial-reductions.md section 7 measures the two-point staging peaking at -0.147 W/m2 of global-mean absorbed shortwave and the three-point form at -0.042, both signed the same way, so the change is at most 0.105 W/m2. Through lib/sensitivity.py at the accepted baseline's planetary albedo that is 0.072 K. The settled flux arms give d(sea ice)/dT as -0.00691 to -0.00892 per K across the three builds, so the merge is worth 0.00050 to 0.00064 in sea ice fraction: a quarter to a third of this comparison's 0.0018 bound, and 3.5 to 4.5 per cent of the 0.0141 effect. THE INSTRUMENT DOES NOT RESOLVE THE MODEL CHANGE.

The residual caveat is spatial and is stated as an argument, not a measurement: the bound is on the global-mean channel and the offset is polar, and the reason a land albedo change is not concentrated there is that high-latitude land carries the modelled snow cover for most of the orbit, which masks the soil albedo the merge changed. Re-cutting all three arms on one configuration is what removes it, and that is the recommended purchase below.

2. THE CONVERTED ARM SETTLES ON ITS DONOR RUNG'S ICE FRACTION. Read from the three convergence reports, means over each run's last twenty orbits: the T21 donor run_0d41aa82c287 settles at 0.07586 with an orbit scatter of 0.00203; the converted T42 arm run_8d0ae7e2d02c settles at 0.07665; the cold T42 arm run_88ed6f9d34ae at 0.06257. B is its DONOR's value to 0.00080, under half the bound, while B - A is 0.01408, eighteen times that. And it is not a frozen field: the remap put 0.08933 on the target grid and the arm relaxed 0.0127 out of it over about fifteen orbits before stopping. This does not settle the row -- two settled ice states at one rung explain the pair equally well -- but under a second margin the target reaches on its own, landing on the donor rung's value at a fifth of the resolving bound is an unexplained coincidence.

3. THE ARM IS FORTY ORBITS, NOT NINETY. Over orbits 20-40 both arms' ice slopes are 4.7e-5 and 3.6e-5 in fraction an orbit, inside the run's own 0.001 stationarity criterion by twenty times, and the window means sit 0.00046 and 0.00010 from the converged tails. B - A read over 20-40 is +0.01444 against +0.01408 over the tails, a gap a fifth of the bound. compare_equilibria.py already reads a twenty-orbit window, so a forty-orbit arm reproduces this comparison at its declared instrument. The 144 and 89 orbits were bought for the TEMPERATURE's memory time.

4. THE ROW'S EXPERIMENT WAS UNDER-SPECIFIED AND NOW HAS A DESIGN. There is no second donor at (T21, dt 45) on this configuration whose settled ice differs from run_0d41aa82c287's by more than the 0.0018 bound: a second cold T21 arm settles in the same place, and convert_restart refuses a conversion across a change of step, which rules out run_14906cb7b914 at dt 30. What IS available for free is that every per-orbit restart of the donor survives, MOST_REST.00000 through MOST_REST.00107, so the donor's ice can be taken anywhere between 0.0022 and 0.080. The lever is the INITIAL ice, and the cold arm is already the zero-ice end of it.

THE RUN, and its threshold declared before it: three T42 arms at dt 45 on canonical-10m-carve2 and the current configuration, forty orbits each.
  A': cold, initial ice ~0.
  B': converted at constant dt from run_0d41aa82c287's final restart, initial remapped ice ~0.089.
  C': converted at constant dt from run_0d41aa82c287/MOST_REST.00005, whose orbit-mean ice is 0.0409, so an initial remapped ice near the middle.
Measure f_init for each from the converted restart's xicec. With L = f_A' + (f_B' - f_A') * (f_init(C') - f_init(A')) / (f_init(B') - f_init(A')):
  GRADED, the imprint accumulates up the ladder, if |f_C' - L| <= 0.0018;
  BIMODAL, two attractors and no accumulation, if f_C' is within 0.0018 of f_A' or of f_B' AND |f_C' - L| > 0.0054;
  NEITHER otherwise, and reported as neither.
The confound is stated: an unsettled donor differs in more than its ice, so C' is a different initial STATE and not only a different initial ice. The conclusion survives it, because a settled ice that depends on the initial state carries an imprint whatever the channel.

COST: two p8 arms pinned one per die under one lock, then the third, at 94 s an orbit measured at loads of 11 to 28. About 2.1 hours of held host lock plus staging, and it settles the row outright with no bias to report because all three arms are on one configuration. This is CHEAPER than the third arm the row asked for, which was 89 orbits and left the model-change bias in the answer.

NOT TAKEN: above the twenty-minute latitude this session was given. The row stays open on that purchase.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-31. The three-arm run is AUTHORISED, launched and QUEUED behind another agent's host lock. Two pre-flight blockers were found and settled before anything was spent; both are durable facts and are in exoplasim/notes/route-step-criteria.md.

WHAT IS RUNNING. One lock_and_run holds the whole thing: arm A' cold on CCD0, then the T42 restart template cut from A's first orbit, then the two conversions, then B' on CCD1, then C' on CCD0 when A' finishes. Two p8 arms pinned one per die at any moment, never more. 40 orbits each.

  A'  cold
  B'  converted at constant dt from run_0d41aa82c287's final restart
  C'  converted at constant dt from run_0d41aa82c287/MOST_REST.00005

PRE-FLIGHT BLOCKER 1, and it changes what a cold arm means above T21. config/planet.yaml sets model.soil_water_source: pedology, which makes staged code 229 a refusal in run_exoplasim.py. Code 229 exists at T21 and nowhere else: build_surface_soil_water.py takes its grid and land mask from a climatology, has no --grid, and the only climatology on the active build is T21's -- which config/pipeline.yaml makes an edge rather than an oversight, since a staged surface field is an input to the run whose output would otherwise build it. A cold arm reads dwmax from the .sra; a converted arm FREEZES it in the restart. So above T21 the converted arm is the only one that can start at all, and the cold arm is not a fallback the route can take. The T85 endurance arm (world-3y2v) is a converted arm for this reason as well as for its price.

The arms therefore run at soil_water_source: uniform, declared. That is not a term switched off to improve an agreement -- there is no field to read at this rung, and the alternative is not running. It has a second effect that is worth having: uniform is what the WORLD-YYX8 pair ran, so these three arms differ from that pair in NWETSOIL 1 -> 2 and in nothing else, which is exactly the bias already bounded at 0.0005 to 0.0006 in ice fraction. The internal control is untouched: all three arms are on one configuration.

The arm config differs from config/planet.yaml in two things and nothing else, verified by diff: the grid triple (resolution T42, latitudes 64, longitudes 128, which the config itself declares operational and transitive) and soil_water_source: uniform. The manifest embeds the whole config, so provenance is self-contained.

PRE-FLIGHT BLOCKER 2. exoplasim/inputs/templates/T42_l10_p8.rest was cut against a staged surface family that has since gained codes 1743, 1751 and 1761, and conversion_surface_reason refuses it: a converted state's static surface records are the template's, so a superseded template hands the run a surface it did not stage. The gate working. It imposes an ORDER that holds at every rung: a template can only be cut from a run of the target rung on the current staging, so the first arm at a new rung is the one every converted arm waits on. That is why A' runs first and B'/C' wait for its first orbit.

THE ASSESSMENT IS WRITTEN AND ITS THRESHOLDS ARE HARD-CODED before any arm reported: scratchpad/assess_arms.py. It refuses to give a verdict at all if any arm's ice slope over its 20-orbit window is at or above 0.001 in fraction an orbit, which is the declared "say so and stop" branch.

HOST STATE AT LAUNCH: load 16.8, and the lock is held by world-24xd, a 1600-cycle LPJ spin-up claimed at 07:07:54 MDT. The host was not free. lock_and_run is queued behind it, which is the designed behaviour; the arms start when it releases.

title: tuned-values.md's fire-floor row is stale and mis-classifies the constant
description:
notes/audits/tuned-values.md carries the GlobFIRM burn-probability floor in its table (the vegdynam.cpp:1435 row) and in the disposition paragraph below it. Two things are now wrong with it.

The floor no longer exists. It was deleted under world-v5j1 and the deletion is registered as a declared divergence from mainline LPJ-GUESS 4.1.1 in biosphere/config/fire.yaml, with the argument in biosphere/notes/fire-model-audit.md section 8.

The classification was wrong while it existed. The row sits in a tuned-values enumeration and the audit's prose says its justification is 'the other model does it'. The constant is not tuned: a fit residual does not arrive at exactly 1e-3 in two codebases, and the provenance is real rather than empty -- LPJmL's src/soil/fire_prob.c, vendored at vendor/lpjml, carries the identical constant. It is IMPLICIT-EARTH. commonoutput.cpp gives 0.001/yr its meaning as a 1000-year reporting cap on fire return interval, and that cap is one per EARTH year: LPJF and LPJmL run NDAYYEAR 365 against this model's 183-day year, so the numeral was 1.996x too frequent in absolute time, beside a distinterval that is converted for exactly that reason.

Under the vocabulary that distinction is the point -- tuned and implicit-Earth are different defects with different repairs -- so leaving it in the tuned enumeration teaches the wrong lesson about a case that is a clean worked example of the other class.

Not done under world-v5j1 because notes/audits/ was outside that task's declared file scope.

Evidence: biosphere/notes/fire-model-audit.md section 8, biosphere/config/fire.yaml.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Done, and the primary source landed mid-task and changed what the row could claim. Thonicke, Venevsky, Sitch and Cramer (2001) -- the GlobFIRM primary, now references/thonicke2001.pdf and INDEX.md -- was read for the one link the row's argument had NOT walked: the chain ran code-to-code (vegdynam.cpp's // c.f. LPJF to LPJmL's fire_prob.c) and stopped short of the paper that could have carried the derivation.

It carries none. The paper states no minimum burned fraction anywhere; Eqn 5 is introduced with 'A is zero when fire conditions were absent during the year', and its own reporting stops at 'more than 900 years' for regions unsuitable to carry fire -- the same diagnostic ceiling commonoutput.cpp applies, not a floor on the state. Sitch et al. (2003), already held, states none either. So the row is confirmed and strengthened: two implementations and two papers, no derivation at the end.

What the paper DOES fit is Eqn 8's four coefficients (0.45, 2.83, 2.96, 1.04), by least-mean-square regression against Portugal, southern California and Kakadu. That is a published fit with an inspectable Earth domain rather than a tuning, it is the curve this project keeps, and it is now recorded as a separate question from the floor.

tuned-values.md section 16 drops the vegdynam.cpp:1435 row and its disposition sentence and gains the reclassification argued in three findings, one per class ruled out. The index table's row 16 says the floor left the class rather than being repaired in it. The same finding is folded into fire-model-audit.md section 8 and fire.yaml's settles block.

title: The labile-carbon humified coefficient's 0.2 to 0.447 bracket is unswept
description:
`modules/somdynam.cpp` now sets the operator's labile carbon as one coefficient
per CENTURY pool class on that class's decomposition: `frac_labile_carbon` 0.6
on SURFMICRO and SOILMICRO, `frac_labile_carbon_humus` 0.2 on SURFHUMUS, SLOWSOM
and PASSIVESOM, nothing on the six litter pools. Both numbers are Li, Frolking
and Frolking (1992) p. 9765's own, and the mapping of DNDC's four pools onto
CENTURY's eleven is the judgement (`world-vyvn`, register entry
`labile_carbon_paths` in `biosphere/config/somdynam.yaml`).

ONE PLACE IN THAT MAPPING CARRIES A BRACKET. DNDC's humads returns 0.2 of its
decomposition to microbial biomass. CENTURY's SLOWSOM returns
`csa = 1 - csp - 0.55` to SOILMICRO, which is 0.447 to 0.450 across the whole
clay range. The two models disagree by a factor of 2.2 about the same quantity
and DNDC's number is the declared one, because the parameter exists to import
DNDC's definition of soluble carbon into a model with no native counterpart to
it. Bracket [0.2, 0.447], declared on `instruction:frac_labile_carbon_humus`.

WHAT IT IS WORTH, by hand. Solving the steady state of `somfluxes` for unit
litter input, the labile carbon moves from 0.70 to 0.88 of what mainline's
single coefficient gives as the humified coefficient crosses its bracket. That
is the largest single uncertainty in the mapping: the PASSIVESOM assignment,
which has no DNDC counterpart at all, moves it by 0.003 over the whole of
[0, 1]. `d_N_max` sits on the roughly linear limb of its saturation, so 0.7 to
1.0 of that reaches both denitrification steps.

DO: sweep it as a second axis of the same matched-arm construction `world-9f1v`
built for `ntransform.cpp` -- same build, same climatology, same instruction
values elsewhere, same seed and patches, compared on NET_DENITRIF, the four soil
gas fluxes and plant mineral-N uptake over complete forcing cycles. Three arms:
mainline's `respsum * frac_labile_carbon`, the split at 0.2, and the split at
0.447.

BLOCKED, and not on cost. No LPJ-GUESS run this project has made reaches its own
BIO-12/BIO-14 acceptance gate: `world-qcse`. A run against a run in that state
cannot say whether a substrate change is right, only what two non-equilibrium
states differ by. The threshold is fixed before the results are seen, per the
project's convention: the bracket is settled if the two split arms differ by
less than the accepted pair's own cycle-to-cycle spread on NET_DENITRIF, and
otherwise it stands as a declared bracket.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 PRE-REGISTERED, BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT: HOW THE ECOLOGICAL RELAXATION TIME IS
ESTIMATED AND WHAT EACH OUTCOME BUYS.

THE PROBLEM WITH WHAT I ALREADY HAVE. The relaxation times on world-3erv came from an
exponential fit of the form a + b*exp(-r*t), and 34 of 64 fields returned an asymptote
outside the record's own range. That is the fit saying the record does not contain the
turn-over, and it is the correct refusal -- but a refused fit gives no number, so the
bracket it produces is bounded below by the record and has no other content. Buying a
spin-up from that is guessing.

A BETTER ESTIMATOR, AND IT NEEDS NO ASYMPTOTE. For y(t) = A - B*exp(-t/tau) the
DIFFERENCE between consecutive equal blocks decays by exp(-Q/tau), where Q is the block
length, and the asymptote A cancels. So split the record into four equal blocks, take
their means m1..m4 and the successive differences d1 = m2-m1, d2 = m3-m2, d3 = m4-m3;
then r = d2/d1 estimates exp(-Q/tau) and tau = -Q/ln(r). This measures the DECAY RATE
over the record rather than the distance still to travel, so a record shorter than tau
can still carry it.

ADMISSIBILITY, DECLARED NOW AND BEFORE ANY FIELD IS READ. This estimator fails softly
and its failure looks like an ordinary number, which is failure-modes class 34, so every
condition is stated up front:
 1. SIGN. d1 and d2 must have the same sign. Opposite signs are not a monotone approach.
 2. CONTRACTION. 0 < r < 1. r at or above 1 is a series that is not decaying, and no
    tau is reported for it.
 3. THE EFFECT MUST EXCEED THE INSTRUMENT. |d1| and |d2| must each exceed twice their
    own standard error, and that standard error is the memory-corrected one from
    `lib/autocorrelation.py:mean_standard_error` with the field's own tau -- not the
    naive one, which is the mistake this whole line of work started from.
 4. CONSISTENCY. The second ratio d3/d2 must give a tau within a factor of two of the
    first. An exponential has one rate; two blocks disagreeing by more than that is a
    series that is not a single exponential, and a single number would misdescribe it.
A field failing any condition reports NO relaxation time. It is not given a default.

THE SPIN-UP DERIVATION, and it follows `lib/run_lengths.py`'s own logic rather than a
new one. That module's `settling_orbits` decays a perturbation to a residual the NEXT
instrument cannot see, and takes its residual from the criterion that judges what
follows. The ecological analogue is exact: the spin-up must leave a residual approach
small enough that the DRIFT it produces across the retained record is inside the
acceptance contract's own `relative_end_to_end_limit`. With the state starting from
bare ground the initial excursion is the full equilibrium level, so

    exp(-S/tau) * (1 - exp(-L/tau)) <= relative_end_to_end_limit

for a spin-up S and a retained record L, both in complete forcing cycles. That is one
equation in the contract's own declared tolerance and the measured relaxation time, with
nothing typed into it.

DECISION RULE, FIXED NOW.
 - Enough fields admissible to bound the slowest: the bracket runs from the slowest
   admissible tau to the slowest tau any field shows, the spin-up is derived from the
   TOP of it because a spin-up must serve the slowest field, and the answer is a number
   with a cost.
 - Some fields admissible, some not: the bracket's bottom is the slowest admissible tau
   and its top is OPEN, bounded below by the record. Following the module's own rule --
   the bottom of the bracket is what a run buys up front and a refusal buys the rest --
   the spin-up is derived from the bottom and declared A FLOOR, not a length.
 - No field admissible: the relaxation time is not measurable from a 1000-cycle record.
   The bracket is a lower bound of the record itself, the spin-up cannot be derived, and
   the row is BLOCKED on a longer diagnostic whose cost I state.

WHAT THE MODULE MUST NOT BE ABLE TO DO AFTER THIS. Confuse the ecological pair with the
climate pair. They are different quantities in different units -- the climate side is in
ORBITS, the ecological side in COMPLETE FORCING CYCLES, and they coincide numerically
only because this world's driver has cycle_years 1. The conversion is the run's own
declared cycle length and is never assumed. Any name I add carries `ecological` and its
unit, and the existing discipline -- memory sizes a span whose MEAN needs an interval,
relaxation sizes a block for a transient to DECAY -- is preserved rather than paralleled.

COST IS PART OF THE ANSWER. Whatever spin-up falls out gets priced from the measured
throughput of the runs on record, and if it is expensive that is reported as the answer
rather than rounded down.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 OUTCOME: RESOLVED. The pre-registered second branch fired -- some fields
admissible, some not -- so both numbers are FLOORS and say so. The headline is that the
spin-up this world's ecology needs costs 55 minutes, and the reason no run has ever had
