THE ESTIMATOR THE PRE-REGISTRATION PROMISED. `lib/lpj_output.py:relaxation_time`. Four
equal blocks of the record; the difference between consecutive block means decays by
exp(-Q/tau) and the asymptote cancels out of the ratio, so tau = -Q/ln(r) needs no
asymptote and a record shorter than tau can still carry it. All four admissibility
conditions were declared before it ran and it fails loudly rather than softly.

Five fields across the two assessed runs clear all four:

    lai.out   BNS       464.8 cycles      memory  48.7
    anpp.out  BNS       767.0 cycles      memory  39.4
    npool.out Total     846.8 cycles      memory  78.3

123 are declined, most for a block difference inside twice its own memory-corrected
standard error or for successive differences that change sign -- which is what a memory
time of 60 to 125 cycles does to blocks of 250. So the relaxation bracket is 59.7 to
846.8 cycles with an OPEN TOP, and a field the estimator declines may be slower still.

THE TWO FLOORS, and they are different quantities sized by different times.

  RETAINED RECORD, from the MEMORY time at the top of its bracket, because a record must
  serve every field it will judge, and at the span multiple `lib/autocorrelation.py`
  declares for any span whose mean is taken:   10 x 125.3 = 1253 cycles.

  SPIN-UP, from the RELAXATION time, with the residual taken from the criterion that
  judges what follows exactly as SETTLING_RESIDUAL_K takes 0.15 K from the offset
  criterion. From bare ground the state starts a full level away, so the approach
  remaining after S cycles is exp(-S/tau) and the drift it puts across a record of L is
  that times (1 - exp(-L/tau)). The contract refuses above `relative_end_to_end_limit`:

      exp(-S/tau) * (1 - exp(-L/tau)) <= 0.05   ->   S >= 2318 cycles

  Nothing in that is typed. Starting from bare ground is the conservative reading and is
  stated: a pool the CENTURY accelerator hands over part-grown needs less.

THE COST, from the runs' own manifests rather than a guess: 990.7 s for 1098 simulated
years and 1824.7 s for 1998, which agree to one per cent and imply 0.9267 s per
simulated year at npatch 5 on 16 ranks over 1617 cells with negligible fixed cost.

    spin-up 2318 + record 1253 = 3571 cycles = 55 minutes at npatch 5, 3.7 h at npatch 20

It is robust to the open top: at a relaxation time of 1500 cycles the total is 4892
cycles and 76 minutes, at 2000 it is 5715 and 88 minutes. The answer stays under two
hours across the whole plausible range.

SO THE 998 WAS EARTH'S CONVENTION ON A CORRECT CONVERSION. The shipped LPJ-GUESS 500
was rescaled into 998 simulation years exactly right, and nothing re-derived it when
this world's relaxation time became measurable. 2318 is 2.32 times it, which is the
factor of two to five narrowed to a number.

WHAT SHIPPED.
 - `lib/run_lengths.py` carries a second timescale pair, in COMPLETE FORCING CYCLES, in
   its own section that opens by naming the three ways it could be confused with the
   climate pair: not the same model, not the same unit, not the same span. It STATES NO
   NUMBER -- both brackets are read from the acceptance artifacts -- which is the
   `tau_relaxation` treatment and the stronger of the module's two.
 - `assess_lpj_run.py` records both timescales on the acceptance artifact whatever the
   verdict, because a run refused for not having settled is exactly the run whose
   timescales size the next one.
 - `build_vesper_pfts.py` reads the spin-up floor instead of rescaling the convention,
   and REFUSES to rescale it, because the derived value is already in simulation years
   and applying the YEAR_COUNT factor to it would be that file's own trap. It falls back
   to the convention only when no assessed run exists, which is the loop reading the best
   available input rather than the first, and records which it used. The emitted file
   carries a DERIVED class of its own so the value cannot be misread as a rescale.
 - `equilibrium_window_gate.py` checks the derivation as an IDENTITY that can fail: the
   spin-up must satisfy the inequality it came from and a spin-up one per cent shorter
   must not. It reads 0.0500 against 0.05, and 0.0514 one per cent shorter.
 - Both quantities are registered in `notes/audits/frozen-derived-quantities.md`, and
   `CLAUDE.md`'s lib entry now says the module holds two pairs.

BLOCKED, AND ONLY THIS: the run itself. The host lock is held until about 17:30 by
world-yyx8's three paired T42 arms, a three-hour claim, so the 55-minute run is not
taken here rather than run around the lock. It is ready:

    scripts/lock_and_run -m "first LPJ run at the derived spin-up (world-r9nz)" \
      .venv/bin/python biosphere/scripts/run_lpj_guess.py \
      --nyear 1253 --npatch 5 --ranks 16 --label derived-run-lengths

`biosphere/generated/vesper_pfts.ins` already carries nyear_spinup 2318. The derivation
does not depend on that run; what the run buys is the re-reading, and it is worth saying
what to watch: the memory time read off this model GROWS with the window it is read on,
which is why both numbers are floors, so the first thing to check on the longer record is
whether the record floor has moved under itself.

title: The endorheic alkalinity bonus is the sump's mechanism applied to the whole basin floor
description:
`ph.endorheic_alkalinity_bonus` is justified as "added where drainage is closed
and salts accumulate". It is applied as a flat additive offset on every
endorheic basin FLOOR cell, whatever that cell's own drainage is doing, and on
the configured build 91.75 per cent of the land area carrying it has local
runoff above zero, at a median of 11.55 mm/yr.

A basin-floor cell with runoff EXPORTS. Its salts go to the sump; they do not
accumulate where the bonus is being added. The mechanism the key describes
belongs to the sump, and the sump is a class Orogen names: `evaporite`, 1.39 per
cent of land area, against the bonus's 15.33. `saltCrustMask` in
vendor/orogen/js/lithology.js zones the basin for exactly this reason -- "the
salt crust is therefore the SUMP, the part that repeatedly floods and dries, not
the basin" -- and the pH block reads none of that zoning.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE TWO ROWS THAT PRECEDE IT, one level up. world-i70y
found a mechanism attached to the wrong variable at the dry end and moved it;
world-5th5 found the closed basin stated three times and left it stated once,
here. What is left is that the one remaining statement is attached to the basin
floor when the mechanism is the sump's.

MEASURED, offline reconstruction through the shipped soil_ph, canonical-10m-
carve2, baseline climatology, land-area weighted:
  the bonus is worth +0.123 pH on the land mean and +0.544 over cells more than
  half endorheic;
  no endorheic-bearing cell reaches Helvaci's 8.5 floor without it, 0 of 926, so
  it is doing all the work of putting a closed basin in range;
  its own derived bracket spans the land mean by 0.341, which is the same order
  as the whole world-5th5 change.

AND IT IS UNCONDITIONAL IN L. A leached basin-floor cell lands on the gibbsite
buffer and then has 0.8 added to it, which is not "the range a closed basin
reaches" by any reading of the source the bracket comes from.

Do: decide what the bonus is a function of. Three candidates and the row should
say which, not leave it open -- the sump fraction of the cell rather than the
endorheic fraction; an attenuation in L so that a draining floor cell loses it
the way a leached parent loses its calcite; or a defence that a closed basin's
floor is alkaline whatever its local runoff, which would need a source that
measures margin soils and not lake water. Helvaci is lake water in one
depositional setting and the config already says it bounds the entry and does
not set it.

Not folded into world-5th5 because it is a FORM change to build_soil.py:soil_ph,
and that row was a mapping fix plus the removal of two duplicate literals. Two
form changes in one edit make neither reviewable, which is the reason world-l442
and world-i70y were split in the first place.
acceptance_criteria: ph.endorheic_alkalinity_bonus is a function of the quantity its own mechanism varies with, or carries a sourced argument for being flat over the basin floor; the effect on modelled pH over endorheic cells is measured and reported.
close_reason: Resolved and committed (b745565ed). The closed basin is now the sump's buffer inside the relaxation rather than a flat offset on the whole basin floor. Deletion would have been wrong: nothing else in the block can exceed calcite saturation, and this world's own Hardie-Eugster divide puts 95.7 per cent of endorheic catchment area past it -- '0 of 926 without it' is evidence the buffers do not carry the closed basin, not a requirement that a floor reach 8.50. Three buffers now, all parent-independent, keyed on the salt-crust share which the generator's own basin_fill rule makes the sump. soda_buffer_ph is a sentinel from the single CLOSED_BASIN_PH_RANGE at the low end 8.50, reclassified implicit-Earth, a demotion from derived. Land mean 6.454 to 6.335; the salt crust is sub-grid at T21 so the new term is worth +0.003 and the change is almost all removal; the term stands on mechanism. Downstream the vegetation model's volatilisation moves by 0.666 land-wide.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 FIXED. The closed basin is now the SUMP's buffer, inside the
relaxation. `endorheic_alkalinity_bonus` and its bracket are gone, along with
soil_ph's `endorheic` argument. Unstaged in the tree.

CRITERION FIXED BEFORE ANY NUMBER OF MY OWN WAS COMPUTED, written to the session
scratchpad first and restated below where each part was answered. C1 the five
prior measurements reproduce or I stop; C2 the form, three questions each with
its deciding observation named in advance, including the falsifier that would
have sent me back to the endorheic fraction; C3 the source, with the value
inside the bracket declared ahead of the sweep; C4 measurement in soilmap units
under both weightings; C5 the instrument, with "inside the spread is not a
reason to skip the change and not a reason to make it" declared in advance; C6 a
check that can fail. Also declared in advance and worth restating: THE SIZE OF
THE CHANGE IS NOT A REASON FOR ANYTHING. A term is right because its mechanism
is, so a correct term that moves the land mean by nothing still stands.

C1: ALL SIX REPRODUCE, on the offline reconstruction against the shipped
soil_ph. Endorheic land area 15.35 per cent, salt crust 1.39; 91.75 per cent of
the bonus-carrying land area drains, median 11.55 mm/yr over the 926 cells more
than one per cent endorheic; the bonus is worth +0.123 on the area-weighted land
mean and +0.543 over endorheic>0.5; 0 of those 926 reach 8.50 without it. Two
notes. The median is stronger than reported when weighted: 24.7 mm/yr by land
area against the 11.55 unweighted. And "926" is the population at endorheic >
0.01; at endorheic > 0 it is 989, which is where the two counts in the row come
from.

C2, Q1: THE MECHANISM IS THE SUMP'S, AND ITS FALSIFIER DID NOT FIRE. Orogen's
`basin_fill` cover rule fires only on `endorheic` and splits by `saltCrustMask`:
`c.cover = c.saltCrust ? evaporite : playa_clastic`, with the mask's own comment
settling it -- "the clastic load drops at the basin margin as alluvial fans and
playa mud, while the dissolved load travels to the lowest ground and
precipitates there when the water evaporates. The salt crust is therefore the
SUMP -- the part that repeatedly floods and dries -- not the basin." The
declared falsifier was more than 5 per cent of evaporite land area outside
`is_endorheic`; the measured figure is 0.000000, exactly, because the class is
produced by that one branch. So the `evaporite` class IS the sump and it is the
quantity the statement is carried by.

C2, Q2: IT BELONGS INSIDE THE RELAXATION. Soda alkalinity accumulates only while
evaporative concentration exceeds what drainage carries out of the profile,
which is the same supply-against-export statement `exp(-s L / u)` already makes,
so the closed basin is a BUFFER the sump relaxes from and not a constant added
to what the relaxation returned. `build_soil.py:soil_ph` now reads

    dry = max(mixture, C)
    dry = dry + sump * (soda - dry)      sump = the cell's salt-crust share
    ph  = G + (dry - G) * exp(-leaching_slope * L / supply)

Three buffers in order G < C < S, each parent-independent, and which one a
gridcell sits near is drainage and zoning rather than rock.

C2, Q3: NOT REDUNDANT, AND DELETION IS THE WRONG ANSWER. Nothing else in the
block can put a cell above calcite saturation -- `dry` is floored at C and the
exponential only descends from it -- so deleting the statement leaves the model
with no expression of the alkaline path at all, on a world whose own
Hardie-Eugster divide puts 95.7 / 94.6 per cent of endorheic catchment area on
it. That is how I read the row's "0 of 926": as evidence the buffers do not
carry it, and therefore against deletion. It is NOT a requirement that a basin
floor reach 8.5, because that number is lake water; reading it over 15 per cent
of land is what installed the defect. Measured for completeness: deleting
outright gives a land mean of 6.3318 against 6.3349 with the sump buffer.

C3: THE SOURCE NOW MEASURES THE MEDIUM IT IS APPLIED TO, AND IT IS STATED ONCE.
Helvaci's 8.5 to 11 is lake WATER in a closed basin, which is what a salt crust
is when it floods -- saltCrustMask's own "repeatedly floods and dries" -- so it
brackets a sump buffer and does not bracket a margin soil. `ph.soda_buffer_ph`
and its bracket are BOTH sentinels, emitted by `carbonate_ph.py` from the single
`CLOSED_BASIN_PH_RANGE` constant, so the measurement is written down once with
its citation beside it; `resolve` refuses a number in either key and says why in
its own words rather than borrowing the pCO2 message, because this one does not
move with pCO2.

THE VALUE IS THE LOW END, 8.50, DECLARED BEFORE THE SWEEP. Helvaci attributes
the boron to circulating boron-rich hot water and lists thermal springs beside
the lake water, and references/INDEX.md already records that the Anatolian type
needs a hydrothermal flux this project cannot place. The top of the range is
therefore the most evaporated brine in a basin fed by something Vesper has no
model for; the low end is the least committal reading and the only point in the
range not chosen by preference.

CLASSIFICATION: IMPLICIT-EARTH, which is a demotion from the "derived" label the
old bracket wore and is the honest one. Helvaci's range minus this world's
calcite pH made the OFFSET move with pCO2 while pinning the absolute pH to
Earth's basins, which is a planet transfer the source cannot support. A soda
brine's pH is set by its own alkalinity at its own pCO2; the repair is a trona
or nahcolite saturation solve at this world's pCO2, needing Pitzer activities at
brine ionic strength, and until then the bracket stands in and gets swept.
Recorded in notes/audits/tuned-values.md beside the gibbsite buffer, which is
where this project enumerates implicit-Earth constants; no row filed, because
the convention there is the audit note and not one bd row per constant.

C4: MEASURED, canonical-10m-carve2 against the baseline climatology, 1639 land
cells, through the shipped soil_ph.

set                    cells   land-area weighted    cos(lat) weighted
all land                1639   6.454 -> 6.335        6.527 -> 6.446
dry, runoff <= 0         254   8.298 -> 8.170        8.227 -> 8.167
wettest quartile         367   5.200 -> 5.165        5.190 -> 5.170
endorheic > 0.5          130   7.626 -> 7.088        same cells, -0.538
endorheic > 0.01         926   6.972 -> 6.790        7.144 -> 6.984
salt crust > 0.1          30   8.248 -> 7.965        8.140 -> 7.869

988 cells move, 764 by more than 0.05 and 83 by more than 0.5, none by more than
1.0; the largest single move is -0.800, the retired offset exactly; 983 of 1639
change at the soilmap's three decimals. No cell rails at either clip before or
after. Cells above the calcite buffer among the 926 fall 324 -> 158, and cells
at or above Helvaci's floor fall 39 -> 0.

THE SALT CRUST IS SUB-GRID AT T21 AND I AM NOT GOING TO DRESS THAT UP. It is
1.39 per cent of land area and no T21 gridcell is more than 0.238 salt crust, so
the new term is worth +0.003 on the land mean and at most +0.064 on any cell,
against the +0.123 the offset was worth. Over the buffer's whole bracket, 8.5 to
11, the land mean moves 0.023. So at this rung the change is nearly all removal.
The term is here because the mechanism is; it is resolution-dependent by
construction and a finer rung resolves more crust.

WHAT READS THE COLUMN, because a land mean is not the consequence. LPJ-GUESS's
ammonia volatilisation enters `ntransform.cpp` as exp(2 * (pH - 10)), so the
change is worth a factor of 0.666 on the land-area mean of that quantity and
0.644 over endorheic-bearing cells: nitrogen loss over the closed-basin floor
falls by about a third. Resolving the crust inside the cell rather than through
the cell's mean pH would raise that mean by a further 8.7 per cent, which is the
ordinary cost of handing a convex consumer one number per cell and is not
specific to this term.

C5: THE INSTRUMENT, swept on the current tree, area-weighted land mean.
leaching_slope [0.35, 1.33] spans 0.631; gibbsite_buffer_ph [4.64, 5.28] spans
0.383; the retired offset over its old bracket spans 0.373. This change is
-0.120, so it is INSIDE all three, plainly. As declared in advance, that is
neither a reason to make it nor a reason to skip it: what makes it a defect
rather than a choice inside a bracket is that the term stated the sump's
mechanism about the whole basin floor and did not decay when the floor drained.
(The row's 0.597 / 0.330 / 0.341 were measured before world-5th5's mapping fix;
the three brackets are unchanged and the spreads moved with the tree.)

C6: THE CHECK, AND IT FAILS ON ALL THREE WRONG FORMS.
`scripts/smoke_test.py:check_closed_basin_is_the_sump`, registered as "the
closed basin is stated about the sump, and it relaxes". A static read: it loads
the real soil_ph and runs six synthetic cells, no artifact. Five assertions with
right answers -- a pure sump at zero export IS the soda buffer (identity); at
one reference runoff it carries strictly less than the full offset, measured
against the same cell with the sump table emptied so the two runs differ by the
statement and nothing else; in the leached limit it falls below the calcite
buffer, at a runoff computed from the declared slope so the arm survives a sweep
of it; a basin-floor cell with no sump never exceeds the calcite buffer at
either end; a half-sump cell is the linear blend exactly. Plus the ordering
G < C < S and a refusal of the retired key by name.

Proved by reverting, three ways, each restored after:
  A the shipped defect, an unconditional additive offset on the basin floor:
    four arms fire, including "a basin-floor cell reads 8.962840, above the
    calcite buffer 8.162840".
  B keyed to the sump correctly but ADDED outside the relaxation: one arm fires,
    and it is the one that exists for it -- "the sump carries +0.337160 over the
    same cell with no sump, and the whole offset is 0.337160".
  C the statement deleted outright: the identity arm fires, "reads 8.162840 and
    the soda buffer is 8.500000".
smoke_test passes 69 checks with the change in place.

WHAT ELSE MOVED. `carbonate_ph.py` emits soda_buffer_ph and its bracket in place
of endorheic_alkalinity_bonus_bracket, with its own refusal message;
`build_soil.py` gained SUMP_GROUPS and two guards that can fail -- the buffer
inside its bracket, and strictly above the calcite buffer at this world's pCO2,
which it is by 0.337 and would not be at a high enough pCO2; smoke_test's
PEDOLOGY_BRACKETS row and one mutation fixture follow the key rename, and the
generic `derived` failure message no longer asserts that every such bracket is a
function of pCO2, because this one is not. Rewritten: pedogenesis.yaml's ph
block, pedology/README.md, pedology/notes/pedogenesis-value-provenance.md
section 3, notes/audits/tuned-values.md and notes/audits/frozen-derived-
quantities.md.

NOT GATED ON THE HARDIE-EUGSTER DIVIDE, and that is a decision rather than a
loose end. The soda buffer applies to every preserved closed basin's sump; this
world's divide puts 95.7 per cent of endorheic catchment area on the alkaline
path, so the ungated statement is right for 95 per cent of it and the remainder
is under 0.001 pH on the land mean at this rung. Gating would need a per-cell
basin identity and a brine_paths artifact that is not written.

STALE, deliberately, and NOT regenerated: pedology/analysis/soil_report.json,
pedology/data/canonical-10m-carve2/soilmap_T21.txt and
land_column_states_T21.txt. They were stale from four changes before this one
and need one build_soil.py run. Nothing CPU-heavy was run for this row: no
build, no model run, no lock_and_run; every number above is the offline
reconstruction calling the shipped soil_ph.

title: The retained record length has a statistical lower bound and still no ecological one
description:
vesper-lpj-equilibrium-window/2 measures each field's trending-cell limit from the run's own record before the acceptance window, and a stationary field exceeds the largest of N such windows with probability 1/(N+1). The declared maximum_false_refusal_rate of 0.05 therefore sets a lower bound on the retained record: 20 windows, 200 cycles at the current 10-cycle window. That is a real derivation of run length, and it is the WRONG KIND.

It bounds the record from the acceptance statistic alone. It says nothing about whether 200 cycles is long enough for the simulated ecosystem to have settled, which is the question the acceptance contract exists to answer. Both bounds have to hold and the larger one wins.

lib/run_lengths.py is where the ecological bound belongs: it already derives a commissioning span from the MEMORY time and a settling block from the RELAXATION time, both bracketed because neither time is measured, and it already keeps the two apart. The biosphere has neither time measured. The 1000-orbit diagnostic lpj_377476c097b549fcaaa07cc7644275ad is the record that would give them: TrIBE was not established at 100 orbits and is still expanding at 1000, which is a relaxation time longer than the retained window and is the reason the run is still refused.

Do: measure the biosphere's memory and relaxation times from that record, add them to lib/run_lengths.py on the same bracketed terms as the climate ones, and state the retained length as the larger of the two bounds. Cites biosphere/notes/equilibrium-trend-null.md.
close_reason: Resolved. world-ioxr: the size arm caught that contract /2's maximum_false_refusal_rate 0.05 was exact per FIELD while the gate refuses per RUN across 64, measured family rate 0.34; and the proposed sqrt(tau) repair was measured not to work, because that correction is for a mean over a span and cannot make a span shorter than its memory carry a trend. slope_standard_errors has no defensible value while the window is what it is. world-3erv: both bounds measured and the ecological one binds in both places. Contract /3 ships a memory-adequacy guard that fails closed on every run, so the invalid test is unreachable.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 PRE-REGISTERED, BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT: WHAT SETTLES THIS ROW.

THE ROW ASKS FOR ONE BOUND AND THERE ARE TWO, on different quantities, and conflating
them is the mistake `lib/run_lengths.py` already exists to prevent. It keeps the MEMORY
time and the RELAXATION time apart and never interchanges them, and the same split
applies here:

 - The MEMORY time bounds the RETAINED record. The contract cuts that record into
   windows of `complete_forcing_cycles` and treats each as a draw. If a field's
   cycle-mean series remembers itself for longer than a window, the window carries
   fewer independent values than the slope fit's 8 degrees of freedom claim, and N
   windows are not N draws.
 - The RELAXATION time bounds the SPIN-UP, which is `nyear_spinup` 998 with
   `freenyears` 200 in vesper_pfts.ins. A run whose ecosystem is still relaxing during
   its retained record has a drift the null construction detrends away from its own
   reference.

Both are measured on the 1000-orbit run lpj_377476c0, which is at literally fixed
forcing, per field on the seven stability tables:

 - MEMORY: `lib/autocorrelation.py:integrated_time` on the spatial-mean cycle series,
   giving tau, the effective sample size, and its own verdict on whether the span can
   support them. `stationary_enough` decides whether tau means anything before tau is
   quoted; a tau reported on a span that module refuses is not a measurement.
 - RELAXATION: an exponential approach to the record's own asymptote, fitted on each
   field's spatial-mean series. The e-folding time is the relaxation time WHERE THE FIT
   IS ADMISSIBLE, and admissible is declared now: the fitted asymptote must lie within
   the record's own range and the e-folding time must be shorter than the record, so
   that the record contains the timescale it claims to measure. A fit whose e-folding
   time exceeds the record is failure-modes class 34 -- a bed shorter than its startup
   -- and is reported as a LOWER BOUND of the record length, never as a value.

DECISION RULE, FIXED NOW.

On the retained record, comparing the ecological bound from the memory time against the
statistical bound of 200 cycles that `maximum_false_refusal_rate: 0.05` already implies:
 - Ecological bound below 200 cycles: the statistical bound binds, the declared rate is
   what sets the retained length, and the row closes with the ecological bound measured
   and recorded as subordinate.
 - Ecological bound above 200 cycles: it binds, the config declares the larger of the
   two, and I state what run length that implies and what it costs.
 - The window itself too short for the memory time -- tau comparable to or larger than
   `complete_forcing_cycles` on the fields that matter: then the window, not the record,
   is the defect, `complete_forcing_cycles: 10` is itself underived, and that is
   reported as a fourth number owing a derivation rather than absorbed quietly.

On the spin-up, from the relaxation time:
 - Relaxation time comfortably inside the existing 998-cycle spin-up: the spin-up is
   sufficient and that is recorded with the measurement.
 - Relaxation time near or beyond it: the spin-up is the binding constraint on
   acceptance, which would explain why a run at fixed forcing is still refused on a
   coherent global drift, and the row hands over a run length with its cost.
 - Fit inadmissible by the rule declared above: the bound is bracketed from below by
   the record and reported as such. A lower bound that already exceeds the statistical
   bound still SETTLES the comparison, so that is a resolution and not a block.

Nothing in this reads whether a run passes. The timescales are properties of the record
at fixed forcing.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 MEASURED: THE ACCEPTANCE WINDOW IS SHORTER THAN THE THING IT TESTS, AND THE
RECORD IS SHORTER THAN THE APPROACH IT IS WATCHING. Both pre-registered branches of this
row fire, and together they answer world-qcse's original question.

Instrument: `biosphere/scripts/derive_trend_null.py <run> --timescales`, reading
`lib/autocorrelation.py`'s estimator and carrying both of its verdicts rather than
quoting a tau it refuses. Measured on lpj_377476c0, 1000 cycles at fixed forcing, 400
sampled cells per table.

MEMORY. The integrated autocorrelation time of the spatial-mean cycle series, per field,
runs 9.3 to 125.3 cycles. The window the contract tests over is 10. Sixty-one of the 64
assessed fields have a spatial-mean tau longer than the whole window; the per-cell
medians run 2.9 to 93.1, and the share of cells whose own tau exceeds the window is 0.22
to 1.00, at or above 0.85 for most woody types. Representative rows:

    table.field          spatial tau   cell tau median   cells with tau > window
    lai.out BNE                 75.3              64.9                     1.00
    lai.out TrIBE               93.5              63.9                     0.97
    lai.out C3G                  9.9               6.3                     0.36
    cpool.out Total            125.3              68.1                     0.89
    npool.out SoilN             60.6              89.0                     0.87
    tot_runoff.out Total        14.9               5.5                     0.33

A trend test over a span shorter than the memory time is not a trend test. It sees one
excursion of a process that has not had time to sample its own distribution, and the
residuals within the span are small because the process is smooth on that scale, so the
ordinary least-squares standard error is small and the slope looks decisive. That is the
whole of the 0.47 to 0.86 flag rate against a nominal 0.081, and it is
`docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md` class 34 exactly: a bed shorter than its startup.

NO CORRECTION RESCUES IT. Inflating the slope standard error by the square root of tau,
which is the correction `lib/autocorrelation.py` owns, moves lai.out's bare flag rate
from 0.47-0.84 down to 0.19-0.46 -- two to three times better, still two to six times
nominal, and still spanning a factor of four across fields. The correction is for a
MEAN over a span; it cannot make a span shorter than tau carry a trend. Applying the
module's own declared bar, RELIABLE_SPAN_MULTIPLE 10, a valid window would be 10 times
tau, so 100 to 1250 cycles, and twenty such windows is 2000 to 25000 retained cycles.
The windowed trend form cannot be made valid on this model at any affordable cost.

RELAXATION, and this is the substantive answer. An exponential approach fitted to each
field's spatial-mean series over the full 1000 cycles is INADMISSIBLE for most fields by
the criterion declared before it was run: 34 of 64 fits put the asymptote outside the
record's own range, meaning the series has not turned over within 1000 cycles, and three
more return a timescale longer than the record. Where a fit is admissible the e-folding
times are 22.9 to 775.9 cycles, mostly in the hundreds: lai.out TrIBE 685.1, aaet.out
Total 775.9, lai.out TeBS 492.4, lai.out C4G 414.1.

`lib/autocorrelation.py:stationary_enough` independently refuses the spatial-mean series
of most fields: the linear trend across 1000 cycles moves them by more than their own
standard deviation. These series are still moving.

WHAT THE TWO BOUNDS ARE.
 - On the RETAINED record, from the memory time and the module's own span bar: at least
   10 times tau, so 100 to 1250 cycles depending on the field. The statistical bound of
   200 cycles that `maximum_false_refusal_rate: 0.05` implied is NOT the binding one for
   the woody types and the slow pools; the ecological bound is larger.
 - On the SPIN-UP, from the relaxation time: at least a few times an e-folding time of
   several hundred cycles, so of order 2000 to 5000 cycles. `vesper_pfts.ins` sets
   nyear_spinup 998. THE SPIN-UP IS SHORT, by a factor of two to five, and that is why a
   run at literally fixed forcing is still drifting coherently in TrIBE after 1000
   further cycles.

So world-qcse's title is literally true and the reason is now measured: no LPJ run has
reached ecological equilibrium because none has been spun up for long enough, and the
acceptance instrument could not say so because its window was an order of magnitude
shorter than the timescale it was watching.

The time base remains correct and is still not implicated. 998 spin-up cycles is 500.0
Earth years and matches the community convention exactly; the convention is simply too
short for this world's woody types and slow pools.

title: relative_end_to_end_limit 0.05 is a declared tolerance with no consumer behind it
description:
biosphere/config/equilibrium_window.yaml declares relative_end_to_end_limit: 0.05 as a DECISION: the residual drift the acceptance contract is willing to carry into a consumer. That disposition is legitimate under the no-tuned-values convention, but the declaration is currently unanchored -- nothing says what 5 per cent of a field's window mean is worth to the thing that reads it.

It is derivable. The consumers are exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_albedo.py, which turns LAI and FPC into a surface albedo and a forest fraction the next climate run is forced with, and pedology's soil carbon feedback. lib/sensitivity.py holds the project's one flux-to-kelvin conversion. A drift of x per cent in the simulated leaf area is worth an albedo change, a top-of-atmosphere forcing and a surface temperature, and the tolerance should be the drift whose forcing is below what the climate arm can resolve.

Do: derive the limit through the albedo-to-forcing-to-kelvin chain, declare it with its bracket, and record what the current 0.05 corresponds to in kelvin. If the derived limit is looser than 0.05 that is information, not a licence to loosen; the row is about giving the number a derivation.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 PRE-REGISTERED, BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT: WHAT SETTLES THIS ROW.

`relative_end_to_end_limit: 0.05` is declared as the residual drift the acceptance
contract is willing to carry into a consumer. That makes it a DECISION, and a decision
is a legitimate input under the no-tuned-values convention -- but only once someone has
said what it is worth to the thing that reads it. Nothing in the tree says.

THE CHAIN, and it is the consumer's own, not one invented for this row. The reducer's
consumers are `exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_albedo.py` in --mode modelled, which
reads a run's `fpc.out`, `biosphere/scripts/score_prediction.py`, and pedology's soil
carbon. The one that closes a loop and forces the next climate run is the albedo:

  relative drift X in the spatial mean of fpc.out
    -> change in tree and grass foliar projective cover
    -> change in SURFACE albedo, through that script's own cover-mixing formula and the
       declared tree_albedo and grass_albedo against the base ground albedo
    -> change in PLANETARY albedo
    -> a top-of-atmosphere forcing in W/m2
    -> kelvin, through `lib/sensitivity.py`, which is the project's ONE flux-to-kelvin
       conversion and must not be re-derived here

The limit is then the drift whose kelvin sits at what the climate arm can actually
resolve, because a drift the next climate run cannot distinguish from zero is a drift
the acceptance contract has no reason to refuse.

DECISION RULE, FIXED NOW. Let D be the derived limit and let 0.05 be the declared one.
 - D within a factor of 2 of 0.05: 0.05 is retained and now carries a derivation. The
   row closes on a derivation rather than a change, exactly as the null row could have.
 - D outside a factor of 2: the limit moves to D, declared with its bracket, and I state
   plainly whether that loosens or tightens the contract and which runs it changes.
 - ANY LINK NOT SIZEABLE FROM ARTIFACTS IN THE TREE: the estimate is BRACKETED rather
   than guessed, per the convention, and the bracket is what gets reported. If the
   bracket is wide enough to contain both 0.05 and its alternatives, the honest outcome
   is that the chain cannot size this number yet: 0.05 stays a DECISION, the bracket and
   the missing link are recorded in the config beside it, and the measurement that would
   close it is named. That is a blocked thread with a named unblocker, not a derivation.

The factor of 2 is fixed here because a chain with this many links -- a cover mixing
rule, two albedo endmembers with their own brackets, a surface-to-planetary conversion,
and a flux-to-kelvin slope that carries a declared bracket of its own -- cannot
credibly resolve better than that, and pretending otherwise would be the instrument
error CLAUDE.md's class 34 warns about.

A SEPARATE THING THIS ROW MUST NOT DO. `lib/sensitivity.py`'s slope is currently
refused on the active build by scripts/check_consistency.py, which reports its two arms
were run on canonical-10m-base against a configured canonical-10m-carve2. If that makes
the slope unusable rather than merely stale, the kelvin link is unavailable, the bracket
branch above is the outcome, and the blocking dependency is named rather than worked
around by picking another slope. Three sensitivities were in simultaneous use once and
they differ by a factor of 2.2; this row will not add a fourth choice.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 OUTCOME: BLOCKED, with a named unblocker, which is the branch the
pre-registration reserved for exactly this. The chain sizes to a number; one link in it
is not measured anywhere in the tree, and its declared uncertainty is wide enough that
the derived limit cannot choose between 0.05 and several alternatives.

THE CHAIN, sized through the consumer's own code rather than an invented route.
`exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_albedo.py --mode modelled` reads a run's fpc.out and
mixes cover into the surface albedo in `composite_rootable`. In the regime that governs
97 per cent of cells the derivative is the rootable fraction times canopy albedo minus
substrate albedo:

  tree albedo        0.143  bracket [0.130, 0.148]   config/planet.yaml
  grass albedo       0.209  bracket [0.190, 0.217]   config/planet.yaml
  substrate albedo   0.25585 land mean bare rock     exoplasim/inputs/t21/albedo_report.json
  rootable fraction  0.83488                          biosphere/generated/vesper_driver_provenance.json
  land fraction      0.432841                         build manifest, landFractionBySurfaceClass
  attenuation        0.5, DECLARED, factor of two     scripts/error_budget.py
  flux to kelvin     159.7 K per flux ratio [155.3, 160.6]  lib/sensitivity.py

A 5 per cent drift in tree and grass cover is worth about +0.064 K of surface
temperature, bracketed +0.032 to +0.128 K.

WHAT THE CLIMATE ARM RESOLVES: 0.15 K for the single-run convergence criterion
(assess_convergence.py's offset tolerance), 0.05 K for its own resolving-power bar (a
threshold discriminates when the statistic's standard error is a third of it), 0.027 K

and 0.017 to 0.031 K for a paired A/B off an equilibrated donor.

SO THE DERIVED LIMIT SPANS 0.02 to 0.23 across the joint bracket, which contains 0.05
and everything a reasonable person would put beside it. Under the pre-registered rule
that is not a derivation.

THE ONE LINK THAT IS MISSING is the surface-to-planetary albedo attenuation. There is no
measured d(planetary albedo)/d(surface albedo) in this tree. `lib/sensitivity.py`
explicitly declines to own it -- "that attenuation is a modelled quantity with a
factor-of-two uncertainty and it belongs with the budget that owns the assumption, not
here". `scripts/error_budget.py` declares 0.5 and says in the same breath that the
honest claim is a factor of two rather than a number. The single measured point is

term rather than a budget. world-ckbt is already open to measure it and names the three

what the climate arm resolves, and world-ckbt as the unblocker -- rather than a

TWO THINGS THE CHAIN EXPOSED, both worth having on the record. `--mode modelled` has

title: The equilibrium window's slope standard error models no memory, and lib/autocorrelation.py exists for that
description:
BIO-12's per-cell trend test in lib/lpj_output.py computes the slope standard error by ordinary least squares over the window's 10 cycle means, which treats them as independent. They are not: patch gap dynamics give a cell's cycle means strong positive memory.

MEASURED (biosphere/notes/equilibrium-trend-null.md, 2026-08-30). For 10 independent points a 2-standard-error slope test has 8 degrees of freedom and a two-sided probability of 0.081. The rate the test actually flags cells with no trend present runs to 0.39 on the patch-driven fields. A within-window circular-shift surrogate, which keeps each cell's marginal distribution but whitens its serial structure, returns 0.007 to 0.09 across fields, close to the independent-samples rate; the memory-preserving detrended long-run null returns 0.001 to 0.40. The whole excess is temporal memory.

lib/autocorrelation.py is the project's module for the integrated autocorrelation time, the effective sample size and the ONE standard error of a mean over a series whose samples carry memory. The reducer reimplements a memoryless one instead, which is the reuse rule as well as a statistical defect.

The contract now calibrates AROUND this rather than repairing it: each field's trending-cell limit is measured from the run's own detrended record, so the inflated flag rate is absorbed into the limit. That is honest and it works, but it costs power, and it means the limit has to be re-measured per run rather than following from the test's own distribution.

Do: establish whether the integrated autocorrelation time can be estimated at all from the retained record (it cannot be from 10 points), and if it can, replace the OLS standard error with lib/autocorrelation.py's. Then re-measure the null: if it falls to the nominal rate the per-field measured limit can go back to being a declared level.
close_reason: Resolved. world-ioxr: the size arm caught that contract /2's maximum_false_refusal_rate 0.05 was exact per FIELD while the gate refuses per RUN across 64, measured family rate 0.34; and the proposed sqrt(tau) repair was measured not to work, because that correction is for a mean over a span and cannot make a span shorter than its memory carry a trend. slope_standard_errors has no defensible value while the window is what it is. world-3erv: both bounds measured and the ecological one binds in both places. Contract /3 ships a memory-adequacy guard that fails closed on every run, so the invalid test is unreachable.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 PRE-REGISTERED, BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT: WHAT SETTLES THIS ROW.

CONTRACT /2 CHANGED WHAT THIS NUMBER IS, and the row has to be re-asked before it can
be answered. Under /1, `slope_standard_errors` was the significance level of the
per-cell test and its value set the test's SIZE, which is why 2.0 being a two-sided
0.081 at 8 degrees of freedom rather than 0.05 mattered. Under /2 the cell half's size
is fixed by CONSTRUCTION: a field is refused when its trending-cell fraction exceeds
the largest fraction the run's own detrended null windows reach, and by exchangeability
a stationary field does that with probability 1/(N+1) whatever sigma is. If that holds,
sigma is no longer a significance level at all. It is a shape parameter of the
statistic, its only effect is on POWER, and its correct value is the one that
discriminates best -- not the one that hits a nominal rate.

That claim is a measurement and not a premise, so it is the first thing measured.

CONSTRUCTION, on the 1000-orbit run lpj_377476c0's 99 detrended null windows, run-level
because the gate refuses when ANY field exceeds:
 - SIZE, leave-one-out: window i's limit is the per-field maximum over the OTHER 98
   null windows; size is the share of i whose undrifted fraction exceeds it in any
   field. Under exchangeability this is 1/N and must not move with sigma.
 - POWER: the same window i with a coherent drift of twice the contract's
   relative_end_to_end_limit injected into every cell, against the same leave-one-out
   limit. Twice the limit, not once, because a drift AT the limit sits on the boundary
   of the criterion's own first condition and its detection rate there is a property of
   the boundary rather than of the instrument.
Swept over sigma in {1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.306, 2.5, 3.0, 4.0}. 2.306 is in the sweep
because it is the two-sided 95 per cent t quantile at the window's 8 degrees of
freedom, which is what 2.0 would have to be for the ORIGINAL reading of this number to
be right.

DECISION RULE, FIXED NOW.
 - If size is flat in sigma at or below 1/N across the whole sweep, the number is not a
   significance level under /2 and the derivation is by power alone, below.
 - If size DOES move with sigma, the exchangeability argument is wrong, /2's
   false-refusal rate is not 1/(N+1), and that is a defect in the contract I just
   wrote: it gets reported and repaired before anything else, and this row waits.

Given size is flat, on power:
 - Power maximised at 2.0, with no other sigma beating it by more than 2 standard
   errors of the PAIRED difference (the windows are the same, so the scatter is the
   count of windows that flip, McNemar): 2.0 is retained and the row closes on a
   derivation -- it is the value that discriminates best at the contract's stated
   alternative.
 - Power maximised elsewhere by more than that: sigma moves to the maximising value,
   declared with the swept bracket.
 - Power flat across the whole sweep, every value within that scatter of every other:
   sigma is IRREDUCIBLE under /2 -- the contract cannot distinguish its values -- and it
   is declared as such with the argument rather than given an invented derivation.

THE ROW'S ORIGINAL CLAIM IS SETTLED SEPARATELY AND EITHER WAY. The measured
false-positive rate of the bare 2-sigma significance test is reported against its
nominal 0.081, per field, so the size of the memory effect is on the record. Whether to
repair the standard error with lib/autocorrelation.py is then decided by the size
result above: if size is fixed by construction at every sigma, a memoryless standard
error cannot bias the contract's false-refusal rate, the repair buys only power, and
the sigma sweep has already priced that -- in which case the repair is declared
unnecessary under /2 WITH the argument, not left open. If size is not fixed, the repair
is required and the row says so.

The sweep reads only detrended surrogates and injected drifts. It never reads the three
runs' observed fractions, so no outcome of it can be driven by which run passes.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 DEFECT IN THE CONTRACT I SHIPPED THIS MORNING. vesper-lpj-equilibrium-window/2
declares `maximum_false_refusal_rate: 0.05`. Its ACTUAL run-level false-refusal rate is
0.34. Found by the size arm of world-ioxr's pre-registered sweep, which existed to check
exactly this and is the reason it was registered as a check rather than assumed.

WHAT IS WRONG. The exchangeability argument is correct PER FIELD: a stationary field
exceeds the largest of N detrended null windows with probability 1/(N+1), and at N=99
that is 0.01. But the gate refuses a run when ANY field exceeds its own limit, and there
are 64 assessed fields across the seven stability tables. The run-level rate is
1-(1-1/(N+1))^F_eff, and it is not the declared number.

MEASURED, on lpj_377476c0's 100 detrended windows, leave-one-out so each window is
judged against the other 99 exactly as the contract judges an acceptance window:

     sigma    size    power at 2x the drift limit
     1.000   0.390    1.000
     1.500   0.310    1.000
     2.000   0.340    1.000    <- declared
     2.306   0.290    1.000
     2.500   0.310    1.000
     3.000   0.320    1.000
     4.000   0.300    1.000

Size is flat in sigma, as the construction says it must be, and sits at 0.30 to 0.39
against a declared 0.05. The helper was validated on synthetic fields first: at 100
windows it returns 0.010 for one field, 0.080 for eight and 0.460 for sixty-four
independent ones, against an analytic 1-(1-1/100)^n of 0.010, 0.077 and 0.474. The
measured 0.34 corresponds to about 35 effective independent fields out of 64, the
remainder being the correlated ones -- C3G in lai, fpc and aaet move together.

CONSEQUENCE FOR WHAT WAS ALREADY REPORTED. lpj_377476c0 passing the cell half on all
seven tables is much weaker evidence than it read as: a settled run passes that half
about seven times in ten, not ninety-nine. The refusal that stands, lai.out TrIBE on the
GLOBAL half at 5.65 standard errors, is untouched by this -- the global half has one
test per field and no such multiplicity in the cell construction.

WHY RAISING N DOES NOT FIX IT. A run-level rate of alpha through an empirical
per-window null needs the null to have the resolution to express it. The finest
per-field probability an N-window null can state is 1/(N+1), so the minimum achievable
run-level rate is about F_eff/(N+1). At F_eff 35 and alpha 0.05 that is 710 windows,
7100 retained cycles, roughly 20 hours of model time at npatch 5 -- and it would have to
be re-measured per configuration. The empirical null cannot deliver a conventional rate
on this many fields at any record this project can afford.

WHERE THE REPAIR HAS TO COME FROM, and it is this row's own subject. The empirical null
was forced in the first place because the per-field flag rate under no trend spans
0.001 to 0.40, and the measurement below says why: the bare slope test's flag rate at
sigma 2.0, with the relative-drift condition removed, is 0.47 to 0.72 by table against a
nominal 0.081 for independent samples.

     table              median over fields   worst field
     anpp.out                 0.695          TeNE  0.849
     lai.out                  0.712          TeNE  0.847
     fpc.out                  0.723          TeNE  0.854
     cpool.out                0.676          SoilC 0.766
     npool.out                0.646          Total 0.726
     aaet.out                 0.723          TeNE  0.864
     tot_runoff.out           0.467          Base  0.562

That is the memory this row was filed about, and it is an order of magnitude, not a
correction. If the standard error is repaired so the per-field rate returns to its
nominal value, the null becomes ANALYTIC, an analytic null has unlimited resolution, and
the run-level rate can be controlled at any declared alpha by an ordinary multiplicity
correction. The empirical per-field null would then no longer be needed at all.

So the two rows are one repair, and it is measured next: whether correcting the slope
standard error with `lib/autocorrelation.py`'s integrated autocorrelation time collapses
the per-field null onto its nominal rate. Until that is settled the contract's declared
rate is wrong and is not quietly left standing.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 OUTCOME. The pre-registered rule's FIRST branch fired, and it was the branch
that said this row waits: "If size DOES move with sigma, the exchangeability argument is
wrong ... that is a defect in the contract I just wrote: it gets reported and repaired
before anything else." Size did not move with sigma -- it was flat at 0.29 to 0.39
across 1.0 to 4.0, as the construction requires -- but it sat at 0.34 against a declared
0.05, so the argument was wrong at run level rather than at field level. That is
reported above and repaired in contract 3 by renaming the rate to what it provably
controls.

THE POWER ARM COULD NOT RANK SIGMA. Power was 1.000 at every sigma in the sweep, so the
registered comparison had nothing to compare. Under the registered rule that reads as
"flat across the whole sweep", whose disposition is IRREDUCIBLE -- but that disposition
is now moot, because the statistic sigma parameterises has been measured to be invalid
at this model's memory time and is being replaced rather than tuned.

THE ROW'S ORIGINAL CLAIM IS SETTLED, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN A CORRECTION. The bare slope
test's flag rate at sigma 2.0, with the relative-drift condition removed, is 0.47 to
0.72 by table against a nominal 0.081 for independent samples, worst field 0.86. That is
an order of magnitude, not a correction. And the repair the row proposed does not work:
inflating the standard error by the square root of the integrated autocorrelation time,
which is the correction `lib/autocorrelation.py` owns, moves lai.out's rate only to 0.19
to 0.46 -- still two to six times nominal, still spanning a factor of four across
fields.

WHY NO CORRECTION WORKS. The measured memory time of these series is 9.3 to 125.3
complete forcing cycles against a 10-cycle window. The correction is for a MEAN over a
span; it cannot make a span shorter than its own memory carry a trend. A slope fitted
inside one memory time sees a single smooth excursion, and its residuals are small
precisely because the process is smooth on that scale.

WHAT SHIPPED. Contract 3 adds a memory-adequacy guard ahead of the trend test, applying
`lib/autocorrelation.py`'s declared span bar to BOTH spans that must carry the memory
time: the record, where tau is estimated, and the window, where the slope is fitted. It
fails closed on every run this project has, so the invalid test is unreachable. The
guard reuses the module rather than reimplementing it, which was this row's point.
`slope_standard_errors: 2.0` remains in the config with its measured behaviour recorded
beside it and no defensible value while the window is what it is.

WHAT DID NOT SHIP, DELIBERATELY. A replacement statistic was built and validated far
enough to be promising -- a two-half-mean comparison against the memory-corrected
standard error, with the per-field significance DERIVED from a declared family rate by a
Sidak correction over a counted family size, measuring a family refusal rate of 0.040
against a declared 0.05 with power 0.31 at the contract's drift limit and 0.92 at twice
it. It surfaced three non-obvious subtleties in one afternoon and I reverted it rather
than ship a third contract in a day on an afternoon's validation. The design and all
three subtleties are carried on world-rnns so none of it is re-derived.

RESOLVED: the row's question is answered, its proposed repair is measured not to work,
the reason is measured, and the module it named is now used where it is valid.

title: playa mud is an evaporite to the pH block and shale to the weathering map, and it is 9 per cent of land
description:
The same defect world-mddi settled for melange, on the same scale, unsettled.

  pedology/scripts/lithology_map.py:PH_GROUP          playa_clastic -> evaporite
  pedology/scripts/lithology_map.py:ROCK_TO_MEYBECK   playa_clastic -> shale, with
                                                      a RECORDED ARGUMENT for shale
  pedology/config/weathering_schemes.yaml             playa_clastic -> shale, both
                                                      schemes

The evaporite pH bin asserts a base-cation supply of 1.0 BY CONSTRUCTION and a
soda buffer at 8.8. The Meybeck reading is 0.1815. That is a factor of 5.5, on
9.3 per cent of land, and it is larger in supply units than the melange
disagreement world-mddi just fixed.

THE ARGUMENT AGAINST THE EVAPORITE BIN IS ALREADY IN THE TREE, in the map's own
comment: playa mud is detrital fill, not an evaporite; it is the host that
evaporites grow in, and mapping it to an evaporite begs the question. That
sentence was written about the solute map and applies unchanged to the pH bin.

AND THE CLOSED BASIN IS COUNTED TWICE. Orogen assigns playa_clastic only under
the basin_fill cover rule, which fires only where the cell is endorheic, so
EVERY playa cell already receives ph.endorheic_alkalinity_bonus. Putting it on
the soda buffer as well states one closed basin in two places.

Not fixed under world-mddi because it is not a mapping fix: it decides which
buffer playa mud reaches at zero export, which is world-i70y's question, and
moving it changes both the supply and the dry end on 9.3 per cent of land.
world-mddi declares it in lithology_map.py:DECLARED_DISAGREEMENTS naming this
row, so the mapping check passes while naming it rather than blessing it.

Do: settle whether playa mud is a clastic parent on the calcite buffer with the
endorheic bonus, or an evaporite parent on the soda buffer without it. Then
delete its DECLARED_DISAGREEMENTS entry, which fails the check if the two
mappings agree.

The same question stands one row down for evaporite itself, where the answer is
different and already recorded: carbonate and evaporite supplies are 1 by
construction and no Meybeck row is being read.
acceptance_criteria: playa_clastic reads the same way in the pH bin and the solute map, or its disagreement carries a settled argument rather than a pointer to this row; the closed basin is stated once.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-howr: the concavity bound needs no delivery phase (the calibration absorbs the level exactly; the bin weights bound the spread), J = 3.4833 against P = 2.2235, DECISIVE, 26 of 195 carved basins movable and none covered by the climate bracket. world-awvh: the tightening does not exist -- lake storage sharpens the overflow's season rather than damping it, the concentrated arm sits on the floor to six decimals, so the bound is ATTAINED and the verdict stands unchanged. world-mddi: three tables read melange and two already agreed; PH_GROUP was falling back on Orogen's origin category against its own chemistry principle. world-5th5: the soda chemistry is right (95.71 per cent of catchment area alkaline) and was being stated about the floor's rock instead of the basin; playa moves to sedimentary_clastic, parent_by_category is derived in every entry, land mean 6.778 to 6.454.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the share in the description, and it makes the row larger.

playa_clastic is 13.9 per cent of the LAND AREA on canonical-10m-carve2, not
9.3. The 9.3 was cos(lat) over T21 land cells, which weights a cell with a
sliver of land the same as a full one; the mesh's own land-area share is
0.13933, and world_state.json carries it.

That makes playa_clastic the third largest rock class on this world's land,
behind granite and continental_clastic, and larger than melange at 6.11 per
cent. The supply disagreement is a factor of 5.5 against melange's 4.29.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 FIXED. Playa mud is a clastic parent, and the closed basin is now
stated ONCE instead of three times. Unstaged in the tree.

CRITERION FIXED BEFORE ANY RESULT WAS COMPUTED. C1 the soda buffer's warrant,
from this world's own Hardie-Eugster divide under both published weightings,
with the branch for each outcome written down in advance including "open a row
rather than silently moving a second bin"; C2 playa's bin, decided on mechanism
before any score; C3 the double-counting test, two artifact tests with the
consequence declared; C4 measurement in soilmap units under both weightings; C5
the block's own guards. Recorded in full in the session scratchpad and restated
below where each was answered.

C1: THE SODA CHEMISTRY IS RIGHT AND THIS WORLD'S OWN CALCULATION CONFIRMS IT.
The divide computed offline exactly as brine_paths.py does it, on
canonical-10m-carve2 and the baseline climatology, writing no artifact:

  discharge weighting  3640 of 4009 resolved basins alkaline, 95.71% of
                       catchment area; Ca/HCO3 median 0.780
  area weighting       4054 of 4462 resolved basins alkaline, 94.59% of
                       catchment area; Ca/HCO3 median 0.789
  single-lithology identity PASSES on both, worst relative error 5.5e-16 and 0.0

So the declared falsification did not fire and the majority-alkaline branch is
the one that applies: a closed basin here does evaporate past calcite
saturation, and the soda VALUE was never the defect.

C2: WHAT WAS WRONG IS WHERE THE MODEL SAID IT. Passing the divide is a property
of the BASIN, computed from its catchment's inflow chemistry. It was being said
as a property of the floor's own ROCK, and on this world the rock carries no
information the hydrology does not: Orogen's basin_fill cover rule assigns
evaporite and playa_clastic FROM the endorheic flag, and on the configured build
is_endorheic on land and those two classes agree over all but 0.023 per cent of
land area, 869 regions out of 664,079.

And playa mud is not the sump. saltCrustMask zones the basin by depth below the
spill point and its own comment settles it: "the clastic load drops at the basin
margin as alluvial fans and playa mud, while the dissolved load travels to the
lowest ground and precipitates there when the water evaporates. The salt crust
is therefore the SUMP -- the part that repeatedly floods and dries -- not the
basin." playa_clastic IS the part of the closed basin where the dissolved load
did not precipitate. The evaporite bin contradicted the class's own definition,
which is the mechanism answer C2 asked for, reached before any number was seen.

I did NOT reuse the carbonate-balance argument here, and that is deliberate. It
convicted Meybeck's misc_metamorphic row for melange because the row's own ion
balance identified WHAT ROCK the row was. The parallel move -- reading the
halite row's Na-Cl dominance as evidence against a soda buffer -- does not hold:
Table 2C is dilute stream water draining an outcrop, and the divide is about
what the water becomes on evaporating. Using it would have been a superficially
parallel argument about a quantity the row does not measure.

C3: YES, DOUBLE COUNTED, AND THREE TIMES RATHER THAN TWICE.
  (a) same land: the identity above.
  (b) same measurement: ph.parent_bracket_evaporite was [8.50, 11.00] and
      endorheic_alkalinity_bonus_bracket is Helvaci's 8.50 to 11.00 minus the
      derived calcite pH. One source, two brackets. parent_bracket_evaporite was
      also a hand-copied restatement of carbonate_ph.py:CLOSED_BASIN_PH_RANGE.
  (c) and the symptom: a playa cell reached 8.8 + 0.8 = 9.6 and was decided by
      ph.maximum, a clip the config says nothing rests on. 7 cells were railed
      there. None is now.

WHAT CHANGED.
  PH_GROUP           playa_clastic  evaporite -> sedimentary_clastic, joining
                     the three other clastic classes that read Meybeck shale.
                     Its DECLARED_DISAGREEMENTS entry is deleted; the stale-
                     declaration rule would have failed on it otherwise.
  pedogenesis.yaml   parent_by_category.evaporite  8.8 -> derived. EVERY entry
                     is now the sentinel. parent_bracket_evaporite deleted; it
                     bracketed nothing.
  carbonate_ph.py    resolve() loses its evaporite special case: every entry
                     must be `derived`, and the refusal says where a
                     closed-basin statement belongs instead.
  smoke_test.py      the ph.parent_by_category.evaporite bracket row is removed
                     with the keys, and check_one_rock_one_reading is inserted
                     beside check_nonlinear_reduction_order. Reverting either
                     mapping now fails the per-commit gate; verified by
                     reverting playa and running smoke_test, which named the
                     class, the factor and the two readings, then restoring.

C4: MEASURED, offline reconstruction re-checked through the shipped soil_ph,
1639 land cells.

  set                    cells   before -> after
  all land, cos(lat)      1639    6.735 -> 6.527   (-0.208)
  all land, land AREA     1639    6.778 -> 6.454   (-0.324)
  dry, runoff <= 0         254    8.405 -> 8.298   (-0.107)
  more than half playa     113    8.566 -> 7.594   (-0.971)
  more than half endorheic 130    8.571 -> 7.626   (-0.945)
  wettest quartile         367    5.266 -> 5.200   (-0.066)

981 cells move, 756 by more than 0.1 pH, 346 by more than 0.5, 144 by more than
1.0; largest single move -2.107; 975 of 1639 change at the soilmap's own three
decimals. Gibbsite window 0.349 -> 0.419 of land area, calcite window 0.328 ->
0.285, neutral 6-7 0.122 -> 0.128.

THE SUPPLY DID THE WORK, NOT THE BUFFER, AND THAT WAS NOT WHAT I EXPECTED.
Playa land is not dry: over cells more than half playa only 5.3 per cent of the
area has zero runoff, against 7.5 per cent for land as a whole, and the median
local runoff is 15.8 mm/yr. So L > 0 almost everywhere the closed basin is, and
a declared supply of 1 against a clastic 0.1355 was holding those cells at the
calcite buffer against drainage that should have leached them. Splitting the two
edits: playa's bin alone is -0.318 on the land mean, and retiring the soda
buffer on top of it is a further -0.006, at most 0.120 on any cell. The soda
buffer's removal is structural, not numerical, and costs nothing today.

THE INSTRUMENT, CHECKED AGAINST THE SIZE OF THE EFFECT. Land mean swept over
the ends of the block's own declared brackets: leaching_slope [0.35, 1.33] spans
0.597, gibbsite_buffer_ph [4.64, 5.28] spans 0.330, endorheic_alkalinity_bonus
over its derived bracket spans 0.341, against this change's -0.324. So the move
is the same order as the uncertainty the block already carries. What makes it a
defect rather than a choice inside a bracket is that it was a mapping error.

C5: THE GUARDS PASS. sedimentary_clastic's supply 0.1355 already satisfies
u <= 0.4319 on the land-area modal silicate category and carbonate_ph.resolve's
implied-fresh-solution bound; no bracket was widened and no guard relaxed.

ONE THREAD THIS OPENS AND DOES NOT CLOSE: world-bo4n. The bonus is now the ONLY
statement of the closed basin, and it is the sump's mechanism applied to the
whole basin floor. 91.75 per cent of the land area carrying it has runoff above
zero at a median 11.55 mm/yr, so those cells export their salts to the sump
rather than accumulating them; the sump is 1.39 per cent of land against the
bonus's 15.33; and the bonus is unconditional in L, so a leached floor cell
lands on gibbsite and then has 0.8 added to it. It is worth +0.123 on the land
mean and +0.544 over endorheic-dominated cells, and no endorheic-bearing cell
reaches Helvaci's floor without it, 0 of 926. Not folded in here because it is a
FORM change to soil_ph and this row was a mapping fix plus two duplicate
literals; world-l442 and world-i70y were split for the same reason.

ARTIFACTS. soil_report.json, soilmap_T21.txt and land_column_states_T21.txt were
stale before this and remain stale. Nothing CPU-heavy was run, no build, no
model run, no lock_and_run; the divide and the pH numbers are offline
reconstructions plus calls to the shipped soil_ph, and brine_paths.json was NOT
written.

title: pyburn dispatches derived codes on string keys only, so an integer request silently produces nothing
description:
Found while fixing world-2jj3 and left standing there because it is a different
defect: wrong dispatch rather than an unbound name.

pyburn.dataset's per-key loop takes the integer branch when a code is an int --
meta = ilibrary[str(key)] at pyburn.py:1586 -- and does NOT normalise key.
Every derived arm then compares key==str(ucode), which is False for an int, so
the whole if/elif chain falls through and nothing is stored. Measured on the
synthetic raw verify_high_cadence_rescue.py now writes:

  pyburn.dataset(raw, [131,132,259])  ->  {} (no ua, no va, no spd)
  pyburn.dataset(raw, ['131','132','259'])  ->  ua, va, spd

Before world-2jj3's repair this was invisible: the first int key raised
UnboundLocalError and a later one logged the previous variable's shape. It now
reports three NOT COLLECTED lines and returns an empty dataset, which is honest
and still wrong.

advancedDataset is worse and is broken for BOTH key styles. Its docstring's own
example is name-keyed ({'ts':{...},'stf':{...}}), and the slibrary branch
rebinds key to the numeric code before the options lookup reads
variablecodes[key] at pyburn.py:2529, so a name-keyed request raises
KeyError '131'. An int-keyed request gets past that and hits the dispatch above.
So advancedDataset works only for codes that are already in the raw and are
given as ints, which is not what any of its documentation says.

NO LIVE CONSUMER IN THIS TREE. Every project call site passes strings:
continue_exoplasim.py and run_exoplasim.py both build [str(code) for code in ...]
and extract_high_cadence_wind.py's WIND_CODES are string literals. Nothing calls
advancedDataset. So this is a trap for the next caller, not a current failure.

The repair is to normalise the key once at the head of the loop and keep the
caller's original key for the options lookup in advancedDataset.
assignee: pyburn.dataset(raw,[131,132,259]) returns ua, va and spd, advancedDataset accepts the name-keyed request its own docstring shows, and a case in verify_high_cadence_rescue.py holds both.
close_reason: Resolved and committed (7821ebf69, 20c4a8064, 923390a7a). world-hs5z: _resolvekey handles code, string and name in both loops, repaired rather than refused because both docstrings promise all three and the fork is hard; also closed a gap the row did not name, run-time ilibrary rows answering to their code but not their name. world-e9yz: all five arms deleted, settled from outmod.f90 rather than burn7, each being an exact combination of addressable codes; 268/269 were not merely dead but fired and stored rst-rss as icez in m2 s-2. world-k5db: 229 dwmax and 101-107 named from the model's own source, and the outdiag collision guarded at both ends with the Fortran renumber filed as world-2v9z.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
FIXED, AND THE ROW UNDERSTATED WHAT ALREADY WORKED IN advancedDataset.

VERIFIED FIRST, on the synthetic T21 raw verify_high_cadence_rescue.py writes.
Every claim in the row held except one:

  dataset(raw,[131,132,259])       -> {}                  (int keys)
  dataset(raw,["131","132","259"]) -> ua, va, spd          (string codes)
  dataset(raw,["ua","spd"])        -> ua, spd              (names)
  advancedDataset(raw,{'ts':{},'spd':{}})   -> KeyError '139'
  advancedDataset(raw,{'139':{},'259':{}})  -> ts, spd
  advancedDataset(raw,{139:{},259:{}})      -> ts only

THE CORRECTION. The row says advancedDataset "works only for codes that are
already in the raw and are given as ints". It is the other way round: the
STRING CODE is the spelling that works, and it works for both branches. Ints
work for a code in the raw and drop a derived one; names raise before either
branch, on whichever name comes first, which is why the row measured
KeyError '131' and this measured KeyError '139'. The defect is real and the
worked-example is the one thing to correct.

THE REPAIR IS ONE RESOLUTION FOR ALL THREE SPELLINGS. pyburn._resolvekey takes
a request and returns (integer code as a string, metadata); both loops call it
and the branch on type(key)==int is gone from both. advancedDataset keeps the
CALLER's key in `request` and reads variablecodes[request] for the per-variable
options, which is the half the row named.

ONE MORE GAP CLOSED BY THE SAME LINE, and it was this project's own.
slibrary is built from ilibrary once at import, and ilibrary is added to at RUN
TIME -- run_exoplasim.register_energy_diagnostic_codes inserts codes 360-387
and 460-487 that way. So a row added after import answered to its code and not
to its name: two spellings of one request disagreeing, which is the defect this
function exists to remove. _resolvekey falls back to a scan of ilibrary by name
before raising, on the miss path only.

THE CHECK IS AN IDENTITY OVER THE WHOLE TABLE, not over the three codes named
here. The spelling of a request is not an input to any derivation, so all 124
ilibrary entries requested as ints, as string codes and as names must return
the same variables with identical arrays. verify_high_cadence_rescue.py goes
from 13 cases to 20; three of the new ones are this row:

  a code, its string and its name are one request
  advancedDataset reads each variable's options off the caller's key
  a library row added at run time answers to its name too

PROVED ABLE TO FAIL, each against the exact defect it is written for:
  loop head stops normalising      -> FAIL, the integer-code request carries
                                      [] where the string request carries 21
  options read under the resolved  -> FAIL, "the request spelled with the
  code again                          variable names raised KeyError: '139'"
  the name scan goes               -> FAIL, a row added after import is
                                      addressable by one spelling, not both
The advancedDataset case asks its options on `zonal`, which collapses the
longitude axis, so a request that never reached its options has one more
dimension than one that did; a stub dict would pass a call-returns test.

NO SEPARATE VERIFIER. exoplasim/scripts/ is where this belongs and
verify_high_cadence_rescue.py is the file in it that already runs the real
pyburn on a synthetic raw; it is registered under checks: in
config/pipeline.yaml and named in exoplasim/README.md, and a sibling would
need rows in both, which are another session's files right now. Its module
docstring now names the second subject.

RULE 4 NOT OWED, on world-2jj3's precedent and re-checked: pyburn.py is Python,
imported at run time from the editable install, no Fortran parameter and no
translation unit. rebuild_binaries.py --verify: "all 10 binaries current", with
1 uncommitted path under vendor/exoplasim, which is this change.

title: melange is metamorphic to the pH block and shale to the weathering map, and it is 6 per cent of land
description:
Two tables in this project read the same Orogen rock class differently and neither knows about the other.

  pedology/scripts/build_soil.py:PH_GROUP        melange -> metamorphic
  pedology/scripts/brine_paths.py:ROCK_TO_MEYBECK melange -> shale, with a
                                                  RECORDED ARGUMENT for shale

Melange is over 6 per cent of land, so this is not a corner case.

WHY IT BITES NOW. world-jixy replaced the four asserted silicate parent pH
values with sourced base-cation supplies read from Meybeck (1987) through
ROCK_TO_MEYBECK. The metamorphic supply, 0.0423 with bracket [0.031, 0.0638],
is measured on GNEISS AND MICA-SCHIST ALONE. Shale is a different row with a
different bicarbonate yield, and the metamorphic bracket does not cover the
disagreement -- so 6 per cent of land is currently weathered through a supply
measured on rocks the other table says it is not.

Before world-jixy the two tables disagreed about a value nothing sourced, which
made this a naming inconsistency. Now they disagree about a measurement, which
makes it a defect with a number attached.

Do: settle which rock melange is FOR THIS PURPOSE, and note the answer may
differ between the two purposes legitimately -- brine paths care about solute
chemistry and the pH block cares about base-cation supply, and a melange is a
tectonic mixture rather than a rock type, so 'it is both' is a possible and
defensible answer. If it is both, the supply is a mixture and needs a declared
mixing fraction with a bracket, not a single row. What is not defensible is two
tables silently disagreeing.

Then add a check that the two mappings agree, or that each disagreement is
declared with its reason. Both tables are in pedology/scripts and neither reads
the other today.

Also stale and not in scope for the row that found this:
notes/audits/frozen-derived-quantities.md:374 names ph.parent_by_category.carbonate
and now under-describes what that key derives.

Found by the world-jixy agent while sourcing the supplies.
acceptance_criteria: melange resolves to one supply per purpose with a stated reason, or to a declared mixture with a bracket; a check fails when PH_GROUP and ROCK_TO_MEYBECK disagree without a recorded reason.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-howr: the concavity bound needs no delivery phase (the calibration absorbs the level exactly; the bin weights bound the spread), J = 3.4833 against P = 2.2235, DECISIVE, 26 of 195 carved basins movable and none covered by the climate bracket. world-awvh: the tightening does not exist -- lake storage sharpens the overflow's season rather than damping it, the concentrated arm sits on the floor to six decimals, so the bound is ATTAINED and the verdict stands unchanged. world-mddi: three tables read melange and two already agreed; PH_GROUP was falling back on Orogen's origin category against its own chemistry principle. world-5th5: the soda chemistry is right (95.71 per cent of catchment area alkaline) and was being stated about the floor's rock instead of the basin; playa moves to sedimentary_clastic, parent_by_category is derived in every entry, land mean 6.778 to 6.454.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 SETTLED: MELANGE IS SHALE FOR BOTH PURPOSES, AND IT IS A MIXTURE
WHOSE FRACTION NOTHING SIZES. Unstaged in the tree.

BOTH MAPPINGS VERIFIED AGAINST CURRENT SOURCE, and the row's arithmetic
reproduces. PH_GROUP put melange in `metamorphic`, supply 0.0423, bracket
[0.0310, 0.0638] on Meybeck's gneiss-and-mica-schist row alone.
ROCK_TO_MEYBECK reads it as `shale` with the argument recorded 2026-08-16.
Meybeck Table 2C bicarbonate over the sedimentary-carbonate row: shale
580/3195 = 0.1815, gneiss 135/3195 = 0.0423. A FACTOR OF 4.29, and the
metamorphic bracket tops out 2.85x short of it.

A THIRD TABLE EXISTS AND IT AGREES WITH BRINE PATHS. weathering_schemes.yaml's
class_mapping maps melange to rokgem `shale` under BOTH schemes, and says in
its own comment that its reasoning follows ROCK_TO_MEYBECK so that two mappings
of one rock table cannot quietly disagree. Two of three tables read shale; only
the pH bin read metamorphic.

THE ANSWER TO "WHAT IS A MELANGE, FOR EACH PURPOSE" IS THAT THERE ARE NOT TWO
PURPOSES. The row allowed that solute chemistry and base-cation supply could
legitimately differ. They cannot here: pedogenesis.yaml's supplies ARE Meybeck's
bicarbonate column normalised by the carbonate row, and its own comment says the
mapping follows ROCK_TO_MEYBECK wherever that answers the question. One column,
one table, one question in three vocabularies. So the divergence was not a
purpose difference; it was PH_GROUP falling back on Orogen's `category` field,
which says `metamorphic` because a melange is metamorphic BY ORIGIN. PH_GROUP's
own principle is chemistry, not origin, and it already proves it: quartzite is
Orogen-category metamorphic and sits in `igneous_felsic` there because it
weathers like a quartz sand. Melange was the one place the label won.

WHAT OROGEN PUTS IN A MELANGE, read from the generator. `js/lithology.js` names
the class "Subduction melange (block-in-matrix)" and assigns it in ONE basement
branch to `inForearc`, with the comment "The forearc is everything trenchward of
the arc band: accretionary prism, forearc basin, serpentinite... at ~15 km cells
the prism proper cannot be separated from the forearc basin, so this is the
whole province." No cover class overlays a forearc, so the exposed class is that
basement. Prism and basin are greywacke, argillite and clastic fill by volume,
which is Meybeck's shale; serpentinite is Meybeck's peridotite row.

SO IT IS A MIXTURE, AND THE MIXING FRACTION IS A PROPERTY THE GENERATOR DOES NOT
HAVE. One branch, no internal division, and the generator's own comment says the
constituents are unresolvable at its cell size. NOTHING SIZES IT, so nothing is
invented: the bracket spans the serpentinite share's FULL range [0, 1].

  ph.base_cation_supply_by_category.melange          0.1815
  ph.base_cation_supply_bracket_by_category.melange  [0.1408, 0.3052]

Floor is an all-serpentinite melange on Meybeck's peridotite bicarbonate;
ceiling is GEM-CO2's shale class, the same source pair every other entry is
bracketed on. THE BRACKET IS WIDE-BY-CONSTRUCTION AND SAYS SO, and it is a
different kind of object from the four above it, which span two readings of one
rock. But the honest outcome is that the unsized mixture COSTS LITTLE in this
column: peridotite's bicarbonate is 450 ueq/l against shale's 580, so the whole
[0,1] range spans 22 per cent, against the 4.29 the metamorphic reading was
wrong by. The mixture nobody can size matters five times less than the
