assignment that was wrong.

The VALUE is the shale row alone and not an outcrop-weighted mixture, which is
the one departure from this block's stated rule, with the reason stated:
Meybeck's outcrop percentages say what fraction of EARTH is peridotite, not what
fraction of a forearc is serpentinite, so weighting by them answers a different
question. The share is carried entirely by the bracket.

ONE ENDMEMBER EXCLUDED, WITH EVIDENCE. A real melange carries limestone blocks
and admitting a carbonate endmember puts the ceiling at 1.0, which is a bracket
that decides nothing. Meybeck's misc_metamorphic row is what that reading looks
like -- Ca + Mg 1740 against HCO3 1730, a near-exact carbonate balance, which is
carbonate dissolution and not silicate weathering -- and it WAS this class's row
until 2026-08-16 and was rejected on exactly that arithmetic. The bracket is
over the silicate province the generator describes.

MELANGE GETS ITS OWN pH CATEGORY rather than joining `sedimentary_clastic`.
That category's 0.1355 is the shale and sandstone rows weighted by EARTH'S
outcrop percentages, which is a statement about Earth's clastic exposure and
says nothing about a forearc; it would have passed the check while diluting
melange with a sandstone weight nothing here justifies.

MEASURED, on the offline reconstruction that reproduces the shipped soilmap
(land mean 6.717 before, exactly world-jixy's figure), and re-checked through
the SHIPPED code path, which returns 6.735 after. 1639 land cells.

  weighting                       land    dry   wetq   melange share of land
  cos(lat) over land cells       6.717  8.278  5.215   9.26%   before
                                 6.735  8.278  5.227           after
  cos(lat) * land fraction       6.763  8.405  5.256   6.11%   before
                                 6.778  8.405  5.266           after

BOTH ARE QUOTED because the two conventions disagree about the melange share
itself, 9.3 per cent against 6.1, and the land-AREA one is what the mesh reports
directly and what world_state.json carries. The row's "over 6 per cent" is the
land-area figure and is right; the 9.3 is an artifact of weighting a cell with a
sliver of land like a full one.

508 cells change at the soilmap's own three decimals; 77 move more than 0.1 pH,
17 more than 0.25, 7 more than 0.5, one more than 1.0, largest +1.125. The 254
zero-runoff cells do not move at all to four decimals, because a supply is
absent from the form at L = 0. Melange reaches 738 cells covering 52.3 per cent
of the land area, but only 45 of them are more than half melange, which is why
the mean moves so little.

A FACTOR OF 4.29 IN THE SUPPLY OF SIX PER CENT OF THE LAND IS WORTH 0.015 pH ON
THE LAND MEAN. That is the form saturating, not the defect being small: a wet
cell is on gibbsite and a dry one on calcite whatever the supply is, so the
supply only decides where the crossing sits. Worth knowing before the next
supply is argued over. The whole unsized mixture is worth a third of that again:
the bracket ends put the land mean at 6.774 and 6.793 against 6.778.

THE CHECK, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A MATCHED LITERAL. New module
`pedology/scripts/lithology_map.py` now HOLDS both tables -- build_soil.py and
brine_paths.py import them from it -- plus a declared-disagreement table and the
check. `build_soil.py:soil_ph` calls `check_or_die` before it builds a soil map,
so a mapping edit cannot reach a soilmap unexamined, and `python
pedology/scripts/lithology_map.py` prints the table and the verdict.

The rule: for each Orogen class, the supply its Meybeck row implies must sit
inside the bracket its pH category declares, or the class must appear in
DECLARED_DISAGREEMENTS with the argument for reading it two ways. It also
compares weathering_schemes.yaml's two class_mappings against ROCK_TO_MEYBECK
through a stated rokgem-to-Meybeck row equivalence. THREE WAYS TO FAIL, all
exercised:
  * revert PH_GROUP alone -> names melange, the factor, and the bracket it is
    outside of;
  * revert BOTH literals so they agree on metamorphic -> the third table catches
    it, which is what makes this more than matching two literals;
  * declare a class that has come to agree -> fails as a stale licence.
The third fired on my own first draft: two gkwm exceptions I wrote were
unnecessary because GKWM has no felsic-volcanic class either, so it agrees with
Meybeck's single volcanic row by both lacking the distinction.

FIVE CLASSES ARE DECLARED APART, and only one of them is open.
  arc_andesite, rift_bimodal -- Meybeck has ONE volcanic row and cannot resolve
    andesite from basalt; GEM-CO2 can and puts it at 0.0725, which IS
    igneous_felsic's own bracket top. One source resolving what the other
    cannot, not two answers. weathering_schemes.yaml splits it the same way.
  evaporite -- the pH supply is 1 BY CONSTRUCTION, so no row is being read.
    Meybeck's halite row is on another basis entirely: cation sum 6.19 TIMES the
    carbonate row's, which is not a fraction of anything.
  water -- not land, no row.
  playa_clastic -- OPEN. See below.

THE SWEEP FOUND A SECOND INSTANCE OF THIS EXACT DEFECT AND IT IS BIGGER:
world-5th5. PH_GROUP puts playa_clastic in the evaporite bin, asserting supply
1.0 and the soda buffer, while ROCK_TO_MEYBECK reads it as shale at 0.1815 with
the recorded argument that playa mud is detrital fill and mapping it to an
evaporite begs the question -- an argument that applies unchanged to the pH bin.
That is a factor of 5.5 on 13.9 per cent of the land area, larger than melange
on both counts. And every playa cell is endorheic by construction (Orogen
assigns the class only under the basin_fill cover rule), so the soda bin and
ph.endorheic_alkalinity_bonus are two statements of one closed basin. NOT fixed
here because it is not a mapping fix: it decides which buffer playa mud reaches
at zero export, which is world-i70y's question, and it moves the supply AND the
dry end on an eighth of the land. It is declared in DECLARED_DISAGREEMENTS
naming world-5th5, so the check names it rather than blessing it, and the stale-
declaration rule deletes that licence the moment the two agree.

ALSO DONE: notes/audits/frozen-derived-quantities.md:374 now names
ph.parent_by_category (every entry but `evaporite`) and calcite_buffer_ph with
its bracket, and says that the key names the buffer a category reaches at zero
export rather than a fresh-parent pH -- so the silicate entries derive too and
the key carries no lithology contrast at all. That is
ph.base_cation_supply_by_category, which is declared and sourced and is NOT in
that class.

STALE, AND LEFT STALE. soil_report.json, soilmap_T21.txt and
land_column_states_T21.txt were already stale before this and remain so; nothing
CPU-heavy was run and no build or model run was started. The measurements above
are all offline reconstruction plus one call to the shipped soil_ph.

NOT DONE, REPORTED FOR A DECISION: the per-commit gate. The check is a static
read and belongs in scripts/smoke_test.py, but that file is contested, so the
function is written and tested and handed over rather than inserted.

title: export_carve_list evaluates a square root on annual discharge and the second arm does not exist
description:
hydrography/scripts/export_carve_list.py:241 evaluates Q**0.5 on an ANNUAL discharge. The square root is concave, so the annual evaluation is biased HIGH against the mean of the per-bin evaluations, by Jensen. This is the same class as world-cpke and world-bpb5 and it is the one member of the class that can be neither fixed nor bracketed today.

WHY NEITHER. hydrography/config/land_water_ledger.yaml declares seasonal_phase_of_catchment_delivery UNREPRESENTABLE. A per-bin discharge needs to know when in the year a catchment delivers its water, and this pipeline does not carry that, so the second arm of the bracket cannot be computed at all. Bracketing a quantity requires two arms; one arm and an unrepresentable other is not a bracket, and inventing the phase would be the tuned-value failure wearing a seasonal costume.

The site is DECLARED with that citation, so a reader meets the limitation where the arithmetic is rather than only in a ledger. What remains open is the disposition: this is currently an undeclared model-form error in the carve list, which is an input to a generation, and rule 7 makes a generation the thing everything below is reconstructed from.

Do, in order: (1) size the error without the phase -- the concavity gives a bound from the discharge distribution's spread alone, which does not need to know WHEN the water arrives, only how uneven it is across bins; if that bound is small the row closes on it. (2) If it is not small, decide whether the carve list can carry a bracketed discharge at all, since a carve verdict is a decision and a bracketed decision is two carve lists. (3) Only if neither settles it, establish what it would take to represent the delivery phase, which is a change to what hydrography computes rather than to how this line evaluates.

Do not close this by making the line per-bin: that is what cannot be done.

Found by the world-bpb5 sweep, which was looking for the third caller of a different defect.
acceptance_criteria: The concavity error in the carve list's discharge term is bounded from the bin spread without needing the delivery phase, and either shown small enough to ignore with the argument recorded, or carried as a declared model-form error whose effect on the carve verdict is stated.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-howr: the concavity bound needs no delivery phase (the calibration absorbs the level exactly; the bin weights bound the spread), J = 3.4833 against P = 2.2235, DECISIVE, 26 of 195 carved basins movable and none covered by the climate bracket. world-awvh: the tightening does not exist -- lake storage sharpens the overflow's season rather than damping it, the concentrated arm sits on the floor to six decimals, so the bound is ATTAINED and the verdict stands unchanged. world-mddi: three tables read melange and two already agreed; PH_GROUP was falling back on Orogen's origin category against its own chemistry principle. world-5th5: the soda chemistry is right (95.71 per cent of catchment area alkaline) and was being stated about the floor's rock instead of the basin; playa moves to sedimentary_clastic, parent_by_category is derived in every entry, land mean 6.778 to 6.454.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
VERIFIED, BOUNDED, AND SETTLED AT STEP 2. The row is true as written; nothing in
it needed correcting.

THE DEFECT, against the files. export_carve_list.py:incision_retain evaluates
cut = coefficient * erodibility * slope**n * Q**m with INCISION_EXPONENT = 0.5
on the ANNUAL overflow, and the site already carried the declaration the
world-bpb5 sweep left. land_water_ledger.yaml lists
seasonal_phase_of_catchment_delivery under `absences` and the text is current:
the path computes catchment runoff as the annual mean of P - E and cannot phase
it, because per-bin clamping would count the wet season's supply twice. So
there is no per-bin discharge and the repair that fixed the evaporation
interval is unavailable. Confirmed.

STEP 1 GAVE A BOUND, AND THE BOUND CHANGED WHAT THE ABSENCE COSTS. Two results,
neither of which needs the phase.

  THE LEVEL IS ABSORBED BY THE CALIBRATION, EXACTLY. Write the truth as
  mean(sqrt Q) = phi * sqrt(Q_annual). `cut` is linear in the coefficient and
  linear in Q**m, and calibrate_coefficient SOLVES the coefficient on every run
  from this same discharge field against Earth's standing-basin density. So a
  phi common to every basin is met by a coefficient of exactly coefficient/phi.
  Measured on canonical-10m-carve1: scaling every discharge to phi = 0.9, 0.5
  and 0.2871 and re-solving returns 299.3884, 538.8992 and 938.5720 against the
  shipped 269.4496, which is coefficient/phi to 2.4e-8, the bisection's own
  resolution; with the coefficient set outright the retain vector matches to
  3.3e-16 and no basin changes class.

  THE SPREAD IS BOUNDED BY THE BIN WEIGHTS ALONE. An overflow is never negative
  and the cycle has the climatology's twelve bins at lib/climatology.py's
  weights, lightest 0.082418. The most uneven admissible discharge puts the
  whole year in the lightest bin: phi in [w_min**(1-m), 1] = [0.2871, 1], so
  the ratio between two basins' phi is within J = 3.4833 and, with the
  population level pinned by the calibration, a basin's cut moves at most a
  factor J either side of the class boundary.

IT IS NOT SMALL ENOUGH TO IGNORE. J = 3.4833 against P = 2.2235, the Poisson
bracket on Earth's count of 15, on sweep_size_floor's own pre-declared
criterion: DECISIVE. It is not the largest lever here either -- the size floor
on the Earth sample moves the same coefficient by 56.3 and is reported beside
the verdict already.

STEP 2 IS SETTLED WITHOUT COSTING A GENERATION, and this is the row's answer. A
bracketed discharge here would be a bracket of ZERO WIDTH, because the second
arm is the first one: the calibration removes any common discount exactly. So
it is not two carve lists and not two generations. What survives is the
cross-basin spread, and an arm for that would have to assign a different phi per
basin, which IS the unrepresentable delivery phase. Step 3 was not reached.

DOES ANY BASIN CHANGE SIDE. On the finished-depression basis, the basis the
coefficient is solved on, with x for the annual cut/depth: 416 basins overflow,
356 cut, 60 keep some rim. 99 are MOVABLE -- x inside (1/J, J) -- of which 67
currently cut and 32 currently stand. 289 hold cut and 28 hold standing under
every admissible delivery phase. x runs 0.23 / 6.65 / 70.8 at p5 / p50 / p95,
so the exposure is a minority of a minority. Against the verdict as exported,
union over the three arms: 26 of the 195 CARVED basins are movable, 24 of the
41 marginal, 49 of the 4,421 preserved. NONE of the 195 carved basins is in the
climate bracket -- 0 of the 290 bracketed basins carve, by construction of the
intersection rule -- so these 26 are an exposure the existing bracket does not
already cover, which is why the flag is per basin and not a count.

WHAT THE SITE NOW CARRIES. incision_retain's declaration keeps the absence and
its citation and gains the two results above. seasonal_concavity computes the
bound in the run that takes the verdict, from the climatology's own bin
weights, over every arm; method.seasonal_concavity goes in the sidecar with the
call, the assumptions and the counts, and every basin record carries
seasonal_concavity_movable, false being the strong statement. The verdict
itself is UNCHANGED and deliberately: the raw concavity is one-sided but the
calibration makes what reaches the verdict two-sided -- 32 standing basins
exposed to being cut against 67 cut basins exposed to standing -- so taking one
side would be a preference dressed as a bound.

THE CHECKS, in export_carve_list.py --selftest, which needs no build and no
climatology. Right answers fixed in advance: identical bins evaluate to the
annual value exactly and uneven bins strictly below it; the bound is attained
by the whole year in the lightest bin and never breached; a common discount is
absorbed by the coefficient exactly while an uncompensated one is not; and the
claim the whole disposition rests on -- under an admissible per-basin phi with
the coefficient re-solved, no basin outside the band changes class. 20 checks
pass, and the three new ones were each demonstrated to fire on an injected
defect: m set to 1, the band narrowed by 1.6x, and the cut/depth ratio scaled.

MEASUREMENT: canonical-10m-carve1, 4,657 basins, baseline_regular_climatology.nc,
coefficient 269.4496, the verdict that produced canonical-10m-carve2. Recorded
in hydrography/notes/carve-verdict-interval.md with its evidence.

WHAT WOULD TIGHTEN IT is a separate row: the overflow is catchment delivery,
whose phase is the absence, PLUS the lake's own surface flux, whose phase is
representable and already binned in surface_water.nc. Bounding them separately
is strictly narrower, and it bites -- the catchment term is a median 2.06x the
overflow on this population.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
FOLLOW-UP: THE BOUND IS ATTAINED, SO IT IS ALSO THE BEST ONE AVAILABLE.

The verdict above left one thread open -- world-awvh, whether the lake's own
per-bin surface flux narrows J below P. It does not, and the row is resolved
with the measurement on it. Storage is why: `lake_balance.solve_periodic`
carries it, and a lake drawn below spill refills before it spills, so storage
SHARPENS the overflow's season rather than damping it. Put a year's delivery in
the lightest bin and the overflow sits exactly on w_min**(1-m) whatever the
lake's own swing.

That upgrades this row's result rather than changing it. J = 3.4833 against
P = 2.2235, DECISIVE, and the 26 carved basins of 195 stay movable -- but the
bound is now known to be ATTAINED rather than merely valid, so there is no
narrower one to be had from anything this pipeline carries. The premise the
bound rested on is also now an identity rather than an assumption: under the
delivery this pipeline represents an overflowing basin sits at spill through the
whole cycle, so its periodic annual overflow equals the spill-level Q to 1.0000.

Also added, because the disposition depends on it: scripts/smoke_test.py now
holds `export_carve_list.LEDGER_ABSENCES_RELIED_ON` to a key under `absences:`
in the ledger. Bounding rather than correcting is a choice that rests on the
delivery phase being unrepresentable, and closing that absence must fail the
gate at this site rather than leave the declaration standing and untrue.

title: Three declared constants parse as strings, because YAML 1.1 wants a sign in the exponent
description:
YAML 1.1's float resolver requires a SIGN in the exponent. '5.0e4' does not match it and resolves to a STRING; '5.0e+4' resolves to a float. PyYAML's safe_load implements 1.1, so three declared constants in this tree are strings today:

  biosphere/config/abiotic_nutrients.yaml:638
    adequacy.residence_time_earth_years              '5.0e4'            str
  biosphere/config/abiotic_nutrients.yaml:639
    adequacy.residence_time_bracket_earth_years      ['5.0e4','1.15e5'] list of str
  pedology/config/outgassing.yaml:36
    earth_silicate_co2_consumption_mol_per_year      '1.17e13'          str

WHAT IS AND IS NOT BROKEN TODAY. abiotic_nutrient_ledger.py floats the VALUE where it reads it, so the adequacy test itself is right. The two BRACKET ends are not floated anywhere: they go into the report as strings, and any comparison against them raises rather than returning a wrong answer. The outgassing constant needs checking the same way.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THESE THREE. A string that looks like a number is the shape that survives every static pass: it reads correctly in the file, it round-trips through the report, and it fails only at the moment something compares against it. world-nfer's tree-wide bracket check had to coerce numeric strings deliberately to avoid reporting an exponent form as a bracket violation, which means the check is currently absorbing this defect rather than surfacing it.

Do: write the three with a signed exponent, or quote them and float at the point of read, whichever this project prefers -- and say which, because the choice should be one rule rather than three decisions. Then add a check that a declared numeric key resolves to a number, which is a right answer available in advance and which world-nfer's coercion currently hides. That check belongs beside the bracket one and should let it stop coercing.

Sweep the whole tree for the pattern rather than fixing these three: any unsigned exponent in any yaml is the same defect whether or not a consumer floats it today.

Found by the world-nfer sweep, which was looking for brackets and not for this.
acceptance_criteria: Every declared numeric scalar in every yaml resolves to a number; one stated rule covers how exponents are written; a check fails when a declared numeric key resolves to a string, and world-nfer's bracket check no longer coerces.
close_reason: Resolved and committed (11c4f189f). Swept every yaml in the tree, 193 files: exactly the four scalars the row named and nothing else. Three keys, three different findings -- the residence-time value latent because it is floated at the read, its bracket LIVE because both ends reach the report as text and any comparison raises, and the outgassing constant worse than latent with no consumer at all, weathering_fluxes.py having restated the same figure as a Python literal at five sites. One rule adopted: a declared numeric is written so the parser resolves it, rejecting quote-and-float-at-read because it puts the fact in two places. check_declared_numerics_resolve_to_numbers uses quoting as the statement of intent so there is no exception list, and the bracket check has stopped coercing numeric strings.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Swept every yaml in the tree outside vendor/, .venv/, .claude/worktrees/, references/ and archive/ -- 193 files, of which 37 are the config/*.yaml and */config/*.yaml declaration population. Four unquoted scalars resolved to strings, all three keys the row names and no others: abiotic_nutrients.yaml adequacy.residence_time_earth_years (LATENT -- abiotic_nutrient_ledger.py floats it at the read), its residence_time_bracket_earth_years pair (LIVE -- copied verbatim into the ledger report, so both ends reach it as text and any comparison raises), and outgassing.yaml requirement.earth_silicate_co2_consumption_mol_per_year (LATENT, and read by nothing at all: weathering_fluxes.py restated the same Gaillardet figure as a 11.7e12 literal at four sites). exoplasim/analysis/arms/*.yaml are gitignored per-arm copies generated from config/planet.yaml, so they carry no declaration the glob misses.

RULE: a declared numeric is written so the PARSER resolves it -- signed exponent, decimal point in the mantissa. Quote-and-float-at-the-read was rejected: it puts the fact in two places and asks every future consumer to remember. Argued in docs/src/practice/conventions.md under Documents and numbers, one line in CLAUDE.md.

smoke_test.py:check_declared_numerics_resolve_to_numbers refuses any unquoted scalar in the declaration files that float() accepts and yaml.safe_load resolved to a string. Quoting is the statement of intent, which is what keeps contract_unit: "1" and form: "0.025" out of it with no exception list. Six fixtures and five controls, both directions. _number has stopped coercing.

title: Acquire the observational support a saturated-fraction closure would need, or take WET-12's reduced form
description:
world-34mx established that WET-2's extent is a PARTITION of five classes and that one of them, the saturated mineral class, has no source: the TOPMODEL saturated-area closure is withdrawn (hydrography/config/topographic_index.yaml carries closure.status withdrawn) and nothing publishes a fraction. The gate now refuses on that rather than on a support mismatch, and no open row covers getting the class back.

TWO ROUTES, and the gate admits only these two.

(a) A NEW SCORE WHOSE SUPPORT RESOLVES THE GAIN. hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 7 owns the route and states the condition as support rather than as instrument: enough grid cells carrying observations that a gain of a few thousandths of an AUC sits above the cells' own scatter. Two continents of bores gave 34 and 37 cells, which is why the declared score missed. More cells is one way there; an areal saturation or inundation observation in place of point depths is another. The criterion and the disposition of a miss must be DECLARED BEFORE the observations are in hand -- that is what was done last time and it is why the withdrawal was a clean outcome rather than an argument. A depth field also needs a regime, which is GW-24 and MIN-6.

(b) A REDUCED FORM UNDER WET-12, stating what dropping the class costs in claims. The gate refuses a class declared absent without both absent_because and licensed_by, so this route cannot be taken silently.

A CONSTRAINT ON EITHER: state what a downstream ledger does with a bracketed class BEFORE any share is written. f_grad is a convention bracket and a consumer takes both arms or neither, so a half-declared class propagates as a silent single arm.

Note for whoever takes (b): wet-12's recorded reduced form currently names the TOPMODEL saturated fraction as the part that forfeits least. That fraction is the withdrawn one, so the recorded reasoning is circular and needs redoing. notes/external-model-survey.md:357 carries the same claim.

Discovered from world-34mx.
acceptance_criteria: Either an observation set is acquired whose support resolves the declared gain, with the criterion fixed beforehand, or WET-12's reduced form is declared with absent_because and licensed_by and with the downstream ledger's treatment of a bracketed class stated first.

title: Penman is evaluated once on annual-mean air on the groundwater path
description:
hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater.py:171 calls climate_fields(config) with no bin_index, so the Penman evapotranspiration on the groundwater path is evaluated ONCE on annual-mean air. That is the same defect carve_verdict.py and surface_water.py were already fixed for, in the same component, left on the third caller.

Penman is nonlinear in temperature through the saturation vapour pressure curve, which is convex, so the annual-mean evaluation is biased low against the per-bin mean in the same direction the world-cpke measurement established for the weathering law. The size here is not known and should not be assumed from that one: the weathering gates select wet and warm cells where the seasonal swing is smallest, and the groundwater path has no such gate, so it samples the full 57 K land seasonal range rather than 3 to 4 K.

The repair already exists and needs no new machinery: climate_fields(config, bin_index=k) is an existing parameter and hydrography/scripts/surface_water.py:591 is the working template for the per-bin loop.

Do: evaluate per bin and combine, measure the correction in the units the groundwater consumer reads, and state whether it is inside or outside the instrument's own scatter. If the binned arrays turn out not to be in scope where the call sits -- which is what blocked the pedology and exoplasim rows under world-cpke -- then bracket it in the report the consumer reads rather than leaving it silent, and say which of the two it is.

Found by the world-cpke sweep, which was not looking for it and could not fix it because another change was in flight in this component.
acceptance_criteria: The groundwater path evaluates Penman per bin and combines, or declares a bracket in its report; either way the correction is measured in consumer units and compared against the instrument's own scatter.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-bpb5 (bd7b823b6): Penman evaluated per bin on the groundwater path; the predicted convex sign was wrong and the measurement disagreed on 15.5 per cent of scored land; median shift +0.090 m is inside the lambda bracket but 352714 regions cross from pinned-at-surface to a solved depth. world-i70y (f7b96b08c): the pH runs between two buffers, the dry end derived from this planet's pCO2 at 8.1628 rather than Earth's 8.2. world-jixy (afcb6ab9c): the base-cation source was already in the tree twice, Meybeck 1987 extracted and Amiotte Suchet 1995 vendored; the 2.32 requirement closes on the whole bracket at ratio 7.38, and the four silicate parent pH values were deleted rather than moved because an affine encoding cannot carry a sourced supply.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
VERIFIED AND FIXED, with one row correction and one mechanism correction.

THE ROW IS TRUE AS WRITTEN on the defect itself. build_groundwater.py:171 took
sw.climate_fields(config) with no bin_index, and the fifth element of that
tuple is cv.penman_open_water on annual-mean air; it reaches the solver as
ET_max at line 501 and nowhere else on this path. climate_fields(config,
bin_index=k) is an existing parameter and surface_water.py:591 is a working
per-bin loop, both confirmed against source. carve_verdict.py and
surface_water.py really were fixed.

THE BINNED ARRAYS ARE IN SCOPE, so this is a fix and not a bracket. Nothing
here is consumed inside a `with nc.Dataset` block: recharge_field opens and
closes its own handle, and cv.bin_mean_open_water already owns the per-bin
Penman loop. It now reads that instead, taking land_albedo from the staged
field the tuple was already returning and discarding.

THE MECHANISM IN THE ROW IS WRONG, and it matters for the sign. Penman is not
convex in temperature. At fixed radiation, humidity and wind it is convex only
below about 270 K; above that the delta/(delta+gamma) energy weighting
saturates and the composite is CONCAVE. Measured on the real climatology, the
bin mean falls BELOW the annual evaluation on 15.5% of scored land, and those
cells are the warm ones: mean 19.6 C with a 22 K seasonal swing, against -7.8 C
and 70 K where the bin mean is above. The dominant term is not the vapour
pressure curve at all but the RECTIFIERS -- max(net_radiation, 0) and
max(es - e_air, 0) -- which is the shape world-cpke identified as making this
class large rather than second order. carve_verdict.py's own _INTERVAL_BRACKET
comment already says so and names the numbers.

PREDICTED SIGN, stated before measuring: bin mean at or above the annual
evaluation everywhere, from convexity. THE MEASUREMENT DISAGREED on 15.5% of
land, for the reason above.

MEASURED, on baseline_regular_climatology.nc against canonical-10m-carve2,
per land region through the export/ExoPlaSim join the consumer uses, over the
3,441,046 regions where the local sink balance gives a positive depth under
both arms. ET_max land median 553 against 530 mm/yr (this world's 182.8-day
year); total land ET capacity 1.175x. The per-cell ratio is 1.005 at p25, 1.094
at p50, 9.55 at p95.

IN CONSUMER UNITS. The artifact already states the local-sink identity,
d = lambda ln(ET_max A / supply), so a ratio f is a depth shift of lambda ln f
exactly and no second solve is needed. At the configured lambda of 1.0 m that
is +0.090 m on the median depth and +2.26 m at the 95th percentile, against a
median local-sink depth of 2.83 m.

AGAINST THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN SCATTER, AND THE MEDIAN IS INSIDE IT. The lambda
bracket groundwater.yaml already sweeps, [0.5, 2.0], multiplies the same depth
by four -- 1.42 to 5.67 m on this median -- and the Gleeson permeability sigma
the artifact's caveat carries is 1.5 to 2.5 orders of magnitude. A +0.090 m
median shift is 3.2% of the depth and roughly thirty times inside the lambda
bracket. THE TAIL AND THE PINNING ARE NOT INSIDE IT: +2.26 m at p95 is 75% of
the local depth there, and 352,714 regions, 8.8% of land with recharge, cross
from "the sink cannot take this cell's recharge" to "it can" -- the table
leaves the surface, which moves at_surface and the seepage a pinned cell
returns rather than shading a depth.

WHY THE BIN MEAN IS THE SHIPPED ARM AND NOT ONE END OF A BRACKET. Two separate
reasons, both on the artifact. The sink is E(d) = ET_max exp(-d/lambda),
nonlinear in the depth and LINEAR in ET_max; a steady-state solve holds d fixed
through the year, so the annual mean of ET_max is the only input the solver can
take and the bin mean is that mean. And the evaporating body is the ground, not
a lake: the seasonal heat storage that makes the annual evaluation defensible
for a deep water body is a ground heat flux of a few W/m2 against a net
radiation cycle an order larger. Both arms are still computed and the spread
goes on groundwater_report.json as `evaporation_interval`, with the sign fact,
the ratio percentiles, the depth shift at three lambdas, and the unpinned count.

ALSO FIXED IN THE SAME PATH. measure_carve_effect (GW-4) read the annual arm
from the same tuple, so it measured the groundwater term against the OTHER end
of cv._INTERVAL_BRACKET from the verdict it claims to be moving; it now reads
the bin mean. cv.bin_mean_open_water gained `clip_at_zero` (default False, so
every existing caller is bit-identical) because the floor belongs to the
consumer and not to the estimator -- a lake can condense, a groundwater sink
cannot run backwards -- and build_groundwater asks for it; on this climatology
no bin is negative anywhere and the two compositions agree exactly, which is a
fact about one climatology and not about the function. The ET_max diagnostic
printed mm per 365.25 days, which is Earth's year and twice this world's; it
now goes through lib/orbit.

SWEPT, hydrography/ only. One more genuine instance:
export_carve_list.py:241 evaluates Q**0.5 on an ANNUAL discharge. The power is
concave, so a seasonally delivered overflow is credited with more cutting than
its season supports. It is NOT fixable and NOT bracketable: Q is built from
catchment runoff, and land_water_ledger.yaml declares
`seasonal_phase_of_catchment_delivery` unrepresentable, so the second arm does
not exist and inventing one would be a term computed from a quantity that
cannot carry it. Declared at the site with that citation. The evaporation
inside Q is already bracketed by cv._INTERVAL_BRACKET and both ends are run.
Everything else in hydrography/ is clear: only four scripts open a climatology,
and the surviving annual reads are either linear, on a time-invariant field
(lsm), or the deliberately annual runoff the ledger argues for.

THE CHECK, to be inserted by whoever holds scripts/smoke_test.py. A sibling of
"no nonlinear function is evaluated on a naive time mean", same two halves:
a LINT that fails a module which takes climate_fields with no bin_index and
never reaches a per-bin evaluation anywhere (this fires on build_groundwater.py
exactly as it stood, and is silent on both legitimate shapes), and a FIXTURE on
the real penman_open_water with the control from the existing check -- identical
bins must agree exactly under even and uneven weights -- plus a curvature
identity checked in BOTH directions, since the leading Jensen term is
(f''/2f) dT^2 and that coefficient must hold still as dT shrinks, positive on a
cold dry column and negative on a warm humid one; and a rectifier arm on a
radiation swing that crosses the zero clamp. Demonstrated to fire on five
distinct injected defects -- the annual-only caller, the radiation rectifier
removed, the deficit rectifier removed, the saturation curve linearised, and
delta frozen constant -- and to pass on the tree. Code handed to the caller.

STALE: nothing new. No water_table.nc exists for any build, and all eight
hydrography/analysis/groundwater_*.json carry source_build precarve-craton on
the bootstrap climatology, so they were already superseded under rule 7.
smoke_test.py passes except for a pedology bracket row this work did not touch.

title: The design flux instrument now refuses on cold_extreme_cap, and that is a declaration decision
description:
world-m61p removed band_amplification_sign, which was neither necessary nor sufficient for the property it stood in for. With it gone the projection scores 0.7775 to 1.0075, drops 41 of 134 candidates, and then REFUSES on the declared cold_extreme_cap of 0.05. That refusal was always there and was hidden behind the broken guard.

The cap is not reachable on this world. The smallest cold-extreme land fraction any scored candidate reaches is 0.117, more than twice the cap. At f0 = 0.945 it is 0.247 -- and f0 is where the projection IS the measured baseline field, so that number is a MEASUREMENT and not a projection. A quarter of this world's land has a coldest bin below -40 C.

So the question is not the projection any more. Either 0.05 is the wrong cap for this terrain, or this terrain is wrong for a 0.05 cap, and that is a declaration decision rather than an arithmetic one. It is why world-m61p did not add the cap to CHOOSABLE_REFUSALS: a refusal ground is a declared thing and choosing one after seeing which candidates it eliminates is exactly the shape the fixed-thresholds convention forbids.

For diagnosis only, with the cap lifted, the uncapped comfort winner is 0.91 at 0.658 and f0 = 0.945 scores 0.620. Those are not a recommendation; they are what the field looks like without the cap.

Do: decide what the cold-extreme cap is FOR. If it encodes a habitability claim, say whose and against what, and whether a super-Earth around a mid-K dwarf at this obliquity is expected to meet it. If it was a placeholder, replace it with a sourced one or record it as a declared preference, which is an input and is meant to stay put. Either way the decision precedes the next flux derivation, because design_flux.json cannot be regenerated until this is settled.
acceptance_criteria: cold_extreme_cap carries a stated purpose and a source or an explicit declared-preference disposition; design_flux.json is regenerated and check_consistency passes on it.
close_reason: Settled by the author 2026-08-30 and committed (5148a930d, and the regenerated artifact). The cap stands as a recorded unmet preference; the flux stays chosen at 0.945, the value the comfort score favours; cold_extreme_cap_admits_no_candidate is a choosable ground because its minimum is over the whole scored range and no run at any flux moves it. The reopen condition is declared beside the ground: a future carve that removes cold-extreme land, or a re-declared cap. check_consistency's design-flux rows all clear.

title: The declared pH parent spacing is 1.80 where the paper's two findings require 2.80
description:
Under world-l442's relaxation form the parent value is the only place lithology enters the modelled soil pH, so the SPACING between parents carries the paper's lithology signal entirely. Slessarev et al. (2016) reports two things about that signal, and together they bound the spacing in an inequality that the leaching slope and the leaching term both cancel out of:

  the carbonate deviation survives     while f = exp(-s*L) >= 0.457
  the modal clastic reaches a one-pH   while f <= 0.294
  gibbsite mode

Both can hold only if (carbonate - G) / (clastic - G) >= 2.80, with G the gibbsite buffer. pedogenesis.yaml's declared parents give 1.80.

NO SLOPE FIXES THIS. That is what makes it a defect in the parent values rather than in the leaching term: s and L are absent from the inequality. world-l442's pre-registered bracket derivation failed for exactly this reason -- its upper end from the deviation gave 0.90 and its lower end from the bimodality gave 2.50, and the falsification condition written down before the sweep fired. The surviving bracket rests on the deviation alone, and the config records that it is one-sided.

WHY THIS IS NEW INFORMATION. pedogenesis.yaml's comment on the parent values used to say no source here sizes them. These two findings now do, jointly, and the declared set falls short. So the parents move from unsourced to sourced-and-contradicted, which is a different disposition and a stronger one.

Do: establish which parent values satisfy the spacing requirement while remaining defensible as fresh-parent pH, and whether the shortfall sits in the carbonate end, the clastic end, or the buffer between them. Note the third structural obstacle world-l442 measured, which this does not fix: 254 cells, 20.6 per cent of land area, have zero runoff, so L = 0 and the parent value reaches the soilmap unmodified there whatever the spacing is. That is world-i70y.

Evidence: the arithmetic is in pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml's comment and in the world-l442 bd comment.
acceptance_criteria: The declared parent values either satisfy the 2.80 spacing the paper's two findings jointly require, or carry a stated reason for departing from it; the pH bracket derivation is re-attempted against the corrected set and its falsification condition is re-checked.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-bpb5 (bd7b823b6): Penman evaluated per bin on the groundwater path; the predicted convex sign was wrong and the measurement disagreed on 15.5 per cent of scored land; median shift +0.090 m is inside the lambda bracket but 352714 regions cross from pinned-at-surface to a solved depth. world-i70y (f7b96b08c): the pH runs between two buffers, the dry end derived from this planet's pCO2 at 8.1628 rather than Earth's 8.2. world-jixy (afcb6ab9c): the base-cation source was already in the tree twice, Meybeck 1987 extracted and Amiotte Suchet 1995 vendored; the 2.32 requirement closes on the whole bracket at ratio 7.38, and the four silicate parent pH values were deleted rather than moved because an affine encoding cannot carry a sourced supply.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 VERDICT, WITH THE CRITERION FIXED FIRST. The parents are NOT moved.
The requirement is re-derived against the two-buffer form world-i70y just
installed, it shrinks by about a third, and it still fails.

VERIFIED, not inherited. On an offline reconstruction that reproduces the
shipped soilmap exactly at its three decimals: the declared parents give
(C - G)/(clastic - G) = 1.8017 where the single-buffer reading of the two
findings requires (6.5 - G)/0.5 = 2.80, with C the derived calcite parent
8.16284 and G 5.1. The row's arithmetic reproduces.

CRITERION, WRITTEN BEFORE ANY SWEEP.
  J1  Under the new form, does any slope satisfy both paper findings with the
      DECLARED parents, by world-l442's own two tests -- the deviation as the
      upper bound, the bimodality as the lower one -- with the single change
      the second buffer forces on the bimodality, that the buffered windows now
      number two and the land-area density is compared over both? If yes the
      declared set stands and the shortfall is a defect of the single-buffer
      form. Falsification, declared in advance: s_lo > s_hi.
  J2  If J1 fails, solve for the parents that satisfy both and require the
      solution inside parent_bracket_silicate.
  J3  Say which end the shortfall sits in.
  J4  Re-derive the closed-form inequality this row states, under the new form,
      whether or not it is satisfiable.

J1: THE FALSIFICATION DOES NOT FIRE, AND THE REASON IS NOT THAT THE MODEL GOT
BETTER. s_hi is unchanged at 0.35 / 0.90 / 1.33 over the wettest quartile's
wettest cell, its area-weighted median and its dry edge, because a carbonate
parent's supply fraction is 1 by construction and its expression is the same one
the single-buffer form had. s_lo does not exist: with two buffers in the model,
the restated bimodality is satisfied at every slope down to the smallest tried,
0.01, because a shallow slope leaves the whole land on the calcite buffer, which
IS one of the two modes and passes a density test trivially. The pass set is not
even contiguous -- it fails only for slopes in [0.66, 0.85], where the land is
split between the modes and enough of it is in transit. A quantity satisfied in
the degenerate limit is not a bound, so world-l442's bracket stays [0.35, 1.33]
at 0.90, all three ends readings of ONE upper bound, and the config now says WHY
the lower one is absent rather than saying it is unreachable.

J4: THE CLOSED FORM, RE-DERIVED. Both findings still close on one cell's supply
fraction u = (parent - G)/(C - G), and the slope and the leaching index still
cancel. A carbonate parent has u = 1 and stays above 6.5 while
f = exp(-sL) >= (6.5 - G)/(C - G) = 0.4571; the modal clastic parent reaches a
one-pH-wide gibbsite mode while f^(1/u) <= 0.5/(C - G) = 0.1633. Both hold only
if

    u <= ln((6.5 - G)/(C - G)) / ln(0.5/(C - G)) = 0.4319

so the modal clastic parent has to sit at or below 6.423. It is declared at 6.8,
u = 0.5550. In this row's ratio form the requirement falls from 2.80 to 2.32 and
the declared values still give 1.80. THE DRY BUFFER RELIEVES ABOUT A THIRD OF
THE SHORTFALL AND DOES NOT CLOSE IT. So the disposition this row opened with
stands: sourced and contradicted.

J2 and J3: WHERE THE SHORTFALL SITS. Not the carbonate end -- it is pinned to
the calcite equilibrium at this world's pCO2 and moves only when pCO2 moves.
Only partly the buffer: G at the top of its own bracket, 5.28, lifts the bound
to 6.695 and at the bottom, 4.64, drops it to 5.792, so no reading of the
gibbsite bracket reaches 6.8, and moving G to buy the inequality would be tuning
a value that has its own derivation. It sits in the SILICATE SET. The value that
satisfies it, 6.423, is inside parent_bracket_silicate [5.586, 8.163], so it is
defensible as a fresh-parent pH by the one test this project has -- but it lands
UNDER the metamorphic entry at 6.6 and level with the felsic one at 6.4, which
breaks the order the config asserts. So the repair is not one number: it is a
re-derivation of all four silicate entries against a source that sizes their
base-cation supply, and no source here does. THE PARENTS ARE THEREFORE NOT
MOVED, and this row stays open with a smaller and sharper requirement.

WHAT MOVING THEM WOULD BE WORTH, as a diagnostic and not a change: shifting the
whole silicate set down by the 0.377 shortfall takes the wettest-quartile
carbonate deviation from 0.90 to 1.99, the neutral share from 0.255 to 0.214 and
the gibbsite-window share from 0.065 to 0.114. That is the right direction on
all three, and the deviation number is inside its own noise -- it rests on single
digits of cells above 6.5 and bootstraps to [0.33, 1.89] at the declared parents
-- so it is evidence about direction and not about magnitude.

NOT A REASON TO STEEPEN THE SLOPE. The inequality has no slope in it. Anything
that closed it by moving leaching_slope would be closing a spacing defect with a
knob, and the bracket's ends are a requirement rather than a range to hunt in.

The config's ph block and pedology/notes/pedogenesis-value-provenance.md
section 3 now carry the re-derived arithmetic. Unstaged in the tree.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the diagnostic paragraph above, and it makes the point harder
rather than softer. The 1.99 quoted there is on the CELL-COUNT wettest quartile
while every other number in that comment is on the AREA-WEIGHTED one, which is
world-l442's convention. On the area-weighted quartile the same diagnostic
shift of the silicate set gives a deviation ratio of 3.80, not 1.99, on 3
carbonate and 2 non-carbonate cells above 6.5. Neutral 0.214 and gibbsite
window 0.114 are unchanged; calcite window 0.429.

Two conventions on the same field returning 1.99 and 3.80 is the instrument
speaking, not the model: at this land population the deviation ratio rests on
single digits of cells and cannot carry a magnitude. Direction is all it
supports, and the direction is toward the paper.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 THE SOURCE EXISTS, THE REQUIREMENT CLOSES, AND THE PARENT VALUES ARE
GONE RATHER THAN MOVED. Unstaged in the tree.

WHAT THE PARENTS RESTED ON: nothing. The config's own comment said the order and
the spacing of the four silicate entries were asserted by the file and that no
source here sized that contrast. The derived silicate bracket bounded them; it
did not set them.

THE SOURCE WAS ALREADY IN THE TREE, TWICE. "No source here does" was wrong.

Meybeck (1987), doi 10.2475/ajs.287.5.401, held, read and EXTRACTED into
pedology/data/reference/meybeck1987_tables.json with its arithmetic identities
re-run. Table 2C is major-ion concentrations for ten rock types in monolithologic
drainage basins under one temperate stream model. At equal runoff a concentration
ratio IS a flux ratio, so its bicarbonate column relative to sedimentary
carbonate rocks is a base-cation supply fraction per lithology directly.
brine_paths.py:ROCK_TO_MEYBECK already maps Orogen's classes onto its rows.

GEM-CO2, Amiotte Suchet and Probst (1995), doi 10.3402/tellusb.v47i1-2.16047,
fetched today and now held and read; its 2003 global form's coefficients are
already vendored as GEM_CO2_consts.dat. The slope of atmospheric and soil CO2
consumption against runoff for 232 French monolithologic basins, converted to an
alkalinity yield by the paper's own stoichiometry, gives the same quantity from a
different measurement. Check that the vendored file and the paper are one model:
carbonate over plutonic and metamorphic is 16.7 against the 17 the paper states.

The two agree to better than a factor of two on every category. The requirement
turns on a factor of 2.32, so they decide it. Nothing was fetched that could not
be got; the two failed fetches today were mis-guessed DOIs of my own and the
files they returned were deleted.

CRITERION, FIXED BEFORE ANY MODEL RESULT WAS SEEN, and the derivation route
chosen on mechanism before its score was known. The form uses the parent ONLY
through u, and u sits in the denominator of an exponent whose numerator is a
leaching index: it is a ratio of a supply FLUX to an export FLUX. Fluxes are
linear in concentration; a pH is the logarithm of an activity. So what a source
must size is the supply ratio, and the parent pH was only its encoding. The
rejected route, reading each parent as a fresh-solution pH and solving Slessarev
eq. (6) at that lithology's measured alkalinity, is reported so the rejection is
inspectable: it returns 6.77 to 7.30, u of 0.54 to 0.72, and FAILS the
requirement on all four. It was rejected before that was computed, because it
sizes a fresh parent pH, which this block says outright is not a state the model
can be in.

THE SOURCED SET, value from Meybeck's bicarbonate column, bracket the minimum and
maximum over every applicable row of both sources and both of Meybeck's columns.

  category               u        bracket             the pH encoding gave
  igneous_mafic          0.1330   [0.1330, 0.1565]    0.8162
  igneous_felsic         0.0401   [0.0310, 0.0725]    0.4244
  metamorphic            0.0423   [0.0310, 0.0638]    0.4897
  sedimentary_clastic    0.1355   [0.0391, 0.3052]    0.5550

All four IMPLICIT-EARTH, by the same test that convicts the gibbsite buffer. Not
tuned: a measured concentration and a measured regression slope are not the
residual of a fit against anything in this model, and neither moved after a
comparison was seen. Not opaque: both sources are held, one is extracted into the
tree and the other reproduces its own published ratio. What is Earth's is the
population. The mineral stoichiometry travels; the temperature the dissolution was
measured at, the soil CO2 that sets how much carbonate the denominator dissolves,
and the carbonate cement Earth's shales carry do not. THE BRACKET DOES NOT STAND
IN FOR THAT: it is the spread between two Earth compilations and says nothing
about the transfer. The repair is a mineral-kinetics supply at this world's
temperature and pCO2, which mineral-reactivity-supply.md records is not buildable
here.

C1, THE REQUIREMENT: CLOSES, and on the whole bracket rather than the declared
point. u <= 0.4319 on the land-area modal silicate category; that category is
sedimentary_clastic at 30.2 per cent of land, its value is 0.1355 and its bracket
tops out at 0.3052. Every other category and every other bracket end is lower.
In this row's ratio form, 2.32 is required and the sourced set gives 7.38.

C2, THE ORDER MOVED, and both sources move it the same way: CLASTIC ABOVE MAFIC
above metamorphic above felsic, where the file asserted mafic above clastic.
Earth's shales carry carbonate cement and a bicarbonate column sees it. The
clastic-over-mafic margin is two per cent on Meybeck alone and is not resolvable
there; GEM-CO2 puts it at 1.9x and settles the direction.

C3, AND THIS IS THE STRUCTURAL FINDING: THE ENCODING CANNOT HOLD THE SOURCED SET.
parent = G + u*(C - G) with the silicate bracket floor at 5.586 cannot express a
supply below 0.159, and three of the four sourced supplies are below it. The map
from a supply to a pH is a logarithm and the encoding is affine. So the four
silicate parent pH values are DELETED rather than moved. ph.parent_by_category
keeps only the role it can carry, naming the buffer each category reaches at zero
export, and every entry but the evaporite is now the `derived` sentinel filled
with the calcite value, which is world-i70y's own verdict stated once instead of
approximated by four numbers that happened to sit below it. The lithology
contrast is declared as ph.base_cation_supply_by_category with its bracket.
parent_bracket_silicate keeps its meaning and gains a check that can fail: a
supply fraction u puts the fresh solution at C + log10(u), and
carbonate_ph.resolve refuses a run whose declared supplies put that outside the
bracket. That is a pH bound on a pH, and a change of pCO2 moves it without moving
any declared supply.

WORLD-l442'S BRACKET, RE-DERIVED: UNCHANGED, AND ITS FALSIFICATION DOES NOT FIRE.
s_hi is 0.35 / 0.90 / 1.33 at the area-weighted wettest quartile's wettest cell,
its median and its dry edge, because a carbonate parent's supply is 1 by
construction and its expression carries no other lithology. s_lo still does not
exist: the density test now passes at EVERY slope from 0.01 to 4.00 with no gap,
where on the declared set it failed in a narrow band, because a set whose
silicates supply four to fourteen per cent of a calcite-saturated soil's base
cations puts the whole silicate land on one buffer or the other at any slope. So
s_lo > s_hi cannot fire; there is no s_lo to compare, and the bracket stays
[0.35, 1.33] at 0.90, three readings of one upper bound.

MEASURED, on the offline reconstruction that reproduces the shipped soilmap
exactly at its three decimals, and re-checked through the SHIPPED code path,
which returns the same four figures to the printed precision. 1639 land cells,
area-weighted, at the declared slope 0.90.

  set        land mean  wet mean  f(6-7)  f gibbsite  f calcite  buffered density
  declared      7.261     6.001    0.255     0.065      0.451        0.258
  sourced       6.717     5.232    0.089     0.399      0.371        0.385
  Slessarev's own two-value model, land mean 5.739

Land mean falls 0.544; 718 cells move more than 0.5 pH and 465 more than 1.0; the
largest single move is 2.129. Over the 254 zero-runoff cells the change is +0.051
and comes entirely from mixing the dry buffers rather than taking a max of them.

THE PAPER'S TWO TESTS. The bimodality is the one that moves and it moves toward
the measurement: the neutral 6-7 share falls from 0.255 to 0.089 and the gibbsite
window rises from 0.065 to 0.399. The carbonate deviation IS NOT RESOLVABLE and
decides nothing here: the declared set gives 0.90 on 6 and 14 cells, bootstrapping
to [0.35, 1.88], and the sourced set puts no non-carbonate cell of the wettest
quartile above 6.5 at all, so the ratio is undefined in 100 per cent of resamples.
As a diagnostic and NOT as a bound, because it was not fixed in advance: swept
over slope, the declared set returns 0.8 to 1.0 everywhere, which is no lithology
signal at all, while the sourced set returns 12 to 18 against the paper's 2.6 in
the middle of the slope bracket. The declared parent contrast was too weak to
generate the paper's second finding; the sourced one generates it.

ARTIFACTS. soil_report.json, soilmap_T21.txt and land_column_states_T21.txt were
already stale before this and remain stale. No build was run: an LPJ-GUESS run
holds the host.

ONE THING THIS OPENS AND DOES NOT CLOSE. build_soil.py:PH_GROUP puts `melange` in
the metamorphic pH category while brine_paths.py:ROCK_TO_MEYBECK reads the same
rock as shale, with a recorded argument for the shale reading. Melange is over
six per cent of land. The two mappings of one rock disagree, the metamorphic
supply bracket is on gneiss and mica-schist alone and does not cover the
disagreement, and this wants its own row.

title: The pedogenesis alkaline end keeps a parent contrast the paper does not have
description:
Slessarev et al. (2016), Methods, 'Water-balance model evaluation': 'For all soils in grid cells where MAP minus PET < 0, the predicted pH was 8.2, and for all remaining profiles, the predicted pH was 5.1.' The DRY end is a single value and is parent-independent, in the same way world-l442 establishes the acid end is.

pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml's ph block keeps a parent contrast at the alkaline end, 6.4 to 7.6 across the silicates, so a dry cell's modelled pH still carries its rock. Whatever the right treatment is, it is not the paper's, and the block cites the paper.

This is separate from world-l442, which is about the ACID end's functional form, and it should not be folded into that change: the two ends are different claims about the same figure and fixing one does not settle the other. A form that relaxes every parent onto a gibbsite buffer as leaching runs says nothing about what happens where leaching does not run.

Do: establish whether the dry end should also collapse to a single value, and if it should not, say what this project is claiming instead of the paper and on what evidence. Measure the effect over the dry cells in the pH the soilmap column carries before deciding it is small.

Found by the world-l442 agent while reading the paper for the acid end.
acceptance_criteria: The alkaline end either collapses to the paper's parent-independent value or carries a stated, sourced reason for keeping a parent contrast; the effect on modelled pH over dry cells is measured and reported.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-bpb5 (bd7b823b6): Penman evaluated per bin on the groundwater path; the predicted convex sign was wrong and the measurement disagreed on 15.5 per cent of scored land; median shift +0.090 m is inside the lambda bracket but 352714 regions cross from pinned-at-surface to a solved depth. world-i70y (f7b96b08c): the pH runs between two buffers, the dry end derived from this planet's pCO2 at 8.1628 rather than Earth's 8.2. world-jixy (afcb6ab9c): the base-cation source was already in the tree twice, Meybeck 1987 extracted and Amiotte Suchet 1995 vendored; the 2.32 requirement closes on the whole bracket at ratio 7.38, and the four silicate parent pH values were deleted rather than moved because an affine encoding cannot carry a sourced supply.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 VERDICT AND MEASUREMENT. Nothing changed in the tree for this row.

VERDICT: THE DRY END SHOULD NOT KEEP THE PARENT CONTRAST WHERE IT IS, AND IT
SHOULD NOT COLLAPSE TO A SINGLE VALUE EITHER. It should relax onto the calcite
buffer as leaching goes to zero, the mirror of the gibbsite relaxation world-l442
just installed at the acid end, with the parent contrast surviving as the
FINITE-leaching deviation rather than as the L = 0 endmember.

WHY NOT SIMPLY ADOPT 8.2. Slessarev's step model is a null model whose purpose is
to measure how much of the variance the sign of the water balance explains, and
the same paper reports the deviation the null model discards. Setting every
parent to 8.2 was measured here: the wettest-quartile share above pH 6.5,
carbonate-bearing against the rest, goes to 0.62x at s = 0.90 and 0.57x at
s = 0.95, against the paper's 2.6x. A full collapse deletes the paper's own
second finding, because under the relaxation form the parent value is the ONLY
place lithology enters. Adopting one end of the figure would cost the other.

WHY THE CONTRAST IS NEVERTHELESS IN THE WRONG PLACE. The mechanism behind the
dry mode is that Ca2+ released by weathering is not exported, so pedogenic
calcite accumulates until it saturates and takes over the buffering. That needs
some Ca supply and zero export, and every silicate parent supplies some. "Granite
takes longer to saturate than basalt" is the only argument for a zero-leaching
contrast and this project cannot make it: Orogen has no time axis, so what a
model here represents is the steady state, and the zero-export steady state is
calcite saturation. pedogenesis.yaml already knows this: the top of its derived
parent_bracket_silicate IS the calcite equilibrium. The block simply does not
push parents there at L = 0. One field is being asked to be two things, the pH
of a soil solution that has not accumulated calcite and the endmember of a soil
that never leaches.

WHAT THIS PROJECT IS CLAIMING INSTEAD OF THE PAPER, as it stands: that a soil
which drains nothing retains its parent's pH, which is a claim about kinetics on
a model with no time axis to express kinetics in. That is not a defensible
position and the row should stay open.

MEASURED, canonical-10m-carve2 against the baseline climatology, area-weighted,
in the pH the soilmap column carries. Dry = runoff <= 0, 254 cells, 20.6 per cent
of land area. The measurement is unchanged by world-l442's form change: at L = 0
the exponential returns the parent exactly, so every number below is the same
before and after it.

  current modelled dry pH   mean 7.303   p05 6.667  p50 7.293  p95 8.078
                            min 6.455    max 8.817
  parent over dry cells     mean 7.239   p05 6.652  p95 8.026  (spread 1.374)
  dry area within 0.5 of the calcite buffer   0.155
  dry area in the neutral 6-7 range           0.298
  endorheic share of dry area                 0.594 (158 cells already get +0.8)

  collapse to the paper's 8.2:                dry mean 7.303 -> 8.200, +0.897;
                                              land mean +0.185; 214 of 254 dry
                                              cells move more than 0.5 pH
  relax to the derived calcite parent 8.163
  plus the endorheic bonus:                   dry mean 7.303 -> 8.227, +0.924;
                                              land mean +0.190; 214 cells > 0.5

THE EFFECT IS NOT SMALL. It is 0.9 pH on a fifth of land area and 0.19 pH on the
land mean, against a form change at the acid end worth 0.079 on the land mean.
The dry end is the larger of the two departures from this figure.

AND IT BLOCKS SOMETHING. world-l442's re-derivation of leaching_slope_bracket
needed a lower bound and the only sourced candidate was the paper's bimodality.
It is unreachable at ANY slope while this row is open: the zero-runoff cells sit
at their parent values in the neutral range, carry 13.3 per cent of the neutral
share, and no leaching slope moves a cell whose L is zero. So this row is a
prerequisite for a two-sided bracket on the leaching slope, not an independent
tidy-up. world-l442's bracket is three readings of one upper bound because of it.

WHAT THE FIX IS, and why it was not made here. A second buffer at the dry end is
a FORM change, the same size as the one world-l442 just made, and this row says
in its own words that the two ends are different claims and should not be folded
together. Two form changes in one edit would make neither reviewable, which is
the reason the values and the form were split on world-l442 in the first place.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 FIXED. The dry end is a second mineral buffer, derived rather than
transplanted. Unstaged in the tree; the artifacts stay stale, see the end.

VERIFIED BEFORE ACTING, not inherited. The offline reconstruction reproduces
pedology/data/canonical-10m-carve2/soilmap_T21.txt EXACTLY at that file's three
decimals, max |difference| 0.000 over all 1639 land cells, under the line form
that wrote it. On that reconstruction: 254 cells, 20.6 per cent of land area,
have runoff <= 0 so L = 0; their area-weighted mean pH under the shipped
relaxation is 7.303; 15.5 per cent of that area is within 0.5 of the paper's
8.2 and 29.8 per cent is in the neutral 6 to 7; collapsing them to 8.2 is +0.897
on the dry cells and +0.185 on the land mean with 214 of 254 cells moving more
than 0.5. Every figure in the prior comment reproduces.

THE FORM. build_soil.py:soil_ph now runs the leaching index BETWEEN two
buffers instead of from a rock to one:

  D = max(parent, C)                 the highest buffer that parent can reach
  u = (parent - G)/(D - G)           its base-cation supply, as a fraction of a
                                     calcite-saturated soil's
  ph = G + (D - G) * exp(-leaching_slope * L / u) + endorheic * bonus

At L = 0 every Ca-bearing parent is at C, which is world-i70y's requirement. As
L grows every parent goes to G, which is world-l442's. The lithology contrast
survives at FINITE L, in u, which is where the paper's own wettest-quartile
carbonate deviation lives. A carbonate parent has u = 1 and its expression is
unchanged from the shipped one, so world-l442's bracket derivation does not
move. D is a max rather than C because the evaporite parent's dry buffer is
sodium carbonate and sits above calcite saturation; a parent that IS a buffer
mineral gets u = 1 by construction.

THE BUFFER IS DERIVED, NOT INHERITED. ph.calcite_buffer_ph and its bracket are
both the sentinel `derived`, filled by carbonate_ph.py from config/planet.yaml's
pCO2_bar through Slessarev's Methods eq. (6). At this world's pCO2 the calcite
equilibrium open to the atmosphere is 8.163 and not Earth's 8.2, and the bracket
is the same equilibrium over the declared soil-air CO2 enrichment, 6.832 at a
hundredfold, so the declared value sits at the TOP of its own bracket for a
stated reason: open to the atmosphere is the condition a laboratory pH is
measured under and a field soil buried in respired CO2 reads below it. So the
classification is DERIVED. It is not tuned, not opaque, and NOT implicit-Earth,
which the gibbsite end beside it is: this one travels to another planet because
it is solved at that planet's declared atmosphere. carbonate_ph.py did already
compute the quantity as parent_by_category.carbonate; it is named separately
because the roles differ, one being the pH of a solution on carbonate rock and
the other where a soil that exports nothing ends up whatever its rock was.

THE FORM WAS CHOSEN ON MECHANISM AND THE REJECTED ONE IS RECORDED. The literal
composed mirror, ph = G + [(parent - G) + (D - parent) f] f with f = exp(-sL),
which is the dry relaxation composed with the acid one at a single leaching
scale, was implemented and measured FIRST. It satisfies both endpoints too. It
was rejected after its numbers were seen, so this selection is POST HOC and is
stated as such. The reason is not its score. It carries a fixed ratio between
the leaching that flushes pedogenic calcite and the leaching that strips primary
minerals, no source sizes that ratio, and the ratio it happens to impose leaves
21 per cent of the calcite offset standing in the wettest quartile, where the
most soluble phase in the profile should be the first thing gone. The supply
form has no such free ratio: at steady state the calcite is present when the
supply exceeds what the drainage exports, lithology enters through the supply
alone, and that is a ratio of two fluxes with no time in it, which is the only
kind of statement docs/src/reference/no-time-axis.md permits here. For the
record its land mean was 7.394 and its deviation ratio 0.83 against the supply
form's 7.261 and 0.90; the two are not separable by the instrument below.

MEASURED, canonical-10m-carve2 against the baseline climatology, 1639 land
cells, area-weighted, in the pH the soilmap column carries. The shipped
soil_ph agrees with the reconstruction to 1.8e-15, so these are the code's.

form                       land    dry   wetq  f(6-7)  f(G+-.5)  f(C+-.5)  bimodal   dev
BEFORE one buffer s=0.90  6.722  7.303  5.913   0.476     0.035     0.080    0.057  1.32
AFTER  two buffers 0.35   7.726  8.227  6.854   0.138     0.000     0.586    0.293  0.82
AFTER  two buffers 0.90   7.261  8.227  5.895   0.255     0.065     0.451    0.258  0.90
AFTER  two buffers 1.33   7.044  8.227  5.555   0.206     0.147     0.413    0.280   inf
Slessarev's step model    5.739  8.200  5.100   0.000     0.794     0.206    0.500   inf

`bimodal` is the land-area density in the two buffered windows, each one pH
unit wide, against `f(6-7)` which is the density in the paper's neutral window.
`dev` is the paper's wettest-quartile carbonate deviation.

Land mean 6.722 -> 7.261, +0.538. Dry-cell mean 7.303 -> 8.227, +0.924; the dry
area within 0.5 of the calcite buffer goes 0.176 -> 0.994. Wet-quartile mean is
almost untouched, 5.913 -> 5.895. 1474 cells move more than 0.05, 862 more than
0.5, 331 more than 1.0, none more than 2.0; largest single move +1.749; 76 cells
do not move; 1563 of 1639 change the printed soilmap value. Five cells rail on
ph.maximum before and after; none rails on ph.minimum either way.

BOTH OF THE PAPER'S TESTS, honestly. Bimodality is the improvement and it is
large: the neutral share falls 0.476 -> 0.255 while the buffered density rises
0.057 -> 0.258, against the step model's 0.500. The distribution has two modes
where it had one. The carbonate deviation goes 1.32 -> 0.90 against the paper's
2.6, which reads as a regression AND IS NOT MEASURABLE. It rests on 5 carbonate
and 8 non-carbonate cells above 6.5 before and 6 and 14 after; a bootstrap over
the quartile gives 1.32 [0.43, 3.42] before and 0.90 [0.33, 1.89] after, and
switching the quartile from area-weighted to cell-count moves the same two
numbers to 1.35 and 1.32. The effect is smaller than the instrument's own
scatter, so the ratio cannot separate these forms and did not choose between
them. It is reported because it is the paper's test, not because it decided
anything. The BRACKET does not rest on it: leaching_slope's three ends come
from the closed form s = ln((C - G)/(6.5 - G))/L, which is deterministic.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX. The parent SPACING, which is world-jixy, and which the
dry buffer relieves by about a third without closing. See that row.

GATE: scripts/smoke_test.py passes, 62 checks, with the new row
("derived", "ph.calcite_buffer_ph", ...) registered in PEDOLOGY_BRACKETS. The
row is `derived` rather than `value` because both the buffer and its bracket are
sentinels; carbonate_ph.resolve refuses a number written into either on every
run, and build_soil.py:soil_ph additionally refuses a buffer outside its own
bracket and a calcite buffer that is not above the gibbsite one.

STALE, deliberately, and NOT regenerated because an LPJ-GUESS run holds all 16
cores: pedology/analysis/soil_report.json,
pedology/data/canonical-10m-carve2/soilmap_T21.txt and
land_column_states_T21.txt. They were already stale from world-l442 and they
need one build_soil.py run. notes/audits/tuned-values.md is superseded on the
ph rows and was not edited, being outside pedology/.

Rewritten in the same change: pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml's ph block,
pedology/README.md, pedology/notes/pedogenesis-value-provenance.md section 3.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 world-5th5 CLOSED THE LAST EXCEPTION TO THIS ROW'S VERDICT. Unstaged in the tree.

This row's fix left one entry of ph.parent_by_category that was not the calcite
buffer: evaporite at a declared 8.8 for sodium carbonate, on the argument that a
solution buffered by soda is not brought back down by precipitating calcite out
of it. That argument is chemically right and this world's own Hardie-Eugster
divide confirms it -- 95.7 per cent of endorheic catchment area on the alkaline
path under discharge weighting, 94.6 under area weighting -- but passing the
divide is a property of the BASIN, computed from its catchment's inflow, and it
was already stated once as ph.endorheic_alkalinity_bonus off the same Helvaci
range and on the same land. Orogen's basin_fill rule assigns the evaporite class
FROM the endorheic flag, so the rock carried nothing the flag did not.

parent_by_category is therefore DERIVED in every entry, which is this row's
verdict without a residue, and carbonate_ph.resolve's refusal no longer carries a
special case. The removal is worth -0.006 pH on the land mean.

Also from that row and bearing on this one: the closed-basin floor is NOT dry.
91.75 per cent of the land area flagged endorheic has local runoff above zero, at
a median 11.55 mm/yr. So the 254 zero-runoff cells this row measured are mostly
NOT the closed basins; they are elsewhere. The dry end and the closed basin are
different populations.

title: Eleven declared brackets outside pedology are read by nothing
description:
world-mro1 closed the pedology half of 'a value outside its own bracket is invisible' with a smoke check over pedogenesis.yaml and surface_classes.yaml. The sweep that wrote it found eleven more brackets in four other components that nothing reads, so a value drifting outside its own declared bracket there still fails silently:

  aeolian/config/dust.yaml
    emission.cd0_bracket
    emission.c_alpha_bracket
    emission.u_star_st_typical_bracket
    drag_partition.z0s_bracket_cm
    source.pavement_residual_erodibility_bracket
    source.arid_bare_ground.enabled_as_bracket
    transport.dust_scale_height_bracket_m
    removal.scavenging_a_bracket
  hydrography/config/groundwater.yaml
    evapotranspiration.lambda_bracket_m
  minerals/config/downstream_prospectivity.yaml
    deposits.bauxite.precipitation_bracket_mm_yr
  ocean/config/carbon_feedback.yaml
    reopening_contract.owners.weathering_and_outgassing_bracket

This is the working agreement's second half applied to a declaration rather than a derived field: a bracket that nothing reads is a statement with no consequence, and it drifts from the value it describes without anything objecting.

Do: extend the check world-mro1 added rather than writing a second one -- its table already carries four dispositions (value, pair, level, derived) and a discovery pass that reports any bracket the table does not name. Widening its file list is most of the work. Expect at least one of the eleven to be a bracket whose value has already moved outside it; that is the finding and not a reason to loosen the bracket.

Note ocean/config/carbon_feedback.yaml's entry is a reopening contract rather than a numeric bracket and may want a different disposition or an explicit exemption.

Found by the world-mro1 sweep.
acceptance_criteria: Every declared bracket in the tree is either read by a check that fires when its value falls outside, or carries an explicit exemption with a stated reason; the check is one implementation, not one per component.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-nfer (829619208): the bracket check is now one implementation over the whole tree with files discovered rather than listed, 81 brackets against 84 rows, and two holes closed in the discovery pass -- it never entered lists, which is where ntransform.yaml's seven live. Every declared bracket in the tree holds. world-x9zl (e9edb8790): three sites, not two; the steering wind is weighted by layer mass from lib/lapse.py's own sigma levels, checked against the climatology's lev to 4e-7. Sea salt forcing moves 0.29 per cent of its own bracket span and volcanic sulfate peak AOD moves -9.9 per cent, which is not inside the scatter. world-xm1t (42e8aca31, 860d193bb): the rescue reported nothing on every segment for two independent reasons, and the root cause was pyburn logging a name only one arm binds.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Extended the world-mro1 check rather than adding a second one. scripts/smoke_test.py: PEDOLOGY_CONFIGS/PEDOLOGY_BRACKETS are now BRACKET_CONFIG_GLOBS/DECLARED_BRACKETS, the check is check_declared_brackets_contain_their_values, and the files are reached by glob over config/*.yaml and */config/*.yaml rather than a hand-kept list, so a component added later arrives with its brackets in scope. 37 declaration files, 81 discovered brackets, 84 table rows. Six new dispositions beside value/pair/level/derived: optional, elsewhere, choice, flag, pending, not_a_bracket. The discovery half now also walks lists (a list contributes no path component, so an entry inserted above a bracket does not unregister it) and mapping-valued bracket keys, both of which it previously walked past.

VERIFIED, all eleven: every one exists at the stated path. Nine are numeric and every value is inside its bracket -- cd0 4.4e-5 in [3.9e-5,4.9e-5]; c_alpha 2.7 in [1.7,3.7]; u_star_st_typical 0.20 in [0.16,0.30]; z0s_cm 3.3e-4 in [1.0e-4,1.0e-3]; pavement_residual_erodibility 0.0 in [0.0,0.25]; dust_scale_height_m 3000 in [2000,5000]; scavenging_a 1.72e-6 in [1.72e-6,8.05e-5]; lambda_m 1.0 in [0.5,2.0]; bauxite minimum_precipitation_mm_yr 1200 in [1200,1700]. NO DRIFT FOUND anywhere in the tree: every value/bracket pair in every declaration file holds. Five values sit exactly on an endpoint (scavenging_a, pavement_residual_erodibility, charnock, the bauxite threshold, belowground_and_exchangeable_multiplier at the HIGH end), which is inside under the inclusive test and would be a violation under a strict one.

The two non-numeric entries of the eleven: source.arid_bare_ground.enabled_as_bracket is dispositioned flag (the arm has to be true and build_dust.py has to still name arid_bare_ground); ocean/config/carbon_feedback.yaml reopening_contract.owners.weathering_and_outgassing_bracket is dispositioned not_a_bracket with the reason written out -- it is an ownership row naming the issue that owns the bracket, and what asserts the exemption is still true is that the value is not two numbers.

BEYOND THE ELEVEN the list was well short. Also unread by anything: dust emission.ce_bracket, subgrid_wind.weibull_shape_bracket and source.erodible_weight_bracket.evaporite. And 46 further bracket declarations the sweep did not reach at all: aeolian/config/sea_salt.yaml (4), volcanic_sulfate.yaml (4), biosphere/config/abiotic_nutrients.yaml (2), bvoc.yaml (4), ntransform.yaml (7, in a LIST), respiration_acclimation.yaml, snow_thermal.yaml, wetlands.yaml (6), config/planet.yaml (4), config/partial_surface.yaml (2), exoplasim/config/ocean_tier.yaml (3 corners of one hull), hydrography/config/topographic_index.yaml, pedology/config/land_column_properties.yaml (3) and outgassing.yaml (7). All are now registered.

biosphere/config/abiotic_nutrients.yaml adequacy.residence_time_earth_years is 5.0e4 and its bracket is [5.0e4, 1.15e5] -- YAML 1.1 wants a sign in the exponent, so all three resolve to STRINGS. abiotic_nutrient_ledger.py floats the value so nothing is wrong today, but the two bracket ends are passed into the report unfloated and a comparison against them would raise. Biosphere is another session s to fix; not touched here.

title: Both aerosol scripts say mass-weighted over the layers and take an unweighted level mean
description:
aeolian/scripts/build_sea_salt.py and aeolian/scripts/build_volcanic_sulfate.py both carry a comment saying the quantity is mass-weighted over the layers below the steering sigma, and both then take an unweighted mean(axis=1) over model levels. ExoPlaSim's sigma levels are not of equal thickness, so an unweighted mean over them is not the mass weighting the comment claims and is not a defensible alternative to it either -- it weights a thin level and a thick one the same.

The comment is the specification and the code does not meet it, so this is a defect and not a documentation gap: whichever is right, the two currently disagree and a reader has no way to know which to trust.

Do: weight by layer mass (the sigma thickness times surface pressure) as the comment says, or change the comment to state and justify what is actually taken. Measure what the correction is worth in the units the consumers read before deciding it is small -- the same sweep that found this measured a sibling defect at -0.96 per cent on volcanic sulfate top-of-atmosphere shortwave forcing, which is thirty times the correction the row it came from was opened for.

Found by the world-vwqw sweep.
