acceptance_criteria: Both scripts weight the level mean by layer mass or state what they take and why; the size of the change is measured in consumer units and reported.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-nfer (829619208): the bracket check is now one implementation over the whole tree with files discovered rather than listed, 81 brackets against 84 rows, and two holes closed in the discovery pass -- it never entered lists, which is where ntransform.yaml's seven live. Every declared bracket in the tree holds. world-x9zl (e9edb8790): three sites, not two; the steering wind is weighted by layer mass from lib/lapse.py's own sigma levels, checked against the climatology's lev to 4e-7. Sea salt forcing moves 0.29 per cent of its own bracket span and volcanic sulfate peak AOD moves -9.9 per cent, which is not inside the scatter. world-xm1t (42e8aca31, 860d193bb): the rescue reported nothing on every segment for two independent reasons, and the root cause was pyburn logging a name only one arm binds.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Fixed at all three aeolian sites; the correction measured in consumer units.

THE DEFECT, verified against the source before the change. build_sea_salt.py
carried "Steering wind: mass-weighted over the layers below the steering
sigma" over `ua[:, below].mean(axis=1)`; build_volcanic_sulfate.py took the
same plain mean with no comment; and build_dust.py took `np.average(ua[:, sel],
axis=1)` with no weights while aeolian/config/dust.yaml declares "the
mass-weighted wind of the layers below steering_sigma". At ten layers this
model's dsigma runs 0.034 to 0.137, a factor of four.

THE WEIGHT. Layer mass per unit area is dsigma * ps / g; within a column ps and
g are common factors and divide out of a normalised vertical mean, so the
weight is dsigma renormalised over the selected levels and no surface pressure
field is read. dsigma comes from lib/lapse.py:sigma_levels, which reproduces
plasim.f90's construction; the climatology's `lev` is checked against it
rather than assumed to match. New shared entry points build_dust.steering_weights
and build_dust.steering_wind; all three scripts call them.

WEIGHTS. sea salt (sigma >= 0.85, two layers): 0.500/0.500 -> 0.718/0.282.
dust and sulfate (sigma >= 0.5, five layers): 0.200 each -> 0.267/0.263/0.233/0.170/0.067.

MEASURED, on baseline_regular_climatology.nc, by running each script's own
chain through its own imported functions with only the steering weight varied.

Sea salt, all_modes. Area-mean steering speed 2.848 -> 2.946 m/s (+3.4%).
Global TOA shortwave forcing -0.252522 -> -0.252981 W/m2, +0.18%. Ocean-mean
forcing +0.09%. Global-mean burden +0.11%, ocean-mean AOD -0.06%. no_spume:
forcing -0.102352 -> -0.102606 W/m2, +0.25%.
AGAINST ITS OWN BRACKET: wet_lifetime_hours 25 [12,40] spans -0.161885 to
-0.321048 W/m2, a span of 0.159 W/m2. The weighting correction is 0.29 per cent
of that span. It is smaller than the instrument's own scatter and the reported
sea salt numbers do not move.

Volcanic sulfate. Area-mean steering speed 3.978 -> 4.614 m/s (+16.0%).
Global TOA shortwave forcing -0.019422 -> -0.019472 W/m2, +0.26%; global-mean
AOD +1.23%; global-mean burden +1.17%; PEAK AOD 0.03363 -> 0.03031, -9.9%; the
solver's mass residual 2.72% -> 1.38%, so the correctly weighted steering field
is also the less divergent one.
AGAINST ITS OWN BRACKET: wet_lifetime_hours 96 [60,150] spans -0.012433 to
-0.029825 W/m2, a span of 0.017 W/m2. The forcing correction is 0.29 per cent
of that span, again inside the scatter. The peak AOD move is not.
The absolute sulfate numbers used outgassing_over_earth = 1.0 because
pedology/analysis/weathering_fluxes.json is absent from this tree; the relative
correction is +0.257% at 0.5 and +0.252% at 2.0, so it does not depend on that
anchor.

Dust: NOT MEASURED. Its steering selection is sulfate's, so the steering wind
moves the same +16%, but the transported column cannot be estimated from what
is on disk: driving the shared solver with the annual-mean emission field in
dust_baseline.nc returns mass residuals of 10 to 130 per cent against an effect
of order 10 per cent, so the surrogate is not an instrument. The dust number
needs a build_dust.py run, which is blocked while the host lock is held.

CHECK. build_dust.check_steering_weights, run per commit from

title: smoke_test's SCRIPT_DIRS omits four components, so every file-based check is blind to them
description:
scripts/smoke_test.py's SCRIPT_DIRS names the component script directories every file-based check walks. It omits aeolian/, ocean/, minerals/ and analysis/. Four components, including two of the newest, are invisible to every check in the gate that works by reading files.

This is not theoretical. world-vwqw's defect -- two aeolian scripts passing an index array where bin centres belong, getting equal weights silently -- lived in aeolian/ and no static pass could have seen it. The check written for it had to build its own file list to reach the files it is about, which is the workaround and not the repair.

Do: add the four directories, then expect the existing checks to start reporting. That is the point, and the findings are the value; treat what they report as a work list rather than as a reason to narrow the list again. Any check that cannot sensibly apply to a component should say so per check rather than by the component being absent from the walk.

Note analysis/ is project-level rather than a component and holds one-off measurement scripts as well as registered steps, so it may want a different rule from the other three. Decide that explicitly rather than by omission, which is what the current state is.

Found by the world-vwqw agent while writing a check that could not see its own subject.
acceptance_criteria: SCRIPT_DIRS covers every directory config/pipeline.yaml names a generator in; the checks that then fire are triaged into fixes or per-check exemptions with a stated reason; world-vwqw's check no longer needs its own file list.
close_reason:
Resolved in worktree-agent-a8e2fa75c75a4789b; six commits, awaiting merge to main.

SCRIPT_DIRS (87e467ef7) now covers every directory config/pipeline.yaml names a generator in: aeolian/scripts, ocean/scripts, minerals/scripts and analysis/ added to the seven that were there. check_registered_in_workflow additionally checks the walk AGAINST THE GRAPH, so the next component becomes visible on the commit that registers its first step rather than silently not; restricted to .py and .sh, because the orogen step's script is the vendored tree and several registered probes are Fortran. Exercised against a narrowed list: it names all four directories.

BOTH WORKAROUNDS REMOVED. world-vwqw's _climatology_call_sites carried a whole-tree os.walk; it now takes SCRIPT_DIRS and finds the same 54 call sites the walk did, none lost, aeolian/ included. The SECOND was TIME_REDUCING_DIRS behind check_nonlinear_reduction_order: it reached minerals/ and analysis/ but omitted biosphere/scripts, and pointing it at SCRIPT_DIRS immediately reported a real defect there.

WHAT FIRED, AND ITS DISPOSITION. Three checks, nine findings, no exemptions taken -- every one was a fix.

1. one grid convention (1): aeolian/scripts/build_dust.py rebuilt the longitude cell width as 360/nlon in the advection metric. Now constructs the Gaussian spec lib/gridding.py owns, takes dlon off it, and passes the latitude axis through require_gaussian_rows, which turns the reconstruction into a check. dx bit-identical at every rung. Shared with build_sea_salt.py and build_volcanic_sulfate.py. 1107a1fb4.

2. every generator is declared (4): aerosol_deposition.py plus the three cGENIE cost drivers, all registered under one_offs with their reasons. 7158d2900.

3. no artifact path carries a resolution literal (9 lines, 5 files): the two SPAT-5 gates spelled exoplasim/inputs/t21/ and orogen_T21_surf_1720.sra -- SPAT-2's own defect inside the gate that judges the tree. Rung from rungs.model_grid, staged field through provenance.staged_surface_field, ledger row chosen by rung name not by position. 4b3e491bd. scarp_relief_transport.py built source/<build>/exoplasim-T42 by hand and the two orogen_resolution drivers documented it; lib/builds.py:mesh_export_at resolves either directory a caller can hold, so callers name the BUILD. 7fe411b9c.

FOUND BY THE SECOND WORKAROUND'S REMOVAL: biosphere/scripts/score_prediction.py reduced tas and pr with a bare .mean(axis=0) over the climatology's time axis. Both now go through climatology.annual_mean_of. 33dc56eac.

THE analysis/ DECISION: analysis/ is on the SAME rule as the components, not a rule of its own. Its one-off measurement drivers are what config/pipeline.yaml's one_offs register is for and 26 of its scripts were already named there, so the register the row worried was missing already exists and already holds them. The two real differences are consequences rather than exemptions: it is flat rather than analysis/scripts, and it has no README, so check_documented_in_component finds none and skips it -- each one-off is documented instead by the notes/audits document it is the driver for. title: spat5_tile_diagnostics: retain per-tile and aggregate surface diagnostics
description:
The last SPAT-5 seam. config/partial_surface.yaml declares which diagnostics are retained per tile and which in aggregate: surface temperature, water and snow stores, sensible and latent heat, evaporation, momentum, absorbed shortwave and net longwave, on both lists. outmod must write both, each tile weighted exactly once at the atmosphere boundary.

BLOCKED BEHIND THE STATE SEAM. Per-tile diagnostics emitted while the absent tile is a copy of the present one are not tile diagnostics; they are the binary answer written out twice under two names, which is the specific failure the seam ordering exists to prevent.

Evidence: notes/audits/partial-cell-tile-state.md
acceptance_criteria: outmod emits the declared per-tile and aggregate diagnostics; the area-weighted per-tile values reproduce the aggregate exactly; partial_surface_decision_gate credits the diagnostics seam.

title: spat5_tile_turbulent and spat5_tile_radiative: evaluate the exchange once per tile
description:
SPAT-5's exchange seams. surflx and the surface radiation each evaluate once today, on whichever tile's publication the shared dt(:,NLEP), dq(:,NLEP), dz0, drhs, dalb and dsalb happen to hold; spat5_seed_turbulent_bundles and radstep's seed copy that one answer into both channels. The per-tile bundles, the endpoint-safe spat5_tile_combine primitive and spat5_restore_exchange_aggregate already exist and are wired, so this seam is the evaluation itself.

Prefer driving the existing kernels twice over the tile boundary bundles to restating their arithmetic: plasimmod's spat5_tile_combine comment already states that reason for the combiner. Doubling surflx has a runtime cost that has to be measured rather than assumed, and the thread working set is subject to the 32 MB target.

BLOCKED BEHIND THE STATE SEAM, and not as a preference. Until both tiles carry their own state the absent tile's boundary is a copy of the present one, so a dual evaluation would evaluate the same surface twice and area-weight two copies of it. analysis/partial_surface_decision_gate.py fails a seam standing on an absent prerequisite.

Evidence: notes/audits/partial-cell-tile-state.md
acceptance_criteria: Turbulent and radiative exchange are evaluated separately per tile and combined by area; the pure-land and pure-ocean reductions are bit-identical to the binary answer; the extensive flux identity closes; the added cost is measured and reported beside the load.

title: spat5_tile_state and spat5_tile_restart: both tiles advance on their own fraction
description:
The first execution seam of SPAT-5's selected tile model. Today exactly one surface owner advances on a cell -- landstep is masked on dls > 0.0 and seastep on dls < 0.5, and landmod.f90:1022 binarises dls -- so the absent tile's boundary is a COPY of the present one and the two bundles agree exactly. That is the invariant this seam must break.

Do: landmod and seamod advance their own prognostic temperature, stores and snow wherever their fraction is positive, and serialise that state (spat5_tile_restart). Neither tile may overwrite the other's temperature, water or snow store in a partial cell, which is what config/partial_surface.yaml already declares.

One asymmetry makes the model side cheaper than it looks: landmod already gates on dls(:) > 0.0, strictly positive, so its form is already 'advance wherever my share is positive' and only the binarisation makes that equivalent to a binary mask. seamod's dls(:) < 0.5 is a hard threshold and is not fraction-shaped; it has to become dlf(:) < 1.0.

THIS SEAM COMES FIRST. An exchange seam taken before it evaluates the same surface twice and area-weights two copies of it: the binary answer, reported through per-tile diagnostics that are not tiles. analysis/partial_surface_decision_gate.py carries the order and fails a seam standing on an absent prerequisite.

Evidence: notes/audits/partial-cell-tile-state.md
acceptance_criteria: Both tiles advance and serialise their own state on every positive-fraction cell; a pure-land cell reduces bit-identically to the binary land answer and a pure-ocean cell to the binary ocean answer; the land and ocean boundary bundles differ on partial cells; partial_surface_decision_gate credits both state seams and the restart seam.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 THE GATE REFUSES THIS SEAM TODAY, and it is right to. partial_surface_decision_gate's seam_order makes both state seams stand on 'declared initial state for both tiles', which requires every initial-state field at status available. Two are blocked on world-qcse. Adding spat5_tile_state to landmod or seamod now would flip the dependency-order check to FAIL -- a seam standing on an absent prerequisite -- and the harm is real rather than bookkeeping: the land tile would begin advancing 11.578 percent of this world's land at the open-water albedo 0.06 under zero canopy, and the shortwave error would be attributed to the tile model. So this row is BLOCKED, not deferred.

THE ENUMERATION IS DONE AND THE ROW'S PREMISE NEEDED ONE CORRECTION. landmod is NOT uniformly fraction-shaped. Beside its thirty-odd dls(:) > 0.0 sites there is landmod.f90:2777, wetalb, 'if (dls(jhor) > 0.5)' -- the wet-soil albedo, so without it the land tile advances a soil moisture whose albedo never responds on any cell the ocean owns. landmod.f90:1494's 0.5 is the GLACIER fraction and stays.

seamod's seven sites, all dls(:) < 0.5, all becoming dlf(:) < 1.0:
  150  seaini's transfer of cts, cicec, ciced, csnow, csst, cmld into the puma arrays -- THE INITIAL-STATE SITE, and why world-cp27 comes first
  186  cold-start sea-ice albedo ramp and sea saturation
  258  flux accumulation into the ice coupler
  278  the accumulated fluxes divided by the accumulation count
  315  icestep's return into dsst, dts, dmld, dicec, diced, dsnow, dsmelt, dsndch
  330  dependent surface variables: dt(:,NLEP), the ice albedo ramp, dqs, drhs, the Charnock roughness, dalb, dsalb, dz0
  391  seaalbarchive, the albedo diagnostic radmod actually used

AND THE BINARISATION IS THREE SITES, NOT ONE: landmod.f90:1022 dls, oceanmod.f90:349 yls, icemod.f90:357 xls. Each module rounds its own copy right after reading the mask, so removing one leaves the others rounding silently. The gate checked oceanmod alone and would have reported the boundary fractional while the land tile still saw a rounded mask; it now checks all three and names the ones that remain.

Evidence: notes/audits/partial-cell-tile-state.md, section 'Every site the first seam has to move'.

title: Give both surface tiles an initial state on partial cells
description:
SPAT-5's tile model needs both tiles defined wherever their fraction is positive, and neither has a value there today. landini sets soil state under 'if (dls(jhor) > 0.0)'; seaini sets dts, dsst, dmld, dicec and diced under 'where(dls(:) < 0.5)'. So a land tile on an ocean-owned partial cell has no soil temperature, water or snow, and an ocean tile on a land-owned partial cell has no sea surface temperature, mixed-layer depth or ice.

This is the gating cost of spat5_tile_state, and it is a boundary-conditions question rather than a model-internals one: what a 90-percent-land cell's ocean tile starts at is a field that build_boundary_conditions.py must emit, beside the code-1720 support it already writes. The storage is not the problem -- landmod and seamod already keep separate NHOR arrays.

Evidence: notes/audits/partial-cell-tile-state.md
acceptance_criteria: Both tiles carry a defined, provenance-stamped initial state on every cell with a positive fraction, emitted by a registered pipeline step, with no sentinel and no unassigned array reaching any tile record.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 THIS IS SMALLER THAN THE DESCRIPTION ASSUMES. Read against the
source, most of the initial state already exists globally; what is masked is
the ASSIGNMENT into each tile's prognostic, not the source it comes from.

OCEAN TILE, on land-owned cells. icemod's ice_cold_start builds the cold-start
profile UNMASKED: zsst(jhor1:jhor2) = tsst_pol + (tsst_eq - tsst_pol) *
cos(deglat)^2 across the whole latitude band, and xcoldsst(:) = zsst(:) with no
mask either. Only the sea-ice branch is masked, on xls < 0.5. When surface code
169 is staged, xclsst is read by mpsurfgp unmasked and carries a -999 sentinel
where the field is absent, which is already the model's own record of what this
world has. Mixed-layer depth is not per-cell at all in the slab configuration:
oceanmod's mldepth is a scalar namelist value, default 50 m, assigned to
dlayer(NLEV_OCE). So the ocean tile has a declared, sourced initial temperature
everywhere and a uniform depth, and seaini's 'where(dls(:) < 0.5)' transfer of
cts, csst, cmld, cicec and ciced into the puma arrays is the only thing that
stops it reaching a land-owned cell.

LAND TILE, on ocean-owned cells. landmod sets dtclsoil(:) = tmelt,
dsoilt(:,:) = tmelt and dtclim(:) = tmelt unmasked at initialisation, and reads
the staged dtclsoil through mpsurfgp unmasked. soilini's
'where(dls(:) > 0.0) dts(:) = dtclsoil(:)' is again the mask, over a source
that is already defined everywhere.

SO THE REMAINING QUESTIONS ARE FEWER AND SHARPER, and they are about what is
DEFENSIBLE rather than what is defined:

  1. Is the analytic cold-start SST under a 90-percent-land cell an acceptable
     starting value, given it then relaxes? It is a declared profile and not a
     fabrication, so this is a statement to make rather than a field to invent.
  2. Soil water and snow: dwatc comes from dwatcini or the dwcl climatology,
     and dwcl defaults to -1.0, a sentinel. dsnowz and dsnowt default to 0.0
     and tmelt. Whether a land tile on an ocean-owned cell starts dry, at
     field capacity, or from dwcl is a real choice and is the one genuinely
     open field here.
  3. dwmax, dforest, dglac and dsoilwfc are staged fields read unmasked, so
     they need checking rather than deriving.

Recommended shape: state the disposition of each initial field explicitly in
config/partial_surface.yaml under tile_model.state, so that world-uiq7 becomes
an execution-gate change against a declared initial condition rather than a
change that has to invent one. Only item 2 looks like new work.

Evidence: notes/audits/partial-cell-tile-state.md

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 MEASURED, AND THE EARLIER COMMENT UNDERSTATED IT. The staged fields
were read directly at T21 by cell class. Over the 620 sea-owned partial cells:

  code 173 dz0clim   0.3446..3.581 m   LAND values already -- the roughness
                                       builder works from mesh.surface_class,
                                       not the ownership mask
  code 174/175/176   0.06 exactly      the water placeholder
  code 212 dforest   0                 no canopy
  code 229 dwmax     0.5 uniform       a placeholder, not a soil capacity
  code 2290          0.01333 uniform   likewise
  code 129 doro      0                 and this one is CORRECT and stays

Against pure land, where the same fields are mesh-derived and span 0.003..0.7183,
0.1038..0.2605, 0..0.5, 0.0199..0.2568 and 0.0206..0.2072.

So the ocean tile needs nothing: its surface properties are model constants
(albsea, dz0sea, drhssea, computed in seastep from dicec), its temperature is
the declared analytic profile computed unmasked, and its mixed-layer depth is a
scalar. THE WORK IS ENTIRELY ON THE LAND TILE, and it splits three ways:

  ALREADY THERE   roughness, and the land surface temperature (tmelt, set
                  unmasked; code 209 is not staged on this world).
  BUILDER WORK    albedo and field capacity. build_surface_albedo.py already
                  COMPUTES the area-weighted land albedo on every cell
                  containing land and then discards it at
                  `land_cells = fraction >= geography_land_threshold`,
                  writing water_albedo instead. The value exists and is thrown
                  away. Field capacity is the same shape of change.
  A DECISION      vegetation. build_lpj_driver.py selects
                  `simulated_land = land & (rootable > 0.0)` where `land` is
                  the BINARY mask, so LPJ has never run on a sea-owned partial
                  cell. BIO-11's f_rootable is mesh-derived and already nonzero
                  on 2026 of 2048 T21 cells, so the rootable ground is there
                  and only the simulated set excludes it. Extending that set is
                  a change to what the biosphere simulates and costs an LPJ
                  re-run; it is not a builder tweak, and it wants its own row.

Orography is not in this class. One atmosphere column carries one orography, so
doro stays the cell's single elevation; the land tile's height within a partial
cell is a sub-grid lapse-rate question and outside a conservative tile model.

DECLARATION LANDED. config/partial_surface.yaml now carries
tile_model.state.initial_state (vesper-partial-surface-initial-state/1) with a
per-field status and source: five available, two incomplete (albedo, field
capacity), one blocked (vegetation). partial_surface_decision_gate treats the
declaration as the first seam and will not credit either state seam while any
field is short of available, so world-uiq7 cannot invent an initial condition
at the moment it is switched on.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 THE SIX AVAILABLE FIELDS ARE VERIFIED AGAINST THE STAGED ARTIFACTS, not against the declaration. On the 620 cells the binary ownership mask gives to the ocean while code 1720 is positive: code 173 roughness 0.3446..3.5809 m over 610 distinct values, code 229 field capacity 0.01654..0.26549 m over 605. Codes 174/175/176 and 212 are one distinct value each -- 0.06, 0.07028, 0.05364 and 0 -- which is the open-water constant the binary mask wrote. No staged field carries a sentinel, and the roughness builder's own land population is 1639 cells, exactly 586 pure land plus 1053 partial, so no positive-fraction cell is unpopulated.

THE SIZE OF WHAT THE TWO BLOCKED FIELDS COST: those 620 cells hold 11.578 percent of the mesh land area binned to the grid. A land tile switched on today would advance an ninth of this world's land at open-water albedo under no canopy.

AND status: available IS NOW A CLAIM THE GATE CAN REFUSE. Each field names the surface codes it reaches the model through; partial_surface_decision_gate reads them off the staged .sra and fails a field declared available whose value is uniform over that population, or whose code is not staged at all. Both branches were exercised: flipping either blocked field to available fails the check and keeps the state seam uncredited. Before this, available was a string nothing checked, and one edit would have credited the seam over the placeholder.

INSTRUMENT CHECK ON THE ROUGHNESS, recorded and not repaired. cell_moments returns the region count beside the variance because the count says whether a spread means anything, and build_surface_roughness reports its median without gating on it. Over the 620 the count runs from 1 with a fifth percentile of 4, against a minimum of 565 over pure land: the sparse support is exclusive to the cells the land tile newly advances on. Ten cells have exactly one land region, so relief sigma is exactly 0 and the roughness is that region's cover class verbatim, 0.6251..2.9698 m. All 112 cells below 30 regions hold 0.0279 percent of land area, which cannot move a surface-energy term against the 0.12 W m-2 tolerance the tile model was selected on. The 212 cells rougher than any pure-land cell are NOT the sparse ones -- median support 112 regions -- so the high tail is the orographic term working on steep coasts.

Evidence: notes/audits/partial-cell-tile-state.md

title: Reconcile the falsified relaxation-time ceiling with current identifiable-fit evidence
description: exoplasim/analysis/convergence/relaxation_ceiling.json currently reports verdict=falsified. Eleven historical artifacts satisfy its evidence predicate; run_8044646ea7f0 has fitted tau 13.680 orbits above its 9.883-orbit derived expectation and records no fit uncertainty. Audit the pre-uncertainty artifacts or remeasure a current controlled arm; do not silently treat a falsified ceiling as a held bound.
acceptance_criteria: The relaxation-ceiling producer has current discriminating evidence, its verdict is survives or an explicit replacement contract is adopted, and lib/run_lengths.py refuses to consume a bracket whose producer verdict is falsified; a no-model regression covers that refusal.

title: Preserve high-cadence raw output when pyburn conversion fails
description: continue_exoplasim.py --high-cadence completed orbit 127 of run_67323a923013, but pyburn raised an unbound local variable error and the runner printed high-cadence raw kept: [] even though MOST_HC.00127 remained at the run root. The extractor successfully read that 2.0 GB raw into 1,463 samples. Make the continuation move or discover the root raw on postprocessor failure, report its actual path, and add a no-model fixture for the failed-conversion branch.
acceptance_criteria: A simulated pyburn failure leaves the raw high-cadence stream at a discoverable provenance-stamped path, the runner reports it rather than an empty list, and the extractor can consume it.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-nfer (829619208): the bracket check is now one implementation over the whole tree with files discovered rather than listed, 81 brackets against 84 rows, and two holes closed in the discovery pass -- it never entered lists, which is where ntransform.yaml's seven live. Every declared bracket in the tree holds. world-x9zl (e9edb8790): three sites, not two; the steering wind is weighted by layer mass from lib/lapse.py's own sigma levels, checked against the climatology's lev to 4e-7. Sea salt forcing moves 0.29 per cent of its own bracket span and volcanic sulfate peak AOD moves -9.9 per cent, which is not inside the scatter. world-xm1t (42e8aca31, 860d193bb): the rescue reported nothing on every segment for two independent reasons, and the root cause was pyburn logging a name only one arm binds.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
VERIFIED, and the defect is wider than the row states.

The report was empty on EVERY high-cadence segment, success or failure, not
only when pyburn raised. Two reasons, both in the same two lines:

  kept = sorted((run_dir / "highcadence").glob("MOST_HC.[0-9]*"))
  kept = [p for p in kept if p.suffix == ""]

  1. The model never puts the raw in highcadence/. exoplasim/__init__.py:891
     renames plasim_hcadence to MOST_HC.NNNNN at the RUN ROOT; the move on
     :916 is `mv MOST_HC.NNNNN*.nc highcadence/`, the netCDF only. With
     clean=not high_cadence the raw is never deleted either, so it simply
     stays at the run root.
  2. Path("MOST_HC.00127").suffix is ".00127", not "", so the second line
     discards everything the first line could have found anyway.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED on orbit 127, read off the run directory. pyburn raised;
Model.postprocess caught it and called integritycheck, which re-ran pyburn
under example.nl -- the REGULAR variable set and the regular twelve-bin
average -- got a loadable file, and returned 0. No exception propagated, the
segment "succeeded", and highcadence/MOST_HC.00127.nc is a 12-sample file
carrying psi, stf, cl, alb and the rest of the regular codes. The raw beside it
holds 1463 samples; extract_high_cadence_wind.py pulled exactly that. So the
2.0 GB was never lost -- it was unreported, and the file that WAS reported is
a mislabelled twelve-bin average.

The loss path is the other branch: when integritycheck also fails, postprocess
raises, _run calls _crash() (__init__.py:1509 `mv <run>/* <run>_crashed/`), and
the raw goes to a sibling directory nothing in the tree records. The
continuation's except clause then writes a manifest into the emptied run dir
and re-raises.

FIXED in exoplasim/scripts/continue_exoplasim.py:
  - high_cadence_search_roots / find_high_cadence_raw /
    discover_high_cadence_years search the run root, highcadence/ and the
    crashed sibling, matching MOST_HC.NNNNN whole rather than by suffix.
  - preserve_high_cadence_raw moves every stream into highcadence/ and writes
    highcadence/high_cadence_raw.json with run id, source_build, sha256, size,
    expected sample count and where it was recovered from. The sidecar matters
    because _crash() moves run_manifest.json away.
  - Called on BOTH paths, and on the failure path inside its own try so a
    rescue fault cannot replace the exception that caused it. The entry also
    lands in the manifest and in the segment record.
  - --rescue-high-cadence runs only the rescue, before any resume machinery,
    so it works on a run _crash() has emptied.
  - validate_high_cadence refuses a converted file whose time length is not
    what the model wrote. expected_high_cadence_samples derives that from
    plasim.f90:776/841-843/896 rather than asserting it: 5850 runsteps at
    interval 4 gives 1463, which is what the extractor measured.

CHECK: exoplasim/scripts/verify_high_cadence_rescue.py, five fixture cases, no
model and no process. The sample count is cross-checked against a brute-force
count of the model's own write condition; a 12-sample netCDF must be refused
and a 1463-sample one accepted; the raw must be found and stamped from the run
root and from the crashed sibling. Proved able to fail: restricting the search
roots to highcadence/ (the superseded behaviour) fails both discovery cases.

STILL STRANDED: exoplasim/runs/run_67323a923013/MOST_HC.00127 (2.0 GB) is at
the run root with no record, and highcadence/MOST_HC.00127.nc beside it is the
12-bin substitute. `python exoplasim/scripts/continue_exoplasim.py --run
run_67323a923013 --rescue-high-cadence` records it. The substituted .nc is left
as it is; it is untracked run output and nothing should read it.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
The stranded raw is rescued. `continue_exoplasim.py --run run_67323a923013 --reconvert-high-cadence` moved MOST_HC.00127 into highcadence/ and stamped it: sha256 6ffe2d8ade8abe5f7bab1099137fa86291ad70142c52290dd63e3e83a9798011, 1995867952 bytes, both reproduced against the file. The rescue path did not carry an expected sample count -- that stamp was built only on the run path -- and now derives it from the manifest's runsteps_per_orbit and the interval.

The substituted .nc is no longer left as it is. world-u0ck has the argument: its root cause is world-2jj3, a pyburn defect that makes HIGH_CADENCE_CODES unconvertible as declared, and the re-conversion works around it in the caller. The 12-bin file is moved aside as MOST_HC.00127.substituted_regular_average.nc rather than deleted, because it is the evidence of what the segment reported, and exoplasim/runs/INDEX.json now names it per orbit.

title: --glacial is an undeclared erosion rate coefficient and it reaches the terrain
description:
`--glacial` is the glacial erosion RATE coefficient and it has no derivation in this project. It reaches the terrain, so it is a tuned-or-opaque constant sitting on the one artifact that leaves the project and changes the world.

HOW IT IS USED, because the obvious reading is wrong. It enters the carving law TWICE. vendor/orogen/js/glacial-ice.js seeds the ice index with `glacIdx[r] = values[r] * glacialStrength`, and vendor/orogen/js/terrain-post.js:640 then carves with `deepening = gCarveRate * Math.pow(iceFlow[r], 0.6) * glacialStrength`. iceFlow accumulates downstream from glacIdx and is therefore proportional to the strength, so total carving depth goes as strength^1.6: 1.0 erodes about 6.9 times as deep as 0.3. The iteration count is NOT a third factor -- gScale = 1.0/gIters at terrain-post.js:558 is commented "scaled so total effect is the same regardless of iter count" and normalises the round(strength*10) iterations back out.

WHY THE MASK DID NOT SETTLE IT. Before --ice-mask the strength did two jobs: it positioned the ice line through the latitude ramp (at 0.8 the line falls at about 58 degrees) and it set the erosion rate. The mask takes over the FIRST job only. So the mask is not an argument for any particular strength, and it retires the reason the superseded builds carried 0.8 -- that number was chosen for the placement job.

WHAT WAS DONE AND WHY. canonical-10m-carve1 is generated at 0.3, the exporter's own unflagged default, chosen for the negative reason that it is the only available value not selected for a job that no longer exists. It is not derived and this row says so.

WHY A DERIVATION MAY NOT BE OPEN. Sourcing an erosion coefficient wants a rate -- mm per year against a duration -- and docs/src/reference/no-time-axis.md says Orogen has no time axis, so "source it or derive it" may be closed by construction here. If so the remaining disposition is the fourth: declare it with a bracket that gets swept, and record the sweep.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is not another full generation. Drop --regions to a small support and generate at 0.3 and at 0.8. If the basin catalogue and the carve verdict do not move between them, the constant is not worth deriving and the bracket is what gets declared. If they do move, the size of the move is what prices the derivation.

Deferred: it does not block the current pass and the value it would replace is recorded on the build's own manifest as glacialErosion, so nothing is silent about what was used.

title: A run whose thread count came from --ncpus cannot be resumed
description:
`run_exoplasim.py --ncpus N` writes N into the loaded config before the manifest is stamped, so the manifest's source_config carries N while the config FILE still carries whatever it declares. `continue_exoplasim.py` compares the two with lib/provenance.py:config_drift and refuses: `model.ncpus: 8 -> 16`. It has no --ncpus of its own, so there is no way to resume such a run at all short of editing the config file the run already hashed.

Found on world-5oyp: the first paired soil-thermal arms were prepared with --ncpus 8 and could not be extended, and the pair had to be re-run from configs declaring ncpus: 8.

The fix is not a matching --ncpus flag. A continuation MUST integrate on the same executable as the segment before it -- the run directory holds exactly one, and ExoPlaSim compiles one per (resolution, layers, threads) -- so the thread count on a resume is not free to differ and should be ADOPTED from the manifest rather than compared against the config. As it stands, a config declaring 16 against a manifest of 8 would, if the drift check were relaxed, resolve a p16 binary into a run whose earlier orbits are p8, which is worse than the refusal.

Cites exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md, the world-5oyp section.
close_reason:
Fixed. continue_exoplasim.py adopts the thread count from the run manifest before the drift comparison, and prints that it did so with the two numbers.

ADOPTION AND NOT AN EXEMPTION, for the reason the row gives: a continuation integrates on the executable the run directory already holds, and ExoPlaSim compiles one per (resolution, layers, threads), so a config declaring 16 against a manifest of 8 must resolve the p8 binary. The manifest's value is written INTO the config so that everything downstream, the binary resolver included, reads one number. Adding ncpus to INERT_CONFIG_KEYS would have been the exemption and is worse than the refusal it replaces -- it would let a p16 binary resolve into a run whose earlier orbits are p8.

smoke_test.py:check_resume_adopts_the_manifest_thread_count holds all three properties: that the manifest is read at all, that the adoption happens BEFORE the comparison rather than after it, and that the value moves manifest-to-config and not the other way. It also fails if ncpus appears in INERT_CONFIG_KEYS.

title: Measure the surface-to-TOA albedo attenuation instead of bracketing it
description:
scripts/error_budget.py carries DEFAULT_ATTENUATION = 0.5 and says in its own words that the honest claim is a factor of two rather than a number. Every albedo item in the budget is multiplied by it, so a factor of two on it is a factor of two on that whole half of the budget.

PHYS-15's paired arm produced the first measurement. A land-mean alb fall of 0.006397 reached a resolved tas separation of +0.1972 K, which requires an attenuation of 0.3045 through lib/sensitivity.py's own conversion. It lands inside the declared bracket at the low end.

One term is not the budget. The attenuation is a property of what sits above the surface -- cloud, water vapour, the shortwave scheme -- rather than of the surface, so it can differ between a term that acts under cloud and one that acts in the clear, and between a term concentrated over one latitude band and one spread over the land. What would settle it is the same measurement on the other albedo items the budget already prices, each of which is an A/B this project can run cheaply now that the donor is equilibrated: the lakes item, the biosphere endmember pair, and the playa_clastic level. Three more points would say whether 0.3 is the number or whether it varies by term, and the answer decides whether DEFAULT_ATTENUATION becomes a measured constant or stays a declared bracket with its spread reported.

The instrument is now cheap. A paired 25-orbit set from run_893e276ee029's equilibrated restart resolves tas to a standard error near 0.02 K, twenty times better than the arms this project quoted its 1.6 to 2.1 K bar from, because those were seeded from a control still relaxing.

Source: exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md, the PHYS-15 arm's MEASURED section; scripts/error_budget.py:108
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 PRE-REGISTERED, BEFORE ANY NUMBER WAS COMPUTED.

THE INSTRUMENT, AND IT COSTS NO MODEL RUN. Three paired equilibrated spin-ups
already on disk differ in `model.land_albedo_source` alone within one build, one
flux and one rung. That key is the budget's own "biosphere: bare rock vs
vegetated" item, so these arms price the second of the three terms the row names:

  canonical-10m-base    run_58f467b0872d lithology / run_893e276ee029 vegetated
  canonical-10m-carve1  run_4b7281ee038a lithology / run_76e441e0a761 vegetated  (uniform soil water)
  canonical-10m-carve1  run_bd7de9ba67a4 lithology / run_8ff97d5e189a vegetated  (pedology soil water)

THE ESTIMATOR is the same back-solve PHYS-15's 0.3045 came from, so the points
compose: the attenuation `a` that satisfies

    dT = sensitivity.planetary_albedo_to_kelvin(d_land * land_fraction * a)

with dT the difference of the two convergence reports' FITTED ASYMPTOTES -- the
declared estimator `lib/sensitivity.py` measures its own slope with -- and
d_land the model's own diagnosed land-mean `alb` over each run's assessed
window, which is the quantity PHYS-15's 0.006397 is.

A SECOND ESTIMATOR is reported beside it and is NOT averaged with it: the same
back-solve on the STAGED code-174 land mean, which carries no snow or
forest-masking response. The two bracket the term.

A THIRD, INDEPENDENT quantity is read straight from `planetary_albedo_in_window`
in the same reports: d(planetary albedo) / d(surface albedo) at equilibrium.
This is NOT a competing attenuation -- it contains the ice and cloud albedo
feedback that the sensitivity slope already carries, so using it in the chain
would double-count. It is expected ABOVE the effective attenuation, and their
ratio is the feedback amplification, reported as that and nothing else.

PREDICTION. The endmember pairs' effective attenuation lands in 0.20 to 0.50,
and the three pairs agree with each other within a factor of 1.5. The ground is
that the attenuation is a property of what sits above the surface -- cloud,
water vapour, the shortwave scheme -- and all three pairs and PHYS-15 act over
the same land under the same atmosphere.

DECISION RULE, FIXED NOW, over the set {PHYS-15's 0.3045} + {the resolved pairs}:

  - spread within a factor of 1.5: DEFAULT_ATTENUATION becomes MEASURED, set to
    the set's central value and declared with the measured spread as its bracket.
  - spread of 1.5 to 2: same move, and the budget keeps printing both columns.
  - spread beyond a factor of 2: a single constant is the WRONG SHAPE. The
    attenuation stays DECLARED, the row's verdict is that it is term-dependent,
    and what each remaining term would cost to measure is named.

RESOLVING POWER, fixed before the numbers: a pair counts only where its dT
exceeds three times the two asymptote half-widths added in quadrature. An
unresolved pair is excluded BEFORE the spread is taken, not reported as a small
number (failure-modes class 34).

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THE INSTRUMENT ITSELF. These arms are not albedo-only. Code
212 (forest fraction) differs in every pair, and codes 175, 176, 1742, 1750 and
1760 move with 174. If a pair's diagnosed d(alb) and its staged d(174) disagree
by more than a factor of 1.5, the diagnosed albedo is carrying a response the
staged field does not, and the pair is pricing the ENDMEMBER SWAP rather than
the attenuation. It is then reported as a per-item effective attenuation for the
biosphere row alone and is NOT folded into a shared constant.

CURRENCY, stated rather than worked around. All three pairs sit on
canonical-10m-base and canonical-10m-carve1; the configured build is
canonical-10m-carve2. `lib/sensitivity.py`'s slope was measured on
canonical-10m-base, so the base pair is internally current with the slope it is
divided by and the two carve1 pairs are a declared cross-build read. There is no
lithology endmember run on carve2, so no pair on the configured build exists to
prefer.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 COMPLETED. The attenuation is measured, DEFAULT_ATTENUATION is 0.38
with a measured span of 0.29 to 0.48, and `notes/audits/albedo-attenuation.md`
carries the finding. No model run was bought.

WHAT THE PRE-REGISTRATION PREDICTED AND WHAT HAPPENED.

  HELD: the three endmember pairs agree with each other within a factor of 1.5.
  They agree within 1.24 on the staged estimator and 1.10 on the diagnosed one,
  across two builds.

  FAILED: the primary estimator's values land in 0.20 to 0.50. On the
  pre-registered PRIMARY estimator, the model's diagnosed `alb`, they land at
  0.598, 0.642 and 0.657. That is above the band and it is the useful failure.

THE FAILURE IS ABOUT THE CONVENTION AND IT IS THE RESULT. The pre-registration
named the diagnosed estimator primary in order to compose with PHYS-15's
published 0.3045. That was the wrong choice, and the measurement is what shows
it: every item `albedo_items` prices is a delta of a STAGED boundary condition
read from `albedo_report.json`, and a run's diagnosed `alb` is that boundary
condition as realised through the modelled snow. Nothing can set the diagnosed
albedo, so it is not a denominator any item can be written in. On the staged
convention the same four arms give 0.292, 0.381, 0.441 and 0.473.

  STAGED    span 1.62, inside the pre-registered 1.5-to-2 band, whose rule is
            "the measured central value with the measured spread, both columns
            kept". That is what shipped.
  DIAGNOSED span 2.13, which the rule would have refused outright.

So which surface albedo the chain means was load-bearing and nothing in the tree
had said. It is said now, in the module docstring, because it decides the answer.

THE FOUR POINTS, on the staged convention, and they rest on TWO TERMS and three
builds rather than on four independent terms:

  soil wetting, canonical-10m-base                    0.292   PHYS-15's NWETSOIL pair
  biosphere endmember, carve1, uniform soil water     0.381   the CLEAN pair
  biosphere endmember, carve1, pedology soil water    0.441
  biosphere endmember, canonical-10m-base             0.473

Three of them are one term on three builds, which tests build-dependence and not
term-dependence. The row's own caution stands and is now quantified: the spread
WITHIN the endmember term across two builds is 1.24, and BETWEEN the two terms on
one build it is 1.62. Term-dependence is the larger effect and the mechanism the
row predicted is the leading explanation: the wetting term acts where the
modelled skin is wet, which is where it rains, and the endmember term is spread
over land that includes the dry closed-basin interiors where the modelled sky is
clearest. That is a HYPOTHESIS. No cloud-weighted decomposition was measured, and
the gap is also consistent with PHYS-15's own 23 per cent uncertainty, which is
the widest of the four.

THE CENTRAL VALUE is the midpoint of the measured span. That rule was not fixed
in advance and the note says so; what makes it safe is that the alternatives do
not matter at this resolution. Midpoint 0.382, median 0.411, mean 0.396, and
0.362 weighting the two terms equally rather than the four points, which is 13
per cent against a bracket that spans 62 per cent. The midpoint is taken because
it does not silently weight the term that happens to have three builds behind it.

THE INSTRUMENT TEST FIRED ON ONE PAIR AND CHANGED NOTHING. The pre-registration
excluded any pair whose diagnosed and staged deltas disagree by more than 1.5.
The carve1 uniform pair disagrees by 1.57; the others by 1.39 and 1.46. Excluding
it leaves 0.292, 0.441, 0.473, whose span and midpoint are unmoved to three
figures, because the excluded point is interior.

THE CONFOUND THE PRE-REGISTRATION NAMED IS DISPROVED RATHER THAN BOUNDED.
`NVEG = 0` in every run, so `dforest` is prescribed from surface code 212, and
`landmod.f90` uses it in exactly one place, `snowcanopymask`. The forest fraction
that moves with the endmember swap is an albedo effect and touches no flux
directly.

A SECOND CONFOUND WAS FOUND AND IS NOT DISPROVED. The base pair and the carve1
pedology pair stage different soil-water field capacities between their arms,
because the pedology field depends on the vegetation; the carve1 uniform pair
stages none in either. That pair is the clean one and it gives the LOWEST
endmember figure, 0.381, against 0.441 and 0.473. The direction says the field
capacity difference contributes warming and puts the endmember term's honest
value at the low end of its own three rows.

THE NULL. `run_88ed6f9d34ae` and `run_8d0ae7e2d02c`, T42 on canonical-10m-carve2,
identical `surface_field_sha256`, identical `source_config`, DIFFERENT executables
and different routes to equilibrium. Two runs handed the same surface albedo must
separate by nothing: they separate by -0.0071 K and 1.8e-06 in planetary albedo.
The endmember signal is 460 times that, and the null carries an executable
difference the measured pairs do not.

WHAT IS OWED, WITH ITS COST AND ITS BLOCKER. The lakes item and the
`playa_clastic` level are unmeasured. Both are staged-field changes rather than
namelist keys, so each needs `build_surface_albedo.py` re-run under a different
rock table or lake compositing, the six albedo codes RESTAGED, and a paired
25-orbit set branched from an equilibrated restart on the configured build.

  THE RUN IS CHEAP: a paired 25-orbit T21 set at eight threads an arm, pinned and
  concurrent under one host lock, brackets at 6 to 25 minutes of wall clock. The
  low end is what PHYS-15's own arms recorded; the high end is 25 orbits at the
  53 s per orbit config-rationale.md measures for T21 on eight ranks, plus the
  concurrency penalty. The bracket is reported rather than closed because no
  timing of a T21 paired arm survives in this tree.

  THE RESTAGE IS THE BLOCKER. `exoplasim/inputs/t21/` is keyed by RUNG ALONE, so
  it holds exactly one build's albedo field at a time and rewriting it replaces
  what the whole tree reads. In a worktree those six paths are symlinks into the
  main checkout, so a restage there is a write into the shared tree while other
  sessions are reading it. That is a real constraint on when these two can be
  measured, not on whether.

Both would sit on canonical-10m-carve2, which carries no measurement here at all:
there is no bare-rock endmember run on the configured build, so no pair on it
exists to prefer. That is the strongest reason to buy them.

CURRENCY, stated rather than worked around. All four arms sit on
canonical-10m-base or canonical-10m-carve1 and the configured build is
canonical-10m-carve2. `lib/sensitivity.py`'s slope is on canonical-10m-base, so
the base rows are internally current with the slope they are divided by and the
carve1 rows are a declared cross-build read. That read is defensible here in a
way it is not for `HYDROLOGICAL_RESPONSE_PER_KELVIN`, and the difference is which
side of the product moves with the terrain: that response composes with an
amplification taken from the configured build's own water balance, so two builds
are two worlds, while the attenuation is a property of the modelled atmosphere
and the two builds differ only in carved closed-basin floors. The AGREEMENT
between the base and carve1 rows is what makes that evidence rather than an
assumption.

WHAT CHECKS IT. `verify_attenuation` re-reads both asymptotes of every pair from
its convergence report, re-derives the attenuation, and refuses when a row no
longer reproduces its declared value or when the span no longer contains it. It
fired once already, on a span rounded inward. The albedo half cannot be re-read
here and is declared, which is the same split `HYDROLOGICAL_RESPONSE_SECANT`
lives with and for the same reason: PHYS-15's two arms are deleted.

title: Replace the band-2 liquid-absorption bound with Nolet's measured optical path
description:
analysis/soil_albedo_wetting.py bounds the one term neither wetting mechanism carries -- the liquid's own absorption in band 2 -- with skin_equivalent_water_m = 0.02 * 0.45, the whole surface layer's pore volume at saturation. That is the layer's water INVENTORY and not the path a photon traverses, so it is an upper bound and the report says so.

Nolet, Poortinga, Roosjen, Bartholomeus and Ruessink (2014), now held as references/nolet2014-surface-moisture-beach-sand-reflectance.pdf, MEASURES the path directly. Their optical model separates an elastic-scattering fraction from an optical path length in water, and that path at saturation is 0.06 to 0.07 cm, which they check against the sample's 288 um median grain as a few grains deep. The project's bound is 9 mm, more than an order of magnitude larger, and the direction is one-signed: band 2's bracket is far less open at its dark end than the declared magnitude says.

The work is to take the path length as the quantity band2_liquid_absorption is evaluated at, with the bracket Nolet's own two-run spread and grain size support, and to say what it leaves: one material, quartz sand at 1.655 g/cm3, against this world's playa mud and fan fill; an analysis stopping at 2100 nm against a 2.49 um working range; and a biconical reflectance factor rather than a flux albedo. Their two regressions are FITTED and do not transfer; the measured path length is what does.

It restages 1742, 1750 and 1760 and reprices the PHYS-15 entry in exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md, so it is a surface rebuild and not a model change.

Source: references/INDEX.md, the nolet2014 row; analysis/soil_albedo_wetting.py:707-717
notes: Related to PHYS-15 and downstream of it: the endmembers this would move are the ones PHYS-15 stages, and the band-2 dark end is the item PHYS-15's own what_is_still_open list carries. It needs no model run and no host lock: analysis/soil_albedo_wetting.py then exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_albedo.py, both cost 'minutes' in config/pipeline.yaml.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
DONE. band2_liquid_absorption is evaluated at Nolet's measured optical path, 0.06 to 0.07 cm at saturation, instead of the surface layer's 9 mm water inventory. The magnitude falls one-signed: band 2's flux-weighted single-pass absorptance 0.5855 -> 0.2484 to 0.2694, band 1's 0.0307 -> 0.0021 to 0.0024.

THE PDF WAS NOT ACTUALLY HELD. references/INDEX.md's row is marked read with section-level detail and the file was in neither the worktree nor the main checkout. Refetched from PLoS (open access, one call) and every claim in the row checked out against it: Eq. (6) Rh = fs Rd exp(-a d); d at saturation 0.06 to 0.07 cm; quartz sand, dry bulk density 1.655 g/cm3, mean and median grain 324 and 288 um; analysis 350-2100 nm because signal to noise falls above 2100; biconical, nadir at 40 cm under a 30 degree source. That absence is now guarded -- see world-y4ht.

ONE CORRECTION TO THIS ROW. There is no 'two-run spread' in d to bracket with. Nolet ran the experiment twice, the two reflectance series agreed to R2 above 0.997 over 400-2100 nm, and only the dataset with more points was carried into the fit -- so d comes from one run. The bracket is Nolet's own reported range for d at saturation, and the independent support is the grain-size check: grains_deep returns 2.08 and 2.43 against the 288 um median, which is the paper's own 'a few grains deep'.

WHY d TRANSFERS AND THE REGRESSIONS DO NOT, stated in the artifact: d is fitted, but against a(l), pure water's own absorption coefficient, so it comes out a geometric length with a physical meaning rather than a residual. Eq. (7)'s water-retention parameters have no such anchor and are not read.

WHAT IT LEAVES, all three in what_the_path_does_not_carry. One material, quartz sand at 1.655 g/cm3 and a 288 um median, against this world's playa mud and fan fill -- and NO DIRECTION IS ASSERTED for it, because penetration into a scattering medium is set by the single-scattering albedo as well as the grain and this tree carries no absolute scattering coefficient. A biconical reflectance factor rather than a flux albedo. And the 2100 nm cut, which is BOUNDED rather than left open: unconstrained_tail reports the band-2 magnitude with the tail's absorptance driven to each extreme, +0.008 and -0.047 on a tail carrying 5.4 per cent of band-2 flux, so the flat extrapolation above 2100 nm cannot be what decides whether the dark end is open. The inventory is kept as the ceiling the path must sit inside; path_inside_its_inventory is true.

IT DOES NOT RESTAGE 1742, 1750 AND 1760, against this row. The classes block of the artifact is bit-identical to the previous one -- only band2_liquid_absorption and the date moved. The magnitude is not a correction and never entered the endmembers; build_surface_albedo.py reads only band2_liquid_absorption.direction, a sentence it stamps on the field's provenance. So the staged fields carry the same numbers, and restaging is what the next commissioning pass does with the LPJ acceptance it is producing now, not something this row buys.

PHYS-15 IS NOT REPRICED, for the same reason: no registered number in it moves. It GAINS the bound, which is what its ceiling rests on -- the entry concludes the tas test does not discriminate because the ceiling is +1.25 K, and that only holds if the unpriced band-2 darkening under it is small. It now is.

title: pipeline.yaml's 15-19 W/m2 land-endmember gap is above the whole span it sits inside
description:
config/pipeline.yaml line 189, in the surface_albedo step's gate: 'the two land endmembers are 15-19 W/m2 apart in absorbed flux (docs/src/pipeline/sequencing.md A3)'. The cited section carries NO number -- it says only 'as far apart in absorbed flux as the largest sweep this project varies on purpose'. So the figure has no producer anywhere in the tree and is a frozen derived quantity of the class notes/audits/frozen-derived-quantities.md enumerates.

It is now measurable, and it does not survive the measurement.

The gate's pair is vegetated -> modelled, the adoption it is budgeting for. The endmember bracket just ran the WIDER pair, lithology -> vegetated, on canonical-10m-base at T21, matched window 37-69 and matched I/O regime on both arms (run_e0c431cf67e2 against run_432e5e46adef):

  planetary albedo   0.3232 -> 0.3369, +0.0137
  absorbed at TOA    4.40 W/m2 globally, 10.30 over land
  absorbed at surface 5.39 W/m2 globally, 12.6 over land
  global mean surface temperature  -2.924 K

--mode modelled takes tree cover from an LPJ fpc.out instead of asserting uniform vegetation everywhere including the deserts, so it is BRIGHTER than vegetated and sits strictly between these two endmembers. Its distance from vegetated is therefore bounded above by the full span, 4.40 W/m2 at TOA. 15-19 is more than three times that, and above every denominator the span can be quoted on except none.

Either the figure is measuring something other than what the sentence says, or it is wrong. It matters because the gate uses it to justify 'adopting it is a forcing change of the first rank and it requires the flux to be re-derived' -- a real cost, budgeted on this number. If the true gap is a few W/m2 rather than fifteen, the re-derivation may still be needed but the argument for it is not the one written.

WHAT SETTLES IT: build_surface_albedo.py --mode modelled needs an fpc.out and LPJ-GUESS does not build until a baseline climatology exists, so the direct measurement waits on loop C. What does not wait: replace the literal with the bound this bracket already establishes, or delete it and let the gate cite the measurement.
close_reason: Corrected rather than tracked. config/pipeline.yaml and docs/src/pipeline/sequencing.md now carry the measured bound -- 4.40 W/m2 absorbed at TOA and 2.924 K for the whole lithology-to-vegetated span, from run_e0c431cf67e2 against run_432e5e46adef on matched windows and matched I/O regime -- with modelled bounded strictly inside it. The re-derivation requirement stands at about seven candidate-grid steps; the ranking claim does not, the span being a fifth of the stellar sweep's 21 W/m2.

title: Two aeolian scripts pass an index array where bin centres belong, silently getting equal weights
description:
Found while sweeping for nonlinear-function-on-an-annual-mean instances; a different class and worth filing separately because it is silent.

Two scripts under aeolian/ call lib/climatology.py's bin weighting with an INDEX ARRAY where the function expects bin centres. Evenly spaced indices produce evenly spaced weights, so the call succeeds and returns a uniform weighting rather than the climatology's own. Nothing raises and nothing looks wrong: a uniform weighting is a perfectly ordinary array.

WHY IT MATTERS EVEN THOUGH THIS WORLD'S BINS MAY BE NEARLY EVEN: lib/climatology.py exists because the bin weights DIFFER BETWEEN I/O REGIMES, which is stated in its own docstring, and because a climatology built over a partial window does not have even bins. A call that ignores its argument is right by coincidence at best and cannot be relied on to stay right when the cadence or the window changes.

The fix is to pass the time coordinate the climatology carries, which is what every correct caller does. The check worth adding alongside is whether the weighting function can detect that it was handed indices rather than centres -- monotone integers starting at zero is a recognisable signature -- and refuse rather than return a plausible uniform array.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-vwqw (e39de02e9): both sites read bin centres off the climatology's own time; the correction is 0.29 per cent of the scripts' own bracket span, smaller than the instrument's scatter, which is the result. The sweep found a larger sibling worth -0.96 per cent on volcanic sulfate forcing and two more hand-rolled instances. world-cpke (10f974442): only one of the seven took a naive time mean, the other six get the ORDER wrong; fix-versus-bracket is decided by whether the binned arrays are still in scope, which the audit table now records. The convex sign held in all 33367 gated cells and the correction is two orders inside Dunne's own S_y.x.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Fixed in the working tree (uncommitted): build_sea_salt.py and build_volcanic_sulfate.py now read `bin_centres` off the climatology's own `time` variable and pass that to `climatology.bin_weights`.

VERIFIED DEFECT. On the current baseline regular climatology the time axis inverts to 182 raw records in 12 bins, counts [15,15,15,15,15,16,15,15,15,15,15,16]. The index spelling returned 1/12 = 0.0833333 for every bin; the correct weights are 15/182 = 0.0824176 for ten bins and 16/182 = 0.0879121 for bins 5 and 11. The two long bins were under-weighted by 5.49% and the other ten over-weighted by 1.11%.

SIZE OF THE CORRECTION, in what the consumers read. Sea salt: global emission +0.0163%; per cell the change reaches 1.32% of the ocean-mean emission. Volcanic sulfate: the source is the outgassing requirement and does not move, so the change arrives through removal and transport only, and the implied global-mean burden moves by about -0.03%. Driver fields: lowest-level wind and steering wind change by at most 0.025 m/s on fields of rms 7.3 and 4.3 m/s; precipitation +0.10% ocean mean; sea ice +0.06%; surface temperature +0.002 K in the mean. Every one of those is two to three orders below the declared brackets these scripts already sweep (wet_lifetime_hours 25 [12,40] for sea salt, 96 [60,150] for sulfate), and below the 0.44% of the orbit a binned file never covers at NLOWIO = 0. The correction is far smaller than the instrument's own scatter on THIS climatology, which is the expected result and not the reason to make it: the call was right by coincidence and stopped being checkable.

CHECK ADDED: scripts/smoke_test.py:check_bin_weights_take_bin_centres, registered in the gate. Two halves. (1) An import-resolved AST scan of every project .py for a call into lib/climatology.py whose centres argument is a synthesised axis (arange/linspace/range/indices). It resolves names rather than matching text, so build_sea_salt's local annual_mean(field, weights) is not confused with the climatology function of the same name. (2) A fixture that reconstructs the bin centres pyburn's binning implies for 403 record counts over 4 and 12 bins, requires infer_ntimes to invert them back to the record count and bin_weights to return the counts themselves, and uses the index spelling as the CONTROL: where the counts are uneven the two answers must be at least half a record apart, and where the bins are truly equal they must agree exactly. Both halves were shown to fire: the scan flagged a reintroduced call, and collapsing bin_weights to uniform produced 642 failures.

SWEPT UP, a different defect in the same family, in build_volcanic_sulfate.py: `np.mean(rh_cell)` set the humidity the single-scattering albedo and asymmetry parameter are read at. Every other global mean in that same function is coslat-weighted, and build_sea_salt's `rh_mean` is too. Unweighted the Gaussian grid reads 70.45% where the area-weighted answer is 74.41%. ssa is 1.000000 at both (sulfate scatters), but the asymmetry parameter moves 0.776917 -> 0.779055 and the backscatter fraction 0.111542 -> 0.110473, about -0.96% on the volcanic sulfate TOA shortwave forcing. That is roughly 30 times the bin-weighting correction. Now area-weighted.

NOTHING IS STALE. aeolian/analysis holds only the dust products; sea_salt_baseline.* and volcanic_sulfate.* have never been produced in this tree, so the fix invalidates no existing artifact. build_dust.py already passed bin centres and is untouched.

THREE FINDINGS LEFT UNFIXED, all outside the scope this session was given.

1. lib/climatology.py's degenerate branch is wrong, not merely conservative. infer_ntimes returns nbin whenever the bin centres are evenly spaced, and its docstring argues that even spacing means nbin divides the record count so every candidate gives the same equal weights. That is false for counts that alternate about a constant pair sum: 18 records in 12 bins gives counts [1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2], whose centres ARE evenly spaced, and the true weights alternate 1/18 and 2/18 -- a factor of two, returned as uniform without raising. Same for 30 records in 12 bins, and for every ntimes near 1.5*nbin. The new fixture excludes exactly those cases and says why, so the gate asserts nothing false, but the hole is real and the honest repair is for infer_ntimes to refuse rather than return nbin when the counts it would imply are not equal. This issue's own suggested fix -- have bin_weights recognise monotone integers from zero and refuse -- also belongs in that module and could not be made from this session's scope.

2. scripts/smoke_test.py's SCRIPT_DIRS does not include aeolian/, ocean/, minerals/ or analysis/, so every file-based check in the gate is blind to four components. Both call sites in this issue lived in one of them. The new check builds its own file list for that reason and says so; widening SCRIPT_DIRS would fix it for all the others but needs a pass over whatever it newly flags.

3. Both aerosol scripts comment "mass-weighted over the layers below the steering sigma" and then take ua[:, below].mean(axis=1), an unweighted mean over levels. The layers below sigma 0.5 on this grid are not equally thick, so the comment describes a weighting the code does not apply.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Sweep continued past the two named call sites: the same equal-weighting defect appears twice more in aeolian/ in a hand-rolled spelling, dividing a sum over the time bins by their COUNT instead of weighting by the records each bin holds. Both fixed in the working tree.

1. aeolian/scripts/build_dust.py, the deposition loop. Two lines above it the optical depth and the emission go through climatology.masked_mean(..., bin_centres, good); the deposition summed over the same bins and divided by len(good). The two products of one script were means over the same bins under different weightings. There is now one `bin_weight` vector, built from the bin centres and renormalised over `good`, and the deposition sum uses it.

2. aeolian/scripts/dust_intensity_levers.py, Emitter.total. `out / len(self.good)`. The Emitter did not read the time axis at all; it now does, and carries the same renormalised weight vector. Its `climatology` parameter and the `climatology` local in main() were renamed `clim_path`, because the module of that name is now imported.

SIZE, by proxy and labelled as one. Neither can be measured without a build_dust run, which is not being taken while the host is busy. The bin structure the reweighting acts on is the near-surface wind: the land-area mean of spd^3, a proxy for the emission's bin-to-bin shape, moves -0.0489% under the correct weights and up to 1.393% in a single cell, and the land mean of precipitation moves -0.0538%. The land-mean proxy spans only 1.48x across the twelve bins, so the reweighting has little room to do more than that. Same order as the sea-salt figure, and again far below the brackets these products carry.

NOW STALE, and deliberately not regenerated: aeolian/analysis/dust_baseline.json and dust_baseline.nc (deposition_low/central/high moved; aod_* and emission_* did not), and aeolian/analysis/dust_intensity_levers.json. Both need a build_dust-class run.

The new gate check does NOT cover this spelling: it looks at what is passed to lib/climatology.py, and a `/ len(good)` divides by a count without calling into that module at all. A static lint for it would be noisy. What holds these two now is that each carries the weight vector beside the masked_mean call that shares it.
