title: Seven more nonlinear functions are evaluated on an annual mean where the ledger declares a bin floor
description:
notes/audits/annual-mean-of-a-nonlinear-function.md enumerates them, found while correcting two instances of the same class in the lake balance and the carve verdict. Both of those were worth 1.17x and 1.57x respectively, so the class is not cosmetic.

THE SHAPE: a nonlinear function of a climate variable evaluated once on the annual mean, where hydrography/config/land_water_ledger.yaml or an equivalent declares the quantity has a bin floor. Jensen's inequality says the two differ, the sign depends on the curvature, and a rectifier -- max(x, 0) -- makes the difference large rather than second order because the annual mean can sit on the flat side of a kink the bins straddle.

THE SEVEN, none in the files the finding agent owned:
  sea salt at U10^3.5 on annual-mean wind
  the WHAK exp(T) * Q^beta in build_soil.py
  the same in weathering_fluxes.py
  the same in thermostat_efficiency.py
  the same again in minerals
  hygroscopic growth on annual-mean humidity
  Planck weighting on a temperature collapsed to one annual AND global scalar

The interval_floor declarations themselves are clean, so the config states the requirement correctly and the code does not meet it.

WHAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN ARITHMETIC, and the reason the two fixed instances did not simply switch to per-bin: the per-bin evaluation is not automatically the right one. Penman carries no heat storage, a term that integrates to zero over a whole cycle but not over a bin, so the annual evaluation is right for a deep water body and the bin evaluation for one with no heat capacity. That case was resolved by BRACKETING between the two, which is the idiom the carve already used. Each of the seven needs the same question asked: is the annual evaluation wrong, or is it one end of a bracket whose other end is the bin evaluation, and what physical quantity is the spread measuring.

DO NOT assume the answer is per-bin everywhere.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-vwqw (e39de02e9): both sites read bin centres off the climatology's own time; the correction is 0.29 per cent of the scripts' own bracket span, smaller than the instrument's scatter, which is the result. The sweep found a larger sibling worth -0.96 per cent on volcanic sulfate forcing and two more hand-rolled instances. world-cpke (10f974442): only one of the seven took a naive time mean, the other six get the ORDER wrong; fix-versus-bracket is decided by whether the binned arrays are still in scope, which the audit table now records. The convex sign held in all 33367 gated cells and the correction is two orders inside Dunne's own S_y.x.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Re-verified all seven rows against source on 2026-08-30 and took the first two measurements. notes/audits/annual-mean-of-a-nonlinear-function.md now carries the corrections, the disposition column and the numbers.

ROW CORRECTIONS. Six of the seven claims are TRUE as written. Row 2 (build_soil weathering_intensity) is PARTLY TRUE: the frost fraction is five lines away and not twenty, and more importantly the binned tas/pr/evap are consumed inside the `with nc.Dataset` block and discarded, so a per-bin evaluation there needs the reads restructured rather than the statements reordered. The audit's table gained a "binned arrays still in scope" column, because that is what decides fix from bracket: sea salt and volcanic sulfate can be fixed where they stand (solve() closes over the binned arrays), the three pedology rows and the two exoplasim rows cannot.

The minerals row's "unweighted .mean(axis=0)" is TRUE and it was the ONLY one of the seven taking a naive time mean; the other six already weight by record count and get the ORDER wrong, not the weighting. In the two exoplasim files the GLOBAL collapse is the larger of the two errors, so a per-bin fix alone would address the smaller term.

Both "defects found on the way" in the audit are now FALSE and were corrected: the bin_weights(np.arange(nbin)) claim is stale in all three files, and lib/climatology.py now RAISES on an index array rather than returning uniform weights, so the mechanism no longer exists; the build_groundwater seven-of-eight unpack is fixed at all three call sites and only the comments were stale. Those comments are rewritten. A separate live arity bug in the same file, measure_carve_effect calling per_basin_forcing with nine arguments where the signature takes ten, is fixed.

WHAT WAS DONE, minerals (the one row not in a directory another agent holds): the naive time means are now lib/climatology.py's record-count weighting, and the WHAK evaluation interval is DECLARED AS A BRACKET in downstream_prospectivity_report.json rather than chosen. Annual is the shipped arm because it is the arm the law was fitted on (pedogenesis.yaml records Dunne's applicability as MEAN ANNUAL air temperature) and because it is the low end; the bin arm is the upper end because the kinetics are Arrhenius and instantaneous. Runoff stays annual in BOTH arms, argued from the land water ledger, and the runoff-per-bin combination is measured and reported as not-an-arm.

MEASURED, on baseline_regular_climatology.nc against canonical-10m-carve2, on the mesh, over the cells each rule's gates select. Only bauxite and laterite_ni scale by the intensity. bauxite 14,158 gated cells, bin/annual 1.0087; laterite_ni 19,209 cells, 1.0080. The predicted sign held exactly: exp() is convex so the bin arm can never fall below the annual one, and across 33,367 gated cells not one did. Over all land the ratio is 1.215 and reaches 23.9x on a single cell.

THE CORRECTION IS SMALLER THAN THE INSTRUMENT AND THAT IS THE RESULT. The gates select wet and warm, which here is also where the seasonal swing is smallest: 3-4 K against a land median of 57 K. The emitted 0-1 prospectivity moves 0.8-0.9% in the area mean and 0.12% at the best cell. pedogenesis.yaml records S_y.x = 0.13 log units, a factor of 1.35 on the law itself, and the e-folding choice between 13.7 and 8.91 K is a further 1.4-1.5x. A 0.9% shift is two orders inside the law's own uncertainty. The runoff-per-bin combination is much larger, 1.25x bauxite and 1.16x laterite, and is the one the ledger refuses.

SWEPT UP, same class, fixed: analysis/emissivity_contrast.py and maps/build_basemap.py both reduced a climatology time axis with an unweighted mean under a threshold; scripts/world_state.py had an unreachable naive reduction after its annual mean and now refuses instead. lib/lapse.py fits the annual-MEAN profile where a least-squares slope is nonlinear in it: measured at 6.799 vs 6.763 K/km, -0.53%, one-signed in 937 of 1,019 cells but not predictable in advance since a slope is not a convex functional. Declared at the site rather than changed, because the per-bin rate varies by 1.21 K/km within a cell, 34x the correction.

THE CHECK. scripts/smoke_test.py gained "no nonlinear function is evaluated on a naive time mean". A lint over every producer that reduces a whole netCDF variable over axis 0 with a bare .mean(), plus a fixture on the real weathering_intensity requiring that the two arms agree EXACTLY when the bins are identical (the control, under both even and deliberately uneven weights), differ by exactly cosh(dT/tau) for a symmetric swing, are strictly above 1 for the convex temperature term and strictly BELOW 1 for the concave runoff term. Demonstrated to fire on four distinct injected defects and to pass on the tree. Two argued-unweighted sites are declared by (file, variable) with their reasons rather than waived: build_dust.py's spd, where the Weibull shape needs mean and variance weighted alike, and derive_design_flux.py's lsm, which does not vary across bins.

LEFT TO OTHER AGENTS, all six remaining rows: aeolian/scripts/build_sea_salt.py and build_volcanic_sulfate.py, pedology/scripts/build_soil.py, weathering_fluxes.py and thermostat_efficiency.py, exoplasim/scripts/dust_forcing.py and build_surface_dust.py. Also unfixed and in scope for whoever holds hydrography: build_groundwater.py:171 takes climate_fields with no bin_index, so Penman is evaluated once on annual-mean air on the groundwater path, which is exactly the defect carve_verdict.py and surface_water.py were already fixed for; climate_fields(config, bin_index=k) is an existing parameter and surface_water.py:591 is the working template.

STALE: minerals/data/<build>/downstream_prospectivity.nc and its report (neither exists yet), analysis/land_emissivity.json and emissivity_contrast.json, maps/build/basemap.npy and every frame inheriting it, world_state.json's climatology-derived temperature, and any consumer of lib/lapse.py's annual lapse rate (unchanged in value; the comment is new).

title: Soil's erosion term never sees lake moisture, while its vegetation already does
description:
build_soil.py takes its runoff from bootstrap_climatology, and a bootstrap is TERRAIN-ONLY by definition -- no lakes, on the first iteration and on every one after. So the moisture that inland open water adds to a continental interior never reaches the denudation term, whatever the loop does.

WHY THIS IS AN OVERSIGHT AND NOT A SEPARATION, which is the part that settles it: soil ALREADY depends on the baseline climatology transitively. The graph reads soil -> lpj_run -> lpj_driver -> baseline_climatology. So one step takes its VEGETATION from a lake-bearing climate and its RUNOFF from a lake-free one. A considered design would not split a single step's forcing across two stages of the same world; a leftover would.

WHAT IT IS WORTH, measured 2026-08-27 on canonical-10m-base against precarve-craton-10m:

  soil depth, median   0.876 m  ->  0.203 m
  AWC, median          112.80 mm -> 25.09 mm
  AWC, p90             306.98 mm -> 174.50 mm

The distribution is bimodal rather than uniformly thin. The top quartile carries 1.454 m and 151.66 mm, which is ordinary; the bottom quartile carries 0.050 m and 10.07 mm, which is bare rock, and 28.9 per cent of land sits at or below 0.10 m.

MOST OF THAT MOVE IS NOT THIS DEFECT and the row should not be read as claiming it. world-9ctm sourced dry_erosion_baseline from Portenga and Bierman, 0.15 to 0.85, and depth goes as the reciprocal of the moisture term, so arid erosion rose 5.67x by a measurement this project accepts. What this row claims is narrower: the arid tail is evaluated against a climate that is missing the interior water the finished world has, so the tail is deeper than the world's own physics implies.

THE CEILING ON THE EFFECT, and it is only a ceiling: hydrography reports area_at_spill_fraction_of_planet 0.0821, so at most 8.2 per cent of the planet is inland open water with every basin full. The actual figure is what surface_water.py computes and that step is currently blocked, so this cannot be sized yet.

CANDIDATE FIXES, none obviously right:
  - soil reads the BEST AVAILABLE climatology, preferring the baseline and taking the bootstrap only when no baseline exists, with the choice stamped in its provenance. Not a silent fallback -- both are the same world at different stages -- but it does cut against the no-fallback rule lib/paths.py enforces, so the argument has to be explicit.
  - a second bootstrap after lakes exist, which costs a run per commissioning.
  - accept the split and say why, which requires an argument nobody has made.

DOCS CONSEQUENCE: docs/src/reference/vocabulary.md defines commissioning as 'terrain-only surface fields, bootstrap run, every derived field rebuilt from the bootstrap climatology, baseline run, convergence'. Whichever fix lands, that sentence moves with it.
close_reason:
Candidate fix one landed, which is the one this row listed first: build_soil.py:529 calls lib/paths.py:best_available_climatology and takes the baseline once one is named, the bootstrap before that. The choice is not silent -- the function returns the stage it chose, soil_report.json carries climatology_stage ('bootstrap' today) beside the path and the sha, and a named baseline that is MISSING raises rather than dropping back, which is what keeps this inside the no-fallback rule rather than around it.

The comment above the call makes this row's own argument: 'This step already took its vegetation from lpj_run, which reaches the baseline through lpj_driver, so pinning the runoff to a terrain-only climate that carries no lakes on any iteration built one soil map out of two stages of one world.' The needs: bootstrap_climatology edge in config/pipeline.yaml is unchanged and now says something else -- the bootstrap is what must EXIST for the step to run at all.

THE DOCS CONSEQUENCE THIS ROW NAMED IS ALSO DONE. docs/src/reference/vocabulary.md's commissioning definition reads 'every derived field rebuilt from the BEST AVAILABLE climatology' with the second-pass argument under it, where it read 'from the bootstrap climatology'.

AND THE EFFECT CAN NOW BE SIZED, which this row said it could not be while surface_water.py was blocked. It is not blocked: on canonical-10m-base the solved lakes cover 4.25 per cent of the planet on the vegetated arm and 3.94 on the bare-rock one, against the 8.21 per cent ceiling this row quoted from area_at_spill_fraction_of_planet. So the interior water the arid tail was missing is about half the ceiling, and from the next pass the denudation term sees it.

title: derive_design_flux's per-band projection assumes a positive warm-season amplification, and four bands violate it
description:
derive_design_flux.py refuses on the first real two-point derivation for this world: 'a band's warm-season amplification is not positive; the projection cannot be trusted'. The guard is correct and the refusal is the right behaviour; what it blocks is the whole derivation.

MEASURED on run_432e5e46adef (flux 0.945) and run_b45380e61f90 (flux 1.000), both converged, global mean moving +8.544 K. Four land bands' WARMEST bin gets colder as the star gets brighter:

  70 to 80 S   coldest +19.28 K   warmest  -0.07 K
  60 to 70 S   coldest +25.04 K   warmest  -1.41 K
  60 to 70 N   coldest +19.60 K   warmest  -2.73 K
  70 to 80 N   coldest +15.82 K   warmest  -2.30 K

The method projects candidate means per 10-degree band by scaling the band's seasonal delta against the global one, so a negative amplification makes the projected field meaningless and the script stops rather than returning a plausible number.

THIS IS NOT A BRACKET PROBLEM AND A THIRD FLUX POINT WILL NOT FIX IT. The sign is a property of how this world's seasons respond, not of where the two points sit. At 32 degrees of obliquity high-latitude summer land is warmed by melting out of snow cover under clear skies; brightening the star adds moisture and cloud and retreats the sea ice, which couples that land to an ocean whose heat capacity damps the summer peak. Winter warms 25 K while summer cools 2 K in the same band.

WHAT IS OPEN is the instrument rather than the thresholds. Candidates worth separating: projecting the two seasons independently rather than through one per-band amplification; using a statistic that does not assume the seasons move together; or accepting that a per-band linear projection cannot represent a world where the seasonal RANGE contracts with warming, and bracketing the comfort score directly from runs instead of projecting it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FLUX, so this row is not read as blocking more than it does: orbit.baseline_flux_earth stays at 0.945 and the world it gives has been judged acceptable on the two points measured -- comfort score 0.657, the best available across the projected range, warmest-bin land mean 23.0 C and coldest-bin -13.8 C. What this row blocks is DERIVING that number rather than choosing it, so 0.945 stands by decision and not by derivation, and config/planet.yaml should say so.

notes/audits/design-flux-two-point-response.md carries the measurement.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-m61p (842af7575): three of the row's claims were wrong and five bands violated the sign test, not four; the test was neither necessary nor sufficient for the warm>=cold identity it stood in for, and a second defect had the projection missing its own anchors by 22.1 per cent. band_amplification_sign deleted; the instrument now refuses on cold_extreme_cap, which world-dnrr carries. world-mro1 (e6e635233, later widened tree-wide in 829619208): the bracket check has four dispositions and a discovery pass, and the row's premise needed correcting -- regolith_depth_bracket_m was already read. world-l442 (fcd495b91): the acid end relaxes onto a gibbsite buffer; the pre-registered bracket derivation FALSIFIED and the reason was the parent spacing, not the slope. world-ysd1 (f7a3e96d9): --purge reaches the seed's own writes, with orgen the single by-name exemption because source/ is read-only under rule 7.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
VERIFIED AGAINST THE SOURCE, and three claims in this row need correcting.

1. "a negative amplification makes the projected field meaningless" is not
   true of the arithmetic. The projection was
     projected(f) = base + amp * slope * (f - f0)
   with amp = (band delta)/(global delta). That is a straight line; nothing
   divides by amp, and it is defined and continuous for either sign. A
   negative warm-season slope is a measurement carried exactly.

2. "projecting the two seasons independently rather than through one per-band
   amplification" is already what the code did: amp["warm"] and amp["cold"]
   are separate per band. That candidate was not open.

3. FIVE bands violate the sign assumption, not four, on the current best
   available climatology. The row's four were measured against
   run_432e5e46adef's bootstrap; best_available_climatology() now returns the
   BASELINE of run_67323a923013, and against run_b45380e61f90 the global span
   is -7.196 K, not 8.544. Bands with a non-positive warm response:
   -80/-70 (-0.243), -70/-60 (-0.597), +60/+70 (-0.574), +70/+80 (-0.475),
   +80/+90 (-0.177).

THE SIGN TEST IS NEITHER NECESSARY NOR SUFFICIENT, and that is the defect.
What must hold for a projected field to be a field is that warm >= cold: they
are the max and the min of the same twelve bins. Per-band crossing fluxes on
the current pair, against the declared candidate range 0.7775 to 1.11:

  -60 to -50   amp_warm +0.292   band range closes at f = 1.083   INSIDE
  +50 to +60   amp_warm +0.182   band range closes at f = 1.098   INSIDE
  -80 to -70   amp_warm -0.243   closes at 1.188                  outside
  +70 to +80   amp_warm -0.475   closes at 1.171                  outside
  +80 to +90   amp_warm -0.177   closes at 1.324                  outside

So the guard refused three bands that stay fields across the whole range and
passed two that stop being fields inside it. Per CELL it is worse: land cells
begin inverting at f = 0.996 and 19.1% of land is inverted at 1.11.

A SECOND DEFECT, found while verifying. The projection did not pass through
its own anchor points. It converted flux to kelvin with
sensitivity.SLOPE_K_PER_FLUX_RATIO = 159.7 while normalising each band's move
by the span the two sources showed, -7.196 K over -0.055 in flux, a local
130.8 K per unit flux. Every band mean at the bracket point came out 22.1% too
far -- a line missing a point it was fitted to.

THE INSTRUMENT AGAINST THE EFFECT. Per-orbit scatter of the band-mean warmest
bin over the bracket run's 10-orbit tail, naive sem (a floor: the base
climatology's own scatter is not in it, and lib/autocorrelation.py reports
reliable=False on 10 samples, tau 1.16):

  +80 to +90   dT +1.27 K   sem 0.86   1.5 sigma   NOT RESOLVED
  -80 to -70   dT +1.75 K   sem 0.67   2.6 sigma   marginal
  +70 to +80   dT +3.42 K   sem 0.93   3.7 sigma   marginal
  -70 to -60   dT +4.30 K   sem 0.42  10.2 sigma   solid
  +60 to +70   dT +4.13 K   sem 0.38  10.9 sigma   solid

Two of the five negative-response bands are real, two marginal, one is noise.
The row's "70 to 80 S warmest -0.07 K" was 0.07 K against a 0.67 K sem.

THE REPAIR, in exoplasim/scripts/derive_design_flux.py:
  - The per-band quantity is now a signed RESPONSE in kelvin per unit flux
    ratio taken between the two points directly, so the projection reproduces
    both anchors. The ratio to the global move is still reported per band as
    the diagnostic 5b argues in; nothing projects with it and nothing tests
    its sign. The canonical slope still converts the candidate range's kelvin
    margins, which is a different and correct use.
  - band_amplification_sign is DELETED. CHOOSABLE_REFUSALS is now empty, with
    the argument in the docstring.
  - The candidates scored are those the projection is a field on; the window
    is reported, contiguity is asserted, an inversion at a MEASURED flux is a
    refusal, and the existing edge-winner refusal now guards the scored ends.

WHAT THE FIXED INSTRUMENT RETURNS. Scored window 0.7775 to 1.0075, 41 of 134
candidates dropped. It does not answer: it refuses on the DECLARED
cold_extreme_cap of 0.05, which was always behind the sign guard. The smallest
cold-extreme land fraction any scored candidate reaches is 0.117, and at 0.945
it is 0.247 -- and 0.945 is f0, where the projection IS the measured baseline
field, so that is a measurement and not a projection. A quarter of this
world's land has a coldest bin below -40 C. With the cap lifted for
diagnosis only, the uncapped comfort winner is 0.91 at 0.658; 0.945 scores
0.620.

CONSEQUENCES, not regenerated:
  - exoplasim/analysis/design_flux.json (basis chosen, refused_at
    band_amplification_sign) stands on a ground the generator no longer
    declares. check_consistency.py's chosen-flux check reads CHOOSABLE_REFUSALS
    from the generator and will FAIL on it until the derivation is re-run.
  - config/planet.yaml's baseline_flux_earth comment, docs/src/pipeline/state.md
    section 5b's "four land bands" paragraph and check_consistency.py's
    section header all restate the deleted refusal.
  - The open question is now the cap, not the projection: either 0.05 is
    wrong for this terrain or this terrain is wrong for 0.05.

CHECK: exoplasim/scripts/verify_design_flux_projection.py, five cases on

title: Arm the soil albedo moisture term once a dry-reachable soil store and a band-2 relation exist
description:
phys-15 declared the modelled soil albedo's moisture dependence ABSENT, with its magnitudes computed and a guard that refuses a field in which any land region sits at or below open water's albedo. This row is what arms it, and it exists because a declared absence names its arming condition or it is just a silence.

THREE PRECONDITIONS, none of which held when phys-15 was declared.

1. A SOIL STORE THAT CAN REACH DRY. dwmax is a PLANT-AVAILABLE capacity, so an empty modelled store is the wilting point at sr_at_wilting_point 0.4114, while the dry endmembers this project holds are laboratory-dry. Mixing across that gap applies a permanent level shift as well as a season, reaching 0.105 to 0.140 in albedo on the evaporite class against a bare-versus-vegetated gap of 0.069 over the whole simulated planet. The residual water content is value: undeclared in the land column contract and is owned by LSHY-3; declaring it fixes the shift's size, not its existence.

2. A BAND-2 RELATION. The model reads the albedo pair at NSIMPLEALBEDO 0. Penndorf (1956) is luminous reflectance, so it brackets band 1 only, and band 2 carries 0.617628 of this star's flux and is where liquid water absorbs. Lekner and Dorf (1988) and Twomey, Bohren and Mergenthaler (1986) are the two that would close it by giving a wavelength-resolved wet-versus-dry relation to apply to the dry spectra already held; both are recorded as unfetchable from this host with their DOIs.

3. A SETTLED SIGN ON SALT CRUST. The sources disagree on the class it matters most for: Malek et al. (1990) and Craft and Horel (2019) make wetted crust much darker in situ, while the twenty-year MODIS series over Uyuni makes wet years brighter. One saturation number cannot carry both, and adopting either without settling it would put a sign into the model that the evidence does not support.

DEPENDS ON DUST-17, which is where the authoritative top emitting-layer liquid water state is defined. Taking a second wetness state here instead is precisely the second central hydrology dust-17 exists to prevent.

exoplasim/notes/soil-albedo-moisture.md carries the declaration, the magnitudes and the guard.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED by phys-15 being reopened. This row was filed as the arming row for a declared absence, on the reading that the modelled soil albedo's moisture term could not be built now. That reading was wrong: the test is whether the term can be modelled MORE CORRECTLY, and the land column contract names the fix itself -- a thin surface layer that dries below the wilting point. The three preconditions this row carried are phys-15's work now, and the DUST-17 dependency has moved back to phys-15.

title: conversion_time_level traps at T21 dt 15 min, below the model's own gravity-wave guard
description:
Found while measuring the CONVDECOMP race (world-tqh4), on arms built for that purpose.

At T21 the model's own guard puts the explicit gravity-wave limit at 18.7 minutes and refuses dt 30 and dt 20. Below the guard, with nconvtime = 1 the model TRAPS on SIGFPE at dt 15 and completes at 12 and 10. With nconvtime = 0 the same bed completes at 15.

So the failure at 15 is THE TERM, not the timestep, and the guard's limit is not where the term becomes usable. An arm wanting conversion_time_level at T21 runs at 12 minutes or below, and the gap between 18.7 and 12 is a range in which the model accepts a configuration the conversion-time diagnostic cannot survive.

WHY THIS IS NOT IN THE WAY OF ANY CURRENT RUN: config/planet.yaml declares energy_diagnostics: true, which is level 1, and does not declare conversion_time_level, so a configured run never allocates zcnow and never reaches this term. That was checked at the root rather than arm by arm -- reaching it requires energy_diagnostics: 2 or conversion_time_level: true explicitly.

WHAT IS OPEN: whether the trap is a genuine stability boundary for the term or an unguarded division inside it, and whether the guard should know about the term at all rather than a caller having to. exoplasim/notes/convdecomp-reproducibility.md carries the measurement.

title: Nothing reads pedogenesis.yaml's brackets, so a value outside its own bracket is invisible
description:
world-9ctm gave the regolith, texture and ph blocks of pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml the brackets they lacked, so the file now declares a bracket for nearly every value it carries. NOTHING CHECKS THEM.

There is already a working model of what this should look like: biosphere/scripts/outgassing_gate.py does exactly this job for its own declaration -- it asserts the bracket is well formed, that its ends are ordered, and that the declared value lies inside it. pedology has no equivalent, so a value edited outside its own bracket, or a bracket whose ends are swapped, reaches a soil build with nothing objecting.

A SECOND CONSTRAINT NEEDS THE SAME GATE AND HAS NO HOME AT ALL. world-34n2 found that maximum_depth_m and erosion_coefficient_per_relief_m are JOINTLY constrained: the land-mean regolith depth the pair produces has to land inside regolith_depth_bracket_m, which brackets the LEVEL and not either key. Neither key's own bracket expresses it, so a sweep that moves them independently can satisfy both and violate the level. That is the constraint most likely to be broken by someone doing the obvious thing.

The check is static and cheap, so it belongs in the per-commit tier rather than the artifact tier. It was run by hand at 12 of 12 passing when the brackets landed; the point of this row is that it runs without being remembered.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-m61p (842af7575): three of the row's claims were wrong and five bands violated the sign test, not four; the test was neither necessary nor sufficient for the warm>=cold identity it stood in for, and a second defect had the projection missing its own anchors by 22.1 per cent. band_amplification_sign deleted; the instrument now refuses on cold_extreme_cap, which world-dnrr carries. world-mro1 (e6e635233, later widened tree-wide in 829619208): the bracket check has four dispositions and a discovery pass, and the row's premise needed correcting -- regolith_depth_bracket_m was already read. world-l442 (fcd495b91): the acid end relaxes onto a gibbsite buffer; the pre-registered bracket derivation FALSIFIED and the reason was the parent spacing, not the slope. world-ysd1 (f7a3e96d9): --purge reaches the seed's own writes, with orgen the single by-name exemption because source/ is read-only under rule 7.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
DONE, in scripts/smoke_test.py: check 15, "every pedology bracket contains the value it brackets". Left unstaged in the working tree.

WHAT IT CHECKS. A table, PEDOLOGY_BRACKETS, names every bracket pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml and pedology/config/surface_classes.yaml declare -- 20 rows -- with the value each one is a bracket ON. Four dispositions, because they are not enforceable the same way:

  value    the file states both. The number has to be inside the bracket. 15 rows.
  pair     the same, with the ends carried as <key>_minimum and <key>_maximum
           beside the value rather than as a list. andisol.volumetric_capacity_allophane
           is the one instance and had no `bracket` in any key name, so a check
           that grepped for the word would have missed it.
  level    the bracket is on a quantity no key states. regolith_depth_bracket_m
           is the row world-34n2 found: maximum_depth_m and
           erosion_coefficient_per_relief_m produce a land mean jointly and
           neither key's own bracket expresses it. Nothing static can evaluate a
           land mean, so what is asserted is that build_soil.py still READS the
           key -- the run-time refusal is the enforcement, and a deleted refusal
           is what this catches.
  derived  the bracket is the sentinel `derived` and carbonate_ph.py fills it
           from config/planet.yaml's pCO2_bar. The sentinel has to be intact,
           the filler has to still name the key, and the value is checked
           against the bracket that module computes at this world's pCO2.

Half of the pairing is a discovery pass, _unregistered_pedology_brackets, which walks both files and reports any bracket the table does not name -- both shapes, the `bracket`-named leaf and the min/max pair sitting beside the value it bounds. A clip is neither, and the sibling requirement is what tells `ph.minimum` apart from a bracket rather than a list of exceptions. So a bracket added later cannot go unchecked silently, which is the failure mode outgassing_gate.py's comment warns about in its own table.

CORRECTION TO THE ROW: the joint constraint is NOT homeless. build_soil.py:1041 reads regolith_depth_bracket_m and refuses a run whose land-mean regolith depth falls outside it. What had no home is the well-formedness of every bracket in the file, and the static half of the joint one, which is that the refusal still exists.

TWO HOLES IT CLOSES that were not in the row. ph.endorheic_alkalinity_bonus (0.8) was checked against nothing: carbonate_ph.resolve derives endorheic_alkalinity_bonus_bracket and never compares the value to it. ph.parent_by_category.evaporite (8.8) against parent_bracket_evaporite was the same -- resolve explicitly excludes evaporite from the silicate check. Both are inside their brackets today, and both are now checked on every commit.

DEMONSTRATED FAILING. Nine fixtures run inside the check itself, each one declaration broken in one way, each asserting the sentence it has to produce: a value outside its bracket, ends the wrong way round, a bracket that is not two numbers, a min/max pair its value sits outside, a derived bracket restated as a number, a value outside the DERIVED bracket, a bracket in the second file, and the two enforcer rows pointed at a file that names no bracket. Live, on the real declaration: ph.leaching_slope forced to 3.00 and catena.slope_transport_bracket reversed to [8.0, 2.0] gave

  FAIL: ph.leaching_slope in pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml is 3.0 and its own bracket is [0.95, 2.45]. A value its bracket does not contain is one of the two, not both
  FAIL: catena.slope_transport in pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml is bracketed [8.0, 2.0], whose low end is above its high end

and both were restored. The declaration passes at 20 of 20.

SWEPT UP. pedology/config/surface_classes.yaml's surface_cover.loess.deposition_g_m2_yr against deposition_bracket, which is the same defect in the same directory and was in no row. land_column_properties.yaml and weathering_schemes.yaml declare no brackets of their own -- the `brackets:` keys in the first are prose provenance pointing back at pedogenesis.yaml. outgassing.yaml is already gated by outgassing_gate.py and is left to it.

STILL UNREAD, outside pedology and reported rather than fixed: aeolian/config/dust.yaml emission.cd0_bracket, emission.c_alpha_bracket, emission.u_star_st_typical_bracket, drag_partition.z0s_bracket_cm, source.pavement_residual_erodibility_bracket, source.arid_bare_ground.enabled_as_bracket, transport.dust_scale_height_bracket_m, removal.scavenging_a_bracket; hydrography/config/groundwater.yaml evapotranspiration.lambda_bracket_m; minerals/config/downstream_prospectivity.yaml deposits.bauxite.precipitation_bracket_mm_yr; ocean/config/carbon_feedback.yaml reopening_contract.owners.weathering_and_outgassing_bracket. Eleven brackets in four components with the same defect this row names.

title: The pedogenesis pH block's FORM is wrong: Slessarev's acid end is parent-independent
description:
Slessarev et al. (2016), read 2026-08-26 for world-9ctm, sources the pH block's alkaline end and refutes its FORM in the same paper.

WHAT IT SHOWS. The global soil pH distribution is BIMODAL on two mineral buffers, calcite near 8.2 and gibbsite near 5.1, with an abrupt step where MAP begins to exceed PET. Predicting only those two values from the SIGN of the water balance explains 42 per cent of the observed variation. Soils in the neutral range are uncommon because that range is held only by slow primary mineral dissolution. The acid end is set by gibbsite WHATEVER THE PARENT ROCK WAS.

WHAT THIS PROJECT DOES INSTEAD. build_soil.py:soil_ph takes every parent material down a line of its own from its own starting value, so the modelled wet cells land wherever each parent's line puts them. No single leaching_slope can put them all on one buffer, because the form has no buffer in it. The values are now individually sourced or bracketed by world-9ctm; the SHAPE they are used in is the defect this row is about.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED WITH THE VALUES. Replacing a parameterisation is a different change from sourcing its constants, and the sourcing was what unblocked the soil step. Doing both at once would have made neither reviewable.

WHAT THE PAPER ALSO SUPPLIES for whoever takes this: the deviations a lithology-aware model should reproduce. Profiles in the wettest quartile are 2.6 times more likely to exceed pH 6.5 where carbonate bedrock is present, and humid-climate soils are less acidic in high-relief landscapes. Those are the two places lithology survives the buffer, so they are the test a replacement has to pass rather than a decoration on it.

references/slessarev2016-water-balance-threshold-in-soil-ph.pdf is held and read.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-m61p (842af7575): three of the row's claims were wrong and five bands violated the sign test, not four; the test was neither necessary nor sufficient for the warm>=cold identity it stood in for, and a second defect had the projection missing its own anchors by 22.1 per cent. band_amplification_sign deleted; the instrument now refuses on cold_extreme_cap, which world-dnrr carries. world-mro1 (e6e635233, later widened tree-wide in 829619208): the bracket check has four dispositions and a discovery pass, and the row's premise needed correcting -- regolith_depth_bracket_m was already read. world-l442 (fcd495b91): the acid end relaxes onto a gibbsite buffer; the pre-registered bracket derivation FALSIFIED and the reason was the parent spacing, not the slope. world-ysd1 (f7a3e96d9): --purge reaches the seed's own writes, with orgen the single by-name exemption because source/ is read-only under rule 7.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
VERIFIED against the paper, and MEASURED on the live land population. Not fixed: the form lives in build_soil.py:soil_ph, which another session holds.

THE SOURCE SAYS WHAT THE ROW SAYS. Slessarev's Methods, "Water-balance model evaluation": "For all soils in grid cells where MAP minus PET < 0, the predicted pH was 8.2, and for all remaining profiles, the predicted pH was 5.1." The acid end is a mineral buffer with no parent term in it at all, and the Methods' "Gibbsite buffer" paragraph derives 5.1 as the mean of the NCSS spatial-sample profiles with non-zero exchangeable Al, from a Gapon exchange relation in CaX/AlX (eq. 7, b0 = 4.96, b1 = 0.32) rather than from lithology.

CURRENT FORM, build_soil.py:434-436, with parent the area-weighted mixture of parent_by_category over the cell's rock classes and L = ln(1 + q/q_ref):

    ph = parent - leaching_slope * L + endorheic * bonus

A line per parent. It has no asymptote, so the parents never converge: they stay leaching_slope-independently spread by exactly their initial spacing, and the wet cells fan out where the measurement clusters.

CORRECT FORM. The acid end must be a parent-independent asymptote the parents relax onto, which is one term:

    ph = gibbsite + (parent - gibbsite) * exp(-leaching_slope * L) + endorheic * bonus

At L = 0 it is the fresh parent, which is what an unleached soil is; as L grows every parent goes to the gibbsite buffer whatever the rock was, which is the observation. It also preserves the paper's own deviation test rather than deleting the lithology term: at finite L a carbonate parent still sits above a felsic one, which is what "profiles in the wettest quartile are 2.6 times more likely to exceed pH 6.5 where carbonate bedrock is present" is a statement about.

MEASURED, on canonical-10m-carve2 against the baseline climatology, 1,639 land cells, in the pH the soilmap column a consumer reads carries. The current form is reproduced to 5e-4 from the mesh and the climatology, which is the artifact's own print precision, so the comparison is exact.

  form                          landmean  wetmean  f(6-7)  f(<5.5)  wet p95-p05
  current  P - 0.95 L              6.801    6.085   0.462    0.038         1.70
  proposed G+(P-G)exp(-0.95 L)     6.706    5.938   0.464    0.024         0.99
  proposed G+(P-G)exp(-1.70 L)     6.515    5.583   0.333    0.119         0.77
  proposed G+(P-G)exp(-2.45 L)     6.389    5.391   0.284    0.231         0.56
  Slessarev's own step model       5.739    5.100   0.000    0.794         0.00

Land-mean pH falls by 0.096 at the declared slope and by 0.412 at the bracket's high end; 48 cells move by more than 0.5 pH at the low end, 645 at the high end. The parameter-free bound is the last row: the paper's own two-value model is 1.06 pH below the current land mean, so the form is worth about a pH unit and the slope is worth up to half of one inside it.

THE DIRECTION IS TOWARD THE OBSERVATION, and the sharpest number is the paper's own carbonate test. Share of the wettest quartile above pH 6.5, carbonate-bearing cells against the rest: the current form gives 1.03x, which is no lithology signal at all; the proposed form at the declared slope gives 1.73x against the paper's 2.6x. At slopes of 1.7 and above nothing in the wet quartile clears 6.5 and the test cannot be evaluated, so the paper's deviation is itself evidence about where in the bracket the slope sits.

WHAT THE REPAIR NEEDS, exactly.

1. build_soil.py:435 becomes the exponential above. One line; nothing else in soil_ph changes.
2. pedogenesis.yaml ph gains `gibbsite_buffer_ph`. 5.1 is Slessarev's, and it is IMPLICIT-EARTH by this project's vocabulary rather than derivable the way the calcite end is: gibbsite solubility carries no CO2 term, so carbonate_ph.py cannot reach it, and the buffer pH is set by the CaX/AlX exchange ratio. A bracket is available from the paper's own eq. (7): CaX/AlX from 0.1 to 10 gives 4.64 to 5.28.
3. `leaching_slope_bracket` MUST be re-derived. Its present ends are one requirement evaluated at two runoffs -- "that the term can carry the modal clastic parent down to 5.1, a drop of 1.7" -- and under the new form that requirement is satisfied by construction at every slope, because 5.1 is the asymptote. The numbers 0.95 and 2.45 are properties of the line and do not transfer; the quantity to bracket is how much leaching it takes to reach the buffer.
4. soil_report.json and pedology/data/<build>/soilmap_T21.txt go stale on the change and need a build_soil run.

The alkaline end is a separate deviation and is NOT covered by this: the paper's dry mode is 8.2 whatever the rock, because arid soils accumulate pedogenic calcite, while this block keeps the parent contrast there (6.4 to 7.6 on silicates) and reaches 8.2 only on carbonate parent or through the endorheic bonus. That is a second, unfixed departure from the same figure and wants its own row.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 VERIFIED AND QUANTIFIED; THE CHANGE ITSELF IS NOT MADE.

The paper, read rather than cited: Slessarev et al. (2016) Methods, "Water-
balance model evaluation" gives 5.1 for every profile where MAP - PET >= 0, and
the "Gibbsite buffer" paragraph derives it as the mean of NCSS spatial-sample
profiles with non-zero exchangeable Al, from a Gapon exchange relation in
CaX/AlX (eq. 7, b0 = 4.96, b1 = 0.32). No lithology term in the acid end.

Current form, build_soil.py:434-436, with parent the area-weighted mixture over
the cell's rock classes and L = ln(1 + q/q_ref):

    ph = parent - leaching_slope * L + endorheic * bonus

A line per parent, no asymptote, so the parents stay spread by their initial
spacing however steep the slope. Correct form is a parent-independent asymptote
the parents relax onto:

    ph = gibbsite + (parent - gibbsite) * exp(-leaching_slope * L)
         + endorheic * bonus

Measured on canonical-10m-carve2 over 1639 land cells, in the pH the soilmap
column carries. The reconstruction reproduces soilmap_T21.txt to 5e-4, that
file's print precision, so the comparison is exact rather than indicative:

  form                      land mean   wet mean   f(6-7)   f(<5.5)   wet p95-p05
  current  P - 0.95 L         6.801      6.085     0.462    0.038      1.70
  proposed s=0.95            6.706      5.938     0.464    0.024      0.99
  proposed s=1.70            6.515      5.583     0.333    0.119      0.77
  proposed s=2.45            6.389      5.391     0.284    0.231      0.56
  Slessarev's own step model 5.739      5.100     0.000    0.794      0.00

Land-mean pH falls 0.096 at the declared slope and 0.412 at the bracket's high
end; 48 cells move more than 0.5 pH at the low end, 645 at the high end. The
parameter-free bound is the last row: the paper's two-value model sits 1.06 pH
below the current land mean.

THE PAPER'S OWN DEVIATION TEST IS THE SHARP ONE. Share of the wettest quartile
above pH 6.5, carbonate-bearing cells against the rest, which the paper puts at
2.6x. Current form returns 1.03x -- no lithology signal at all. The proposed
form at the declared slope returns 1.73x. At s >= 1.7 nothing in the wet
quartile clears 6.5, so the paper's deviation is itself evidence about where in
the bracket the slope sits, which is a derivation route the row did not have.

WHAT THE FIX NEEDS, and why it is not a one-line edit:
  1. build_soil.py:435 becomes the exponential.
  2. pedogenesis.yaml gains gibbsite_buffer_ph, 5.1, implicit-Earth: gibbsite
     carries no CO2 term so carbonate_ph.py cannot reach it. A bracket of 4.64
     to 5.28 follows from the paper's eq. 7 at CaX/AlX of 0.1 to 10.
  3. leaching_slope_bracket MUST BE RE-DERIVED. Its ends are "carry the modal
     clastic parent down 1.7 to reach 5.1", which the new form satisfies by
     construction at every slope, so 0.95 and 2.45 are properties of the LINE
     and do not transfer. Carrying them across would be a tuned pair wearing a
     derivation that no longer applies.
  4. soil_report.json and the soilmap go stale.

The alkaline end is a separate defect and is now world-i70y: the paper's dry
mode is 8.2 whatever the rock, while this block keeps a 6.4 to 7.6 parent
contrast. Fixing the acid form says nothing about it.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 FORM CHANGED, VALUE ADDED, BRACKET RE-DERIVED. Unstaged in the tree.

build_soil.py:soil_ph now reads

  ph = G + (parent - G) * exp(-leaching_slope * L) + endorheic * bonus

with G = ph.gibbsite_buffer_ph. Verified against the offline reconstruction to
0.0 at the declared slope, so the numbers below are the shipped code's.

GIBBSITE_BUFFER_PH: 5.1, bracket [4.64, 5.28], IMPLICIT-EARTH. The prior
judgement holds but its reason was one step short. Not tuned: 5.1 is a measured
population mean, the NCSS spatial sample with non-zero AlX, not the residual of
a fit. Not opaque: the derivation is in the Methods and the paper is held. What
makes it Earth's is the INPUT to that derivation, not the derivation. Eq. (7),
pH = 4.96 + 0.32 log10(CaX/AlX), puts 5.1 at an exchange ratio of 2.7, and that
ratio is a property of Earth's lithology, weathering and biological cycling. The
Gapon exchange chemistry travels to another planet; the population it was
averaged over does not. "carbonate_ph.py cannot reach it" is true and is why
there is no sentinel, but it is a statement about this project's tooling rather
than about the number's planet. The repair is a cation-exchange model that does
not exist here, so the bracket stands in: CaX/AlX over 0.1 to 10, two decades
DECLARED because the paper publishes the fit and not the ratio's field range.

LEACHING_SLOPE_BRACKET: [0.35, 1.33], declared value 0.90. Was [0.95, 2.45] at
0.95.

  Criteria were written to scratchpad BEFORE any sweep. Upper end: the paper's
  wettest-quartile carbonate deviation must still exist in the model, closed
  form s = ln((carbonate - G)/(6.5 - G))/L, at L = the quartile median. Lower
  end: the paper's bimodality, gibbsite window [G-0.5, G+0.5] holding at least
  as much land area as the paper's own neutral window [6, 7], equal widths so
  the shares compare as densities. Declared value 1/ln 2 = 1.443, one e-folding
  of the parent-to-buffer offset at the reference runoff, with the pre-declared
  rule that a value outside the bracket is replaced by the end it exceeds.
  Falsification condition declared in advance: s_lo > s_hi.

  THE FALSIFICATION FIRED. s_hi = 0.90, s_lo = 2.50. Restricting the bimodality
  test to the paper's own positive-water-balance class, which is more faithful
  to the source and is stated here as POST HOC, gives 2.12, still above. The
  bracket is empty under either reading.

  WHY, and it is not the slope. The two paper findings are a constraint on the
  parent SPACING that the slope cancels out of. Carbonate stays above 6.5 while
  the retained offset fraction f = exp(-sL) >= (6.5 - G)/(carbonate - G) =
  0.457; modal clastic reaches a one-pH-wide gibbsite mode while f <=
  0.5/(clastic - G) = 0.294. Both hold only if (carbonate - G)/(clastic - G) >=
  2.80. Declared parent values give 8.163 and 6.8 over G = 5.1, ratio 1.80. f,
  s and L all cancel: NO slope and no leaching index satisfies both. Second
  reason: 254 cells, 20.6 per cent of land area, have zero runoff, so L = 0 and
  no slope moves them at all; they carry 13.3 per cent of the neutral share and

  WHAT THE BRACKET IS NOW. One requirement, the deviation test, evaluated at

  OF AN UPPER BOUND AND THERE IS NO SOURCED LOWER ONE; the config says so.

MEASURED, canonical-10m-carve2 against the baseline climatology, 1639 land
cells, area-weighted, in the pH the soilmap column carries. The reconstruction
reproduces soilmap_T21.txt to 5.0e-4, that file's print precision.

  form                          landmean  wetmean  drymean  f(6-7)  f(<5.5)  wet p95-p05
  current  P - 0.95 L             6.801    6.015    7.303   0.462    0.038      1.85
  proposed G+(P-G)exp(-0.35 L)    6.944    6.425    7.303   0.550    0.000      1.13
  SHIPPED  G+(P-G)exp(-0.90 L)    6.722    5.913    7.303   0.476    0.017      1.01
  proposed G+(P-G)exp(-1.33 L)    6.598    5.666    7.303   0.385    0.072      0.85
  Slessarev's own step model      5.739    5.100    8.200   0.000    0.794      0.00

  Land mean 6.801 -> 6.722, net -0.079: the form alone is -0.096 at fixed slope
  and the slope move 0.95 -> 0.90 gives back +0.016. 849 cells move by more

  Cells railed on ph.maximum fall 15 -> 5; none rails on ph.minimum either way.

  DIRECTION, both ways, honestly. Against the paper's deviation the change is

  the rest, goes from 0.75x area-weighted (1.03x per cell) to 1.32x (1.31x per

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 THE BRACKET RE-DERIVED AGAINST A SOURCED PARENT SET. It does not move,
and its falsification does not fire. Detail and the derivation are on world-jixy.

world-jixy replaced the four declared silicate parent pH values with a sourced
base-cation supply per lithology, from Meybeck (1987) Table 2C and from GEM-CO2.
Re-running this row's derivation against that set:

s_hi is 0.3503 / 0.9041 / 1.3296 at the area-weighted wettest quartile's wettest
cell, its median and its dry edge. UNCHANGED to four decimals, and structurally
so: a carbonate parent's supply is 1 by construction and the closed form
s = ln((C - G)/(6.5 - G))/L carries no other lithology.

s_lo still does not exist. The bimodality density test now passes at EVERY slope
tried from 0.01 to 4.00 with no gap, where on the declared set it failed in a
narrow band around 0.66 to 0.85. The reason is the sourced set itself: silicates
supplying four to fourteen per cent of a calcite-saturated soil's base cations
are on one buffer or the other at any slope, so there is never enough land in
transit to fail a density test. A quantity satisfied over the whole range tried
is not a bound, so the falsification condition s_lo > s_hi cannot fire, and the
bracket stays [0.35, 1.33] at 0.90, three readings of one upper bound.

WHAT DID CHANGE IS THE DEVIATION THE UPPER BOUND PROTECTS. This row measured the
proposed form at the declared slope returning 1.73x against the paper's 2.6x, and
the shipped two-buffer form on the declared parents returns 0.90x on the
area-weighted quartile, which is no lithology signal at all. On the sourced set
the ratio is 12 to 18 in the middle of the slope bracket and undefined at 0.90
because no non-carbonate cell of the wettest quartile clears 6.5. The deviation
is now generated rather than absent, and it is not resolvable at the declared
slope on either set. Reported; it is not taken as a bound, because that
requirement was not fixed in advance.

title: Three derived model constants default from a compiled sentinel instead of being declared in config
description:
vdiff_lamm, gamma and rcritwidth are all derived at model start from a compiled sentinel rather than read from config/planet.yaml. The consequence is recorded by scripts/check_consistency.py, which warns 'namelist keys the runs never recorded: CLOUDABS, GAMMA, RCRITWIDTH -- absent from the namelist and never claimed on the manifest, so the model used its compiled value and no artifact says which'.

WHY THAT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. A run's manifest is what a later reader reconstructs the run from. A value that reaches the model only through a compiled default is invisible to it, so two runs that integrated different constants are indistinguishable in the record, and an A3 arm on that constant cannot be built as one binary differing by one namelist key -- it has to be a code fork, which the protocol does not accept.

The same argument settled vdiff_lamm's route in world-sjja: run_exoplasim.py now writes model.asymptotic_mixing_length_m unconditionally and expected_namelist_keys checks it, and the model prints which branch it took. What is open is whether the DERIVED VALUE should also be declared in config/planet.yaml rather than left to the sentinel.

THE THREE ARE ONE DECISION AND ARE FILED AS ONE ROW ON PURPOSE. Settling them apart is how they came to differ. Each is a constant with a derivation that exists; the question is only where the derived number is stated and what refuses a run that did not state it.
close_reason: Closed

title: run_exoplasim.py has no --purpose, so A3's diagnostic labelling has no guard
description:
sequencing.md A3 requires that the segments of a short A/B be labelled DIAGNOSTICS, so a tail never enters a convergence window or a climatology. Nothing enforces it at prepare time: run_exoplasim.py takes no --purpose, so every arm's first segment is written as `spinup` with `canonical_lineage_eligible: true`.

So the labelling that A3 depends on is applied after the fact if at all, and the failure is silent in the direction that matters -- a diagnostic tail that keeps the default label is indistinguishable later from production orbits, and the canonical lineage is exactly the thing that must not absorb one.

THERE IS A SECOND, STRUCTURAL HALF and it is worth solving together, because fixing one alone makes the other worse. WORLD-U9HQ found that A3's fourth condition is currently UNTESTABLE: assess_convergence reads only PRODUCTION orbits, so labelling a segment a diagnostic is precisely what hides it from the convergence test that would judge it. A guard that enforces the label without addressing that leaves every A/B arm unable to demonstrate its own settling.

DO: give run_exoplasim.py a --purpose that reaches the segment record and the manifest, default it to nothing rather than to spinup so an unlabelled arm is a refusal rather than a silent production segment, and decide how a diagnostic segment demonstrates settling -- either assess_convergence gains a mode that reads them, or the arms declare their window some other way and that is written down.

Found by the A3 bundle arms. Source: sequencing.md A3, world-u9hq.
close_reason: Closed

title: --purge cannot reach a leaf step's own output
description:
scripts/pipeline.py --purge walks DOWNSTREAM from its seed, so a step that nothing else 'needs' can never purge its own bulk. Measured on the tree at b36fc957:

  --purge spatial_support     0 files
  --purge wetness             0 files
  --purge topographic_index   0 files
  --purge hydrography         5 files

The three leaves each declare a complete 'writes' set and each has real output on disk -- spatial_support alone is 49.6 MB across five rungs -- and --purge reports success having deleted none of it. hydrography, which those three depend on, purges normally, so this is the walk's shape and not a defect in any one row.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSING CONVENIENCE. CLAUDE.md rule 7 makes 'what is now worthless' the question after every change, and --purge is the tool that answers it. For a leaf the answer is currently 'nothing', silently and with a success exit. A step's own output is the first thing a change to that step invalidates, so the one case the tool must always get right is the one it always gets wrong.

It also defeats the completeness rule the graph is maintained under. config/pipeline.yaml requires 'writes' to name the COMPLETE set of a step's outputs precisely so --purge deletes exactly that, and the file's own comment records what a row naming only its report costs. A leaf can satisfy that rule perfectly and still purge nothing, so the rule is untestable at every leaf.

DO: make the seed's own writes part of what --purge deletes, rather than only the writes of steps reachable from it. Check the fix against the property the walk already has and must keep -- CLAUDE.md's smoke_test 'purge never reaches the terrain, from any seed' asserts that no seed reaches orogen, and adding the seed's own outputs must not open a path to source/{build}/ from the orogen seed itself.

A check with a right answer is available and should land with it: for every step in the graph, --purge <step> must include every path that step's own 'writes' names. That is an identity over the graph rather than a spot case, and it fails today at every leaf.

Found by the SPAT-3 agent while registering spatial_support, and confirmed independently across all three leaves and one non-leaf.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-m61p (842af7575): three of the row's claims were wrong and five bands violated the sign test, not four; the test was neither necessary nor sufficient for the warm>=cold identity it stood in for, and a second defect had the projection missing its own anchors by 22.1 per cent. band_amplification_sign deleted; the instrument now refuses on cold_extreme_cap, which world-dnrr carries. world-mro1 (e6e635233, later widened tree-wide in 829619208): the bracket check has four dispositions and a discovery pass, and the row's premise needed correcting -- regolith_depth_bracket_m was already read. world-l442 (fcd495b91): the acid end relaxes onto a gibbsite buffer; the pre-registered bracket derivation FALSIFIED and the reason was the parent spacing, not the slope. world-ysd1 (f7a3e96d9): --purge reaches the seed's own writes, with orgen the single by-name exemption because source/ is read-only under rule 7.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Fixed in the working tree (scripts/pipeline.py, scripts/smoke_test.py; unstaged).

Reproduced on canonical-10m-carve2: --purge wetness and --purge topographic_index each reported 0 of 114 steps and 0 files while their reports sat on disk; --purge spatial_support reported 60 steps and 8.14 GB and omitted its own 4 files / 1.7 MB, which --purge hydrography lists.

downstream() keeps its meaning (strictly downstream, so the orogen cut is stated once against reachability). New purge_set() = downstream | {seed}, with orogen the single by-name exemption because its writes is source/{build}/ and rule 7 makes that read-only. New purge_writes() returns the per-step writes entries a purge would expand, in graph order; cmd_purge walks it and smoke_test asserts over it, so the plan a check reads is the plan the delete walks.

After: --purge wetness 1 of 114, 1 file; --purge topographic_index 1 of 114, 1 file; --purge spatial_support 61 of 114 with its own 4 files; --purge orogen unchanged at 71 of 114 and still does not name source/.

Check added: 'purge deletes every path the seed's own writes names' -- for every step but orogen, every entry in that step's writes appears in the plan --purge <step> builds. Run against the old walk it returns 184 failures across the graph. The terrain check's old 'seed not in doomed' assertion is replaced by one over the delete set: no purge plan, from any seed, may name a path under source/. Putting orogen back into purge_set makes that one fire.

scripts/smoke_test.py: 57 checks, 0 failed. --status, --plan and --register unchanged.

title: dsoilwf is one shape for the planet and the capacity split is not
description:
LSHY-3 chose the layered land water column, and the layer shape that makes LSHY-5 possible is the one LPJ-GUESS already groups at: nlsoilw 2, dsoilwz [0.5, 1.0], which is the 500 mm upper and 1000 mm lower of pedology's fifteen 100 mm physical layers.

dsoilwf, the capacity of each layer as a fraction of dwmax, is declared at landmod.f90:178 as real :: dsoilwf(NLSOILWX) in landmod_nl -- ONE shape for the whole simulated planet. The split it stands for is not one shape. Measured on pedology/data/precarve-craton-10m/soilmap_T21.txt over its 1,019 land cells, using land_column_properties.py's own per-layer usable-share loop:

  upper-layer capacity share   p0 0.3333  p25 0.3333  p50 0.4699  p75 0.7132  p95 0.8540  p100 0.8882, mean 0.5302

The geometric value is 500/1500 = 0.3333 and it holds EXACTLY where the regolith fills the column, which is 26.5 per cent of land. Everywhere else the regolith contact and the bedrock fraction reweight the column toward the top, and the median cell sits 41 per cent above the geometric split while the p95 sits at 2.6 times it.

So a single namelist dsoilwf is a model-form approximation with a measurable cost, and any single value picked for it is wrong for most of the map. Picking the one that makes a comparison come out is the tuned value this project forbids.

TWO DISPOSITIONS AND THEY ARE NOT EQUIVALENT.
  1. Promote dsoilwf to a per-cell FIELD, which is what every other surface property of this kind already is -- dwmax itself arrives as surface code 229, and albedo and roughness are fields. The split is a pure function of texture and regolith depth, both of which pedology already emits, so the producer exists and what is missing is the surface code, the writer and the read in landmod.
  2. Keep it a namelist array and DECLARE which statistic of the per-cell distribution it is, reporting the spread beside it so a reader can see what one shape costs.

Route 1 is the one that matches the rest of the surface. Route 2 is defensible only as a stated reduction, never as a default.

NOT A DEFECT TODAY: dsoilwf is inert while nlandwcol = 0, and the default (/1.0, 0.0, .../) puts everything in one layer, which is the exact bucket reduction. This binds the moment nlsoilw goes above 1.

Source: LSHY-3, landmod.f90:174-179, pedology/scripts/land_column_properties.py's per-layer loop, pedology/config/land_column_properties.yaml geometry block.
close_reason:
ROUTE 1, the per-cell FIELD, which is what every comparable surface property already is.

The split crosses as surface code 2290, one record per water layer, written by build_surface_soil_water.py from the same per-layer usable shares awc_mm is the integral of -- so the split and dwmax are ONE arithmetic rather than two that can drift. dsoilwf becomes the fallback shape; landwfrac renormalises per cell and REFUSES above one layer wherever a land cell's dwmax came from a soil, so the fallback cannot quietly stand in for a field it is not equal to. write_sra now takes (nlev,nlat,nlon).

MEASURED over this build's 1,019 land cells at the declared 0.5/1.0 m cut: upper share p50 0.4699, p95 0.8540, max 0.8882, mean 0.5302, against the geometric 0.3333 which holds exactly on 28.85 per cent of land -- the 26.50 per cent where regolith fills the column plus the cells sitting at the bedrock capacity ceiling.

Bitwise unchanged at layers: 1, and verify_land_column_reduction.sh still PASSes with all four negative controls breaking as required.

The restart record dsoilwfc is recorded as optional on resume with its cold value, which WORLD-T16E's new check_resume_policy gate caught at merge rather than at the first resume of a pre-2290 restart.

title: Fetch Blackadar (1962) and Shah and Coulman (1978): the two primaries the four just-read papers name
description:
Reading Louis (1979) and Li et al. (1992) each pushed the chain one paper further, and both endpoints are the thing that actually settles a tuned value.

BLACKADAR (1962). Louis eq. 22 is Blackadar's mixing length l = kz/(1 + kz/lambda), and Louis calls lambda 'an adjustable parameter', taking it as 100 m. fluxmod.f90:47 runs ECHAM's 160 m. Neither is derived. Blackadar sets lambda from the geostrophic wind and the Coriolis parameter, which is a rule that carries to another rotation rate and is therefore the only route that transfers to a 30-hour rotator. Blackadar, The vertical distribution of wind and turbulent exchange in a neutral atmosphere, J. Geophys. Res. 67(8), 3095-3102, 10.1029/JZ067i008p03095. NOT held. This is the whole of what world-x6q8's mixing-length half waits on.

SHAH AND COULMAN (1978). Li et al. (1992) table 7 gives Kc = 0.017 kg C/m3 and Kn = 0.083 kg N/m3 and attributes both to Shah and Coulman rather than measuring them, stating the units per cubic metre of an unnamed volume exactly as Xu-Ri does. So the michaelis_menten_divisor question (world-nga5) is not closed by Li and never was going to be: whether the divisor is available water or layer depth, a factor of 6.7 to 30 on denitrification, is decided in Shah and Coulman. Shah and Coulman (1978), Kinetics of nitrification and denitrification reactions, Biotechnology and Bioengineering 20(1), 43-72, 10.1002/bit.260200105. CONFIRM THE DOI before fetching -- INDEX.md's own rule, and this citation reaches us third-hand.

Do: fetch both, file them, add INDEX rows, then reopen world-x6q8's mixing length and world-nga5.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md, the four-papers section.
notes:
2026-08-26. HALF DELIVERED, HALF BLOCKED ON ACCESS. Blocked rather than open,
because what remains is not work this project can do.

BLACKADAR (1962) IS HELD, FILED AND READ. paperfetch failed on every automated
route (doi.org 403, Scholar captcha, sci-hub 403) and it was recovered from a
Wayback snapshot of a university copy: 8 pages matching 3095-3102, filed as
references/blackadar1962-the-vertical-distribution-of-wind-and-turbulent-exchange.pdf
with an INDEX row. It settled world-awm5's mixing-length half, and the answer is
a SCALING and not a value -- his eq. 25 makes the asymptotic length proportional
to the geostrophic wind over the Coriolis parameter, but the coefficient is
matched to one observed wind deflection at one site, he names u*/f as equally
acceptable a priori, and his lambda is the boundary layer's asymptote where
ECHAM's 160 m is whole-column. What transfers to a 30-hour rotator is the 1/Omega.

SHAH AND COULMAN (1978) CANNOT BE OBTAINED, and the DOI was confirmed against
Crossref BEFORE fetching as this row required, since the citation reaches us
third-hand: exact match on title, authors, journal, 20(1), 43-72, 1978. Closed
on every route checked -- Unpaywall is_oa false with no OA locations, OpenAlex
closed with any_repository_has_fulltext false, Semantic Scholar CLOSED with an
empty PDF URL, Wiley paywall, sci-hub 403, no Wayback snapshot.

  Shah, D. B. and Coulman, G. A. (1978), Kinetics of nitrification and
  denitrification reactions, Biotechnology and Bioengineering 20(1), 43-72,
  10.1002/bit.260200105

It needs institutional access or an author copy. NO SECONDARY SOURCE WAS
SUBSTITUTED, which is the whole point of this row: Li et al. (1992) table 7
attributes Kc and Kn to Shah and Coulman rather than measuring them, so a
restatement of a restatement settles nothing. WORLD-NGA5's michaelis_menten
divisor -- whether Kc and Kn are per cubic metre of soil solution or of soil, a
factor of 6.7 to 30 on denitrification -- stays unsourced on it.
close_reason:
Both primaries held, filed and read; the chain ends here.

BLACKADAR (1962) recovered from a Wayback snapshot of a university copy after every automated route failed (doi.org 403, Scholar captcha, sci-hub 403). 8 pages matching 3095-3102. It settled world-awm5's mixing-length half, and the answer is a SCALING rather than a value: his eq. 25 makes the asymptotic length proportional to the geostrophic wind over the Coriolis parameter, but the coefficient is matched to one observed wind deflection at one site, he names u*/f as equally acceptable a priori, and his lambda is the boundary layer's asymptote where ECHAM's 160 m is whole-column. What transfers to a 30-hour rotator is the 1/Omega, and vdiff_lamm now derives from the rotation rate with the geostrophic wind carried as a declared bracket.

SHAH AND COULMAN (1978) SUPPLIED BY THE AUTHOR after this row reported it closed on every route checked -- Unpaywall is_oa false, OpenAlex closed, Semantic Scholar CLOSED, Wiley paywall, no Wayback snapshot. Verified before reading, per the Li precedent where a paper arrived under another paper's slug: the PDF's own title page and embedded metadata are Shah and Coulman, 30 pages. Filed under its own name.

IT SETTLES WORLD-NGA5, which is what it was fetched for. Its chosen constants are Ks = 83 mg/liter for nitrate nitrogen and Ks = 17.4 mg/liter for organic carbon -- 0.083 and 0.0174 kg m-3, which are Xu-Ri's table 11 and Li's table 7 EXACTLY, so both secondaries transcribed the numbers faithfully and only the volume was lost in the chain. That volume is the SOLUTION'S, and not by inference from the units: the values were measured in a CONTINUOUS STIRRED TANK REACTOR on dissolved substrates, with no soil in the experiment at all, and the paper draws the contrast itself -- soil scientists work in soil columns, sanitary engineers in CSTRs, and this is the second kind.

So ntransform.cpp's divisor, the depth of available water in the upper layer, is CORRECT, and the factor of 6.7 to 30 on denitrification closes in favour of the branch already running. Li's magnitude argument for the per-cubic-metre-of-SOIL reading is withdrawn: it rested on an assumed bulk density and on a coincidence of numerals between two different volumes, and provenance beats it.

biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml's michaelis_menten_divisor entry moves from unsourced to agrees, with the withdrawn argument recorded so it is not re-derived. references/INDEX.md carries both rows as read.

title: maximum_depth_m needs a depth-to-bedrock product; Heimsath and Portenga do not bear on it
description:
pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml regolith.maximum_depth_m = 5.0 is a pure prefactor: every cell's regolith depth and therefore land-mean plant-available water capacity scale with it exactly.

notes/audits/tuned-values.md row 4 said the source was the same pair as row 3. Both are now read and that was WRONG. A production function integrates to a steady-state depth against an erosion rate, which is row 3's bracket; it does not integrate to a maximum reach. Heimsath's form has no asymptote at all -- the divergence as erosion vanishes is why pedogenesis.yaml replaced it. Portenga and Bierman (2011) measure denudation, not the depth a weathering front reaches.

Do: acquire a measured depth-to-bedrock distribution and take the asymptote from it. Shangguan, Hengl, Mendes de Jesus, Yuan, Dai (2017), Mapping the global depth to bedrock for land surface modeling, JAMES 9, 10.1002/2016MS000686, is the global product and is not held. Until it is, the config labels the value a declared prefactor.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md row 4.
close_reason: Closed

title: vdiff_c is a constant where Louis derives it as a function of z/z0
description:
vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/fluxmod.f90:56 declares vdiff_c = 5. as one of the three Louis stability-function coefficients, used at :323, :887 and :888.

Louis (1979), 10.1007/BF00117978, read 2026-08-25, does NOT give c as a constant. His eq. 20 derives it from a free-convection dimensional argument as

    c = C* a^2 b sqrt(z/z0)

with C* = 7.4 for momentum and 5.3 for heat and moisture, a^2 the neutral drag coefficient and z0 the roughness length. Eq. 24 gives the corresponding free-atmosphere form, again with a z-dependence. So a single vdiff_c is a DROPPED DEPENDENCE, not a different fit, and the two limbs also want different C*.

MAGNITUDE. exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_roughness.py derives a per-cell roughness spanning 0.025 to 11.2 m, a factor of 450 in z0 and 21 in sqrt(z/z0). All of it is flattened into one number, and the flattening is over the same field world-u8ds is about.

This is a form question and not a tuning one, which is why it is filed apart from world-x6q8. Do: decide whether the surface limb should carry sqrt(z/z0) explicitly, using the roughness field the model already has at zzlev; if it should, the two limbs need separate C* for momentum and heat as well.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md row 10; references/INDEX.md Louis row.
close_reason:
PREMISE WITHDRAWN AGAINST THE EXPRESSION: the surface limb ALREADY carries sqrt(z/z0) and a^2.

mktcoe forms zdenom = 1 + 3*vdiff_c*vdiff_b*sqrt(-zri*(zbz0+1))*zkblnz2. fluxmod declares zbz0 as z/z0 and sets it to znl/dz0 from this world's own roughness field, and zkblnz2 = (vonkarman/ALOG(zbz0+1))**2 IS Louis's neutral drag coefficient a^2. Factoring out the Richardson number leaves his eq. 20 term for term, and the constant fixes C* alone at 3*vdiff_c = 15 against his 7.4 for momentum and 5.3 for heat.

THE MAGNITUDE ARGUMENT WAS WRONG IN THE DECIDING DIRECTION. sqrt(z/z0) never appears in eq. 20 without the a^2 beside it, and the two run OPPOSITE, because a^2 carries ln(z/z0) in its denominator. Across the roughness field's own 0.025 to 11.2 m the product a^2*sqrt(z/z0+1) moves by 2.7 at a lowest-level height of 331 m -- 1.9 at 150 m, 3.3 at 600 m -- and is NOT MONOTONIC in z0, against the 21 this row claimed for sqrt(z/z0) alone.

The two limbs are separated as well, in the numerator rather than in c: 2b for momentum against 3b for heat gives an enhancement of 1.50 here against Louis's 7.4/5.3 = 1.40, the same distinction to within the scatter he reports on his own values. Splitting C* would import one fit's numbers into another fit's algebra.

So no numeric and no form change: IRREDUCIBLE, recorded with the argument at the value and in tuned-values row 10. Verified independently at merge against the current source, because a wrong refutation leaves a real defect in the model.

THE MIXING-LENGTH HALF IS DELIVERED RATHER THAN DEFERRED. Blackadar (1962) is obtained, filed and read: his eq. 25 makes the asymptotic length proportional to the geostrophic wind over the Coriolis parameter. The VALUE does not transfer -- the coefficient is matched to one observed wind deflection at one site, he names u*/f as equally acceptable a priori, and his lambda is the boundary layer's asymptote where ECHAM's 160 m is whole-column. The SCALING does: it goes as 1/Omega, so vdiff_lamm now derives from this world's rotation rate with the geostrophic wind carried as a declared bracket.
