title: Make the cloud-fraction fits' grid dependence explicit: world-khn declared it and left the tuning
description:
world-khn asked whether these constants encode a cell size and closed by
DECLARING that they do: "anchored to T21 rather than re-keyed, because a
per-rung table would be the same undeclared fit written more times. No numeric
changed." That was the right answer to that question. It leaves the other one
open, and under `docs/src/practice/conventions.md`'s no-tuned-values rule a
tuning that names itself is still a tuning.

THE TWO CONSTANTS.

vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/rainmod.f90:2086:

    parameter(zcca=0.245,zccb=0.125)

the convective cloud fraction as `zcca + zccb*log(convective rain rate)`. The
declaration above it states the defect and no source: "The rate it is fitted
against is a CELL MEAN, so the same simulated storm spread over a smaller cell
gives a larger rate and more cover."

vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/rainmod.f90:207:

    rcrit(:)=MAX(0.85,MAX(sigma(:),1.-sigma(:)))

the cell-mean relative humidity at which stratiform cloud starts. Same shape:
"it encodes an assumed distribution of humidity WITHIN the cell ... the
horizontal assumption has no NLAT term anywhere."

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS RANK SUGGESTS. rcrit enters as
`((rh - rcrit)/(1 - rcrit))**2`, so at the eight interior levels `1/(1-rcrit)^2`
is 44 and a 0.01 move in the floor moves modelled cloud fraction by 0.01 to 0.03
absolute wherever the modelled relative humidity sits near threshold. Cloud
fraction is the largest single lever on planetary albedo, so a first-order
radiative quantity rests on two fits anchored to a truncation.

THE SCALARS THEMSELVES ARE IRREDUCIBLE and this issue is not asking for a
source. What they encode is a subgrid distribution, and the subgrid scale is a
property of the mesh rather than of the world, so no paper can supply either
number for this grid.

Do: make the resolution dependence EXPLICIT rather than declared, so that a
tuning which cannot be sourced is at least checkable across the thing it depends
on. ExoPlaSim already ships rcritmod and rcritslope for exactly this and neither
appears anywhere outside vendor/. Derive an NLAT-dependent form for the
humidity-distribution width, wire the two keys, and sweep them across the
ladder. A tuning that is a declared function of the grid can be tested against
the grid; one anchored to T21 with a comment cannot.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md row 13; supersedes the tuning half of
world-khn, whose resolution half is correctly closed.
close_reason:
Resolution dependence made EXPLICIT and DERIVED, which is what this row asked for, rather than declared.

THE NLAT TERM GOES ON THE WIDTH. rcrit encodes the subgrid humidity distribution's width, and cloud onset sits a distance proportional to that width below saturation. Specific humidity is a passive scalar, so Kolmogorov-Obukhov-Corrsin gives variance proportional to L^(2/3), hence sigma as L^(1/3), and a cell's width goes as 1/NLAT: 1-rcrit = (1-rcrit_T21)*(32/NLAT)^(1/3). Keyed by a new rcritwidth, derived from NLAT unless given a positive value, with rcritmod and rcritslope keeping their existing meanings on top as the sweep handles.

RCRITMOD IS THE WRONG OPERATOR AND WAS NOT USED, which is worth recording because it is the obvious choice: it MULTIPLIES rcrit, and the factor that gives the right floor at T85 drives the sigma limb's end levels past 1.0, where (rh-rcrit)/(1-rcrit) divides by zero. Width scaling is bounded below 1 by construction.

The floor goes 0.85 to 0.869, 0.881, 0.896 and 0.906 at T31, T42, T63 and T85, and 1/(1-rcrit)^2 -- the lever this row prices -- from 44 to 58, 71, 92 and 112. T21 is bit-identical BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by arithmetic: the unit factor is SKIPPED rather than applied, because 1-(1-x) is not a float identity for every x.

ZCCA AND ZCCB DO NOT TAKE THIS SCALING and stay irreducible for a different reason, argued at the value: their exponent is set by an unresolved convective area fraction the scheme does not carry, so no exponent between the L^-2 diluting limit and the cell-filling limit is derivable from what is there. A tuning that is a declared function of the grid can be tested against the grid; one whose exponent is unknowable cannot, and saying which is which is the honest state.

Prediction registered. Also fixed in passing: rainmod issued the rcrit broadcast twice.

title: Delete GLOBFIRM's 0.001 burn-probability floor: its only justification is another model's floor
description:
vendor/lpj-guess/modules/vegdynam.cpp:1435:

    else if (fireprob<0.001) fireprob=0.001; // c.f. LPJF

GLOBFIRM is the live fire model (biosphere/scripts/run_lpj_guess.py:148 sets
firemodel "GLOBFIRM"), so this is not dormant. The floor puts a minimum burned
fraction of 0.1 per cent per year on every patch of the planet, forever,
including patches the moisture term says cannot carry fire, and the whole of its
justification is that another model does it.

Ask whether the thing should exist before fixing it: deleting is a fix. A floor
with no mechanism behind it is not a physics term, and the Thonicke et al.
(2001) curve above it at :1361 already returns a small positive probability
wherever fuel and dryness allow one. What the floor changes is the cells where
that curve returns essentially zero, and those are the cells where a nonzero
answer is a claim rather than a rounding.

Do: measure what the floor is currently doing -- how many gridcells are held at
it and what share of total burned area they carry -- then remove it if that
share is what it looks like. If it turns out to be load-bearing, that is a
finding about the curve and not a reason to keep an undefended constant.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md
close_reason: Resolved and committed (672d7c5e6, 8f2fdac69, and this). world-5wl5: the carriers were already emitted and declared as writes; the screen names them by path, with the partition and extensiveness identities checked where the arithmetic is. world-v5j1: the floor is a reporting cap applied to model state in Earth years -- implicit-Earth, not opaque, the chain terminating in a restatement -- and removing it breaks nothing because zero was already reachable and the one division was already guarded. world-h3qg: the execution claim is per entry with arms that must be claimed, so a thirteenth divergence is a finding rather than an inherited true.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
VERIFIED AND DONE. The floor is deleted; the deletion is a declared divergence.

The row's line number was right (vegdynam.cpp:1435) but two of its statements were not.

1. The provenance is REAL, not a claim someone wrote down. 'LPJF' is the FORTRAN LPJ this file's own reference block cites as Sitch et al., and its maintained descendant carries the identical constant: LPJmL's src/soil/fire_prob.c, vendored at vendor/lpjml, returns 0.001 for any fire_frac below 0.001. Two independent implementations state the number. Neither derives it, so walking the chain -- which is the OPAQUE repair -- terminates in a restatement.

2. The row's label is tuned-value and the classification is wrong. A fit residual does not arrive at exactly 1e-3 in two codebases and no comment claims a fit. The constant is IMPLICIT-EARTH, and mainline's own source is what proves it. commonoutput.cpp writes firert_gridcell += 1000.0 under '// Set a limit of 1000 years' below the same threshold, so 0.001/yr is a reporting cap on the fire return interval that had been applied to the model state -- and the cap is one per EARTH year. LPJF and LPJmL both run NDAYYEAR 365; this model's year is 183 absolute days, so the numeral delivered a whole Earth year of the floor every 183 days: 1.996x the hazard, the same factor the VESPDRV4-to-V5 magic exists to catch. distinterval, the same class of quantity read 140 lines below, IS converted for that reason and reaches the model as 199.594 against an Earth calibration of 100. Rescaling by 0.501 was refused: it repairs the unit of a number with no derivation, and the quantity is a diagnostic cap, not a mechanism.

WHAT BREAKS IF IT GOES: nothing, and the source says so. fire() already returns fireprob = 0.0 from its MINFUEL branch before the floor, so zero is reachable in the shipped model and every consumer already handles it. The single division, commonoutput.cpp's 1.0/patch.fireprob, is already guarded by the same 0.001 -- the floor is what kept that guard DEAD for fuel-bearing patches. Removing it makes the guard live and does not move the reported return interval (floored patch reported 1/0.001 = 1000 yr; the guard reports 1000 yr); what changes is that a patch the moisture term says cannot burn stops reporting burned area. All other consumers are linear in fireprob. The Thonicke Eqn 9 denominator has no root on the reachable domain (min 0.185 at s'=-0.612), so there was no singularity to cover.

WHAT IT WAS WORTH: it bound where s < 0.00914, fewer than 1.67 fully-flammable-day-equivalents out of 183. There it added a 0.001/model-year stand-replacing fire hazard against distinterval's 0.00501 -- 20 per cent on top of generic disturbance, 2.32 expected fires and P=0.902 of at least one over nyear_spinup 2318. Not a rounding on cohort age structure. The gridcell COUNT the row asked for cannot come from the source; biosphere/config/fire.yaml's comparison_arm names the paired run that would measure it, and no LPJ-GUESS run passes acceptance yet (world-qcse).

CHANGED: vendor/lpj-guess/modules/vegdynam.cpp (deletion + DECLARED DIVERGENCE FROM MAINLINE block recording mainline's line verbatim); new biosphere/config/fire.yaml register; biosphere/notes/fire-model-audit.md section 8; docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md.

VERIFICATION: syntax-only compile of the edited TU with the build's own include paths at -std=c++14, clean, with a negative control confirming the check can fail. A link was not available (host lock held by a climate series). Execution verification is not available at all and is recorded as execution_verified: false with why_not_verified.

OWED: no gate reads fire.yaml -- world-zq9v, filed, biosphere/scripts/ was outside this task's scope. notes/audits/tuned-values.md's fire row (line ~1151 and the disposition paragraph ~1161-1172) is now stale and mis-classifies this as tuned; also out of scope.

title: gamma, the precipitation re-evaporation fraction, has no derivation on either side
description:
vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/rainmod.f90:78 declares
`gamma = 0.01`, the fraction of the sub-saturation deficit falling precipitation
evaporates per timestep, applied at four sites around :2475. It sets how much
precipitation reaches the ground, which is P minus E over land directly.

The rung-keyed branch that made it 0.007 at T42 is gone and the declaration
records why, but it also records the part that is still open: "with no
derivation on either side". Upstream had 0.01 and 0.007, a 43 per cent step, and
neither carries one. That 43 per cent is the only scale anyone has ever put on
this number.

Do: derive it. A per-timestep evaporated fraction is not a published quantity;
what is published is a fall speed and a ventilated evaporation rate for a
drop-size distribution, from which a per-step fraction follows given the layer
depth and the step. Kessler (1969), *On the Distribution and Continuity of Water
Substance in Atmospheric Circulations*, 10.1007/978-1-935704-36-2, is the
canonical form and is not in references/. This is a derivation to do, not a
number to copy, and the derived form will carry this world's gravity and layer
depths where the constant does not.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md
notes:
Kessler (1969) fetched, filed and READ 2026-08-25. The derivation this issue asked for CLOSES, and it is in the declaration at rainmod.f90:78. Commit c5c286bb, comment only.

THE DERIVATION. Kessler's table 4 gives rain evaporation for a Marshall-Palmer distribution as dM/dt = k3 N0^(7/20) m M^(13/20) in g m-3 s-1, with k3 = 1.93e-6 his tabulated evaporation coefficient, N0 = 1e7 m-4 so N0^(7/20) = 282, m the saturation deficit and M the rain water content, both g/m3. His mean volume-weighted fall speed is 38.8 N0^(-1/8) M^(1/8) = 5.17 M^0.125 m/s. The four sites evaporate gamma*(qsat-q)*dsigma/deltsec2, which per unit area is gamma * deficit * dz / deltsec2 once dsigma*ps/ga is written as the layer air mass. Kessler's rate over the same layer is k3 N0^(7/20) deficit M^0.65 dz. THE LAYER DEPTH CANCELS:

    gamma = 5.44e-4 * M^0.65 * deltsec2,   M = P / V

THREE CONSEQUENCES A CONSTANT CANNOT CARRY. gamma is proportional to the timestep, which the declaration already inferred from the form and now has a derivation under. It goes as P^0.578. And it carries ga^(-0.289) through the drop terminal speed, 0.926 of Earth here.

MAGNITUDE. At deltsec2 = 3600 s (this project's 30-minute step doubled) the derived value is 0.039 at 0.5 mm/day, 0.10 at 3 mm/day, 0.22 at 10 mm/day. The declared 0.01 is below all of it: it is the Kessler value at 0.048 mm/day, sixty times below a global-mean rate. A grid-mean flux understates M and so understates gamma, making those floors.

WHAT IS LEFT, and it is the whole of the issue now. Replace the constant with the derived form in the four where-blocks around rainmod.f90:2475, computing M per level from zprl, zprc, zprsl and zprsc, which they already hold. Not done here because the batch that read the paper was forbidden to compile or run, and this is a first-order change to P minus E over land that must not ship unverified.

THE RUN THAT SETTLES ITS EFFECT: a matched T21 L10 pair from the same restart, one arm at the compiled gamma = 0.01 and one at the derived form, both with the energy fixer on and both segmented for a climatology rather than a diagnostic, compared on land P minus E, the runoff field hydrography reads, and the modelled high cloud fraction. One rebuild of the T21 configuration precedes it (rule 4: rebuild all, not one).

Kessler's own caveats travel with the form: the single-drop fit is accurate to about 40 per cent, a constant N0 misrepresents evaporation because the process depletes small drops preferentially, and the rate is for standard air density with no altitude variation.
close_reason:
Derived from Kessler and integrated at all four sites, per cell, carrying this world's gravity and layer depths where the constant did not.

gamma = 5.4395e-4 * (P/zvcoef)^0.577778 * deltsec2 with zvcoef = 5.17*sqrt(ga/9.80665), P the layer flux in g m-2 s-1 read through mkrain's own output conversion. The derivation was reproduced independently rather than transcribed: k3*N0^(7/20) = 5.4395e-4, the exponent 13/20 * 8/9 = 0.577778, and the gravity term ga^(-0.289) = 0.9257.

At deltsec2 3600 s the derived value is 0.036 at 0.5 mm/day, 0.101 at 3 and 0.381 at 30. The declared 0.01 is the Kessler value at 0.055 mm/day -- so the constant was not merely unsourced, it was the right answer for a rain rate this world's land does not see.

THE SENTINEL IS LIVE, NOT INERT, and deliberately: run_exoplasim.py writes no GAMMA key, so the derived form is what the next commissioning integrates. Physics is not a knob -- the derived term goes in because it is the correct one and the unsourced constant is what needs the switch. A positive gamma in rainmod_nl restores the literal at all four sites, which is the control arm AND a check that can fail, since it must be bit-identical.

The snow sites evaluate the rain form because Kessler supplies no snow analogue. That is declared at the value rather than hidden, and it is a known limitation and not a regression.

PREDICTION REGISTERED BEFORE ANY ARM, in exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md: land P minus E falls 10 to 50 per cent; the mechanism is sub-cloud MOISTENING rather than a scaling of the flux, so the response is SUBLINEAR in the gamma ratio, because at 0.01 the scheme already sits at the deficit-limited transition; sub-cloud relative humidity rise is the discriminating measurement; and a RISE in land P minus E is wrong outright. Kessler's own caveats travel with the form: the single-drop fit is good to about 40 per cent, a constant N0 misrepresents evaporation because the process depletes small drops preferentially, and the rate is for standard air density.

Run held per the batch rule; one rebuild of every binary precedes it.

title: Report the roughness field's own land mean beside the dz0land anchor it is rescaled onto
description:
exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_roughness.py derives a per-cell land
roughness field from this world's lithology and subgrid relief, spanning 0.025
to 11.2 m, and then bisects a free orographic coefficient (:302-313) so that the
area-weighted land mean of that field equals EXOPLASIM_DZ0LAND_M = 2.0 (:137).
aeolian/config/dust.yaml:152-153 confirms it from the consumer side: "its land
mean is anchored to 2.0 m so the value ExoPlaSim was tuned against does not
move."

THE DECISION IS INSPECTABLE AND THE ANCHOR IS NOT. Anchoring the mean and
supplying only the pattern is a recorded design decision
(docs/src/reference/config-rationale.md:764-766) and is defensible. What it
anchors ON is a compiled default whose only documentation in the model source is
the comment "roughness length land". Nothing in this tree establishes that 2.0 m
is anything but an unexamined number, so the tuned value is the target, and the
bisection is the step that discards a physically sourced land mean in favour of
it.

Reach: land sensible heat and land evaporation, therefore the carve criterion's
numerator. notes/audits/opaque-constants.md finding 7 prices the neighbouring
gravity error on the same coefficient at 8.4x land exchange. The ladder half is
already instrumented: analysis/spatial_reduction_gap.py:376-395 records that the
solved coefficient rises by 1.98 from T21 to T170 to hold the mean, so two rungs
built with the defaults differ by their terrain AND by their calibration.

Do: report the field's own unrescaled area-weighted land mean beside the
anchored one, and run --target-mean at that value as an arm. That is a sourced
number this project already computes, and reporting it converts the anchor from
an assumption into a bracket. It needs a decision, not a paper.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md
notes:
2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER, from a pass over the needs-decision set.
RECLASSIFIED, the reporting half needs nothing from the author: run the field's own unrescaled land mean beside the anchored one and the --target-mean arm. A decision about whether to keep anchoring on EXOPLASIM_DZ0LAND_M arrives only once those two numbers can be seen together.

2026-08-26, REOPENED, on the same rule that reopened PHYS-15: the test is
whether the quantity can be modelled MORE CORRECTLY, not whether the current
disposition is defensible. It closed with the orographic coefficient DERIVED
from PlaSim's own vendored Earth boundary dataset and the Earth-to-Vesper
transfer carried as a swept bracket. That was the best available with no
literature; four papers that would replace the bracket with a derivation were
listed as unfetchable and ARE NOW ALL HELD:

  mason1988.pdf     what an area-averaged roughness length IS over
                    heterogeneous ground, which is the quantity the bisection
                    currently obtains by solving onto a reference
  wood1993.pdf      the pressure force an orographic roughness stands in for
  beljaars2004.pdf  the operational scheme Elvidge measures the spread of
  lettau1969.pdf    roughness from element geometry rather than from a fit

A CITATION ERROR TO CARRY FORWARD RATHER THAN REPEAT. The report closing this
row cited the first as Mason (1985) with DOI 10.1002/qj.49711146808. Both are
wrong: it is Mason (1988), Q. J. R. Meteorol. Soc. 114(480), 399-420,
10.1002/qj.49711448007, and that DOI names Mishra, Patwardhan and George (1985)
on the monsoon onset vortex. references/mishra1985.pdf is that paper and is not
wanted here. Verify a PDF is the paper it is named for before citing it.

WHAT STANDS AND MUST NOT BE UNDONE, because it is measurement: 2.0 m is
IMPLICIT-EARTH rather than tuned, established by reducing the vendored dataset's
code 173 over its own land; earth_reference_land_z0() computing the anchor at
build time rather than carrying a literal; both refusals; and the finding that
the Earth dataset's cover term and this world's no-orographic arm agree to 8 to
10 per cent, so the transfer imports subgrid RELIEF and not somebody else's land
cover. What is open is only whether the coefficient can be sourced instead of
solved.
close_reason:
RESOLVED, and the bisection is gone rather than sourced. The orographic coefficient no longer exists: the orographic term is computed from this world's own subgrid slope with no fitted constant in it, and Earth's figure is now a labelled COMPARISON rather than a target.

WHAT IT RESTS ON. Wood and Mason (1993) Eq. (33): the effective roughness of hilly ground is the length whose drag coefficient at the pressure scale height equals the SUM of the hills' pressure drag and the ground's skin friction, added in the DRAG COEFFICIENT. simba.f90:474 combines in quadrature in the LENGTH, which is the model's convention rather than the literature's, and the builder now follows the derivation. Beljaars et al. (2004) Eq. (6), Ca = 2*alpha*beta*Cmd*thetabar^2, QUADRATIC IN SUBGRID SLOPE rather than linear in relief amplitude, with their Eqs. (4) and (5) supplying h_m, l and alpha so none is assumed. Mason (1988): the cell average is of drag coefficients at the BLENDING HEIGHT, 27.3 m here against a lowest model level at 114.0 m, so the builder had been averaging an order of magnitude too high. Slope from Export.local_slope_deg, the mesh's own plane fit.

WHY THE OLD RELATION WAS STRUCTURALLY WRONG, which is the finding worth keeping: a coefficient multiplying an ELEVATION SPREAD has to carry the missing horizontal scale inside itself, and the horizontal scale of a within-cell spread IS THE CELL. That is why it drifted by a factor of 1.98 across the ladder.

DISPOSITION: derived, with a swept bracket on two attributions read out of the papers -- the wavelength attributed to the resolved slope (1 to 4 mesh spacings, entering only through logarithms) and WM93's two turbulence closures. Together they move the land mean by about 4 per cent.

NUMBERS on canonical-10m-base: derived land mean 0.4026 m at T21 and 0.4103 at T42, against an Earth reference of 2.2049 and 1.2145. The full ladder spreads by 0.9 per cent where the solved coefficient moved by 1.98.

WHERE THE DISTANCE FROM EARTH IS, checked rather than assumed: the two planets' COVER roughness agrees to within a fifth and neither is derived from the other, so the entire gap is the RELIEF term. Verified from the artifact: Earth's surface part 0.3162 m against this world's unrescaled 0.3751 m.

THE DEFAULT ARM CHANGED. A build writes the derived field; the Earth-anchored arm is a labelled diagnostic and no lineage may rest on it. The derived arm also builds at EVERY rung, where the anchored default refused above T42 because the model ships a boundary dataset at two rungs only.

TESTS THAT CAN FAIL, on every build: alpha from Eq. (5) returns 11.994 against the paper's 12.0, h_m/lambda returns 0.1047 against 0.1, Lettau's Colorado worked example returns exactly 12.5 m, and Eq. (33) with no hills is an identity on the cover roughness.

LETTAU (1969) DOES NOT AGREE at this scale and that is reported rather than gated: about two orders above the WM93 enhancement, because it is purely geometric and grows linearly with element size where WM93 saturates.

A LIMIT OF THE GENERATOR, stated rather than bracketed: Ca is quadratic in slope, slope variance is dominated by the shortest wavelength present, and Orogen's terrain-information floor is near 20 km while the scheme's band is below 5 km. Supplying the missing band would mean importing Earth's topographic spectrum under a derivation's name.

The magnitude argument in fluxmod.f90 and tuned-values.md section 10 rested on the superseded span and has been re-taken: the product moves by 5.2 rather than 2.7 at 331 m, and the conclusion is unchanged.

title: Derive the free-tropospheric mixing length for this atmosphere; fetch Louis (1979) for the three fives
description:
vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/fluxmod.f90:47 declares
`vdiff_lamm = 160.` and its own comment states the position exactly: "160 m is
ECHAM's and is a fit to Earth's free troposphere. It is not obviously
transferable, and it is left at ECHAM's value because nothing in this project has
measured a replacement -- not because 160 m has been shown to apply here."

It is the single number setting free-tropospheric vertical diffusivity, through
`zmixm = lamm*k*z/(lamm + k*z)` and, through zlamh, its heat counterpart.

Beside it at :56-58 the three Louis stability-function coefficients, all 5.0,
cited to ECHAM REPORT 218, which the declaration correctly calls "a report and
not a derivation": "None of the three is separately justified there or here;
they are one fitted set and are used as one."

TWO SEPARATE PIECES OF WORK.

(a) The mixing length is a derivation this project can do. 160 m is a length
scale of Earth's free troposphere and this atmosphere's scale height is 0.766 of
Earth's, so a scaled value follows the way clwhsc's did under world-ofn. Doing
it is a physics claim and it will move the surface fluxes, so it wants the same
treatment clwhsc got: derive, state the rule in the declaration, and let the
namelist key override.

(b) The three fives want their primary read before anything is claimed about
them. Louis (1979), *A parametric model of vertical eddy fluxes in the
atmosphere*, Boundary-Layer Meteorology 17, 187-202, 10.1007/BF00117978 (DOI and
pagination confirmed against Crossref), is not in references/. Reading it
establishes whether the set is Louis's own or ECHAM's re-fit, which is a
different question from whether it transfers, and the answer decides whether a
replacement is even meaningful.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md
close_reason:
Part (b) is answered and part (a) is re-filed. Louis (1979) read 2026-08-25.

THE THREE FIVES ARE ECHAM'S RE-FIT, NOT LOUIS'S, which is exactly what this issue asked. Louis fits F = 1 - b Ri/(1 + c sqrt(|Ri|)) unstable and F = 1/(1 + b' Ri)^2 stable, with b = 2b' = 9.4 chosen so dF/dRi is continuous across neutrality -- a constraint, not a fit. His c is not a constant: c = C* a^2 b sqrt(z/z0) with C* = 7.4 momentum and 5.3 heat. The model's b=c=d=5 with 2b and 3b folded in corresponds to Louis's b near 10 and 15 against his 9.4. And no replacement follows from the primary: Louis states his own values 'are rather uncertain because of the large scatter in the observations'. Disposition IRREDUCIBLE, now checked rather than asserted.

PART (a) IS REFUTED AS PROPOSED. 160 m is not Louis's either -- his eq. 22 is Blackadar's form, he calls lambda 'an adjustable parameter' and took it as 100 m. Nothing in Blackadar's or Louis's form makes lambda proportional to a scale height, so scaling 160 m by 0.766 the way clwhsc was scaled has nothing under it and is NOT done. clwhsc's scaling worked because the quantity was a geometric height in a formula whose neighbours already scaled as 1/g; lambda is not that. What transfers is Blackadar (1962), where lambda follows from the geostrophic wind and the Coriolis parameter. Not held. Fetching it is world-80ia.

A new finding fell out and is world-awm5: vdiff_c being one number is a dropped roughness dependence, not a different fit, over a field spanning a factor of 450 in z0.

Comment only in fluxmod.f90; no numeric changed, no symbol touched, no binary affected. Commit c5c286bb.

title: th2oc is the model's only water vapour continuum and has no derivation
description:
vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/radmod.f90:72 declares
`th2oc = 0.024` with the comment "absorption coefficient h2o continuum (lwr)".
No unit, no source, no derivation anywhere in the tree.

IT IS THE FOURTH MEMBER OF THE jtune TUNING TABLE. radmod.f90:976-989 records
that upstream carried a per-(NTRU, NLEV) tuning here -- tswr1, tswr2, tswr3 and
th2oc -- selected through a flag that never fired at any truncation. The other
three are named as tunings in their own declarations; this one is not, and it is
the only one of the four this project has never re-weighted or bracketed.

WHAT IT DOES. Sasamori's broadband absorptances have no window absorption at
all, so this is the entire continuum contribution to the modelled longwave. It
is applied at radmod.f90:3463 as
`zah2o = min(zah2o + (1 - exp(-th2oc*zsumwv)), 1)`.
docs/src/reference/config-rationale.md:776-778 reaches th2oc and only to
establish that there is no shortwave counterpart; it never asks where 0.024 came
from.

MAGNITUDE, bracketed because the column path needs a baseline to measure.
Setting th2oc to zero, which the surrounding `if(th2oc > 0.)` supports, removes
between 0.012 and 0.058 of broadband absorptance over a pressure-weighted column
path of 0.5 to 2.5 g/cm2. Against a clear-sky greenhouse trapping of order
150 W/m2 that puts the term at roughly 2 to 9 W/m2, hence 2 to 7 K by
lib/sensitivity.py.

Do: this needs a correlated-k or line-by-line calculation with the MT_CKD
continuum on this path. references/INDEX.md records that Mlawer et al. (2012),
10.1098/rsta.2011.0295, read, "does not supply an evaluable continuum" -- the
coefficients ship as data with LBLRTM -- so the paper alone does not close it.
It is the same correlated-k bundle exoplasim/notes/corrk-cross-check.md says the
project does not have and which blocks h2o_sw_level's bracket. The two open
together and should be scoped together.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md
close_reason:
DECLARED BRACKET, SWEPT -- the third of the four dispositions -- and the value stays blocked on a bundle this project does not have.

Sourcing it is not available and the evidence already said so: references/INDEX.md records Mlawer et al. (2012) read and "does not supply an evaluable continuum", the coefficients shipping as data with LBLRTM. So the route to a VALUE is a correlated-k or line-by-line calculation with MT_CKD on this path, the same bundle corrk-cross-check.md says the project lacks and which also blocks h2o_sw_level. The two open together, unchanged.

THE BRACKET IS DERIVED RATHER THAN GUESSED, which is what makes it a disposition instead of a shrug. th2oc stands in for the window, so it cannot add more absorptance than the window's own Planck share: over 250 to 300 K at the largest path that caps it at 0.038 to 0.050. Bracket [0.0, 0.038], arms end to end, with the static conversion's high lean stated.

AND THE INHERITED 0.024 IS HALF ITS OWN CEILING. It already claims 0.052 of broadband absorptance at the mean path and 0.136 at the maximum -- more than half the whole window. That is the finding, and it is not what a residual coefficient should look like.

CORRECTED IN tuned-values.md ROW 8 while here: its column path range of 0.5 to 2.5 g/cm2 was too narrow. The model's own paths run 0.04 to 6.08 with a mean of 2.23, so the term is worth roughly 5 to 12 K end to end rather than the 2 to 7 that row carried, and its disposition moves from REPLACEABLE, SOURCE NEEDED to DECLARED BRACKET, SWEPT.

title: Report a size-floor sensitivity beside the carve verdict: a 33x lever is undeclared
description:
The carve incision coefficient C is solved so that this world's basin
population reproduces Earth's density of overflowing-but-still-standing basins.
hydrography/scripts/export_carve_list.py:319 `calibrate_coefficient`, target at
:142-144 (EARTH_STANDING_BASINS 15, EARTH_BAND_LAND_MKM2 78.9,
CALIBRATION_LATITUDE 35.0). The file admits it: "Calibrated here rather than
declared, because the target moves", and hydrography/notes/retain-fraction.md:47
says the reason is that the relaxation window is undefined rather than
unmeasured.

C ITSELF IS IRREDUCIBLE and this issue is not about it.
docs/src/reference/no-time-axis.md establishes that the relaxation window C
absorbs cannot exist here, so no dataset can supply it, and re-solving against
this world's own basins every run is the right treatment of a quantity like
that.

THE UNDECLARED LEVER IS THE SIZE FLOOR. export_carve_list.py:137-139 says so in
its own words: the floor "is what this mesh can resolve and it decides the
answer: counting from 10 km2 instead gives a density 33 times higher and reads
as 'carve almost nothing'." It is 1,000 km2, defended as a resolution argument,
but the mesh cell is 285 km2 and the median overflowing basin at spill is
7,338 km2, so 1,000 sits between the two and is chosen rather than derived. A
factor of 33 on the target sits on that choice and nothing reports it.

For scale on how much C moves: retain-fraction.md:310-312 gives the marginal
class moving by a factor of 1.9 across the Poisson bracket on Earth's 15, and a
single verdict change moved the solved C from 161 to 235.9, outside its own
published 128 to 218 bracket.

Do: run the floor across its plausible span and report the solved C and the
marginal count beside the verdict, converting a hidden 33-fold lever into a
declared bracket. One re-run of a script, no new data.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md
close_reason:
The size floor on the Earth sample is declared and swept, and C stays irreducible.

EARTH_SIZE_FLOOR_KM2 names the floor and EARTH_STANDING_BY_FLOOR carries the ladder; --measure-earth-floors is the HydroLAKES x HydroBASINS query itself rather than a record of it, and it reproduces the published fifteen at 1,000 km2 exactly. sweep_size_floor re-solves at every rung over a span the build derives -- median land mesh cell area at the bottom, median area at spill of the overflowing basins at the top, 71.4 to 2,687 km2 on precarve-craton-10m -- and writes the whole ladder to the carve list's sidecar under method.calibration.size_floor_sensitivity, beside the verdict.

The criterion was fixed before the sweep ran: the floor's lever against the Poisson error on the Earth count, solved on the same population. Across the span C moves 131.9 to 1076.9, a factor of 8.17, against 1.77 for the Poisson bracket at the floor in force; the marginal class moves 422 to 46, a factor of 9.17, against 1.80. DECISIVE on both, by about five to one. The recomputed Poisson factor of 1.80 agrees with the 1.9 retain-fraction.md published on precarve-craton, so the lever is measured against a scatter known independently of it. The preserved count is 3,854 at every rung, which is the control: C cannot reach preservation, so a floor that moved it would mean the sweep was moving something else.

C itself is declared irreducible: no-time-axis.md establishes the relaxation window it absorbs cannot exist here, so no dataset can supply it.

hydrography/notes/retain-fraction.md carries the sweep; notes/audits/tuned-values.md row 5 is rewritten to IRREDUCIBLE for C, DECLARED AND SWEPT for the floor. Four selftest cases that can fail were added, including a negative control requiring SUBORDINATE on a table whose count does not move with the floor; 11 checks, 0 failed. Merged to main as 64ebd3d3.

NOT DELIVERED, and separately blocked: the carve_list.json artifact itself. basins.nc on BOTH builds predates retained_fraction -- verified on main, the variable is absent from precarve-craton and precarve-craton-10m alike -- so export_carve_list.py refuses before it calibrates and the carve_list step is unrunnable for every build in tree. build_hydrography.py writes the field, cost minutes, and regenerating a derived artifact is a STEP rather than an issue (conventions.md), so it is not filed. The sweep was validated end to end against a scratchpad copy carrying an identity retained_fraction.

title: Bracket the pedogenesis values that carry no source and no bracket
description:
pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml is a disciplined file whose `catena`,
`water`, `andisol` and `bedrock_water` blocks all ship brackets with an
instruction not to tune within them. The `regolith:` and `texture:` blocks and
the `ph:` block do not, and those are exactly where the tuned values are.

| where | value | what is missing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| :236 | clay_conversion 0.55 | no comment on the value, no source, no bracket; numerically identical to clay_yield at :298, which WAS fitted to a SoilGrids slope of 0.543 |
| :565 | dry_erosion_baseline 0.15 | the mechanism is argued and the value is not attached to it |
| :619-633 | the pH block: six parent values, leaching_slope 0.9 at :629, endorheic_alkalinity_bonus 0.8 at :633 | no comment on ANY value, no citation, no bracket, nothing in README, notes or references |
| :301 | sand_to_silt_loss_ratio 2.0 | no source; the surface-area sentence beside it is backwards, so the number did not come from the reasoning printed next to it |

Magnitudes. clay_conversion is near-linear at this world's weathering intensity,
so a 10 per cent move is +9.2 per cent converted clay. dry_erosion_baseline is
21 per cent of the moisture term at the land mean and 100 per cent of it over

leaching_slope moves land-mean soil pH by 0.04 per 10 per cent and wet-cell pH
by 0.13; the endorheic bonus is a flat 0.08 over the closed-basin fraction that

Do: ship a bracket on each, in the same form the rest of the file uses, so what
is unknown is declared unknown and gets swept rather than quoted. This is not
new physics and does not wait on a paper. For leaching_slope specifically,
SoilGrids `phh2o` over the sixteen type localities
pedology/scripts/validate_against_earth.py already joins to would bracket it
directly -- with the caveat pedogenesis.yaml:277 itself raises, that those sites
have absorbed one fit already.

clay_yield at :298 is NOT in this list: it is an admitted Earth fit whose
derivation is re-runnable and whose out-of-range application the file already
records. It is disclosed, and disclosure is the standard being asked for
here.

title: The vegetation model's snow carries solid ice's heat capacity, not its own
description:
vendor/lpj-guess/modules/soil.cpp's update_snow_properties computes the
modelled snowpack's volumetric heat capacity as ice Ih's specific heat times a
local ice_density of 917 kg/m3, not times the prognostic snowdens beside it:

    static const double ice_density = 917.0; // kg m-3
    Csnow = (0.185 + 0.689 * (K2degC + dailyairtemp) * 0.01) * J_PER_KJ;
    Csnow *= ice_density;

That is the defect landmod's snowcap had and GRAV-8 fixed there, third
instance: a volumetric heat capacity is a density times a specific heat, and
the density in question is the snow's. The specific heat itself is right --
snow is ice Ih plus air and the air carries a negligible share of the mass --
so only the density is wrong.

Worth: at fixed water equivalent a pack's thermal mass should not depend on
its density at all, because its thickness goes as 1/rho and its heat capacity
per unit volume as rho. Here the capacity is pinned at solid ice's while the
thickness still goes as 1/rho, so the modelled pack's thermal mass per unit
water equivalent is 917/snowdens too high: 3.33 at snowdens_start 275 and 1.83
at snowdens_end 500. Ci[] takes Csnow directly for every active snow layer of
the multilayer solve, and Dsnow = Ksnow/Csnow carries the same factor into the
diffusivity, so the modelled pack is both too slow to warm and too slow to
cool.

This is a divergence from LPJ-GUESS 4.1.1 rather than from the CNP fork: the
whole of update_snow_properties outside the conductivity block is byte-
identical to guess_4.1/modules/soil.cpp's, and it is on by default under
data/ins/global.ins's iftwolayersoil 0.

Do: derive Csnow from snowdens the way landmod's landini derives snowcap from
rhosnow, and register it beside the conductivity entry in
biosphere/config/snow_thermal.yaml with mainline's line recorded verbatim, so
biosphere/scripts/snow_thermal_gate.py checks both halves. Found while settling
world-gjov and deliberately not folded into it: that row was the conductivity
relation, and a heat capacity is a different quantity with a different
argument.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text: 2026-08-30, branch worktree-agent-aa7af1d18be6ea483, commit 91cb8290a. DONE. Csnow now derives from snowdens rather than a local ice_density of 917: soil.cpp's update_snow_properties multiplies Fukusako's specific heat by the prognostic snow density, and the local constant is deleted with it. The specific heat is unchanged and is right -- the modelled pack is ice Ih plus air and the air carries under a thousandth of the mass -- so only the density moved and the argument is dimensional. Registered as snow_heat_capacity_density in biosphere/config/snow_thermal.yaml with mainline's two lines verbatim; snow_thermal_gate.py carries a new fixture proving the appended entry is checked by the loop and not covered by the first entry's verdict, 17 of 17 fixtures. IT COMPILES: the full 124-file build succeeded at exit 0. IT IS REACHED: driver.cpp:926 calls Soil::soil_temp_multilayer every day, which calls update_snow_properties, whose Csnow becomes Ci[] for every active snow layer under iftwolayersoil 0. Nothing is execution-verified: no LPJ-GUESS run this project has made has passed acceptance and the register's arms block is empty. WORTH: thermal mass per unit water equivalent falls by 917/snowdens, 3.33 at snowdens_start and 1.83 at snowdens_end; diffusivity at 273.15 K rises 1.24e-7 to 4.12e-7 m2/s at snowdens_start and 3.50e-7 to 6.42e-7 at snowdens_end. THE CHECK THAT COULD HAVE FAILED AND DID NOT: at landmod's rhosnow of 330 the repaired line gives 682,111 J/m3/K against that column's snowcap of 330*2090 = 689,700, 1.1 per cent apart. That residual is the two columns' SPECIFIC heats differing, up to 17 per cent at -40 degC, filed as world-a2lv. Could not fetch Fukusako (1990), Int. J. Thermophys. 11, 353-372, 10.1007/BF01133567; it is not needed for this change, which does not touch the specific heat.

title: swr does not bound its clear-sky transmissivities or its layer reflectivities, and four of its divisors are one minus them
description:
world-px61 read every masked divisor in radmod.f90 and settled the masked
part of the class: swr's two-stream is preset on every lane, so on a lane
losun discards every quotient divides by exactly 1. Nine of those divisors
are not bounded on a lane losun KEEPS, and the mask never had anything to
do with it.

The two shapes:

  1 - A(u)/zsolar_b, at zto3t, zto3u, ztwvt, ztwvu, ztco2t, ztco2u and the
  three spelled-out absorptance denominators. This is the clear-sky band
  transmissivity. A(u) is Lacis and Hansen's absorptance as a fraction of
  TOTAL incident flux and zsolar_b is band b's share of it, so the quotient
  is the fraction of the BAND the absorber removes and the divisor vanishes
  when it removes all of it. Whether it can is not a property of the
  formulae alone: o3uvw, o3visw, h2osww, h2oswl and co2sww are namelist
  re-weightings for a non-solar host and are not confined to 1, and zsolar1
  falls as the host gets redder, which is the direction this planet's host
  is. lwr clamps its counterpart -- ztaucs to [zero, 1-zero], radmod.f90 --
  and swr clamps nothing.

  1 - R_above*R_below, the adding method's denominator, at four sites in
  the downward loop, the upward loop and the flux loop. Both factors are
  layer reflectivities the scheme sums from a Rayleigh term, a cloud term
  and an aerosol term without bounding the sum. The cloud term
  1 - 1/(1 + zb1*ztau1/zmu0) approaches 1 as the beam cosine falls, so
  zrb1 = zrcs + zrcl1*dcc can exceed 1 at low sun under thick cloud even
  though each term is below it. The scattered-beam pair the divisors
  actually use is the tighter of the two -- zrcl1s is capped near 0.94 by
  the optical-depth ceiling and zrcsu by the Rayleigh coefficient -- but
  the bound involves the surface pressure and is not comfortable.

Do: establish whether either can reach zero on a lane this planet's
configuration produces, by evaluating the two expressions over the model's
own ranges of the absorber amounts, the band weights and zsolar1 rather
than by argument. If either can, the remedy is a clamp of the same kind
lwr already applies to ztaucs, and it CHANGES STORED VALUES, so it is a
physics change and is reported as one. If neither can, the bound belongs
in lint_masked_domains.py's CLASSIFIED rows, which currently cite this
issue instead of a bound.

Evidence: notes/audits/masked-where-blocks.md.
close_reason:
Measured over the model's own ranges rather than argued, and THE TWO FAMILIES GOT DIFFERENT ANSWERS.

FAMILY A, the clear-sky transmissivities of the form 1 - A(u)/zsolar_b: all three absorptances CAN exceed their band's share. Water vapour's has a finite asymptote that this configuration puts 24 per cent above 1, and the divisor crosses zero at 2090 precipitable cm against a model maximum of 212.9 -- a 9.82x margin. On the Sun the same asymptote crosses five orders of magnitude further out, so the margin is a property of THIS host and of three namelist re-weightings none of which is confined to 1. Clamped at all nine sites on lwr's own form, with zcstr preset to 1 OUTSIDE the mask so a lane the mask discards still divides by exactly 1.

IT IS BIT-IDENTICAL ON THIS CONFIGURATION -- the tightest of the nine floors is 0.2016 -- so it is a GUARD and not the physics change this row anticipated. That is the answer to the row's own question about which it would be.

FAMILY B, the adding method's 1 - R_above*R_below at four sites: cannot reach zero at all. Bounded by caps already in the code (zlwp at 1000 g/m2, and R+T at most 1 per layer), giving floors of 0.005799 and 0.034467 against a perfect reflector and 0.1298 and 0.4763 at the model's own fields. Those go into lint_masked_domains.py's CLASSIFIED rows as BOUNDS, which is what the row asked for in that branch, and the lint now reports zero unclassified.

Fixed in passing at the remedy site: two swr rows in lint_masked_domains.py justified a bound through tswr1, a coefficient world-f9ig deleted. Rewritten onto the Stephens table interpolation.

title: The climate column and the ecology column compute snow conductivity from different relations
description:
landmod's landini derives snowdiff from the snow density through Fourteau et al. (2021) Eq. (18), while vendor/lpj-guess/modules/soil.cpp computes its Ksnow from Sturm et al. (1997) -- the relation notes/audits/cryosphere-material-properties.md declined, and the one the needle-probe evidence argues against. Sturm's sits below BOTH arms of the published kinetics bracket at every density in the range the two components span, and at the declared snow density it is close to half the value the climate column uses.

So one snowfall, at one density, insulates the ecology column's soil about twice as well as the climate column's. That is one material property with two values inside one project, the class notes/audits/ocean-tier-implicit-earth.md finding A1 was written about and the class icemod's CKAPSN was, and it is larger than the arm-to-arm bracket between the two published limits.

Evidence: notes/audits/cryosphere-material-properties.md, section 'A cross-component finding: the two columns run different snow'. analysis/ice_properties.json's snow_conductivity_bracket carries all three relations evaluated across the density range, including Sturm as LPJ-GUESS runs it.

Do: decide which relation both columns run, and make it ONE declaration rather than two agreeing ones. This is a change to vendor/lpj-guess, not to a constant, so it is not the ocean tier's and was not fixed where it was found. Note that LPJ-GUESS's snow density is prognostic across a range while ExoPlaSim's is a single namelist key, so the two cannot be reconciled by matching values -- only by matching the relation, which is what makes this separable from grav-8.
notes:
SETTLED. The relation is Fourteau et al. (2021) Eq. (18), the 263 K row, and it
is ONE DECLARATION: lib/snow.py. Neither compiled model can import a Python
module at runtime, so landmod.f90's landini and soil.cpp's
update_snow_properties each restate the adopted row as a literal and
snow.check_restatements() holds both to that one table, checking the three
coefficients, the normalising ice density the fit was made against, and
landmod's own snowdiff default against the relation at its declared rhosnow.
scripts/smoke_test.py runs it as a check of its own and
biosphere/scripts/snow_thermal_gate.py runs it again on the register side.
analysis/ice_properties.py imports the relation instead of carrying a third
copy.

THE THREE CHECKS, VERIFIED HERE RATHER THAN TAKEN ON REPORT. Riche and
Schneebeli (2013)'s abstract states that of a long-heating needle probe, a
guarded heat flux plate and a direct numerical simulation on identical samples
the simulation is the most reliable, with the needle probe out by -25 to +25 per
cent through anisotropy. Sturm sits below BOTH arms of the bracket at every
density from 156 to 550 kg/m3, and below every one of Fourteau's five
temperature rows. Fourteau's Eq. (18) coefficients were read off the paper
verbatim and its ice density confirmed at 917; the fast arm is above the slow
arm at every density, so the adopted row is the bracket's UPPER endpoint and the
residual is one-signed. That sentence is in the source on both sides, in the
register, and in the audit.

A GENERATED HEADER WAS THE ALTERNATIVE AND WAS REJECTED: the tree already
generates framework/vesper.h for the vegetation model, but landmod.f90 is
committed model source read and edited by hand, so a generated header fixes one
consumer and leaves the other restating, which is two declarations with the
drift moved.

DECLARED DIVERGENCE, FROM THE RELEASE. update_snow_properties arrived
byte-identical to guess_4.1/modules/soil.cpp's apart from the stripped licence
header (checked against the Zenodo 8065737 tarball) and is ON BY DEFAULT under
data/ins/global.ins's iftwolayersoil 0, where Ksnow becomes Ki[] for every
active snow layer of the multilayer solve. Mainline's four lines stand verbatim
beside the changed one in the source; biosphere/config/snow_thermal.yaml is the
register and the gate checks all three halves plus a tree-wide scan for the
superseded coefficients with comments stripped. Eleven fixtures, ten built to be
wrong in a named way.

WHAT IT IS WORTH. The modelled snow conducts 1.50 to 2.30 times better across
275 to 500 kg/m3 (2.30 at 250, the snowdensityconstant override that is off).
At fixed water equivalent the pack's insulating resistance falls to 44 to 67 per
cent of what it was, so the temperature drop across it per unit ground heat flux
falls by the same factor; a 100 mm water equivalent pack at 275 goes from 3.47
to 1.55 m2 K per W/m2 and at 500 from 0.45 to 0.30. The diffusivity rises with
the conductivity, so the pack tracks the simulated air faster. WHICH WAY THE
SIMULATED SOIL TEMPERATURE MOVES IS NOT SETTLED BY THAT: the change couples the
modelled soil more tightly to the air in both directions. Decomposition reads
the soil temperature, so the run is named in the register's comparison_arm and
cannot be made here -- LPJ-GUESS does not build until a baseline climatology
exists, which is also why nothing has consumed the superseded value.

The climate column's numbers are UNCHANGED: landmod's arithmetic is byte-for-
byte what it was and only comments moved. No binary needs rebuilding for this.

Found and not fixed: world-2aij, the same function's Csnow at solid ice's
density rather than the snow's.

title: Glacial ice's heat capacity is computed at liquid water's density, and its conductivity is unsourced
description:
landmod.f90 carries two material constants of the modelled GLACIAL ice, for the ice glaciermod grows and that weights the soil column's thermal properties by dglac. Neither is in the ocean tier's scope, so world-04ok did not reach them. Evidence: notes/audits/cryosphere-material-properties.md, section 'The glacial-ice pair'.

sicecap, the heat capacity per unit volume, factorises exactly as one thousand times the specific heat of ice -- LIQUID WATER's density, not ice's. At glaciermod's own declared rhoglac the product is about a sixth smaller; at pure ice Ih's density about a twentieth smaller.

THIS IS GRAV-8's DEFECT, THIRD INSTANCE. GRAV-8 exposed rhoglac as a namelist key so the gravity bracket could be run, and made snowcap follow rhosnow because a volumetric heat capacity is a density times a specific heat. WORLD-A9S5 made snowdiff follow rhosnow for the same reason. sicecap follows nothing, so a bracket that moves rhoglac moves the ice orography and leaves the thermal mass of the ice behind.

sicediff, the conductivity, stands at the same number as icemod's CKAPI. DO NOT DEDUPLICATE THE TWO: glacial ice is fresh and sea ice is brine-bearing, and their conductivities differ by a term in the ice's salinity over its temperature. What is true is that neither is sourced, and the fresh one is the one a standard CAN settle, because it is a pure substance in the way the sea-ice constants are not.

Do: derive sicecap from rhoglac in landini the way snowcap and snowdiff are derived from rhosnow, using the specific heat of ice Ih at a declared temperature -- analysis/ice_properties.py already computes it from IAPWS-06 over the relevant range. Then source sicediff for FRESH ice and declare it in config/planet.yaml beside surface.cryosphere, stating in the same place why it is not CKAPI. This CHANGES RESULTS wherever dglac is non-zero.
notes:
THE SOURCE FOR sicediff IS NOW HELD, 2026-08-25. The 'Do:' line asks for fresh ice's conductivity from a standard, and IAPWS-06 cannot supply it: a Gibbs function carries density, specific heat and compressibility but no transport property. Yen (1981), CRREL Report 81-10, is what does -- references/yen1981-review-of-thermal-properties-of-snow-ice-and-sea-ice.pdf, read 2026-08-25, its 'Thermal conductivity of ice' section. Eq. (33) fits lambda = a exp(bT) to seven measurement sets over the whole range; Table 3 gives a second arm fitted only above the 150-195 K data gap, and analysis/ice_properties.py evaluates both over the temperature range the modelled ice occupies.

Two things that bear on the value. First, pure ice at the temperatures glacial ice occupies is ABOVE the number sicediff currently carries, by roughly a tenth. Second, that is the right direction for the gap to be in: glacial ice is bubbly, and Yen's Figure 22 shows conductivity falling steeply with air content, so the declaration should be pure ice's reduced for the air fraction glaciermod's rhoglac implies rather than pure ice's outright. That makes sicediff derivable from rhoglac the same way sicecap is, which is the shape this row already wants for the capacity.

Still NOT deduplicable with CKAPI, and Yen sharpens why: his Eq. (71) shows the sea-ice brine term SUBTRACTING from bubbly ice, so the two constants sit on opposite sides of pure ice's value for different reasons and their agreeing today is a coincidence.
close_reason:
Both constants now derive from rhoglac, in glacierprep, where the density is declared -- deriving them in landini would need landmod to use glaciermod, which is a cycle.

sicecap is rhoglac times the IAPWS-06 specific heat of ice Ih at a declared temperature: 1.719635e6, seventeen per cent below the liquid-water-density value it replaces. That was GRAV-8's defect in its third instance, and sicecap now follows rhoglac the way snowcap and snowdiff already follow rhosnow, so a bracket that moves the ice density no longer moves the ice orography and leaves its thermal mass behind.

sicediff is Yen Eq. (33) pure ice reduced by his Eq. (37) Maxwell bubbly factor at an air fraction of 0.0731: 1.961145, 3.4 per cent below the 2.03 it replaces. CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the Eq. (37) factor 0.894266 and the unreduced Eq. (70) 0.896094 agree to 0.2 per cent.

NOT DEDUPLICATED WITH CKAPI, and the reason is now sourced rather than asserted: Yen Eq. (71) subtracts the brine term from exactly this bubbly ice, so the two constants sit on opposite sides of pure ice for different reasons and their agreeing today is a coincidence.

THE LARGER UNCERTAINTY IS THE DECLARED TEMPERATURE, and it is named rather than hidden: over 233.15 K to melting, conductivity moves 1.256 and capacity 1.162, against 1.04 between Yen's two arms. A temperature-dependent pair is a change to the material model and is named, not made.

Nothing moves today: dglac is identically zero in every climatology this world has.

title: Coarsen the ocean's parallel regions: at 36 x 36 x 16 the barriers cost more than the threads buy above four
description:
genie-goldstein's tstepo_flux, co, coshuffle and velc are threaded and bit-for-bit at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 threads. Measured on the shipped worjh2 36 x 36 x 16 case over 100 model years, at a host load of 3.3 to 6.0, the speedup peaks at 1.30 on FOUR threads and falls to 1.09 on sixteen, against the parallelism note's sixteen-thread Amdahl bound of 12.47.

Amdahl is not what stops it and correctness is not what stops it. The evidence is the instruction count, which is load-invariant: the threaded arm retires 0.7 per cent more instructions than the serial one at two threads, 2.1 at four, 5.0 at eight and 11.8 at sixteen. That growth is the OpenMP runtime entering regions, dividing loops and waiting at barriers.

The cause is granularity. tstepo_flux enters one parallel region per ocean timestep and takes a barrier at each of sixteen levels, and the loop it divides is 36 rows. On sixteen threads that is two or three rows of 36 columns between barriers.

Three routes, and they are not exclusive:

1. Measure at 72 x 72 x 16 first, before changing anything. The work between two barriers scales as the cell count and the barrier cost does not, so the recommended grid puts four times the work between the same barriers. This may need no code change at all, and doing it first is what keeps a fix from being fitted to the worst case.
2. Widen the divided loop. Collapsing j and i into one iteration space, or dividing over j only at the outermost level and running k inside each thread where fb allows it, both raise the work per barrier.
3. Take fewer regions. tstepo_flux, co and velc each open and close their own; one region per ocean timestep spanning several routines would open one.

Acceptance is unchanged: analysis/cgenie_omp.py's bit-for-bit test on both shipped regression cases at 1 and 16 threads, plus the omppoison arm. And per the fixed-in-advance rule, the criterion for any change here is stated before it is built: a change is worth keeping if the speedup at the grid it targets rises AND the answer stays bit-for-bit.

Source: notes/audits/cgenie-embm-free-path-and-threading.md section 5b
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-ap7w: the collapse was contention, confirmed by instruction counts reproducing to 0.12 per cent across three campaigns while serial rates are suppressed beside a documented neighbour; the caveat that the host was never quiet travels with every number. world-2lbs: the turnover is four at 36x36 exactly as claimed and EIGHT at 72x72, so the shipped grid was the worst case, decision row 2 fired, and no coarsening was built -- the pre-registered NOWAIT change stands recorded with its trigger unfired, ocn-20's retention pattern.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Measured 2026-08-30, analysis/cgenie_omp.py --cost series under one lock hold; criteria fixed in advance in notes/audits/cgenie-parallelism-and-coupling-support.md section 7a, results 7b-7g.

Route 1 answered the row: at 72x72x16 (the recommended grid) the turnover is EIGHT threads, not four -- speedup 1.63 at eight, falling to 1.28 at sixteen (16.0 s worse than eight against 6.8 s combined scatter). At the shipped 36x36x16 the turnover of four is confirmed (eight worse than four by 1.00 s against 0.81 s combined scatter). Per the pre-registered decision table, NO coarsening of the parallel regions is built: the shipped grid was the worst case and the grid this project would run is past the turnover the row worried about. The 1.63 is a floor: a game process held ~5.7 cores throughout (loads 6-12 recorded beside every repeat); the neighbour can only have cost the team time.

Mechanism sharpened: user-mode instruction overhead at sixteen threads is only +2.3%, against +11.8% kernel-plus-user in the earlier campaign -- the barrier cost is mostly kernel futex sleep/wake under the passive wait policy, and most of the sixteen-thread collapse at the shipped grid is hyperthread-sibling placement (bound one-per-core: 15.38 s vs unbound 20.16 s), not barriers.

Section 7g records a derived-but-unbuilt change: NOWAIT on tstepo_flux's per-level DO is exact under SCHEDULE(STATIC) (the k-dependence rides fb(l,i,j) at the same rows, which static scheduling pins to the same thread at every level) and would remove fifteen of sixteen barriers per step; it stays unbuilt because the pre-registered trigger did not fire -- ocn-20's retention pattern.

title: Thread the ocean routines the first pass left serial, and BIOGEM's column sweep
description:
The first threading pass took genie-goldstein's tstepo_flux, co, coshuffle and velc, which the audit measured at 53.28, 3.31 and 6.20 per cent of retired instructions at 36 x 36 x 16. What is left in the same class and still runs on one thread:

- goldstein.F's own per-cell loops, 3.06 per cent: flux assembly, island superposition and boundary copies.
- jbar, 1.50 per cent: a pressure integral down each column.
- krausturner, called from tstepo inside a do i, do j loop that is already the right shape.
- tstepsic and gold_seaice, 0.56 per cent and the sea-ice driver's own loops.
- BIOGEM's do n=1,n_vocn sweep over vectorised columns. In the shipped BIOGEM regression configuration BIOGEM, ATCHEM and the GEM libraries are 25.06 per cent of the run, larger than anything left in the ocean.

ubarsolv stays serial and that is settled, not deferred: its forward elimination and back substitution both carry a dependence along the band that no recomputation removes, it is 1.83 per cent at the shipped grid, and its share grows only 1.53 per doubling, so it never binds at or below twice muffingen's declared 72 ceiling.

tstipa is NOT on this list. It is EMBM's implicit step, and EMBM is not in the offline recipe.

The acceptance test is the one analysis/cgenie_omp.py already applies: bit-for-bit against the tree at 4038c12e on both shipped regression cases, at 1 and at 16 threads, plus the omppoison arm.

Source: notes/audits/cgenie-parallelism-and-coupling-support.md sections 2c and 3c

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Handed from the world-ap7w/world-2lbs measurement session, 2026-08-30, so this row does not re-derive the plan.

A BIOGEM cache-counter series was built, queued, and then cut at session close-out by the coordinator; nothing was measured. What it would have measured, and the tooling that now exists for it: analysis/cgenie_omp.py grew a --cost-biogem path (the shipped eb_go_gs_ac_bg configuration, 14 tracers at 36x36x8, rewritten only in length -- the same three keys cgenie_cost.biogem_cost rewrites) and a worbe2_36x36x8 --cost-case as the matched physics comparator differing only in the geochemistry. The queued series was: 25y repeat for the startup bound, then 100y x 3 repeats at one thread, for both cases, under one lock hold, ~15 min plus two builds. Its question is world-ap7w's amended residue: BIOGEM retires 5.94 G instructions per second where the physics runs 15-18, measured twice hours apart, so it is a property of the geochemistry; the cache-misses-per-kilo-instruction ratio between the two matched cases says whether that is a miss rate or an IPC property of the code. perf events are wired (instructions,task-clock,cache-misses,cache-references, parsed with the :u qualifier handled).

Inputs this row now has from the measured session (notes/audits/cgenie-parallelism-and-coupling-support.md sections 7a-7g, data in analysis/cgenie_omp.json):
- The scaling turnover is 4 threads at 36x36x16 and 8 at 72x72x16 (1.63x floor at eight, beside a ~5.7-core neighbour), so threading the remaining routines is worth more at the recommended grid than the shipped-grid numbers suggest.
- The barrier cost above the turnover is mostly KERNEL futex sleep/wake under the passive wait policy (user-mode instruction overhead at sixteen threads is +2.3%; the earlier +11.8% was kernel-plus-user), and most of the sixteen-thread collapse at the shipped grid is hyperthread-sibling placement, not barriers (bound one-per-physical-core 15.38 s vs unbound 20.16 s).
- Section 7g derives, and deliberately does not build, the cheapest synchronisation change: NOWAIT on tstepo_flux's per-level OMP DO is exact under SCHEDULE(STATIC) because the level-to-level dependence rides fb(l,i,j) at rows static scheduling pins to the same thread; it removes 15 of 16 barriers per ocean step. Its pre-registered trigger did not fire at the grids measured; if this row's BIOGEM threading raises the value of larger teams, that analysis is the first change to reach for, acceptance unchanged (bit-for-bit on both shipped regression cases at 1 and 16 threads, plus omppoison).

title: Five of the six convergence criteria test a point estimate where one tests an upper bound
description:
The extrapolated offset criterion tests |offset| + half_width < 0.15 K: an UPPER BOUND, so a statistic whose interval reaches the threshold fails. The other five test |x| < threshold: POINT ESTIMATES, so a statistic sitting near the threshold passes or fails on its own scatter at whatever probability that scatter implies.

The asymmetry is defensible as it stands. The offset statistic is an extrapolation -- a fitted slope multiplied by a modelled relaxation time -- so its error is amplified before the comparison, while the other five are direct measurements of the quantity the threshold is in. Four of six using the point form also makes the offset the outlier rather than the rule.

What makes it worth a decision rather than a shrug is that the resolving rows now measure each statistic's error, so the question can be asked quantitatively for the first time: a criterion whose statistic's error is a third of its threshold passes a state sitting exactly on the threshold about half the time, and the project has no statement about whether that is intended.

CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED BEFORE ANY DECISION SO THE DECISION IS NOT TAKEN FROM IT: adopting the upper-bound form for the storage criterion would flip run_ec32946bec89 from pass to fail. Its storage is 0.0961 W/m2 with a standard error of 0.0303, and 0.0961 + 0.0303 = 0.1264 against a 0.12 threshold. That is why this is a row and not a change: a criterion chosen after the run it judges is not a criterion.

Do: decide, on the principle rather than on that number, whether a convergence criterion states a point estimate or an upper bound, and apply one answer to all six. Then re-assess every run under whichever form is chosen.

Evidence: exoplasim/scripts/assess_convergence.py criteria and resolving_power
close_reason: Adopted the upper-bound form for all six criteria: |statistic| + its standard error < threshold, each with its own statistic's error, thresholds unchanged. The argument, including why the change was still honest after runs had been judged under the point-estimate form (nothing canonical has been run, so every run in the tree is disposable), is recorded in assess_convergence.py beside the thresholds and in exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md. Every run whose output is on disk was re-assessed: run_ec32946bec89 moved from pass to fail on the storage criterion, run_14906cb7b914 did not move, run_ade7373b4c90 was re-assessed at the longest window its 28 orbits support. Filed world-bg2i for lib/rungs.py's now-wrong commissioning detail (the ladder is off limits in this worktree) and world-r43f for refreshing the three run manifests from the main checkout.

title: The offset criterion's resolving row prices the fallback statistic even when the fit was used
description:
assess_convergence.py builds the extrapolated_offset row of resolving_power from `_OFFSET_STATISTIC_TERMS * tau_expected * slope_se`, which is the standard error of the FALLBACK statistic: offset = slope * tau_expected, half_width carrying the same product again. When the exponential fit IS usable the statistic tested is a different one -- the fitted asymptote's offset and the fit's own autocorrelation-corrected half width -- and its error is not that product.

On run_ec32946bec89 the fit was used: |offset| + half_width = 0.0670 + 0.0323 = 0.0993 against a 0.15 K allowance, while the row reports a standard error of 0.0573 and resolves = false. So the report says the window cannot resolve a criterion whose statistic on that run has an error of about a third of what the row assumes.

The direction is conservative -- it flags non-resolution that may not be there -- but the row is describing a statistic the run did not use, and a reader cannot tell which case a given row is. It also makes window_orbits_for_offset_criterion (38 orbits on that run, against a derived default of 35) a fallback-only number.

Do: branch the row on whether the fit was used, as the criterion itself does, and price each case from the statistic actually compared with the threshold. NOT to be decided from what it would declare about any existing run: fix the form, keep RESOLVING_FACTOR and OFFSET_TOLERANCE_K where they are.

Evidence: exoplasim/scripts/assess_convergence.py, the resolving rows loop and fit_usable; exoplasim/analysis/convergence/run_ec32946bec89_convergence.json
close_reason: The offset criterion's resolving row now prices the estimator the verdict was taken on. The branch that chooses between the exponential fit and the drift fallback settles the row's standard error and its label in the same place, and the criteria and the resolving rows are generated from ONE table, so a row cannot describe a different statistic than its own criterion. Rows gained statistic_error_source and verdict_interval; the offset row gained statistic_source, repeated as resolving_power.offset_statistic_source, and window_orbits_for_offset_criterion is now labelled as the fallback form's arithmetic. RESOLVING_FACTOR and OFFSET_TOLERANCE_K unchanged. On run_ec32946bec89, the one run where the fit was used, the row moves from resolves false to true.

title: Classify the masked divisions in radmod.f90, the remainder world-d016 left
description:
world-d016 extended lint_masked_domains.py to bare-name divisors, which took the masked-division population from 133 parenthesised sites to 345 across three spellings, and read every one outside radmod.f90. Every non-radmod divisor is now either floored at its site or carries a row in the script's CLASSIFIED table with the argument that says why it cannot vanish.

radmod.f90 was left unread. It was being edited concurrently on another branch, and a CLASSIFIED row is keyed on the argument TEXT: a row written against a version that no longer exists is a claim about nothing, and it would drop out of the table on the next read anyway.

What is left: 102 sites, 45 distinct divisor keys, all in swr and lwr. See them with

    python exoplasim/scripts/lint_masked_domains.py --kind divide

Several are the same shapes world-d016 settled elsewhere -- 1.+ztcon(:) and 1.+0.042*zo3(:)+... are sums of a positive literal and a non-negative term, ra4d-style floors are already in place, and zmu0+zero carries its own floor. Others are not: 1.-zra1s(:)*zrb1s(:,jlev) and 1.-zr1s(:,jlev)*zrl1s(:,jlev) are one minus a product of two reflectances, which vanishes when both reach 1, and 1.-ztau0(:) vanishes at unit transmission. Those need reading rather than pattern matching.

Do: read every reported divisor in radmod.f90 in context, floor the ones whose masked complement can reach zero with a floor argued to be a no-op on the lanes the mask keeps, and add the rest to the CLASSIFIED table. When the count reaches zero, --kind divide can join the gate the way --kind intrinsic already has: change the default kind, or add a second checks row in config/pipeline.yaml that runs it.

Evidence: notes/audits/masked-where-blocks.md.
notes:
Read as one pass, as the description said it had to be: several of the
divisors ARE the indeterminate locals.

VERIFIED POPULATIONS, against the file as it stands after the ztau1/ztau2
band split landed. lint_masked_domains.py --kind divide: 103 sites, 45
distinct divisor keys, not the 102 the description carried -- the split
added one. lint_masked_locals.py: 56, as stated, 53 in swr and 3 in lwr.
Both checked by positive control on the tree before being believed:
dropping the inner ztau2 floor in swr's cloud chain makes exactly one new
division site appear and nothing else move; dropping the zto3t preset
makes exactly zto3t reappear in the locals pass.

FIXED. swr's 53 locals are preset on every lane at the transparent
atmosphere over a black surface -- zero absorber amount, unit
transmissivity, zero reflectivity, zero flux. That settles the masked-local
class and, at the same time, nine of the divisions: on a lane losun
discards every masked quotient now divides by exactly 1, 1.-r*r included.
No stored value moves; on every lane losun keeps, each local is assigned
