title: The export's grid_cell_area and gauss_weights disagree about the same grid
description:
Every ExoPlaSim grid export ships both grid/gauss_weights.bin and grid/grid_cell_area.bin and they describe the same Gaussian grid.

gauss_weights.bin reproduces the Gauss-Legendre construction to about 3e-15 at every rung, so it IS the quadrature the model's global budget is taken over. grid_cell_area.bin, whose manifest entry calls itself 'exact grid geometry' and 'the correct weight for area-averaging any gridded field, exact for both uniform and Gaussian latitudes', differs from those weights by 22 per cent in the POLAR row at every rung -- 21.99 at T21, 22.10 at T42, 22.13 at T85 -- and the polar disagreement does not shrink with resolution. In the interior it does: 0.156 per cent at T21, 0.040 at T42, 0.010 at T85, which is the signature of an O(1/N) construction that agrees in the limit and never at the poles. Both files are uniform along longitude, so this is a row-boundary construction rather than a mesh aggregation.

Measured 2026-08-25 by analysis/ocean_remap.py; the numbers are in analysis/ocean_remap.json under export_area_disagreement, and notes/audits/ocean-grid-crossing.md section 3 has the argument.

Why it matters: a global mean or a global integral taken with grid_cell_area is taken over a different partition of the sphere from the one the spectral model integrates over, so it closes against a grid nobody runs. The effect is concentrated in the two polar rows, which is where an area weight is smallest and therefore where a 22 per cent error is easiest to miss.

Do: enumerate every consumer of grid_cell_area.bin in the tree and say, per consumer, whether it wants the quadrature weight or a geometric cell area; then either correct the exporter (vendor/orogen) or state in source/README.md which of the two files is authoritative for which question. lib/remap.py and analysis/ocean_remap.py already take the weights and say why. Do NOT reconcile them by picking whichever is closer; they answer different questions and one of the two descriptions is wrong.
close_reason: Settled: grid_cell_area was the BINNING partition, not the cell. vendor/orogen/js/geometry.js:latitudeEdges builds row boundaries midway in the SINE of latitude, which is exactly right for rowForLatitude deciding which row a mesh point falls in; gridCellArea reused those edges as cell boundaries. It is therefore a real partition of the sphere that closes to 4 pi R^2 to the last bit, which is why the disagreement survived -- a wrong partition passes every conservation check a right one passes, and section 2's negative control is this same construction missing the known-integral bar by seven orders. It was also 25.0 per cent wide in the polar row of the UNIFORM grid-512x256 export, where the cell boundary is unambiguously midway in latitude, so the manifest's 'exact for both uniform and Gaussian latitudes' was false in both arms. FIXED IN THE GENERATOR rather than by relabelling, because nothing in the tree wants a binning area and four documents were recruiting readers to use it as a weight: geometry.js gains cellSinEdges (Gauss-Legendre intervals on a Gaussian grid, midway in latitude on an equally spaced one), gridCellArea takes them, latitudeEdges is untouched and its docstring now names which of the two questions it answers, and three tests in tools/test-integration.mjs hold the construction to an identity against the weights with the binning partition as a control that must MISS. Documents corrected: FIELD_META for both cell_area and grid_cell_area, the grid block's areaWeighting and latitudeNote, tools/README.md, UPSTREAM-NOTES.md (so a merge cannot collapse the two functions silently), and source/README.md's weighting rule, which now separates all four quantities -- mesh dual area, grid cell area, quadrature weight, and cos(lat), which is none of them. CONSUMERS: one real, pedology/scripts/thermostat_efficiency.py, which read grid_cell_area from planet.nc; it now goes through the new lib/gridding.py:export_grid, which constructs the boundaries from the manifest and never reads the field, so it is right on both sides of the change. WHAT IT WAS WORTH, measured rather than assumed, on precarve-craton's planet.nc: both polar rows are entirely land, and the endorheic land-area fraction moves 0.143 per cent at T21 and 0.010 at T42, global land fraction 0.163 and 0.052, land-mean elevation 0.104 and 0.040 -- diluted by the polar rows' 0.70 to 0.045 per cent area share and by nothing else, so a polar-restricted diagnostic takes the full 22 per cent. FOUND ON THE WAY AND FIXED: pedology/scripts/weathering_fluxes.py:grid_cell_area_km2 carried a THIRD construction, midway in latitude, 5.79 per cent wide at the pole and not converging, feeding absolute silica, CO2 and (via phosphorus_budget.py) phosphorus fluxes where nothing damps it; it now takes lib/gridding.py:gaussian_grid and guards the axis. PER RULE 7 this makes a FIELD worthless and no build: terrain is untouched so no export is superseded, but every export on disk carries the old partition in grid/grid_cell_area.bin and in planet.nc's grid_cell_area, and pedology's absolute per-cell products with it. Nothing under source/ was edited. cos(lat) as an area weight is a fourth quantity at about 30 sites, measured at 1.81 per cent polar and about 1e-4 on real global means, and is filed as world-clbj. Evidence in notes/audits/ocean-grid-crossing.md section 3.

title: tswr1, tswr2 and tswr3 are the analytic fits Stephens et al. (1984) withdrew
description:
Found reading Stephens, Ackerman and Smith (1984) for world-jimc.

radmod's swr names 'Stephens (1978) + Stephens et al. (1984)' as the source of its cloud transmissivities. The 1984 paper exists to correct the 1978 one, and its correction is precisely the part radmod does not take.

p. 687, on the 1978 analytic formulas for the scheme's single-scattering albedo and backscatter fractions: 'Unfortunately, these formulas contained errors and better results are obtained when the parameter values are taken directly from the tables provided.' Its Table 1(a) replaces the single-scattering albedo table and smooths beta1 and beta2. The replacement is almost entirely at low sun, and the 1978 table was not even monotone in mu0: 1 - omega at tau_N = 1 goes from 0.0173 to 0.0017 between the two at mu0 = 0.1, a factor of ten; at tau_N = 10 it goes 0.0028 to 0.0002; at tau_N = 100, 0.0012 to 0.0000. The revision removes near-infrared cloud absorption at grazing incidence.

radmod.f90:2447-2449 carries analytic fits of the withdrawn shape instead:

  zb1  = tswr1*SQRT(zmu0)                                  tswr1 = 0.077
  zb2  = tswr2*SQRT(zmu0)/ALOG(3.+0.1*ztau)                tswr2 = 0.065
  zom0 = 1 - tswr3*zmu0*zmu0*LOG(1000/ztau)                tswr3 = 0.0055

all three with the mu0 dependence the 1984 tables are monotone against, and tswr3 is the one this project already re-weights through model.cloud_absorption_scale. The 1984 revision touches NOTHING in the tau(W) relation: it restates Eqs. (1)-(3) unchanged and never reprints (10a) or (10b), so this is independent of world-jgen and the two can be settled separately.

TWO MORE STATED LIMITS OF THE SCHEME, recorded here so they are not re-derived. Stephens (1978) p. 2127 on the cloud-over-reflecting-surface correction: 'care must be observed when (12) is applied for larger surface albedos', with the tabulated error growing sharply above a = 0.75, which is every snow and sea-ice cell. And p. 2132: 'The parameterization is less effective at lower solar elevations', which at 32 degrees of obliquity is a larger share of the year here than on Earth. The second is what the 1984 revision addresses, so it retires only if the 1984 tables are adopted.

Do: decide whether to table-interpolate the 1984 omega, beta1 and beta2 rather than evaluate the withdrawn analytic forms. Tabulation is 12 optical depths by 10 zenith cosines and is not a scheme change; what it costs is a bilinear lookup per layer per band on the radiation step, against three evaluations of SQRT and LOG it replaces. Cost that before deciding. If it is adopted, cloud_absorption_scale needs re-deriving against the tabulated omega rather than against tswr3, because it scales a coefficient that would no longer exist.

Evidence: exoplasim/notes/cloud-water-reference.md, section 'The Stephens fit, read'; references/stephens1984-shortwave-parameterization-revised-to-improve-cloud-absorption.pdf [step: rebuild_binaries]
notes:
PREMISE IS WRONG AS STATED, and the corrected finding is larger than the one it
replaces.

WHAT THE 1984 PAPER WITHDREW. Stephens et al. (1984) p. 687, read from the scan:
"these formulas contained errors and better results are obtained when the
parameter values are taken directly from the tables provided". The formulas are
Stephens (1978) Eqs. (11a) and (11b), p. 2125: surface polynomials in
x = ln(tau_N) and y = mu0 whose coefficients are that paper's Table 1. radmod
evaluates nothing of that shape. tswr1*sqrt(mu0),
tswr2*sqrt(mu0)/ln(3+0.1*tau) and 1 - tswr3*mu0^2*ln(1000/tau) are three
one-coefficient fits of PlaSim's own, and radmod's comments call them tunings.
So they are NOT the withdrawn formulas and the withdrawal does not reach them.

WHAT IS TRUE. 1984 Table 1(a) replaces the 1978 single-scattering albedo table
at 99 of 108 entries and is monotone in mu0 where the 1978 table was not
(1 - omega at tau_N = 1, mu0 = 0.1: 0.0173 -> 0.0017). Tables 1(b) and 1(c) are
the 1978 backscatter tables with TWO points altered in each, matching the
paper's own "only a couple of points in each table" (p. 689) -- so beta1 and
beta2 are essentially unrevised, and the issue's "smooths beta1 and beta2" is
technically right but immaterial.

QUANTIFIED, and this is the finding. exoplasim/scripts/stephens_tables_vs_fits.py
carries both papers' tables, asserts those alteration counts and the 1984
monotonicity so a slipped digit fails the script, and compares the fits with the
tables at the optical depths this model's layers reach (from world-jgen's
bracket artifact):

  beta2 from the fit is about HALF the tabulated value over tau_N 10 to 200
  the fitted co-albedo is about TWICE the tabulated one at high sun
  beta1 is within about 20 per cent over the same range

Both band-2 errors push the same way, so tabulated cloud reflects far more in
the near infrared: band-2 cloud reflectance would rise by up to 0.22. On the
same cover and insolation as world-jgen's bracket, over a black surface so it is
a magnitude upper bound, that is -6.6 to -27.4 W/m2 and -5.4 to -22.3 K, cooling.
Artifact: exoplasim/analysis/stephens_tables_vs_fits.json, 2026-08-25.

SO THE 'Do:' LINE IS MIS-FRAMED. Table interpolation is not "not a scheme
change". It is a different shortwave cloud scheme worth tens of W/m2, it would
strand cloud_absorption_scale (which scales a coefficient the tables do not
have), and the cost that matters is not the bilinear lookup -- which is two
clamped searches and four multiply-adds per layer per band against three
transcendentals it removes, so it is not the obstacle.

OPEN, and the question is the user's:

  Does this model's shortwave keep PlaSim's tuned cloud coefficients, or adopt
  Stephens's tuned tables and re-derive the balance around them?

It cannot be answered before world-jgen's T21 pair runs, because that pair is
what says whether the inherited tswr1 is still where it should be, and tswr1 was
tuned against the optical depth world-jgen corrects. No code change made here.

DECIDED BY THE USER AND IMPLEMENTED, 2026-08-25. Adopt the tables and re-derive
the balance around them. The reasoning is the standard rather than the result:
a tuned value is a number someone picked with an opaque process, and that is
not an acceptable provenance for anything in this tree. A sourced value that
DISAGREES with the tuned one is the expected outcome.

WHAT swr READS NOW. Stephens et al. (1984) Tables 1(a), 1(b) and 1(c),
bilinearly interpolated in (tau_N, mu0) as p. 689 prescribes, in both the
direct and the diffuse stream, beta1 at the range-1 optical depth and beta2 and
the co-albedo at the range-2 one. tswr1, tswr2 and tswr3 are gone from the
module, from radmod_nl, from the broadcasts and from the threadprivate list.
The tables are module parameters and the lookup is one pure interpolator behind
three elemental wrappers, so the where constructs in swr are unchanged in shape.

THE EDGES. Both axes clamped, and the clamp argued at the tables rather than
assumed. Past tau_N 500 unreachable: swr caps the layer water path at
1000 g m-2 and Eqs. (10a)/(10b) put that at tau_N 138 and 146, where tau_N 500
needs about 14000. Below tau_N 1 it binds routinely, since the thinnest layers
sit near 0.03, and it is inert: the clamp holds beta and the co-albedo, not the
reflectance, which goes to zero with tau in both bands whatever beta is. Below
mu0 0.1 it holds the last tabulated column, which is exactly the column the
1984 revision corrected; extrapolating past it would put back the shape the
revision removed. Stephens (1978) p. 2132 and Stephens et al. (1984) p. 690 are
the papers own statements of where the scheme stops.

THE CO-ALBEDO FLOOR. Table 1(a) reaches exactly zero at grazing incidence on a
thick layer and the two-stream u-factor divides by the co-albedo. Floored at
SQRT(EPSILON(1.0)), the threshold and the argument the aerosol optics in the
same routine already use. At the floor the two-stream reflectance reproduces
Stephens Eq. (1) to 1.4e-5 over every optical depth and beam cosine this model
reaches, against a bar of 1e-4 declared before it was measured.

cloud_absorption_scale IS NOT STRANDED AND ITS VALUE DID NOT CHANGE.
cloud_band_weight.py derives it as <1-omega0>_star / <1-omega0>_sun from liquid
water k(lambda) through Mie, never mentioning tswr3; Stephens tables carry the
same solar range-2 flux weighting in that denominator. It now arrives on a new
radmod_nl key CLOUDABS, default 1.0 (the Sun), multiplying the interpolated
co-albedo in both streams. check_consistency compares it against
cloud_band_weight.json and that row is untouched.

CHECKS THAT CAN FAIL, in smoke_test. stephens_tables_vs_fits.py reads radmod
324 table entries back against its own transcription of both papers, including
the (mu0, tau) transpose, and checks the conservative floor against Eq. (1).
Verified to fail on a deliberately slipped digit.

THE BALANCE, like for like with cloud_absorption_scale applied to both sides
because that is what the model does: -25.4 to -6.5 W/m2 and -20.6 to -5.3 K,
cooling, on the same cover and insolation as world-jgen bracket and over a
black surface with all the cover on one layer, so a magnitude upper bound. To
offset it the design flux ratio would move by +0.026 to +0.102 from 0.945.
config/planet.yaml now says so at baseline_flux_earth, which was already
PROVISIONAL. derive_design_flux.py cannot be re-run until a commissioning pair
exists on the current source.

THE RUN THAT SETTLES IT, and it is not run here: one T21 commissioning pair on
the current model source, control against arm, same executable, same config
hash, same geography hash. It settles world-jgen at the same time, because both
changes are in the source together.

Verified with exoplasim/scripts/verify_model_compiles.py; smoke_test 41/41;
check_consistency unchanged at 3 failures and 10 warnings, the same three the
base commit had (surface inputs, runs vs staged surface fields, cycle
capability, all about absent binaries and regenerated surface files). No binary
built and nothing run.
close_reason: Stephens et al. (1984) Tables 1(a)-(c) adopted in swr, bilinearly interpolated in both streams; tswr1, tswr2 and tswr3 deleted. cloud_absorption_scale survives unchanged in value on a new key CLOUDABS multiplying the tabulated co-albedo. Edges clamped and argued; co-albedo floored at SQRT(EPSILON(1.0)) and checked against Stephens Eq. (1). The port is checked against both papers in smoke_test. Balance moves -25.4 to -6.5 W/m2 and -20.6 to -5.3 K, offset by a flux ratio of +0.026 to +0.102; the design flux is declared to move and one T21 commissioning pair settles it and world-jgen together.

title: radmod's cloud optical depth is Stephens Eq. (10b) used for both shortwave bands
description:
Found reading Stephens (1978) for world-jimc, against the paper rather than radmod's header.

WHAT THE PAPER GIVES. Stephens (1978) p. 2124 fits TWO broadband optical depths by least squares to Mie calculations on eight standard cloud models, one per spectral region, split at 0.75 um:

  log10(tau_N1) = 0.2633 + 1.7095 ln(log10 W)   0.3 to 0.75 um, Eq. (10a)
  log10(tau_N2) = 0.3492 + 1.6518 ln(log10 W)   0.75 to 4.0 um, Eq. (10b)

W in g m-2. Both are the code's form: 10^(a + b ln x) is 10^a x^(b ln 10), so (10a) is prefactor 1.8336 exponent 3.9363 and (10b) is 2.2346 and 3.8034.

WHAT radmod DOES. radmod.f90:2433, one ztau for both bands:

  ztau(:) = 2.0 * ALOG10(1.5+max(0.,zlwp(:)))**3.9

2.0 and 3.9 is Eq. (10b) to within 3 per cent at every path above 20 g m-2, and radmod splits its two shortwave bands at 0.75 um, exactly where (10a) gives way to (10b). So band 2 gets its own equation and band 1 gets band 2's. Eqs. (1)-(3) built on tau are ported verbatim as zrcl1, zrcl2 and ztcl2; the defect is in tau alone.

IT IS ONE-SIGNED. (10b) is above (10a) everywhere, so band-1 cloud is too optically thick: ztau over Eq. (10a) is 1.05 at 1000 g m-2, 1.08 at 90, 1.19 at 20, 1.87 at 5.4. Through zrcl1 at mu0 = 0.5 that is band-1 cloud reflectance high by 0.012 to 0.025 over the paths this model's low cloud layers carry, and by more above them. The model reflects too much visible from cloud and therefore runs cold.

THE +1.5 IS THE SAME LINE AND THE SAME ARM. Stephens's form is singular at W = 1 g m-2 and undefined below it; the offset is a domain guard and radmod's comment says so. But it also returns a non-zero optical depth where the paper's is going to zero, and this model's top three layers live there: at 2.15 g m-2 the fork's band-1 reflectance is 8.6 times Eq. (10a)'s, at 3 g m-2 it is 3.7 times, and the two agree to 30 per cent only above about 10 g m-2. The guard is right to exist; below 1 g m-2 it should return zero optical depth rather than 0.11.

WHAT IT IS WORTH, as a bracket and not a measurement. Band 1 carries 0.3824 of this star's flux through the model's own split against 0.517 for the Sun, so the port error costs less here than on Earth. A reflectance excess of 0.012 to 0.04 over a cloud fraction of 0.4 to 0.7 is 0.6 to 3.4 W m-2 of extra reflected shortwave at the top of the atmosphere, which through lib/sensitivity.py at a planetary albedo of 0.25 to 0.35 is 0.5 to 3.1 K, cold. That chain has no cloud fraction field, no overlap and no surface in it and all three reduce it, so it leans high.

Do: a T21 pair on a settled baseline, control against an arm in which band 1 takes Eq. (10a), band 2 takes Eq. (10b), and the domain guard returns zero optical depth below 1 g m-2 instead of the offset. HOLD tswr1 at its inherited value in that arm: it was tuned against the optical depth being corrected, and an arm that moves both reports nothing about either. A correct tau that worsens an agreement at the inherited tuning is information about tswr1.

NOT DONE IN THE BATCH THAT FOUND IT: the machine claim forbade a rebuild and a run, and a numeric change to the shortwave that cannot be run is worse than the finding written down.

Evidence: exoplasim/notes/cloud-water-reference.md, section 'The Stephens fit, read'; references/stephens1978-radiation-profiles-in-extended-water-clouds-ii-parameterization-schemes.pdf [step: rebuild_binaries]
notes:
VERIFIED AGAINST THE PAPER, then FIXED.

Premise confirmed. Stephens (1978) p. 2124 read from the scan: Eq. (10a)
log10(tau_N1) = 0.2633 + 1.7095 ln(log10 W) for 0.3 to 0.75 um, Eq. (10b)
0.3492 + 1.6518 ln(log10 W) for 0.75 to 4.0 um. radmod's zsolar1/zsolar2 split
at 0.75 um (radmod.f90:372-373), and zrcl1 is Eq. (1), the conservative solution
the paper reserves for the band below 0.75 um. The single ztau tracked (10b)
within 3 per cent from 20 to 10000 g/m2 and ran 4 to 19 per cent above (10a)
over the same range. One-signed, band 1 too bright.

its own prefactor and exponent, cited. tswr1, tswr2, tswr3 and clwref untouched.

THE DOMAIN GUARD WAS NOT CARRIED ACROSS AND NOT REPLACED BY ZERO EITHER. The
issue's arm proposed zero optical depth below 1 g/m2. That still leaves the
1 to 10 g/m2 window on an extrapolated fit whose implied effective radius,
through Stephens Eq. (7), is 134 um at 2.15 g/m2. Below 10 g/m2 -- the bottom of
Figs. 1a and 1b -- each band is now continued LINEARLY in the water path,
matching its own fitted value at 10, which is Eq. (7) at the effective radius
the fit implies there: 8.2 um band 1, 6.7 um band 2. Continuous, zero at zero
water, no new constant. THE ARM DEFINITION IN THE 'Do:' LINE IS THEREFORE
SUPERSEDED; run the arm as it now stands in the tree.

CONSEQUENCE: the correction is not one-signed everywhere. Over the seven layers
carrying real cloud water (7 to 90 g/m2) band-1 cloud gets less bright, a
warming; in the top three (under 2.5 g/m2) it gets brighter, because the linear
continuation returns more optical depth than the +1.5 offset did. The second is
much the smaller.

BRACKET, replacing the hand chain: +0.9 to +2.1 W/m2 at the top of the
atmosphere, +0.7 to +1.7 K, WARMING. exoplasim/scripts/cloud_optical_depth_bracket.py,
artifact exoplasim/analysis/cloud_optical_depth_bracket.json, measured 2026-08-25
on the bootstrap climatology of run_2b20e3324bb0. Carries the model's own layer
water paths, its own total cloud cover with random overlap, its own zenith
geometry over the day, and band-1 surface albedo through Stephens Eq. (12);
its band-1 incident flux agrees with the climatology's rst+rsut to better than
1e-4. Leans high: no band-1 gas absorption or Rayleigh, no interlayer multiple
reflection. Width is the spread over where in the column the cover sits, which
is not written out.

NOT DONE: the run. T21 pair on a settled baseline, control against the arm now
in the tree, tswr1 HELD at 0.077. Machine claim forbids running it here.
Verified with exoplasim/scripts/verify_model_compiles.py; not compiled to a
binary and not run.

SUPERSEDED IN TWO PLACES BY world-f9ig, 2026-08-25.

1. THE HELD-tswr1 RUN CANNOT BE RUN. world-f9ig deleted tswr1, tswr2 and tswr3
and put Stephens et al. (1984) Tables 1(a)-(c) in swr in their place. There is
no coefficient left to hold. The band-1 backscatter is now interpolated from
Table 1(b) at the layer own range-1 optical depth, which removes the reason
the hold existed: the control and the arm no longer share a coefficient that
was tuned against the quantity being corrected.

2. THE ARTIFACT IS WORTHLESS, not stale.
exoplasim/analysis/cloud_optical_depth_bracket.json d_reflectance columns and
the +0.9 to +2.1 W/m2 bracket above were computed with beta1 = tswr1 sqrt(mu0).
cloud_optical_depth_bracket.py now interpolates Table 1(b) instead, and the
artifact has not been regenerated because it needs a climatology and none is
declared. The LAYER OPTICAL DEPTHS in it are unaffected and are what
stephens_tables_vs_fits.py consumes.

WHAT SETTLES BOTH IS NOW ONE T21 PAIR, not two. Both changes are in the model
source together, so a control on the pre-world-jgen tau relation and the fits
against an arm on the current source measures the pair; separating them needs a
third arm and nothing requires that separation.
close_reason:
Band 1 was evaluating Stephens Eq. (10b) and now evaluates Eq. (10a), with band 2 keeping (10b) and each fit continued linearly below 10 g/m2 to its own fitted value there.

THE ARTIFACT WAS WORTHLESS RATHER THAN STALE and that was the outstanding half: cloud_optical_depth_bracket.json's d_reflectance columns were computed with beta1 = tswr1*sqrt(mu0), the analytic fit world-f9ig deleted. Regenerated on the current source: +0.73 to +2.00 W/m2, +0.59 to +1.63 K, WARMING, with a geometry check that can fail -- the chain's band-1 incident flux reproduces the climatology's own rst + rsut to better than 1e-4.

TWO OF THIS ROW'S OWN INSTRUCTIONS ARE SUPERSEDED and the tree now says so where the definition lives. The domain guard is a linear continuation below 10 g/m2 rather than returning zero optical depth below 1 g/m2. And the hold on tswr1 is lifted, because no such coefficient exists any more -- so the control and the arm no longer share a coefficient that was tuned against the quantity being corrected, which was the whole reason for the hold.

THE CORRECTION IS NOT ONE-SIGNED, against this row's claim. The seven layers carrying real cloud water get less bright and the top three get brighter; the second is much the smaller, which is why the net is warming.

The narrowing is the field's. Cover is 0.578 against the bootstrap's 0.61 and planetary albedo 0.314 against 0.270: less cloud is less of this correction, and a brighter surface returns more of what the cloud lets through through Stephens Eq. (12). Both act from above, and the lower end barely moves because the uniform arm sets it. The geometry check holds on the new field at 3.8e-5 relative.

world-f9ig's companion bracket moved with it, since stephens_tables_vs_fits.py reads this artifact's layer optical depths, cover, insolation and albedo: -23.37 to -7.22 W/m2, -15.98 to -4.94 K. +18.43 W/m2 measured is still inside it and the -12.3 K drift is still inside its kelvin.

What settles this row is unchanged: the T21 pair, which now has a baseline to branch from.

title: h2o_sw_level_bracket's high end is 0.0005 below its own derivation
description:
world-o3t1 gave h2o_sw_level a generator that derives it, exoplasim/scripts/shortwave_band_weights.py --level, writing exoplasim/analysis/h2o_sw_level.json. The VALUE reproduces: the derivation gives 1.162547 and config carries 1.163, inside the half-unit-in-the-last-place the config's own three decimals allow, so check_consistency.py now holds it.

THE BRACKET DOES NOT, at one end. The derivation gives 1.129283 and 1.206523; config carries [1.129, 1.206]. The low end is fine. The high end is 0.000523 away, past the 0.0005 half-ulp bound by 2.3e-5, because 1.2065 was truncated rather than rounded when it was retyped. So no bracket row was added to check_consistency.py's rows list -- adding one today would fail on that last digit.

WHY IT WAS NOT JUST FIXED: the batch that found it was told not to change any model.* key, because a T21 reconvergence was in flight. The fix is one character in config/planet.yaml.

SIZE OF THE EFFECT, so nobody mistakes this for a physics finding: 0.001 of this key is 0.01 K of mean surface temperature by exoplasim/notes/corrk-cross-check.md's own 0.10 K per 0.01, against a bracket half-width of 0.038 and 0.38 K. It is a retyping defect, not a measurement one, and it matters only because the check that would catch the NEXT retyping cannot be armed on the bracket while it stands.

Do: set model.h2o_sw_level_bracket to [1.129, 1.207] when a config change is safe, then add the bracket row to the rows list in scripts/check_consistency.py's 'derived radiation scalings match their artifacts' block, reading exoplasim/analysis/h2o_sw_level.json at ('bracket', 1) and ('bracket', 0). The row helper walks tuple keys of dict names only, so an index step needs the walk extended or the artifact needs bracket_low/bracket_high scalar nodes; the latter is smaller.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
THE TRUNCATION IS GONE AND NO CONFIG VALUE CHANGED. Checked against the artifact rather than this row: fce6645c8 repointed CORRK_PATH_CM at the baseline climatology, which moved CORRK_RATIO_TO_EQ21 from 1.127592 to 1.126163, and the generator rewrote exoplasim/analysis/h2o_sw_level.json at value 1.1610740529999999 and bracket [1.1278522445, 1.20499441]. Config carries 1.161 and [1.128, 1.205]. The distances are 7.4e-5, 1.5e-4 and 5.6e-6 against the 5e-4 the third decimal allows, so all three round-trip and 1.207 is not the number to write -- 1.2065 was the OLD derivation's high end.

THE CHECK IS ARMED, which was the half that could not be done while the high end stood. It needed neither a walk extension nor bracket_low/bracket_high nodes: the row helper already compares a list leaf element by element, which is how model.vegetation_albedo_bracket is held, so the row is ('bracket',) on the same artifact the value's row reads. check_consistency now compares 15 keys where it compared 14, and 'derived config values match their artifacts' passes with h2o_sw_level_bracket in the list. A bracket is two numbers and either can go stale alone; both are now held.

ONE THING THE ROW DID NOT COVER. The comment block above the key restated the values as prose -- 12.7 per cent, a level of 1.163, a bracket of 1.129 to 1.206 -- and fce6645c8 moved all three without it. That is the same retyping route this row is about, one file earlier: a second copy of a declared value with nothing holding the two together. The bracket restatement is deleted rather than corrected, since the keys are two lines below it; the argument that needed a number, that the continuum is why the level is not the no-continuum floor, keeps it and now reads 1.126. Committed separately from the check so it can be ordered at merge, since a long LPJ-GUESS run may hash config/planet.yaml.

SIZE, restated so nobody reads this as physics: no value moved at all. This was a check being armed.

title: A config key removed by a refactor makes every in-flight run unresumable, and the guard cannot tell that from a setting changing
description:
continue_exoplasim.py's config_drift check refuses to resume when config/planet.yaml differs from a run's manifest. That is CLIM-17's protection and it is right. What it cannot distinguish is a key whose REMOVAL cannot change what the model integrated.

Observed today, killing a running commissioning. WORLD-F997 moved the ladder's three timestep quantities into lib/rungs.py and removed model.resolution_timestep_minutes from config, which was a TABLE nothing reads at run time -- grep finds no reader in exoplasim/scripts or lib, and model.timestep_minutes, the key that actually sets the step, was untouched at 45.0. A T21 development run at 28 orbits then refused every continuation with: model.resolution_timestep_minutes: {...} -> None. The run had to be restarted from cold.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE RUN. This project runs many agents against one config while a commissioning is in flight, and a commissioning is about seventy orbits at T21 and far longer up the ladder. Any agent removing or renaming a config key -- even a pure refactor with no behavioural content -- kills every run in progress. Today that cost nineteen minutes. At T85, where the escalation ends, an orbit is 492 s and the same event costs most of a day.

Do: decide whether the guard can safely distinguish a key that no run-time code reads from one that does, and if it can, say what evidence establishes 'no reader' well enough to resume on -- a grep is not it, and the AST gate world-sf6b built for unbound names is the shape of an instrument that could answer it. If it cannot be made safe, the alternative is procedural and should be recorded instead: config is frozen while a commissioning is in flight, and a key change waits.

Note the asymmetry that makes this worth solving rather than living with: a FALSE resume integrates a run under a configuration nobody declared, which is CLIM-17's failure and is silent. A false REFUSAL costs a restart and is loud. So any relaxation has to be provably one-directional. Evidence: exoplasim/scripts/continue_exoplasim.py config_drift, config/planet.yaml, world-f997, run_ade7373b4c90
close_reason:
FIXED. The guard is not loosened and there is no flag; what is added is a way to declare a REMOVAL in advance so the guard can distinguish it from a value change.

lib/provenance.py:REMOVED_CONFIG_KEYS takes the shape of the fork's mainline_divergences files, which is the precedent that has held: the values the key held are recorded verbatim beside the removal, and the gate checks BOTH halves -- the key must be gone from config/planet.yaml, and the artifact's recorded value must be one the declaration names. A run whose manifest holds any other value had the key's VALUE move under it before the key went; that is real drift and is still refused. An undeclared removal is still drift. An ADDED key is still drift, because an added key can be read; the tool for a declarative addition is the consumer's inert set. A rename is therefore half declarable and half refused, which is correct while the new name is read.

Making the declaration is deliberate and recorded: it cannot be written without reading what the config held, it carries the issue that removed the key, the paths the meaning moved to and a written argument for why the removal cannot change what a run integrated, and it lives in git rather than on a command line.

removal_problems() is the honesty check and check_consistency runs it as a row of its own, not only under --self-test. It fails on a declaration the tree no longer bears out: the key back in the config, a moved_to path that is not there, or the key's name appearing in any Python source outside where it moved. That last is the answer to 'what evidence establishes no reader' and it is stated for what it is -- a TEXTUAL trace with the same blind spot SURFACE_UNREAD_MODEL_KEYS records, which is why the written argument is the other half and is not optional. The AST route was not needed to close this: the mechanical half only has to keep the declaration honest, not to establish the claim on its own.

A resume that rests on a declaration prints it. Six self-test cases with their controls; 25 cases 0 failed. Verified against run_ade7373b4c90, whose manifest holds the removed table: the removal applies and the run's real drift, model.timestep_minutes 45.0 -> 30.0, is still refused.

The procedural alternative (freeze config while a commissioning is in flight) is not adopted for removals and is not needed for them. It remains the only answer for a key whose value changes, which is what the guard exists to catch.

docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md class 35 carries the argument.

title: Build the grid-to-grid conservative remap the ocean crossing needs, and check it against a known integral
description:
lib/gridding.py owns MESH-to-grid reduction by field semantics. The atmosphere-to-ocean crossing OCN-10 specifies is GRID-to-grid, and no operator for it exists.

It is cheaper than it looks and it has an exact answer. ExoPlaSim's grid is uniform in longitude with Gaussian latitudes; GOLDSTEIN's igrid = 0 is uniform in longitude and uniform in the SINE of latitude, and initialise_goldstein.F:496 makes every ocean cell's area exactly equal. Neither grid's cell boundaries depend on the other coordinate, so the overlap area factorises into a longitude overlap times a sine-of-latitude overlap: two one-dimensional sparse matrices, exact in floating point, no polygon intersection, and the planetary radius cancels because every weight is a ratio of areas.

Do, and each is a rule the contract states rather than a choice the call makes:
- Normalisation by field semantics. Intersection over DESTINATION area for an extensive total; intersection over COVERED area for a rate or a density, which is what net heat flux, freshwater flux and wind stress take. A field of ones must remap to ones under the second.
- Carry the coverage fraction with the result. A discarded fraction is a conservation identity that can no longer be evaluated.
- An unmapped destination cell is an ERROR, not a nearest-neighbour backfill. lib/gridding.py:243-254 currently backfills and returns the count; for this crossing an ocean cell with no atmosphere-ocean area over it is a mask disagreement, not sparse coverage.
- Register the closure residual in advance and stamp it in the artifact: sum(F_src*A_src*frac_src) against sum(F_dst*A_dst). references/esmf/ holds itself to about 1e-9 relative on analytic fields, which is the shape of a check that can FAIL.
- State where a flux over an atmosphere-ocean cell that is land in the ocean grid GOES, and the converse. The masks come from the same Orogen mesh at different resolutions and cannot agree at the coast; the residual is a coastline-shaped field, not noise. references/climber-x/src/geo/coast_cells.f90 solves the same problem for river discharge and the answer here has to cover heat and salt too.

The other direction is a separate operator: sea surface temperature, the ice state and the exported surface velocity are intensive states, so the crossing is an interpolation with nothing to conserve, and routing an extensive quantity through it is the error the two words in lib/gridding.py exist to prevent.

Source: notes/audits/cgenie-parallelism-and-coupling-support.md section 5, notes/external-model-survey.md section 55
notes:
2026-08-25, built in fanout-AC. notes/audits/ocean-grid-crossing.md carries the measurements; analysis/ocean_remap.json carries every check with its tolerance.

WHAT EXISTS. lib/gridding.py gains grids as CELL BOUNDARIES (GridSpec, gaussian_grid, goldstein_grid, gaussian_latitudes, require_gaussian_rows) because that module already owns the column expression and smoke_test's check_one_grid_convention forbids a second file deriving one. lib/remap.py is the operator. analysis/ocean_remap.py builds it, checks it and writes analysis/ocean_remap.json and analysis/ocean_remap_weights.npz; it is registered as the 'ocean_remap' step in config/pipeline.yaml and lib/remap.py is in CLAUDE.md's lib list.

EVERY RULE THE ISSUE STATED IS IMPLEMENTED. Normalisation by field semantics: three semantics (extensive_total, flux_density, intensive) over the two normalisations, required and closed, no default. Coverage travels with every result. An unmapped destination cell raises rather than backfilling. The closure residual is registered in advance (lib/remap.py:CLOSURE_TOLERANCE = 1e-12 relative, from the float64 round-off floor and three orders tighter than the ESMF precedent's 1e-9) and stamped in the artifact. A source cell with no valid destination under it goes to the nearest valid destination cell in the CONSERVING matrix only and the ledger reports how much area moved and how far; an intensive state there is dropped and counted, because there is nothing to conserve.

MEASURED, seventeen checks, none failed. Conservation 4.6e-18 relative at T21 against 36 x 36 and 5.8e-18 at T85 against 72 x 72. The known integral (3*sin(lat)^2 - 1, analytically zero, returned exactly by Gauss-Legendre) comes back at 2.6e-15 on the source and 2.7e-15 across the crossing. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL FIRES: midpoint-between-nodes row boundaries return 4.0e-3, seven orders above the bar, so the bar discriminates. A grid crossed with itself is the identity to 2.1e-16 under all three semantics; rotating the ocean's phi0 by one column rolls the answer to 2.7e-17.

THE COAST, measured against the export's own surface_class with the ocean wet mask standing in as the remapped ocean fraction cut at a half: T21 to 36 x 36 orphans 12 source cells, 0.567 per cent of the sphere, furthest move 12.4 degrees; T42 to 36 x 36, 168 cells, 2.086 per cent, 10.3 degrees; T85 to 72 x 72, 465 cells, 1.344 per cent, 9.8 degrees. Conservation is exact across all of them because the rule names where the flux goes.

FOUND ON THE WAY, filed as world-yolx: the export ships grid/gauss_weights.bin and grid/grid_cell_area.bin describing the same grid and they disagree by 22 per cent in the polar row at every rung, without converging there. The crossing takes the weights, because the model's budget is a quadrature.

NOT DONE, and deliberately: the other direction. Sea surface temperature, ice state and exported surface velocity are intensive states with nothing to conserve, and lib/remap.py will carry an intensive field either way, but what it does coarse-to-fine is piecewise-constant. Whether that is what the next climate run should be forced with is section 5e of the coupling audit and belongs with OCN-10.
close_reason: Built. lib/gridding.py carries the grid constructors, lib/remap.py the separable conservative operator, analysis/ocean_remap.py the acceptance test against an integral with an analytic answer, registered as the ocean_remap step. Seventeen checks pass at tolerances fixed in advance and three orders tighter than the ESMF precedent; the midpoint negative control misses the bar by seven orders, so the test discriminates. Every rule the issue stated is implemented, including the coast rule and the refusal to backfill an unmapped destination cell. The reverse direction is OCN-10's, not this row's.

title: The storage criterion has no resolving row, and its threshold is the one a short window cannot see
description:
exoplasim/scripts/assess_convergence.py reports resolving_power.rows for five criteria: the four slopes and the extrapolated offset. The sixth criterion, abs_state_storage_lt_0.12_w_m2, has no row, so every verdict says what its window can resolve for five of the six thresholds it applied and is silent about the one whose threshold was derived most recently.

It is not a formality. 0.12 W/m2 corresponds to about 0.0094 K per orbit of mixed-layer drift, and at the T21 baseline's stationary scatter the standard error of a fitted temperature slope does not fall to a third of that until roughly thirty orbits. The criterion's own derivation already notes the estimator resolves about 0.11 W/m2 on a 10-orbit block, which is its own threshold. Do: add the storage row to resolving_power, computed from the storage estimator's own error rather than from the temperature slope proxy, so the report says whether the criterion discriminated or flipped. Evidence: exoplasim/scripts/assess_convergence.py, the STORAGE_TOLERANCE_W_M2 derivation comment
notes:
FIXED, and the answer is that the criterion IS a criterion at the window now derived and was a formality at the one it was written against.

The estimator is the least-squares slope of the planetary heat content divided by the orbit, so its error is the standard error of that slope in the same units, with the same residual-memory correction the other slopes carry. close_state_energy returns the series it fitted so nothing re-sums it; assess_convergence adds the abs_state_storage row, the storage residual's own scatter, tau and lag-1, and window_orbits_for_storage_criterion. A raise fires if the rows ever stop covering the criteria.

MEASURED 2026-08-25 on run_ec32946bec89's 35-orbit window: scatter 1.09e7 J/m2, lag-1 0.798, tau 6.70 (from inside the window, so a floor). Standard error 0.0303 W/m2, three times it 0.091 against 0.12, so it RESOLVES. Required window 28.8 orbits, 15.3 if orbits were independent, 31.8 at tau 9. It does not bind the window: the offset criterion needs about 38 on the same run. At the 10-orbit window used before the window was derived the standard error was 0.197 W/m2, LARGER than the threshold itself.

THRESHOLD UNCHANGED. What is corrected is the prose of its derivation: the measurability half compared a run's 10-orbit and 20-orbit storage estimates, which are NESTED blocks, not an independent pair and not a scatter, and 0.11 was not the estimator's standard error on either. The threshold rests on the temperature bound (0.118, rounded to 0.12) alone, which was fixed before any of this was read, and at the window now in use the measurable floor is 0.090 and no longer binds.

Also measured on run_14906cb7b914: storage standard error 0.0289 W/m2, resolves.

Arithmetic in exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md. Related: world-s8n3 asks whether this criterion should test a point estimate or an upper bound, and records that the upper-bound form would flip run_ec32946bec89.
close_reason: The storage criterion has its resolving row, computed from the storage estimator's own slope error in W/m2 rather than a temperature proxy, plus the window it needs. It resolves at the 35-orbit window (0.030 W/m2 standard error against a 0.12 threshold, needing at least 29 orbits) and did not at the 10-orbit window (0.197 W/m2, larger than its own threshold). Threshold unchanged at 0.12; the measurability half of its derivation was corrected because it compared nested blocks. Commit eeff1400.

title: The derived relaxation time is argued to be a ceiling and has never been checked against a fitted one
description:
The reconvergence criterion in exoplasim/scripts/assess_convergence.py fits the post-conversion decay at the relaxation time the slab and the run's own radiative damping imply, and holding that time FIXED is what makes the test cheap. It is conservative only while the derived time is a CEILING on the true relaxation, and that is currently an argument rather than a measurement: the damping is an equilibrium response and a transient sees a stronger one, the heat capacity is a full ocean mixed-layer column applied to a planet with land, and the reservoirs that lengthen it are under a tenth of that column. The argument is in exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md.

Every convergence report already records relaxation_orbits_fitted beside relaxation_orbits_expected, so the comparison accumulates and nobody has taken it. Do: on every run that has both and whose fit is usable, compare the two, and say whether the derived value bounds the fitted one. If it does not, the criterion needs a bracket over the relaxation time and the record length it needs grows; exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md carries what that costs. Evidence: exoplasim/scripts/assess_convergence.py, exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md, world-hduy
notes:
CHECK TAKEN. exoplasim/scripts/check_relaxation_ceiling.py states the rule and applies it to every convergence artifact; config/pipeline.yaml carries it as step relaxation_ceiling.

THE RULE. An artifact is EVIDENCE only when the exponential fit was USED rather than the drift fallback (identifiable from the artifact: the fallback sets temperature_remaining_offset_k exactly equal to remaining_offset_implied_by_drift_k), and the fitted tau is identifiable from its own series -- finite, positive, and no longer than the span fitted. The ceiling is FALSIFIED by an excess larger than the fit's own standard error on tau, and by any excess where no such error is recorded; the unbracketed case counts against the ceiling deliberately, because the criterion's conservatism rests on the claim and a possible violation that cannot be dismissed is not a pass.

MEASURED 2026-08-26, eight artifacts. Three evidence, one falsifies, none discriminates.
 8044646ea7f0  13.68 vs 9.883  FALSIFIES by 3.80, unbracketed
 ade7373b4c90   6.92 vs 10.142 holds, unbracketed
 ec32946bec89   6.27 vs 10.120 holds
 14906cb7b914  44018 vs 10.099 not evidence: fallback taken AND fit degenerate (world-5gqy)
 2b20e3324bb0, 78c22fb1a1bd, aaa95662e21a: fallback taken
 4182235e9781: tau 34.8 over 26 orbits fitted

VERDICT: the ceiling does not survive as stated and is not refuted either. The one artifact above the derived time is 38 per cent above with no error on its fit; its derived 9.8833 is also the pre-correction value built from an uncited density and specific heat. The two below are below by about the same margin the one above is above, which is a scatter and not a bound. assess_convergence now records relaxation_orbits_fitted_standard_error, and on the one run that carries it the error is 3.75 orbits against a 3.85-orbit gap, so a single run barely separates the two.

CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this stays actionable: the fallback's remaining offset should be read as an estimate rather than the bound its comment claims. lib/run_lengths.py already brackets the relaxation time by the fitted evidence (6.27 to 13.68) rather than taking the derived value, so nothing new depends on the ceiling. What would settle it is more runs whose approach the fit can grip; the check accumulates and a settled run adds nothing. Evidence in exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md.
close_reason: Check written, stated as a rule that can fail, and run on every convergence artifact: exoplasim/scripts/check_relaxation_ceiling.py, pipeline step relaxation_ceiling. Three of eight are evidence; run_8044646ea7f0 fits 13.68 against a derived 9.883 and falsifies the ceiling, two hold by a similar margin, and none discriminates. So the ceiling argument does not survive as stated and is not refuted. lib/run_lengths.py consequently brackets the relaxation time by the fitted evidence rather than the derived value. Commits dce547f4, 937804cd, e73f1f4a.

title: Re-cut the wetness partition against the periodic lake cycle
description:
world-9iy5 built the crossing: surface_water.py:paint_lake_cycle paints each time bin's lake area onto regions, and surface_water.nc now carries lake_cycle_bins_wet, lake_cycle_fraction and lake_cycle_decided per region. The quantity WET-2's seasonal_inundation class needs exists at the support it needs.

WHAT IS LEFT IS THE PARTITION, and it is a decision rather than an implementation. hydrography/config/wetness.yaml's three resolved classes are cut against the ANNUAL solve: open_water is surface_water.nc:lake, the equilibrium paint; playa is what that paint leaves exposed inside the depression footprint; dry_mineral is the residual. The cycle cuts the same ground differently -- a region under water in every bin is permanent open water, one under water in some bins is seasonal inundation, one never under water inside the footprint is playa -- and the two cuts overlap in the strandline, because the annual equilibrium area sits between the cycle's trough and its peak.

So adding seasonal_inundation means deciding WHICH SOLVE DECIDES OPEN WATER. Taking it from the cycle makes open_water the always-wet set and is the coherent reading, but it changes a class wetness.yaml says surface_water.py alone decides, and it narrows playa to the floor that is exposed all year, which pedology/scripts/build_surface_classes.py also means by the word. Keeping open_water on the annual paint leaves seasonal_inundation defined as a remainder against a different solve, which is the double count assign_exclusive exists to refuse.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the two paints measured against each other. How much area is wet in the annual paint and not in every bin, how much is wet in some bin and not in the annual paint, and whether the disagreement is the strandline or something larger. Neither paint exists on disk -- config/planet.yaml carries baseline_climatology: null and hydrography/data/<build>/ has no surface_water.nc -- so this is blocked behind a declared baseline climatology and one surface_water run, cost: minutes.

Do: once surface_water.nc exists, measure the two paints against each other, choose the cut, and state it in wetness.yaml per class. Then build_wetness.py:classify_regions gains one mask and assign_exclusive enforces the rest. Its header already says the crossing exists and the partition does not.

Discovered from world-9iy5.
notes:
2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER, from a pass over the needs-decision set.
RECLASSIFIED, not a standing question: it is settled during the pipeline run, when the two paints exist and can be measured against each other.

title: A commissioning run is still specified without the span its own error bar needs
description:
world-wdsk settled the rule: a production span of about twenty times tau after the approach is where a window mean's interval actually covers, and batch length rather than batch count is what has to be bought first. exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md carries the measurement.

Nothing consumes that rule when a run is LAUNCHED. assess_convergence.py reports the window its criteria would need, which tells you after the fact that the run you already paid for is too short; compare_equilibria.py returns INDETERMINATE, which tells you the same thing about a comparison. Both are refusals after the wall clock is spent. The specification side has no equivalent: the orbit count for a commissioning run is still chosen by hand, and the 40-orbit precision arm that reversed sign when it was re-run at 85 is what that costs.

Do: decide where the orbit count for a commissioning run is declared, and have it derive from the approach length plus about twenty tau rather than being typed. Two things make this awkward and both need a decision rather than a guess:

- Tau is not measured and cannot be measured here (world-wdsk: fixing it needs of order a thousand orbits at equilibrium). So the declared span has to carry a tau ASSUMPTION, stated and cited, and the honest form is a bracket rather than a number.
- The approach length is operational experience with no artifact behind it, about 70 orbits at T21 from cold and 10 to 20 on reconversion, and it moves with the rung. Whatever consumes it has to follow the resolution ladder the way assess_convergence's window now does.

The alternative worth pricing first, per the working agreement about asking whether a thing should exist: do not declare a span at all, run until the instrument stops refusing, and checkpoint often enough that the extra orbits are cheap. That may be strictly better than any assumed tau and it should be ruled in or out before the derivation above is built.
notes:
SETTLED, and the alternative was priced first as the working agreement asks.

THE ALTERNATIVE IS RULED OUT, not on preference: declaring nothing and running until the instrument stops refusing would be strictly better if the refusal were the same bar. It is not. The convergence window is sized so the offset criterion's slope error resolves its threshold, about 38 orbits on run_ec32946bec89, while the production span a window mean's interval needs is 84 orbits at the OPTIMISTIC end of the memory-time bracket. The instruments therefore stop refusing tens of orbits before the climatology's interval is bought, so a refusal can only decide whether to buy MORE. Both are kept.

WHERE IT IS DECLARED: lib/run_lengths.py, machine-readable, in the pattern lib/rungs.py:ESCALATION_ROUTE already sets. docs/src/pipeline/sequencing.md section A decides it and carries the argument; config/pipeline.yaml gates bootstrap_run and baseline_run on it; exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md carries the arithmetic.

THE TAU ASSUMPTION IS STATED AND BRACKETED, not guessed: commissioning length = approach + 20 * tau_memory, with tau_memory 4.2 to 10.43 (the AR(1) at the measured lag-1 of 0.615, and the fast-plus-slow mixture the slower branch is stood up with). At T21 from cold the approach of about 70 gives 154 to 279 orbits, and the DECLARED length is the floor.

THE APPROACH LENGTH IS AN ARGUMENT rather than a constant, so a caller has to state which approach it means; it stays operational experience with no artifact behind it and it moves with the rung. It is deliberately not put in lib/rungs.py: the resolution ladder is being worked on main and per-rung approach lengths above T21 have never been measured. That measurement is the remaining gap.

TWO TAUS KEPT APART, which is the substance of the module: the MEMORY time prices a mean's interval and the RELAXATION time prices a decay, and a span derived for one was being spent on the other.
close_reason: The orbit count for a commissioning run is declared in lib/run_lengths.py and derived: approach plus twenty times the memory time, bracketed 154 to 279 orbits at T21 from cold, with the declared length the floor. sequencing.md section A decides it and pipeline.yaml's bootstrap_run and baseline_run gates cite it. The alternative of running until the instrument stops refusing was priced and ruled out: the convergence window is sized for the offset criterion's slope error, about 38 orbits, against a production span of at least 84, so the refusal is a weaker bar and can only decide whether to buy more. Commit e73f1f4a.

title: Two T42 ladder arms were deleted without an archive identity, so what they were is unrecoverable
description:
archive/ exists so that the IDENTITY of a run survives the deletion of its payload, and CLAUDE.md's layout says so: 'archive/ Identity of things whose payload has been deleted. Tracked.' Two runs escaped it.

MEASURED 2026-08-25. run_1d39fef9bfc2 and run_42aaf441b10b are the two arms of the T42 ladder comparison that notes/audits/resolution-ladder.md draws its conclusion from, and world-yyx8 is blocked on them. Neither is:

- in exoplasim/runs/ (three run directories are on disk)
- in exoplasim/runs/INDEX.json (nine runs)
- a stub under archive/runs/ (57 entries)
- listed in archive/runs/_bulk_2026-08-24/INDEX_AT_DELETION.json

So there is no record of their configuration, their executable sha, their source_build, or how many orbits they carried. The only surviving trace is exoplasim/analysis/ladder/run_1d39fef9bfc2__vs__run_42aaf441b10b.json, which carries per-metric summary statistics and the two window index ranges and nothing else.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE TWO RUNS. Run ids are UUIDs and carry no meaning, so INDEX.json and archive/ are the only things that say what a run was (CLAUDE.md rule 6). A deletion path that bypasses both turns a run id into a dead string, and an audit that cites one becomes uncheckable. The resolution-ladder audit is in that position now.

Do: find the deletion path that removed these two without writing a stub or an INDEX_AT_DELETION entry, and close it so a run cannot leave the tree without leaving its identity. Then decide whether the resolution-ladder audit's rows can still be cited given that neither arm can be identified, let alone re-measured. Whether to re-run the two arms is world-yyx8 and is a separate question from whether the deletion path is sound.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 THE ROW'S DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG, AND THE SWEEP FOUND A THIRD RUN.

The row says to "find the deletion path that removed these two without writing
a stub". There is no such path. Neither run was EVER in exoplasim/runs/
INDEX.json: checked across the last 60 revisions of that file, and
`git log -S` over all history returns nothing for either id in INDEX.json or
under archive/. They were never registered, not registered and then lost.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT. exoplasim/scripts/index_runs.py BUILDS INDEX.json by
SCANNING exoplasim/runs/. The identity lives in a run manifest inside the run
directory, which is untracked and is deleted with the payload. So INDEX.json
records what EXISTS, not what has existed, and a run created and deleted
between two scans leaves nothing tracked at all. archive/runs/README.md says an
INDEX_ENTRY.json is "that run's row from INDEX.json at the time it was
archived", so archiving inherits the same gap: it can only preserve a row that
was captured while the payload was on disk.

CLAUDE.md rule 6 says INDEX.json "is the only record of what each run was". It
can only be that if a run is registered at CREATION. run_exoplasim.py writes a
manifest and does not touch INDEX.json.

A THIRD RUN, not named in the row: run_900548ae632e, T42 at dt 45, blew_up at
46 orbits. exoplasim/notes/route-step-criteria.md:110 marks it "no, and no
stub" beside run_1d39fef9bfc2 on line 111, and lib/rungs.py already carries a
`record_gone` field for both. So the project had partially recorded this and
had not filed the mechanism.

RECONSTRUCTED WHAT SURVIVES. The row says the ladder comparison json is the
only trace. It is not; there are six, and between them they carry more than the
row assumes, including two NAMELISTS. archive/runs/run_1d39fef9bfc2/,
run_42aaf441b10b/ and run_900548ae632e/ now hold RECONSTRUCTED.json each --
named differently from INDEX_ENTRY.json on purpose, because they are not copies
of a real index row and must not be mistaken for one. Each cites the artifact
every field came from and lists what is unrecoverable rather than omitting it.

AND THE RECONSTRUCTION FALSIFIED AN AUDIT. See the comment on world-yyx8: the
two ladder arms differ in NFILTEREXP, 16 against 8, and notes/audits/
resolution-ladder.md said they differ only in where they start.

STILL TO DO, and it is the actual repair: register a run in INDEX.json at
creation so the index is an append-only ledger rather than a directory
listing. That is a change to run_exoplasim.py and index_runs.py and is not
made here -- exoplasim/scripts is held by another change in flight.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 CLOSED. The mechanism is repaired and the epistemic state is on the
record.

THE REPAIR, which is what the row's "Do" asked for. exoplasim/runs/INDEX.json is
now a LEDGER of every run that has existed. Two halves, both needed:

  register at creation   run_exoplasim.py calls index_runs.register the moment
                         the manifest is written -- before a single orbit -- and
                         again when the block ends however it ends, including on
                         a blow-up, which is the run least likely to be
                         reindexed by hand and which lib/rungs.py reads as a
                         ladder verdict. continue_exoplasim.py re-registers
                         after each segment. Never fatal: it warns with the
                         command to run by hand, because a bookkeeping error
                         must not cost a model run.
  merge, never replace   a rescan updates the rows it can see and KEEPS every
                         row it cannot. A vanished directory keeps its last
                         known row untouched -- orbit count, executable sha,
                         config sha, source build, climatologies, none of it
                         re-derivable -- and gains payload_present false, the
                         date first noticed, and whether an archive/runs/ stub
                         holds its extracted products. Keyed by directory, since
                         a crashed preparation legitimately shares a run id.
                         Atomic and under flock: two arms of a pair are two
                         processes writing one record.

scripts/smoke_test.py:check_run_index_is_a_ledger refuses the regression on an
identity: a merge against a scan that sees nothing must return every row it was
given with its identity fields untouched, and a scan that DOES see a run must
still win for that run's live fields, so a ledger that ignored the scan fails
the same gate. Verified to fail when merge is replaced by a listing.

scripts/archive_runs.py partitions only rows that still have a payload, and no
longer rewrites archive/runs/README.md -- a tracked document about three record
shapes, only one of which that script knows about, which it reverted on every
pass. scripts/pipeline.py's post-purge message no longer says a reindex is
needed to stop the index describing a tree that has moved; it says the reindex
is safe because it keeps rows.

THE SWEEP: FORTY, not two. `python exoplasim/scripts/index_runs.py --recordless`
writes archive/runs/RECORDLESS.json, every run id the tree cites that no record
can identify. Forty, thirty-three of them cited by a document. Generated rather
than listed, so it shrinks by itself as identity is recovered.

WHAT THIS DOES TO notes/audits/resolution-ladder.md, which the row asked to be
decided. Four of the ten runs it cites are recordless, and the answer differs by
row, so the note now carries a table splitting its conclusions by whether they
can be re-read:

  the criterion flickers, window 20 removes it   data yes (85 annual records in
                                                 run_8044646ea7f0's convergence
                                                 report), provenance no
  the hyperdiffusion defect is worth 3.0 K       yes, both asymptotes survive
  the step moves the equilibrium more than the   NO -- run_4fe5e6050df5's
    rung does                                    294.567 K has no surviving
                                                 artifact at all
  the controlled T42 pair, and the ice finding   yes, in full: three runs in the
                                                 ledger with payloads on disk

So the audit's LOAD-BEARING conclusion is the fully checkable one. What rests on
runs nobody can identify is the convergence-criterion timing, which survives as
data without its provenance, and the -1.300 K resolution step, which does not
survive at all and is now labelled as evidence that cannot be checked. The
timestep step, 1.591 K on two re-readable endpoints, alone carries the ladder's
operative constraint that rungs compared at different steps report truncation
error as resolution sensitivity.

The note also now names its estimator: the 3.0 K reads temperature_asymptote_k
where the timestep table reads temperature_mean_k, and using two without saying
so invited the numbers to be compared.

notes/audits/run-identity.md is the finding. Filed: world-gck6 (re-measure the
T42 endpoint), world-qc1k (seventeen other documents cite recordless runs and do
not say so, with the three-disposition procedure), world-bot7 (maps/ frames use
the same UUID-plus-scanned-index pattern). Correction comment added to
world-yyx8: its refutation stands, but the attribution of the old 2.5 W/m2 to
the filter exponent rests on one surviving analysis file.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS: the forty. Registration prevents the next one and recovers
none of them, and most cannot be recovered.

title: Declare the aeolian deposition MASS artifacts as the ANUT-7 carriers
description:
The carrier world-hfsm asked for now exists. Two artifacts, both mass and only mass, both declared as writes of their existing steps in config/pipeline.yaml:

  aeolian/analysis/sea_salt_deposition.nc  and  .json
  aeolian/analysis/volcanic_sulfate_deposition.nc  and  .json

Each carries wet and dry removal per size bin in kg m-2 s-1, a field per element (deposition_Ca, deposition_Mg, deposition_K, deposition_S, deposition_Na, deposition_Cl, deposition_Sr, deposition_Br, deposition_F for sea salt; deposition_S for sulfate), and land and ocean means in mg per m2 per Earth year in the JSON. Each netCDF variable carries element_mass_fraction_of_dry_aerosol as an attribute.

Do, in biosphere/config/abiotic_nutrients.yaml, which this batch deliberately did not touch because biosphere belongs to another owner:

  screen.candidates.marine_aerosol.carrier: aeolian/analysis/sea_salt_deposition.nc
  screen.candidates.volcanic_sulfate_deposition.carrier: aeolian/analysis/volcanic_sulfate_deposition.nc

and replace each carrier_note, which currently says only what the carrier is NOT.

Why these are separate files rather than variables in sea_salt_baseline.nc and volcanic_sulfate.nc, and why that must not be 'simplified' later: screen.forbidden_carriers names aeolian/analysis/volcanic_sulfate.nc and aeolian/analysis/sea_salt_optics.json BY PATH, and abiotic_nutrient_ledger.py:check_screen refuses any candidate whose carrier string contains one of them. Those files hold optical depth. A carrier file has to hold mass and nothing else, or the gate is right to refuse it.

Phosphorus is deliberately absent from the sea-salt element list, matching the config's existing excluded_elements: [P] and its reason.

The magnitude anchor cannot be read yet. aeolian/config/sea_salt.yaml carries Chadwick et al. (1999)'s 600 +/- 400 mg Ca per m2 per Earth year and build_sea_salt.py prints the land mean against it, but a real comparison needs a declared baseline_climatology; a bootstrap-climatology exercise of the machinery put the land mean well below the band, which is the expected direction because Chadwick's site is a small wet tropical island and this is a global land mean.

Source: world-hfsm, biosphere/notes/abiotic-nutrient-ledger.md ANUT-7 register
close_reason: Resolved and committed (672d7c5e6, 8f2fdac69, and this). world-5wl5: the carriers were already emitted and declared as writes; the screen names them by path, with the partition and extensiveness identities checked where the arithmetic is. world-v5j1: the floor is a reporting cap applied to model state in Earth years -- implicit-Earth, not opaque, the chain terminating in a restatement -- and removing it breaks nothing because zero was already reachable and the one division was already guarded. world-h3qg: the execution claim is per entry with arms that must be claimed, so a thirteenth divergence is a finding rather than an inherited true.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text: batch:4 verification pass, producer side. Confirmed against source and graph rather than the README: both carrier pairs are real writes of their steps (config/pipeline.yaml sea_salt and volcanic_sulfate rows list the deposition .nc/.json), the writer is aeolian/scripts/aerosol_deposition.py, nc units kg m-2 s-1 per bin wet/dry plus a field per element with element_mass_fraction_of_dry_aerosol attributes, JSON land/ocean means area-weighted in mg per m2 per Earth year. No new artifact is needed; the declaration is the whole fix. The land means were already cos(lat)-weighted, so the world-vwqw unweighted-mean sweep did not touch the carriers; neither carrier has ever been generated in this tree, so nothing existing is invalidated. Added this pass: build_volcanic_sulfate.py now runs the same wet/dry partition identity build_sea_salt.py runs (the scale height is spelled twice there and the mass residual cannot see one spelling moving), and aerosol_deposition.py --self-test gained check 4: the written file's area integral reproduces the input's, bins and elements partition the total, the integral is invariant under an area-weighted change of support, and the unweighted aggregation is shown to move it by 1.8e-2 so the check is seen to fail. A static smoke_test check (carrier JSON reproduces its own element split) is drafted and exercised on fixtures but smoke_test.py is contested this batch; the code is with the batch coordinator. REMAINING, and it is the whole of this row's Do: the two carrier lines and carrier_notes in biosphere/config/abiotic_nutrients.yaml, which belongs to the biosphere owner. Stale and deliberately left: dust_baseline.json/.nc and dust_intensity_levers.json (commit e39de02e9 records why); regenerating them queues behind the held host lock and this row does not need them.

title: The material properties of the modelled sea ice and its snow are Earth's and no configuration can reach them
description:
Six constants of the adopted ocean tier are compile-time `parameter`s in icemod.f90 and each is an Earth measurement standing where nothing says it was chosen for this world. They are what exoplasim/scripts/ocean_tier_gate.py --strict refuses on, together with the namelist keys that are reachable but still carry an unsourced Earth number.

  CRHOI   density of ice; the mass of a metre of modelled ice everywhere, and with CRHOS the snow-ice flooding threshold as the DIFFERENCE
  CPI     specific heat of ice; the heat capacity of the skin-temperature layer through zrcpl = xmind*CRHOI*CPI
  CPSN    specific heat of snow
  CKAPI   heat conductivity in ice
  CKAPSN  heat conductivity in snow
  CLFSN   heat of fusion of snow

THE CONDUCTIVITY PAIR IS THE SHARPEST. CKAPI and CKAPSN set the conductive flux through the modelled ice and the insulation the snow on it provides, which is what fixes the equilibrium thickness at a given surface energy balance -- and scripts/error_budget.py already carries 'sea ice does not move' with the peer that runs this configuration reporting EXCESSIVE ice. A second one-signed term in the same direction, unreachable from any configuration, is not something to leave undeclared beside the first.

Do, in the order the audit's own preconditions take: DECLARE what the modelled sea ice and its snow are made of, in config/planet.yaml beside ocean.sea_ice_fusion_j_kg, which is the one property of this set that was already declared and is the precedent for the shape. Then EXPOSE the six as icemod_nl keys at their current values and write them from run_exoplasim.py the way TFREEZE, CRHOS, CPS, CLFI, XMAXD and HLEAD already are, so a bracket arm can move them. Expose and declare; do not change a number, and say so in the commit.

Not all six need a Vesper value. Some may be correctly Earth's because the modelled substance is the same water; the point is that the declaration says which, and that nothing is inherited by default. The gate's --strict arm is where the residue is visible and where it goes empty.

Evidence: notes/audits/ocean-tier-implicit-earth.md section A3, and exoplasim/config/ocean_tier.yaml for the six declarations and what each one bites.
close_reason: All six settled and there are no compile_time constants left in the ocean tier declaration; --strict's residue is down from 14 to 8, and the 8 are other rows' namelist keys. CRHOI, CPI, CKAPI: value UNCHANGED, now icemod_nl keys written from config/planet.yaml surface.cryosphere, DECLARED for the reason CLFI already was -- each is a function of a brine volume the model does not carry. CLFSN: DERIVED from IAPWS-06 and changed by 0.08 per cent; snow has no brine so it is the one derivable member. CPSN: DELETED, it was read nowhere in the vendored tree and exposing it would have put an inert key in icemod_nl. CKAPSN: HANDED from landmod's snowdiff through iceini, see world-a9s5. Gravity checked and CANCELS: parts per million on the density under a column far thicker than the model carries. analysis/ice_properties.py implements IAPWS-06 and reproduces the release's own check table to 7e-10 before reporting. notes/audits/cryosphere-material-properties.md. Not measured in kelvin; no binary built, no run made. Beside these, landmod's glacial-ice sicecap/sicediff were found unsourced and filed as world-fg8w.

title: close_state_energy.py copies TMELT out of icemod.f90, which no longer declares it
description:
exoplasim/scripts/close_state_energy.py:80 carries `TMELT = 273.16  # icemod.f90: freezing point` as a module literal and uses it at :152 to weight the sea-ice part of the modelled surface heat content. This is the exact failure class lib/sea_water.py exists to prevent: four analysis scripts once carried CRHOS and CPS as literals attributed to oceanmod.f90, which did not own them, and every slab heat capacity built from the copies was 4.75 per cent too large with nothing failing.

Two things are now wrong with this one rather than one. The attribution is stale: world-xdmj removed icemod.f90's `parameter(TMELT=273.16)` because pumamod's tmelt is a planet_nl key and icemod's compile-time copy split from it silently, so icemod now TAKES the melting point through iceini and the line the comment points at is gone. And the comment calls it a freezing point, which is a different quantity in this model: TFREEZE is the sea-water freezing point at the declared salinity and is one of lib/sea_water.py's four, while tmelt is the melting point of the modelled water and is planet_nl's.

Do: read it from the model rather than copying it. tmelt does not belong in lib/sea_water.py -- that module is the four numbers SALINITY reaches the model through, and this is not one of them -- so either extend that module with a separate planet-water accessor or add one beside it, and say in its docstring which of the two quantities it is. Then check the rest of exoplasim/scripts and analysis/ for the same literal: exoplasim/scripts/verify_land_column_reduction.f90:277 declares its own `real, parameter :: TMELT = 273.16` but that is a standalone Fortran probe with no access to the model's modules, so it is a different case and may be a correct one.

Evidence: notes/audits/ocean-tier-implicit-earth.md section A1.
notes:
FIXED. lib/sea_water.py gains melting_point(run_dir), documented as a FIFTH number explicitly apart from the four salinity numbers: the run's own planet_namelist first, p_earth.f90's planet_ini assignment second, SystemExit if neither states it. The owner is pumamod through planet_nl, which is what exoplasim/config/ocean_tier.yaml's melting_point handoff already declares; icemod's 'real :: tmelt = 273.16' is the receiver it overwrites from ptmelt at iceini, so the comment pointing at icemod was pointing at a copy.

close_state_energy.py threads it into heat_content beside CRHOS and CPS and records it as planet_water in the report. BEHAVIOUR PRESERVED: run_ec32946bec89 sets no TMELT, p_earth assigns 273.16, so every storage number is bit-identical and no convergence verdict moves.

SWEEP: the only other copied model constant of this kind in exoplasim/scripts and analysis/ was this one. analysis/spatial_reduction_gap.py already READS tmelt with ra1/ra2/ra4 from p_earth.f90 rather than copying, so it is not the same class. verify_land_column_reduction.f90:277's parameter TMELT is a self-contained synthetic fixture whose residual bound is internal, and is a correct case as the issue anticipated. vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/pyburn.py:237 carries _TMELT = 273.16 attributed to plasimmod.f90; that is inside the vendored model and untouched here.

smoke_test check 'the state closure's melting point follows the run' fails on a re-added module literal, on a run override being ignored, and on the accessor returning anything within a kelvin of TFREEZE.
close_reason: Routed through lib/sea_water.py:melting_point(run_dir), read from the run's planet_namelist or p_earth.f90's planet_ini assignment and raising if neither states it. The quantity is named correctly as the melting point rather than a freezing point, and kept explicitly apart from TFREEZE in the module docstring. No number changed: 273.16 both ways on the run on disk. Commit eb9c88b3.

title: Re-take the cGENIE wall clock on a quiet host, and separate the throughput collapse from contention
description: OCN-3's cost is measured in retired instructions, which are load-invariant, and that number does not need re-taking. Two things do. (1) The seconds a reader has to wait were all taken at host loads of 8 to 27 while a sibling integrated on sixteen threads; every wall fit in analysis/cgenie_cost.json is labelled with its load and marked contaminated. Re-take with scripts/machine.py --claim held, using analysis/cgenie_cost.py --reuse-builds --repeats 3, which rebuilds nothing. (2) MORE IMPORTANTLY, instructions per second sit between 15.6 and 18.3 G/s for every 36 x 36 class case and at about 6 G/s for BOTH large-state configurations measured -- 72 x 72 x 16 physics, and 36 x 36 x 8 with fourteen BIOGEM tracers. Those two are different in kind and were measured at different times, which argues for a working-set-versus-cache effect rather than a shared load, but it is an inference. If it is real, wall clock grows FASTER than instructions under refinement and the measured r^4 is a LOWER bound: a doubling would cost nearer 50 times than 18, and the T85-matched extrapolation moves with it. perf stat with a cache-miss count on a quiet host settles it. Source: notes/audits/cgenie-build-cost-and-grid-ceiling.md sections 4b and 4c
notes:
AMENDED 2026-08-25, and part 2 is PARTLY SETTLED before this row was worked. Re-measuring the same seven cases hours later at lower load put 72 x 72 x 16 at 15.5 G instructions per second, in the middle of the 11.4 to 18.3 band every other physics case occupies. The 6.3 seen earlier was the contended window, not the state leaving cache, so r^4 in instructions IS r^4 in seconds for the physics and the T85 extrapolation does not move. What survives is narrower and is about the BIOGEOCHEMISTRY: the BIOGEM case retires 5.94 G instructions per second, measured twice hours apart at 5.96 and 5.94, which is a property of the geochemistry rather than of the host.
