That makes ocean biogeochemistry 2.68 times the physics in instructions and about 5.4 times in seconds, and it is the ratio a spin-up should be planned on. A cache-miss count would say why.

THE THREADED SPEEDUP IS NOW ALSO WAITING ON THIS ROW, 2026-08-25. genie-goldstein's tstepo_flux, co, coshuffle and velc are threaded and reproduce the tree at 4038c12e bit-for-bit at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 threads, so what is left is what it BUYS. That is a wall-clock quantity and it could not be taken: the host ran at a one-minute load average between 85 and 112 on 32 logical cores throughout, so a sixteen-thread arm would have been measuring the queue. The instruction counts taken in the same window are unaffected and are in analysis/cgenie_omp.json, because a single-threaded process retires the same instructions whatever else is running.

The command, with scripts/machine.py --claim held: python analysis/cgenie_omp.py --cost --arm omp --threads 1 --threads 2 --threads 4 --threads 8 --threads 16 --years 100. It builds once and runs the worjh2 36 x 36 x 16 case at 100 model years per thread count, which is the arm the parallelism note's shares are for. Read wall_seconds, not instructions: OMP_WAIT_POLICY is passive so a waiting thread does not spin, but retired instructions still are not a cost on a threaded process.

What to hold it against: the parallelism note's sixteen-thread Amdahl bound of 12.47 for the physics and 9.42 for the BIOGEM configuration, both of which assume everything parallel is threaded, where four routines are.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-ap7w: the collapse was contention, confirmed by instruction counts reproducing to 0.12 per cent across three campaigns while serial rates are suppressed beside a documented neighbour; the caveat that the host was never quiet travels with every number. world-2lbs: the turnover is four at 36x36 exactly as claimed and EIGHT at 72x72, so the shipped grid was the worst case, decision row 2 fired, and no coarsening was built -- the pre-registered NOWAIT change stands recorded with its trigger unfired, ocn-20's retention pattern.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
Measured 2026-08-30; notes/audits/cgenie-parallelism-and-coupling-support.md sections 7a (criteria, fixed before the series) and 7b-7h (results); data with per-repeat loads in analysis/cgenie_omp.json. Verdicts by thread:

(1) Wall clock re-taken, with the honest caveat: the host was never quiet. The lock excluded every agent for the whole series (one hold, 15:30-16:22), but a game process held ~5.7 cores across both dies throughout; one-minute load 6-12 beside every repeat, recorded before and after each. Within that: run-to-run scatter (measured FIRST, six repeats per end) is 1.7% at one thread and 1.9% at sixteen; task-clock is within 0.3% of wall in every serial repeat, so the process never queued for a core.

(2) The throughput collapse WAS contention, now confirmed with counters attached: retired instructions reproduce across three campaigns to 0.12% (246.34 G user-mode at 36x36x16, 1114.36 G at 72x72x16, both carrying the threading branch's 18% serial saving -- the doubled-grid saving is newly measured). Beside the game the serial rates are 15.0 and 11.6 G/s against 17.0 and 15.5 in the earlier low-load window: the suppression grows with the state (13% vs 25%) at flat MPKI, which is the working-set direction this row suspected, manifest as a neighbour effect, not a model defect. The 32 MB working-set target is NOT exceeded: MPKI is 1.8-4.4 per thousand everywhere except unbound sixteen threads (5.15, attributable to sibling-sharing beside the game; bound one-per-core the same team reads 4.39), and MPKI falls with grid size at fixed threads, as a cache-resident set predicts.

(3) The threaded speedup, which was waiting on this row: turnover 4 threads at 36x36x16 (confirming world-2lbs there), turnover 8 at 72x72x16 with 1.63x at eight as a floor. Against the Amdahl bounds held out (12.47): far below, and the gap is now mechanistically located -- kernel futex sleep/wake at the barriers plus thread placement, per the instruction-scope decomposition in section 7d.

(4) The BIOGEM 5.94 G/s cache-count question was NOT measured: a queued --cost-biogem series (instrument now in analysis/cgenie_omp.py) was cut at session close-out; the plan and inputs are recorded on world-hkcj, whose column-sweep territory it is.

title: Establish whether muffingen runs outside MATLAB, and what it produces above 36 x 36
description: OCN-18 established the MODEL's usable resolution ceiling and demonstrated a 72 x 72 x 16 integration, but the connector was not exercised. muffingen's declared range is [1-72] for par_max_i and par_max_j, annotated on every example configuration, so 72 x 72 is the top of what it CLAIMS and nothing above 36 x 36 ships. Two questions remain and they are separable from the ceiling. (1) Does it run under Octave: the manual says MATLAB throughout and states no position either way, and the only interface that decides it is the low-level netcdf.* family, used in about 170 places, which Octave provides through a separate package. (2) Does the automatic island machinery stay correct above 36 x 36: muffingen.m:1033 calls find_grid_islands and :1054 find_grid_islands_update, and the manual records that hand-drawn island paths could leave the circulation unsolved somewhere with no complaint, which is why the automatic version exists. Note also that references/muffingen is GPL-3 where cGENIE is MIT, so consuming its output is unencumbered but vendoring the generator is not. Source: notes/audits/cgenie-build-cost-and-grid-ceiling.md section 3f
notes:
Split out of ocn-18 on 2026-08-25 when the model half of that row closed.

2026-08-25, worked in fanout-AC. BLOCKED on a host binary; both sub-questions are advanced and neither is closed. notes/audits/cgenie-build-cost-and-grid-ceiling.md section 3f is rewritten with the evidence.

(2) ABOVE 36 x 36 -- largely answered from shipped artifacts. muffingen has been run at 48 x 40 x 16: vendor/cgenie/genie-paleo/fm0000bb holds the complete output set (.k1 of 50 by 42 numbers, which is 48 by 40 plus the format's one-cell border, plus .paths, .psiles, wind stress, albedo, mask), the generator's own configuration (par_max_i=48, par_max_j=40, par_max_k=16, par_gcm='foam') and its run log. The log's steps 14 and 15 show the AUTOMATIC island machinery running at that resolution and reporting 'total # true islands = 3'; the interactive editors were entered and declined. Two shipped cGENIE configurations compile against it, muffin.C.fm0000bb and muffin.CB.fm0450ab.BASES. It is the only world above 36 x 36 among the 234 that carry a muffingen log. Statically the machinery carries no dimension literal: make_genie_grid.m takes n_i/n_j/n_k as arguments and find_grid_islands.m, find_grid_islands_update.m and make_grid_psiles.m take their extent from the mask handed to them. So the DEMONSTRATED connector ceiling is 48 x 40, not 36 x 36, and the audit's earlier 'nothing above 36 x 36 ships' was wrong. 72 x 72 remains declared and undemonstrated.

(1) OCTAVE -- narrowed hard, still not demonstrated. The netCDF dependency is confined to the four GCM input arms: every file touching netcdf.* is named for the model it reads (fun_read_*_hadcm3x/_foam/_cesm/_rockee and the matching make_grid_winds_*), the whole interface is five read-only entry points (open, close, inq, inqVarID, getVar), nothing creates or writes netCDF, and the two ncread calls in the tree are inside comments. The mask/k1/k2/blank arms leave every par_nc_*_name empty, read input through load() on a plain ASCII .dat, and take winds from make_grid_winds_zonal, which reads nothing. opt_user=false and opt_plots=false disable every ginput and every figure. So the arm this project would use needs no netCDF package and no display, and the question is core Octave rather than Octave Forge.

BLOCKER, and the reason this stays open: probed for the binaries 'octave' and 'octave-cli' on PATH and neither is present; there is no 'matlab' either. The distribution packages it as extra/octave 11.3.0-1 (also cachyos-extra-znver4/octave) and it is not installed. Nothing was routed around.

THE TEST TO RUN once one of them is present: copy references/muffingen/EXAMPLE_MASK_waterworld.m, raise par_max_i and par_max_j (72 for the declared top, 48 x 40 first to reproduce a known-good answer), keep opt_user=false and opt_plots=false, and run muffingen.m headless. That exercises the grid constructor, the automatic island machinery and the file writers with no netCDF and no display, and it answers both halves of this row at once.
close_reason: DEMONSTRATED under GNU Octave 11.3.0, headless, with no Octave packages installed: 16 muffingen v0.9.26 configurations completed. Known-good reproduction first: genie-paleo/wworld re-run from its own shipped MATLAB-generated configuration gave BYTE-IDENTICAL .k1, .paths and .psiles and the same island result. Three incompatibilities, none of them netCDF and none a toolbox: get(0,'Diary') is a MATLAB-only root property, and two plot blocks (source/make_grid_winds_zonal.m, and muffingen.m's two albedo profiles) are not guarded by opt_plots; this host has no graphics toolkit at all, so they are fatal here rather than cosmetic. par_max_i and par_max_j are IGNORED on the mask/k1/k2 arm -- fun_read_k1 takes [jmax,imax] from the input file's own size -- so the connector's resolution is set by what Orogen writes, not by a parameter, and the declared [1-72] governs only the GCM arms. Given genuine high-resolution input: 48x40 gives a .k1 of 50x42, exactly the shape of the shipped fm0000bb, with the same border rows, wrap columns and land codes; 72x72 gives 74x74 and psiles 72x73. A synthetic 72x72 world with six landmasses was resolved into exactly six true islands with six paths and psiles indices 0..7, so the automatic machinery scales. The k1 arm round-tripped a thirteen-level bathymetry cell for cell; the mask arm cannot, since it sets a uniform ocean depth, so the Orogen connector writes a .k1 rather than a mask .dat. Usability is structural, against fm0000bb and wworld as the format reference: no generated world was integrated by cGENIE, and that is named in the audit as not established. notes/audits/cgenie-build-cost-and-grid-ceiling.md section 3f is rewritten with the evidence and carries the reproduction recipe; muffingen is GPL-3 and stays unvendored.

title: oroini rescales groundoro by OROSCALE on every model invocation, so a non-unit oroscale compounds
description:
glaciermod.f90 glacierini reads groundoro out of the restart record groundsg on a restart (the mpgetgp at the top of the nrestart branch), and oroini then multiplies it by oroscale unconditionally. ExoPlaSim invokes the executable once per orbit, so oroini runs once per orbit and groundoro leaves the run as the staged code-129 field times oroscale raised to the number of invocations. glacierini then applies oroscale to doro a second time within the same call, on top of the copy oroini already scaled through groundoro.

Inert today and verified so: config/planet.yaml declares no orography scaling and nothing writes OROSCALE, so the p_earth.f90 and plasimmod.f90 default of 1.0 stands, and run_ade7373b4c90 carries groundsg bit-equal to its staged N032_surf_0129.sra in all 28 of its restarts.

Two consequences worth separating. The scaling belongs on the cold path only, where the staged field first enters the model; on a restart the field has already been scaled. And OROSCALE is a planet_nl key that nothing writes, so the value the model integrates comes from a compiled default rather than from the config.

Do: scale groundoro only when nrestart == 0, and remove the second application to doro in glacierini; or, if the compounding is left standing, declare OROSCALE in expected_namelist_keys so a non-unit value cannot arrive unnoticed. restart_surface.py refuses to compare code 129 whenever OROSCALE is not 1.0 and cites this issue.
notes:
FIXED on fanout-Y8, commit 5e45c59e.

PREMISE RE-CONFIRMED against the code as it now stands. oroini's
groundoro(:) = groundoro(:)*oroscale sat inside the nglacier branch and ran on
every invocation; glacierini's two doro(:) = doro(:)*oroscale lines (one per
nglacier branch) ran a second application in the same call. On the COLD path
with nglacier = 1 that already gave doro = staged*oroscale^2 + glacieroro*
oroscale, which the issue did not name; on the restart path both compounded per
invocation, on the nglacier = 0 branch as well because doro comes back out of
the restart there.

FIX: one line, glaciermod.f90:181, in the nrestart == 0 branch immediately
after mpsurfgp('doro',...) and before groundoro(:) = doro(:). oroini's scaling
and both glacierini scalings removed. That is the only place the staged field
enters the model, so it is the only place a scale on the staged field belongs.

BIT-EQUALITY PRESERVED BY CONSTRUCTION: every operation removed and added is a
multiplication by exactly 1.0 at the compiled default, which is the identity in
IEEE for every finite value and preserves the sign of zero. The order of
operations for doro changes from (groundoro*1 + glacieroro)*1 to groundoro +
glacieroro, which is the same sum. So groundsg stays bit-equal to the staged
code 129 and the run_ade7373b4c90 evidence stands unchanged.

ENUMERATED, over the whole vendor/exoplasim tree including files no build
compiles: readers/writers of oroscale are now surfmod.f90:484 (already
nrestart == 0 guarded, and its doro is re-read from the .sra by glacierini
anyway) and glaciermod.f90:181. groundoro is written at glaciermod.f90:164
(restart read), :182 (cold), and published at :750; read by oroini's geopotential
loop, outmod's code 267 and the three diagnostic gathers. Nothing else. No
namelist, restart record, pyburn code, diagnostic print or .sra reader changes.

SECOND CONSEQUENCE ALSO SETTLED: OROSCALE was a planet_nl key nothing wrote.
configure_otherargs now writes OROSCALE@planet_namelist = 1.0 on every prepare
and every resume, and expected_namelist_keys checks it unconditionally -- no
orography scaling is an assertion about this world rather than a knob, so it
follows NSTORMDIAG's pattern rather than a config key. NOT routed through
configure(orography=), whose branch also forces NGLACIER and would fight the
glacier settings. check_consistency puts it in the designed
'never recorded' warning for the two runs that predate the key, and fails
nothing.

KNOCK-ON: doro == groundsg + dglacsg is now exact at ANY oroscale rather than
only at 1.0, because nothing scales doro after oroini writes it.
restart_surface.py says so, its two stale glaciermod cites are re-located by
content, and the OROSCALE exclusion's reason is restated (the record is the
staged field times the scale, once -- it is the .sra that is not the right
thing to compare against, not the record that is ill defined).

FILED world-zq1k: the same function's NGLACIER != 1 exclusion carried a reason
that is not true -- glacierini sets groundoro from doro before the nglacier
switch, so groundsg is not left at zero -- and the fix moved the line it cited.

VERIFICATION: static, as required. smoke_test 36/36 including 'the model source
compiles under the declared flags'; check_consistency's three failures are the
pre-existing unlinked surface payload and unbuilt binaries. No binary rebuilt
and no model run.
close_reason: OROSCALE applied once, on the cold path where the staged field enters the model; oroini's and glacierini's applications removed. Bit-equal at the compiled 1.0 by construction. OROSCALE now written and checked on every prepare and resume, so the value integrated is declared rather than compiled.

title: Paint the periodic lake cycle onto regions, and run it once a baseline climatology exists
description:
world-15i0 delivered the solver, its criteria and the sub-annual producer.
Two things remain and neither is a decision.

1. THE ARTIFACT HAS NEVER BEEN PRODUCED. config/planet.yaml carries
   baseline_climatology: null, so surface_water.py refuses to run at all, and
   the only climatology in the tree is bootstrap_regular_climatology.nc, a T42
   bootstrap on the superseded precarve-craton while source_build is
   precarve-craton-10m at T21. The worktree also has no surface .sra inputs, so
   climate_fields cannot resolve the land albedo it hands Penman. The periodic
   block in surface_water.py main() is therefore verified by its parts --
   solve_periodic against ten checks on synthetic basins and against the real
   9,403-basin set, the per-bin read against the identity that its bin-weighted
   mean reproduces the annual read -- and not by a product. Run it once a
   baseline climatology is declared.

2. THE CROSSING TO REGIONS IS NOT BUILT. surface_water.nc now carries each
   basin's lake area in every time bin, which is per BASIN.
   hydrography/config/wetness.yaml's seasonal_inundation class is per REGION,
   and stays declared-and-absent until a bin's area is painted onto regions.
   That is the same operation paint_lakes already performs for the annual
   solve, once per bin, and it is what unblocks WET-2's seasonal half for
   closed basins and WET-8 and WET-10's seasonal aquatic methane area.

DO NOT merge that area with a floodplain's, which does not exist and should not
have an owner yet, or with a seasonally saturated soil, which is a water
content and not an area.

Discovered from world-15i0.
notes:
PART 2 DONE, PART 1 BLOCKED. fanout-Y8, commits 7b3d067a and aeff5037.

ITEM 2, THE CROSSING TO REGIONS: BUILT.
surface_water.py:paint_lake_cycle. paint_lakes's fill is hoisted into
_fill_order and _paint, because the order depends on the terrain and the basin
membership and NOT on how much water is in a basin, so it is the same order in
every bin and the sort runs once rather than per bin. paint_lakes is unchanged
in behaviour and is now a one-bin call of the same machinery.

surface_water.nc gains three per-region variables:
  lake_cycle_decided    the owning basin closed its year. READ FIRST.
  lake_cycle_fraction   share of ONE CYCLE the region spends under water,
                        weighted by the bins' own lengths rather than counted.
  lake_cycle_bins_wet   the exact integer the permanent/seasonal split is
                        taken on.
solve_periodic's refusal CROSSES rather than being dropped: a basin whose year
did not close gets a zero budget in every bin and decided false over every
region draining to it, so a zero can never mean both dry all year and never
solved. surface_water_report.json carries the painted areas and the counts.

--selftest, seven checks, each able to fail and none an outcome that could only
differ:
  one bin at full weight reproduces the annual paint REGION FOR REGION
  a steady area gives every painted region the whole cycle and no ring
  the duration is weighted by the bins' own lengths, not averaged over bins
    (the check that separates cycle units from bin counts)
  bins_wet equals an independently taken per-bin count
  a varying forcing does produce a ring, so the fixture is not vacuous
  a refused basin is undecided rather than dry
  a region in no basin is never decided

The two things world-15i0 established are honoured and unchanged: the catchment
term is still the annual one in every bin, and the bin lengths are the
normalised climatology weights, which are already in Vesper's year.

ITEM 1, THE ARTIFACT: STILL BLOCKED, and not on anything this agent can settle.
config/planet.yaml carries baseline_climatology: null, the only climatology in
the tree is a T42 bootstrap on the superseded precarve-craton while
source_build is precarve-craton-10m at T21, and the worktree has no surface
.sra so climate_fields cannot resolve the land albedo it hands Penman.
hydrography/data/<build>/ carries no surface_water.nc on either build. Declaring
the baseline climatology is a loop decision, so this stays open.

FILED world-t8i5: the crossing exists and the PARTITION does not. WET-2's
seasonal_inundation cannot become a resolved class until it is decided which
solve decides open water -- the annual equilibrium area sits between the cycle's
trough and its peak, so open_water, playa and seasonal_inundation overlap in the
strandline, and settling it needs the two paints measured against each other on
an artifact that does not exist. wetness.yaml now says that rather than 'the
crossing is missing', and build_wetness.py's header no longer claims nothing in
the component carries a season.
close_reason:
The artifact exists and the painting is verified in it. hydrography/data/canonical-10m-base/surface_water.nc carries lake_cycle_decided, lake_cycle_fraction and lake_cycle_bins_wet over 10,000,005 regions against 12 time bins, plus the per-bin basin area, level and volume. Built twice, on the vegetated bootstrap climatology and on the bare-rock endmember's own: 1160 basins carry a publishable season, 0 refused for not closing, water closes to 4.9e-16 per basin and 2.2e-15 over the set against a declared 1e-10, and 409,158 regions are under water in every bin with 17,793 in some and not all.

All three conditions this row recorded as blocking item 1 are false now: config carries a climatology, the tree's climatology is on the configured build at the configured rung, and the surface .sra inputs exist so climate_fields can resolve the land albedo it hands Penman.

It was built on the BOOTSTRAP climatology rather than a baseline, and that is the correct reading of the row rather than a shortfall. docs/src/pipeline/loops.md's invariant, recorded this cycle, is that a step reads the BEST AVAILABLE input and not the first available one; lib/paths.py:best_available_climatology returns the stage it chose and stamps it. That it will be re-derived on the baseline when the loop turns is true of every derived artifact in the tree and is not a reason to hold a row open.

Item 2 was split off as world-t8i5 and stays open.

title: A 20-orbit window cannot separate an equilibrium from the model's own low-frequency variability
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 on run_4769c35837df, one 85-orbit T21 run at dt 45, eight-byte, no comparison involved. Its four non-overlapping 20-orbit means of global-mean surface temperature are 291.355, 291.835, 291.757 and 291.651 K -- spread 0.210 K, range 0.480 K. The per-orbit series has lag-1 autocorrelation 0.615, so a 20-orbit window carries roughly five independent samples.

That is a statement about the WINDOW LENGTH and not about whether the run converged. Cold-start convergence at T21 is about 70 orbits (operational experience, recorded in exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md), so orbit 84 is past it; the movement between windows is the model's low-frequency variability, which is what the autocorrelation says it is.

The consequence is that any criterion evaluated on one 20-orbit window is measuring variability as much as state. A convergence verdict, a drift-per-orbit threshold and a two-run comparison all inherit it. world-omn is the row whose subject is what the convergence window's noise costs, and this is a measurement for it; world-yj9o is the same fact reaching compare_equilibria.py's SEM.

Do: establish how long a window has to be before its mean is stable to the tolerance a criterion needs. The evidence above is one run and four windows, which fixes the scale and not the number. The 85-orbit series is on disk and a longer one would settle it; the arithmetic is that a window's standard error goes as sqrt((1+r1)/(1-r1)/n), so reaching 0.05 K against a 0.10 K orbit-to-orbit scatter and r1 = 0.615 needs about 17 independent samples, which is about 70 orbits rather than 20.
notes:
Answered by world-omn and world-yj9o. The window length is bracketed at 21 to 44 orbits with an estimate of 34.1: the binding criterion is the extrapolated offset, whose statistic is |offset| + half_width with both terms carrying the same slope error times the relaxation time, and var(slope) = scatter^2 * tau * 12 / (n(n^2-1)). assess_convergence.DEFAULT_WINDOW_ORBITS is 35 and is computed from three cited inputs rather than typed.

CORRECTION TO THIS ISSUE'S ARITHMETIC. 'about 17 independent samples, which is about 70 orbits' conflates n_eff with n: sigma * sqrt(tau/n) <= 0.05 at sigma = 0.10 and tau = 4.195 needs n >= 16.8 ORBITS, not 17 independent samples.

AND THE 0.210 K IS AN UPPER BOUND, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Applying the stationarity guard declared in lib/autocorrelation.py to the four window means quoted here, 291.355 / 291.835 / 291.757 / 291.651, the fitted trend moves them 0.243 K against a scatter of 0.210 K, so the span is refused: the first of those windows covers orbits 0 to 19 of a cold start whose approach runs to about 70. That spread is the tail of the approach contaminating the variability. The same guard refuses every tail of run_ade7373b4c90 too. The project has no equilibrium series long enough to fix tau, both instruments now say so rather than assuming a number, and what would settle it is a production span at equilibrium of at least ten times tau, about 40 orbits after the approach has finished. exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md carries all of it.

--- 2026-08-25, the length question answered separately from the tau question ---

Measured on synthetic series whose tau is known in closed form, against lib/autocorrelation.py's own estimator. Criteria fixed before the run: tau RECOVERED = median estimate within a tenth of the truth and relative RMS below a fifth; an interval COVERS = a nominal 95 per cent t-interval contains the true mean between 92.5 and 97.5 per cent of the time. Two processes: a true AR(1) at r=0.615 (tau 4.19) and a fast-plus-slow mixture that is deliberately not AR(1) (tau 10.43). Written up in exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md.

FIXING TAU IS OUT OF REACH. The estimator is biased low everywhere below a few hundred times tau. As a fraction of the truth, with the span in multiples of that process's own tau in brackets: at 20 samples 0.56 (5x) and 0.19 (2x); at 85 samples 0.85 (20x) and 0.44 (8x); at 300 samples 0.93 (72x) and 0.74 (29x); at 1200 samples 1.00 (286x) and 0.91 (115x); at 5000 samples 1.01 (1192x) and 0.97 (479x). AR(1) first meets the criterion at 1200 samples, the mixture at 5000, so about 290 and 480 times their own tau. That matches the analytic scaling for a truncated lag sum. In orbits that is of order a thousand AT EQUILIBRIUM, two orders of magnitude beyond anything this project runs. Tau will not be fixed here by direct estimation, ever.

BOUNDING A WINDOW MEAN DOES NOT NEED TAU FIXED. Non-overlapping batch means take the scatter of the batch means as the error of the grand mean; it needs batches long compared with tau but never needs tau's value. Coverage measured at r=0.615: 4 batches of 5 tau (span 20 tau) 0.940; 8 of 5 tau (40 tau) 0.938; 4 of 10 tau (40 tau) 0.951; 8 of 10 tau (80 tau) 0.951. Estimating tau inside the same span instead covers 0.898, 0.920, 0.933, 0.940 at those lengths. Batches of 2 tau miss the criterion however many there are, so BATCH LENGTH is what has to be bought first, not batch count.

THE ANSWER: a span of about TWENTY TIMES TAU after the approach is where an honest interval starts. This is stricter than the ten-times-tau figure recorded earlier in the note; ten times tau is where tau becomes usable, twenty is where the interval actually covers.

For a T21 commissioning run: about 70 orbits of approach (operational experience) plus about 20 tau. If tau is near what an AR(1) at lag-1 0.615 implies, that is about 80 orbits and the run is about 150. If the model carries the slower component, tau is larger and the span scales with it. THE BRACKET IS THE RESULT, and what removes it is not a better estimate of tau but a run long enough to batch, which reports its own interval without needing tau at all.

The twenty-orbit window is therefore short by a factor of about four even under the optimistic branch, and it is short in the BATCH LENGTH, which no number of extra windows repairs.
close_reason: Answered. The window rule is a span of about twenty times tau after the approach, measured against lib/autocorrelation.py on synthetic series with tau known in closed form, criteria fixed first: batch means reach the coverage criterion there, batches of two tau miss it however many there are, and estimating tau inside the same span covers worse at every length. Fixing tau itself needs about 290 to 480 times tau, of order a thousand orbits at equilibrium, so it is not a target this project can design against and the recommendation is reported as a bracket. Written up in exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md, which also supersedes its own earlier ten-times-tau figure. The sibling arithmetic that put this at seventeen independent samples and seventy orbits conflated n_eff with n; the relation gives about seventeen orbits, and it is the wrong question anyway because the 0.210 K spread it was fitted to is contaminated by the approach. Consuming the rule when a run is specified rather than after it is spent is world-cikl.

title: Source the allophane content of andic material against a development measure
description: pedology/notes/mineral-reactivity-supply.md section 2: the mineral-aware arm's allophane proxy is one conversion away. build_soil.py emits andic as an AREAL fraction and the mass weighting is arithmetic, since the andic bulk density is already declared and blended. What is missing is the allophane concentration WITHIN andic material. Parfitt (1990) is read and gives an upper end only: its Table 3 profiles are named as the greatest concentrations in New Zealand, 10 and 22 per cent in the topsoil horizons and 16 to 38 per cent below, up to 60 per cent in deep deposits, with no distribution over allophanic soils. Substituting the maxima puts a factor of several into a quantity a protection coefficient is linear in, and a concentration that did not respond to development would contradict pedogenesis.yaml's own development axis. The bar: a source giving allophane content over allophanic soils against a development measure, not a review's extremes. Note the second gate, recorded in the same note: even with all four proxies the mineral-aware arm cannot be written, because no read source supplies a parameterised transfer from a proxy to a protection coefficient.
close_reason: Resolved and committed, and the row's bar was the wrong one. Parfitt (2009) 10.1180/claymin.2009.044.1.135 was fetched and read and states that for allophane formation 'the effect of time is subordinate to these factors' -- silicic-acid activity, Al availability, co-precipitation, leaching regime, organic matter and pH. So allophane content against a DEVELOPMENT measure indexes on the weakest control. world-wxhr restates the bar on leaching regime, which is the axis that controls it and which this pipeline has: the andisol block already gates andic development on a precipitation threshold. The review also supplies the distribution-shaped statements the row said were missing -- 2 to 22 per cent allophane across Icelandic field soils, under 6 per cent in Atlantic volcanic island horizons -- so substituting maxima is no longer the state of the evidence, though neither range can place a cell and the proxy stays undeclared. Three sources that index content on the controlling axis were sought and could not be reached from this host and are filed as INDEX rows: Parfitt, Russell and Orbell (1983) 10.1016/0016-7061(83)90029-0, Singleton et al. (1989) 10.1071/SR9890067, Parfitt and Kimble (1989) 10.2136/sssaj1989.03615995005300030057x. The second gate stands and none of this touches it. Section 4 of the same note moved the other way while working this row: polyvalent cation saturation is now derivable and merely unwired, world-rzyz.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESOLVED, and the row's own bar turned out to be the wrong one.

THE SEARCH. Crossref-confirmed DOIs first, then paperfetch. Fetched and READ: Parfitt (2009), 'Allophane and imogolite: role in soil biogeochemical processes', Clay Minerals 44(1), 135-155, `10.1180/claymin.2009.044.1.135`, via Google Scholar.

SOUGHT AND NOT REACHED, both 403 at publisher, Google Scholar and Sci-Hub:
  Parfitt, Russell, Orbell (1983). Weathering sequence of soils from volcanic ash involving allophane and halloysite, New Zealand. Geoderma 29(1), 41-57. `10.1016/0016-7061(83)90029-0`
  Singleton, March, Otsuka, Parfitt (1989). Allophane and halloysite content and soil solution silicon in soils from rhyolitic volcanic material, New Zealand. Aust. J. Soil Res. 27(1), 67-77. `10.1071/SR9890067`
  Parfitt, Kimble (1989). Conditions for Formation of Allophane in Soils. SSSAJ 53(3), 971-977. `10.2136/sssaj1989.03615995005300030057x`
Also queried and rejected as off-target: Takahashi et al. (1993) Geoderma, Mizota et al. (1988) Geoderma, Gerard et al. (2007) EJSS, Nanzyo et al. (2020) SSPN. All four INDEX rows for the unreached ones are filed as sought and not reached, with the reason each would matter.

THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE ROW. Parfitt (2009) states on the controls of allophane formation that 'the effect of time is subordinate to these factors' -- the factors being silicic-acid activity in the soil solution, Al availability, the opportunity for co-precipitation, leaching regime, soil organic matter and pH. So allophane content against a DEVELOPMENT measure is content against the weakest control, and a transfer built on it would carry the residual variance of all the others. The row asked for the subordinate axis.

THE AXIS THAT DOES CONTROL IT IS ONE THIS PIPELINE HAS. Parfitt reports the New Zealand aeolian case in the exact form the andisol model already runs on: halloysite and no allophane at 1000 mm of rainfall, only allophane at 1600 mm, the switch turning on soil-solution silicon crossing about 10 mg/l. pedogenesis.yaml's andisol block already gates andic development on a precipitation threshold. What is absent is the CONTENT above the threshold, not the threshold. world-wxhr restates the bar there.

AND THE FACTOR OF SEVERAL IS OFF THE TABLE. Parfitt (2009) supplies the distribution-shaped statements Parfitt (1990) Table 3's named maxima could not: 2 to 22 per cent allophane across Icelandic field soils at 11 to 42 per cent C (Sigfusson et al. 2008), and under 6 per cent in Atlantic volcanic island mineral horizons. Both are ranges over real populations rather than national extremes. Neither can place a CELL, which is why the proxy stays undeclared and world-wxhr is open.

THE SECOND GATE STANDS AND NOTHING HERE TOUCHES IT. The mineral-aware arm cannot be written even with all four proxies, because no read source supplies a parameterised transfer from a proxy to a protection coefficient. That is recorded in the note's last section and in every row filed here.

SECTION 4 MOVED THE OTHER WAY, found while working this row. Its claim that no held source supplies a cation exchange pedotransfer from texture and organic carbon is no longer true: Sahrawat (1983) supplies the capacity and Solly et al. (2020) the polyvalent share against pH, so polyvalent cation saturation is DERIVABLE and merely unwired. world-rzyz owns the wiring, and it does not open the arm either.

title: The ecological stream writes no orbital position per interval
description:
Worldbuilding: Vesper's simulated climate hands its simulated biosphere one block per ecological interval, and this is about what that block does not carry.

biosphere/notes/ecological-climate-forcing-audit.md finding 4 requires each forcing interval to record its start, end, duration, ORBITAL POSITION, local solar phase, and grid and source identity. The ecological stream carries the first three explicitly, as codes 600, 601 and 602 from outmod.f90:ecogp. It carries no orbital record at all.

Local solar phase is fine without one: rotation is uniform, so the artifact builder derives it exactly from the interval start and config/planet.yaml's rotation period, and biosphere/config/ecological_forcing_contract.yaml declares it derived for that reason. Orbital position is NOT derivable the same way. The orbit is eccentric, so true anomaly is not linear in absolute time, and the only place the model publishes it is code 50 on unit 40, the regular stream, at that stream's own output cadence. Taking it from there means matching an ecological interval against a different stream's records by position, which is exactly the cross-stream inference the explicit interval bounds exist to refuse.

Do: one writescalar of orbnu*180./PI beside the three bounds in ecogp, where the value is already in scope, as a fourth interval-record code. Then set the row's status in biosphere/config/ecological_forcing_contract.yaml from not_produced to produced with its code, which check_forcing_contract.py already checks against outmod.f90.

Rule 4 applies: after any change under vendor/exoplasim, rebuild every binary. This is one writescalar in an output routine and changes no integration, but the ecological stream's restart record set is serialized behind the ecovers marker, so check restart_schema.py covers whatever is added.

Source: biosphere/config/ecological_forcing_contract.yaml interval_record, biosphere/notes/ecological-climate-forcing-audit.md finding 4, vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/outmod.f90:ecogp
close_reason: ecogp writes orbnu*180./PI as code 603 beside the interval bounds; contract row is produced at version 2 and the gate checks it against outmod.f90. Value is the true anomaly at the interval's last accumulated timestep, stated in the comment and the row. compare_eco_streams compares it across a restart; ECO_STREAM_CODES extends to 603.

title: Retain crosses to Orogen on a different depth basis than it was computed on
description:
The carve list's `retain` is a fraction, and the two sides of the interface take
it as a fraction of two different depths in two different units. Neither side is
locally wrong and neither states which depth it means.

HYDROGRAPHY divides by the FINISHED depression, in metres.
export_carve_list.py: retain = clip(1 - cut / depth_at_spill, 0, 1), with
depth_at_spill_m from basins.nc, whose spill and sink are both measured on the
conditioned terrain and converted through the height curve.

OROGEN spends it against the NATURAL depression, in model units.
basins.js buildBasinProtection: carveAllowance = (1 - retain) * selected[i].depth,
where depth is what detectBasins measured on the PRE-CONDITIONING surface in the
dimensionless elevation parameter.

Orogen cannot change basis: protection is built before erosion, so the finished
depth does not exist yet, and the carve operates on model elevations. So the
conversion belongs on the hydrography side, or the interface has to declare the
basis and hydrography compute retain in it.

MEASURED 2026-08-25 on both registered builds, notes/audits/basin-catalogue-floor.md,
section "Preserved is not the same as still closed". Natural/final depth is a
median 1.24 in model units and 1.69 in km, the height curve being quartic on
land. In physical metres of rim, the incision Orogen is permitted against the
incision intended runs, on precarve-craton-10m:

  retain 0.90   p05 0.35   median 2.69   p95 8.68
  retain 0.50   p05 0.25   median 2.12   p95 8.39
  retain 0.10   p05 0.75   median 1.69   p95 6.88

so it is a factor of thirty across the population, not a scale factor to divide
out. Carried through to the surviving impoundment, an intended 0.25 delivers a
median 0.47 with a 5th percentile of 0.01 and a 95th of 1.00 -- the 1.00 end
being basins where erosion already took the rim below the allowance floor and
the allowance does nothing at all.

IT BITES THE MARGINAL CLASS ALONE. retain 1 gives an allowance of zero and is
bit-identical to no allowance; retain 0 clears noLower outright. Both cross
exactly. The marginal class is the one the whole retain machinery exists for:
hydrography/notes/retain-fraction.md calls the notched through-flowing valley
one of the few landforms this project decides rather than inherits, and it is
the only class the crossing does not carry.

WHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A PATCH. The conversion needs the NEXT
generation's natural depth, which does not exist when the list is written, so
any conversion uses this build's natural-to-final ratio as the estimate of the
next one's. That is defensible -- the ratio is a property of the conditioning
rather than of the carve list -- but it is an assumption that has to be declared
and it changes the terrain, so it is not a silent fix.

Do: choose the basis the interface declares, then either convert in
export_carve_list.py against natural_spill_depth (now carried in basins.nc and
on lib/orogen.py Basin) or state the basis in vendor/orogen/tools/README.md and
in the carve list header. Thresholds before results: whichever is chosen, the
residual after conversion is reported as a bracket, not a point.

Discovered from world-o3b6.
notes:
FIXED on fanout-Y8, commit da9029ee.

BASIS CHOSEN: the carve list's retain is a fraction of the depression's NATURAL
spill depth in the generator's dimensionless elevation parameter -- what
buildBasinProtection already spends (1-retain) against. Orogen cannot change
basis, so the conversion went on the hydrography side, and the basis is now
declared in three places: vendor/orogen/tools/README.md on the file format,
basins.js on buildBasinProtection and inciseOutlets, and the carve list header.

CONVERSION: export_carve_list.py:to_natural_relief_basis, applied to
retain_incision on BOTH climate arms before the max and before the verdict, so
the verdict follows the instruction Orogen receives.
  retain = 1 - (1 - retain_finished) * retainedFraction
Both endpoints pass through exactly. BasinSet gained retained_fraction (optional
read, so no other consumer of a pre-field basins.nc breaks); export_carve_list
refuses with a named rebuild instruction if it is absent.

MEASURED, from finalPreserved.retainedFraction and natural.spillDepth in both
manifests, as permitted incision over intended in model units:
  precarve-craton      before p05 0.75 / med 1.26 / p95 2.71 -> after 1.0000 flat
  precarve-craton-10m  before p05 0.73 / med 1.24 / p95 2.65 -> after 1.0000 flat
Exact on every basin whose instruction the mechanism can express.

SATURATION, reported not absorbed: an intended cut deeper than the whole natural
relief cannot be an allowance and saturates to carve. Needs retainedFraction >
1/(1-retain), so only basins the conditioning left DEEPER. On -10m of 9,401 with
a ratio: 0 at retain 0.90, 94 at 0.50, 1,103 at 0.10. Counted per pass in the
sidecar as carve_list_basis.verdict_class_moved.

RESIDUAL AS A BRACKET: the ratio is this generation's estimate of the next one's.
retainedFraction p5/50/95 is 0.369/0.797/1.340 and 0.378/0.804/1.372, so the
residual bracket about the median ratio is [0.46, 1.68] -- against the factor of
thirty the mismatch carried.

VERIFICATION: export_carve_list.py --selftest, 7 checks, all can fail. The
identity check is that the permitted incision equals the intended one; a
companion check asserts the UNCONVERTED crossing fails that identity, so the
first is not vacuous. test-basins.mjs 47/47, smoke_test 36/36.

NOT REGENERATED: no carve list exists in the tree (baseline_climatology is null),
so nothing published moved. The generation is the user's call.

SIDE NOTE for the pedology owner: pedology/scripts/thermostat_efficiency.py
reads carve_list.json basins[].retain as the share of a basin that stays
decoupled. That number is now a fraction of the natural relief in model units
rather than of the previous generation's finished depression in metres, which is
a better proxy for what survives the next carve, not a worse one. No action
needed; recorded so the change of meaning is not silent.
close_reason: Interface declares the natural-relief-in-model-units basis; export_carve_list converts before writing. Permitted incision now equals intended exactly, held by a selftest identity with a non-vacuity companion check. Saturation and the ratio's residual bracket reported per pass. Not regenerated.

title: pyburn's potential-temperature branch carries theta across loop iterations and reuses the wrong meta
description:
pyburn.py's `dataset()` and `netcdf()` both derive potential temperature in a
block that reads `thetah` and `theta` as locals left behind by an earlier turn
of the variable loop:

    elif key==str(thetahcode) or key==str(thetafcode):
        if "theta" in rdataset or "thetah" in rdataset:
            if key==str(thetahcode):
                meta = ilibrary[key][:]
                meta.append(key)
                variable,meta = _transformvar(...,thetah,meta,...)
            elif key==str(thetafcode):
                variable,meta = _transformvar(...,theta,meta,...)

Two findings, one block, both in `dataset()` and again in `netcdf()`.

1. `thetah` and `theta` are bound only in the `else` arm, on the turn that
   derives them. The condition tests `rdataset`, which the `else` arm fills, so
   at runtime the names do resolve -- but the array they resolve to is the RAW
   one from that earlier turn while `rdataset` holds the TRANSFORMED one, and
   nothing states that dependence. pyflakes F821 reports it; the symtable check
   smoke_test now runs deliberately does not, because the names ARE bound in
   the scope and the code works.

2. The `thetafcode` arm of that same branch does not do `meta =
   ilibrary[key][:]; meta.append(key)` before calling `_transformvar`, so it
   passes whatever `meta` the previous iteration left. The `thetahcode` arm two
   lines above does. So a request for full-level potential temperature that
   follows a request for the half-level field labels the full-level array with
   the previous variable's metadata.

Reaching either needs both potential-temperature codes (279, 280) requested
from one file. This project's postprocessing does not request them, so nothing
here is wrong today.

Do: settle whether the reuse should read back from `rdataset` or keep the raw
local under an explicit name, and give the `thetafcode` arm its own `meta`.
Fix both copies -- `dataset()` and `netcdf()` carry the block verbatim.

Source: world-sf6b, which repaired the names in the same two files.
close_reason: NOT A DEFECT, verified by running both copies. A harness stubbing readfile and asking dataset() and advancedDataset() for 279 and 280 in both orders, and with an unrelated code between, returns thetah with half_level metadata over nlev+1 levels and theta with full_level metadata over nlev -- before the change as well as after. The full-level arm does not inherit the previous iteration's meta: the loop head reassigns meta from ilibrary[key] every turn. The raw thetah/theta locals are the correct arrays to pass on, since rdataset holds the transformed copy. Kept a behaviour-neutral clarity change: both arms build meta the same way, and the arrays are bound to None before the loop with the reuse arm testing that, which clears the pyflakes F821. The block is in dataset() and advancedDataset(), not netcdf().

title: Solve the closed-basin lake balance as a periodic steady state, for a seasonal inundated area
description:
`world-la19` settled who owns a seasonal inundated area and split the quantity
in three. This is the one part that is hydrography's and that needs no curve,
model or preprocessor this project does not already have.

WHAT EXISTS. `basins.nc` carries each basin's level, area and volume at 128
levels from `build_hydrography.py`'s priority-flood ordering, which is exactly
the curve a filling depression needs. The coupling matrix already crosses a
per-basin quantity to the climate grid. The baseline climatology carries time
bins and `lib/climatology.py` owns their weights.
`carve_verdict.penman_open_water` already integrates the diurnal cycle for a
Jensen reason, so evaluating it per time bin is not a new kind of evaluation.

WHAT CHANGES. `surface_water.py` reduces the climatology with `annual_mean` at
read time and solves for one equilibrium, exiting unless it converges to it.
Instead it integrates each basin's storage through the climatology's own bins
against that basin's curve, with open-water evaporation evaluated per bin, and
the convergence criterion becomes a PERIODIC steady state: the year must close
on itself to a declared tolerance, in the basin's own volume, and a basin that
does not close is refused rather than reported. That is a new criterion, not a
new solver.

WHAT BLOCKS IT, and it is not this row's to lift. `open_water_evaporation` and
`surface_runoff` carry `interval_floor: annual` in
`hydrography/config/land_water_ledger.yaml`, both owned by LSHY-6, and the
first's note says why: the producer is annual and ExoPlaSim cannot supply it at
all, because routed water lands in `driver` and never evaporates -- the absence
`open_water_evaporation_from_routed_water` records that. A sub-annual basin
balance booking against an annual floor is exactly the refusal the ledger
exists to make, so those two floors have to come down first.

DECLARE BEFORE RUNNING, since the answer is a size and not a yes: the periodic
closure tolerance in the basin's own volume, and what counts as a basin having
a seasonal cycle worth publishing. The size is set by residence time -- a deep
terminal lake holds years of supply and its area barely moves within one, while
a shallow playa's is nearly all seasonal -- so the honest product is a per-basin
seasonal amplitude with the low-capacity basins carrying it, not a claim that
every preserved basin has a season.

WHO CONSUMES IT. WET-2's seasonal half for closed basins only; WET-8 and WET-10
for a seasonal aquatic methane area, which must not be merged with a floodplain
area that does not exist or with a seasonally saturated soil, which is a water
content and not an area.
close_reason:
Delivered: lake_balance.solve_periodic integrates each basin's storage through the climatology's own bins against its own hypsometric curve, with the year required to close on itself. The criteria were declared before the solver was run -- closure at 1e-3 of the basin's own capacity with a 1e-6 km3 floor, a basin that does not close within 400 cycles refused rather than reported, closure propagating down the spill cascade, and a cycle published only where the swing clears a tenth of the mean area AND one mean mesh cell. surface_water.py now reads the lake terms per bin and writes the cycle; reference_level_air and climate_fields take an optional bin index and are bit-identical without it.

THE TWO FLOORS ARE DOWN. lake_precipitation and open_water_evaporation move from annual to a new climatology_bin value, and the ledger's TIMING finding against lake_precipitation delivering an annual mean into open_water is gone. The row named surface_runoff as the second floor; it was already instantaneous, and the term that was actually annual was lake_precipitation.

TWO THINGS THE ROW DID NOT ANTICIPATE. Runoff cannot go per bin: over a closed cycle the annual mean of P-E is exactly the runoff a cell generated, and per-bin clamping double counts the wet season. So the catchment's delivery is flat through the year and the missing phase is declared as land_water_ledger.yaml:seasonal_phase_of_catchment_delivery, whose closure is the same decision as adopting drunoff. And bin lengths are in the year the FLUXES are per, which here is Vesper's, not Earth's -- a fixed point does not care how long a year is, so a closure test cannot catch a year-unit mix and the selftest carries a check that can.

The fixture caught a real integrator defect: on precarve-craton-10m the first version reported four basins with a seasonal area swing of up to 1.9 under a forcing with no season, because an explicit step bounded only by capacity alternates across a flat basin floor. Bounded by the local stability limit as well, the periodic solve reproduces the equilibrium solve to machine precision on 9,403 of 9,403 live basins with nothing flagged seasonal.

Remaining work is world-9iy5, and neither part is a decision: the artifact has never been produced because config/planet.yaml carries baseline_climatology null, and the per-region painting that turns the per-basin cycle into wetness.yaml's seasonal_inundation class is not built.

title: The ladder's timestep per rung is declared in three places with three different values
description:
config/planet.yaml model.resolution_timestep_minutes gives T42: 45.0 and T85: 45.0. docs/src/pipeline/sequencing.md section D's escalation runs T42 at dt 30 and T85 at dt 22.5, and calls those the intended values, PROVISIONAL on world-37tn. notes/audits/resolution-ladder.md:108 says 'The ladder therefore runs T42 at dt 22.5, which that note measures as clean at kappa 8 and which is also the step T170 needs' -- and gives a reason the other two do not: comparing rungs at ONE step rather than each at its own margin, because the spectral core's energy residual falls from 0.31 to 0.12 W/m2 when the step is halved, so a ladder whose rungs each ran at their largest stable step would be comparing equilibria that differ by truncation error as well as by resolution.

Three answers, and each is load-bearing somewhere: the config's value is what a run actually gets (check_consistency enforces model.timestep_minutes against the row for the ACTIVE rung), the sequencing chapter is what the escalation plan says it will do, and the audit note carries the only argument for choosing one.

This is what makes a cost per rung a bracket rather than a number: cost scales as 1/dt at fixed rung, so T42 at 22.5 costs twice T42 at 45. Measured seconds per step per rung are in notes/audits/resolution-ladder-wall-clock.md and price all three.

Do: settle on one and make the other two derive from it or cite it. The audit note's argument -- one step across the ladder so the rungs differ only by support -- is the only one of the three that gives a reason, and it is the one the config does not carry.
close_reason: FIXED, commits dc1d3772 f940a1c7 on fanout-X2. The three values are three QUANTITIES and the code now says so. lib/rungs.py declares each once: STABILITY_CEILING_MINUTES (the coarsest step a rung is measured to start clean at, read out of exoplasim/analysis/stability_probe.json at kappa 8 and tau_scale 1 and CHECKED against it by check_stability_ceilings, not copied), ESCALATION_ROUTE (the ordered (rung, step) sequence sequencing.md section D decides, checked against that chapter by check_timestep_restatements), and COMMISSIONING_EVIDENCE (what a run of commissioning length has shown about one pair, which a 900-step probe cannot say). The fourth quantity the audit note carried, every rung at one step, is deliberately NOT carried: SPAT-8 was its only consumer and closed, and the note now says so. model.resolution_timestep_minutes is removed from config/planet.yaml along with an orphaned duplicate of its own descriptive comment that had been left above hyperdiffusion still calling the table 'adopted'; model.timestep_minutes stays, because it is the active step ONE run is configured at, it selects a binary, and a diagnostic arm deliberately moves it. Four dead entries for the removed key are gone from lib/provenance.py's inert sets. The prose cites in notes/audits/resolution-ladder.md, opaque-constants.md, model-earth-centrism.md and exoplasim/notes/parameter-decisions.md are rewritten, the last of which was still carrying the contaminated gamma-8 table.

title: config declares a T170 timestep the stability grid refuses
description:
config/planet.yaml model.resolution_timestep_minutes gives T170: 22.5 and its comment's ceiling column gives the same value with 'dt 30 starts and blows up after 3.8 min'. exoplasim/analysis/stability_probe.json has T170 at dt 22.5, kappa 8, outcome refused_only_at_length, and exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md:278 puts the coarsest step T170 will start clean at dt 15, with its own table reading 'T170 | refuses | refuses | refuses | late | runs | runs' across dt 60, 45, 30, 22.5, 15, 10. So the adopted T170 step is one step above what the grid the table cites measures.

WHY IT SURVIVED: scripts/check_consistency.py compares model.timestep_minutes against the table entry for the ACTIVE rung only, so a table row for a rung nothing is running is checked against nothing. The active rung is T21 and the check reports ok.

This is not urgent because nothing runs T170, and it is not harmless either: the ladder's cost projections are quoted off this table, and a step that refuses is not a cost.

Do: settle the T170 row against world-37tn's re-measurement rather than against the contaminated grid, and give check_consistency a check over EVERY row of the table and not only the active one -- a table whose unused rows are unchecked is a table that goes wrong silently the moment the rung is escalated. Related: world-37tn, world-qnue.
close_reason: FIXED, commit dc1d3772 on fanout-X2. The contradiction was a two-verdict reading of a three-verdict grid. stability_probe.json's outcomes are refused, no_refusal_in_steps and refused_only_at_length, and T170 at dt 22.5 is the third kind -- it starts and dies inside the probe's own range -- so it is not a ceiling in either direction. The coarsest cell T170 is clean at is dt 15, and lib/rungs.py's STABILITY_CEILING_MINUTES declares 15.0. That also restores the note's own finding that the 1/N rule over-predicts T170 by a full step, which the 22.5 row had silently undone. Two other rows moved for the same reason: T21 and T42 are clean in every column the probe measured, so their measured ceiling is 60.0 and not the 45.0 config declared; 45.0 was the route step, which is a different quantity (world-f997). EVERY ROW IS CHECKED NOW, not only the active rung's. rungs.check_stability_ceilings re-derives each rung's ceiling from the probe grid and reports any disagreement, and rungs._check_route refuses at import if any route step is above its rung's ceiling; both run from scripts/check_consistency.py and scripts/smoke_test.py. So a row for a rung nothing is running is no longer checked against nothing, and an unprobed ladder rung (T31, T63, T106) raises rather than being interpolated -- T170 is the standing evidence that the 1/N fit would be the wrong thing to interpolate with. PROVISIONAL and coupled: the ceilings are read from the grid world-37tn is re-taking, so when that grid changes check_stability_ceilings fails loudly instead of the table drifting.

title: The model build is bit-reproducible only from one absolute path, so no worktree can produce a registered binary
description:
notes/audits/aocl-and-model-build-flags.md:73-74 states the model build is bit-reproducible: same sources, same flags, same compiler give a byte-identical executable. MEASURED 2026-08-25 and the claim needs one more term. Building T21 l10 p16 production from a git worktree whose vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src is byte-identical to the main checkout's (diff -rq reports no difference) gives sha 139866b6541c6393 against the manifest's 9152c06dc9b6be09. The cause is model.compile_flags.f90_opts carrying -g: the DWARF records absolute source and build paths, and 'strings' finds 343 occurrences of the worktree path in the executable it does not find in the main checkout's.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is what makes this worth a row rather than a footnote: rebuild_binaries.py --verify run in a worktree reports every locally built binary as absent from the manifest, and any consumer check against binary_manifest.json refuses it. So a worktree can compile the model -- which is the one way to verify a Fortran change, and the shared briefing tells agents to do exactly that -- and cannot then run anything through the registry check. The route that works today is build_model.py --no-publish plus run_exoplasim.py --binary, which stamps the run as an arm; that is correct for an experiment and wrong as the only way to run the model you just built.

Do: state the path dependence beside the reproducibility claim, and settle whether the build should be path-independent (-fdebug-prefix-map or -ffile-prefix-map against the repo root, which keeps -g's usefulness and makes the sha a function of the source alone) or whether a per-checkout manifest is the right model. The first would also let one manifest describe every checkout.
close_reason:
FIXED. The cause is not -g. gfortran stores the source path of every I/O statement in .rodata for its runtime diagnostics; that string survives with no debug flags at all, and the path reaches it through the cpp line markers CMake's preprocess-and-scan writes, which gcc(1) states -ffile-prefix-map does not remap ('Directories referenced by directives are not affected'). Measured: 343 such lines carried the build root. CMake's Ninja generator always hands the compiler an absolute source path (verified for a source dir inside the bin dir and for a generated file in the bin dir), and its Fortran preprocess rule carries no launcher hook, so no flag and no generator arrangement reaches it.

exoplasim/scripts/prefix_map_launcher.py applies the -ffile-prefix-map options ALREADY on the compile line to those markers, registered by build_model.py as CMAKE_Fortran_COMPILER_LAUNCHER. plasim/CMakeLists.txt keeps the declaration: the binary-directory map lost its trailing slash so it now reaches DW_AT_comp_dir, and the SHTns prefix is mapped because the include's path reaches the line table.

ACCEPTANCE TEST, and it can fail: exoplasim/scripts/verify_build_path_independence.py stages the driver, config and plasim/src into two roots differing in depth and length, shows the two stagings byte-identical, builds each through build_model.py itself and compares. T21 l10 p16 production is 599021395fd30d3c from both. Negative control, same source and same CMakeLists with the launcher removed: ef1de3eb99b44e43 against 3d88e3c121622de1. No absolute path remains in the executable and the runtime diagnostics now name the bare source file.

rebuild_binaries.py stamps build_inputs (the shas of plasim/CMakeLists.txt and the launcher) because both change every executable and nothing hashed either; assert_launcher_registered() reads the wiring back out of build_model.py.

The published binaries are not rebuilt here (the machine claim is held elsewhere) and --verify now reports the drift. One manifest can describe every checkout once they are.

title: The radiation's pow calls are scalar because every one sits inside a where block
description:
Found while pricing clim-84. Retired-instruction measurement and a compiled object, both in exoplasim/notes/radiation-scheme-price.md.

THE FINDING. All 22 non-integer ** sites in swr and lwr are inside where/elsewhere blocks. GCC does not vectorise a masked array assignment, so libmvec's eight-wide pow is never reached. Compiling radmod.f90 with the declared flag line and reading the object confirms it: nm -u lists pow, exp, log, log10 and the vector _ZGVeN8v_exp, _ZGVeN8v_log, _ZGVeN8v_sin, _ZGVeN8v_cos, and NO _ZGVeN8vv_pow. Relocations: 87 scalar pow call sites, 146 scalar exp, 98 scalar log, 25 log10, against 169 vector exp and 44 vector log.

WHAT IT IS WORTH. Masked scalar pow is 116 retired instructions per element; the same expression written so GCC can vectorise it is 15.2, a factor of 7.6. Masked scalar exp is 45.3 against 5.1 vectorised, 8.9. The whole of radiation's libm share is 9.74 percent of T170 (pow 6.69, log 1.70), which is the ceiling on any of this.

WHY IT IS A DECISION AND NOT A FIX. Three reasons, and they need the user.
1. It is not bit-identical. libmvec's vector routines carry a looser ULP bound than the scalar ones, so every result moves. Rule 4 also applies: it is a model source change and every published binary goes stale.
2. The masks are not decoration. They select between two absorptance formulas by path amount -- Sasamori below a threshold, a logarithmic form above it -- so removing them means evaluating both branches. merge() was measured and does NOT recover the vectorisation: 107 instructions per element, indistinguishable from where.
3. It may be wasted work. clim-84's verdict is that a band-resolved swap is not refused on cost, and a swap deletes lwr and swr outright. This is the same wasted-work argument clim-84 makes about the exp/log identity, applied to a larger prize.

DO NOT take this without clim-61 being settled first.
notes:
2026-08-25. THIS COMPOUNDS WITH CLIM-59'S FOUR-BYTE ARM AND NEITHER MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN WITH THE OTHER IN PLACE.

The mechanism, corrected by the user: FP32's gain is not memory bandwidth, it is SIMD LANES. This host is znver4 with AVX-512 and the build uses -march=znver4, so a vector register holds 16 floats against 8 doubles and everything that vectorises does twice the work per instruction. Pure lane-doubling would be about 2x; CLIM-59 measures 27.5 per cent at T21 and 39.2 per cent at T85, six of six paired rounds each, with the T85 figure independently reproducing 39.69 per cent taken at T170 on a different bed on a different day.

So the shortfall against 2x is dominated by work that does not vectorise at all -- which is precisely this row's subject. CLIM-84 established that every non-integer ** in the radiation sits inside a where block, that compiled radmod.o references scalar pow and no _ZGVeN8vv_pow, and that masked scalar pow costs 116 instructions per element against 5.1 for a vector exp.

THE CONSEQUENCE: fixing the masking moves work OUT of the bucket four bytes cannot help and INTO the bucket where four bytes doubles the lanes. The two should exceed either alone. It also explains the rung scaling without appealing to working set: the mix shifts, because at T85 the spectral transforms take a larger share against a physics column count that grows more slowly.

DO NOT GUESS THE SIZE OF IT -- BENCH IT. The user's instruction. The experiment is a paired interleaved A/B on the pattern CLIM-59 used, arm order flipped each round, on one bed per rung, and it needs FOUR arms rather than two because the question is whether they compound: FP64 masked, FP64 vectorised, FP32 masked, FP32 vectorised. Anything less measures one effect while the other is held at an arbitrary setting. Round-to-round self-scatter must be reported, not just the mean; CLIM-59's T21 arm was refused outright by bench_ab at 37.2 per cent self-scatter while T85 passed as readable-but-noisy at 24.5, so bed length matters and short beds will not settle this.

The sequencing constraint from CLIM-84 still stands and is not softened by any of the above: this change is NOT bit-identical, merge() was measured and does not recover it at 107 instructions per element, and it must not be taken before CLIM-61 settles. What has changed is only that the case for taking it is stronger than the instruction count alone suggested.

2026-08-25, MEASURED. Four arms at T21 NLEV 10 on sixteen threads, paired and interleaved with the starting arm rotated by round, three instruments: exoplasim/notes/masked-radiation-and-four-bytes.md, with every round in exoplasim/analysis/radiation_mask_arms_*.json.

THEY COMPOUND AND THEIR GAINS MULTIPLY. Against the eight-byte masked model, on a host at load 1.49 with nothing else running: unmasking lwr's four absorptance selections -4.25 per cent of wall clock [-3.68, -4.30], four bytes -25.53 [-24.67, -26.17], both -27.63 [-27.33, -28.99], against -28.53 predicted by multiplying the two alone. Self-scatter 0.37 to 1.87 per cent, six of six rounds in every arm, nothing dropped. The excess over the multiplicative prediction is 0.34 points on a bed that resolves about 1.85, so THE INTERACTION IS NOT RESOLVED IN COST and is recorded as consistent with multiplying. In retired instructions it IS resolved and is sub-multiplicative by 3.40 points with a spread of 0.0013: both changes act on the same work, because unmasking's whole effect is to hand the radiation's pow to the vectoriser where four bytes has already halved what a lane costs. The row's hypothesis is right in its conclusion and wrong in its arithmetic - they overlap rather than stack.

THE FOUR-BYTE ARM REPRODUCES CLIM-59 INDEPENDENTLY: 25.53 per cent on the clock and 26.93 in cycles against that row's 27.5 at T21, different bed, different day, different instrument.

THE LARGEST FINDING WAS NOT THE QUESTION. Removing the masks takes 23.79 per cent off the model's RETIRED INSTRUCTIONS and 4.25 per cent off its CLOCK. IPC falls from 1.601 to 1.292. The masked scalar pow calls were largely hidden - independent per element, no carried dependence, absorbed by an out-of-order window. CLIM-84's per-element counts stand; reading a factor of 7.6 in instructions as a factor of 7.6 in cost does not, and that inference is what radiation-scheme-price.md's two-scheme comparison rests on. Noted on CLIM-61.

SAFETY, and it is what makes the arm admissible: all eight expressions already carry an unconditional floor inside the argument - max(0.,.) before each fractional power, max(1.E-30,.) before each logarithm - so both branches are finite on every lane and neither can raise what -ffpe-trap catches. probe_unmasked_absorptance.f90 shows the two forms bit identical over 65536 elements spanning fourteen decades plus the exact thresholds and exact zero, in both precisions, with vectorisation off. With it on the maximum absolute difference is 2.2e-16 at eight bytes and 1.2e-7 at four, on absorptances bounded into [0,1]: that is libmvec's ULP bound and nothing else, so the restructuring is exact and only the library moves results.

NOT ADOPTED. The sequencing constraint stands and the measurement makes the case for taking it WEAKER rather than stronger: 4.25 per cent of wall clock at T21, falling as the rung rises, for a change that moves every result and makes every published binary stale. radmod.f90 is left masked; exoplasim/scripts/patch_unmasked_absorptance.py holds the arm and carries both forms verbatim so neither can drift. This row stays OPEN behind CLIM-61.

WHAT IS NOT MEASURED: one rung only. The radiation's share falls as the rung rises while four bytes rises, so the interaction is a T21 number. The eighteen ** sites outside lwr's level-pair loop were left alone: swr's where(losun) blocks elide work rather than select a formula, so unmasking them computes the shortwave on the night side, and one raises zmu0**1.7 on a negative cosine.

title: The wetland extent gate assumes a saturated fraction that hydrography has withdrawn
description:
`biosphere/scripts/wetland_gate.py` refuses a wetland extent whose
`extent.saturated_fraction_support` is anything but `climate_grid`, and
`biosphere/notes/wetland-activation-contract.md` section 3 gives the reason:
GW-26 settled that a saturated fraction is a fraction of a climate-grid cell's
land population and a native-mesh one has no population to be a fraction of.

That refusal is still correct and is not what this row is about. What has
changed is that the fraction itself no longer exists. `world-n9sd` withdrew the
saturated-area closure: `hydrography/config/topographic_index.yaml` carries
`closure.status: withdrawn`, `build_topographic_index.py` implements no closure
and its artifact carries no `f_sat`, and `build_wetness.py` forms no saturated
mineral class. The withdrawal is the disposition that config declared for a
missed score before any fraction was computed, and the score missed;
`hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md` section 7 also measures that no
narrower criterion could have licensed it, because the gain is at or below the
scatter the score's own support puts on it on every arm.

So a wetland extent keyed on a saturated fraction has no source. The gate's
current state is not wrong -- `biosphere/config/wetlands.yaml` declares
`saturated_fraction_support: undeclared` and the gate refuses that too, so
nothing has been let through -- but the refusal it would give names the wrong
reason, and `_satisfiable_declaration`'s fixture sets `climate_grid` as though
a satisfiable extent were one declaration away.

Do: decide what a wetland extent is keyed on now that no saturated fraction is
published, then say so in `wetlands.yaml` and in the gate's refusal text. The
two candidates hydrography can actually supply are the RESOLVED fields --
`water_table.nc`'s `at_surface` and `seepage_m3_s` per region, which is what
SURF-7 was redirected to for the same reason -- and `wetness_<grid>.nc`'s
resolved class shares. Whether either is a wetland extent is the decision; a
saturated fraction is not available to be one.
notes:
HANDOVER from the hydrography side, fanout-Y8. biosphere/ is not this agent's to edit; what follows is what hydrography can and cannot supply, established against the artifacts and configs, plus the exact edit that follows from it.

PREMISE RE-CONFIRMED. hydrography/config/topographic_index.yaml carries
closure.status: withdrawn, withdrawn_because
the_declared_score_missed_and_no_narrower_support_can_resolve_the_gain.
build_topographic_index.py implements no closure. build_wetness.py forms no
saturated_mineral class and refuses if that status ever says anything else.
subgrid-water-table.md section 7 measures the instrument: on all eight arms of
both Earth bore sets the gain the terrain half carries over the cell-mean depth
is at or below the spread the SUPPORT puts on it, and the support is 34 and 37
cells, so a criterion restricted to fewer cells resolves it less. Reviving a
saturated fraction needs a different INSTRUMENT -- an areal saturation or
inundation observation -- not a narrower criterion.

1. NO WETLAND EXTENT CAN BE KEYED ON A SATURATED FRACTION AT ANY SUPPORT. The
gate's WET-EXTENT-SUPPORT-NOT-GRID refusal accepts climate_grid, which is now
the one value naming a field nothing publishes. Its statement is still true and
is no longer the operative one.

2. THE THREE CLASSES HYDROGRAPHY RESOLVES TODAY ARE NOT WETLANDS. wetness.yaml
resolves open_water (the solved equilibrium lake surface), playa (the exposed
floor of a closed basin that does not fill) and dry_mineral (the residual, named
as one). None of the three is a wetland, so wetness_<grid>.nc's resolved class
shares cannot supply a wetland extent as they stand: it would be a fourth class
that does not exist.

3. TWO CANDIDATES, WITH THEIR COST AND THEIR LICENCE.

(a) water_table.nc at_surface and seepage_m3_s, per region. Where the solved
table meets the surface -- a groundwater DISCHARGE extent. Resolved, so it has a
support; crosses to the grid as a categorical area share through
lib/gridding.py:cell_fraction; needs no closure, which is why SURF-7 was
redirected to it. IT DOES NOT EXIST: hydrography/data/<build>/ carries no
water_table.nc on either registered build, nor any topographic_index_*.nc or
wetness_*.nc. Cost is the groundwater step then groundwater_access, both
cost: minutes in config/pipeline.yaml, with groundwater needing surface_water and
a baseline climatology first -- and config/planet.yaml carries
baseline_climatology: null, so it is blocked behind that.
LICENCE, and it travels with the extent or the extent is not licensed: the depth
field scores 0.4581 against Earth's Australian bores, below the 0.5 of no
discrimination, and 0.6655 on the United States unconfined set. It works where
lateral flow sets the head and not where the local sink does.
groundwater_access_<grid>.nc reports the sink_fraction regime share per cell,
including its two kinds of no-answer. A tile mixing the licensed regime with the
unlicensed one is a number with no verdict attached, which is what wetness.yaml's
refusals.area_proxy_from_cell_mean refuses in the other direction.

(b) surface_water.nc's per-bin closed-basin lake area -- seasonal inundation.
The quantity EXISTS per basin. The crossing to regions is world-9iy5, the same
paint_lakes operation once per bin. It is only the closed-basin third of the
seasonal quantity: a floodplain's inundated area needs a
height-above-nearest-drainage CDF and a routing model, neither of which exists
and neither of which should have an owner yet, and a seasonally saturated SOIL is
a water content rather than an area.

4. WHAT IS STILL A BIOSPHERE DECISION. Whether a groundwater discharge extent IS
a wetland extent. It is a change of quantity: at_surface says the solved table
reaches the surface, which is necessary for a wetland and not sufficient --
persistence and the vegetation's use of it are what wetlands.yaml's own
regime_selector would have to carry. Hydrography can say what the field is and
where it is licensed; it cannot say that it is a wetland.

5. THE EXACT EDIT, all of it in biosphere/.
 - biosphere/config/wetlands.yaml: extent.saturated_fraction_support stops being
   the field the extent is keyed on. Add extent.source naming the hydrography
   artifact and field, from the closed set {water_table.nc:at_surface,
   surface_water.nc per-bin closed-basin lake area, none}. KEEP
   saturated_fraction_support and keep it meaning what hydrography's own
   wetness.yaml:196 says it means -- the support any REVIVED closure would have
   to live at, a refusal that does not depend on the closure existing -- so the
   two configs agree on one reading of one field.
 - wetland_gate.py:_extent_refusals: add a refusal that fires on climate_grid
   too, whose reason is the WITHDRAWAL and not the support. Cite
   hydrography/config/topographic_index.yaml closure.status, build_wetness.py
   forming no saturated class, and subgrid-water-table.md section 7 for why no
   narrower criterion can license one. An extent keyed on a saturated fraction is
   refused because the fraction does not exist.
 - wetland_gate.py:_satisfied (near the candidate["extent"] block): stop
   setting saturated_fraction_support to climate_grid. That fixture exists to
   show the gate is satisfiable in principle, and setting the withdrawn quantity
   makes it assert something false -- that a satisfiable extent is one
   declaration away. It should set the new extent.source instead.
 - biosphere/notes/wetland-activation-contract.md section 3: the support argument
   stays and stops being the reason. Rewrite rather than mark.

6. NOTHING TO FIX ON THE HYDROGRAPHY SIDE. wetness.yaml, build_wetness.py,
topographic_index.yaml, subgrid-water-table.md and hydrography/README.md all
already state the withdrawal and what each waiting row takes. Checked this pass.

BLOCKED ON OWNERSHIP, not on a question. Leaving open for the biosphere owner.

2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER, from a pass over the needs-decision set.
RECLASSIFIED, an investigation, not a decision: which of the two resolved fields hydrography can supply is a wetland extent is answerable from the artifacts.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
VERIFIED AND ACTED ON, with two corrections to the row.

PREMISE HOLDS. topographic_index.yaml carries closure.status: withdrawn,
withdrawn_because the_declared_score_missed_and_no_narrower_support_can_resolve_the_gain.
build_topographic_index.py implements no closure and writes no f_sat; what it
writes is the index per region and f_sat_max, the terrain rank statistic.
build_wetness.py forms no saturated_mineral class and raises if that status ever
says anything else. Nothing in biosphere/ or hydrography/ computes a saturated
fraction another way: the only occurrences of the name outside those two
scripts and the notes were wetlands.yaml's declaration field and the gate.
Neither topographic_index_*.nc, wetness_*.nc nor water_table.nc exists on any
build under hydrography/data.

CORRECTION 1. The row says the crossing of surface_water.nc's per-bin
closed-basin lake area to regions "is world-9iy5". world-9iy5 is CLOSED and the
crossing exists: surface_water.nc on canonical-10m-base and on
