canonical-10m-carve2 carries lake_cycle_decided, lake_cycle_fraction and
lake_cycle_bins_wet over region x time_bin. That candidate is published today,
not pending.

CORRECTION 2. The row and the handover state the reopening condition as "a
different INSTRUMENT -- an areal saturation or inundation observation -- not a
narrower criterion". subgrid-water-table.md section 7, which owns the route,
states it as SUPPORT: enough grid cells carrying observations to put a gain of a
few thousandths of an AUC above the cells' own scatter, where two continents of
bores gave 34 and 37. More cells is one way to get there and an areal instrument
is another. The refusal text now states it as its producer does.

DEAD CODE OR FAIL-CLOSED CONTRACT: fail-closed, and the clause was reachable
rather than dead. saturated_fraction_support was a live PRECONDITION producing a
refusal on every invocation, so no input was unreachable. The defect was in the
ACCEPT branch: climate_grid was the one value it admitted and it names a field
nothing publishes, so a single edit to wetlands.yaml would have cleared that
precondition while no fraction existed, and _satisfied set exactly that value,
asserting that a satisfiable extent was one declaration away. Deleting the
clause would have LOOSENED a gate whose whole subject is a quantity that has
gone.

THE ANSWER TO THE INVESTIGATION. Neither resolved field is a wetland extent,
because a wetland extent is not one field. WET-2's classification is a PARTITION
of five classes, and the two candidates each supply at most one of them:
lake_cycle_fraction is the closed-basin part of seasonal inundation, at_surface
would be evidence toward the saturated mineral class and does not exist. So the
declaration is now one source PER CLASS, from a closed set, with each named
artifact checked against the builds under hydrography/data.

CHANGED.
- wetlands.yaml: extent.class_sources, five classes each undeclared;
  saturated_fraction_support moved out of the preconditions and declared
  climate_grid, the same reading as wetness.yaml refusals.saturated_fraction_support
  -- the support any REVIVED closure would live at, which supplies no fraction.
- wetland_gate.py: EXTENT_CLASSES, EXTENT_SOURCES and WITHDRAWN_SOURCE; a probe
  that reads hydrography's closure declaration on every invocation rather than
  carrying a copy of the verdict; a probe over which named artifacts any build
  carries. Six new refusals: CLASS-SOURCE-WITHDRAWN (what a reader meets today,
  carrying the withdrawal and both reopening routes), SATURATED-FRACTION-WITHDRAWN,
  CLASS-SOURCE-UNKNOWN, CLASS-SOURCE-NOT-PUBLISHED, CLASS-ABSENT-UNLICENSED,
  CLOSURE-REVIVED and CLOSURE-UNREADABLE. _satisfied no longer sets
  saturated_fraction_support; it declares the saturated mineral class absent
  under a WET-12 licence, which is the only route that satisfies the gate.
  Fixtures 22 -> 29, all passing.
- wetland-activation-contract.md section 3 rewritten and section 7 step 2 with it;
  biosphere/README.md; the awetland_area_native.out reason, which blamed the
  support rather than the absence.
- subgrid-water-table.md: "WET-2 has one support and three classes and does not
  carry that cost" now says what the cost actually is.
- scripts/smoke_test.py: check_withdrawn_closure_has_no_consumer. Fails if the
  closure is revived, if wetness.yaml stops declaring the class absent, if a
  biosphere class is keyed on the withdrawn fraction or on a source outside the
  gate's closed set, or if the two components drift on saturated_fraction_support.
  All five branches exercised against a mutated copy of the tree.

title: pyburn._transformvar and _transformvectorvar reference four names that do not exist
description: An AST sweep of vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/pyburn.py for names loaded and never bound finds four besides the readallvariables break that has been repaired: 'vairable' in _transformvar (line 839, plainly a typo for 'variable'), 'nlats' in _transformvar (966-968), and 'variable' and 'gpvuar' and 'rottlgridvar' in _transformvectorvar (1091, 1095, 1204, 1356). Each sits inside a branch, so the function raises NameError only when that branch is taken and the postprocessor otherwise runs. Which branch each is, and whether any Vesper output stream reaches it, is the first question; a name that cannot be reached is a deletion and a name that can is a repair. The sweep script is an ast walk comparing Load names against module-level bindings, function locals, arguments, comprehension targets and builtins.
notes:
BRANCHES AND ORIGIN, 2026-08-25 (line numbers after the readallvariables restore in 5dcdf64b).

UPSTREAM, not fork-introduced. All four names are present with the same counts in the first version of vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/pyburn.py this repo has, so they came in with the vendored ExoPlaSim and have never executed there either. Worth a row in docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md and an upstream report.

WHICH BRANCH REACHES EACH. pyburn's _transformvar and _transformvectorvar dispatch on a 'mode' argument: grid, spectral, fourier, synchronous, syncfourier. THIS PROJECT ONLY EVER PASSES mode="grid" -- six call sites, in run_exoplasim.py, continue_exoplasim.py and run_stellar_cycle.py, all 'grid'. So four of the five are unreachable from anything here:

  vairable        _transformvar:905          mode spectral, spectral input, len(shape)==1
  nlats           _transformvar:1032-1034    mode syncfourier, 'lat' in dims
  gpvuar          _transformvectorvar:1270   mode synchronous, spectral input, len(uvar.shape)==3
  rottlgridvar    _transformvectorvar:1422   mode syncfourier, len(rottlgriduvar.shape)==4
  nlats           _transformvectorvar:1403-5 mode syncfourier

THE FIFTH IS THE ONE TO LOOK AT. The name 'variable' at _transformvectorvar:1157 and :1161 is under mode == 'grid', a SPECTRAL vector pair, in the else arm of len(uvar.shape)==3 -- so a two-dimensional (time, spectral) vector pair with no level axis. It reads variable.shape[1] where uvar.shape[1] and vvar.shape[1] are meant; the name is a copy-paste from _transformvar, which does have a 'variable'. Nothing this project writes appears to take it -- the (u,v) pairs the model writes spectrally carry a level axis, and the surface vector fields are written as grid -- but it is in the mode we actually use, so 'unreachable' needs to be established rather than assumed. That is the first question on this row.

vairable, gpvuar and rottlgridvar are MISSPELLINGS of names bound in the same scope, not omissions, which is why they have survived: the branch has never executed anywhere. The failure they would give is the one world-ro6 just gave us -- a NameError in the postprocessor after a run has already integrated its orbits.
close_reason: Repaired all five names in pyburn.py (vairable->variable, nlats->nlat x2 sites, variable->uvar/vvar, gpvuar->gpuvar, rottlgridvar->rottlgriduvar) and four more the same sweep found in gcmt.py (fname, lf.filestem->self.filestem, eqstream(file)->eqstream(dataset), zlon->lon). Each had a right answer bound in the same scope. Also repaired _transformvectorvar's syncfourier loop, which gave each of the two arrays one half of the joined meridian where the scalar loop writes both halves of its one array -- fixing only the names would have replaced a NameError with half an array of zeros. All upstream: every one is present in subtree-import commit 28abfadd, recorded in docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md for reporting. Nothing this project runs reaches any of them: all six call sites pass mode='grid'. The generalisation is a new smoke_test gate, 'no name is loaded that nothing binds', asked of CPython's symtable over this project's Python and the model's; self-tested against a pyburn.py with readallvariables deleted the way world-ro6 deleted it, where it names readfile:641. Follow-up world-yzhs filed for the theta/thetah forward reference the narrower criterion correctly does not report. Commit 4d79249e.

title: Route the four remaining staged-albedo reads through provenance.staged_surface_field
description:
world-xgtj put the one door in lib/provenance.py:staged_surface_field and wired
pedology/scripts/build_surface_classes.py through it. Four call sites still build
exoplasim/inputs/<rung>/orogen_<RUNG>_surf_0174.sra by hand from model.resolution
and record nothing about which build's field they read:

  hydrography/scripts/carve_verdict.py
  hydrography/scripts/export_carve_list.py
  hydrography/scripts/surface_water.py
  exoplasim/scripts/dust_forcing.py

They were left in this state because the batch that added the door did not own
those files; the work is the same three lines each, and build_surface_classes.py
is the worked example.

Do: replace each hand-built path with staged_surface_field(174, config), read the
file at the record's path, and stamp the record into the product that script
writes. The carve path additionally needs a --for-build flag threaded to
staged_surface_field, because the overshoot measurement is a DELIBERATE
cross-build read: the staged albedo is the right one while the carved build is
staged and the wrong one for anything re-run on the pre-carve build afterwards.
The declaration NAMES the build, so it admits that build and refuses every other.

Source: notes/audits/carve-overshoot.md, world-xgtj
close_reason: All four call sites now resolve through provenance.staged_surface_field(174, config) and stamp the returned record into their own product: staged_background_albedo in carve_verdict.json, in carve_list.json's sidecar, in surface_water_report.json, and in place of the bare path in dust_forcing's surface_field block and per-cell netCDF metadata. carve_verdict.py and export_carve_list.py take --for-build, which declares the deliberate cross-build read by NAMING the build, admitting that one and refusing every other. climate_terms lost its now-unused resolution parameter. notes/audits/carve-overshoot.md's paragraph rewritten from defect to arrangement. A sweep of every path built under exoplasim/inputs/ found one further reader outside this issue -- analyze_smoke.py, whose rung comes from the run being analysed rather than the config, so the door needs a rung argument; filed as world-miy4 rather than bodged, along with the note that run_exoplasim.py:surface_sra builds the same path legitimately as the staging step. smoke_test 31/31 with --skip-compile. Commit a4fd0c1f.

title: spectral_tail.py reports a tail slope fitted across the roundoff-dead top of the rung
description:
exoplasim/scripts/spectral_tail.py cuts the spectrum at m = NTRU before fitting anything, so the FFT band above the model's truncation -- the only place the floating-point roundoff floor is visible -- is discarded and the script cannot measure a floor at all.

Its two CRITERIA are unaffected and stay: the bite point is the FIRST wavenumber whose ratio to the extrapolated inertial range falls below 1/EXCESS_FACTOR, so roundoff at the top cannot move it, and the pile-up test looks for excess ABOVE the law.

Its reported tail_slope is affected. It is fitted over m = NTRU/3 .. NTRU, and at T42 the last four wavenumbers of that band are at or near roundoff: measured eddy kinetic energy falls 10.3 dex between m=35 and m=42 against a floor of 2.6e-15. A tail slope of -39, which the script's own docstring quotes as what a heavily over-damped run gives, is that artifact rather than a property of the damping.

Evidence: exoplasim/notes/filter-spectral-price.md, sections 'The top of every rung is dead' and 'How many zonal wavenumbers a rung carries'; exoplasim/analysis/rung_spectral_budget.json.

Do: give spectral_tail.py the roundoff floor filter_spectral_cost.py already measures -- keep the FFT band above NTRU, take the floor as its median, and either end the tail fit at the last wavenumber standing FLOOR_MARGIN clear of it or refuse to report a tail slope. Whichever, the reported number has to say which wavenumbers it was fitted over. Do not change the two criteria.
close_reason: spectral_tail.py keeps the FFT band above NTRU, measures the roundoff floor as its median (the same measurement filter_spectral_cost.py makes), and ends the tail fit at the last wavenumber standing FLOOR_MARGIN=100 clear of it, naming the band beside the slope and refusing where no dead band exists. FLOOR_MARGIN is now defined once, in spectral_tail.py, and imported by filter_spectral_cost.py. The two criteria are untouched and still read on m<=NTRU, so no verdict changes. Guarded by a new smoke_test check with a right answer: a synthetic T42 tail of known slope on a roundoff floor, which the old band returns as about -23 whatever it is given. Note filter-spectral-price.md's paragraph on this rewritten; exoplasim/README.md row updated. Stale artifact tracked separately. Commit e0af9378.

title: Preserved basins lose their depression to the drainage conditioning, 18 of them entirely
description:
A preserved basin is a promise that the drainage conditioning will not carve an
outlet through it. On both registered builds the conditioning takes relief out
of nearly every preserved basin anyway, and out of a few it takes all of it.

Measured 2026-08-25 from `basins.preserved[].finalPreserved` in each manifest,
and from `capacity_km3` in `hydrography/data/<build>/basins.nc`. BOTH BUILDS ARE
PRE-CARVE and neither carries a preserve or carve list -- `drainageHypothesis`
is empty on both -- so nothing below is a verdict being honoured.

| build | preserved | retainedFraction < 1 | retainedFraction == 0 | median retainedFraction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| precarve-craton | 3,621 | 2,988 | 3 | 0.796 |
| precarve-craton-10m | 9,419 | 7,702 | 18 | 0.804 |

The 18 at 10M are exactly the ones a downstream water balance cannot use: 16 of
them carry `capacity_km3` of exactly zero in `basins.nc`, so they are preserved
closed basins that impound nothing.

The cause is NOT the depth floor and not the height-curve saturation. On
precarve-craton-10m none of the 16 is shallow -- their published `depthKm` runs
from 0.046 to 1.644 km, and 15 of the 16 clear the declared 0.05 km floor in
kilometres, so `world-yril` making the floor physical leaves every one of them
in the catalogue. Their `finalPreserved.spillDepth` is 0: the depression the
catalogue measured on the pre-conditioning surface is not on the final terrain.

Two questions, and they are separate:

- Is a median retained fraction of about 0.80 the intended behaviour of
  `buildBasinProtection` and `priorityFloodCarve`, or is protection leaking?
  `vendor/orogen/tools/test-basins.mjs` asserts that preserved basins keep
  their rims, and it passes, so whatever it asserts is not this.
- Should a basin whose relief the conditioning removes entirely still be
  published as preserved? It is published with `selectedBy: 'threshold'`,
  `retain: 1` and a hypsometry curve computed on the pre-conditioning surface,
  none of which the final terrain supports.

Do: decide what a preserved basin is entitled to, then either fix the
conditioning or refuse to publish a basin whose `finalPreserved.spillDepth` is
zero as preserved. `notes/audits/basin-catalogue-floor.md` carries the
measurement.
close_reason:
Settled. Protection is NOT leaking: its contract covers the drainage-enforcement carve only, assertDividesNotLowered proves it holds at both call sites, and the relief loss comes from mechanisms the pipeline deliberately leaves enabled -- erosion over protected cells, the unprotected sink, and sharpenRidges/applySoilCreep which take no protection and run after the carve. A sixth of the preserved population comes out DEEPER, which a breach cannot produce. So a median retained fraction of 0.80 is intended behaviour.

What was not honest was the publication, and that is fixed: Basin.still_closed, basins.nc has_impoundment / natural_spill_depth / retained_fraction, BasinSet.has_impoundment, and export_carve_list.py now counts the basins whose retain comes from the 1 m depth guard rather than from a water balance and says so in the header and sidecar. No verdict, retain, capacity or hypsometry value changes.

The basins are NOT refused publication as preserved: their depression exists on the next generation's pre-conditioning surface, so a preserve instruction for them is still meaningful, and dropping them from preserved[] would break the drainage_terminal and finalCatchment.rootSink references. Naming the state is the fix; deleting the record is not.

Larger finding split out as world-74rx: retain crosses the interface on two different depth bases and the marginal class is the only class it does not carry. notes/audits/basin-catalogue-floor.md carries both measurements.

title: somdynam.cpp's phosphorus divergences have no register and no gate
description:
Worldbuilding: this is about the vendored LPJ-GUESS-CNP fork's simulated soil phosphorus.

vendor/lpj-guess/modules/somdynam.cpp now carries a declared divergence from the
vendored CNP fork -- PMASS_SAT, the labile-P saturation threshold, converted into
the fork's own Hedley-labile currency by 6.6 under WORLD-Z01O -- and it is
recorded only in a source comment and in
biosphere/notes/phosphorus-cycle-parameterisation.md.

modules/ntransform.cpp has the pattern this should follow:
biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml holds mainline_divergences with a verdict, what
settles it and what it is worth, and biosphere/scripts/ntransform_gate.py checks
BOTH halves of every entry -- that mainline's form is recorded in the source, that
it is not what the model runs once comments are stripped, and that the changed
line still is. So a divergence there can become neither a silent fork nor a
silent revert. somdynam.cpp has neither, so PMASS_SAT can be reverted to 0.002
with the record left behind and nothing will say so.

Note one structural difference: ntransform.cpp diverges from LPJ-GUESS release
4.1.1, which the tree can name by Zenodo record and SVN revision. somdynam.cpp's
phosphorus is the CNP fork's own, so the reference point is the vendored subtree
commit and not a release, and the register has to say so.

Do: add biosphere/config/somdynam.yaml (or extend an existing phosphorus
declaration) with mainline_divergences on the ntransform.yaml schema, and a gate
that checks it on the same three conditions. The gate belongs in
scripts/smoke_test.py's list if the other gates are there.

Source: docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md, biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml,
biosphere/scripts/ntransform_gate.py, biosphere/notes/phosphorus-cycle-parameterisation.md
close_reason: biosphere/config/somdynam.yaml registers the three phosphorus divergences from the vendored CNP fork (pmass_sat_labile_currency, surfhumus_ptoc_ramp, surfhumus_ptoc_init -- the premise named only the first) and biosphere/scripts/somdynam_gate.py checks them on ntransform_gate.py's three conditions plus the ramps and invariants those constants drive. The reference point is the subtree commit b368b893, not a release, and the gate refuses a register naming no 40-hex commit. Registered in config/pipeline.yaml as a needs of lpj_run, in biosphere/README.md, and in docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md, whose 'there is no somdynam.yaml and no gate' paragraph is rewritten. Verified against five in-memory reverts of the real source; each caught. Commit 4babaa40.

title: swr's cloud arrays are read but never written when NCLOUDS = 0
description:
Found while settling clim-68. radmod.f90's swr declares zrcl1, zrcl2, zrcl1s, zrcl2s, ztcl2 and ztcl2s as automatic locals (NHOR,NLEV) and writes them ONLY inside 'if (nclouds==1)'. Every read of them further down is guarded by a multiplication rather than a branch -- zrcl1(:,jlev)*dcc(:,jlev)*nclouds in the range-1 reflectivity, zrcl2/zrcl2s in the range-2 pair, and (1.-ztcl2(:,jlev))*dcc(:,jlev)*nclouds in the transmissivity -- so at NCLOUDS = 0 the factor is zero and the operand is whatever the stack held. Zero times a stale non-finite word is not zero, and the FPE trap is armed inside the radiation.

This is the same class as world-5a0 and world-bhs, which preset swr's other scratch for exactly this reason and left comments saying so; those two covered the where-mask lanes, not the nclouds branch.

UNREACHABLE BY CONFIGURATION TODAY: NCLOUDS = 0 is set only by exoplasim/__init__.py's columnmode='clear' path, and 'columnmode' appears nowhere in this project outside vendor/. clim-68 also now stages NSWRCL but not NCLOUDS.

Do: preset the six arrays to the clear-sky values (reflectivities 0, transmissivities 1) above the 'if (nclouds==1)', with the comment saying why, and stage NCLOUDS alongside NSWRCL in run_exoplasim.py's configure_otherargs so a run records it. Bit-identical at NCLOUDS = 1, because both branches already write every element there. Rule 4: it is a model source change, so every published binary goes stale and all must be rebuilt.
close_reason: The six clear-sky presets the NSWRCL=1 arm already carried are hoisted above 'if (nclouds==1)', so they also cover NCLOUDS=0 where nothing wrote them. Minimal Fortran, since radmod.f90 belongs to another batch: six lines moved, nothing else touched. Bit-identical at NCLOUDS=1 -- the NSWRCL=0 arm writes every element of all six over its jlev loop and the NSWRCL=1 arm made the same preset itself. Reflectivity 0 and transmissivity 1 are what no cloud means, so the preset is the right answer, not merely a defined one. run_exoplasim.py stages NCLOUDS at radmod's compiled 1 beside NSWRCL and expected_namelist_keys checks it; continuations inherit it through the shared configure_otherargs. verify_model_compiles.py and lint_masked_domains.py both clean, smoke_test 32/32. Rule 4: every published binary is now stale and must be rebuilt; not done here because the batch forbids building on this host. Commit 69488106.

title: Background land albedo is staged per rung and not per build, and no consumer records which build's it read
description:
Five scripts read `exoplasim/inputs/<rung>/orogen_<RUNG>_surf_0174.sra` with the path built from `model.resolution` alone: hydrography/scripts/carve_verdict.py, hydrography/scripts/export_carve_list.py, hydrography/scripts/surface_water.py, pedology/scripts/build_surface_classes.py and aeolian/scripts/dust_forcing.py. config/pipeline.yaml shows `surface_albedo` writes that path per rung while being a loop A step, so the directory holds exactly one build's albedo at a time. Nothing checks which, and no verdict, report or sidecar records which it used.

Rule 5 says pointing one component at another's output is deliberate and never defaulted, and this is the one input on the carve path where the pairing is neither declared nor stamped. It bites hardest on the overshoot measurement, which is a DELIBERATE cross-build read by construction: the staged albedo is the right one while the carved build is staged and the wrong one for anything re-run on the pre-carve build afterwards, with no error either way.

Do: stamp the file's path and sha256 into every product that reads it, so the pairing is auditable after the fact, and give the two hydrography consumers an explicit flag for the declared cross-build case. Whether the file should be build-namespaced like hydrography/data/<build>/ is the larger question and reaches pedology, aeolian and the ExoPlaSim staging.

Source: notes/audits/carve-overshoot.md
close_reason: lib/provenance.py:staged_surface_field is the one door: it reads the provenance record beside the .sra, refuses a field staged from another build, refuses one with no record at all, and returns {path, sha256, terrain_hash, build} for the consumer to stamp. The deliberate cross-build read declares itself by NAMING the build, so it admits that build and still refuses every other including the active one -- a boolean would have let the silence back in. pedology/scripts/build_surface_classes.py reads code 174 through it and records the result. smoke_test carries a fixture guard built from lib/orogen.py's own registry, verified to fail when the build comparison is removed. The four remaining call sites -- the three hydrography ones and exoplasim/scripts/dust_forcing.py, including the --for-build flag the carve path needs -- are world-z7bu; this batch did not own those files.

title: The basin catalogue's depth floor is compared in model units and published in kilometres
description:
`selectBasins` compares a depression's depth in the model's DIMENSIONLESS elevation parameter against BASIN_MIN_DEPTH_KM, while the constant, `resolution.minDepthKm` and the published `selectionCriteria.minDepthKm` all name a physical depth. The model-unit-to-km curve is quartic above sea level, linear below it, and saturates at model elevation 1, so one threshold is many physical depths: measured over depressions within 2 per cent of the threshold, it demanded between 0.000 and 0.492 km with a median of 0.085 km on precarve-craton-10m. 22.1 per cent of the preserved set there is shallower than the declared floor, and 16 preserved basins have a lake capacity of exactly zero because they lie wholly above the saturation.

Comparing in model units is defensible: that is the currency the terrain noise the floor exists to reject lives in. What is not defensible is that no consumer can tell. basins.js now publishes `minDepthComparedIn` and `minDepthIsPhysical` so a reader of the manifest is not misled, which is the part that could be fixed without moving terrain.

This is now the floor that DECIDES the catalogue at the settled region count: relaxing it at 10M admits 2,521 basins against the area floor's 1,105 and the cell floor's 8. No refinement of the mesh moves it.

Do: decide whether the comparison should be `b.depthKm`. It is a criterion change, so it changes the preserved set and the terrain and costs a generation: 9,419 preserved becomes 7,471 at 10M, dropping 2,077 and admitting 129. Both directions are populated, so the floor is loose near sea level and tight on high ground rather than simply too loose. Belongs with the activation decision in hyd-20 and PHYS-13's ice mask, in one generation rather than three.

Source: notes/audits/basin-catalogue-floor.md
notes: Measured 2026-08-24 by hydrography/scripts/catalogue_floor.py on both registered builds; hydrography/analysis/catalogue_floor.json is the product. No selection logic was changed.
close_reason: FIXED. selectBasins now compares BASIN_MIN_DEPTH_KM against b.depthKm; the declared value stays 0.05 km. basinResolutionContext publishes minDepthComparedIn: 'km' and minDepthIsPhysical: true. test-basins.mjs gains a fixture whose depth and depthKm disagree in both directions so the currency is asserted rather than assumed. Nothing in source/ changes: a selection criterion reaches a catalogue only through a generation, and that generation is world-q5ig's; measured on the terrain now on disk it carries 9,419 preserved to 7,471 at 10M, dropping 2,077 and admitting 129. catalogue_floor.py now takes the currency from basins.resolution.minDepthComparedIn and treats a manifest without the field as the model-unit selection it was, so the reproduction control still reconstructs the selection each export was made with. Non-local: a physical depth floor is gravity-dependent because relief scales as 1/g while area does not, so the gravity test now asserts one-way shrinkage plus order-invariance of the survivors instead of set-identity. Discovered and filed as world-o3b6: the zero-capacity preserved basins are not the depth floor's doing.

title: Run loop A with the ice mask: bootstrap at --glacial 0, commission, then regenerate with --ice-mask
description:
PHYS-13 landed the generator half: vendor/orogen/js/glacial-ice.js takes the ice placement from outside, export-planet.mjs has --ice-mask FILE, analysis/ice_mask_freezing_height.py --write-mask produces it, and config/pipeline.yaml carries ice_mask as a step orogen needs. What remains is executing loop A, which is a generation and therefore the user's call.

The two passes, and why it cannot be one. Generate with --glacial 0, an honest null rather than an Earth-calibrated guess. Commission that build to a baseline. Write the mask from its climatology. Regenerate with --ice-mask. It cannot be one pass because Orogen has no climate to place ice from before it makes the terrain, and it cannot be bolted on afterwards because glacial, hydraulic and thermal erosion share one iteration loop and a mid-loop priority flood cuts outlets through the depressions glaciation makes; a later glacial pass would leave them undrained and move the drainage network and the basin catalogue.

Two things to carry through it. The mask is matched BY REGION INDEX and its sidecar names the mesh (seed and region count), so a mask from another build is refused rather than reindexed; keep it that way. And per docs/src/reference/no-time-axis.md an ice field says WHERE ice sits and never for how long, so the glacial strength slider it is scaled by stays a declared choice.

What it would change, measured as a limit on precarve-craton-10m against the T21 bootstrap climatology: glaciated land area 33.727% under the ramp against 0.967% under the criterion, ice supply down 8.8x, and the disagreement is altitude rather than latitude. notes/glacier-rough-pass.md extension 2026-08-25.

What a regeneration makes worthless, from scripts/pipeline.py --purge orogen: 55 files across hydrography, the climatologies, surface water, groundwater, soil, land column, dust and the world state, plus every UUID-named run, which the graph has no path for and archive_runs.py handles. Nothing is worthless until that generation actually happens: with no --ice-mask the generator is bit-identical to before.
notes: 2026-08-25, user decision: THE 10M BUILD IS BEING REGENERATED WITH AN ICE MASK BEFORE COMMISSIONING. PHYS-13 is fixed and vendor/orogen/js/glacial-ice.js takes glacial placement from a climatology, but the export on disk predates it and carries the Earth-calibrated latitude placement, so activating it as it stands would not inherit the repair. The regeneration is the Phase 0 exit, and the purge cost recorded on this row -- 55 files across hydrography, both climatologies, surface water, groundwater, soil, land-column and dust, plus every UUID-named run, which the graph has no path for -- is accepted rather than weighed. Every run and staged surface artifact has already been deleted this session, so most of that cost is already paid.
close_reason:
Not a task. This row describes EXECUTING THE PIPELINE -- generate, commission, write the mask, regenerate -- and running the pipeline is what the pipeline is for. A row that says 'run loop A' is the same class as a row that says 'regenerate a stale derived artifact', which CLAUDE.md already rules out: stale derived artifacts are the resting state of the tree, not a work list.

Everything it carried is enforced or recorded somewhere that outlives it, which is why closing loses nothing:
  THE TWO-PASS SEQUENCE is in config/pipeline.yaml's orogen step under first_pass and in docs/src/pipeline/sequencing.md section D, added 2026-08-25. It names the apparent cycle (orogen needs ice_mask, ice_mask needs baseline_climatology, which needs a build), says it is a pass boundary rather than a cycle, and gives the four steps with --glacial 0 as the first.
  WHY IT CANNOT BE ONE PASS OR A LATER BOLT-ON is in the same two places: Orogen has no climate to place ice from before it makes the terrain, and glacial, hydraulic and thermal erosion share one iteration loop whose mid-loop priority flood cuts outlets through the depressions glaciation makes.
  THE MASK'S MESH IDENTITY is enforced in vendor/orogen/js/glacial-ice.js's validateIceMask -- matched by region index, refused on a seed or region-count mismatch -- rather than remembered.
  THE NO-TIME-AXIS POINT is at glacial-ice.js:49, beside the slider it constrains.
  THE MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, glaciated land area 33.727 per cent under the Earth ramp against 0.967 under the criterion with ice supply down 8.8x and the disagreement being altitude rather than latitude, is in notes/glacier-rough-pass.md.

The generation is a user decision and remains one; it does not need a row to stay that way, because config/pipeline.yaml marks orogen cost: hours, which the file says is what must never run by accident.

title: The ice_mask_freezing_height record does not reproduce from the climatology it names
description: analysis/ice_mask_freezing_height.json records lapse_k_per_km_warmest 7.372 K/km and 1.657% of land below freezing against exoplasim/analysis/climatology/bootstrap_regular_climatology.nc. Re-running the same script against the file at that path now gives 6.520 K/km and 0.967%: lib/lapse.py returns 6.5198 for that climatology directly, so the difference is the climatology and not the script. The recorded numbers were measured on a climatology that path no longer holds, and PHYS-13's notes quote the 7.372 figure and the sub-grid warm bias derived from it. Consequence: any statement resting on 7.372 K/km or on the 7.8 K mean and 21.9 K p90 sub-grid warm bias is a measurement of a superseded climate. Do: re-measure against the declared climatology and correct the figures the notes carry, or record which run the 7.372 belongs to. Nothing about the MECHANISM changes either way; only the magnitudes.
close_reason:
Filed against a working agreement. CLAUDE.md: stale derived artifacts are the resting state of the tree, not a work list -- regenerate when a step you are running needs them, and otherwise leave them. analysis/ice_mask_freezing_height.json is a derived artifact with a generator and a row in config/pipeline.yaml, so its being stale is not a task; it regenerates when the pipeline reaches it. Confirmed by trying: the regeneration needs --grid-export because the T21 climatology has 32 latitude rows and only the T42 export keeps raw/, which is exactly the coupling the pipeline supplies and a hand-run does not.

WHAT WAS REAL HERE AND IS NOW FIXED. Documents do not regenerate, and three of them asserted the superseded magnitudes as fact. notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md and notes/external-model-survey.md now say the 7.372 K/km rate and the 7.8 K / 21.9 K sub-grid warm bias were measured on a climatology that no longer exists at the path they name, that lib/lapse.py returns 6.5198 for the file now there, and that the numbers should be read from the artifact rather than from prose. The MECHANISM those sections exist to state -- the surface energy balance is evaluated too warm for high ground because the model sees a cell mean, so a temperature-driven ablation scheme returns zero ice confidently and for the wrong reason -- is unaffected and is retained. notes/glacier-rough-pass.md is left alone: it already declares itself a rough pass owing a redo.

This is the conventions rule doing its job in reverse. Numbers belong in world_state.json and in dated notes carrying a 'measured on'; a number asserted in prose with neither is how a superseded climatology outlives the run that produced it.

title: The adopted land column states carry no uncertainty bracket, and lshy-1 which owned it is closed
description:
WORLD-OF6N adopted the Clapp-Hornberger closure on Cosby Table 4 as the central case for every consumer's soil hydraulic states. Its uncertainty is Cosby's residual variance WITHIN texture classes, which Cosby et al. report as large -- larger than everything else in the land column property contract's uncertainty put together -- and no artifact in this repository carries it. pedology/config/land_column_properties.yaml declares it undeclared under owner lshy-1, and lshy-1 is closed, so the sentinel points at nothing.

The declared endmember brackets in pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml do NOT stand in: they parameterise pedology's endmember volumetric mixture, which is the derivation that was not adopted. They still bracket the soil map's own awc column and nothing else.

Consequence: the states every consumer installs have no declared spread at all, and the report's percentiles are a spread ACROSS THE MAP rather than an uncertainty. Do: carry Cosby's within-class residual variance as a declared source in the contract's uncertainty block, apply it coherently as the contract requires, and repoint the sentinel's owner at this issue. Evidence: pedology/config/land_column_properties.yaml uncertainty.sources, pedology/notes/land-column-property-contract.md, pedology/analysis/land_column_properties_report.json adopted_case.adopted.limitation
close_reason: Cosby Table 4's S.D. rows are declared in the contract's uncertainty block and evaluated by land_column_properties.py:cosby_parameter_spread; contract_states takes a deviate triple and applies a case coherently across every state and all fifteen layers. The report's uncertainty_cases block carries the envelope: on precarve-craton-10m at T21 the capacity runs x0.628 to x1.850 of the central case at the median cell, against the gravity shift's 0.072, a factor 11.7 and larger on every cell. Labelled an envelope, not a distribution, because Cosby publishes no correlation between the three residuals. The sentinel is gone and the endmember sources no longer claim an owner. Emitted states are unchanged: consumers install the central case. Commit 5a59e803.

title: earth_calibration.py has no unconfined arm, so GW-24's third named check cannot be run
description:
GW-24 and hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 3 both name three commands that must be run before the unconfined transmissivity can be turned on, and the third is 'python hydrography/scripts/earth_calibration.py # with the unconfined arm'. That arm does not exist. stage_solve calls gw.solve with thickness_m only and never passes aquifer_base_m; stage_calibrate's TRANSMISSIVITY sweep varies D confined at 100, 1000, 5000 and 20000 m and has no unconfined counterpart; and there is no --unconfined or --thickness-m flag on the script at all.

This matters because the Earth harness is the only arm that scores against measured water table depth, it runs at 1,736,112 regions with its mesh, fields, permeability and drainage stages already cached under hydrography/data/earth_validation_cache/edge15.19km, and it is therefore the cheapest real-mesh answer to GW-24's question available.

Do: add an unconfined arm to stage_solve and to stage_calibrate's transmissivity sweep, passing aquifer_base_m = elev - D so it reads the same thickness field the confined form reads as a multiplier, with the solution artifact named per arm the way solution_name already names the drain and lambda variants. Declare, before running it, what would count as the unconfined form reaching a dependence structure that raising D uniformly did not: GW-21's rho(model, elevation) and rho(model, recharge) against the observed values, and the Pearson agreement, both moving at the SAME D rather than one at the expense of the other.
close_reason: FIXED, arm added and criterion declared first. The evidence relocated: the transmissivity sweep is stage_diagnostics', not stage_calibrate's. THE CRITERION IS IN config/groundwater.yaml under aquifer.unconfined_criterion, written before the harness had an unconfined arm to run, and the harness reads it from there rather than restating it: at ONE thickness the unconfined arm must put both Spearmans -- against elevation and against recharge -- closer to the observed values than the confined arm at that same thickness, AND raise the Pearson against observed depth. Two of three at one thickness and the third at another is a MISS, which is exactly what raising D uniformly already does (GW-21) and is what asking for one D refuses. THE ARM: --unconfined passes aquifer_base_m = surface - D and --thickness-m overrides D; solution_name and the earth_calibration.json run key both carry the form so the two never overwrite one another; stage_solve, stage_score and stage_calibrate all take it; the transmissivity sweep now runs both forms at each declared thickness and evaluates the criterion; the saturated-thickness floor's binding share is reported because a cell on that bound has a depth that is a lower bound rather than a value. NOT RUN: the unconfined solver path is verified live by groundwater.py --dupuit-test (Kirchhoff 4.9e-15 and 1.1e-14 against 1e-12, the analytic parabola 3.6e-12 against 1e-3, the round-off guard refusing the case built to trip it), but the Earth sweep is eight solves on 1.7 million regions writing into hydrography/data/earth_validation_cache, which is a symlink shared with the main checkout, so it belongs on main and not in a worktree. Command recorded in hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 3. Confined stays the default everywhere and every cached artifact keeps its name.

title: The top wavenumbers of every rung carry floating-point roundoff, and the cost-per-rung accounting does not know it
description:
Measured 2026-08-25 by exoplasim/scripts/filter_spectral_cost.py, which reads the roundoff floor from the FFT band above the model truncation rather than assuming one.

The last zonal wavenumber standing 100x clear of that floor is m=20 of 21 at T21 and m=41 of 42 at T42, and the approach is not gentle. At T42 the eddy kinetic energy falls 1.0e-3 at m=35, 4.6e-4 at m=36, 1.6e-4 at m=37, 2.3e-5 at m=38, 1.4e-6 at m=39, 4.2e-8 at m=40, 1.4e-10 at m=41 and 4.8e-14 at m=42 against a 2.6e-15 floor: four decades in three wavenumbers and eight in seven. At T21 the same shape runs m=18 to m=21.

TWO CAUSES AND ONLY ONE IS THE DAMPING. A triangular truncation gives m = NTRU exactly one meridional mode against NTRU at m = 1, so the mode count alone empties the top whatever the damping does; the filter and the hyperdiffusion do the rest. The share is not separated here.

WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A CURIOSITY. SPAT-11 prices a rung by its wall clock and compares rungs by truncation, and a rung's top wavenumbers cost transform work while carrying nothing. Whatever the right accounting is, it is not the one that treats T42 as 42 usable zonal wavenumbers against T21's 21.

It also bounds what any spectral diagnostic can be read at. The first version of filter_spectral_cost.py read the filter's depth at m = NTRU and returned the roundoff floor; it now reads at 0.8 of the truncation and REFUSES unless the spectrum there stands 100x clear. Any other diagnostic reading near the truncation has the same exposure and none of them currently check.

Evidence: exoplasim/notes/filter-spectral-price.md, section 'The top of every rung is dead'; exoplasim/analysis/filter_spectral_cost_arms.json.
close_reason: Answered, and the anticipated accounting change is NOT needed. CARRIED WAVENUMBERS, on the criterion already declared (the filter leaves at least 1/EXCESS_FACTOR of the flow's own amplitude): m <= (ln2/(2 kappa))**(1/gamma) * NTRU = 0.822N at kappa 8 gamma 16, at EVERY rung. T21 carries 18 zonal wavenumbers of 22, T42 carries 35 of 43. Upper bound, because the filter is a function of total wavenumber and the count is in zonal. filter_spectral_cost.py --rungs writes exoplasim/analysis/rung_spectral_budget.json and reads no run. THE SHARE IS SEPARATED. At T42 between m=35 and m=42 the measured 10.3 dex fall is -6.57 to the filter's own f^2, -2.68 to the hyperdiffusion by difference, at most -0.90 to the mode count and -0.16 to the run's own inertial slope. The mode count is the SMALLEST of the three mechanisms, not the dominant one: a triangular truncation takes m=NTRU down by a factor NTRU against m=1, 1.6 dex at T42, and cannot put anything at roundoff. filter-spectral-price.md's section heading said the opposite and is rewritten. THE COST ROW CLOSES ON A NULL. Legendre work at zonal wavenumber m is NTRU-m+1 modes over every latitude, so the uncarried top is 18 per cent of the wavenumbers and 3.3 to 4.0 per cent of the Legendre work -- the same fraction at every rung, because the filter is scale-free in n/NTRU, so it cancels out of a rung-to-rung ratio rather than distorting one. SPAT-11's recorded Legendre ratios are already modes x latitudes and are reproduced exactly (7.9x T85/T42, 26.2x T127/T42); its cost model is right and only the '42 usable zonal wavenumbers against 21' framing is not. The resolved degrees of freedom are (N+1)(N+2)/2: 253 at T21 and 946 at T42, a factor 3.74 where the truncations differ by 2. The exposure of other spectral diagnostics is world-qzcb. Commits 67154ee3, d2e2bd00.

title: Form the saturated mineral class in build_wetness.py once f_sat is licensed
description:
build_wetness.py carries take_saturated_out(), which is the two-support rule WET-2's classification rests on -- the saturated share is min(f_sat, dry_mineral) and the mineral class keeps the rest, never added beside the resolved classes -- and it is exercised by two fixtures under --selftest, including the double-count one. It is NOT wired into the artifact, and main() exits by name rather than quietly if it is ever reached with a license and both inputs present.

Two things are missing and one is a decision.

MISSING: f_sat is scored and not licensed (world-n9sd), and water_table.nc does not exist on the active build at all -- pipeline.py --status has groundwater MISSING, so there is no cell-mean depth to put in the closure.

THE DECISION: f_grad is a BRACKET and a consumer takes both arms or neither, so the saturated share is not one field. build_groundwater_access.py already solved the same shape for the permeability bracket by writing every fraction along a member axis, and that is the precedent; but a classification whose classes are bracketed is a different object from one whose classes are numbers, and what a downstream ledger does with a bracketed partition has to be said before it is written.

Do: once world-n9sd licenses the fraction and a water table exists, decide the member-axis question, wire take_saturated_out() into main(), and add the clamp's binding frequency and the area it removes to wetness_report.json -- the clamp is a disagreement between a solved result and a statistic, and one that binds everywhere is a finding rather than a detail.
close_reason: NOT TO BE DONE, and take_saturated_out() is deleted rather than wired. The class it would have formed needs f_sat, and world-n9sd withdrew the saturated-area closure on its declared score's verdict, so there is no input and there will not be one from this route. The member-axis decision this row named -- what a downstream ledger does with a partition whose classes are bracketed -- is not answered here and does not need to be: it is recorded in hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 7 as something a REVIVED closure must settle before any share is written, and build_wetness.py now refuses outright if topographic_index.yaml's closure.status ever says anything but withdrawn, so the question cannot be skipped by a later wiring. The double-count fixture stays under --selftest, generalised from 'a saturated share' to 'an unresolved grid share', because it guards check_partition against whatever unresolved class arrives next rather than against this one. wetness.yaml's saturated_mineral entry now reads as permanently absent with the withdrawal as its reason instead of as pending a license, and the closure identity that keeps such a class OUT of the resolved classes rather than beside them is kept as the rule a revival would inherit.

title: A seasonal inundated area has no owner, and three rows are waiting on one
description:
WET-2 asks for a mutually exclusive wetness classification AND a SEASONAL area artifact. The classification exists as of build_wetness.py; the seasonal half cannot be produced by any artifact in this pipeline, and the reason is structural rather than missing effort.

Nothing in hydrography carries a season. The lake solve is an annual equilibrium and surface_water.py exits unless it converges to one. The groundwater solve is a steady state. Every term reaching those stores in hydrography/config/land_water_ledger.yaml declares an annual interval_floor, and the ledger's own rule is that closure is required at every interval down to the model timestep, so an annual total is explicitly not a partition of a year.

A seasonal inundated area needs a store that empties and refills inside the year. Two candidates exist and neither is hydrography's: ExoPlaSim's land water column, and LPJ-GUESS's soil column. CaMa-Flood's answer is a third shape again -- two prognostic scalars, channel and floodplain storage, with depth, flooded fraction and area all diagnostic off a precomputed height-above-nearest-drainage CDF per routing cell -- and notes/external-model-survey.md section 52a records both that its runtime cost is small and that the HAND preprocessor it needs does not exist here and is not what build_hydrography.py's per-basin level/area/volume curves are.

DECISION REQUIRED, and it is not one this component can take on its own: which component owns a seasonally varying inundated AREA, on which support, and driven by which store. Until that is answered, wetness_<grid>.nc declares seasonal_inundation and peat absent with the reason, which is the fail-closed state and not a workaround.

Do: answer the ownership question, then file the implementing row against whichever component it lands in.
close_reason: DECIDED, and the decision is that it is three quantities wearing one name. (1) A closed BASIN's inundated area through the year is HYDROGRAPHY's, and it needs no curve, model or preprocessor this project does not already have: basins.nc carries level/area/volume at 128 levels, the coupling matrix already crosses a per-basin quantity to the grid, the climatology carries time bins with lib/climatology.py owning their weights, and carve_verdict.penman_open_water already integrates the diurnal cycle for the same Jensen reason so a bin is not a new kind of evaluation. The cost is that surface_water.py integrates basin storage through those bins instead of over annual_mean and its convergence criterion becomes a PERIODIC steady state where the year closes on itself -- a new criterion, not a new solver -- plus LSHY-6 lowering the annual interval_floor on open_water_evaporation and surface_runoff, which a sub-annual balance may not book against and which is annual because the producer is annual and ExoPlaSim cannot evaporate routed water at all. The size is set by residence time, so the honest product is a per-basin seasonal amplitude carried by the low-capacity basins. Filed as world-15i0. (2) A FLOODPLAIN's is a routing cell's, needs a HAND CDF and a routing model neither of which exists here, and SHOULD NOT HAVE AN OWNER YET; external-model-survey.md section 52a already records that the basin curves are a different quantity sharing the word. (3) A seasonally saturated SOIL is not an inundated area: ExoPlaSim's land column and LPJ-GUESS's soil column both carry a water CONTENT and neither carries an area, and turning one into the other is a saturated-fraction closure, which world-n9sd withdrew. Naming them as candidates was a category error rather than a shortlist. So wet-2, wet-8 and wet-10 each have to say which of the three they need; a methane ledger treating 'seasonally inundated' as one class would book two supports and a category error into one number. Recorded in hydrography/notes/land-water-ledger.md and hydrography/config/wetness.yaml.

title: Declare a regime-restricted criterion for f_sat before running it, or withdraw the fraction
description:
GW-26's declared score was run 2026-08-25 and MISSED, so consumers_licensed is false and no consumer may take f_sat. hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 6 carries the evidence.

The miss is the DEPTH's, not the terrain statistic's, and the harness measured that rather than arguing it. The ceiling any cell-scale predictor has at f_sat's own support is 0.6574 in Australia, and the cell-mean depth reaches 0.4581 there -- below the 0.5 of no discrimination -- so the support is not what failed. On the United States unconfined bores, where lateral flow rather than the local sink sets the head, the same depth reaches 0.6655 and f_sat clears both declared conditions on all four arms, adding +0.0034 to +0.0068 over the depth alone. That is the regime split water_table.nc already reports per cell in sink_fraction.

So the open question is whether the fraction is licensed WHERE THE DEPTH HAS A REGIME IT WORKS IN, which is the same restriction MIN-6 and SURF-7 are already asking of the depth field itself: both were scored over all cells and re-measuring them on cells where the sink did not set the depth is what those rows now ask for.

Do: DECLARE the restricted criterion -- which sink_fraction cut, which observation sets, which bar, and whether a partial license is a thing a consumer may take at all -- and commit it BEFORE running anything. The numbers above are already in hand, so a criterion chosen now that fits them is not a criterion; that is the whole reason this is a separate row rather than a re-score. Then run earth_calibration.py --stage fsat with the restriction and let it decide.

ALSO OPEN AND SETTLED BY THE SAME RUN: the upper end of f_grad_bracket_per_m erases the quantity. At 2.5 per metre the exponential in the depth spans so much more than f_sat_max does that the ranking becomes the depth's ranking exactly -- the Australian receiver-drop arm returns the cell-mean depth's own AUC to fifteen digits. The bracket is not a spread around one answer, and a consumer taking that arm alone is taking the depth under another name. Whether that end of the bracket stays is part of this decision.
close_reason: WITHDRAWN, and the withdrawal is measured rather than defaulted. The instrument was measured first: a cell-scale predictor carries one value per cell, so the independent units of this score are the cells and not the bores, and the two sets reach it through 34 and 37. earth_calibration.py's new _paired_gain_spread resamples those cells and re-scores both predictors on the same resample, reporting the scatter beside every gain (reported, never compared against, on auc_ceiling's precedent). On all eight arms of both sets the gain the terrain half carries over the cell-mean depth is at or below its own scatter: the largest gain anywhere, +0.0191, has a spread of 0.0213 and an interval reaching zero, and the US arms that pass gain half their own scatter. So NO regime-restricted criterion can license the fraction: restricting to the cells where the sink did not set the depth runs on fewer cells, which makes the scatter larger, and no cut of sink_fraction turns this instrument into one that resolves the effect. Declaring a cut and running it would be running an instrument already known to be blind to it. The withdrawal is therefore the disposition topographic_index.yaml declared for a miss before any fraction was computed. closure.status: withdrawn; build_topographic_index.py implements no closure and its artifact carries no saturated fraction; build_wetness.py forms none and refuses if that status ever says otherwise. The f_grad upper end question goes with it: at 2.5/m on the receiver-drop arm the gain and its spread are both exactly zero, the closure IS the depth, and the bracket is kept only as what a revived closure would have to bracket. What survives is the whole terrain half, the index and f_sat_max, whose variance is mostly within cells. hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 7. Filed world-34mx for the biosphere wetland gate, which assumed the fraction.

title: The clear-sky and all-cloud limits of band-resolved surface downward shortwave
description:
SEMI takes downward shortwave at the surface in four components: two bands by two SKY LIMITS, clear and overcast. WORLD-3QFZ routed the two ALL-SKY components, codes 185 and 186, because two readers for them exist today; the two sky limits have no reader that is not SEMI, and SEMI is a candidate rather than a component.

Where the two arms stand in the model, so this does not have to be re-derived:

The clear-sky arm costs nothing. radstep already re-calls swr with dcc zeroed under ndiagcf > 0, before the normal call, and stores four numbers from it in dclforc. dfdsw1 and dfdsw2 are filled by that call and then overwritten by the normal one, so capturing them into a clear-sky pair between the two calls is two array copies. The catch is that they would be identically zero whenever ndiagcf is 0, which is a code that is silently zero depending on a namelist switch, and world-j0az's finding is that a code no product carries is worse than no code.

The all-cloud arm has no precedent. CLIMBER-X's atmosphere computes solar_sur_c beside solar_sur_s; ExoPlaSim's normal call gives the cloud-weighted sky only, so an overcast limit is a THIRD swr call per radiation step. That is a real per-step cost and it needs a switch, and a switch needs a route through configure_otherargs.

Also unresolved and named in world-3qfz: SEMI's six derivatives of downward shortwave with respect to albedo and elevation are analytic derivatives of CLIMBER-X's single-layer transmission-factor product, written out by hand around the l_dswd_dalb guard in its src/atm/swr.f90. Through ExoPlaSim's multi-layer adding cascade they must be re-derived or taken by finite difference, which is two more swr calls on the ndiagcf pattern. Decide which BEFORE porting anything that consumes them.

Do this when SEMI is adopted, not before. exoplasim/notes/semi-scoping.md section 3 has the field-by-field account, and its 'Not emitted, and this is the model change' paragraph now describes only these two arms.
notes:
world-AA, 2026-08-26. NOT DONE, and the premise was re-verified against the code rather than the note before saying so.

STILL TRUE, checked line by line in vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/radmod.f90 as it now stands:
- radstep's clear-sky diagnostic is at line 1483. Under ndiagcf > 0 it saves dcc and both surface albedo bands, zeroes dcc, calls swr, and stores four numbers into dclforc: dswfl(NLEP), dswfl(1), dfu(1), dfu(NLEP). None of them is band-resolved and none is a downward flux.
- dfdsw1 and dfdsw2 are the band-resolved surface downward pair and they are filled inside swr at lines 3031-3032 as zfd1*zftop1 and zfd2*zftop2. The clear-sky call happens BEFORE the normal one, so they hold the clear-sky pair between the two calls and are overwritten by the normal call. Capturing the clear-sky arm is still two array copies.
- The all-cloud arm still has no precedent anywhere in the file. The normal call gives the cloud-weighted sky only, so an overcast limit is still a THIRD swr call per radiation step.

WHY IT IS NOT DONE, two blockers that stand independently:
1. The issue's own instruction. Nothing but SEMI reads these two limits, SEMI is a candidate rather than a component, and clim-63 (establish SEMI as the surface mass balance candidate) is open. Emitting four diagnostic fields for a consumer that does not exist is the code world-j0az establishes is worse than no code.
2. Verification needs a run. A new postprocessor code, a new namelist switch through configure_otherargs and a third swr call per radiation step are all changes whose correctness is only observable in output. The batch that looked at this held no machine claim and was instructed not to rebuild or run.

ON THE REFRAMING THIS BATCH WAS HANDED, so it is not tried again: the clear-sky limit for this star's spectrum IS computable without the model, from lib/stellar.py's band split and Rayleigh coefficient. What is not available is anything to check it against. Every run on this build was archived to identity and deleted and config/planet.yaml declares baseline_climatology: null, so there is no model clear-sky surface downward shortwave in the tree to compare a derived limit with. Deriving the number alone would be a prediction nothing tests, which is the shape CLAUDE.md rules out. Sequence: adopt SEMI (clim-63), then emit the fields, then the derived limit becomes a test that can fail.

The derivative question the description names is still open and still has to be decided BEFORE anything consuming the six derivatives is ported: re-derive through the adding cascade, or finite difference on the ndiagcf pattern at two more swr calls per radiation step.

title: Nothing can run an unpublished build arm, so no precision or flag arm can be taken past a compile
description:
run_exoplasim.py:3049 and continue_exoplasim.py:706 compose the registry's executable name and take the copy in the run directory; run_stellar_cycle.py:295 composes it against the registry. None has a flag naming a binary. build_model.py can build an arm (--extra-flag, --drop-flag, --frame-pointers, --precision) and --no-publish leaves it in its own build directory, which is the whole point -- an arm that publishes overwrites the shipped binary, world-v3d -- but there is then no route from that executable to a run.

make_profile_bed.py is the only script that takes --binary-dir and --binary, and what it builds is a short profiling bed, not a spin-up.

This is what blocks the empirical half of clim-59: the four-byte arm builds (verified, T21 l10 p16) and cannot be integrated. It blocks every other arm the same way -- any question of the form 'does this build differ from production over many orbits' is unanswerable while an arm cannot be run.
design: An arm's executable is named by the CALLER, not resolved by the registry's naming rule, and the run records that it was an arm: the run's manifest must not read as a production run. Give the run pipeline a way to be handed a binary path, refuse to treat such a run as part of any canonical lineage, and make the arm's identity (its build directory tag) part of the run manifest so it cannot be mistaken for the shipped model later.
acceptance_criteria: A build made with --no-publish can be integrated for a named number of orbits, and the resulting run_manifest.json says which arm it was and that it was not the registry's binary.
close_reason: FIXED, commit a89f2833, verified end to end. build_model.arm_identity() describes an executable a caller names and refuses two paths rather than describing them: the registry's published binary (a run composes that name itself, so --binary would only let an ordinary run acquire an arm block) and anything outside a build_model.py build directory (an arm's identity IS its directory name, which tag() composes from every input that changes a byte, so an executable from elsewhere carries no statement of what makes it differ). run_exoplasim.py --binary copies the arm over the run directory's own copy under the registry's name, inside that run directory and nowhere else; the published binary, the registry naming and binary_manifest.json are untouched, so build_model.py's refusal to publish an arm is not weakened. The run stamps executable.arm (path, build tag, build root) and canonical_lineage_eligible=false, index_runs.py carries the build tag into runs/INDEX.json, and continue_exoplasim.py refuses --purpose post_equilibrium_climatology on such a run while allowing spinup and diagnostic. A continuation restores the arm the prepare recorded and refuses if it is gone or its sha has moved under the same tag -- without that, exo.Model.__init__ silently overwrites an arm with the shipped binary at the start of every segment after the first. VERIFIED: build_model.py --res T21 --ranks 16 --precision 4 --no-publish produced build/t21_l10_p16_production_real4/plasim.x, and run_exoplasim.py --binary on it integrated one orbit and postprocessed it; run_9592a038a1c0's manifest reads status smoke_complete, completed_orbits 1, canonical_lineage_eligible false, executable.arm.build_tag t21_l10_p16_production_real4.

title: Snow thermal conductivity is held fixed while snow density is a namelist key
description:
landmod's snowdiff = 0.31 W/m/K is a fixed namelist key beside rhosnow, but the thermal conductivity of snow is a steep function of its density: Sturm et al. 1997 gives k = 0.138 - 1.01*rho + 3.233*rho^2 with rho in g/cm3, which at 330 kg/m3 returns about 0.157 W/m/K, half the value declared here. So the two disagree at the shipped density and they cannot both be right.

Consequence for GRAV-8's bracket: glaciermod's comment says rhosnow and rhoglac are namelist keys 'so the bracket can be run'. GRAV-8 made the heat capacity follow the density, which is arithmetic and exact. Conductivity does not follow by arithmetic, so a bracket on rhosnow today moves the pack's thickness and its thermal mass and leaves its conductivity where it stands. The ground heat flux under a pack goes as k/z, so the bracket is only half a bracket.

Do: choose a measured density-conductivity relation with its source (Sturm 1997 and Yen 1981 are the two candidates), state which and why, and derive snowdiff from rhosnow in landini the way snowcap now is. This CHANGES RESULTS at the shipped density and that is information, not a reason to refuse: it is a correct term replacing a value that does not match the density beside it.

Also settle icemod's CKAPSN = 0.31, the same number as a hardcoded parameter, which GRAV-8 left alone because only the density was declared twice in a way that could be deduplicated.
close_reason: Fixed, and the issue's own premise did not survive checking, which is the substantive result. Sturm et al. (1997) is a needle-probe set; Riche and Schneebeli (2013) put three methods on identical samples and found the needle probe least reliable, biased up to a quarter either way by the pack's anisotropy, and its stated 0.1 W/m/K uncertainty at 95 per cent confidence is comparable to the value it predicts at seasonal-snow density. Fourteau et al. (2021) computes the conductivity numerically WITH the latent heat carried by vapour diffusing through the pore space -- a real term in a pack under a gradient -- and at the shipped density returns within a few per cent of what the model already carried. Sturm would have HALVED it, insulating ice the error budget already reports as excessive. So: landini derives snowdiff from rhosnow through Fourteau Eq. (18) at 263 K, snowdiff leaves landmod_nl the way snowcap did under GRAV-8, and icemod's CKAPSN is handed from it through iceini instead of being a second compile-time statement of the same material property. The defect was real and it was the RELATION, not the value. Temperature choice is second-order: about six per cent across Fourteau's whole 223-273 K span against a factor of two between published relations. Calonne (2011), the slow-kinetics arm of the remaining bracket, could not be fetched; recorded in references/INDEX.md. notes/audits/cryosphere-material-properties.md.

title: Decide where geography_land_threshold sits, now that what it floods is measured
description:
notes/audits/coastline-threshold-cost.md measures what the 0.5 land threshold costs. config/planet.yaml records geography_land_threshold as DETERMINED and docs/src/reference/config-rationale.md states its cost as a coastline effect without sizing it. It is now sized, and one row of the measurement has a rule behind it rather than a preference.

source/README.md's first rule rejects land_mask because it puts dry closed-basin floor below sea level under water. The threshold does the same thing through a different door: a cell whose land share falls below 0.5 goes to the slab ocean whatever its elevation. The share of below-datum land it floods is 6.44% at T21, 3.18% at T42, 1.32% at T85, 0.82% at T127, 0.47% at T170 -- the most rung-sensitive quantity in the ledger, falling by a factor 14 across the ladder while the coastline area rounding falls by 3.2.

Do: decide whether 0.5 stays. It is a threshold and therefore a decision, not a measurement, so it belongs to the user. Three things the decision has to separate, and they are not the same question: whether the boundary should be fractional at all (spat-5, and the model cannot take a fraction -- oceanmod.f90:256 hard-binarises yls at 0.5); whether the threshold should conserve land AREA, which a different value could do and which still would not conserve WHICH land; and whether below-datum land should be exempt from the threshold outright, which is the only form that keeps the rule the fork was built around.

Not a defect to fix silently: build_boundary_conditions.py reports the cost in both signs and the threshold is unchanged.
notes:
MEASURED and ARGUED 2026-08-25; the value is UNCHANGED and the decision is the user's. build_boundary_conditions.py:coastline_ledger now prices every candidate rule in candidate_rules as part of each boundary build, and notes/audits/coastline-threshold-cost.md carries the full ladder table and the argument.

The three questions the issue said to separate, answered:

1. Fractional boundary: not available. oceanmod.f90:326-329 hard-binarises yls at 0.5 whatever the builder writes. That is SPAT-5 and is a model change, not a threshold change.

2. Area-conserving threshold: 0.491 at T21 falling to 0.465 at T170. Conserves land area to within 0.02 per cent at every rung, recovers almost none of the below-datum land (6.44 to 6.05 per cent at T21) and makes the land VOLUME closure WORSE (+2.23 to +3.19 per cent). It buys the number that does not carry the sign of the preserved terrain with the one that does.

3. Below-datum exemption: the only form that keeps source/README.md's first rule, and the measurement refuses it. Exempting any cell holding below-datum land recovers 100 per cent of that terrain and at T21 inflates model land area by 46.8 per cent, promotes 32.3 per cent of the model's land out of open ocean and takes the volume closure to +40.7 per cent. Its cost falls by 52 across the ladder and is nearly fair at T170, but a rule cannot be adopted on its behaviour at a rung the project does not use. A share-based exemption is INERT: at 25 per cent of the cell no cell qualifies at any rung, because the below-datum land the threshold floods sits in cells that are mostly OCEAN.

RECOMMENDATION: 0.5 stays. It is also the only value that makes the rounding SINGLE -- at 0.5 the builder's mask and the model's own binarisation agree; at any other value the cell is rounded twice by two rules that do not know about each other, and every area-conserving value is below 0.5. The route out of the residue is the RUNG: below-datum land dropped falls by 14 across the ladder while the coastline area rounding falls by 3.2.

THE QUESTION FOR THE USER: confirm geography_land_threshold stays at 0.5 on the evidence above, or name which of the three alternatives to adopt despite its priced cost.
close_reason:
Stays at 0.5. Every alternative was priced across the ladder and each is worse on its own terms, so this was a conclusion rather than a decision.

Exempting any cell holding below-datum land -- the rule CLAUDE.md rule 1 points at -- recovers 100 per cent of that terrain and inflates model land area by 46.8 per cent at T21, promotes 32.3 per cent of model land out of open ocean, and takes the volume closure to +40.7 per cent. That is the same class of error it fixes, five times the magnitude. It is nearly fair by T170, but a rule cannot be adopted on its behaviour at a rung the project does not run.

A share-based exemption at 25 per cent of the cell is INERT: no cell qualifies at any rung, because the below-datum land being flooded sits in cells that are mostly ocean.

Area-conserving lands at 0.491 at T21 falling to 0.465 at T170: it conserves area to 0.02 per cent, recovers almost no below-datum land, and makes the volume closure worse.

And 0.5 has a reason none of them has: oceanmod.f90:326-329 binarises yls at 0.5, so it is the one builder threshold at which the cell is rounded ONCE rather than twice by two rules. Every area-conserving value sits below it.

The residue is real and stays declared: 6.44 per cent of below-datum land drops to ocean at T21, falling to 0.47 at T170. The route out of it is the rung, not the threshold, and the escalation already walks to T85. coastline_ledger prices every candidate on every boundary build, so the numbers regenerate rather than being frozen here.

title: Settle the subgrid saturation gap against the first accepted baseline climatology
description:
notes/audits/nonlinear-spatial-reductions.md section 2 fixes the decision procedure for the subgrid-elevation saturation gap BEFORE the climatology that answers it exists, and world-b99f corrected the arm that produces it. What remains is one comparison.

Do: once a baseline climatology is accepted, call lapse.environmental_lapse_k_per_km on it for the land-area-weighted environmental rate, and compare against the critical-lapse table in that section at the rung in use (3.95 to 7.07 K per km across T21 to T170 and the reference-temperature bracket, against a dry adiabat of 12.75). Above it the reduction needs a sub-grid orographic term in the surface evaporation and that term belongs to spat-5's partial-surface decision; at or below it the reduction is admissible and no operator is needed.

BLOCKED until then: config/planet.yaml carries baseline_climatology: null, and every run and climatology on disk is worthless independently of that (land_longwave_emissivity moved to 0.9357 and a longwave surface-reflection defect in radmod.f90 was fixed). Do not answer this from a run that predates the accepted lineage.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
The first of the two grounds for the block is gone; the second is what still holds, and it is now checkable rather than argued. Found 2026-08-30 while extending SPAT-7's arms onto the ocean support.

GROUND ONE, GONE. config/planet.yaml no longer carries baseline_climatology: null. It points at exoplasim/analysis/climatology/baseline_regular_climatology.nc, whose own netCDF attributes name run_67323a923013 on canonical-10m-carve2 -- the configured source_build -- built 2026-08-28 from 57 orbits, year indices 70 to 126. The prose block above the key still says "DECLARED ABSENT AGAIN" and describes a null that is not there, so a reader grepping for the state of the key gets the wrong answer.

GROUND TWO, UNCHANGED IN SHAPE AND MOVED IN ITS NUMBERS. The row's block cites land_longwave_emissivity at 0.9357; config/planet.yaml now carries 0.930897, so the constant has moved again since the block was written and the climatology on disk predates at least one such move. The climatology stamps vesper_config_sha256 = 30061eeeb8b63917561867d8beb74bf018b28e2df0d662fce08d26f3089d9ed7, which is what a staleness check compares against; scripts/check_consistency.py is the gate that decides it and this comment does not pre-empt it.

What has NOT changed is the decision procedure, which notes/audits/nonlinear-spatial-reductions.md section 2 fixed before any climatology existed and which is still one comparison: lapse.environmental_lapse_k_per_km against the critical-lapse table at the rung in use. Nothing about that needs revisiting; what the row is waiting for is a baseline whose config the current one is.

title: Every stability_probe.json entry predating world-anl names no executable, and the timestep ceilings rest on some of them
description:
exoplasim/analysis/stability_probe.json holds 22 entries written before the probe recorded provenance. None can be attributed to a binary: an entry carries no executable name, sha or template path, the file's single 'generated' field is rewritten on every write so there is no per-entry timestamp, find_template selected by modification time, and run directories are untracked. The four routes and why each closes are in notes/audits/executable-provenance-at-the-consumer.md.

They are measurements of an unnamed model. That matters because model.timestep_minutes per rung and model.filter_kappa in config/planet.yaml were settled against the refusal boundary this probe maps, and a boundary measured on a superseded executable is a boundary for a model that no longer exists.

An entry written after world-anl carries executable, executable_sha256 and build_profile, so the two are told apart by the presence of the field.
design: Re-derive rather than reason about them. The probe is cheap by construction -- that is why it exists -- so the cells that carry a decision are the ones to re-run, not all 22. Which cells those are is the first question: the ceilings the ladder actually adopted, and the kappa arms the filter requirement rests on.
acceptance_criteria: Every entry in stability_probe.json that a config value cites names the executable that produced it.
close_reason: ANSWERED, commit b0f62545, deliverable in notes/audits/executable-provenance-at-the-consumer.md. The premise holds and its scope is larger than the issue states: stability_probe.json was re-measured entire on 2026-08-24 (220b7142) and the probe learned to record its executable the next morning (8b68dc30, world-anl), so all 60 entries carry no attribution rather than 22 of them, and the proposed discriminator -- presence of executable_sha256 -- is correct and currently selects nothing. The re-derivation list is sixteen cells: the adopted step per rung from model.resolution_timestep_minutes, the two cells bracketing each rung's refusal boundary, the four cells where the filter changes the verdict at both arms (which is the whole of what model.filter_kappa rests on -- the filter buys a step at T85, T127 and twice at T170, and nothing at T21 or T42), and the two escalation steps sequencing.md section D uses that the config table does not. The other forty-four are interior points of a cost curve and a refusal map that no declaration cites. world-37tn is re-taking the grid on the current model with the probe that records provenance, so the sixteen come with it if that re-measurement is complete; two consequences are filed rather than fixed here because they live in files a sibling batch owns: world-ngef (a partial re-run leaves a mixed file whose note asserts attribution it does not have, because the dedup key is per cell and the note is per file) and world-6qrr (config's adopted T170 step is one step above what the grid it cites measures, invisible because check_consistency only checks the active rung's row).

title: A run's prepare never compares its executable against binary_manifest.json
description:
run_exoplasim.py:3049 composes the executable name and records its sha in run_manifest.json, and run_stellar_cycle.py:295 does the same against the registry, but neither compares that sha against exoplasim/binary_manifest.json. continue_exoplasim.py:706 compares the segment's executable against the sha the PREPARE recorded, which catches a rebuild DURING a run's life and not a run whose whole life ran on an unregistered binary.

The registry is gated by scripts/check_consistency.py, which calls rebuild_binaries.verify(), and CLAUDE.md rule 8 requires it before an expensive run. That is a gate a caller has to remember rather than one it cannot skip, and an orbit is the most expensive thing in the project to have to re-integrate.

The lookup now exists: rebuild_binaries.unregistered(exe) returns None or a line naming both shas. Evidence and the full consumer sweep: notes/audits/executable-provenance-at-the-consumer.md
design: Refuse at PREPARE rather than warn: a run has not cost anything yet at that point, and the executable it is about to copy in is the one every orbit after it will be integrated by. Record the manifest verdict in run_manifest.json beside the sha that is already there, so a run's provenance says not just which file but whether it was a registered one.
acceptance_criteria: A prepare against an executable the manifest does not register stops with both shas named. A run_manifest.json written after this says which manifest entry its executable matched.
