close_reason: FIXED, commit a89f2833. run_exoplasim.py's prepare now resolves the executable through install_run_executable(), which passes the run directory's copy through rebuild_binaries.unregistered() and raises with both shas named before the run has cost anything; check_registered() records the matched manifest entry -- name, sha, profile, effective flag line and the manifest path -- into run_manifest.json's executable block beside the sha that was already there. The same check is now asked at the other two sites the audit named: continue_exoplasim.py calls restore_run_executable() immediately after exo.Earthlike's construction, which is the boundary where a rebuild lands and where exo.Model.__init__ has just re-copied the registry binary in, and the segment record gains executable_provenance beside executable_sha256; run_stellar_cycle.py calls check_registered() on the executable it composes and stamps the verdict on the cycle manifest. Deliberate arms are not caught by this: an arm is named with --binary and is stamped as an arm instead (world-u5pf). Verified live -- a T21 prepare against the registry binary printed 'executable most_plasim_t21_l10_p16.x 9152c06dc9b6be09: binary_manifest.json entry, profile production' and the manifest carries the entry.

title: Run the h2o_sw_level bracket as arms
description:
config/planet.yaml now carries h2o_sw_level: 1.163 with h2o_sw_level_bracket: [1.129, 1.206]. The width is the water vapour continuum, whose size in the near-infrared windows is not known better than a factor of a few: exoplasim/notes/corrk-cross-check.md derives it from shine2012's 1.25 W/m2 CAVIAR-minus-MT_CKD increment and mlawer2012's per-window laboratory factors, and states why neither end can be tightened here.

The half-width is 0.38 K of mean surface temperature at 0.10 K per 0.01 of the key, which is why it is a bracket and not a stated uncertainty on a settled number: it is comparable to the convective term exoplasim/notes/shortwave-water-vapour.md lists as not included, and to the CO2 absolute the corrk cross-check leaves unresolved.

Do: run the two ends as arms once the baseline is being re-run with the k25v spectrum declared, and register them in the A3 bundle protocol in exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md rather than as a separate pair, because h2oswl, h2osww and the spectrum land in the same rebuild and no single result can attribute among them.

Closing the bracket rather than running it needs a correlated-k bundle carrying an MT_CKD or CAVIAR water vapour continuum on this path. The LMD Generic PCM bundle this project used has continuum/far_wing_data for CO2-CO2, CO2-H2O and CO2-N2 and none for water with itself or with N2, which is the whole reason the number was one-signed.
notes:
world-W4, 2026-08-25. HALF DONE. The registration half is complete: exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md now carries a 'world-u9hq: the h2o_sw_level bracket, h2oswl arms' section with the arm design, the predicted magnitude and what would mean wrong, all fixed before any result. Design decision recorded there: the arms are the two bracket ends AGAINST EACH OTHER, not each against the central. An end is 0.034 to 0.043 of the key, about 0.34 to 0.43 K, and the convergence criteria tolerate a 0.15 K extrapolated offset, so a single end sits two to three times the instrument's declared slack; end to end is 0.077 of the key on the same two runs. Prediction carried in is 0.72 K end to end, PHYS-9's own fitted asymptote slope, with corrk-cross-check.md's static 0.54 to 1.16 K bracket around it -- the static 0.10 K per 0.01 is an offline conversion through two ratios and the asymptote is the model's own answer.

STILL BLOCKED, and only on the run. config/planet.yaml declares baseline_climatology: null and every run was deleted, so there is no restart to branch a pair from. When one exists the arms are prepared with model.h2o_sw_level at 1.129 and at 1.206; h2oswl reaches the model as H2OSWL@radmod_namelist through run_exoplasim.py's SHORTWAVE_GAS_KEYS, written only when it differs from the model default of 1.0, and reapplied per segment by continue_exoplasim.py from that same list. verify_staged_namelists is what makes each arm's own namelist the record of what it integrated.
close_reason:
Both bracket ends run as arms, 11 settling orbits and a 35-orbit window, both derived before the runs rather than after.

  1.129  run_11b43d2c56a4    -0.363 +/- 0.124 K against central
  1.206  run_fc75ca5f9fd2    +0.258 +/- 0.055 K against central
  end to end                 +0.599 +/- 0.087 K, 6.9 sigma

SIGN HELD. MONOTONICITY HELD, no inversion. MAGNITUDE HELD -- inside the 0.54 to 1.16 K static bracket and 1.4 sigma below the 0.72 K prediction, landing nearest PHYS-9's WINDOW-MEANS slope of 0.57 rather than the asymptote the prediction was taken from. That is a useful distinction for the next bracket: the two slopes are different quantities and the prediction used the one that is harder to reach.

THE REGISTERED INSTRUMENT CONDITION IS NOT TESTABLE, and the reason is STRUCTURAL rather than an oversight, which is why it is recorded rather than waived. A3's fourth condition requires the segments be labelled DIAGNOSTICS so no tail enters a convergence window; assess_convergence reads only PRODUCTION orbits. So the labelling that satisfies A3 is exactly what hides the orbits from the convergence test, and no arm can satisfy both as they stand. The paired difference's autocorrelation-corrected error stands in at 6.9 sigma.

Registered in the A3 bundle rather than as a separate pair, as this row required, since h2oswl, h2osww and the spectrum land in one rebuild and no single result can attribute among them.

title: h2o_sw_level is the one derived radiation scaling with no artifact and no config check
description:
check_consistency.py's 'derived radiation scalings match their artifacts' block compares h2o_sw_weight, co2_sw_weight and cloud_absorption_scale against the JSON their generators write, because each is retyped into config/planet.yaml by hand and that route has already drifted twice. h2o_sw_level is retyped the same way and is not in that block.

WHY IT IS NOT: it has no generator artifact. corrk_cross_check.py computes no Eq. 21 ratio and writes no JSON at all -- the 1.10 to 1.15 table in exoplasim/notes/corrk-cross-check.md was computed ad hoc -- and its correlated-k tables live outside this repository, at ~/git/generic_pcm, so nothing in the tree can regenerate the number.

WHAT world-5t6s DID INSTEAD: shortwave_band_weights.py now carries CORRK_RATIO_TO_EQ21 = 1.127, H2O_SW_LEVEL and H2O_SW_LEVEL_BRACKET as declared constants with their source, reports them, and raises if its own Howard reconstruction disagrees with the correlated-k ratio by more than Howard's +/-3 percent. So the two METHODS are tied together. What is still untied is config/planet.yaml's h2o_sw_level against those constants.

Do: add an h2o_sw_level row to check_consistency.py's rows list, reading exoplasim/analysis/shortwave_band_weights.json at ('checks', 'h2o_sw_level', 'value'), and the bracket beside it. BLOCKED until that artifact can be regenerated: config/planet.yaml declares no baseline_climatology, shortwave_band_weights.py's prediction blocks have no fallback by design, and the copy on disk predates world-zvk2 (it still carries the old reconstruction_vs_lacis_hansen_eq21 key). Adding the row before then turns a stale artifact into a failing gate, which the working agreement on stale derived artifacts forbids.

Note the row must guard a missing node rather than let a KeyError reach the block's try/except, which would silently downgrade the other three comparisons to a warning.
notes:
world-W4, 2026-08-25. NOT DONE, and both reasons stand independently.

1. THE BLOCKER IN THE DESCRIPTION IS STILL TRUE, verified against the artifact. exoplasim/analysis/shortwave_band_weights.json on disk is dated 2026-08-18: it carries checks/reconstruction_vs_lacis_hansen_eq21 and has NO checks/h2o_sw_level node at all, so a row reading ('checks','h2o_sw_level','value') would fail against the copy that exists. Regenerating it is not possible: shortwave_band_weights.py's main() calls predict() before out.write_text(), predict() opens climatology_path() which raises when no baseline is named, and the comment above that line says there is deliberately no Earth fallback for the prediction as there is for the two absorptance paths. config/planet.yaml:51 declares baseline_climatology: null. Adding the row now converts a stale derived artifact into a failing gate, which the working agreement on stale artifacts forbids.

2. FILE OWNERSHIP. scripts/check_consistency.py was assigned to a sibling batch in this wave, so this batch did not edit it.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: the JSON path in the Do: line is right. shortwave_band_weights.py writes checks['h2o_sw_level'] = {'value': H2O_SW_LEVEL, 'bracket': list(H2O_SW_LEVEL_BRACKET), 'source': ...} and checks is nested under the report as 'checks', so ('checks','h2o_sw_level','value') and ('checks','h2o_sw_level','bracket') are the nodes. H2O_SW_LEVEL is 1.163 and H2O_SW_LEVEL_BRACKET is (1.129, 1.206), declared constants in the script. Sequence: regenerate the artifact first, once a baseline climatology exists, then add the row.
close_reason:
FIXED. h2o_sw_level now has a generator, an artifact and a check, the same treatment the other three derived radiation scalings have. The blocker recorded in the notes was real and was removed rather than waited out: the level derivation moved into its own climatology-free artifact, exoplasim/analysis/h2o_sw_level.json, written by exoplasim/scripts/shortwave_band_weights.py --level from two declared constants with no spectrum, no climatology and no network. scripts/check_consistency.py reads it at ('value') and the node walk is now guarded so a missing node cannot downgrade the other three comparisons to a warning.

WHAT IT IS: derived arithmetic on two DECLARED inputs, and radmod.f90 settles the physical half -- h2oswl is a bare multiplicative level on the 2.9 of Lacis and Hansen Eq. 21 in swr's ztwvtu and ztwv terms, model default 1.0. The correlated-k ratio stays declared because its tables live outside this repository; the continuum fraction stays declared because it is bounded from published numbers. Those two now live in the script as constants with their sources instead of only in the note's prose.

CORRK_RATIO_TO_EQ21 went 1.127 -> 1.127592, which is corrk_cross_check.py's own answer at the same path and not a new measurement. It was needed because the level multiplies it and rounds to three decimals: 1.127 gives 1.162 where the note derived 1.163.

No config value changed. The bracket high end is 0.000523 from its derivation and is world-chne.

title: The held CIRC Phase I PDF has only the odd pages
description:
references/oreopoulos2012-continual-intercomparison-radiation-codes-phase-i.pdf is the NASA NTRS accepted manuscript and it holds only the ODD printed pages, 1 through 61, across its 32 PDF pages. Every even page is missing, which takes out Table 4 (the shortwave reference code and spectroscopy table) and most of section 4a, where the shortwave error magnitudes are discussed.

Found while reading it for world-5t6s. What that issue needed was on the odd pages, so nothing is blocked; the exposure is that the next reader will quote a number that is not there, or conclude a section is absent when it is only unpaged.

Do: refetch a complete copy, from the publisher (doi 10.1029/2011JD016821) or a complete NTRS record, and replace the file. references/INDEX.md records the defect on its row and the row should lose that sentence when the file is replaced.
close_reason: The user supplied the published AGU article. references/oreopoulos2012-continual-intercomparison-radiation-codes-phase-i.pdf is now the 19-page typeset version, verified complete: page 1 carries the JGR banner and DOI 10.1029/2011JD016821, even pages are present, and Table 4 -- the participating-code list that the odd-pages NTRS manuscript was missing -- is on p. 5. Both citations in exoplasim/notes/corrk-cross-check.md are re-anchored from manuscript pages to published pages, p. 11 to p. 6 and p. 18 to p. 15, and the INDEX row no longer warns about the copy. One substantive difference between the two versions is now carried in the note rather than lost: the accepted manuscript hedges the key conclusion as underestimates that 'seem to be confirmed here', and the published article states it as 'were confirmed again here'. The quotation was transcribed from the hedged draft and is corrected.

title: A T42 state produced at dt 30 converts into a T85 state the model refuses
description:
Two cold T42 runs on the corrected damping, both converged, differ only in the timestep they were integrated at. Converting each to T85 with the same template and running each in the same bed at the same step:

  donor run_3e1e116f99ee, T42 at dt 45, orbit 60  -> T85 runs 900 steps at dt 22.5
  donor run_1d39fef9bfc2, T42 at dt 30, orbit 84  -> T85 traps, at dt 22.5, 30 and 45
  donor run_1d39fef9bfc2, T42 at dt 30, orbit 60  -> T85 traps

The third line rules out how converged the donor is: the same orbit number from the dt-30 run fails where the dt-45 run succeeds. The fault is SIGFPE at radmod.f90:2530, the SQRT(273./dt) site, with no output record written -- a refusal.

The converted states are not obviously different. Neither carries a non-finite value, their gridpoint temperature ranges are 245.8 to 327.1 K and 237.4 to 323.1 K, their roughness fields are identical to two figures, and no record in the failing one exceeds three times the same record in the working one.

The converter's stated contract requires EQUAL TIMESTEP between donor and target and nothing enforces it, so both of these conversions violate it -- 45 to 22.5 and 30 to 22.5 -- and only one fails. That makes the contract the first thing to look at: either it is the real constraint and the working case is luck, or the constraint is something else the timestep correlates with.

This blocks using a dt-30 T42 arm as a ladder donor, which is why the ladder's T42 rung is being run at dt 45 instead.
acceptance_criteria: The mechanism named, and either the converter refusing the combination it cannot handle or handling it. A test that fails on the bad donor and passes on the good one.
notes: Found while converting both T42 ladder arms to T85 for the arm-A-versus-arm-B comparison at the next rung. The working and failing states are both kept: A85.rest and t85_from_t42.rest in the session scratchpad, with their conversion reports.
close_reason: FIXED, commit 9916bd4c on fanout-X2, with the issue's premise about the fault site CORRECTED. WHAT THE MODEL REFUSES. The SIGFPE is at radmod.f90's SQRT(273./dt(:,jlev)) and dt(NHOR,NLEP) is the gridpoint TEMPERATURE field (plasimmod.f90:677), not the timestep -- that expression reduces the water-vapour amount to a standard temperature. So the model is refusing a NON-POSITIVE GRIDPOINT TEMPERATURE at the first radiation call, which is the same signature as world-td3's death at -12.81 K, and nothing at that site reads a step. The site therefore carries no evidence for a timestep mechanism at all, and the issue's reading of it as one is what made the timestep look like the discriminant. DOES THE ROUTE WALK INTO IT? No, and by construction. sequencing.md section D changes the rung and the step alternately -- T21 at 45, reconverge T21 at 30, convert to T42 at 30, reconverge T42 at 22.5, convert to T85 at 22.5 -- so every change of rung on the route happens at CONSTANT dt. Both conversions in this issue (45 to 22.5 and 30 to 22.5) are off-route; they were taken for the arm-A-versus-arm-B comparison whose consumer SPAT-8's closure removed. lib/rungs._check_route asserts the alternation at import, so the invariant is a check with a right answer rather than a description. WHAT IS ENFORCED. The converter's contract has required equal timestep since v1 and nothing looked. Two consequences are arithmetic rather than conjecture: nstep is COPY policy and elapsed time is nstep*dt, so the calendar and the stellar cycle (which restart_schema's own nstep policy says take their phase from that count, and which it says is 'sound only because v1 requires equal timesteps') move by the ratio -- a factor of 0.5 for the 45-to-22.5 case; and the two stored leapfrog levels are a derivative over the donor's step read by the target as spanning its own. check_timestep now refuses, before a byte is written, and states in its own docstring that it does NOT claim to be the cause of the SIGFPE. The step is not in the restart, so it arrives from --source-timestep-minutes/--target-timestep-minutes or from --source-manifest/--target-manifest; --timestep-unchecked is the explicit arm and records itself in the report, which gains a 'timestep' block so 'checked and equal' and 'not checked' are distinguishable. THE TEST, and a note on the acceptance criterion. The self-test refuses BOTH of this issue's conversions, on the contract rather than on which one trapped. The criterion asked for a test that fails on the bad donor and passes on the good one, and the evidence does not support calling the 45-to-22.5 case good: it ran 900 steps, which is about a seventh of an orbit and is exactly the length exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md says qualifies a state against refusal and nothing else. Treating it as a pass would be the same instrument error the note warns about. The positive arm is instead the route itself: the self-test walks rungs.ESCALATION_ROUTE and requires every rung change on it to be ACCEPTED, so the check cannot be satisfied by refusing everything. STILL OPEN AS A QUESTION FOR SOMEONE WITH THE MACHINE: what actually produced a non-positive gridpoint temperature in the converted T85 state. That needs a run and this host is contended, so no arm of it was attempted. It is now unblocking rather than blocking: the ladder's T42 rung runs at dt 30 on the declared route and converts to T85 at dt 30's own reconvergence, so no route conversion needs the answer.

title: Run the world-bhs probe at -O3 with -ffpe-trap, now that the masked domains are floored
description:
world-5a0 and world-6tp made every masked domain-sensitive intrinsic and every Magnus-Teten divisor in plasim/src safe on the lanes a where block excludes, and recorded the argument for each site that needed no floor. That is the SOURCE half. The behavioural half is the probe world-bhs died on: the T42 orbit that faulted eight orbits in, from the same restart, on a binary built at -O3 with -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow.

The probe is what distinguishes 'the sites this pass could see are floored' from 'the class is gone'. lint_masked_domains.py over-reports by construction and still cannot see a mask's physics, a division by a bare name, or an intrinsic reached through a call inside a where. Only a run at the optimisation level whose transforms fire says whether anything is left.

It was not run when the source work landed because the run writes under exoplasim/runs/, which the batch working the source could not touch, and because the host was contended and a run under contention is not a measurement of anything the probe cares about. Neither is a reason the probe does not need running.

Do:
  python exoplasim/scripts/build_model.py --res T42 --ranks 16 --extra-flag=-O3 --no-publish
then the world-bhs restart on that binary, one orbit further than the eight it died at. PASS is a completed segment with a finite restart, checked by compare_restarts.py against the -O2 arm from the same state; a SIGFPE names a site the source sweep did not reach, and that site is the finding.

Two things this is NOT. It is not a timing comparison: -O2 and -O3 were already measured at the same speed and that verdict is not re-opened here. And a PASS does not retire the -O2 decision, which stands on its own measurement.

Evidence: notes/audits/masked-where-blocks.md, notes/audits/model-build-flags.md.
notes:
2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S DECISION: DEFERRED. The measured wall-clock difference
between -O2 and -O3 is negligible here, so adopting -O3 is not worth pursuing
now and the probe is not being bought.

WHAT THE DEFERRAL DOES AND DOES NOT CONCEDE, because the two are different
questions and this row is the second one. Whether -O3 is worth ADOPTING is
settled by that wall clock and the answer is no. Whether the masked-domain
class is GONE is not settled by it: -O3 is used here as an INSTRUMENT, because
its transforms fire where -O2's do not, and lint_masked_domains.py cannot see a
mask's physics, a division by a bare name, or an intrinsic reached through a
call inside a where. So this row remains the only thing that could distinguish
"the sites that pass could see are floored" from "the class is gone", and it is
being left unanswered rather than answered.

WHY THAT IS ACCEPTABLE NOW: production compiles at -O2, the profile the model
actually runs, and no masked-domain fault has appeared there. The exposure is
therefore to a hazard on a profile nothing runs.

REOPEN ON EITHER OF: production moving to -O3 or any flag whose transforms
fire like it, in which case this runs BEFORE the first commissioning run on it;
or a masked-domain fault appearing at -O2, which would show the class is live
on the profile that matters and make this probe the cheapest way to enumerate
what is left.

title: The soil heat solver ignores the soil water the model already carries
description:
notes/audits/soil-thermal-inertia.md.

Successor to world-yip, which specified the wrong term. landmod.f90:tands builds zcap and zdiff from the scalars soilcap and soildiff, and the soil column's thermal inertia is therefore one number for the whole simulated planet. The model carries the soil water prognostically -- dwatc, and dwatcl under the layered scheme -- and the soil heat solver does not read it.

Measured with analysis/soil_thermal_inertia.py on a medium-textured mineral column, thermal inertia in J/m2/K/s^0.5: saturation from air dry to saturated is 406 to 1992, a factor 4.91; bulk density at the dry end is a factor 1.61; parent-material mineralogy is a factor 1.36 at saturation and exactly 1.00 at the dry end, because Johansen's dry conductivity carries no mineralogy. landmod's pair is 2078, which that column does not reach even saturated.

So the recorded 3.3x over-damping of the playa and evaporite classes is a moisture difference, not a lithology one: those surfaces are dry and the model gives them a saturated soil's inertia. It reaches the diurnal and seasonal surface temperature amplitude, evaporation, P - E and the dust emission threshold.

Do: make zcap and zdiff functions of the column's own water. No surface code, no restart record, no generator and no new field is needed -- only landmod, and namelist keys for the dry and saturated endpoints so the scheme is declared rather than compiled.

BLOCKED ON A DECLARATION, not on effort. pedology/config/land_column_properties.yaml carries thermal.composition_dependent: undeclared, owned by lshy-5. dwatc is a bucket store in metres against dwmax, a plant-available capacity, and a degree of saturation is a fraction of PORE volume; the porosity and the retention mapping that turn one into the other belong in that contract. Choosing them inside landmod would be calibrating against numbers with no derivation.
acceptance_criteria: zcap and zdiff respond to the column's own soil water through a declared relation whose endpoints are namelist keys, and the saturation mapping comes from the land column property contract rather than from landmod.
close_reason:
zcap and zdiff are now functions of the column's own water, through a declared relation whose four endpoints are namelist keys, and the saturation mapping comes from the land column property contract rather than from landmod -- which is what LSHY-5 unblocked and why this row was blocked on a declaration rather than on effort.

soilwtherm is ONE routine read by both tands and landphase, and it takes the LAYER's water by the midpoint mapping landphase already declares. Capacity is linear in effective saturation; conductivity goes through the Kersten number.

THE CONTROL ARM NEEDS NO SWITCH: setting a dry endpoint equal to its saturated partner recovers a constant column BITWISE, because a + 0.0*Ke is a.

ONE-SIGNED, AND LARGER THAN THIS ROW ESTIMATED. Measured on the build's median column the endpoints are 0.2088 and 1.4332 W/m/K and 1.1111e6 and 2.9689e6 J/m3/K, giving a thermal inertia of 482 dry to 2063 saturated. The retired constant, 2078, sits ABOVE the saturated endpoint and above every state the store can reach -- 1342 empty, 1834 full -- so the correction is 12 to 35 per cent in one direction everywhere, rather than a redistribution.

Fixed in a file this row did not name: close_state_energy.py held SOILCAP = 2.4e6 as a copy of the landmod scalar and used it for the soil reservoir of a STORAGE-TREND closure, so a fixed capacity misstated the soil differently in wet and dry orbits. It now reads the run's own endpoints from landmod_namelist, falling back to the source, on the same terms it already reads its sea water.

title: The sea-salt Earth check's absolute arm fails low, and it is the ocean-mean wind
description:
world-fgak gave `aeolian/scripts/sea_salt_source.py`'s Earth check three bars,
fixed before it ran. Measured 2026-08-25, two pass and one fails, and the two
that pass are what make the failure diagnostic rather than ambiguous.

PASSES. The size-range arm, M86E/M86, comes out at 1.1515 against Grythe et
al. (2014) Table 2's 5.20/4.51 = 1.1530, off by 0.13 per cent against a 5 per
cent bar. That ratio carries no wind at all -- the Monahan function factorises
into a whitecap term in U10 and a size term in Dp, so the wind cancels exactly
between two rows of the same function -- so it tests the mass integration, the
size grid and the bin-edge handling and nothing else. The bin-sum identity is
1.25e-5 against a 1e-3 bar. The integrator and the source function are right.

FAILS. The absolute arm. Ours is 2.75 Pg/yr for M86 over its own Dp 0.8-8 um
range against Grythe's 4.51, a ratio of 0.610, and the bar is the 3.3 to 11.7
Pg/yr that published implementations of Monahan span (Grythe section 5.2,
quoting Lewis and Schwartz 2004). We are 17 per cent below the bottom of a
factor-of-3.5 band.

WHAT THAT LOCALISES IT TO. Grythe attribute that spread "largely" to
"differences in the models' surface wind", which is the one term this check
cannot control, and the two passing arms exclude the source function and the
integrator. So it is the wind treatment: `earth_check.ocean_mean_u10_m_s: 7.0`
with a Weibull of shape 2.

THE ARITHMETIC, since emission goes as U10^3.41 at fixed moment ratio. Entering
the band at all needs an ocean-mean U10 of 7.38 m/s; reproducing Grythe's own
M86 exactly needs 8.09 m/s; the top of the band is 10.70 m/s. So the miss is
about one metre per second on an assumed mean.

AND THE ASSUMPTION HAS NO SOURCE. The config's comment attributed 7.0 m/s to
Grythe's Fig. 3. THE PAPER STATES NO OCEAN-MEAN 10 M WIND SPEED ANYWHERE. What
it gives is the mode, section 5.2, "the most frequent wind speeds are 5-7 m s-1
with a long-tailed distribution towards higher wind speeds", and the
conclusions' "wind speeds in the range 5-14 m s-1 are very frequent and are
responsible for about 80 per cent of the global SSA production". A mode read as
a mean on a long-tailed distribution is low by construction, which is the sign
of the miss.

DO. Source a global ocean-area-weighted mean 10 m wind speed, from a reanalysis
product rather than from Grythe, and enter it with its source. Check the AWS
Registry of Open Data first per docs/src/reference/external-data.md. The second
term to check while there is the Weibull shape: `subgrid_wind.weibull_shape: 2.0`
is the declared fallback and the config says the fitted value should come from
the high-cadence extract that `--gust-samples` names, so this check is running
on the fallback.

DO NOT tune either number to make the arm pass. The bar was fixed before the
run and the miss is the information. If a sourced mean wind still leaves the
arm outside the band, that is a finding about this component's wind treatment
and belongs in a note.

Evidence: aeolian/scripts/sea_salt_source.py `_earth_check`, and the block above
`earth_check` in aeolian/config/sea_salt.yaml.
close_reason:
FIXED. Both terms the issue named were sourcing defects and both are sourced now. Commits 899d912d and f0022ea3.

THE WIND. earth_check.ocean_mean_u10_m_s is 7.566 m/s, MEASURED rather than cited: NOAA NCEI Blended Global Sea Surface Winds v2.0, the 1991-2020 monthly climatology, the file's own scalar windspeed field and its own ocean mask, cos(latitude) weighted over 694,835 ocean cells covering 71.42 per cent of the sphere, every cell finite in every month, month-weighted and day-weighted annual means agreeing to four decimals. Documented by Saha and Zhang (2022). The route and its two traps are now in docs/src/reference/external-data.md.

The scalar-versus-vector distinction was verified against the same file rather than assumed: in January the area-mean windspeed is 7.540 m/s against 4.133 for the area-mean of sqrt(u^2+v^2), a factor of 1.8, and at U10^3.41 that is two orders of magnitude. NBS speeds are 10 m EQUIVALENT-NEUTRAL, and u10_from_level reaches U10 by a Charnock roughness and a neutral log profile with no stability function, so that is the like-for-like kind rather than a bias to correct.

ALL THREE ARMS NOW PASS: M86 3.59 and M86E 4.13 Pg/yr inside the 3.3-11.7 band, size-range ratio off by 0.13 per cent against a 5 per cent bar, bin-sum identity 1.25e-5 against 1e-3. Nothing was tuned: the bars were fixed in world-fgak before the first run and the wind was sourced without reference to them. Note the issue's own arithmetic was a hair optimistic -- 7.38 m/s still fails, because M86 lands at 3.30 on a band bottom of 3.3.

THE WEIBULL SHAPE, the issue's second term, was a real defect of the same shape. The check read subgrid_wind.weibull_shape, which is THIS WORLD's and is refitted at build time from a high-cadence extract, so a Vesper refit would have moved an Earth verdict for a Vesper reason. It now reads its own earth_check.weibull_shape, sourced to Monahan (2006) Part I section 5, which asks exactly this question of QuikSCAT and answers that the Rayleigh PDF -- Weibull shape 2 -- is a reasonable approximation to the GLOBAL POOLED PDF of ocean wind speed. The pooled PDF is the right object because the check applies one moment ratio to one global mean production; the same paper's Fig. 3 shows the LOCAL shape running 2 to 6, which is why a typical local value would have been the wrong number. Behaviour preserved at 2.0. The separation matters: at the sourced wind the gated arms pass at 1.6 and 2.0 and FAIL at 2.6, the top of this world's own bracket.

A THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SAME DEFECT, found in the sweep and fixed: sea_salt_optics.py defaulted its emitted-shape wind to earth_check.ocean_mean_u10_m_s, so an EARTH constant shaped a VESPER optics product and sourcing the Earth check would have moved analysis/sea_salt_optics.json as a side effect. It is now optics.emitted_shape_u10_m_s, value unchanged at 7.0 so the artifact does not move, with the sensitivity measured rather than asserted: across the 8 per cent wind change the worst mass extinction efficiency moves 1.2e-3 relative and the worst single-scattering albedo 1.1e-5.

Both Monahan (2006) papers are now held and recorded as read in references/INDEX.md.

CORRECTION for the record: exoplasim/runs/run_ade7373b4c90 could NOT have sourced this number. earth_check.ocean_mean_u10_m_s is EARTH's, sitting beside Earth's ocean area and Earth's mean SST and used only to reproduce Grythe's Earth production. This world's own ocean-mean U10 is a different quantity and build_sea_salt.py already measures it from the climatology and reports it as surface_layer.ocean_mean_u10_m_s.

title: Re-run the emissivity contrast test at a finer rung before the field question is settled for good
description:
notes/audits/surface-longwave.md finding 2.

world-38y was closed on a measurement taken at T21: a per-cell land emissivity out of the lithology map buys, over a scalar set at its own land mean, an area-weighted 0.47 W/m2 of surface net longwave against a criterion of 1.4, and 0.17 at the out-of-band bound the held spectral library cannot rule out.

That verdict is resolution-dependent and says so. The area-weighted spread on the native mesh is three times the T21 one, which is worth about 1.2 W/m2 -- at the criterion rather than under it -- and the contrast is enriched on closed-basin cells, which are the cells the carve verdict integrates evaporation over.

Do: run analysis/emissivity_contrast.py against the finest rung this project settles on, with a climatology on that grid, and record the verdict. The criterion is fixed in the script and must not move. If it passes there, the field route is a surface code, a surfcode row, an NHOR array in radmod fed by mpsurfgp beside ddustcol, a builder of the same shape as build_surface_roughness.py, and no restart record -- the field is static.

The second thing that would reopen it is a hemispherical spectral library reaching past 20 micrometres, which would settle the out-of-band bound.

title: Classify the 133 masked divisions lint_masked_domains reports
description:
lint_masked_domains.py --kind divide reports 133 divisions whose divisor is parenthesised and which sit inside a masked where block in plasim/src. A where masks the ASSIGNMENT and not the evaluation, so a divisor that is zero only on the lanes the mask excludes still raises the divide-by-zero the declared -ffpe-trap stops on, and a denormal divisor overflows the quotient. That is the same mechanism world-5a0 settled for the domain-sensitive intrinsics.

Most of the 133 are safe by inspection -- sums that cannot vanish, such as 1.+ztcon and zcap+zdiff -- and the pass cannot tell those from the ones that can reach zero, so it reports all of them. Two of the class have already been found by reading: radmod's zsca1/zext1, where the three quotients beside it were floored and it was not (fixed under world-5a0), and rainmod's 1./real(icctot) (same). The remainder has not been read.

The pass also reports a DIVIDE only where the divisor is parenthesised. A division by a bare name is the same hazard and is not in the 133, so the population needs re-deriving before it is worked, not just reading.

Do: read every reported divisor in context, floor the ones whose masked complement can reach zero with a floor argued to be a no-op on the lanes the mask keeps, and record the rest in the script's CLASSIFIED table with the argument that makes each safe. Extend the pass to bare-name divisors first, so the population is the real one.

Evidence: notes/audits/masked-where-blocks.md, section 'What is not settled'.
notes:
Population re-derived first, as the Do: required: the pass reported a division only where the divisor was PARENTHESISED, so 133 measured the parser and not the class. All three spellings are reported now (parenthesised expression, bare name, name with a subscript or argument list) and the population is 345 sites / 156 distinct divisor keys.

Every key outside radmod.f90 is read and settled: 98 CLASSIFIED rows with the argument that says why the divisor cannot vanish, nine defects fixed. Two kinds of defect. (1) The divisor IS the mask negated -- initpm's TWOPI*restim and TWOPI*tfrc, where both arrays are declared = 0.0 so the divisor is zero on EVERY lane by default; mkicec's 2.*picedo; five in kuo; mkcflux's two conduction divisors. All floored at 1.0e-30, not tiny(), because -ffpe-trap=overflow is declared beside the zero trap. (2) The divisor is INDETERMINATE MEMORY -- tands, mktsoil and mkdca divide by automatic locals with no initialiser that are written only inside the mask. Fixed by presetting on every lane (tands, mkdca) and by dropping the mask from mktsoil's elimination and keeping it only on the two statements that write dsoilt.

radmod.f90 is the remainder: 45 keys, 102 sites, the whole of what --kind divide still reports. Left because the file was being edited on another branch and a CLASSIFIED row is keyed on argument text. Split to world-px61.
close_reason:
Settled outside radmod.f90; the radmod remainder is split to world-px61.

Population re-derived first: the pass reported a division only where the divisor was parenthesised, so 133 measured the parser. All three spellings are reported now and the population is 345 sites / 156 distinct keys. 98 non-radmod keys carry a CLASSIFIED row with the argument that says why the divisor cannot vanish; nine were defects and are fixed. Two kinds: the divisor IS the mask negated (initpm's restim and tfrc, both declared = 0.0 so the divisor is zero on every lane by default; mkicec's picedo; five in kuo; mkcflux's two conduction divisors) -- all floored at 1.0e-30 rather than tiny(), because -ffpe-trap=overflow is declared beside the zero trap; and the divisor is INDETERMINATE MEMORY (tands, mktsoil, mkdca divide by automatic locals with no initialiser written only inside the mask) -- fixed by presetting on every lane and, in mktsoil, by dropping the mask from the elimination and keeping it only on the two statements that write dsoilt. Every fix is bit-identical on the lanes the mask keeps, argued at each site.

radmod.f90 was left unread: 45 keys, 102 sites, the whole of what --kind divide still reports. The file was being edited on another branch and a CLASSIFIED row is keyed on argument text. world-px61. Commit f6e37fc2.

title: The surface humus pool's C:P is a fixed 150 with no source for a humus pool
description:
Worldbuilding: this is about the simulated soil in the vendored LPJ-GUESS CNP fork.

vendor/lpj-guess/modules/soil.cpp initialises sompool[SURFHUMUS].ptoc to 1/150
under a block citing Parton, Stewart and Cole (1988) Fig. 2. That figure is the
P submodel's flow diagram and carries no C:P values. The block's other three
values are Fig. 3's, p. 115: 80, 200 and 80 are the ctop_max ends of the active,
slow and surface microbial lines, and setptoc() overwrites all three on the
first call to somfluxes(), so their provenance barely matters.

SURFHUMUS's 150 is different in two ways. It is not a Fig. 3 endpoint -- 150
appears in that paper only as the lower bound on the C:P of new plant material
for wheat (p. 112) and as the structural litter C:N -- and nothing overwrites
it. SURFHUMUS is in the nitrogen ramp and not the phosphorus one, its setptoc
line is commented out because the paper has no humus pool to take a
(ctop_max, ctop_min) pair from, and WORLD-16PB removed it from the phosphorus
immobilisation branch's ptoc reduction list. So 150 is now the surface humus
pool's C:P for the whole of a run, unchanging, and it is the phosphorus content
of every transfer out of SURFSTRUCT, SURFFWD, SURFCWD and SURFMICRO into it.

This is the residual of WORLD-16PB: that issue asked what sets the surface humus
pool's C:P and the answer, structurally, is the initialisation. What is open is
the value.

Do: find a source for a surface humus C:P, or decide the pool should take one of
the ramped pools' P:C on the grounds that it feeds SLOWSOM. Note that the value
is load-bearing in a way it was not before, because it no longer drifts.

Blocks bio-10 only if it is judged to bite under ifplim 1; it is live under
ifplim 0 as well, because ptoc is read by transferdecomp regardless.

Evidence: biosphere/notes/phosphorus-cycle-parameterisation.md,
references/parton1988-century-c-n-p-s-grassland-model.pdf p. 112 and p. 115.
notes:
2026-08-25, branch fanout-W6, commit 638a9653. FIXED, and by the second of the two options in the Do line: the pool takes a ramped pool's P:C, on the slow pool's line.

WHAT WAS TRUE. sompool[SURFHUMUS].ptoc = 1/150 in soil.cpp, never overwritten, and transferdecomp (somdynam.cpp:761) reads sompool[receiver].ptoc with NO ifplim guard, so it set pinc for every transfer into surface humus in both configurations. Verified in source.

WHY 200 AND 90 ARE NOT AN UNSOURCED IMPORT. The pair is Parton, Stewart and Cole (1988) Fig. 3's slow line. The identification of surface humus with the slow pool is the fork's OWN, stated twice: (1) setntoc(soil, nmin_mass, SURFHUMUS, 30.0, 15.0, 0.0, NMASS_SAT) is character-for-character SLOWSOM's pair off SLOWSOM's driver, so the nitrogen side already ramps this pool as the slow pool at the surface, from the soil's mineral nutrient; (2) soil.cpp's own alternative P initialisation, commented out beside the live one, sets SURFHUMUS and SLOWSOM to the same 1/90. SURFHUMUS's only outflow is to SLOWSOM.

WHY NOT A MEASURED HUMUS C:P. It is the wrong KIND of quantity, not merely a missing one. setptoc sets the P:C at which a pool RECEIVES carbon -- a stoichiometric target that moves with labile P by the McGill and Cole (1981) phosphatase mechanism the paper builds on. A forest-floor C:P measurement is an emergent bulk ratio. A fixed number is the wrong shape for this argument however well sourced, which is what 1/150 was. No paper was fetched, because the fetch would not have answered the question.

CHANGES. somdynam.cpp: setptoc(soil, pmin_mass, SURFHUMUS, 200.0, 90.0, 0.0, PMASS_SAT) uncommented. soil.cpp: initialisation 1/150 -> 1/200, the slow line's ctop_max end, which is the pattern its three neighbours follow and which makes the value not load-bearing again -- somfluxes overwrites it on the first call, inside equilsom as well (equilsom calls somfluxes(patch, true, false) at somdynam.cpp:2224). Both are DECLARED DIVERGENCES from the vendored CNP fork with its own lines verbatim beside them.

WORLD-16PB. That issue's Do line asked for the set setptoc covers and the set the P immobilisation branch flexes to be the same set. SURFHUMUS is back in the flexing list, because it is re-derived now. That arm is unreachable in both directions (the || !ifplim short-circuit takes ifplim 0 and the else-if is false under ifplim 1), so no behaviour changes by it.

WHAT MOVES. Under ifplim 0 the PMASS_SAT pin holds fac at fmax, so the surface humus pool's C:P is a fixed 90 instead of a fixed 150 and the phosphorus riding carbon into it rises by 1.67. Under ifplim 1 it ramps 200 to 90 with labile P like the other three. It no longer ratchets in either.

Nothing execution-verified. LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree; the three changed source lines are shape-identical to their neighbours and were checked by reading, not by compiling the module.
close_reason: The surface humus pool ramps 200 to 90 off labile P on Parton Fig. 3's slow line, under the identification the fork's own nitrogen ramp already makes; the unsourced fixed 1/150 initialisation moves to 1/200 and is overwritten on the first somfluxes call. Declared divergences from the vendored CNP fork. Commit 638a9653.

title: Measure the uniqueness identity and the reduction identity on the planet
description:
The synthetic arm is in and has controls that go red: `groundwater.py
--uniqueness-test`, recorded in `hydrography/notes/water-table-convergence.md`.
What it does NOT give is a result on this world's own mesh, and two declared
checks are waiting on the same thing.

    python hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater.py --uniqueness-check --climatology <path>
    python hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater.py --reduction-test --climatology <path>

Why neither has been run. `config/planet.yaml` declares no
`baseline_climatology`, so both need `--climatology` named by hand, and the only
climatology on disk for `precarve-craton-10m` is the BOOTSTRAP one from
`run_2b20e3324bb0`. And the reverse trajectory starts with every land cell free,
so it factors the whole 4,328,736-cell land set of this build before a single
cell is pinned; the host these were attempted on had about 29 GB free under a
load average of 25, and a direct factorisation of that graph does not fit.

Do: run both on a host with the memory, or after a baseline climatology is
declared, and record what they return in
`hydrography/notes/water-table-convergence.md` beside the synthetic arm. The
bars are unchanged: `SCHEME_HEAD_RELATIVE` for the uniqueness arm under the
confined form, bitwise for the reduction arm.

The reduction arm has not been measured since GW-15 landed at all: until
world-qq10 it left the sink and the baselevels at their defaults, so its
documented one-command form could not have met its bitwise bar.
notes:
2026-08-25, coordinator. THE MEMORY CLAIM WAS ABOUT CONTENTION, NOT CAPACITY, AND THE ORDERING WAS COSTING A FACTOR OF TWO.

MEASURED, on a planar-graph Laplacian matched to this operator's nonzeros per row:

  n            COLAMD                    MMD_AT_PLUS_A
  399,424       50.3 M entries  1.5 s     27.5 M  1.1 s
  1,000,000    145.1 M          6.2 s     78.5 M  3.6 s
  1,999,396    335.6 M         23.4 s    168.0 M  8.0 s

Fitted fill exponents 1.178 and 1.123, so at this build's 4,328,736 land cells the factor is 834 M entries against 400 M: about 10.0 GB against 4.8 GB at 12 bytes an entry, before SuperLU's working set, which runs about 1.5 to 2 times the finished factor. This host has 61 GB. Both fit; the smaller one fits comfortably.

What was hit was free memory under a five-way fan-out, not the machine: at the time of the attempt about 29 GB was free at load average 25, and the same host later showed 15 GB free with 35 GB of swap in use for the same reason. The description said a direct factorisation of that graph does not fit, and that is too strong. It does not fit ALONGSIDE a fan-out. Corrected here rather than in the description so the original claim and its correction both stay visible.

FIXED IN PASSING, and it is why the numbers above are worth having: scipy's spsolve defaults to COLAMD, which orders for an unsymmetric pattern. This operator's pattern IS symmetric -- a graph Laplacian with Dirichlet rows -- so minimum degree on A + A^T is the right ordering and COLAMD was paying for generality the matrix does not have. groundwater.py now passes permc_spec MMD_AT_PLUS_A, with the table above recorded at the call site. All five arms of --uniqueness-test still return their required verdicts; the only movement is third_start at 5.296e-10 to 5.295e-10 m, roundoff from a different pivot order and four orders inside the 1e-9 bar. The dupuit round-off guard still refuses its trip case.

WHAT REMAINS BLOCKING is the climatology and not the memory. config/planet.yaml declares baseline_climatology null, so both commands still need --climatology named by hand and the only one on disk for this build is the bootstrap from run_2b20e3324bb0. Run them when a baseline exists, or on an idle host against the bootstrap if a provisional answer is wanted; the bars are unchanged.

ONE THING THE MEMORY BLOCKER HAS NOT BEEN TRIED AGAINST, 2026-08-25, from GW-8's instrument arm. solve() calls spsolve with permc_spec='MMD_AT_PLUS_A' and SuperLU's DEFAULT pivoting, which reorders rows during the factorisation and can undo the symmetric ordering it was just given. On the whole-mesh Laplacian with a single pinned cell that costs everything: 6.8 M nonzeros in the factor with diag_pivot_thresh=0 and SymmetricMode at 80,000 regions, against a 2.5 GB working set and no answer without them. The matrix solve() factors is symmetric positive definite too, so no pivoting is the correct setting there rather than merely the fast one.

It is NOT known to help here. On a synthetic of solve()'s own shape -- a free set inside a Dirichlet boundary, spatially coherent conductivity across Gleeson's 3.4 orders -- at 55,977 free cells the factor is 1,042,714 nonzeros and a 0.55 GB peak IDENTICALLY either way, and the four-times larger arm did not finish. So the two settings are indistinguishable at the one size measured and unmeasured above it. Worth trying before concluding the reverse trajectory does not fit: it is a two-line change to solve() and costs a factorisation to test. hydrography/notes/mesh-geometry.md carries the numbers.

2026-08-25, batch BQ, NEGATIVE RESULT ON THE ORDERING LEVER. The fill halving measured above was taken with splu on a synthetic planar-graph Laplacian. It does NOT carry to this operator at the size solve() actually runs: on a synthetic of solve()'s own shape at 55,977 free cells the fill is IDENTICAL with COLAMD and with MMD_AT_PLUS_A. SuperLU's default partial pivoting reorders for stability and undoes a symmetric ordering unless SymmetricMode is set with diag_pivot_thresh 0, which spsolve cannot pass and splu can. So the permc_spec keyword now in solve() is free and correct and is not known to buy anything on the forward solve; the comment at the call site says so rather than leaving the table reading as a promise.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THIS ISSUE. The memory argument stands but the remedy changes: the reverse trajectory would need splu with options SymmetricMode True and diag_pivot_thresh 0.0, not spsolve with permc_spec. That is the one lever this blocker has not been tried against, and it is cheap to try. A whole-mesh attempt under SymmetricMode reached 6.8M nonzeros against a 2.5 GB working set without it at 80,000 regions, so the direction is right at scale even though the crossover between 55,977 and the full land set is unmeasured -- the larger arm did not finish under contention.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
ADJACENT RESULT, 2026-08-30, from GW-24's arm rather than as work on this row. The REDUCTION arm of the pair this row wants has now been run on the planet, under the UNCONFINED form:

  build_groundwater.py --climatology <bootstrap> --unconfined --reduction-test

on canonical-10m-carve2, 10,000,005 regions and 30,000,009 faces. PASS and bitwise: seepage equals recharge on every land cell at a worst absolute difference of 0.0 m3/s, largest absolute basin Qg 0.0 over 4,462 basins, closure relative residual 1.408e-16 against 1e-10. hydrography/analysis/groundwater_reduction_test.json carries it.

That is NOT this row's arm and does not close it. This row wants the CONFINED reduction identity and the CONFINED uniqueness identity, and the confined reduction arm is a different assembly even though both reduce to the same surface-only balance. It does however retire one worry: the reduction case reaches its verdict quickly on this build, because zero permeability leaves nothing to solve, so the confined reduction arm is cheap and is not what the memory or wall-time blocker is about.

TWO OF THIS ROW'S THREE STATED BLOCKERS ARE GONE. A baseline climatology now exists for the active build, so neither command needs one named by hand for want of one; and world-fvpt, which is why build_groundwater.py refused with its own defaults at all, is fixed and closed.

WHAT REMAINS IS THE UNIQUENESS ARM AND ITS COST, and the measurement to put beside this row's memory argument is that a CONFINED solve of the real case on this build ran past 40 minutes alone on the host at 2,600% CPU and about 16 GB before being killed, without writing. The reverse trajectory starts with every land cell free, so it is the larger of the two. Recorded on world-wfge.

title: CH4_oxid and CH4_vgc are read from indeterminate memory until the first methane call
description:
Soil::init_states in vendor/lpj-guess/modules/soil.cpp initialises every other member of the gas set -- CH4, CH4_gas, CH4_diss, CH4_ebull_ind, CH4_ebull_vol, CH4_gas_vol, tiller_area and the rest -- and does not touch CH4_oxid[NLAYERS] or CH4_vgc[NLAYERS] at all. Both are therefore indeterminate memory on a freshly constructed Soil, and both are absent from Soil::serialize.

They are safe today only because Soil::methane writes every active layer before reading it: CH4_oxid at soilmethane.cpp:1098 before the reads at :1099-:1102, CH4_vgc at :745 before the reads at :749-:754. That is an ordering property of one routine, not an invariant, and it holds only for the active layer range: a read at an index below IDX would return whatever the allocation held.

Do: initialise both in Soil::init_states alongside the members beside them. Check whether upstream leaves them uninitialised too; if so this is a declared divergence recorded beside the mainline behaviour rather than a bug this project introduced.

Source: biosphere/notes/soil-restart-state.md finding 6.
close_reason: Fixed. Soil::init_states now sets CH4_oxid and CH4_vgc, both zero and both DERIVED: CH4_vgc is CH4_gas_vol over the layer volume and CH4_gas_vol is zeroed on the line above, CH4_oxid is min(CH4, 0.5*O2) and both are zeroed. So zero is what each writer in soilmethane.cpp would produce from the state init_states leaves. No result changes: every read of either is preceded by a write in the same enclosing condition, which is also why neither belongs in Soil::serialize. Upstream (the vendored CNP fork, commit b489c42f) leaves both uninitialised, so this is a declared divergence, recorded in the source and in biosphere/notes/soil-restart-state.md finding 6. Commit 4b1b9184.

title: climate.dtr has a source now; the driver seam has no array to carry it
description:
world-j0az closed the producer half: codes 201 and 202 reach the regular product as `tasmax`/`tasmin`, so the near-surface AIR temperature range `climate.dtr` means exists in a climatology postprocessed since that change.

What still refuses is the seam. `vesperinput.cpp` fails `ifbvoc 1` outright and sets `climate.dtr = 0.0`, because the fourth driver array is `maxt - mint`, the SURFACE range, and `VESPDRV6` has no fifth array. `bvoc.cpp:daytime_temp` is dtr's only reader and `cfinput.cpp` builds dtr from air-temperature extrema, which fixes the meaning beyond argument.

THE DECISION, and it is a decision rather than a consequence. Adding a fifth array means `VESPDRV7`, a new read in `vesperinput.cpp`, a field in `vesperinput.h`, an `interp_monthly_means_conserve` call, and lifting the refusal. That is investment in a transport `biosphere/notes/ecological-climate-forcing-audit.md` calls integration scaffolding and says should not be versioned again around a fixed bin count -- EFOR-1 chooses the replacement and EFOR-3 builds it, and the ecological stream (EFOR-2) already carries the same air extrema as codes 625 and 626 at an interval it declares.

So: either
  (a) VESPDRV7 with a fifth array, which unblocks ifbvoc now on the 12-bin path, or
  (b) leave the refusal standing and let EFOR-3's transport carry the range, which is where it belongs.

What settles it is whether BVOC is wanted before EFOR-3 lands. If it is, (a); if not, (b) and this issue closes against EFOR-3.

Evidence: vendor/lpj-guess/modules/vesperinput.cpp lines 21-23, 242-248, 464-489; vendor/lpj-guess/modules/vesperinput.h line 80; biosphere/scripts/build_lpj_driver.py MAGIC and the fourth array; biosphere/notes/ecological-forcing-field-contract.md, 'Open, and at the driver seam'.
close_reason:
2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER: option (b). Leave the refusal standing and let EFOR-3's transport carry the air-temperature diurnal range. Do not add VESPDRV7.

The reasoning, in the author's words: 'always do the work now' assumes the work is durable, and this work is not. biosphere/notes/ecological-climate-forcing-audit.md says this transport should not be versioned again around a fixed bin count, EFOR-3 replaces it wholesale, and a fifth array on VESPDRV7 is about thirty lines that EFOR-3 then deletes. The only thing it buys is ifbvoc running on the 12-bin path before EFOR-3 lands, and BVOC is not wanted that badly.

CLOSED AGAINST EFOR-3 rather than left open, because what remains is a requirement on another row and not work on this one. That requirement is now written into EFOR-3's notes with the trap that matters: climate.dtr means the AIR temperature range, the current driver's fourth array is the SURFACE range, and an EFOR-3 artifact that carries the surface range under that name would satisfy the seam and be wrong.

WORLD-UA4A stays open and is the fail-closed marker in the meantime: vesperinput.cpp's refusal fires inside the run, and that row moves it into bvoc.yaml so bvoc_gate.py names the precondition before anything starts.

title: The snapshot stream's temperature extrema cover a partial, variable window
description:
`SNAPSHOT_CODES` carries 320 and 321, maxt and mint. In the snapshot stream they are not extrema over the snapshot interval and not extrema over anything a consumer can name.

plasim.f90 calls `outaccu` every timestep, `snapshotgp` every `nstps` steps, and `outreset` only after `outgp` at every `nafter` steps. So a snapshot record of 320/321 holds the running extremum accumulated since the last REGULAR output write. The window it covers is (nstep mod nafter) timesteps, which varies from record to record and is zero on the record that follows a write.

Every other field in the snapshot stream is an instantaneous sample, which is what the stream is for; these two are a partial accumulation wearing the same shape. A consumer that reads the stream as samples and takes a variance or a distribution over 320/321 is reading a sawtooth of window lengths.

Three ways out and they are not equivalent:
  - drop 320/321 from SNAPSHOT_CODES. An instantaneous extremum is ts itself, code 139, which the stream already carries.
  - give the snapshot stream its own extrema with their own reset in snapshotgp, which is a second pair of accumulators and a second pair of restart records.
  - keep them and declare in the product metadata that they are partial accumulations, which pyburn's FIELD_NOTES can now carry.

The first is the cheapest and loses nothing the stream does not already have. Found while adding 201/202 to REGULAR_CODES under world-j0az; 201/202 were deliberately NOT added to SNAPSHOT_CODES because they would inherit the same defect.

Evidence: vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/plasim.f90 lines 826, 831, 883, 888; outmod.f90:snapshotgp writes tempmin/tempmax at codes 320/321.
close_reason: snapshotgp no longer writes 320/321 and SNAPSHOT_CODES no longer asks for them, on the world-j0az precedent that kept 201/202 out. The running extrema are cleared only by outreset on the regular cadence, so a snapshot record covered (nstep mod nafter) timesteps. Regular-stream extrema unchanged; nothing reads maxt/mint from a snapshot product.

title: Run the three clwref arms now that the route from config exists
description:
world-n1nu put clwref on a route from config/planet.yaml into rainmod_nl: model.cloud_water_reference_kg_m3 is declared at rainmod.f90's compiled value, run_exoplasim.py writes CLWREF@rainmod_namelist unconditionally, continue_exoplasim.py reapplies it per segment, and expected_namelist_keys covers it. The arms are now a run rather than a code change, and nothing has run them.

Do: the three points in exoplasim/notes/cloud-water-reference.md -- 0.000105, 0.00021 as control, 0.00042 -- on ONE binary and ONE restart, and read them against that note's predictions and its three falsifying conditions. The control must be bit-identical to a run that declares nothing, which the route makes structural rather than coincidental: the declared default is read out of rainmod.f90 rather than copied.

The note also states the decision procedure if an arm fails to equilibrate or crosses the sea-ice transition (run the 0.75x and 1.33x pair and read the slope from those), and states that lib/sensitivity.py's slope is LOCAL and must not be used to convert a response this size. Predicted beyond 2 K per arm, plausibly 5 to 10 K, larger arm cooling.

Evidence: exoplasim/notes/cloud-water-reference.md; world-8h6 states the bracket; world-n1nu built the route.
close_reason:
All three arms run on ONE binary and ONE restart, and all three falsifying conditions held.

  0.5x clwref 0.000105  run_7536d6b7288a   +4.34 K, TOA +4.04 W/m2, sea ice -0.040
  control     0.00021   run_57a43e1fc3f4   60 orbits
  2.0x        0.00042   run_ccb8ee8384e6   -4.64 K, TOA -3.42 W/m2, sea ice +0.058

BIT-IDENTITY PASSED, and structurally rather than coincidentally: run_0730a12ecfbd with the config key DELETED stages CLWREF = 0.00021 out of rainmod's own default and writes a MOST_REST.00000 bit-identical to the control's. That is what world-n1nu's route was for -- the declared default is read from the source rather than copied, so a control that declares nothing and a control that declares the default are the same run.

The three conditions: neither arm under 1 K -- both above 4. 2.0x cools and 0.5x warms -- the assigned sign is the measured sign. More than 2 K -- held at better than twice.

THE PLAUSIBLE RANGE MISSED LOW, by 0.4 to 0.7 K against its 5 to 10 K, and the prediction is LEFT AS WRITTEN. Worth recording why it is interesting rather than embarrassing: that bound had been widened UPWARD after PHYS-11, and this time the model responded LESS. A range that was moved once and then missed in the other direction is evidence about the range, not about the arms.

lib/sensitivity.py's slope is local and was not used to convert a response this size, per the note's own instruction.

title: Nothing stops a new unguarded write(nud) from reaching plasim_diag from every thread
description:
world-0ihs found thirteen write(nud,...) sites that every thread reached, fixed them, and left the convention resting on nothing but the next author reading notes/audits/shared-diagnostics-unit-under-threads.md. There are ~928 sites across 24 files in vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src and the model gains more; the whole run is one OpenMP parallel region, so an unguarded one is NPRO interleaved copies in the diagnostics file and makes it non-deterministic run to run.

The check that would fail: no write(nud,...) or write(*,...) in plasim/src is reachable by a thread other than 0 without either an enclosing mypid == NROOT test, an enclosing npro == 1 test, or an enclosing !$omp critical. That is answerable statically and the two passes are already written and proven: a lexical guard walk over if/else/select nesting, then a fixed point over the call graph for 'every call site is under a root guard or in a subroutine that is itself root-only'. The scratch versions reduced 928 sites to 214 to 13 and were then read one by one to confirm.

Do: put those two passes in exoplasim/scripts/ as a gate, seed it with the current set as the passing state, and add it to scripts/smoke_test.py. The parser must over-report rather than under-report -- the scratch version cleared its guard stack on 'end where', which turns a guarded site into a reported one and never the reverse, and that is the safe direction. reproducibility_matrix.py declares a plasim_diag-only disagreement as this candidate first, so a gate here also sharpens that verdict.

Not done under world-0ihs because that issue's Do: was the sweep, and a gate is a new component with a documentation row of its own.
close_reason: Gated. exoplasim/scripts/lint_diag_writes.py holds the two passes (lexical guard walk, then the call-graph fixed point), registered in config/pipeline.yaml and exoplasim/README.md and run by scripts/smoke_test.py. It permits four answers -- mypid == NROOT, npro == 1, !$omp critical, or a procedure the call graph shows is reached only through those -- and forbids everything else. The exception table is EMPTY: every existing write passes on a rule, not a row. Twenty fixtures run before the tree does. It found a fourteenth unguarded site the first sweep missed (hurricanemod entropy_deficit's print statement, which is unit 6 too) and one guard written as mypid == 0. Commit 4691c0c9.

title: The land column scheme reaches the model from nowhere: no config route for landmod_nl's LSHY-3 and LSHY-5 keys
description: LSHY-3 landed a selectable land liquid water scheme and LSHY-5 landed soil phase, and neither can be selected. nlandwcol, nlsoilw, nlandwdrain, dsoilwf, dsoilwz, nlandwphase, drhslow and nrhsexp are landmod_nl keys with compiled defaults, and run_exoplasim.py's configure_otherargs -- the one route a namelist key takes from config/planet.yaml to the model, and the one continue_exoplasim reapplies per segment -- carries none of them. Only ALBFOREST and DSMAX reach landmod_namelist. So the whole selection is reachable only by hand-editing a namelist in a run directory, which continue_exoplasim would overwrite on the next segment, and no artifact would record which scheme a run integrated. The consequence is that every registered hypothesis except the default is unrunnable and the bracket LSHY-3 exists to make a runtime selection is still a code fork in practice. Do: add the keys to configure_otherargs and to the declared-namelist check beside ALBFOREST and DSMAX, with a config block that declares the scheme, and derive them the way the icemod keys are derived rather than defaulting them silently. Found while adding world-p9qq's drainage output code 231: the code is now in REGULAR_CODES unconditionally because there is no configuration to gate it on. Evidence: vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/landmod.f90 landmod_nl, exoplasim/scripts/run_exoplasim.py configure_otherargs
close_reason:
FIXED in 913e2ab1. The eight landmod_nl keys reach the model from config/planet.yaml's surface.land_water_column: scheme (bucket|layered) -> NLANDWCOL, layers -> NLSOILW, lower_boundary (impermeable|free_drainage) -> NLANDWDRAIN, layer_capacity_fraction -> DSOILWF, layer_thickness_m -> DSOILWZ, soil_phase -> NLANDWPHASE, evaporation_limiter.theta_low/.exponent -> DRHSLOW/NRHSEXP. All eight go through configure_otherargs, so continue_exoplasim reapplies them per segment, and all eight are in expected_namelist_keys, so a continuation that drops one fails its own staging check instead of reverting silently.

SHOULD IT EXIST: yes, for all eight. Every one has Fortran that reads it, both LSHY-3 kernels are compiled in and checked bitwise against each other by verify_land_column_reduction.sh, the limiter pair is the axis pair that separates this model from cGENIE's ENTS, and LSHY-5's phase is the term that disagrees with LPJ-GUESS. None is a route to a hypothesis with no reader: LSHY-3's third hypothesis, gradient-driven flow, is not implemented and is deliberately not given a config word.

DERIVED THE WAY THE ICEMOD KEYS ARE: the compiled defaults are READ out of landmod.f90 and landcolumn.f90 (landmod_default, landmod_default_array, land_water_layer_limit), never copied, which is lib/sea_water.py's argument. So a config that omits the block reproduces the compiled value by construction. Verified end to end rather than assumed: each key routes through configure_otherargs, exoplasim._edit_namelist and namelist_value back to exactly the value the Fortran declares -- NLANDWCOL 0, NLSOILW 1, NLANDWDRAIN 0, DSOILWF 1.0, DSOILWZ 1.5, NLANDWPHASE 0, DRHSLOW 0.0, NRHSEXP 1. The config declares those, so the current world is unchanged.

An import-time check ties the word 'bucket' to landmod.f90's own nlandwcol default and 'impermeable' to nlandwdrain's, so an inverted mapping stops the file loading rather than putting every run on the other scheme under a config that reads as the default; proved to fire against a mutated copy of the source.

Two refusals fire at config read rather than after a model launch: soil_phase without a layered column (landini refuses the same combination) and a layer count that disagrees with the per-layer list lengths (landini CANNOT catch that -- it reads the first nlsoilw entries of an array whose tail is compiled zeros, so a short list runs with a zero).

REGULAR_CODES code 231 left alone: the comment beside it argues for carrying drainage unconditionally on its own merits, and that argument is unaffected. Running the arms is lshy-7, whose notes now record that the reductions are configurable.

title: Sweep Soil::serialize against the Soil class: 70 members are not restart state
description:
world-c4j8 added the six members biosphere/config/wetlands.yaml requires. A sweep of the whole Soil class in framework/guess.h against the body of Soil::serialize finds 70 of its 174 scalar and fixed-array members still absent, and several of those are prognostic across the year boundary a restart actually happens at:

- firstHydrologyCalc and firstTempCalc are bools recording whether those routines have ever run. A restart resets them to their constructed value and the code takes the first-call branch on a column that is not on its first call.
- CH4[NLAYERS], CH4_diss, CH4_gas, CO2_soil, CO2_soil_prod: the dissolved and gaseous stores the methane model advances daily. CH4_gas_yesterday, CH4_diss_yesterday, CH4_gas_vol and O2 ARE serialized, so the restart carries yesterday's copy of a store and not the store.
- T[NLAYERS] and T_soil[NLAYERS], where T_old and T_soil_yesterday are serialized.
- sub_water[NSUBLAYERS_ACRO], acro_co2, snowdens, dec_snowdepth, maxthawdepththisyear, mthaw[12], dthaw[MAX_YEAR_LENGTH].
- IDX, MIDX, SIDX, SIDX_old, ngroundl, nsublayer1, nsublayer2, num_evaplayers: the layer indices every array access is taken through.

Do: decide per member whether it is prognostic or recomputed before the first read after a restart, serialize the prognostic ones, and record the recomputed ones as recomputed so the next sweep does not re-litigate them. Then run biosphere/scripts/verify_lpj_restart_continuity.py, which is what turns the list into a verdict.

The reproduction of the sweep is a parse of the Soil class body in framework/guess.h against the member names streamed in Soil::serialize; biosphere/scripts/wetland_gate.py:_serialized_members already does the second half.

Found while repairing Soil::serialize under world-c4j8.
close_reason: All 70 unserialized members classified, each with the file:line that settles it, in biosphere/config/soil_restart_state.yaml; biosphere/scripts/soil_restart_state_gate.py checks Soil::serialize against it and refuses on an unclassified member, a contradicted classification, a dropped name, an unevidenced verdict or a non-empty lost block, with six fixtures built to be wrong in a named way plus the live declaration which must be granted. Seven were genuinely lost and are now carried: acro_co2, dmoss_wtp_limit and dgraminoid_wtp_limit, which canopy_exchange reads the day before hydrology_peat writes them, and dec_snowdepth, dthaw, mthaw and maxthawdepththisyear, which a day-0 restart rebuilt but an arbitrary-day one does not. The issue's other premises were wrong and the evidence is recorded: firstTempCalc and firstHydrologyCalc are not the first-call hazard they look like (every block firstTempCalc guards tests restart or first_year beside it, upstream's own arms present at the subtree merge; firstHydrologyCalc is tested nowhere), the CH4/CO2 _yesterday asymmetry is the design because today's store is rebuilt from the carried copy each day, T and T_soil come from T_old and T_soil_yesterday, and IDX/MIDX/SIDX are recomputed daily. One latent trap repaired without changing a number: init_hydrology_variables now runs on the restart path, since it is the only writer of alwhc_init. No state files exist in the tree, so the changed layout invalidates nothing. Nothing here is execution-verified beyond a g++ -fsyntax-only pass; the behavioural half needs a compiled model and a baseline climatology. biosphere/notes/soil-restart-state.md carries the argument. Follow-ups filed on the six dead members, on CH4_oxid/CH4_vgc reading indeterminate memory, and on land-use change reading the wet/dry pools before the day writes them.

title: get_mineral inverts Cosby's heads as if this world's gravity were Earth's
description:
vendor/lpj-guess/modules/soilinput.cpp SoilInput::get_mineral builds the simulated soil's wilting point and field capacity by inverting Cosby et al. (1984) eqn 1 at two matric heads:

    double Psi_wilt = min(pow(10.0, -4.2), Psi_s);
    double Psi_whc  = min(pow(10.0, -2.0), Psi_s);

10^4.2 and 10^2.0 are heads in CENTIMETRES OF WATER, and a head is a pressure only through the local gravity: p = rho*g*h. At Earth's gravity 10^4.2 cm is -1.554 MPa, which is the conventional permanent wilting point, and 10^2.0 cm is -0.0098 MPa. Nothing in the inversion reads config/planet.yaml's gravity, so on this world the same head is a different suction and the simulated soil's wilting point is the water content at a HEAD rather than at the suction plants work against. Plants wilt at a pressure, not at a column height.

The direction is knowable: at higher gravity the same suction is a smaller head, so the true wilting point is WETTER than the code's and the available water capacity gawc is overstated. Everything keyed on wcont therefore shifts, which is the whole soil water column, the Gerten drainage and every moisture response in ntransform.cpp.

Found while placing Stark and Firestone (1995)'s water-potential axis onto Soil::wfps for world-xmiq. It moves both sides of that comparison together, so it does not invalidate it, but it is what the comparison rests on.

Do: decide whether the two heads are the quantity the soil model means, or whether the two POTENTIALS are and the heads should be derived from them and this world's gravity. Note that Cosby's regressions are fitted in head units, so the air-entry Psi_s carries the same question. Files: vendor/lpj-guess/modules/soilinput.cpp. Related: biosphere/notes/implicit-earth-assumptions.md.
notes:
2026-08-25, coordinator. THE MECHANISM IS RIGHT AND THE STATE IS WRONG. The heads in get_mineral are indeed inverted as if gravity were Earth's, but converting Psi_wilt alone mixes two frames. Cosby eqn 1 inverts on Psi_s, the AIR-ENTRY head, and air entry is a capillary PRESSURE that Cosby recorded as an Earth head exactly as the wilting point is. Convert one and not the other and the ratio Psi_s/Psi_wilt changes for a reason that is bookkeeping rather than physics.

Done consistently the wilting point does not move at all. theta_wilt = theta_s*(h_ae/h_wilt)^(1/b); both heads scale by g_earth/g_vesper together, the ratio is invariant, and so is theta_wilt. The only state whose DEFINING pressure carries gravity is field capacity, because it is a drainage equilibrium at rho_w*g*L and nothing else in the closure is defined by a balance against gravity.

Measured on the configured build's T21 map, 1019 cells, AWC relative to the shipped code: consistent Earth-equivalent frame (curve fixed, field-capacity head 100 -> 131 cm) 0.9283; consistent Vesper frame (h_ae and h_wilt both divided by 1.3063, field-capacity head 100 cm) 0.9283, identical as it must be; this issue as written, wilting head converted and air-entry head not, 0.9627. The 0.963 is the artifact.

CONSEQUENCE: this is not a separate correction that composes with WORLD-OF6N's closure_at_vesper_suction candidate. It IS that candidate, reached from the other side, and landing both would apply the gravity conversion once and a frame-mixing artifact once. Settle it inside of6n and close this as subsumed rather than landing 0.963 separately.
close_reason: SUBSUMED into WORLD-OF6N, which adopted closure_at_vesper_suction. The mechanism named here is right and the state named here is wrong, and the arithmetic settles which. Available capacity on the configured build's T21 map, 1019 cells, relative to the shipped code: consistent Earth-equivalent frame, curve fixed and field-capacity head 100 -> 130.63 cm, 0.9283 median (0.9242-0.9324); consistent Vesper frame, air-entry and wilting heads both divided by 1.3063 and field-capacity head 100 cm, 0.9283 median, agreeing with the first to 5.6e-17 volumetric as an identity requires; this issue as written, wilting head converted and air-entry head not, 0.9626 median. The 0.963 is a frame-mixing artifact and not a correction: air entry is a CAPILLARY pressure and the wilting point is a PLANT pressure, both invariant, both recorded as Earth heads, and the closure reads them only through their ratio, so done consistently the wilting point does not move at all. Field capacity is the only state whose defining pressure carries gravity. Implemented by evaluating the closure in PASCALS in pedology/scripts/land_column_properties.py contract_states, where each Earth head becomes a pressure once at Earth gravity and this world's g enters at one place; frame_consistency runs all three frames every time the contract runs and fails if the two consistent ones disagree, if the pressure derivation disagrees with the head one, or if the frame-mixed variant becomes indistinguishable from them. Landing this beside of6n would have applied the gravity conversion once and the artifact once. The Stark and Firestone comparison this was found under is unaffected and its axis is now settled as a pressure axis: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md is updated.

title: A stock-LPJ-GUESS-4.1.1 comparison arm for the eleven declared ntransform divergences
description:
biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml declares eleven divergences from mainline LPJ-GUESS 4.1.1 in modules/ntransform.cpp and data/ins/global_soiln.ins, all verdict 'keep' under world-i2ch. None is execution-verified: LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree, so every verdict rests on arithmetic on the declared forms and on Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008), Weier et al. (1993), Linn and Doran (1984), Greaves and Carter (1920) and Stark and Firestone (1995).

The arm: same build, same climatology, same instruction file except f_nitri_gas_max, and modules/ntransform.cpp reverted to the release in the stock arm. The port already exists, so this is a second compile and a second run and no new code. Compare NET_NITRIF, NET_DENITRIF, NO_SOIL, N2O_SOIL, N2_SOIL, NH3_SOIL and the mineral nitrogen the simulated plants take up.

WHAT IT SETTLES, exactly. It CANNOT say which divergence is right: both arms are Earth calibrations and the disagreements are between Earth calibrations. It CAN bound what they are worth, which no by-hand number in the note can, because each of those is a change to a COEFFICIENT and the Michaelis-Menten terms and the min() against the pool stand between a coefficient and a flux. The five also do not point the same way on mineral nitrogen -- the gas share raises it, the crossed read, the pH correction and the temperature clamp lower it, by amounts that depend on a gridcell's water, pH and temperature -- so which dominates is not answerable by hand at all.

BLOCKED on LPJ-GUESS building, which needs a baseline climatology that does not exist. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md, the comparison-arm section.
