title: Should the scarp relief thresholds carry the 1/g relief scaling?
description:
computeScarpPotential's two relief thresholds are now a measured Earth escarpment (analysis/escarpment_relief_anchor.py, Copernicus GLO-90 over the southern African Great Escarpment). They are applied to Vesper heights that already carry Orogen's 1/g relief scaling, and the thresholds themselves are NOT scaled. So a higher-gravity planet, having less relief for the same tectonics, hosts fewer scarps. That is the behaviour the numerator fix (lith-25) deliberately introduced when it converted the rise through scaledHeightKm.

The competing argument, not adopted because this project holds no source for it: the relief a sub-grid cliff NEEDS is itself gravity-dependent, since a strength-limited cliff height goes as strength/(rho g), which is the same 1/g Orogen applies to relief. If that is right the two scalings cancel and the gate is gravity-invariant in model units, and the thresholds should be multiplied by reliefScale where they are used. analysis/escarpment_relief_anchor.json reports what the pair would be under that reading (vesper_reference_only), so adopting it is a one-line change and a re-run, not a new measurement.

What would settle it: a sourced relation for the maximum maintainable height of a rock slope in terms of gravity and rock strength, applied to the cover/basement contrast this gate is about. Culmann-type slope stability is the obvious family. Until then the module carries the unscaled form and says so.
close_reason: Adopted: the thresholds carry reliefScale. Sourced on Schmidt and Montgomery (1995) as quoted at Montgomery (2001) eq. 7, Hc = 4C sin(theta) cos(phi) / [rho g (1 - cos(theta - phi))], argued there to a limit on topographic development, which is the landscape-scale form this term needs. Same power of gravity as the sigma/(rho g) ceiling planet-params.js already applies to the numerator, so the two cancel and only the Earth strength ratio survives, which an Earth-measured pair already carries. SCARP_MIN_RELIEF argued separately as a percentile of a relief distribution Orogen multiplies by reliefScale. Commit e878145d; test 'the relief gate is gravity-invariant' fails on the reverted code at max score difference 0.246.

title: Decide whether the acclimated respiration path runs, given it has no respcoeff/cton compensation
description:
pcar-11 settled the memory: biosphere/config/respiration_acclimation.yaml declares acclim_resp_tau bracketed 7 to 30 absolute days with BOTH ends now sourced -- the fast end Gifford (2003), the slow end Table S1 of the Thum et al. (2019) QUINCY supplement, which gives the acclimation of the temperature response of maintenance respiration that memory length for its Eq. S23, the relation respiration_acclimated() implements. The one-factor sensitivity over the bracket is registered in that file and executed by biosphere/scripts/acclimation_gate.py on every invocation.

So the memory length is no longer what blocks the option. What blocks it is the compensation asymmetry: the standard path divides respcoeff by the tissue C:N windows, leaving sapwood and fine-root maintenance respiration invariant under world-xms4's window rescaling, while the acclimated path has no such compensation and would move maintenance respiration by up to the full rescaling factor. biosphere/scripts/run_lpj_guess.py therefore keeps acclimated_respiration 0, which is also what the CNP fork's own global_p.ins selects.

Do: decide whether the acclimated path runs. If it does, set memory.run_value_days in the declaration to the arm the run sits on -- the QUINCY end is the sourced value for this exact formulation -- write the matching acclim_resp_tau into the instruction file, and say what happens to maintenance respiration under the window rescaling with no compensation in the path. acclimation_gate.py --strict refuses an acclimated path with no declared memory length, and its declaration check refuses a run instruction whose tau the declaration does not carry.
notes:
2026-08-25, branch fanout-W6, commit 76e1e6df. FIXED. THE DECISION: the acclimated respiration path DOES NOT RUN, and it is now declared rather than inherited.

WHERE THE DECISION LIVES. biosphere/config/respiration_acclimation.yaml gains a "path" block: runs false, a reason, and a reopens_on. acclimation_gate.py holds run_lpj_guess.py's acclimated_respiration to path.runs, so flipping the switch without moving the decision is a gate failure, as is a path block with no argument or with nothing that would change it. Two new fixtures cover those; 18 of 18 pass and the gate exits 0.

WHAT DECIDES IT, and it is not the memory length. respiration_acclimated() (canexch.cpp:2887) takes no respcoeff argument at all. It substitutes Sprugel et al. (1996)'s two fixed reference rates, 0.25 for wood and 1.0 for fine roots, for a coefficient that Pft::init_cton_limits (guess.h:2572-2578) has already normalised by the tissue C:N windows. Three things move together when the switch is thrown and only one of them is acclimation:

LEVEL. Arithmetic on the vendored Earth plant parameters -- respcoeff 1.0, cton_root 29, cton_sap 330, frac_mintomax 2.78, frac_maxtomin 0.9, and cton_leaf_min from Pft::init_cton_min's leaf-longevity regressions -- gives a normalised respcoeff of 0.63 to 1.72 across leaf longevities of 6 to 60 months. The acclimated wood coefficient is 0.17 to 0.30 and the fine-root one 0.69 to 1.21 over growth temperatures of 0 to 30 C. So the switch moves sapwood maintenance respiration DOWN by a factor of 2 to 10 and fine-root maintenance respiration by up to about 2 in either direction, before any acclimation dynamics run. Earth parameter values, not Vesper's; the structure and the order of the change are what carry across.

WHAT IT DEPENDS ON. The normalised coefficient carries each simulated plant type's LEAF LONGEVITY, through cton_leaf_min, and carries no temperature. The acclimated one carries GROWTH TEMPERATURE and no leaf longevity, and is the same two numbers for every plant type in the model. They are not two calibrations of one coefficient.

INVARIANCE. The normalisation is what makes sapwood and fine-root maintenance respiration invariant under a tissue C:N window rescaling, which is why world-xms4's factor of 1.7905 left respiration() alone. The acclimated path scales as 1/cton_sap and 1/cton_root, so the same rescaling would move maintenance respiration by up to that factor with nothing sourcing the move.

NOT A PHYSICS-IS-A-KNOB REFUSAL. Acclimation of respiration to a growth temperature is real and is not what is refused. What is refused is a switch that carries two unsourced changes with it and makes them inseparable from the one that is sourced, so no result on that path could be attributed to acclimation. The vendored fork's own global_p.ins selects 0 for the same switch.

WHAT REOPENS IT: an acclimated path whose basal level is reconciled with the respcoeff normalisation, so the two paths differ in the acclimation term and in nothing else. That is a change to respiration_acclimated() and to Pft::init_cton_limits, not an instruction-file setting.

memory.run_value_days KEEPS ITS undeclared SENTINEL, and the declaration now says that under path.runs false the sentinel is the SETTLED value and not a pending one: nothing is on either arm, and the gate already refuses a number there while the run takes the standard path. The declaration records that the QUINCY end is the sourced value for this exact formulation if the path is ever turned on.

TWO STALE STATEMENTS CORRECTED IN PASSING. parameters.cpp's acclim_resp_tau refusal said QUINCY's memory length was "in a supplement this project does not hold"; pcar-11 fetched it, and the comment now names Table S1 and Eq. S23. The physiology audit's recommended order called the acclimated path "the configured" one, which it is not.

WORLD-VNBC is now reduced to its mechanism half: the decision it needed is taken, and what remains there is making build_vesper_pfts.py state the path rather than inherit it from whichever vendored instruction file it imports. The run instruction already overrides the inherited value and plib takes the later declaration, so nothing runs on the wrong path today.

EXECUTED: biosphere/scripts/acclimation_gate.py with its fixtures, scripts/smoke_test.py, and the level arithmetic above in Python. READ FROM SOURCE: everything about the model. LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree, so neither path has been run.
close_reason: Decided: the acclimated path does not run. Declared as path.runs in biosphere/config/respiration_acclimation.yaml with its argument and what would reopen it, and acclimation_gate.py holds the run instruction to it. The switch is not acclimation alone: it also moves the sapwood basal rate down by 2 to 10, swaps a leaf-longevity dependence for a growth-temperature one, and gives up invariance under the tissue C:N window rescaling. run_value_days keeps its undeclared sentinel as the settled value. Commit 76e1e6df.

title: Give LPJ-GUESS a mid-year save point so the restart round trip can name a lost quantity
description:
framework/framework.cpp serializes exactly once, at the end of simulation year state_year - 1, and a restarted run sets date.year = state_year and begins at day 0. There is no other save point and a restarted run can never reach state_year - 1 again, so LPJ-GUESS cannot express either a mid-year stop or ExoPlaSim's zero-step round trip: there is no second state file to compare the first against.

Consequence: biosphere/scripts/verify_lpj_restart_continuity.py has to compare a whole run against a split one over every simulated year from the restart point, and a lost quantity shows up as a year of divergence rather than as the one record that differs. world-8yyh was found by the zero-step form precisely because that form names the lost state directly.

Do: add a save point the caller can place on an arbitrary simulated day, and a restart that resumes on that day rather than at day 0 of state_year; then add the --round-trip mode to verify_lpj_restart_continuity.py, on the model of exoplasim/scripts/verify_restart_continuity.py.

Source: biosphere/notes/wetlands-peat-methane-audit.md finding 3, found while repairing Soil::serialize under world-c4j8.
close_reason: framework.cpp now takes a save point on any simulated day (state_day), a save point separable from the restart point (save_year/save_day), a restart that resumes on the day after the state it read, and permission to do both in one run with save_path naming where it writes. Date::set_day places the date with the flags next() would have left; VesperInput::getclimate reloads whenever the loaded year is not the wanted one, so a mid-year resume runs on interpolated forcing and the seasonal landmarks day 0 would have set. verify_lpj_restart_continuity.py gained --one-day (state files compared one simulated day either side of an arbitrary-day split, the mode that names lost state) and --round-trip (state written again with no day in between). Defaults reproduce the old single save point exactly. Compile-checked with g++ -fsyntax-only against a synthetic vesper.h; no mode has been RUN, because the model does not build until a baseline climatology generates framework/vesper.h, and each mode exits naming what is missing. Follow-ups filed: the untagged archive format cannot name the member behind a byte offset, and only the vesper input module is day-addressable.

title: Run the groundwater access reduction on the first accepted water table
description:
hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater_access.py exists and passes its own six invariants on synthetic input, but it has never been run on real data: water_table.nc does not exist for this build and baseline_climatology is null, so the groundwater step it reduces has not been run. PLHY-5 built the producer; this runs it.

Do, once a baseline climatology and a water table exist:
  python hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater.py
  python hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater_access.py --water-table <central> --water-table <sigma -1> --water-table <sigma +1>

Then report, from the artifact rather than from expectation: the land share with a water table inside the vendored LPJ-GUESS soil column at 1.5 m, how much of it disappears at the -1 sigma permeability arm, and how much of the accessible area sits in cells where sink_fraction says the evapotranspiration sink rather than the flow solve set the depth. The last of those decides how much of the access is a recharge map in a water table's units, which hydrography/README.md says every depth consumer has to ask.

No consumer may treat the access area as skill until that is answered: the depth field's skill is regime-dependent and the area inherits it.

title: Regenerate the staged roughness fields: the surface term is now reduced in ce
description:
exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_roughness.py now reduces the surface roughness term in the exchange coefficient rather than in the length, and writes the length that reproduces the cell's area mean of ce. SPAT-7, notes/audits/nonlinear-spatial-reductions.md section 3.

Every staged exoplasim/inputs/*/orogen_*_surf_0173.sra predates that and is therefore WORTHLESS rather than stale, under CLAUDE.md rule 7. Nothing was regenerated in the SPAT-7 batch, deliberately: the batch was told not to write staged artifacts.

The anchored land mean is preserved by construction, so the change is in the distribution. At T21 the roughest land cell falls from 7.572 to 7.526 m and the smoothest from 0.003781 to 0.003772 m; the cells that move most are the closed-basin floors, where averaging the lengths had put a canopy minority in charge of a playa cell's exchange coefficient and overstated its evaporation by up to a third.

Do: rebuild 0173 at the configured rung, and at any other rung that carries one, and note that the roughness report now carries a surface_aggregation block naming the operator and the reference-height bracket.
close_reason: The builder already reduced the surface term in ce; what was wrong was that it did so with three inline bincounts while claiming lib/gridding.py owned the operator. Now routed through gridding.cell_expectation, the NONLINEAR operator, which takes the law as a callable. Behaviour preserved exactly at T21: land mean 2.0000 m, max 7.526 m, min 0.00377 m, coefficient 0.00406. The report's surface_aggregation block names the operator, the law and the population, and carries the Jensen gap in ce (land-area-weighted -1.18 per cent, worst cell -45.8 per cent at T21) and the transfer ledger. NOT regenerated: every staged exoplasim/inputs/* was deleted before this batch, so there is no worthless 0173 left to rebuild and the regeneration happens when the pipeline runs.

title: The subgrid-elevation saturation deficit crosses its bar inside its bracket
description:
build_boundary_conditions.py averages elevation over a cell's land and hands the model one height. Temperature is linear in height through a lapse rate, so that reduction is EXACT for temperature. Saturation vapour pressure is exponential in temperature, so the cell's own spread of heights raises the mean saturation deficit above the one computed at the mean height, and evaporation consumes that.

Measured on precarve-craton-10m at every ladder rung, notes/audits/nonlinear-spatial-reductions.md section 2, bracketed over the lapse rate (4.0 to 9.8 K per km) and the reference air temperature (the liquid-water span) because neither is known before a climatology exists. The land-mean relative gap in e_sat runs 0.35 to 7.7 percent against a declared 1 percent bar, and the bar is crossed on 11 to 56 percent of land area depending on the corner. The 95th-percentile cell reaches 26 percent at the wet corner.

So this one CROSSES ITS BAR INSIDE ITS BRACKET and is not resolved. At the dry-adiabatic, cold corner it is material at every rung; at the moist, warm corner it is below the bar from T85 up.

Do: re-run analysis/spatial_reduction_gap.py's saturation arm against the first accepted baseline climatology, with the lapse rate and reference temperature taken from it rather than swept. If it stays above the bar, the correction is a sub-grid orographic term in the surface evaporation and belongs to SPAT-5's partial-surface decision, not to a finer grid: refinement moves it by less than the bracket does.
close_reason: Arm corrected and the criterion fixed in advance. Two defects repaired before re-measuring, both committed first: the lapse bracket's ceiling was Earth's g/cp where lib/lapse.py already treats this planet's dry adiabat (12.75 K/km) as the ceiling a measured rate must fall below, and the arm evaluated an idealised Clausius-Clapeyron where the model evaluates plasimmod.f90's Magnus-Teten with a phase switch at tmelt. The 1% bar was NOT moved: there is nothing sourced to move it to. The corrected bracket is 0.32% to 12.0% and still crosses, so the arm returns NO VERDICT -- but the undecidedness is now known to sit entirely on the lapse-rate axis, and the arm reports the critical lapse rate per rung (3.95 to 7.07 K/km) so a climatology settles it with one comparison. That comparison is world-bjpg.

title: subgrid_slope carries the mesh's length, not the terrain's gradient
description:
pedology/scripts/build_soil.py:subgrid_slope divides the within-cell elevation spread by the MESH spacing and hands the result to the catena term as a gradient. The spread is a legitimate cell statistic; the divisor is a length that belongs to the mesh, so the statistic carries the mesh's resolution into a quantity the pedogenesis model reads as terrain.

Measured on the same T42 cells on this project's two builds of the same planet at the same seed, notes/audits/nonlinear-spatial-reductions.md section 6: the elevation spread the statistic is built from moves 1.6 percent, which is the terrain converging. The inferred gradient DOUBLES, 1.968, because the divisor halved. This is the same shape as the compound topographic index's shift of about ln 2 between the same two builds: a statistic that carries a length transports as a rank and not as an absolute value.

The consequence for the catena divisor is 1.8 percent of regolith depth at these gradients, so this is not urgent on its own. It matters for what it means: anything keyed on the absolute value of that gradient, a threshold above all, inherits the mesh rather than the world.

Do: either state in build_soil.py that the quantity is a rank-transporting statistic and refuse any absolute threshold on it, as hydrography/config/topographic_index.yaml does for the index, or normalise it against a declared reference spacing so the number is comparable between builds. Deleting it is also an answer: ask what breaks if the catena term takes the elevation spread directly.
close_reason: Mechanism measured, not assumed: the residual after the mesh-spacing ratio is 1.000 at every land quantile p50-p99, so the shift is an explicit length in the definition (the CTI mechanism), not a ball-population bias and not the self-affine scale dependence the one-edge scarp gradient has. Repaired by declaring the run: catena.gradient_baseline_km = 30 km in pedology/config/pedogenesis.yaml, above Orogen's ~20 km terrain-information floor and the same baseline the scarp relief term uses. Over it the two builds agree to 1.069x against the 1.15x bar. slope_transport is unchanged because it is declared against real hillslope gradients. Regolith depth at the land mean rises 11.8%; the staged soil map is worthless rather than stale. Evidence: analysis/subgrid_slope_support.py and .json, notes/audits/nonlinear-spatial-reductions.md section 6. Commit 3b328c86.

title: Anchor the scarp relief thresholds against a measured escarpment, then adopt the 30 km form
description:
computeScarpPotential's relief term is measured over ONE mesh edge, and an absolute smoothstep on it does not transport between region counts. notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md measures the whole of it on both builds.

WHAT IS ALREADY FIXED (lith-25): the numerator now converts through scaledHeightKm so the ratio is a real rise over a run and carries the 1/g relief scaling, and the neighbour filter uses the same surface_class land test as the cell itself instead of an elevation-sign test that discarded 5 to 9 per cent of land on dry closed-basin floors.

WHAT IS LEFT is one atomic change that cannot be split: swap the relief estimator for the form that transports, and restate the two thresholds at the same time.

THE FORM IS MEASURED AND CHOSEN. Relief below the MEAN land elevation within a fixed 30 km neighbourhood, over 30 km, holds to within 1.15x between the 2.5M and 10M builds at every quantile where it is defined (0.909, 0.932, 1.046, 1.134 at p75 to p99), against 1.41 to 1.70 for the present one-edge form. A minimum-over-the-ball form was tested and rejected: a minimum is an extreme-value statistic biased by how many cells the ball holds.

WHY IT IS BLOCKED ON AN EXTERNAL NUMBER. The 30 km form's distribution is an order of magnitude below the one-edge form's, so SCARP_MIN_GRADIENT 0.002 and SCARP_FULL_GRADIENT 0.010 cannot be carried across. Choosing replacements by matching the areal extent the present gate produces would be calibrating against the defect this row exists to remove, and CLAUDE.md fixes thresholds before results are seen.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: relief over 30 km at the foot of a Great Escarpment-type plateau margin, from a real DEM. Two values are wanted, matching the smoothstep's own stated meanings -- below the first there is no relief to hang a cliff on, at and above the second relief is not the limiting factor. Candidates: the southern African Great Escarpment, the Western Ghats, the Serra do Mar. notes/dem-substitution.md already surveys DEM routes into this project.

CONSEQUENCE OF THE CHANGE: scarp_potential in every export becomes worthless rather than stale. Its only consumer is analysis/orogen_resolution_controls.py, which reads it to measure resolution dependence.
close_reason:
Done as one atomic change: estimator and both thresholds moved together.

ANCHOR (the external number the row was blocked on): Copernicus DEM GLO-90 over the southern African Great Escarpment, block-averaged to both mesh spacings and put through the same estimator. analysis/escarpment_relief_anchor.py, with domains and rule fixed before the run. SCARP_MIN_RELIEF 0.00036 and SCARP_FULL_RELIEF 0.0075, each bracketed 1.13x by the two supports: 32 m and 683 m of regional prominence over 91 km.

ESTIMATOR IS NOT THE ONE THIS ROW NAMED. analysis/scarp_relief_transport.py reproduces the published one-edge shift to 1 per cent (harness validated) and then finds the 30 km mean form missing the 1.15x bar at 1.277x at p95 and 1.344x at p99. A control build at 2,600,001 regions puts the realisation noise floor at 1.03-1.05x, so the misses are terrain: the 15-30 km band is where a finer mesh still finds relief above Orogen's ~20 km information floor. Of the candidate set declared before the run, only a 15 km mean above a 90 km mean clears the bar (0.933, 0.973, 1.051, 1.134). The 0.909-1.134 row does not reproduce and is replaced in notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md.

Sign corrected too: relief is a RISE above the neighbourhood mean, which is what the measure's one-sidedness requires.

Both balls walk the land subgraph from surface_class (rule 1). Two falsifiable tests added; both fail on an injected sign defect. Generated end to end at 2.6M regions: 11.07 per cent of land non-zero, 1.33 per cent above 0.25.

scarp_potential in every export is worthless rather than stale. Open follow-up: world-jh0u on whether the thresholds should carry the 1/g relief scaling. Commits 7ad78cc6, 786d0569.

title: The nitrification dry limb's constants are unsourced: base 3 and rate 5 have no source
description:
vendor/lpj-guess/modules/ntransform.cpp nitrification: nit_act is min(1.0, exp(5*log(3)*(wfps - 0.6))), a fall by a factor of 3 for every 0.2 WFPS below the optimum. World-nga9 settled that this limb should EXIST -- Greaves and Carter (1920) table 5 has 20 of 22 soils rising to an optimum at 50 or 60 per cent of water-holding capacity, and nothing else in the operator limits nitrification as the soil dries, substrate_partition's aerobic share GROWING as it does. It did not settle the constants and no source states them.

Against Greaves and Carter's 22-soil mean, normalised to the 60 per cent treatment (10.9, 16.9, 30.6, 61.9, 86.0, 100.0 at 10 to 60 per cent WHC), the limb runs at 0.54 to 0.67 of the measurement over 0.1 to 0.5 WFPS -- low by about a third. Against the scatter of the same table, each soil normalised to its own maximum, it is inside the measured range at every one of those points, but that range is 0.00 to 1.00 at 10 per cent WHC and 0.17 to 1.00 at 40. The bracket is too wide to refuse or confirm any monotone limb, so it is not an instrument for this.

Also unrecoverable from that paper: the per cent WHC to WFPS conversion. Greaves and Carter report no bulk density or porosity for any of the 22 soils, and Linn and Doran (1984) performed no conversion at all -- comparison of their fig. 1 with Greaves and Carter fig. 2 shows per cent WHC read straight onto a per cent WFPS axis. So the limb's placement on the WFPS axis rests on an identity relabelling.

Do: find a source that states a dry-end moisture response on nitrifier activity on a stated axis, or declare the constants a Vesper choice with their bracket. Do NOT fit a curve to Greaves and Carter table 5. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md, the nitrification water response section.
close_reason:
A source exists and it is Stark and Firestone (1995), now fetched, read and registered: references/stark1995-mechanisms-for-soil-moisture-effects-on-nitrifying-bacteria.pdf. It measures nitrification against soil WATER POTENTIAL in a silt loam, in two treatments that separate the two mechanisms -- shaken slurries with NH4 in excess, so only cell dehydration acts, fitting k = 15.4*exp(0.58*psi) with r2 0.958, and moist soil, where substrate diffusion acts too.

The axis problem that defeated Greaves and Carter does not arise, because this model already carries a potential axis and nothing has to be relabelled. SoilInput::get_mineral builds wilting point and field capacity by inverting Cosby (1984) eqn 1 at heads of 10^4.2 and 10^2.0 cm, which are -1.554 and -0.0098 MPa, and Soil::wfps is (wcont*gawc + gwp)/gwsats, which is Theta/Theta_s exactly. So Cosby eqn 1 makes potential a power law in water-filled pore space, per gridcell, out of the sand and clay the model already reads.

Placed there and anchored where they anchor, at -0.1 MPa: their moist soil falls to 0.510 at -0.5 MPa and 0.333 at this model's wilting point; the limb gives a median 0.526 (IQR 0.519-0.619) and 0.364 (IQR 0.356-0.424) over the current soil map's 4105 gridcells. The bracket is 0.333 to 0.430, the two treatments, and the limb is inside it near the moist-soil end, which is the end it should be at: the operator has no other term for substrate diffusion and substrate_partition's aerobic share GROWS as the soil dries.

ALSO SETTLED, and it narrows the question permanently: base 3 and rate 5 are ONE number. The limb is exp(5*log(3)*(w-0.6)), a slope of 5.493 per unit WFPS written as two factors, so any pair with the same product is the same limb and no measurement can separate them. There is no second source to look for.

VERDICT: the constants stay UNSOURCED and --strict still refuses on function:nitrification_activity. One silt loam can refuse a slope and cannot state one, its -2.7 MPa point is drier than the model's wilting point and so outside the reachable window, and the measurement is a 24 h laboratory incubation. What the slope PRODUCES is now a separate entry, form:nitrification_activity_dry_limb, compared as derived against that bracket, verdict agrees. Nothing was fitted: no curve to Greaves and Carter's 1920 table, and no slope to one silt loam.

Found while doing it and filed separately: get_mineral inverts Cosby's heads as if gravity were Earth's, world-slpa. It moves both sides of this comparison together, so it does not invalidate it, but it is what the comparison rests on.

title: Make both consumers read the land column property contract and delete their own pedotransfer
description: LSHY-1 built pedology/config/land_column_properties.yaml and measured what the duplicate derivations currently produce, which was explicitly the step BEFORE removal. On the 4105-cell soil map pedology's awc has a median of 84.6 mm against LPJ-GUESS's Cosby derivation at 145.3 mm, a median ratio of 1.61 with a 10th-90th range of 0.90 to 2.55, and a median absolute difference of 48.6 mm; they correlate at 0.793 because both start from related texture and depth and they are not the same capacity. Removing either path changes every downstream result, so it needs permission and a declared attribution. Do: have build_surface_soil_water.py and the LPJ input path both read the contract rather than deriving, delete soilinput.cpp's get_mineral pedotransfer and vesperinput.cpp's regolith rescaling in favour of contract-supplied per-layer states, and report the change in land runoff ratio and E/R against a paired baseline. Blocked on: which derivation the contract's central case should reproduce, which is a decision about the world and not about the code. Evidence: pedology/notes/land-column-property-contract.md, pedology/analysis/land_column_properties_report.json
notes:
2026-08-25, batch BD. NOT DONE, and it is blocked on one question that only the user can answer. Everything that can be settled without it is settled and committed (63d9d635).

THE NUMBERS IN THE DESCRIPTION ARE FROM THE SUPERSEDED BUILD. 4105 cells, 84.6 against 145.3 mm, ratio 1.61, gap 48.6 mm is pedology/data/precarve-craton/soilmap.txt. The configured build is precarve-craton-10m and its T21 soil map has 1019 cells: pedology 112.8 mm median against LPJ-GUESS 188.4, ratio 1.585 median with 0.81 to 2.40 p10-p90, median absolute difference 54.7 mm, Pearson 0.797. The report on disk has always been the second set.

WHAT THE COST IS, now in the report as unification_cost and printed by the script. Three candidates, and they are NOT symmetric.
  closure at Cosby's own suction: ExoPlaSim dwmax 112.8 -> 188.4 mm median, x1.585 (0.81 to 2.40); LPJ-GUESS unchanged.
  closure at Vesper's suction, which is this contract read literally: dwmax 112.8 -> 175.2 mm, x1.471 (0.75 to 2.22); LPJ-GUESS 188.4 -> 175.2 mm, x0.928 (0.924 to 0.932). The only candidate that moves both consumers.
  pedology's endmember mixture: dwmax unchanged; LPJ-GUESS 188.4 -> 112.8 mm, x0.631 (0.417 to 1.232).

THE QUESTION IS NARROWER THAN THE DESCRIPTION SAYS. The contract already NAMES its retention closure (Clapp-Hornberger on Cosby Table 4) and already declares field capacity as a drainage equilibrium at rho_w*g*L. Read literally that determines the states from texture, and the second candidate is what the contract says. Pedology's endmember mixture is not a retention curve at all: no saturation, no air entry, no exponent. Adopting it is a change to the DECLARATION, and saturation and matric potential would then have to come from somewhere else. So the question is: does the contract keep the closure it declares, or does the world's soil description stop being a retention curve?

THE ALLOPHANE TERM IS NOT THE DISAGREEMENT, which the contract's materials block reads as though it is. It is zero on 586 of 1019 cells, a median of 0 mm and a p90 of 7.7 mm, against a median absolute gap of 54.7 mm. What separates the two derivations is that the declared endmember capacities and the Cosby inversion are different numbers for the same texture.

WHAT CANNOT BE PRODUCED ON THIS BUILD. The change in land runoff ratio and in E/R needs a paired baseline; probe_runoff_response.py needs a climatology to back-solve potential evaporation from and config declares baseline_climatology null. So the capacity change is costed and its climate consequence is not available at all until a commissioning produces a climatology.

NOTHING ON THE LPJ-GUESS SIDE IS EXECUTION-VERIFIED. It does not build on this tree until a baseline climatology exists, so every LPJ number here is a transcription of the vendored source evaluated offline.

THE LPJ-SIDE CHANGE, SPECIFIED RATHER THAN MADE (four sibling batches are in vendor/lpj-guess). modules/soilinput.cpp SoilInput::get_mineral lines 360-400 is the Cosby inversion: b, logPsi_s, Theta_s, and the two clamped heads. modules/vesperinput.cpp apply_regolith_scaling is the per-layer share-above-contact plus bedrock-fraction rescaling. Under any candidate both would be replaced by a read of contract-supplied per-layer states, and get_soil's fifteen assignments (gawc, gwp, gwsats, awc, wp, wsats, wtot, perc_base, thermdiff_*) are the surface the replacement has to fill. perc_base is the one that cannot come from the contract: flow.saturated_conductivity is undeclared and LPJ's perc_base = 5.87 - 0.29*b is a dimensionless drainage exponent, not a conductivity.

THE EXOPLASIM SIDE IS BUILDABLE AND WAS NOT BUILT, deliberately: exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_soil_water.py reads pedology's awc column and converts mm to m, so it is a pass-through and not a third derivation. Nothing changes there until the contract EMITS a per-cell capacity, which it does not today -- land_column_properties.py compares and does not write a field. Emitting one is the first code step after the decision.

WORLD-NGA10 IS CLOSED AND ITS CLAMP IS IN THE CODE. The contract's transcription and its report both still said get_mineral clamps nothing; both are fixed. No current value moved -- no cell of this map is inside the region.
close_reason: FIXED. Adopted closure_at_vesper_suction: the contract read literally, Clapp-Hornberger on Cosby Table 4 evaluated at the suction the contract's own potential convention declares, rho_w*g*L at this planet's gravity read from config/planet.yaml. WORLD-SLPA is subsumed. THE ONE DERIVATION is pedology/scripts/land_column_properties.py, which computes the states in PASCALS -- each Earth-recorded head becomes a pressure once at Earth gravity, and this world's g enters at the single place a drainage equilibrium is defined -- and emits them per cell to pedology/data/<build>/land_column_states_<res>.txt: b, theta_s, theta_fc, theta_wp, awc_mm and one weathered-bedrock usable share per physical layer. CONSUMERS READ. exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_soil_water.py takes awc_mm and converts mm to m; it was always a pass-through and what changed is which capacity the world has. biosphere/scripts/build_lpj_driver.py writes the states and shares per cell as driver format V7, replacing regolith depth and bedrock fraction. DELETED. soilinput.cpp SoilInput::get_mineral's Cosby inversion -- b, logPsi_s, Theta_s, the two clamped heads, the two inverted contents -- replaced by a read of the new public SoilInput::ContractStates, with fail() by name when a driver has not set them. vesperinput.cpp apply_regolith_depth becomes apply_column_geometry, which multiplies by the shares the driver carries and derives nothing; the weathered-bedrock rule was implemented there AND transcribed in the contract script, and now exists once. PERC_BASE IS NOT A BLOCKER. title: Emit the wetland, peat and methane diagnostics the acceptance contract retains
description:
biosphere/config/wetlands.yaml acceptance.retained_outputs names fifteen tables an accepted run has to retain together, and none of them exists in the vendored fork. biosphere/scripts/wetland_gate.py --check-run already rejects a run directory that is missing any of them, so this row is the model-side half of WET-11.

What has to be emitted: the aggregated and the native-mesh surface fractions per wetness class, kept separate rather than one aggregate; the daily-to-monthly water table; the routed and groundwater exchange; the peat C-N-P stocks with the depth bracket; production, oxidation, diffusion, plant transport and ebullition as SEPARATE monthly fluxes rather than a net emission; the dry-soil sink; the aquatic sources; and the water, C-N-P and atmospheric methane residuals.

The separation is the point. WETCHIMP and the LPJ-GUESS MCMC calibration both show a plausible total arising from compensating extent, production, oxidation and transport errors, so a net emission table cannot be accepted however well it agrees. The fork currently writes wetland_water_added.out and nothing else on this path.

The gate also refuses a residual above acceptance.residual_tolerance, fixed at 1e-6 relative before any run exists, and refuses a run whose manifest names an arm the declaration did not register.

Source: biosphere/notes/wetlands-peat-methane-audit.md finding 11, biosphere/notes/wetland-activation-contract.md section 6. Split out of WET-11 because the contract, the retention list, the pre-registered arms and the rejecting check landed 2026-08-24 while the batch that wrote them was barred from vendor/lpj-guess.
notes:
PARTIAL, commit b5347bbb. The premise 'none of them exists in the vendored fork' was wrong for four: mwtp.out is patch.soil.mwtp; mch4_diffusion.out, mch4_plant.out and mch4_ebullition.out are Fluxes::CH4C_DIFF, CH4C_PLAN and CH4C_EBUL, and the .ins files already named those exact filenames. What was broken is that their table PARAMETERS were file_mch4diff/file_mch4plan/file_mch4ebull while run_lpj_guess.py derives the parameter name from the filename stem, so an activated run would have written an instruction file plib rejects. Renamed in commonoutput and every .ins. The fork also writes wetland_water_added.out, which world-c4j8 removed: the created-water diagnostic can carry nothing but zero once the infiltration path is bounded.

The other eleven wait on a MODEL, not on an output routine, and biosphere/notes/wetland-activation-contract.md section 6 records which one each waits on:
- mch4_production.out, mch4_oxidation.out: WET-6. Soil::CH4_prod and Soil::CH4_oxid are computed per layer in the detailed peat path and accumulated nowhere, but the SIMPLIFIED inundated path has no production or oxidation term at all -- its CH4:CO2 constant is an emission factor with oxidation folded in. A table emitted now carries a real number over one path and a zero beside a non-zero emission over the other, which is world-qzra's defect with a wrong number instead of an absent one.
- mch4_drysoil_uptake.out, mch4_aquatic.out: WET-8. Neither process exists in the module.
- mwetland_exchange.out: PLHY-4, the same absence hydrology.water_ledger refuses on.
- awetland_area.out, awetland_area_native.out: WET-2 and WORLD-D9U4. No mutually exclusive wetness classification, and no declared support for a saturated fraction.
- apeat_stock.out: WET-4, which owns the depth bracket a stock is reported against.
- aresidual_water.out, aresidual_cnp.out, aresidual_ch4.out: the ledgers themselves. A residual computed over a graph with undeclared terms is not a residual.
STILL PARTIAL after commit 9d466b8a, and the eleven remain owned elsewhere. What
that commit adds is the refusal, because the absence was worse than absent: run_lpj_guess.py
derives one instruction row per retained filename stem, so an activated run would have written
file_mch4_production and ten siblings that modules/commonoutput.cpp never declares, and plib
would have aborted the run while parsing, naming one unknown parameter and nothing about why.
acceptance.retained_output_status now records per table whether the fork can emit it and which
model the rest wait on, and wetland_gate checks both halves against commonoutput.cpp -- a table
declared emitted whose parameter is absent, and one declared waiting whose parameter has arrived.
Five new fixtures, two against the live source in both directions. 22 of 22 get their verdict.

VERIFIED, not asserted: the four emitted tables' parameters are declared in commonoutput.cpp and
named in the .ins files, and the other eleven are not, which is what the two live-source fixtures
rest on. No model behaviour changed and no table was added.

title: Measure the ExoPlaSim soil-bucket zero clip, the one water crossing no component owns
description: landmod.f90 wandr adds the net water flux to dwatc and then raises the store back to zero with AMAX1(AMIN1(dwmax,dwatc),0.). Where that clip fires it creates water, while the latent heat that removed the water has already been paid to the atmosphere by fluxmod. It is bounded and may be zero: fluxmod.f90 limits evaporation to dwatc/deltsec before the tendency is applied, so the clip can only fire when a withdrawal that limiter did not see arrives in the same timestep. The candidate path is snow exhaustion, where landmod tands charges devap against dsnowz and returns the unabsorbed remainder to dwater after the snowpack clips at zero. Registered in hydrography/config/land_water_ledger.yaml as the term bucket_floor_creation, from the boundary node unowned_source, because a crossing nobody owns is what a ledger exists to make countable. Do: add a per-cell accumulator for the clipped mass and the equivalent latent heat, carry it through the restart, and report it as a land water budget residual. If it is identically zero over a full orbit, remove the term from the ledger and say so. Evidence: hydrography/notes/land-water-ledger.md
close_reason: Measured, and there is no crossing. The bucket floor in landmod's land water step is unreachable in exact arithmetic: fluxmod's humidity solve takes AMAX1 against the level humidity so the surface evaporation never adds water, the line below it caps that same withdrawal at the store divided by the timestep on every land cell whatever the snowpack holds, and every other contribution to the surface flux adds because rainmod builds the snowfall rate as a subset of the total precipitation rate. The snow-exhaustion path this issue named is the wrong suspect: the cap is unconditional, so a snowpack absorbs part of a withdrawal already limited against the soil store and leaves the store fuller than bare ground would, not emptier. Same conclusion for the layered column, where negatives originate only in the top layer and cascade downward, so a column total at or above zero leaves every layer at or above zero. What survives is the rounding of an exactly cancelling difference. land_water_ledger.py:bucket_floor_bound sweeps the chain in the model's own real kind over 27,952,428 combinations, 537,264 of them with the cap binding and 1,965,203 with the snowpack exhausted, and the worst crossing is 2.78e-17 m of water: 1.54e-2 kg on the largest T21 land cell in one timestep, and 6.38e4 kg over a whole orbit if every land cell clipped at every step, which is 1.2e-12 of the land soil water stock. Two falsification arms remove one closing property each and both produce a macroscopic crossing (85.6 mm and 5.4 mm), so the bound is a measurement and not a null result. The term is out of the ledger graph and into absences with the bound; unowned_source stays because it is the destination the boundary_receives_from_inside mutation is built on. landcolumn.f90's comments now say the floor is unreachable and why. No accumulator, no restart record and no ledger term were needed. Commit 919f02d2.

title: Declare the respiration acclimation memory and register its sensitivity before turning the acclimated path on
description:
PCAR-3 gave respiration_acclimated() the growth-temperature state it needed: Climate::tacc_air and Soil::tacc_root, exponential running means of the daily air and 25 cm soil temperature with an e-folding time of acclim_resp_tau ABSOLUTE days, seeded from the first temperature each gridcell sees and serialized. parameters.cpp refuses acclimated_respiration 1 unless acclim_resp_tau is declared, because a default there is an undeclared physiological memory.

The baseline therefore runs the standard respiration path, acclimated_respiration 0, which is what the CNP fork's own global_p.ins selects and what divides respcoeff by the tissue C:N windows, leaving sapwood and fine-root maintenance respiration invariant under the WORLD-XMS4 window rescaling. The acclimated path has no such compensation and moves maintenance respiration by up to the full rescaling factor.

acclim_resp_tau is BRACKETED 7 to 30 absolute days: the fast end is Gifford (2003), which reports respiration acclimating in as little as a week; the slow end is the month-long growth-temperature window the acclimating land-surface literature conventionally uses, and this project holds no source for it. Over one seasonal cycle of this world the bracket spans keeping 0.97 to 0.70 of the cycle's amplitude in the growth temperature and lagging it 6 to 23 days, which is a basal-rate range of 1.71 to 1.47 against 1.74 on the instantaneous temperature the routine used to run on.

Do: settle the memory length or declare which end of the bracket the run is on, register a one-factor sensitivity over it, and only then set acclimated_respiration 1 in biosphere/scripts/run_lpj_guess.py. biosphere/scripts/acclimation_gate.py --strict refuses an acclimated path with no declared tau.
close_reason: Declared in biosphere/config/respiration_acclimation.yaml with the one-factor sensitivity registered over the bracket and executed by acclimation_gate.py. Both bracket ends are now sourced: the QUINCY supplement was fetched and Table S1 gives the slow end for this exact process. acclimated_respiration stays 0; the enabling decision is world-uhfh.

title: config/pipeline.yaml checks rows are exempt from both registration checks in smoke_test
description:
smoke_test.py:check_registered_paths_exist builds its list from graph['steps'] plus graph.get('one_offs'), and check_documented_in_component does the same. Neither reads graph['checks'].

So a row under 'checks:' can name a script that does not exist, or one that is named in no component README, and both checks pass. check_registered_in_workflow does read 'checks' (line ~361), so the gap is only in the two that verify a row rather than accept one.

That is live: verify_uninitialised_reads.sh was added under 'checks' by world-rmto and is only covered because it is also named in exoplasim/README.md by hand. verify_model_compiles.py is in the same position.

Do: add graph.get('checks', []) to the entries list in check_documented_in_component and to the named list in check_registered_paths_exist. Both are one line. Not done under world-rmto because scripts/smoke_test.py was outside that batch's file ownership.
close_reason: check_registered_paths_exist and check_documented_in_component now include config/pipeline.yaml's checks rows. Proven failing: pointing the verify_uninitialised_reads row at a nonexistent path turns both red and smoke_test exits 1. All four existing checks rows were already correct.

title: The denitrification N2 share: Xu-Ri table 11 and Weier tables 4 and 5 disagree, and the operator runs at the Xu-Ri end
description: modules/ntransform.cpp denitrification now partitions the reduced NO2 flux by Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 9 eqns 5, 6 and 7 with table 11's RNODN under 0.2 per cent and RN2ODN 0.2 to 4.7 per cent mean 2 per cent, which leaves 97.8 per cent of the reduced nitrogen as N2 at 22 C and carries no dependence on water-filled pore space. Weier et al. (1993) tables 4 and 5, the paper the moisture response beside it is taken from, give N2 shares with medians 0.565, 0.744 and 0.796 at 60, 75 and 90 per cent WFPS and a union interquartile range of 0.333 to 0.938. The operator sits above all of it. Both are Earth calibrations and neither is this world's; world-nga2 replaced an unsourced three-function branch with the scheme's own equations and declared the disagreement rather than settling it. Do: decide which calibration the world's denitrification gas partition runs on, or declare the bracket as the model boundary. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md
notes:
2026-08-25, branch fanout-W6, commit cbe6dbc0. FIXED, by the second option in the Do line: the bracket is DECLARED AS THE MODEL BOUNDARY, and nothing is picked.

THE DISAGREEMENT, unchanged: Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 9 eqns 5 to 7 with table 11's RNODN under 0.2 per cent and RN2ODN mean 2 per cent leave 97.8 per cent of the reduced nitrogen as N2 at 22 C with no WFPS dependence; Weier et al. (1993) tables 4 and 5 give medians 0.565, 0.744 and 0.796 at 60, 75 and 90 per cent WFPS with a union interquartile range of 0.333 to 0.938.

WHY THE OPERATOR STAYS AT THE XU-RI END, argued rather than asserted: the partition is not separable from the sequence it divides. Table 9 eqns 1 to 4 produce the reduced NO2 flux that eqns 5, 6 and 7 split, and eqn 1's temperature response is the same f_den_T that appears inside eqns 5 and 6, so moving the N2 share to Weier would put one step of a four-step sequence on a different calibration from the three above it and from the response inside it. Weier cannot supply the rest of the step either: four soils, one temperature, acetylene block, and NO never measured, so it has no NO limb to take. The two can be compared and cannot be mixed term by term.

WHAT IS DECLARED: no N2, N2O or NO number this model reports is a prediction of this world's denitrification gas partition. It is the DyN scheme's partition, at the DyN end of a two-calibration Earth disagreement, and the reported N2O:N2 ratio in particular is a floor rather than an estimate. The cost is stated and not argued away -- 0.978 is above the whole 0.333 to 0.938 union and carries no WFPS dependence where Weier's medians rise across it.

THE DECLARATION NEEDED A KIND IT DID NOT HAVE. A calibration entry in biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml may now carry a "boundary" line: for an entry the sources CANNOT settle, as opposed to one not yet read. The "verdict" still says what the arithmetic says and this one stays "outside"; --strict stops refusing on that entry alone; and ntransform_gate.py prints every boundary under its own heading on each invocation so a boundary cannot become invisible. A "boundary" on an entry the sources do settle, or one with no owner, is a gate failure, and there is a fixture for each. The gate reports 20 of 20 fixtures passing and --strict still refuses on the seven unsourced calibration entries and five undeclared Vesper preconditions that remain.

NOT AN ERROR AND NOT A DIVERGENCE TO REVERT. world-nga2's replacement stands: it removed a hard zero N2 below 0.7 WFPS that Weier refutes directly, an N2O:NO regression attributed to a paper that never measured NO, a logistic in temperature from a single-temperature study, and a hard zero NO above the branch. No constant and no equation in the operator changed here.

EXECUTED: biosphere/scripts/ntransform_gate.py and its fixtures, and scripts/smoke_test.py. READ FROM SOURCE: everything about the operator. LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree, so no arm of this disagreement has been run.
close_reason: Declared as the model boundary rather than settled: the operator runs Xu-Ri's partition because it is not separable from the reduction sequence it divides, and the Weier bracket 0.333 to 0.938 is declared around it under a new boundary kind in biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml that --strict does not refuse on and the gate always names. Commit cbe6dbc0.

title: The nitrification water response is not in Xu-Ri table 8 and double-counts moisture
description: Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 8 eqn 1 is NO3inc = Nmax * ftemp * NH4_aerobic, with no moisture term, because the WFPS partition upstream is where the paper puts the moisture control on nitrification. modules/ntransform.cpp nitrification multiplies it by nit_act, min of a rising exponential in water content and the falling line 4 - 5w, which peaks at exactly 1.0 at a water content of 0.6 and is exactly zero at and above 0.8. So the operator stops nitrifying entirely on any gridcell wetter than 0.8 of available capacity, a hard zero the paper does not have, and it applies a moisture control that substrate_partition has already applied. Its argument is also get_soil_water_upper rather than wfps(0), so its peak moves with texture the way the partition's did before world-b2i2. Do: establish whether a later LPJ-GUESS paper added nit_act, and if not, ask whether it should exist. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md
notes:
Established: no held LPJ-GUESS paper adds nit_act. Smith et al. (2014), which documents the active C-N generation, has no moisture term on nitrification at all; its appendix C f(W), a quadratic above 60 per cent WFPS and a Gaussian below it, is the SOM decomposition scalar, a different function in a different place. Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 8 eqn 1 is Nmax*ftemp*NH4_aerobic with no moisture term, because the WFPS partition upstream is where that paper puts the moisture control.

Done: the calibration entry is narrowed to name exactly the two things that are unsettled and nothing else. The FORM, a curve that peaks at exactly 1.0 at a water content of 0.6 and is exactly zero at and above 0.8, so nitrification stops entirely on any gridcell wetter than that, applied on top of substrate_partition's control. The ARGUMENT, get_soil_water_upper, a fraction of available capacity, where every other moisture response in the operator is Soil::wfps(0), so its peak moves with texture the way the partition's did before world-b2i2. No constant was moved and no replacement curve was fitted.

Open, and the reason this issue is not closed: whether nit_act should exist is a decision, not a finding. Removing it makes nitrification exactly table 8 eqn 1 and removes a double-counted moisture control and a hard zero the paper does not have; it also removes the only dry-end limitation on nitrifier activity in the operator, since substrate_partition offers MORE aerobic nitrogen as the soil dries. Keeping it keeps an unsourced curve with unsourced constants on an argument no other response uses. Both arms are defensible and neither is settled by a source.

SOURCING ATTEMPT 2026-08-24, at the user's request: is there a paper that
supports nit_act rather than removing it?

The shape to source is a nitrification response peaking at a water content of
0.6 and reaching exactly zero at 0.8. That is the classic water-filled pore
space curve, and its origin in the soil literature is:

  Linn, D.M. and Doran, J.W. (1984), "Effect of Water-Filled Pore Space on
  Carbon Dioxide and Nitrous Oxide Production in Tilled and Nontilled Soils",
  Soil Science Society of America Journal 48(6), 1267-1272,
  DOI 10.2136/sssaj1984.03615995004800060013x

NOT HELD and NOT FETCHABLE: paperfetch identified the work and found no PDF on
any route. references/INDEX.md holds nothing by Linn, Doran, Del Grosso, or
Parton 1996, and no DAYCENT or NGAS description -- checked by name.

Why it is the right candidate and not a guess: Linn and Doran is where the
peak-near-60-per-cent-WFPS-then-decline shape enters this literature, and it is
what DAYCENT's and NGAS's nitrification moisture functions descend from. If it
supports a curve of nit_act's form, the term is sourced and stays with its
bracket; if it supports the shape but on WFPS rather than on fraction of
available capacity, then the FORM survives and the ARGUMENT is still wrong,
which is the second half this issue already names.

TWO THINGS IT WOULD NOT SETTLE EVEN IF FETCHED. It cannot license applying the
curve ON TOP OF substrate_partition's control, because that is a structural
question about this operator rather than about the curve -- Xu-Ri puts the
moisture control in the partition and has no moisture term on nitrification at
all (table 8 eqn 1). And it is Earth soil work, so it cannot settle any of the
five Vesper preconditions the gate refuses on.

So the decision this issue records is unchanged and still open. What changed is
that the alternative to removal now has a name and a DOI.
FETCHED AND READ 2026-08-24. Linn and Doran (1984) is now held at
references/linn1984-water-filled-pore-space-co2-n2o.pdf. It splits this issue
in two, and settles one half.

SETTLED, AND DONE: THE ARGUMENT. The paper's stated objective is to replace per
cent water-holding capacity with per cent water-filled pore space as the index
of soil aeration, because WHC "depends on soil type, and the methods for its
determination vary and are often poorly defined" (p.1268) -- the same objection
world-b2i2 made to get_soil_water_upper in substrate_partition, argued by the
paper the curve descends from. Fig. 1 draws relative nitrification against per
cent WFPS. get_soil_water_upper is a fraction of AVAILABLE capacity, which is a
third quantity: neither the axis the curve is drawn on nor the index its
underlying data were measured in. nitrification now reads Soil::wfps(0). No
constant moved; the peak is still 0.6 and the zero still 0.8, now in WFPS. The
calibration block carries this as form:nitrification_activity_argument, verdict
agrees, and --strict no longer refuses on it.

NOT SETTLED, AND NOW CONTRADICTED: THE SHAPE. Fig. 1 carries four traces and
only the dashed one is nitrification; the caption attributes it to Greaves and
Carter (1920) and says the data were "originally expressed as percentage
water-holding capacity", so it is a 1920 dataset replotted onto an axis it was
not measured on. The two solid traces are Linn and Doran's own O2 and CO2, which
are respiration; the dotted one is Nommik's denitrification. Their own N2O
cannot stand in: they "did not determine if N2O production resulted from
microbial nitrification ... or denitrification" (p.1271) and only assume
nitrification dominated because their soils sat below 70 per cent WFPS, so
tables 4 and 5 are NOT a nitrification measurement.

Read off fig. 1 at 400 dpi to about +/-0.03, the nitrification trace is 0.11,
0.18, 0.32, 0.62, 0.86, 1.00 at 0.10 to 0.60 WFPS and 0.61, 0.40, 0.11 at 0.65,
0.70, 0.80. nit_act gives 0.064, 0.111, 0.192, 0.333, 0.577, 1.000, 0.750,
0.500, 0.000. So the rising limb runs at 0.54 to 0.67 of the trace across the
whole dry side, and the falling limb at 1.23 to 1.25 of it just above the peak
before dropping to a hard zero at 0.80 where the trace is still near 0.11 and
where the figure has no datum beyond. The paper's own fitted functions,
WFPS/0.6 rising and 0.6/WFPS falling, are bounded by the paper to 0.30-0.70
WFPS, never reach zero, and are fitted to the respiration data (0.92 and 0.86 at
0.65 and 0.70, against the nitrification trace's 0.61 and 0.40). The 0.8 that
does appear in the paper is Nommik (1956)'s threshold above which significant
DENITRIFICATION loss occurs. So the hard zero is contradicted rather than merely
unsourced, and the entry moved from verdict unsourced to verdict outside, which
--strict still refuses on. Bracket: table 1 gives nitrification's maximum
activity as a single number, 60, over 22 soils with 0-100 tested, and states no
interval; the paper's own table 3 samples respiration at 53, 60, 64-65, so the
peak can be placed only inside about 0.53 to 0.65. No curve was fitted to the
figure, because a curve digitised off a replotted 1920 figure would be another
unsourced curve wearing a citation.

STILL OPEN, AND STILL THE USER'S DECISION: THE STACKING. The paper cannot
license it, but it argues against rather than being silent. Fig. 1 is annotated
WATER LIMITING below 60 per cent WFPS and AERATION LIMITING above it, and the
abstract names the mechanisms: "Below 60% WFP, water limits microbial activity,
but above 60%, aerobic microbial activity decreases -- apparently the result of
reduced aeration" (p.1267). Those are two different mechanisms and this operator
already carries one. substrate_partition splits every pool on WFPS and hands
nitrification only NH4_mass_d, the aerobic part, which IS aeration -- so the
falling limb applies a control the partition has already applied, and the paper
is what identifies it as the same control. The rising limb is not a double
count: water limitation on nitrifier activity is not aeration, the partition
does not represent it, and the partition cannot, because its aerobic share GROWS
as the soil dries. Below 0.6 WFPS nit_act is the only dry-end limit on
nitrification anywhere in the operator.

So the decision the user faces is now sharper than "keep or delete". The three
arms are: delete the whole term, which makes nitrification exactly table 8 eqn 1
and removes the only dry-end limit; keep only the rising limb, which is the arm
the paper's own mechanism labels support and which removes the double count and
the contradicted zero while keeping the water limitation; or keep both limbs and
refit them, which needs a source this project does not have, since Greaves and
Carter (1920) is not held and fig. 1 is a replot of it. Nothing here chooses.

NOT EXECUTION-VERIFIED. LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree: framework/vesper.h
is generated and the chain to it runs through a baseline run and a baseline
climatology that do not exist. Everything above is against the source, the
declaration and the paper.
SETTLED 2026-08-24. Greaves and Carter (1920), Soil Science 10(5) 361-387, is
now held and read: references/greaves1920-influence-of-moisture-on-bacterial-activities.pdf.
It is the primary measurement behind Linn and Doran fig. 1's nitrification
trace.

WHAT IT MEASURED, AND ON WHAT AXIS. Net nitric nitrogen accumulated over a
21-day incubation at 28-30 C of 100 gm of soil amended with 2 gm of dried
blood, on 22 Cache Valley farm soils, moisture restored every 3 days, five or
six determinations averaged per point. Not a nitrification rate, not a field
rate, and on an added substrate. The axis is per cent of each soil's
water-holding capacity, defined in its methods as the Hilgard method modified
by Briggs: soil settled by jarring into a screen-bottomed cup 5 cm x 1 cm,
wetted from below to maximum uptake, drained 30 minutes, weighed before and
after drying. So per cent WHC is a fraction of a gravimetric water content at
DRAINED SATURATION, running 31 to 78 per cent across the 22 soils (table 3),
and the paper uses "per cent of saturation" for it interchangeably.

THE CONVERSION CANNOT BE DONE FROM THIS PAPER, AND LINN AND DORAN DID NOT DO
ONE. No bulk density or porosity is reported for any of the 22 soils; table 2
is particle size, tables 8 and 9 are moisture equivalents. Comparison settles
what Linn and Doran did: their fig. 1 trace read at 0.10 to 0.80 is 0.11, 0.18,
0.32, 0.62, 0.86, 1.00, 0.40, 0.11, and Greaves and Carter's own 22-soil mean
normalised as their fig. 2 normalises it ("the quantity produced at 60 per cent
is taken as 100") is 10.9, 16.9, 30.6, 61.9, 86.0, 100.0, 39.5, 9.6 at 10 to 80
per cent WHC. Same points, same terminal point, same normalisation: per cent
WHC was read straight onto a per cent WFPS axis, by the paper whose stated
objection to WHC is that it is ill-defined.

RISING LIMB: SUPPORTED. 20 of the 22 soils form most nitrate at 50 or 60 per
cent WHC (nine at 50, eleven at 60); the paper states the optimum as "somewhere
between 50 and 60 per cent of saturation" (p.373). 19 of 22 rise without a
reversal to their own optimum; the other three dip by under 2 per cent of their
maximum on the way. The two soils that do not peak at 50 or 60 are soil 20, a
fine sand, and soil 22.

WET END: NO ZERO AT 0.8. At 80 per cent WHC the 22-soil mean is 9.6 per cent of
the optimum and no soil is at zero (per-soil normalised values run 0.024 to
0.69). Table 5 and fig. 2 both stop at 80 and carry no point beyond. The only
statements past it are prose: "very slight" at 90 per cent WHC, and "All soils
ceased to nitrify when saturated" at 100. So the primary zero is at drained
saturation, which the model's upper layer cannot reach.

THE TWO ANCHORS ARE MUTUALLY INCONSISTENT. Mainline's peak at 0.6 needs 100 per
cent WHC to map to 1.0 WFPS (the identity Linn and Doran used); its zero at 0.8
needs 100 per cent WHC to map to 0.8, which would put the optimum at 0.44-0.48.
No single linear map gives both.

DECISION: rising limb kept, falling limb removed. nit_act is now
min(1.0, act_dry). The falling limb is doubly disqualified -- a double count of
the aeration substrate_partition already applies, and a terminus the primary
measurement contradicts -- while the rising limb is water limitation, is
supported across 22 soils, and is the only dry-end limit on nitrification in
the operator, the partition's aerobic share GROWING as the soil dries.

THE COST, STATED: with the double count gone the wet-end decline is the
partition's alone and is shallower than the measurement. The partition's
aerobic share at 0.7 and 0.8 WFPS is 0.63 and 0.40 of its 0.6 WFPS value
against the measurement's 0.395 and 0.096; mainline's stacked pair gave 0.32
and exactly 0. The measurement sits between them. That magnitude belongs to the
partition's midpoint and shape, which world-nga8 owns.

DIVERGENCE DECLARED per world-i2ch: mainline's line is recorded verbatim in
ntransform.cpp beside the changed one, biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml
declares it under response_functions.nitrification_activity.divergence, and
ntransform_gate.py gained a `divergence` check that fails both if the record
goes missing and if the code goes back to running it.

RESIDUAL, now world-xmiq: the rising limb's own constants. Against the 22-soil
mean the limb runs at 0.54 to 0.67 of the measurement over 0.1 to 0.5 WFPS.
Against the per-soil scatter it is inside the range at every point, but that
range is 0.00-1.00 at 10 per cent WHC and 0.17-1.00 at 40, too wide to refuse
or confirm any monotone limb. No curve fitted here.
close_reason: Settled from the primary source. Greaves and Carter (1920) is now held and read: it supports the rising limb (20 of 22 soils peak at 50-60 per cent WHC) and refuses the falling one (9.6 per cent of the optimum at 80 per cent WHC, its only zero at saturation, and no single linear WHC-to-WFPS map giving mainline both its peak at 0.6 and its zero at 0.8). Linn and Doran attribute the decline above the optimum to aeration, which substrate_partition already applies. nit_act is now min(1.0, act_dry); mainline's line is recorded beside it and the divergence declared under world-i2ch. The rising limb's constants are still unsourced and are world-xmiq.

title: substrate_partition's midpoint and shape have no source; the bracket on the midpoint is 0.50 to 0.66 WFPS
description: The argument of substrate_partition's curve is settled: Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 7 gives DyN's aeration variable as water-filled pore space and its nitrification section as the WFPS of the top 50 cm, and the operator now reads Soil::wfps(0) (world-b2i2). The FORM is not settled. Xu-Ri gives none, pointing instead at PnET-DNDC's anaerobic balloon, so richards_curve(0.05, 0.95, 7.5, 0.5, wfps) is the port's own. The midpoint 0.5 sits at the bottom edge of the bracket the operator's own comment implies twice over: Pilegaard (2013), which it cites, puts the crossover from nitrification- to denitrification-dominated emission at 0.60 WFPS, while the comment's own words put the steepest change at 0.66. The shape parameter 7.5 has no source at all; the comment says the curve is complete by 0.75 WFPS and it reaches 0.83 there. Do: pick the midpoint from a source, or declare the form unsourced with this bracket. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md
close_reason: Declared, not fitted. substrate_partition keeps richards_curve(0.05, 0.95, 7.5, 0.5, wfps) and the refusal is narrowed into two entries because the midpoint and the shape are unsettled to different degrees: function:wet_fraction carries the midpoint 0.5 with its 0.50-0.66 bracket, the spread between Pilegaard's 0.60 crossover and the operator's own comment's 66 per cent, with the declared value at the bottom edge; form:wet_fraction_shape carries the shape parameter 7.5, which has no source and no bracket at all. Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) settles the argument and only the argument, delegating the form to PnET-DNDC's anaerobic balloon. No number was moved: a midpoint picked from a bracket neither paper states would be an invention dressed as a source.

title: nh3_max applies the pH dependence Xu-Ri table 5 eqn 6 already carries, a second time
description: Composing Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 5 eqns 2, 3 and 4 gives NH3gas = NH4 * ftemp^2 * Wcont * (1 - Wcont) * fpH with fpH = exp(2 * (pH - 10)) from eqn 6. modules/ntransform.cpp nh3_volatilization is that expression multiplied by a further nh3_max, 0.001 above pH 6 and 0.00001 at or below. Table 5 has no such factor and the paper's text says why it needs none: the NH3/NH4 ratio 'is virtually zero (about 0.001) in solutions with pH below 6, but approaches unity (about 0.90) in solutions with pH above 10', which is what fpH alone delivers, 3.4e-4 at pH 6 and 1.0 at pH 10. nh3_max therefore applies that ratio twice, and its step at pH 6 adds a factor-100 discontinuity on top of a smooth exponential. Over the pH range the soil map carries, the paper's maximum daily volatilised fraction of NH4 reaches 9.2e-2 and the operator's 9.2e-5, so NH3_SOIL is three orders of magnitude below the paper's formulation on the 96 per cent of gridcells above pH 6 and five orders below it on the rest. Do: settle whether nh3_max is a rate constant the port intends separately or a duplicate of fpH. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md
close_reason: nh3_max is removed. The operator's ammonia multiplier is now exactly Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 5 eqns 2, 3, 4 and 6, whose fpH = exp(2*(pH-10)) already carries the NH3/NH4 ratio the paper's text describes. It was a rate constant nowhere in the paper and a duplicate of fpH, plus a factor-100 step at pH 6 on a smooth exponential. Over pedology's pH range the daily coefficient of NH4_mass now reaches 9.2e-2 where it reached 9.2e-5: at pH 6.5 it is at most 2.3e-4 per day against 2.3e-7, and at pH 8.5 1.2e-2 against 1.2e-5. It remains a pool multiplier inside [0,1], and the bound is now one order of magnitude rather than four, which makes pedology's pH clip load-bearing. Calibration entry function:nh3_multiplier is now 'agrees'.

title: f_denitri_max and f_nitri_gas_max are unsourced rate ceilings read in the opposite processes to their names
description: Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 9 eqns 3 and 4 are DNmax * ftemp * S/(S + Kn) with no maximum-rate constant beside them, and table 11 lists none. The port multiplies eqn 3 by f_denitri_max 0.33 and eqn 4 by f_nitri_gas_max 0.25, ceilings on the daily denitrified fraction that neither paper states. Separately, the two gas constants are read in the opposite processes to the ones their names and global_soiln.ins's own comments give them: f_denitri_gas_max, commented 'Maximum gaseus losses in denitrification', is read in nitrification, and f_nitri_gas_max, commented for nitrification, is read in denitrification. The values differ, 0.33 and 0.25, so the crossing is not cosmetic. Do: settle whether the crossing is intended, and declare the two ceilings or remove them. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md
close_reason: Established that the USE was wrong, not the names: global_soiln.ins's comment, parameters.h's doc comment, parameters.cpp's inline comment and the declareitem help string all agree with the names f_denitri_gas_max and f_nitri_gas_max, and only the two reads in ntransform.cpp disagreed. The instruction file's values corroborate the declarations, 0.33 for both steps of the reduction sequence against 0.1 and the nitrification gas share. Four declarations against one use, so the reads moved and nothing was renamed; the NO2-to-gas ceiling is now 0.33 where it was 0.25, a factor of 1.32 on that coefficient. Both rate ceilings stay unsourced and refusing: table 9 eqns 3 and 4 carry no maximum-rate constant and table 11 lists none, and no value was invented for either.

title: The denitrification N-gas partition contradicts Weier et al. (1993), the paper it cites
description: modules/ntransform.cpp denitrification splits the reduced NO2 pool between NO, N2O and N2 with three functions, two of which cite Weier et al. (1993) and one of which cites Pilegaard (2013). Weier is now held and read, and it does not support them. (a) Below 0.7 WFPS the operator sets n2_inc to 0 and routes the whole pool to NO and N2O. Weier tables 4 and 5 report N2/N2O ratios at 60 and 75 per cent WFPS across four soils, nine C-by-N treatments and five days, with medians 1.3 and 2.9; N2 is the majority product in 61 per cent of the 60 per cent WFPS observations and 80 per cent of the 75 per cent ones. (b) f_n2o_n2_water with f_n2_n2o_temperature give an N2 share at 25 C of 0.000 below 0.70 WFPS, 0.119 at 0.70, 0.120 at 0.75 and 0.846 at 0.90, against Weier's medians of 0.565, 0.744 and 0.796 with interquartile ranges 0.333-0.778, 0.545-0.870 and 0.630-0.938. It matches only at the wet end and inverts the trend below it. (c) f_n2o_no_water, the N2O:NO ratio, is attributed to Weier, which measured N2 and N2O by acetylene block and never measured NO. (d) f_n2_n2o_temperature, a logistic with midpoint 5 C and width 10 C, is in neither paper; Weier incubated at one temperature. Its sign agrees with Xu-Ri table 9 eqns 5 and 6. Do: re-derive the partition against Weier tables 4 and 5, or declare the port's form as unsourced with the bracket already in biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md
close_reason: Re-derived, but against Xu-Ri rather than Weier, which is the third option the Do line did not list and is better than either it did. The partition is now table 9 eqns 5, 6 and 7 with table 11's RNODN (under 0.2 per cent) and RN2ODN (0.2-4.7 per cent, stated mean 2 per cent), so NO and N2O are RNODN*ftemp and RN2ODN*ftemp of the reduced NO2 and N2 is the remainder, at every water-filled pore space. That removes the branch at 0.7 WFPS, the hard zero N2 below it that Weier tables 4 and 5 refute directly, the N2O:NO regression attributed to a paper that never measured NO, the N2O:N2 curve and the logistic in temperature from a single-temperature study: four unsourced calibration entries collapse into one that agrees with its source. What it does not settle is the size of the N2 share, 0.978 at 22 C against Weier's medians 0.565, 0.744 and 0.796, union interquartile 0.333-0.938. Two Earth calibrations disagree; the operator runs at the DyN end because every other equation in it is DyN's, and form:denitrification_n2_share carries that disagreement as an 'outside' verdict owned by world-bzqj. Total denitrification does not move and all three gases leave the soil, so the partition changes what is reported and not what the simulated plants can reach. Also registered while rewriting the function: the 0.4 WFPS threshold below which the operator denitrifies nothing, which neither paper states, as world-q4qy.

title: Band-resolved downward shortwave at the surface is computed and discarded, in both sky limits
description:
radmod.f90's swr computes zfd1 and zfd2, the per-band downward flux, at every level interface and then immediately sums them into dfd, so the band split exists inside the routine and never leaves it. Codes 176 and 177 are the NET surface shortwave and longwave; the downward fluxes exist only as dfd and dftd in the level-resolved output, codes 405 and 407, and neither is band-split.

Any surface energy balance downscaled off this model needs four fields it cannot currently get: visible and near-infrared downward shortwave at the surface, in the clear-sky and the all-cloud limit. references/climber-x/src/smb/semi.f90 takes exactly those four and smb_def.f90's comments confirm the second axis is clear against cloudy, not direct beam against diffuse.

The clear-sky arm has a precedent in the tree: ndiagcf re-calls swr with the cloud fraction zeroed and stores the result in dclforc. The all-cloud arm has none -- CLIMBER-X's atmosphere computes an overcast limit alongside the clear one, and ExoPlaSim's normal call gives the cloud-weighted sky only.

Separately, SEMI's six derivatives of downward shortwave with respect to albedo and elevation are analytic derivatives of CLIMBER-X's own single-layer transmission-factor product, written out by hand around the l_dswd_dalb guard in src/atm/swr.f90. They are inseparable from that scheme. Through ExoPlaSim's multi-layer adding cascade they would have to be re-derived or taken by finite difference, on the ndiagcf pattern of extra swr calls. Decide which before porting anything that consumes them.

Do: add the four diagnostics through radmod, outmod, pyburn and the diagnostic print block, and record the derivative decision. Diagnostics only, so no restart record is involved.

Source: exoplasim/notes/semi-scoping.md section 3
notes:
CORRECTION TO THE CLOSE REASON, same day. The incident BROADBAND surface shortwave was not missing outright: outmod already accumulates aecoswd from dfd(:,NLEP) and writes it as code 615 on the ecological stream. What 185 and 186 add there is the BAND SPLIT, which has no other source, and what they add on the REGULAR stream is an incident flux where 176 carries only the net. The FRADPAR anchoring is the reader that could not be served any other way.

A THIRD IN-MODEL READER turned up while checking: simba.f90 forms its light-limited GPP as rlue * ... * dfd(jhor,NLEP), an Earth light use efficiency per joule of BROADBAND flux. Dormant at NVEG = 0 and recorded in notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md with no issue against it; now world-4a5r, which names dfdsw1 as the route that did not exist before this commit.
close_reason: Routed, not stopped, and for readers that are not SEMI. dfdsw1/dfdsw2 keep each band's surface downward flux in swr; afdsw1/afdsw2 accumulate through outmod and the restart; codes 185 and 186 are registered in pyburn as rsds1/rsds2 and in run_exoplasim's REGULAR_CODES. The two readers that exist today are both in the biosphere: FRADPAR is a SURFACE fraction anchored on a top-of-atmosphere band ratio, priced at about 10 per cent in biosphere/notes/lpj-guess-porting-audit.md, and 185+186 is the incident surface shortwave the ecological forcing contract's open insolation row wants where the driver passes net. Nothing was being wasted: zfd1 and zfd2 are transmission factors the sum needs, so there was nothing to stop computing. The clear-sky and all-cloud LIMITS, which are SEMI's four fields, are world-qk4i and now block clim-63 in this issue's place; the derivative decision is recorded there too. Commit 4e99df67.

title: Derive a two-band snow albedo on a grain-size axis for this star, from the spectra already in the tree
description:
specblock.f90 ships fsnowalb, msnowalb and csnowalb -- fine, medium and coarse granular snow reflectance over the same 965 wavelengths every other endmember uses -- and no code path selects among them. radmod.f90 integrates the iceblend family instead, whose mixture fractions combinedspec-snow_ice.ipynb solved by bisection against a broadband albedo target under a 5772 K blackbody, so the albsmin-to-albsmax ramp interpolates between two Earth-target mixtures on surface temperature and is not a grain axis.

Deliverable: weight each of the three grain-resolved spectra against this star's spectrum through analysis/ice_albedo.py's existing arithmetic, giving a two-band snow albedo on a three-point grain-radius axis, and fit the functional form used by references/climber-x/src/smb/smb_surface_par.f90's snow_albedo_dang to those points rather than importing its published coefficients.
