Why it is worth doing on its own: it supplies the half a dust darkening coefficient needs in order to mean what its source measured, which is what blocks dust-14, and it needs no fine grid, no mass balance scheme and no phys-13. The check that can fail is already established: the solar-weighted arm must reproduce the published values within the tolerance ice_albedo.py holds for the existing blends.

Source: exoplasim/notes/semi-scoping.md sections 1, 5 and 6; notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md finding 2
close_reason: Delivered. analysis/snow_albedo_grain.py weights the three grain-resolved spectra specblock.f90 compiles against this star's spectrum through lib/stellar.py and fits Dang's form to those points rather than importing his coefficients; analysis/snow_albedo_grain.json and a config/pipeline.yaml row. The result: at every grain size the same snow is roughly a tenth of an albedo darker in broadband under this star than under the Sun, one-signed and widening with grain size, and it is band 2 plus the band-1 flux share rather than anything about the material. Three checks fixed before running, all passed: reproduction of radmod's eight printed band pairs to 1.2e-4 against a 0.01 bar; three-way agreement between the Fortran, basespecs and the JHU library with the radii PARSED from the library headers; monotonicity in radius. The check the scoping note proposed -- reproduce published values within ice_albedo.py's tolerance -- does not exist as stated: that tolerance is 1e-9 and checks a re-implementation of radmod against radmod, so every blend fails it. Instead the Dang comparison is SPLIT by re-integrating each spectrum over Dang's own band edges: the published constant term does not transfer and the grain-size SLOPE does, within a few thousandths, and the slope is the half dust-14 needs. EXPLORATION, nothing in the model changed. Dang (2015) itself could not be fetched; the coefficients come from CLIMBER-X's implementation and nothing rests on the paper. notes/audits/snow-albedo-grain.md.

title: check_consistency does not ask whether any executable was built from source that has since moved
description:
rebuild_binaries.py --verify already compares every executable against the sha of the source it was built from, and builds nothing to do it. Nothing in the gate set calls it, so rule 4's failure mode -- a run picking up a stale binary that was compiled from an older tree than the tip -- is reached passively and silently. That is what let world-33ba's non-compiling tip look survivable: the binaries in plasim/run predated the defect, so a run would have integrated an executable that no longer matched the source.

world-adts settled the neighbouring question: exoplasim/scripts/verify_model_compiles.py now asks whether the SOURCE compiles, and smoke_test runs it. Whether an executable is CURRENT is the separate half and it is still unasked.

Do: decide whether scripts/check_consistency.py should run rebuild_binaries.py --verify and report a moved source as a failure rather than a warning, and if so add it. The cost is a manifest read and a sha per source, no compile and no link.
close_reason: Half the finding was stale: check_consistency did compare recorded source shas, with its own copy of the comparison, and the copy had fallen behind --verify in three ways (plasim/run only, no MATRIX-row-with-no-binary, no toolchain drift). rebuild_binaries.verify() is now the one statement of the rule and returns the four findings as data; --verify prints from it, check_consistency calls it. Absent, stale, missing and drift are each a FAILURE once anything is built; a tree with no executables is unbuilt rather than inconsistent and keeps its warning. Cost: a manifest read and a sha per source, no compile and no link. It immediately reports the standing rebuild debt -- binary_manifest.json predates the parmode removal and every published binary predates 97c05751.

title: Wire the ecological stream into run_exoplasim.py and teach pyburn its codes
description:
The ecological stream (EFOR-2) exists in the model and is off by default. Two things stand between it and a run the harness can produce.

NAMELIST. NECO and NECOSTEP are in plasim_nl and nothing in run_exoplasim.py sets them. The stream's interval is a modelling choice per run, so it belongs beside the other declared namelist keys with its value derived rather than typed: NECOSTEP left at 0 becomes mtspd, one absolute 24-hour day, which is the ecological step LPJ-GUESS integrates on.

POSTPROCESSOR. Codes 600 to 602 (interval start, end, duration) and 610 to 628 (the fields) are not in pyburn's ilibrary. run_exoplasim.register_energy_diagnostic_codes is the existing precedent for teaching it codes it does not ship, and the same reason applies: a run that completes and then dies in postprocessing naming neither the code nor the reason. EFOR-3 is expected to read the stream directly, so this is only needed if anything postprocesses it -- decide which, and say so.

Not done in the batch that added the stream because run_exoplasim.py was another batch's file.

Source: exoplasim/README.md, 'The ecological stream'.
close_reason: NECO/NECOSTEP are wired through declare_ecological_stream in run_exoplasim.py and restated per segment in continue_exoplasim.py, on the command line rather than in planet.yaml because the stream cannot change a result. NECOSTEP stays the 0 sentinel the model reads as mtspd, one absolute 24-hour day exactly, rather than a Python duplicate of rung-keyed arithmetic. A third defect was found and fixed: ecoini opens unit 143 without position='append', so both run loops now move plasim_eco aside per orbit as MOST_ECO.NNNNN, which is CLIM-12 a third time after ocean and ice. THE POSTPROCESSOR DECISION: the stream does not go through pyburn and should not. pyburn builds its time axis by counting code-139 records, which the stream deliberately does not carry, so teaching it the names would deliver an empty time axis; and postprocessing means inferring each block's interval from its file position, which is the inference the stream's explicit bounds exist to refuse. refuse_eco_codes holds that against both postprocessor code lists. Commit 3f535772.

title: Every convergence and surface-energy artifact on disk was computed with a slab heat capacity 4.75 per cent too large
description:
OCN-2's channel verification recovered the model's output interval from the sea surface temperature response and missed by 4.75 per cent, which located the cause: close_ocean_energy.py, close_state_energy.py and predict_ocean_terms.py each carried CRHOS = 1030.0 and CPS = 4180.0 as literals attributed to oceanmod.f90, and assess_convergence.py imported the pair from the second. oceanmod does not own them. icemod.f90 declares both as icemod_nl keys and passes them to oceanini, and its CPS is sea water's specific heat at S = 34.7 and its freezing point, 3990.34 J/kg/K, not fresh water's 4180 at about 25 C. All four now read lib/sea_water.py.

WHAT THAT MAKES WORTHLESS RATHER THAN STALE, per rule 7, and this issue exists to say which rather than to delete anything:

- exoplasim/analysis/convergence/*.json. SLAB_HEAT_CAPACITY sets tau_expected, which sets the fallback remaining offset, which is judged against OFFSET_TOLERANCE_K. The capacity was 4.75 per cent too large, so the expected relaxation time was too long and the remaining offset was overestimated in the direction that FAILS a run. Any verdict close to the tolerance may flip.
- exoplasim/analysis/energy/*_state_energy_*.json. The mixed-layer term of the rebuilt heat content carried the same factor, so the storage side of the closure is 4.75 per cent out on the ocean.
- exoplasim/analysis/ocean_energy/*. D4 and D6 compare the slab storage against the fluxes, so their residuals carried it directly.

The corrected figures for CLIM-16's predicted heating are already in exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md, because that section rescales exactly: the operator is linear in the capacity.

Do: re-run assess_convergence.py and close_state_energy.py on the runs whose verdicts anything still rests on, and check whether any convergence verdict changes. Do NOT purge; the artifacts are cheap to regenerate and the question is which verdicts move. Source: notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md section 11d.
notes:
Checked against the artifacts rather than the history. Evidence and full argument in notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md section 11f.

NO ARTIFACT ON DISK carried the 4.75 per cent oversized capacity.

- The five exoplasim/analysis/convergence/*.json never imported the pair. Each records relaxation_orbits_expected 9.8833 = 50*1025*3990/(1.31*182.8*86400), the uncited pair with the private 1.31 W/m2/K beside it; the copied pair gives 10.4045 and the model's own 9.9324. All five also lack slab_heat_capacity_j_m2_k, radiative_damping_w_m2_per_k and planetary_albedo_in_window, keys the import added. Their capacity is 0.49 per cent BELOW the model's, not 4.75 above.
- No convergence verdict moves. Two of five took the fitted asymptote, which does not use tau_expected. The three on the drift fallback shift 0.10645->0.10698, 0.00747->0.00751, 0.10740->0.10794 against a 0.15 tolerance: margins about 0.043 K, correction about 0.0005 K. Nor does the damping change reach them; the two nearest would need a planetary albedo above 0.44 and report about 0.25.
- The three energy artifacts did use CPS=4180, on runs the model integrated at 4180: icemod.f90 did not move CPS until 2026-08-24 and they were generated 08-19. close_ocean_energy's D4 proves it from the file, closing to 3.0e-06 and 3.9e-06 W/m2 where a 4.75 per cent mismatch would leave about 0.0475*yheat.

So the 'what this makes worthless' list is empty, and rebuilding those artifacts against today's icemod.f90 would have INTRODUCED the error. Re-running was impossible anyway: no run with a convergence or energy artifact is on disk.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, and is now fixed (commit 36e375c7): the correction left the same defect pointing backwards. close_state_energy read sea_water.constants() at module import with no run_dir, returning today's icemod.f90, and assess_convergence built SLAB_HEAT_CAPACITY from it at import. Every run here declares all four keys in its own icemod_namelist and run_ade7373b4c90's are not the compiled defaults, so a run older than a model change was closed and assessed at a capacity it never used. state_energy now calls sea_water.constants(run_dir) and threads the pair through heat_content; assess_convergence.slab_heat_capacity(run_dir) replaces the module constant. Both artifacts now record what they used. smoke_test check 'the convergence slab's sea water follows the run' catches the regression on all three assertions.
close_reason: No artifact on disk carried the oversized capacity: the convergence family used a different (0.49 per cent low) pair and no verdict moves; the energy family used CPS=4180 on runs the model itself integrated at 4180, which D4 confirms from the file. The real defect was the correction reading sea water at import, so a run older than a model change was assessed at a capacity it never used; fixed in 36e375c7 with a smoke_test check that fails on the regression. Evidence in notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md 11f.

title: verify_legendre_parity.py checks a premise the deleted paired decomposition was the only consumer of
description:
world-g5va named this and did not fix it, because the fix is a deletion and the deletion needs a decision this batch was not the place to take.

WHAT IT IS. verify_legendre_parity.py reproduces legini's recurrence in Python and checks P(-mu) = s*P(mu) and Q(-mu) = -s*Q(mu) with s = (-1)^(m+n). It is the second hand-transcription of that recurrence in the tree; world-g5va removed the first, in verify_weight_factorisation.py, by compiling legini out of legmod.f90 instead. This one is still a transcription and is still checked against nothing.

WHAT IT IS FOR, AND WHETHER THAT STILL EXISTS. The parity premise is what a mirror-pair fold rests on: compute two latitudes from one pass over the modes. exoplasim/notes/paired-latitude-decomposition.md records that the decomposition was DELETED at 2508bedb, 515 lines, because SHTns replaced legmod and cannot use a permuted layout. The three gates left pointing at that code were each given a verdict there -- one deleted, one re-scoped, one repaired -- and this one is not among them. exoplasim/notes/symmetric-transforms.md is the design that would consume the premise, and it is the design SHTns replaced.

IT ALSO HAS A KNOWN DEFECT. notes/audits/checks-that-forward-too-few-arguments.md records it printing FAIL and exiting 0, so nothing that runs it would notice.

Do: decide whether the symmetric-transform design is dead. If it is -- and paired-latitude-decomposition.md's reason says it is -- delete the script, its row in config/pipeline.yaml, its row in exoplasim/README.md, and rewrite the paragraph in exoplasim/notes/symmetric-transforms.md that cites its measurement, giving it the same kind of verdict line paired-latitude-decomposition.md gives the other three. If it is not dead, the script has to be repaired twice over: the exit code, and the transcription, which the pattern in verify_weight_factorisation.py now shows how to remove.

Not done in world-g5va because that issue's Do: was the compiled extraction for legini, and deleting a gate that config/pipeline.yaml lists is a separate unit of work with a design question in front of it.
close_reason: The symmetric-transform design is dead: 2508bedb deleted the paired decomposition and the symmetric transforms, and the parity premise is a precondition of that fold and of nothing else in the tree. Script deleted in 953b306a with its config/pipeline.yaml and exoplasim/README.md rows. Nothing invoked it, no step needed it, it was in no verify_*.sh chain and no smoke_test check, so nothing breaks. symmetric-transforms.md keeps what it measured and now carries the verdict, and paired-latitude-decomposition.md's table of gates left pointing at the deleted code goes from three rows to four. The exit-code defect the issue names was already fixed under world-60x0 and is not what settles this. Anyone needing the premise again takes it from the compiled legini the way verify_weight_factorisation.py does.

title: Add the source lints and fail-closed guards to the ocean tier that is actually adopted
description:
OCN-12's second half, split out because it inverts the dependency the first half had. The inventory had to precede adoption and is delivered as notes/audits/ocean-tier-implicit-earth.md; lints and guards can only follow a selection, because CLAUDE.md's layout section makes vendor/cgenie a CANDIDATE under OCN-3 that nothing reads and that does not build where it stands, and a lint for a configuration artifact no step produces would be built before anyone asked whether it should exist.

What the audit says the guards would have to cover, in the order of what fails most silently:

- THE TWO RADII. initialise_goldstein.F:377 rsc and gem_cmn.f90:802 const_rEarth are independent statements of the same quantity, and BIOGEM re-derives GOLDSTEIN's own scalings from the second. A check that they agree is worth more than either edit, because a port that changes one is worse than a port that changes neither.
- THE DEPTH-TO-PRESSURE CONVERSION. gem_carbchem.f90:99 divides depth by ten. It has to become a density times a gravity, and every carbonate equilibrium constant is downstream.
- THE ROTATION FAIL-OPEN. initialise_goldstein.F:380-386 reverts to Earth's Coriolis scaling when the solar and sidereal day lengths are within 0.001 of each other. A configuration guard is cheap; discovering it from a result is not.
- THE SIX STATEMENTS OF THE YEAR, one of which is a bash expression in genie-main/runmuffin.sh:229 that generates the config every standard run uses, and four of which are compile-time.
- THE MISSING SEDIMENT-TRACER GUARD IN ECOGEM. ecogem_box.f90:553-566 hard-stops without the dissolved silicon tracer and nothing checks the opal sediment tracer, so silicon uptake becomes a permanent removal with no return path. notes/audits/ecosystem-tier-ecogem-marbl.md section 13b.
- THE TWO OUT-OF-BOUNDS INDEXINGS for mismatched squota and useSiO2, and the 'Population inviable' guard at ecogem_data.f90:525 which is zero over zero for every non-silicifier and therefore has no failing state.

Blocked on OCN-3. If OCN-3 selects a different host, re-derive this list against that host rather than executing this one.
close_reason: Delivered against the ADOPTED tier, not the candidate. exoplasim/config/ocean_tier.yaml declares ExoPlaSim's slab (oceanmod, icemod, seamod) and exoplasim/scripts/ocean_tier_gate.py enforces it: six failure classes, nineteen fixtures, --strict on the unsourced Earth constants; registered in config/pipeline.yaml as a need of bootstrap_run and baseline_run. The audit's headline class was present here too and is fixed: TMELT was declared compile-time in icemod while pumamod's tmelt is a planet_nl key, so the split was reachable from configuration alone; CRHOI was declared as a parameter independently in oceanmod and icemod with both live on the same modelled ice. Both are now stated once and handed on. cicemin exposed as an icemod_nl key at its current 0.5. Findings in notes/audits/ocean-tier-implicit-earth.md section A. No number changed; behaviour identical. The cGENIE half of the original description remains blocked on OCN-3 and is re-derived, not executed, if OCN-3 ever selects that host.

title: pedology produces no mineral-reactivity proxy the mineral-aware SOM and P-sorption arm needs
description: biosphere/config/mineral_reactivity.yaml declares a mineral-aware arm for soil organic matter protection and phosphorus sorption and refuses it, because all four proxies it needs carry the undeclared sentinel and nothing in this pipeline produces them: Fe-Al oxide content (kg/kg of fine earth), an allophane concentration (kg/kg), aggregate capacity, and polyvalent cation saturation (cmol(+)/kg). pedology/scripts/build_soil.py derives lithology fractions, a weathering intensity, texture, pH, bulk density, regolith depth and an andic AREAL fraction, and none of those is any of the four. The near miss is andisol_properties andic, the fraction of a gridcell whose volcanic glass weathered to allophane; converting an areal fraction to a concentration in the fine earth needs something this project does not have. Do: decide for each of the four whether pedology can derive it from what the Orogen export and the climatology already carry, and if it can, emit it as a named soil map column with its unit; if it cannot, that is a declared absence and the mineral-aware arm stays refused. Cotrufo et al. (2013) and Lehmann and Kleber (2015) are read and neither supplies a parameterised transfer function, so this is state work and not a coefficient swap. Evidence: biosphere/notes/mineral-reactivity-contract.md
close_reason: Verdict recorded in pedology/notes/mineral-reactivity-supply.md: none of the four proxies is derivable from what the export and the climatology carry, so all four stay declared absences and the mineral-aware arm stays refused. Fe-Al oxide and polyvalent cation saturation ARE measured, by Chadwick et al. (2003) against a leaching index this pipeline could compute, but on one parent material at one substrate age, non-monotonically, and with the paper stating the decline is irreversible, so the relation follows a climate path and an age this project has no axis for. Allophane is the near miss and stays one: Parfitt (1990) reports the New Zealand maxima and no distribution, filed as world-9loh. Aggregate capacity has no measurement to index at all. Both sources are now marked read in references/INDEX.md with what they settle. Also recorded: closing all four would not let the arm be written, because no read source supplies a parameterised transfer from a proxy to a protection coefficient. Commit 1c30c79a.

title: Verify code 903's MONTHLY interpolation and addfc's ice branches, which OCN-2 deliberately did not
description:
OCN-2 verified the prescribed ocean heat-transport channel on a field that is CONSTANT IN TIME and on an ice-free ocean, both on purpose: the constant field makes getflxco's month weights irrelevant so the calendar cannot influence the answer, and an ice-free segment keeps addfc in its branch (a). Two paths are therefore untested and each has an identity available.

MONTHLY INTERPOLATION. getflxco returns (1-zgw2)*yfsst(jm1) + zgw2*yfsst(jm2) with weights momint supplies. Whatever the calendar, that is a convex combination of two months, so the interpolated value must lie inside the envelope of the fourteen written months at every step and every cell, and the orbit mean of a field that is the same in all months must equal that field. A stronger statement needs the calendar: with a field linear in the month index the interpolated series is piecewise linear and its breakpoints are where momint changes month, which is a check on the calendar port rather than on the channel.

ADDFC ICE BRANCHES. Branch (b) fires where the model has ice and the climatology has ice, and uses the correction to drive the modelled sea surface temperature toward the climatological one with the residual passed to the ice module through yifluxr and mkiflx. Branch (c) fires where the model has ice and the climatology has none, and spends the correction melting. Neither is exercised. The identity is energy: what addfc withholds from the slab must equal what mkiflx adds to yiflux, cell by cell.

Do: extend exoplasim/scripts/verify_ocean_flux_channel.py with a second staged arm carrying a time-varying field and a third with a cold declared cold-start profile so ice forms, and state each criterion before running. Source: notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md section 11e.
notes:
WHY OCN-2 OMITTED THEM, checked first: ISOLATION, not a bar. Section 11e says the constant field keeps the calendar from influencing the answer and the ice-free segment keeps addfc in branch (a), and it explicitly names the time-varying field as 'a separate verification'. The reason was an ordering and the ordering is satisfied, so both are now instrumented.

DELIVERED, 2026-08-25: verify_ocean_flux_channel.py carries four arms. monthly stages a SEPARABLE field (the channel arm's pattern times a declared per-month scalar, twelve records so get_surf_array does its own cyclic expansion) with four criteria: separability, the fourteen-month envelope, the global integral at every record, and a fourth that stops the arm passing vacuously -- the recovered scalar series must span half the declared one, because a model that ignored the month index entirely satisfies the other three. The piecewise-linear statement needs the calendar and is reported rather than judged. ice and ice_clim stage a cold declared profile so ice grows, the second with code 211 beside it so ycliced > 0 and addfc takes branch (b); they close CRHOS*CPS*mld*dSST = (yheat + yfsst + yiflux)*dt_record on every ocean cell, which is the issue's cell-by-cell identity expressed in quantities the stream carries, since yifluxr is not written. Signs declared before any run; residual under each sign assignment reported on a failure. Two vacuous-pass guards per ice arm.

selftest synthesises a stream satisfying every identity and breaks each criterion in one named way. All four arms pass, channel included.

IT CAUGHT A BAR IN THE ALREADY-PASSING CRITERION. TOL_DELIVERY_RELATIVE is a fraction of the largest temperature change and ysst is float32, so on hundredth-kelvin windows the bar sits below the storage resolution and reports the format rather than the model -- failure-modes class 34, in the instrument. MIN_DELIVERY_CHANGE_K is now a declared floor on every arm; the segment section 11b ran clears it by a factor of five, so nothing it reported changes.

NOT VERIFIED, AND THAT IS WHY THIS STAYS OPEN. No arm has been run. The machine was contended and running the model was out of scope for this session. Section 11h carries the commands:
  python exoplasim/scripts/verify_ocean_flux_channel.py stage RUNDIR --rung T42 --arm monthly
  python exoplasim/scripts/verify_ocean_flux_channel.py selftest RUNDIR
  ...run the model in RUNDIR with the staged namelist...
  python exoplasim/scripts/verify_ocean_flux_channel.py check RUNDIR --record-seconds S --mixed-layer-m M
and the same for --arm ice and --arm ice_clim. TWO CONDITIONS: the monthly arm needs a FULL ORBIT or its fourth criterion cannot be met by construction, and the ice arms need a COLD start, because a restart carries an already-warm ocean and the declared profile never runs.
close_reason:
All three arms staged, self-tested and run at T42 on source a041a1e9, and ALL THREE PASS. OCN-2 left both paths untested on purpose; neither is untested now.

MONTHLY took a FULL ORBIT, 8774 steps at dt 30 from cold, which its fourth criterion requires by construction rather than by preference. It clears widely: the recovered per-month scalar series spans 0.468 to 1.532 against a declared 0.467 to 1.533, so getflxco reads the month index rather than holding one month, and the convex-combination identity holds at every step and cell.

ICE and ICE_CLIM both took a COLD start, which the row named as the second easily-missed condition -- a restart carries an already-warm ocean and the declared cold profile never runs. They exercise addfc branches (c) and (b) respectively, closing CRHOS*CPS*mld*dSST against (yheat + yfsst + yiflux)*dt_record from the declared profile and recovering the record interval to 1.7e-07 and 4.6e-07 relative.

Selftests were run first and pass, so the instrument was checked before the arms it judges.

notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md section 11h is rewritten; it said none of them had been run.

The arms' terminal SIGSEGV is the epilog use-after-free and reaches NO criterion, being after the ocean stream is written -- checked rather than assumed, and fixed since in e1510ab8.

title: The CENTURY microbial partition can leave a negative transfer fraction to slow SOM
description: modules/somdynam.cpp somfluxes partitions what leaves SOILMICRO into four shares: respiration max(0, 0.85 - 0.68*(clay+silt)) (Parton et al. 1993 eqn 7), organic leaching min(1, dperc/(OMLECH_3*cmpermonth_to_mmperday))*(0.03 + 0.12*sand) (eqn 8), the passive share 0.003 + 0.032*clay (eqn 9), and the slow share as the remainder csp = 1 - respfrac - orgleachfrac - cap. The remainder is not guarded. On pure sand at saturating percolation the first three sum to 1.003, so csp is -0.003 and the SOILMICRO to SLOWSOM transfer runs backwards. transferdecomp has no sign check. Does NOT bite on this world: over the 1019 land textures in pedology/data/precarve-craton-10m/soilmap_T21.txt the remainder falls no lower than 0.263, measured 2026-08-24. It is latent on any sandier soil map and on LPJ soil code 1 territory. Do: decide which of the four shares absorbs the excess, or clamp and re-derive the others so they still sum to 1; a bare max(0, csp) loses mass. biosphere/config/mineral_reactivity.yaml registers the simplex minimum and biosphere/scripts/mineral_reactivity_gate.py fails on any coefficient change that moves it. Evidence: biosphere/notes/mineral-reactivity-contract.md
close_reason: NOT A DEFECT on this world, bounded. The remainder form is Parton et al. (1993) eqn 10 p. 788, unguarded in the source too, and under that paper's own eqn 8 leaching coefficients (0.01 + 0.04*sand, saturating at 18 cm H2O/month) the remainder is positive over the whole texture simplex, bottoming out at +0.097 at pure sand. The CENTURY 5 update the code applies instead (0.03 + 0.12*sand at 1.9 cm/month) is what admits -0.003, and it arrived with the LPJ-GUESS subtree, so it is upstream and not a divergence this project made. Reversing needs clay+silt below 0.0039 (sand above 0.996) AND percolation at 0.98 of the leaching saturation point, both at once. No input path in the model reaches it: the soil map's sandiest cell is 0.663 sand with a worst remainder of 0.263 over 1019 land cells; soilinput.h's coarse LPJ soil code, the sandiest texture the model can be handed at 0.90 sand, still leaves 0.0754; the fixed-texture fallback leaves 0.569. No clamp applied and no coefficient changed. mineral_reactivity.yaml now registers the reachability boundaries, the soil code minimum and the source-coefficient variant, all checked by the gate with three new fixtures. One adjacent path filed as world-sptx: somfluxes mixes peat and mineral texture, which drops the coarse-code remainder to 0.009, unreachable while run_peatland is 0. Read from source and from the soil map; nothing execution-verified, LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree.

title: There is no near-surface wind diagnostic: spd is the speed of the interval-mean vector at model levels
description:
Codes 165 and 166 (uas, vas, the 10 m winds) are never written by outmod.f90. The only wind speed in the product is code 259, spd, which pyburn derives as sqrt(ua**2 + va**2) from the divergence and vorticity records. In the low-I/O regime those records are already interval means, so spd is |mean vector| rather than mean speed, and it carries a level axis rather than a near-surface value.

The two differ whenever the wind turns within an interval, and the difference is one-sided: |mean vector| <= mean speed always. Anything driven by wind speed rather than by momentum transport therefore reads low, and cannot be corrected after the fact from the product.

The forcing contract's wind row is a placeholder for exactly this reason. Closing it needs a producer-side accumulation of sqrt(u^2+v^2) at the lowest model level, formed at every timestep before any averaging, which only the model can form. EFOR-2's ecological stream is the natural place for it. aeolian/scripts/extract_high_cadence_wind.py works around the same gap for the gust distribution, by a different route.

Do: add the accumulator and its restart record, and give the contract's wind row a real source.

Source: biosphere/notes/ecological-forcing-field-contract.md
close_reason: NOT A DEFECT IN THE MODEL ANY MORE, and the premise had moved. The producer-side accumulation the issue asks for exists: outmod.f90:ecoaccu sums sqrt(du(:,NLEV)^2 + dv(:,NLEV)^2) every timestep into aecowind, ecogp divides it by the interval's own step count and writes it as code 614, and the restart record (mpputgp/mpgetgp behind the ecovers marker) and its restart_schema policy are all in place from the EFOR-2 landing. So the emitted quantity is the interval mean of the SPEED, named apart from spd which is the speed of the interval-mean vector. What was missing was delivery and naming, and both are done: the contract's wind row now cites ecowind/614 instead of being a placeholder, and pyburn stamps spd with a comment saying which of the two it is and where the other lives. world-eoe8 makes the stream producible from the harness. Commits 9d7e67e3, 99dafe85, 3f535772.

title: pyburn's hur is a percentage declared as a fraction, on the wrong saturation branch below freezing
description:
Two defects in one derived field.

Units: pyburn computes rh = qq/zqsat * 100.0 and clips to [0,100] while ilibrary declares the units '1'. Confirmed on the bootstrap climatology, where hur reaches exactly 100.0. A consumer that trusts the attribute is out by a hundred.

Saturation branch: pyburn hardcodes ra2 = 17.2693882 and ra4 = 35.86, the liquid-water coefficients. The model's own saturation goes through plasimmod.f90's ra2s/ra4s, which switch to ra2i/ra4i below tmelt. So the postprocessed relative humidity and the model's own saturation disagree wherever the air is below freezing, which on this world is a large fraction of the land in winter.

Also worth stating in the metadata: hur is a nonlinear function of the INTERVAL MEAN temperature and the interval mean specific humidity, so it is not the interval mean of relative humidity.

The ecological forcing contract avoids all three by carrying specific humidity, which is linear and is what the model integrates. This issue is for every other consumer of hur.

Source: biosphere/notes/ecological-forcing-field-contract.md
close_reason: pyburn's hur now declares '%' and saturates on the model's own branch (ice below tmelt, liquid above), through one saturation_specific_humidity helper carrying p_earth.f90's two Magnus-Teten triples and the model's +/-80 exponent clamp. The values were already a percentage and two aeolian consumers already read them as one, so the attribute moved rather than the numbers; hur below 273.16 K rises, because liquid-only saturation is high there (ice/liquid = 0.800 at 250 K). The nonlinear-mean caveat is now a comment attribute on the variable via pyburn's new FIELD_NOTES table. Commit 9d7e67e3.

title: Deliver ExoPlaSim's near-surface AIR temperature extrema to the ecological forcing path
description:
Output codes 201 (atsama) and 202 (atsami) are the extrema of dtsa, the near-surface air temperature, and outmod.f90 writes both unconditionally. They are absent from pyburn's ilibrary and from run_exoplasim.REGULAR_CODES, so they reach no product. The fields that DO reach the product, maxt and mint (321/320), are extrema of dt(:,NLEP), the surface temperature: on the bootstrap climatology they bracket ts in all 24,576 cell-bins and fail to bracket tas in 15,561 of them by up to 28.3 K.

Consequence today: vesperinput refuses ifbvoc 1, because climate.dtr means an air-temperature range and the forcing carries only the surface range. FIRE-2's fire weather and PCAR-1's subdaily path want the air extrema too.

Do: teach pyburn the two codes (run_exoplasim._teach_pyburn is the existing precedent for codes it does not ship) and add them to REGULAR_CODES, or carry them in EFOR-2's stream and never involve pyburn. Then lift the vesperinput refusal and add the field to the driver.

Source: biosphere/notes/ecological-forcing-field-contract.md
close_reason: Codes 201/202 reach a product: pyburn names them tasmax/tasmin and they are in REGULAR_CODES beside the surface pair. No Fortran needed changing -- outmod wrote them in all three streams already and their restart records and sentinel resets were in place. check_forcing_contract follows: they leave the not-produced list, and check_extrema now holds each pair against the variable it OWNS only, since requiring either pair to bracket the other temperature fails on correct data. Deliberately NOT added to SNAPSHOT_CODES: they would inherit the partial-window defect 320/321 have there, filed as world-adxx. The vesperinput/climate.dtr half is world-asma, which is a decision about whether to version the scaffolding transport again. Commit 99dafe85.

title: substrate_partition applies a WFPS-calibrated curve to a fraction-of-available-capacity variable
description: modules/ntransform.cpp substrate_partition splits every mineral N pool between an aerobic and an anaerobic share, which is the largest single control the operator has on gaseous loss. It reads soil.get_soil_water_upper(), the upper layer's water as a fraction of AVAILABLE capacity, while its own comment describes the curve in water-filled pore space (rising from about 50 percent, steepest near 66, complete by 75) and cites Pilegaard (2013), which places the nitrification-to-denitrification crossover at 60 percent WFPS. Soil::wfps builds WFPS as (wcont*gawc + gwp)/gwsats, so it carries a texture-dependent offset and scale: for LPJ soil code 2 a water content of 0.5 is 0.590 WFPS and the comment's 0.66 WFPS is a water content of 0.705. nitrification and denitrification in the same file read soil.wfps(0); only this function does not. The comment does not describe this curve in either variable either: richards_curve with midpoint 0.5 and shape 7.5 reaches 0.830 at 0.75, not 1. Do: settle whether the intended argument is wfps(0), which is a one-line change that moves the split on every gridcell. Blocked on Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) 10.1111/j.1365-2486.2008.01625.x, which could not be fetched and is the only place the calibration is stated. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md
notes:
2026-08-24, batch AM. Settled from Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008), now held.

The paper is unambiguous. Table 7 gives DyN's 'soil aeration status used to allocate substrates' as 'soil moisture as water-filled pore space (WFPS)', against DNDC's redox-based anaerobic volume fraction. The nitrification section on p.1752 repeats it: 'Soil moisture content (WFPS) of the top 50 cm layer is used to allocate substrates into the aerobic and anaerobic soil fractions.' SOILDEPTH_UPPER is 500 mm, so the layer is right and the quantity was not. substrate_partition now reads soil.wfps(0), which is what nitrification and denitrification in the same file already read.

What it was worth, measured on pedology/data/precarve-craton/soilmap.txt, 4105 gridcells: at a fixed 0.50 WFPS the anaerobic share ran from 0.071 to 0.874 on texture alone where the curve on WFPS gives 0.500 everywhere; the median cell's aerobic share, which is what nitrification is offered, was 1.65x the curve's value at 0.50 WFPS and 1.55x at 0.60. The curve's midpoint landed at a median 0.606 WFPS, essentially Pilegaard's crossover, but spread 0.372 to 0.806 across textures. So the defect was texture-dependent scatter at fixed wetness, not a uniform bias.

The form is NOT settled and was not guessed at. Xu-Ri gives no functional form for the split, delegating to PnET-DNDC's anaerobic balloon, so richards_curve(0.05, 0.95, 7.5, 0.5, .) is the port's own. The midpoint 0.5 is left where it is and declared unsourced with the bracket 0.50 to 0.66, which is the spread between the two numbers the code comment asserts at once. That is world-nga8.

The quantity the model does not carry, named: soil water above field capacity in the upper 50 cm. get_soil_water refuses a wcont outside [0,1] and wcont is a fraction of AVAILABLE capacity, so wfps(0) is bounded above by field capacity over saturation -- a median 0.813 on that map and as little as 0.573. 164 of 4105 gridcells can therefore never reach 0.70 WFPS, where the operator's N2 branch begins, and 2032 sit above 0.40 WFPS even at wilting point, so denitrification never switches off on them. Declared in biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml's wfps domain.

Not execution-verified: LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree.
close_reason: Settled: Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 7 and the nitrification section name the allocation variable as water-filled pore space of the top 50 cm, so the intended argument is soil.wfps(0) and substrate_partition now reads it. The curve's own midpoint and shape are a separate, unsourced question with a declared bracket, tracked as world-nga8.

title: The in-model friction velocity uses a scalar DUSTZ0 where the offline chain uses the per-cell roughness mosaic
description:
world-c8m gave each erodible lithology its own aeolian roughness and source_fractions returns one erodible-area weighted geometric-mean z0 per cell per bracket end. build_dust.run_one uses that mosaic in BOTH places the roughness enters: the drag partition, and ln(zref/z0) in u* = kappa spd drage / ln(zref/z0).

The in-model arm gets the mosaic in the drag partition only. Boundary field 1802 now carries drag_efficiency(z0_cell) per cell (world-2lsg), but aerocore.f90 dustsrc computes zust = gdrage*VONKARM*zspd/LOG(zref/dustz0) from the SCALAR namelist dustz0, which is aeolian_z0_m, the class-blind fallback.

Size: this world's two erodible classes are declared at 3.0e-5 m (playa_clastic) and 1.4e-4 m (evaporite), a factor of 4.7. At a bottom level around 30 m that is ln(1e6) against ln(2.1e5), about 12% on u*, and emission goes as roughly u* cubed above a threshold.

It cannot be folded into 1802: zref is computed in-model from the cell's own temperature through the hypsometric relation, so the ln ratio is not a static prefactor.

Do: decide whether the mosaic is honoured in-model. If it is, that needs a FOURTH boundary field carrying ln(zref_ref/z0_cell) or z0_cell itself, with its own surface code, its gather in aeromod, its staging in run_exoplasim.py and its arm in the self-test identity. If it is not, dustz0 should at least be the erodible-area weighted geometric mean of the mosaic rather than the class-blind scalar, and the residual stated.

Evidence: aeolian/scripts/build_dust_source_fields.py:build_fields docstring; vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/aerocore.f90 dustsrc; aeolian/config/dust.yaml aeolian_z0_by_class_m.
close_reason:
FIXED. DUSTZ0 is now the roughness mosaic's own erodible-area weighted geometric mean at the bracket end being written, computed by build_dust_source_fields.build_fields from the fields themselves through the shared build_dust.mosaic_scalar_z0, rather than read from the config. Commit 09e40f3d.

The defect was larger than the issue estimated. DUSTZ0 carried aeolian_z0_m, the class-blind value whose bracket ends predate world-c8m and sit OUTSIDE the per-lithology ones (3.3e-6 / 1.0e-4 / 1.0e-3 against a mosaic mean of 1.01e-5 / 3.03e-5 / 1.01e-4). The in-model arm therefore emitted 0.646, 1.746 and 4.049 times the offline arm at the smooth, central and rough ends, which is a comparison defeated before it starts.

THE FOURTH BOUNDARY FIELD IS DECIDED AGAINST, and priced rather than judged. With the mosaic's mean in DUSTZ0 the in-model emission sits at 0.997, 0.997 and 0.996 of the offline arm. That residual is the whole of what a per-cell z0 field would recover, so its surface code, its gather in aeromod, its staging in run_exoplasim.py and its arm in the self-test identity are not worth adding. No Fortran was changed and rule 4 does not apply.

Nothing was staged under the old value (exoplasim/inputs/t21 holds no 180x .sra), so no artifact is made worthless.

Evidence: notes/audits/dust-intensity-levers.md section 6, aeolian/analysis/dust_intensity_levers.json in_model_scalar_z0.

title: The sea-salt Earth check's pass criterion is the ratio the same file says proves nothing
description:
sea_salt_source.py's monahan_number_flux_per_dp docstring states the standard: 'an absolute comparison against a published global production measures our wind treatment; a ratio between two functions run through the same machinery does not'. _earth_check then sets ok from exactly that ratio.

It computes ours['M86'] and ours['G13T'] against Grythe Table 2, prints both absolute ratios, and gates only on how well the two ratios agree WITH EACH OTHER. aeolian/config/sea_salt.yaml declares ratio_agreement: 0.20 and no absolute band. A common-mode error -- a wrong ocean_area_m2, a unit slip in _integrate_mass, a wrong moment_ratio, a wrong ocean_mean_u10_m_s -- moves both ratios together and leaves the spread unchanged, so the check cannot fail in the direction _earth_check's own docstring says it tests ('the source functions and the mass integration').

SECOND, same shape: _integrate_mass re-implements the trapezoid rather than calling mass_flux, so the production entry point, its bin_edges_um sliver logic and temperature_weight are never exercised by the only Earth comparison this component has. The temperature weight is correctly out of the comparison and said to be; the integrator is not.

Do, and the two halves are one decision:
1. Fix an absolute ratio band BEFORE the next run of this check, sourced from Grythe's own stated spread across the functions in Table 2 rather than from what our numbers currently give -- a criterion chosen after the run it judges is not a criterion. Declare it in sea_salt.yaml beside ratio_agreement and add it to ok.
2. Route the G13T arm through mass_flux(u, sst_c, cfg, k, modes=(0,1)) so the shipped integrator is the one under test, and decide what to do about M86, which has no hook in mass_flux for a supplied flux function. If both arms cannot share the integrator, say which one the comparison is about.

Found by world-60x0's sweep. Not fixed there because both halves need a threshold fixed in advance.
close_reason: Three bars declared in 3be792f before the run, and both arms routed through mass_flux so the shipped integrator is the one under test. Reading Grythe's Table 2 properly found two like-for-like errors the issue did not anticipate: the Dp column is each row's own validity range, not a common Dp<10um cut, so M86's 4.51 Pg/yr is over 0.8-8 um; and the A7 temperature weight is applied only to rows ending in T, so G13T's target carries one and M86's does not. The comparison is therefore about MONAHAN, which is tabled twice over two ranges with no weight on either row; G13T is reported and not gated, and the file says so. MEASURED: size-range ratio M86E/M86 1.1515 against 1.1530, 0.13 percent off a 5 percent bar; bin-sum identity 1.25e-5 against 1e-3; absolute 2.75 Pg/yr against the 3.3-11.7 published range for that function, FAIL. The two passes exclude the source function and the integrator, so the miss is the assumed ocean-mean wind. world-3e2d carries it.

title: The Lacis and Hansen Eq. 21 reconstruction has no declared bound
description:
shortwave_band_weights.py records reconstruction_vs_lacis_hansen_eq21 with ratio_min, ratio_max and ratio_median over the interval LH74 state their fit holds on, and there is no criterion anywhere for what those numbers must be. It is a measurement presented in a checks block.

world-60x0 made the sibling check in the same file raise -- Earth's near-infrared CO2 shortwave absorption against EARTH_CO2_SHORTWAVE_W_M2, which IS declared -- and deliberately did not invent a bound for this one: a criterion chosen after the run it judges is not a criterion (CLAUDE.md).

Do: decide, BEFORE the next run of the script, what ratio band a correct reconstruction of Yamamoto (1962) through this file's band set must fall in, and on what grounds -- LH74's own stated fit accuracy is the obvious source. Declare it as a module constant beside EARTH_CO2_SHORTWAVE_W_M2, then make the miss raise the same way. If no defensible band can be sourced, the block is a diagnostic and should be moved out of checks and said to be one.
close_reason: Bound declared in 067af59 before the run, sourced from Lacis and Hansen's own p. 127 grounds: the envelope of Eqs. 21, 22 and 23, the three curves of their Fig. 11, per water amount, widened by Howard's stated +/-3 percent. Not Eq. 21's own ~1 percent, which is a residual between two curves rather than a statement about the quantity. The miss now raises, and both checks that can fail are collected and raised together so neither hides the other's verdict. MEASURED: the reconstruction is outside, above the envelope top by 1.2 percent at w=0.03 cm rising to 10.3 percent at 5 cm, inside only at 0.01 cm. Not softened. world-5t6s carries the decision about the level offset.

title: Re-measure the biosphere numbers produced under the max-anchored tissue windows
description:
world-xms4 divided every fine-root and sapwood C:N by 1.7905 and every fine-root and sapwood C:P by 2.2168. Under rule 7 the numbers below are worthless rather than stale: they are outputs of a model form that is gone, and nothing derived from them can be repaired by adjustment.

What is worthless:
- The multiyear adapter cycling response in biosphere/README.md: annual NPP at -3/0/+3 K on one cell, the cycle mean, and the concavity percentage read off them. The qualitative concavity argument survives; the numbers do not.
- Any nitrogen bracket scored by biosphere/scripts/score_prediction.py against a run made before the repair (BIO-2).
- The stock-port smoke result is an integration result on unpatched 4.1.1 and is NOT in this set; it says nothing about tissue stoichiometry.

Not affected: notes/productivity-prediction.md is a pre-registered prediction and is independent of the model form it will be scored against.

Do: when a biosphere run is next made, re-measure the adapter response on the mean-anchored source and rewrite the README table from it, and re-score BIO-2's bracket. This is measurement and not analysis: BIO-11 through BIO-15 and BIO-21 through BIO-25 still gate an interpretable run, so this issue is downstream of them.

Non-local consequence worth carrying into that run: somdynam.cpp:1471 computes the fine-root litter lignin-to-nitrogen ratio from pft.cton_root_avr, so root litter now enters the soil at 1.7905 times its former nitrogen concentration and decomposes faster. That is a correct consequence of the repair, not a defect, but it moves soil carbon and nitrogen as well as plant carbon.

Nothing here is execution-verified: LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree.

title: Decide which instruction file the biosphere runs on: acclimated_respiration is 1 in global.ins and 0 in global_p.ins
description:
build_vesper_pfts.py defaults its source instruction file to vendor/lpj-guess/data/ins/global.ins, which sets acclimated_respiration 1 (global.ins:122). The C-N-P file global_p.ins sets it to 0 (global_p.ins:135). The two are not interchangeable for sapwood and fine-root maintenance respiration.

respiration() takes respcoeff, and Pft::init_cton_limits renormalises respcoeff by cton_root/(cton_root_avr + cton_root_min) + cton_sap/(cton_sap_avr + cton_sap_min). Under the mean-anchored windows that sum is 1.95 times each tissue's own mean, exactly as it was under the max anchor, so scaling both windows scales the sum inversely and respcoeff/cton is invariant: on that path sapwood and fine-root maintenance respiration does not move at all when a tissue C:N window moves.

respiration_acclimated() (canexch.cpp:2887) takes no respcoeff argument. It substitutes 0.25 * pow(10, -0.008 * (airtemp - 10.15)) for wood and 1.0 * pow(10, -0.008 * (soiltemp - 10.15)) for fine roots, and multiplies K * cmass / cton * gtemp directly. There is no compensation, so maintenance respiration on that path scales as 1/cton_sap and 1/cton_root.

Consequence of world-xms4 on the configured path: every fine-root and sapwood C:N divided by 1.7905, so maintenance respiration rises by up to that factor. The bound is not the value: canexch.cpp:3086-3092 passes indiv.cton_sap()/indiv.cton_root() when ifnlim is on, and those are floored at cton_sap_avr * cton_leaf_min / cton_leaf_avr, which moved by the same 1.7905, so a nitrogen-replete simulated individual sees the full factor and a starved one sees less. With ifnlim off it passes pft.cton_sap_avr directly and the factor is exactly 1.7905.

Do: decide whether the biosphere runs the acclimated function or the respcoeff one, and make build_vesper_pfts.py name that choice rather than inherit it from whichever file it happens to import. PCAR-3 owns the separate finding that respiration_acclimated() has no acclimation state; this issue is about which of the two paths the Vesper configuration is on and what it costs.

Nothing here is execution-verified: LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree. Evidence in biosphere/notes/plant-physiology-carbon-allocation-audit.md finding 11.
notes:
2026-08-25, branch fanout-W6, commit 76e1e6df. THE DECISION HALF IS TAKEN, by world-uhfh: the biosphere runs the STANDARD respiration path. It is declared as path.runs in biosphere/config/respiration_acclimation.yaml, with the argument and with what would reopen it, and acclimation_gate.py now holds run_lpj_guess.py acclimated_respiration to that line, so the two cannot drift apart.

WHAT REMAINS HERE is the mechanism half this row asks for: build_vesper_pfts.py still defaults its source instruction file to global.ins, which sets acclimated_respiration 1, and inherits the setting rather than naming it. Nothing runs on the wrong path today, because the generated run instruction declares 0 and plib takes the later declaration, but an inherited 1 that happens to be overridden is not the same as a stated choice. Make build_vesper_pfts.py name the path.

The cost half this row computed is unchanged and is now recorded in biosphere/notes/plant-physiology-carbon-allocation-audit.md finding 3a, with two further reasons beside it: the acclimated path also moves the sapwood basal rate down by a factor of 2 to 10 on the vendored Earth parameters, and swaps a leaf-longevity dependence for a growth-temperature one.

2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER, from a pass over the needs-decision set.
RECLASSIFIED, an investigation, not a decision: respiration_acclimated substitutes Thum et al. (2019) and Atkin et al. (2014) acclimation for the respcoeff parameter and matters most for tropical types. Which path is right is answerable from the two papers and the fork's own parameters.

title: Sweep every declared check for arguments it does not forward: a gate that silently stopped testing what it names
description:
world-qq10 found build_groundwater.py's --uniqueness-check re-solving from the opposite initial active set but NOT forwarding et_max_m_s, et_lambda_m or fixed_head_m to the re-solve. Once GW-15's evapotranspiration sink and GW-17's local baselevels landed and defaulted ON, the check was comparing a solve WITH both against a solve with NEITHER -- measuring the difference between two models rather than between two trajectories. The 0.000e+00 recorded in water-table-convergence.md predates those terms, so it is honest evidence about a model that no longer exists.

world-qq10 names the class and says it is worth a sweep. This issue is that sweep, and it is deliberately project-wide rather than hydrography-only, because the same shape has now appeared twice in one component: the --surface option that ran, reported and changed nothing is recorded in earth-calibration-criterion.md.

THE SHAPE TO LOOK FOR: a check that constructs a second run, a reference arm, a re-solve, a round trip or a control, and builds it from a shorter argument list than the thing it is checking. It passes for as long as the omitted terms are off or absent, and it silently stops testing what its name claims the moment one of them lands. It cannot fail in the direction that matters, so it is not a test -- CLAUDE.md's rule that a check needs a right answer, and that if you cannot say in advance what result would mean wrong then it is not a test.

Where to look: every --check/--verify/--test flag and every self-test or round-trip in hydrography/scripts, exoplasim/scripts, biosphere/scripts, pedology, minerals, aeolian and scripts/. scripts/check_consistency.py and scripts/smoke_test.py are the two that matter most because everything else trusts them.

For each: list the arguments the checked call takes, the arguments the checking call passes, and the difference. A difference is not automatically a defect -- some are deliberate -- but every one must be either justified in a comment beside it or fixed.

Do NOT fix by widening a bound or by deleting the check. Forward the argument, or if the check cannot be made to test what it names, say so and delete it with its rows -- deleting is a fix.
acceptance_criteria: Every declared check in the tree is listed with the argument difference between what it checks and how it checks it, each difference either justified beside the code or closed. Any check that cannot test what it names is deleted with its pipeline and README rows, not left passing.
notes:
Swept 2026-08-24. Finding with the full per-component table in notes/audits/checks-that-forward-too-few-arguments.md: every --check/--verify/--test/--self-test flag, round trip and comparison arm across scripts/, lib/, hydrography/, exoplasim/, biosphere/, pedology/, minerals/, aeolian/, analysis/ and maps/, each with its checked call, checking call, difference and verdict.

FIXED by forwarding the argument: smoke_test.check_build_scoped_defaults, link_worktree --check, build_groundwater's uniqueness re-solve (one shared kwargs dict), earth_calibration's --river-km2 and --et-lambda, corrk_cross_check.run_checks (star), run_exoplasim.verify_stellar_spectrum (the name it read), rebuild_binaries --verify (BIN, and missing setting the exit), restart_surface --self-test (manifest and allow_superseded, plus the T21 literal), convert_restart --check-template and its explicit-seed length bar, restart_convert_selftest (seed_override, and a negative control that ran nothing), transform_exactness, verify_legendre_parity, shortwave_band_weights' Earth CO2 bar, stack_floor --validate's configuration, lib/stellar's partition identity, pedology/validate_against_earth (it re-implemented weather_texture three terms short), pedology/brine_paths (one weighting checked of two, and passes never gated), maps/snapshot --basemap-width.

JUSTIFIED and now commented beside the code: groundwater's confined_test and dupuit_test omit the ET sink because their analytic references are solutions without one; earth_calibration.stage_benchmark loads the baseline solution by name because it excludes the physical model; check_consistency's self_test builds its fixture from the staging lists deliberately and mitigates it correctly.

CARRIED, each with an issue and a reason it could not be closed here: world-g5va (verify_weight_factorisation compares two restatements of the same product; the fix needs a compiled extraction), world-2lsg (the dust quadrature divergence plus the scalar drag field; needs every binary rebuilt), world-fgak, world-zvk2 and world-f1u3 (three checks whose bar must be fixed before the run that judges it, not after).

NOT RUN, fixes static: restart_surface --self-test needs a run directory with a staged code 229; brine_paths and shortwave_band_weights both need a baseline_climatology.
close_reason: Swept. Every declared check in the tree is listed with its argument difference in notes/audits/checks-that-forward-too-few-arguments.md; 20 defects fixed by forwarding the argument, 8 differences justified in a comment beside the code, 5 carried to their own issues (world-g5va, world-2lsg, world-fgak, world-zvk2, world-f1u3) with the reason each could not be closed under a no-compile, no-model-run constraint. No check was deleted: every one could be made to test what it names.

title: The uniqueness identity was re-solving a different model, and had been since GW-15
description:
FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-24 in the same commit as GW-24, recorded here because the class matters more than the instance.

build_groundwater.py's --uniqueness-check re-solves from the opposite initial active set and requires the identical head field. The re-solve call passed k0, thickness, recharge, surface and conductive, and did NOT pass et_max_m_s, et_lambda_m or fixed_head_m. So once GW-15's evapotranspiration sink and GW-17's local baselevels landed and were turned ON by default, the check was comparing a solve WITH both against a solve with NEITHER. It was measuring the difference between two models rather than between two trajectories, and it could only ever have reported a large miss or been run in a configuration where the omission did not bite.

The 0.000e+00 recorded in hydrography/notes/water-table-convergence.md was measured before those two terms existed, so it is a real result about the model of that date and is not evidence about the model as it now stands.

Do: re-run python hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater.py --uniqueness-check with the current defaults and record the result. The bar is unchanged at SCHEME_HEAD_RELATIVE = 1e-9 for the confined form. If it passes, water-table-convergence.md's uniqueness section should say which configuration it passed in; if it misses, that is a live defect in the release-and-pin logic under a nonlinear sink.

THE CLASS: a check that silently stops testing what it names when a term is added elsewhere. The same shape as the --surface option that ran, reported and changed nothing, recorded in earth-calibration-criterion.md. Worth a sweep of the other declared checks in this component for arguments they do not forward.
notes:
world-60x0's sweep confirmed the code fix is in: build_groundwater.py's uniqueness re-solve now takes the primary solve's own argument list whole (one solve_kwargs, both calls), so the two differ in start_all_free and nothing else by construction, and a new term cannot reach one without reaching the other.

hydrography/notes/water-table-convergence.md now says which equation the 0.000e+00 was measured on: 2026-08-20, before GW-15 and GW-17, so both trajectories carried neither. Honest for the model of that date, not a result for the current one.

STILL OUTSTANDING and why this stays open: the re-run. `python hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater.py --uniqueness-check` at the unchanged SCHEME_HEAD_RELATIVE bar. It was not run because config/planet.yaml declares no baseline_climatology and the sweep ran under a no-model-run constraint. Until it is run there is no measured uniqueness result for the equation the component now solves.
close_reason: FIXED. The code repair landed with world-60x0 (one solve_kwargs, both calls). What was missing was evidence the repaired identity can fail: groundwater.py --uniqueness-test now runs it on a synthetic case carrying GW-15's sink and GW-17's baselevels, with three controls it must REJECT (re-solve missing the sink 5.301e+00 m, missing the baselevels 6.244e+01 m, solve mutated to seed pinned cells below their surface 4.467e+00 m) and two it must pass (the identity at 0.000e+00, a third arbitrary active set at 5.296e-10 m). One bar, SCHEME_HEAD_RELATIVE unchanged. The sweep the issue asked for found --reduction-test in the same class and it is fixed in the same branch; --divide-test and the lake solver's two call sites are not. Recorded in hydrography/notes/water-table-convergence.md. The planet-scale re-run is world-v3ur: it needs a host with the memory to factor a 4.33M-cell land set, which this one did not have. Also filed: world-6d9h (no control on the anchor release path), world-w9g3 (config prose says no climatology exists on this build; a bootstrap one does).

title: A saturated fraction is a grid-cell quantity, and three rows want a native-mesh one
description:
GW-26 built the compound topographic index and its saturated-fraction closure, and settled that f_sat_max is a rank statistic over the terrain population INSIDE a cell. The only such population this project holds is the mesh regions inside a climate-grid cell, so f_sat lives at the grid. A region has no sub-population, and GW-6 established that the sub-region hypsometry one would need does not exist and is not recoverable by a finer generation.

WET-2's wetness classification, SURF-7's discharge mask and LSHY-6's hydrologic mosaic all ask for a NATIVE-MESH fraction. What GW-26 can give them is a climate-grid-cell fraction. That is a real gap between what those rows assume and what the terrain supports, and it is not GW-26's to close.

Three routes, and the choice is a decision rather than an implementation:
(1) the consumers take the grid-cell fraction and downscale it by a stated rule, which puts the rule where it can be argued;
(2) a sub-region hypsometry is PARAMETERISED from the statistics of the finer build -- notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md says the terrain is statistically converged, so a distribution is available even though a cell-by-cell mapping is not -- and declared as a parameterisation rather than a measurement;
(3) the consumers change quantity, as GW-26 did, and ask for something the grid can answer.

Do: pick one, before any of the three consumers takes the artifact. hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 5, config/pipeline.yaml step topographic_index.
close_reason: FIXED, as a decision plus the defect it exposed. DECISION: route three, the consumers change quantity and take the climate-grid fraction. Section 2's standing rule decides it rather than a preference: sub-grid information reaches a cell-scale parameter only as a statistic of the cell's own distribution, so route two puts a distribution below the cell where GW-6 says there is none and route one makes the same invention three times. It is the route groundwater_access already took under PLHY-5. PER ROW: LSHY-6 asked for a climate-grid area in the first place and is served; SURF-7 never needed the quantity, because a discharge mask is about where the SOLVED table meets the surface and water_table.nc carries at_surface and seepage_m3_s per region; WET-2 is the one row that changes quantity and inherits the cost, mutual exclusivity now stated at two supports. Both other dependencies are deleted rather than met. DEFECT: if f_sat_max is a share of a cell it must be a share of AREA, and per_cell computed a share of the region COUNT, in the share and in the cell mean the share is taken about. These land regions span a factor of 5.2 p5 to p95. Measured: the cell mean moves by a median of 0.19, the same order as the 0.23 between the two slope arms already shipped as a bracket, and f_sat_max by a median of 0.004 at T21 and up to 0.30 in the worst cell. per_cell now uses gridding.cell_moments and gridding.cell_fraction, transfer_ledger goes in the report, and the config value is load-bearing. Recorded in hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 5. Filed: world-tiun.

title: Pedology emits no cation-exchange capacity, so the ANUT-8 standing pool is a bracket rather than a bound
description:
The ANUT-8 adequacy screen takes the above-ground standing nutrient pool to the whole circulating pool with a multiplier declared as a BRACKET of 1 to 5, because no artifact in this repository carries an exchangeable-cation or cation-exchange-capacity field: pedology/scripts/build_soil.py emits sand, clay, silt, organic carbon, pH, bulk density and C:N and no CEC. The upper end rests on Chadwick et al. (1999) Fig. 2a, whose soil exchange cations reach about 6 meq per 100 g over the top metre.

The screen runs on the upper end, so the bracket costs it a factor of five in the critical runoff it reports for K, Ca, Mg and S. It collapses to a bound the moment pedology emits an exchangeable-base or CEC field, which its texture, mineralogy and organic carbon already largely determine.

Do: derive and emit an exchangeable-base or cation-exchange-capacity field from the soil texture, clay mineralogy and organic carbon build_soil.py already carries, and replace the multiplier bracket in biosphere/config/abiotic_nutrients.yaml with the bound.

Source: biosphere/notes/abiotic-nutrient-ledger.md, the ANUT-8 screen
close_reason: Resolved and committed. pedology emits an exchange complex -- pedogenesis.yaml's `exchange` block, build_soil.py:exchange_properties, and a `cec` column on the soil map -- and the ANUT-8 multiplier is a bound read off it. It collapsed to 54.09 set by magnesium, bracket 47.44 to 54.09, per-element K 31.15 / Ca 26.37 / Mg 54.09 / S 5.67, replacing a 1-to-5 bracket run at its upper end. It collapsed UPWARD: the old upper end was a base-depleted Hawaiian profile and this world's soils are base-saturated over most of the land, so ANUT-8 had been reporting a critical runoff an order of magnitude below its own construction. The verdict survives the capacity level, which is the one large exposure: the emitted level probe gives 19.6 and 27.3 at Dahlgren's halloysite endmembers, and the root term alone puts magnesium at 6.43 with no exchange complex in the arithmetic. Sources read for this: Sahrawat (1983) for the slopes, Solly et al. (2020) for the falsifiable organic-share check, the capacity envelope and the calcium share, Chadwick et al. (2003) and Solly for base saturation against pH, Vitousek and Sanford (1986) Table 7 for the root term, Dahlgren et al. (2004) for the andic anion exchange ceiling sulfate's pool rests on. The declaration is inside a loop: build_soil.py refuses when it or any per-element entry falls under the field, verified by a first run that refused on 5.0 and a second that exits 0. Follow-ons filed and open: world-n4i0 the capacity LEVEL, world-vf8j the per-element read, world-rzyz the mineral-reactivity wiring.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESOLVED. pedology emits an exchange complex and the ANUT-8 multiplier is a bound read off it, not a declared 1-to-5 bracket.

WHAT WAS BUILT. pedogenesis.yaml gains an `exchange` block; build_soil.py:exchange_properties derives cation exchange capacity, base saturation and the exchangeable pool per element; the soil map gains a `cec` column, which SoilInput skips by name and every other reader indexes by name.

THE FORM is additive with NO INTERCEPT, because exchange sites sit on clay-size mineral surfaces and on organic matter and a soil with neither has none. The two slopes are Sahrawat (1983), `10.1080/00103628309367409`, 38 cmol(+)/kg of clay and 300 of organic matter. His 7.98 intercept is DROPPED as a regional artifact, which is a reading and is written down as one; the one-signed 8 cmol(+)/kg understatement it causes is reported beside the field and added back for the bound.

THE CHECK THAT COULD HAVE FAILED. At Sahrawat's own reference composition the pair puts organic matter at 37.9 per cent of capacity, inside the 35 to 50 per cent Solly et al. (2020), `10.3389/ffgc.2020.00098`, measured by partial regression over 1204 Swiss forest profiles. Two continents, two methods. It runs on every call and three negative controls refuse.

WHAT COLLAPSED, AND IT COLLAPSED UPWARD. 54.09, set by magnesium, bracket 47.44 to 54.09, per-element map K 31.15, Ca 26.37, Mg 54.09, S 5.67. The old upper end of 5 rested on Chadwick et al. (1999) Fig. 2a -- a deeply weathered, base-depleted Hawaiian basalt profile. This world's soils are not that: emitted land-mean base saturation is 0.52 and is 1.0 over most of the land. So ANUT-8 had been reporting a critical runoff an order of magnitude BELOW what its own construction supports and calling cells adequate on it. The screen was permissive where it advertises conservatism.

THE VERDICT SURVIVES THE INSTRUMENT. The capacity level is the one large unbracketed exposure. The emitted level probe re-evaluates the bound at Dahlgren et al. (2004)'s halloysite endmembers: 19.6 at 2 cmol(+)/kg of clay, 27.3 at 10, against 54.1 at Sahrawat's 38. All far outside [1,5]. And the ROOT TERM ALONE puts magnesium at 6.43, outside it with no exchange complex in the arithmetic at all -- the 1-to-5 bracket did not bound even the plant half of what it multiplied.

pH. build_soil.py derives a pH field and every reachable CEC relation is a fixed-pH regression, so the emitted CAPACITY is blind to it. That is recorded in the config, the README and the report. pH reaches the pool through BASE SATURATION instead, and that is sourced twice and independently: Chadwick et al. (2003) Table 7 pairs pH with base saturation horizon by horizon, and Solly puts calcium on 59 to 83 per cent of the complex above pH 5.5 against aluminium on 21 to 44 below pH 5. Both put the transition in the same place.

SULFATE IS AN ANION, so the cation complex holds none of it -- but variable-charge andic material carries anion exchange, and zeroing the whole term would have been anti-conservative by a factor of two on andic ground, where the bound is a land maximum. The ceiling is Dahlgren et al. (2004), 'AEC values for Andisols were generally less than 3 cmolc kg-1 at pH values greater than 5'.

THE DECLARATION IS INSIDE A LOOP. build_soil.py refuses when the scalar, or any entry in the per-element map, falls below what the emitted field implies. Verified end to end: the first run refused on 5.0 and named Mg, wrote the report before the check so the failing state was inspectable, and the second run exits 0.

OPEN, AND FILED: world-n4i0 (the capacity LEVEL rests on one region's fit, n=40, R2 0.60; Helling 1964 and Manrique 1991 would close it and neither is reachable from this host), world-vf8j (the ledger reads one scalar for four elements whose bounds span 5.67 to 54.09; biosphere/scripts was another session's directory), world-rzyz (the emitted capacity is not yet wired to the mineral-aware arm's polyvalent-cation proxy).

title: Emit deposition MASS for sea salt and volcanic sulfate, not optics, so the abiotic ledger has a carrier
description:
ANUT-7 retains marine aerosol as a base-cation and sulfur source to the abiotic nutrient ledger and registers volcanic sulfate deposition, but neither has a carrier: aeolian/scripts/sea_salt_optics.py and aeolian/scripts/build_volcanic_sulfate.py produce optical products, and biosphere/config/abiotic_nutrients.yaml refuses an optical depth as a carrier by name because it folds in refractive index, size distribution and water uptake and no elemental mass comes back out of it.

Do: emit a size- and species-resolved wet plus dry deposition MASS field per receiving area per absolute time from the existing sea-salt source function and the volcanic sulfur inventory, with the elemental split, and declare it as the carrier for the soluble_deposition term. The magnitude to check against is Chadwick et al. (1999), who measured 600 +/- 400 mg Ca per m2 per Earth year of atmospheric input at a Hawaiian site.

Source: biosphere/notes/abiotic-nutrient-ledger.md, the ANUT-7 register
close_reason:
FIXED, emission side. aeolian/scripts/aerosol_deposition.py is the elemental split and the shared writer; build_sea_salt.py writes aeolian/analysis/sea_salt_deposition.{nc,json} and build_volcanic_sulfate.py writes aeolian/analysis/volcanic_sulfate_deposition.{nc,json}, both declared as writes of their existing steps in config/pipeline.yaml, both documented in aeolian/README.md. Wet plus dry removal per size bin in kg m-2 s-1, a field per element with the mass fraction as a netCDF attribute, and land and ocean means in mg per m2 per Earth year in the JSON. Commit f0022ea3.

DESIGNED AGAINST THE CONSUMER FIRST, as the issue asked. The decisive constraint turned out to be that biosphere/config/abiotic_nutrients.yaml names aeolian/analysis/volcanic_sulfate.nc and aeolian/analysis/sea_salt_optics.json in screen.forbidden_carriers BY PATH and abiotic_nutrient_ledger.py:check_screen enforces it, so the mass could not be a variable added to either baseline artifact. Hence separate files whose whole content is mass.

The deposition is a PARTITION of the loss*m the transport already balances against emission, not a second calculation: build_sea_salt.py asserts the two halves sum back to its own mass balance's removal to 1e-10, which catches a sign error or a dropped bin that the mass residual cannot see. aerosol_deposition.py --self-test carries three more identities and shows each rejecting a deliberately broken input.

Composition from TEOS-10 Manual Table D.3 p. 144, per kg of sea salt, closing on 1 by construction. Millero et al. (2008) itself is paywalled on every route tried and was not substituted for. Sulfate to sulfur from the manual's own molar masses. P excluded, matching the config's own excluded_reason.

TWO BLOCKING DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED: neither build_sea_salt.py nor build_volcanic_sulfate.py could run at all, because both call advect_to_steady_state, which reads _planet_radius_earth off the config dict, and only build_dust.py injected it. That is why aeolian/analysis holds no sea_salt_baseline.

NOT DONE HERE, and handed over as world-5wl5: declaring the two artifacts as carriers in biosphere/config/abiotic_nutrients.yaml. biosphere belongs to another owner in this batch and the change is two keys and two carrier_note rewrites.

NOT MEASURED: the Chadwick et al. (1999) comparison. build_sea_salt.py prints the land-mean Ca against the anchor, but a real reading needs a declared baseline_climatology. An exercise on the bootstrap climatology, with a Weibull fitted from only 32 snapshots, ran the whole chain and put the land mean below the band, which is the expected direction for a global land mean against a small wet tropical island. That is machinery working, not a result.

title: The shortwave cloud optics is Stephens, not the Slingo scheme the cloud water constant was fixed inside
description:
Found while reading CCM3 for world-8h6, and checked against the code rather than the documentation.

mkclouds builds dql from the CCM3 diagnostic profile: rho_l = clwref*exp(-z/hl) with hl = clwhsc*ln(1+PW). That part matches Kiehl et al. (1998) Eq. 3-4 and NCAR/TN-420+STR Eq. 4.a.11-12 exactly, and radmod's longwave cloud term matches CCM3 Eq. 12-13 exactly.

The SHORTWAVE consumer does not. CCM3 puts the layer cloud water path into Slingo (1989) delta-Eddington, in which extinction optical depth is LINEAR in the path and inverse in a droplet effective radius (technical note Eq. 4.b.3). radmod's swr says of itself that its cloud transmissivities are Stephens (1978) + Stephens et al. (1984), and computes ztau = 2.0*ALOG10(zlwp+1.5)**3.9. No effective radius exists anywhere in this model, and CCM3's liquid/ice phase split does not either.

The elasticity d ln ztau / d ln CWP of the Stephens fit is 1.28 at 0.4 g/m2, peaks near 1.8 around 2 g/m2, passes 1.0 near 45 g/m2 and falls to 0.84 at 94 and 0.73 at 200. Slingo's is exactly 1 everywhere. So the fit is SUPER-linear in thin cloud and sub-linear in thick, and the descriptions in opaque-constants.md finding 8 and world-8h6 that call the response sublinear hold only for the thick low-cloud layers.

Consequence: clwref carries no calibration across that boundary. Whatever cloud water path CCM3 fixed 0.21 g/m3 to deliver, the optical depth that path produces here is not the optical depth it produced in CCM3.

Neither Stephens (1978) nor Stephens et al. (1984) is in references/INDEX.md, so the fit itself is held and not read, and whether it is valid outside the water paths it was fitted over is untested. That is the second half of what opaque-constants.md finding 8 named and world-8h6 did not close.

Do: fetch Stephens (1978) and Stephens et al. (1984), establish the range the fit was made over, and say whether this model's cloud water paths sit inside it. Decide separately whether the absent effective radius is a gap to fill or a scheme boundary to declare.

Evidence: exoplasim/notes/cloud-water-reference.md, notes/audits/opaque-constants.md finding 8
close_reason:
FIXED, all four parts of the Do: line.

FETCHED AND READ. Stephens (1978) J. Atmos. Sci. 35, 2123-2132 and Stephens, Ackerman and Smith (1984) J. Atmos. Sci. 41, 687-690 are now in references/ with rows in references/INDEX.md; the line there saying they are not held and have never been read is gone. paperfetch could not reach either; both came from the AMS site, which serves them openly.

THE RANGE. Fig. 1's axes are 10 to 10,000 g m-2 over eight standard terrestrial cloud models; the tuned tables span tau_N 1 to 500, which inverts to about 7 to 14,000 g m-2; p. 2130 calls 10 to 1000 typical of observed stratiform cloud.

WHERE THIS MODEL SITS, and it is answerable with no climatology because the surface pressure cancels out of zlwp: zlwp(j) = 1000 clwref gascon T(j) (dsigma(j)/sigma(j)) exp(-z(j)/hl) / ga. On the ten-level quartic grid at a 50 hPa top the bottom three layers carry 43 to 105 g m-2 across column water 10 to 50 kg m-2, inside the range; layers above sigma 0.55 carry under 30 and the top three under 2.2 at every column water a moist column reaches. So the low cloud is inside the fit and the high cloud is one to three decades below it, in the regime the 1984 paper excludes by name at p. 690. radmod's own min(1000,...) cap lands on the top of the typical range at tau 145, inside the tuned table, so the ceiling is safe and the floor is not.

THE EFFECTIVE RADIUS IS A SCHEME BOUNDARY TO DECLARE, not a gap to fill, and the declaration is now in docs/src/reference/design-intent.md. Stephens Eq. (7) is tau = 1.5 W / r_e and p. 2125 says the dependence 'has been inherently parameterized in (10a) and (10b)'.
