The model does not lack an input its own scheme wants; it carries Earth's stratiform r_e(W) silently, near 5 um at 100 g m-2 and 11 um at 1000. Supplying r_e means replacing Stephens with Slingo, which is a scheme decision.

clwref DOES NOT MOVE, and that is falsifiable rather than preferred. It is a condensate density set by microphysics, and no single value can transfer CCM3's calibration anyway: the scale factor s that makes 2*log10(1.5+sW)**3.9 equal a linear 1.5W/r_e is a different number at every path, spreading 36 per cent over 20 to 300 g m-2 at r_e = 14 um, 63 per cent at 10 um and 86 per cent at 8 um.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND WHILE READING, filed rather than fixed because both need a rebuild and a run this batch was forbidden: world-jgen, radmod's single ztau is Stephens Eq. (10b) applied to both bands where the paper gives (10a) for band 1, one-signed and worth 0.6 to 3.4 W m-2 at the top of the atmosphere by a hand chain that leans high; and world-f9ig, tswr1, tswr2 and tswr3 are analytic fits of the shape the 1984 paper withdrew in as many words.

Finding: exoplasim/notes/cloud-water-reference.md, section 'The Stephens fit, read'.

title: clwref has no route from config into the model, so its arms cannot be run
description:

The arms cannot be run as things stand. clwref is a rainmod_nl key (rainmod.f90, declared in the module, in the namelist block, broadcast by mpbcr in rainini) but run_exoplasim.py writes no CLWREF and config/planet.yaml declares no key for it, so every run to date has taken the compiled 0.00021.

Do: add a model key to config/planet.yaml at the compiled value, have run_exoplasim.py write CLWREF@rainmod_namelist unconditionally the way it already writes TSWR3@radmod_namelist for PHYS-11, and cover it in expected_namelist_keys. The baseline value does not move; only the arms do.

Then run the three points -- 0.000105, 0.00021 as control, 0.00042 -- on one binary and one restart, and check them against the predictions and the three falsifying conditions in the note. The 1.0x arm must be bit-identical to the control.

Evidence: exoplasim/notes/cloud-water-reference.md
close_reason:
FIXED in 913e2ab1, for the route. config/planet.yaml declares model.cloud_water_reference_kg_m3 at rainmod.f90's compiled value, configure_otherargs writes CLWREF@rainmod_namelist unconditionally the way it writes TSWR3@radmod_namelist, continue_exoplasim reapplies it per segment because it imports that one function, and expected_namelist_keys covers it -- rainmod_namelist is a new file in that check's want dict.

The compiled default is READ out of rainmod.f90 (rainmod_default) rather than copied, so the note's requirement that the 1.0x arm be bit-identical to the control is a property of the route rather than a coincidence to re-verify. Confirmed end to end: the config's 0.00021 routes through configure_otherargs, exoplasim._edit_namelist and namelist_value back to exactly the value rainmod.f90 declares, and the two arm values 0.000105 and 0.00042 route unchanged. rainini reads rainmod_nl from unit 11 and echoes it, and clwref is in that namelist block. The baseline value does not move.

SHOULD IT EXIST: yes. world-8h6 fixed the bracket, its arms and its three falsifying conditions before any result, and clwref sets both the shortwave cloud optical depth and the longwave cloud emissivity, so the arms have a predicted magnitude far above the instrument.

NOT DONE HERE, and spun out as world-s8rv: running the three points. That needs a binary, a restart and three integrations, and this batch may not write under exoplasim/runs/. exoplasim/notes/cloud-water-reference.md's 'what is not settled' section now states that the route exists and that the arms are what remains.

title: Delete the resolution-privileged branches in plasim.f90 and radmod.f90: no rung is a special case
description:
Three sites still branch on the truncation and present T21/T31/T42 as privileged configurations. None of them changes what any run of this project integrates, and keeping them makes the source look as though a rung is special when the project's position is that it is not.

1. plasim.f90's `if(NTRU==42)` sets nhdiff=16, ndel=4 and the four tdiss* directly. It runs BEFORE `read(11,plasim_nl)` a dozen lines later, and run_exoplasim.declare_hyperdiffusion now writes NHDIFF, NDEL and all four TDISS* into that namelist unconditionally from both the prepare and continue paths, for every rung, refusing a rung the config does not list. So the branch executes and is then overwritten on every run. Deleting it is a no-op for this project.

2. radmod.f90's jtune block branches on NTRU==21/NTRU==1, NTRU==31 and NTRU==42 to set tswr1, tswr2, tswr3 and th2oc. It is UNREACHABLE at every rung -- world-ys9 has the full argument: every branch is gated on NDCYCLE, ndcycle's compiled default is 1, and read(11,radmod_nl) is 88 lines below the block, so ndcycle is always its compiled value when the test is made and jtune is always 0. Every run directory this project has produced prints 'No radiation setup for this resolution'. This issue does the DELETION; world-ys9 owns the finding.

3. rainmod.f90's `if(NTRU==21 .and. NLEV==5) nshallow=0` is a T21/L5 branch. NLEV 5 is not a configuration this project builds. Report it; do not edit rainmod.f90 -- a sibling batch owns that file right now.

The T42 hyperdiffusion VALUES are not lost by this and must not be: config/planet.yaml's hyperdiffusion block already carries them as order_alpha 4 and cutoff_fraction 0.381, explicitly recorded as inherited from T42, and applies them as a FRACTION of the truncation so confinement is the same at every rung rather than an absolute wavenumber worth 71 per cent of T21's spectrum and 8.8 per cent of T170's. Deleting the branch removes the privileged CASE, not the numbers.

Do: delete 1 and 2, with the run-log line that announced 2's failure. Say what a run that does NOT write the hyperdiffusion keys would now get, since that is the only behaviour change and it is outside this project's paths.
acceptance_criteria: No (else)if on NTRU remains in plasim.f90 or radmod.f90. smoke_test and check_consistency unchanged. The report states what changes for a caller that does not write the hyperdiffusion namelist keys.

title: Surface humus P:C ratchets down because SURFHUMUS is in the N ramp and not the P one
description:
The surface humus P:C ratchets downward without bound, because it is in the
nitrogen C:N ramp and not the phosphorus C:P one.

somdynam.cpp sets the C:N of SLOWSOM, SOILMICRO and SURFHUMUS from the mineral
N pool at the top of som_dynamics_century, and the C:P of SLOWSOM, PASSIVESOM
and SOILMICRO from the labile P pool. The two sets are not the same. But the
phosphorus immobilisation branch further down scales sompool[SURFHUMUS].ptoc by
ptoc_reduction alongside SLOWSOM and SOILMICRO, exactly as the nitrogen branch
does. SLOWSOM and SOILMICRO are re-derived by setptoc on the next call;
SURFHUMUS is not, because its setptoc line is commented out. So its P:C is
multiplied down every time the branch fires, from the 1/150 soil.cpp
initialises it to, and never restored: the surface humus pool asymptotically
receives carbon carrying no phosphorus at all.

Uncommenting the setptoc line is not the fix on its own. Parton, Stewart and
Cole (1988), the source of every other pair in those calls, has no humus pool,
so the commented line's 200 and 90 would import SLOWSOM's pair without a
source.

Beside it, and cheaper: the nitrogen branch short-circuits on || !ifnlim and the
phosphorus branch has no || !ifplim, so the phosphorus decay-rate reduction and
this ratchet can both fire with phosphorus limitation off. Reaching them needs
daily immobilisation above the pinned 2 gP/m2, which is not a realistic daily
flux, so it is an asymmetry to close rather than an active defect in the
current configuration. Close it in the same change and say which behaviour was
preserved.

Do: decide what sets the surface humus pool's C:P, then make the set of pools
setptoc covers and the set the immobilisation branch reduces the same set.
Nothing here is execution-verified; LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree.

Source: biosphere/notes/phosphorus-cycle-parameterisation.md,
vendor/lpj-guess/modules/somdynam.cpp (the setptoc block in
som_dynamics_century and the phosphorus immobilisation branch below it),
vendor/lpj-guess/modules/soil.cpp sompool[SURFHUMUS].ptoc
notes:
2026-08-25, branch fanout-W6, commit 638a9653. FOLLOW-THROUGH, and it supersedes one line of the close reason above. world-shcp gave SURFHUMUS the slow pool's phosphorus ramp -- setptoc(soil, pmin_mass, SURFHUMUS, 200.0, 90.0, 0.0, PMASS_SAT) is uncommented -- so the pool IS re-derived now, and SURFHUMUS is back in the P immobilisation branch's ptoc reduction list. The set setptoc covers and the set that branch flexes are one set again, which is what this row Do line asked for; the invariant is kept from the other side rather than by exclusion. That arm is still unreachable in both directions, so no behaviour changes by it.

The reason the setptoc line was kept commented -- that Parton, Stewart and Cole (1988) has no humus pool to take a (ctop_max, ctop_min) pair from -- is answered rather than overruled: the pair is Fig. 3 slow line, and the identification of surface humus with the slow pool is this fork own, stated by setntoc giving SURFHUMUS exactly SLOWSOM (30, 15) off SLOWSOM driver and by soil.cpp own commented alternative P initialisation setting SURFHUMUS and SLOWSOM to the same 1/90.
close_reason: FIXED in somfluxes, two changes. (1) SURFHUMUS removed from the ptoc reduction list in the phosphorus immobilisation branch: it has no phosphorus ramp to re-derive it, so flexing it down there was a one-way ratchet on the surface humus pool's P:C rather than the within-day iteration it is for SLOWSOM and SOILMICRO. The invariant kept is that a pool flexed there must be one setptoc re-derives; PASSIVESOM is the harmless other direction, re-derived and never flexed. The commented-out SURFHUMUS setptoc line stays commented, because Parton, Stewart and Cole (1988) has no humus pool to take a (ctop_max, ctop_min) pair from. (2) || !ifplim restored to the first condition, which its nitrogen twin has and the copy dropped; the whole P block is the N block with n substituted for p, down to every comment inside it still saying nitrogen. Behaviour preserved under ifplim 1 exactly: !ifplim was already false there, so that arm has never been reachable under phosphorus limitation and still is not. Under ifplim 0 it now means what ifnlim 0 already means. Both arms are unreachable now and both are kept, upstream's form intact. Correction to the finding: the ratchet was reachable only under ifplim 0, not ifplim 1 as parameters.cpp and the note said. What kept it rare there is the second job PMASS_SAT does: somfluxes ends by pinning soil.pmass_labile to PMASS_SAT whenever !ifplim, so pmin_mass is exactly 2 gP/m2 at the start of every call and the arm fires only on a day whose net P immobilisation exceeds that, which the whole daily SOM carbon throughput at the model's richest C:P is an order of magnitude short of. The ifplim 1 refusal's fourth reason is dropped; it still refuses on PFRAC_LEAFTOSAP, PCONC_SAT and PMASS_SAT. Syntax-checked with g++ -fsyntax-only against a synthetic vesper.h; nothing execution-verified, LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree.

title: Reconcile setptoc's labile-P threshold with the Hedley-labile pool the fork feeds it
description:
setptoc's labile-P saturation threshold and soil.pmass_labile are two different
operational pools, so the soil organic C:P ramp saturates everywhere.

PMASS_SAT = 0.002 kgP/m2 is now derived and is NOT the defect. It is Parton,
Stewart and Cole (1988) Fig. 3, p. 115, read directly: that figure plots the C:P
of the passive, slow and active soil organic matter against labile P over an
axis running 0 to 2.0 gP/m2, as straight lines from 200 to 20, 200 to 90 and 80
to 30, which are the three (ctop_max, ctop_min) pairs the fork passes to
setptoc and its fmax exactly. setptoc's linear form is that figure's lines and
it sets the P:C of the pool receiving carbon, which is the paper's own
construction. Do not change the constant.

The defect is the driver. Parton's labile P is isotopically exchangeable or
anion-exchange-resin extractable orthophosphate over 0 to 20 cm (p. 115).
soil.pmass_labile is the Hedley-labile pool of Wang et al. (2010) and Yang et
al. (2013), labile inorganic plus labile organic, which Dantas de Paula et al.
(2025) adopt deliberately to stand in for the biomineralisation pathway the
model does not carry. Their own global numbers separate them: 2.11 PgP
simulated labile P, 3.6 PgP Hedley-labile, 0.319 PgP Olsen over 0 to 20 cm,
which over 1.3e14 m2 of ice-free land are 16, 28 and 2.4 gP/m2. Parton's 2.0
gP/m2 sits on the last. The fork's own kplab, the Langmuir half-saturation for
labile P, is 10 to 78 gP/m2 by soil order, so the threshold is 5 to 39 times
below where the fork's own isotherm expects labile P to be halfway to
saturating.

Consequence: fac exceeds fmax nearly everywhere, and the slow, passive and soil
microbial pools sit at their minimum C:P always, which is their most
phosphorus-rich end. Size of the effect, by hand off the fork's own published
run: litter plus soil C 1474.1 PgC over litter plus soil P 51.9 PgP is a bulk
organic C:P of 28.4 by mass, and moving each pool from its minimum to its
mid-range multiplies its C:P by 5.5, 1.61 and 1.83, so the model's largest
phosphorus stock is up to five times too large. Yang et al. (2013) put organic
soil P at 8.6 +/- 6 PgP for 0 to 50 cm.

Do: decide between converting the threshold into this fork's labile-P currency
and driving setptoc with a resin-equivalent fraction of soil.pmass_labile. It
is a modelling decision, not arithmetic, and a second obstacle sits behind it:
LPJ-GUESS-CNP simulates SOM as a bulk pool with no explicit depth, which its
own authors state, so there is no depth on the receiving side to convert to.
Physics is not a knob here: a threshold that worsens the comparison against
Yang's organic P is still the right threshold if it is the right threshold.

Source: biosphere/notes/phosphorus-cycle-parameterisation.md,
references/parton1988.pdf Fig. 3 p. 115,
references/dantasdepaula2025-lpjguess-phosphorus-cycle.pdf Table 1 and Table A1,
references/yang2011-hedley-phosphorus-pedogenesis.pdf
notes:
2026-08-25, branch fanout-W6, commit fd11a26d. FIXED, by the user's decision: CONVERT THE THRESHOLD, one constant, at the LOW end of the bracket.

vendor/lpj-guess/modules/somdynam.cpp: PMASS_SAT = 0.002 * 6.6 = 0.0132 kgP/m2, replacing the vendored CNP fork's 0.002. One constant, not two: PMASS_SAT's second reader, the !ifplim pin on soil.pmass_labile at the 'If no phosphorus limitation or during free phosphorus years' block, is DEFINED as holding labile P at the value where the C:P ramp stops responding, so it follows the threshold by definition rather than as a side effect. Splitting them would invent a second number with no independent derivation.

WHY 6.6 AND NOT 11.3 OR THE MIDDLE. 6.6 = simulated labile P 2.11 PgP / Olsen-extractable 0.319 PgP; 11.3 = observational Hedley-labile 3.6 PgP / the same Olsen figure. setptoc consumes the model's own simulated pool, so 6.6 is the ratio between the two quantities actually wired together; 11.3 would additionally carry the model's 41 per cent under-prediction of its own observational target, counting that error twice.

VERIFIED AND RECORDED (the bonus). commonoutput.cpp writes the pinned pmass_labile into PO4_mass (line 1454, PO4_mass += patch.soil.pmass_labile * to_gridcell_average, out at out_soil_ppool) and into availp (line 1518, out at out_ppool). So the reported labile P moves from 2.0 to 13.2 gP/m2, the same order as the fork's own simulated 16 gP/m2 instead of an order below it. It is still a constant meaning 'not limiting' and still not a simulated stock.

BLAST RADIUS. Under ifplim 0, the configuration this project runs, the pin moves with the threshold, fac still arrives at fmax, and every soil organic C:P ratio is unchanged: INERT for carbon and phosphorus flows, live only in the reported stock. Under ifplim 1 it bites -- the three pools ramp instead of saturating, worth up to a factor of five on the model's largest phosphorus stock by the arithmetic already in the note.

DECLARED DIVERGENCE. PMASS_SAT = 0.002 is the vendored CNP fork's own value, upstream and default, so the change is recorded as a divergence with mainline's line verbatim beside it under a DECLARED DIVERGENCE FROM MAINLINE heading, on the ntransform.cpp pattern. Note the difference from ntransform.cpp: this diverges from the CNP FORK, not from release 4.1.1, which has no phosphorus. somdynam.cpp has no register file and no gate, so nothing mechanically stops a silent revert; filed as world-v46r.

THE ifplim REFUSAL. parameters.cpp's refusal of ifplim 1 dropped the PMASS_SAT clause. What still stands: PFRAC_LEAFTOSAP (BIO-34), a nitrogen ratio for sapwood plus bark whose proportional form the one phosphorus measurement rejects; and PCONC_SAT (WORLD-PIDX), which carries nitrogen's saturation value on a ramp its cited source does not contain, so the surface microbial pool's C:P never leaves its maximum. WORLD-16PB is recorded there as settled.

READ FROM SOURCE, not executed: every claim about the model. EXECUTED: only the arithmetic of the constant itself (0.002 * 6.6 = 0.0132; 13.2 gP/m2) in an isolated compile. LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree.
close_reason: Threshold converted into the fork's labile-P currency by 6.6 in vendor/lpj-guess/modules/somdynam.cpp, as one constant with the !ifplim pin following it by definition; declared as a divergence from the vendored CNP value 0.002; the PMASS_SAT clause is out of parameters.cpp's ifplim refusal. Commit fd11a26d.

title: PCONC_SAT has no phosphorus source: the litter-P ramp is not in the paper it cites
description:
PCONC_SAT is the litter-P saturation threshold, the fmax argument of setptoc()
for the surface microbial pool, and it carries NCONC_SAT's 0.02 exactly. The
paper this row was blocked on has been obtained and read, and it does not
settle this constant, because it does not contain the mechanism.

Parton, Stewart and Cole (1988) has no surface microbial pool and no C:P ramp
driven by a litter concentration. Its only C:P ramps are the three soil pools of
Fig. 3, driven by labile P. Litter phosphorus in that model is not ramped at
all: the structural pool is fixed at C:P 500 and the metabolic pool receives the
remainder of the plant residue P (p. 115). So the ramp PCONC_SAT belongs to is
the nitrogen side's structure carried across, the pair 80 and 30 the fork passes
with it is Fig. 3's ACTIVE SOIL line applied to a surface pool, and the value is
nitrogen's.

The bound stands and the paper does not move it. PCONC_SAT is compared against
litter_pmass / (litter_cmass * 2), a phosphorus fraction of litter dry mass,
whose whole attainable range is 3.1e-4 to 7.6e-4 for senesced-litter C:P of 1596
to 660 by mass (McGroddy et al. 2004 Table 1). 0.02 is 26 to 64 times above the
richest litter this model can produce, so fac never reaches fmax and the surface
microbial pool sits at its MAXIMUM C:P of 80 always. Any replacement that lets
the ramp span is at or below 7.6e-4; nothing anchors it from below, so this is a
bound and not a bracket.

Do: choose between the two things that would settle it, which is a modelling
decision and not a measurement.

  1. A measurement of surface-litter microbial biomass C:P against litter
     phosphorus concentration, which is what the nitrogen constant has in Parton
     et al. (1993) Fig. 4 and what phosphorus does not have anywhere held here.
  2. Deleting the constant, by driving the surface microbial pool's C:P from the
     same labile P the soil pools use, which is what Parton does for the active
     pool. The reason the nitrogen code does not is real -- surface litter is
     not in contact with the mineral soil's available nitrogen -- so this is a
     structural argument and not a simplification.

A same-relative-position transfer off the nitrogen pair would give 9.3e-4,
bracketed 7.1e-4 to 1.7e-3. It is recorded in the note and NOT adopted: it would
calibrate a phosphorus threshold against a nitrogen threshold's position, and
the problem is not that the position is unknown but that the ramp has no source
at all.

PMASS_SAT, which this row used to carry, is settled and split out. It is Parton,
Stewart and Cole (1988) Fig. 3's own saturation point, 2.0 gP/m2 = 0.002 kgP/m2,
and it is not changed; what is open there is the pool it reads, as WORLD-Z01O.

Source: biosphere/notes/phosphorus-cycle-parameterisation.md,
references/parton1988.pdf p. 115, BIO-34
notes: 2026-08-24, branch fanout-X, commit be1bcee0. THE PAPER WAS OBTAINED AND READ (references/parton1988.pdf). It settles PMASS_SAT and NOT PCONC_SAT, so this row is rescoped to PCONC_SAT alone and stays OPEN. PMASS_SAT is Parton, Stewart and Cole (1988) Fig. 3 p. 115 read line for line: that figure plots soil organic C:P against labile P over an axis running 0 to 2.0 gP/m2 for the passive, slow and active pools, as straight lines from 200 to 20, 200 to 90 and 80 to 30, which are the fork's three setptoc argument pairs and its 0.002 kgP/m2 fmax exactly; setptoc's linear interpolation is that figure's lines, fmin 0 is its origin, and setptoc sets the P:C of the pool RECEIVING carbon, which is the paper's own construction (p. 115). So the constant is derived, is NOT a copy of the 0.002 inside NMASS_SAT, and is unchanged. The defect moved to the driver and is now WORLD-Z01O: Parton's labile P is resin-extractable orthophosphate over 0 to 20 cm and soil.pmass_labile is the Hedley-labile pool, eight times larger in the fork's own published run. This row's remaining half has no source and cannot get one from this paper, because that model has no surface microbial pool and no litter-concentration C:P ramp. Nothing is compiled or executed.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text: 2026-08-30, branch worktree-agent-aa7af1d18be6ea483, commit ce14b1d46. DONE, and the answer is neither of the two options this row named. THE MEASUREMENT EXISTS AND IT REFUTES THE FORM. Option 1 asked for a measurement of surface-litter microbial biomass C:P against litter phosphorus concentration. Mooshammer et al. (2014) is fetched, held and read, and it is that: Table 2, recalculated from Xu et al. (2013) over n = 405, regresses microbial biomass C:P on soil C:P with slope 0.015, R = 0.078, R2 = 0.006, P = 0.118, and the log-log form gives R = 0.000, P = 0.992, the fitted microbial C:P moving 66.5 to 67.3 while its regressor moves 156 to 1611. Its text carries the litter case directly: in decomposing litter, resource C:N and C:P are strongly negatively correlated with the gross N and P MINERALISATION FLUXES while the decomposer communities are homeostatic in those element ratios (Mooshammer et al. 2012), and Achat et al. (2010) find the same in forest soils. What varies with a resource's phosphorus content is the flux out of the decomposer, not the stoichiometry of the decomposer. THE CONTROL THAT COULD HAVE FAILED AND DID NOT is the nitrogen row of the same table: microbial C:N on soil C:N, P = 0.044 and log-log P < 0.001. So option 2 is wrong too: the pool's C:P is driven by NOTHING, not by labile P. CHANGE: PCONC_SAT and both setptoc(SURFMICRO) calls are removed, with the litter phosphorus mass they read. The surface microbial pool holds the C:P soil.cpp initialises it to. WORTH AT MOST 2.4 PER CENT: the ramp ran over 1.6 to 3.8 per cent of its declared span and returned 79.2 to 78.1 against the 80 it was initialised at. NCONC_SAT, THE CONSTANT IT COPIED, IS NOW EXACTLY SOURCED: Parton et al. (1993) p. 791 says the surface microbial C:N 'increases from 10 to 20 as the N content decreases from 2.0% to 0.01%', which is the setntoc pair and its fmax as a litter dry-mass fraction. So PCONC_SAT was a sound derivation belonging to the other element -- the implicit-Earth shape with the element substituted for the planet. parameters.cpp's ifplim refusal now names PFRAC_LEAFTOSAP alone. somdynam.yaml gains mainline_form: removed, whose third check asks what holds the quantity now rather than which line replaced it, so a deletion cannot leave a modelled quantity set by nothing and pass; 24 of 24 fixtures. COMPILES (mpic++ -fsyntax-only clean; full link queued behind another agent's run). Not execution-verified and inert under ifplim 0. FILED world-634q: the fixed 80 the pool now holds is Fig. 3's active soil ctop_max applied to a pool that paper does not have, which is the standing its three neighbours share; the obvious substitution is refused there because measured microbial biomass C:P is 66.5 by MOLE, 25.8 by mass, and this model's ratios are mass ratios over conceptual pools. COULD NOT FETCH Mooshammer et al. (2012), Ecology 93, 770-782, 10.1890/11-0721.1, and Xu, Thornton, Post (2013), Glob. Ecol. Biogeogr. 22, 737-749, 10.1111/geb.12029; both reach this project through Mooshammer et al. (2014).

title: A re-run of a band-shape derivation leaves the staged 175/176 stale with nothing saying so
description:
build_surface_albedo.py reads band2/band1 from analysis/rock_albedo_bands.json and analysis/vegetation_albedo.json, and stamps their sha256 into albedo_report.json under band_shape_inputs. Nothing compares that stamp against the files as they now stand.

check_consistency.py's 'generated inputs vs their config' compares the artifact's CONFIG stamp against the current config, which is the right check for a config key and cannot see this: model.vegetation_albedo_bands is now inert for this generator (it is read by run_exoplasim as ALBFOREST and by nothing else here), and the rock shapes were never a config key at all. title: Apply the BIO-24 unit contract to the phosphorus inputs: texture-path pwtr and the sorption kinetics
description:
BIO-24's contract is written and the nitrogen side is applied; the phosphorus side is stated and NOT applied, because the phosphorus sources were being worked separately at the time.

Two divisors in modules/somdynam.cpp still divide an Earth-year rate by the simulation year, so each delivers an Earth year of phosphorus every orbit, close to twice the published rate per unit absolute time:

  soilpadd(): daily_pwtr = soil.soiltype.pwtr / date.year_length()
  file scope: USORB, USSORB and UOCC = published rate / date.year_length()

Both should divide by VESPER_EARTH_YEAR_DAYS instead. UOCC is declared and never used, so occlusion is absent from this model rather than slow, and the divisor there is cosmetic until something reads it.

Do: change both divisors, and state in BIO-5 that the pwtr field it emits is kgP/m2 per EARTH year. Register the change in the state column of the phosphorus rows of biosphere/notes/time-base-unit-contract.md, which already carries the contract, the reader and the arithmetic.

The gridded pwtr path is already a daily calculation driven by runoff and needs no change; it is also inactive, since it requires file_pwtr and this world supplies none.

Source: biosphere/notes/time-base-unit-contract.md
notes: APPLIED 2026-08-24 on branch fanout-T. Both divisors now VESPER_EARTH_YEAR_DAYS: soilpadd's texture-path daily_pwtr and the file-scope USORB/USSORB. Which decay path each is on was established first, and every P quantity in somdynam.cpp is reached only through som_dynamics_century, the live ifcentury 1 path; som_dynamics_lpj carries no P at all, so this does not overlap the TAU_* correction. UOCC was deleted rather than converted: it was dead, so its divisor was cosmetic and converting it would have made an absent process look like a slow one. USORB's equilibrium does not move, since USORB equals USSORB; only the approach time changes, from about 150 orbits to about 150 Earth years. The gridded pwtr route needed no change. The contract note's two P rows and its 'what is not settled' section are updated. Nothing is compiled or executed.
close_reason: Both phosphorus divisors converted to VESPER_EARTH_YEAR_DAYS under the BIO-24 contract, the contract's P rows updated, UOCC deleted rather than converted. Commit 1d83626b.

title: Raise NAERSP: primary carbonaceous and biogenic SOA are two radiative species, not one spare slot
description: radmod.f90 sets NAERSP = 4 and its own comment allocates the four to mineral dust, sea salt, volcanic sulfate and one spare held for the carbonaceous aerosol CLIM-29 is waiting on. That leaves biogenic SOA with nowhere to go: the SOA audit's finding 8 is that modelled SOA is mostly scattering with a weakly absorbing brown-carbon end while primary fire carbonaceous carries black carbon and absorbs, and section 2 of the multi-species note establishes that one scalar optical set cannot describe two species with different single-scattering albedos. Sharing the slot would re-create the defect the species array was built to remove. The interactive path tightens it: naerosp is ndustrad + iaerint, so the transported tracer spends one of the four. Raising the parameter costs memory in aodsp and nothing else, because every species loop is bounded by naerosp rather than unrolled. Not urgent: neither smoke nor SOA has a burden yet. What must not happen is the two arriving into one slot because four was the number when the array was written. Source: aeolian/notes/multi-species-aerosol.md section 10, biosphere/notes/bvoc-soa-atmospheric-coupling-audit.md finding 8.
notes:
One-line parameter change in vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/radmod.f90 plus the aerofile column count, which readdat takes from naerosp. Rebuild every binary after it, per CLAUDE.md rule 4.

MEASURED 2026-08-25, and the answer is that the slot is warranted. The measurement, the bars and the corrected cost are in aeolian/notes/multi-species-aerosol.md section 10.1. NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE: radmod.f90 belongs to the radiation, and this batch owned only aeolian/ and dust_forcing.py. Handed over.

THE BARS, fixed before the optical properties were fetched. The instrument is radmod's per-species optical set. Its demonstrated resolving power is the pair the species array was built for, mineral dust and sea salt. Bar 1: separate slots are needed if the two carbonaceous species' band-1 single-scattering albedos are at least as far apart as dust and sea salt at the DECLARED measured indices, which is 0.0336, the smallest separation the array already exists to resolve. Bar 2: and, independently, if their implied critical surface albedos fall on opposite sides of a surface albedo this world carries, so a blend gets the SIGN wrong somewhere rather than only the size.

BOTH FIRE, AND NOT NARROWLY. Bond and Bergstrom (2006) section 9.1 recommend 0.20 to 0.30 with a central 0.25 for FRESH light-absorbing carbon, from six measurements in their Table 7 p. 51. Dubovik et al. (2002) Table 1 retrieve 0.88 at 440 nm for African savanna smoke and 0.94 for boreal smoke, the aged end. Shrivastava et al. (2017), through finding 8 of the SOA audit, puts modelled SOA at nearly white. The most generous possible pairing -- the most SCATTERING smoke ever measured against an SOA that is only nearly white -- still leaves about 0.06, which is 1.8x bar 1; the fresh end leaves 0.75, twenty times it. For one slot to suffice, SOA would have to be about as absorbing as boreal smoke, at which point the audit's own correction was wrong.

Bar 2 is not close at all. Through exoplasim/scripts/dust_optics.py:critical_surface_albedo, fresh carbonaceous sits just BELOW the albedo of open water, so it warms over every surface this world has including the ocean; a conservative scatterer sits at essentially 1, so it cools over everything including snow. They are on opposite sides of the entire surface table. Even the aged, most-scattering smoke end still straddles the bright closed-basin fill and the sea ice, which are the surfaces this world is unusual for.

THE CHANGE, exactly: parameter(NAERSP = 4) becomes 5, at the NAERSP declaration in radmod.f90, plus the source comment above it which enumerates the four and names the spare.

WHAT IT COSTS, and this row's own description was WRONG about it. 'Raising the parameter costs memory in aodsp and nothing else' understates it. aodsp(NHOR,NLEV,NAERSP) is not the only NAERSP-dimensioned array that scales with the grid: ddustod(NHOR,NLEV,NAERSP) and ddustcol(NHOR,NAERSP) do too, and all three are on radmod's threadprivate list, so the cost is one copy PER THREAD and CLAUDE.md's 32 MB working-set rule counts the whole team. Per extra species that is NHOR*(2*NLEV+1) reals per thread at 8 bytes under -fdefault-real-8. On sixteen threads at ten layers: 0.33 MB for the team at T21, 1.31 at T42, 5.25 at T85, 21.00 at T170. Free at the rung this world runs at, NOT free at the top of the ladder, where the four species already there cost four times as much again. Whoever makes the change should say which rungs they priced it at.

WHAT IT DOES NOT TOUCH, checked in the source. readdat(aerofile,naerosp,8,aeroqs) takes the column count from naerosp and not from NAERSP, and its dummy kdata(nitems,ndim) shares the leading dimension 8 with aeroqs(8,NAERSP), so the aerofile format is unchanged and an existing file stays valid. radini already refuses naerosp > NAERSP with a message naming the parameter. Every species loop is bounded by naerosp. dustsc, dusthsc and dustqlw are declared and broadcast with an explicit NAERSP extent so they follow the parameter; confirm the driver writing those namelist keys does not hardcode four entries.

Bond and Bergstrom (2006) and Dubovik et al. (2002) are now held and recorded as read in references/INDEX.md.
close_reason:
NAERSP is 5. Biogenic SOA and primary fire carbonaceous no longer have to share the slot, so the two cannot arrive into one and re-create the defect the species array was built to remove.

PRICED ACROSS THE LADDER, which the row asked for. Because NHOR is NLON*NLAT/NPRO, the TEAM total is thread-count independent at NLON*NLAT*(2*NLEV+1) reals per species: 0.33 MB at T21, 1.31 at T42, 5.25 at T85 and 21.00 at T170. Free at the rung this world runs at, and not free at the top of the ladder -- which is the honest form of the row's "costs memory in aodsp and nothing else".

CONFIRMED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, per the row's own instruction: the driver writes ONE namelist value into each of DUSTSC, DUSTHSC and DUSTQLW rather than four, so raising the parameter does not reach it. The aerofile format is unchanged, readdat taking its column count from naerosp and not from NAERSP, and radini still refuses naerosp > NAERSP by name.

title: Give the volatile organic outputs back their compound and patch identity
description: Add output tables to the vendored CNP fork that carry the emission module's nine monoterpene compounds and the patch axis, monthly, rather than the endocyclic/other pair and the PFT/stand means commonoutput.cpp declares today. The module computes all nine internally and the output layer collapses them; alpha- and beta-pinene have different highly oxidized molecule yields and isoprene can suppress monoterpene nucleation, so a lumped terpene mass cannot reconstruct the branch a chemistry operator takes. Patch resolution matters for the same reason disturbance history does in the isoprene study this project read. This is the first precondition biosphere/scripts/bvoc_gate.py refuses on: BVOC-UNDECLARED-SOURCE-COMPOUND-RESOLVED-OUTPUT and BVOC-UNDECLARED-SOURCE-PATCH-RESOLVED-OUTPUT. bvoc_gate.ACTIVATED_OUTPUTS names the files an activated run retains and run_lpj_guess.py retains them only in the granted case, so the harness side is done. Source: biosphere/notes/bvoc-activation-contract.md section 2, biosphere/notes/bvoc-soa-atmospheric-coupling-audit.md finding 1.
notes: Vendored fork work: vendor/lpj-guess/modules/commonoutput.cpp and the .ins output declarations. Requires no simulation. The gate's evidence block reports compounds_with_an_output_table against nine on every invocation, so progress is visible without a run.

title: Four benchmark and profiling scripts still launch with mpiexec, and there is no MPI build
description:
Found by sweeping for mpiexec while fixing world-7b2. reproducibility_matrix.py and sweep_compiler_flags.py were the two this batch owned and are fixed; these four are the rest, and each launches something that is either a threaded binary or a probe with no MPI build behind it.

• exoplasim/scripts/bench_ab.py:57 -- launcher('mpi') returns ['mpiexec','-np',ranks,'./probe_ab.x']. The other arms are omp and are complete; this one is a launcher for a probe build that world-38b removed. It is a named arm rather than a default, so it fails loudly when asked for, which is why this is P2 and not P1.
• exoplasim/scripts/bench_rank_layout.py:223 and :261 -- the whole script is rank-to-core placement under mpiexec. Under OpenMP that is OMP_PLACES / OMP_PROC_BIND, which is a different instrument, not a renamed one. Related to world-9eq, which asks the same question of the NOTE this script produced; the two should be settled together.
• exoplasim/scripts/perf_rank.sh and exoplasim/scripts/profile_transforms.sh:51,75 -- profile_transforms mpiexec's perf_rank.sh, which exists to give each rank its own perf.data filename. One process with N threads is one perf.data, so the filename problem the script solves does not exist under this runtime. The host-specific 'perf ring buffer does not fit inside an mpiexec'd rank' finding at perf_rank.sh:18-23 is worth keeping wherever this lands.

The hazard is the same in each: after a rebuild, most_plasim_*_p16.x is the THREADED binary, so mpiexec -np 16 starts 16 copies of a 16-thread executable in one directory over one set of restart files.

Not done under world-7b2 because these four were outside that batch's file ownership. NOT the same as world-d5l, which is about --parmode reaching build_model.py from the verification shell gates.
close_reason: Six scripts, not four: verify_filter_fold.sh (a bit-identity gate, which could not run at all) and stability_probe.py were found by sweeping the tree for the same call and are fixed too. bench_ab.py's mpi launcher was the DEFAULT rather than a named arm, so the issue's P2 framing understated it. Fixed in 41ad6cbb. bench_ab.py, profile_transforms.sh, verify_filter_fold.sh and stability_probe.py keep their reason to exist and are repointed at the one-process launch line exoplasim/__init__.py uses. perf_rank.sh and bench_rank_layout.py are deleted: their instrument, not just their launcher, is gone. What that costs is the concurrent-job latency-versus-throughput axis, filed as world-2shk; the notes those arms produced are world-9eq's, and neither cites the deleted script by name. No benchmark was run -- the host is contended.

title: Whether any unguarded write(nud,...) races into plasim_diag now that a Fortran unit is shared across threads
description:
plasim.f90:opendiag opens nud (unit 6) to plasim_diag under 'if (mypid == NROOT)'. mypid is a thread id since world-38b. A Fortran unit belongs to the PROCESS, not the thread, so that one open makes unit 6 the diagnostics file for EVERY thread.

Under MPI a non-root rank's write(nud,...) went to that rank's own stdout and out of the record, so an unguarded site was invisible. Under threads it lands in plasim_diag beside the root's, in whatever order the threads reach it. There are roughly 800 write(nud,...) sites across 24 files in vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src; the PlaSim convention guards them with mypid == NROOT, but that convention was load-bearing for correctness only from world-38b onward and has not been checked since.

Two consequences if an unguarded site exists: plasim_diag becomes non-deterministic run to run, and interleaved Fortran list-directed writes to one unit from several threads are not merely reordered but can be torn.

Do: grep every write(nud,...) and write(*,...) in plasim/src for one not dominated by a mypid == NROOT guard, and either guard it or send it to a per-thread unit. This is a whole-tree grep and needs no build.

Found while re-deriving reproducibility_matrix.py over thread counts under world-7b2; that script now declares a plasim_diag-only disagreement as this candidate first. Filed rather than fixed because plasim/src was outside that batch's file ownership.
close_reason: Thirteen sites were genuinely reachable by a thread other than 0; all thirteen fixed in 20748115. Method, the full enumeration and the rule a new site follows are in notes/audits/shared-diagnostics-unit-under-threads.md. Three classes with three different correct fixes: global facts get mypid == NROOT, per-thread cell reports get a critical section and the thread id in the record (a root guard would silence every thread but 0), and leaf modules with no mypid to test get a critical section. mpabort was failing for a reason other than ordering: open/write/close of unit 44 from any aborting thread.

title: verify_omp_collectives.f90 calls ilatperm, which no longer exists, so that gate cannot compile
description:
Found while working world-h8o.

exoplasim/scripts/verify_omp_collectives.f90:88-95 checks that a thread receives the latitudes ilatperm says it does:

    do jl = 1 , NLPP
       iwant = ilatperm(mypid*NLPP + jl)

ilatperm was deleted from the whole tree by 2508bedb with the paired latitude decomposition. This file is compiled against the model sources by verify_omp_collectives.sh, so the reference is unresolved and the gate cannot build. Unlike verify_latitude_pairing.py it does not fail with a message naming the cause; it fails in the compiler.

The gate itself should stay: it is the only reader of mpsumr and it checks each of mpimod_omp.f90's 39 collectives against an answer written down in advance. It is declared in config/pipeline.yaml:700 and exoplasim/README.md:346.

Do: the scatter is contiguous again, so the property this block should assert is the CONTIGUOUS placement it now has -- thread r receives latitudes r*NLPP+1 .. (r+1)*NLPP -- which is a right answer of the same kind and is what mpscgp is documented to do. Replace the ilatperm call with that, or delete the block if the mpscgp/mpgagp round trip immediately above it already covers placement. Verify by building the gate, which this session was not permitted to do.
close_reason:
REPAIRED, commit b0e96d51. Verified by building and running the gate, which the filing session was not permitted to do.

The gate stays: it is the only reader of mpsumr and the only check of mpimod_omp's 39 collectives against answers written down in advance, and only the placement block was broken.

The block is NOT redundant with the mpscgp/mpgagp round trip above it, which was the alternative the issue offered. A scatter and a gather sharing one permutation are still mutually inverse, so they compose to the identity while every thread holds latitudes other than the ones it is assumed to hold. Measured rather than argued: on a throwaway copy outside the tree with both mpscgp and mpgagp sliding every thread's block by one latitude with wrap, the round trip passed and the placement check rejected it on all 8 threads.

ilatperm replaced by the contiguous placement mpimod_omp.f90:196 now implements, jg = mypid*NLPP + jlat -- the same kind of right answer as the mpscsp check below it. Built and run at NLAT 32 on 8 threads: PASS.

No model source changed. pipeline.yaml:702 and exoplasim/README.md:348 still describe the gate correctly and needed no edit.

title: verify_symmetric_transform.py cannot build its negative controls: the symmetric paths are gone from legmod
description:
Found while working world-h8o, which asked for this file to be checked in the same pass.

Running it as the tree stands raises SystemExit("could not build the sp2fc control: the lines it perturbs have moved"), so the gate has not run since 2508bedb.

WHY. The issue expected the mirror path to survive with only the LPAIRLAT selector gone. It did not. 2508bedb deleted the symmetric/mirror computation from all three routines: legmod.f90's sp2fc (:392), sp2fcdmu (:442) and dv2uv (:492) are now plain full-latitude multiplies over pmat/qmat, with no mirror index and no parity accumulators. The lines the controls perturb --

    fc(1,m,k) = ze1 - zo1 / fc(2,m,k) = ze2 - zo2
    pv(1,m,k,v) =  (zuz2e - zuz2o) + (zvd1e - zvd1o)

-- do not exist in the source any more, and the script refuses rather than running a control-free comparison, which is the right refusal.

The PARAMOD injection of 'logical, parameter :: LPAIRLAT = .true.' at :65 and :123 is now inert: nothing in the lifted routine bodies reads it, because LPAIRLAT is gone from the whole tree.

WHAT IS LEFT WORTH TESTING, and it is not nothing. The positive half is still a test with a right answer independent of any layout: the routines are run against an associated Legendre table computed by scipy at Gauss-Legendre nodes, so every latitude's answer is known in advance. That matters more than it did, not less, because the fork's own change to these routines is live -- the per-mode factor is hoisted into the FIELD (zsp = fsp*sp) instead of into the weight, and dv2uv scales pz and pd by fmu and fmv before the loop. A wrong factor there is exactly what the scipy table catches.

Do: decide whether this gate exists. If it does, it is no longer 'the symmetric transform' gate and should be renamed and re-scoped to what it now covers -- the transform against an independent Legendre table, including the per-mode factor hoist -- with negative controls anchored to lines that exist (perturbing the hoisted factor, or swapping pmat for qmat, are the mistakes the hoist invites). Repairing it by deleting the control assertions is NOT a fix: a gate that cannot fail is worse than one that does not run. Its config/pipeline.yaml row and exoplasim/README.md row have to match whatever is decided.
close_reason:
RE-SCOPED AND RENAMED to exoplasim/scripts/verify_inverse_transform.py, commit 50a9b80c. It exists, and the finding was right about why.

Verified the finding first: running it raised SystemExit on the sp2fc control, and grep confirms 2508bedb deleted the symmetric computation from all three routines rather than only the LPAIRLAT selector. Broken since 2026-08-22, and its pipeline.yaml row is in the one_offs list, which by that list's own comment produces no artifact any step consumes -- so nothing depended on its result.

WHAT IT CHECKS THAT NOTHING ELSE DOES. verify_banded_transform.sh covers the ANALYSIS direction and the tables: legini's pmat and qmat against scipy, the scatter's band placement, the weights, and fc2sp with its reduction. It does not touch the SYNTHESIS loops, and its own note says dv2uv is not driven there. It also does not touch fsp, fmu or fmv, which are the fork's per-mode factor hoist and are not tables. verify_shtns_model.sh compares NSHTNS=0 against NSHTNS=1 end to end, which cannot localise and cannot see sp2fc at all where it is called identically in both arms -- glaciermod.f90:229,305 and surfmod.f90:496 call legmod's sp2fc for orography under both settings.

RE-SCOPED, not repaired into something that always passes. The per-mode factor is no longer unity, so a factor carried to the wrong mode cannot cancel; dv2uv runs at NLEV 2 with different fields per level; planetary vorticity is driven and referenced by the identity the code's own comment claims. Seven negative controls replace three, each anchored to a line that exists and each required to apply exactly once or the gate exits.

Run at NTRU 10 / NLAT 16 and NTRU 21 / NLAT 32. Both arms pass, worst residual 7.105e-15 against a 1e-12 scaled bound; all seven controls rejected between 1.52e+00 and 1.36e+03. Twelve to fifteen orders separate the passing arm from the failing ones.

pipeline.yaml row and exoplasim/README.md row updated in the same commit. No smoke_test exemption existed. Three stale pointers to the old name fixed in commit e919c068; the two in files this batch was told not to touch are filed as world-5td1.

title: A second MODEL arm for verify_threaded_numerics.sh: --ranks 1 is still a build_model.py configuration
description:
world-d5l replaced verify_threaded_numerics.sh's missing reference with an independent driver, which answers the question for the TRANSFORM. The gate's other half -- does the band decomposition change the answer after a timestep of physics -- now has only the wrongband control and no second arm, so its growth curve is not run there.

The finding: build_model.py still accepts --ranks 1. It refuses only ranks below one and rank counts that do not divide NLAT, so most_plasim_<res>_l10_p1.x is a buildable, differently named binary with NPRO=1, NLPP=NLAT, one band covering the globe, and mpimod_omp's reductions reduced to a single slot. That is a genuinely different execution path through the same source, and it is not the trap world-d5l's refusal was written against: the trap was that dropping --parmode made the mpi arm build the threaded binary under the threaded binary's own name, and p1 is a different name.

It is NOT an independent implementation and must not be described as one: a defect present in code both configurations run is invisible to it, which is exactly why the independent driver was built instead. What it would restore is the growth curve at last-bit scale on the band question specifically, with its birth bound, its jump bound and the reassociation floor refusal, all of which are still carried by verify_shtns_model.sh and could be lifted back.

THE QUESTION IS FOR THE USER, not for a session to take: is a second arm that shares the source worth having beside the independent driver, or does the driver plus verify_shtns_model.sh's curve cover enough? Do not add it inside another issue.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded: either verify_threaded_numerics.sh gains a --ranks 1 arm with the growth curve, or the reason it stays with one model arm is written down.
close_reason: 2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER: the latter. The independent driver plus verify_shtns_model.sh's growth curve cover enough, and verify_threaded_numerics.sh keeps one model arm. The reason is written into that script's header, which is what this row's acceptance criterion asked for -- two builds of one source can agree and both be wrong, so a second arm sharing the source adds a build configuration to maintain and no coverage, while the curve a p1 arm would restore is already run on the NSHTNS pair. The header also records that --ranks 1 remains buildable and is not the trap world-d5l's refusal was written against, so the next reader finds the option and the reason it was declined together rather than rediscovering the first.

title: dv2uv's planetary vorticity term is checked by nothing since the MPI arm went
description:
The MPI arm caught a race in dv2uv's planetary vorticity handling, and world-38b removed that arm. world-d5l's driver does not replace it: dv2uv is a synthesis routine with no partial sum and no reduction, its only band dependence is the pmat and qmat rows for the thread's own latitudes, and verify_banded_transform.f90's table arm checks those rows directly. verify_symmetric_transform.py checks dv2uv's loop and its mirror combination against a scipy table. Neither drives the plavor block at legmod.f90's dv2uv, which applies planetary vorticity per latitude to mode w=2 rather than by adding it to pz in place.

The obstacle to adding it is the vector convention, not the arithmetic: writing an independent reference for U and V from spectral divergence and vorticity needs the sign and factor relation between the model's Fourier packing and the vector spherical harmonics pinned, and getting it wrong gives a driver that looks independent and is not. probe_shtns_vector_conventions.f90 was written to discover exactly that relation and zeroes plavor first for the same reason.

Do: pin the vector convention by running probe_shtns_vector_conventions.f90, then add a dv2uv arm to verify_banded_transform.f90 whose reference is dv2uv of (pd, pz + plavor at mode w=2) with plavor zero, compared against the model's dv2uv of (pd, pz) with plavor set. The plavor definition is then the physical one -- an addition to the (0,1) vorticity mode -- rather than the model's own formula, so the comparison is not circular. Cite exoplasim/notes/banded-transform-reference.md, section 'What a pass does not cover'.
acceptance_criteria: Either dv2uv's planetary vorticity term is driven against an independent reference under the bands, or the reason it cannot be is recorded with the convention that blocks it.
notes:
PARTLY CLOSED, at one thread, under world-2div. The premise of the two sentences above has changed and the remaining gap is narrower than the description states.

verify_symmetric_transform.py did NOT check dv2uv's loop: it had not run since 2508bedb, which deleted the mirror combination the sentence names. It is now verify_inverse_transform.py, and it DOES drive the plavor block. The reference is the identity this issue's own 'Do' line proposes: dv2uv(pd, pz) with plavor set equals dv2uv(pd, pz - plavor at mode w=2) with plavor zero. The identity is exact, so the arm is analytic rather than a self-comparison -- the reference subtracts plavor from the first Fourier component of mode w=2 and takes the ordinary matrix-vector product with pmat*fmu and qmat*fmv in numpy. That pins the mode, the component, the two outputs it touches, the two signs and the two factors.

THE VECTOR CONVENTION IS NOT AN OBSTACLE TO THAT ARM and does not need pinning for it. The reference never converts between the model's Fourier packing and vector spherical harmonics; it defines plavor by where it enters the vorticity coefficient, which is exactly the non-circular definition this issue asks for. probe_shtns_vector_conventions.f90 is needed for a driver that computes U and V independently, which is a different and larger thing.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, and it is the whole of what is left: the term is driven at NLPP == NLAT, one thread, on lifted loops. It is not driven UNDER THE BANDS. The plavor block indexes qmat(2,l) and pmat(2,l) by the thread's own latitude, so a thread holding the wrong rows applies the right correction at the wrong latitudes and the one-thread arm cannot see it. Adding the same identity as an arm of verify_banded_transform.f90 is still the work, and it is now a transplant of a reference that exists and is proven rather than a derivation.

A negative control exists and is exercised: verify_inverse_transform.py's dv2uv/plavorsign flips the sign of the removal in pu and is rejected on 2112 values at NTRU 10.
close_reason: Done in 796fcea4 as ARM D of verify_banded_transform. The remaining gap the notes named -- the term driven at NLPP == NLAT and not under the bands -- is closed by a transplant of the identity, not a derivation: banded_transform_reference.py now writes the winds dv2uv has to produce from RELATIVE vorticity with no planetary term, and the driver hands the model that vorticity plus P at mode w=2, so the mode, component, sign and factor are pinned by where P goes in. Reference format version 1 -> 2. Bound 4*NTP1*(eps*Tsum + Ptol*(1+Qmax)*Fmax), declared before the arm ran. The control, plavorband, shifts the correction by the thread's own index inside its band and is a NO-OP at one thread by construction: 1.582e-15 and passing at one thread, 0.455 and failing at four, which is the demonstration that no one-thread driver can see the class. The gate now refuses fewer than two threads; samelats already had that property and would have passed there for the wrong reason. Green at T21 on two and four threads and T85 and T170 on eight, all three cases, all four controls rejected. The vector convention turned out not to be the obstacle, exactly as the issue notes said. One thing stated rather than left to be found: fmu(2) is zero because mode w=2 is m=0, so the model's pv planetary line adds nothing for any P and no control on it can have teeth.

title: Run verify_threaded_numerics.sh once end to end on a settled bed
description:
world-d5l rewired verify_threaded_numerics.sh: it now runs verify_banded_transform.sh as its independent side and keeps the shared-band control against the model itself, comparing the control against the threaded arm rather than the removed reference arm. The driver half is proven across T21 to T170 with three controls. The gate as a whole has not been executed: it builds the model and needs a settled bed, and neither was available to the session that wrote it.

Do: run `exoplasim/scripts/verify_threaded_numerics.sh <bed> <res> <n>` once on a settled bed. Confirm the independent side passes, the threaded arm produces a restart at one step, and the wrongband arm is rejected either on the numbers or by refusing to run. Then close world-d5l.
acceptance_criteria: The gate has been run end to end on a bed and its verdict recorded.
close_reason:
Run end to end at T21 on sixteen threads, on a cold T21 bed with SEED fixed. All three of the issue's confirmations hold, but only after a defect the run exposed.

THE DEFECT. The gate's model half had never executed. build_arm asked build_model.py to publish under the registry's naming, and the wrongband control writes a '! CONTROL:' marker into plasimmod.f90, which build_model.py refuses to put under the registry's tag (world-70k). That arm exited 'build failed or stale' every time. The threaded arm, when it did build, published -- overwriting the shipped binary with an arm, which is world-v3d's failure mode. Both arms now build with --no-publish --print-path, as verify_shtns_model.sh already did. No bound, tolerance or control changed.

THE VERDICT, after that.
  independent side, dense / corner / zonal: ARM A1, A2, B, C all pass; noweight, slideband and samelats all rejected
  threaded arm at one step: a restart, from 9497fd35d121903e
  shared-band control: built as 96cb4e2f53030c15, rejected by refusing to run

The control being rejected by a crash rather than on the numbers is the outcome the script's header declares in advance, and its three exclusions hold: the patch applied, the build succeeded, and the same binary configuration ran to completion unpatched.

One rung. The bed is T21, so the gate has not been run where the band tiling divides differently.

Recorded in exoplasim/notes/banded-transform-reference.md.

title: T42 at dt 45 blows up in the 47th orbit from a state with no trend
description:
run_900548ae632e, T42, kappa 8, MPSTEP 45.0, -O2, cold start, 85 orbits asked for. It integrated 46 orbits of ordinary climate and took a SIGFPE inside the 47th, at vsqrtsd on 273./dt(jhor,2) in swr. Read out of the register at the trap, dt is -12.81 K: a gridpoint at a negative absolute temperature, at the second level from the top. dt is dt(NHOR,NLEP) in plasimmod and is temperature rather than a tendency, and the instruction is reached down the scalar losun branch past a cmpb/je that skips night lanes, so it is a daylight cell rather than a masked-lane artifact.

Nothing was building towards it. Level 2's coldest cell holds about 190 K with no trend across the whole run, and none of the four restarts before the failure carries a non-positive temperature anywhere. One cell went from roughly 190 K to below zero inside one orbit.

The linear stability boundary does not explain it. exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md fits the stable step as roughly 1/N and measures T127 at dt 30, which puts T42 near 90 minutes -- twice the step that failed here. So this is not the CFL boundary those probes found.

The practical consequence is already taken: the ladder runs T42 at dt 22.5. What is open is the mechanism. Candidates worth separating are a genuine nonlinear instability, which is not obliged to be monotone in the step; a single physics parameterisation producing an unbounded tendency at one cell, which the level-2 location and the suddenness both fit; and something specific to the second level from the top, where the note's earlier T127 blow-up also lived.

The reproducer is cheap and exists: MOST_REST.00046 of run_900548ae632e_crashed reaches the trap in one orbit, about 90 seconds.
acceptance_criteria: The mechanism named and demonstrated on the reproducer -- which term drives one cell's temperature below zero in a single orbit -- and either a fix or a stated stable-step rule for T42 that a 46-orbit run does not falsify.
notes:
Found while re-running the resolution ladder's arm A after world-1nz. Distinct from world-bhs, which was optimisation-dependent: the world-bhs probe orbit completes at -O0, -O1, -O2 and -mno-avx512f and produces 69 non-finite restart records only at -O3. This one traps at -O2 on a genuinely negative temperature.

2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S DECISION: DEFERRED until it recurs. Not abandoned, and the
distinction is the reproducer.

WHY DEFERRING IS THE RIGHT CALL HERE RATHER THAN A RETREAT. The practical
consequence is already taken -- the ladder runs T42 at dt 22.5 and not 45 -- so
what is open is the MECHANISM and nothing downstream waits on it. And the cheap
reproducer this row rests on is gone: the row says MOST_REST.00046 of
run_900548ae632e_crashed reaches the trap in about ninety seconds, and that run
is not in exoplasim/runs/, not a stub under archive/runs/, and not in any
INDEX_AT_DELETION.json. Verified this session rather than assumed.

So the choice was between buying a fresh blow-up to diagnose a timestep the
ladder does not use, or waiting. The next occurrence arrives WITH its own
reproducer, which is the evidence this row actually needs, and a blow-up bought
on purpose at a step nothing runs would cost orbits to produce a state the
project has no other use for.

WHAT TO DO IF IT RECURS, so the next reader does not start from scratch:
preserve the crashed run directory and its restarts FIRST, before anything else,
because that is what was lost last time -- and the loss is world-ww6z's failure
mode, a run leaving the tree without its identity. Then the row's own three
candidates are still the right ones to separate: a genuine nonlinear instability,
which is not obliged to be monotone in the step; a single physics
parameterisation producing an unbounded tendency at one cell, which the level-2
location and the suddenness both fit; and something specific to the second level
from the top, where the note's earlier T127 blow-up also lived.

NOTE THAT THE MODEL HAS MOVED SINCE THE OBSERVATION. Batch 2 changed rainmod,
fluxmod, radmod, seamod, landmod, plasim and outmod, so a recurrence is not
guaranteed to be the same defect and must not be assumed to be.

2026-08-26, ADDENDUM: the deferral is not a cap on anything, and the stability
ladder is what will settle it.

WORLD-37TN is measuring T42's ENDURANCE at dt 45 on the current model as a
candidate for the escalation's conversion step. That is the same experiment this
row wants, arriving for a different reason and paid for by a different budget.
So this row does not wait for someone to buy a blow-up: either the ladder finds
T42 endures 45 -- in which case this defect is very likely retired by whatever
batch 2 changed across rainmod, fluxmod, radmod, seamod, landmod, plasim and
outmod -- or it reproduces, and the ladder blocks on the mechanism with a fresh
crashed directory to diagnose from.

That is the condition this deferral was written against, so a recurrence is the
deferral working rather than a surprise.

2026-08-26, WHERE THIS ROW'S EVIDENCE NOW SITS IN THE TREE. lib/rungs.py's
COMMISSIONING_EVIDENCE row for (T42, 45.0) carries binds: False, so
timestep_problems no longer REFUSES that pair and commissioning_caveats reports
it at launch instead. The argument for demoting it is that the claim has no
artifact left to check against -- run_900548ae632e, its provenance and its
reproducer are all gone -- and a refusal taken on a profile the model no longer
has is failure-modes class 34. Reinstating the refusal is one field, and a
recurrence is what buys it back on a run that exists.

title: verify_latitude_pairing.py is a pipeline gate that tests a function deleted from the model
description:
exoplasim/scripts/verify_latitude_pairing.py lifts 'ilatperm' verbatim out of vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/plasimmod.f90 and compiles it inside a parameter module to check the paired latitude decomposition's index map. plasimmod.f90 no longer contains ilatperm.

Verified 2026-08-24 by running the script's own extraction regex against the current source: no match, so extract() reaches 'raise SystemExit("ilatperm not found in " + SRC)' and the gate exits non-zero having checked nothing.

The paired latitude decomposition was deleted in 2508bedb, 'Delete the paired latitude decomposition, 515 lines', because SHTns replaced legmod and cannot use the permuted layout, so there was nothing left to buy and two grid layouts to carry. That commit removed ilatperm, the LPAIRLAT parameter, seven paired branches in legmod, four in mpimod, three blocks each in utilities and utilities_omp, the un-permute in plasim.f90 and shtnsmod's refusal. It predates the wave-2 fan-out.

The gate is still declared: config/pipeline.yaml:677 lists it, exoplasim/README.md:321 has its row, and scripts/smoke_test.py:909 carries a named SPAT-2 exemption for it.

This is exactly the class world-en0 closed by DELETING verify_fold_indexing.sh and verify_fold_exactness.sh, on the reasoning that repointing them would have made them pass vacuously, which is worse than not running. The same applies here and more simply: there is no function to repoint at.

Do: ask whether the thing should exist before fixing it. The decomposition is gone, so the property the gate checks is not a property of anything in the tree. Delete verify_latitude_pairing.py with its pipeline.yaml row, its README row and its smoke_test RUNG_TABLE_EXEMPT entry, the way world-en0 did.

Check verify_symmetric_transform.py in the same pass but do NOT assume it goes with it: it lifts sp2fc and sp2fcdmu out of legmod.f90, both of which still exist, and checks them against an associated Legendre table from scipy, which is a test with a right answer independent of the decomposition. What it may no longer exercise is the MIRROR path, since 2508bedb removed the paired branches from legmod, and its PARAMOD still injects 'logical, parameter :: LPAIRLAT = .true.'. Establish whether that injection now does nothing before touching the file.

Source: exoplasim/notes/paired-latitude-decomposition.md, which described the decomposition as live and now records that it was retired.
close_reason:
verify_latitude_pairing.py DELETED with its config/pipeline.yaml row, its exoplasim/README.md row and its scripts/smoke_test.py RUNG_TABLE_EXEMPT entry, the way world-en0 deleted verify_fold_indexing.sh and verify_fold_exactness.sh.

Re-verified by running it: it exits on SystemExit('ilatperm not found in vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/plasimmod.f90'). grep over the whole of vendor/exoplasim finds no ilatperm anywhere, so there was nothing to repoint at. Broken since 2508bedb on 2026-08-22, two days, and nothing depended on its result: its pipeline.yaml row is in the one_offs list, which by that list's own comment produces no artifact any step consumes. world-38b touched the file on 2026-08-24 without noticing it was already dead.

verify_symmetric_transform.py checked in the same pass and it does NOT go with it -- but it does not pass either, and the issue's expectation about it was wrong. The mirror path is not merely unselected: 2508bedb deleted the symmetric computation from sp2fc, sp2fcdmu and dv2uv outright, so all three are now plain full-latitude multiplies and the lines the negative controls perturb do not exist. The script refuses rather than running control-free, which is the right refusal. Its LPAIRLAT injection is inert. Filed as world-2div, with the argument that the positive half -- the routines against a scipy Legendre table -- is worth MORE now than it was, because the fork's per-mode factor hoist is live in those loops and the table catches a wrong factor.

Two more broken things found in the same sweep and filed rather than fixed: world-8y1e (verify_omp_collectives.f90:90 calls ilatperm, so that gate cannot compile) and world-nfwi (legmod's three inverse transforms still declare k, ze1/ze2/zo1/zo2 and dv2uv's sixteen parity accumulators, none of them used, under comments describing a mirror latitude they no longer compute).

title: config/planet.yaml's atmosphere preamble still says radmod has no CH4 and no N2O term
description:
config/planet.yaml lines 158-164, the paragraph immediately above the 'atmosphere:' key, reads:

  What this block CAN say is bounded by what the model reads. PlaSim's longwave
  is Sasamori (1968) over water vapour, CO2 and ozone, and the shortwave adds
  Rayleigh and the same three; radmod.f90 has no CH4 and no N2O term, so there
  is nothing here to set them to. Their absence is a property of the radiation
  scheme rather than a composition choice ... Adding either means adding a band,
  not a key.

Every clause of that is now false, and the block DIRECTLY BELOW IT contradicts it:

- radmod.f90:190-191 declares 'ch4' and 'n2o' as radmod_nl keys, broadcast at :1112-1113, in the namelist at :919.
- The longwave band that carries them is resident in radmod.f90 (CLIM-42), with zch4a0 at :3064 and the rest of the band constants beside it.
- config/planet.yaml:199-200 sets pCH4_bar: 0.0000016 and pN2O_bar: 0.0000003, MEASURED 2026-08-20 under CLIM-43 from Rugheimer et al. (2013), and run_exoplasim.py:171-172 converts both to the ppmv radmod_nl wants.
- The CH4/N2O block's own text prices the band: 'At these abundances against zero it lowers global mean outgoing longwave by 0.799 W/m2.'

So a reader grepping config/planet.yaml for CH4 lands on the reason it cannot be set, four lines above where it is set. CLAUDE.md: 'Rewrite superseded content; do not mark it.'

Do: rewrite that paragraph to say what the longwave now carries -- water vapour, CO2, ozone and the CLIM-42 trace-gas band -- and what it still does not, which is the honest bound the paragraph was written to state. Keep the one-signed direction argument for whatever absorbers remain absent. The pCO2 paragraph above it is unaffected and its 'currently unbacked' outgassing check is a separate matter.

Filed by the notes/audits sweep, from notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md finding 5, whose own text this supersedes in the same direction.
close_reason:
config/planet.yaml's atmosphere preamble now names what the longwave carries -- water vapour, CO2, ozone and the resident CLIM-42 trace-gas band -- and keeps the one-signed direction argument for the absorbers that remain absent: no CO, no SO2, no NH3, no collision-induced continuum for N2 or CO2. Verified against radmod.f90 rather than against the note: ch4 and n2o are radmod_nl keys at :190-191, in the namelist at :919, broadcast at :1112-1113.

Fixed in every instance, not only the cited one. The same false claim was restated in analysis/trace_gas_forcing.py's module docstring and in exoplasim/notes/trace-gas-absorbers.md's opening; both are now framed as the OFFLINE line-by-line reference the resident band is measured against, which is what they compute and is the standing use for them. notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md finding 5's closing paragraph, which recorded the contradiction as live, now records it as rewritten. No number moved anywhere.

title: An absent surface field is not an error, and the compiled land mask default is all land
description:
surfmod.f90's get_surf_array handles an ABSENT surface file by writing '* Init <name> [code = NNNN] internally *' to the diagnostic unit, leaving kread at 0, and returning. mpsurfgp then leaves the array untouched, so the module default stands. There is no error path and no way to tell that line from the thirteen other codes a healthy run initialises internally.

The default that matters is plasimmod.f90's dls = 1., the land/sea mask, which is ALL LAND. With doro at 0.0 the model integrates a flat, entirely continental planet and produces a full set of numbers for it.

world-fuh closed the neighbouring half -- check_surf_header now refuses a file whose header words 5 and 6 disagree with NLON and NLAT, by name -- and its close reason records that the dls default was deliberately left: 'The dls=1. all-land default is in plasimmod.f90, batch A's file, and is untouched.' So the WRONG-GRID case refuses and the ABSENT case does not.

Why it matters here rather than upstream: upstream ships Earth boundary fields, so absent means the user removed them. This project supplies every field itself and deletes the shipped ones on purpose (configure()'s rm *.sra), so absent is the state a staging bug produces, and finding 9 of the audit records that T85, T127 and T170 have executables and no surface family at all.

Nothing integrates that way today: the project-side surface_field_report raises on a missing intended code and declare_hyperdiffusion raises on a rung with no table entry. This is about the model refusing for itself rather than relying on a driver that a direct invocation bypasses.

Do: decide which surface codes are REQUIRED for a run to be meaningful -- the land/sea mask 172 and the orography 129 at least -- and make surfini abort naming the code when one of those is absent, rather than falling back to a compiled default. Codes that are genuinely optional keep the internal-init line. Rule 4 applies: this is model source, and every binary needs rebuilding.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 3.
close_reason:
get_surf_array now ABORTS when the file for code 129 or code 172 is absent, naming the code, the file it expected and the compiled default that would otherwise have stood. The required set is exactly {129 orography, 172 land/sea mask}, declared on the ground that those are the two whose plasimmod defaults are a WORLD rather than a value -- dls = 1. is all land and doro = 0.0 is flat -- and together they integrate a flat entirely continental planet and produce a full set of numbers for it. Every other code keeps the internal-init line unchanged.

Placed in get_surf_array rather than in surfini, so it covers every caller of mpsurfgp at once: surfini reads both codes and landmod.f90:422-423 reads them again, and either route alone would have left the other unguarded.

NON-LOCAL IMPACTS ENUMERATED. Aqua and desert planets keep the fallback -- landmod reads 129 and 172 with no mode guard of its own, so the refusal is conditioned on naqua == 0 .and. ndesert == 0, matching restart_surface.py:338 which already treats those modes as the ones that replace the mask. Restart runs never reach the branch. Code 172 is also read as yls by oceanmod and xls by icemod, all three from the same N<NLAT>_surf_0172.sra, so one file satisfies them all. Beds already carry both: bench/bed_check holds N064_surf_0129.sra and N064_surf_0172.sra, make_profile_bed.py copies N???_surf_*.sra, and _bed_guard.sh already refuses a bed with no surface files at all. No namelist key, no restart record and no output field, so restart_schema.py and pyburn are untouched. Syntax checked free-form against stub modules.

RULE 4: model source changed, so every binary is stale. python exoplasim/scripts/rebuild_binaries.py then --verify. Not done here; this session was not permitted to compile.

The audit finding at notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 3 now records the closure rather than the live defect.

title: archive_builds.py's EXPECTED_GRIDS is a literal list that no build on disk satisfies
description:
scripts/archive_builds.py:56-57 declares

    EXPECTED_GRIDS = ["exoplasim-T21", "exoplasim-T42", "exoplasim-T63",
                      "exoplasim-T85", "grid-512x256"]

with the comment 'A build is these five exports. Fewer means it is still being generated.' It is used at :150 as a completeness gate: a build directory missing any of the five is printed as 'incomplete' and SKIPPED, so its payload is never archived.

Measured 2026-08-24 against the tree:
- source/precarve-craton-10m/ (the ACTIVE build) holds exoplasim-T21, T42, T85, T127, T170. It has neither exoplasim-T63 nor grid-512x256, so it can never be archived, whatever else is true of it.
- source/precarve-craton/ holds exoplasim-T21, T42, T63, T85, T127 and grid-512x256, so it passes.

The list is also the last ladder restatement world-ltc's SPAT-2 lint does not reach: it is rung names inside path strings with no dimensions beside them, so neither check_no_rung_literal_in_a_path nor check_no_rung_table_outside_rungs fires. world-ltc's own description names archive_builds.py:56-57 as one of the remaining copies and its close reason does not say what happened to it.

Do: decide what a COMPLETE build is, and derive the check rather than list it. The grids a build actually carries are a property of the export recipe in source/README.md, not of this script; if the set is meant to be the ladder it should come from lib/rungs.py, and if it is meant to be the grids that build was generated at it should come from the build's own manifest. Either way the gate must pass for a build that is finished, or it silently disables archiving.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 10.
close_reason:
EXPECTED_GRIDS is gone. lib/builds.py:incomplete_exports replaces it and is derived: a build is finished when every grid export it CARRIES is written through -- manifest.json, planet.nc, README.txt and a non-empty grid/ -- with a Gaussian export also having to name a rung in lib/rungs.py.

Re-measured against the tree first. The active build precarve-craton-10m holds T21, T42, T85, T127 and T170 and has neither exoplasim-T63 nor grid-512x256, so it could never have been archived; precarve-craton holds T21, T42, T63, T85, T127 and grid-512x256 and passed on a T63 that source/README.md records as no longer emitted. Both now pass, and precarve-craton becomes archivable. Nothing was executed.

The set could not be derived the way the issue's second option suggests: a grid export's manifest.json describes its own fields and says nothing about its siblings, so a build cannot be asked which grids the recipe of its own day emitted. What it can be asked is whether anything under it is half written, which is the property 'still being generated' actually names. A directory holding README.txt and nothing else is treated as ABSENT rather than unfinished, because the exporter writes that file from a template needing nothing computed and such a directory carries no payload to lose -- source/precarve-craton/exoplasim-T127 is one, and calling it unfinished would have blocked an otherwise complete build.

The mid-generation refusal never rested on this check alone and the docstring now says so: lib/orogen.py's registry refuses an unregistered terrain hash, mesh_export_of refuses a build with no raw/ carrier or with two, and the caller skips the configured build.

Checked against controls chosen before the dry run was read: a finished build passes, a build with grid/ files and no manifest is refused naming the missing files, a README-only directory passes, exoplasim-T99 is refused as not a rung. Also made the mesh-carrier RuntimeError print its reason instead of continuing silently.

This was the last SPAT-2 ladder restatement world-ltc's lint could not reach, and it is removed rather than exempted.

title: run_2b20e3324bb0 integrated the physics filter at NFILTEREXP 8, not the declared 16
description:
Found by the retrospective gate added under world-e6m (scripts/check_consistency.py, 'runs vs the namelists they staged').
