title: Dust deposition reaches the soil and never reaches the cryosphere
description:
Dust deposition reaches the soil and never reaches the cryosphere: nothing consumes the deposition field as a term in the model's snow and ice albedo, and `build_dust.py` reads snow only as an emission suppressor

Source: `notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md` finding 2
notes:
BLOCKED ON clim-63 BY DECISION, 2026-08-24. Not to be solved separately.

Scoping found that CLIMBER-X's dust-on-snow is NOT the prognostic reservoir this issue's audit finding assumed. dust_in_snow (references/climber-x/src/smb/smb_surface_par.f90:179) is diagnostic: dust_con = dust_dep/max(1e-7,snow) is the concentration in FALLING snow, times a melt-concentration factor 1+(w_snow_max-w_snow)/w_snow_dust capped at five, on the reasoning that dust is not removed with meltwater. The only genuinely new state is a seasonal w_snow_max, one scalar per cell.

What blocks a cheap graft is the OTHER end. CLIMBER-X's snow albedo takes snow_grain AND dust_con together, because dust absorption scales with the snow's optical grain radius. This model has no grain size at all -- landmod interpolates albsmin to albsmax on surface temperature. So every published dust-darkening coefficient is calibrated in a model WITH grain size, and transplanting one onto a grain-free ramp gives a coefficient that does not mean what its source measured. That is an undocumented value used as an anchor, which this project does not do.

Two routes were considered and the cheap one is refused:
- Graft a darkening onto the existing albsmin/albsmax ramp. Small diff, consistent tier, but the coefficient can only be a declared bracket rather than a derived value, and it would be redone when a grain size arrives.
- Adopt the physics with SEMI. clim-63's own description records that snow_par carries lsnow_dust, w_snow_dust and dust_con_scale, and that SEMI's four-component visible/near-infrared albedo and shortwave structure IS this project's 0.75 um split from lib/stellar.py. So the dust term arrives with the surface mass balance, calibrated against the grain size it was measured with.

USER DECISION: solve it correctly once with clim-63 rather than partially twice. This issue stays open as the record of the term and its measured size, and closes when clim-63 delivers it.

The size, unchanged and re-measured 2026-08-24: deposition over the glacier band is 1.97 to 19.56 g/m2 per Earth year across the aeolian roughness bracket, against a literature range of 1 to 5 g/m2 END-OF-SEASON LOAD for 0.03 to 0.08 broadband albedo reduction. Every arm is at or above that range in the units it reports, the effect is one-signed, it acts on summer ablation which is the term state.md 5b's glacier result turns on, and 1782 land cells carry mean snow depth above 1 cm so it is not glaciers only. It also puts a cryosphere term under the aeolian roughness bracket, which spans five orders of magnitude and was understood as controlling emission and direct forcing only.

PREMISE CONFIRMED 2026-08-24, exoplasim/notes/semi-scoping.md section 1. The
decision to wait rested on a correct reading. surface_albedo computes the snow
grain size and the dust concentration and hands BOTH to one albedo routine;
inside snow_albedo_dang the black-carbon-equivalent loading is
H = c/c0*(r/r0)**0.73, so the darkening scales with grain radius by a stated
power, and snow_albedo_ww reaches the same structure through separate new-snow
and aged-snow dust curves weighted by the same grain size. Adopting SEMI does
settle this row's blocker, and the calibration that arrives with it is Dang et
al. 2015 with dust_con_scale at unity, a CLIMBER-2 grain ageing law tuned to
MARv3.6 using CROCUS over Greenland, and w_snow_dust as the melt concentration
length.

A GRAFT ONTO THE EXISTING RAMP IS WORSE THAN THE ROW ALREADY SAID.
combinedspec-snow_ice.ipynb, in the tree, builds each iceblend as a weighted
mixture of clear ice, frost and coarse, fine and medium granular snow, with the
CLEAR ICE fraction solved by bisection against a broadband albedo target under a
5772 K blackbody. So the albsmin-to-albsmax endpoints differ in how much clear
ice is mixed in, tuned to a solar number, and the temperature ramp between them
is not an ageing law. A dust coefficient there would be unanchored twice over.

A THIRD ROUTE EXISTS AND IT IS A USER DECISION. specblock.f90 already ships
fsnowalb, msnowalb and csnowalb -- fine, medium and coarse granular snow
reflectance over the same 965 wavelengths -- and nothing selects among them.
analysis/ice_albedo.py already reproduces radmod's star-weighting arithmetic.
Between them a two-band snow albedo on a three-point grain-radius axis FOR THIS
STAR is derivable from data in the tree, with a check that can fail, needing no
fine grid, no mass balance scheme and no PHYS-13. That is WORLD-DD48, added as a
second blocker here. It supplies exactly the missing half a published dust
coefficient needs, so it is a shorter honest route to closing this row than
waiting for SEMI. What it does not supply is how the grain size EVOLVES, which
still arrives with a mass balance. The user's instruction was to solve it
correctly once rather than partially twice, and this is a candidate for the
correct single solve that was not on the table when that call was made.

THE PARAMETERISATION'S OWN PAPER IS HELD NOW, 2026-08-25: references/dang2015-parameterizations-for-narrowband-and-broadband-albedo-of-snow.pdf, supplied by the user. Three things it settles that this row will need, none of which the CLIMBER-X implementation states.

1. The (r/r0) exponent in the black-carbon-equivalent loading is not a fitted constant of the darkening law. It is the exponent that COLLAPSES the family: Dang's Eq. (7) combines the impurity mixing ratio and the grain radius into one predictor and the exponent is varied until the albedo-reduction curves for different radii merge onto one curve. The paper gives two values, one for the all-wave and visible bands and a much smaller one for the near infrared, and it states a validity range in the combined predictor plus a floor on the grain radius below which the collapsed form should not be used, and a ceiling on impurity loading. Those declarations come with the exponent and belong in whatever implements it.

2. THE DUST TERM IS A VISIBLE-BAND TERM. The paper states that adding mineral dust does not significantly change the near-infrared band albedo, because dust grains and snow grains absorb similarly averaged over 0.7 to 4.0 um -- which is why CLIMBER-X sets the near-infrared darkening to zero rather than omitting it by oversight. That matters here: notes/audits/snow-albedo-grain.md found the comparison against the published coefficients came out small at BOTH ends in the visible and only awkward in the near infrared, so the band this row actually acts in is the band where the grain axis transfers cleanly.

3. Two things this project had read out of CLIMBER-X are wrong against the paper and are corrected in analysis/snow_albedo_grain.py: the Table 1 band edges are 0.3-0.7 and 0.7-4.0 um, and the zenith correction is r*(1 + a*(mu-0.65))**2, with the square on the whole bracket rather than on the angle difference. Read the paper's forms, not the implementation's, when this row is taken.

title: Basin deflation driven by nocturnal-inversion low-level jets is sub-resolution
description:
Basin deflation driven by nocturnal-inversion low-level jets is sub-resolution: the Bodele-class mechanism (`washington2005-bodele-low-level-jet.pdf`) lives in the lowest few hundred metres and ten sigma layers cannot form it, so gust sampling measures the tail the model produces and not the jet it cannot. One-signed: basin emission is understated wherever inversion jets dominate, and the shallower boundary layer at 1.31 g sharpens exactly that regime

Source: `notes/external-review-abl-obliquity-dust-carbon.md` point 1
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open as a DECLARED gap on GW-6 and GRAV-6's precedent: the process is real, it is not representable at L10, and a parameterisation fitted to nothing would be precision theatre. The honest revisit is vertical resolution, L20 at T85 under loop D, where `close_term_energy.py` re-measures the energy terms anyway. Until then the dust artifacts carry the gust-tail emission and this row is why the basin end of it is a floor [step: dust]
close_reason:
ABSENT AND NOT REPRESENTABLE, declared. Complete work under the rule that an absent process is a declared gap provided it is declared.

The finding is now a measurement rather than a level count. The baseline climatology's bottom two sigma levels are 0.98282 and 0.92191; through the hypsometric relation at this world's gravity and a 280 K near-surface temperature that is a lowest full level near 110 m and a second near 510 m, so two levels below a kilometre and one below half. A Bodele-class nocturnal inversion and the jet core above it both fall inside the single lowest layer, whose wind is that layer's mean. The obstacle is not that the jet is weakly resolved, it is that the model has no interior to the layer the jet lives in, so no amount of high-cadence sampling recovers it.

Gravity neither causes nor relieves it: sigma levels sit at heights proportional to the scale height and the nocturnal boundary layer compresses by the same factor, so the count of levels inside it is unchanged. 1.31 g concentrates the same surface cooling into less air, which makes the regime more likely to matter, not more likely to resolve.

It is a FLOOR rather than a bracket, and that is the part that was not stated anywhere a reader lands: no end of the declared roughness or vegetation brackets moves it, because the missing wind is absent from every arm. Declared now in three places: aeolian/README.md 'what it does not do', the subgrid_wind block of aeolian/config/dust.yaml where the fitted shape is set, and notes/external-review-abl-obliquity-dust-carbon.md point 1, which carries the measurement.

The L20 revisit is left as a bracket, not a number: any level rule that doubles the count while keeping its shape roughly halves the near-surface layer thickness in log-sigma, putting the lowest level in 30-60 m and the second in 130-250 m. What replaces the bracket is the sigma array of a built L20 executable. Not built here: the resolution ladder is being reworked on main and this batch must not touch it.

It gathers `dprl + dprc`, flips them in latitude like every other field `aero_main` gathers, and applies Sportisse (2007) below-cloud scavenging `Lambda = scava * p**scavb` behind `lwetdep`, default 0 so ONE BINARY RUNS BOTH ARMS per the rewritten A3. Same form and coefficients as the offline chain, so the two can be compared rather than contrasted; column-uniform rather than below a diagnosed cloud base, which is the offline chain's own approximation and is declared. `scava` and `scavb` get no Fortran default -- `aero_ini` aborts -- because they live in `aeolian/config/dust.yaml` and a default here would be a fourth place to go stale. description:
One aerosol, one radius, one density. `plasimmod.f90:99` fixes `parameter(NAERO = 1)`; `apart` and `rhop` are photochemical-haze values shared by every bin

Source: `notes/dust.md`, `aeolian/notes/in-model-dust.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18, SINGLE MODE, and the check this task proposed turned out to be VACUOUS. Only `Qext/apart` enters the optical depth, so the mass extinction efficiency round-trips for ANY radius, and for either DUST-12 dataset -- they differ 0.32% in MEE, because MEE is set by the real part while the datasets differ in absorption. So the result does not depend on DUST-12 either way. What `apart` actually controls is SETTLING, and there the optical 0.98 um is 4.8x too long-lived for the burden and 16x too slow for the emitted mass. Generic PCM carries dust as one aerosol kind with one effective radius, which supports the single mode, but DECOUPLES the optical radius from the sedimentation radius; ExoPlaSim can too, through that same identity. Recommended: `apart` = 2.21 um, burden-matched, with the aerofile's four Q values per band scaled by 2.251, which leaves optical depth, SSA, backscatter and the band ratio unchanged because each is a ratio. NOT APPLIED, deliberately: it only bites once `apart` reaches `radmod`, which is upstream defect 1, and applying now would churn a tracked aerofile for no effect. DECLARED COST of the single mode: total deposition still equals emission in steady state, so the cost is WHERE it lands -- one lifetime is one travel distance, and the coarse 73% of emitted mass goes 3.4x too far while the sub-micron fraction goes 30x too short, so both ends of the phosphorus argument come out wrong in opposite directions. The offline chain therefore keeps producing the size-resolved deposition field that pedology and phosphorus read [step: rebuild_binaries]

title: Replace the fixed-width binary and monthly interpolation in VesperInput with a streaming
description:
Replace the fixed-width binary and monthly interpolation in `VesperInput` with a streaming reader for EFOR-3: deliver exact chronological intervals and optional subdaily vectors, preserve interval duration and local-solar phase, refuse gaps/overlaps, and integrate to LPJ's current 24-hour hydrology/biogeochemistry boundary in the consumer rather than encoding that boundary in the forcing format

Source: `biosphere/notes/ecological-climate-forcing-audit.md` findings 1 and 4
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; parser, round-trip and constant/phase-wrap fixtures require no LPJ-GUESS run and extend BIO-20 [step: lpj_driver, lpj_run]

PARTIAL, commit 1eb8d29d. Two of the issue's claims are settled and two wait on EFOR-3.

DONE. The monthly interpolation is gone: VesperInput::interpolate called interp_monthly_means_conserve, which manufactured a smooth daily curve between bin centres with no source behind it, and VesperInput::integrate_year replaces it with each absolute day's duration-weighted mean over the intervals overlapping it. Identity when an interval is one absolute day, conserving for any interval structure, invents nothing. The fixed cadence is gone: VESPDRV8 carries an interval table with explicit start, end, duration in absolute seconds and local solar phase, ANY COUNT, so twelve a year and one per climate-model timestep are the same code path and the 24-hour boundary is the consumer's rather than the format's. read_driver refuses a gap, an overlap, a duration disagreeing with its own bounds, and a table that does not reach the year, on four separate messages. Precipitation travels as a mean rate rather than a per-interval total. Breaking V7 cost nothing: no vesper_driver.bin exists.

REMAINING, and both wait on EFOR-3.
- The SOURCE is still a 12-bin climatology, so the intervals are the producer's bins rather than a chronological sequence. Nothing further changes here when EFOR-3 lands: the format and the reader already take any interval count.
- The reader is not STREAMING. read_driver loads every cell's whole time series into memory, which is right for a few hundred intervals and wrong for a chronological artifact over many orbits. Sizing that is a property of EFOR-3's artifact, and building a streaming reader against a format that does not exist would be choosing the format from the reader, which is the order EFOR-1 exists to protect.
- Subdaily vectors are DECLARED and refused rather than delivered: the header carries the sample count and read_driver refuses a non-zero one by name, because this module has no operator that reads them. EFOR-3 delivers the samples; PCAR-1 and FIRE-1 consume them.

Verified: build_lpj_driver.py --self-test executes the integration operator and the header layout on seventeen fixtures. vesperinput.cpp is g++ -fsyntax-only clean against a synthetic vesper.h and is NOT executed; LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree.

2026-08-25, user correction. THE TWELVE-BIN SOURCE IS NOT A CONSTRAINT. This batch left the remaining half blocked on EFOR-3 on the grounds that the source is a 12-bin climatology and a reader must not choose its own format. The second half of that reasoning is right and the premise is wrong: this project CONTROLS what the climatology emits. build_climatology.py is ours, lib/climatology.py is ours, and twelve is a convention rather than a property of the model.

WHAT THE MODEL ACTUALLY OFFERS, from lib/climatology.py's own header: 36 raw records per orbit at NLOWIO = 1, and 182 at NLOWIO = 0, which is the regime a climatology is required to use. So the available time resolution is 182 samples per orbit and the binning is a reduction WE choose.

AND TWELVE IS THE AWKWARD CHOICE. 182 = 2 x 7 x 13, so twelve does not divide it: the clean regime bins as [15]*5 + [16] + [15]*5 + [16], two bins carry a sixteenth record, and under equal weighting those two are under-weighted by 5.5 per cent while the other ten are over-weighted by 1.1 per cent -- which lib/climatology.py exists to correct and which already produced one artefact, a reported 1.19x excess on bin 0 that was an artefact of assuming eleven equal bins. 13, 14, 26 and 91 all divide 182 exactly. A bin count that divides removes the weighting correction and the class of error that comes with it.

SO THE ORDER IS STILL EFOR-1'S -- contract before transport -- and the contract is now written (biosphere/config/ecological_forcing_contract.yaml, 19 rows). What EFOR-4 needs is a DECISION about what the climatology emits for the forcing path, not an artifact from EFOR-3. VESPDRV8 already carries an interval table with explicit bounds and any count, so the consumer side is ready for whatever is chosen.

Do: decide the bin count the ecological forcing path needs, on what the CONSUMING processes require rather than on what is convenient to emit -- the contract's process cadence registry is where that argument belongs -- and prefer a count that divides 182 unless something needs otherwise. Then emit it. The streaming half of this row stands on its own merits and is a separate question from the bin count.

2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER, from a pass over the needs-decision set.
RECLASSIFIED, derivable, not a decision: the bin count follows from what the CONSUMING processes require, and the contract's process cadence registry is where that argument already belongs.

notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; the source change and no-simulation checks can proceed independently, but any timing or climate run requires explicit permission [step: baseline_run]. THE CONSUMPTION SIDE IS PRICED AND IT IS ONE SCALAR, 2026-08-22. SPITFIRE reads lightning from an input file whose default is literally named `lightning_fixed`, in `hectare-1 d-1`, and uses it in ONE LINE multiplying by two Earth-tuned constants whose product is 0.008, one being Earth's cloud-to-ground flash fraction. There is NO lightning parameterisation anywhere in LPJmL and the coupled-model path where a live field would arrive is commented out. So what this row produces plugs in unchanged as a per-cell-per-day ignition density -- the architecture is portable and only the field is missing. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 51a. THE HARD INPUT IS ALREADY COMPUTED, 2026-08-22, verified in source: THIS ROW NEEDS AN OUTPUT HOOK, NOT NEW PHYSICS. Both convection schemes in the vendored fork already derive a convective cloud-top level and pressure -- `rainmod.f90:576,596` declares `itop` "cloud top level" and `zptop` "cloud top pressure" and sets them through the Kuo scheme, and `rainmod_bm.f90:424,440` does the same for Betts-Miller. Both are ROUTINE-LOCAL and neither is exported, which is the whole of the gap. THAT MAKES PRICE-RIND DIRECTLY IMPLEMENTABLE and rules out the updraft-mass-flux and ice-flux families, which need diagnostics this model does not carry. The cleanest statement of the scheme is WRF's `module_ltng_cpmpr92z.F`, 101 lines with about 20 lines of physics: `flashrate = 3.44e-5*zkm^4.9/60` over land and `6.57e-6*zkm^4.9/60` over ocean after Michalon (1999), gated on cloud-top temperature below freezing, scaled by cell area. Its inputs are the neutral-buoyancy level, geopotential height there, terrain height, temperature and a land mask -- all available. CARRY THE CALIBRATION CAVEAT: the coefficient and the 4.9 exponent are an Earth fit that cannot be re-derived here, so THE FIELD IS DEFENSIBLE IN SHAPE AND NOT IN ABSOLUTE MAGNITUDE, and what FIRE-3 consumes should be normalised to a declared global flash rate rather than taken as a rate. A ZERO-MODEL-CHANGE FALLBACK if the hook proves awkward: Romps et al. (2014) makes flash rate proportional to CAPE times convective precipitation, and convective precipitation is already an output field. `notes/external-source-inventory.md`

title: Glacial erosion carries no gravity term, and Glen's law makes ice velocity go as g^3 (2.23x
description:
Glacial erosion carries no gravity term, and Glen's law makes ice velocity go as `g^3` (2.23x here)

Source: `notes/audits/orogen-gravity.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
blocked on the downscaling pass, deliberately. AMENDED: two further facts make a g^3 term precision on the wrong quantity. `iceFlow` accumulates a CELL TALLY, seeded from the glaciation index and summed downstream, where the hydraulic path was deliberately given `flowSeed = cellArea / refCellKm2` so its accumulation is a real drainage area; the two accumulators disagree about what is resolution-independent, and the same valley collects about four times the ice flow at four times the region count, carving as `iceFlow^0.6`. And per PHYS-13 the index feeding it is an Earth-calibrated latitude threshold blind to this planet's obliquity, spectrum and rotation. Fix the ice mask first. The sub-grid judgement also survives measurement: at four times the region count the mean edge is 7.59 km against a 1-5 km valley, and reaching 1.5 km edges needs about 256 million regions, 26x the run measured. See `notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md`. The audit's recommendation was Option B, carry it as a declared gap: `iceFlow` is a heuristic accumulation rather than a Glen's-law velocity, so a rigorous g^3 on it is precision theatre. Decisive on top of that, a glacial valley is 1-5 km against a 15.19 km mesh cell, so the process is SUB-GRID and cannot be resolved here at any gravity. It belongs with the downscaling machinery, which has to persist sub-grid hypsometry anyway [step: orogen]. AMENDED 2026-08-22, and this does NOT reopen the row: the objection that a `g^3` velocity on an Earth-calibrated ice mask is precision on the wrong quantity is unchanged. What is new is that the `(rho_i g)^n` term has a published reference implementation to take whole rather than a term to bolt on, in BIG-MITgcm's MITgcmIS -- shallow ice, Glen's law at n = 3, Positive Degree Day mass balance, no basal sliding or calving -- and that it costs about 1 CPU-hour per 40,000 years, so ice sheet flow is a SMALL component rather than a large one. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 4. TAKING THE SOLVER IS NOT TAKING THE MODEL, and the split is where the work is. The flow half is a few lines of algebra and the two routes to it, native on the region mesh or a port off the cubed sphere, are costed by CLIM-62 rather than assumed here. The mass balance half is not usable here at all: its ablation is driven by 2 m air temperature alone, with no shortwave, albedo or spectrum, which is structurally blind to the term this world differs on most over ice, and its accumulation assumes densification into glacial ice is instantaneous, which is GRAV-8's missing physics assumed away. So the deliverable from that paper is Eq. 2 to 4, and `A_dot` is the other ninety percent. GRAVITY ENTERS AT FOUR POWERS, NOT ONE, 2026-08-22, from SICOPOLIS's own algebra in `references/climber-x/src/ice_sico/`. The g^3 velocity scaling this row states is CONFIRMED independently: driving stress is g^1, Glen `creep = sigma^2` makes it g^3, so 2.23x. TWO THINGS THIS ROW DOES NOT CARRY. (1) STRAIN HEATING IS g^4, `creep(sigma)*sigma^2`, giving 2.91x -- the thermal feedback is a HIGHER power than the flow, so a simulated ice sheet here goes temperate more readily than the velocity scaling implies, and temperate ice re-enters the flow through the rate factor and the sliding switch. (2) BASAL SLIDING IS ONLY g^(p-q), which is g^1 under the default Weertman exponents p=3 q=2, against g^3 for deformation -- SO THE DEFORMATION-TO-SLIDING RATIO SHIFTS BY g^2 = 1.71x AND THE MODE OF FLOW CHANGES, not just its speed. `c_slide` is dimensional, `m/(a*Pa^(p-q))`, so its Earth-tuned value is wrong here by exactly that factor. AND TWO EARTH GRAVITIES HIDE IN PER-METRE COEFFICIENTS WITH NO `G` ON THE LINE, failure-mode class 32 in its unit form: `BETA = 8.7d-04 K/m`, the Clausius-Clapeyron gradient per metre OF ICE, is `dTm/dp` times `rho_i*g` and must become 1.136e-3 here, propagating into the pressure-melting point, the cold-temperate transition position and temperate-layer drainage; and the sub-shelf freezing point's 7.64e-4 per metre is the same shape, becoming 9.98e-4. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 45a-b. AND A CHEAP ISOSTASY IMPLEMENTATION WITH A NON-OBVIOUS SIGN, 2026-08-22 -- adjacent to this row rather than answering it, since Landlab carries no glacial erosion law. Its `flexure` component is not a plate PDE but a superposition of analytic point-load Green's functions, with Airy as a one-line short-circuit. Gravity enters at exactly ONE place, the mantle specific weight, at power 1. What propagates is worth stating because the sign surprises: flexural parameter goes as `g^-1/4` (0.935x here), deflection per unit LOAD IN NEWTONS as `g^-1/2` (0.875x), but **deflection per unit ice or sediment THICKNESS as `g^+1/2`, 1.143x** -- because a load is a weight, so heavier gravity makes a given thickness depress the bed MORE even though response per newton falls. Airy cancels gravity exactly. Two defects before copying: the 1-D class omits the cell-area factor the 2-D path applies, so its result is off by the grid spacing, and the gFlex wrapper's step method calls a name that does not exist. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 53c. AND THE MISSING TERM HAS A SOURCE, 2026-08-22. iSOSIA's `source/glacial.c:1375-1470` carries BOTH erosion terms in about 90 lines of C with no solver coupling -- quarrying after Iverson (2012) as `q = Kq*pe^3*u_b*(slope+0.55)^2`, and abrasion as `a = Ka*u_b^ap*sqrt(1+bslope^2)*cos(bslope)` with an optional `pe^3` variant and a sediment-cover factor. IT IS COMPLETELY SEPARABLE: it reads per-cell scalars and writes erosion rates. AND THE GRAVITY ENTRY POINT IS EXPLICIT AND LOAD-BEARING: line 1416 sets `pe = 0.01*te` with the comment recording that `te` is normalised by `rho_ice*g`, so that 0.01 IS EARTH'S GRAVITY BAKED INTO A CONSTANT and becomes 0.01306 here. With `pe^3` in the quarrying law, **gravity enters quarrying as g^3 INDEPENDENTLY of the g^3 already priced through Glen's law** -- which is precisely the term this row says is absent. The real cost is not the law but its second input: effective pressure needs a subglacial hydrology assumption, where sliding speed comes from the ice dynamics already held. The coefficients are Earth-calibrated so absolute erosion rates are not transferable, BUT THE GRAVITY SCALING IS CALIBRATION-FREE, which is what this row asks for. `notes/external-source-inventory.md` THE EXPONENT IS BRACKETED, 2026-08-25, and the bracket is why the term still cannot be written. The 2.23x this row quotes is g^3 on ice VELOCITY at fixed thickness, and that is not what iceFlow is. iceFlow is an accumulated supply, so the FLUX is what is conserved and thickness adjusts: q = u H ~ g^n H^(n+2) gives H ~ g^(-n/(n+2)) and u ~ g^(n/(n+2)) = g^0.6, not g^3. Crossed with an erosion-rate exponent between 1 and 2, and with Iverson quarrying carrying its own p_e^3 on top, the bracket at 1.30626 Earth gravity is: E ~ u flux fixed g^0.60 = 1.17x; E ~ u^2 flux fixed g^1.20 = 1.38x; quarrying p_e^3 u flux fixed g^1.80 = 1.62x; E ~ u thickness fixed g^3.00 = 2.23x; E ~ u^2 or quarrying thickness fixed g^6.00 = 4.97x. The bracket spans a factor of 4.2 and its width is dominated by a STRUCTURAL choice, not a coefficient: whether thickness or flux is conserved. Orogen carries no thickness, no sliding law and no effective pressure, so nothing in the model decides which end applies. A g^3 on iceFlow^0.6 would be neither end and would not be dimensionally the same object, since 0.6 is an exponent on an accumulated supply and n is an exponent on a stress. This SHARPENS Option B rather than reopening the row: the reason not to bolt a gravity term on is not only that the quantity is heuristic, it is that the model lacks the state that decides the term's power. Recorded with the algebra in notes/audits/orogen-gravity.md, section 'The exponent is not one number'. SEPARATELY, the mechanism half this row deferred to PHYS-13 has landed: vendor/orogen/js/glacial-ice.js takes the ice placement from a climatology through --ice-mask, so the Earth-calibrated index feeding iceFlow is fixable and world-q5ig runs it through loop A. That does not change this row's verdict, because the sub-grid argument is untouched -- a 1 to 5 km glacial valley against a 7.60 km mesh -- and neither is the exponent bracket above. AND THE GATE HALF OF PHYS-13 IS NOT A DEFECT: the glacial altitude gate is dimensionless, and that is the gravity-INVARIANT form, because the relief ceiling goes as 1/g from sigma/(rho g) and a dry-adiabatic freezing height goes as 1/g from Gamma = g/cp, so the two cancel. Re-anchoring it to fixed kilometres would introduce an error. So the only unmodelled gravity dependence in the generator is the erosion term this row names, and it stays a declared gap.

2026-08-25, coordinator. THE BLOCKER MAY NOT BE A BLOCKER: EXOPLASIM CARRIES AN ICE THICKNESS.

P0A left this open because the bracket's width is a structural choice -- whether thickness or flux is conserved -- and Orogen carries no thickness, no sliding law and no effective pressure, so nothing in the model decides which end applies. That is true of OROGEN. It is not true of the PIPELINE.

glaciermod.f90 carries dsnowz, the snow and ice column in liquid water equivalent metres, and it is prognostic and unbounded: line 282 is 'where (dsnowz(:) > 30.0) dglac = 1.0 !If we have more than 30 m of lq H2O equivalent in snow/ice, it is a glacier', and line 689 clears the glacier below 0.1 m. glacieroro carries the ice-loaded orography, which pyburn reports as code 268 icez, glacier_geopotential in m2 s-2 -- a height once divided by the configured gravity. Code 232 glac is the cover fraction and code 141 snd the surface snow thickness. Code 211 sit is SEA ice and is not this.

WHY THAT COLLAPSES THE BRACKET RATHER THAN NARROWING IT. The five-row table exists because H had to be INFERRED from a conservation assumption: fix the thickness and Glen's law gives u ~ g^3, conserve the flux and H adjusts to g^(-n/(n+2)) leaving u ~ g^0.6. With H supplied per cell by the climate model neither assumption is needed -- u follows from Glen's law on a measured H, and the only remaining exponent is the erosion-rate one, which is a much narrower and better-sourced question than the 4.2x structural span.

THE ROUTE ALREADY EXISTS. PHYS-13 built --ice-mask, which takes glacial PLACEMENT from a climatology, one float32 per mesh region in region order with a mesh-identity check on seed plus region count. A thickness field travels the same path with the same validation; this is the same coupling, carrying a second field.

CAVEATS, so this is not read as done. dsnowz is a local column with no ice dynamics -- ExoPlaSim does not flow ice, so it gives thickness and not flux, and Orogen's iceFlow is an accumulated supply along flow paths. Whether a no-flow thickness is the right H for an erosion law that wants a flowing glacier is the question this row now turns on, and it is a better question than the one it was stuck behind. There is also no climatology yet: config/planet.yaml declares baseline_climatology null, so this waits on the same commissioning PHYS-13's mask does.

Do: establish whether dsnowz is an admissible H for the erosion term, and if it is, carry it on the ice-mask path and reduce the bracket to the erosion-rate exponent alone.
close_reason:
dsnowz is NOT an admissible H, so the bracket does not reduce to the erosion-rate exponent and keeps its full 4.2x width. What changes is that the blocker is named exactly: a thickness field would not have unblocked this, and the thing that would is a solver.

FOUR REASONS, all properties of the two codebases. It integrates the local surface mass balance alone, dH/dt = b, where a glacier's thickness solves continuity with a flux divergence -- and glaciermod's own header says it is a coupling slot for an external model that SETS the height. It is zero by construction over the ablation zone and trunk, which is where a glacier erodes, and largest at the accumulation summit where a real sheet is nearest stagnant, so it is ANTI-CORRELATED with the wanted field rather than a noisy estimate of it. It cannot decide the exponent, which is the whole width of the bracket: a thickness carrying no ice dynamics does not measure the thickness-versus-flux choice, it imposes the thickness-fixed limb, so the bracket would look collapsed while having been settled by an artefact of the coupling -- worse than the honest bracket. And it is a cell mean against a law quartic in H: u ~ H^4, q ~ H^5, and <H>^4 is not <H^4>.

MEASURED, which is the instrument check: the raw newdsnow dump glacierstop writes, across all six T21 runs on disk, glacier module on and the snow cap lifted (DSMAX = -1, confirmed in each run's landmod_namelist), 25 to 50 orbits. Deepest dsnowz is 0.122 to 0.211 m water equivalent, 0.14 to 0.25 m of ice at rhoglac 850. ZERO cells of 2,048 reach GLACELIM's 2.0 m on any run, zero reach the 30 m the module itself names as the minimum for a sheet to flow, and zero have completed the glacier persistence clock. Glen's law would be evaluated more than two orders of magnitude below where ice flows at all. Run length is not the binding reason: phys-13 measured the sub-grid orography warm bias that causes it.

WHAT WOULD BE ADMISSIBLE AND WHAT IT COSTS: the erosion terms want basal sliding velocity and effective pressure, both OUTPUTS of an ice-dynamics solve, and no ExoPlaSim field substitutes for a solve. What ExoPlaSim can legitimately hand across is the solve's other side, a surface mass balance, and that is the strong direction -- the published reference scheme drives ablation from 2 m air temperature alone, blind to shortwave, albedo and spectrum, which is what this world differs on most over ice. The flow algebra is what must be acquired, and clim-62 costs its two routes.

Sub-grid argument untouched: a 1 to 5 km valley against the 7.60 km mesh. Evidence in notes/audits/orogen-gravity.md.

notes:

open; first implement the trait/unit contract and no-simulation allometry/allocation fixtures, including the analytical check that self-weight similarity alone makes a fixed-height stem about 14% wider and 31% more voluminous at 12.81 m/s2; treat that result as a mechanics-arm check rather than a universal realized biomass multiplier; model-form measurements are blocked on BIO-12/BIO-14, BIO-22, DEMO-4, PLHY-6/PLHY-7 and explicit permission for LPJ-GUESS runs [step: vesper_pfts, lpj_run, soil, surface_albedo]. title: Snow density is a constant and there is no compaction
description:
Snow density is a constant and there is no compaction, so the one snow term that carries gravity is absent. 330 kg/m3 is declared twice, `rhosnow` at `landmod.f90:73` and `CRHOSN` as a hardcoded `parameter` at `icemod.f90:24`, and both are used the same way, as `dsnowz * 1000 / rhosnow`, to convert water equivalent to physical thickness. That thickness sets the snow thermal layer thicknesses `zsntop` and `zsnowz` in `landmod` and the combined ice-plus-snow threshold at `icemod.f90:591`, so the constant reaches surface albedo through cover depth, the ground heat flux through layer thickness, and the sea ice diagnostic. PALADYN's self-loading term after Kojima (1967) is LINEAR IN `g`, so at 12.81 against 9.81 m/s2 compaction runs 1.306x Earth's for the same load and viscosity and this planet's simulated snowpack should sit thinner for the same water equivalent

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3b, `notes/audits/inherited-earth-constants.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. The DIRECTION is known and one-signed; the MAGNITUDE is not, because the viscosity depends on temperature and load and this world's snow temperatures are not Earth's -- so a prognostic density is the only route to a number, and a re-chosen constant would be a second guess wearing the first one's clothes. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is what the term is worth on cover depth and albedo, priced offline against an existing climatology before any source change. Deduplicating the two declarations is correctness-neutral and available immediately, and it is not cosmetic: the `icemod` copy is a hardcoded `parameter`, beyond namelist reach, so it cannot be bracketed where it stands [step: rebuild_binaries, bootstrap_run]. MODERATED 2026-08-22 by a third implementation. ClimaLand declares `AbstractDensityModel` and ships exactly one, `MinimumDensityModel`, computing `rho = rho_min*(1-q_l) + rho_l*q_l` -- a minimum dry-snow density blended toward liquid by liquid fraction, with NO self-loading compaction and no gravity term. So two of three land models omit compaction entirely, and this model's constant is CONVENTIONAL at this complexity level rather than anomalous. That is a real difference from PHYS-14's flat band arrays, where the structure existed and the value denied it; here the structure is absent nearly everywhere. IT DOES NOT MAKE THE TERM UNIMPORTANT, and the reason is the one that raised the question: a term that can be omitted on Earth is one whose EARTH magnitude somebody judged small, and that judgement does not transfer at 1.306 g without being re-made. So this row's question is not why the term is missing -- it is missing almost everywhere -- but whether the Earth-calibrated judgement of negligibility survives this planet, which is the price this row already asks for. FOR THE PRICING: no model does all of it. ClimaLand captures wet-snow density through liquid content, which PALADYN explicitly neglects; PALADYN captures fresh-snow temperature dependence and self-loading, which ClimaLand omits. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 23d. A THIRD RUNG EXISTS, AND A SECOND PATH TO ALBEDO, 2026-08-22. ClimaLand's `MinimumDensityModel` sits between the constant and PALADYN's prognostic compaction: `rho_snow = rho_min*(1-q_l) + rho_liq*q_l`, interpolating toward liquid water by LIQUID MASS FRACTION with depth diagnosed from it. It has no load term and therefore NO GRAVITY TERM, so it does not answer this row's argument, which stands -- but it shows a density responsive to melt state is available without solving compaction, and the constant here misses that effect as well as the gravity one. SEPARATELY AND MORE IMPORTANT FOR THIS ROW'S SCOPE: ClimaLand's snow albedo multiplies by `min(1 - beta*(rho_snow/rho_liq - x0), 1)`, so in peer practice snow density reaches albedo DIRECTLY as a grain-size proxy and not only through cover depth as this row has it. At the 330 kg/m3 constant that factor is 0.874. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 37a

DEDUPLICATION DONE 2026-08-25, commit e8054980. icemod's hardcoded CRHOSN is gone: crhosn is a module variable set in iceini from a new argument that seaini passes landmod's rhosnow into, so 330 is declared once and the namelist key reaches the sea-ice column too. landini runs before seaini in surfini and no crhosn site is reached at initialisation, so what icemod reads is always the value the namelist set. Correctness-neutral, as the row said it would be.

AND THE BRACKET WAS NOT SOUND. snowcap, the snow layer's heat capacity per unit volume, was a SEPARATE namelist key held fixed while rhosnow moved. It is not independent: volumetric heat capacity is density times the specific heat of ice, and layer thickness is water equivalent over that same density, so the thermal mass of a given snowfall does not depend on the density at all. A bracket on rhosnow was therefore moving the pack's thermal mass with it, which is not something the density does. landini now derives snowcap = rhosnow * 2090 after the broadcast and it has left landmod_nl; at the shipped rhosnow the value is 0.6897E6 to the digit, so no result changes. Nothing in the tree ever set it.

THE OTHER HALF OF THE BRACKET IS STILL OPEN and is world-a9s5: snowdiff is density-dependent in the same way and is NOT coupled, because choosing which measured conductivity relation to use is a decision with a source rather than arithmetic, and Sturm 1997 at 330 kg/m3 returns about 0.157 W/m/K against the 0.31 declared here. So a bracket on rhosnow today moves thickness and thermal mass correctly and leaves conductivity where it stands, and the ground heat flux under a pack goes as k/z.

WHAT REMAINS IN THIS ROW is the compaction term itself, unchanged in scope. It was NOT added at rebuild_binaries and the reason is this row own sequencing: the deliverable is what the term is worth on cover depth and albedo, priced offline against an existing climatology BEFORE any source change, which is bootstrap_run work. hydrography/config/land_water_ledger.yaml still declares snow_compaction an unrepresentable and that statement is still true: the density is still a constant and there is still no compaction. Adding a prognostic density now would import Kojima viscosity coefficients as a fresh set of Earth-calibrated constants without the pricing that says what they are worth at 1.306 g.
close_reason:
PRICED OFFLINE against a bootstrap climatology BEFORE any source change, which is this row's own sequencing -- and the pricing reverses the row's framing three times.

THE RATE RATIO IS NOT THE STATE RATIO. Compaction runs 1.306x Earth's, linear in g as PALADYN's Kojima term says. The DENSITY it produces runs 1.06x -- 161 to 170 kg/m3 at the median -- because this world's modelled snow does not survive long enough for the load term to dominate. Reading the rate as a state overstates it fivefold, and that is the shape of the row's own headline.

THE CONSTANT IS WORTH SIX TIMES WHAT GRAVITY IS. On the pack's conductive resistance z/k, the compiled 330 gives a median 0.291 m2K/W against 2.044 at a prognostic 161 and 1.780 at 170: prognostic over constant is 6.05 (p5 1.96, p95 17.2), where this-g over Earth-g is 0.864.

AND A GRAVITY-ONLY PAIR CANNOT SEPARATE THE TERM FROM THE ARM. Gravity moves the resistance 15.8 per cent; the vapour-kinetics bracket the conductivity already carries moves it 53.1 per cent at the same density. Checking the instrument against the size of the effect is failure-modes class 34, and here it decides the experiment.

ON THE MODELLED SURFACE ALBEDO IT IS EXACTLY ZERO. landmod takes cover fraction as dsnow/(dsnow+snowcovz) in WATER EQUIVALENT, so density cancels identically; the only density-to-albedo path is the canopy burial depth in snowcanopymask, read only when forhgt > 0, which it is not. Recorded with two external checks: ClimaLand's density-albedo beta is a free parameter with no citation, and PALADYN puts no density in albedo at all.

SO THE PAIR WORTH BUYING IS THE CONSTANT AGAINST A PROGNOSTIC DENSITY, not two gravities -- which is the opposite experiment to the one this row implied, and adding a prognostic density now would import Kojima viscosity coefficients as fresh Earth-calibrated constants to settle a term smaller than the bracket already present.

title: Glacier orography is built from Earth's mass and radius rather than the model's gravity.
description:
Glacier orography is built from Earth's mass and radius rather than the model's gravity. `glaciermod.f90:352-356` computes `radius = 6.371e6` and `grav = gconst*p_mass/(radius+dz)**2` with `p_mass` Earth's mass, evaluating to 9.8200 m/s2 against the model's `ga = 12.81`. Glacier thickness is converted to geopotential with that value and every reader divides by `ga` to recover metres, INCLUDING PRINTOUTS IN THE SAME FILE, so **a glacier enters the orography at 0.767 of its physical thickness, understated by 23.3 percent**. The `dz` recovered from ground geopotential on the line above is wrong by the reciprocal for the same reason, and `radius = 6.371e6` overrides a latitude-dependent ellipsoid form sitting commented out two lines up, leaving the WGS84 constants dead

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 56b
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:

Rule 4's gate is discharged: all 12 binaries rebuilt from `vendor/exoplasim` at b7854949, `--verify` reports all 12 current against the sha of the source they were built from, and `check_consistency.py` passes `binaries carry current patches` at 29 checks 0 failed. A COMPILE PROVES THE CODE BUILDS AND NOT THAT THE NUMBERS ARE RIGHT; the correction is 1.4 m of elevation at the current snow cap and linear in thickness, so its value is in landing before the external ice-sheet path uses it. The clean negative is re-swept and now reads zero non-`ga` gravities anywhere in the surface modules.

title: Declare this world's ROTATION DIRECTION and its PRIME MERIDIAN
description:
Declare this world's ROTATION DIRECTION and its PRIME MERIDIAN, both of which are currently defaulted rather than chosen. `config/planet.yaml` carries a signless `rotation_hours: 30.0` and nothing anywhere says prograde or retrograde; the model runs it prograde by omission, because a positive rotation period becomes a positive rotation speed. `maps/README.md` says the prime meridian is drawn heavier and nothing says which meridian it is or what fixes it. THESE ARE COUPLED, and the IAU convention is what couples them: `archinal2018-iau-cartographic-coordinates-and-rotational-elements.pdf` defines prograde as `W` increasing with time and retrograde as `W` decreasing, where `W` is the angle from the ascending node to the prime meridian -- so rotation direction and meridian phase are one declaration, not two. The report also provides for exactly this world's case: "for planets or satellites with no accurately observable fixed surface features, the expression for W defines the prime meridian", so what is available here is a PHASE, not a landmark. Longitude is positive east by construction -- `maps/projections.py` fixes the handedness -- which is IAU-correct for planetocentric and is nowhere written as a decision

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 49c, `references/archinal2018-iau-cartographic-coordinates-and-rotational-elements.pdf`

title: Give the water table an internal sink
description:
Give the water table an internal sink

Source: `hydrography/notes/groundwater-et-sink.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20. Groundwater evapotranspiration, EXPONENTIAL in water table depth on Shah, Nachabe and Ross (2007), whose finding is that "the decline of ET with DTWT is better simulated by an exponential decay function than the commonly used linear decay" -- MODFLOW's EVT package uses the linear form and this does not. Head-dependent, so a Newton step folded into the active-set loop, and benign where GW-9's exponential transmissivity was not: dE/dh is POSITIVE and lands on the diagonal with the sign that strengthens diagonal dominance. OFF unless asked for, and the inert path is `np.array_equal` to the pre-change result with closure's ET door reading exactly 0.0. Closure now has three doors and balances at 1e-15 to 1e-13. A PREDICTION WAS RECORDED BEFORE IMPLEMENTING AND ONE HALF OF IT FAILED, which is the finding. Pinning went as predicted, 95.5% to 0.0%. The model did NOT acquire skill: residual standard deviation 40.05 m, which IS the observed 40.05, Pearson +0.031, 0.1% of variance. And the miss is not the predicted missing tail -- the whole distribution is compressed, the model spanning a factor of 1.9 between its 5th and 95th percentiles against the observations' 56.5. The mechanism works exactly as designed and that is how we know: `d = lambda ln(ET_max/R)` makes the model a near-deterministic function of recharge at Spearman -0.977, and the real water table is not one, at -0.156. A logarithm turns Australia's factor of 900 in recharge into a factor of 13 in depth, and the recharge present compresses it further. THE SINK STAYS: right physics, real source, removes a state the data says is wrong, free when off. It is necessary and not sufficient, and what is left is GW-6, which this measures for the second and sharper time

title: Make aquifer thickness spatially varying
description:
Make aquifer thickness spatially varying, from a sediment-thickness source rather than the constant 100 m that is Gleeson's map depth

Source: `hydrography/notes/groundwater-et-sink.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and NARROWED by GW-17: a uniform 2 km with local baselevels already fixes the RANGE, taking the 95th percentile depth from 6.9 m to 52 m against an observed 42 m, so what a spatially varying thickness has left to buy is PATTERN. On the evidence it will not buy much: no resolvable field predicts observed depth above Spearman 0.27, and height above the nearest river -- the mechanism thickness would strengthen -- is the weakest at 0.064. Do it for the range being physically sourced rather than assumed, not expecting skill [step: hydrography]

IMPLEMENTED AND OFF, 2026-08-24, and the row's own framing needs a correction. aquifer.thickness_source: cover_thickness in hydrography/config/groundwater.yaml, with --aquifer-thickness-source on build_groundwater.py, takes the saturated thickness from the export's own surviving cover over basement, floored at Gleeson's 100 m. It is a THICKNESS and not a history, so docs/src/reference/no-time-axis.md does not refuse it: the field is the thickness that is there now, not an accumulation over a duration. THE FLOOR IS SOURCED, not chosen: Gleeson's 'on the order of 100 m' is the depth his lithology maps describe and that depth exists wherever there is rock, so the cover adds basin fill on top of a shallow subsurface already there, and exposed basement keeps the floor rather than dropping out of the conductive network on a zero.

THE CORRECTION. This row says a uniform 2 km already fixes the RANGE and what a spatially varying thickness has left to buy is PATTERN. Measured on precarve-craton-10m: floored at 100 m, 35.9% of land sits on the floor because it carries no cover at all, the land median is 365 m, the 95th percentile 998 m, the maximum 2950 m, the area-weighted mean 380 m, and ONLY 0.4% OF LAND REACHES 2 km. So a sourced thickness does not source that range, it contradicts it over 99.6% of the land. The prediction, written into the config before any run: the depth range shrinks and cratonic cells move from lateral-flow control back towards the local recharge-and-ET balance, which sink_fraction reports per cell. A loss of range with no gain in pattern is a real possible outcome and the run decides.

IT COSTS NOTHING STRUCTURALLY, which is the difference from GW-24. A spatially varying D under the confined form leaves T independent of the head, so the matrix stays fixed, the problem stays a linear complementarity problem, and every identity is untouched. GW-18 hands the solver a MULTIPLIER; GW-24 hands it a DATUM off the same field. One field, two readings, and only the second changes the class of the problem -- so they are not the same change.

THE FLOOR MAY NOT GO LOWER, and GW-6's rule is why. The unconfined form's cell mean is exact only where the saturated column is about three times the sub-grid relief: at 100 m against this world's median neighbour spread of 20 m the Jensen term is under 0.02%, and against the roughest quartile's 117 m it reaches tens of percent. A thinner floor puts the parameterisation into the range where it has no cell mean, which is Fan's disqualification.

OPEN pending the run: python hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater.py --aquifer-thickness-source cover_thickness --uniqueness-check, then the same arm through hydrography/scripts/earth_calibration.py with an Earth sediment thickness, which this project does not yet hold and which is the second half of this row. What to read: the 95th percentile depth against GW-17's 52 m, sink_fraction, and Pearson on cell means. hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 4.

SIZED AGAINST THE INSTRUMENT, 2026-08-25, and GW-8 does not stand in the way. A sourced thickness is a multiplier on the transmissivity spanning a factor of thirty across this world's land -- 100 m on the floor to 2,950 m at the maximum -- which is an ORDER-ONE perturbation to the operator and not a small one. groundwater.py --instrument scores the operator on a transmissivity RESPONSE against an exact analytic answer and finds the response carried with a relative error of 0.12193 at an amplitude of 0.01 and 0.12193 at 0.2: the error is a fraction of the RESPONSE, not of the field, because the confined assembly is linear in T. So the discretisation carries a thickness field at the same relative accuracy it carries anything else, and GW-8's 12% is not a reason to leave this off. hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 4 carries the sizing.

SHOULD IT EXIST: yes. The row already argues that a thickness is a state and not a history, so docs/src/reference/no-time-axis.md does not refuse it, and it is not inside the ledger's transient_saturated_storage absence either: that absence is storage CHANGE, and a per-cell D is a static parameter field. It costs nothing structurally, which is the row's own finding.

ONE OBSTACLE REMOVED. report_path and the water table's own filename did not carry --aquifer-thickness-source, so the sourced arm would have written groundwater_report.json and water_table.nc over the constant run's. Both now tag the variant, so the pair can be run and compared without either taking the product's name.

STILL OPEN, AND WHAT IS MISSING IS A RUN THAT HAS NEVER EXISTED ON THIS BUILD. hydrography/data/precarve-craton-10m carries no water table at all, under either thickness source, so the comparison this row rests on has no baseline arm either. The pair is

    python hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater.py --climatology exoplasim/analysis/climatology/bootstrap_regular_climatology.nc
    python hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater.py --aquifer-thickness-source cover_thickness --climatology exoplasim/analysis/climatology/bootstrap_regular_climatology.nc

the second now writing water_table_cover_thickness.nc beside the first, and config/planet.yaml declares no baseline_climatology so the forcing must be named by hand and its numbers are a bootstrap's. Each arm is a Voronoi dual and an active-set solve on 10,000,005 regions; this host carried a load average of 17 to 52 with another session on it and could not give them clean hours.

title: The water table's dependence structure is wrong
description:
The water table's dependence structure is wrong, and it is not resolution and not the arithmetic. Measured on Earth at three cell sizes: the model is a monotone function of recharge, Spearman -0.90 to -0.93 where the truth is -0.27, and carries no elevation signal at all, -0.047 to -0.003, while the observations' strengthens as cells shrink, +0.125 to +0.199. The suspect is the sink rather than the transmissivity: with `E(h) = et_max exp(-(z-h)/lambda)` the supply-and-sink balance has the closed form `d = lambda ln(et_max A / supply)`, which `et_balance_depth` computes directly and which mentions no neighbour, so at `lambda` = 1 m it is a local clamp that can express a few metres of range from recharge alone and leaves nothing for the lateral term to organise

Source: `hydrography/notes/earth-calibration-criterion.md`, `hydrography/notes/water-table-convergence.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and the answer is neither of the two things this row first blamed. CORRECTION, and it is this row's own: an earlier draft proposed re-running with Fan's depth-decaying transmissivity and said GW-9's argument against it "was never measured". Both halves were wrong. The argument IS quantitative and sits in `groundwater.py:transmissivity`: `exp(h/f)` is convex, so a cell mean over a water table varying within the cell by `sigma` carries `exp(sigma^2/2f^2)`, and 100 m of sub-grid relief against the 0.95 m `f` Fan reaches on steep bedrock makes that `exp(5000)` -- not a correction to apply but a statement that the parameterisation has no value at this cell size, and refining to 7.60 km does not rescue it. And the proposed experiment is the one that already failed: `water-table-convergence.md` records that Picard on the transmissivity LIMIT-CYCLES, because `T` moves by a factor of e per e-folding length so the map is not a contraction, and the damping that stopped the oscillation held the water balance residual flat instead of converging. Two solvers died there. Do not re-run it. MEASURED INSTEAD. The sink does set depth locally: median depth is linear in `lambda`, 5.12/10.23/25.51/50.86/126.35 m at 1/2/5/10/25 m, and rho(model, recharge) is pinned at -0.90 throughout. But raising `D` from 100 m to 20 km moves rho(model, elevation) -0.047 to +0.466 and rho(model, recharge) -0.902 to -0.245, bracketing the observed +0.125 and -0.272, so the dependence structure IS reachable with the formulation in hand, and agreement still does not follow: Pearson stays between +0.058 and +0.101 across `D` over 200-fold, `lambda` over 25-fold, and the sink on or off. SECOND CORRECTION: this row and GW-6 quoted Pearson and said no skill. On RANK the model has Spearman +0.276, +0.291 at best, which is not nothing and the claim is withdrawn. What it is, though, is exactly the recharge field's own rank agreement, -0.272, so the flow solve recovers what its forcing already carried and adds under 0.02. R^2 stays negative and worsens with `D`, -0.365 to -7.025, because the spread overshoots to 45 and 75 m against the observed 28.5. So the limit is the INPUTS, not the formulation and not the mesh: recharge, GLHYMPS at 15 km and a cell-mean elevation do not determine this water table, and no rewriting of a flow equation adds information its forcing lacks. What would reopen it is a better forcing, not a better solver: a recharge product that is not itself a climatology-derived proxy, or a permeability field with real aquifer structure rather than surface lithology. The saturated-thickness form `T = K (h - z_bottom)` remains the one untried formulation worth a look, being linear in head and so free of both the Jensen term and the factor of e that killed the exponential, but on this evidence it would be tidying rather than a fix [step: hydrography]

title: The Earth calibration has only ever been run on Australia
description:
The Earth calibration has only ever been run on Australia, and `docs/src/reference/external-data.md` says take Australia FIRST, not only. The second leg was never run and was never tracked. It matters more now than when that was written: GW-21 concluded the limit is the INPUT FIELDS rather than the formulation or the mesh, and that conclusion rests on one region; and the confound flagged against it, that Australia contains the Great Artesian Basin and a bore screened below the water table measures a potentiometric head in a confined aquifer, is Australia-specific

Source: `docs/src/reference/external-data.md`, `hydrography/notes/earth-calibration-criterion.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and it OVERTURNS the Australian verdict rather than confirming it. On 73,451 bores the USGS labels unconfined -- a water table, which is what the solver computes, rather than the potentiometric head a confined bore reads -- the cell-mean correlation is +0.2599 against Australia's +0.0703, and the model's spread is 20.72 m against an observed 28.94 where in Australia it was 1.91 against 18.36. Fitting a two-parameter bias correction on half the cells and scoring the other half over twenty splits gives held-out R2 = 0.0646 with a standard deviation of 0.0216, clearing the declared 0.07 bar on 9 of them: it STRADDLES the bar rather than passing it, and one favourable split alone read +0.0748. Repeated on the wide domain, modelled from 15 to 60 north and 130 to 60 west so neither land border is a fake coast, the answer moves in the third decimal, which retires that worry and says `score_bbox` was already doing the work. THE FINDING IS A REGIME. Where the sink takes the recharge locally the steady state collapses to `lambda ln(et_max A / supply)` and the flow solve contributes no variance; where lateral flow carries it the solve does real work, which is why the same model behaves differently on two continents. That is measurable per cell, so `water_table.nc` now ships `sink_fraction` beside the depth and a consumer can ask which of three cases a cell is in: a recharge map near 1, a pinned and seeping cell when `at_surface` is also set, or a flow solution. So the depth field's restriction is a regime statement rather than a blanket failure. What this does NOT establish is which regime Vesper is in: the sink takes a median 97.0% of recharge on this build, but that is a bootstrap climatology on pre-carve terrain, and applying a carve verdict once took endorheic land from 60.10% to 43.06%, so the premise is a property of the open loop. Re-read `sink_fraction` after a baseline. Canada stays unfetched and stays lowest priority for the reason already recorded. Superseded plan: cheaper than it looks, because the expensive parts are already built and region-independent: the Fibonacci mesh and its `Geometry` are GLOBAL and cached, GLHYMPS is local at 1.3 GB and needs only a different bbox, and recharge is a global Zenodo product read by byte-range window, so the US needs different row and column indices and nothing else. What is new is a US DEM window and the wells. The USGS route in `external-data.md` is live and needs no key, PROBED 2026-08-20: `api.waterdata.usgs.gov/ogcapi/v0/collections/field-measurements/items?parameter_code=72019` returns 200 with `value`, `unit_of_measure` of ft, `monitoring_location_id`, `vertical_datum` and a `qualifier` carrying Static, which is the pumping filter `external-data.md` says Fan's four columns cannot support. `numberMatched` is absent so the volume is unknown and it will need pagination. Fan's own `US_obs_wtd.txt.gz` at 7 MB is the fallback and is on the recovered AquaKnow mirror, but it lacks the well-use metadata that makes the filter possible. Canada stays lowest priority for the reason already recorded, that it is provincial rather than national and repeats the US regime. What would settle GW-21: if US rank skill is again its recharge field's own, the input-limited finding generalises; if it is materially better, Australia's confined systems were the problem and the Australian verdict is too harsh [step: hydrography]

title: Groundwater leaves an unconfined aquifer through unmapped first and second order gullies
description:
Groundwater leaves an unconfined aquifer through unmapped first and second order gullies at hundreds of metres, not by crossing a 15.19 km cell to a mapped river, and the solver knows only the mapped network. So recharge has no local outlet and piles up until a REGIONAL gradient can carry it, which is the shape GW-21 measured: without the evapotranspiration sink 91.4% of cells pin at the surface, and with it the depth is a local recharge balance. The discarded input is real and is the right size. Binning the 1.855 km ETOPO into the 15.19 km Australian mesh, at a median 95 pixels a cell, the within-cell relief the mean throws away is 14.8 m of standard deviation and 25.9 m from mean to minimum at the median, against an observed water table depth whose median is 7.6 to 9.8 m. The relief being averaged out is about three times the signal being predicted

Source: `hydrography/notes/earth-calibration-criterion.md`, `docs/src/reference/external-data.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done, tested at its bounding limit 2026-08-20, and it does not hold, but the investigation found a real defect and that is the part to keep. `C -> infinity` is a fixed head at the cell's own valley floor, which `fixed_head_m` supplies for free, so the family is bounded without a solver term: 22,284 of 26,372 Australian land cells have 10 m or more of relief to vent into, at a median of 30 m, and draining them INVERTS the correlation below the cell mean, +0.0703 to -0.0575, and costs below the bore, +0.1341 to +0.0492, over-draining to a median 25.5 m against an observed 12.9. Both ends of the family are without skill, so a finite `C` would have to beat both, which nothing measured suggests. THE DEFECT, which is the useful half: the model's depth hung from the DEM CELL MEAN and the bore's from the ground at the bore, two different surfaces, and bores sit a mean 8.4 m below their cell mean because wells are in valleys. Hanging both from the DEM takes Pearson +0.0703 to +0.1341 with NO change to the model, the largest single improvement anywhere in this work, and it means every earlier score including GW-3's and GW-21's was measured against the wrong surface. It is still not skill: R2 -3.05, spread 36.18 m against 28.19 observed, because a flat cell head plus each bore's own ground gives the depth all of the relief. Do NOT mix the observation's own surveyed elevation in: it disagrees with the DEM at sd 51.97 m and that lands whole on the residual, R2 -18.0. What remains open is the middle of the bracket rather than the drain: the true within-cell behaviour sits between a model spread of 3.96 m and 36.18 m with the observations at 28.19, which is a three-number target for any sub-grid parameterisation. Superseded approach kept for the record: a head-dependent sub-grid drain per cell rather than a finer mesh, `Q = C max(0, h - z_valley)`, with `z_valley` from the within-cell DEM minimum or `mean - 2 sigma` and `C` scaled by a drainage-density proxy. That is a Robin condition and the solver has no term for it; the existing `fixed_head_m` gives its `C -> infinity` limit for free and BOUNDS the effect, so run that first. TWO THINGS TO WATCH, both from measurements already taken. A direct correlation of within-cell relief against observed depth is only -0.10 Spearman against recharge's -0.27, but that test is confounded by the bias `external-data.md` records from Fan, that wells sit in valleys, so the bores already report valley-floor depths and relief cannot predict them; the real mismatch is that a CELL-MEAN head is being scored against VALLEY-SITED bores, which is what this term would fix. And a sub-grid drain is another LOCAL sink, so it risks reproducing the evapotranspiration sink's pathology; the difference that matters is that its balance is set by terrain, `h = z_valley + Q/C`, where the sink's is set by recharge, `d = lambda ln(et_max/supply)`, which is the dependence GW-21 found missing. Falsifier: Pearson rising off 0.07 and rho(model, elevation) moving toward the observations' +0.20. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY: this is measurable on Earth, where a 1.855 km DEM sits under a 15.19 km cell, and NOT on Vesper, where `notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md` finds the generator designs nothing below about 20 km, so `z_valley` there would have to be parameterised rather than measured. That is GW-6 with a job to do [step: hydrography]
close_reason: done, tested at its bounding limit 2026-08-20, and it does not hold, but the investigation found a real defect and that is the part to keep.

title: Depth-dependent transmissivity is the governor the model lacks
description:
Depth-dependent transmissivity is the governor the model lacks, and it is not the same lever as transmissivity MAGNITUDE. GW-21 raised constant `D` from 100 m to 20 km and did move the dependence structure onto the observed values, rho(model, elevation) -0.047 to +0.466 and rho(model, recharge) -0.902 to -0.245, but that raises `T` everywhere at once. A depth-dependent `T` raises it only where the table is SHALLOW, which is a self-limiting local governor rather than a global flattening, and the uniform sweep cannot stand in for it

Source: `hydrography/notes/water-table-convergence.md`, `hydrography/notes/earth-calibration-criterion.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and NOT via Fan's exponential, which is excluded twice over and measured both times: `exp(h/f)` is convex so a cell mean carries `exp(sigma^2/2f^2)`, which at 100 m of sub-grid relief against the 0.95 m `f` Fan reaches on steep bedrock is `exp(5000)`, and Picard on it LIMIT-CYCLES because `T` moves by a factor of e per e-folding length so the map is not a contraction. Two solvers died there; do not re-run it. The form to try is saturated thickness, `T = K (h - z_bottom)`, the textbook unconfined case the constant `D` currently approximates as confined. It is depth-selective, so it carries the governor; it is LINEAR in head, so cell-averaging is exact and there is no Jensen term; and it is Boussinesq, which under the Kirchhoff substitution `u = (h - z_bottom)^2 / 2` is exactly linear for uniform `K` and `z_bottom`, so the fixed point that killed the exponential does not arise. The `h <= z` box constraint survives the substitution monotonically, as `u <= (z - z_bottom)^2 / 2`, so the complementarity structure is kept [step: hydrography]

IMPLEMENTED AND OFF, 2026-08-24, and the premise is HALF WITHDRAWN. The form is the one this row named: T = K (h - z_bottom), saturated thickness, linear in the head and so with an exact cell mean at any resolution, which is what Fan's exponential lacked. groundwater.py carries it behind aquifer.transmissivity: unconfined and --unconfined; the confined default assembles exactly as before and the confined 1-D analytic case reproduces to 2e-15.

WHAT IS WITHDRAWN. This row calls it 'the governor the model lacks' and says the uniform sweep cannot stand in for it. The first half does not survive its own size. The unconfined correction to the head is depth/2D, the fraction of the saturated column the table has drained. On the Australian anchor -- 8 mm/yr, 15 km to a baselevel, Gleeson median K -- that is 0.48% (0.09 m) at GW-17's 2 km, 1.9% (0.7 m) at 1 km, 14% (15 m) at this world's sourced median of 365 m, and at 100 m the confined mound is already 381 m over 15 km so the table pins and the sink sets the depth instead. Against a model spread of 1.91 m in Australia and 20.72 m in the United States and observed spreads of 18.36 and 28.94 m, the term is negligible in the configuration that reproduces the observed RANGE and large only in the configuration already known wrong for a different reason. The second half stands: it is a different lever from magnitude, and it is in.

AND IT IS MEASURABLE WITHOUT SOLVING FOR IT. build_groundwater.py now reports saturated_column_drained from the CONFINED run -- depth/D per cell at the 50th, 75th, 95th and 99th percentiles -- because that IS the fraction the confined transmissivity is wrong by. The decision to enable --unconfined rests on that number from the run in hand.

WHAT IT COSTS, measured on a synthetic 1-D aquifer via groundwater.py --dupuit-test. The Kirchhoff identity is exact on a flat base, 4.6e-15 and 1.1e-14 against a bar of 1e-12 declared first, and the analytic Dupuit parabola is recovered to 3.6e-12 against a declared 1e-3. But: (1) T depends on the head, so the LINEAR complementarity structure goes and --uniqueness-check stops being an identity, becoming a measurement against UNCONFINED_HEAD_RELATIVE = 1e-6, declared before any unconfined run; (2) the static dry set survives only because min_saturated_thickness_m is strictly positive, which is why that floor is structural; (3) the Picard rate is governed by the SAME number as the effect -- 8 passes at a saturated-column contrast of 1.12, 12 at 1.60, 18 at 5.07, and no convergence in 60 at 24.9; (4) a SLOPING aquifer base, which is what a real one has, is a different problem and not a perturbation: at 1 in 1000 the Kirchhoff identity departs by 17.6% and the solution by 15.4% from the flat-base parabola, so the exactness above is the instrument and not the solver.

OPEN BECAUSE IT NEEDS A RUN THIS HOST COULD NOT GIVE IT. Nothing here touched the real mesh, and convergence rather than algebra is where the two previous depth-dependent solvers died. To settle it:
  python hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater.py --unconfined --uniqueness-check
  python hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater.py --unconfined --reduction-test
  python hydrography/scripts/earth_calibration.py   # with the unconfined arm
answering, in order: does it converge on 10M regions inside the pass budget; does the reduction identity still hold bitwise at zero permeability; do the two active-set trajectories land within 1e-6 relative; and does the dependence structure GW-21 showed is reachable by transmissivity MAGNITUDE alone become reachable in a way that also moves the AGREEMENT, which raising D uniformly never did. hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 3.

SIZED AGAINST THE INSTRUMENT, 2026-08-25, and GW-8 does not stand in the way. Reading GW-8's 12% as a noise floor on solved fields would have said this term is unmeasurable except at the 365 m thickness, where the model is already known wrong. That reading is refuted and GW-8 is closed on the measurement: groundwater.py --instrument fits the TRUNCATION error at an order of 0.004 in the cell size over a 64-fold refinement of Orogen's own generator -- it does not converge at all -- while the SOLVED head's error fits 1.994 to 2.008 and is 2.766e-06 relative on precarve-craton, an extrapolated 6.9e-07 on the active build. Every entry in this row's own table (0.48% of the head at 2 km, 1.9% at 1 km, 14% at 365 m) is orders above that. So the mesh is not the limit, and the row's own half-withdrawal stands unchanged: what limits the term is the model's between-cell spread, not the discretisation. hydrography/notes/mesh-geometry.md carries the tables and hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 3 carries the sizing.

SHOULD IT EXIST: yes, and the ledger does not refuse it. config/land_water_ledger.yaml declares transient_saturated_storage unrepresentable and owned by PLHY-4, and that absence is seasonal head, aquifer storage and a transient capillary or baseflow response. T = K (h - z_bottom) evaluated at the STEADY head is still an equilibrium and adds no storage term, so the groundwater store's declared limit is untouched.

TWO OBSTACLES REMOVED. report_path and the water table's own filename did not know about --unconfined, so an unconfined run without --output would have written groundwater_report.json and water_table.nc over the product every note cites and every consumer resolves; both now carry the variant tag, so the arms can be compared without either clobbering the product. And earth_calibration.py, which the third of this row's three named commands calls, has NO unconfined arm at all -- stage_solve never passes aquifer_base_m and stage_calibrate's D sweep is confined only -- so that command cannot be run as written. Filed as world-2bni.

STILL OPEN AND THE BLOCKER IS UNCHANGED. Nothing here touched the real mesh. The three commands need a Voronoi dual and an active-set solve on precarve-craton-10m's 10,000,005 regions, and this host carried a load average of 17 to 52 with another session on it throughout.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTERED 2026-08-30, BEFORE THE FIRST RUN ON THE ACTIVE BUILD.

The active build is now canonical-10m-carve2 and a BASELINE climatology exists for it (run_67323a923013, 57 orbits). Neither was true when this row was last worked, so the numbers in the notes above were measured on precarve-craton-10m and are not this build's.

WHAT IS ABOUT TO BE MEASURED AND THE BAR IT IS JUDGED BY.

1. MATERIALITY ON VESPER. This row's own text says the decision to enable --unconfined rests on saturated_column_drained from the CONFINED run in hand, because that IS the fraction the confined transmissivity is wrong by, and the head correction is half of it. Bar declared now: the term is material only if the MEDIAN saturated_column_drained is at least 0.05, so that the confined head is wrong by at least 2.5% on typical land. Below that the correction is under a twentieth of the model's own between-cell spread wherever that spread is of the order of the depth, and cannot move a between-cell correlation. Reported alongside and not part of the bar: the 75th, 95th and 99th percentiles.

2. CONVERGENCE FEASIBILITY. groundwater.py --dupuit-test measured Picard at 8 passes at a saturated-column contrast of 1.12, 18 at 5.07 and no convergence in 60 at 24.9. Declared now: the ratio of the 99th to the 1st percentile of the saturated column on conductive land is the predictor, and a value above 25 predicts non-convergence in the budget. It is a PREDICTION recorded before the unconfined run, not a bar the run must clear.

3. THE IDENTITIES, already declared elsewhere and not restated here: --uniqueness-check against UNCONFINED_HEAD_RELATIVE = 1e-6, --reduction-test bitwise at zero permeability, and config/groundwater.yaml aquifer.unconfined_criterion for the Earth harness (declared 2026-08-25, three conditions at one thickness).

WHAT WOULD MEAN WRONG: a uniqueness measurement above 1e-6 relative, a reduction identity that is not bitwise, or a solve that does not converge in the pass budget. Any of those refuses the unconfined arm on this mesh regardless of what the criterion above says.
