title: Every Earth score this project has recorded hangs the model's depth from the DEM CELL MEAN
description:
Every Earth score this project has recorded hangs the model's depth from the DEM CELL MEAN and the observation's from the ground at the bore. Those are different surfaces: measured on 48,552 Australian bores, the DEM at a bore sits a mean 8.4 m below its cell mean, because wells are in valleys, which is the bias Fan states and `external-data.md` records. Hanging both from the DEM takes Pearson +0.0703 to +0.1341 with no change to the model at all, which is the largest single improvement found in this work and makes it a measurement defect rather than a modelling one

Source: `hydrography/notes/earth-calibration-criterion.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and the answer is that the default STAYS `cell-mean`. Treating the two surfaces as ends of a subdued-replica family, `h(x) = h_cell + alpha (z(x) - z_cell)`, and sweeping alpha shows the three measures disagreeing about where to stand: Pearson peaks near 0.8, Spearman and R2 are both best at 1.0, and the rule declared before looking at correlations, match the observed 28.49 m spread, picks 0.36 and is worse than either end on two of three. The attribution is why: `delta`, where a bore sits within its own cell, predicts observed depth at Pearson +0.1290 ALONE, against the model's +0.0703, so the near-doubling is a geometric covariate folded into the model's score rather than model skill recovered. A joint least squares on model and `delta` reaches R2 +0.0208 against a statistical fit's 0.2098. `--surface dem-at-bore` stays available and labelled, and this sharpens GW-21: the model does not merely fail to add to its recharge forcing, it is out-predicted by pure geometry carrying no groundwater physics at all. Two things to settle before flipping it. The corrected scoring is not simply better: Pearson nearly doubles while R2 goes -0.365 to -3.05 because the spread goes to 36.18 m against 28.19 observed, since a flat cell head plus each bore's own ground gives the depth ALL of the within-cell relief. Neither surface is right and GW-23 brackets the truth between them, so the honest default may be to report both rather than pick. And restating the archived numbers matters: GW-3's R2 = 0.017 against a bar of 0.07, and GW-21's conclusion that the inputs limit the score, were both measured against the wrong surface. title: Compute a compound topographic index on the native mesh and derive a saturated-AREA closure
description:
Compute a compound topographic index on the native mesh and derive a saturated-AREA closure from it, which is the quantity GW-6 declared unrecoverable as a DEPTH. `f_sat = f_sat_max * exp(-f_grad * z_grad)` under TOPMODEL is how PALADYN obtains wetland area without resolving the valley-to-ridge gradient, and the change of quantity is the point: a per-cell saturated FRACTION rather than the per-cell depth GW-3 and GW-22 measured as regime-dependent. PALADYN takes `f_sat_max` from ETOPO1 because CLIMBER-X has no sub-grid terrain; here the 15.19 km region mesh under a roughly 300 km T42 cell IS that population, and `hydrography` already holds the upslope contributing area the index needs beside a local slope. SHAPE: one artifact per (build, grid) on the coupling-matrix precedent, carrying the index and the closure, with `f_grad` DECLARED and bracketed rather than fitted. It is NOT GRID-2's hypsometry -- an elevation distribution is not a topographic index -- though both come off the same mesh

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3a, `hydrography/notes/earth-calibration-criterion.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and it must be scored against something that can FAIL before any consumer takes it: the fraction is untested here, inheriting the depth's bias through `z_grad` is the obvious failure mode, and the bar is declared before the score. Use the same two-continent observation sets the depth was scored on, which are already cached. Consumers are WET-2's wetness classification, SURF-7's discharge mask and LSHY-6's mosaic, and none may take it before that score exists. A DECISION rides along and must be stated rather than defaulted: PALADYN estimates its grid-cell mean water table from column water content and not from a lateral solve, so whether that estimator and this project's Dupuit-Forchheimer solution are reconciled or kept as separate estimators is open [step: hydrography, groundwater]. A SECOND INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATION, WITH FOUR THINGS THIS ROW LACKS, 2026-08-22. ClimaLand's `src/standalone/Soil/Runoff/Runoff.jl` implements SIMTOP, Niu et al. (2005). (1) A FACTOR OF TWO AND ONE CONSTANT FOR BOTH FLUXES: `f_sat = min(f_max*exp(-f_over/2*z), 1)` while `R_ss = R_sb*exp(-f_over*z)`, so the surface decay is HALF the subsurface decay and a single calibrated constant sets both -- bracketing it moves surface and subsurface runoff together, which the form as stated here does not show. (2) The `min(...,1)` cap is explicit. (3) PARAMETER PROVENANCE SPLITS EXACTLY THE WAY THIS ROW WANTS: `f_over` and `R_sb` are labelled "calibrated" in their docstrings, while `f_max` is "computed from the topographic index CDF per grid cell" -- terrain-derived, and computable here from the region mesh -- which independently supports declaring and bracketing `f_grad` rather than fitting it. (4) ICE: the saturated column is computed TWICE, including ice for the surface saturated fraction and liquid-only for the subsurface flux, so frozen ground makes saturation-excess surface runoff but no subsurface flow. Neither this row nor PALADYN's form carries that, and it matters in a cold winter hemisphere. ON THE DECISION THIS ROW FLAGS: ClimaLand also estimates water table depth from column water content rather than a lateral solve, so the column estimator is the field's normal practice and the Dupuit-Forchheimer solution is the departure that needs the argument. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 36. A THIRD CONSUMER OF THIS INDEX, WITH A CALIBRATION REQUIREMENT, 2026-08-22. CLIMBER-X's three wetland-extent schemes at `src/lnd/surface_hydro.f90:565-613` -- SIMTOP, DYPTOP and a CTI-CDF lookup -- all key off a per-gridcell compound topographic index, after PALADYN and ClimaLand's SIMTOP. THE CONSTRAINT THAT RIDES ALONG: `cti_mean_crit = 5.5` is an absolute threshold below which no wetland forms, so this row's index needs an absolute calibration and not merely a consistent ranking, and the score this row demands has to test the index on that footing. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 42d

BUILT 2026-08-24, UNSCORED, AND CONSUMED BY NOTHING. hydrography/scripts/build_topographic_index.py, config in hydrography/config/topographic_index.yaml, pipeline row topographic_index, README section, artifact hydrography/data/{build}/topographic_index_{grid}.nc plus hydrography/analysis/topographic_index_report.json. Terrain only: no climate, no water table, no solve. Runs in 22 s on the 10M-region active build.

THE SHAPE THIS ROW ASKED FOR HAD TO BE SHARPENED, and this is the part that changes what the three blocked consumers can take. A saturated fraction is a fraction of a POPULATION. The only population this project holds is the mesh regions inside a climate-grid cell, so f_sat_max lives AT THE GRID and there is no per-region saturated fraction; manufacturing one needs a sub-region hypsometry, which is exactly what GW-6 says does not exist. WET-2, SURF-7 and LSHY-6 all want a native-mesh fraction and what is available is a climate-grid-cell one. Filed as a separate row.

THE ABSOLUTE CALIBRATION THIS ROW'S OWN NOTE DEMANDS IS NOT AVAILABLE AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL. CLIMBER-X's cti_mean_crit = 5.5, its cti_min, its CDF tabulated on integer bins 1..15 and its cut at 14 above which f_wet_max is zeroed are all calibrated against an index computed on Earth at about a kilometre. Measured here on precarve-craton-10m onto the configured grid: land mean index 15.91 (plane-fit slope) and 16.14 (receiver-drop slope), cell mean 13.01/15.49/18.59 at the 5th/50th/95th, and 80.7% of the cells that hold enough regions have a cell mean ABOVE 14 -- so CLIMBER-X's rule applied literally returns no wetland almost everywhere, which is a statement about two indices' scales rather than about this world. It is not fixable: a carries a length, so the distribution shifts with the mesh, and the measured shift between this project's own two builds (7.60 against 15.19 km) is 0.86 on the plane-fit arm and 0.80 on the receiver arm, both near ln 2. The SLOPE is not the cause -- the two arms differ by 0.23 in the land mean -- though it is the GW-9 defect one level removed and is one-signed upward. So: the config REFUSES absolute thresholds by name, the script writes no product keyed on one, and f_sat_max is a within-cell RANK statistic (share of the cell's regions above the cell mean) which survives any additive shift. That is the half that transports.

THE SUB-GRID POPULATION IS REAL: median within-cell index spread 2.23 against a between-cell spread of 1.78, so more of the index's variance is inside the cells than between them. f_sat_max comes out at 0.348/0.436/0.548 at the 5th/50th/95th.

f_grad IS DECLARED AND BRACKETED AT [1.25, 2.5] per metre, and the bracket IS the convention ambiguity: CLIMBER-X ships f_wtab = 2.5 for exp(-f_wtab z) while ClimaLand writes exp(-f_over/2 z), so the same numeral means half as much per metre there. Mixing them is a silent factor of two. min(...,1) is explicit.

OPEN BECAUSE THE SCORE NEEDS THE EARTH HARNESS, which this host could not run. The bar is declared in the config BEFORE any fraction was computed: on Australian depth-consistent bores and on US bores labelled unconfined, the AUC for an observed water table within 1 m must exceed 0.573, which is what the cell-mean depth reaches alone, reported for both f_grad arms. The attribution is exact rather than argued: f_sat is strictly monotone in the depth for a fixed f_sat_max, so ranking by f_sat with a constant f_sat_max reproduces ranking by depth exactly and any gain is f_sat_max's and nothing else's. A MISS means the index adds nothing to the depth it multiplies and the fraction should be withdrawn, not shipped with a caveat. The report carries consumers_licensed: false and scored: false, and the pipeline gate says no consumer may take it.

STILL OPEN AND UNTOUCHED BY THIS: the estimator decision. PALADYN and ClimaLand both estimate a grid-cell mean water table from column water content rather than from a lateral solve, so the column estimator is normal practice and this project's Dupuit-Forchheimer solution is the departure needing the argument. Also not carried: ClimaLand's ice split, computing the saturated column twice so frozen ground makes saturation-excess surface runoff but no subsurface flow. hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 5.
SCORED 2026-08-25 AND THE ROW IS DONE. earth_calibration.py --stage cti and --stage fsat compute the same index on the Earth mesh and run the declared score; the support, the comparator and the attribution identity were declared in config/topographic_index.yaml in the commit BEFORE the first score, because bar_auc 0.573 is the depth's discrimination per bore against the mesh REGION it falls in and f_sat lives at a climate-grid cell. The license is its own artifact, hydrography/analysis/topographic_index_score.json, and it is the AND over every observation set the config requires; build_topographic_index.py READS it rather than declaring it, so a build of the artifact cannot license itself.

VERDICT: MISS, consumers_licensed false. Australia misses on all four arms, the United States unconfined set passes on all four. The attribution identity holds to 0.00e+00 everywhere, so every difference is the terrain half's and nothing else's. The ceiling any cell-scale predictor has at that support is 0.6574 in Australia against a cell-mean depth of 0.4581, which is below chance -- so the support is not what failed, the depth is, and it is the sink-dominated regime water_table.nc already reports per cell. Where the depth works, f_sat adds +0.0034 to +0.0068.

TWO THINGS THE RUN SETTLED THAT THE ROW DID NOT ASK. The upper end of f_grad_bracket_per_m erases the terrain half entirely: at 2.5 per metre the ranking becomes the depth's ranking to fifteen digits. And the index's scale offset is measured on real ground now -- the same index on Earth's own DEM at 15.19 km has a land mean of 16.43 to 17.37, as far above CLIMBER-X's tabulated range as this world's is -- so the refusal of absolute thresholds rests on a measurement rather than an inference from one world.

hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 6. The regime-restricted criterion is world-n9sd and is deliberately NOT taken here: these numbers are in hand, so a criterion chosen now would not be one. Still untouched by this: the estimator decision, and ClimaLand's ice split.
close_reason: Built, and now SCORED against the criterion the config declared first. earth_calibration.py --stage cti / --stage fsat run it on both continents; the license lives in hydrography/analysis/topographic_index_score.json and build_topographic_index.py reads it. Verdict is a miss and consumers_licensed is false: Australia misses on every arm because the cell-mean depth is below chance there, the United States unconfined set passes on every arm, and the ceiling measurement says the miss is the depth's rather than the support's. The regime-restricted criterion that could license the fraction is world-n9sd, filed rather than run, because these numbers are already in hand.

description:
Measure the net groundwater term `Qg` per basin and report how many carve verdicts it moves, as a measurement, BEFORE deciding whether it enters the criterion

title: Valley-to-ridge water table texture is sub-grid and stays sub-grid
description:
Valley-to-ridge water table texture is sub-grid and stays sub-grid: Fan et al. (2013) put the well-articulated gradient at decameters to kilometres, against a 15.19 km region

Source: `hydrography/notes/groundwater-scoping.md` section 5, `hydrography/notes/groundwater-et-sink.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open as a DECLARED gap on GRAV-6's precedent, and now MEASURED TWICE. GW-3 scored the solver at 70,119 Australian bores with no skill at all. GW-15 then added the physics that was actually missing, removed the surface pinning entirely, and the skill did not appear: Pearson +0.031, 0.1% of variance, with the model spanning a factor of 1.9 in depth against the observations' 56.5. The model is a function of recharge at Spearman -0.977 and the real water table is not, at -0.156. So the variance is terrain at a scale this mesh cannot hold, and no sink, thickness or conductivity recovers it. NOW ANSWERED for the resolution route, `notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md`: a generation at four times the region count adds at most 12% to relief at any separation from 5 to 200 km, and the pre-erosion substrate is converged outright, so a finer Orogen does not hold the missing texture and cannot supply it. The generator's noise sits at fixed physical wavelengths and its erosion cuts at whatever the mesh scale is. Sub-grid hypsometry has to come from a parameterisation or external data. CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY ON EARTH 2026-08-20, which is the stronger test because Earth's topography has real content at every scale where Vesper's generator has none. The same case at 15.19, 10.74 and 7.60 km raises the CEILING from 0.6335 to 0.7408 and more than doubles the model's own spread, 1.91 to 4.33 m, while Pearson does not move at all: +0.0703, +0.0665, +0.0711. The dependence structure says why. The model is a monotone function of recharge at every cell size, Spearman -0.90 to -0.93, where the truth is -0.27; and against elevation the two diverge as the mesh refines, the observations' terrain signal strengthening +0.125 to +0.161 to +0.199 while the model's decays to -0.003. So GW-6 is NOT a resolution gap and was never going to be closed by a finer mesh on either planet. GW-21 then took the formulation apart and found the limit is neither: on RANK the model reaches Spearman +0.28, which is precisely its recharge field's own +0.27, so it recovers what its forcing carried and adds nothing, and the dependence structure can be tuned onto the observed values by transmissivity alone without agreement following. The binding constraint is the input fields IN THAT REGION, and GW-22 then showed the qualifier matters: scored on United States bores labelled unconfined the same model reaches Pearson +0.2599 against Australia's +0.0703, with a spread of 20.72 m against 28.94 where Australia gave 1.91 against 18.36. So this gap is regional rather than universal. Where the evapotranspiration sink takes the recharge locally the depth is a recharge map and the sub-grid texture this row is about is the least of its problems; where lateral flow carries it the solve does real work. `water_table.nc` ships `sink_fraction` to tell the two apart per cell. Which regime VESPER is in is not yet established, because the current forcing is a bootstrap climatology on pre-carve terrain. SHARPENED 2026-08-20: the 0.28 those rows measured against was never computed by anything, and is corrected to 0.2098, what a gradient boosting fit over every resolvable field reaches held out with the model EXCLUDED, from `earth_calibration.py --stage benchmark`. Both halves hold at once: the fields support only 0.2098 against a between-cell ceiling of 0.6335, and the model reaches +0.0193 alone and ADDS to that fit, 0.2098 to 0.2381. An earlier draft of this row called it information-negative from the -0.0467 and 0.1435 against 0.1411 measured on bores that fail the consistency filter; on the clean subset it is not, and that reading is withdrawn. See GW-21 [step: hydrography]

SETTLED AS A RULE 2026-08-24. The finding was complete and the gap was never the missing part; what was missing was a statement of what a cell-scale parameter is allowed to claim. hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md now carries it as a rule with a decision procedure: a parameterisation is admissible at cell scale only where it HAS a cell mean, tested by computing the Jensen term rather than by argument, and sub-grid information may reach a cell-scale parameter only as a statistic of the cell's own distribution, never as a resolved gradient or a within-cell position. The second clause is GW-25's: a bore's position inside its own cell out-predicts the groundwater solve on Pearson, +0.1290 against +0.0703, so a model that consumes a within-cell position is scoring a covariate. APPLIED TO THE THREE ROWS QUEUED BEHIND IT, with numbers: Fan's exponential carries exp(200) to exp(5000) against this world's measured neighbour elevation spread (land median 20.4 m on precarve-craton-10m, 33.8 m on precarve-craton, upper quartile 117 and 177 m) and is inadmissible; GW-24's unconfined column is linear and therefore exact above its floor, with a relative Jensen term of 0.013% at three times the relief and 8.3% at one times, which is why GW-18's floor may not go below Gleeson's 100 m; GW-26's f_sat_max is a rank statistic over the one population that exists and is the legitimate route. The declared gap itself is unchanged and is recorded in the note's section 1.
close_reason: Settled as a standing rule rather than a task. The finding was already complete and measured five ways; what was missing was the licence it gives a future parameter, and hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md now states it as a decision procedure -- a cell-scale parameter is admissible only where the parameterisation has a cell mean, tested by the Jensen term, and sub-grid information reaches it only as a statistic of the cell's own distribution. The rule is applied with numbers to GW-24, GW-18 and GW-26 in the same note, and hydrography/README.md points at it from the transmissivity section. The gap itself is not closed by this and cannot be; it is recorded as section 1 of the note, where a reader looking for it will land.

title: The discrete elliptic operator's noise floor is about 12% relative RMS against the analytic
description:
The discrete elliptic operator's noise floor is about 12% relative RMS against the analytic Legendre eigenvalue above l=1, distributed truncation rather than bad faces

Source: `hydrography/notes/mesh-geometry.md`, `hydrography/notes/earth-calibration-criterion.md`
notes:
SETTLED 2026-08-25 by measurement, criteria committed before the run (commit 58e26f5c). The 12% is real and unchanged; the reading of it as 'the mesh-scale noise floor of any field solved with this operator' is REFUTED, and that reading is what would have blocked GW-18 and GW-24.

groundwater.py --instrument. Over a 64-fold refinement of meshes from Orogen's own generator at the active build's own jitter, the TRUNCATION error fits an order of 0.004, 0.004 and 0.005 in the cell size at l = 2, 3, 4: it does not converge, and 20,000 regions carry the same 12% as precarve-craton's 2,500,001. That is why GW-3's Earth mesh reproduced it, and it is a property of the jittered-Fibonacci Voronoi family rather than of a mesh or a cell size: the Voronoi face is perpendicular to the generator segment but not centred on it, and the offset is a fixed fraction of the cell.

The SOLVED field's error is a different quantity and converges at second order, 1.994 / 1.998 / 2.008, three orders below the truncation error at the coarsest mesh: 2.766e-06, 5.629e-06 and 9.437e-06 relative on precarve-craton, and an extrapolated 6.9e-07 to 2.3e-06 on the 10,000,005-region active build. The l = 2 arm misses its declared 1e-10 linear-solve residual at 1.38e-10 and is labelled as missing; the sweep's own trend predicts 2.80e-06 there against the 2.766e-06 measured.

And the error is a fraction of the SIGNAL. Scored on the response to a transmissivity perturbation against an exact analytic answer, it is 0.12193 of the response at amplitude 0.01 and 0.12193 at 0.2, because the confined assembly is linear in T. A perturbation of relative size a is carried with an absolute error of about 0.12 a, so a small effect is not drowned.

hydrography/notes/mesh-geometry.md carries the tables; hydrography/README.md and config/pipeline.yaml carry the check. Non-local, and the second half is a NEGATIVE result worth keeping. SuperLU's default pivoting undoes MMD_AT_PLUS_A on the instrument arm's matrix, which is the whole mesh with a single pinned cell: 6.8 M nonzeros in the factor with diag_pivot_thresh=0 and SymmetricMode against a 2.5 GB working set and no answer without them, at 80,000 regions. It does NOT do so on solve()'s matrix, which is a free set inside a Dirichlet boundary. Measured on that shape with a spatially coherent conductivity across Gleeson's 3.4 orders: 55,977 free cells, nnz(L+U) 1,042,714 and a 0.55 GB peak, IDENTICAL both ways. So solve() is left alone and WORLD-V3UR's memory blocker is not relieved by this.
close_reason: Measured and re-characterised. The 12% is the operator's truncation error and stands; the noise-floor reading is refuted by --instrument, which is now in the tree with its criteria committed before its first run. The solved head's mesh error is 2.8e-06 on precarve-craton, so the discretisation is not what limits GW-18 or GW-24.

title: Fan's e-folding constants are read off a REGIONAL DIP rather than a hillslope gradient
description:
Fan's e-folding constants are read off a REGIONAL DIP rather than a hillslope gradient, one-signed toward a deeper flatter water table

Source: `hydrography/notes/groundwater-scoping.md` section 7b
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and settling it found a SECOND and larger defect that subsumes the first. The slope mismatch is real: Fan fits `f = a/(1 + b*slope)` against a hillslope gradient at about 1 km, `local_slope_deg` is a 15.19 km plane fit that `minerals/README.md` documents as an upper bound on regional dip, and gradient falls with the scale it is measured over, so `f` comes back too large. BUT THE FLOOR IS INCOHERENT AT ANY SLOPE, and that is what broke GW-1. Cell-averaging `T = A exp(h/f)` over a water table varying within the cell by `sigma` gives a factor `exp(sigma^2 / 2 f^2)`; at 100 m of sub-grid relief against the bedrock floor of 0.95 m that is `exp(5000)`, which is not a correction but the statement that the parameterisation CANNOT BE EVALUATED AT A CELL MEAN. The solver's measured `|z|/f` of 4588, against an `exp` argument limit near 709 in double precision, is the same fact arriving as an overflow. The requirement is a scale rather than a tuned value: the effective e-folding length for a cell cannot be smaller than the relief that cell contains, which makes the factor `exp(0.5)`. Fan's numbers are not wrong, they are being asked a question three orders of magnitude from where they were fitted. Consequence for GW-1: the blocker is the FORMULATION, not the iteration, and Newton would converge a model that applies a metre-scale parameter at 15 km -- worse than not converging, because the answer would look like a result. The sub-grid relief this needs is the same quantity GRAV-6 parks glacial erosion behind
close_reason: done 2026-08-20, and settling it found a SECOND and larger defect that subsumes the first.

title: Route the zero-catchment-runoff basins whose lake surface has P > E through the marginal band

notes:

title: The endorheic basin catalogue is resolution-limited rather than physics-limited.
description:
The endorheic basin catalogue is resolution-limited rather than physics-limited. `selectionCriteria` declares floors of 0.05 km depth, 1000 km2 area and 12 mesh cells, and at the build's spacing the 12-cell floor is 3526 km2, so nothing below 2646 km2 survives and the carve list is drawn from a set the mesh floored rather than the criterion selected. Preserved goes 3,621, 6,345, 9,419 across one, two and four times the region count, and at four times the smallest preserved depression is 1000 km2 exactly, the declared floor having finally taken over from the mesh. The large end does NOT settle: the biggest basin is 3,059,665 km2 at the build and 5,499,601 at four times, one south polar basin remeasured 80% larger rather than two merging, and it is not erosional, since catalogues with `--glacial 0` are byte-identical

Source: `notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. Not a defect in the floor, which is a signal-to-noise criterion and correctly relaxes as the mesh becomes able to hold smaller depressions. It is a statement about what this build can see: the declared physical floor only starts binding near 8.8M regions. DECIDED 2026-08-20: the next generation raises the region count, and the reference export at 10,000,005 is registered as `precarve-craton-10m`. It is NOT the build to activate, because a generation meant to be commissioned should also carry the PHYS-13 ice-mask decision; the two changes belong in one generation, not two. The count is settled at 10,000,005 by the saturation measurement below, the reference export carries the full grid set and its hash is registered in `lib/orogen.py`, so remaining work is one generation at that count carrying PHYS-13's mask, and then pointing `source_build` at it. THE LADDER IS NOW T21/T42/T85/T127/T170, T63 is dropped, and `precarve-craton-10m` carries all five with every grid verified to the same terrain hash; `rebuild_binaries.py`'s MATRIX gains the two missing rungs so no truncation has an export without an executable. What is left of this row is the DECISION to activate, which rule 7 makes consequential and which should carry PHYS-13's ice-mask change in the same generation. CEILING ON THE COUNT, measured: Orogen's terrain noise sits at fixed physical wavelengths and the finest it DESIGNS is about 20 km, so `elevation_pre_erosion` gains only 8% of semivariance per lag doubling below 10 km against 26% at 50 km. The 7.60 km mesh at 10,000,005 regions already oversamples that floor by 2.6x. MEASURED AT 25,000,000 and the catalogue SATURATES there: preserved goes 3,621, 6,345, 9,419, 9,649 across 2.5M, 5M, 10M and 25M, so four times again the region count adds 2.4% against the 48% the previous step added, while detected depressions keep climbing 286,534 to 646,725 because every new one is below the declared 1000 km2 floor. That is the crossover working as predicted: once `minCells` stops binding the physical criterion governs and refining further buys nothing. So 10,000,005 is not adequate-with-margin, it is where this converges, and it is the recommendation; 25M costs 3,875 s and 21.1 GB against 10M's 1,093 s and 9.0 GB, superlinear in time, for 230 more basins; 50,000,000 is 3.40 km rather than the sub-km it looks like, since edge goes as the square root of the count, and a 1 km edge needs about 577 million regions, roughly 17 hours and 517 GB. Below the floor a finer mesh manufactures erosion texture at the mesh scale rather than resolving terrain. Sub-km relief is a synthesis problem, not a region-count one. Note what activating costs under rule 7: `precarve-craton` has been consumed by a commissioned run, so superseding it makes the climatology and everything derived from it worthless rather than stale [step: orogen]
MEASURED 2026-08-24 on both registered builds by hydrography/scripts/catalogue_floor.py, which reproduces selectBasins' threshold path and nesting rule and is checked against the published preserved set id for id before it reports anything. notes/audits/basin-catalogue-floor.md; product hydrography/analysis/catalogue_floor.json.

RESOLUTION-LIMITED: true on precarve-craton, where relaxing minCells and re-selecting gives 8,084 against 3,621 preserved, so the mesh keeps out more basins than the catalogue holds. FALSE on precarve-craton-10m, where the same relaxation adds 8. Measured against the preserved set rather than by cell-area arithmetic, and the two differ: 18 depressions there clear depth and area and fail on cells, but 10 of them sit inside an already-selected basin and would never have been preserved. resolution.bindingFloor is computed from the MEAN cell area, so it is a statement about the typical depression and not a guarantee; basins.js now says so in bindingFloorBasis.

PHYSICS-LIMITED: true at 10M in AREA. Relaxing minAreaKm2 adds 1,105 basins there and nothing at all on precarve-craton, so the two builds sit on opposite sides of the crossover.

NEITHER, IN DEPTH, on both builds, and this is the part the row did not know: the depth floor is compared in dimensionless model elevation, and at 10M it is the floor that DECIDES the catalogue, relaxing it admitting 2,521 against area's 1,105 and cells' 8. No region count moves it. Filed as world-yril, which belongs in the same generation as this row's activation decision and PHYS-13's ice mask.

Rule 1's residue, by AREA because a share of land is an area share: 1.157e6 km2 outside any preserved basin at 10M, 0.364 per cent of land. The area is converged and the count is not, so refining the generation does not close it; world-bvl9.

Also found and filed: world-34gu, the relief curve saturating at model elevation 1 over 0.25 per cent of land by area, which is why 16 preserved basins at 10M have a lake capacity of exactly zero.

STILL OPEN for the reason the row already gave: what is left is the DECISION to activate a finer build, which is a loop A generation and the user's call, and which should carry PHYS-13's ice mask and now world-yril's depth floor in one generation rather than three.
close_reason:
2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER. NOT A TASK. What was left of this row was the decision to activate a finer build, and that is a loop A generation -- pipeline execution, not tracked work.

THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE IS ALSO ANSWERED, and answered the other way: at 10M regions the catalogue is NOT resolution-limited in area. notes/audits/basin-catalogue-floor.md measures it -- relaxing minAreaKm2 at precarve-craton-10m adds 1,105 basins and about 9.9e5 km2 while relaxing minCells adds 8, so the DECLARED area floor binds and the mesh floor no longer does. The two builds sit on opposite sides of that crossover. So the catalogue at 10M is governed by a fixed physical size in real km2, which is what "physics-limited rather than resolution-limited" asked for.

Three rows carry what did not close and each stands on its own evidence: world-bvl9 (is 1000 km2 the right physical floor), world-34gu (the relief curve saturating at model elevation 1, which is why 16 preserved basins have exactly zero capacity), and world-yril (the depth floor compared in dimensionless elevation rather than km, which reaches the next generation's selection).

title: Bound the seasonal lake-energy omission before choosing a lake implementation
description:
Bound the seasonal lake-energy omission before choosing a lake implementation: derive area/depth classes from accepted native-mesh basin hypsometry; compare the present soil-column surrogate with reduced water-column/ice, majority-cell slab/per-cell mixed-layer and SPAT-5 tile brackets; cross depth and phase physics with a freshwater-to-saline/brine property bracket; retain lake temperature, ice, evaporation phase and energy/water closure; then test only recorded marginal basins for carve-verdict flips from seasonally resolved evaporation and coupled precipitation/runoff

Source: `notes/audits/surface-hydrology-fire-carbon-followup.md` finding 4, `exoplasim/notes/lake-representation.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; the present lakes have soil thermal mass, not zero mass, CLIM-26's annual moisture response does not bound seasonal phase, and a freshwater FLake precedent cannot stand in for closed-basin brines; analytical/offline reduced bounds require no climate run, while every coupled lake or carve response experiment requires explicit permission [step: surface_water, surface_soil_water, boundary_conditions, baseline_run, carve_verdict]. THE NAMED-ALIKE COMPONENT DOES THE OPPOSITE THING, AND THE RIGHT PEER IS ELSEWHERE, 2026-08-22. Landlab's `priority_flood_flow_router` is a RichDEM wrapper, RASTER-ONLY, and it FILLS OR BREACHES EVERY DEPRESSION -- no preserve list, no sink set, no terminal-sink mode, with closed boundaries excluded by being set to positive infinity, i.e. treated as a wall rather than a sink. `hydrography/drainage.py` seeds its heap with preserved basin sinks and keeps them terminal. THE ACTUAL PEERS ARE `DepressionFinderAndRouter`, which accepts a user-supplied pit array and a `reroute_flow=False` mode that leaves sinks terminal and runs on non-raster grids, and `LakeMapperBarnes`, which is grid-agnostic outside D8 and carries the feature that matters most -- `fill_surface` can be a DIFFERENT FIELD from `surface`, so the rock keeps its depression while a water level is written separately -- exposing lake volumes, areas, depths and outlets directly. That is the peer for the lake solver. FLOW ACCUMULATION CHECKED A THIRD TIME AND CORRECT here, as in this fork and unlike CLIMBER-X. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 53a-b

BOUNDED 2026-08-25, notes/audits/lake-energy-omission-bound.md. The bound the
title asks for is delivered, in closed form, with no climate run and no basin
data. Three terms, ranked: freezing is absent entirely and dominates (1 m of
lake ice is worth a 93 K seasonal swing of the surrogate); the water column's
sensible heat is bounded by an amplitude ratio running from 1.21 at 0.5 m to
0.03 at 100 m at the weakest defensible damping, with the surrogate exactly
equivalent to a 2 m lake and over-damping below that; and the seasonal phase
can be wrong by at most 40.6 Earth days, a quarter orbit less the surrogate's
own 5.1 day lag, unconditionally.

THE PROPERTY BRACKET IS NOT A DRIVER and does not need crossing with depth:
salinity and depth enter through the same rho*c*d product, salinity moves rho*c
by under a factor 1.2, and the depth axis spans a factor 200. Salinity matters
only through the freezing point, which is a threshold on term 1.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CHOICE: do not choose on depth classes. lake-representation.md's
levers 2 and 4 (per-cell dwmax, per-cell mixed layer) address only the middle
term; lever 3 (mask flip to slab ocean) is the only one that brings ice, and
none of them addresses the mass term the ledger already owns under LSHY-6,
which is larger. The bound belongs against
open_water_evaporation_from_routed_water rather than in a new entry: world-6u38.

cannot be derived: the accepted build precarve-craton-10m carries ZERO

the superseded precarve-craton, and a pre-carve build is a limit not a state.

permission.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTERED 2026-08-30, before the measurement, for the arm that closes the bound's DOMINANT term.

notes/audits/lake-energy-omission-bound.md ranks freezing first and then leaves it open: 'the energy omission is bounded below by zero where lakes do not freeze and is dominated by ice where they do, and which of those applies is a climatology question, not a hypsometry one.' When that was written config/planet.yaml carried baseline_climatology: null. It no longer does. The threshold is now answerable offline, with no run.

WHAT IS MEASURED. Over the solved lake area of canonical-10m-carve2 at T21, from exoplasim/analysis/climatology/baseline_regular_climatology.nc (run_67323a923013, 57 orbits), matched to hydrography/data/canonical-10m-carve2/support_exoplasim-T21.nc BY INDEX and never by longitude (CLAUDE.md rule 3; both are the same 32x64 rung).

H1. THE FREEZING TERM IS ON. More than 10 per cent of solved lake area sits in a cell whose seasonal minimum surface temperature falls below the freezing point. FALSIFIED below 10 per cent, and a falsification OVERTURNS the audit's headline: with term 1 off, term 2 is the ranking term, depth classes do rank the levers, and 'do not choose on depth classes' would have to be withdrawn.

H2. WHERE IT IS ON IT DOMINATES UNCONDITIONALLY. No lake cell's seasonal surface temperature range reaches the 93 K that one metre of lake ice is worth against the surrogate's 3.295e6 J/m2/K. FALSIFIED by any lake cell whose range exceeds 93 K, which would put the sensible term back in contention with the phase term.

H3. SALINITY IS A THRESHOLD WITH LEVERAGE ONLY NEAR THE CROSSING. The share of lake area whose seasonal minimum lies within the fresh-to-brine freezing-point depression is small compared with the share already below it, so the property bracket cannot change the verdict. FALSIFIED if the lake area inside the depression band is comparable to the area below the fresh freezing point.

THE INSTRUMENT, checked before believing the number. The climatology has 12 time bins over a 182.80 Earth-day orbit, so one bin is 15.2 days and a bin MEAN understates the true seasonal minimum. The arm therefore reports a BRACKET and not a number: min over bins of ts is the warm end and min over bins of mint is the cold end. A verdict that is not the same at both ends is reported as no verdict.

THE CAVEAT THAT TRAVELS WITH IT, declared before the result. surface_water.nc on this build is forced by bootstrap_regular_climatology, not by the baseline whose temperatures this arm reads, so the lake SET is a bootstrap answer while the temperature field is a baseline one. surface_water.py already resolves best_available_climatology and the artifact is merely older than the baseline; it is not regenerated here because hydrography/data is symlinked into the main checkout and other sessions are live. The arm therefore also measures the freezing share over ALL land area, so that a verdict which holds on both populations does not rest on which cells hold lakes.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESULT 2026-08-31, against the pre-registration above. Two of three registered claims FAILED and are reported as results rather than re-registered. notes/audits/lake-energy-omission-bound.md carries the measurement; hydrography/scripts/lake_mosaic_cost.py is the instrument and hydrography/analysis/lake_mosaic_cost.json the output.

H1 HELD. 55.8 per cent of solved lake area freezes at the bin-mean end of the bracket and 63.7 per cent at the within-bin end, against the 10 per cent that would have falsified it. The all-land population gives 50.9 and 56.4, agreeing to within six points, so the verdict does not rest on a lake set solved under the bootstrap forcing. The audit's headline stands: the freezing term is ON over most of this world's lake area, so depth classes do not rank the levers.

H2 FAILED, and the failure is the useful part. 12.1 per cent of lake area sits in cells whose seasonal surface temperature range exceeds the 93 K one metre of ice is worth, reaching 127 K. The instrument was checked before the failure was believed: those cells are polar (median |lat| 74.7 deg, none below 63.7), low-lying, and carry a median annual maximum snow depth of 0.03 m, so the range is a high-latitude seasonal cycle on a 182.80-day orbit and not a snow-surface artifact. The audit's 'by more than any seasonal temperature range this planet can have' was false and is now removed.

WHAT THE FAILURE BUYS is the number the single figure hid: the EQUIVALENT ICE THICKNESS, the depth of ice whose latent heat equals that cell's own seasonal sensible exchange. Over the lake area that freezes it runs p5 0.28 m, p50 0.58 m, p95 1.27 m, max 1.37 m. Above its own crossover the phase term dominates the sensible term the depth classes are about; below it, it does not. The ranking survives on a measured crossover instead of an assertion, and a lake implementation now has a number to be judged against.

H3 FAILED. 23.9 per cent of lake area has a seasonal minimum between the fresh freezing point and the NaCl eutectic, against 31.9 per cent already below the eutectic. That is comparable, not small, so the freezing-point depression decides whether the dominant term switches on over a quarter of lake area. Salinity is still not a property-bracket driver -- term 3 is unchanged -- but the THRESHOLD it sets has leverage the audit did not allow it. The eutectic is used as a bracket width and never as this world's freezing point, because the lake chemistry is not declared.

BUILD FACTS REFRESHED off the stale ones. Zero INLAND_WATER regions survives the move to canonical-10m-carve2 and is still structural. The depth straddle is STRONGER carved than pre-carve: 45.2 per cent of lake area shallower than 10 m against 54.8 deeper, median 10.7 m, sitting almost exactly on the only class boundary the three terms identify. The pre-carve caveat is retired; the bootstrap-forcing one is not.

WHICH OMISSION THIS BOUNDS, which the row has to answer because the lake blend is inert. The energy bound is on the SURROGATE -- landmod.f90's soil heat solver standing in for a lake -- and that surrogate runs on every land cell whatever the blend does, so the bound is NOT contingent on the blend. What IS contingent is the mass term: the staged 0229 field carries lakes: null, so the lake tile is absent rather than mis-averaged, and that absence is priced separately under LSHY-6 at 0.40 to 0.68 times the 0.12 W m-2 bar. Two omissions, two prices, and the energy one sits inside the mass one exactly as this audit already said.

ARM VERDICT: the bound the title asks for is COMPLETE, and its dominant term is now closed rather than posed.

THE ONE ARM STILL OPEN, named separately from the bound above. The marginal-basin carve-flip test is BLOCKED, and the block has changed shape: it was blocked on an artifact and is now blocked on a DECISION plus a write this session declines to make.

WHAT LIFTED. config/planet.yaml no longer carries baseline_climatology: null; it names baseline_regular_climatology.nc, run_67323a923013 on canonical-10m-carve2 over 57 orbits. The artifact half of the old block is gone.

WHAT IS LEFT, and it splits in two.

1. THE COUPLED HALF NEEDS PERMISSION. Carve flips from coupled precipitation and runoff require a climate run, which this row has always flagged needs-permission. Unchanged.

2. THE OFFLINE HALF NEEDS A WRITE THIS SESSION DECLINED. Flips from seasonally resolved evaporation alone need no climate run: surface_water.py already solves the lake balance per climatology bin and resolves best_available_climatology, so re-solving it on the baseline and re-running carve_verdict.py is the whole of it, at cost: minutes for each. It was not done here because hydrography/data/canonical-10m-carve2/surface_water.nc is a SYMLINK into the main checkout, so writing it from a worktree overwrites the shared tree while other sessions are live. smoke_test already guards the staged-field case of exactly this hazard.

So the offline arm is a one-command job for a session running in the main checkout, and its result changes the carve verdict or does not. Naming it is not taking it, and this is the reason it was not taken rather than a deferral.

title: Measure the overshoot: re-evaluate an already-carved set against the climate that carving
description:
Measure the overshoot: re-evaluate an already-carved set against the climate that carving produced, and report how many would no longer have carved

Source: `docs/src/pipeline/loops.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
blocked -- it applies to a verdict taken on carved terrain, and a pre-carve base restarts the count at iteration 1 [step: carve_verdict]
WORKED 2026-08-24. notes/audits/carve-overshoot.md is the finding.

THE STRUCTURAL ANSWER, which needed no run. The intersection bracket is over the VEGETATION state and cannot cover the carve's own antitone feedback. Both arms run on pre-carve terrain, differing only in land_albedo_source, so both are cold relative to the world their own carve produces. The set algebra is exact: an overshooting basin is one the intersection cut, so both arms cut it, so it is never in the set the two arms disagree about. The bracket width therefore carries no information about the overshoot in either direction, and the exit predicate was one measurement short rather than complete. config/pipeline.yaml loop A and docs/src/pipeline/loops.md now carry both numbers.

THE ROUTE, and the one that does not work. Re-running the verdict on the carved build measures the NEXT PASS, not the overshoot: a carved rim leaves no impoundment, so the basin is absent from that build's basins.nc and export_carve_list.py already carries it forward at 0 as not re-decidable. The route that isolates the feedback holds the geometry still and moves only the climate: re-take the verdict on the PRE-CARVE build's basins and coupling under the CARVED build's baseline climatology. carve_verdict.py and export_carve_list.py already take those three flags separately, so no new machinery is needed to produce the re-evaluation.

BUILT: hydrography/scripts/carve_overshoot.py, the comparison, with four controls on fixtures under --self-test (identity, permutation, coverage, sign), all four of which fail on a comparison that ignores its second argument. It refuses a re-evaluation that does not cover every applied carve rather than scoring the unknown case as a zero. export_carve_list.py's sidecar now records each arm's retain and a per-basin bracketed flag, so the bracket's MEMBERSHIP survives the pass rather than only its width.

STILL BLOCKED, and the blocker is more basic than the row said. It is not that a pre-carve base restarts the count at iteration 1; it is that no first verdict exists at all. world_state.json has hydrography.carve_verdict null in all three fields and carve_list null; current_climate is invalidated with no baseline_climate_report.json for any climatology this build produced; and every carved-zoned identity in archive/builds is a stub with no payload. The measurement waits on a first verdict, a carve, and the carved build's own baseline, all three loop A actions and the carve the user's call.

Filed while here: world-xgtj, the background land albedo .sra being staged per rung and not per build, which is the one input on the carve path whose build pairing is neither declared nor stamped and which bites the overshoot measurement specifically.

2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER, from a pass over the needs-decision set.
RECLASSIFIED, examined during the pipeline run rather than in advance. The author's estimate is that a two-pass loop on each looped item is what reaches an appropriate determination, so the overshoot is read off the second pass rather than declared before the first.

title: The pedology parameter that closes the loop to the climate is uncited. pedogenesis.yaml's
description:
The pedology parameter that closes the loop to the climate is uncited. `pedogenesis.yaml`'s `water:` block gives volumetric plant-available water as "standard textbook mid-range values", and the `catena:` block's four constants carry reasoning but no source and no `declared` label

Source: `notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md` finding 4, `docs/src/pipeline/steps.md` section 3.6
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18. Two papers fetched and read, and BOTH turned out to license the mechanism and not the numbers, which is the answer rather than a shortfall. Saxton and Rawls (2006) is the standard texture-to-water basis, 1,722 A-horizon USDA/NRCS samples at 33 and 1500 kPa, and it fixes the SHAPE the block relies on -- plant-available water peaking at intermediate texture. It does not fix the three endmember values, because the regression is over a continuous mixture and the paper excluded samples above 60% clay, so a pure endmember is outside its data; reading values off it would be `docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md` class 9. Heimsath et al. (1997) gives the first empirical soil production function, `-(de/dt) = (77 +/- 9) exp(-(0.023 +/- 0.003) h)` um/yr, and names "mechanical processes as freeze-thaw" as its own reason for the exponential form, which sources the frost term; but its control variable is hillslope CURVATURE where `catena:` uses tan(beta), a stated simplification rather than an equivalence. So all seven constants are labelled DECLARED with brackets, on the `aeolian/config/dust.yaml` model, and `build_soil.py` reports the spread the way the row asked: water capacity comes out 96.1 to 167.7 mm around 127.3, a factor of 1.75 on the field that sets ExoPlaSim's `dwmax` and whose overflow IS its runoff. Re-running the soil to get that exposed a second staleness and rule 7 decided it, as with the albedo: the soil on disk was built from the BOOTSTRAP climatology while `config/planet.yaml` names the baseline, so it was rebuilt on the baseline and code 229 regenerated from it

title: computeScarpPotential gates on an absolute rise over run, the 0.002 to 0.010 smoothstep
description:
`computeScarpPotential` gates on an absolute rise over run, the 0.002 to 0.010 smoothstep, but the gradient a mesh can measure depends on its spacing: 15.19 km cells average away drops that finer cells resolve, so the same escarpment reports a steeper gradient and crosses the smoothstep sooner at a higher region count. The 150 km influence band scales correctly through `SCARP_EDGE_KM / edgeKm`, 10 hops against 20; the gradient thresholds do not scale at all

Source: `notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. `scarp_potential` is therefore not comparable across region counts, and a finer generation strengthens scarps for reasons partly real, the landform is better captured, and partly calibration, the thresholds were tuned at some other spacing. MEASURED at four times the region count: cells with non-zero `scarp_potential` go 12.456% to 14.999%, the mean where non-zero goes 0.1316 to 0.1986, a rise of 51%, and the 99th percentile land slope goes 5.015 to 8.427 degrees, while relief at fixed separation rose at most 12%. The gap between 51% and 12% is the calibration. Separating the two needs the thresholds restated against a known escarpment gradient rather than left at their inherited values [step: orogen]
close_reason:
Answered, and two defects found in the same pass are fixed. Commit 9862d4eb; evidence in notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md.

THE VERDICT. The gate does not transport, and it is NOT the compound topographic index's failure mode. CTI shifts by exactly ln 2 because its argument a/tan(beta) carries a LENGTH, so the shift is deterministic and subtractable. A gradient is a length over a length and carries none; it fails because the surface is self-affine, so the shift is empirical, and it is not even one number -- land gradient rises 1.408x at the median and 1.695x at p99 between the 2.5M and 10M builds. No single factor or exponent removes it. The exported field moves with it: scarp_potential above zero goes 0.2822 to 0.3410 of land, above 0.25 goes 0.0506 to 0.0949, mean where non-zero 0.1247 to 0.1924.

A NORMALISED FORM TRANSPORTS AND A RANK FORM IS NOT NEEDED. Bar declared before the runs at 1.15x on every quantile p50-p99, baseline declared at 30 km. Relief below the MEAN land elevation within 30 km, over 30 km: 0.909, 0.932, 1.046, 1.134 at p75-p99, inside the bar; its p50 is structurally zero because the measure is one-sided, which leaves the bar undefined rather than missed. Relief below the MINIMUM within the same ball fails (1.285, 1.053, 1.110, 1.206, 1.247) and the reason is worth keeping: a minimum is an extreme-value statistic biased by how many cells the ball holds, and the fine mesh holds three times as many.

TWO DEFECTS FIXED, both unambiguous. (1) The numerator differenced r_elevation, the generator's shaping parameter, against a denominator in km, so it was not a rise over a run at all: dh/de = 120e^3(1-e) is zero at sea level, peaks near 12.7 km/unit at e=0.75 and returns to zero at the ceiling, and the coded and physical distributions differ by 7x at p99. It also ignored the 1/g relief scaling, so the same terrain scarped identically at any gravity. Now converts through scaledHeightKm and pipeline.js passes reliefScale. (2) The neighbour filter was r_elevation[nb] <= 0, an elevation-sign test inside a function whose own land test is surface_class -- CLAUDE.md rule 1. It discarded every downhill neighbour on a dry closed-basin floor below sea level: 5.3 per cent of land at 2.5M and 8.6 at 10M, four fifths endorheic. Three assertions in tools/test-lithology.mjs made the same substitution and are fixed with it; one was failing against the corrected code for exactly that reason. 32/32 tests pass.

THRESHOLDS PRESERVED at 0.002 and 0.010, now labelled in the module as inherited rather than anchored. Adopting the 30 km form moves the distribution an order of magnitude, so they cannot be carried across, and picking new ones by matching the areal extent the present gate produces would calibrate against the defect. world-xgaj carries the estimator swap and the threshold restatement as one atomic change, with the external anchor it needs named.

description:
Replace Orogen's static 30-degree absolute-latitude `shelfClass()` choice between `carbonate` and `shelf_clastic` with one downstream, support-aware substrate classification driven by accepted sea-surface/column state, carbonate chemistry and biological carbonate production versus ANUT-6 terrigenous sediment supply; retain the latitude map only as a labelled bootstrap, preserve tectonic basement and cover thickness, and emit provenance plus unknown/mixed fractions rather than forcing a binary answer where inputs do not separate them

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` section 8g, `biosphere/notes/implicit-earth-assumptions.md` finding 8
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; classification/schema and constant-state fixtures require no model run, while production state depends on OCN-11 support, OCN-13 chemistry, OCN-14 biology and ANUT-6 sediment delivery. This is the marine-geology instance of the latitude-use rule and belongs here rather than in BIO-29 or an ocean model [step: orogen, soil]

THE LABELLED-BOOTSTRAP HALF IS DONE, 2026-08-25, commit 35b6ae9e. SHELF_SUBSTRATE_BOOTSTRAP is declared in vendor/orogen/js/lithology.js beside shelfClass and emitted as manifest.lithology.shelfSubstrateBootstrap, naming the two classes, the rule, the constant, what it stands for and what supersedes it; it replaces the prose climateCaveat key, which nothing read. A test asserts the label still describes the classifier over a whole planet and fails on an injected ten-degree drift. NO CELL CHANGES CLASS and no terrain moves.

WHAT IS STILL BLOCKED, and it is the whole replacement: a declared canonical climatology (config/planet.yaml has baseline_climatology null), then OCN-11 support, OCN-13 chemistry, OCN-14 biology and ANUT-6 sediment delivery. notes/audits/orogen-lithology.md carries the finding.

DO NOT RE-FIT THE 30 DEGREES AS AN INTERIM. The SIGN of the correction is not known. At 32 degrees obliquity the annual-mean insolation profile normalised to the equator goes 0.879 to 0.891 at 30 degrees and 0.790 to 0.813 at 40, which moves an annual-mean band POLEWARD; the seasonal amplitude at 30 degrees rises from 0.199 to 0.265 of the stellar constant and the winter minimum falls from 0.161 to 0.117, which cuts EQUATORWARD for a factory needing sustained warmth. Which wins depends on ocean heat transport and mixed-layer depth. The K2.5V primary adds a third axis the latitude rule cannot express at all: less PAR per unit total flux through water moves the DEPTH window, and shelfClass has no depth term -- shelfCells is a distance from the coast, not a water depth.

ALSO REJECTED, with reasons: deleting the split (the two classes differ by a factor of nearly five in erodibility, which feeds elevation, so picking one is a larger claim than the proxy makes and it would move terrain); and driving it from Orogen's own climate module (climate-config.js clamps the ITCZ at 20.27 degrees and puts the subtropical highs at 31.27, Earth constants of the same kind).

2026-08-26, WHAT THE REPLACEMENT COSTS IN THE PIPELINE GRAPH, which nothing
else records. Today the classifier is COMPILED IN: shelfClass lives in
vendor/orogen/js/lithology.js and the orogen step's needs are [carve_list,
ice_mask]. A downstream, support-aware classification is a field computed
outside Orogen and consumed AT GENERATION, which makes it a THIRD loop-A input
alongside those two -- the same shape as the ice mask, arriving by the same
route. So landing this row means adding its generator step and the orogen edge
to config/pipeline.yaml in the same commit, per the rule that an artifact no
step generates does not exist. Budget it here rather than discovering it at the
end.

AND THE HEAD OF THIS ROW'S OWN BLOCK LIST IS CIRCULAR IF READ LITERALLY. It
requires a declared canonical climatology; that requires a commissioned
baseline, which requires a build, and this row changes the build. Loop A
resolves inputs of this class by ITERATION rather than by clearing them first,
which is what the orogen step's first_pass note already records for ice_mask.
The asymmetry that keeps the base INTERIM in the meantime is that the ice mask
has an honest null for the first pass, --glacial 0, and the shelf substrate has
none: this row rejects deleting the split and rejects re-fitting the 30
degrees, so the first pass necessarily carries the labelled Earth bootstrap.

title: Recheck the playa clastic fraction and what it is derived
description:
Recheck the playa clastic fraction and what it is derived FROM, because it is being quoted as a property of this world and it is neither stable nor reconstructible. FOUR THINGS AT ONCE. (1) IT IS DERIVED FROM ENDORHEISM, not independent of it: `vendor/orogen/js/lithology.js`'s `basin_fill` cover rule fires on `when: (c) => !!c.endorheic` and assigns `evaporite` where `saltCrust` and `playa_clastic` over the rest, so opening a basin removes the flag and the cover reverts to parent material. The fraction therefore moves with the carve list exactly as the endorheic figures do, and rule 9 applies to it: 0.23869 is a pre-carve LIMIT. (2) THE QUANTITY IT DEPENDS ON IS NOT REPORTED. `world_state.json` gives `endorheic_fraction_of_land = 0.7629` beside an `endorheic_note` that carefully distinguishes `drainage_share_of_land` from `basin_floor_share_of_land` -- and the key itself says which it is nowhere. The lithology depends on the second and the reported number appears to be the first. (3) EVAPORITE IS INVISIBLE: the `lithology_land_fractions` block is truncated to six classes and evaporite is below melange's 0.0617, so the basin-fill total, which is playa plus evaporite, cannot be reconstructed from the artifact at all. (4) A STATED FIGURE DOES NOT RECONCILE: `vendor/orogen/tools/README.md` says the split is about 10 percent salt to 90 percent clastic and that this is a planet with "a fifth of its land in closed basins", but playa alone is 0.23869, which under that split implies a basin floor near 0.265

Source: `vendor/orogen/js/lithology.js`, `vendor/orogen/tools/README.md`, `world_state.json`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and NARROWED to two vendored-prose edits: the measurement is done and all four questions are settled. MEASURED 2026-08-22 on `precarve-craton`, area-weighted over `surface_class` land: basin floor `is_endorheic` 0.267620 of land, playa clastic 0.238693, evaporite 0.028487, basin fill 0.267180, salt share of fill 0.106621, fill share of basin floor 0.99836. Basin fill IS the endorheic set: no fill cell lies outside it, and the 0.000439-of-land residual inside it is basement stripped of its veneer. THE REPORTING HALF IS CLOSED: `scripts/world_state.py` now emits `endorheic_catchment_share_of_land` and `endorheic_basin_floor_share_of_land` as two named keys, and `lithology_land_fractions` is no longer truncated to six, which is what hid `evaporite` at tenth and made basin fill unreconstructible. WHAT IS LEFT is prose in the vendored subtree, so it wants the fork-note convention in `docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md` applied in the same pass: `vendor/orogen/tools/README.md:303-306` says "a fifth", which understates the measured share by about a quarter and carries ~2.8 W/m2 per 0.10 where the measured share gives ~3.9; `vendor/orogen/js/lithology.js:148` says 12.65 percent and ~1.7 W/m2 and needs the same treatment. Both derived figures reproduce from their own share, so each moved with it and the ARGUMENT IS STRONGER, not weaker. A SECOND FIGURE IN THAT PARAGRAPH IS STALE AND DEMONSTRABLY SO: "effective 0.32 rather than 0.50" reproduces exactly from a playa clastic albedo of 0.30, which `lithology.js`'s own header records as corrected to 0.19 on Post et al. (2000); on current albedos and the measured 10.66/89.34 split the effective basin-fill albedo is 0.2231. THE CONSUMER WARNED: LSHY-1's retention closure rests on "a quarter of this land is playa clastic". The magnitude its argument wants is basin FILL at 0.26718 rather than playa alone at 0.23869, and both are pre-carve LIMITS rather than states, so the claim stands at roughly the size it assumed but permanently as an upper bound. `pedology/README.md`'s thermostat table shows the direction, 25.6 percent pre-carve to 15.8 configured to 11.7 projected [step: orogen]
close_reason:
Both halves closed. The reporting half was already done; what was left was prose in the vendored subtree quoting closed-basin shares that had moved, and the derivation itself written down nowhere a consumer would find it.

VERIFIED ON THE ARTIFACT, both builds, area-weighted over surface_class. Basin fill IS the endorheic set: fill outside is_endorheic is exactly 0.000000 on both, and the residual inside it carrying no fill is 0.00044 (2.5M) and 0.00047 (10M) of land, basement stripped of its veneer. playa_clastic 0.238693 / 0.279782, evaporite 0.028487 / 0.029225, fill 0.267180 / 0.309006, salt share of fill 0.106621 / 0.094576, effective fill albedo 0.2231 / 0.2193.

WHAT IT IS DERIVED FROM, now in notes/audits/orogen-lithology.md: playa_clastic is a RESIDUAL of two geometric conditions -- inside a preserved closed basin (COVER_SEQUENCE basin_fill fires on !!c.endorheic and nothing else), and not within LITHO_SALT_CRUST_DEPTH_FRAC of the sink (saltCrustMask takes the rest). No grain size, no water chemistry, no depositional process enters at any point.

AND THE CLASS IS NOT ONE SURFACE. Half of it sits above 83 per cent of its basin's relief, so it is dominated by the basin MARGIN and not the floor -- the second half of Orogen's own class name, 'Playa mud / alluvial fan fill'. On physical gradient bands fixed before measuring, between a third and a half of it lies on gradients a mud flat does not have (>=1e-3), and 5.6 to 9.4 per cent on outright fan gradients (>=1e-2). The two builds bracket it; the split is itself resolution-dependent for the same self-affine reason lith-25 records.

PROSE FIXED. vendor/orogen/tools/README.md said 'a fifth of its land in closed basins' with ~2.8 W/m2 per 0.10, and lithology.js said 12.65 per cent with ~1.7. Both now state the sensitivity as a coefficient that does not move with the carve list, about 1.4 W/m2 per 0.10 of albedo error per 0.10 of land covered, and point at the artifact instead of carrying a share. 'Effective 0.32 rather than 0.50' reproduced from a playa albedo of 0.30 that the same file records as corrected to 0.19; the effective fill albedo is near 0.22.

The 'fork-note convention' the earlier notes name does not exist as a documented convention in docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md -- its Orogen section lists what the fork adds and defines no per-file marker -- so CLAUDE.md's own rule (do not write current values into prose; point at world_state.json) was applied instead. Commit 846ec121.

title: Build one versioned, vertically explicit vadose/land-column hydraulic and thermal property
description:
Build one versioned, vertically explicit vadose/land-column hydraulic and thermal property artifact: physical and rootable layer geometry; mineral, organic, andic and weathered-bedrock fractions; porosity, retention curve, wilting/field-capacity/saturation states, conductivity/permeability and heat properties; pressure/head conventions with Vesper gravity; units, provenance and correlated uncertainty cases. Compare pedology AWC, ExoPlaSim `dwmax` and LPJ's Cosby/Lawrence derivation before removing duplicate consumer-side pedotransfer and organic-mixing paths; keep aquifer transmissivity a separately scaled groundwater property joined at the declared contact

Source: `biosphere/notes/soil-land-surface-hydraulic-consistency-audit.md` finding 1
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; schema, converter and checked-in-map comparison require no model execution; do not collapse the contract back to one AWC scalar or substitute vadose conductivity for aquifer transmissivity [step: soil, surface_soil_water, lpj_driver]. THE RETENTION CLOSURE IS A FAMILY CHOICE THIS CONTRACT LEAVES IMPLICIT, 2026-08-22. `references/climaland/src/standalone/Soil/retention_models.jl` declares `AbstractSoilHydrologyClosure` with `vanGenuchten` and `BrooksCorey` as its two implementations, and parameterises `RichardsParameters` over the closure type so the choice is made at construction. This project sits entirely in ONE family without having recorded that a family was chosen: LPJ-GUESS's Cosby (1984) derivation is a Clapp-Hornberger form and PALADYN uses Clapp-Hornberger too. The two differ most in their tails -- Brooks-Corey has a discontinuous air-entry point and a power-law tail, van Genuchten is smooth through saturation -- which matters here specifically, because a quarter of this land is playa clastic, so wetting and drying through near-saturation is a common state rather than an edge case. That rests on the PLAYA FRACTION -- which LITH-27 establishes is itself derived from endorheism, since Orogen assigns basin fill on `!!c.endorheic`, so it carries the same pre-carve limit and moves with the carve list. The argument is therefore about a class of surface this terrain produces, not about a settled area, and it survives only in that weaker form until LITH-27 reports what the derived fraction is. NOT an argument for switching: an argument that this contract should carry the closure as a NAMED property with its family stated, so a consumer knows which it is reading and a later comparison has something to vary. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 23b
close_reason: Delivered as pedology/config/land_column_properties.yaml, pedology/scripts/land_column_properties.py and pedology/notes/land-column-property-contract.md, with a pipeline row that surface_soil_water needs. Two geometries (fifteen 100 mm physical layers to 1.5 m, rootable to 1.0 m) with each consumer's mapped against them; four materials with their vertical rules stated; four retention states with their ordering checked; one NAMED retention closure with its family stated, which is the thing the notes asked for; correlated uncertainty cases with the reported spread labelled a lower bound because Cosby's within-class variance is not carried anywhere; and the aquifer boundary declared separately scaled and joined at the contact. Gravity is declared where it enters: saturation is pore geometry and does not move, the wilting point is a plant pressure and does not move, field capacity is a drainage equilibrium over a stated length so its matric pressure is rho_w*g*L and it does. The declared 1 m length reproduces Cosby's own field-capacity suction exactly under Earth gravity and the check fails if it stops. Available capacity comes out at 0.928 of Earth's, bracketed 0.923 to 0.931, reported and not applied for two stated reasons. The comparison the row required is done with no model run and reproduces the audit's finding 1 independently: pedology 84.6 mm median against LPJ's 145.3, ratio 1.61 median and 0.90-2.55 p10-p90, median absolute difference 48.6 mm, Pearson 0.793. WORLD-NGA10's unclamped Cosby region is derived analytically as 1.58*sand + 0.63*clay < 0.17 and the map's MARGIN from it reported (0.494 against a bound of 0.17, minimum saturation headroom 0.0248 volumetric) rather than a count of zero; the clamp is specified here rather than edited into soilinput.cpp, which a sibling batch owns. The declaration check is run against ten contracts broken in named ways and catches every one; it caught a real omission in this contract on its first run. Eight properties carry the sentinel with their owners named. REMOVING the duplicate consumer-side paths was explicitly gated on this comparison and is world-of6n, which changes results and needs permission.

Ten control volumes from the air column over a land cell to a terminal boundary at the coast; twenty-one directed terms in kilograms of water, each with one source, one destination, one owner, a declared interval floor and the artifact that would supply it; seven named absences; and one owner per store with every shadow copy in a second component written down.
