title: Replace the active ExoPlaSim scalar bucket behind a selectable reduction with a restart-exact
description:
Replace the active ExoPlaSim scalar bucket behind a selectable reduction with a restart-exact climate-side land column that consumes LSHY-1 and produces LSHY-2's infiltration, storage, surface-runoff and drainage terms; register the current bucket, a parsimonious multilayer scheme and gradient-driven flow as explicit hypotheses, include Vesper gravity in potential flow, expose free-drainage/bedrock/aquifer lower boundaries, and serialize every layer, phase and partial accumulator. Treat the current steady groundwater product only as a fixed-head or orbit-mean exchange bracket unless PLHY-4 establishes a transient saturated-storage state; do not synthesize seasonal head

Source: `biosphere/notes/soil-land-surface-hydraulic-consistency-audit.md` findings 2, 3 and 6
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; source and analytical reduction/restart fixtures require no simulation, but timing, climate response and solver selection require explicit permission; coordinate the LPJ-only controls under PLHY-2 [step: groundwater, surface_soil_water, baseline_run]. AMENDED 2026-08-22: the parsimonious multilayer hypothesis now has a named candidate at this project's THROUGHPUT rather than a CMIP one. PALADYN is five soil layers to 3.9 m on Clapp-Hornberger properties with a free-drainage lower boundary, `references/climber-x/src/lnd/soil_hydro.f90` and `surface_hydro.f90`, and the licence question is already answered: ExoPlaSim is GPL version 2 or later, so a GPL-3 combination is permitted with the combined work under GPL-3. Take the formulation and not the tree, and its uniform default `ksat`, `psisat` and `b` are Earth configuration that LSHY-1 already owns. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 3 and 6. TWO OF THIS ROW'S THREE HYPOTHESES SHIP AS INTERCHANGEABLE COMPONENTS, 2026-08-22. `references/climaland/src/standalone/` carries `Bucket` and `Soil` as peer standalone models against a shared interface, with `Soil/rre.jl` the Richards equation -- so the current bucket and gradient-driven flow, two of the three hypotheses this row wants registered, exist as swappable implementations rather than as a plan. That is the SUMMA pattern of Clark et al. (2015) built, and Clark is already in `references/INDEX.md` as the argument FOR registering them this way. Read it for STRUCTURE only: ClimaLand is CMIP-class and GPU-oriented, so it is not a candidate for adoption, and PALADYN stays the EMIC-class implementation reference because it runs at a comparable cost. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 23a and 23c. A PEER IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SAME ABSTRACTION DISAGREES BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, 2026-08-22, and this project's side is the permissive extreme. Both ExoPlaSim and cGENIE's ENTS scale land evaporation by a soil-moisture factor and differ in that factor: `landmod.f90:418` is LINEAR, `min(1, W/(drhsfull*Wmax))` with `drhsfull = 0.4` at `:53`, so it evaporates at the POTENTIAL RATE for any bucket above 40 percent full; `surflux.F:1334` is QUARTIC, `min(1, (W/bcap)**4)`, reaching potential only at a full bucket. At equal fractional fill the ratio runs 39x at 0.4, 16x at 0.5, 8x at 0.6 and 2x at 0.8, agreeing only when full. Compare the SHAPE only: capacity differs too, ExoPlaSim's `wsmax` being a uniform scalar against ENTS's carbon-dependent `bcap`, and ENTS's `k8`/`k9`/`k10` arrive by namelist and are NOT shipped in the vendored tree, so the capacity half cannot be closed from here. Neither limiter is right and this is a bracket, not an adoption -- but the replacement column this row specifies should carry the limiter as a DECLARED choice with the bracket beside it rather than inheriting the linear form silently. The direction reaches the carve: at a given bucket state the permissive form sends more precipitation to evaporation and less to runoff, and `scripts/error_budget.py` already records E/R as amplified into the carve. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 32a. AND THE LIMITER HAS A SHAPE VOCABULARY PLUS A SCOPE WARNING, 2026-08-22. ClimaLand's `src/standalone/Vegetation/soil_moisture_stress.jl` carries `beta = min(1, max((theta-theta_low)/(theta_high-theta_low),0)**c)`, cited to Egea et al. (2011), `references/egea2011-water-stress-in-coupled-photosynthesis-conductance-models.pdf`. THE THREE PARAMETERS ARE THE RIGHT AXES for the replacement column's limiter and both behaviours above sit on them -- ExoPlaSim at `c = 1` with the knee at 0.4 of capacity, ENTS at `c = 4` at full capacity -- so implementing the general form makes the bracket a runtime selection rather than a code fork. DO NOT CITE EGEA FOR IT: that paper is about water stress in coupled photosynthesis-stomatal conductance models and its beta multiplies PHOTOSYNTHESIS, applied to `An` in `photosynthesis_farquhar.jl:335` and deliberately not re-applied in stomatal conductance, evaluated on ROOT-ZONE AVERAGED moisture weighted by root distribution. ExoPlaSim's `drhs` and ENTS's `beta` multiply the SURFACE EVAPORATION FLUX over vegetated and bare ground alike from a store with no depth. Same algebra, different flux. THE THIRD AXIS SURVIVES THAT CORRECTION AND IS THE USEFUL ONE: `theta_low` is the wilting point or residual water fraction, and both models here pin it at zero, so each approaches zero flux only as its store approaches empty and water held below the wilting point is still available to be removed. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 33

LANDED 2026-08-24, AND WHAT IS LEFT IS A DECISION AND NOT CODE.
plasim/src/landcolumn.f90 is new and depends on nothing -- no plasimmod, no
resmod, no grid -- so the kernels compile alone and the reduction can be RUN
rather than asserted. landmod dispatches on nlandwcol: 0 is the scalar bucket
(default, and bit-identical), 1 the layered column of nlsoilw layers with
nlandwdrain selecting an impermeable or free-draining base. Restart records
dwatcl and ddrain are written every step whatever the scheme, so a run can
switch at a restart boundary without a cold start, and are read under a lowered
nexcheck so an older restart still resumes.

THE REDUCTION IS CHECKED BITWISE, exoplasim/scripts/verify_land_column_reduction.sh:
both kernels over twenty thousand steps, at default real and at -fdefault-real-8
because that is what the model builds with, requiring exact equality of store and
runoff. Three negative controls must break it and all three do. column_step takes
a layer to capacity with AMIN1(cap, w) rather than the algebraically identical
w - AMAX1(0., w - cap), because a reduction right to a tolerance cannot tell a
refactor from a physics change.

The evaporation limiter is now three axes (drhsfull, drhslow, nrhsexp) with
defaults that are the active form exactly, taken by BRANCH and not by algebra
since x**1.0 is not bitwise x. ExoPlaSim's linear knee at 0.4 and ENTS's quartic
at a full store are now one runtime axis instead of two forks.

TWO OF THREE HYPOTHESES ARE REGISTERED. Gradient-driven flow is named and not
implemented, because it needs an unsaturated conductivity and a matric
potential and pedology/config/land_column_properties.yaml carries both as
undeclared. That is a dependency and not a gap.

BLOCKED ON ONE QUESTION, which is the user's: WHICH SCHEME SHOULD THE BASELINE
RUN, and at what layer shape? Nothing in the code decides it. What would settle
it is a paired run -- nlandwcol 0 against nlandwcol 1 at a declared nlsoilw and
lower boundary, on the same build and boundary conditions -- compared on the
land runoff ratio and on E/R, which scripts/error_budget.py already records as
amplified into the carve. That is a climate response case and the row's own
status line says those require explicit permission. Until it is answered the
default is 0 and nothing has changed.

Also open: world-p9qq, the drainage flux has no diagnostic output code, so
ddrain is unreadable downstream. Identically zero under the default lower
boundary, which is why it did not block this.

2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER. LAYERED, and the question 'is there any advantage to bucket' is answered NO on
fidelity. Read out of the source rather than argued:

THE BUCKET IS A STRICT SPECIAL CASE. landmod.f90:160 states it and
exoplasim/scripts/verify_land_column_reduction.sh checks it bitwise: nlandwcol 1
at nlsoilw 1 with an impermeable base IS the bucket, operation for operation.
So choosing layered forfeits nothing and the bucket survives as an exact control
arm whatever is chosen. The only advantages it has are historical -- every run
on disk used it, so its restart layout and behaviour are known, and no run has
ever integrated nlsoilw > 1.

WHAT THE BUCKET MAKES IMPOSSIBLE, which is the real content. nlandwphase = 1
REQUIRES nlandwcol = 1, because phase is a property of a layer and a scalar
store has no layer to freeze -- so LSHY-5's frozen-soil consistency between the
climate column and the ecology column cannot be reached on the bucket at all.
The same shape blocks WORLD-JSFM (a soil heat solver that reads the column's own
water), DUST-17 (an authoritative TOP emitting-layer liquid water state) and
PHYS-15 (soil albedo in effective saturation over the top 0.02 m). Every one of
those wants depth-resolved water and the bucket has no depth: dwmax is a
capacity in metres of water and says nothing about how deep the column is.

WHAT IS STILL OWED IS THE LAYER SHAPE, AND IT IS A DERIVATION RATHER THAN A
CHOICE. NLSOILWX is 8 (landcolumn.f90:44). Pedology's physical column is 15
layers of 100 mm to 1.5 m, and LPJ-GUESS already groups those 5 upper and 10
lower. The shape that makes LSHY-5 possible is the one the two columns SHARE, so
nlsoilw 2 at dsoilwz [0.5, 1.0] is the candidate, with dsoilwf taken from
pedology's own per-layer awc rather than picked -- inventing the capacity split
would be a tuned value in the place this contract exists to prevent.
pedology/config/land_column_properties.yaml is where that lands.

NOT CHOSEN HERE AND STILL ABSENT: gradient-driven flow, the third registered
hypothesis. It needs an unsaturated conductivity and a matric potential, both
carried as undeclared in that same contract. Registering two and naming the
third is the honest state.

SO THIS ROW IS NO LONGER WAITING ON THE AUTHOR. It waits on the layer shape
being derived, and then on the paired arm -- nlandwcol 0 against 1 at the
declared shape, on one build, compared on land runoff ratio and E/R -- which is
a climate response case and keeps its needs-permission label.

2026-08-26, THE DECISION IS TAKEN AND THE SHAPE IS DERIVED AS FAR AS IT GOES.

SCHEME: layered. The author's answer, on the reading above -- the bucket is a
bitwise special case, so nothing is forfeited, and it is what makes LSHY-5,
WORLD-JSFM, DUST-17 and PHYS-15 reachable at all.

GEOMETRY: nlsoilw 2, dsoilwz [0.5, 1.0] m, lower boundary impermeable. Not
chosen -- taken from the boundary the ecology column already groups at.
land_column_properties.py declares LPJ_SOILDEPTH_UPPER_MM 500 over
LPJ_NSOILLAYER_UPPER 5 and LPJ_SOILDEPTH_LOWER_MM 1000 over the remaining ten of
LPJ_NSOILLAYER 15, so [0.5, 1.0] is exactly that grouping and is the only
two-layer cut at which the two columns share a boundary. Sharing the boundary is
the whole point: LSHY-5 is about the climate column and the ecology column
agreeing on snow, frozen soil and thermal state, and they cannot agree across
geometries that do not meet.

CAPACITY SPLIT: NOT DERIVABLE INTO THE NAMELIST, and that is a finding rather
than remaining effort. See WORLD-VJBZ, filed and now blocking this row. dsoilwf
is one shape for the planet; the split is 0.3333 at the geometric value where
the regolith fills the column, which is 26.5 per cent of land, and runs to 0.8882
elsewhere with a median of 0.4699. One namelist number is wrong for most of the
map and choosing the one that makes a comparison come out is a tuned value.

CONFIG IS NOT FLIPPED, deliberately. surface.land_water_column stays scheme
bucket. Two reasons and either alone decides it: at layers 1 the layered scheme
is bit-identical to the bucket, so flipping now buys literally nothing; and at
layers 2 it is an unverified model form on the carve path, because the split it
would run on does not exist yet and the paired arm that measures what the change
is worth -- nlandwcol 0 against 1 on one build, compared on land runoff ratio and
E/R -- has not been run. The config comment records the decision so the next
reader finds the intent and the gate together.

ORDER, now that it is settled: WORLD-VJBZ (make the split expressible), then the
paired arm, then the flip.
close_reason:
SCHEME AND GEOMETRY LANDED; the paired arm is held and is not this row's.

config/planet.yaml declares scheme layered, layers 2, layer_thickness_m [0.5, 1.0] -- the land column contract's own 500 mm upper and 1000 mm lower grouping, and the only two-layer cut at which the climate column and the ecology column share a boundary, which is what LSHY-5 needs because two columns cannot agree about frozen soil across geometries that do not meet. layer_capacity_fraction carries the thickness-proportional fallback; the split itself is surface code 2290 under WORLD-VJBZ.

WHY LAYERED, settled by the author on the reading that the bucket is a bitwise special case: nlandwcol 1 at nlsoilw 1 with an impermeable base IS the bucket, operation for operation, so choosing layered forfeits nothing while the bucket forfeits nlandwphase, and with it LSHY-5's frozen-soil consistency, WORLD-JSFM's moisture-dependent soil heat, DUST-17's top emitting-layer water and PHYS-15's soil albedo.

WHAT THE PAIRED ARM WOULD SETTLE is stated where the values are: nlandwcol 0 against 1 on one build at one rung, timestep and orbit count, read on the land runoff ratio and on E/R. The bucket arm is an EXACT control rather than an approximation of one, which is what makes that comparison worth buying.

title: Close the fast vegetation--climate water loop around LSHY-3
description:
Close the fast vegetation--climate water loop around LSHY-3: choose either a shared/online operator or an explicit fixed-point outer iteration with convergence criteria; have LPJ provide chronology-bound LAI, canopy capacity, stomatal conductance and root demand by source/layer; let the climate-side owner compute interception, soil evaporation, transpiration and latent heat from its actual state; return fulfilled uptake to LPJ and debit it once. Retain an LPJ-owned water column only as a named structural control, and reject unconverged replay of vegetation controls into changed climate

Source: `biosphere/notes/soil-land-surface-hydraulic-consistency-audit.md` finding 4
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; interface, iteration and zero/limited-demand fixtures follow LSHY-2/LSHY-3 and EFOR-8, while any coupled response requires BIO-12/BIO-14 and explicit permission for both model runs [step: lpj_driver, lpj_run, baseline_run]. AN EMIC-CLASS CLOSURE OF THIS LOOP IS SMALLER THAN THIS ROW ASSUMES, 2026-08-22. cGENIE's ENTS closes it with THREE ALGEBRAIC FUNCTIONS of two prognostic carbon pools, not a land-surface model: bucket capacity `min(k8, k9 + k10*Csoil)` at `setup_ents.F:474`, roughness `max(0.001, kz0*Cveg)` at `:476`, and a soil albedo interpolating sand to peat in `Csoil` at `initialise_ents.F:239`. ExoPlaSim prescribes all three as `wsmax`, `dz0clim` and `dalbclim`. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: ENTS has no stomatal term in its evaporation either -- `fv` and `fws` feed photosynthesis, and the comment at `surflux.F:1386` distinguishing bare-soil evaporation from evapotranspiration sits above a formula identical in both cases -- so the entire vegetation-to-water coupling there runs through the capacity. That is the cheap closure worth pricing against this row's fuller one. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 32b

title: Make snow, frozen-soil and thermal state consistent across climate and ecology
description:
Make snow, frozen-soil and thermal state consistent across climate and ecology: couple phase-aware hydraulic and thermal properties from LSHY-1 into the ExoPlaSim column, conserve water and energy through accumulation/melt/freeze/thaw, make frozen pore space affect infiltration and flow, and deliver the authoritative SWE, melt, soil temperature and liquid/ice states through EFOR-8 instead of centrally reconstructing them in LPJ

Source: `biosphere/notes/soil-land-surface-hydraulic-consistency-audit.md` finding 5
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; constant-column, phase-change and restart fixtures can proceed without execution; climate and ecological response cases require explicit permission [step: surface_soil_water, baseline_run, lpj_driver, lpj_run]. AMENDED 2026-08-22: `references/climber-x/src/lnd/soil_temp.f90` is the phase-aware 1-D column at this throughput and is the formulation to compare against. The SNOW half is worse than this row assumes and is now GRAV-8's: density is a constant with no compaction at all, so the one snow term carrying gravity is absent. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 3 and 3b

THE CLIMATE-SIDE HALF LANDED 2026-08-24; THE DELIVERY HALF IS EFOR-8's.
landcolumn.f90 gains phase_step, which freezes and thaws one soil layer against
its own cold or heat content relative to melting and is limited by the water
actually there, and frozen_impedance, which is the CONDUCTIVITY form and is
used by nothing because the scheme that would need it has no conductivity to
reduce. column_step now takes the layer ice: ice occupies pore space, so it
comes off the capacity and a frozen layer overflows sooner. That is the
infiltration impedance this row asked for and it needs no conductivity at all.
At zero ice cap - 0.0 is bitwise cap, so LSHY-3's reduction still verifies.

WATER AND ENERGY CLOSE FOR THE SAME REASON: the mass that changes phase and the
temperature change are the same number read two ways. The latent heat is
als - alv, which landmod's own snowmelt already uses, because the model declares
vaporisation and sublimation and derives fusion as the difference.

THE TOLERANCE IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN, and that is the part worth reusing. The
energy identity is read through a temperature difference near 273 K, so its
relative precision is degraded by the ratio of the absolute temperature to the
change; each case carries its own bound from machine epsilon and that ratio,
and the reported number is the worst residual over its own bound. It comes out
at 0.12 and 0.066 at BOTH default real and -fdefault-real-8, which is the
confirmation the bound is the right scaling rather than a constant that happened
to pass. A fourth negative control books the exchange at the latent heat of
vaporisation and must break the energy identity while leaving the water identity
intact; it exceeds its bound by six orders at real-4 and fifteen at real-8.

landmod gains dsoili (soil ice by layer, restart record and schema policy),
dsoilwz (the water column's layer THICKNESSES, which the model has never had --
dwmax is a capacity in metres of water and carries no depth) and nlandwphase,
which defaults to 0 and refuses to run without the layered column.

THE TWO COLUMNS SHARE NO BOUNDARY and the mapping is declared: a water layer
takes the temperature of whichever dsoilz layer contains its midpoint. The
alternative -- making one column a sub-partition of the other -- changes the
soil heat solver's geometry and is a larger decision than this row.

WHAT REMAINS, AND WHO OWNS IT.
- Delivering the authoritative SWE, melt, soil temperature and liquid/ice
  chronology through the forcing contract is EFOR-8's row, and LPJ's
  independent reconstruction stays a named structural control until it lands.
  vendor/lpj-guess was off limits to this batch.
- The snow half is GRAV-8's and is worse than this row assumed: ExoPlaSim's
  snow density is the constant rhosnow = 330 with no compaction while LPJ-GUESS
  ages its snow from 275 to 500, and snow DEPTH is what sets the insulating
  thickness over the soil, so the two columns insulate differently from the
  same snowfall.
- Composition-dependent SENSIBLE heat capacity is still a constant. The phase
  half is now declared in pedology/config/land_column_properties.yaml under
  thermal.phase_dependent; thermal.composition_dependent still carries the
  sentinel and this row owns it.
- Turning nlandwphase on is a climate response case and needs the same
  permission LSHY-3's scheme selection needs.
AMENDED 2026-08-25 by WORLD-GJOV: the snow CONDUCTIVITY half of "the two columns
insulate differently from the same snowfall" is settled and is not this row's or
GRAV-8's any more. lib/snow.py declares Fourteau et al. (2021) Eq. (18) once;
landmod.f90 and vendor/lpj-guess/modules/soil.cpp each restate the adopted row as
a literal and snow.check_restatements() holds both to it, run by
scripts/smoke_test.py and by biosphere/scripts/snow_thermal_gate.py. The ecology
column previously ran Sturm et al. (1997), which is below both arms of the
published kinetics bracket at every density the two components span.

WHAT REMAINS OF THE SNOW HALF IS THE DENSITY AND THE DEPTH, which is GRAV-8's and
is untouched: ExoPlaSim's rhosnow is one namelist key with no compaction while
LPJ-GUESS ages snowdens from 275 to 500, and depth is what sets the insulating
thickness. Sharing the RELATION is what makes that separable -- the two could
never have been reconciled by matching conductivity values, because equal values
at one density is a coincidence at one point of two curves.

A second inconsistency of the same class was found beside it and is world-2aij:
soil.cpp computes the modelled snow's volumetric heat capacity at solid ice's
density rather than the snow's, which is landmod's snowcap defect third instance.
close_reason:
THE DECLARATION THIS ROW OWNED IS MADE, and it is what WORLD-JSFM was blocked on.

thermal.composition_dependent carries the volume-weighted mixture with c_solid and c_water, taken from the same Farouki source the conductivity comes from rather than a second one. Ice is given water's properties, which is exact at nlandwphase 0. The ORGANIC term is a registered ABSENCE under a declared property, owned by sdec-10 and undeclared for the same reason materials.organic.fraction_from is -- a silent zero there would have been a choice made by omission.

thermal.saturation_mapping and thermal.endpoints are new, declared as medians with their p5-p95 spread, recomputed from the build's own states and refusing on drift. Four mutations were tested and all four caught, so the refusal is demonstrated rather than asserted.

MEASURED: effective saturation spans 0.4114 at an empty store to 0.7877 at a full one, p5-p95 0.309-0.541 and 0.699-0.863.

DELIVERY OF THE STATE ITSELF STAYS EFOR-8'S. What this row settles is the contract; carrying the authoritative SWE, melt, soil temperature and liquid/ice states across to the ecology column is the forcing artifact's job and is not done here.

title: Preserve the hydrologic mosaic through native-mesh to climate-grid crossings
description:
Preserve the hydrologic mosaic through native-mesh to climate-grid crossings: combine BIO-11/BIO-17 rootable/open-water fractions, PLHY-5 groundwater-accessible area and SPAT-3/GRID-2 hypsometry into conservative response tiles or an equivalent subgrid distribution on any accepted T21/T42/T85/T127/T170 support; keep upland soil, lake/playa and groundwater-fed fractions distinct, make routed/seepage/baseflow water available to open-water evaporation, and reject cell-mean AWC or water-table depth as an area proxy

Source: `biosphere/notes/soil-land-surface-hydraulic-consistency-audit.md` finding 7, `biosphere/notes/spatial-support-ecological-aggregation-audit.md` finding 5
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; aggregation and limiting-case fixtures can use existing coupling matrices without either model, while unresolved below-mesh placement remains declared under GW-6 [step: hydrography, groundwater, surface_soil_water, baseline_run, lpj_driver]
world-d9u4 SETTLED 2026-08-25 and this row needs nothing built for it. It asks for the native-mesh to climate-grid crossing to preserve the mosaic and explicitly rejects a cell-mean water table depth as an area proxy; a climate-grid saturated AREA is what that asks for, and GW-26's f_sat_max is one. The fraction arrives as one of this row's response-tile shares beside PLHY-5's accessible area. The dependence on a NATIVE-MESH fraction is deleted rather than met. hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 5.
PARTLY BUILT 2026-08-25 by the same artifact as WET-2, hydrography/scripts/build_wetness.py.

WHAT THIS ROW ASKED FOR AND NOW HAS. The native-mesh to climate-grid crossing keeps upland soil and lake/playa distinct as conservative area shares that partition the cell's land exactly, checked rather than assumed, through lib/gridding.py's CATEGORICAL operator -- so the mosaic survives the crossing instead of being averaged into one medium-wet surface. The row's own refusal is enforced by name in hydrography/config/wetness.yaml and read at startup: a cell-mean water table depth or available water capacity may not stand in for an area fraction, and the script exits if the key says otherwise.

WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT HAVE, in order of what unblocks it.
1. THE GROUNDWATER-FED TILE. world-d9u4 settled that this row's dependence on a native-mesh fraction is deleted and that GW-26's climate-grid saturated AREA arrives as one of its response-tile shares. GW-26 has now been SCORED and MISSED, so that share is not licensed and this row is not served after all. PLHY-5's groundwater_access is the other candidate tile and needs water_table.nc, which does not exist on the active build. world-n9sd is the row that decides whether a fraction is licensed at all.
2. BIO-11's ROOTABLE SURFACE AND BIO-17's OPEN-WATER FRACTION do not exist as artifacts anywhere; the nearest thing is a local variable inside exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_albedo.py. wetness_<grid>.nc emits the open-water share this row needs from that side, and hydrography/config/wetness.yaml states the closure identity BIO-11 will have to satisfy rather than asserting it.
3. ROUTED, SEEPAGE AND BASEFLOW WATER REACHING OPEN-WATER EVAPORATION is not in this artifact and is not hydrography's to place: it is the ledger absence open_water_evaporation_from_routed_water, already owned by this row, and it is a change to the climate column's land surface. The area basis it needs -- the cell's open-water area rather than the land cell -- is what this artifact now supplies.
4. HYPSOMETRY, SPAT-3/GRID-2. Not used and not needed for the tiles that exist: every class here is resolved per region, so a within-cell distribution is a measurement rather than an inference.
2026-08-25. THE GROUNDWATER-FED TILE IS NOW DECLARED AND REFUSED BY NAME in
hydrography/config/wetness.yaml, which is what this file does with a class that
has no source, and build_wetness.py publishes it in classes_absent. What it
would take, and the two candidate routes fail differently:

GW-26's saturated-area closure is withdrawn PERMANENTLY, and reviving it needs a
different INSTRUMENT rather than a narrower criterion. world-n9sd measured the
instrument itself: resampling the cells, the gain the terrain half carries over
the cell-mean depth alone is at or below its own scatter on all eight arms of
both Earth sets, so point bore depths at cell scale are blind to the effect and
no cut of sink_fraction makes them see it. An AREAL observation -- a measured
saturation or inundation extent -- is what would license a revival.

PLHY-5's groundwater_access needs NO closure at all. build_groundwater_access.py
already evaluates the access criterion on the native regions where the depth
lives and crosses an AREA, which is exactly this tile. It needs water_table.nc,
and no build in source/ has one: hydrography/data/<build>/ carries none on
either. The cost is the `groundwater` step then `groundwater_access`, both
cost: minutes in config/pipeline.yaml, with groundwater needing surface_water
and a climatology first.

EITHER ROUTE CARRIES THE REGIME OR IT IS NOT LICENSED. The depth it comes from
scores 0.4581 against Australia's bores, below the 0.5 of no discrimination, and
0.6655 on the United States unconfined set. groundwater_access_<grid>.nc already
reports the sink_fraction regime share per cell including its two kinds of
no-answer; a share that mixes the licensed regime with the unlicensed one is a
number with no verdict attached.

FIXED IN PASSING, and it was blocking: wetness.yaml had been unparseable since
6a494436. A class description gained a bare "three: " inside a plain scalar, so
yaml.safe_load raised and build_wetness.py died on its first config read.
--selftest never caught it because it returned before read_config(). The scalar
is a block scalar now, and the first two selftest checks are that the config
loads with its refusals intact and that every class either names a source or
says why it has none.

THE TWO INTERVAL FLOORS THIS ROW OWNS ARE DOWN, under world-15i0.
lake_precipitation and open_water_evaporation move from annual to a new
climatology_bin value now that surface_water.py reads the lake terms per bin,
and the ledger's TIMING finding against lake_precipitation is gone. Item 3 of
this row's list, routed and seepage water reaching open-water evaporation, is
unchanged and is still the climate column's to place.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTERED 2026-08-30, before the measurement. The land-hydrology instance of notes/audits/ocean-support-nonlinear-reductions.md, whose method is reused rather than re-derived: expand about the cell mean, COMPUTE the correction, compare it against the size of the effect the term carries, and separate a control that CAN fail from the arms that matter.

WHAT THE OCEAN SIDE ESTABLISHED AND THIS SIDE INHERITS. A gate that asks only for conservation cannot see this class of loss, because the affine quantity passes it exactly. There the affine quantity was ocean volume in depth; here it is the bucket capacity in the lake fraction, and world-cyu3 already records that the blend (1 - f_lake) * C_soil + f_lake * lake_dwmax_m is literally the area-weighted mean of a two-point capacity distribution and adds no curvature of its own. So the control passes here for the same reason it passed there, and the arms that matter are the ones conservation cannot see.

P1. CONTROL, and it is the arm that can fail. support_exoplasim-T21.nc's mosaic shares partition the cell exactly: surface_share sums to 1, f_barren + f_nonbarren = 1 on covered land, and land/ocean/inland-water areas sum to the mesh area. A nonzero residual indicts the crossing, not the physics.

P2. THE MOSAIC SURVIVES TO THE SUPPORT AND DIES AT THE CONSUMER. build_spatial_support.py emits f_land, f_solved_lake, f_barren and hydrologic_share as distinct conservative shares through gridding's CATEGORICAL operator, so the crossing itself keeps the tiles apart. build_surface_soil_water.py --lakes then collapses the two-tile capacity distribution to one scalar BEFORE the model's two convex consumers. The loss is therefore located at the blend and not at the reduction, and P2 is falsified if the support does not in fact carry the tiles separately.

P3. THE COLLAPSE IS NOT A SMALL PERTURBATION. world-cyu3 bounds the gap above by f_lake * |C_soil - lake_dwmax_m|. lake_dwmax_m is 0.2 m and this build's evaporable_mm has a median of 85.9 mm, so |C_soil - lake_dwmax_m| exceeds C_soil itself on the median cell: at f_lake = 1 the blend more than doubles the capacity rather than nudging it. PRE-REGISTERED CLAIM: the capacity perturbation, expressed as a fraction of the cell's own soil capacity, exceeds 100 per cent on more than half the lake-bearing land area at f_lake = 1, and the operative question is therefore what f_lake actually is. FALSIFIED if the measured f_lake over lake-bearing cells is small enough that f_lake * |delta C| stays under the bar below on nearly all of that area.

NO SIGN IS PRE-REGISTERED FOR THE SIZE across the ladder, for world-cyu3's reason: f_lake's spread depends on how many cells straddle a shoreline. Only T21 support exists on this build, so no ladder claim is made at all.

THE BAR, declared before the result and not invented for it: the accepted baseline run's 0.12 W m-2 state-storage tolerance, which config/partial_surface.yaml already selected the tile operator against and which the land audit's albedo arm already reports in. A capacity error reaches it through the wetness factor min(1, w/(0.4 C)) at landcolumn.f90:370 and thence the latent heat flux, so the arm reports the wetness-factor gap converted into W m-2 of latent heat against 0.12, and states the conversion rather than asserting a percentage.

WHAT THIS ARM DOES NOT COVER, declared before the measurement. The groundwater-fed tile, which needs water_table.nc and therefore the groundwater solve; that step is cost: hours in config/pipeline.yaml and was measured this week at 2600 per cent CPU for over 40 minutes without writing (world-wfge). It is a checkpoint with a price, not a run this arm starts.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESULT 2026-08-31, against the pre-registration above. notes/audits/land-mosaic-support-reductions.md carries the finding; hydrography/scripts/lake_mosaic_cost.py is the instrument and hydrography/analysis/lake_mosaic_cost.json the output.

P1 CONTROL PASSES. The mosaic shares partition the cell: surface_share sums to 1 within 3.0e-8, f_barren + f_nonbarren the same, and land + ocean + inland-water equals the mesh area exactly. The first two are the float32 the shares are stored at; the areas are float64 and close to zero.

P2 HELD, and it is the answer to this row as posed. THE CROSSING PRESERVES THE MOSAIC. build_spatial_support.py emits upland-soil, lake and barren as distinct conservative shares through gridding's categorical operator. The loss is one step further down, at the consumer, where build_surface_soil_water.py collapses the two-tile capacity distribution into one scalar before two nonlinear laws read it. A fix aimed at the crossing would be aimed at the half that is already correct, and that is worth stating because this row's title invites exactly that fix.

P3 FAILED, by its own stated falsifier. f_lake over lake-bearing cells is median 0.0105, mean 0.0487, max 0.6867, and the capacity perturbation as a fraction of the cell's own soil capacity is 0.48 per cent at the median rather than the over-100 per cent I registered. Only 2.6 per cent of lake-bearing land area is perturbed by more than 100 per cent. The measured f_lake is small enough that the effect stays under the bar, which is the falsification condition as written.

THE TWO LOSSES, priced separately because the blend is inert, against the 0.12 W m-2 bar on the planet mean:

  the whole lake tile, absent today          -0.048 to -0.082 W m-2   0.40 to 0.68 x bar
  the mixing term, if the blend were staged  +0.016 to +0.028 W m-2   0.14 to 0.23 x bar

NEITHER REACHES THE BAR at either end of the bracket. The absent tile is two to three times the mixing term, which is the ordering that matters: staging the blend buys back most of what is missing and tiling buys back the remainder. Worst cells are -16.0 and +9.9 W m-2, so the term is concentrated rather than absent.

THE INSTRUMENT WAS REBUILT MID-MEASUREMENT and the first version's numbers were discarded. Recovering the potential latent heat flux as hfls / beta looks exact; beta is under 0.05 on 48 per cent of this planet's land bins and the quotient reaches 1e17 W m-2. It is capped at the available surface energy rss + rls instead, and the upper end of every bracket above gives each cell its whole net radiation to evaporation.

A POPULATION DECLARED RATHER THAN DROPPED: on 55 of 1,639 land cells the climatology's soil water exceeds the staged bucket capacity, by up to 0.068 m on a 0.049 m bucket. Every number is reported with and without them and the verdict is the same on both; filed as world-tp4f because a bucket cannot hold more than its capacity and one of those two artifacts is wrong.

THE SIGN IS NEGATIVE on the absent-tile arm, meaning staging the lake tile AS CONFIGURED would lower the wetness factor and lower the latent heat flux. lake_dwmax_m exceeds the staged soil capacity on cells holding 55.8 per cent of lake-bearing land area. That is world-kvr's inversion measured in W m-2 rather than in millimetres.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTERED 2026-08-30, BEFORE READING ANY WATER TABLE ON THIS BUILD.

THE ROW'S PREMISE IS ALREADY HALF WITHDRAWN BY THE CONFIG ITSELF, and this is recorded before the measurement so it is not read back as a result. minerals/config/downstream_prospectivity.yaml no longer substitutes rainfall for water table depth and no longer says it does: the invented 500 mm/yr wet cap was REMOVED rather than re-derived, on Sillitoe (2005) p. 736 stating there is no wet bound on rainfall at all, and the surviving dry bound of 10 mm/yr is Reich et al. (2009)'s own measured precipitation figure from the Atacama rather than a proxy for anything. The phrase this row quotes -- that the config says in its own comments it substitutes rainfall because nothing better exists -- returns no match in the current file. So the work left is not a REPLACEMENT. It is whether a depth term should be ADDED where the rule currently applies none and names the absence.

WHAT WOULD LICENSE ADDING ONE, declared now:
  1. A SOURCED boundary, not an invented threshold. Reich and Vasconcelos (2015) p. 306 put oxidation in the vadose zone and the capillary fringe and secondary sulfides below the water table where pO2 falls to about 1e-40 atm. That is a boundary at the water table itself and needs no number chosen here. Any term requiring a depth THRESHOLD in metres is refused unless a read source states one; this project has read Reich 2009, Reich and Vasconcelos 2015 and Sillitoe 2005 and none of them gives a water table depth threshold, only a leached-cap thickness of several hundred metres, which is a profile thickness and not a modelled steady-state depth.
  2. A FIELD THAT MEANS SOMETHING WHERE THE RULE FIRES. hydrography/notes/earth-calibration-criterion.md establishes a three-way rule per cell: sink_fraction near 1 means the depth is the local recharge-and-evapotranspiration balance and is a recharge map in a water table's units; low sink_fraction with at_surface set means the cell is pinned and seeping and the depth is 0 by construction; low with at_surface CLEAR is the only case where the lateral term did the work, and GW-22 measured per-cell skill only there. A depth term is therefore SELF-GATING on that third case rather than applied everywhere, which is what config/pipeline.yaml's groundwater gate asks these rows for.
  3. A MATERIALITY FLOOR, declared now at 5%: if fewer than 5% of the land cells carrying non-zero porphyry_cu_mo prospectivity fall in the third case, the term is not added, min-6 closes on the measurement rather than on the rule, and the absence is recorded with its number. Below one cell in twenty the added machinery would be reporting this planet's groundwater regime rather than its deposits.

WHAT WOULD MEAN WRONG: adding any depth threshold in metres that no read source states; or applying a depth term over cells where sink_fraction says the depth is the recharge field wearing a water table's units.

ORDER: this row is taken LAST, after gw-24 and gw-18, because both move the field it reads and CLAUDE.md's loop agreement requires a step to read the best available input rather than the first.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTERED 2026-08-30, SECOND ENTRY, BEFORE ANY SCORING OF THE FLAG.

THE MECHANISM'S OWN DEPTH IS OUT OF THE INSTRUMENT'S RANGE, and this is recorded before the flag is scored so the flag test is not read as the whole question. Reich and Vasconcelos (2015) p. 306 make the qualifier a leached cap reaching 'several hundred meters ... particularly when the water table was deep enough', and Sillitoe (2005) p. 736 makes a tropical climate the most favourable for rapid supergene upgrading GIVEN A DEEP WATER TABLE. The modelled steady-state depth on Earth has a median of about 5 m and a 95th percentile of about 52 m across every configuration this project has run. The depth the sources make the control is an order of magnitude above the instrument's entire range, so a depth term keyed on 'deep enough' cannot be evaluated by this field however skilful the field is. failure-modes class 34.

WHAT IS LEFT THAT THE INSTRUMENT COULD CARRY is one boolean and not a depth: a cell whose water table is AT THE SURFACE has no vadose zone, and Reich and Vasconcelos put oxidation in the vadose zone and the capillary fringe with secondary sulfides below the water table where pO2 falls to about 1e-40 atm. That boundary is at the water table itself and needs no number chosen here. water_table.nc ships it as at_surface.

AND THAT FLAG HAS NEVER BEEN SCORED. hydrography/analysis/earth_calibration.json carries fourteen runs and every one of them scores the DEPTH: Pearson, held-out R2, ceiling, spreads. None scores at_surface against anything. earth_calibration.py carries  in its results and prints it, and no bar has ever been put on it.

THE TEST, DECLARED NOW, BEFORE IT IS RUN. On the bore-carrying cells of both scored sets, split the cells by the model's at_surface flag and compare the OBSERVED cell-mean depth between the two groups.

  PASS: the observed cell-mean depth is LOWER in model-pinned cells than in model-unpinned cells, by more than the standard error of that difference, on the United States unconfined set, which is the regime GW-22 measured skill in.

  MISS: the difference is at or below its own standard error, or has the wrong sign.

A flag that cannot order the two groups cannot exclude anything, so a miss refuses the term outright. Reported beside it and not part of the bar: the share of bore-carrying cells the model marks pinned in each set, and the observed depth distribution in each group, because a flag that is RIGHT but fires on almost nothing is a different disposition from one that is wrong.

WHAT WOULD MEAN WRONG: adding the term on a flag whose discrimination is at or below its own scatter, which is the same error hydrography/README.md records for the f_sat closure, withdrawn on exactly that ground.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
VERDICT 2026-08-30: CLOSED, AND THE TERM IS REFUSED ON RANGE. Both halves of this row are settled and neither needed the Vesper solve.

1. THE PREMISE IS WITHDRAWN. The rainfall proxy this row is filed against was supergene copper's maximum_precipitation_mm_yr: 500.0, and commit 61557243a deleted it on 2026-08-18, five days before this row was created. It went as CONTRADICTED rather than as unsourced -- Sillitoe (2005) p. 736 states there is no wet bound on rainfall at all -- and nothing replaced it. The phrase this row quotes, that the config says in its own comments it substitutes rainfall because nothing better exists, returns no match in the current file. Bauxite's and nickel laterite's precipitation thresholds are not proxies either: Price et al. (1997) and Butt and Cluzel (2013) state them as rainfall criteria. So there is nothing to REPLACE, and the question is whether a depth term should be ADDED where the rule now applies none and names the absence.

2. IT SHOULD NOT, AND THE REFUSAL IS ON RANGE RATHER THAN SKILL. This is the pre-registered instrument check and it fails by two orders of magnitude. Reich and Vasconcelos (2015) p. 306 make the control a leached cap of several hundred metres, 'particularly when the water table was deep enough'. The modelled 95th percentile over Earth land is 6.86 m in the configuration this component runs, and reaches 52 to 60 m only under a uniform 2 km aquifer thickness -- which GW-18 has now measured against the only sediment thickness this project holds and found contradicted over 99.3% of the land on canonical-10m-carve2. It is structural and not a setting: with the sink dominant the depth is lambda ln(ET_max / R), so a hundred metres needs an evaporative demand e^100 times the recharge.

3. THE WEAKER TERM WAS TESTED AGAINST THE BAR DECLARED BEFORE IT AND MISSES. A field that cannot say how deep can still say whether there is a vadose zone at all, which is the boundary the mechanism sits on and needs no threshold in metres. Splitting the bore-carrying mesh cells of the cached 15.19 km Earth solves by at_surface:

  Australia, all:            53,410 bores, 3,276 cells, 0 marked at_surface
  United States, unconfined: 73,451 bores, 6,870 cells, 1 marked at_surface

The declared test -- observed cell-mean depth lower in model-pinned cells by more than the standard error of the difference -- cannot be run, because one group is empty on both continents. Declared disposition for a miss was to refuse the term outright, and that stands. The flag is not WRONG on scored ground, it is absent from it; and the same solver marks about a quarter of Vesper's land at the surface, so it is a term that does nothing where it can be checked and a great deal where it cannot.

4. THE MATERIALITY FLOOR I PRE-REGISTERED IS MOOT. It gated on the share of porphyry-bearing land in the flow-dominated regime, which only matters if a term exists to apply there. Points 2 and 3 refuse the term before the regime question is reached, so minerals/data was not built for this and the 5% floor was never tested. Recorded so it is not read as having passed.

WHAT LANDED. minerals/config/downstream_prospectivity.yaml now carries the refusal beside the rule, because a reader who knows this project models a water table will ask why the rule ignores it. hydrography/notes/groundwater-et-sink.md carries the at_surface measurement with its table beside the existing MIN-6 range finding. hydrography/notes/groundwater-scoping.md section 6 no longer claims three rules key on a water table through a rainfall proxy. config/pipeline.yaml's groundwater gate no longer points this row at a restricted re-measurement; SURF-7 still asks for its own and was sharing the sentence.

NO SOURCE WAS MISSING. Reich (2009), Reich and Vasconcelos (2015), Sillitoe (2005) and Sillitoe (2010) are all held and read, and none of them states a water table depth threshold. That is why no number was invented here.

title: Fix the prospectivity normalisation, which is unstable across builds. Weights-of-evidence
description:
Fix the prospectivity normalisation, which is unstable across builds. Weights-of-evidence requires a point set of known deposits and REFUSES TO RUN without one, and every validation tool in ArcSDM takes deposit points as a required parameter; there is no unsupervised prospectivity path in the toolbox at all. So the supervised-method tension does not apply here: an exhaustive search of `minerals/` for prior, posterior, contrast, training or AUC returns nothing, and the word it uses is FAVOURABILITY, which is correct for an unsupervised index. THE DEFECT IS ELSEWHERE AND IS REAL: `normalise()` divides by `field[land].max()`, a single cell's value, so A NEW BUILD PRODUCING ONE UNUSUALLY FAVOURABLE CELL RESCALES THE ENTIRE FIELD DOWNWARD. `minerals/README.md` states that comparing one deposit type against another says nothing, which covers the cross-type case and not the temporal one; its argument against quantiles is about the top of the distribution and does not address the stability of the divisor. AND ONE HONEST STRUCTURAL POINT: these fields are untestable within this world by construction, which meets this project's own standard that a check with no possible wrong answer is not a test. The `grounding` attribute grades the provenance of the RULE rather than the correctness of the FIELD -- a good move that no document draws out loud. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 49d

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 49d
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22, and there were FOUR duplications rather than the three this row named. `minerals/scripts/prospectivity_scale.py` is now the one copy of `normalise`, `host_ceiling` and `host_weight` -- the fourth was `host_weight`, inlined at `build_prospectivity.py:119-124` and defined again at `build_downstream_prospectivity.py:153`. THE DIVISOR IS NOW A PROPERTY OF THE RULE: `input_ranges` in both configs give each modifier's declared range, `ceiling()` mirrors the score expression term for term, and `normalise` RAISES if any land score exceeds the ceiling -- a closed form that disagrees with the expression it bounds has a right answer, so it is a test and not a diagnostic. THE OLD DIVISOR WAS A SEAFLOOR CELL ON A LAND-ONLY FIELD: `r_stress` maxes at 5.5358 over all cells against 4.7084 over land, compressing the stress term by about 3.8x. It is replaced by `stress_reference = 1.449732`, which is Orogen's own `maxStress`, the `STRESS_PERCENTILE = 0.97` quantile of `r_stress` above `STRESS_PROPAGATE_MIN`. VERIFIED AGAINST AN IDENTITY RATHER THAN ASSUMED, and re-verified independently: `min(1, min(1, r_stress/1.449732) * 3.0)` reproduces the exported `r_t_foldBelt` to 1e-6 on 99.39 percent of 1,079,396 land cells, and every one of the 6,600 misses has `r_t_foldBelt == 0`, the cells Orogen skips as internally-ocean. Rounding to 1.45 holds on only 31.58 percent, so the full figure is declared rather than tidied. CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING: orogenic_au's attainable maximum is 6.4 against a raw maximum of 5.4399 on this build, so the field now tops out at 0.850 where the old divisor reported 1.0 by construction. ONE SUBSTANTIVE RULE CHANGE, argued in the config: `ca_excess` was `Ca/HCO3 - 1`, unbounded above, so a single basin at Ca/HCO3 = 40 would set the divisor for every gypsum basin. It is now `1 - HCO3/Ca`, the exact mirror of the alkaline side's `1 - Ca/HCO3`, same ordering and bounded 0-1 by the ratio rather than by a build. NOTED IN PASSING: `elevation.js:543` comments the quantile as 95th where the constant is 0.97.
close_reason: done 2026-08-22, and there were FOUR duplications rather than the three this row named.

title: Establish what a multi-layer column ocean costs and what it is worth. NLEV_OCE = 1
description:
Establish what a multi-layer column ocean costs and what it is worth. `NLEV_OCE = 1` in `oceanmod.f90` is a source constant and the module is already written for `NLEV_OCE > 1`: `vdiffkl` is in `oceanmod_nl`, line 255 branches on it, and line 229 collapses the general case to the slab. What is missing is a layer count, a `dlayer` profile, and a measurement of what the change does to the seasonal amplitude that `mixed_layer_depth_m: 50.0` currently sets on an orbit half Earth's length. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is a viability verdict, a cost and an effect, not the change

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` finding 1
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. It is a source constant, so CLAUDE.md rule 4 costs a full `rebuild_binaries.py` pass rather than one executable, and that is most of the price. The prediction A3 requires can be made offline and before anything is compiled: a column of N layers coupled by `vdiffkl` has a computable impulse response, and the seasonal damping follows from it. This is the cheapest change in the note that acts on a term `config/planet.yaml` already declares as ExoPlaSim's default arriving unnamed [step: rebuild_binaries, bootstrap_run]. A SPECTRAL TERM THE SLAB HIDES, 2026-08-22: water's e-folding depth never exceeds 0.51 m anywhere above 0.75 um, and 61.8 percent of this star's flux sits there against 46.3 percent of the Sun's, so a larger share of the shortwave is deposited in the topmost water as heat. A one-layer slab cannot see this. A multi-layer column can, and its penetrative solar heating would be MORE surface-concentrated than Earth tuning assumes, stratifying the top of the column more strongly -- so this belongs in the case for the column rather than being discovered after it. OCN-10 already names net and penetrative solar in its forcing contract. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 40e
2026-08-28 EXPLORATION COMPLETE, NEGATIVE ADOPTION VERDICT. ocean/config/column_response.yaml and analysis/ocean_column_response.py/json reproduce oceanmod:vdiffo's semi-implicit elimination at the configured 30-hour day, 32 ocean steps/day and 182.8-day orbit. The one-layer result agrees with the analytic harmonic response and every tested column closes thickness-weighted heat to <=1e-12. At vdiffkl=1e-4, the 50 m slab responds 0.012232 K per W/m2; intended 50 m subdivisions respond 0.039257 (2 layers), 0.035092 (4), and 0.034153 (10), or 2.79-3.21x the slab. Thus the term is material and profile/diffusivity dependent, not a cheap correction. The old issue premise is structurally false: oceanini unconditionally sets dlayer(NLEV_OCE)=mldepth, so a declared 10+40 m profile runs as 10+50 m unless source is changed; mksst also deposits all yheat in level 1, so levels do not implement penetrative shortwave. Cost is viable/O(N), with two persistent real fields, one restart real and about 40 scratch bytes per horizontal cell per layer. Verdict: do not adopt in the active tier. cGENIE/GOLDSTEIN is the adopted resolved ocean, and adding a second materially active vertical reservoir to ExoPlaSim requires an explicit state/energy coupling decision rather than turning on this dormant diffuser. No source edit, rebuild or climate run is warranted by the rejected exploration. Full smoke 56/0, docs and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Exploration delivered: exact discrete response, closure, cost and source audit show the multilayer path is viable but material, underdetermined, top-only heated and incompatible with its namelist-only premise; rejected for the adopted GOLDSTEIN tier.

title: Define and version one chronological atmosphere/land/ice-to-ocean forcing contract
description:
Define and version one chronological atmosphere/land/ice-to-ocean forcing contract: interval bounds and absolute time; source/destination support; wind stress; net and penetrative shortwave, longwave, sensible and latent heat; precipitation, evaporation, routed river and groundwater discharge; sea-ice freeze/melt and brine/freshwater exchange; salt and required solutes; units, signs, masks and state-versus-flux semantics. Assign every heat, water and salt term one owner, preserve correlated forcing, and retain temperature or salinity restoring only as named numerical controls rather than physical sources

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` section 8a
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; schema, synthetic conservation and restart/interval fixtures require no model run and extend EFOR-1's conventions without reusing its land-ecology artifact. Production fields depend on accepted climate, LSHY-2, ANUT-6 and OCN-11; any ocean integration requires explicit permission [step: baseline_run, hydrography]. A REFERENCE INTERFACE EXISTS and it is closer than expected: `vendor/cgenie/genie-plasim` is a complete Planet Simulator sharing TWENTY-FOUR OF ITS TWENTY-FIVE MODULES with `vendor/exoplasim`, the sole exception being `geniemod.f90`, the coupling itself. So a PlaSim-to-GOLDSTEIN exchange already exists against the same `pumamod` state this model carries. It moves net solar, evaporation, precipitation, runoff and two staggered wind-stress pairs to the ocean, and returns sea surface temperature, ice temperature, height, fraction and albedo, alongside area, mask, an atmospheric pressure term and CO2. Read it before specifying from first principles -- and note the term it will not give you: every exchange array is dimensioned 360, an Earth year of daily fields compiled in rather than configured, against this world's 180.7 days. What replaces that is this contract's to state. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 10b and 10c. AN ARCHITECTURAL FORK THIS ROW DECIDES BY IMPLICATION AND SHOULD DECIDE EXPLICITLY, 2026-08-22. The published ExoPlaSim-to-cGENIE path does NOT do what this contract specifies. It keeps EMBM running and supplies ExoPlaSim's DYNAMICS to it -- `ea_` parameters appear 13,688 times across shipped configs against 7,314 `go_`, the regrid README sets `ea_11`, and EMBM's namelist reads `xu_wstress`, `yu_wstress`, `xv_wstress`, `yv_wstress`, `u_wspeed` and `v_wspeed` from files, which is exactly what that path converts. EMBM then computes the surface heat fluxes itself, with its transport tunable through `diffamp`, `diffwid`, `difflin`, `betaz` and `betam`. THIS ROW SPECIFIES THE OTHER ARCHITECTURE: a contract carrying net and penetrative shortwave, longwave, sensible and latent heat, i.e. ExoPlaSim computing the fluxes and no EMBM. Both are viable and they cost different things. Keeping EMBM avoids OCN-5's loop but means running a second atmosphere whose transport coefficients are calibrated for Earth, on a planet with 30-hour rotation and 32 degree obliquity -- and re-tuning them so a coupled answer comes out is what failure-modes class 16 forbids. Dropping EMBM keeps ExoPlaSim as the only atmosphere and requires the loop. The second is more consistent with everything else here, but this row should CHOOSE rather than imply. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 28c. A PUBLISHED INSTANCE OF THIS CONTRACT EXISTS AND CAN BE READ OFF, 2026-08-22. cGENIE ships a PlaSim, and `vendor/cgenie/genie-plasim/src/fortran/` is a strict SUBSET of ExoPlaSim's module set plus exactly one file: `geniemod.f90`, 71 lines, pure declaration. THE WHOLE COUPLING SURFACE IS ONE ARRAY-DECLARATION MODULE, which is far smaller than this row assumes. Ocean to atmosphere, 6 used: sst, ice temperature, sea-ice height, sea-ice fraction, SEA-ICE ALBEDO, and CO2. Atmosphere to ocean, 17, each a full seasonal cycle: latent and sensible transfer COEFFICIENTS rather than fluxes, netsolar, solfor, insolar, inlong, sat, spec_hum, pressure, evap, precip, runoff, wind stress as two level pairs, and windspeed. Take this as the starting draft of the contract rather than deriving one. The unit and resolution traps a port hits are in the survey section. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 30 THE RETURN SET IS BOUNDED, 2026-08-24, and sea ice is NOT in it. Section 7b of the ocean audit settles the authority question: ExoPlaSim's icemod stays authoritative for sea ice, so the fields returned from the ocean are heat-flux convergence, via surface code 903 under oceanmod's nfluko = 1, and OCEAN SURFACE VELOCITY, which is what OCN-21's advection term consumes. Ice fraction, thickness and albedo travel the other way, as forcing the ocean receives. Do not specify them as returns: icemod's read_ice_surface channel exists and taking it would sever the ice-albedo feedback within a run, remap a threshold field across every rung of the ladder, and put a class-16 correction on the model's own ice. The atmosphere-to-ocean half of the contract is unchanged.

OCN-2 SETTLED ONE TERM OF THIS CONTRACT, 2026-08-24, and it is not the one it looks like. The zero-integral condition on a prescribed ocean heat transport holds on the OCEAN, not on the globe. `oceanmod.f90:getflxco` interpolates surface code 903 over the whole grid and only `addfc` restricts it to `yls < 1`, so the part of a globally zero-integral field that falls on land is discarded and what the ocean receives has the ocean-area-weighted mean of the land part as a net source. Measured on the T42 verification field, that residual is -0.919 W/m2 of ocean for a field whose global integral is 2e-8. It is a property of the land mask, so it moves with every build and every carve, and it cannot be a constant in the contract. `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` section 11e.

THE REGRIDDING HALF IS SPECIFIED AND world-gb0t CARRIES IT, 2026-08-25. notes/audits/cgenie-parallelism-and-coupling-support.md section 5. Holden's precedent restricted itself to a matched grid to avoid interpolation, and that reason does not transfer intact: this coupling is offline, so the feedback path is gone, but a non-conservative regrid of a CLIMATOLOGY is a permanent spatially structured spurious source in an ocean integrated for of order 10,000 years, where a synchronous coupling's error is transient. So the requirement changes shape rather than relaxing, from "avoid interpolation" to "the crossing conserves exactly and the residual is reported". AN ARGUMENT FOR THIS ROW'S ARCHITECTURE THAT THE RECORD DID NOT CARRY: a surface flux is nonlinear in the surface state, so the average of the flux is not the flux of the average. With ExoPlaSim computing the fluxes, what crosses IS the flux, already evaluated at the atmosphere's resolution, and averaging it is a conservative linear operation. The eliminated offline-regrid architecture would have had EMBM recompute the fluxes from coarse state, putting the nonlinearity back at 5 to 10 degrees. THE PART WITH NO CLEAN ANSWER is the coastal mask disagreement: the two masks come from the same Orogen mesh at different resolutions and cannot agree, so every joule and kilogram over an atmosphere-ocean cell that is ocean-grid land has to go somewhere NAMED or the budgets close with a coastline-shaped residual.
