title: Build the ocean spatial-support and bathymetry contract from the accepted 10M Orogen export
description:
Build the ocean spatial-support and bathymetry contract from the accepted 10M Orogen export: conservative wet area and volume; partial coasts; depth/hypsometry; shelves, sills, straits and closed marginal seas; routed river mouths; explicit bathymetric smoothing and connectivity changes; ocean-grid identity; and conservative maps to every T21/T42/T85/T127/T170 atmosphere. Require area/volume/constant closure and resolution/connectivity diagnostics against the native mesh rather than treating a convenient coarse ocean grid as truth

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` section 8b, `biosphere/notes/spatial-support-ecological-aggregation-audit.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; extends SPAT-1 through SPAT-5 and SPAT-8/10, and its geometry/remap fixtures require no climate or ocean run. Host-specific grid generation follows OCN-3; any circulation adequacy or timing measurement requires explicit permission [step: orogen, hydrography, boundary_conditions]. AMENDED 2026-08-22: the requirement to declare bathymetric smoothing and connectivity changes explicitly now has an OBSERVED case and not only an argument. BIG-MITgcm removes isolated oceanic points and lakes irrespective of size, and sets every point shallower than 20 m to 20 m, as a numerical-stability step in grid preparation. On a world whose generator produces closed basins in quantity that is not a detail -- and note the pre-carve build's 76 percent endorheic drainage is a LIMIT under rule 9 rather than a state, since the carve loop exists to open basins, so what matters is that the class of feature exists and the step deletes it irrespective of size. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 4. A GENERATOR ROUTE EXISTS AND NEEDS NO GCM. muffingen is at `references/muffingen/`, GPL-3.0, and `EXAMPLE_BLANK.m` sets `par_gcm=''` with every netCDF input name empty, so it will build `.k1`, `.paths` and `.psiles` from a supplied mask and topography alone rather than from another model's output -- which is this row's route from the Orogen bathymetry. `EXAMPLE_K2_supercontinent.m` is the idealised-world precedent beside it. Note the constraint OCN-18 turned up: island count drives a compile-time bound defaulting to 5, so the contract has to REPORT the island count a candidate configuration resolves, not merely produce one. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 10d and 10f. MUFFINGEN GENERATES SEVEN THINGS AND THIS PROJECT ALREADY HAS BETTER VERSIONS OF SEVERAL, so this contract must state which are taken and which are overridden -- the defaults are all ON. `EXAMPLE_BLANK.m` enables `opt_makemask`, `opt_maketopo`, `opt_makeocean`, `opt_makerunoff`, `opt_makewind`, `opt_makealbedo` and a sediment option. Runoff routing is `hydrography`'s, with drainage networks, catchments and a lake solver; albedo is `build_surface_albedo.py`'s and PHYS-14's; mask and bathymetry come from Orogen rather than being regridded from another model's output. WHAT ONLY MUFFINGEN KNOWS HOW TO BUILD is the grid topology, `.k1`, `.paths` and `.psiles`, and that is what to take. `opt_makezonalwind` must be OFF: the wind it would generate is a synthetic zonal profile fitted to Earth's circulation, and this world's stress is what ExoPlaSim computes at 30-hour rotation and 32 degree obliquity. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 18a and 18b. THE MECHANISM FOR THE FAR SIDE OF DISCHARGE EXISTS AND IS SMALL, 2026-08-22. `references/climber-x/src/geo/coast_cells.f90:115-186` delivers runoff, calving and weathering flux to N ocean cells per coastal cell, about 190 lines, with an ORDERED neighbour list: the cell itself, then 3x3 neighbours SORTED BY FEWEST OCEAN NEIGHBOURS FIRST, then a fixed 28-entry distant stencil reaching four cells in longitude. The embayment-first ordering is the non-obvious part -- freshwater goes preferentially into enclosed water rather than straight to open ocean. `river_discharge()` here stops at the land margin, so this is the liftable shape for the far side. NOTE ALSO `fix_runoff.f90`, which exists purely because the hi-res routing destination and the coarse ocean fraction disagree; that is the mesh-versus-grid disagreement this project has not hit only because discharge stops early. AND A CHOICE THIS PROJECT MADE SILENTLY: the peer's land/ocean fraction threshold is LATITUDE-DEPENDENT, `f_crit + max(0, f_crit_eq-f_crit)*cos(lat)**30`, doubled at the poles, against this project's scalar `geography_land_threshold: 0.5`. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 47e-f THE REGRIDDER IS NOW LOAD-BEARING, 2026-08-24. Section 59 eliminates the synchronous architecture, whose affordability came from matching the atmosphere and ocean horizontal grids to avoid interpolation. Offline full-flux buys the ocean's independence from the resolution ladder and pays for it HERE: this row's support and bathymetry contract is the only thing standing between a coarse ocean grid and every rung of T21/T42/T85/T127/T170, so it must be correct at each of them rather than at one. That makes SPAT-11's ESMF conservation identity -- sum(F_src*A_src*frac_src) == sum(F_dst*A_dst) under destination-area normalisation, with the fraction field travelling with the result -- a requirement of this contract and not an improvement to it. A VECTOR FIELD JOINS THIS CONTRACT, 2026-08-24. Section 7b's sea-ice decision has the ocean returning a surface VELOCITY, which world-pt8's advection term consumes on the atmosphere's grid at every rung of the ladder. That is the first vector this contract carries, and a vector does not remap like a scalar: state what happens to direction under the mapping, and whether the components are remapped separately or the field is rotated, rather than leaving it to the caller. The ESMF conservation identity this row already inherits is a statement about extensive scalars and does not cover it, so a vector needs its own check with a right answer -- solid-body rotation is one that can fail.

THE COUPLING RESOLUTION HAS A RECOMMENDATION AND A DECISION PROCEDURE, 2026-08-25. notes/audits/cgenie-parallelism-and-coupling-support.md section 4. The cost constraint that made this a price question is gone: EMBM is 12.5 to 19.9 per cent of the instructions and the offline architecture does not run it, EMBM also sets the timestep so an EMBM-free ocean inherits its own limit instead, and a tenth of what remains is world-1pkd. Composed at 72 x 72 x 16 that takes 13.65 G instructions per model year to about 5.3, so a 20,000-year physics spin-up is roughly two hours on one core. Recommendation: 72 x 72 x 16 with igrid = 0, the top of muffingen's declared range; 36 x 36 x 16 rejected on the connectivity section 8b says is absent there rather than on price; 64 x 64 x 16 the tiebreak, because 64 ocean longitudes divide every rung's longitude count except T31's. THE PROCEDURE THIS ROW OWES: report, per candidate ocean grid, the straits and sills the Orogen mesh says exist and how many the grid resolves, then take the COARSEST candidate that resolves them and among those prefer one whose longitude count divides the accepted rung's. That criterion is fixed before the inventory is seen. The budget rests on one assumption that has NOT been demonstrated: no EMBM-free configuration has been built or run, and genie.F offers only two surface-flux paths, each gated on an atmosphere module being in the recipe.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text: Canonical-10m-carve2 now has accepted terrain/hydrography support and atmosphere climatology, but SPAT-5 remains open. The ocean support builder therefore remains fail-closed: partial coast semantics, ocean-grid connectivity/bathymetry, and their native-mesh closure diagnostics are not yet accepted.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
SIZED, on terrain alone, and the answer changes what the contract has to carry. notes/audits/ocean-support-nonlinear-reductions.md is the finding, analysis/ocean_support_reduction.py the measurement, analysis/ocean_support_reduction.json the artifact. Measured 2026-08-30 on canonical-10m-carve2 at every rung of the ladder and on the 36 x 36 GOLDSTEIN grid, with the bars declared and committed before the measurement ran.

THE CELL-MEAN DEPTH IS NOT AVAILABLE AS A DEFAULT. Ocean volume is affine in depth, so a support built entirely on cell-mean depths closes volume exactly -- measured at 1.7e-16 relative against a 1e-12 bar at every support -- and misplaces the ocean area on either side of a depth horizon by 12 to 49 times the loop's own sea_ice_area bar of 0.001 of planetary area. The sign changes between 1.75 and 2.00 km on every support: below that the coarse support invents deep water and above it loses it. Refinement shrinks the peak by a factor of 3.8 from T21 to T170 and T170 still carries twelve times the bar. The 36 x 36 GOLDSTEIN candidate is worse than T21, at 49 times.

CONNECTIVITY DOES NOT CONVERGE, AND THAT IS NOT A RESOLUTION ARGUMENT. The detached deep-water area disagrees with the mesh's by up to 83 Mkm2, does not keep its sign, and T170 lands further from the mesh at a 1.5 km horizon than T85 and T127 do. The mechanism is a percolation transition: between 1.50 and 1.75 km the mesh's largest connected body falls from 161 to 54 Mkm2 and the count of separately connected bodies above the area bar rises from 12 to 20. An area measured across that transition moves by the size of a basin when a support moves one passage by one cell. So this row cannot be discharged by choosing the finest grid that fits the budget; what a candidate has to reproduce is the horizon at which this world's deep water separates and the bodies it separates into.

THE 0.5 WET MASK IS A SECOND MECHANISM AND IS NOW PRICED. At zero horizon there is no depth threshold at all, so the whole binarised gap is the mask: 3.3 to 5.0 times the bar across the Gaussian ladder and 12.3 on the GOLDSTEIN grid. analysis/coastline_threshold_cost.json already prices the LAND side of the same cut; nothing carried the ocean side.

WHAT THE CONTRACT MUST CARRY. A per-cell depth DISTRIBUTION rather than a cell depth. lib/gridding.py:cell_quantiles is the operator and area_fraction_above reads a share back out of it; hydrography's land support already does exactly this. config/pipeline.yaml's ocean_support gate has been amended to say so, because as written it asked only for extensive preservation and the cell mean satisfies that exactly.

BLOCKED ON THIS ROW'S SEAM: world-erln. config/spatial_support.yaml's aggregation_operators vocabulary has no term for a distribution reduction, and lib/spatial_support.py refuses any operator outside it, so a SPAT-1 contract carrying a hypsometry cannot be validated today.

THE CAPACITY ARM IS FIXED RATHER THAN DEFERRED. 0.12 W m-2 over this world's ocean area is 0.050 PW, so a passage carrying H PW is material at a fractional capacity error above 0.050/H: 50% at 0.1 PW, 5.0% at 1 PW, 2.5% at 2 PW. The first accepted ocean run answers it with one comparison against that table rather than a re-measurement.

title: Apply the implicit-Earth audit to the selected circulation and ecosystem sources before
description:
Apply the implicit-Earth audit to the selected circulation and ecosystem sources before adoption: inventory every calendar/day/year constant, rate time base, radius/gravity/rotation/reference-pressure value, equation-of-state and salinity range, geothermal/tidal/closure assumption, initial hydrography, latitude/hemisphere branch, Earth nutrient inventory, Redfield or fixed stoichiometry, PAR/photon conversion, sinking speed and supplied trait. Allow latitude only for geometry/Coriolis/diagnostics; replace environmental classifiers with forcing/state/traits; add source lints and fail-closed activation guards where possible

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` section 8c, `biosphere/notes/implicit-earth-assumptions.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; source and configuration audit requires no model execution and begins during OCN-3/OCN-4 scoping. It extends BIO-22/BIO-29's contract without making terrestrial tasks own external ocean code. AMENDED 2026-08-22: `ClimaParams.jl` carries a block headed *Planetary and Orbital Parameters (Earth Defaults)* -- radius, gravitational acceleration, rotation rate, orbital semi-major axis, total solar irradiance, obliquity, eccentricity and longitude of perihelion -- which is an externally maintained enumeration of the quantities this audit inventories. Read it before auditing a source by hand. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 5. INVENTORY STARTED 2026-08-22 on the circulation side, and GOLDSTEIN's NON-DIMENSIONALISATION is the first hit. `initialise_goldstein.F:376-391` hardcodes `rsc = 6.37e6` and `gsc = 9.81`, Earth's radius and gravity, exposing neither, while `sodaylen`, `sidaylen`, `yearlen`, `nyear` and `par_dsc` are all in `ini_gold_nml`. Four derived scales carry the hardcoded pair into everything: `tsc = rsc/usc` sets every non-dimensional time, `rhosc = rh0sc*fsc*usc*rsc/gsc/dsc` carries both, `opsisc` scales the overturning streamfunction and `rfluxsc` the heat flux. At 1.20 Earth radii and 1.306 Earth gravity, three of those are wrong by 1.20 and `rhosc` by about eight percent, IN A MODEL THAT IS ENTIRELY NON-DIMENSIONAL -- so a reported overturning would be twenty percent low and would look plausible. AND ROTATION FAILS OPEN: `fsc` is `4*pi/sidaylen` only when solar and sidereal day lengths differ by more than 0.001, otherwise it reverts to Earth's `2*7.2921e-5` for backwards compatibility, so a configuration that sets them equal gets Earth's Coriolis scaling silently. That is the pattern this project's conventions forbid, in the one planetary constant the source does parameterise. Line 642 also records a scale having been wrong before and corrected offline. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10e. INVENTORY EXTENDED TO THE GEOCHEMISTRY SIDE 2026-08-22, and it splits differently from the circulation side. THE CALENDAR IS COMPILE-TIME AND STATED MORE THAN ONCE: `genie-main/src/fortran/cmngem/gem_cmn.f90:585-587` declares `conv_yr_d = 365.25` as a `PARAMETER` with TWO COMMENTED ALTERNATIVES ON THE SAME LINE, 360.00 and 365.0, then `conv_yr_hr = 24.0 * conv_yr_d` with the 24-HOUR DAY AS A LITERAL, then `conv_yr_s`. Every per-year to per-second conversion in BIOGEM and SEDGEM runs through it and none of it is namelist-reachable, so the year length is a recompile. The 360.00 comment is live: the PlaSim coupling's seasonal arrays are dimensioned 360, so the codebase holds a 365.25-day geochemistry calendar beside a 360-day atmosphere coupling. `conv_yr_s` is 31,557,600 s against this world's 15,794,006, so every rate carried through it is 2.00x out. A SECOND AND INCONSISTENT STATEMENT: `sedgem_box_archer1991_sedflx.f90` hardcodes `3.15e7` TWELVE TIMES as its own seconds-per-year, converting the organic matter decay constant to a per-year rate. That is 0.183 PERCENT SHORTER than the model's own `conv_yr_s`, so a port that fixes `conv_yr_d` leaves sediment diagenesis on an Earth year and nothing fails. `gem_cmn.f90:802` likewise carries `const_rEarth = 6.37E+06` as a `PARAMETER`, a second independent statement of the radius GOLDSTEIN's `rsc` also hardcodes. THE GOOD NEWS, AND IT REDIRECTS THIS AUDIT'S EFFORT: BIOGEM's stoichiometry is NOT hardcoded -- `biogem_lib.f90:179-184` puts all four Redfield ratios in `ini_biogem_nml` and `par_bio_red_PC_flex` switches C:P to flexible entirely, so this row's "Redfield or fixed stoichiometry" item is already exposed and the fixed ratios are a default rather than an assumption. THE PORTING DIFFICULTY IS NOT UNIFORM: biogeochemical parameters are namelist-exposed, physical scaling constants are compile-time `PARAMETER`s, so an audit sampling evenly spends its effort in the wrong place. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 40. RATE TIME BASE SPLITS THREE WAYS and only one is a unit conversion, 2026-08-22 -- and note that a day inside a UNIT is invisible to a search for constants. (1) PHYSICAL/KINETIC, decided: `par_bio_remin_sinkingrate` and three siblings in `m d-1`, plus `par_bio_remin_CH4rate`, `par_scav_Fe_Ks` and `par_bio_remin_opal_K` in `d-1`, are settling speeds and reaction rates where the day is 86400 s and nothing else, so a port to a 30-hour rotation must NOT rescale them. (2) BIOLOGICAL, AMBIGUOUS: `par_bio_tau`, "biological production time-scale (days) (OCMIP-2)", was calibrated where the light cycle is 24 hours while the model resolves no diurnal cycle, so whether it moves with rotation is a modelling decision and should be recorded as an open choice rather than silently converted. (3) NOT TEMPORAL AT ALL: `par_bio_c0_I`, half saturation for light in W m-2 after Doney et al. (2006), is the marine twin of BIO-25's `CQ`; and `par_bio_I_eL` is a SINGLE SCALAR light e-folding depth in metres, which is the sharper case because its error is one-signed -- water is transparent in the blue-green and strongly absorbing in the red and near-infrared, a K dwarf puts more flux where water absorbs more, so THE PHOTIC ZONE IS SHALLOWER than a solar-calibrated e-folding depth implies. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 40d. A THIRD TIME CONVENTION, 2026-08-22, and this one carries a misleading comment. `references/climber-x/src/main/timer.f90:44-55` fixes `nday_year = 360` and `sec_year = 31556926`, the Julian year, then defines `sec_day = sec_year/day_year` with the inline comment "8.765813d4, actual seconds per day". IT IS 87658 s AND IT IS NOT A DAY -- it is a Julian year cut into 360 parts, 1.5 percent long. So every per-day rate in that model is per 1/360 Julian year. Three trees, three conventions, none configurable: cGENIE's compile-time 365.25, its separate hardcoded 3.15e7, and this. The audit should expect the convention to differ BETWEEN modules of one model, not only between models. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 42e. INVENTORY EXTENDED AGAIN 2026-08-22, and the count of independent year statements in cGENIE is SIX, not two. Beyond `conv_yr_d` and the sediment module's `3.15e7`: `genie_control.f90:190` declares `global_daysperyear = 365.25` SEPARATELY, in another module with no cross-reference, and it is what reaches the insolation routine -- so the orbital year and the biogeochemical year travel by different constants and nothing checks they agree; `initialise_genie.F:110` sets a one-hour master timestep beside an Earth solar constant; config files carry `ma_genie_timestep` as a literal second-count with a 360-day alternative commented adjacent; a dead 360-day calendar sits in `genie-lib`; AND `genie-main/runmuffin.sh:229` computes `3600.0*24.0*365.25/...` AS BASH LITERALS and appends the result to the generated config, WHICH MAKES A SHELL SCRIPT THE AUTHORITATIVE STATEMENT OF THE YEAR LENGTH for every standard run. The atmosphere's mole inventory is likewise Earth's by construction and stated three times -- `par_atm_th = 7777.0` m tuned so 1 ppm CO2 equals OCMIP's 2.123 PgC, `conv_atm_mol`, and that same literal repeated inline where the named constant was already in scope. FROM CLIMBER-X, three more of the same class: `ocn/eos.f90:85` computes ocean pressure as `p = 0.1*(-z)` bar, which is Earth gravity times seawater density WITH NO 9.81 AND NO DENSITY ON THE LINE; `constants.f90:79` welds `frac_vu = 0.45` as the sole shortwave band weight with no namelist path and no stated split wavelength, against this project's derived 0.382 at 0.75 um; and `atm_params.f90:240` welds `atm_mass = 5.12e18` kg with reference surface pressure DERIVED from it. Also THREE DIFFERENT CORIOLIS FLOORS in three components of one model -- `5e-5` as a literal in sea ice, `1e-5` in the atmosphere namelist, `5e-6` in the ocean's -- the first binding equatorward of about 20 degrees, so it replaces the Coriolis parameter over a fifth of the globe rather than guarding a small number. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 43c and 46b TWO EARTH-FITTED CORRECTIONS ADDED TO THE INVENTORY, 2026-08-24, and they are properties of the ocean and sea-ice components rather than of the coupling, so they survive section 59's architecture elimination and reach the adopted offline path. (1) A reasonable ocean circulation and salinity distribution required an Atlantic-Pacific moisture flux adjustment, varied over 0 to 0.32 Sv and set by comparison against Talley's basin freshwater budgets; the superseded IGCM coupling needed 0.79 Sv, REVERSING THE SIGN of the simulated flux. (2) The sea-ice component carries energy flux corrections diagnosed against observed present-day sea-ice thickness. Vesper has no such basins and no such observations, so these are routes to a reasonable answer that are CLOSED here rather than expensive, and an adequacy claim resting on the components' Earth behaviour inherits them silently. A third, scf, is closed by OCN-17's verdict and moved to OCN-3 as a declared bracket. notes/external-model-survey.md section 59d.

INVENTORY DELIVERED 2026-08-24 as `notes/audits/ocean-tier-implicit-earth.md`, using `model-earth-centrism.md`'s method, grouping and vocabulary unchanged, with one column added because the candidates are external: namelist-reachable against compile-time. Every cite in these notes was re-located against the tree as it stands and the current line numbers are in the audit. THE LARGEST NEW ITEM IS NOT A CONSTANT A SWEEP WOULD REACH. `gem_carbchem.f90:99` computes `loc_P = dum_D/10.0`, seawater density times EARTH gravity with neither on the line, and it feeds every pressure-corrected equilibrium constant in the carbonate system. Through the model's own correction at 2 C, calcite is 1.066x more soluble than computed at 1000 m, 1.200x at 3000 m, 1.266x at 4000 m and 1.331x at 5000 m, so the lysocline and the CCD sit substantially shallower than SEDGEM would place them. MARBL inverts on this axis and is CLEAN: pressure is a driver-supplied interior forcing and MARBL hardcodes no depth-to-pressure conversion. SECOND: the radius is stated TWICE and the two halves read different copies. `initialise_goldstein.F:377` `rsc = 6.37e6` builds cell area at `:496`; `gem_cmn.f90:802` `const_rEarth` builds BIOGEM's, SEDGEM's and ATCHEM's at `biogem_data.f90:1994`, `sedgem_data.f90:507` and `atchem_data.f90:231`, AND BIOGEM re-derives GOLDSTEIN's own scalings from it at `biogem.f90:2620, :3140, :4277` and four output sites. A port that fixes `rsc` alone leaves the geochemistry on the other radius and nothing compares them. At 1.20 radii the modelled surface is 0.694 of Vesper's, so every inventory is 30.6 per cent small. THIRD, and it is a live defect rather than an Earth-centrism: `err_gold.F:234` hardcodes `saln0 = 34.9` in a local shadowing the namelist variable, while a shipped standard config runs the ocean at 33.9. A one-PSU inconsistency between the ocean and its own error function. FOURTH: the tuned block at `cgenie.eb_go_gs_ac_bg.p0055c.BASES.config:95-134` carries SEVEN ocean and sea-ice parameters to sixteen figures, not one. OCN-17's declared bracket covers `scl_tau` only; the isopycnal and diapycnal diffusivities, the inverse minimum drag and the sea-ice eddy diffusivity are the same class and were unnamed. Their observational targets compile to binaries scoring against Levitus fields, inert here. NEW GAPS FILLED: equation of state is a Winton and Sarachik linearisation whose every coefficient is divided by `rhosc` and whose thermobaric term states its Earth domain in a comment; the salinity clamp is in the carbonate chemistry at 26-43 PSU, namelist, silent, and the fits under it are Earth ionic composition; there is NO tidal scheme and what stands in for it is `ediff.F`'s bottom-intensified profile whose own comment cites Earth abyssal-mixing observations, dormant by default; geothermal is namelist, default off, set to Earth's 100 mW/m2 by every shipped config and multiplied by `conv_yr_s` so it carries the 2.00x calendar, and Vesper's is BRACKETED at 100 to 131 mW/m2 with the radiogenic content undetermined; initial hydrography is two hemispheres of uniform water with the initial salinity anomaly not settable at all; convective adjustment is clean. LATITUDE: four physical uses, all in GOLDSTEIN -- an equatorial drag multiplier of 9 with compile-time width, the hemisphere branch, a polar mixed-layer zonal-mean substitution, and a dormant hosing band at Earth's North Atlantic latitudes -- plus basin index hacks whose own comments name Greenland and the Arctic. BIOGEM, SEDGEM, ECOGEM and MARBL are CLEAN; MARBL has no latitude in `src/` at all. EARTH NUTRIENT INVENTORY IS CONFIGURATION, NOT SOURCE: `ocn_init` is a 107-element namelist array defaulting to zero, so this is the one item in the row that costs nothing to port and is a Vesper decision rather than an extraction. MARBL's abiotic-DIC module is the exception and welds three. PAR: the named cites verify, and the structural finding is that BIOGEM HAS NO PAR FRACTION AT ALL -- `biogem_box.f90:701-704` attenuates the full shortwave field by one scalar e-folding depth, so there is nowhere to put the correction. ECOGEM's PARfrac 0.43 becomes 0.365, MARBL's f_qsw_par 0.45 becomes 0.382, ECOGEM's 0.2174 becomes 0.2140. A FIFTH buried ECOGEM literal beyond the four recorded: `ecogem_box.f90:308` diazotroph N:P 40.0 with the source's own comment saying it still needs parameterising. SINKING AND GRAVITY: the rotation half was already settled; the GRAVITY half was not, and it is BRACKETED at 143-163 m/d for `par_bio_remin_sinkingrate` and 114-131 m for MARBL's `parm_POC_diss` because the settling regime is not determined here. CLIMAPARAMS.JL IS NOT IN THIS TREE. It appears only as a dependency line in `references/cloudmicrophysics/Project.toml` and in this project's own notes; there is no vendored copy and no 'Planetary and Orbital Parameters (Earth Defaults)' block anywhere, so the 2026-08-22 amendment's instruction to read it first is not executable as things stand. Acquiring it is a fetch, not a blocker, and the inventory was taken without it. WHAT REMAINS OPEN AND WHY: the row's second half, 'add source lints and fail-closed activation guards where possible', is NOT done and should not be done yet. CLAUDE.md's layout section makes vendor/cgenie a CANDIDATE under OCN-3 that nothing reads and that does not build where it stands, and the row itself says 'the SELECTED circulation and ecosystem sources'. Nothing is selected. Writing lints into a tree nothing reads, or a check for a configuration artifact no step produces, would build the thing before asking whether it should exist. The audit's closing section states the seven preconditions a tier would have to meet instead, which is the scoping answer. This row is gated on OCN-3.

title: Evaluate the published ExoPlaSim-to-cGENIE forcing path before reusing
description:
Evaluate the published ExoPlaSim-to-cGENIE forcing path before reusing it, and resolve the scaling factor it ships with. `acapirala/exoplasim_genie_regrid` v1.2 (`10.5281/zenodo.10802839`) converts ExoPlaSim wind stress, wind velocity and planetary albedo onto cGENIE's grid and carries topography converters both ways, and its README instructs the user to set the wind-stress scaling `ea_11`/`go_13` to 2.0 for ExoPlaSim v3.0.6 and 2.6 for v3.3.0, moving `bg_par_gastransfer_a` from 0.715 to 1.1 alongside. Identify what physical quantity that multiplier stands in for, whether it corrects the atmosphere, the regridding or the ocean's drag closure, and whether it is documented anywhere but the README; then either derive it, bracket it, or declare it. `vendor/exoplasim` is a fork of neither release, so neither pair of numbers transfers unchecked. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is an explanation of the knob and a verdict on reuse, not a coupled run

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` sections 9b and 9f
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open and CONDITIONAL on OCN-3 selecting cGENIE, though the reading is worth doing either way because the same question would arise for any prescribed stress field. A tuning multiplier on a physical forcing is a knob under this project's conventions, and inheriting one silently is exactly the failure `docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md` class 16 names. Both published couplings are one-way, so this row supplies OCN-10's atmosphere-to-ocean half and leaves OCN-5's return path and exit predicate untouched [step: baseline_run]. A MECHANISM AND A PLACE TO LOOK, from `vendor/cgenie/` 2026-08-22. cGENIE's ocean expects wind stress at TWO STAGGERED LOCATIONS, and says so itself: `genie-main/genie_loop_wrappers.f90` lines 34 and 36 annotate `ocean_stressx2_ocn` as stress at the u point and `ocean_stressx3_ocn` as stress at the v point, and `genie.F:342-360` accumulates both over `kocn_loop` steps and divides, so what arrives is a time mean of a C-grid-staggered stress. A regridding route supplying one field where two are wanted, or missing that averaging, would need a compensating multiplier of about the size this row is asking about -- and the scaling being applied on BOTH the atmosphere and the ocean side, `ea_11` and `go_13`, is what an interpolation mismatch looks like rather than a physical correction. Check that FIRST. It is a hypothesis with a mechanism, not the explanation this row still owes. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10c. A SECOND PLACE TO LOOK, beside the staggering: muffingen itself writes `bg_par_gastransfer_a = 0.722` into the configurations it generates, and the published regrid path instructs moving that to 1.1 alongside the wind-stress scaling. So the gas transfer half of this row's knob has a generator DEFAULT to be compared against rather than only a README instruction. `references/muffingen/muffingen.m`, `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10f. A SECOND MECHANISM, and the likelier of the two, 2026-08-22. muffingen GENERATES a synthetic zonal wind stress: `source/make_grid_winds_zonal.m` says so in its own header, and `par_tauopt` selects the regime -- case 1 annotated modern Northern Hemisphere or paleo Eocene, case 2 a water world, case 3 automatic from a zonal gateway in the mask. THE SAME SWITCH ALSO WRITES `bg_par_gastransfer_a`, with the calibration in the comments reaching 0.722. So wind stress and gas transfer are COUPLED IN THE GENERATOR BY DESIGN, and the regrid path's instruction to set the stress scaling to 2.0 or 2.6 AND move gas transfer from 0.715 to 1.1 is not two independent corrections but one adjustment about wind made in the two places muffingen couples. It also explains the 0.715: muffingen's own default is 0.722, so the path starts at the generator's value and raises it. ASK FIRST WHAT THE EXOPLASIM STRESS IS BEING COMPARED AGAINST -- muffingen's synthetic profile, or an observational product -- because the multiplier is a ratio and its denominator has not been identified. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 18c. THE MULTIPLIER IS `scf`, THE WIND STRESS SCALING, 2026-08-22, and this supersedes the two earlier hypotheses rather than adding a third. `initialise_embm.F:1195` uses it in the stress non-dimensionalisation as `...*rh0sc*dsc*usc*fsc/(rhoair*cd*scf)`, beside the drag coefficient. It appears in BOTH `ini_embm_nml` and `ini_gold_nml`, and `initialise_goldstein.F:2110` passes it on as `go_scf` -- which is why the shipped configurations set `ea_11` and `go_13` to the SAME value, 1.531013488769531300, and why the README moves both together. So the answer to what physical quantity the multiplier stands in for is: it does not stand in for one. It is a scaling that reconciles a supplied stress product against the drag closure the components were tuned with, and 2.0 or 2.6 is that factor for an ExoPlaSim-derived stress against a default tuned for cGENIE's own wind product. The C-grid staggering of section 10c and the gas-transfer coupling of 18c are consequences of the same quantity rather than separate mechanisms. WHAT REMAINS FOR THIS ROW is whether the factor should be DERIVED -- from the ratio of the two stress products over a common grid -- or declared, and it cannot be inherited because `vendor/exoplasim` is a fork of neither release the README names. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 28d. SCOPE CLARIFIED 2026-08-22: there are TWO published paths and this row tracks one. The offline `acapirala/exoplasim_genie_regrid` route moves wind stress, winds and albedo. cGENIE's in-tree `genie-plasim` is a different and fuller arrangement, handing over 17 fields including the latent and sensible transfer coefficients, both downward radiative streams and the moisture terms. Do not conflate them when resolving the scaling factor. Whether EMBM still runs under the in-tree arrangement is not settled by its declaration module and was not confirmed. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 30b

THE BRACKET IS SEVEN PARAMETERS WIDE, NOT ONE, 2026-08-24. `vendor/cgenie/genie-main/configs/cgenie.eb_go_gs_ac_bg.p0055c.BASES.config:95-134` carries the wind stress scaling beside the ocean isopycnal and diapycnal diffusivities, the inverse minimum drag, eight EMBM diffusion and advection parameters and the sea-ice eddy diffusivity, all to sixteen significant figures, and `definition.xml:2516-2524` names three ensemble optimisations against Earth observations as the provenance of the first. The other six ocean and sea-ice values are the same class and this row named only `scf`. Their observational targets are first-class build products: `errfn_ea_go_gs.f90` and its siblings compile to binaries scoring the model against Levitus fields through `err_gold.F`, and on Vesper every one is inert, so the model's own error function cannot be used to re-derive them. notes/audits/ocean-tier-implicit-earth.md finding 15.
close_reason: Verdict 2026-08-24: DO NOT INHERIT. Holden et al. (2016) states what scf is for -- the frictional-geostrophic ocean dissipates wind energy, so increased surface wind strengths are required to compensate and drive a reasonable circulation. Conventional ensemble range 1 to 3, widened to 2 to 4 for the T21 coupling in anticipation of understated Southern Ocean zonal wind stress, and varied as one of six subjectively tuned ocean parameters over a 50-member ensemble. So it is not a regridding artifact and not derivable from the ratio of two stress products over a common grid: it is a class-16 knob, and the README's 2.0 and 2.6 are two settings of it. If GOLDSTEIN is adopted, scf is DECLARED as a bracket and the bracket is reported -- that requirement moves to OCN-3. The row's other half is also resolved: the offline regrid path this row tracks belongs to the EMBM architecture, which section 59b eliminates, so there is no path to reuse and the dependency on OCN-3 was dropped as moot. notes/external-model-survey.md sections 59b and 59e.

title: Establish the usable resolution ceiling of the EMIC ocean before any adequacy claim rests
description:
Establish the usable resolution ceiling of the EMIC ocean before any adequacy claim rests on 36 x 36 x 16, and separate the model's limit from the connector's. MEASURE the wall clock of one short integration at 36 x 36 x 16, 48 x 40 x 16 and 36 x 36 x 32, which all ship as working configurations, and at one grid finer than any that does, to test the r^4-per-model-year estimate that section 9g reads off the `ubarsolv` loop structure rather than from a run; the component is serial, so cores cannot absorb the growth. Fix `nyear` by an explicit stability criterion rather than by the default 100, since `dt = sodaylen*yearlen/(nyear*tsc)` is a namelist consequence with no Courant check anywhere in the component. Then determine what muffingen's `.k1`, `.paths` and `.psiles` generation does above 36 x 36, whether the resolved island count exceeds the compile-time `GOLDSTEINMAXISLES` default of 10, and whether it runs under Octave at all. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is a resolution/cost curve and a ceiling with its cause named

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` sections 9a, 9g and 8b
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open and CONDITIONAL on OCN-3 selecting cGENIE. It matters because the tier's entire attraction is its price and that price is a property of 36 x 36 rather than of the model, so an adequacy verdict at the shipped grid and a cost verdict at a usable one are not the same measurement. Section 8b's straits, sills and partial coasts are what a finer grid would buy, and with the resolved tier dropped they ride ENTIRELY on this row: resolution is now the only lever on connectivity, so if the grid that represents them is unaffordable the outcome is a declared unresolved-connectivity bracket rather than quiet acceptance of whatever the shipped grid represents. Edwards and Marsh's finding that errors reduce only moderately with a doubling of resolution is the reason to measure that benefit rather than assume it. This row sets the ocean's own support; OCN-11 still owns the map from the 10M export, and SPAT-8 replays loop A at whatever support is chosen [step: orogen, hydrography]. PARTLY ANSWERED 2026-08-22 from the vendored tree, and this row's island figure is CORRECTED: `genie-main/genie_control.f90:79` sets `#define GOLDSTEINMAXISLES 5`, not 10. Counting the maximum island index in all 294 shipped `.psiles` files gives a range of 1 to 8, with 89 of them -- about thirty percent -- above the default. So raising the macro is ROUTINE rather than exceptional, island count is a per-geography property driving a compile-time bound, and a new geography can need a rebuild before it runs at all. That bears on OCN-11 as much as here, since this world's island count is not knowable until a candidate configuration is generated. RESOLUTION: muffingen's settings annotate `par_max_i` and `par_max_j` as `[1-72]`, but of the shipped configurations 131 are 36 x 36, five are 18 and one is 12, and nothing is above 36 -- a declared range, not a demonstrated one, which is the distinction this row exists to draw. Shipped depth is `par_max_k=17` with one extra level, and `par_A_frac_threshold=0.50` matches this project's `geography_land_threshold` in convention. STILL NEEDS A DOWNLOAD: muffingen is a separate repository and `genie-paleo` holds only its outputs, settings and logs, so what it does above 36 x 36 and whether it runs under Octave are not answerable from here. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10d. OCTAVE REMAINS OPEN with the tree now local at `references/muffingen/`: it is MATLAB `.m` with a LaTeX manual under `DOCS/`, and a search finds no Octave statement either way. The manual is where to look. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10f THE CEILING NOW HAS A CONSTRAINT TO BE MEASURED AGAINST, 2026-08-24. Section 59 decides the coupling architecture as offline full-flux on exactly the property this row measures: that the ocean's grid is chosen for ocean adequacy and does NOT climb the T21/T42/T85/T127/T170 ladder with the atmosphere. So this row's resolution/cost curve is what the decision rests on, and it acquires a second deliverable beside the ceiling -- a statement of the ocean grid's independence from the atmosphere rung, since the published synchronous coupling gets its affordability from matching the three horizontal grids and this project deliberately does not. The eliminated architecture also supplies the negative datum: matching at T170 is a 512 x 256 ocean, eight times linear on a serial r^4 component, about 4000x. That is the number this row's curve should be read against.

ANSWERED 2026-08-25, and this row's deliverable is in notes/audits/cgenie-build-cost-and-grid-ceiling.md with analysis/cgenie_stability.json and analysis/cgenie_cost.json as its evidence. THE CEILING HAS TWO CAUSES IN TWO COMPONENTS AND THE OCEAN IS NEITHER OF THEM FIRST. The criterion is the model's own instrument: genie-goldstein/src/fortran/diag.f already forms the maximum advective Courant number over every wet cell and prints it as Cn, but nothing acts on it and diag is called only behind debug_loop, so at shipped settings a run past the limit completes and reports success. A GRID THAT RUNS IS NOT A GRID THAT IS STABLE. The one hard guard in the physics is EMBM's, at surflux.F:900-954, where a failed Newton solve for the sea-ice surface temperature executes a bare stop -- and setting EMBM's own debug_loop turns that guard into a silent clamp. At the shipped ndta=5 the boundary is nyear 30/35 at 36x36x16 and nyear 140/160 at 72x72x16, and at the last stable point the ocean's own Cn is 0.39 and 0.32, a factor of three of unused headroom on both grids. EMBM's boundary is a property of dtatm alone: pairs at matched dtatm with ocean timesteps a factor of two apart fail in the SAME CELL. Sub-step EMBM properly and the ocean's own limit appears, at Cn=1 near nyear 13 (36x36) and nyear 52 (72x72). BOTH LIMITS ARE QUADRATIC IN RESOLUTION, so a refinement costs r^4 -- section 9g's exponent, relocated off the barotropic solve entirely. THE COST IS MEASURED IN RETIRED INSTRUCTIONS because the host was contended: 1.776 to 5.330 Ginstr per model year across the shipped 36x36 grids and 13.787 at 72x72x16. A CAUTION THIS ROW SHOULD CARRY FORWARD: ndta is NOT a sub-step knob on its own. katm_loop sets how often EMBM is called and defaults to 1, so EMBM advances kocn_loop/ndta times the ocean's time and that is one only when the two are equal; raising ndta alone slows the atmosphere's clock and nothing complains. A first sweep did exactly that and read wrong. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED: whether muffingen runs outside MATLAB, and what it produces above 36x36. Its declared range is [1-72] on every example configuration, so 72x72 is the top of what the connector claims and this row demonstrates only that the MODEL runs there. Also open: whether the 2.8-fold drop in instructions per second at 72x72 is the state leaving cache or the contended window, which needs a quiet host to separate and makes r^4 a LOWER bound on wall clock until it is.

THE WORK OF THIS ROW IS COMPLETE and it is held open only by its dependency on OCN-3, which cannot close until an ADOPTION DECISION is made that is not an agent's to make. Nothing further is owed here: what is left of the original description is the connector, split out as world-crky, and a quiet-host wall re-take, world-ap7w.
close_reason: 2026-08-26. Unblocked and closed by OCN-3's adoption decision. This row's own notes already recorded THE WORK OF THIS ROW IS COMPLETE and it is held open only by its dependency on OCN-3. The resolution/cost curve and its ceiling with the cause named are delivered: the model runs to 72x72, which is the top of muffingen's declared [1-72] range, and r^4 is a LOWER bound on wall clock until a quiet host separates the 2.8-fold drop in instructions per second at 72x72 into cache versus contention. What is left of the original description is not this row's: the connector question -- whether muffingen runs outside MATLAB and what it produces above 36x36 -- is world-crky, and the quiet-host wall re-take is world-ap7w.

title: Profile the EMIC ocean at the shipped grid BEFORE optimising either half
description:
Profile the EMIC ocean at the shipped grid BEFORE optimising either half of it, then parallelise the half that pays. There is no disabled parallelism to re-enable: the OpenMP in `tstepo.F:74-90` wraps duplicate-copy experiments and the block in `biogem.f90:718-735` calls `sub_wasteCPUcycles1`/`2`, so threading is new work. Attribute runtime between the barotropic solve, tracer advection and BIOGEM's tracer loops at 36 x 36 x 16; then decompose what threads, which is BIOGEM's `do n=1,n_vocn` sweep over vectorised columns and the 3D loops in `tstepo_flux`, and NOT `ubarsolv`, whose forward elimination and back substitution both carry loop-carried dependences. Delete the dead duplication at `tstepo.F:32-35` and `62-68` first: six arrays filled every ocean timestep and read by nothing. Validate against `genie-knowngood/`, which ships per-component reference output for four configurations

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` sections 9g and 9h
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open and CONDITIONAL on OCN-3 selecting cGENIE. The profile is the deliverable that orders everything after it, and it is cheap next to either piece of work: the barotropic solve dominates GROWTH with resolution while BIOGEM's tracers may dominate RUNTIME at the shipped grid, and those are different claims that this project has not separated. The dead-copy deletion is correctness-neutral and available immediately. Threading is what makes a finer grid affordable at all, since the component currently cannot spend a second core [step: any]. CITATIONS VERIFIED 2026-08-22 against the vendored tree, and two are stronger than written. `tstepo.F` declares the six arrays at lines 32 to 35 -- two full four-dimensional tracer arrays, two more tracer copies and two density copies -- and fills all six at lines 62 to 68 every ocean timestep, while the `tstepo_flux_t` calls that would consume them are COMMENTED OUT along with the whole OpenMP block, leaving `call tstepo_flux()` as the only live call. And `sub_wasteCPUcycles1` and `2` are real subroutines at `biogem_lib.f90:2267` and `:2289`, with the block that would call them commented out too: it was a scheduling experiment on deliberately wasted cycles, so there is not merely no parallelism to re-enable, there is none to read for intent either. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10a. THE VALIDATION SURFACE IS THINNER THAN THIS ROW IMPLIES, and it imposes an ORDER. `genie-knowngood/` is four netCDF files covering three components, not four: BIOGEM 3-D fields at 1.9 MB, an ENTS year-20 average, and GOLDSTEIN year-20 and year-10 averages, since two configurations cover the same component. Twenty and ten model years, so a short-run regression surface rather than an equilibrated comparison -- adequate for this row, worth knowing before it is asked to carry more. THE COMPARATOR IS BETTER THAN EXPECTED and already exists: `genie-main/src/c/compare.cpp` built as `nccompare.exe`, taking a relative tolerance IN ULPS and an absolute floor, which is the right measure for a reordering because it asks how far a result moved in representable numbers. THE ORDER: the GOLDSTEIN reference carries `opsi`, reported through `opsisc = dsc*usc*rsc*1e-6`, and `rsc` is Earth's radius hardcoded. So every number in the suite is a number at Earth's parameters, and the radius work under OCN-3 and OCN-12 destroys its applicability as its first act. This row is a correctness-preserving change at fixed physics, which is exactly what the suite is for -- so DO IT BEFORE the planet parameters move, or lose the validation surface. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 13. THE TWO THREADING TARGETS ARE NOT COMPARABLE, established by static analysis 2026-08-22, and this row treats them as one decomposition. BIOGEM'S SWEEP THREADS: every argument in the `do n=1,n_vocn` body is indexed by `n`, `loc_dtyr` is a read-only scalar, the reduction onto the grid happens after the loop, and both callees clear the three checks that would break it -- no `SAVE` or `DATA`, no writes to module-scope arrays since `bio_remin`, `bio_part`, `ocn` and `phys_ocn` are all reached through dummy arguments, and NO INITIALISED LOCALS anywhere in `biogem_box.f90`. That last is CLIM-51's implicit-SAVE class, which found 103 sites in `plasim/src` with no compiler flag that reveals them; across all of BIOGEM and ECOGEM the pattern appears 23 times and none is in the file holding this work. `tstepo_flux` DOES NOT: it includes `ocean.cmn` twice and that declares 44 COMMON BLOCKS, so GOLDSTEIN's state is global by construction and every variable the loop touches must be proved read-only or made private. In BIOGEM privacy is the default and sharing explicit; in GOLDSTEIN the reverse. THIS CHANGES WHAT THE PROFILE IS FOR: if it says `tstepo_flux` dominates, the answer is not "thread it" but that the threading route is expensive there and OCN-20's algorithmic route matters more, so the profile decides between two DIFFERENT KINDS of work rather than two candidates for the same kind. Caveats on the counts: they are an upper bound that does not separate module-scope declarations from procedure-body ones, and this is one level into the call tree. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 14

PROFILED 2026-08-25, and the profile half of this row is DONE; the parallelisation half is not, so this stays open. analysis/cgenie_profile.py and analysis/cgenie_profile.json are the driver and the artifact; notes/audits/cgenie-parallelism-and-coupling-support.md is the finding. At 100 model years, 36 x 36 x 16 and 72 x 72 x 16, both -mcmodel=medium: tstepo_flux is 53.3 and 46.6 per cent of retired instructions, ubarsolv 1.83 and 2.57, EMBM 12.5 and 19.9. The serial share is below the 5 per cent line the criterion fixed in advance, so the verdict is that threading is possible and Amdahl is not what limits it; with the world-1pkd heap defect removed first, Amdahl bounds sixteen threads at 12.5 and 11.3. The serial share grows a measured 1.41 per doubling, which puts it near 3.7 per cent at 144 x 144 and 5.2 at 288 x 288, so it never becomes the binding constraint below muffingen's declared ceiling.

THREE THINGS THE PARALLELISATION HALF NOW KNOWS. First, the obstacle is a build flag rather than the loop structure: makefile.arc's gfortran SHIP block carries -fno-automatic, which puts every procedure-body local in static storage, so it is SHARED inside a parallel region unless it is named PRIVATE. Demonstrated with a loop whose right answer is known: 177,007 of 200,000 cells wrong at eight threads, none at one thread, none with private(scratch). gfortran ACCEPTS private on such a variable and emits exactly one diagnostic for the whole translation unit, so there is no per-variable gate. Second, the flag looks removable: every DATA statement and every save in genie-goldstein, genie-embm and genie-goldsteinseaice is explicit and sits in a driver, a diagnostic or a netCDF writer rather than in a per-cell kernel, so -frecursive is the cheap first step and genie-knowngood with nccompare's ULP tolerance is a test that can fail. Third, tstipa is a Jacobi iteration rather than a line solve, so EMBM's implicit step is data-parallel over cells as well.

AN INSTRUMENT TRAP THIS ROW PAID FOR. kernel.perf_event_max_sample_rate is 3000 per second on this host and throttles a sampler while perf report still reports zero lost samples. A period of 2e6 delivered 7133 of the 14090 samples it demanded and moved the per-symbol shares by up to a factor of 1.6. More samples come from a LONGER run at a period the kernel honours, never from a shorter period, and sample_rate_ok() in the driver now checks it. The profile is also state-dependent: the same binary over 10 model years and over 100 differs by more than the two grids differ, because the run starts from a uniform 10 degree ocean and stratifies.

AND THE ARM THAT MATTERS TO A REAL BUDGET, the shipped BIOGEM regression case at 36 x 36 x 8 with fourteen tracers, ATCHEM and BIOGEM on, 100 model years: parallel 84.17 per cent, serial 1.08, heap 11.17, unclassified 2.43, sixteen threads bound at 9.42 with the heap removed. The unclassified tail is small per-cell GEM routines that the pre-fixed rule counts AGAINST the parallel fraction, so the bound is conservative. Two things there that the cost note's 2.68 ratio does not say: tstepo_flux is still the largest single routine at 37.94 per cent, larger than BIOGEM, ATCHEM and the GEM libraries together at 25.06, so most of what the biogeochemistry costs is the OCEAN carrying its tracers; and that cost is not proportional to the tracer count, since seven times the tracers costs about twice the transport. The parallelism worth having is over CELLS, not over tracers, which is the opposite of what section 9h of the ocean audit expected.

DONE 2026-08-25, and what is left is named. The profile this row asked for exists (notes/audits/cgenie-parallelism-and-coupling-support.md) and the parallelisation it ordered is built: notes/audits/cgenie-embm-free-path-and-threading.md.

The dead duplication went first, as this row required, and world-1pkd carries it. -fno-automatic came out of makefile.arc's gfortran SHIP and TEST blocks in favour of -frecursive, which is what made the 390-name, 81-array enumeration unnecessary; genie.job now raises the stack and sets OMP_STACKSIZE, which is required rather than precautionary because the eb_go_gs_ac_bg regression case segfaults before its first timestep otherwise. tstepo_flux, co, coshuffle and velc are threaded over j, and tstepo_flux's one real dependence -- fs, the southern face, filled by the previous row -- is removed by recomputing one row per thread block.

Every arm reproduces the tree at 4038c12e BIT-FOR-BIT on both shipped regression cases, at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 threads, including two poison arms that compile -finit-real=snan so a local read before it is written cannot pass for an answer.

Serial cost at the shipped grid over 100 model years, retired instructions: 302.68 G before, 246.64 G after, -18.5 per cent. The instrument agrees with the sibling's sampled 302.4 G to 0.09 per cent.

WHAT IS LEFT, and each has its own row rather than sitting here. The threaded speedup peaks at 1.30 on four threads and falls to 1.09 on sixteen, against an Amdahl bound of 12.47, and the cause is synchronisation granularity rather than the decomposition: at 36 x 36 x 16 a thread gets two or three rows of 36 columns between barriers. That is the coarsening row. The routines still serial -- goldstein's own loops, jbar, krausturner, the sea ice, and BIOGEM's n_vocn column sweep -- are a second row. ubarsolv stays serial and that is settled, not deferred.
close_reason: 2026-08-26. Unblocked and closed by OCN-3's adoption decision. The profile is taken and the attribution made: serial cost at the shipped grid over 100 model years fell from 302.68 G to 246.64 G retired instructions, -18.5 per cent, with the instrument agreeing with a sibling's sampled figure to 0.09 per cent, and the dead duplication is gone. The four routines that pay -- tstepo_flux, co, coshuffle, velc -- are threaded and bit-for-bit at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 threads against both shipped regression cases plus the poison arm. ubarsolv stays serial and that is settled rather than deferred. Everything left already has its own row: the coarsening question is world-2lbs, the routines still serial and BIOGEM's column sweep are world-hkcj, and the barotropic solve itself is OCN-20.

title: Replace the barotropic streamfunction solve with one that does not grow as r^3 per timestep
description:
Replace the barotropic streamfunction solve with one that does not grow as r^3 per timestep, and prove it against the existing reference output. `invert.f:32` orders the Psi points lexicographically as `k = i + j*n`, which is what fixes the bandwidth at `imax` and makes `ubarsolv`'s two triangular sweeps cost about `2*imax*(jmax+1)*(imax+1)` per ocean timestep with `gap(mpxi*mpxj, 2*mpxi+3)` in storage. Price a fill-reducing reordering against an iterative treatment of the elliptic streamfunction equation, and cost the island machinery FIRST, since `ratm`, `psisl`, `erisl` and `matinv_gold` all assume the present factorisation and `GOLDSTEINMAXISLES` bounds them. Any iterative scheme changes results to within a declared tolerance rather than exactly, so fix the tolerance and the acceptance comparison before choosing

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` sections 9g and 9h
notes: 2026-08-28 CONDITIONAL OPTIMISATION REJECTED. OCN-19's prerequisite measurement does not fire OCN-20: ubarsolv is 1.83% of retired instructions at 36x36x16 and 2.57% at 72x72x16 (2.81% after correcting EMBM subcycling), against the pre-registered >20% threshold for putting the algorithmic route before threading. The one-off LU factorisation in invert is not per-timestep; only the two triangular sweeps recur. Even the conservative asymptotic projection reaches 11.2% only at 288x288, beyond the adopted 36x36 support and present defensible range. An iterative replacement would make each step tolerance-dependent and redesign island basis handling (psisl/ubisl/erisl); reordering must also preserve the periodic seam and island solves. Retain the shipped direct factorisation and bitwise reference surface. Reopen only for an accepted support >144x144 or a fresh profile measuring ubarsolv >20%. Decision recorded in notes/audits/cgenie-parallelism-and-coupling-support.md and ocean/README.md; mdbook and git diff --check pass. No source change or benchmark was warranted.
close_reason: Conditional replacement rejected: measured serial share is 1.83-2.81%, far below the pre-registered 20% trigger; retain the bitwise direct solver and reopen only for >144x144 accepted support or a fresh >20% profile.

title: The sea ice is thermodynamic-only and that is an undeclared structural term rather
description:
The sea ice is thermodynamic-only and that is an undeclared structural term rather than a decision. `icemod.f90` runs thermodynamics with no ice dynamics and no transport, which is the same configuration BIG-MITgcm runs and names as a stated limitation, reporting excessive ice as its consequence at a comparable resolution. So the term is not negligible on peer evidence, and nothing here has priced it or written it down. `references/climber-x/src/sic` is the reference implementation in this model class, `sic_dyn.f90` and `transport_sic.f90`

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3f, `notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open and BLOCKED, and the blocker is physical rather than a queue: sea ice dynamics is driven by wind stress and ocean currents, and this ocean is a slab with horizontal transport deliberately off under CLIM-16, so a dynamics scheme would be advecting ice across a motionless ocean. What is NOT blocked and is what this row asks for first: state the term in `analysis/error_budget.json` as a structural item beside no-q-flux, with the direction taken from the peer report rather than guessed, so the omission is declared where a reader of the budget will find it. The scheme itself follows the ocean and not this row [step: baseline_run]. SHAPE CORRECTED 2026-08-22, and the block confirmed. This row says sea ice dynamics is driven by wind stress and ocean currents; the EMIC-class answer needs only the second. `vendor/cgenie/genie-goldsteinseaice/tstepsic.f` announces itself as a "2nd order explicit transport code using upper level ocean velocities", and `tstipsic.f` builds its advective coefficients from `u(1,i,j)` and `u(2,i,j)` with `diffsic` beside them. There is NO ice momentum equation, no internal stress, no wind stress on the floe, and a separate `uice` field exists commented out at every use site. So the ladder runs: thermodynamic only here, advection by upper-ocean velocity in cGENIE, and a full dynamic-thermodynamic scheme in CLIMBER-X's `sic_dyn.f90`. THE BLOCK STANDS EXACTLY -- a slab ocean has no velocity field, so there is nothing to advect with -- BUT THE EVENTUAL FIX IS SMALLER than this row implies: an advection term on two prognostic fields using a velocity the ocean would already produce. That strengthens the case for declaring the term in the error budget NOW, since the declaration is not deferring an expensive decision. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 19. RELATED, 2026-08-22: in cGENIE's in-tree PlaSim coupling the sea-ice ALBEDO is supplied by the ocean model as `genie_alb_sic`, so PlaSim's own ice albedo pair does not set it. That is the pair which survives `radmod`'s open-ocean overwrite and which PHYS-14 owns, so a future coupling moves it out of this project's hands rather than needing it fixed first. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 30b. PRICED, AND THE BLOCK IS SCHEME-DEPENDENT RATHER THAN ABSOLUTE, 2026-08-22 -- verified in source before acting on it. THE COST, from CLIMBER-X's EVP scheme (Hunke and Dukowicz 1997, elliptical yield curve, C-grid, from SIS2): FIVE new prognostic 2-D fields in the restart, `ui`, `vi` and the three stress-tensor components; ice concentration PROMOTED to prognostic and separately advected, a sixth; five forcing fields in; an EVP subcycle of 50 steps per sea-ice step against an SIS2 default of 432; one flux-corrected transport pass per advected field; and guards it cannot run without -- a velocity clamp at `cfl_fac*dx/dt` with `cfl_fac = 0.1` "for CFL stability near the Poles", a viscosity cap, and a stress limiter called every step. THE BLOCK: this row says a slab ocean has nothing to advect with, which is exactly right for cGENIE's advection-by-upper-ocean-velocity and NOT right for EVP, which is a MOMENTUM solve. `sic_dyn.f90:603` forms the forcing as `(Cor + PFu)*mi_u + (fxic_now + tauxa)` -- Coriolis, sea-surface tilt, internal ice stress and WIND STRESS -- with ocean velocity entering only as the drag reference at `:593`. With `uo = vo = ssh = 0` the tilt vanishes and drag becomes drag against still water, while wind stress, internal stress and Coriolis remain. Wind-driven ice over a motionless ocean is a reduced but coherent configuration, which is what free-drift approximations do. THE ROW'S CONCLUSION IS UNCHANGED -- declare the term in the error budget first -- but restate the block as applying to one family of schemes rather than to sea-ice motion. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 43a-b DECLARED 2026-08-24, which closes this row's first and unblocked ask. scripts/error_budget.py now carries 'sea ice does not move' as a structural item with the peer's direction and no invented kelvin, beside no-q-flux. THE BLOCK LIFTS AS A CONSEQUENCE OF THE ARCHITECTURE DECISION rather than by its own work: offline full-flux adopts a circulation host that produces the ocean surface velocity this row said did not exist, so the remaining work is the advection term itself. AND THE AUTHORITY QUESTION IS SETTLED, notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md section 7b: ExoPlaSim's icemod stays authoritative and the ocean returns a VELOCITY, not an ice state. The alternative was available -- read_ice_surface already takes 14-month climatological ice cover and thickness, nice = 0 prescribes ice outright and nfluko = 1 diagnoses a correction against it -- and is rejected on four grounds, the first decisive: prescribed ice cannot respond to the atmosphere within a run, which severs the albedo feedback the design flux, the extreme-cold land fraction and the stellar cycle's grand minima all turn on. So this row's eventual scope is an advection term on ExoPlaSim's own prognostic ice, driven by the ocean's velocity: a change under vendor/exoplasim, so rule 4 applies. NOT INHERITED: the published synchronous coupling supplies ice temperature, height, fraction and albedo FROM the ocean, which is right without a lag and does not transfer to an offline arrangement.
close_reason: Declared 2026-08-24, which is what this row asked for. scripts/error_budget.py now carries 'sea ice does not move' as a structural item beside no-q-flux, with the direction taken from the peer report rather than guessed and no kelvin invented, since the correction requires an ocean surface velocity this slab does not have. The row's premise -- an undeclared structural term rather than a decision -- is resolved: it is now a declared term. Two things moved out rather than staying here. The AUTHORITY question is settled in notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md section 7b: ExoPlaSim's icemod stays authoritative and the ocean returns a velocity, not an ice state. The CORRECTION is world-pt8, blocked on OCN-3 and OCN-11, which implements the advection term against that decision. The albedo half was always PHYS-14's.

title: The two-band ocean albedo is collapsed to one value by the same default that computes it.
description:
The two-band ocean albedo is collapsed to one value by the same default that computes it. Section 29 established that `radmod.f90:2892-2903` overwrites the open-ocean albedo with a zenith formula under `necham = 1`; what it did not record is that **`dsalb(1,:)` and `dsalb(2,:)` receive the IDENTICAL expression**, so the band index -- a physical dimension -- holds one value. This project sets `two_band_albedo: true` specifically to obtain spectral surface albedo, and `solarini` duly computes 0.0744 and 0.0636 for the two ocean bands; over ice-free ocean, which is most of the planet, that is undone every radiation step for the direct beam. The diffuse component is read before the overwrite and does keep both bands

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 58c
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and it is the SAME DECISION as OCN-7's remaining half rather than a separate one: the choice between ECHAM-3 and Briegleb, the choice of whether either should be spectral, and this collapse are one change to one expression. Fold this into whatever OCN-7 concludes rather than costing it twice [step: baseline_run]
close_reason:
Both zenith branches wrote the same broadband value into dsalb(1,:) and dsalb(2,:), so the band index -- a physical dimension -- held one value over ice-free ocean for the direct beam. Fixed: the fit carries doceanalb's own band ratio across the replacement, normalised so zsolars(1)*zofrc1 + zsolars(2)*zofrc2 = 1 identically. That is the same identity build_surface_albedo.py already enforces on codes 174 to 176, so both sides of the boundary now construct a two-band surface albedo the same way rather than each asserting it.

MEASURED: band 1 +9.85 per cent, band 2 -6.10. An independent recomputation of solarini's integral on the same 965-point grid gives +10.78 and -6.67, and THE 1.5 PER CENT GAP IN BAND 1 IS WORLD-A0Y'S zdenom1 DEFECT REACHED FROM A SECOND DIRECTION, matching that row's separately reported 1.47 per cent. Two independent paths to one defect.

Predicted +0.02 to +0.15 W/m2 and -0.02 to -0.13 K, registered with four falsifiers. The load-bearing one is that the BROADBAND must not move at all: this redistributes between bands and does not change the total, so a broadband shift means the normalisation is wrong rather than the physics interesting.

WHY THE BLOCKING EDGE ON OCN-7 WAS REMOVED RATHER THAN FORCED PAST. This row said the collapse is 'the SAME DECISION as OCN-7's remaining half' and should be folded into whatever OCN-7 concludes rather than costed twice. That fold has now happened -- it is one change to one expression and it is made. What is left of OCN-7 is a different question: a sourced bound on the SPATIAL span, which needs a modelled water-leaving reflectance that OCN-14 owns and that does not exist. That does not gate the collapse, so the edge was correct while the two were one undone change and is stale now that the change is done. Both are relates-to. OCN-7's bound was deliberately not smuggled into this row's prediction.

title: Establish cGENIE's viability and MEASURED cost as the offline circulation host
description:
Establish cGENIE's viability and MEASURED cost as the offline circulation host, now that the resolved tier is off the board: whether it builds here; licence/version/provenance; how it consumes Vesper radius, gravity, rotation, calendar and pressure; what a candidate global configuration generated from the 10M bathymetry and mapped to the T21/T42/T85/T127/T170 atmosphere ladder looks like; what initial hydrography and boundary closures it requires; and what spin-up, restart and tracer costs are in wall clock and storage ON THIS MACHINE rather than quoted from a paper. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is a viability verdict and a measured cost, not a run

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` sections 6, 8b, 8c and 9
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. Offline is the only affordable coupling class, because equilibrating a deep ocean takes thousands of model years against orbits priced in wall-clock hours; the pattern to copy is aeolian, downstream of one climate and upstream of the next. Report this row's cost in wall clock AND in whatever unit the coupling cadence makes meaningful, because CPU-hours per simulated year assumes every component advances on one clock and this pipeline is asynchronous: cost per PASS is the number that decides affordability at loop A's cadence, not cost per simulated year. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 2. Two of its questions are already answered by the vendoring. OCN-12 owns the inventory; what this row takes from it is that the answer is not binary and the radius and gravity half is source work rather than configuration. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10e. AN ORDERING FALLS OUT OF THE VALIDATION SUITE and belongs here because this row owns the parameter change. `genie-knowngood/`'s GOLDSTEIN references are overturning streamfunctions reported through `opsisc`, which carries Earth's hardcoded `rsc`, so every number in the suite is a number at Earth's parameters. Moving radius and gravity for this planet destroys the suite's applicability as its first act. Either let OCN-19 and OCN-20 land first, since they are correctness-preserving changes at fixed physics and the suite is exactly what they need, or DECLARE a replacement acceptance test before the parameters move -- and it cannot be a comparison against those files. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 13c.
