It is offline-tracer acceleration for carbonate chemistry once the circulation is settled, and does nothing for the circulation itself. Its own header also records that it cannot handle a CO2 pulse, since it needs ocean-surface to atmosphere disequilibrium to work. So the claim that equilibrating a deep ocean costs thousands of model years stands unmodified. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 26. THE COST MECHANISM IS IN THE TREE, 2026-08-22. `genie-plasim/src/fortran/plasim.f90:604-655` implements PlaSim-GOLDSTEIN gearing: with `ngear = 1` the atmosphere integrates for `ngear_years_plasim` years while accumulating daily means, then RETURNS IMMEDIATELY for the next `ngear_multiple - 1` blocks while the ocean is driven from the stored seasonal cycle, so the atmosphere runs one block in `ngear_multiple`. That is what makes a coupled ocean affordable and it should enter this row's cost model, not be rediscovered after it. The non-obvious part: the SST-dependent terms are recomputed live against `tstar_ocn` every geared step -- latent via saturation specific humidity, net longwave, sensible -- and only the coefficients and downward fields are replayed, because naive replay of net heat flux severs the feedback that holds SST. The source comment says "Needed for stability". Evaporation is deliberately not recomputed, for moisture conservation. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 30c. ACCELERATOR INVENTORY, 2026-08-22: cost here is not one mechanism but two, controlled differently. Gearing skips the ATMOSPHERE on a fixed schedule with no adaptive guard, `ngear_multiple` being a plain integer. GEMlite skips the BIOLOGY AND CIRCULATION for geochemistry with the two-sided adaptive guard in section 35b. Price them separately; they compose, and only the second bounds its own error. Note also that GEMlite keeps a SECOND live copy of the ocean state -- its header says "there is an entirely seperate `ocn` for BIOGEM" -- which is the duplicate-state hazard rule 5 exists for and would need a provenance answer before adoption. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 35PORTING COST IS ASYMMETRIC AND SHOULD BE PRICED THAT WAY, 2026-08-22: the geochemistry is namelist-configurable while the calendar and the physical scaling constants are compile-time `PARAMETER`s stated in more than one place, so adoption cost sits in the physics core rather than spread evenly. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 40. A PER-ITERATION ADOPTION COST THIS ROW SHOULD CARRY, 2026-08-22. `genie-paleo` is 286 pre-baked Earth geographies and no code, and the cost for a NEW geography is not the bathymetry -- that regrids -- it is the `.psiles` and `.paths` pair, which is TOPOLOGICAL: an integer island-label map and a HAND-ORDERED list of (direction, i, j) triples tracing a closed integration circuit around each island for the barotropic streamfunction solve. These cannot be produced by regridding a heightfield; muffingen generates them interactively. SO IT IS MANUAL WORK PER BUILD, AND IT INVALIDATES ON EVERY GENERATION THAT CHANGES CONTINENT CONNECTIVITY -- which is what a new Orogen generation does. Price it per iteration of loop A, not once. Also note the tuning infrastructure is inert here: three `errfn_*` programs and a HadCM3 target file compile to binaries that score the model against observed phosphate and alkalinity, and this world has nothing to tune against. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 46d ARCHITECTURE DECIDED 2026-08-24, and this row narrows to it: offline full-flux. The alternatives are eliminated in notes/external-model-survey.md section 59 and the audit's section 6 is rewritten to match, so this row no longer carries an open architecture question and its cost measurement is scoped to the offline case. THE COST ARGUMENT IS CORRECTED, and the correction matters to what this row measures. Holden et al. (2016) reports 75 simulated years a day coupled with PLASIM at 98 percent of the load and GOLDSTEIN essentially free, so a dynamic ocean does not cost what the ocean costs -- it costs being obliged to integrate the ATMOSPHERE for the ocean's thousands of years. Offline is chosen because it is the only class in which the ocean's cost does not climb the T21/T42/T85/T127/T170 ladder with the atmosphere. WHAT THIS ROW MUST NOW REPORT, beyond its existing questions: (1) the ocean's wall clock AT A FIXED GRID, stated as independent of the atmosphere rung, since that independence is the whole basis of the decision and an unmeasured claim is not one; (2) scf as a DECLARED BRACKET with the bracket reported, inherited from OCN-17's verdict -- it is a tuned parameter for GOLDSTEIN's wind-energy dissipation, conventional range 1 to 3, not derivable from a stress-product ratio; (3) whether the two Earth-fitted corrections of section 59d have Vesper analogues, which they do not, so any adequacy claim resting on the components' Earth behaviour inherits them. TWO CONFIGURATION QUESTIONS ADDED BY THE SEA-ICE DECISION, 2026-08-24. Section 7b makes ExoPlaSim's icemod authoritative for sea ice, so the candidate host must be configured so that its OWN sea-ice component does not also own it: establish whether genie-goldsteinseaice can be disabled or run diagnostically without breaking the ocean's surface heat and freshwater budgets, since brine rejection and the ice-covered fraction feed them. That is a viability question about this host, not an implementation, and it belongs in this row's verdict. Second, this row must report whether the host EXPORTS an ocean surface velocity in a usable form, because world-pt8's advection term consumes it and section 7b's whole argument is that the ocean returns a transport agent rather than an ice state. The published in-tree coupling never needed this, since it hands ice the other way, so it is not evidence that the field is available.

ONE ITEM FOR THE VIABILITY QUESTION THAT IS NOT A COST, 2026-08-24. `vendor/cgenie/genie-main/src/fortran/cmngem/gem_carbchem.f90:99` computes ocean pressure as `loc_P = dum_D/10.0`, which is seawater density times EARTH gravity with neither on the line, and it feeds every pressure-corrected equilibrium constant in the carbonate system. At 1.306 gravity the true conversion is 0.13156 bar/m, so through the model's own correction at 2 C calcite is 1.266x more soluble at 4 km than the model computes and 1.331x at 5 km: the lysocline and the carbonate compensation depth sit substantially shallower than SEDGEM would place them, and nothing looks wrong. This is the sharpest single item this row has to weigh, because it changes what the tier would SAY about Vesper rather than what it costs to run. MARBL inverts on the same axis and is clean, pressure being a driver-supplied forcing. SECOND: `initialise_goldstein.F:377` `rsc` and `gem_cmn.f90:802` `const_rEarth` are two independent statements of the planet radius, and BIOGEM re-derives GOLDSTEIN's own scalings from the second, so a port that changes one is worse than a port that changes neither. notes/audits/ocean-tier-implicit-earth.md findings 1 and 4.

THE COST HALF IS MEASURED, 2026-08-25, and the row is not closable on it. notes/audits/cgenie-build-cost-and-grid-ceiling.md is the finding; analysis/cgenie_cost.py is the driver and analysis/cgenie_cost.json the artifact. IT BUILDS, RUNS AND REPRODUCES ITS OWN REFERENCE: the shipped eb_go_gs case run against genie-knowngood agrees on all 28 shared floating-point fields to a worst relative difference of 4.3e-21. Five things had to be settled to get there and none is a source defect: the tree's hardcoded GENIE_ROOT/RUNTIME_ROOT/NETCDF_DIR, the netCDF FORTRAN bindings, one executable per GRID through a config's <build> block (rule 4's shape on a second model), the genie.exe target because nccompare wants the legacy netCDF C++ header, and a serial make because finc.py is Python 2. Above 36x36x16 the link also needs -mcmodel=medium, which costs 3 per cent. COST PER OCEAN-YEAR, IN RETIRED INSTRUCTIONS because the host was contended throughout and wall clock measures that: 2.973 Ginstr per model year at 36x36x16 physics-only, 13.787 at 72x72x16, and the shipped BIOGEM case at 36x36x8 with 14 tracers is 4.708, or 2.65 times the physics at the same grid. INITIALISATION IS NOT A COST: every intercept from the two-run-length fit is below one model year's worth of work and every one is negative. That reproduces the published EMIC figures rather than quoting them -- about 7 hours for a 20,000-year biogeochemical spin-up on one core here against the 24 to 48 quoted, a hardware generation apart. THE BAROTROPIC SOLVE IS INVISIBLE at these grids: the pre-registered arm, 64x32 against 36x60 at nearly equal cell count and 1.686 times the ubarsolv work, returned 0.956, inside the tracer-dominated band and 0.6 per cent from that hypothesis's prediction. That settles section 9h's runtime half without a profiler and leaves OCN-19 the within-tracer attribution. THERE IS NO THREAD-COUNT AXIS: every $omp string outside genie-plasim is commented out in column one so it is not a sentinel, MPI is only in the vendored PlaSim, and three live use omp_lib statements have no call against them. Cost is one core against simulated years and parallelism is across EXPERIMENTS, which is why an offline ocean can run beside a commissioning instead of queueing behind it. TWO OF THIS ROW'S OWN QUESTIONS ARE ANSWERED BY READING THE RECIPE. There are exactly two surface-flux paths for GOLDSTEIN and each is gated on an atmosphere module: genie.F:279 under flag_ebatmos, and :402 under flag_plasimatmos INSIDE the flag_goldsteinseaice block. So the host's sea ice cannot be turned off on the driven path -- it is what carries it -- and with neither atmosphere flag set the ocean receives no surface forcing at all. The driven path is nevertheless the shape offline full-flux wants: surflux_goldstein_seaice takes surface temperature, humidity, pressure, insolation, downward longwave, net heat, wind speed and the transfer coefficients as INPUT. It also returns an ice state, which is the quantity section 7b makes ExoPlaSim authoritative for. AND THE OCEAN SURFACE VELOCITY IS EXPORTED, as a first-class coupling field: goldstein.F:780-781 fills ustar_ocn and vstar_ocn every ocean step from u(1..2,i,j,kmax), genie_global.f90:278-279 dimensions them, and gold_seaice_wrapper already consumes them. It is non-dimensional and its scale go_usc=0.05 m/s is exported beside it. world-pt8's premise holds. scf ENTERS LINEARLY at goldstein.F:199-205, so the ocean's own Courant ceiling inherits OCN-17's declared 1-to-3 bracket directly. WHAT REMAINS: the Vesper-parameter port (radius and gravity, which are source work), OCN-10's forcing contract, and a quiet-host wall-clock re-take. Nothing here adopts anything: vendor/cgenie still has no consumer, no pipeline row and no step.
close_reason:
2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER. ADOPTED. cGENIE is the offline circulation host. The exploration this row was opened for is finished, and the adoption decision -- which was the only thing holding it open -- is taken.

WHY THE TWO BLOCKING EDGES WERE REMOVED RATHER THAN FORCED PAST. ocn-3 depended on OCN-11 and OCN-10 while its deliverable was a VIABILITY VERDICT: costing a candidate configuration needed a sketch of the bathymetry and of the boundary closures. The decision replaces that verdict, and it inverts the direction -- OCN-10 and OCN-11 are now what adoption OBLIGES, not what it waits on. Forcing the close would have left the graph asserting a prerequisite that is no longer one. Both are relates-to now.

What the row established and what carries forward: it builds here; surflux_goldstein_seaice takes fluxes and the atmosphere's own transfer coefficients as INPUT rather than a state to recompute them from, which is exactly the contract the offline exchange needs; the ocean surface velocity is exported as a first-class coupling field, so world-pt8's premise holds; and scf enters linearly at goldstein.F:199-205, so the ocean's Courant ceiling inherits OCN-17's declared 1-to-3 bracket.

WHAT ADOPTION NOW OBLIGES, none of it discharged here. The Vesper-parameter port -- radius and gravity -- is source work. OCN-10's forcing contract and OCN-11's bathymetry and support contract are the two artifacts nothing crosses the boundary without. OCN-5 must DECLARE the loop's forcing procedure, provenance chain and exit predicate AND add the loop and its steps to config/pipeline.yaml in the same commit: until that lands the ocean is adopted in intent and absent from the graph, and an artifact no step generates does not exist. WORLD-U9KG's precondition binds from today -- an adoption decision for any cgenie component states which calibration switches are off, which factors are at 1.0 and which reference files are absent, BEFORE the component is wired to anything.

Unblocks OCN-18, OCN-19 and OCN-20, each of which was complete and held open only by this.

title: Scope ECOGEM as the ecosystem tier, with driver-agnostic MARBL as the named fallback
description:
Scope ECOGEM as the ecosystem tier, with driver-agnostic MARBL as the named fallback: licence/version/provenance; tracer and trait-count cost; restart and diagnostic state; required C-N-P-S-Fe-Si, alkalinity/DIC/O2 and optical inputs; absolute-time, K-star photon, gravity/sinking and temperature dependencies; what the covarying trait space must DECLARE; and every fixed Earth relation or inventory that survives. Darwin leaves the board with MITgcm, being an MITgcm package, and this costs nothing on the axis that mattered: trait-based ecology was never the discriminator between them, since both make community composition emerge from a declared trait space. Compare ECOGEM against MARBL on interface burden and on what each supplies as fixed Earth types. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is a scoping note

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 12, 16 and 40d, `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and BOTH CANDIDATES ARE NOW LOCAL AND READ: ECOGEM inside `vendor/cgenie/genie-ecogem` from the vendoring, MARBL at `references/marbl/`, BSD-style from UCAR and in references rather than vendor because this row's deliverable is a scoping note. THE COMPARISON SPLITS SCIENTIFIC AGAINST ENGINEERING and should not be forced to a winner. ECOGEM WINS THE ECOLOGY, on the mechanism this row names: the cost is a FILE SWAP, verified at source: `par_ecogem_plankton_file` is a namelist string, `sub_init_populations` counts data lines and sets `npmax` from them, and every plankton-dimensioned array is ALLOCATABLE, so the ladder runs 1 / 8 / 9 / 11 / 16 / 18 / 64 populations across nine shipped `.eco` files with no recompilation. Sixteen is the reference configuration and not the price this row once quoted. TWO CORRECTIONS TO WHAT THAT LADDER MEANS: the 0.6 to 1900 um log spectrum is `8P8Z`'s, not the ladder's -- `32P32Z.eco` is a different grid, phyto 0.10 to 1224 and zoo 0.15 to 2800 with the offset not mirrored, so the sixty-four rung changes the size RANGE and not only the count; and the `3Diat4ZP_PiEu` against `NoDiat4ZP_PiEu` pair is not a free on/off pre-registration, since the diatom file carries 11 rows against 8, so it is a guild ADDED rather than a switch thrown. THE TRAIT SPACE THE ROW ASKS ABOUT IS NOT THE DATA FILE: it is 36 allometric `_a`/`_b` coefficient pairs in `ini_ecogem_nml`, applied as 39 `coef_a * volume ** coef_b` statements, so a population is a size and the traits follow. MARBL is the structural opposite and NOT because its count is locked -- `PFT_defaults` accepts `user-specified` and the shipped `+cocco` variant moves the count -- but because it has no allometric generator at all: 38 hand-set parameters per autotroph with a poison default of `1e34`. That, and not the file swap, is why ECOGEM wins the ecology. MARBL WINS THE ENGINEERING, and also not closely: regression tests, baselines, build tests, `code_consistency.py`, YAML settings with a JSON form carrying per-configuration defaults, declared dependencies, units and datatypes -- AND A STANDALONE DRIVER -- which is a TEST HARNESS and not an offline model: `marbl.F90` dispatches ten single-shot test names and `call_compute_subroutines` calls the compute routines once per column, with no time loop and no tracer update. It can answer a tendency-sensitivity question and cannot produce a spun-up state. ECOGEM has no entry in `genie-knowngood`, no test suite, no settings schema and no driver of any kind. STOICHIOMETRY IS NOT A WASH, and the earlier reading missed where ECOGEM keeps its: BIOGEM exposes `par_bio_red_POP_PON` and others in `ini_biogem_nml` with `bio_part_red` four-dimensional, but ECOGEM buries four Redfield literals in its own BIOGEM coupling arithmetic -- 138/106, two 16.0 and 6.625 -- none of them namelist-reachable. MARBL exposes three and derives seven from a fixed chain. THE PHOTON AXIS INVERTS TOO: MARBL's `f_qsw_par = 0.45_r8` is a Fortran `parameter` with no YAML entry and its six attenuation literals are hardcoded, while ECOGEM's `PARfrac`, `k_w` and `k_chl` are all namelist, so ECOGEM is the one correctable from a configuration file. A SECOND BURIED SOLAR CONSTANT, and it is this project's own recurring defect: `ecogem_box.f90:298` converts light as `E0 = PARlocal/0.2174`, which is 4.5998 umol/J and is the marine twin of the fixed 550 nm Earth coefficient BIO-25 found in LPJ photosynthesis. Read the two together. WHAT TO ACT ON WITHOUT DECIDING, restated now the driver is understood: what MARBL can be made to answer before an ocean host exists is a TENDENCY at a stated state, not a candidate, so the sequencing advantage is real but much narrower than it read. AND THE TWO ARE NOT INDEPENDENT CHOICES: ECOGEM cannot be extracted from cGENIE, so if OCN-3 selects cGENIE it is nearly free, and if OCN-3 does not, ECOGEM is unavailable at any price and MARBL's true cost is the tracer transport host underneath it. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 12, 13a and 16. A SPECTRAL PRECONDITION FOR ANY ECOSYSTEM TIER, 2026-08-22, which applies to ECOGEM and MARBL alike and not only to BIOGEM: marine light limitation is specified as an irradiance half-saturation in W m-2 and a SINGLE SCALAR light e-folding depth in metres, both solar calibrations. Water is transparent in the blue-green and strongly absorbing in the red and near-infrared, so a K dwarf's redder flux gives a SHALLOWER photic zone and production confined nearer the surface. The direction follows from the spectrum alone; the magnitude needs `k25v_hr.dat` integrated against water absorption, which is a desk calculation and should precede tier selection rather than follow it, since it changes the vertical structure any tier resolves. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 40d. MAGNITUDE COMPUTED, 0.712, from artifacts already in the tree and with no new number. `exoplasim/data/water/hale_querry_1973_liquid_water.dat` gives water's absorption above 0.75 um, and the LONGEST e-folding depth anywhere in that range is 0.51 m, so all of shortwave band 2 is deposited in the top metre or two as heat and what reaches the photic zone is band 1 and nothing else. Band-1 flux fraction is 0.382 for k25v -- reproducing the project's canonical `flux_fraction_band1` exactly -- against 0.537 for a 5772 K Planck, which is `analysis/vegetation_albedo.py`'s own solar reference. THIS STAR DELIVERS 71 PERCENT AS MUCH LIGHT BELOW THE SURFACE LAYER. Limits, none of which change the sign: it is the flux reaching below the surface layer and not the photic DEPTH, which additionally needs visible attenuation that is not extracted here; and it is pure water, where productive water's chlorophyll and CDOM absorb more in the blue and partly offset it. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 40e EVIDENCE POINTER, filed 2026-08-22: the comparison this row rests on is now `notes/audits/ecosystem-tier-ecogem-marbl.md`, read at source and carrying its own limits section; `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 12c and 16 are the earlier reading and have been corrected in place where that note contradicted them. WHAT REMAINS BEFORE THIS CLOSES is the SILICON axis and nothing else: the row asks for required C-N-P-S-Fe-Si inputs, and `squota` and the silicifier path were traced structurally only. `references/INDEX.md:516` records Naidoo-Bagwell et al. (2024), the EcoGEnIE 1.1 diatom extension, as `held` rather than read, and the note states that any silicon comparison between the tiers needs it first.

DONE 2026-08-24, and the row's last open item is closed. `notes/audits/ecosystem-tier-ecogem-marbl.md` section 13 reads the SILICON axis at source in both tiers and reads Naidoo-Bagwell et al. (2024), which `references/INDEX.md` now records as read. ECOGEM: silicon is compiled in unconditionally and gated by two namelist logicals plus a per-population real; the silicifier is selected by the word `diatom` in column one of the `.eco` file and the `.eco` files carry NO silicon column at all, so all five silicon traits come from four live allometric `_a`/`_b` pairs in `ini_ecogem_nml`. There is no silicon half-saturation parameter, it is vmax/affinity and the model prints it. The Si:C quota is size-INDEPENDENT while the kinetics are not. One of the nine shipped plankton files has a silicifier row and one base config in the tree combines ECOGEM with the silicon tracers. `ocn_select(io_SiO2)` is enforced with a hard stop; `sed_select(is_opal)` is NOT, and without it silicon uptake is a permanent removal with no return path and nothing catches it. There is no dissolved organic silicon tracer. `kexcSi` and `par_diatom_vmax_mod` are dead knobs a Vesper retune would reach for. Two out-of-bounds indexings for mismatched squota/useSiO2, and the 'Population inviable' guard is 0/0 for every non-silicifier so it has no failing state. MARBL: one unconditional dissolved tracer, a per-autotroph tracer created only for a silicifier, and OPAL IS NOT A TRACER -- it is a column-diagnostic sinking particle, so it has no prognostic inventory. Its half-saturations carry the 1e34 poison default but `silicifier` itself defaults to FALSE, so a user-specified set that forgets it gets no opal cycle and nothing to trip on. Opal production is the carbon fixation rate times the quota, so it inherits the whole light path. Grazing remineralisation 0.22 as a bare parameter with a comment saying 60 per cent, a burial step function of three inline literals, an unnamed 40 km ballast length and two inline dust literals, none settings-reachable. Its column silicon budget check is real and LOUD; its global closure needs a host reduction it cannot compute, and the standalone driver has no time loop so it cannot produce an inventory. THE GRAVITY QUESTION SECTION 9 REDIRECTED IS ANSWERED ON THE OPAL PATH: BIOGEM states a sinking SPEED and a dissolution RATE separately and both are namelist, where MARBL states only their ratio as a fixed length and cannot be rescaled from inside. Live speed in the published config is 49.689 m/d, not the 125.0 beside it, which a backwards-compatibility branch disables. THE PAPER'S CAVEAT: its Table 2 attaches two of the four live silicon parameter families to references absent from its own reference list, so half of them are test cases rather than anchors. This row SCOPES and does not select: ECOGEM cannot be extracted from cGENIE, so the ecosystem tier is not an independent choice and OCN-3 decides it.
close_reason: Scoping note complete: notes/audits/ecosystem-tier-ecogem-marbl.md, whose section 13 closes the silicon axis, the only item the row had left. Both tiers read at source, both compared on interface burden and on what each supplies as fixed Earth types, and references/INDEX.md moves Naidoo-Bagwell et al. (2024) from held to read. This scopes and does not select: ECOGEM cannot be extracted from cGENIE, so the ecosystem tier is not an independent choice and OCN-3 decides it.

title: DECLARE the forcing procedure, provenance chain and exit predicate for the ocean-transport
description:
DECLARE the forcing procedure, provenance chain and exit predicate for the ocean-transport loop before its first pass, and add the loop and its OCN-2/OCN-10/OCN-11 steps to `config/pipeline.yaml` in the same commit. An ocean model forced by a climatology a zero-transport slab produced, and restored toward that climatology's own sea-surface temperature, returns a transport of zero by construction. Use flux forcing with no temperature restoring, retain weak salinity restoring only as an explicit control, and converge heat transport, SST/ice, global energy, freshwater/salt closure and the climate fields that drive the carve verdict

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` sections 7, 8a and 8f
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and a DECISION rather than a measurement, which is why it is a task and the run is not. Ocean physics is inside loop A because transport can move design flux and the carve verdict; SPAT-8 must replay it at every candidate support. Ocean biology stays outside loop A while OCN-16 is closed, and opening carbon feedback creates a separate declared loop rather than silently extending this one. THE CANDIDATE SATISFIES HALF OF THIS ROW BY CONSTRUCTION AND CANNOT SATISFY THE OTHER HALF, 2026-08-22. cGENIE has NO sea-surface temperature or salinity restoring: `surf_ocn_sic.F` computes surface flux terms, `fx0o`, `evap`, `fxsen` and the sea-ice counterparts, and the ocean takes fluxes from whichever atmosphere it is coupled to. The one name that looks like restoring is not -- `rel` in `common /ocn_relax/` is used at `velc.f:103` as `u = rel*u1 + (1-rel)*u`, a numerical under-relaxation between solver iterates, so record it as a solver control lest somebody retire it as physics. The genuine explicit control is `get_hosing.F`, freshwater forcing with `hosing`, `hosing_trend` and `nyears_hosing` in `ini_gold_nml`, called UNCONDITIONALLY from `goldstein.F:259` and added to the freshwater flux at line 297 -- always in the path, inert only by parameter value, which is why a zero default is not the same as an absent term and it belongs in the provenance chain. THE SPLIT: this row's warning joins two failures with an "and" -- forced by a slab-derived climatology AND restored toward its SST. The candidate rules out the second by construction. Nothing in it rules out the first, because that defect is in what this project SUPPLIES. So read the requirement as two with different owners: no restoring is checkable once against cGENIE; flux forcing that does not encode the answer is this project's and is what the declared procedure is actually for. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 27. THE MECHANISM, DERIVED 2026-08-22, and it is sharper than this row's own statement. cGENIE tunes its atmosphere to make room for its ocean: `tstipa.f` moves heat and moisture as `betaz(l)*uatm(1,i,j)` and `betam(l)*uatm(2,i,j)` plus `diffa`, and `ini_embm_nml` exposes `diffamp(2)`, `diffwid`, `difflin`, `betaz(2)` and `betam(2)`, so the atmosphere-ocean transport PARTITION is a tuned quantity there. THIS PROJECT CANNOT DO THAT. On a slab with `nhdiff` off the ocean transports nothing, so ExoPlaSim's atmosphere carries the entire poleward load through resolved dynamics, with no coefficient to turn down. Hand those fluxes to a dynamic ocean and the total becomes an atmosphere already carrying everything plus an ocean carrying more. THE FLUX-FORCED FAILURE IS THE OPPOSITE SIGN FROM THE RESTORED ONE this row describes: not zero transport, but OVER-transport, because the flux field was computed under the assumption that the ocean does nothing. THIS APPLIES TO THE ARCHITECTURE OCN-10 SPECIFIES AND NOT TO THE PUBLISHED PATH, which keeps EMBM and lets it compute the heat fluxes with a tunable transport -- see OCN-10's fork. Under the no-EMBM architecture the loop is necessary rather than stylistic -- a single pass cannot converge the partition, because the atmosphere in the forcing climatology has not been told the ocean exists. And it is why OCN-2 comes first: the return path is `nfluko = 1` reading surface code 903 under the comment "prescribed advection", and verifying that channel with a known field is cheaper than discovering it is wrong once a circulation exists to blame. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 28. A PEER EXIT PREDICATE WORTH COPYING, TWO-SIDED, 2026-08-22. cGENIE's GEMlite accelerator is controlled in `genie-main/genie.F` by ENTRY ON A RATE and EXTENSION ON AN ERROR INTEGRAL: `:621-638` extends the full-model phase whenever the year-on-year pCO2 change exceeds `gem_adapt_dpCO2dt`, default 0.1 ppm/yr, so the accelerator never engages while the system is moving fast; `:808-823` extends the accelerated phase only while cumulative drift from its starting pCO2 stays under `gem_adapt_DpCO2`, default 0.1 ppm. Unbounded extension is off by default with the reason recorded at the switch, and `gem_yr_min`/`gem_yr_max` bound the phase at 10 and 1000. THE PRECONDITION THAT MAKES IT WRITABLE is a single scalar summarising the accelerated subsystem's drift that is already computed; name that number for the ocean-transport loop when declaring this row's exit predicate, because without one the predicate can only be a fixed schedule. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 35 THE HAND-OVER RULE IS SUPPLIED, 2026-08-24, from the eliminated synchronous architecture where it is a working arrangement rather than an inference. Terms that depend on ocean temperature are recomputed LIVE against it -- saturation specific humidity and hence latent heat, net longwave, and sensible heat -- while only the transfer coefficients and the downward radiative and moisture fields are replayed. The source comment gives the reason: naive replay of net heat flux severs the negative feedback that holds sea surface temperature. Evaporation is deliberately NOT recomputed, for moisture conservation, with rescaling precipitation and runoff considered and rejected as no better. Adopt that split in this row's forcing procedure rather than deriving one. Section 59 also removes this row's architecture ambiguity: the loop is required, because offline full-flux is the decided class and it is the class in which nobody owns the partition. notes/external-model-survey.md sections 59f and 59g.

OCN-2 IS DONE AND THE CHANNEL IS VERIFIED, 2026-08-24. Surface code 903 under `nfluko = 1` reproduces a prescribed field cell for cell to 1.9e-6 W/m2, carries it over land as well as ocean, keeps its area-weighted global integral, and delivers it to the slab at the declared heat capacity and output interval, the last recovered to 3.2e-7 relative from the sea surface temperature response alone. So this loop's return path is no longer an assumption. `exoplasim/scripts/verify_ocean_flux_channel.py` is the instrument and re-running it on a new rung or a new build is one `stage` and one `check`. Two things it did NOT verify and this row inherits: the MONTHLY interpolation, because the verification field is constant in time on purpose so the calendar cannot affect the answer, and `addfc`'s ice branches, because the segment is ice-free. `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` section 11.

title: Cost a spatially varying, K-star-weighted two-band ocean albedo. seamod.f90:155-158 applies
description:
Cost a spatially varying, K-star-weighted two-band ocean albedo. `seamod.f90:155-158` applies two namelist scalars everywhere `dls < 0.5`, so scope a versioned surfcode/writer/config path that carries Fresnel/background water separately from OCN-14 pigment/particle water-leaving reflectance, preserves ocean fraction and support provenance under SPAT-4/5, and reduces exactly to the current scalars. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is the interface cost and a sourced optical bound, not implementation

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` finding 5a and sections 8b/8e
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. The present 0.014 to 0.28 K price is explicitly DECLARED and suggests this does not earn its place alone; it must not become a central pathway until its optical span is sourced and OCN-14 supplies a modelled state. The interface remains cheap if another reason later requires spatial ocean albedo [step: surface_albedo]. THE SPECTRAL HALF IS ANSWERED, NEGATIVELY, 2026-08-22. `exoplasim/surfacespecs.py`'s `oceanblend` weighted against a 5772 K Planck gives a broadband 0.070, reproducing `doceanalb = 0.069` and confirming it as the provenance; weighted against `k25v` it gives 0.068. Water's reflectance is low and nearly flat across the 0.75 um split, 0.076 against 0.065, so a K-star reweighting of the ocean albedo is worth 0.002 and does not earn its place -- which is the same verdict this row already reached from the temperature side, now reached independently from the spectrum. WHAT REMAINS IS THE SPATIAL HALF ONLY, and the two-band interface question, since `doceanalb(1:2)` is a band array holding one value in both elements like every other surface in the model. PHYS-14 owns that defect class; this row keeps the spatial variation. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 11c. THIS ROW'S PREMISE IS PARTLY WRONG AND ITS INSTRUMENT ALREADY EXISTS, 2026-08-22. `seamod.f90:155-158` does apply two namelist scalars, and then `radmod.f90:2895-2904` OVERWRITES the open-ocean part with a zenith-dependent formula, so in the default configuration those scalars survive only for the land and sea-ice fractions and `doceanalb` contributes nothing to open water. THERE ARE THREE BRANCHES, by `necham` and `necham6`: the default `necham=1` gives ECHAM-3, `min(0.05/(zmu0+0.15), 0.15)`; `necham6=1` gives Briegleb, which is the same formula cGENIE integrates in `ocean_alb.F`; both zero gives the constant. SO THE SPATIAL VARIATION THIS ROW ASKS TO COST IS ALREADY PRESENT AND ZENITH-DRIVEN, and what is available is a free A/B between two shipped parameterisations. Flux-weighted daily means: they agree within about ten percent at high sun -- 0.058 against 0.052 at the equator, 0.075 against 0.079 at 45 degrees equinox -- and diverge to 1.64x at 45 degrees solstice and 1.82x at 60 degrees winter, because ECHAM-3's cap binds above 79.5 degrees zenith and Briegleb has no ceiling. THE DIVERGENCE REGION IS LARGER HERE: at 32 degrees obliquity against Earth's 23.4 more of the year sits in the low-sun regime, and that is the winter hemisphere where sea ice forms. Both zenith branches are spectrally flat, which the source states in a comment rather than denying, so the negative spectral result above is unaffected. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 29 SECTION 11's OCEAN EXEMPTION SURVIVES ITS OWN CORRECTION, 2026-08-24, but for a different reason than stated. PHYS-14 was overturned -- radmod already star-weights the surface blends and the flat declarations never reach the radiation -- so 'nothing weights these spectra' was never true of the Fortran. The ocean conclusion is unaffected: water is dark and nearly flat across the split, and re-weighting doceanalb for this host is worth about 0.002 either way. What DOES reach this row is world-a0y: the same zdenom1 and zdenom2 that mis-normalise the ice surfaces normalise the ocean and ground ones in the same block, so doceanalb carries the same 1.47 percent band-1 error. That is larger than the 0.002 spectral question this row was closing, and it is a different question -- a defect rather than a design choice. Do not fold it into this row's verdict; world-a0y owns it.

THE INTERFACE COST IS DELIVERED, 2026-08-25, priced structurally because the host was contended and a wall-clock number taken there would look like a measurement. notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md section 12.

THE BAND INDEX ALREADY DOES NOTHING OVER OPEN WATER. radmod's upward loop writes the SAME expression into dsalb(1,:) and dsalb(2,:) over open water under necham = 1 and under necham6 = 1, so seamod's value survives only with both zenith branches off. A two-band ocean albedo installed in seamod is discarded before the shortwave reads it, and the term has to land inside radmod's own expression. That is the headline of the interface cost and it puts the change in a file this row does not own.

THE STAGING HALF COSTS NOTHING. Codes 175 and 176 are already a two-band, month-resolved, per-cell surface albedo channel: written by build_surface_albedo.py over the WHOLE grid, read by mpsurfgp as (NHOR,14), carried in the restart by mpgetgp/mpputgp, month-interpolated into dalbclim1/dalbclim2, and consumed only over land. No new surface code and no new .sra column are needed. What is needed is a decision about what those two codes MEAN, since they are the background LAND albedo today and one artifact would then answer to two generators.

A SEPARATE OCEAN PAIR IS NOT CHEAP AT THE TOP OF THE LADDER. 2*14*nlat*nlon*8 bytes at -fdefault-real-8 against the 32 MB die target: 1.75 MiB and 5.5 per cent at T42, 7.00 MiB and 21.9 per cent at T85, 28.00 MiB and 87.5 per cent at T170. A single-month pair is a fourteenth of that, and whether the field needs a seasonal cycle is OCN-14's question because the water-leaving part of it is pigment and particles.

THE ARITHMETIC IS THE SMALL PART. Two streaming loads of eight bytes per ocean cell per band per radstep, against six arrays the albedo block already streams; one divide, one add and one AMIN1 removed. It vectorises unchanged: unit stride preserved, no gather, no branch, no loop-carried dependency. The change is memory traffic, not control flow.

WHAT REMAINS AND WHY THIS ROW STAYS OPEN. The deliverable is the interface cost AND a sourced optical bound. The bound on the SPECTRAL question was already delivered negatively at about 0.002; the bound on the SPATIAL span needs a modelled water-leaving reflectance and a Fresnel term derived from this star, and OCN-14 owns the first. Nothing was benchmarked and no source was changed.

2026-08-26. BLOCKED ON OCN-14 AND ONLY ON THAT; the structural half landed.

WHAT IS DELIVERED. The interface cost was already delivered. The SPECTRAL bound
was already delivered negatively, at about 0.002. And seamod.f90 now records
where its two scalars survive and where radmod discards them, so a later spatial
ocean albedo is not installed at a point the shortwave never reads -- which was
the failure this row could otherwise have walked into after OCN-14 lands.

OCN-22 IS CLOSED AND IS NOT THIS ROW. The band collapse was the half these two
shared, and folding it in here rather than costing it twice is what this row's
own notes asked for; the fold is made. Its blocking edge on this row is
converted to relates-to, because it was correct while the two were one undone
change and is stale now that the change is done.

WHAT REMAINS IS ONE THING: a sourced bound on the SPATIAL span, which needs a
modelled water-leaving reflectance. OCN-14 owns that and it does not exist. It
was deliberately NOT smuggled into OCN-22's registered prediction, which covers
the band redistribution alone.

title: Orogen places the ice that carves this terrain by latitude and dimensionless elevation alone.
description:
Orogen places the ice that carves this terrain by latitude and dimensionless elevation alone. At the build's `glacialErosion` of 0.8 the ice line falls at 58 degrees latitude, positioned by the erosion slider and nothing else, and the altitude gate is in the model's elevation parameter so the snowline tracks maximum relief, which scales as 1/g, rather than a freezing altitude set by lapse rate and surface temperature. `glacIdx` consults no temperature at all: not the K2.5V spectrum, not the 32 degree obliquity, not the 30 hour rotation, and not even Orogen's own temperature field, which `computeTemperature` produces after `runPostProcessing` has already eroded. All three leading parameters point the same way, toward less polar ice than an Earth-tuned 58 degree threshold gives

Source: `notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. The correction needs no new physics, but NOT the field first proposed here. `glac` is identically zero across all twelve bins and all 8,192 cells while the run manifest records `"glaciers": true`, and `snd` peaks at 0.29 m, which is seasonal snow. That zero is a fact about the grid, not the planet: the sub-grid peak excess `orog_max - orog_mean` on land averages 1.065 km and 2.969 km at the 90th percentile, so at the measured warm-season lapse rate of 7.372 K/km the model evaluates its own high ground about 7.8 K too warm on average and 21.9 K too warm in the top tenth, and no ice survives that. USE INSTEAD the warmest-month surface temperature, which is smooth and genuinely resolved at T42, corrected to each mesh region's own elevation through `lib/lapse.py`'s freezing-height criterion. `maps/build_basemap.py` lines 379-385 already implement exactly this for the basemap's ice shading. Measured that way, land below freezing in the warmest month goes from 0.002% on the model's orography to 1.657% on the 15.19 km mesh, and `analysis/ice_mask_freezing_height.py` is the registered computation. Raising the model truncation is not the alternative: T85 is about 150 km against a 7.59 km mesh, so the peak excess stays sub-grid at any resolution the model can afford. Drive `glacIdx` from that mask instead of `polarDist` and close it through loop A, which exists to feed a commissioned climate into the next generation; the terrain-before-climate ordering that blocks it inside one pass is not a constraint across iterations. SHAPE OF THE FIX, decided 2026-08-20: an ice mask consumed AT GENERATION like the carve list, `--ice-mask FILE`, not a post-hoc terrain alteration. Glacial, hydraulic and thermal erosion share one iteration loop and a mid-loop priority flood at `GLACIAL_MID_FLOOD_FRAC` exists to cut outlets through the depressions glaciation makes, so a separate later pass would leave them undrained and move the drainage network and the basin catalogue. Bootstrap with `--glacial 0`, an honest null, then commission and regenerate with the mask. Two constraints on it: mapping `glac` from the ExoPlaSim grid back to the mesh is a rule 3 crossing and must go by index or a shared coordinate source, and per `docs/src/reference/no-time-axis.md` a current ice field can only say WHERE ice was, never how long, so the strength slider stays a declared choice rather than a measurement. Subsumes the mechanism half of GRAV-6 [step: orogen]. AMENDED 2026-08-22: this row is also upstream of any ice sheet mass balance, not only of the carve terrain. Every candidate scheme in this class drives ablation from surface temperature, which makes the 7.8 K mean and 21.9 K top-tenth warm bias measured here the single most damaging input error such a scheme can be given. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 4 LADDER-PROOF, 2026-08-24, which upgrades this row from a correction to the permanent instrument. At 1.20 Earth radii the circumference is 48,090 km, so the ladder gives cell widths of 751 km at T21, 376 at T42, 188 at T85, 125 at T127 and 94 at T170 -- against a 7.60 km Orogen mesh. The top of the ladder is still twelve times coarser than the terrain the ice sits on, so the 1.065 km mean and 2.969 km 90th-percentile sub-grid peak excess stays sub-grid at EVERY rung this project will run. glac = 0 is therefore a permanent property of the model's orography rather than a statement about the world, and no resolution converts it into one. This row's mesh diagnostic is not a stopgap until the grid improves: it is the answer, and the model's glacier module is carried for its orographic feedback on cells it can resolve rather than as the instrument that locates ice. Same class of argument as the offline ocean decision -- the quantity wanted lives at a scale the atmosphere will not be run at. notes/glacier-rough-pass.md, extension 2026-08-24.
close_reason:
Generator fixed. WHERE the ice goes now lives in vendor/orogen/js/glacial-ice.js with two sources: --ice-mask FILE, one float32 per mesh region in region order with a sidecar naming the mesh, which is a climatology's answer and therefore carries the spectrum, the obliquity and the rotation by construction; and the Earth-calibrated latitude ramp when no mask is given, unchanged and now saying at the call site what it does not know. Consumed at generation like the carve list, matched by region index, refused on a mesh-identity mismatch as soon as the mesh exists. manifest.params records the mask's provenance and which of the two placed the ice. analysis/ice_mask_freezing_height.py --write-mask produces the mask and gained --grid-export, without which it could not be produced against a climatology at a truncation other than the mesh export's; it is now a step in config/pipeline.yaml that orogen needs, rather than an out-of-graph verdict. tools/test-glacial.mjs, 10 tests.

Behaviour preserved: with no mask the placement is bit-identical, verified against the pre-change generator at 20,000 regions with Vesper radius and gravity and all four erosion sliders live (finalElevation 6cf056ac, preErosion 252ec271). So nothing downstream is worthless yet.

One half of the finding is NOT a defect and is closed as such. The dimensionless altitude gate does not track maximum relief in a way that needs correcting: the relief ceiling goes as 1/g from sigma/(rho g), a dry-adiabatic freezing height goes as 1/g from Gamma = g/cp, and the two cancel, so the dimensionless form is the gravity-invariant one and re-anchoring it to fixed kilometres would introduce an error. Algebra in the module header, pinned by a test, recorded in notes/audits/orogen-gravity.md. What the ramp cannot know is the surface temperature, and measurement confirms that is the whole of it: the ramp and the criterion agree on the ice line to within the transition width (mean |lat| 54.8 against 56.2 degrees) and disagree on altitude (mean elevation_km 0.84 against 2.28), with glaciated land area 33.727% against 0.967% and ice supply 8.8x lower. notes/glacier-rough-pass.md extension 2026-08-25; all limits, pre-carve build and bootstrap climatology.

title: Snow, glacier ice and sea ice albedo are spectrally FLAT and solar-weighted
description:
Snow, glacier ice and sea ice albedo are spectrally FLAT and solar-weighted, and they are the only surface endmembers never re-derived for this star. `plasimmod.f90:428-432` declares `dsnowalbmx(2) = 0.8`, `dsnowalbmn(2) = 0.4` and `dglacalbmn(2) = 0.6` -- two-element BAND arrays initialised from a scalar, so the simulation's snow reflects identically either side of the 0.75 um split. That is the same defect `config/planet.yaml` records having fixed for vegetation, where "one identical field used to assert that a canopy reflects equally either side of the split". It also means the k25v spectrum fix did nothing for snow: the two-band machinery carries a star's shape by moving flux BETWEEN bands, and moving flux between two equal numbers changes nothing. THE DERIVATION IS DONE AND THE NUMBERS ARE IN THE NOTE. `exoplasim/surfacespecs.py` ships the ECOSTRESS blends the constants came from, `iceblendmax`, `iceblendmin`, `glacalbmin`, `seaicemax` and `seaicemin`, interpolated to the same 965 wavelengths `k25v.dat` uses, and only `pRT.py` reads them. Weighted by a 5772 K Planck they reproduce 0.8, 0.4 and 0.6 to within 0.016, WHICH IS THE CHECK THAT VALIDATES THE INTEGRAL before anything is concluded from the other column. SIX FOR SIX on that check, the worst by 0.016 and the ocean to three decimals. Weighted by `k25v` the band pairs are 0.983/0.585, 0.508/0.273, 0.764/0.406, 0.892/0.473 and 0.636/0.339, with broadbands 0.736, 0.362, 0.541, 0.631 and 0.451 -- so fresh snow is about 0.064 too bright, old snow 0.038, glacier ice 0.059, MAXIMUM SEA ICE 0.069 and minimum sea ice 0.049, every one in the direction that weakens the ice-albedo feedback at the cold end. Sea ice is the largest single error in the set and the one surface with no configuration key at all, so `dicealbmx` and `dicealbmn` are in this row's scope beside the land three. The OCEAN is exempt and that is a result rather than an omission: `oceanblend` moves 0.070 to 0.068 because water is nearly flat across the split, so it does not earn a key

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 11, `notes/audits/inherited-earth-constants.md`, `docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md` class 31
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and what is left is SHAPE rather than derivation: a provenance-stamped analysis product on `analysis/vegetation_albedo.py`'s pattern, an anchoring convention for the band pair like `vegetation_albedo_bands` so the flux-weighted combination reproduces the broadband value, keys in `config/planet.yaml`, and a decision on the sea ice pair, which belongs to `icemod` rather than `landmod` and has no config key at all today. `iceblendmax` against `iceblendmin` is already the grain and impurity bracket this row asked for, so that is answered too. HIGH LEVERAGE and unchanged: these drive the feedback that dominates the cold end, so this reaches the bare-rock endmember arm, PHYS-13's ice mask, the extreme-cold land fraction capping the design flux, and what the stellar cycle's grand minima are worth [step: surface_albedo, bootstrap_run]. THE SHAPE QUESTION IS SETTLED BY PRECEDENT ON BOTH SIDES, 2026-08-22. ExoCAM's modified CLM sets `albice(numrad) = (/ 0.80, 0.55 /)`, land ice albedo by waveband, under a header saying the CLM defaults are too high and citing Paterson (1994) p.59 for a FULL-SPECTRAL value of about 0.5 with CAM3 and Pritchard et al. (2008) as precedent. Two things follow. The two bands hold DIFFERENT numbers in an independent implementation, which confirms the flat arrays here are anomalous rather than conventional. And the values are anchored against a stated full-spectral target, which is the same convention `vegetation_albedo_bands` already uses -- so the anchoring rule this row needed is settled: the band pair reproduces the broadband value, and the broadband value is the one derived from the spectrum. As a sanity check the numbers line up the right way: section 11's `glacalbmin` gives 0.766/0.455 under the Sun against CLM's 0.80/0.55, lower because `glacalbmin` is the GLACIAL MINIMUM blend, old or dirty ice, while Paterson's 0.5 is a general glacier figure. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 22. A PREDICTOR THIS MODEL DOES NOT HAVE FOR SNOW, AND IT IS WORTH AS MUCH AS THE ONE IT DOES, 2026-08-22, and ORTHOGONAL to the spectral reweighting this row already settled. ExoPlaSim's snow albedo is a linear ramp in SURFACE TEMPERATURE between 263.16 K and `tmelt`, `landmod.f90:394-405`, blended by forest fraction, with no zenith term. ClimaLand's is `min(1 - beta*(rho_snow/rho_liq - x0), 1) * (alpha_0 + d_alpha*exp(-k*cos_z))` -- zenith angle and snow density as a grain-size proxy, with no temperature term. Disjoint predictors for the same physics. At ClimaLand's calibrated `alpha_0 = 0.59`, `d_alpha = 0.40`, `k = 1.96` and the density factor 0.874 at 330 kg/m3, the ZENITH TERM SPANS 0.565 TO 0.865, a range of 0.30, against this model's ENTIRE temperature range of 0.40 from `dsnowalbmn` to `dsnowalbmx`. Flux-weighted daily means at 32 degrees obliquity run 0.599 at the equator equinox to 0.783 at 60 degrees winter, an 0.18 swing that is absent, largest in the winter hemisphere at high latitude where the snow is. NOTE THE INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY IT EXPOSES: section 29 established that ExoPlaSim applies a zenith-dependent albedo to open ocean BY DEFAULT, so the same physical effect is present for one surface and absent for another inside one model, and both cases live in the same low-sun regime. ClimaLand's values are Earth solar-spectrum calibrations and do not transfer; the form and the magnitude argument do. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 37b-c. THE MISSING PREDICTOR IMPLEMENTED, PLUS A DUST PATH, 2026-08-22. `references/climber-x/src/sic/surface_par_sic.f90:111-260` carries two snow-albedo schemes -- Warren-Wiscombe and Dang et al. (2015) -- BOTH taking prognostic grain size AND dust concentration, with grain size corrected for solar zenith angle. Snow grain size is a prognostic in the restart. That is section 37's missing zenith predictor implemented in an EMIC, with a second predictor beside it this project has no representation of at all. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 43f SCOPE MADE CONCRETE 2026-08-24. The derivation is done and validated; what this row delivers is four things and no new physics. (1) analysis/ice_albedo.py writing analysis/ice_albedo.json, on analysis/vegetation_albedo.py's pattern: re-weight iceblendmax, iceblendmin, glacalbmin, seaicemax and seaicemin from vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/surfacespecs.py against k25v, split at 0.75 um, provenance-stamped with spectrum sha256, library, spectra_used and a band recombination residual. The Sun-weighted column is the BUILT-IN test that can fail: it must reproduce 0.8, 0.4, 0.6, 0.7 and 0.5, six for six with the worst at 0.016. (2) The anchoring convention, matching vegetation_albedo_bands against vegetation_albedo: the band pair's star-flux-weighted combination reproduces the broadband value, and the broadband value is the one derived from the spectrum. (3) Keys in config/planet.yaml for all five. (4) The sea ice pair specifically, dicealbmx and dicealbmn, which live in icemod rather than landmod and have NO configuration key today -- that is scope this row ADDS rather than inherits. THE ROUTE IS NOT THE PYTHON API: exoplasim/__init__.py exposes only snowicealbedo, one scalar for all snow AND ice, which flattens the entire set. Namelist writes or a fork change. THE MACHINERY IS ALREADY LIVE, which is why this binds: the project sets two_band_albedo: true and runs at NSIMPLEALBEDO = 0, so the two-band path is on and does nothing for these surfaces because both bands hold one number. Landing values, K2.5V band1/band2 against the current constant: snow max 0.983/0.585 vs 0.8, snow min 0.508/0.273 vs 0.4, glacier 0.764/0.406 vs 0.6, sea ice max 0.892/0.473 vs 0.7, sea ice min 0.636/0.339 vs 0.5. Every one currently too bright, one-signed against the ice-albedo feedback at the cold end, and in the SAME direction as OCN-21's now-declared ice-motion term. THE ZENITH PREDICTOR IS OUT OF SCOPE and now has its own row, world-spd; this row is the spectral reweighting only.
close_reason: OVERTURNED 2026-08-24, and replaced by what checking it found. THE PREMISE IS FALSE: radmod.f90:600-790 already carries these five blends as Fortran arrays over the same 965 wavelengths, weights each by the configured stellar spectrum, splits at 0.75 um and assigns dsnowalb, dsnowalbmn, dsnowalbmx, dicealbmn, dicealbmx and dglacalbmn. radini runs at plasim.f90:513, BEFORE surfini reads any surface namelist, so the flat two-element declarations at plasimmod.f90:428-432 are defaults that are overwritten before they are used. The run says so: 'Finalized Albedos' in run_2b20e3324bb0 records snow max 0.968/0.585, sea ice max 0.879/0.473 and glacier 0.752/0.406. The bands hold different numbers and they are this star's, so the simulation's snow does NOT reflect identically either side of the split and the k25v fix DID reach it. What sections 11a-11c established is narrower than they claimed: it is surfacespecs.py, the PYTHON copy, that nothing weights. The error was reading declarations without checking a run. NO KEYS ARE ADDED, and that is the substantive half of this verdict rather than a saving. Writing config values for these would freeze the constants against the spectrum and override a computation that is correct in form -- so the shape work this row's scope described is not deferred, it is WRONG. WHAT REPLACED IT: analysis/ice_albedo.py, registered as the ice_albedo step, which reproduces radmod's arithmetic to machine precision and measures the one real fault it exposes -- a numerator on the 965-point grid divided by a denominator on the 2048-point grid, band 1 low by 1.47 percent relative on every surface, one-signed DARKER. That is world-a0y. The orthogonal zenith predictor is world-spd. notes/external-model-survey.md sections 11d and 11e.

title: Soil albedo carries no moisture dependence
description:
Soil albedo carries no moisture dependence, and the blocker is a missing state variable rather than a missing parameterisation. `dalbclim1` and `dalbclim2` at `landmod.f90:118-119` are PRESCRIBED STATIC fields on the same 0.75 um band split this project uses, and this project's own albedo products are moisture-blind too -- `analysis/rock_albedo.py`, `analysis/playa_albedo.py` and the surface-class builder all lack a wet/dry axis. Wet ground is darker than dry ground, so on land with a strong seasonal wetting cycle this is a seasonal albedo term with no representation. The parameterisation is standard: ClimaLand's `CLMTwoBandSoilAlbedo` after Lawrence and Chase (2007) is `alpha_band = alpha_dry*(1-S_e) + alpha_wet*S_e` on exactly that band pair, so it drops into the existing structure. WHAT IS ABSENT IS `S_e`: it is the effective saturation over the top 0.02 m, and ExoPlaSim's land is one scalar bucket with no depth, so there is nothing to evaluate it from

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 39
notes:
2026-08-27, MEASURED. f is no longer unmeasured and the row's last item is done.

f CAME OUT OF THE RESTART, not a new diagnostic. landmod.f90:1553 writes dwatcl
with mpputgp and dwmax and dsoilwfc sit beside it, so dwatcl(:,1) over its own
layer capacity is wetalb's arithmetic read back. Over run_893e276ee029's settled
block f has a land-area mean of 0.3283 and is BIMODAL -- median 0.0096, p90
0.9997, a third of the land above 0.5 -- which is what a 0.02 m store in a
tipping-bucket cascade does. The mixing is therefore evaluated per cell and
meaned; the fall at the mean f is 1.45 times the mean of the per-cell falls.

THE ARM. run_a1c35075747c (NWETSOIL = 1) against run_598eb57c5a34 (0), 25 orbits
each from run_893e276ee029/MOST_REST.00209. Same binary and same seed by md5,
one namelist line apart, both diagnostic at one I/O regime, both passing every
diagnostic settling criterion at a 25-orbit window -- which is below the derived
41, so the offset criterion is not tested at its designed power.

MEASURED land-mean alb fall 0.006397, inside the registered 0.003780 to 0.006745,
resolved at 5.7 times the arms' own bar. The wet arm's own background fall is
0.006709 against 0.006745 predicted before the run. Monotonicity holds at 5.3e-16
and the evaporite refusal at 4.2e-16. f moved 0.3313 to 0.3257 between arms, so
the feedback on it is inside the noise and the term is nearly linear in it.

WORTH 0.287 W/m2 and +0.20 K at the attenuation the arm itself measured, or
0.471 W/m2 and +0.32 K at the declared 0.5. That is the same size as this
project's dust radiative item, 0.34 to 0.61 W/m2.

TWO FINDINGS BEYOND THE ROW. The mask costs 4.6 per cent and not the 44 the
prediction's lower end assumed, because snow and wetting are anti-correlated: a
frozen skin already reads as dry. And the registered claim that tas could not
separate was WRONG -- it did, at +0.1972 K -- because the 1.6 to 2.1 K bar was
imported from arms seeded from an unsettled control. A paired arm's power is set
by how settled its DONOR is at least as much as by its length, and this pair's
tas standard error is twenty times smaller at the same run length. The separation
is the first measurement of error_budget.py's attenuation: world-ckbt.

THE GUARD THIS NEEDED. --restart-from refused the NWETSOIL = 0 arm on "codes
differ" because 1742/1750/1760 leave intended_surface_codes at the switch off.
That was over-strict: landmod.f90:833-835 reads them through mpsurfgp outside
any nrestart test, so a restart cannot freeze them in either direction. The
exemption is now restart_surface.REREAD_EVERY_START, which already carries that
claim checked in the Fortran, and it covers the content test as well as the set
test; the interactive dust source map 1801-1803 was in the same position. The
inline block is donor_surface_reason and smoke_test drives it. No
--superseded-surface-ok was used: the donor's surface is the current one and its
frozen dalbcl is bit-identical to the staged 174 in all fourteen months.

WHAT REMAINS IS world-znr7 ALONE, band 2's dark end, which needs no run.
close_reason: Modelled, armed, staged and now measured. The moisture term runs in landmod under nwetsoil = 1 on a per-cell Sadeghi mixing between a dry and a saturated endmember derived per class and per band for this star; f is measured at a land-area mean of 0.3283 and found bimodal; and the paired arm resolves a land-mean alb fall of 0.006397, inside the bracket registered before the run, worth 0.287 W/m2 and +0.20 K at the attenuation the arm itself measured. title: Make the star's band-1 flux share canonical. Three values were in use: 0.3777 from k25v.dat
description:
Make the star's band-1 flux share canonical. Three values were in use: 0.3777 from `k25v.dat`, 0.3862 from `k25v_hr.dat`, and 0.4184 printed by the model

Source: `notes/audits/physics-review.md` finding 2
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-17, and it was NOT an integration question. THE MODEL'S 0.4184 IS NOT THIS STAR: `radmod.f90:813` takes the spectrum branch only when `NSTARFILE > 0`, and no run's `radmod_namelist` carries it -- all four have `STARBBTEMP = 4965.0`, `NSTARTEMP = 1` and no `STARFILE` -- so `solarini` has been building a 4965 K Planck curve and printing its partition. `lib/stellar.py` reproduces `solarini` and matches every printed digit: 0.418350 for the blackbody against the model's 0.418350399, 0.384383 for `k25v_hr.dat`, and 0.517000 for the 5772 K identity `radmod.f90:207` states. The mechanism is that `exo.Earthlike(workdir=...)` re-copies the shipped namelists, and both `continue_exoplasim.py` and `run_stellar_cycle.py` reconstruct the model on an existing run without `starspec`; `run_exoplasim.py` was the only driver that staged the spectrum and it runs one orbit, so `MOST_DIAG.00000` of every run reports 0.384383 and every file after it reports 0.418350. Worth +0.024 on broadband snow albedo, double the 0.013 estimated, and it moves sea ice, glacier, ground and ocean albedo too. Canonical value is 0.384383, computed rather than stored, with `check_consistency.py` failing when a copy drifts. THREE THINGS FOUND ON THE WAY, all larger than the task. `solarini` integrates its 5772 K Rayleigh reference over the WRONG array, having overwritten `wv1`/`wv2` with the file's wavelengths first, so `rcoeff` is 0.209732 against 0.712517 -- which inverts the fix order, since declaring the spectrum without patching that would weaken Rayleigh scattering 3.4x. `dust_forcing.py` carried a FOURTH value, 0.2566, from counting the bin width twice. And the physics review's water-vapour ratio of 1.204 was read off the blackbody, so PHYS-1 is worth +9 to +12 W/m2 rather than +6.5 to +9. Spun out as SPEC-1 and SPEC-2

title: Integrate Penman over the diurnal cycle rather than evaluating it at 12-bin means
description:
Integrate Penman over the diurnal cycle rather than evaluating it at 12-bin means

Source: `hydrography/scripts/carve_verdict.py`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-17. Saturation vapour pressure is convex at about 6.7%/K, so the daily mean of e_s exceeds e_s of the daily mean and a bin-mean evaluation understates the deficit that drives Penman -- Jensen, and one-signed. The range is measured from the model's own `maxt` and `mint`, 8.08 K land-mean and 12.32 K at p90, and a sinusoid between them is integrated at 24 points; `delta` gets the same treatment, since a diurnal-mean e_s with a point-evaluated slope would be inconsistent in the flattering direction. Worth +0.59% on land-mean Penman, about half the +1.2% estimated, because the convexity is on the DEFICIT and Penman's radiative term dilutes it. Carve 1725 -> 1721. DIRECTION: the audit was right and I was wrong -- it raises E and closes basins, the SAME direction as PHYS-4, which only looked opposite while PHYS-4's stable premise still stood. Kept regardless of size: the diurnal cycle exists

title: Preserve groundwater access through every mesh-to-climate-grid crossing
description:
Preserve groundwater access through every mesh-to-climate-grid crossing: integrate groundwater-accessible area and the conserved ET/seepage flux on native hydrography regions with the support-matched coupling matrix, use SPAT-3/GRID-2 hypsometry where the access criterion is terrain-conditioned, carry `sink_fraction`, `at_surface` and uncertainty regimes through aggregation, and reject mean water-table depth as an oasis/riparian-area proxy

Source: `biosphere/notes/plant-hydraulics-groundwater-audit.md` finding 6, `biosphere/notes/spatial-support-ecological-aggregation-audit.md` finding 5
notes: The follow-up that runs this on real data is world-36ho. (The close reason names world-tk1h, which was a placeholder written before the issue existed; world-36ho is the real id.)
close_reason:
hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater_access.py reduces water_table.nc onto the climate grid as an AREA and never as a mean depth. The access criterion is evaluated on the NATIVE REGIONS, where the depth lives, and what crosses is the fraction of the cell's land below each declared access depth, with the extensive area beside it. No hypsometry is used and none is needed: the within-cell depth distribution is in hand, so reconstructing it from GRID-2's would be an inference where there is a measurement -- that hypsometry is for criteria that are terrain-conditioned and have no native evaluation.

sink_fraction crosses as three regime area shares plus its own undefined share, at_surface and the excluded lithologies as their own shares, and the Gleeson permeability bracket as a member axis (--water-table once per member, labelled by each file's sigma). So the regime flags hydrography/README.md requires every depth consumer to preserve are preserved by construction rather than by discipline.

Every fraction is a fraction of the cell's own LAND population from surface_class, so there is no per-region access fraction: GW-6, and world-d9u4's constraint, the same one topographic_index states for f_sat_max.

The step guards its own index alignment with gridding.require_index_alignment against the coupling matrix for the same rung.

VERIFIED BY --selftest ONLY, and deliberately: water_table.nc does not exist for this build and baseline_climatology is null, so the step it reduces has not been run. The six invariants have right answers rather than plausible ones -- seepage and land area close, the sink regimes partition, access is monotone in the threshold and saturates at both ends, and the negative control the artifact exists for: a narrow shallow strip in a deep cell must survive, which a depth-averaging reduction fails while every conservation check still passes.

No consumer reads it yet. wet-2, plhy-7 and sdec-3 are the rows waiting on it, and world-tk1h is the follow-up to run it on the first accepted water table.

title: Register standard LPJ-GUESS versus LPJ-GUESS-HYD as a no-retuning structural sensitivity
description:
Register standard LPJ-GUESS versus LPJ-GUESS-HYD as a no-retuning structural sensitivity: port plant water potentials, resistance, VPD regulation, vulnerability and cavitation mortality with Vesper gravity in `rho*g*h`, combine it with GRAV-7's gravity-aware support allometry, define coherent hydraulic/structural strategy priors rather than independent Earth-trait draws, and assess hydraulic mortality jointly with DEMO-4

Source: `biosphere/notes/plant-hydraulics-groundwater-audit.md` findings 1, 7 and 8
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; blocked on BIO-23, PLHY-2 through PLHY-4, GRAV-7, BIO-12/BIO-14, DEMO-4 and explicit permission for LPJ-GUESS runs; capacitance, turgor-limited growth, drought leaf shedding and biotic mortality remain declared omissions of the bracket [step: vesper_pfts, lpj_run, soil, surface_albedo]. A UNIT TRAP THIS PORT WILL HIT, AND A REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION, 2026-08-22. ClimaLand's `plant_hydraulics.jl` is an independent implementation of what this row ports: the plant as a Darcy medium, `F = -K_eff*((psi2-psi1)/(z2-z1) + 1)` at `:197` with a harmonic-mean conductivity, and a Weibull vulnerability curve `K = K_sat*exp(-(psi/psi63)**c)` at `:256` after Liu (2020) and Sperry (2016), both per-PFT. THE TRAP IS THE UNIT. That gravitational term is written as a bare `+1`, which is right only because `psi` is in metres of HEAD, and head is `P/(rho*g)`, so the convention absorbs gravity and hides it. `toml/default_parameters.toml:49-53` stores `psi_63 = -408.163...` whose own description reads "Computed by -4 / 0.0098. Holtzman's original parameter value is -4 MPa" -- 0.0098 MPa/m being `rho*g` at EARTH gravity. So the stored number is a plant property times Earth. The same -4 MPa here is -312.26 m of head, exactly `1/1.306` of it. AND THE USE SITE MAKES IT WORSE: `soil_moisture_stress.jl:82` converts back with `psi*rho_water*grav`, so carrying `psi_63 = -408.16` forward while setting `grav` to 12.81 commits the error TWICE and presents the stress function with -5.22 MPa where the literature says -4. THE RULE TO CARRY: any plant-hydraulics parameter published as a PRESSURE and stored as a HEAD carries the gravity of whoever stored it, and nothing in the stored value says so. Failure-mode class 32 in its unit form. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 41. AND AN INDEPENDENT MODEL PUTS THE SAME CEILING IN A MORTALITY TERM, 2026-08-22. FATES uses `grav_earth` in exactly two places and one is plant hydraulics, as the gravitational head of the plant water column. At 12.81 m/s2 that head term rises 30.7 percent, raising the fractional loss of conductivity at a given soil water potential and therefore raising hydraulic-failure mortality -- **effectively capping tree height through a mortality rate rather than an allometric limit**. That is section 41c's hydraulic ceiling arriving by a second route in a second model, which strengthens the case for treating it as physics rather than as an allometric convention. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 54d

title: The no-soilmap fallback reads uninitialised memory into per-layer soil thermal properties.
description:
The no-soilmap fallback reads uninitialised memory into per-layer soil thermal properties. `modules/soilinput.cpp:696-772` `soil_parameters()` -- the path taken when `file_soilmap` is unset -- never writes `porosity_gridcell[]`, `org_frac_gridcell[]` or `min_frac_gridcell[]`, and `Soiltype()` does not initialise them. With `iforganicsoilproperties 1` and any soilcode other than 8, `modules/soil.cpp:3319-3321` reads those arrays into the per-layer heat capacity and thermal conductivity. Separately at `:735`, `soiltype.wtot` indexes `data[soilcode - 1][1]`, an out-of-bounds read at soilcode 0

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 57
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and NOT EXERCISED in the live configuration, which passes `file_soilmap` -- so this is a latent trap on a documented and reachable fallback rather than a live defect. Fix or fail closed: an unset soilmap should refuse rather than proceed on uninitialised thermal properties [step: lpj_run] SOURCE CHANGE LANDED 2026-08-22 AND NOT COMPILED, so this row is blocked on a build rather than on effort. Fixed AND fail-closed. `soilinput.cpp:736` rewrites `wtot` as `gawc[0]+gawc[1]+gwp[0]+gwp[1]`, which is an identity rather than a guess -- `SoilInput::get_soil` computes it exactly that way at `:651` -- so the out-of-bounds index is gone rather than corrected. `:764-780` fills the three per-layer arrays from the same table entries the scalar `organic_frac`, `porosity` and `mineral_frac` two lines above already use, which is the degenerate case of what `get_soil` derives from a `SoilC` column and invents nothing. `guess.h` gains `UNSET_SOIL_FRAC = -1.0` and both read sites in `soil.cpp` refuse on the sentinel, a zero default having been a different silent-wrong. Every input path was checked so the guard cannot fire on a valid configuration. CORRECTION 2026-08-22: this is NOT clearable by a recompile. LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree at all -- `framework/vesper.h` is a GENERATED header, and `pipeline.py --plan vesper_header` runs the chain to it through `baseline_run` and `baseline_climatology`, neither of which exists. So this row sits behind the same baseline run as CLIM-71, not behind a compile, and nothing here is verified by execution. Do not fit the header against the bootstrap climatology to make a build succeed; BIO-19 owns that ambiguity and choosing a climatology to serve a compile is not a way to settle it.
close_reason: Fixed. The no-soilmap fallback in soil_parameters was already repaired (three per-layer arrays filled from the same table row as the scalars; wtot rewritten as the gawc/gwp identity, removing the data[soilcode-1][1] out-of-bounds read; UNSET_SOIL_FRAC sentinel with both soil.cpp read sites refusing on it). Verified against the artifact, not the note. Two sibling paths of the same class were still open and are now closed in 1b04388a: (1) SoilInput::get_soil_organic's soilcode==8 early return wrote only the three arrays and returned, leaving every Soiltype scalar unwritten -- get_soil is the sole populator, so texture, percolation, the Gerten capacities, thermal diffusivities, wtot, awc/wp/wsats, the P sorption constants and soilcode were read from constructor state; it now defers to soil_parameters for the same code, whose per-layer fill for code 8 reproduces the replaced loop exactly. (2) soiltype.soilcode was stored as soilcode-1 there, so LPJ code 9 (Vertisols) aliased to 8, which update_layer_fractions reads as the organic soil and answers with the whole-profile scalars, discarding the per-layer profile just computed; it now stores the code as read, as the other two writers do. Soiltype's constructor also left soilcode unwritten and now takes UNSET_SOILCODE. NO RUN IS INVALIDATED: no LPJ-GUESS run on this world exists. pipeline.py --status reports lpj_run MISSING and biosphere/runs/ does not exist; the chain to it runs through baseline_climatology, which is MISSING. run_lpj_guess.py always writes file_soilmap and exits if it is absent, and build_soil.py emits a named-column map so SoilInput::soil_code is false, which means none of the three paths is on the live route in any case. Verified by g++ -fsyntax-only on soilinput.cpp, soil.cpp, somdynam.cpp, vesperinput.cpp, demoinput.cpp and guess.cpp against a throwaway vesper.h; the tree cannot be linked because framework/vesper.h needs a baseline climatology (BIO-19, CLIM-71).

description:
Reconcile the CNP fork's phosphorus topology with one declared equation set: decide whether sorbed P enters a reversible strongly-sorbed stock or an explicit terminal occlusion sink, then align `pmass_strongly_sorbed`, `UOCC`, `Patch::pcont()`, flux names, serialization, outputs and mass-balance boundaries with that decision; register the published annual rate units and the provenance of the saturation constants

TOPOLOGY CHOSEN AND IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24 on branch fanout-T, commit efb0756f, docs 5d53a7ec. The reversible sorbed to strongly-sorbed exchange, per Dantas de Paula et al. (2025) Appendix A2 and Wang et al. (2010) Eq. D10. Soil::pmass_strongly_sorbed is assigned, so both terms are real and the stock fills to the size of the sorbed pool where the net flux goes to zero. The transfer is internal, so it is no longer reported as an external P_SOIL loss, and Patch::pcont() counts it; double-booking would break the balance. USORB and USSORB are registered as per Earth year and now divide by VESPER_EARTH_YEAR_DAYS under world-ith2. WHAT SDEC-2 ALSO ASKED FOR AND DOES NOT GET HERE: the provenance of PMASS_SAT and PCONC_SAT, split out as world-pidx and blocked on Parton, Stewart and Cole (1988), doi 10.1007/BF02180320, which could not be obtained.
