title: Audit and bound the active soil-N transformation operator for Vesper pressure, O2
description:
Audit and bound the active soil-N transformation operator for Vesper pressure, O2, gas diffusion, pH and water-table redox state; connect BIO-23's atmospheric boundary and SDEC-3's layers to nitrification, denitrification, volatilisation and N-gas partitioning, with no-simulation conservation/range fixtures and a declared Earth-calibrated response-function bracket

Source: `biosphere/notes/soil-decomposition-biogeochemistry-audit.md` finding 8
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; affects mineral N availability in the present `ifntransform 1` baseline, independent of disabled methane under BIO-28; response measurement requires an accepted baseline and explicit permission [step: lpj_driver, lpj_run, soil, groundwater]

2026-08-24, batch AG. The audit, the register, the bounds and the fixtures are DONE and committed; the response-function BRACKET is BLOCKED on two papers and is why this stays open.

DONE. biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md registers every constant with the file the model reads it from, and biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml carries the machine-readable form: twelve response functions with their forms, literals, domains and roles, four products of factors that each multiply one pool mass, and five Vesper preconditions all carrying the undeclared sentinel (surface pressure, pO2, soil gas diffusivity, water-table redox, the atmospheric boundary). biosphere/scripts/ntransform_gate.py checks the constants against global_soiln.ins, every literal against modules/ntransform.cpp, every function over its whole domain against the range its role allows, and every product against 1; seven fixtures, six built to be wrong in a named way; --strict refuses while a precondition is undeclared. Registered in config/pipeline.yaml as a step lpj_run needs.

Three defects found and repaired, none of them in finding 8. (a) The soil map pH never reached the operator: get_mineral read the ph column into a local SoilProperties and neither get_soil path copied it onto Soiltype::pH, which stayed at -1.0, so nh3_volatilization took its no-pH branch on every gridcell. (b) That branch could not work: it evaluated Dawson (1977) against climate.aprec_lastyear, which nothing assigns, while climate.aprec is reset at day 0 and never accumulated, so it returned 8.5 everywhere every day. It now refuses by name rather than substituting a constant. (c) The operator only conservation check was an assert, compiled out by every Release build; it is now compiled in with a bar relative to the nitrogen present, fixed before any result.

BLOCKED, and the reason. Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008), Terrestrial nitrogen cycle simulated with a dynamic global vegetation model, Global Change Biology 14(8) 1745-1764, 10.1111/j.1365-2486.2008.01625.x, is the source of every table this operator cites. Weier et al. (1993), Denitrification and the dinitrogen/nitrous oxide ratio as affected by soil water, available carbon, and nitrate, SSSAJ 57(1) 66-72, 10.2136/sssaj1993.03615995005700010013x, is the source of the denitrification moisture response and its two gas ratios. Neither could be fetched (paperfetch, DOI and title, open access and sci-hub all refused). Without them no constant can be checked against its calibration and no Earth-calibrated response bracket can be declared, because a bracket needs the range of soils and conditions each curve was fitted over. Pilegaard (2013) WAS fetched and read and its row is in references/INDEX.md.

Filed and not fixed here: world-b2i2 (substrate_partition applies a WFPS-calibrated curve to fraction-of-available-capacity, which is the largest single control on gaseous loss and is also blocked on Xu-Ri), world-qzra (climate.aprec dead accumulator, out_seasonality a permanent zero), world-cz3n (pH_soil is a declared instruction parameter nothing reads).

What holds without the papers: no response function can create nitrogen, verified over every declared domain. Two bounds hold for a reason rather than by construction and are argued in the note. All of these are bounds on coefficients, so they survive the fine-root C:N repair, which moves every pool size and every absolute flux and none of them.
2026-08-24, batch AM. The two papers arrived and the bracket is now DECLARED. references/xuri2008-terrestrial-nitrogen-cycle-dgvm.pdf and references/weier1993-denitrification-n2-n2o-ratio.pdf are both held, read and recorded in references/INDEX.md.

biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml gains a calibration block: twenty entries, one per constant and per response function, each naming its source, what that source states, and the verdict. Eight agree. Five are OUTSIDE the range their own source gives: f_denitri_gas_max 0.33 against Xu-Ri table 11's RNON+RN2ON of 0.2-4.2 percent (world-nga3); nh3_max applying a second time the pH dependence table 5 eqn 6 already carries, which puts NH3_SOIL three to five orders below the paper's formulation (world-nga7); the denitrification temperature response clamped at its 22 C value where table 9 eqn 1 has no min (world-nga6); and the N2 share above 0.7 WFPS plus the 0.7 branch point itself, both against Weier tables 4 and 5 (world-nga2). Seven are in NEITHER paper: f_denitri_max and f_nitri_gas_max (world-nga4), the Michaelis-Menten divisor (world-nga5), substrate_partition's midpoint and shape (world-nga8), the nitrification water response (world-nga9), and the N2O:NO ratio and the N2:N2O temperature sigmoid (world-nga2). One more issue was filed off the same work: world-nga10, get_mineral's unclamped Cosby inversion.

Brackets declared, each from a paper: f_nitri_max 0.1 to 0.403 /day (Xu-Ri table 11 gives Nmax at 20 C, the model applies it at a 38 C peak where the curve is 0.248); the nitrification gas fraction 0.002 to 0.042 (table 11); the NO share of it 0.33 to 0.98 (table 11); the denitrification moisture exponent 8.09 to 14.06 (Weier table 2's geometric and arithmetic means); the N2 share of denitrification gas 0.333 to 0.938 (Weier tables 4 and 5, 401 observations); substrate_partition's midpoint 0.50 to 0.66 WFPS.

The gate's refusal is narrowed rather than lifted: --strict now names five Vesper preconditions and twelve calibration entries and refuses on exactly those. Neither paper settles any precondition; both are Earth work at Earth pressure and pO2 and neither carries a water table.

Nothing is execution-verified. LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree until a baseline climatology exists.
close_reason: The audit, register, bounds, fixtures and the Earth-calibrated response bracket are all done and committed. Every constant now carries a verdict against Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) or Weier et al. (1993). What remains is not this issue: the five Vesper preconditions are owned by sdec-3 and bio-23 and by the gate's own refusal, and the nine calibration disagreements are world-nga2 through world-nga10.

title: Close accepted seasonal methane fluxes, including any separately conserved OCN-13 marine
description:
Close accepted seasonal methane fluxes, including any separately conserved OCN-13 marine source, through BVOC-6's Vesper oxidant/transport bracket: solve lifetime, OH feedback, atmospheric imbalance and global/latitudinal CH4, feed only a converged provenance-bound abundance to ExoPlaSim's radiative band, and prohibit combining modelled sources with the fixed-modern-Earth-flux 1.6 ppmv state

Source: `biosphere/notes/wetlands-peat-methane-audit.md` finding 10, `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` section 8d
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; reduced chemistry interface follows WET-8/BVOC-6 and admits OCN-13 only as a named source, not a second atmospheric owner; replacement of `pCH4_bar` and every chemistry/climate response experiment require accepted closure and explicit permission [step: lpj_run, baseline_climatology, baseline_run]. A reduced form of the LIFETIME half exists and this row should be costed against it: `references/climber-x/src/ch4/ch4_model.f90` is a partitioned-lifetime box, tropospheric OH against separate chlorine, soil and stratospheric sinks, with an OH temperature sensitivity and OH sensitivities to CO, NOx and VOC precursors. The STRUCTURE transfers and the calibration does not: the precursor sensitivities are fitted to anthropogenic Earth emissions read from a file, the chlorine term is Earth stratospheric chemistry, and the OH field is a photochemical product of the host's ultraviolet -- which for this star is not an open question, since `atmosphere.pCH4_bar` already records that Rugheimer et al. (2013) computed the photochemical steady state at this effective temperature. A constant respiration fraction still yields a flux and never an abundance, so `atmosphere.pCH4_bar` stays this row's alone. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3f. A ROUTE, NOT JUST A FLOOR, 2026-08-22. `vendor/cgenie/genie-atchem/atchem_box.f90` carries six methane oxidation schemes. The default is Osborn and Wigley (1994), `tau = tau0*(CH4/C0)**N`, with the comment "omitting [OH], [NOx] etc etc" and a clamp at half the reference concentration where the calibration curve ends. **`sub_calc_oxidize_CH4_schmidt03` is the same functional form with the constants EXPOSED** as `par_pCH4_oxidation_tau0`, `C0` and `N` rather than hardcoded, and its header names its calibration: a fit to the 2-D photochemistry model of Schmidt and Shindell (2003). So this row's oxidant and lifetime half reduces to DERIVING THREE NUMBERS from a photochemistry calculation for this host -- and `atmosphere.pCH4_bar` already records that Rugheimer et al. (2013) computed the photochemical steady state at this effective temperature, which is the same class of calculation. The conservation structure comes with it and is what this row wants: `O2 -= 2*fracdecay*CH4`, `CO2 += fracdecay*CH4` with 13C and 14C carried, `CH4 *= (1-fracdecay)`, per grid cell rather than as a global box. LEAVE THE `claire06` AND `goldblatt06` FAMILIES ALONE: they take a whole-atmosphere conversion factor with no grid indices and are Archean anoxic-atmosphere formulations, built for a kind of planet this one is not. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 20a. THE MASS-TO-CONCENTRATION CONVERSION IS A PLANET PROPERTY AND MUST BE DERIVED, NOT INHERITED, 2026-08-22. Any box-model methane budget needs a Tg-to-ppb factor, and CLIMBER-X's `src/ch4/ch4_model.f90:40` derives its 2.7476 Tg CH4 per ppb from EARTH's atmospheric mass of 5.1480e18 kg (IPCC, Prather et al. 2012). Column mass is `P/g` over `4*pi*R^2`, so with this world's 1 bar summed from `planet.yaml`'s partial pressures, 1.20 Earth radii and 12.81 m/s2, the atmosphere is 1.088x Earth's and the factor becomes 2.990 Tg CH4 per ppb: A GIVEN SOURCE IN Tg/yr PRODUCES ABOUT 92 PERCENT OF THE ppb IT WOULD ON EARTH. The same rescaling applies to any N2O or CO2 budget. ALSO A SPIN-UP CONSTRAINT for the seasonal budget this row closes: CLIMBER-X derives peat potential from a THIRTY-YEAR inundation memory, a 360-month ring buffer at `src/lnd/lnd_params.f90:379`, so a peat fraction cannot be established from one model year. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 42b and 42d. THE LIFETIME IS COMPUTABLE AND THE DOOR IS NAMED, 2026-08-22. CAABA/MECCA carries the sink as real chemistry -- `CH4 + OH` with a modified-Arrhenius rate, OH from `H2O + O1D`, O1D from ozone photolysis -- and carries NO prescribed lifetime anywhere, so it must be derived offline as `1/(k*[OH])`. THE BLOCKING QUESTION IS ANSWERED NEGATIVELY FOR JVAL: its fitted cross-section coefficients were generated with a hardcoded 176-element ATLAS-2 SOLAR spectrum as the integration weight, so a different star needs that array replaced and the preprocessor re-run over a 19,393-line generated file. THE TRACTABLE DOOR IS CLOUDJ: `input/cloudj/FJX_spec.txt` holds the solar photon flux as EIGHTEEN NUMBERS in a text file, and CAABA accepts `photrat_channel='cloudj'`. CAVEAT THAT MUST NOT BE DROPPED: whether CLOUDJ has ever been exercised in this release is NOT determined -- there is no `caaba_cloudj.nml` and no testsuite entry where RADJIMT and TRAJECT both have one. Build-check before planning around it. SEPARATELY, `messy_jval.f90:1544` converts pressure to overhead column as `N_A/(M_air*g)` with Earth gravity, making every O2 and O3 slant column 1.306x too large here regardless of spectrum. AND THE SCOPE LIMIT: a box model gives a LOCAL chemical destruction rate, not a global lifetime -- that needs the local rate weighted over the atmosphere's mass and OH distribution, an offline integration over an ExoPlaSim climatology using a grid of box results. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 48

title: Derive one mutually exclusive native-mesh wetness classification and seasonal area artifact
description:
Derive one mutually exclusive native-mesh wetness classification and seasonal area artifact: persistent peat-forming land, saturated non-inundated mineral soil, seasonal inundation, open lake/river/playa water and dry mineral soil; use hydrography, native groundwater state and sub-grid topography, aggregate fractions rather than thresholds, close against BIO-11's rootable surface and forbid latitude selection or double counting

Source: `biosphere/notes/wetlands-peat-methane-audit.md` finding 2
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; interface/area-closure work extends PLHY-5 and can proceed without LPJ-GUESS, while the groundwater driver must preserve persistence and seasonality rather than expose mean coarse-cell depth alone [step: hydrography, groundwater, soil, lpj_driver]. WET-12 names the reduced form of this classification, which is the TOPMODEL saturated fraction from GW-26's index; it is the part of the fallback that forfeits least, and mutual exclusivity is what it gives up. WHY THE LATITUDE PROHIBITION BITES, PRICED 2026-08-22. The fork's decomposition already selects by latitude and the step is large: `somdynam.cpp` gives a saturated mineral soil a moisture modifier of 0.360 on every pool, against 0.025 on the slow and passive pools for a high-latitude peatland stand, a factor of 14.4 on the long-lived carbon, switched at `PEATLAND_WETLAND_LATITUDE_LIMIT = 40.0`. NOTE ALSO that the general curve, Friend et al. (1997) Eqn 53 after Parton et al. (1993), BOTTOMS OUT AT 0.360 at full saturation rather than falling to zero -- so on that curve alone saturation does not preserve carbon, and the classification this row derives is doing all the work. THE MECHANISTIC ALTERNATIVE that needs no category: ClimaLand's DAMM implementation limits respiration by oxygen as `theta_a**(4/3)` through a Michaelis-Menten factor, so anoxia is a computed consequence of air-filled porosity rather than a stand type. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 34. THE INUNDATION SCHEME IS SMALLER THAN EXPECTED AND ITS COST IS PREPROCESSING, 2026-08-22. CaMa-Flood's ENTIRE floodplain representation is one precomputed array per cell -- a TEN-BIN CDF OF HEIGHT ABOVE NEAREST DRAINAGE, stored at each decile of flooded AREA -- turned at init into a storage-versus-level curve of ten nested prisms. The runtime prognostic state is TWO SCALARS, channel and floodplain storage; depth, flooded fraction and area are all diagnostic, recovered by walking the storage bins. The closure making it work is that channel and floodplain share one water surface elevation. THE COST IS NOT THE PHYSICS: `fldhgt` is not generated anywhere in the CaMa tree -- it comes from an external DEM upscaling package -- so adopting this means writing the HAND-CDF preprocessor against the region mesh ourselves. AND HAND DOES NOT EXIST HERE: `build_hydrography.py` computes level/area/volume curves at 128 levels but PER CLOSED BASIN from the priority-flood ordering, which is a lake curve. CaMa's is per routing cell keyed on height above the channel. Different quantity, same word. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 52a
world-d9u4 SETTLED 2026-08-25 and this is the one of the three rows that changes quantity. GW-26's saturated fraction lives at the CLIMATE GRID and there is no native-mesh one; a sub-region hypsometry would have to be invented and GW-6 says it is not there. So this classification splits by support: the RESOLVED classes -- open lake, river and playa water from surface_water.nc, and dry mineral soil from the depth field -- stay per region, and the saturated non-inundated mineral class is unresolved and crosses as a climate-grid AREA share. The mutual exclusivity this row requires is then a constraint stated at two supports rather than one: the resolved classes partition a cell's land area between them and the saturated share is taken out of what they leave. That cost belongs to this row. hydrography/notes/subgrid-water-table.md section 5.
PARTLY BUILT 2026-08-25, AND WHAT IS LEFT IS BLOCKED RATHER THAN UNDONE. hydrography/scripts/build_wetness.py, config in hydrography/config/wetness.yaml, pipeline row wetness, README section, artifacts hydrography/data/{build}/wetness_exoplasim-{res}.nc and hydrography/analysis/wetness_report.json.

WHAT IS THERE. One class per land region -- solved open water, the exposed floor of a closed depression, dry mineral soil -- and per grid cell the AREA share of each over the cell's land, through lib/gridding.py's CATEGORICAL cell_fraction and never a majority label. Exclusivity is ENFORCED, not assumed: a region two classes claim is refused, land no class claims is refused unless a residual is named, and the shares must partition the cell or nothing is written. --selftest hands every rule a case built to violate it and all are caught, including the double count this row is about -- the saturated share ADDED beside the resolved classes instead of taken out of them -- and the negative control, a small lake surviving a cell that is almost all upland.

THE PLAYA RULE HAS AN IDENTITY BEHIND IT rather than an argument. A region is playa when its depression-filled surface is at or below its basin's spill and the solved lake does not cover it; the land that rule selects totals the same area basins.nc carries as area_at_spill_km2 from its own hypsometry, and on the active build the two agree exactly. That matters because the endorheic CATCHMENT is 81% of this world's land and the depression footprint is 21% of it, so the catchment version of the rule would have been wrong by a factor of four while still returning a plausible fraction. A fixture for that mistake is in --selftest.

WHAT IS BLOCKED, EACH WITH A ROW. saturated_mineral: f_sat is scored and NOT licensed (world-n9sd), and water_table.nc does not exist on the active build; the two-support rule is written and fixture-tested as take_saturated_out() and main() refuses by name rather than quietly if it is ever reached with a license -- world-71fe. seasonal_inundation and peat: nothing in this pipeline carries a season, and which component owns a seasonally varying inundated AREA is a decision this component cannot take -- world-la19. river_water: surface_water.nc carries a discharge and no channel width, so a river AREA cannot be formed from it; discharge stays a rank and a mask. Each of the four is declared absent IN THE ARTIFACT with its reason, which is the fail-closed state.

NOT DONE HERE AND NOT THIS ROW'S: declaring the classification in biosphere/config/wetlands.yaml's extent block, which is what wetland_gate.py reads and refuses on. That is WET-1's contract.

title: Separate methane production and oxidation from the fork's globally tuned respiration ratios
description:
Separate methane production and oxidation from the fork's globally tuned respiration ratios: consume vertically resolved substrate, temperature, saturation/redox and electron-acceptor state from SDEC-3/SDEC-8, preserve the existing carbon subtraction/checks, expose production and oxidation independently, and retain the detailed 0.085 and simple 0.027 ratio models only as named Earth structural bounds rather than latitude regimes

notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; reduced operator and conservation fixtures follow WET-4/SDEC-3/SDEC-8; parameter-response experiments require accepted hydrology/vegetation and explicit permission [step: soil, groundwater, lpj_run]. WET-12 names the reduced form, a constant anaerobic respiration fraction, and records that it forfeits exactly what this row exists to expose: production and oxidation cease to be separable. SUBSTRATE AND REDOX HAVE A MECHANISTIC REFERENCE FORM, 2026-08-22. ClimaLand implements DAMM, Davidson et al. (2012), in `Soil/Biogeochemistry/co2_parameterizations.jl`: respiration is `Vmax(T) * MM_sx * MM_o2` with substrate `Sx = p_sx*Csom*D_liq*theta_l**3` and oxygen availability `D_oa*O2_f*theta_a**(4/3)` on Millington-Quirk tortuosity, each entering through its own Michaelis-Menten factor. That gives limitation at BOTH ends of the moisture range from two separate mechanisms, against this fork's single empirical humped curve plus a categorical override. It is the shape this row's vertically-resolved substrate/saturation/redox consumption would take. Its Arrhenius term is written in centered form so the reference rate and the temperature sensitivity are near-orthogonal under calibration, which is worth copying. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 34a SCOPE LIMITS ON DAMM, from the paper rather than the port: it is a RESPIRATION KERNEL for soluble substrates, offered by its authors as a core module informed by other modules for microbial dynamics and substrate supply, so it replaces CENTURY's temperature and moisture response functions and NOT its pool structure; and it was evaluated on lab enzyme assays plus one trenched plot at Harvard Forest, so the FORM transfers and the coefficients are an Earth site calibration. `references/davidson2012-damm-dual-arrhenius-michaelis-menten.pdf`. A SECOND MODEL WITH THE SAME DEFECT, AND A PUBLISHED BRACKET, 2026-08-22. CLIMBER-X emits land methane as a fraction of soil respiration, and `nml/lnd_par.nml:236-238` sets `ch4_frac_wet = 0.082` and `ch4_frac_peat = 0.082` -- ONE TUNED NUMBER FOR TWO RESERVOIRS -- with its own comments recording that it sits OUTSIDE the cited published range for BOTH: above Spahni 2011's wetland 0.024-0.0415 and below Spahni's peat 0.2-0.25, against Riley 2011's 0.2 for wetlands. The published values put peat and wetland fractions five to ten times apart and this model collapses them. That raises this row's evidence for globally-tuned ratios from one model to two, and supplies a STARTING BRACKET that is published rather than invented. Its peat path does carry the oxic/anoxic split the wetland path lacks, `f_oxic_peat = w_table_peat/acro_h`. Temperature modulation is `q10_ch4 = 1.8` referenced to 295 K, another Earth anchor. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 42c

title: Perform a conservative non-N/P nutrient-adequacy screen for K, S, Ca, Mg
description:
Perform a conservative non-N/P nutrient-adequacy screen for K, S, Ca, Mg, Fe and biologically important trace elements using parent stocks, atmospheric/geologic delivery, loss and plausible plant demand; declare the terrestrial CNP model boundary and fail-closed co-limitation brackets instead of assuming that C-N-P limitation proves general nutrient sufficiency

Source: `biosphere/notes/abiotic-nutrient-delivery-audit.md` finding 8
notes:
SCREEN PERFORMED; ONE HALF REMAINS AND NEEDS AN EXECUTION WINDOW.

Done, in biosphere/config/abiotic_nutrients.yaml and biosphere/notes/abiotic-nutrient-ledger.md:

- The bound, its direction and the verdict rule were fixed before any result was seen. T_acc(X) = Q_high(X) / F_low(X); ADEQUATE if T_acc <= one soil residence time; NOT SETTLED otherwise, which is a bracket and never a verdict of inadequate; NOT ADEQUATE only if the optimistic supply is below the pessimistic pool.
- It does NOT compare supply against gross uptake. In steady state most of gross uptake is met by litter return, so that version fails for every element including ones Earth plainly has enough of; running it first gave a critical runoff near 100 m/yr, and a threshold nothing can pass is not a screen.
- Q_high is an upper bound from Vitousek and Sanford (1986) Table 2 maxima, with sulfur from the same table's maximum biomass at CENTURY's minimum plant C:S of 190 (Parton, Stewart and Cole 1988). F_low is a lower bound: Meybeck (1987) Table 2C per-lithology dissolved release, with marine aerosol, dust, ash and recycling all set to zero. Residence time is root-zone depth over Portenga and Bierman (2011) denudation, 5.0e4 to 1.15e5 Earth yr, run at the SHORT and stricter end.
- One input is a bracket, not a bound, and it is reported: the above-ground to whole-pool multiplier, 1 to 5, because pedology emits no CEC field. Filed as world-hsmd. The screen runs on the upper end.
- Output is a critical runoff in mm per Earth year per element per lithology. POTASSIUM BINDS: 36.8 on sandstone to 193.1 on peridotite, against 0.3 to 49.9 for calcium and 0.1 to 14.1 for magnesium. Sulfur is easy except on volcanic rock at 83.7.
- Fe REFUSES: not in Meybeck's major-ion set, supply is particulate and reductive, no artifact carries an iron phase. The trace set REFUSES: Gaillardet, Viers and Dupre (2014) is where a per-lithology trace-element table would live and its own conclusion is that no such world-scale table exists. A refusal is a result and is kept apart from adequacy.
- The CNP model boundary is declared: any LPJ-GUESS result here is a C-N-P result and not a nutrient-limitation result.

REMAINING, and why it is not done: the land fraction below the potassium threshold. It needs the runoff field, and this wave was not permitted to run anything that reads the export payload and a climatology. The bracket reported instead is 0 to 29.9% of land, from the registered land-structure table's 14.2% hyper-arid plus 15.7% semi-arid and the fact that runoff never exceeds precipitation.

The command that would settle it: evaluate the critical-runoff table in biosphere/generated/abiotic_nutrient_ledger_report.json per mesh region, taking local runoff from pedology/scripts/solute_routing.py:region_runoff_m3_yr -- P minus E clamped at zero, NOT the model mrro, which is river-routed net divergence and understates land runoff by 6.6x -- the lithology from the export, and the join to the climate from lib/gridding.py:climatology_cells and nothing else. Minutes, read-only, needs an available compute window.

description:

notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; the scientific derivation is independent of an LPJ run and should precede adoption of modelled albedo [step: vegetation_albedo, surface_albedo]. AND THE LEAF-TO-CANOPY BOUND UNDER IT IS NOT ONE-SIGNED, 2026-08-22. `analysis/vegetation_albedo.py:33-35` asserts without argument that "a canopy treatment would give a smaller ratio than a leaf one", and the bracket runs from no correction to the leaf ratio on that basis. CANOPY ALBEDO DEPENDS ON THE SINGLE-SCATTERING ALBEDO `alpha + tau`, NOT ON REFLECTANCE ALONE: a leaf transmitting strongly in the near-infrared raises omega_NIR without raising omega_PAR, so the canopy keeps more of its NIR albedo relative to PAR than the leaf does, and since a K dwarf moves flux INTO the near-infrared that AMPLIFIES the correction rather than diluting it. ClimaLand's `pfts.jl` carries the missing column, CLM5.0 Table 2.3.1 giving `tau_NIR/alpha_NIR` of 0.286 needleleaf, 0.556 broadleaf tree and 0.971 GRASS. Running this project's own band pair through the semi-infinite similarity result gives canopy k25v/sun ratios of 1.1379, 1.1848 and 1.2226 against the leaf-level 1.1501 -- SO THE STATED BOUND HOLDS FOR ONE OF THREE CLASSES AND FAILS FOR THE OTHER TWO, grass included, which is where this project's per-class table already shows the largest shift at 0.303 to 0.333. THIS DOES NOT GIVE A CANOPY RATIO and must not be used as one: the similarity result carries no leaf angle distribution, no clumping, no soil background, no finite LAI and no direct/diffuse split, and the transmittances are an Earth calibration. It establishes only that the SIGN is not determined by leaf reflectance alone, so the bracket's upper end may not be an upper end. Settling it needs leaf TRANSMITTANCE, which a reflectance library does not carry -- a data gap rather than a derivation gap. THE CLASS DEPENDENCE RUNS ALONG THIS ROW'S OWN TREE/GRASS SPLIT, which makes the separate endmembers more necessary than the row currently argues. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 38

Integrating `k25v_hr.dat` against a 5772 K Planck: over 400-700 nm the solar value is 4.567e-6 mol/J, which REPRODUCES the shipped 4.6e-6 and validates the integral before anything is read off the rest; over the declared 400-750 nm window it is 4.743e-6 on the Sun and 4.864e-6 on this star. title: Give the canopy snow mask a prognostic canopy snow store with interception and unloading
description:
snowmaskmod distinguishes intercepted canopy snow from ground snow: the interception weight moves the forested snow endmember toward the caller's exposed-snow endmember, so a fully loaded canopy gives the albedo of open snow whatever its cover. What it does NOT do is predict that weight. forint is a declared standing fraction, so interception and unloading are not represented and the seasonal course of canopy snow is absent.

Predicting it needs a canopy snow store with a mass balance: snowfall intercepted up to a capacity that scales with plant area, unloaded by wind and by melt, and taken out of the throughfall that reaches the ground snowpack. That is a new prognostic reservoir, so it changes the surface water balance, needs restart records that exoplasim/scripts/restart_schema.py must cover, and cannot be inert.

Note also that the weight is an EFFECTIVE optical fraction and not a geometric one: canopy snow is patchier and more shaded than the snowpack, so the fraction that brightens the canopy like open snow is smaller than the fraction of the canopy holding snow. A store predicts the geometric fraction, so the conversion between them has to be stated when it lands.

Do: only after BIO-33 has activated the structural axes, and with explicit permission, since it moves the surface energy and water balance of every snow-covered forested cell.

title: Drive the canopy snow mask from reported canopy height and plant area, per gridcell
description:
BIO-30 built the canopy/snow mask operator, snowmaskmod, and left every structural axis inert at values that return the one-scalar mask bit for bit. forhgt, forpai and forint in landmod's namelist are the axes, and they are scalars standing in for fields.

Do:
1. Emit a per-gridcell canopy height and plant (or stem) area index from the vegetation component, alongside the tree cover that already arrives as surface code 212, and state which convention the index is in: landmod's extinction default of one is the coefficient Essery (2013) reports with the index counting leaves and stems, while a leaf-angle-resolved index wants about a half and twice the index for the same masking.
2. Carry them into landmod as fields, with the namelist scalars as the fallback for a cell no field covers, and pass them per cell to snowcanopymask instead of the scalars.
3. Only then activate them, which needs accepted vegetation (BIO-17) and explicit permission: it moves the surface energy balance of every snow-covered forested cell, so every climatology downstream of the change is worthless in rule 7's sense rather than stale.

The check that must keep passing throughout is exoplasim/scripts/verify_snow_mask.sh, whose reduction arm is bitwise: with the fields absent the operator must still return the canopy cover itself.

Reading upstream's two masking fractions back through the same gap-fraction law puts them at plant area indices of about 0.96 and 0.51 at an extinction coefficient of one. A closed forest carries more, so activation is expected to mask MORE snow in forested cells, not less.

2026-08-24, branch fanout-Z. THE PFRAC_LEAFTOSAP HALF IS SETTLED AS FAR AS IT CAN BE: the constant CANNOT BE DERIVED, and the refutation now rests on two READ papers instead of one summary. (1) WHAT 6.9 IS. Friend, Stevens, Knox and Cannell (1997) Table 4 p. 254 gives X_C:N(f/p) = 0.145, the relative C:N ratio between foliage and BARK PLUS SAPWOOD, in kgC/kgN per kgC/kgN; its reciprocal is 6.897. The companion X_C:N(f/r) = 0.86 inverts to 1.163, which is PFRAC_LEAFTOROOT. Text p. 274 gives the fit: a mean across NINE species from Turner (1980) and Turner and Lambert (1981), Eucalyptus spp. and planted Douglas-fir, with a 13 percent bark weighting; the root figure is Pinus radiata SEEDLINGS from Nambiar and Fife (1991); both applied to every plant type, in Eqs. 42-44, to hold relative TISSUE C:N fixed during annual nitrogen reallocation. THE PAPER HAS NO PHOSPHORUS IN IT: the word occurs once, in a reference title. So 6.9 is nitrogen, for a tissue that includes bark, off nine temperate species. (2) THE EXPONENT CLAIM IS RIGHT AND IT IS THE PAPER'S OWN. Heineman Table 3, type II major axis, n = 58: P 2.10 (95% CI 1.52-3.17) and 2.22 (1.85-2.67) on phylogenetic contrasts; N 1.25 (0.83-1.95) and 1.01 (0.84-1.23). The paper writes 'significantly > 1' for Ca, K, Mg and P and calls N isometric, which is the internal control that makes the P result mean something. THREE CORRECTIONS the summary did not carry, now in references/INDEX.md: Table 3's caption prints the model backwards as log(leaf) ~ log(a) + log(wood) x b, and since MA regression is reciprocal-symmetric that inverts the exponent to 0.48 rather than relabelling it (the intercepts settle the direction: at the Table 2 wood means the fitted lines give leaf P 1117 ug/g and leaf N 1.90 percent one way, and leaf P 0.87 ug/g the other); the wood is the OUTER 5 cm annulus, not whole sapwood, with a 35 percent radial P decline behind it; the leaves are SHADE leaves, defended only on rank order. SCOPE: one regional gradient, 58 paired species all lower montane at Fortuna, western Panama, 700-1500 m, three volcanic substrates, no needleleaf, temperate or boreal type in the sample. It licenses rejecting the proportional form for P with N as its control; it licenses no global exponent, no whole-sapwood level, no sun-leaf level, and no scalar of any value. A forced scalar is BRACKETED 10.1 to 15.5, the ends being the outer-annulus sample-mean proportion and that mean corrected for the 35 percent radial decline; RECORDED AND NOT ADOPTED. THIS ROW REMAINS OPEN ON A MODELLING DECISION ONLY THE USER CAN MAKE: proportional or power form for simulated sapwood C:P; endpoint or tissue mean; and what anchors the level, given one Panamanian gradient. (1) PCONC_SAT IS SETTLED AND SPLIT OUT AS DONE, under WORLD-PIDX: the measurement that row was waiting for exists (Mooshammer et al. 2014, held and read), a decomposer community's biomass C:P is homeostatic with respect to its resource's phosphorus content, and the ramp and its threshold are REMOVED. Rep. 6:20099, fetched and read: the same RMA regression of woody stem on leaf concentration for 335 woody species in 198 genera at 12 forest sites across eastern China, 18.7 to 50.9 N and -5.7 to 25.3 C MAT. The phosphorus exponent is 1.58 tropical, 0.97 temperate, 0.80 boreal; 1.36 at 23.2 N down to 0.71 at 50.9 N; 1.26 / 0.96 / 0.70 for evergreen broadleaf / deciduous broadleaf / conifer; 1.86 legume against 0.88 non-legume. It correlates with MAT and not with precipitation or soil total N or P. THE EXPONENT CROSSES 1 INSIDE THE CLIMATE RANGE A GLOBAL MODEL SPANS, so Heineman's 2.10 is that gradient's tropical extreme rather than a universal rejection of isometry. The internal control holds: Yan's nitrogen exponents run the same way and less steeply, 1.30 / 0.97 / 0.89 by biome. A proportional form is therefore the unbiased default over the whole range, with a residual that is one-signed within a biome and changes sign between them -- at a fixed scalar the model under-supplies the simulated tropical types' sapwood P demand relative to leaf and over-supplies the boreal ones'. (3) WHAT REMAINS IS THE LEVEL, and the number on it is a factor of twenty BETWEEN TISSUES, not between elements. Yan's leaf P over twig stem P, read off Fig. 4a against its own axis, is 0.77 at 18.7 N to 2.63 at 50.9 N; Heineman's outer 5 cm bole annulus brackets a forced scalar at 10.1 to 15.5; Friend's nitrogen bark-plus-sapwood figure is 6.9 where Yan's nitrogen twig ratio is 1.8 to 3.0. This model's sapwood pool is the whole living sapwood of the simulated individual, mass-dominated by bole and large branches rather than terminal twigs, so its value belongs at the bole end -- where the phosphorus bracket sits and where the applied 6.9 does not. Adopting 10.1 to 15.5 would import one Panamanian lower montane site's climate into every simulated plant type, and Yan's 3.4-fold latitudinal span of the same ratio is the measure of what that costs. THE VALUE IS NOT CHANGED and the refusal STAYS, with its wording corrected in guess.h and parameters.cpp: it no longer claims the form is rejected. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is not a decision anyone can make from what is here: paired leaf and WHOLE-SAPWOOD phosphorus concentrations over more than one region. Not in the accessible literature. title: The CNP fork has no terminal phosphorus occlusion at all
description:
The CNP fork has no terminal phosphorus occlusion at all, so the P cycle has no ultimate sink. `UOCC` is declared and never used anywhere; `Soil::pmass_occluded` is initialised to zero, serialised, and never assigned; and `guess.cpp:616` has the occluded pool commented out of the P conservation sum, which is harmless only because the pool is always zero. Decide whether Vesper's phosphorus cycle closes with an occlusion loss or declares its absence, and note that Wang et al. (2010) deliberately omits the flux, saying it would add computation with little impact at decade to century scales

Source: BIO-33, `references/wang2010-cnp-terrestrial-biosphere.pdf` section 2.3, `vendor/lpj-guess/framework/guess.cpp:616`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and ASK WHETHER IT SHOULD EXIST BEFORE BUILDING IT: the omission is the cited source's own choice and is defensible at the timescales a run covers, so the deliverable may be a declared gap rather than a flux. What is NOT defensible is the current state, where a dead constant and a commented-out conservation term make an absent process look like a slow one. Either way `UOCC` goes or gets used [step: lpj_run]
DECIDED AND LANDED 2026-08-24 on branch fanout-T, and the premise was half wrong. Soil::pmass_strongly_sorbed was ALSO never assigned anywhere in the tree, so Wang et al. (2010) Eq. D10's back term vanished and that line was not a transfer between two pools: it was an unstoppable first-order drain of the sorbed pool at USORB, 0.52 to 0.97 gP/m2 per Earth year against Spmax of 77 to 145, booked as an ecosystem P loss, against a default weathering supply of 0.003 gP/m2 per Earth year. So the P cycle did have a terminal sink; it was mis-plumbed and unbounded. It hid because Patch::pcont excluded the destination pool, which balanced the books, and because MassBalance::check_patch_P is declared in guess.h and called from nowhere in this tree. The pool is assigned now, the transfer is internal and no longer reported as a loss, and pcont counts it. OCCLUSION IS A DECLARED ABSENCE: UOCC is deleted, it had no citation anywhere in the tree, occluded P is terminal so an unbracketed rate would set this world's long-run soil P stock, and equilsom's 40000-model-year solve does not save and restore the sorbed pools the way it does pmass_labile, so a terminal sink inside it would drain every cell over a span the run does not represent. pcont counts pmass_occluded anyway so that adding a flux later is a change to one file. The argument is in biosphere/notes/phosphorus-cycle-parameterisation.md. Nothing is compiled. Commit efb0756f.
close_reason: Occlusion declared absent with its argument, UOCC deleted, and the real defect at those lines fixed: the strongly sorbed pool was never assigned, making the sorption flux an unbounded drain rather than the transfer Wang et al. (2010) Eq. D10 describes. Commit efb0756f.

title: Record in docs/src/pipeline/loops.md that the biosphere reaches the climate through albedo
description:
Record in `docs/src/pipeline/loops.md` that the biosphere reaches the climate through albedo, roughness and forest fraction only, and not through transpiration

Source: `notes/audits/missed-couplings.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-17, and VERIFIED in the vendored ExoPlaSim 3.4.2 source rather than asserted. Land evaporation is `mkevap`, and its whole dependence on the land surface is `zkdiff = drhs * zkonst1 * dtransh / dt` at `fluxmod.f90:658`: `dtransh` carries roughness, so that channel is real, and `drhs` at `NVEG = 0` is one bucket, `min(1, dwatc/(0.4*dwmax))`, with the five `dsoilz` layers holding temperature rather than water. No root, canopy, interception or stomatal term exists in `landmod.f90`, `fluxmod.f90` or `surfmod.f90`. Two refinements to the claim as written. Forest fraction is NARROWER than it sounded: at `NVEG = 0` it only mixes the snow albedo's forested and unforested endpoints, so it is radiative and reaches evaporation not at all. And there is a FOURTH channel one step removed, `dwmax` from pedology carrying LPJ-GUESS soil carbon, already bounded near-inert at 1.06x on runoff for a 3.75-fold bucket change, so the word "only" needed it. The finding worth more than the task: switching SIMBA on would NOT supply the missing physics. It does couple back at `nveg == 2`, but `dsc`, its "stomatal conductance", is prescribed -- allocated to `rinidsc` at `simba.f90:157`, optionally read as surface code 1606, and never assigned again -- and `dlai` is computed and used nowhere but output. So the absence is a property of the model, not of this project's configuration
close_reason: done 2026-08-17, and VERIFIED in the vendored ExoPlaSim 3.4.2 source rather than asserted.

THE SLOPE IS 202 K per unit flux ratio, 34% above the 150.2 it replaces, corroborated at 201.3 to 203.4 by four further estimates across two terrains. THE DENOMINATOR WAS THE SECOND ERROR AND COMPOUNDED THE FIRST: a top-of-atmosphere forcing is an absorbed-flux change, so the divisor is `S/4 * (1 - alpha)` = 242.8 W/m2 rather than the incident 321.54, giving 0.832 K per W/m2 against 0.467 in use. The claimed 3.4x gap between the local slope and the stellar sweep's sensitivity was 1.9x once the local conversion was right, so most of it was arithmetic rather than the ice transition -- though the sweep is still the wrong sensitivity to use at the baseline. And the ORDERING moved: nothing reorders inside the albedo column, where a slope is a uniform multiplier, but the W/m2 items that previously sat under "no conversion invented" now have kelvin, and shortwave-only in-model dust lands SECOND in the whole budget at 3.3 to 3.6 K. A REUSABLE SHAPE FOR THE OXIDANT BRACKET, AND ITS LIMIT, 2026-08-22. CLIMBER-X has NO atmospheric chemistry, but `src/ch4/ch4_model.f90:179-183` carries a reduced form this row can take the STRUCTURE of: reciprocal lifetimes added over four sinks -- OH, tropospheric chlorine, soil and stratosphere -- with OH represented by a fitted log-linear surrogate in the methane burden plus NOx, CO and VOC emissions and a linear temperature term. IT IS A SURROGATE FOR OH, NOT OH, and its anchors are two independent Earth baselines, 1056 ppb and 286.83 K. Take the reciprocal-addition shape and the sink decomposition; re-fit or bracket every coefficient. NOTE WHAT IT DOES NOT SUPPLY: the VOC term is a prescribed anthropogenic emission series read from file, so this gives a consumption interface and no producer, and ozone there is a prescribed radiative boundary condition that is never an oxidant. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 42a. A SECOND REUSABLE FORM, BETTER CONDITIONED, AND ONE FAMILY TO REFUSE, 2026-08-22. cGENIE's `genie-atchem` has six CH4 sink schemes and NONE is photolysis -- one well-mixed box, no OH, the source saying "omitting [OH], [NOx] etc etc". TAKE THE POWER LAWS IN PARTIAL PRESSURE: `tau = tau0*(pCH4/C0)**N`, with `schmidt03` the better-conditioned variant, namelist-settable and calibrated over 1x to 200x C0 against the default's 8x. REFUSE THE POLYNOMIAL EMULATORS: `claire06` and `goldblatt06` fit photochemical output as polynomials in log10 of ABSOLUTE MOLE INVENTORIES in Tmol, not mixing ratios, which anchors them to Earth's atmospheric mass -- 1.088x here per section 42b -- and the source itself warns "neither O2 nor CH4 are truncated at edge of training values here, so USE CAUTION". A TRAP EVEN IF ADOPTING THE DEFAULT: `par_atm_CH4_photochem` defaults to a scheme that reads only compile-time constants, so the three namelist `par_pCH4_oxidation_*` values are SILENTLY IGNORED unless the scheme string is also changed, while the run log prints them as though in force. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 46a. AND A THIRD MODEL, THIS ONE WITH ACTUAL CHEMISTRY, 2026-08-22. Where cGENIE and CLIMBER-X offer parametric lifetimes to take the SHAPE of, CAABA/MECCA offers 2,323 gas-phase reactions of which 414 are photolysis, with OH, O1D and the quenching competition explicit. That makes it the instrument for deriving this row's oxidant bracket rather than another source to fit one from. Its photolysis door and the gravity correction it needs are in `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 48
2026-08-24, the interface and the refusal landed; the bracket did not, because deriving it needs a chemistry model run and this host is not to run one. WHAT EXISTS NOW. biosphere/notes/bvoc-activation-contract.md section 4 states the contract: no central SOA yield is declared, a fixed mass yield is a screening bound that is labelled as one, and the bracket must carry a required signature (driven by this star's ultraviolet, the modelled ozone column, water vapour, temperature and the adopted soil/fire nitrogen-oxide sources; returning precursor loss AND the changes to ozone, oxidizing capacity, carbon monoxide and methane lifetime), a named instrument, and two ends that differ. biosphere/config/bvoc.yaml carries oxidants.interface, oxidants.instrument and oxidants.bracket as undeclared sentinels.

THE INCONSISTENCY IS NOW EXPOSED MECHANICALLY rather than described. biosphere/scripts/bvoc_gate.py refuses activation as BVOC-TRACE-GAS-STATE-NOT-CLOSED whenever config/planet.yaml still prescribes pCH4_bar or ozone and oxidants.trace_gas_state_closed is false, naming the keys it found. That flag is BVOC-6's and WET-10's to set and nobody else's. This was the half of the row that could be finished without a run, and it is the half that would otherwise never announce itself: nothing crashes when a biosphere-derived flux is combined with a fixed-Earth-flux oxidant state.

REMAINING, and it is a run: derive both bracket ends with the acquired tropospheric gas-phase box model at references/caaba-mecca/ (notes/external-source-inventory.md records it read and acquired, release 4.6.0), under this star's photolysis and with the gravity correction that tree needs. That is a compile and a run and requires explicit permission. The parametric forms surveyed elsewhere supply a SHAPE only and every coefficient in them is Earth-fitted; the polynomial-emulator family fitted in absolute mole inventories is refused outright because it is anchored to Earth atmospheric mass.

CITATION DRIFT FOUND: this row's earlier notes cite notes/external-model-survey.md sections 42a, 46a and 48. That file's body stops at section 11g while its own index table lists sections into the fifties, so none of those three citations resolves. The CLIMBER-X partitioned-lifetime methane box IS in the file, findable by content near the ch4_model.f90 paragraph. Filed nothing for the survey itself; see the batch report.

notes:

Three were the instrument. `align` floored `nrec // nbin` when the year is not a whole number of write intervals, worth 13.102 to 0.353. It then used EQUAL-WIDTH bins where pyburn's hold different record counts, 0.353 to 0.191. The fourth was the DATA. The model writes one record per 24.00 h and this planet's day is 30.00 h, exactly 40 timesteps against 32, so the regular output samples the diurnal cycle at FIVE PHASES forever while the ocean and ice streams accumulate every step and are a true integral. Predicted before the run: raise the sampling and the bias collapses. At NWPD = 8, ten phases and 1462 raw records an orbit against 182, D1 goes +0.0534 to +0.0079 -- a factor of 6.8 against the 2.8 that random noise would give, which is aliasing rather than variance. So the atmosphere and the streams agree to 0.008 W/m2 and the model's surface energy budget closes. D2 through D5 were at machine zero throughout. Found on the way and guarded: the streams follow their own counters and ignore NWPD, so the two sides only share a clock at NWPD = 1 and the closure now refuses any other case rather than tiling bins it does not share a clock with [step: bootstrap_convergence, baseline_convergence]

Three defects in the `NLOWIO = 1` path, and the counter was NOT the cause. `plasim.f90:857` and `:1086` save six SPECTRAL accumulators through `mpputgp`/`mpgetgp`, whose dummy is declared `pp(NHOR,klev)`; Fortran reinterprets the `(NESP,NLEV)` array and moves 5,120 of 19,040 elements at T42/L10/p16, so levels 4-10 are restored as ZERO while `naccuout` survives intact at 90 and the first write of each call divides 159 samples by 249. `outmod.f90:394` then subtracts the whole `plavor` from an accumulator holding only 0.638554 of it, leaving `-(1-delta)*plavor` in the (n=1,m=0) vorticity mode -- solid-body rotation, a retrograde 160.8*cos(phi) m/s on levels 4-10. That is the entire wind signature, and it explains every part of it: `ua` only because plavor lives in vorticity, worsening downward because the spurious wind is level-independent while the real one falls, and temperature escaping because `aast` holds the deviation from `t0`. Humidity is separate: `sqout` is recomputed only at output steps but summed every step and is not in the restart, and since 5850 mod 160 = 90 its phase walks with a 16-orbit period, measured at 0.946 correlation over 90 orbits. PREDICTIONS STATED BEFORE MEASURING, which is what makes this a mechanism rather than a story: the surviving coefficients must show no anomaly and the truncated ones must all show the same one, giving delta = 159/249 to six figures with a relative residual of 3e-7; a 6018-step run must give a DIFFERENT constant, predicted -0.127108 and measured -0.127108; orbit 0 of every run must be clean, and it is; and the wind anomaly must be a level-independent `cos(phi)` solid body of -53.59 m/s with nothing fitted, measured -53.44 to -53.56 on levels 3-9. The trap named in the task, `naccuout` persisting while the accumulators do not, was ELIMINATED with evidence: it is restored correctly, and the gridpoint accumulators share the same counter and are clean

title: Every NLOWIO = 0 field written by a binary WITHOUT the nlowio broadcast is part instantaneous
description:

The signature is exact -- for code 139 the only matching latitude rows are 0 to 3, which is `NLAT/NPRO = 4`, which is NROOT's slice, NROOT being the one rank that reads the namelist. 60 of 64 rows, 93.75% of the grid, carried interval means where instantaneous samples were intended, the exact opposite of the point of `NLOWIO = 0`. Worst: surface temperature 139 by 14.93 K, cloud cover 162 by 0.99, albedo 174/175 by 0.57 and 0.46. THE TWO CONSUMERS THAT COULD HAVE BEEN HURT ARE BOTH CLEAR, checked structurally and on the same output: CLIM-1 because `outdiag` has no `nlowio` branch and `naccuout` is incremented outside the guard, so all 28 energy terms, all 28 3D terms and every comparand are byte-identical, with `aprl` 142 as the independent check; DUST-5 because 131/132/259 are derived from vorticity 138 and divergence 155, neither of which differs, and the gust fit reads the high-cadence stream, whose writer never mentions `nlowio`. Affected codes are surface state, cloud, albedo, roughness and entropy: 139, 140, 141, 159, 161, 162, 170, 173, 174, 175, 183, 184, 207-211, 265, 267-269, 298, 322-324, 327. title: pyburn's reader was QUADRATIC in record count
description:
pyburn's reader was QUADRATIC in record count: `readallvariables` grew every variable with `variables[kcode] = np.append(variables[kcode],field)` once per record, and np.append reallocates and copies the whole accumulated array each call

Source: `notes/audits/pyburn-postprocessing-cost.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18. Records are collected per code and joined once with np.concatenate; `readvariablecode` had the same pattern and is fixed with it. One T42 orbit at `NLOWIO = 0`, 2.4 GB raw, driven with the exact kwargs `Model.run()` forwards and unprofiled both ways: 304.0 s to 29.4 s, 10.3x, np.append calls 3,062,749 to 1, and all 123 output variables BITWISE IDENTICAL. It reproduces the pipeline's own history -- `continue_exoplasim.py` records 387 s an orbit and this bench gives 81 s model + 304 s pyburn = 385 s; the same orbit is now 110 s. The triple loops over (time, lat, lon) in the omega/wa/streamfunction branches were vectorised in the same patch and are the smaller half. THE DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG TWICE AND THAT IS THE DURABLE PART: cProfile charged 246 s to 6.0e6 tiny np.append calls in the loops, which is what a profiler costs for six million call events rather than what numpy spends, and the same 246 s actually belonged to the ~81k LARGE appends in the reader -- one function, two callers, call counts three orders of magnitude apart and opposite per-call costs. The ratio was the tell, not the tottime column. Separately, a claim that `example.nl`'s 216 duplicated codes were being processed was an artefact of the measuring harness: pyburn ignores `variables` when a `namelist` is passed, and the pipeline passes none. Consequences: the `NLOWIO = 0` penalty in `continue_exoplasim.py` is much smaller, and the 1.09x for two concurrent 8-rank runs was a workaround for this defect -- run at 16 ranks [step: rebuild_binaries, climatology]

title: Price the interior moisture source: the water a catchment delivers to a closed basin
description:
Price the interior moisture source: the water a catchment delivers to a closed basin evaporates over land in the world `hydrography/` describes and is exported to the ocean in the model, which has no lake, so the moisture source moves off the continent. It is 5.6 to 6.6% of land precipitation, sited in the arid interiors, on a planet whose land is 76.2% endorheic

Source: `notes/audits/unpriced-terms.md` finding 1, `exoplasim/notes/lake-representation.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-19, and the measurement DEFLATED it and flipped its sign. `carve_verdict.py` now computes the area-weighted integral every run into `runoff_source.endorheic_inflow`, with an identity that closes to 0.00% -- inflow equals lake net evaporation plus the runoff generated over the lake bed plus what spills to the ocean, those being the only doors out of the endorheic system. Endorheic catchments deliver 69% of land runoff off 76% of the land, credible where the 97% that prompted this was not, and the cause was multiplying an UNWEIGHTED per-basin mean by the total catchment area rather than the clamp, which is worth 4.2%. The substantive correction is that gross lake evaporation is the wrong quantity: what the atmosphere gains from a lake is its evaporation against what the model already evaporates on that ground, and this world's land is several times rougher than open water, so the model's own evaporation exceeds Penman on 2,484 of 4,105 land cells. The term is -2,374 km3/Earth-yr, -0.9% of land precipitation, and NEGATIVE, so the intuitive direction was wrong as well as the size. The estimator uses catchment means rather than lake-footprint values and is biased against the lake; it would have to be wrong by a factor of six to reach what was first claimed. Not a dust-scale item
close_reason: done 2026-08-19, and the measurement DEFLATED it and flipped its sign.

title: Mineral dust is the only aerosol this project has ever considered. No sea salt over an ocean
description:
Mineral dust is the only aerosol this project has ever considered. No sea salt over an ocean that is 57% of the surface, no volcanic sulfate beside the arc classes the pedology treats as continuing, and no mention of either anywhere in the repository

notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-19, and the answer is that sea salt is the SAME SIZE as mineral dust and the OPPOSITE SIGN: -0.16 to -0.89 W/m2 of global-mean top-of-atmosphere shortwave forcing across every declared bracket end, against dust's +0.34 to +0.61, and `analysis/error_budget.json` now carries both. Built as a component rather than an estimate: `aeolian/scripts/sea_salt_source.py` (Grythe et al. 2014 eq. 7), `sea_salt_optics.py` (OPAC indices and growth at ambient humidity, Mie on the k25v spectrum) and `build_sea_salt.py` (emission, transport, burden, optical depth, forcing), registered as steps `sea_salt_optics` and `sea_salt`. The EARTH CHECK is a ratio between two published source functions through one machinery, so our wind treatment divides out: Monahan 1986 and G13T come out at 0.705 and 0.680 of Grythe's Table 2 values and those agree to 3.5%. Three optics checks pass, including inverting OPAC's volume mixing to recover water's refractive index at 1.3328 against 1.333. Two results are reported and neither corrects the other, because Grythe's 30 um spume mode's lower tail dominates the mass below the 10 um cut and their own reported production excludes it. COST was correctly estimated as a model change for putting it IN the climate, and that half is not done: the fork refuses two aerosol paths at once on purpose. Two defects found on the way are recorded in the audit -- `hur` is in percent while its units attribute says otherwise, and the shared transport solver is in advective rather than flux form. CLIM-28 carries what is left

description:
Sulfate and volcanic aerosol are still untouched, and the arc classes are the one place this pipeline treats volcanism as continuing. Sea salt turned out to be the same size as mineral dust and the opposite sign, so the prior that a second aerosol is negligible is now measured to be wrong once

Source: `notes/audits/unpriced-terms.md` finding 2
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-19. Volcanic sulfate is BUILT and MEASURED SMALL: -0.013 to -0.032 W/m2 across every declared bracket end, one to two orders of magnitude below dust and sea salt, from a global-mean optical depth of 0.0035. `aeolian/scripts/build_volcanic_sulfate.py`, step `volcanic_sulfate`, with OPAC's sulfate tables in `exoplasim/data/sulfate/`. The SOURCE IS A COUPLING rather than a scaling and that is the point: Carn et al. (2017)'s satellite-measured passive volcanic SO2 flux scaled by `weathering_fluxes.py`'s own implied outgassing requirement, 1.10x Earth's, distributed over the arc classes the fork places about the volcanic front; the step refuses to run without the weathering artifact rather than falling back to a literal. The scale-height bracket moves the answer not at all, which confirms settling is irrelevant at 0.1 um and wet removal sets it. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT IS MOSTLY WORTH IS THE BOUND: the sulfate pathway here is weak, so reaching sea salt's forcing would need a sulfur flux over ten times Earth's, and that covers both sulfur sources this project cannot compute -- explosive eruptions, which need the eruption history `docs/src/reference/no-time-axis.md` says does not exist, and marine biogenic sulfur, which is Earth's LARGEST natural sulfur source and has no counterpart here because LPJ-GUESS is terrestrial and this project has no marine biosphere at all. `analysis/error_budget.json` carries the item for that reason rather than for its size. CLIM-29 carries what the bound does not reach
