title: vendored-upstreams.md's reason for building cgenie outside the repo is superseded
description:
docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md says analysis/cgenie_profile.py builds from a git archive export outside the repository 'because a worktree's ignored build products are symlinks into the main checkout and a build in place would write there.'

That reason no longer holds for a worktree linked after 2026-08-31. vendor/cgenie is in scripts/link_worktree.py's SKIP_COMPILED, so its build output is not linked at all and a build in place stays in the worktree. Worktrees standing before that change keep the links they already have, so the sentence is true of them and stale for everything new.

The out-of-tree build may still be the right arrangement on its own merits -- a clean export is a different guarantee from an unlinked directory. Decide which reason the document should give, and rewrite it to that; do not mark the old one.

## Context
notes/audits/worktree-write-through.md
acceptance_criteria: The passage states the reason that is currently true, or the out-of-tree build is justified on the ground that actually holds.

title: Every generator of a linked artifact should refuse at its write door
description:
exoplasim/scripts/sra.py:refuse_a_write_through_a_symlink is the only write door in the tree that refuses a path which is or sits under a symlink. It covers exoplasim/inputs/<rung>/ because write_sra is the single door all four staged-field builders go through. No other writer tests is_symlink.

world-ov4u added a ledger that REPORTS a write-through after it lands. A door PREVENTS it, and the two are complements rather than alternatives: a read-only link cannot be built at all, because a symlink carries no permissions of its own and the only enforceable mode is the target's in the main checkout, which is shared with every other worktree.

notes/audits/worktree-write-through.md enumerates what a worktree can regenerate through a per-file link. Seven groups have no door:

  biosphere/scripts/build_vesper_header.py -> vendor/lpj-guess/framework/vesper.h. The measured case: it invalidated the main checkout's LPJ binary on 2026-08-31.
  the source/<build>/<grid>/ regrid writer. source/ is read-only by rule 7, so a write-through there is a direct violation.
  the exoplasim/analysis/climatology/ writers. Downstream components read these.
  the hydrography/data/<build>/ product writers.
  aeolian/analysis/dust_baseline.nc.
  exoplasim/analysis/ladder and the prerebuild_binaries record.

FIRST DECIDE WHERE THE HELPER LIVES. sra.py's copy is bespoke and lives in exoplasim/scripts/, which nothing outside exoplasim imports. One shared refusal in lib/ that every writer calls is the alternative, and it needs a row in CLAUDE.md's lib/ list. Do not copy the function per component.

## Context
notes/audits/worktree-write-through.md, and world-4o59 which put the first door on write_sra
acceptance_criteria: Each generator named above either refuses a write through a symlink, or carries the argument for why writing through is correct there. One shared implementation, not per-component copies.

title: The orphaned-surface gate names one consumer and the other one is what it cost
description:
scripts/check_consistency.py's 'runs vs the surface fields they staged' arm correctly reports a run whose staged .sra has been regenerated since. Its verdict is 'the file under that code has been regenerated since, so the run is on a surface the tree no longer holds and nothing can be seeded from it'.

SEEDING IS NOT THE ONLY THING THAT BREAKS, and the other one is what actually cost work. An offline calculation that reads that run's climatology against exoplasim/inputs/<rung>/ is pairing a soil water with a bucket from a different iteration. world-q3p9 is that failure: the climatology's soil water came out above the staged bucket on 55 land cells, which a store clipped at every timestep cannot produce, and the arm reporting it was run_67323a923013 with exactly codes 229 and 2290 orphaned -- which this gate was already saying at the time.

The check's history explains the framing: it generalises run_exoplasim.py's donor refusal, which is about seeding by construction. Generalising the population did not generalise the consequence.

DO. Extend the verdict to name the second consumer and the door for it: lib/provenance.py:run_surface_field resolves the field a run consumed, and staged_surface_field's paired_with_run refuses the cross-iteration read. One sentence, so that a reader who hits this FAIL learns what to do about a climatology as well as about a restart.

Ask first whether the message is the right place: an alternative is that the gate stays as it is and the door's docstring carries the pointer, which it already does in the other direction. The case for the message is that the gate is where a reader lands with the problem in front of them.

NOT FIXED HERE: scripts/ was outside the file scope of the session that found it.

Evidence: scripts/check_consistency.py, the 'runs vs the surface fields they staged' arm; world-q3p9.

title: A run keeps the .sra bytes it staged but not the record that says what generated them
description:
A run directory holds its own copy of every staged surface field, and run_manifest.json records the sha256 of each. What it does not keep is the per-code provenance record that sat beside the field in exoplasim/inputs/<rung>/ when it was staged.

WHAT THAT COSTS. For surface code 229 that record is the only place three facts live: whether the lake blend was applied (`lakes`), which climatology the soil column was weathered under, and which pedology land_column_states file the capacity came from. Once the field is restaged the record is overwritten, and the run's copy of the .sra becomes bytes with a hash and no derivation.

MEASURED 2026-08-31. hydrography/scripts/lake_mosaic_cost.py now reads the capacity run_67323a923013 integrated, through lib/provenance.py:run_surface_field. It can report lake_blend_is_inert for the STAGED field, because the record is there, and cannot report it for the field that ran. The report says so by name rather than assuming the two agree.

WHY IT IS P3 AND NOT HIGHER. The sha256 in run_manifest.json is enough to say WHICH field ran and to refuse a wrong pairing, which is the failure that costs a wrong number. This is about being able to say WHAT that field was without the generator's record, and it degrades gracefully: a consumer that needs the derivation can refuse rather than guess, which is what the report does now.

DO. Decide whether run_exoplasim.py's stage_surface_extras should copy the per-code *_provenance.json beside the .sra it copies, or whether run_manifest.json should absorb the records inline. Ask first whether the sha is enough: a record that is a copy of a file that still exists somewhere is a second copy to keep in step, and the case for it is that the original is overwritten by design.

Evidence: notes/audits/land-mosaic-support-reductions.md section 2; hydrography/scripts/lake_mosaic_cost.py, the blend_is_inert comment.
close_reason:
The record is copied rather than absorbed, and the ask-first question came out in favour of the copy. A second copy of a file that still exists is normally a thing to keep in step; here the original is OVERWRITTEN BY DESIGN at the next staging, which is exactly the case a copy is for. Absorbing the records inline into run_manifest.json was the alternative and it would have duplicated source_config per code or forced a subset, and choosing which facts survive is the same mistake as losing them.

run_exoplasim.py:stage_surface_provenance copies each record in beside the fields it staged, over every intended code rather than the extras alone, because the landmap and topomap are covered by boundary_conditions_report.json and it is overwritten like the rest. run_manifest.json lists what was copied under surface_field_provenance. lib/provenance.py:staged_surface_records maps codes to records so the directory's two naming conventions stay in one place, and a record covering seven codes is copied once.

run_surface_field now reports provenance_record: the run's own copy where one exists, and None where a run kept none. None means the derivation is gone rather than that it can be looked up elsewhere, which is the honest state for every run taken before this.

Not retrofittable to run_67323a923013: the record beside its 229 field was overwritten on 2026-08-30 and the tree has no copy. Verified against the live inputs directory: four records cover the twelve staged codes and all four copy byte-identically. lib/provenance.py --selftest carries eleven refusals now, two of them this pair.

f1d9ca287.

title: staged_surface_field does not find the per-code provenance record beside a staged .sra
description:
CLAUDE.md's lib/ list calls lib/provenance.py:staged_surface_field 'the one door onto a staged .sra keyed by the rung', and rule 5 rests on it. It does not open for surface code 229.

MEASURED 2026-08-31. Calling staged_surface_field(229, config) against exoplasim/inputs/t21/ raises: 'orogen_T21_surf_0229.sra has no provenance record beside it naming code 229, so the build it was staged from is unknown.' The record IS beside it: exoplasim/inputs/t21/orogen_T21_surf_0229_provenance.json carries output, output_sha256 matching the bytes on disk, and source_config.source_build = canonical-10m-carve2. The resolver appears to look for a different record -- a boundary_conditions-style report naming the code -- rather than the per-code _provenance.json that build_surface_soil_water.py actually writes.

WHY IT MATTERS. The refusal is correct in FORM: an unstamped staged field is unobservable and refusing beats trusting. But the field here IS stamped, so the door refuses a caller that is doing the right thing, and the caller's only route forward is to hand-roll the sha check and the build read -- which is exactly the duplication the door exists to prevent, and which is what hydrography/scripts/lake_mosaic_cost.py:read_staged_capacity now does with a comment saying why.

The failure mode is silent in the direction that matters: a future caller that hits this refusal and reaches for the path directly, without the sha check, gets no error at all.

DO. Either teach staged_surface_field to accept the per-code <stem>_provenance.json as a stamp, or make build_surface_soil_water.py write the record the resolver already looks for. One of the two, not both, and whichever is chosen the other side gets a check that fires when they disagree. Then delete read_staged_capacity from lake_mosaic_cost.py and call the shared door.

Ask first whether the per-code record should exist at all: if the resolver's format is the intended one, the fix is the writer and the extra file goes.

NOT FIXED HERE: lib/provenance.py and exoplasim/ were outside the file scope of the session that found it.

Evidence: hydrography/scripts/lake_mosaic_cost.py:read_staged_capacity and its docstring.
close_reason:
The resolver was wrong, not the writer, and no second record was added. staged_surface_field read only the KEY terrain_hash while artifact_build in the same module already treated a named source_build as an artifact's identity; the door now resolves a named build through lib/orogen.py's registry and refuses a record whose hash and name are two different builds. build_surface_soil_water.py is unchanged: the four sibling records fill terrain_hash from the export's own identity and this generator opens no export, so writing a registry-derived hash under that key would be a weaker claim wearing the same name.

read_staged_capacity is deleted from hydrography/scripts/lake_mosaic_cost.py and no hand-rolled reader of a staged 0229 remains. lib/provenance.py --selftest carries nine refusals with right answers, two of which fail on the old code, and is registered under one_offs.

317cf8774, f2f3c29ba, 59ee0b3c4.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESOLVED 2026-08-31. The resolver moved, not the writer, and no second record exists.

THE ASK-FIRST QUESTION, answered. The per-code _provenance.json SHOULD exist and the extra file that would have to go is the one the row offered to add. Four records sit beside a staged field in exoplasim/inputs/t21/: albedo_report.json, boundary_conditions_report.json, roughness_t21_report.json and orogen_T21_surf_1801_provenance.json. All four carry a top-level terrain_hash. orogen_T21_surf_0229_provenance.json carries source_config.source_build and no terrain_hash, and it carries a great deal besides -- the capacity split's whole derivation, the states file it read and its sha, the config stamp the drift guard compares against. Writing a second, report-style file to satisfy the resolver would duplicate an identity and leave two files to keep in step.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG. _staged_reports already scanned both naming conventions; the resolver read only the KEY terrain_hash. artifact_build, thirty lines above it in the same module, already treats source_build in a sidecar as the artifact's identity. So two functions in lib/provenance.py disagreed about what stamps an artifact, and the refusal was correct in form on a field that was stamped.

THE REPAIR. _record_build_name reads the name wherever a writer put it -- top-level source_build, top-level build, or source_config.source_build -- and _record_terrain_hash resolves it through the registry in lib/orogen.py. That is the same registry build_stamp writes the explicit hash from, so the two routes cannot disagree about a registered build.

THE CHECK THAT FIRES WHEN THEY DISAGREE, which the row asked for: a record carrying BOTH a terrain_hash and a build name that the registry resolves to a different hash is refused, naming both and the file. It lives in the resolver rather than in a writer because a record carrying both is the ordinary case for four of the five files and a record whose halves name two builds is unusable in either direction.

WHY build_surface_soil_water.py DOES NOT GAIN A terrain_hash KEY. The four siblings fill it from mesh.terrain_hash -- the export's own identity, read from the file. build_surface_soil_water.py opens no export unless --lakes is passed, so the only hash it could write is the registry's answer for the configured build name, which is what the resolver now derives anyway. Writing it would put a weaker assertion under a key whose four other occurrences mean something stronger. The record names its build; that is the stamp.

read_staged_capacity IS GONE from hydrography/scripts/lake_mosaic_cost.py, replaced by the shared door. No hand-rolled reader of a staged 0229 remains in the tree: run_exoplasim.py:2076 globs for the file's PRESENCE and reads the sidecar's climatology for the bootstrap-lineage guard, which is a different question and correctly not this door's.

lib/provenance.py --selftest carries nine refusals with right answers, registered under one_offs in config/pipeline.yaml. Two of the nine fail on the old code.

317cf8774, f2f3c29ba, 59ee0b3c4.

title: Five assessed quantities carry the tightest tolerance in the tree rather than one derived through their own consumer
description:
Five assessed quantities take the tightest tolerance in the tree rather than one
derived through their own consumer.

WHAT IS TRUE. `biosphere/config/equilibrium_window.yaml`'s `assessed` block gives
every quantity its own tolerance and says where each came from. Six of the eleven
are derived: the two `fpc.out` cover quantities through the albedo chain to
surface temperature, and the four `score_prediction.py` quantities through the
band half-widths pre-registered in `notes/productivity-prediction.md`. The other
five carry 0.05 with the derivation recorded as "the tightest tolerance derived
in this tree, applied conservatively to an unpriced chain":

  cpool.out SoilC                 read by pedology/scripts/build_soil.py
  cpool.out Total                 read by lpj_acceptance.yaml closure.carbon
  npool.out Total                 read by lpj_acceptance.yaml closure.nitrogen
  aaet.out Total                  read by lpj_acceptance.yaml closure.water
  tot_runoff.out Total            read by lpj_acceptance.yaml closure.water

THE TWO ARE DIFFERENT CASES and only one of them is a missing derivation.

SoilC HAS A CHAIN AND IT HAS NOT BEEN PRICED. `build_soil.py:organic_properties`
turns soil carbon into an organic mass fraction and a bulk density through the
Adams reciprocal mixing rule, the organic fraction enters the volumetric water
capacity additively beside the texture and allophane terms, and that capacity
sets the climate model's `dwmax`, whose overflow IS its runoff. So a drift in
SoilC reaches a climate-visible quantity by a route this project already has
every link of, and pricing it is the same shape of work as the albedo chain
above. It also sets the exchange complex's organic term, and it is loop B's exit
quantity.

THE CLOSURE'S FOUR TOTALS MAY NOT OWE A DRIFT TOLERANCE AT ALL. The closure
compares a pool's change against its own flux over the window, which is a
CONSERVATION test and holds whether or not the pool is drifting. So the honest
question for those four is not "what tolerance" but "does this reader impose
one", and the answer may be no -- in which case they leave the assessed set and
keep their bounds as diagnostics, exactly as the per-plant-functional-type
columns now do. Ask that before deriving anything.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY: nothing, and that is why it is P3. Every one of the five
settles on the record on disk except `cpool.out` Total, which bounds at 0.0503
against 0.05 -- and that is a drift refusal, so a looser tolerance would be
answering a real drift by moving the bar and the derivation must not be reached
for on those grounds. What would make this bite is a chain that prices SoilC
TIGHTER than 0.05, which would lengthen every future run.

CITES: biosphere/config/equilibrium_window.yaml (the assessed block),
biosphere/notes/equilibrium-trend-null.md (what each quantity owes),
pedology/scripts/build_soil.py:organic_properties,
biosphere/config/lpj_acceptance.yaml (the closure block).

title: Measure the attenuation on the lakes and playa_clastic items, on the configured build
description:
world-ckbt measured the surface-to-planetary albedo attenuation on TWO terms and
put scripts/error_budget.py's DEFAULT_ATTENUATION at 0.38 with a measured span of
0.29 to 0.48. notes/audits/albedo-attenuation.md is the finding. Three of its
four points are one term on three builds, so the span between the two TERMS,
1.62, is the whole of the bracket and two more terms would say whether it is
really term-dependence or the widest point's own uncertainty.

The two the row named and did not get are the lakes item and the playa_clastic
level, both already priced in albedo_items.

WHY THEY WERE NOT MEASURED. Both are staged-field changes rather than namelist
keys. Each needs build_surface_albedo.py re-run under a different rock table or
lake compositing, the six albedo codes restaged, and a paired 25-orbit set
branched from an equilibrated restart. exoplasim/inputs/t21/ is keyed by RUNG
ALONE, so it holds exactly one build's albedo field at a time and restaging
replaces what the whole tree reads; in a worktree those six paths are symlinks
into the main checkout, so a restage there writes into the shared tree while
other sessions read it. That is the constraint, and it is about WHEN rather than
whether.

COST. The run is cheap: a paired 25-orbit T21 set at eight threads an arm,
pinned and concurrent under one host lock, brackets at 6 to 25 minutes of wall
clock. The low end is what PHYS-15's own arms recorded; the high end is 25 orbits
at the 53 s per orbit docs/src/reference/config-rationale.md measures for T21 on
eight ranks, plus the concurrency penalty. The bracket is reported rather than
closed because no timing of a T21 paired arm survives in this tree.

WHY IT IS WORTH BUYING BEYOND THE THIRD AND FOURTH POINTS. Every arm behind the
current constant sits on canonical-10m-base or canonical-10m-carve1. There is no
bare-rock endmember run on canonical-10m-carve2, so the configured build carries
no attenuation measurement at all. Both of these would.

WHAT ELSE THEY WOULD SETTLE. The leading explanation for the two terms differing
is that the attenuation is a property of the modelled atmosphere: the wetting
term acts where the modelled skin is wet, which is where it rains, and the
endmember term is spread over land that includes the dry closed-basin interiors.
The lakes item is concentrated on the bright playa and salt crust of exactly
those interiors, so it is the sharpest available test of that hypothesis: if the
mechanism is right, the lakes item should land at or above the endmember term
rather than with the wetting term.

Fix the prediction before the arms run.

Source: notes/audits/albedo-attenuation.md, "What is still owed"; world-ckbt.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
PRE-REGISTERED, before any arm runs. Evidence in
notes/audits/albedo-attenuation.md, section 'What is still owed'; commit d173940bf.

THE ARMS. playa_clastic albedo 0.19 against 0.33, on canonical-10m-carve2 at
T21, both branched from ONE existing equilibrated T21 restart on that build at
the configured flux 0.945. 0.19 is the export's own table entry and 0.33 is the
top of the class's declared range; the staged value is 0.23, which sits below
that range. Staged land-mean delta 0.011920, measured not assumed.

THE PREDICTION. The hypothesis is that the attenuation belongs to the modelled
atmosphere over the cells a perturbation acts on, and playa_clastic IS the dry
closed-basin interior material where the modelled sky is clearest. So the
playa point lands AT OR ABOVE the endmember term: in 0.38 to 0.55. The
hypothesis is REFUTED if it lands at or below the wetting term's 0.292 plus its
own uncertainty. A point between 0.292 and 0.38 is neither and widens the
bracket, which is also a result.

THE BARS, all carried over from world-ckbt unchanged and none chosen here. The
arms must separate by at least three times the quadrature sum of the two fitted
asymptote half-widths, or the pair reports unresolved and no attenuation is
taken from it. A pair whose diagnosed and staged land-mean deltas disagree by
more than 1.5 is excluded as pricing the swap rather than the attenuation.
The span rule stands: within 1.5 a measured constant, 1.5 to 2 a measured
constant with the measured spread, beyond 2 a single constant is the wrong
shape.

THE LAKES ARM IS REFUSED AND THAT IS A VERDICT, not a deferral. Predicted
separation 0.107 to 0.178 K against a pair quadrature half-width of 0.028 to
0.067 K observed across every pair on disk: 1.6 to 6.3, failing its own 3x bar
over much of its bracket. The attenuation it would return carries a half-width
of 20 to 48 per cent against a bracket that is 25 per cent wide, so it would be
a point wider than the thing it is meant to narrow. It becomes buyable at an
amplified lake contrast or at about four times the orbits. The playa arm tests
the same hypothesis on the same footprint with 1.8 times the amplitude, so
nothing is lost by refusing it now.

WHAT THE PERTURBATION IS WORTH, measured 2026-08-31 from three
build_surface_albedo.py runs into a scratch --output differing only in
model.lithology_albedo_overrides.playa_clastic.albedo:

  0.23 -> 0.25   d(staged land mean) +0.0017028459   share 0.08514230
  0.23 -> 0.33   d(staged land mean) +0.0085142296   share 0.08514230
  0.25 -> 0.33   d(staged land mean) +0.0068113837   share 0.08514230

Exactly linear to eight figures across a factor of five in step size. Code 212,
the forest fraction, is byte-identical across all three, so the override moves
albedo alone and the confound the endmember pairs had to disprove is absent
here by construction.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
THE BLOCKER, established before touching anything. The row's stated blocker is
out of date and two others are real.

THE RESTAGE IS SAFE. exoplasim/scripts/sra.py:refuse_a_write_through_a_symlink
fires on all seven codes this worktree links -- 0174, 0175, 0176, 0212, 1742,
1750, 1760 -- and write_sra is the single door all four surface builders go
through. The generator's write order is wet codes, then dry codes, then forest,
then the report, so the FIRST write raises SystemExit and nothing is written at
all, the report included. Verified against the live paths: every one refuses.
exoplasim/inputs/t21/albedo_report.json is a tracked real file in the worktree,
not a link, so an edit to it stays here. world-4o59 closed this and the row
predates it.

WHAT A RESTAGE WOULD TOUCH, exactly: those seven .sra, which are ignored by
.gitignore:362 and are symlinks into /home/cfutro/docs/world, plus
albedo_report.json, which is tracked. Nothing else.

THE SAFE ROUTE NEEDS NO NEW STAGING DIRECTORY AND NO CODE. Remove this
worktree's seven symlinks -- removing a symlink does not touch its target --
and let build_surface_albedo.py write real files at its default output. The
worktree then holds its own complete staged T21 albedo surface, every consumer
that resolves exoplasim/inputs/<rung> here reads it, and the main checkout is
untouched. New run directories are real directories here; the existing ones are
all symlinks and are only read. Restore with rm of the seven, git checkout of
albedo_report.json, and link_worktree.py.

A rung-keyed VARIANT directory would be the wrong repair. run_exoplasim.py's
surface_sra and lib/provenance.py's staged_surface_field both resolve
exoplasim/inputs/<rung> with no override, and adding one introduces a permanent
way to run the model on a surface that is not the staged one, which is exactly
the silence rule 5 exists to close. Not worth it for one measurement.

BLOCKER 1: NO BINARY IS CURRENT. exoplasim/scripts/rebuild_binaries.py --verify
reports all ten configurations in the matrix as not built against the model
source at vendor/exoplasim. Rule 4 asks for every binary, so the arms cost a
full rebuild before the first orbit. I did not price it and did not run it:
vendor/exoplasim is outside my brief's file scope.

BLOCKER 2: NO T21 RESTART IS ON A SURFACE THE TREE STILL HOLDS.
check_consistency.py fails 'runs vs the surface fields they staged' for every
T21 run and says nothing can be seeded from them. Five live T21 runs on
canonical-10m-carve2 at flux 0.945 exist -- run_0d41aa82c287, run_5994d1f9624e,
run_67323a923013, run_71b36de31f0c, run_ef6fa5447420 -- and branching BOTH arms
from one of them is what makes it survivable: the common transient from the
surface change is identical in both arms and cancels in the difference of the
two asymptotes, which is the estimator.

THE STAGED SURFACE IS BEHIND THE GENERATOR BY MORE THAN THE LAKES ITEM IS
WORTH. world-znr7 rewrote analysis/soil_albedo_wetting.json after the surface
was staged, and today's generator moves the staged land mean by -0.003474 and
the soil-wetting bound from 0.015707 to 0.010121, a 36 per cent fall in the
budget's second-largest albedo item. check_consistency.py already reports both;
this is the tree's resting state and I did not regenerate it.

THE PRICE. Two arms, SEQUENTIAL rather than concurrent, 40 orbits each, T21 on
eight ranks under one host lock: 45 to 95 minutes of wall clock. Low end is the
rate PHYS-15's own arms recorded, high end is 53 s per orbit from
docs/src/reference/config-rationale.md plus per-arm setup. Sequential is
deliberate: the estimator's floor across independent integrations is under a
hundredth of a kelvin and two arms sharing a die do not hold that, so twenty
minutes buys two arms as identical as this host can make them. Plus two 38 s
generator runs, plus the unpriced rebuild.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
STATUS: BLOCKED, on two things neither of which is the restage.

1. No binary in the matrix is built against the current model source
   (rebuild_binaries.py --verify). vendor/exoplasim is outside my brief's file
   scope, so I did not rebuild. Unblocking is a rebuild of every binary per
   rule 4, then --verify.
2. No T21 restart is on a surface the tree still holds. Survivable by branching
   both arms from one of the five live T21 runs on canonical-10m-carve2, as
   above, but it is a decision to take deliberately rather than by default.

The prediction, the arms, the bars and the price are registered above and do
not need revisiting when this unblocks. The lakes arm is separately RESOLVED as
refused on the instrument check, not deferred: it does not become a task again
until someone buys the amplified contrast or four times the orbits.

I did not start the arms.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-31 COORDINATOR: ONE OF THE TWO BLOCKERS IS NOT REAL, checked in the main checkout.

Blocker (1), that rebuild_binaries.py --verify reports all ten configurations not built against the current model source, is a WORKTREE ARTIFACT and not a property of the tree. In the main checkout:

  model source: vendor/exoplasim @ 923390a7a
  all 10 binaries current

scripts/link_worktree.py DELIBERATELY does not link the model binaries, and docs/src/reference/environment.md gives the reason: a link both hides a worktree's own edit behind the main checkout's binary and lets a rebuild in the worktree overwrite that binary, which is rule 4 with the safety off. So a worktree correctly sees no binaries, and --verify in one reports absence rather than staleness. Rule 4 is satisfied and the arms need no rebuild. That removes the unpriced cost from the estimate.

Blocker (2) STANDS and is the real one: check_consistency reports that no T21 run is on a surface the tree still holds, so nothing can be seeded from it. The proposal on the row -- branch BOTH arms from one of the five live T21 runs on the configured build, so the common transient cancels in the difference of asymptotes -- is sound in principle and has not been validated. Validating it is the next step and is cheap: it is a claim about what the restart carries, answerable from the run records without integrating anything.

COST, WITH THE REBUILD REMOVED: 45 to 95 minutes wall clock for two sequential 40-orbit T21 p8 arms under one lock_and_run, plus two 38 s generator runs. Sequential is right and the row's reason is right: the estimator's floor is under 0.01 K and two arms sharing a die do not hold that.

NOT SCHEDULED YET, and the ground is contention rather than doubt about the value: three agents are working and one runs a multi-minute assessment repeatedly under the same lock. The registered prediction stands as written -- the playa point lands at or above the endmember term, in 0.38 to 0.55, refuted at or below 0.292 plus its own uncertainty -- and it must not be rewritten when the arms are eventually bought.

The lakes arm stays REFUSED on the instrument, which is the right call and is not revisited by any of this.

title: verify_entry_points rewrites a tracked artifact, so running a gate dirties the tree
description:
scripts/verify_entry_points.py starts all 160 entry points to prove the import graph resolves. exoplasim/scripts/rootable_albedo_gate.py is one of them, and STARTING it runs it: it writes exoplasim/analysis/rootable_albedo_gate_report.json, which is TRACKED. So the gate leaves the tree dirty by exactly one line, the report's `generated` timestamp, with every other byte identical.

WHY IT MATTERS AND IT IS NOT COSMETIC. A gate that mutates tracked state is a gate an agent cannot run freely. This project's standing practice is to run the gates and commit as you go with explicit paths, and the churn lands between the two: the modification was already present in `git status` at the start of this session and reappeared the moment the gate ran again, so it is recurring, not a one-off. What it costs is a meaningless commit or an agent stopping to work out whose change it is -- this session did the latter.

The report's content is deterministic. Only the timestamp moves, so nothing about the world is being recorded and nothing downstream can tell the two versions apart.

THE QUESTION BEFORE THE FIX is which of the two things should give, and both are defensible so it is a decision rather than a defect to grind out:

  - The gate should not RUN what it only needs to START. verify_entry_points wants to know that a module's imports resolve and its argument parser builds; scripts that do their work at import or under a bare `main()` on no arguments are the ones it cannot ask that of without side effects. Whether other entry points also write on a bare start is not established here and is the first thing to measure.
  - Or the report should not carry a wall-clock `generated` at all. Its purpose is to say which tree state the checks passed on, and a content hash or the config hash the artifact already stamps says that better -- a timestamp changes when nothing did, which is the property causing this.

Evidence: exoplasim/scripts/rootable_albedo_gate.py; scripts/verify_entry_points.py; config/pipeline.yaml step rootable_albedo_gate.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 IT IS EIGHT SCRIPTS, NOT ONE, and the row's own argument is what the widened walk turned up. Running scripts/verify_entry_points.py once on a clean tree left EIGHT tracked artifacts modified:

  analysis/coastline_threshold_cost.json
  analysis/ocean_column_response.json
  analysis/ocean_shortwave_penetration.json
  analysis/partial_surface_gate_report.json
  analysis/partial_surface_decision_gate_report.json
  analysis/subgrid_slope_support.json
  exoplasim/analysis/rootable_albedo_gate_report.json
  ocean/analysis/carbon_feedback_gate_report.json
  ocean/analysis/transport_loop_gate_report.json

Most became visible when world-6247 widened SCRIPT_DIRS to reach analysis/ and ocean/, so the count grew with the walk rather than with the tree.

WHAT IT COST, measured on the spot: staging with git add -u after running the gate swept all nine into the index alongside an unrelated change, which is the failure the project's own standing instruction about explicit paths exists to prevent. Caught before commit, and it is exactly the mechanism this row predicted -- 'a meaningless commit or an agent stopping to work out whose change it is'.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 SETTLED, and the framing that made it a decision was based on a false premise. The row offered two options: stop RUNNING what only needs to START, or drop the wall-clock the write differs by. The second was never a fix. The gate ran 27 entry points to completion, nine of which write tracked reports; removing the timestamps would have hidden nine of the writes and left the gate running 27 unrelated gates as a side effect of a start check, silently rewriting whatever they write that git does not track. So it is one disposition, not two.

WHAT MADE IT NINE. verify_entry_points asked 'does this start' by running python <script> --help and reading the exit status. --help short-circuits only where there is a parser to short-circuit it, and 27 of the 212 entry points build none, so on them --help was an argument nothing read and the script did its whole job. All nine of the modified artifacts map to a no-parser script; none maps to a script that builds one.

THE REPAIR. The probe is chosen per script from the source: --help where it constructs an ArgumentParser, and otherwise the module body executed under a __name__ that is not __main__, which runs every import and no work. Still one child per entry point, so the cost is unchanged. 91d9892e7.

AND THE PROBE'S OWN PRECONDITION IS NOW CHECKED. --help is safe because argparse exits before the rest of the start path, which is a property of the script: a parser built after a read or a write short-circuits nothing. help_short_circuits() refuses a help-mode entry point whose start path does anything before constructing its parser. Measured tree-wide: 185 help-mode entry points, 0 refused, and the six with any statement ahead of the parser have only imports, a docstring or a global. 06b48e91a.

MEASURED: a full pass on a clean tree leaves git status clean.

title: maps/ frames use the same UUID-plus-scanned-index pattern the run index just lost forty runs to
description:
maps/frames.py says a frame is a UUID with a row in maps/data/<build>/INDEX.json
saying what it is, and maps/README.md says INDEX.json is tracked while the frames
are not, calling it the same rule as exoplasim/runs/.

It is the same rule, and until world-ww6z it was the same DEFECT on the run
side: exoplasim/runs/INDEX.json was rebuilt by scanning the directory, so it
recorded what existed rather than what had existed, and forty runs were created
and deleted between two scans and left nothing tracked anywhere
(notes/audits/run-identity.md, archive/runs/RECORDLESS.json).

WHAT TO SETTLE: whether maps/data/<build>/INDEX.json is written at frame
creation and merged on a rescan, or rebuilt from a directory listing. If it is
rebuilt, a rendered frame that is deleted or overwritten loses its identity the
same way, and the repair is the same shape -- maps/snapshot.py registers the row
when it writes the frame, and the reindex merges rather than replaces.

WHY THIS IS P3 AND NOT P2. A frame is a rendering of state that other artifacts
hold: unlike a climate run, it can be made again from its inputs, so a lost frame
identity costs a re-render rather than an unrepeatable measurement. It is worth
closing because the pattern is copied and the next copy may not be re-derivable.

Not measured here; maps/ was outside the file scope of the work that found it.

title: wetlands' retained_outputs is described by a count that the list outgrows
description:
`biosphere/config/wetlands.yaml:274` and `biosphere/README.md:500` both say
"The other eleven wait on a MODEL, not on an output routine" about the
`acceptance.retained_outputs` list beneath it. The count is a summary of a
collection that is appended to: adding a retained output leaves the sentence
asserting a number the list no longer has, and nothing re-derives it.

Same shape as world-h3qg, milder because it is prose rather than a gate-enforced
claim. Found sweeping for that shape; the files are outside the scope that row
was worked in.

DO: say it by the mechanism rather than the count. Section 6 of the contract
already names which model each output waits on, so the sentence can point at
that instead: an output with no quantity behind it in the fork today waits on a
model, and section 6 names which. If the gate over this file can tell the two
classes apart, having it print the split re-derives the number on every run
rather than freezing it.

title: outdiag numbers its diagnostic arrays onto codes the ordinary output already uses
description:
A MODEL-SOURCE DEFECT WHOSE REPAIR IS FORTRAN. Filed from world-k5db, where
everything reachable from Python was done and this was what remained.

outmod.f90:outdiag numbers its four optional diagnostic blocks off the loop
index and writes them into the SAME unit the ordinary output goes to:

  ndiaggp2d = N   jcode = jdiag      codes 1..N
  ndiaggp3d = N   jcode = 20+jdiag   codes 21..20+N
  ndiagsp2d = N   jcode = 50+jdiag   codes 51..50+N
  ndiagsp3d = N   jcode = 60+jdiag   codes 61..60+N

The 2-D spectral block collides at N = 1. outsc writes the orbital elements as
codes 50 to 54 on the same unit, so ndiagsp2d = 1 makes the model write code 51
twice per output step: once as the ecliptic longitude, a length-1 scalar
record, and once as a length-NESP spectral array. All four keys are in
plasim_nl, so this is reachable from a namelist and not only from the Fortran.
snapshotdiag carries the same numbering onto unit 140.

WHAT IT PRODUCED BEFORE THE GUARDS. pyburn.readallvariables keeps the FIRST
record's header per code and refactorvariable reshapes the whole joined array
by it, so the two record sets were concatenated and read as extra timestamps of
whichever came first -- a variable with the wrong time axis and the wrong
values under the name ilibrary supplies, with nothing downstream able to tell.

TWO GUARDS ARE IN, AND NEITHER IS THE REPAIR.
  pyburn.readallvariables now refuses a code whose records disagree in length,
  naming the code and both lengths. That is the far end: it fires when the raw
  is read, after the run.
  scripts/smoke_test.py:check_no_enabled_diagnostic_block_collides fails if any
  file in exoplasim/scripts, the shipped namelists or config sets one of the
  four keys to a value whose codes reach an ilibrary row. That is the near end:
  it fires at the commit that enables the block. Nothing in this tree sets any
  of them, so it passes today.
  Both were proved able to fail: setting ndiagsp2d=3 in example.nl reports
  codes 51, 52, 53 landing on lambda, zdec and rdist.

THE REPAIR is to move the diagnostic blocks onto a code range nothing else
uses -- the model has 600 upward free, and the ecological stream already lives
there with its own unit -- or to give them their own unit as the ecological
stream has. Either is a Fortran change under vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/
src/, which world-k5db's agent was scoped out of.

WHY IT IS P3 AND NOT HIGHER. It is latent: nothing sets the keys, and both ends
now refuse rather than answer wrongly. It becomes live the first time someone
wants Frank's diagnostics, and the smoke check will say so before the run.

title: Codes the model writes that pyburn cannot name
description:
Found in the world-e9yz sweep, which asked the reverse question: not which
derivation arms are unaddressable, but which of the model's OWN outputs are.

Parsed every literal code handed to writegp/writesp/writescalar in
vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src and compared against pyburn.ilibrary.
115 codes are written; these are not ilibrary keys, so dataset() raises
"Unknown variable code requested" for them and the record sits in the raw
unreachable:

  229  dwmax, field capacity in metres (plasimmod.f90:851). Written
       UNCONDITIONALLY by outgp, snapshotgp and hcadencegp, so it is in every
       raw this project has ever produced. It is the bucket capacity the land
       column integrates against, and pedology and hydrography both reason
       about plant-available water.
  101-107  dclforc, the cloud forcing diagnostics, under ndiagcf > 0 only.
  600-628  the ecological stream. NOT A GAP: run_exoplasim.refuse_eco_codes
       argues why that stream is read directly and never postprocessed.

Codes 360-387 and 460-487 are the energy budget terms and are NOT in this
class either: run_exoplasim.register_energy_diagnostic_codes inserts rows into
pyburn.ilibrary at call time. That is the project's own precedent for closing
one of these -- a row from the caller, not a fork edit -- and it is why
_resolvekey now resolves a run-time row by name as well as by code.

A SECOND FINDING IN THE SAME PARSE, and it is a collision rather than a gap.
outdiag's diagnostic loops number their output from the loop index:
jcode = jdiag (gp2d), 20+jdiag (gp3d), 50+jdiag (sp2d), 60+jdiag (sp3d). With
ndiagsp2d > 0 the sp2d block writes codes 51 upward, which ilibrary reads as
the orbital elements -- 51 lambda, 52 zdec, 53 rdist, 54 rasc. Nothing in this
project sets any ndiag* key, so it is latent; a run that did would get orbital
element names on diagnostic arrays with no complaint from either side.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE 229: a consumer. The model source gives its meaning and its
unit without guesswork, so the row is not the hard part; the name it should
carry in a table other code indexes by name is a decision, and it should be
made by whoever needs the field rather than in advance.
close_reason: Resolved and committed (7821ebf69, 20c4a8064, 923390a7a). world-hs5z: _resolvekey handles code, string and name in both loops, repaired rather than refused because both docstrings promise all three and the fork is hard; also closed a gap the row did not name, run-time ilibrary rows answering to their code but not their name. world-e9yz: all five arms deleted, settled from outmod.f90 rather than burn7, each being an exact combination of addressable codes; 268/269 were not merely dead but fired and stored rst-rss as icez in m2 s-2. world-k5db: 229 dwmax and 101-107 named from the model's own source, and the outdiag collision guarded at both ends with the Fortran renumber filed as world-2v9z.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
DONE, EXCEPT THE HALF THAT IS FORTRAN, WHICH IS world-2v9z.

229 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED AND IT HAS A LIVE READER. dwmax is not an idle
diagnostic: build_surface_soil_water.py STAGES it as code 229, restart_surface.py
carries it as SurfaceRestartField(229, "dwmax"), restart_schema.py's policy row
says "field capacity, staged code 229", and under NVEG=2 coupled vegetation OWNS
it -- so the model evolves the value that was staged. world-cp27 is about to
change what is staged, from a 0.5 uniform placeholder on 620 sea-owned partial
cells to a mesh-derived value, taking the derived population from 1019 cells to
1639. Confirming that change means reading code 229 back off a run, and until
now dataset() answered "Unknown variable code requested: 229". So: a live reader,
and a field written unconditionally by all three record writers.

THE ROW GOES IN THE TABLE, NOT IN A CALLER. run_exoplasim.register_energy_
diagnostic_codes inserts codes 360-387 and 460-487 into pyburn.ilibrary at call
time and argues that this keeps the vendored tree untouched, because a .venv
reinstall would drop a patch. That argument does not hold here: ExoPlaSim is
installed EDITABLE from vendor/exoplasim, so pyburn.py IS the installed file,
and the fork is hard as of 2026-08-21 so there is no upstream merge to carry a
divergence through. A run-time insertion is also conditional and lives on the
run path, so a scratch script calling pyburn.dataset would still not be able to
name the field. 229 is written unconditionally exactly as 267, 268 and 269 are,
and those are rows.

  "229": ["dwmax", "field_capacity", "m"]

No name was invented. dwmax is the model's own (plasimmod.f90:851, "field
capacity (m)") and is what this project already calls it at three sites.

101-107 ARE NAMED THE SAME WAY, from radmod.f90:1799-1834. The cloud forcing
diagnostic is the second radiation call made with dcc zeroed, so each of the
seven is the CLEAR-SKY twin of a row that was already here, and each takes that
row's name with CF's cs suffix, that row's long name, and that row's units:

  101 rsscs  <- 176 rss     104 rlutcs <- 179 rlut    106 ssrucs <- 204 ssru
  102 rlscs  <- 177 rls     105 rsutcs <- 203 rsut    107 strucs <- 205 stru
  103 rstcs  <- 178 rst

Not refused the way the ecological codes are, because there is no reason to:
these are ordinary gridpoint records on the ordinary units, written exactly as
176-179 are. pyburn could always read them; it had no names. Refusing a feature
over a missing table row would have been the wrong shape of answer.

Read back end to end on a fixture carrying the records: ["229"], [229] and
["dwmax"] all return dwmax at field_capacity / m, and ["101","107"] and
["rsscs","strucs"] agree likewise.

600-628 ARE A DELIBERATE REFUSAL AND IT SAYS WHY -- checked, not assumed.
run_exoplasim.refuse_eco_codes carries the argument (the stream writes its own
interval bounds so nothing infers an interval from a record's position, and
pyburn's only notion of time is counting code-139 records), names the codes it
refuses, and names compare_eco_streams.py as where the stream IS read. It is
called on both the prepare path and the continuation path. What it did not have
was anything watching it refuse; it does now.

THE outdiag COLLISION: GUARDED AT BOTH ENDS, REPAIRED AT NEITHER. The numbering
is jcode = 50+jdiag for the 2-D spectral block against outsc's orbital elements
50-54 on the same unit, so ndiagsp2d = 1 writes code 51 twice per step. It was
worse than unaddressable: readallvariables keeps the first record's header per
code and refactorvariable reshapes the joined array by it, so the two record
sets came back as extra timestamps of whichever was first. readallvariables now
refuses a code whose records disagree in length; smoke_test refuses a tree that
enables a block whose codes reach a library row. Neither is the repair -- that
is a Fortran renumber, world-2v9z.

CODE 152 SAYS WHAT IT IS. It was a bare KeyError('152') from before the loop,
which reads as a request having gone wrong. It is not: log surface pressure is
read once before any variable is looked at, and every pressure level, every
pressure field and every derivation that uses a pressure is built from it, so
its absence is a file that cannot be read at all rather than a variable that
could not be produced. The refusal now says so and lists the codes the file
does carry.

AND ONE THING NOBODY FILED. The body of readallvariables was REPEATED inside
_decoderecord, unreachable after that function's return and complete with its
docstring -- residue of the restore argued in the comment above readallvariables,
where the function was pasted back without the stub body being removed. It never
ran. What it cost is that an edit to "the" accumulation loop had two candidates
and only one of them live; this was found by an assertion that the text being
replaced appeared exactly once, and it did not. 57 lines deleted.

CHECKS. smoke_test goes to 67 with two static invariants, which is where the
model-source-against-pyburn pairing already lives and where an EDIT is what
breaks them:
  every code the model writes is named or refused with a reason
      -- a row, or a declared refusal, and nothing else. Proved able to fail by
         removing the 229 row and by removing the 101 row.
  no enabled diagnostic block lands on a library code
      -- proved able to fail by setting ndiagsp2d=3 in example.nl: reports
         codes 51, 52, 53 landing on lambda, zdec and rdist.
verify_high_cadence_rescue.py goes 20 -> 23 with the three that need pyburn to
actually run:
  the ecological stream's codes are refused out loud
      -- proved by stubbing refuse_eco_codes to a no-op
  one code carries one record shape, or the read is refused
      -- paired: two extra records of the SAME length under one code must still
         read. Proved by disabling the length guard
  the reader's own missing prerequisite says it is one
      -- proved by disabling the 152 refusal; also fails if the refusal goes
         back to a bare KeyError
The two static ones were written in the verifier first and MOVED, so each
invariant has one home.

RULE 4 NOT OWED and checked rather than assumed: pyburn.py is Python, imported
at run time from the editable install, no Fortran parameter and no translation
unit, and no Fortran was edited. rebuild_binaries.py --verify: all 10 binaries
current.

title: Tighten the carve list's concavity bound with the lake's own per-bin surface flux
description:
export_carve_list.py:seasonal_concavity bounds the concavity error in Q**m from
the bin weights alone: an overflow is never negative, so phi lies in
[w_min**(1 - m), 1] and no basin's cut can move more than J = 1/w_min**(1 - m)
either side of the class boundary. On canonical-10m-carve1 that is J = 3.4833,
which is DECISIVE against the P = 2.2235 Poisson bracket, and it leaves 26 of
the 195 carved basins flagged seasonal_concavity_movable.

THE BOUND IS LOOSER THAN IT HAS TO BE, because it treats the whole overflow as
having an unknown phase. It does not. Q = runoff * (catchment - area_at_spill)
- (E - P) * area_at_spill: the catchment term's phase is the declared absence
seasonal_phase_of_catchment_delivery, but the LAKE SURFACE term's phase is
representable and is already carried per bin in surface_water.nc. Bounding the
two separately is strictly narrower than bounding their sum.

IT BITES ON THIS POPULATION. The catchment term is a median 2.06 times the
overflow over the 416 basins that overflow, because the lake evaporates about
half of what its catchment delivers. So concentrating the delivery into one bin
puts far more than the annual overflow into that bin, and the square root of it
is correspondingly larger than the flat bound assumes. A first estimate holding
the lake term flat puts the per-basin floor at a median 0.58 over the movable
set against the 0.2871 in force, which would take J below the Poisson ratio and
make the whole term SUBORDINATE.

WHAT IT NEEDS is a per-bin open-water evaporation over each basin.
carve_verdict.bin_mean_open_water owns the per-bin Penman loop and reduces the
bins before returning, so this wants a way to get the bins out of the one
estimator rather than a second loop in export_carve_list.py -- two hand-written
evaluations of one criterion is the failure that function exists to avoid.

The bound must stay a bound: the minimum of the weighted mean of sqrt(max(C_k +
L_k, 0)) over all nonnegative catchment deliveries C with the known annual
mean, at the measured per-bin lake term L_k. Not an estimate of phi, which
would need the phase.

Evidence: hydrography/notes/carve-verdict-interval.md, "The concavity in the
discharge term". Found by world-howr.
close_reason: Resolved and committed. world-howr: the concavity bound needs no delivery phase (the calibration absorbs the level exactly; the bin weights bound the spread), J = 3.4833 against P = 2.2235, DECISIVE, 26 of 195 carved basins movable and none covered by the climate bracket. world-awvh: the tightening does not exist -- lake storage sharpens the overflow's season rather than damping it, the concentrated arm sits on the floor to six decimals, so the bound is ATTAINED and the verdict stands unchanged. world-mddi: three tables read melange and two already agreed; PH_GROUP was falling back on Orogen's origin category against its own chemistry principle. world-5th5: the soda chemistry is right (95.71 per cent of catchment area alkaline) and was being stated about the floor's rock instead of the basin; playa moves to sedimentary_clastic, parent_by_category is derived in every entry, land mean 6.778 to 6.454.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
RESOLVED: THE TIGHTENING DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG. I
filed this row and its estimate; both are corrected here.

WHAT THE ROW CLAIMED. That bounding the catchment term and the lake's own
per-bin surface flux separately is strictly narrower than bounding their sum,
with a first estimate putting the per-basin floor at a median 0.58 against the
0.2871 in force, which would have taken J below P = 2.2235 and made the
seasonal-concavity term SUBORDINATE.

WHY IT IS WRONG. That estimate modelled the per-bin overflow as the
instantaneous net, `delivery + (P - E)` over the lake, floored at zero. That is
the NO-STORAGE limit and it is not what the pipeline computes.
`lake_balance.solve_periodic` carries lake storage, and storage does not damp
the overflow's season -- IT SHARPENS IT. A lake drawn below spill has to refill
before it spills again, so a deficit season that in the no-storage model absorbs
delivery and forces the overflow to spread instead delays the spill and
concentrates it further. The lake's deficit season is exactly what made the
tightening look available.

MEASURED, through the pipeline's own lake balance on its own synthetic set: six
basins spanning a factor of a hundred in capacity, 12 bins whose lightest weight
is 0.043478 so the floor is w_min**(1-m) = 0.208514, two delivery phases
carrying the same annual water, four lake evaporation swings.

  lake swing   flat delivery   whole year in the lightest bin
  0.0          1.000000        0.208514
  0.3          0.991854        0.208514
  0.6          0.963500        0.208514
  0.9          0.865745        0.208514

The concentrated arm sits ON the floor to six decimals for every basin, and the
lake's own swing does not move it by a part in a million. A bound narrowed by
the lake's per-bin flux is precisely a bound this sweep would have lifted off
the floor. The no-storage net on the same forcing returns a ratio strictly
above the floor, which is the control and the mechanism in one.

THE SAME RUN CLOSES THE BOUND'S OWN PREMISE, which world-howr had to state as
an assumption. Under the delivery this pipeline represents, an overflowing basin
sits AT spill through the entire cycle -- cycle-mean area over area at spill
measures 1.0000 -- so its periodic annual overflow equals the spill-level Q the
carve verdict computes, to 1.0000. There is no separate area-convention error to
file. And under the adversary's concentrated delivery the drawn-down lake
evaporates over less area and passes MORE water, putting the worst admissible
cycle 0.03 to 2.6% ABOVE the floor rather than below it: the bound holds and is
slightly conservative.

SO THE VERDICT DOES NOT MOVE. J = 3.4833 against P = 2.2235 stands, the call
stays DECISIVE, and the 26 carved basins of 195 remain flagged
seasonal_concavity_movable. The term does NOT become subordinate. Nothing in
the carve list changes.

WHAT CHANGED IN THE TREE. `seasonal_concavity`'s "what would tighten it"
paragraph said the opposite of the truth and is replaced by the finding; the
same correction went into `incision_retain`'s declaration at the site, the
sidecar's `assumptions` (the mean-equals-Q half is now stated as the identity it
is, not a convention) and a new `the_bound_is_attained` key. The note carries
the sweep with its numbers.

CHECKS ADDED, each demonstrated to fire on an injected defect. In
`export_carve_list.py --selftest`, which needs no build and no climatology: the
two delivery phases carry the same annual water; a flat delivery on a flat lake
evaluates to the annual value exactly; the whole year in the lightest bin
attains the bound at every lake swing (fires when the delivery is split across
two bins); the reported floor IS the attained one (fires when phi_floor is
scaled); and the no-storage net reads the same forcing as less concentrated. 26
checks pass.

AND ONE STATIC CHECK, in scripts/smoke_test.py: "every ledger absence a module
relies on still exists". The choice to BOUND this error rather than correct it
rests entirely on seasonal_phase_of_catchment_delivery being unrepresentable --
with a delivery phase the correction is computable and a bound is the wrong
instrument -- and that dependency lived only in prose.
`export_carve_list.LEDGER_ABSENCES_RELIED_ON` names it and the gate holds every
such name to a key under `absences:`. Fires both ways: on the absence being
renamed or closed, and on the declaration going missing.

This row should be closed as resolved with no change to the carve list. I
cannot close it under my brief.

title: Three pyburn derivation arms are unreachable and two label their output with another code's name
description:
Found in the world-2jj3 sweep of which codes pyburn derives versus finds in the
raw. Neither defect is an unbound name and neither was fixed there.

UNREACHABLE. natmcode (270), sruncode (271) and freshcode (275) each have a
derivation arm in dataset() and in advancedDataset(), and none of the three is a
key of pyburn.ilibrary. The head of the per-key loop raises 'Unknown variable
code requested' before any arm is reached, so net atmospheric radiation, surface
runoff-to-bucket and precip-plus-evap cannot be asked for at all. The arms
compute them correctly; they are simply not addressable.

MISLABELLED. swatmcode (268) and lwatmcode (269) are ilibrary keys, but they are
keyed as ['icez','glacier_geopotential','m2 s-2'] and
['netz','net_geopotential','m2 s-2']. Both codes are also written by the model
into the raw -- they are in run_67323a923013's high-cadence stream -- so the
'already present' branch takes them and the shortwave/longwave net-atmospheric
arms are dead. A caller asking for 268 gets the glacier geopotential under the
name icez, which is what the model wrote and is NOT what the arm below it
computes. The collision is silent in both directions.

MEASURED on run_67323a923013's raw and on pyburn's own tables; no model run.

Establish which numbering is right before repairing either. burn7's code table
is the upstream authority and the fork has diverged from it in places, so a fix
that renumbers 268/269 to free them for swatm/lwatm changes what every existing
namelist in the tree means.
assignee: Every derivation arm in pyburn is reachable by the code it is written for, no two codes share a name, and the disposition of 268/269 is recorded against burn7's table rather than chosen.
close_reason: Resolved and committed (7821ebf69, 20c4a8064, 923390a7a). world-hs5z: _resolvekey handles code, string and name in both loops, repaired rather than refused because both docstrings promise all three and the fork is hard; also closed a gap the row did not name, run-time ilibrary rows answering to their code but not their name. world-e9yz: all five arms deleted, settled from outmod.f90 rather than burn7, each being an exact combination of addressable codes; 268/269 were not merely dead but fired and stored rst-rss as icez in m2 s-2. world-k5db: 229 dwmax and 101-107 named from the model's own source, and the outdiag collision guarded at both ends with the Fortran renumber filed as world-2v9z.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
FIXED BY DELETION, ALL FIVE ARMS, AND THE NUMBERING QUESTION IS SETTLED BY THE
MODEL RATHER THAN BY burn7.

VERIFIED FIRST. 27 arms in dataset() and the same 27 in advancedDataset;
exactly three of their codes -- 270, 271, 275 -- are not ilibrary keys, and no
two ilibrary entries share a name. Both halves of the row hold. Two facts it
did not have:

  - the three unreachable arms are broken twice over. Each opens with
    meta = ilibrary[key][:], so even reached they would raise KeyError.
  - the 268/269 arms are not merely dead. On a raw that does not carry those
    records they FIRE: dataset(raw,["268"]) reached the shortwave arm and
    would have stored rst - rss under the name icez in units of m2 s-2.
    Reproduced on the synthetic raw before the change.

WHICH NUMBERING IS RIGHT: THIS MODEL'S. outmod.f90 writes glacier elevation as
268 and ground-plus-glacier elevation as 269, unconditionally, from all three
record writers -- outgp (unit 40), snapshotgp (140) and hcadencegp (141/142) --
and ilibrary names them icez and netz to match. The raw is the authority for
what a code means in it, so burn7's swatm and lwatm lose. Nothing was
renumbered and no namelist in the tree changed meaning.

WHY DELETED RATHER THAN GIVEN LIBRARY ROWS. Each of the five is an exact
arithmetic combination of codes that ARE addressable, so nothing is lost and no
name had to be invented:

  268 shortwave net in atmosphere = 178 - 176
  269 longwave net in atmosphere  = 179 - 177
  270 net atmospheric radiation   = 261 - 262
  275 precipitation + evaporation = 260 + 182
  271 water added to the bucket   = 260 + 182 - 221

271 is the clearest: its own arm carried the comment that actual runoff is
precip + evap + melt + soil water - bucket max, which is not what it computed,
and code 160 is the model's own surface runoff. Adding three rows would have
meant inventing three names and three unit strings for quantities with no
consumer, in a table other code indexes by name.

WHAT THE DIVERGENCE COSTS: nothing in merge terms. ExoPlaSim is a HARD FORK as
of 2026-08-21 (docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md) and pulling upstream
is not expected to be possible again, so this is decided on this project's
terms alone. A repair worth sending upstream has to be written for upstream
separately, and for 268/269 there is nothing to send: upstream's own model
writes glacier elevation there.

THE CHECKS ENUMERATE THE ARMS AGAINST THE TABLES, in both directions.
verify_high_cadence_rescue.py goes from 13 cases to 20; two of the new ones are
this row:

  every derivation is reachable by the code it is written for
      -- every arm's code is an ilibrary key, and no two entries share a name.
         Satisfied by deleting the arm OR by adding the row; what it refuses is
         the state that was there.
  no derivation shadows a code the model writes itself
      -- an arm for a code the model puts in the raw can never run, because the
         already-present branch takes it first, and the arm and the library row
         disagree about what the code IS. The model source is the other half of
         the pair, which is what makes this checkable rather than a restatement.

PROVED ABLE TO FAIL, by putting each defect back:
  a 270 arm with no library row -> FAIL, "dataset has a derivation arm for code
                                   270 (natmcode) and it is not an ilibrary
                                   key, so no request can reach it"
  a 268 arm on this model's 268 -> FAIL, "dataset derives code 268, which the
                                   model writes into the raw itself"
Both checks also report a dispatch line their parser cannot read, so an arm
written as key=="270" rather than key==str(natmcode) fails them rather than
being invisible to them -- proved by injecting exactly that.

A THIRD SHAPE THIS ROW DOES NOT NAME, found in the same sweep and fixed here:
an arm whose INPUT records are absent from the raw raised a bare KeyError from
the middle of the per-key loop, naming neither the variable requested nor the
reason, and took every variable that would have followed with it.
dataset(raw,["260"]) on a stream with no precipitation records is the whole
reproduction. That is the disposition world-2jj3 settled for a code with no arm
at all, and it gets the same answer for the same reason: the default request
when no namelist is given is EVERY key in ilibrary, which is the request the
high-cadence conversion makes. pyburn._DERIVATION_INPUTS now declares what each
arm reads, a missing input is reported and the arm skipped, and a case holds
the table against the arms in both directions.

title: A climatology built from spin-up orbits now refuses, and needs a declared record count if one is ever wanted
description:
world-jqm4 made lib/climatology.py refuse an evenly spaced time axis over an even bin count, because such an axis is genuinely ambiguous: 36 records at dt 160 and 18 at dt 320 produce a bit-identical axis and nothing in the file separates them.

THE ONE LIVE CONSEQUENCE. The first output file of most runs is an NLOWIO = 1 spin-up orbit, whose centres are evenly spaced. build_climatology.py calls bin_weights per source file, so a climatology built from spin-up orbits now REFUSES where it previously returned equal weights, which were wrong whenever the record count landed in the alternating class.

That is the right answer today and this row is not a request to soften it. Such a product is separately tainted -- the first record of each orbit is corrupt and the winds are vector-cancelled at NLOWIO = 1 -- and build_climatology.py already stamps it so consumers can refuse. Nothing in the pipeline builds one deliberately.

If one is ever wanted, the route already exists and does not involve relaxing the refusal: bin_weights, annual_mean, annual_mean_of and masked_mean take an optional ntimes, and the declaration is checked against the centres for bin pattern and gap shape before use. build_climatology.py should read the record count from the run's namelist and pass it, so the count is DECLARED from the run rather than inferred from an axis that cannot carry it.

Filed because the world-jqm4 agent surfaced it and had no authority to create rows, and because an untracked 'worth checking' loop is what the no-poison-seeds convention exists to prevent.
acceptance_criteria: Either build_climatology.py declares the record count from the run's namelist when a source file's axis is ambiguous, or this row is closed with a statement that a spin-up climatology is never wanted and the refusal is the whole answer.

title: Re-seed the world-5oyp soil thermal pair from a settled donor
description:
The measured pair -- run_ae5aaf479f57 against run_8f75d23c0730 -- branched from run_14906cb7b914's MOST_REST.00034 at 35 orbits, which is not settled: both arms drift together for all 50 orbits and neither passes assess_convergence.py --assess diagnostic. Failure-modes class 37 says a bar taken on an unsettled donor buys a wrong REFUSAL rather than a wrong number.

Nothing resolved by that pair is at risk, since a smaller bar only resolves it further. One refusal is: global-mean ts separates by +0.097 +/- 0.037 K against a bar of 0.104, a refusal taken at 0.93 of its threshold, and class 37 records standard errors of 0.017 to 0.031 K for arms of this length seeded from a settled donor. tas already resolves at +0.240 +/- 0.034 K and the term's own quantity, the land seasonal range, resolves at 9.8 to 1, so this changes no verdict that has been taken -- it decides whether the surface temperature separation is small or was merely unmeasurable.

What settles it: the same two arm configs, exoplasim/analysis/arms/jsfm_interp.yaml and jsfm_const.yaml, seeded from run_893e276ee029, the settled 210-orbit baseline on canonical-10m-base, at whatever length the new donor's own scatter prices. One binary, one restart, four landmod_nl keys apart, segments diagnostic.

Cites exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md, the world-5oyp measured section, and docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md class 37.

title: config2xml.py does not parse, and nothing has ever called it
description:
vendor/cgenie/genie-main/config2xml.py raises SyntaxError at line 27 -- a missing comma after "ma_flag_ichem" : ["ichem",".FALSE.","ci"] -- so ast.parse refuses the file. Verified on current main.

It is a Python 2 legacy converter from the old ASCII .config format to the XML one, and nothing invokes it: no makefile, no genie.job, no shell script in the tree. The only trace of it is a provenance string in three shipped configs' author attribute, recording that they were produced by it once.

Its flag map is also incomplete against the tree it would convert: ma_flag_plasimatmos is absent, and so is ma_flag_fluxatmos, which world-e3gp added. So even repaired it would silently drop the two atmosphere flags that matter here.

THIS IS WORLD-YWA8'S SHAPE, and the question is the same one: ASK WHETHER IT SHOULD EXIST BEFORE FIXING IT. Deleting is a fix. A converter for a format this project does not use, which does not parse, which nothing calls, and whose flag map cannot express the current recipe is a candidate for deletion rather than for a comma. The danger of leaving it is the one world-ywa8 names: its name makes it look like the route from a .config to a runnable job, which is what the next reader looking for that route will try.

If it stays, it needs the comma AND the two missing flags AND a caller, or it is the same row again next year.

Found by the world-e3gp agent while working genie-main. Source: notes/audits/cgenie-embm-free-path-and-threading.md

title: provenance.py rebuilds the registry's name index and takes the last duplicate
description:
lib/provenance.py:778 builds its own inverse index over the terrain registry:

    named = {v['name']: k for k, v in _KNOWN_TERRAIN_HASHES.items()}

WORLD-0B83 added the same index to lib/orogen.py as registry_entry(name=...), built once at import and RAISING on a duplicate name, because a name addresses both a source/<name>/ directory and a <component>/data/<name>/ one, so two entries sharing a name is an ambiguity nothing downstream can resolve. The dict comprehension above silently takes the LAST entry instead.

CLAUDE.md's lib/ list exists to make this answerable: orogen.py owns the export and the build registry, and reuse rather than reimplement is the rule the list is there to serve. Two indexes over one registry is two things to keep in step, and they already disagree on the case that matters.

DO: have provenance.py call orogen.registry_entry(name=...). Check for other in-place inversions of _KNOWN_TERRAIN_HASHES while there -- this one was found by a sweep that was not looking for it, so it is not evidence that it is the only one.

Found by the world-0b83 agent while re-checking its routed defects against current main.

title: Four consumers reach a build without the registry's verdict on it
description:
WORLD-0B83 made the registry's refusal a declared field and gave check_consistency.py a 'build activatable' row that reads it. That guard covers ONE route: config/planet.yaml's source_build, read at gate time. Four consumers reach a build by another route and none consults the registry.

1. minerals/scripts/build_prospectivity.py:102 and pedology/scripts/weathering_fluxes.py:161 take --source-build, which overwrites config['source_build'] IN MEMORY after the guard has run. Each then writes into <component>/data/<that build>/ and stamps source_build with it, so a product made on a refused build lands beside a production one with nothing distinguishing them. That is the batch-P0C shape exactly, and P0C is what world-0b83 cites as the cost of not knowing which build is active.

2. analysis/ice_mask_freezing_height.py:68 takes --build, an export root defaulting to the configured build and overridable to anything. Same shape.

3. scripts/world_state.py:90, builds(), reports the active build with no reference to its registry entry. Materially wrong on the tree as it stands rather than theoretical: config names precarve-craton-10m, the registry refuses it, and world_state.json is the file everything quotes the current build from.

READING A REFUSED BUILD IS LEGAL AND MUST STAY LEGAL -- notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md measured one, and a result is only readable while its build is still recognised, which is why world-0b83 kept registration and activation separate. So the fix is not a refusal at the flag. It is that the ARTIFACT should say so: a product built on a refused build carries a stamp naming the refusal, and world_state.json reports the verdict beside the build rather than the build alone. Then a comparison product cannot be mistaken for a production one at the point where that mistake is actually made, which is reading the artifact months later.

Source: world-0b83, re-checked against current main after that row landed.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
2026-08-30 THREE OF FOUR CONSUMERS DONE. lib/provenance.py:build_stamp is the
one place that says what a product records about its build, and it carries
three states rather than two: registered and activatable; registered and
REFUSED, with the registry's own words quoted; and never registered at all,
which is not a refusal and must not read as one.

  minerals/scripts/build_prospectivity.py  report carries build_verdict
  analysis/ice_mask_freezing_height.py     report carries build_verdict
  scripts/world_state.py                   world_state.json carries it beside
                                           the active build, regenerated

Reading a refused build stays legal at every one of them; nothing was turned
into a refusal at the flag.

STILL OPEN: pedology/scripts/weathering_fluxes.py:161, the fourth consumer,
same --source-build shape. Not done because another change was in flight in
pedology/scripts at the time and two concurrent edits to one file is how a
last-writer-wins defect gets made. It is a one-line addition of the same stamp

Also worth noting for whoever finishes it: check_consistency.py's existing
"build activatable" row is unchanged and still guards the config route. The
stamp is additive and does not replace it.
