title: The Li et al. (1992) PDF is filed under another paper's slug
description:
references/li1992-parameterization-of-cloud-optical-properties.pdf IS Li, Frolking and Frolking (1992), A model of nitrous oxide evolution from soil driven by rainfall events: 1. Model structure and sensitivity, J. Geophys. Res. 97(D9) 9759-9776, 10.1029/92JD00509. Verified from the PDF's own title page and its embedded Title and Author metadata before it was read.

The slug belongs to a DIFFERENT Li et al. (1992), on the parameterization of cloud optical properties. INDEX.md's convention is <firstauthor><year><suffix>-<slug>.pdf and this file breaks it, in the direction failure-mode class 9 is about: a reader who greps the filename concludes the project holds a radiation paper it does not, and a reader looking for the nitrous oxide model concludes it is missing and re-fetches.

Do: rename to li1992-a-model-of-nitrous-oxide-evolution-from-soil.pdf in the MAIN checkout (references/ PDFs are untracked and symlinked into worktrees, so a worktree cannot do it), then update the three places that name the file: references/INDEX.md, biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml's calibration.sources.li1992, and this issue.

Both INDEX.md and ntransform.yaml currently carry the wrong name deliberately, each with a line saying so, so that nothing re-fetches on the strength of it. Remove those lines with the rename.

Evidence: references/INDEX.md, the Li row.
close_reason: FIXED in the main checkout. Renamed to li1992-a-model-of-nitrous-oxide-evolution-from-soil.pdf and references/INDEX.md updated; the row now records that it arrived under another paper's slug rather than warning that it still carries one.

title: An adoption decision for any cgenie component states which calibration switches are off
description:
vendor/cgenie/genie-rokgem/src/fortran/rokgem_lib.f90:207-285 declares
opt_calibrate_T_0D, _R_0D, _P_0D, calibrate_weath, four calibrate_weather_*
factors and opt_calibrate_T_2D, _R_2D, _P_2D, with par_data_T_0D, par_data_R_0D
and par_data_P_0D as the Earth global means to calibrate to and par_ref_T0_2D,
par_ref_R0_2D, par_ref_P0_2D as Earth pattern files to reproduce.

This is not a list of constants. It is machinery whose PURPOSE is to rescale
modelled temperature, runoff and productivity until they match Earth
observations, with the reference patterns shipped as data files. It is the
most concentrated instance of the class anywhere in the tree, and
notes/audits/ocean-tier-implicit-earth.md does not reach it.

Beside it, references/INDEX.md's Holden et al. (2016) entry records three more
in the same family's ocean coupling: scf, which that paper states is "a TUNED
ensemble parameter, not a regridding artifact and not derivable from a
stress-product ratio"; an Atlantic-Pacific moisture flux adjustment set against
Talley (2008) basin budgets; and energy flux corrections diagnosed against
observed present-day sea-ice thickness.

NOT A FIX, A PRECONDITION. cgenie is the candidate under OCN-3, nothing reads
it, and it does not build where it stands, so none of these is in the world's
numbers today. What this issue asks for is that any adoption decision for a
cgenie component states, before the component is wired to anything, which
calibration switches are off, which factors are at 1.0, and which reference
files are absent -- so that the answer is not discovered from a result.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md
notes:
2026-08-26, TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW'S OWN PREMISE, and one path discharged.

THE PREMISE IS OUT OF DATE. This row says "cgenie is the candidate under OCN-3,
nothing reads it, and it does not build where it stands". OCN-3 closed on
adoption on 2026-08-26, and it DOES build and run here: the world-e3gp work
built and ran it four times, and both shipped regression cases pass bit-for-bit.
What remains true and is the load-bearing half is that nothing READS it -- OCN-5
owns adding the loop to config/pipeline.yaml, and until that lands an artifact
no step generates does not exist.

WORLD-E3GP DISCHARGED THIS ROW FOR ITS OWN PATH, before wiring rather than
after, which is the order this row asks for. The driven surface-flux path
reaches only genie-goldstein and genie-goldsteinseaice; `grep calibrate` over
both returns nothing and genie-rokgem -- the concentrated instance this row was
filed about -- is not reachable from it. Two things the path does carry are
declared in notes/audits/cgenie-embm-free-path-and-threading.md section 1f: scf
shipped at 2.00 against definition.xml's own "plausible range 1 to 3" with three
fitted values beside it (1.6674 EnKF, 1.1841 ACCPM, 1.3005 NSGA-II), entering
linearly at goldstein.F:199-205 so any sweep returns OCN-17's bracket rather
than a number; and delta_flux, the residual by which the surface solve fails to
conserve, computed and dropped on a driven path because there is no atmosphere
to hand it back to -- a diagnostic the forcing contract may read and never a
correction.

WHAT THIS ROW STILL OWES is every OTHER component: rokgem's opt_calibrate_T/R/P
family in both 0-D and 2-D with its Earth reference patterns, and the three in
Holden et al. (2016)'s ocean coupling. Each needs the same declaration before
it is wired to anything.

title: Record the tuning knobs that are dormant, with the switch that arms each
description:
A tuning no run reaches costs nothing today and costs everything on the day
someone throws its switch. oceanmod's Earth radius is the precedent: dormant at
NHDIFF=0, under a scheduled A/B that would have returned arms wrong by 1.44 with
nothing in the output to say so, and the CLIM-16 bracket that had already run
needed relabelling after the fact.

The inert set, from notes/audits/tuned-values.md section 18, each with what arms
it:

| where | value | armed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| radmod.f90:76 | tpofmt 1.00, self-declared "tuning of point of mean transmittance" | nothing. It sits at its identity, no run sets it, and it is a live multiplier at :3591 with no source, so any run that moves it moves an unsourced knob |
| carbonmod.f90:97-98 | tune1 5.41, tune2 2.20, "Tuning adjustment to make global average match" | NCARBON = 1 |
| hurricanemod.f90:50-114 | the empirical pLCL parameters and CL, which the header calls an admitted fudge | the diagnostic switch; run_exoplasim.py:2629 already refuses it on these grounds |
| simba.f90 | Earth-fitted throughout, turnover times scaled by the ORBITAL period | NVEG = 1 |

| pyburn.py:2003, :2843 | tstar[tstar<255] = 0.5*(255+tstar), ECMWF's cold-surface guard, calibrated on Earth's surface temperature distribution | anything reading psl. Nothing does yet, and at 32 degrees of obliquity the guard fires over a large share of land for much of the orbit |

oceanmod case expensive: each row above gets a line at its declaration naming
the switch and the fact that the value is a tuning, so that whoever throws the

the one that also wants a decision, because a knob at its identity with no
source is a key that should either be sourced or removed.

Evidence: notes/audits/tuned-values.md
notes:
2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER, from a pass over the needs-decision set.
RECLASSIFIED, source it. The dormant knobs get their declaration lines; tpofmt is sourced or removed rather than left at its identity.

title: smoke_test's unbound-name pass prints a wall of SyntaxWarnings from the vendored model Python
description:
`check_no_unbound_names` compiles every .py under vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim to ask CPython's symbol table which loaded names nothing binds. Compiling `makestellarspec.py` and `pyburn.py` emits about twenty SyntaxWarnings for invalid escape sequences (\\l, \\* in non-raw strings), twice over, on every run of the gate. They are byproduct: the gate's own verdict lines are then buried, and a reader learns to scroll past a gate's stderr, which is the habit a gate exists to prevent.

Two candidate fixes and they are not equivalent. Fixing the escapes in the vendored source is the real one and it is an upstream-facing edit under vendor/exoplasim. Suppressing the category around the compile call is cheap but hides a real (if harmless) defect class from every future reader.

Found while splitting the per-unit subprocess passes out of smoke_test (world-hb7z). Not folded into that work because it is a change to what the vendored source SAYS, not to where a gate runs.

title: cos(lat) is used as an area weight on Gaussian rows in about thirty places
description:
Found while settling world-yolx, and it is a FOURTH area weight rather than another instance of that row's defect.

About thirty sites take a global or land mean over an ExoPlaSim Gaussian grid with 'np.cos(np.deg2rad(lat))' as the weight. cos(lat) is not a partition of the sphere: it is the metric factor of an equal-angle band, and a Gaussian row does not have one. Against the quadrature weights it is wide in the polar row by 1.767 per cent at T21, 1.796 at T42, 1.805 at T85 and 1.808 at T170, converging to about 1.81 and not to zero, and 0.39 per cent in the second row. The interior converges normally: 0.0292 per cent median at T21 down to 0.0009 at T170.

WHAT IT IS WORTH, so the decision is informed rather than assumed. Measured on source/precarve-craton/exoplasim-T42/planet.nc: the global land fraction moves 0.0088 per cent and the land-mean elevation -0.0062 per cent. That is two orders below anything those scripts quote, because the two polar rows hold 0.178 per cent of the sphere at T42 and the error is diluted by that share. So this is not urgent and it is not what world-yolx was about, where the same class of error was 22 per cent in the export's own cell-area field and 5.8 per cent in pedology's local one.

IT IS STILL WRONG, and the fix is cheap because the right answer is already in the tree in two forms: about thirty OTHER sites recompute 'leggauss(nlat)[1][::-1]' in place and are correct, and lib/gridding.py:export_grid now constructs an export grid's cell boundaries from its manifest. The highest-leverage single site is exoplasim/scripts/build_climatology.py:229, which is the project's headline climatology summary and weights every global and land seasonal mean with cos(lat).

Do: replace cos(lat) with the quadrature weight at every site that means an AREA WEIGHT, leaving alone the sites where cos(lat) is a metric term rather than a weight -- aeolian/scripts/build_dust.py's advection dx, maps/build_basemap.py's polar-convergence blur and east-west spacing, and lib/gridding.py's KD-tree points are metric and must not be touched. Prefer one shared accessor over a thirty-first in-place leggauss.

Sites, area-weight use only: exoplasim/scripts/build_climatology.py:229; build_surface_dust.py:213,274; build_surface_soil_water.py:240; compare_equilibria.py:187; dust_forcing.py:510; shortwave_band_weights.py:832,872; spectral_tail.py:123; hydrography/scripts/carve_verdict.py:376, export_carve_list.py:990, surface_water.py:744; pedology/scripts/build_soil.py:786, probe_runoff_response.py:159; biosphere/scripts/build_lpj_driver.py:293, score_prediction.py:105; analysis/emissivity_contrast.py:164,188, snow_albedo_zenith.py:96; aeolian/scripts/build_dust.py:195,741, build_dust_source_fields.py:471, build_sea_salt.py:216, build_volcanic_sulfate.py:183,262, aerosol_deposition.py:113, dust_intensity_levers.py:196,332. Re-locate each by content; line numbers drift.

Source: notes/audits/ocean-grid-crossing.md section 3, and source/README.md's weighting rule, which now names cos(lat) as a fourth thing that is none of the three.

title: Take dzu out of ocean.cmn: velc no longer uses the COMMON member and nothing else ever did
description:
ocean.cmn declares dzu(2,maxk) in /ocn_vars/. velc was its only reader and writer anywhere in the tree, and initialise_goldstein.F:524-525 only zeroes it. Threading velc over j made it a local, dzu_col, because one array in a COMMON block is one array for the whole process and would have been shared between the threads.

The COMMON member is now written by nothing and read by nothing. Removing it changes the block's layout in every file that includes the header, which is why it was left in place rather than taken out in the threading commit.

Do: delete dzu from ocean.cmn's declaration and from the /ocn_vars/ list, delete the zeroing in initialise_goldstein.F, and check the two commented-out crma declarations above it while there. Acceptance is analysis/cgenie_omp.py's bit-for-bit test on both shipped regression cases.

title: Decide whether surf_ocn_sic should exist: compiled, wrapped, and called by nothing
description:
genie-goldstein/src/fortran/surf_ocn_sic.F describes itself as a surflux routine for models using only c-GOLDSTEIN's ocean and sea-ice modules. It is in genie-goldstein's makefile, it has surf_ocn_sic_wrapper in genie_loop_wrappers.f90, and no line of genie.F calls that wrapper. outm_surf_ocn_sic.f and gold_ocnsic_avg.F exist to serve it.

It is not the driven path this project wants and that is settled: it takes atmospheric STATE -- lowest-level temperature, humidity, pressure, height and winds -- and computes the turbulent fluxes from bulk formulae on the OCEAN grid, and derives the wind stress from the lowest-level winds itself. A surface flux is nonlinear in the state, so that is the coarse-grid evaluation the offline exchange exists to avoid.

So the question is whether it goes. It is roughly 800 lines plus its output and averaging routines, it is the IGCM3 coupling this project does not use, and the danger of leaving it is that its name makes it look like the answer to the next reader asking how to drive GOLDSTEIN without an atmosphere. Deleting is a fix; ask what breaks if it simply goes.

Source: notes/audits/cgenie-embm-free-path-and-threading.md section 1c

title: The convergence verdict has two names in two places, and reading the file for the stdout's key returns None
description:
assess_convergence.py writes the run's verdict twice under different vocabularies. The FILE, exoplasim/analysis/convergence/<run>_convergence.json, carries completed_orbits and sufficiently_equilibrated_for_worldbuilding. The STDOUT payload carries orbits and pass. Same facts, different keys, and json.load on the file returns None for both stdout names with no error.

That is a silent wrong answer rather than a crash, and it is the shape this project treats as worst: a consumer keying on  reads None, and None is falsy, so a converged run reads as not converged and nothing complains. The coordinator hit exactly this today on run_ec32946bec89 -- read the file, got orbits None and pass None on a run whose six criteria were all true, and spent a diagnosis on a defect that was not there.

Do: decide which vocabulary is canonical and make both artifacts speak it, or have the file carry both names for one value. Prefer the file's names if either -- completed_orbits and sufficiently_equilibrated_for_worldbuilding say what they mean, where  does not say pass what -- and note that the stdout payload also carries , the path to the file, so the two are already linked in one direction. Check for readers of either name before renaming; scripts/world_state.py and the pipeline's convergence steps are the places to look. Evidence: exoplasim/scripts/assess_convergence.py:658 (report) and :789 (payload)

title: build_sea_salt.py --climatology does not cover the snapshot resolver, and both aerosol steps name the wrong climatology
description:
Two small things found while making the sea-salt deposition carrier run at all (world-hfsm).

1. config/pipeline.yaml gives the sea_salt, volcanic_sulfate and dust steps needs: [bootstrap_climatology, ...], but build_sea_salt.py, build_volcanic_sulfate.py and build_dust.py all resolve their input through lib/paths.py:climatology_path(), which reads config/planet.yaml's baseline_climatology and refuses to fall back. So the graph says one thing and the scripts do another, and the scripts cannot run at all until a baseline is declared. Either the steps need bootstrap_climatology because loop A runs them before a baseline exists, in which case the scripts should resolve the bootstrap, or they need the baseline, in which case the graph is wrong. It is one fact and it is currently stated twice, differently.

2. build_sea_salt.py --climatology overrides the regular climatology but not the SNAPSHOT one: solve() calls snapshot_climatology_path() for the Weibull fit when --gust-samples is absent, and that resolver raises the same SystemExit. So the escape hatch is half an escape hatch and a caller has to know to pass both flags.

Neither is urgent and neither is a wrong number. Evidence: aeolian/scripts/build_sea_salt.py main() and solve(), config/pipeline.yaml steps dust, sea_salt and volcanic_sulfate.

title: The code 129 exclusion under NGLACIER != 1 is wider than the reason it was given
description:
restart_surface.py:not_comparable withdraws code 129 whenever NGLACIER is not 1. The reason it carried was that glaciermod's oroini leaves groundoro at zero because the scaling line sat inside the nglacier branch, and that reading does not hold: glacierini's cold branch sets groundoro(:) = doro(:) BEFORE the nglacier switch (glaciermod.f90:182), and nothing else writes groundoro except the restart read and the mpputgp that publishes it. So under NGLACIER = 0 the restart's groundsg is the staged field exactly, the same as under NGLACIER = 1.

What does change under NGLACIER = 0 is the OTHER half: glacieroro stays zero, oroini does not rebuild doro from groundoro, and the doro record is the spectrally fitted staged field rather than groundsg + dglacsg. So the pair of records the code 129 check reads means something different, which is a real reason to withdraw the check -- but it is not the reason the code states and it may not require withdrawing the groundsg comparison at all.

Do: establish what groundsg holds under NGLACIER = 0 against the artifact, then either narrow the exclusion to the doro identity alone and keep comparing groundsg, or restate the reason. This project runs NGLACIER = 1, so nothing is currently mis-reported; the defect is that a gate would refuse for a reason that is not true.

Discovered from world-6qee, whose fix moved the line the old reason cited.
close_reason:
THE EXCLUSION IS REMOVED RATHER THAN NARROWED, and the answer is wider than this row expected: NGLACIER takes neither half of code 129 away.

groundoro is written in exactly two places in the whole model -- glacierini's cold branch, BEFORE the switch, and the restart read -- so groundsg is the staged field times oroscale under either setting. Measured on run_57cecaa8391b: groundsg equals the staged N032_surf_0129.sra on all 2,048 cells at a maximum absolute difference of 0.0, dglacsg is nonzero on 411, and doro == groundsg + dglacsg on every cell.

THE doro IDENTITY IS NOT BROKEN UNDER NGLACIER = 0 EITHER, which is the half this row expected to survive as the real reason. oroini is only ever called from inside the nglacier block, so glacieroro stays at its declared zero and doro stays the field glacierini read from the .sra. The identity therefore holds trivially rather than failing -- it is UNINFORMATIVE there, not wrong, and an uninformative check that passes is not a reason to stop making it.

So the row's premise was right that the stated reason does not hold, and its proposed remedy -- narrow the exclusion to the doro identity -- turned out to be unnecessary as well.

title: The high-cadence stream carries the same partial-window temperature extrema the snapshot stream just dropped
description:
Worldbuilding: this is about what ExoPlaSim writes for Vesper's high-cadence wind stream, not about weather anywhere real.

outmod.f90:hcadencegp writes tempmin and tempmax at codes 320 and 321 to whichever unit its caller passes, 141 or 142. Those are the running extrema outaccu extends every timestep and only outreset clears, and outreset runs after outgp on the REGULAR cadence, so a high-cadence record covers (nstep mod nafter) timesteps: a window that varies record to record and is empty on the record after a regular write. That is exactly the defect world-adxx removed from snapshotgp.

It is filed separately rather than fixed with adxx because the argument that settled adxx does not transfer. adxx rested on every OTHER field in the snapshot stream being an instantaneous sample; the high-cadence stream is not that shape -- it writes asigrain at code 319, which is an accumulation cleared by the same outreset, so the stream already mixes accumulations with samples and the same question is open for 319.

Nothing is at stake today. The stream is off by default (nhcadence and nwritehurricane both 0), this project does not enable it, and its declared field list is the winds for DUST-5, per the world-4vp comment in plasim.f90. No product carries 320, 321 or 319 from unit 141 or 142.

Do: settle what the high-cadence stream IS -- a sample stream, in which case 319, 320 and 321 come out, or a stream with its own accumulation window, in which case it needs its own reset and the restart records that go with it. Either way state it where the stream is declared. Deciding it before DUST-5 turns the stream on is cheaper than deciding it from the output.

Source: vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/outmod.f90:hcadencegp; world-adxx.
close_reason:
SETTLED: the high-cadence stream is a SAMPLE stream. Codes 320 and 321 come out, and 319 becomes the instantaneous rate snapshotgp computes rather than the asigrain accumulator, so every field in the stream is the state at the step it is written on.

The alternative -- a stream with its own accumulation window -- would mean a second accumulator set, a second reset and a second pair of restart records, bought for a consumer that has not asked: the declared field list is DUST-5's winds. Deciding it before the stream is turned on is what made it cost nothing, which is the row's own argument and it holds.

The decision and the rejected alternative are stated where the stream is declared, so the next reader does not re-derive them.

A BUG FOUND AND FIXED IN THE SAME ROUTINE: writegp(kunit,dsnow,kunit,0) passed the unit number as the code, so the snow depth came out correct on unit 141 and labelled 142 on the hurricane unit.

title: analyze_smoke.py reads a staged surface field without the door, and the door has no rung argument
description:
world-z7bu routed the four remaining code-174 readers through
`lib/provenance.py:staged_surface_field`. A sweep of every construction of a
path under `exoplasim/inputs/` found one more reader it does not cover, and one
place the path is built legitimately.

THE READER. `exoplasim/scripts/analyze_smoke.py` reads staged code 0129, the
geopotential, to compare the supplied topography against the model's own:

    supplied_elevation = _sra.read_sra(
        INPUTS / res.lower() / f"orogen_{res}_surf_0129.sra", ...) / gravity

Same class as the five already closed: the path is keyed by the rung alone, the
build that staged it is unrecorded, and the comparison it feeds says nothing
about which build's topography it read.

WHY IT IS NOT A THREE-LINE CHANGE. `res` here comes from the RUN being analysed
(`rungs.rung_of_latitudes(lat.size)`) and deliberately not from the config -- a
smoke run at one rung once read another rung's files, which is SPAT-2.
`staged_surface_field` takes the rung from `config["model"]["resolution"]`, so
routing this through it as written would reintroduce exactly that. The door
needs to accept a rung, and whether that is an argument or a second entry point
is the decision.

NOT A DEFECT, recorded so the next sweep does not re-raise it:
`run_exoplasim.py:surface_sra` builds the same path, and that is the STAGING
step itself -- the one place the path is legitimately constructed rather than
resolved. `stability_probe.py`'s `INPUTS / rung.lower()` appears only inside an
error message and reads nothing.

Do: give `staged_surface_field` a way to be asked for a rung other than the
config's, and route analyze_smoke.py through it. Then consider whether the class
can be closed by a lint -- "no consumer builds a path under exoplasim/inputs" --
which needs the writers and the stager enumerated first.

title: analysis/spectral_tail.json carries a tail slope no run backs
description: world-qzcb changed how spectral_tail.py fits the tail slope: it now ends the fit at the last wavenumber standing clear of the measured roundoff floor rather than at the truncation. exoplasim/analysis/spectral_tail.json was written before that and its tail_slope is the old fit; the run it names, run_ef2169a0f038, is no longer on disk, so it cannot be regenerated. The file's bite_wavenumber, peak_excess and verdict are unaffected, because neither criterion changed. Do: regenerate the file on the next T42 run whose spectrum is wanted, or delete it. Nothing reads it today.

title: A four-byte arm's run cannot be continued: restart_surface.py hard-codes real*8
description:
exoplasim/scripts/restart_surface.py:302 sizes a restart record as 8*months*ncells and refuses anything else: 'restart record is 8192 bytes, expected 16384 for 1 x 2048 real*8'. That is what a T21 run integrated by a --precision 4 arm produces, so continue_exoplasim.py refuses every segment after the first on such a run. Observed 2026-08-25 continuing run_9592a038a1c0, whose arm is t21_l10_p16_production_real4; the arm itself was correctly restored into the run directory first, so this is the surface check and not the executable route.

The refusal is not wrong -- reading a four-byte record as eight would be silently garbage -- and the message says so. What is missing is that the record width is a property of the executable that wrote the file, and the run manifest now names that executable and its arm, so it is derivable rather than assumed.

CONSEQUENCE for clim-59: a four-byte spin-up has to be taken in one run_exoplasim.py --run-years N call, because it cannot be resumed. That is workable at T21 and is a hazard at any rung where a run has to be segmented.

Do: take the record width from the run's own executable rather than from a literal -- the manifest's executable.arm.build_tag carries 'real4' when it is a precision arm -- or state in the refusal that a precision arm is a known and unsupported case.

title: stability_probe.json's note asserts attribution the file may not have
description:
exoplasim/scripts/stability_probe.py rewrites the file's single 'note' field on every write, and at HEAD that note says each probe names the executable that produced it and that an entry without executable_sha256 predates that. The dedup key on write is (rung, dt_minutes, kappa), so a partial re-run replaces exactly the cells it re-took and leaves the rest beside them -- and the note then makes a claim about the file that is true of the new entries and false of the old ones. The per-entry discriminator survives; the file-level statement is what goes wrong.

The current file is the whole of that case: it was re-measured entire on 2026-08-24 (220b7142) and the probe learned to record its executable the next morning (8b68dc30), so all 60 entries carry no attribution while the note as written asserts otherwise for whatever is written next.

Do: make the file-level statement derivable rather than asserted -- write the count of attributed entries beside the note, or refuse to leave an unattributed entry in a file the same pass has just written to. Evidence and the sixteen decision-bearing cells: notes/audits/executable-provenance-at-the-consumer.md.

title: Nothing fails when config names a build the registry refuses
description:
config/planet.yaml:42 sets source_build: precarve-craton-10m while lib/orogen.py:166 marks that build NOT ACTIVATABLE AS IT STANDS, and nothing enforces either statement -- no gate reads the registry note, so a configured build the registry refuses runs silently.

The disagreement itself resolves on the planned regeneration: the 10M export was generated before PHYS-13, carries Earth-placed glacial ice, and is being regenerated with an ice mask before commissioning, which gives it a new terrain hash and a registry entry with no refusal on it.

What does NOT resolve on its own is the missing guard. Do: have scripts/check_consistency.py fail when source_build names a build whose registry entry is marked unactivatable, so the next time the two disagree the tree stops instead of measuring. Evidence for why it matters: batch P0C could not tell which build was active and measured the basin catalogue on both, and the answers differ in kind -- relaxing minCells adds 4,463 basins on precarve-craton and 8 on precarve-craton-10m, so whether the catalogue is resolution-limited is TRUE on one and FALSE on the other.
close_reason:
The registry's refusal is a declared field now, and check_consistency.py fails on it.

lib/orogen.py recorded five builds it will not have active as PROSE -- 'NOT ACTIVATABLE AS IT STANDS' in a comment, 'Do not use.' at the end of a note, 'SUPERSEDED by <hash>' inside three others -- which no gate can read, so a configured build the registry refuses ran silently. Entries now carry an optional refusal sentence; its ABSENCE is the only statement that a build may be named as source_build, and the five that carry one are withdrawn-basin-floor-drift, carved-zoned, carved-zoned-v2, carved-zoned-v4 and precarve-craton-10m. Registration is untouched and has to be: reading a refused build's export stays legal, because a result is only readable while the build it came from is still recognised.

The guard is check_consistency.py's 'build activatable' row, resolving by hash where there is an export to hash and by name otherwise so it still answers when the build is absent. Placed there and not in smoke_test.py because the tier is set by the cost of the STATE and not of the check: a refused build in config is a legitimate transient, and a per-commit gate that fails on it stops the commits that resolve it, while what must never happen is that the disagreement survives into something that MEASURES. An unregistered build gets WARN rather than FAIL, deliberately, because Export.__init__ already raises on an unregistered hash so that state is loud rather than silent.

THE GUARD LANDS RED ON THE TREE AS IT STANDS, which is correct and is the finding. config names precarve-craton-10m and every terrain row in check_consistency reads ab0d679bd81360cd -- basins.nc, all three coupling matrices, regions.nc, surface_water.nc and all four surface reports -- so the derived products have all been rebuilt on the refused build and the tree is INTERNALLY CONSISTENT ON IT. 'build activatable' is the only row in 48 that catches that, which is the batch-P0C shape standing in the tree today.

Shown red twice, each paired against a green control so a failure cannot be the check failing at everything: plain check_consistency reports the refusal, against the same run handed precarve-craton in memory which reports 'registry allows precarve-craton (by hash)'; and --self-test with activation_refusal stubbed to None reports 'a refused build fails activation: expected FAIL, got ok'. Baselines measured by checking the three files out to pristine main: 47 checks / 1 failed before, 48 / 2 after -- exactly one new check and one new failure. Verified on main after merge: smoke_test 43/0, --self-test 29/0, check_consistency 48 checks / 2 failed, the second being the pre-existing stale binaries.

THE DISAGREEMENT ITSELF IS NOT THIS ISSUE and is unresolved: it closes when the 10M export is regenerated with the ice mask fixed, giving a new terrain hash and an entry with no refusal, or when source_build is repointed. docs/src/reference/builds.md carries 'Registered is not the same as activatable either'. Merged to main as part of the batch-1 fan-out.

title: The dry closed-basin floor the catalogue misses is set by minAreaKm2 and does not close with region count
description:
CLAUDE.md rule 1 says reconstructing land as `land_mask | is_endorheic` misses the depressions too small to enter the basin catalogue. Measured by area on both registered builds, that residue is 1.286e6 km2 on precarve-craton and 1.157e6 km2 on precarve-craton-10m, 0.405 and 0.364 per cent of land.

The AREA is converged and the COUNT is not: four times the region count multiplies the missed pieces by 3.6, from 4,560 regions to 16,406, while leaving their total area within 10 per cent, because every newly resolved depression falls under the declared 1000 km2 area floor and none is kept. The deepest ground outside every preserved basin is -0.513 km against -0.591 km inside one, so this is ordinary dry basin floor in small pieces rather than shallow ground.

So the floor rule 1 warns about is a property of `minAreaKm2` and not of the mesh, and no finer generation closes it. Lowering the area floor would; nothing else will.

Do: decide whether 1000 km2 is the right landform floor for this planet, whose land area is roughly twice Earth's, or whether the residue is small enough to stand as a declared limit. Either answer wants writing down where the rule is stated, because the current wording says the catalogue has a floor without saying where it is.

Source: notes/audits/basin-catalogue-floor.md
notes:
2026-08-26, REOPENED. A NUMBER I GAVE THE AUTHOR WAS WRONG AND IT CHANGED THE
DECISION THEY TOOK ON IT. The close above rests on '285 km2 a mesh cell, so the
floor is three to four cells'. That is the 2.5M build's figure, carried over
from world-7vj6's text, not this one's.

THE MEASURED CELL AREAS, from this issue's own audit table
(notes/audits/basin-catalogue-floor.md):

  precarve-craton       2,500,001 regions    293.80 km2 a cell
  precarve-craton-10m  10,000,005 regions     73.45 km2 a cell

So at the active build 1000 km2 is 13.6 cells, not 3 to 4.

AND THERE IS A SECOND FLOOR THE CLOSE DID NOT MENTION. selectBasins keeps a
depression only if it clears BOTH minAreaKm2 and minCells, the latter 12
(terrain-config.js:562, commented 'resolution floor, not a size opinion'), and
basins.js:1376 publishes effectiveMinAreaKm2 = max(minAreaKm2, minCells * cell)
with bindingFloor naming which one bound. At 73.45 km2 a cell the cell floor
stands at 881.4 km2, so the area floor binds by 13 per cent and not by much.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE PROPOSAL OF 285 km2: it would be INERT. 285 is 3.9 cells,
far below the 12-cell floor, so setting it changes nothing at all -- minCells
takes over at 881.4 and the catalogue is identical. Any value below 881.4 has
that property at this build.

THE REACHABLE MOVE, and what it buys: lowering minAreaKm2 to the cell floor or
below adds 1,105 basins and about 9.9e5 km2, which is 86 per cent of the
1.157e6 km2 residue this row is about. That is the audit's own measurement of
relaxing the area floor at 10M.

THE COST, and it is the reason this is a decision rather than an obvious yes.
It inverts what hyd-20 closed on. At 10M the catalogue is currently
PHYSICS-LIMITED -- a fixed size in real km2 decides it -- and putting the area
floor at or below the cell floor makes it RESOLUTION-LIMITED again, so the floor
becomes a property of the build rather than of the planet and moves with every
regeneration. Going below 881.4 needs minCells lowered too, and minCells is what
gives a depression enough cells for basinHypsometry to build a capacity curve
from; capacity is what the carve criterion compares fill against, so a basin
with too few cells enters the catalogue with a curve nothing should trust.

THE THREE OPTIONS, stated so the choice is between named alternatives:
  1. KEEP 1000 km2. Physics-limited, 13 per cent above the cell floor, 0.364
     per cent of land declared as a limit.
  2. SET IT TO THE CELL FLOOR, 881.4 km2 at this build. Gains the 1,105 basins.
     The two floors coincide, so the catalogue becomes resolution-limited at
     this build and at every finer one.
  3. LOWER BOTH. Reaches below 881.4 and trades hypsometry reliability for
     catalogue completeness. Needs its own evidence about how few cells still
     gives a usable capacity curve; nothing measures that today.

source/README.md is corrected: it now carries both floors, both builds' cell
areas, the crossover, and the fact that a value below 881.4 is inert here.
close_reason:
2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S DECISION: BASIN_MIN_AREA_KM2 = 850. Landed in vendor/orogen/js/terrain-config.js:561.

WHAT IT DOES. selectBasins requires both this and BASIN_MIN_CELLS, so the binding floor is max(850, 12 * cell). At precarve-craton-10m the cell is 73.45 km2 and twelve of them are 881.4, so 850 is INERT at that build and the mesh decides; it binds at 10,369,311 regions and above, 3.7 per cent finer. The catalogue is therefore resolution-set at today's build and physics-set at any refinement of it, where the previous 1000 was the reverse -- binding by 13 per cent at 10M and never reached again above 8.81M.

WHAT IT BUYS, measured before the change: about 1,105 more basins and 9.9e5 km2 at 10M, 86 per cent of the 1.157e6 km2 that sat outside every preserved basin.

IT REACHES NOTHING UNTIL A GENERATION. A selection criterion enters a catalogue only through one, so both builds in source/ keep the 1000 km2 selection and source/README.md now says so rather than describing the tree as though the change had propagated.

A CLAIM THAT DEPENDED ON THE OLD FLOOR IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN LEFT. source/README.md's mesh-resolution section argued that the basin catalogue converges at 10M from the counts 3,621 / 6,345 / 9,419 / 9,649 across 2.5M / 5M / 10M / 25M regions, 'because minCells has stopped binding and the declared 1000 km2 floor governs'. Under 850 the crossover moves to 10.37M, so at 10M the CELL floor binds again and that sentence is evidence about the old floor. The counts under 850 are higher and whether they still converge across those four region counts is not measured; the README now says to re-take it from the next generation rather than carrying the numbers across the change. The semivariance and erosion-texture argument the section actually rests on has no floor in it and is untouched.

DO NOT LOWER IT FURTHER WITHOUT LOWERING minCells, which does nothing on its own -- and minCells is what gives a depression enough cells for basinHypsometry to build the capacity curve the carve criterion compares fill against, so moving it is a trade rather than a tightening. Recorded at the constant.

title: The relief curve saturates at model elevation 1 and a quarter per cent of land shares one elevation
description:
`elevToHeightKm` in vendor/orogen/js/color-map.js clamps with `Math.min(elev, 1)`, so every land cell at or above model elevation 1 is published at the same `elevation_km`, which is 6 times the relief scale. Measured on the two registered builds: 2,953 cells on precarve-craton and 11,251 on precarve-craton-10m, 0.259 and 0.249 per cent of land BY AREA, and both builds report the same maximum land elevation to four decimals.

The share is converged across a fourfold change in region count, so this is a property of the curve rather than of the mesh. The consequence in the basin catalogue is sharp: a depression whose sink and spill both sit above the clamp has a published physical depth of exactly zero, and hydrography/data/*/basins.nc carries 5 and 16 preserved basins with `capacity_km3` of exactly zero as a result.

Do: decide whether the clamp is intended as a physical ceiling on relief or is an artefact of a curve fitted on [0,1]. If it is intended, the flat top is a plateau the terrain does not otherwise have and downstream slope, drainage and hypsometry all read it as one. If it is not, the curve needs a branch above 1.

Source: notes/audits/basin-catalogue-floor.md
notes:
Found while measuring the basin catalogue's depth floor. The relief curve is not the basin catalogue's file; filed rather than fixed.

2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER, from a pass over the needs-decision set.
RECLASSIFIED, an investigation, not a decision: establish whether elevToHeightKm's Math.min(elev, 1) is a deliberate ceiling on relief or an artefact of a curve fitted on [0,1], by reading the curve rather than by asking.
close_reason:
ARTEFACT OF THE SHAPE FUNCTION'S DOMAIN, not a physical ceiling, established by reading the curve rather than by argument.

s(t) = t^4(5-4t) is a Hermite interpolant whose four defining conditions are all endpoint conditions on [0,1]: s(0)=s'(0)=s''(0)=0 for the flatlands, s(1)=1 with s'(1)=0 for the peak compression. s' is negative above 1, so the polynomial turns over, reaches zero at t=1.25 and goes below sea level beyond, and Math.min(elev,1) was the guard against that inversion. The codebase already names [0,1] as the domain: applyDetailNoise refuses to invert the same polynomial at elev >= 0.99. The physical ceiling on relief exists and is a separate object, scaledHeightKm's 1/g out of sigma/(rho g), applied after this curve.

FIXED with a branch above the domain, s(t) := t, giving RELIEF_KM_PER_UNIT * elev. Continuous at the join where s(1)=1 already, gradient equal to the curve's own mean gradient across its domain, strictly increasing everywhere, no constant the curve did not already have, bit-identical below 1, and applied before reliefScale so selection stays gravity-invariant.

MEASURED on both builds: the parameter runs to 1.3687 and 1.4280, the clamp published 0.259 and 0.249 per cent of land by area at one identical height (2,953 and 11,251 cells), and unclamped the raw polynomial would have put 49 and 134 cells below sea level.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW'S FRAMING, both measured. First, THE BRANCH MOVES THE TERRAIN, which the row did not say: selectBasins compares BASIN_MIN_DEPTH_KM against selectionDepthKm, which is this curve applied to a depression's spill and sink, so 108 and 390 catalogue depressions cross the depth floor UPWARD and none downward. Basin ids survive, being built from sink region plus member set; hashes.basinCatalogue does not. Second, the clamp is NOT why basins.nc carries zero capacity -- it accounts for 2 of the 5 on precarve-craton and NONE of the 16 on precarve-craton-10m, whose sink and spill are equal at ordinary heights of 0.003 to 2.671 km over one or two mesh cells. notes/audits/basin-catalogue-floor.md had already reached that split from the other side and attributes them to a retained fraction of zero.

A TEST THAT CAN FAIL: tools/test-basins.mjs asserts strict monotonicity from 0.001 to 2.0. Verified both ways at merge -- the clamped implementation gives 48 pass / 1 fail on it, the branch 49 / 0.

Evidence in notes/audits/relief-curve-domain.md. source/README.md and the export's own metadata in data-export.js both said the curve stops at 1 and now say it does not. No generation run.

title: A constant named GLACIAL_MID_FLOOD governs a priority flood that runs with glacial erosion off
description: vendor/orogen/js/terrain-post.js runs a carve-biased priority flood at GLACIAL_MID_FLOOD_FRAC of the erosion loop, with the comment 'cut outlets through basins created by glaciation'. The gate is on the iteration index alone, and totalIters is the max of the hydraulic, thermal and glacial counts, so the flood fires whenever ANY of the three runs. A build generated with --glacial 0 still gets it, carving outlets through depressions glaciation did not make, at a strength named for glaciation. The name, the comment and the GLACIAL_ prefix on the constant all misattribute it. Found while implementing the ice mask for PHYS-13; it is why a zero ice mask is not equivalent to --glacial 0. Do: decide whether the flood belongs to the hydraulic path (rename the constant and the comment) or to the glacial one (gate it on glacial erosion actually running). Either is a terrain change for builds where the two disagree, so it goes through loop A. The constant lives in terrain-config.js.
notes:
2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER, from a pass over the needs-decision set.

THE FLOOD IS HYDRAULIC. Rename the constant and the comment; do not gate it on
glacial erosion running.

The author's reason, which corrects this row's framing: a build generates with
--glacial 0 because Orogen's glacier module is not used until a glacier mask
exists, and that is a SEQUENCING fact about the first pass rather than a
statement that the flood is misplaced. The row read the two as one thing. What
survives is only the naming defect -- a hydraulic priority flood carrying a
GLACIAL_ prefix, a glacial comment, and a constant named GLACIAL_MID_FLOOD_FRAC
-- and that is a rewrite in terrain-config.js and terrain-post.js.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BATCH: this stops being a terrain DECISION and becomes a
rename with no numeric effect, so it no longer has to be settled inside the
generation it was filed against. It still lands before the generation, because a
constant that misnames what it governs is read by whoever tunes it next.
close_reason:
The flood is hydraulic and now says so. GLACIAL_MID_FLOOD_FRAC, GLACIAL_MID_FLOOD_CARVE and -- found in the same sweep -- GLACIAL_INITIAL_CARVE are HYDRAULIC_*, declared in the hydraulic section of terrain-config.js, and the mid-loop comment no longer attributes the depressions to glaciation: it records that the gate is a fraction of totalIters, the max of the three iteration counts, so the flood fires in a generation with glacial erosion off and that is INTENDED, because thermal erosion closes depressions too. That is the author's correction to this row's framing -- a build generates with --glacial 0 because the glacier module waits on a mask, which is sequencing rather than evidence about the flood.

GLACIAL_INITIAL_CARVE was the same defect found in the same file and is fixed with it: it is the pre-loop priority flood, gated on the hydraulic iteration count alone. GLACIAL_POST_SMOOTH is genuinely glacial, gated on glacIdx, and is left alone.

PURE RENAME, VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: terrain-config.js's export name-to-value table is identical under the rename map across all 389 exports -- zero values moved, zero names unaccounted for -- and terrain-post.js differs from its base only in comments and in the order of names inside one import list. All 49 Orogen node tests pass. No generation run; both builds in source/ keep their selection until the batch's single later generation consumes this.

title: The cf input module's mineral soil path now fails without land column contract states
description:
WORLD-OF6N removed SoilInput::get_mineral's Cosby retention inversion. get_mineral now reads SoilInput::ContractStates, which a driver sets before get_soil, and calls fail() by name when none is set. VesperInput sets them from the driver file; CFInput, the upstream NetCDF input module registered as cf and compiled under HAVE_NETCDF, does not.

So an LPJ-GUESS run with input module cf and a mineral soil map now fails at the first gridcell instead of deriving its own retention curve. That is deliberate: this fork's soil has one description, and a second derivation reachable through another input module is the defect that was removed. It is recorded because it is a capability that used to work and because the failure is at run time rather than at compile time.

Do: decide whether cf is a supported input module for this fork. If it is, it needs a route to the contract's states, which means a per-cell states reader independent of the vesper driver. If it is not, removing the module is the cleaner answer and the fail() message should say so. Evidence: vendor/lpj-guess/modules/soilinput.cpp SoilInput::get_mineral, vendor/lpj-guess/modules/cfinput.cpp REGISTER_INPUT_MODULE and its soilinput.get_soil call

title: The inert-config-set honesty guard is a substring match over generator source and trips on prose
description:
scripts/check_consistency.py's "inert config sets vs their generators" check reads each generator's whole source file and reports a contradiction when the tail of an inert key name appears anywhere in it, comments and docstrings included. The key model.layers is one character from the ordinary English word, so a docstring saying "integrated over its fifteen layers" fails the gate for exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_soil_water.py while the code reads no such key.

Found by tripping it while rewriting that docstring under WORLD-OF6N, and worked around by rewording the prose. The guard's claim is worth keeping -- a key listed inert whose name appears in the generator's source is a claim the source contradicts -- but a match that cannot tell code from commentary makes the gate a constraint on how documents are written.

Do: match against the source with comments and string literals stripped, or against a key ACCESS form rather than the bare name. Either keeps the guard and drops the false arm. Evidence: scripts/check_consistency.py, the loop over INERT_CONFIG_KEYS that builds the contradicted list; lib/provenance.py INERT_CONFIG_KEYS entry for surface_soil_water

title: The andic hydraulic effect is now a declared absence: allophane is read and nothing responds to it
description:
Before WORLD-OF6N, pedology's endmember mixture carried an additive volumetric capacity term for allophane and LPJ-GUESS had none, so the andic effect was a DISAGREEMENT between two derivations. The adopted closure is Clapp-Hornberger on Cosby Table 4, which is a texture regression with no andic term, so the disagreement is gone and what is left is an absence: pedology emits an andic fraction per cell, soilinput.cpp reads it onto Soiltype::andic_frac, and no equation in the retention closure responds to it.

Allophane holds water in a way texture does not predict, so this is a real property of the simulated soil that the description does not carry. It is small on the current map -- zero on more than half the cells, a median of nothing and a p90 of a few per cent of pedology's own capacity -- but the map moves with the carve list and with volcanism, and the term was never bounded against a map that had more arc terrain.

Do: either declare an andic modifier to the retention states in pedology/config/land_column_properties.yaml with a source, or declare the absence in the materials block as a limitation with its magnitude bounded. Evidence: pedology/config/land_column_properties.yaml materials.andic, pedology/analysis/land_column_properties_report.json adopted_case.andic_term_mm and andic_is_not_the_disagreement, vendor/lpj-guess/modules/soilinput.cpp get_mineral

title: Decide which of the records this project added should be optional on restart
description:
A record read under the default nexcheck that a restart file does not carry stops the model, with the record's name printed by get_restart_array. That is loud and correct as a failure mode; what is undecided is which records it should apply to.

At least three gridpoint records this project added are read that way: persistt (glaciermod.f90 glacierini, in the nrestart > 0 branch) and assolu and asthru (plasim.f90 read_atmos_restart, WORLD-3QFZ's band-resolved surface downward solar accumulators, which sit ABOVE the accuvers guard rather than inside it). A restart written before each existed therefore cannot be resumed at all, which notes/audits/ecological-stream-restart-continuity.md recorded for persistt as a blocker to its own measurement.

world-onw8 built the machinery this needs: has_restart_array in restartmod and mpgetgp_found in mpimod_omp read a may-be-absent record, leave the caller's array alone when it is not there, and report which happened. So the work is a decision per record and not an implementation.

The decision is not automatic. Rule 7 says every build, run and climatology is disposable until the canonical climatology lineage is declared, so refusing to resume an old restart may be exactly right and the cheaper answer may be to re-commission. An accumulator over an output window (assolu, asthru) loses a partial window and nothing else, which is the case world-onw8 already made optional for adrain. A prognostic clock (persistt) is not the same: starting it at zero delays glacier formation by up to the persistence threshold, so an absent record there is a state loss, not a lost window.

Do: enumerate the records this project added against upstream, classify each as accumulator or prognostic, and decide per record whether it goes through mpgetgp_found with a stated cold value or stays a hard stop. Evidence: notes/audits/absent-restart-records.md.
close_reason:
Decided per record, over the 29 the fork adds against the vendored subtree's base. Pristine 3.4.2 is unreachable offline, the subtree having arrived as one squashed commit, and the note says so rather than implying a comparison it did not make.

persistt STAYS A HARD STOP. It is a prognostic clock and not an accumulator: a zero reading puts a cell one step from glaciation back to the start of glacpersec, silently, and bounded by no window. Rule 7 makes re-commissioning the cheaper answer, so refusing to resume an old restart is exactly right here.

Everything already optional is now RECORDED rather than inferred -- Policy.resume with its cold value -- and check_resume_policy holds that table against the read call sites in BOTH directions, failing on a record declared optional whose call site is not, and on one declared required whose call site already tolerates absence. It runs inside check_policy_covers_source, which smoke_test.py already calls.

The check earned itself immediately: it found eleven records the by-hand enumeration had missed -- six spectral accumulators, five orbital scalars, and the four geometry stamps.

title: SIMBA's light use efficiency is applied to broadband, and band 1 now exists
description:
simba.f90's light-limited GPP is 'zgppl = rlue * zbeta * zft * zveg * dfd(jhor,NLEP)': an Earth light use efficiency of 3.4e-10 kg C per joule applied to the BROADBAND surface downward shortwave. rlue was calibrated where the photosynthetically active fraction of that broadband flux is about 0.45; under this star it is about 0.30 to 0.33, so light-limited GPP as SIMBA computes it is overstated by roughly 1.4 times. simba.f90's own module header says so. The finding is recorded in notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md and had no issue.

WHAT CHANGED: world-3qfz gave the model dfdsw1, the surface downward flux in shortwave band 1, as a live array beside dfd. The correction is no longer a constant somebody has to choose: the light term can read the band the model itself computes, with rlue rescaled by the SUN's PAR-to-band-1 ratio rather than by a whole-spectrum guess. lib/stellar.py owns the split and biosphere/scripts/build_vesper_header.py already does this arithmetic for FRADPAR.

Dormant, not wrong-today: SIMBA is unreachable at NVEG = 0, which every run of this project sets. It is one namelist key away, and a dormant Earth constant reads exactly like a live one to whoever throws the switch. Same shape as world-9d1's carbonmod note.

Do: decide whether the light term reads band 1 or a rescaled rlue on broadband, and record the choice where the constant is declared. Note that this is one item in a paragraph of SIMBA Earth fits -- ct_crit, q10, co2_ref, co2_sens, the biome fits and three Earth-Sun albedo constants -- that all fire on the same switch.
notes:
2026-08-26, AUTHOR'S ANSWER, from a pass over the needs-decision set.
RECLASSIFIED, an investigation, not a decision: whether the light term reads band 1 follows from lib/stellar.py's split and simba.f90's own header.

title: Two live Earth-gravity defaults in gcmt.py, in a module nothing imports
description: vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/gcmt.py:1010 eqstream(file, radius=6.371e6, gravity=9.80665) and :1462 tlstream(dataset, radius=6371.0e3, gravity=9.80665, substellar=0.0) carry Earth's radius and gravity as DEFAULT ARGUMENTS, so a caller that omits them silently analyses this world with Earth's. WORLD-9D1 swept the dormant Earth code in this fork and named radmod's Berger series and vernal equinox, rainmod_bm's Betts-Miller timescales, hurricanemod's thresholds, carbonmod, LSG and icemod_template; it did not reach gcmt.py, so these two are a gap in that sweep rather than a new class. Found while sweeping for Earth's dry adiabat used as a lapse ceiling, after WORLD-B99F found one in analysis/spatial_reduction_gap.py: 9.8 K/km is Earth's g/cp and this world's is 12.75, and lib/lapse.py is the owner of that fact. Nothing in this project imports gcmt, so nothing is wrong today and no result is affected. ASK WHETHER IT SHOULD EXIST BEFORE FIXING IT: gcmt.py is upstream ExoPlaSim's analysis module, this project reads its exports through pyburn and lib/ instead, and a module no consumer imports is a candidate for deletion rather than for a guard. If it stays, the two signatures should take their values from config/planet.yaml the way every other consumer does, or refuse when they are not supplied. Evidence: vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/gcmt.py:1010 and :1462, lib/lapse.py, notes/audits/nonlinear-spatial-reductions.md

title: Attach the lake-energy bound to the ledger's open_water_evaporation_from_routed_water entry
description:
notes/audits/lake-energy-omission-bound.md bounds the seasonal lake-energy omission in closed form and finds it sits INSIDE the mass omission hydrography/config/land_water_ledger.yaml already declares at open_water_evaporation_from_routed_water, not beside it. The ledger's bucket_floor_creation entry already carries the pattern: a measured_bound field on an existing unrepresentable entry.

Do: add a measured_bound to open_water_evaporation_from_routed_water citing that note. The bound has three parts and the ranking is the point. The surrogate soil column is semi-infinite at the orbital frequency and worth 0.79 m of water, so a 2 m lake is represented exactly and the error reverses sign below that; the seasonal amplitude ratio runs to 0.03 at 100 m at the weakest defensible damping; the seasonal phase can be wrong by at most 40.6 Earth days, a quarter orbit less the surrogate's own lag, unconditionally; freezing is absent entirely and dominates both, 1 m of lake ice being worth a 93 K seasonal swing of the surrogate; and the freshwater-to-brine property bracket enters through the same rho*c*d product as depth and is worth less than one step of the depth axis.

Filed rather than done because hydrography/ was owned by another batch when the bound was measured.

title: make_profile_bed.py and reproducibility_matrix.py each restate the manifest comparison
description:
Both check an executable against exoplasim/binary_manifest.json before running it, correctly, and each states the comparison itself: make_profile_bed.py:383-391 and reproducibility_matrix.py:359-381. rebuild_binaries.unregistered(exe) is now that comparison, kept beside the code that writes the manifest. Three statements of one rule is three things to keep in step, which is the argument rebuild_binaries.verify()'s own docstring makes about check_consistency.py.

Behaviour to preserve: make_profile_bed's --allow-unregistered downgrades the refusal to a warning, and reproducibility_matrix collects a verdict per bed executable and reports them together rather than stopping at the first.

title: Howard reconstruction and correlated-k part by 14 percent at the dry end
description:
Measured 2026-08-25 for world-5t6s, over the amounts exoplasim/notes/corrk-cross-check.md tabulates. The Howard-band reconstruction in exoplasim/scripts/shortwave_band_weights.py and the HITRAN2020 correlated-k answer are the same defined quantity and agree to 0.2 to 1.5 percent everywhere from 0.1 to 10 precipitable cm, 0.26 percent at the 2.7891 cm operating path. At 0.01 cm they are 14.4 percent apart, reconstruction 1.319 times Eq. 21 against correlated-k's 1.153.

The three candidates are all on the reconstruction side and all named already: Howard's weak-band fit extrapolated below the amounts he measured, the 0.72 and 0.81 um bands he never measured at all, and WEAK_BLUE_SCALE, which carries them at the 0.94 um band's shape scaled to 0.30 and 0.10 with no source behind the factors. The dry end is where those three matter most, because the strong bands have barely started absorbing.

NOT GATED, deliberately. A T42 column spans roughly 0.3 to 5 cm, so the model does not operate there; h2o_sw_weight is a ratio in which a dry-end level error largely divides out; and world-5t6s's gate is at the operating path, which is where the number that is used comes from.

Do: settle whether the dry-end divergence is the blue bands or the small-w extrapolation, by recomputing the reconstruction with the blue bands dropped and comparing the residual against correlated-k at 0.01 and 0.03 cm. That is the same arm the file already computes as weight_without_0.72_0.81um, so it needs no new machinery. If it is the blue bands, WEAK_BLUE_SCALE gains a measured value instead of a guessed one.
close_reason:
The dry-end divergence is the SMALL-W EXTRAPOLATION, not the blue bands, on a criterion fixed in the note before the arm ran.

Dropping the 0.72 and 0.81 um bands -- the arm the file already computed as weight_without_0.72_0.81um, so it needed no new machinery -- accounts for 0.183 of the divergence at 0.01 precipitable cm and 0.307 at 0.03, leaving 11.77 and 6.07 per cent residual. So the blue bands are a minority of it and the extrapolation below the amounts Howard measured is the rest.

THE MECHANISM IS MEASURED BAND BY BAND rather than inferred: correlated-k over Howard's own intervals runs 1.02 at 6.3 um, 0.75 at 1.1, 0.35 at 0.94 and 0.021 at 0.81 -- monotone in band weakness, which is what an extrapolation below the fitted range does.

WEAK_BLUE_SCALE GAINS A MEASURED BRACKET AND NOT A MEASURED VALUE, and the constants do not change. Substituting correlated-k into two of nine bands would make the reconstruction partly a comparison with itself, and it moves both aggregates AWAY from correlated-k. Worth 0.034 K, so this was never going to be a physics finding; what it is, is the difference between a guessed factor and a bounded one.

Reported rather than argued away: the correlated-k side missed its own pre-fixed 0.5 per cent bar, at 3 to 8 per cent.

title: Check the soil thermal conductivity coefficients against Farouki (1981) itself, not against Lawrence's restatement
description: analysis/soil_thermal_inertia.py applies the Johansen (1975) interpolation between dry and saturated soil thermal conductivity as Farouki (1981) tabulates it, but WORLD-YIP took the formulation through lawrence_2007's secondary statement of it because the monograph could not be fetched from this host. The user has since supplied it: references/farouki1981-thermal-properties-of-soils.pdf. A restatement is enough for the FORM of a relation and not enough for its coefficients, and the whole finding that dry soil conductivity is a function of bulk density alone -- which is why WORLD-YIP's per-class lithology field was measured and then not built -- rests on where mineralogy enters, which is a coefficient question. Do: read the monograph's Johansen tabulation, check the Kersten number, the dry and saturated conductivity relations and the quartz-fraction dependence against what the script implements, and record the result in notes/audits/soil-thermal-inertia.md. If a coefficient differs, re-run analysis/soil_thermal_inertia.py and say whether the factor table moves -- the load-bearing row is parent material at the dry end, currently 1.00. Evidence: analysis/soil_thermal_inertia.py, notes/audits/soil-thermal-inertia.md, references/INDEX.md
close_reason:
Read against the monograph itself, Section 7.11 and Table 24, pp. 112-113, which is what this row asked for -- a restatement is enough for the FORM of a relation and not for its coefficients.

EVERY COEFFICIENT CHECKS OUT: 0.135, 64.7, 2700 and 0.947, the geometric-mean k_sat with porosity on the water term, k_quartz 7.7, k_water 0.57, grain density 2700.

WHAT THE RESTATEMENT LOST IS TWO TEXTURE BRANCHES, and one of them matters here: the coarse Kersten form 0.7*log10(Sr)+1, and k_other = 3.0 for a COARSE soil below 0.20 quartz -- which is most of this world's parent materials. It also lost the stated validity floors, Sr above 0.1 fine and 0.05 coarse.

THE LOAD-BEARING ROW DOES NOT MOVE. The branch enters k_solid, k_solid enters k_sat, and k_sat is multiplied by a Kersten number that is zero at the dry end, so parent material at the dry end is still exactly 1.00 -- which is what WORLD-SY9's refutation rests on. At saturation the branch takes the lithology spread DOWN, from 1.36 to 1.23. Inside Farouki's own stated range the moisture sweep is 4.54 (439 to 1992) against 4.91 computed to air dry.

TRAP RECORDED for the next reader: Table 24 misprints 0.137 for 0.135 and 0.39 for 0.039. The body text is the row to copy.

title: earth_calibration.py hand-rolls two mesh reductions lib/gridding.py already owns
description:
Found by world-d9u4's sweep of this component for reductions written by hand.
`hydrography/scripts/earth_calibration.py` bins DEM pixels and recharge pixels
onto the synthetic Earth mesh with raw `np.bincount` twice: the elevation mean
and within-cell relief, and the recharge mean. Both take a plain per-pixel count
mean with no area weight, and the relief takes the variance as a difference of
moments, which is the form `lib/gridding.py:cell_moments` replaced because it
does not return zero on a constant field.

CLAUDE.md's `lib/` list is explicit that these are to be reused rather than
reimplemented, and `cell_moments` takes an arbitrary binning, so it applies here
directly with the pixel areas as weights.

SIZED FIRST, so this is not filed as a number that moved. A lat/lon pixel's area
carries `cos(lat)`, and over the 15 km span of one mesh region that varies by
about 0.4% at 60 degrees and 2.7% at 85, so the area weight is not what is wrong
with these means. The difference-of-moments form is likewise safe at the ratio
here, a relief of tens of metres about a mean of hundreds. This is a REUSE
finding, not a correctness one, and it is filed at P3 for that reason: the value
is that the next person reading it does not have to size it again.

Do: express both on `cell_moments` with the pixel area as the weight, and say in
the commit that the numbers did not move materially.

title: config/planet.yaml says this build has no climatology; a bootstrap one is on disk
description:
`config/planet.yaml`'s `baseline_climatology` block reads "There is no
climatology on this build -- every run was archived to identity and deleted --
so nothing downstream may read one until a commissioning produces one."

`exoplasim/analysis/climatology/bootstrap_regular_climatology.nc` exists, and
its attributes say `vesper_source_build: precarve-craton-10m`, `vesper_geography:
3080098d`, 12 orbits from `run_2b20e3324bb0`, created 2026-08-24, 32x64, and
`low_io: 0`. `exoplasim/runs/INDEX.json` lists that run as
`climatology_complete` with 85 orbits and 11.42 GB on disk.

The null is still right -- the comment is explicit that this key takes the
BASELINE run's regular climatology and not the bootstrap's -- so this is the
prose beside it that is out of date, not the value. It matters because it is the
sentence a reader checks before deciding whether an arm needing a climatology
can be run at all.

Do: rewrite the block to say that the only climatology on this build is the
bootstrap one, that it is what `--climatology` can be pointed at by hand, and
that the key stays null until a baseline exists.

title: The anchor release path in the water table solve has no control
description:
`solve` pins one cell of a free block that reaches no fixed head, and may later
release it and strike it off the candidate list. The comment in
`groundwater.py` records what that mechanism was fixed FROM: four permanent
anchors held 2.5e-9 of the planet's recharge as invented water because the
release test was forbidden to touch them.

`--uniqueness-test`'s controls do not reach it. A cell carrying GW-15's sink
anchors itself, so with the sink on -- the default -- a free block only reaches
the explicit anchoring code where `et_max` is zero, and a synthetic case built
with a sink-free enclosed block still placed its anchor identically from both
trajectories and never needed to release it. A `permanent_anchor` mutation of
`solve` was built and measured 0.000e+00 on that case: a control with no teeth,
so it was not shipped.

Do: build a case where an anchor is placed and then released, and add
`permanent_anchor` to `UNIQUENESS_CONTROLS` once it can be shown going red. A
block whose recharge is small enough that its shallowest cell turns out
infeasible is the shape to aim at.

title: somfluxes mixes peat and mineral texture: leaching reads soiltype.sand_frac, respiration reads get_siltfrac
description:
Worldbuilding: this is about the simulated soil in the vendored LPJ-GUESS CNP fork.

vendor/lpj-guess/modules/somdynam.cpp somfluxes takes the microbial pool's
respired share and its passive share from Soil::get_clayfrac() and
get_siltfrac(), which return soiltype.clay_frac_peat and silt_frac_peat on a
high-latitude peatland stand, but takes the organic leaching share from
soil.soiltype.sand_frac directly, which is always the mineral texture. So on
such a stand the three shares are not one texture.

The peat fractions are never assigned anywhere in the tree: guess.h's Soiltype
constructor sets sand_frac_peat = clay_frac_peat = silt_frac_peat = 0.0 and
nothing writes them, which decayrates_century already relies on (its
texture_mod_peat comment says '= 1'). So on a peatland stand the respired share
sits at its 0.85 maximum and the passive share at 0.003 while leaching still
scales with mineral sand. The remainder to slow SOM falls to 0.009 at the
coarse LPJ soil code's 0.90 sand and reverses above 0.975 mineral sand.

Not reachable today: biosphere/config/wetlands.yaml has requested false, and
run_peatland 0 is written into the instruction file whenever the wetland gate
has not granted activation. This is a prerequisite of activating it, not a
current defect.

Do: decide whether the peat texture fractions should be assigned at all, and if
they stay zero, whether the leaching share should read get_sandfrac() so all
four shares come from one texture. Note that a peat sand fraction of zero would
zero the leaching coefficient's texture term, which is a different model of
peat leaching, not obviously the right one.

Evidence: biosphere/notes/mineral-reactivity-contract.md, the paragraph
beginning 'One path does approach it'.

title: Only the vesper input module can serve a mid-year LPJ-GUESS restart
description:
WORLD-FUJ4 added state_day, so a restart can resume on any simulated day rather than only day 0. VesperInput::getclimate was made day-addressable to match: it indexes dtemp/dprec/dinsol by date.day and now interpolates whenever the loaded year is not the wanted one rather than only on day 0, and it sets the seasonal landmarks on a mid-year resume.

The other input modules were not touched. demoinput, cfinput and the CRU reader under cru/guessio serve their forcing in stream order, so a run resuming at day D on one of them would read the year's first day of forcing into day D. Nothing refuses this: state_day is a framework parameter and the framework does not know which module is loaded.

The Vesper harness only ever runs -input vesper, so no configuration this project uses is exposed. Do: either have the framework refuse state_day >= 0 unless the loaded input module declares itself day-addressable -- an InputModule virtual that defaults to false -- or make the stream readers seek. The first is the smaller change and states the limitation where it bites.

Source: the state_day documentation in vendor/lpj-guess/framework/parameters.h.

title: The LPJ-GUESS state file cannot name the member that differs
description:
WORLD-FUJ4 gave verify_lpj_restart_continuity.py a --one-day mode that compares two runs' state files one simulated day either side of a restart. It can say the two arms are in different states and where in the byte stream they first diverge; it cannot say which member.

The reason is the archive format. framework/archive.h streams raw object bytes through operator&, in the order each serialize() writes them, with no names, no lengths and no record boundaries; framework/guessserializer.cpp writes one such stream per rank with only meta.bin beside it. A byte offset maps to a member only through the full layout of everything before it, including the variable-length stands, patches and individuals, so it is not recoverable from outside the model. ExoPlaSim's restart is a named-record format, which is why exoplasim/scripts/verify_restart_continuity.py reports per record.

Do: give the archive an optional labelled mode -- a mark(name) the serialize bodies call at chosen points, written to a side-car manifest of (name, offset, length) alongside the state file -- so a state-file diff resolves to a member. Only the classes the fixture cares about need marking; the manifest is a debugging artifact and does not change the state file itself. Then --one-day reports members rather than offsets, and biosphere/scripts/soil_restart_state_gate.py's lost block gets a behavioural counterpart.

Until then, the localisation the fixture offers is the offset plus the one-day output tables. Source: biosphere/notes/soil-restart-state.md, and the docstring of verify_lpj_restart_continuity.py.

title: Land-use change reads the nitrogen wet/dry pools before the day writes them
description:
The twelve wet/dry pools NH4_mass_w through labile_carbon_d are absent from Soil::serialize and are correctly absent: ntransform.cpp:208-220 rebuilds all twelve from the serialized totals at the top of every daily substrate_partition, before any read in that module.

One read precedes it. landcover_dynamics runs on date.day == 0, before the patch day loop, and Stand::ncont() at modules/landcover.h:129-132 sums the _w and _d terms into the land-use-change nitrogen flux; add_from_stand at landcover.h:186-196 and landcover.cpp:1536-1546 reach them the same way. On a restart with run_landcover set, that read sees the constructed zeros, so anflux_landuse_change is under-reported for the one transition on the resume day. The mixed values themselves are harmless, being overwritten later the same day.

The flux is a diagnostic, not a driver, so this is a reporting error rather than a state error, and it is one day of one run. Do: either have ncont() take the totals rather than the split, or call substrate_partition before landcover_dynamics. Establish which the mainline intends before changing the order -- this is a fork of a widely used model and the ordering is upstream's.

Source: biosphere/notes/soil-restart-state.md, the wet/dry section of biosphere/config/soil_restart_state.yaml.

title: Delete the six Soil members nothing reads
description:
The restart-state sweep under WORLD-SC4T classified every member of the Soil class and found six that no code in vendor/lpj-guess reads at all. Deleting is a fix; the question is whether they should exist, not whether they are correct.

- alwhc[NSOILLAYER] is written by init_hydrology_variables and by update_layer_water_content every day, and IS serialized, and has no reader anywhere in the tree. Its only input, alwhc_init, therefore also feeds nothing live.
- SIDX_old is assigned at soil.cpp:3602 and :3627 and read nowhere.
- k_CO2 and Ceq_CO2 are computed daily by update_daily_gas_parameters and never consumed: the transport step replaces CO2 diffusion with co2_store.
- CH4_gas_yesterday is written at soilmethane.cpp:1218, serialized, and read by nothing.
- firstHydrologyCalc is set true in init_states and cleared at soil.cpp:1773, and no code tests it.

Two are serialized, so removing them shrinks the state file; the rest are memory and daily arithmetic. Check each against upstream before deleting: this is a fork of a widely used community model and a member dead HERE may be live in a configuration this project does not compile. Where it is dead upstream too, the removal is a declared divergence recorded beside the mainline behaviour, on the pattern the ntransform constants use.

Source: biosphere/notes/soil-restart-state.md finding 6, and biosphere/config/soil_restart_state.yaml.

title: No instrument measures concurrent-job throughput now that bench_rank_layout.py is deleted
description:
world-4act deleted bench_rank_layout.py: 407 lines of Open MPI --map-by, --bind-to, pe-list and PE index-space semantics measuring N concurrent mpiexec jobs, none of which the threaded build has. What went with it is the LATENCY-versus-THROUGHPUT axis over concurrent jobs, and that pair is a real distinction this project made deliberately: exoplasim/notes/rank-layout-benchmark.md established that a layout can lose on one and win on the other and that averaging them destroys the only useful thing they say. bench_ab.py cannot replace it -- it runs one job at a time.

The question is currently SETTLED and that is why this is P3: exoplasim/notes/smt-rank-layout.md put production at sixteen threads and refused oversubscription. This is only needed if the thread count, the SMT policy, or running several climate runs at once is revisited.

What a replacement would have to do, so it is not re-derived from scratch: N concurrent one-process jobs at a declared thread count each, thread placement set through OMP_PLACES and OMP_PROC_BIND rather than a launcher's pe-list, the placement VERIFIED against /proc/self/status before any arm is timed rather than assumed (bench_rank_layout.py's central finding was that a launch line can silently drop per-unit binding and then the arm reports a slow layout when the launch was the fault), and latency and throughput reported separately and never averaged.

It cannot be built and validated on a contended host: its acceptance is a timing number.

Related: world-9eq, which asks what becomes of the notes those measurements produced.

title: Refresh the aggregation audit's subgrid_slope bullet: the divisor is now declared
description:
biosphere/notes/spatial-support-ecological-aggregation-audit.md finding 4 still says build_soil.py's subgrid_slope 'divides the within-cell elevation spread by native mesh spacing, so changing region count changes the inferred slope'. That was true and is the finding world-uyfb rests on, but the divisor is now catena.gradient_baseline_km, a declared 30 km, and the statistic transports between this project's two builds to 1.069x against a 1.15x bar (analysis/subgrid_slope_support.py).

The bullet is one sentence in a file this batch did not own (biosphere/** was three sibling batches' ground), so it is left for whoever owns that note next. Rewrite it rather than mark it: state what the statistic is now and that its magnitude is a spread over a declared length rather than a hillslope gradient, so no absolute threshold anchored on measured hillslopes belongs on it.

title: soilinput.cpp writes soiltype.runon three times and nothing reads it
description:
world-c4j8 removed the soiltype.runon = wetland_runon assignment in modules/soil.cpp and the read beside it: runon into a wetland stand is PLHY-4's exchange, and while that exchange's flux is undeclared the term is absent rather than approximated by a namelist scalar.

modules/soilinput.cpp still assigns soiltype.runon = wetland_runon at three places (around lines 496, 752 and 844) and nothing reads the member any more. That is state written and never read, which is the shape world-qzra is about: a symbol that looks live and carries nothing.

Do: remove the three assignments and the SoilType::runon member in framework/guess.h, or, if PLHY-4's exchange is to be delivered through soiltype, leave one write and say what reads it.
