The wetland_runon namelist parameter itself stays declared: biosphere/scripts/run_lpj_guess.py writes it into every instruction file and plib's badins requires it, so removing the parameter without changing that script breaks every run.

Not done under world-c4j8 because soilinput.cpp was owned by another batch in the same wave.

title: Supply the outgassing supply side: segment bracket, source partition, mass scaling exponent
description:
The seven undeclared fields in pedology/config/outgassing.yaml, each of which outgassing_gate.py already refuses by name. VOLC-8 built the gate; this supplies what it asks for.

supply.mass_scaling_exponent and .mass_scaling_source. The supply currently rests on the planet's mass in Earth masses -- an exponent of exactly 1, asserted in prose with no reference. Radiogenic heat production scales with mass at fixed bulk composition, but outgassing tracks melt production, which tracks heat FLUX through a surface, and the two do not carry the same power of mass. Declaring the exponent means declaring which chain is being claimed.

supply.per_km_segment_bracket and .per_km_segment_source. Per-kilometre CO2 flux along a plate boundary spans more than a hundredfold in the observed record, so a uniform fault-length verdict is not a bracket. Wanted as [low, high] mol CO2 per km per year against an external source.

supply.source_partition and .degassing_efficiency. How the global requirement splits across ridge, arc/recycled, plume/rift and metamorphic, with mantle and slab carbon, melt production and degassing/retention efficiencies exposed rather than folded together.

supply.atmosphere_versus_ocean_split, owned with OCN-13: which fraction reaches the atmosphere and which the ocean's hydrothermal and chemical boundary. OCN-13 may consume a source bracket without opening the carbon feedback.

WHAT THE TERRAIN CAN AND CANNOT GIVE, already declared in the same file. Boundary geometry and RELATIVE throughput are measurable on the accepted 10M support: ridge, convergent-margin, continental-rift and plume/arc proxies. An ABSOLUTE plate rate is not -- Orogen's velocities are in arbitrary units and the model has no time axis -- and neither is a thermal history. The gate refuses any absolute-rate claim on those grounds, so this row's deliverable is dimensionless geometry plus an external bracket, never a terrain-only capacity verdict.
close_reason: All seven fields declared from external sources, commit d4021768. Exponent 1.0, bracket [1.0, 1.34], on the MELT-PRODUCTION chain from Kite, Manga and Gaidos (2009); the declared value is the floor of the bracket and is numerically what the earlier code used, so no margin moves. Per-km bracket [1.52e6, 4.74e8] mol/km/yr from Le Voyer et al. (2019)'s 711 ridge segments, cross-checked against Brune et al.'s continental-rift census at 4.6e7. Four-way partition assembled from Marty and Tolstikhin (1998) plus a separately sourced metamorphic term, with every numerator, bracket and source in the file. Degassing efficiency exposed for ridge and arc, marked FOLDED for plume/rift and metamorphic. Ocean/atmosphere split 0.297 with bracket [0.04, 0.63], declared as a delivery location and not a fate; OCN-13 should read that the bracket is an order of magnitude wide. The gate gained six refusal codes for a declaration that is declared and WRONG -- disordered bracket, non-pair bracket, value outside its bracket, fractions not summing to 1, fractions disagreeing with their fluxes, a missing class -- with a fixture each, 17/17. requested stays false; the one remaining refusal is OUTGASSING-REQUIREMENT-ARTIFACT-MISSING, which needs a climatology and belongs to VOLC-8.

title: Give the land column's drainage flux a diagnostic output code
description: landmod.f90 carries ddrain, the drainage out of the base of the land column, as a prognostic with a restart record under LSHY-3's selectable scheme. It has no output code, so a run on nlandwcol = 1 with nlandwdrain = 1 produces a flux nothing downstream can read: hydrography/config/land_water_ledger.yaml's drainage term names it as a producer and the postprocessor cannot deliver it. Identically zero under the default impermeable lower boundary, which is why this did not block the scheme landing. Do: add an outmod writegp and an accumulator on the pattern drunoff uses, register the code in vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/pyburn.py, and take the record through exoplasim/scripts/restart_schema.py for the accumulator. Evidence: hydrography/notes/land-water-ledger.md
close_reason: Genuinely absent, not merely unrouted: ddrain appeared nowhere in outmod, so it reached the restart and nothing else. Added as code 231, name mrrob / subsurface_runoff, on the pattern drunoff uses. The accumulator adrain is declared in landmod beside the flux it accumulates rather than beside aroff in plasimmod, because the land column owns it and that keeps plasimmod and plasim.f90 out of the change; it is accumulated in outaccu, divided and written in outgp, written instantaneously in snapshotgp and hcadencegp, zeroed in outreset, and carried through landmod's own restart put and get under the same lowered nexcheck the layered store uses, so a restart written before the record existed resumes and loses at most a partial output window. Registered in pyburn's ilibrary and in run_exoplasim's REGULAR_CODES, unconditionally: ddrain is identically zero under the default impermeable base, but a code the model writes and no product carries is exactly the state world-j0az found the air extrema 201/202 in, and the cost is one 2D field per output bin. restart_schema carries adrain as an ACCUMULATOR with model_reset zero, and its coverage check is clean. outmod's five affected subroutines gained an explicit use landmod; four already reached landmod by re-export through glaciermod, which is not a dependency worth leaving implicit. Verified: smoke_test 28 of 28 including the syntax pass, and a T21 l10 p4 production binary builds from this tree unpublished. Every PUBLISHED plasim.x is now stale under rule 4. Commit 9d151d7e.

title: biosphere/generated/ is neither tracked nor ignored
description: Eight scripts under biosphere/scripts/ write to biosphere/generated/ through _paths.py:19 GENERATED -- the two gates' reports, the LPJ driver, the Vesper header and PFT files, and the abiotic nutrient ledger. git tracks none of it and .gitignore excludes none of it, so the directory sits permanently untracked-and-unignored. That is the exact shape a 'git add -A' sweeps into the tree, which the project's standing rule about staging explicit paths exists to prevent. No other component has a 'generated/' directory in git ls-files, so the convention is that these are outputs; the .gitignore entry is what is missing. Do: add biosphere/generated/ to .gitignore with the one-line reason the file's other entries carry, or, if any of those products is meant to be durable, say which and track that one. Found while running ntransform_gate.py under world-nga9.
close_reason: biosphere/generated/ added to .gitignore in both forms, with the reason. Nothing in it is durable: every file is written by a step registered in config/pipeline.yaml and nothing outside biosphere/ reads any of them; the record each gate argues is in biosphere/notes/, which is tracked.

title: Denitrification switches off entirely below 0.4 WFPS, a threshold neither paper states
description: modules/ntransform.cpp denitrification runs only when water_cont_m3 > 0 and wfps_upper > 0.4, so below 0.4 water-filled pore space the operator denitrifies nothing at all. Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) has no such switch: table 9's rates fall with the moisture response and with substrate availability and never turn off. Weier et al. (1993) measured at 60, 75 and 90 per cent WFPS only and says nothing about the dry end. On the current Vesper soil map 2032 of 4105 gridcells are above 0.4 WFPS even at wilting point, so on half the map the switch never closes and on the rest it decides whether denitrification happens at all. Registered as unsourced in biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml. Do: source the threshold or state it as a declared deviation. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md

title: get_mineral's Cosby inversion can return a field capacity above saturation
description: modules/soilinput.cpp get_mineral inverts Cosby et al. (1984) for field capacity and wilting point without clamping the matric head against the air-entry value: Theta_whc = Theta_s * (Psi_whc/Psi_s)^(1/b) with Psi_whc fixed at 10^-2. Where Psi_whc exceeds Psi_s the result is above saturation. That happens for low-sand, low-clay textures, sand at or below about 0.10 with clay at or below about 0.26 at sand 0, reaching Theta_whc/Theta_s of 1.135 at pure silt. In that region Soil::wfps(0) exceeds 1 at field capacity, which is outside the domain biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml declares for it and outside the domain of every WFPS response function in modules/ntransform.cpp. No cell of either current Vesper soil map is in the region, both being sand 0.17 or above, so nothing is wrong today; the map is what keeps it right rather than the code. Do: clamp Theta_whc at Theta_s in get_mineral, or state the texture region as a declared limit on the soil map. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md
close_reason: Both matric heads in get_mineral are clamped at Psi_s, the air-entry value, so Theta_whc and Theta_wilt cannot exceed Theta_s. Cosby et al. (1984) eqn 1 holds only below air entry; above it the pore space is full. The code is what keeps it right now, not the map. No cell of either current Vesper soil map is in the affected corner (sand at or below about 0.10 with clay at or below about 0.26), both maps being sand 0.17 or above, so no current soil property changes. The inversion appears nowhere else in the tree.

title: The denitrification temperature response is clamped at its 22 C value, which Xu-Ri table 9 eqn 1 does not do
description: modules/ntransform.cpp denitrification computes f_den_T as min(1.0, exp(308.56 * (1/68.02 - 1/(soil_T + 46.02)))). The exponential is exactly Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 9 eqn 1 and is 1 at 22 C, with an implied Q10 of 2.04 over 15 to 25 C against the 'about 2' the paper's text claims. The min is the port's: table 9 eqn 1 carries none, unlike table 5 eqn 7 and table 10 eqn 1 which both state one. The paper's function exceeds 1 above 22 C, reaching 1.21 at 25 C, 1.61 at 30 C, 2.07 at 35 C and 3.15 at 45 C, so the clamp holds warm-soil denitrification at its 22 C rate. Something has to bound it, because the operator's conservation identity needs every coefficient of a pool mass to stay at or below 1, and the paper does not say what. Do: decide what bounds it, or state the clamp as the declared deviation it is. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md
close_reason: The min(1, .) is gone from f_den_T; the response is now exactly Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 9 eqn 1, which carries none. It is 1.21 at 25 C, 1.61 at 30 C, 2.07 at 35 C, 3.15 at 45 C and 8.07 at the top of the declared temperature domain, so warm-soil denitrification is no longer held at its 22 C rate. The premise that something had to bound it was wrong: both transformations it multiplies are already written as min(pool, pool * coefficient), so neither can take more nitrogen out of a pool than the pool holds. That is now declared as clamped_by on the two denitrification products, and the gate checks the min() is still in the source rather than requiring a product below 1. The -40 C guard stays: the exponent diverges at -46.02 C and the function is 5e-21 there.

title: The denitrification Michaelis-Menten divisor makes Kc and Kn soil-solution concentrations, which Xu-Ri does not state
description: modules/ntransform.cpp denitrification divides by water_cont_m3 = wcont * gawc[0] / 1000, the depth of AVAILABLE water in the upper layer, to remove the per-cubic-metre from k_C and k_N. Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 11 gives Kc as 0.017 kg C m-3 and Kn as 0.083 kg N m-3 without saying per cubic metre of what, and sources both to Li et al. (1992), which this project does not hold. Per cubic metre of SOIL the divisor would be the 0.5 m layer depth instead. The two differ by 6.7x to 30x over the reachable water contents of the LPJ soil codes, and a smaller divisor saturates the Michaelis-Menten terms sooner, so the soil-solution reading is the one that maximises denitrification. Do: fetch Li, Frolking and Frolking (1992), DNDC, and settle the volume. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md
notes:
Li et al. (1992) READ 2026-08-25 and it does NOT close this. Its table 7 gives Kc = 0.017 kg C/m3 and Kn = 0.083 kg N/m3, attributes both to Shah and Coulman (1978) rather than measuring them, and states the units exactly as Xu-Ri does: per cubic metre of an unnamed volume. So the primary carries the same silence and the chain runs one paper further.

WHAT IT DID ADD, recorded in biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml's entry: a magnitude. DNDC's own soluble carbon runs at 10 to 20 mg C per kg soil across its sensitivity runs, initialised at 20. Kc = 0.017 kg C/m3 is 17 mg C per kg soil at a bulk density near 1 Mg/m3 -- same units, same magnitude as the pool it half-saturates, which is where a half-saturation belongs. Under the soil-solution reading Kc would be about 5 mg C per kg soil, a third of that pool. The magnitude match favours the per-cubic-metre-of-SOIL divisor, which is the LOWER-denitrification branch and NOT the one the operator runs.

That is evidence and not proof: it rests on an assumed bulk density and it is not enough to move a factor of 6.7 to 30 on denitrification. Shah and Coulman (1978) is what settles it; fetching it is world-80ia.

Verdict stays unsourced. Commit 865de8aa.
close_reason:
SETTLED AGAINST THE PRIMARY, and the operator is right. Shah and Coulman (1978) is held and read (supplied by the author 2026-08-26; WORLD-80IA).

The question was whether Kc and Kn are per cubic metre of soil solution or of soil -- a factor of 6.7 to 30 on denitrification over the reachable water contents of the LPJ soil codes, with the soil-solution reading the one that maximises it and the one modules/ntransform.cpp runs, dividing by water_cont_m3 = wcont * gawc[0] / 1000.

THE ANSWER IS THE SOLUTION'S, and it is not an inference from the units. Shah and Coulman's chosen constants are Ks = 83 mg/liter for nitrate nitrogen and Ks = 17.4 mg/liter for organic carbon -- 0.083 and 0.0174 kg m-3, which are Xu-Ri's table 11 and Li's table 7 exactly, so both secondaries carried the numbers faithfully and only the volume was lost. Those values were measured in a CONTINUOUS STIRRED TANK REACTOR on dissolved substrates, and there is no soil in the experiment at all: the paper draws the contrast itself, recording that soil scientists work mainly in soil columns while sanitary engineers work mainly in CSTRs, and this work is the second kind. A concentration measured in a reactor's liquid is a concentration per cubic metre of liquid.

So the operator's divisor is correct and no code changes. What changes is the register: biosphere/config/ntransform.yaml's michaelis_menten_divisor moves from unsourced to agrees, and its source is now the primary rather than a secondary's silence.

THE MAGNITUDE ARGUMENT FROM li1992 IS WITHDRAWN, and is recorded as withdrawn rather than deleted so it is not re-derived. It read Kc = 17 mg C per kg soil against DNDC's own soluble carbon of 10 to 20 mg C per kg soil and concluded the per-cubic-metre-of-SOIL reading matched -- which would have been the LOWER-denitrification branch and not the one running. It rested on an assumed bulk density and on a coincidence of numerals between two different volumes, and the provenance beats it.

CARRY THE EXPERIMENTAL FRAME when quoting anything else from this paper: it is waste-water treatment at 25 C, and its own conclusion that denitrification is first order holds over waste-water nitrate concentrations rather than over a soil's.

title: Derive the tree-cover artefact bar from a measured canopy-to-verdict sensitivity
description:
biosphere/notes/forcing-replay-preregistration.md fixes the forcing-construction artefact bar on tree cover at 1.0 percentage point, derived from the albedo endmembers: land-mean albedo runs 0.276 bare to 0.179 vegetated, so a point of canopy is 0.001 of land-mean albedo, which is two orders of magnitude inside the albedo bracket's width.

That derivation is sound as far as it goes and it is not the quantity the bar wants. What the bar should be one fifth of is the smallest tree-cover difference the protocol has to resolve, and that is a property of loop C's verdict, which is qualitative in config/pipeline.yaml ('re-take the verdict on modelled vegetation; if basins flip, re-enter A') and of the pipeline decision in biosphere/README.md, which says 'substantially less canopy' without saying how much.

Do: measure what change in canopy fraction moves the climate enough to change loop C's verdict, and replace the bar with one fifth of it. Until then the 1.0 point figure stands and is declared rather than derived, which is what this issue records.

Source: biosphere/notes/forcing-replay-preregistration.md, 'The thresholds'.

title: The BVOC gate should carry the air-temperature diurnal range as a named precondition
description:
vesperinput.cpp:init now refuses ifbvoc 1, because bvoc.cpp's daytime_temp reads climate.dtr as a near-surface AIR temperature range and this world's forcing carries only the SURFACE temperature range.

That refusal is correct and fail-closed, but it fires inside the run rather than in the gate. biosphere/config/bvoc.yaml is where each BVOC precondition is declared with the undeclared sentinel, and bvoc_gate.py is what reports which ones are unmet before anything starts. The air-temperature range belongs there as one more precondition, so the gate names it alongside the oxidant chemistry and the aerosol arms rather than the run dying on it.

Do: add the precondition to bvoc.yaml, have bvoc_gate.py report it, and cite the issue that would satisfy it.

Source: biosphere/notes/ecological-forcing-field-contract.md

title: td2m (code 168) is requested from pyburn and never produced by anything
description:
run_exoplasim.REGULAR_CODES and SNAPSHOT_CODES both request code 168, dew point temperature at 2 m. outmod.f90's writegp call sites do not include 168 and pyburn has no derivation branch for it, so pyburn's dispatch loop sets derived=True, matches no branch, and drops it silently. Confirmed absent from exoplasim/analysis/climatology/bootstrap_regular_climatology.nc.

Nothing currently reads td2m, so this costs nothing today. It is a request that looks satisfied and is not, and a consumer writing against REGULAR_CODES has no way to tell the difference from the list alone.

Do: either remove 168 from both lists, or derive it in pyburn from hus, ps and ta at the lowest level and say which saturation branch it uses. Removing is the cheaper answer while the contract takes near-surface humidity as specific humidity.

Source: biosphere/notes/ecological-forcing-field-contract.md
close_reason: 163, 168, 171 and 238 removed from REGULAR_CODES and SNAPSHOT_CODES: all four were requested and written by nothing, and pyburn drops an underivable code silently. 163 duplicates 164 clt, 171 duplicates nothing the model writes, 238 has no prognostic, 168 is a dew point the contract does not want. smoke_test now refuses a requested code nothing produces.

title: pH_soil is a declared instruction parameter that no line of LPJ-GUESS reads
description: framework/parameters.cpp:504 declares pH_soil with a parse range of 3.5 to 8.5 and parameters.h:186 externs it. Nothing reads it: the only pH the model uses is Soiltype::pH, which the soil map supplies, and no shipped .ins sets pH_soil. It is a knob that looks like the way to give the model a pH and is not. Do: either wire it as the declared pH for an input path that has none (which is the case sdec-8 made the operator refuse on) or delete the declaration. Deleting is a fix. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md

title: climate.aprec is a dead accumulator and out_seasonality reports it as a permanent zero
description: framework/guess.h declares Climate::aprec, the annual precipitation sum, and Climate::aprec_lastyear. modules/driver.cpp:544 resets aprec to 0.0 at day 0 and nothing anywhere adds to it; aprec_lastyear is assigned nowhere at all, only initialised to 0.0 in the constructor and serialised in guess.cpp. modules/miscoutput.cpp:1096 writes aprec into out_seasonality, so that column is a permanent zero for every gridcell of every run. ntransform.cpp was the other reader and no longer is: its Dawson pH fallback, which evaluated 3810/(762+aprec_lastyear)+3.5 and therefore always returned 8.5, was replaced by a refusal under sdec-8. Do: either accumulate aprec daily in driver.cpp and assign aprec_lastyear at year end, which makes out_seasonality report a real number and has to state the year length it is a sum over per biosphere/notes/time-base-unit-contract.md, or remove both members and the out_seasonality column. driver.cpp and miscoutput.cpp are outside the files sdec-8 owned. Evidence: biosphere/notes/soil-nitrogen-transformation-parameterisation.md

title: The three dust boundary fields cannot express --variant arid_bare_ground, so the in-model arm has no vegetation bracket
description:
build_dust.run_one's baseline variant emits from erodible*f_clay, which is exactly what boundary field 1801 carries. --variant arid_bare_ground instead uses bare = max(erodible, where(dry, land_fraction*weight, 0)) with dry = pr[t]*year*1000 < precipitation_mm_per_earth_year, evaluated PER TIME BIN.

A static .sra boundary field cannot carry a per-timestep precipitation test, so build_dust_source_fields.py writes the baseline variant and says so in its provenance. The consequence: vegetation cover is item 4 of aeolian/README.md's declared bracket list, the offline arm brackets it and the in-model arm has no counterpart, so an in-model emission total is not comparable across that bracket end.

Do: either accept it as a declared gap of the in-model port, or give dustsrc the test it needs. The model has precipitation in memory, so an in-model form is available: a second erodible fraction plus a declared precipitation threshold in aero_nl, with dustsrc choosing between them per timestep. That is a design decision, not a defect fix.

Evidence: aeolian/scripts/build_dust.py:run_one bare/variant block; aeolian/scripts/build_dust_source_fields.py build_fields and its variant_note provenance key.
notes: Evidence: notes/audits/dust-intensity-levers.md section 8 (renumbered when the drag-partition measurement was added as section 7), and aeolian/analysis/dust_intensity_levers.json block vegetation_bracket.
close_reason:
ACCEPTED AS A DECLARED GAP OF THE IN-MODEL PORT, with the price measured rather than assumed. Commit 9d5ca4bc.

--variant arid_bare_ground raises the emission by 1.165, 1.176 and 1.198 at the smooth, central and rough ends of the roughness bracket, measured on the same climatology and source map the baseline artifact used. The gap is therefore one-signed and under a fifth, against a roughness bracket of 10.6 and a subgrid wind shape worth a factor of 40. An in-model emission total is a floor by that much rather than a quantity of unknown standing, which is what makes the gap declarable.

Giving dustsrc the test would cost a second erodible boundary field, a declared precipitation threshold in aero_nl, a per-timestep branch in the source term, its staging and its arm in the self-test identity, to reach a bracket end worth under 20 percent. It is not worth that, and this is a decision on a bracket rather than leaving a known-wrong thing in place: the baseline variant the three fields carry is correct for what it claims to be.

Recorded where a reader meets it: the .sra provenance variant_note now carries the price, and aeolian/README.md item 4 of the bracket list says the variant is worth under a fifth and why that makes the in-model gap declarable.

Evidence: notes/audits/dust-intensity-levers.md section 7, aeolian/analysis/dust_intensity_levers.json vegetation_bracket.

title: stack_floor --validate reports an agreement percentage with no bar
description:
world-60x0 forwarded the configuration into stack_floor's --validate: the binary's registry name carries its rung, level count and thread count, so the parse arm now follows the executable instead of the command-line defaults, and a contradicting flag is refused. Before that, --validate against a binary built at another thread count printed an agreement percentage that meant nothing, and with no --rung it printed one per rung of which at most one could mean anything.

WHAT IS STILL MISSING is a bar. validate()'s docstring says the parse total and the BSS total 'must agree -- a check with a right answer rather than a comparison that can only differ', and then prints 'agree to X%' and returns. Nothing can fail.

A bar was deliberately not invented under world-60x0: the percentage is already on screen, and a criterion chosen after the run it judges is not a criterion (CLAUDE.md).

Do: work out what the two sums CAN legitimately differ by -- the nm arm sees only BSS symbols matching <local>.<n> with _MOD_ excluded, so module-level arrays and compiler temporaries are in one arm and not the other, and that difference is derivable rather than measurable. Declare it as a module constant, then raise when the disagreement exceeds it. If the difference is not derivable, say so and label the line a measurement rather than a validation.

title: The Earth comparator has no sediment thickness, so GW-18 cannot be scored there
description:
GW-18 sources the aquifer thickness on Vesper from the export's own cover_thickness. The Earth harness in hydrography/scripts/earth_calibration.py has no counterpart: it uses the same scalar D the Vesper run used, which is how GW-3's thickness sweep and GW-17's 2 km came to be scalars in the first place.

So the thing GW-18 changes cannot be scored against the bores that are the only external test this component has, and a Vesper-only run of it would move numbers with nothing to judge them by.

Do: find and record a route to an Earth sediment or regolith thickness on the same footing as ETOPO and GLHYMPS already have in docs/src/reference/external-data.md, or state that none is available and that GW-18 is therefore a Vesper-only change whose effect is reported and not validated. Check the AWS Registry of Open Data before an API, per CLAUDE.md. Pelletier et al.'s soil and sedimentary deposit thickness and the GlobSed marine sediment compilation are the obvious candidates and neither has been checked.

Blocks the second half of GW-18.

title: The Vesper-over-Earth cloud water ratio table is still on the fallback sigma set, and the issue that owned the redo is closed
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 5 carries a per-layer table of Vesper-over-Earth liquid water at 25 kg/m2 precipitable water: 7.2 at sigma 0.038, 4.1 at 0.12, 2.6 at 0.21, 1.9 at 0.32, 1.5 at 0.44, 1.2 at 0.57, 1.0 at 0.70, 0.89 at 0.82, 0.81 at 0.92, 0.78 at 0.98.

Finding 20's correction records that those sigma values are plasim.f90's neqsig == 0 fallback, and every run on record carries NEQSIG = 4 and PTOP = 5000 with sigma 0.02500, 0.09372, 0.18812, 0.29717, 0.42058, 0.55432, 0.69069, 0.81826, 0.92191, 0.98282. The two differ most at levels 1 and 2, which is exactly where a cloud water profile's ratio is largest, so the table's top entries are wrong by a large factor. The 'What it cost' paragraph beneath it (1.5 to 4 times the calibrated water in mid and upper cloud, 11 to 22 per cent less in the lowest three layers, column integral 5 to 7 per cent low) is computed from the same table.

The correction assigns the redo to world-ofn, which is CLOSED, so nothing owns it. Filed to close that loop.

Do: recompute the table on the NEQSIG = 4 set and rewrite finding 5's table and its 'What it cost' paragraph. State in the redo what the two columns are, since the current text does not: whether 'Earth' means the same sigma level on Earth's own heights and gravity, or the calibrated CCM3 configuration. The comparison cannot be checked without that.

Not blocking: exoplasim/notes/cloud-water-reference.md computes cloud water path, optical depth and cloud emissivity per layer on the correct sigma set for world-8h6's arms, and does not depend on this table.

Evidence: notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md findings 5 and 20
close_reason:
Recomputed on the NEQSIG = 4 set every run carries, and NAMING THE TWO COLUMNS -- which the old text never did -- showed the prose was wrong.

The recorded numbers were Vesper-over-Earth layer cloud water PATH. The "What it cost" paragraph read them as inherited-over-derived. Those two are a fixed factor 0.7656 apart, so the prose was wrong by 1.31 in the column: the Earth coefficient put 31 per cent MORE water in the column and NO LAYER CARRIED LESS, where the text said the column integral was 5 to 7 per cent low and the lowest three layers 11 to 22 per cent under. Both the table and that paragraph are rewritten, and each column is now stated.

It rests on an identity that can fail rather than on a recomputation nobody can check: Vesper over Earth must be exactly (gascon/ga)/(287.0/9.80665) in every layer, which holds to 1.2e-15, and it reproduces cloud_optical_depth_bracket.json's own water paths to 2.2e-16.

The redo was assigned to a closed row, which is why nothing owned it; that loop is closed here.

title: Citations of the deleted NTRU==42 and jtune branches survive in four files
description:
world-677x deleted the NTRU==42 hyperdiffusion preset from plasim.f90:readnl
and the jtune shortwave table from radmod.f90:radini. Four documents outside
that batch's file ownership still describe them as present, three of them by

- config/planet.yaml:569, in the model.hyperdiffusion comment: 'ExoPlaSim
hard-codes these for T21 and T42 only (plasim.f90:1544) and every finer rung
silently falls through'. True of upstream, no longer true of this fork. The

- exoplasim/scripts/run_exoplasim.py:1259, declare_hyperdiffusion's docstring,
same claim plus 'readnl applies the branch and THEN reads the namelist' as the

is still what sets these -- but its stated premise is gone.
- notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md:69 cites plasim.f90:1544-1551 and :1187
cites radmod.f90:968-1030.
- notes/audits/inherited-earth-constants.md:217-218 and :486 describe the
jtune table as pinning tswr1 and tswr2 at T21 and name world-ys9 as open on it.
world-ys9 is closed by the deletion; tswr1 0.077, tswr2 0.065 and th2oc 0.024
are radmod module defaults at radmod.f90:72-75, not T21 tunings, and the

Prefer citing symbols and subroutines over line numbers in the rewrite, since
that is what made these stale.
notes:
Five more sites say 'compiled branch' where 'compiled defaults' is now what
they mean. The wording is not load-bearing but it points a reader at a branch
that is gone:
scripts/check_consistency.py:309 and :353 (the second is a FAILURE MESSAGE a
reader sees on a real failure today), exoplasim/scripts/stability_probe.py:178,
exoplasim/scripts/run_exoplasim.py:1257 and :1295.
The behaviour each describes is unchanged: an absent key or a scalar still
leaves levels 2..NLEV on plasimmod's defaults, which is why the length
comparison and the NLEV*value replication both stay.

title: Layer-count and nlat-privileged branches in plasim.f90 readnl and initpm
description:
Found while deleting the truncation-privileged branches (world-677x). Three
sites in plasim.f90 privilege a configuration on an axis other than the
truncation. None of them changes what this project integrates, and none is
safe to delete on the same argument world-677x used, so they are recorded
rather than removed.

1. readnl, if (NLEV==10): sets tfrc(1)=20 d, tfrc(2)=100 d, tfrc(3:NLEV)=0 for
a ten-layer atmosphere. It runs BEFORE read(11,plasim_nl) and
run_exoplasim.py:declare_dry_constants writes TFRC unconditionally, so it is
overwritten on every run of this project exactly as the NTRU==42 preset was.
Deleting it changes what a ten-layer run that does not write TFRC integrates,
which the NTRU==42 deletion also did; the difference is that ten layers IS
this project's configuration, so the blast radius for other callers is wider.
Decide whether the fork keeps upstream's ten-layer default at all.

2. readnl, the two if (NLEV==20 .and. nrdrag==1) blocks: these run AFTER
read(11,plasim_nl), so at twenty layers with nrdrag 1 they would silently
overwrite the TFRC this project declares from config. nrdrag's compiled
default is 0 (plasimmod.f90:292) and nothing in exoplasim/scripts or
vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/__init__.py sets it, so the blocks are unreachable
here today. They become a live hazard the moment the vertical ladder reaches
twenty layers. A declared TFRC being overwritten by a compiled branch is the
failure class verify_staged_namelists exists to catch, and it would not catch
this one because the namelist FILE would still hold the declared value.

3. initpm, the if (mpstep <= 0 .and. ntspd <= 0) ladder: picks mpstep from
nlat in three arms commented T21, T31 and 'T42 and more', with the first two
hand-picked and the third a formula. This project writes MPSTEP from
model.timestep_minutes on every prepare and every continuation, so the ladder
is unreachable here. Deleting the two hand-picked arms WOULD change what an
auto-timestep run integrates at those truncations, so it is not a no-op and
was left alone.

Evidence and the reading are in exoplasim/notes/resolution-tuned-parameters.md
section 3.
close_reason:
Three decisions on ONE RULE, which is POSITION rather than which configuration a branch names: a preset ABOVE read(11,plasim_nl) is a default that a declaration beats and that verify_staged_namelists can read on disk; BELOW it, a preset is an override no declaration can beat and nothing on disk records.

NLEV==10 STANDS. It is above the read, and tfrc is a per-level array, so a drag profile cannot be written without a layer count. That is what separates it from the NTRU==42 deletion, where nhdiff was an absolute wavenumber and needed no configuration to be meaningful.

THE TWO NLEV==20 nrdrag BLOCKS ARE DELETED, and nrdrag with them: nothing set it, no namelist file anywhere names the key, and the switch had nothing left to switch. Their values are recorded in the note on the NSHALLOW footing rather than lost. These were the live hazard -- below the read, so at twenty layers with nrdrag 1 they would have silently overwritten a declared TFRC, and verify_staged_namelists would NOT have caught it because the namelist FILE would still hold the declared value.

initpm'S LADDER STANDS, refused on a measured number rather than on caution: folding the T21 arm into the formula gives 60 minutes, which is exactly T21's STABILITY_CEILING_MINUTES, so a caller who declared no timestep would default to the rung's ceiling with no margin at all. The hand-picked arm's 45 sits below it, which is the whole reason it is hand-picked.

title: Re-decide terminal phosphorus occlusion: Parton 1988 p.117 gives the rate BIO-35 called undocumented
description:
Terminal phosphorus occlusion: the rate constant has a source after all, so the
declared absence rests on two reasons and not three.

BIO-35 declared occlusion absent and deleted UOCC = 1.0e-5 per year, on three
reasons, the first of which was that the rate constant was undocumented. That
one is now refuted. Parton, Stewart and Cole (1988) Fig. 2 carries an occluded
P box, and p. 117 gives the rate that fills it: K3 = 1.0e-6 per month applied to
secondary P and multiplied by the same combined moisture-temperature factor the
decay rates use, which at that factor's maximum is 1.2e-5 per year, within 20
percent of the deleted UOCC. So the constant was undocumented in this tree, not
unsourced, and the CENTURY P submodel the fork claims to implement does have a
terminal sink where Wang et al. (2010) section 2.3 explicitly does not.

The other two reasons stand and the decision is not automatically reversed:
equilsom spins the SOM pools for 40000 model years as a numerical device and
does not save and restore pmass_sorbed or pmass_strongly_sorbed across it, so a
terminal sink inside that loop drains every cell over a span the run does not
represent; and a simulated soil's pedogenic age on this world is set by
hydrography and pedology, so an occlusion loss belongs with the initial
phosphorus stocks ANUT-1 through ANUT-10 own rather than as a flux inside the
vegetation model.

Do: re-decide with the source in hand. If the answer is still absence, the
argument in biosphere/notes/phosphorus-cycle-parameterisation.md is already
rewritten to rest on the two surviving reasons and needs nothing further. If it
is a flux, note that K3 acts on Parton's secondary P over 0 to 20 cm at a
monthly step, not on this fork's strongly sorbed pool at a daily one, which is
the same pool-definition question WORLD-Z01O is about, on a flux nothing can
undo.

Source: references/parton1988.pdf p. 117 and Fig. 2,
references/wang2010-cnp-terrestrial-biosphere.pdf section 2.3,
biosphere/notes/phosphorus-cycle-parameterisation.md

title: The C, N and P mass balance checks are declared and never called
description:
MassBalance::check_patch(), check_patch_C(), check_patch_N(), check_patch_P(), check_indiv() and their init_patch()/init_indiv() partners are declared in vendor/lpj-guess/framework/guess.h and defined in guess.cpp, and grep over the whole vendored tree finds no caller for any of them. The conservation checks the model carries do not run.

This is not cosmetic. It is why the phosphorus defect BIO-35 found could stand: somfluxes() drained the sorbed pool into a strongly sorbed pool it never wrote and booked the difference as an ecosystem loss, and Patch::pcont() excluded the destination pool, so the books balanced by construction and nothing ever asked.

A check needs a right answer, and these have one: a conservation law. Do: decide where in the daily loop init_patch/check_patch belong, wire them, and decide what a failure does. Note that under ifplim 0 and ifnlim 0 the model pins pmass_labile to PMASS_SAT and NH4_mass to NMASS_SAT at the end of somfluxes() without reporting a flux, so the balance is broken by design in those configurations and the check has to know that before it can be turned on.

Source: biosphere/notes/phosphorus-cycle-parameterisation.md, BIO-35

title: The band split's bracket is set by which rock stands for a lithology, not by how it was prepared
description:
analysis/rock_albedo_bands.json reports two spreads per class. The spread between sample PREPARATIONS is narrow -- continental_clastic 1.31 to 1.55 across coarse, fine and solid; granite 1.16 to 1.27; carbonate 1.08 to 1.12 -- which is the prediction the method rests on and it holds in 18 of 18 rock and soil classes that carry more than one preparation. The spread between SAMPLES within a class is two to four times wider: continental_clastic 1.09 to 2.14, gneiss 0.98 to 2.10, shelf_clastic 1.09 to 2.16.

So the residual uncertainty in the two-band substrate is a mineralogy question, not a laboratory one, and it is largest exactly where the land is: continental_clastic and playa_clastic are together over 40 percent of this land.

What would narrow it is a proxy chosen per class from fewer, better-matched samples rather than from a whole ECOSTRESS taxon -- the taxon is currently the selector, and rock.sedimentary.sandstone spans quartz arenite to arkose, whose iron content is what sets the near-infrared slope. Narrowing needs the class definitions in vendor/orogen/js/lithology.js read against the library's own sample descriptions, which are in each spectrum's header and are not currently consulted.

Not a defect: the central values are usable and the bracket is reported, which is what CLAUDE.md asks for. This row says what it would take to make the bracket smaller.
close_reason:
Narrowed with evidence, and the negative result is the more useful half.

Proxies are now chosen per SAMPLE from each spectrum's own Name and Description read against vendor/orogen/js/lithology.js, under the rule the taxon was already chosen by -- mineralogy, not grain size, induration or weathering -- with every rule fixed before any ratio was recomputed and the taxon's own numbers kept per class so the narrowing is a measurement rather than an assertion.

WHAT NARROWED. rock.sedimentary.shale files seven whole-rock chips of a phosphate ore plus one phosphatic shale described as oolitic collophane, and every class naming shale inherited all eight. On removal: melange 0.848 to 0.493, pelagic 1.136 to 0.811, foreland_clastic 1.056 to 0.804, shelf_clastic 1.069 to 0.886, continental_clastic 1.056 to 0.807. It also MOVES THE CENTRAL RATIO -- shelf_clastic by 0.151, continental_clastic by 0.115 -- so it is a correction and not only a tightening. Out on the same rule elsewhere: eight hydrothermally altered tuffs, obsidian as glass, anorthosite from the basalt family, serpentine marbles from carbonate, alkaline syenites from arc_andesite.

THE NEGATIVE RESULT, and it is what this row was really asking. lithology.js's basin_clastic rule states that an intracratonic basin fills with quieter, more mature clastics than a foreland one, and maturity IS mineralogy -- so greywacke and arkose leave continental_clastic. That moves its central ratio by 0.001 and WIDENS the bracket from 0.807 to 0.928. The per-class rules leave shelf and foreland untouched and widen arc_andesite 0.313 to 0.486. They stay, because a proxy is chosen by what the class IS and dropping one for widening a bracket is a tuning with an extra step. What they establish is that COMPOSITIONAL MATURITY IS NOT WHAT SETS THE NEAR-INFRARED SLOPE.

WHAT DOES, AND WHY NO RULE CAN USE IT. The descriptions record iron directly. Splitting the sandstone taxon on it gives 1.444 iron-stained against 1.253 unstained, bracket width 0.683 against 0.330 -- half the width of the whole taxon's 0.655. Reported as residual_after_selection and deliberately NOT used as a selector: lithology.js chooses no side of that axis, a red bed and a grey quartz arenite are both intracratonic clastics, and five samples is not a population. So the substrate's remaining bracket is waiting on a decision about this world's clastic iron, not on more spectra and not on a finer taxonomy.

The staged surface albedo .sra files are stale against this, as any generator re-run leaves them. Merged to main as part of the batch-2 fan-out.

title: Four grass spectra cannot settle whether tree and grass need separate band ratios
description:
analysis/vegetation_albedo.py measures band2/band1 at 3.146 for tree (n=350) and 2.558 for grass (n=4) under k25v. The pre-fixed test -- the grass sample must lie entirely below the trees' tenth percentile -- misses at 2.713 against 2.710, so both cover endmembers take the population ratio 3.005 and carry the per-class ratio as the other end of the bracket. band_ratio_separates_tree_from_grass records the outcome.

The difference is not small: at the grass level of 0.209 the two ratios give band pairs of [0.093, 0.281] and [0.107, 0.272], so band 1 moves by 0.014 over whatever fraction of a modelled cell is grass. This star puts 0.618 of surface shortwave in band 2.

What settles it is more spectra, not more argument. The ECOSTRESS green-vegetation VSWIR set carries four grass spectra against 350 tree and 199 shrub, and the trees' own ratios run 1.78 to 4.92, so a class mean here is only as good as its sample. A grass-specific reflectance set -- ECOSTRESS non-VSWIR grass entries, the USGS grass mixture POSEIDON carries, or a library this project does not hold -- would give the test something to run on.

bio-18's own note argues the same class dependence from leaf TRANSMITTANCE, via CLM5 tau_NIR/alpha_NIR of 0.971 for grass against 0.556 broadleaf. That is a separate route to the same question and it needs transmittance, which a reflectance library does not carry. Either route closes this; neither is done.

title: error_budget.py states the ocean-diffusion mislabel factor inverted, as (a_earth/a)**2
description:
scripts/error_budget.py:387-390 reads: 'hdiffo divided the requested coefficient by Earth's radius squared on an angular grid, so a bracket arm realised (a_earth/a)**2 times what it declared'.

That expression is upside down. zfac = hdiffk/plarad/plarad, so the old code applied hdiffk/a_earth^2 where the correct metric is a^2. The effective true diffusivity is therefore K = hdiffk * (a/a_earth)**2, which at PLARAD 7645464.0 against the deleted parameter(PLARAD=6.371E6) is 1.4401 -- an arm realised MORE than it declared, not 69% of it. Every other site now states it correctly and consistently: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md:300, notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md:404, notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md:234, notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md:71.

This prose is copied into analysis/error_budget.json, so the artifact carries the inverted factor too. It is only the symbolic expression that is wrong -- the paragraph's substantive claims, that the label was wrong and the conservation claim was not, are right.

Do: (a/a_earth)**2, and say 1.4401 so the direction cannot be read off the symbols alone. Regenerating error_budget.json is the caller's decision, not part of the text fix.

Found under world-vho, which corrected every other site. Not fixed there because scripts/error_budget.py was outside that batch's file ownership.

title: failure-modes class 11 states the parallel-width rule in ranks, and there are no ranks
description:
docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md class 11 reads 'Changing the rank count changes the answer ... an A/B must hold the rank count fixed, and a bracket run at one rank count is not comparable to a control at another.'

The RULE is live and the mechanism is unchanged: NLPP is NLAT/NPRO whether NPRO counts ranks or threads, so two widths group their partial sums differently. The WORD is wrong -- world-38b removed the MPI build and NPRO is a thread count. A reader looking for what to hold fixed in an A/B is told to hold fixed a thing the project no longer has.

The same class 11 paragraph above it says 'polar at T42 on 8 ranks. Write to 70+mypid instead', which is also a thread now.

Do: restate class 11 in parallel width / thread count, keeping the mechanism and the 83-of-199 magnitude as the measurement they are. notes/audits/model-reproducibility.md, which it cites, now carries the scope statement that the measurement was taken under MPI and that the width-dependence is expected to survive but has not been re-measured.

Not done under world-7b2 because docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md was outside that batch's file ownership.

title: lib/rungs.py's RUNGS table does not say that a rung above T170 needs the Legendre envelope re-measured
description:
verify_banded_transform.f90 bounds legini's pmat and qmat at 4*NTRU^2*eps. The coefficient is an envelope MEASURED over lib/rungs.py: the ratio to NTRU^2*eps runs 0.12 to 0.35 across the ladder and is still climbing at T170, so the bound is not argued above the top rung. Both the gate header and exoplasim/notes/banded-transform-reference.md now say so under world-issy.

Neither is where a rung gets added. lib/rungs.py:27 is, and RUNGS carries only the self-check that a rung's name and its latitude count agree. Someone adding a rung above T170 there gets no signal, and the first thing they see is ARM A failing on a build that is sound.

Do: one line at RUNGS pointing at the re-measurement, or a check that refuses a rung above the measured envelope until the note's table covers it. The measurement is Python and needs no build: legini_recurrence at exoplasim/scripts/verify_weight_factorisation.py:34.

Not done under world-issy because lib/rungs.py was outside that batch's file ownership.
close_reason:
No rung above T170 will ever be added, so the warning has nothing to warn about. The user's decision: T85 is the operating support and T170 is the top of the declared ladder; there are no runs above it and there never will be.

What the row asked for was a note at lib/rungs.py:27, where a rung gets added, saying that verify_banded_transform's 4*NTRU^2*eps envelope is MEASURED over the existing ladder -- the ratio to NTRU^2*eps runs 0.12 to 0.35 and is still climbing at T170 -- so the bound is not argued above the top rung. That is a true statement about the envelope and it is already recorded where it belongs: the gate header and exoplasim/notes/banded-transform-reference.md both carry it under WORLD-ISSY. What this row added was a third copy at the point of an edit nobody will make.

If a rung above T170 is ever wanted, the envelope is one of several things that would need re-establishing, and the ladder registry is not the right place to enumerate them one at a time -- lib/rungs.py now carries the escalation route, the stability ceilings and the commissioning evidence as three separately-named quantities (WORLD-F997), and adding a rung means re-deriving all three. That is a larger act than a comment can guard.

title: Two do-not-touch files still name ilatperm and verify_symmetric_transform.py
description:
Left by 2508bedb and by world-2div's rename. Both are one-line comment repairs in files batch R was told not to touch, so they are filed rather than fixed.

exoplasim/scripts/verify_threaded_numerics.sh:48 says a band's global position is 'set by the transfer routines through ilatperm rather than by the pointer offset'. ilatperm was deleted by 2508bedb. The REASONING is still correct and is the reason the neighbour-band control was rejected as a control: mpimod_omp's mpscgp and mpgagp set the global position by their own 'jg = mypid*NLPP + jlat' arithmetic. Only the name is wrong.

exoplasim/scripts/verify_banded_transform.f90:56-57 says dv2uv's 'loop and its mirror combination are checked by exoplasim/scripts/verify_symmetric_transform.py'. There is no mirror combination in dv2uv since 2508bedb, and the script is now exoplasim/scripts/verify_inverse_transform.py, which checks the loop at one thread against the matrix-vector product with the table and the per-mode factors it is handed, planetary vorticity included. exoplasim/notes/banded-transform-reference.md has already been corrected the same way under world-2div; the driver header and the note now disagree.

Do: repair both comments. Neither changes behaviour.
close_reason: Both comments repaired in 7fc4dc3c, plus a third instance the sweep found. verify_threaded_numerics.sh:48 named ilatperm for the reason the neighbour-band control was rejected; it now names the actual mechanism, mpimod_omp's mpscgp and mpgagp setting jg = mypid*NLPP + jlat themselves (verified at mpimod_omp.f90:196 and :216). verify_banded_transform.f90:56-57 pointed dv2uv's loop and 'its mirror combination' at verify_symmetric_transform.py; dv2uv at legmod.f90:484-524 has no mirror combination, and the script is verify_inverse_transform.py, so the header now says what that script actually checks. The sweep for every symbol deleted with the paired decomposition (ilatperm, LPAIRLAT, verify_latitude_pairing, verify_symmetric_transform) turned up one more live reference: exoplasim/notes/threads-instead-of-ranks.md:248 carried LPAIRLAT as a standing caveat for a future 32-thread arm. The layout is gone so the caveat is void; removed, leaving the restart incompatibility as the one thing to carry in. Every other hit is inside a note that states the deletion in its own banner. No behaviour changed.

title: legmod's three inverse transforms carry dead parity locals and comments for a mirror latitude they no longer compute
description:
Found while working world-h8o.

2508bedb removed the symmetric/mirror computation from legmod.f90's sp2fc, sp2fcdmu and dv2uv and left their declarations and comments behind. As the tree stands:

- sp2fc (:392) and sp2fcdmu (:442) each declare 'integer :: k ! Index for the mirror latitude' and 'real :: ze1, ze2 ! partial sums over the symmetric modes' with 'zo1, zo2' beside them. None of the five is assigned or read; the body is a plain multiply over pmat/qmat for every latitude l.
- dv2uv (:492) declares k the same way plus the sixteen parity accumulators zvz1e ... zud2o under the comment 'Eight products, each needing a symmetric and an antisymmetric partial sum.' The body uses none of them.

Nothing is wrong with the numbers: these are unused locals, and gfortran does not warn at the levels this build uses. The cost is that a reader of legmod finds a comment describing an algorithm the routine below it does not implement, and the fork's actual change to these routines -- hoisting the per-mode factor into the field -- is documented in the same comment block as though the parity split were still there.

Rule 4 applies: this is model source, so it means rebuilding every binary. It is comment-and-declaration only and should be batched with the next legmod edit rather than done alone. Deleting unused locals cannot move a result, and the restart sha is the check.
close_reason:
DONE, commit 2e5847e7. Declarations and comments only; no executable statement changed.

Verified dead before removing, not assumed: grep -w over vendor/exoplasim, exoplasim, scripts, lib and docs finds all twenty of dv2uv's parity accumulator names only in their own declarations. legmod.f90 carries no preprocessor directives at all, so there is no #else arm to check -- the eleven duplicated OMPSHARED sites a sibling batch noted are call sites in plasim.f90, not in legmod.

Removed: k, ze1/ze2/zo1/zo2 from sp2fc and sp2fcdmu; k, the unused j, the sixteen accumulators and the 'Eight products' comment block from dv2uv. The j and w declaration comments said 'within one m' and 'the first spectral mode of one m', which described the split loop that is gone; they now say what the loops do.

THREE MORE INSTANCES the issue did not enumerate, same defect, same commit: 'k ! Loop index for southern latitude' in uv2dv, qtend and mktend, the FORWARD transforms whose paired branches 2508bedb removed in the same pass. gfortran -Wunused-variable found them and now reports nothing at all in the file.

Verified after: legmod.f90 compiles standalone against plasimmod out of this worktree, and verify_inverse_transform.py, which lifts all three inverse routines verbatim, returns the same residuals as before the edit. stack_floor.py sums declared local ARRAYS only and its table is unchanged.

Rule 4: what this adds to the standing rebuild debt is legmod.f90 alone. The check on the rebuild is that the restart sha does not move.

title: The Legendre table bound in verify_banded_transform.f90 is an envelope over lib/rungs.py and not beyond it
description:
verify_banded_transform.f90 bounds legini's pmat and qmat against the reference at 4*NTRU^2*eps. The FORM is derived from the recurrence: an NTRU-long chain in m with an NTRU-long chain in n inside it, each step contributing eps to values of order one. The COEFFICIENT is an envelope measured across the declared ladder: legini's own recurrence differs from the reference by between 0.12 and 0.35 times NTRU^2*eps from T21 to T170, so four clears it by eleven to thirty-three times.

The ratio is still climbing at the top of the ladder -- 0.12 at T106, 0.34 at T127, 0.35 at T170 -- so the envelope is not argued above T170. Adding a rung there would need it measured again before the bound is used, and the gate would otherwise fail a sound build at the new rung.

Do: when a rung above T170 is added to lib/rungs.py, re-measure legini's table error against the reference at that rung and either confirm 4*NTRU^2*eps still clears it or re-derive the coefficient. The measurement is a Python one and needs no build: legini's recurrence is already reproduced in exoplasim/scripts/verify_weight_factorisation.py. The table it extends is in exoplasim/notes/banded-transform-reference.md.
acceptance_criteria: Either the ladder still tops out at T170, or the envelope has been re-measured at the new top rung.
close_reason:
Acceptance criteria met on the first branch: lib/rungs.py:27 still tops out at T170, so nothing needed re-measuring and nothing was. The bound 4*NTRU^2*eps is UNCHANGED and no gate result moves; the envelope was NOT widened to cover any rung that has not been checked.

What the re-verification found, in bc3befa1: the gate's own header disagreed with the table it rests on. It read '0.16 at T21 rising to 0.35 at T170, so four clears the whole declared ladder by between eleven and forty times'. The measured column in exoplasim/notes/banded-transform-reference.md is not monotone -- 0.16 at T21, 0.20 at T31, 0.19 at T42, 0.21 at T63, 0.16 at T85, 0.12 at T106, 0.34 at T127, 0.35 at T170 -- and the minimum 0.12 puts the widest clearance at thirty-three, not forty. The header now states the measured range, says in terms that the column is a maximum and not a trend the next rung can be read off, and names the note.

The honesty half is stated in both places a reader can land: the gate header and the note now each say the envelope holds over lib/rungs.py and not beyond it, that a rung above T170 does not inherit the bound, and that a gate failure at a new top rung before the re-measurement is a bound never argued for that rung rather than a defective build. Both name legini_recurrence at exoplasim/scripts/verify_weight_factorisation.py:34 as the reproduction that makes the re-measurement a Python one needing no build.

Left as a separate row: lib/rungs.py is where a rung is actually added and carries no signal at all. Filed as world-tanr, outside this batch's file ownership.

title: Two comments justify a live rule by a build file the CMake rework deleted
description:
Both are correct rules resting on a stale reason, which is the shape CLAUDE.md's "rewrite superseded content" exists for: a reader checking the justification finds nothing.

1. scripts/smoke_test.py:737, check_omp_directive_line_length:

     The bar is 132, which is what `most_compiler_omp` passes as
     `-ffixed-line-length-132`

   most_compiler_omp was deleted with the make-based build on 2026-08-22, and -ffixed-line-length-132 is not in config/planet.yaml's f90_opts either -- notes/audits/model-build-flags.md measured it and found the executable byte-identical without it, so it left the line. THE BAR IS STILL 132 AND STILL RIGHT, for a better reason than the one stated: these are .f90 files, gfortran compiles them as FREE form, and 132 columns is gfortran's free-form default. That is also why the flag was a no-op. Restate the reason as the language default rather than as a flag nobody passes, so the check does not read as depending on something that could be dropped again.

2. vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/aeromod.f90:275:

     The two variables stay separate because radmod cannot use aeromod: aeromod
     already uses radmod, and make_plasim compiles it second.

   The circular-use argument is right and is the reason `rad_apart => apart` is aliased in rather than the two being merged. make_plasim is gone; the compile order now comes from the _sources list in plasim/CMakeLists.txt, and Ninja scans the use statements. Name that instead. Rule 4 applies to this one: it is model source, so touching it means rebuilding every binary, and it is a comment-only change -- worth batching with the next aeromod edit rather than doing alone.

Not in this issue, because they are deliberate historical explanations and read correctly in the past tense: build_model.py's "WHAT THIS REPLACED" block, rebuild_binaries.py:387, restart_schema.py:72, vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/__init__.py:72-73, sweep_compiler_flags.py:47 and aerocore.f90:1408.

Found by the notes/audits sweep.
close_reason:
Both rules kept, both justifications rewritten.

smoke_test.py's check_omp_directive_line_length: the 132-column bar is now stated as gfortran's free-form default for .f90 files, which is a property of the language, with most_compiler_omp's -ffixed-line-length-132 mentioned only as the flag notes/audits/model-build-flags.md measured to be a no-op for that reason. The bar is unchanged at 132.

aeromod.f90:275: the circular-use argument is unchanged and is still why rad_apart => apart is aliased in rather than the two variables being merged; it no longer cites make_plasim's compile order, which is now plasim/CMakeLists.txt's _sources list with Ninja ordering by the use statements. Comment-only change to model source, batched with world-qml's surfmod.f90 edit in the same session so it costs no extra rebuild.

The past-tense explanations the issue excluded were left alone.

title: A comparison build has no way to name its compiler
description:
exoplasim/scripts/build_model.py:236 sets compiler = 'gfortran' and hands CMake the bare name, so a build takes whichever gfortran is first on PATH. The private toolchain prefix at ~/toolchains/gcc-16.1.1 exists for exactly one purpose, a deliberate compiler comparison, and docs/src/reference/external-data.md states as a standing rule that it is not to go on PATH.

Before world-38b the route was OMPI_FC, read by the MPI wrappers the build invoked. The MPI build is gone, so that route is gone with it, and the prefix currently serves only the standalone probes that take their compiler on the command line.

The build directory tag names every input that changes a byte of the executable, and the compiler is one -- so a --compiler argument has to reach tag() the way --extra-flag does, or two toolchains will land in one directory and reuse each other's objects. binary_manifest.json already records compiler_versions per build, which is the check that the argument took.
acceptance_criteria: A comparison build can name an absolute compiler without putting the prefix on PATH, and two toolchains cannot share a build directory.
notes:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-24 against base e919c068. VERDICT: STILL TRUE, and the acceptance criteria cannot be met without editing exoplasim/scripts/build_model.py, which was outside this batch's file ownership. NOT DONE. Left open.

The premise, cites re-located by content:
- build_model.py:236 'compiler = "gfortran"', :237 shutil.which on the bare name, :272 '-DCMAKE_Fortran_COMPILER={compiler}'. So a build takes whichever gfortran is first on PATH.
- tag() at :162-178 composes res, l<levels>, p<ranks>, profile, optional fp, a sha of drop+extra, and the patched-source hash. The compiler is NOT in it, so two toolchains would land in one build directory and reuse each other's ninja objects. That is the half that makes this a correctness issue and not an ergonomics one.
- docs/src/reference/external-data.md:352-357 already names this issue by id as the reason the prefix has no route: 'Giving a comparison build an explicit compiler path is world-f1l, and until it lands the prefix serves the standalone probes.' That paragraph has to be rewritten in the same commit that lands the argument.

ONE CORRECTION TO THIS ISSUE'S OWN TEXT, found by reading the artifact rather than the description. 'binary_manifest.json already records compiler_versions per build, which is the check that the argument took' is not accurate on two counts, and a --compiler argument that relied on it would record the WRONG compiler silently:
- compiler_versions is not per build. It is one global 'toolchain' block for the whole rebuild. A per-binary entry carries sha256, resolution, layers, ranks, parmode, profile, effective_f90_opts and the source hashes, and no compiler at all.
- rebuild_binaries.py:239-244 asks the version of the BARE names gfortran, gcc, cmake, ninja, so it reports whatever is first on PATH regardless of what build_model.py was told to use. Under a --compiler argument that is exactly the compiler that did NOT build the binary.

So the change is three parts, not one:
1. build_model.py grows --compiler, defaulting to 'gfortran'. Accept an absolute path; keep the shutil.which check for a bare name and use os.access(X_OK) for a path.
2. The compiler reaches tag(). Hash it like extra flags rather than spelling it out, since a path cannot go in a directory name: a 'c' + sha256(compiler)[:8] component, omitted when the compiler is the default so every existing build directory keeps its name and nothing rebuilds.
3. The compiler is recorded PER BINARY in binary_manifest.json, and its version is asked of the compiler that was actually invoked rather than of the bare name. Without this the manifest cannot answer 'which toolchain built this', which is the only check that the argument took.

Cross-check that the argument works, needing no trust in the manifest: readelf -p .comment on the binary. external-data.md:361-366 records the tell -- a 16.2.1 build shows both 16.1.1 and 16.2.1 strings because glibc's crt1.o is old, and a genuine 16.1.1 build shows only 16.1.1.

Nothing was built or run.

title: The cGENIE candidate's genie-plasim carries the fftmod NLON 48 defect world-78e fixed in plasim
description:
vendor/cgenie/genie-plasim/src/fortran/fftmod.f90:9 lists nallowed = (8,16,32,48,64,96,128,256,384,512,1024,2048,4096) and its gp2fc at :44-60 is the same 8 - 4 - (3 or 2) chain the plasim copy has: radix 8, then radix 4 while four or more remain, then ONE radix-3 or radix-2 tail. That is 8 * 4**k * r with r in 1, 2, 3. For n = 48 the tail count is 6, the radix-4 pass fires on it and leaves 1, and neither tail runs, so 32 of the required 48 is applied and fc2gp overshoots the other way. No error either way. The comment at :13 claims 8-3-2, which is not what the loop does.

This is the same defect world-78e fixed in vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/fftmod.f90 and world-clb found in the puma and sam trees before world-6ak deleted those.

Nothing acts on this today. CLAUDE.md's layout records vendor/cgenie as the CANDIDATE offline ocean under OCN-3, not an adopted component: nothing reads it, and it does not build where it stands. genie-plasim is cGENIE's own atmosphere, which is not what the candidate would be adopted for, and T15 is not a rung this project uses. So this is filed to keep the finding rather than to schedule work.

Do: if cGENIE is ever adopted, or if genie-plasim is ever compiled, remove 48 from that table and add the comment world-78e wrote, before any T15 run.
close_reason: Fixed in 7fc4dc3c, and the 'does it matter for an unadopted tree' question answered first. It does not matter today, and the reachability is settled by one parameter rather than by the tree being unread: genie-plasim takes its grid from geniemod.f90:6 'parameter(NLAT_ATM = 32)' with NLON = NLAT + NLAT at plasimmod.f90:77, so the resolution is compile-time and fixed at N64. N48 could not be selected without a source edit to that parameter -- which is the same edit that would have hit the wrong transform, with no error either way. Fixed anyway rather than left documented: vendored-upstreams.md says a cGENIE fork is expected rather than optional (OCN-19, OCN-20), so the delta costs nothing on a pull, nallowed is only a whitelist read by fftini at :109-111, and removing 48 turns a silent wrong transform into a clear refusal. Applied as world-78e applied it -- 48 out, NRES 13 to 12, and the comment saying what the radix chain does -- with one difference recorded in the comment: this tree ships no fft991mod, so 48 there would need a radix 6. Defect re-verified before the fix: dfft4 does 'la = la / 4' at :237, so for n = 48 la goes 6 to 1 and neither tail fires. The finding and the reachability argument are in notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md section 6.

title: The correlated-k bundle's IR and VI band sets do not meet, and 0.00017 of the star's flux falls in the gap
description:
Found by world-134's rewrite of exoplasim/scripts/corrk_cross_check.py, which now computes and names the gap rather than letting it appear as a summation error (corrk_cross_check.py:272-292).

Measured on the 376 ppm table: the IR band set ends at 1974.95 cm-1 and the VI band set begins at 2000 cm-1. The two halves are joined without overlap and do not meet, so a 25.05 cm-1 window sits inside the table span and inside no band. Integrating this star's spectrum over it gives 0.00017 of the flux in the span.

Why this is a finding and not just bookkeeping: flux in the gap is flux the correlated-k tables carry no absorption coefficient for. Wherever the bundle is used to price a band-resolved scheme, that sliver is implicitly treated as transparent in both gas sets. 1.7e-4 is small against the band weights it would perturb, but it is a structural hole rather than a rounding term, and it is at 5 um, between the shortwave and thermal halves, where the two schemes hand over.

Do: establish whether the gap is an artifact of how the bundle was assembled here or is present upstream in the source tables; then either close the two sets against each other, or record the gap as a declared property of the bundle with its flux, so a consumer prices it rather than inheriting it silently. Decide BEFORE clim-61 uses the bundle to price a band-resolved shortwave and longwave.

Do NOT close the gap by widening a band edge to make the arithmetic tidy: the check that found this telescopes exactly for a contiguous partition, and moving an edge to silence it removes the only instrument that can see it.
acceptance_criteria: The gap is either closed in the bundle or declared with its flux fraction in the bundle's own metadata, and corrk_cross_check reports which. clim-61 is not run against an undeclared gap.
close_reason:
Closed by closing the join, in commit f1dbe00d. The gap is NOT a property of the bundle: upstream the two sets OVERLAP -- narrowbands_IR.in runs 10-3000 cm-1 in 40 bands, narrowbands_VI.in 2000-30000 in 38, each contiguous inside itself to the bit, sharing 2000-3000 -- and the Generic PCM never concatenates them, rad_correlatedk_read_opacity_tables.F90:361 setting IR_VI_wnlimit = 3000. and handing WNOI and WNOV to two independent solvers. Both band files are byte-identical between the 376 and 1000 ppm tables. corrk_cross_check.py makes the join itself because it needs one flux-weighted partition, and its cut at a round 2000 was what opened the hole: the IR grid has no edge at 2000, its nearest below being 1974.952011, so dropping every IR band reaching past 2000 dropped the sliver with them.

The join is now the VI set's own first edge, read from the data, and the straddling IR band is truncated to it rather than dropped, keeping its own k-distribution -- the only opacity the bundle carries over that sliver. No edge is widened. The hole detector stays and now RAISES rather than folding the hole into the sum, each half is checked for internal contiguity on load, and the run reports the join and the truncation by name. It reads 0.97204 in 76 bands + 0.00000 in 0 gaps = 0.97204 in one piece.

Two corrections to the issue as filed: 0.00017 is the SOLAR fraction, not this star's, which is 0.00025 because the gap sits at 5 um where the cooler host's boost is about 1.5; and the joined set was 75 bands, not 78, 78 being the two raw sets before the cut.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the reason this took a model edit. --fit reads radmod.f90's four coefficients back out of the source, so the join change showed there as a disagreement. The refit was re-landed: zca1 3.1020E-4, zcb1 19.857, zca2 3.8291E-3, zcb2 3.9587E-3. Absorptance at this planet's CO2 path 0.005027 -> 0.005051, +0.5% and +0.008 W/m2 of Earth-mean insolation, against the fit's own 3.3% rms. Binaries must be rebuilt (world-klr).

clim-61 is unblocked, with one thing to carry: it must NOT inherit this script's join. The two sets are meant to be used separately over their own spans by two solvers, and the 2000-3000 cm-1 overlap the join throws away is real data a thermal scheme wants. Recorded in exoplasim/notes/corrk-cross-check.md, section 'The join between the IR and VI sets, and the hole it used to leave'.

title: Derive lake_dwmax_m from the seasonal water balance of the lake cells
description:
world-vus put model.lake_dwmax_m into config/planet.yaml and removed the hardcoded 0.2 m fallback from build_surface_soil_water.py, carrying the value unchanged. The DIRECTION is derived and stated in the config comment -- drhs reaches 1 above 40 percent of dwmax at landmod.f90:52-53, so a shallower bucket saturates the wetness factor on less water, and this planet's lakes sit in arid cells where the water to fill a deep bucket is not there. The VALUE is not.

The derivation: the depth at which a lake cell's own seasonal precipitation keeps its soil water above 0.4 * dwmax through its driest output bin. That needs per-cell seasonal precipitation and evaporation over the lake cells, so it needs a baseline climatology; config/planet.yaml carries baseline_climatology: null.

Note the ceiling the builder already records: a cell's annual evaporation is capped by its own precipitation plus storage however dwmax is set, because routed river water accumulates into driver (landmod.f90:1390) and never reaches dwatc. So the quantity being derived is a SEASONAL partition, not a sustained rate.

Do: once a baseline climatology is declared, take the per-cell driest-bin soil water over cells with a non-zero lake fraction and solve for the largest dwmax that keeps drhs at 1 through it. Report the spread across lake cells, because one number for all of them is itself an approximation.

Source: world-vus
notes:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-24 against the merged tree (base aaeaed55). VERDICT:
BLOCKED, on config/planet.yaml's `baseline_climatology: null`. The finding is
unchanged; only its line cites moved.

Confirmed in the current tree:
- config/planet.yaml carries model.lake_dwmax_m: 0.2 with the direction argued
  and the value marked underived, and build_surface_soil_water.py:192-198 reads
  it with no fallback and refuses without the key. world-vus landed.
- The mechanism: drhsland = 0.25 and drhsfull = 0.4 are declared at
  landmod.f90:103-104 (the issue and the config comment both said :52-53, which
  is now the snow and glacier albedo block; corrected in this pass), and the
  application is
    drhs(jhor)=AMIN1(1.,dwatc(jhor)/(drhsfull*dwmax(jhor)))
  at landmod.f90:516-517. So drhs still reaches 1 above 40 per cent of dwmax.
- The ceiling the builder records is intact: routed river water accumulates
  into driver at landmod.f90:1527 (the issue said :1390) and never reaches
  dwatc, so what is being derived is still a SEASONAL partition.
- exoplasim/inputs/t21/orogen_T21_surf_0229_provenance.json records
  mean_lake_fraction_of_land_cells 0.171 and the land-mean dwmax before and
  after the lake write, so the cells the derivation ranges over are identified.

What blocks it: the derivation needs per-cell seasonal precipitation and
evaporation over the lake cells through the driest output bin, and there is no
climatology on this build. check_consistency reports the same.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
UNBLOCKED, and the direction argument is inverted against the field that now exists. Found 2026-08-30 while sizing SPAT-7's land/soil-water reduction.

THE BLOCK IS GONE. config/planet.yaml no longer carries baseline_climatology: null. It points at exoplasim/analysis/climatology/baseline_regular_climatology.nc, whose own attributes name run_67323a923013 on canonical-10m-carve2, which is the configured source_build, created 2026-08-28 over 57 orbits. The prose block above the key still reads "DECLARED ABSENT AGAIN" and describes the null it no longer is; a reader grepping for the state of the key lands on the wrong one.

THE VALUE IS NOT MERELY UNDERIVED, ITS EFFECT IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE STATED DIRECTION. The comment argues for a bucket shallower than 0.5 m so that a lake cell saturates drhs on less water and evaporates at the potential rate. 0.5 m is ExoPlaSim's uniform default, and soil_water_source is pedology, so 0.5 m is not what the field carries. Measured on the pedology states files: evaporable_mm has a median of 85.9 mm on canonical-10m-carve2 over its 1639 land cells and 51.6 mm on canonical-10m-base over 1019, and 74.1 and 82.8 per cent of cells respectively sit below 200 mm. lake_dwmax_m = 0.2 m is therefore DEEPER than the derived soil capacity on three quarters of land cells, so blending it in raises the capacity there, which raises the water needed to reach 0.4 * dwmax and lowers both the wetness factor and the saturation-excess runoff. That is the direction the comment argues against.

The direction argument itself is sound and is not what is wrong. What is wrong is that it was written against ExoPlaSim's uniform default and never re-read against the pedology field that replaced it.

Do, unchanged in shape: solve for the largest dwmax that keeps drhs at 1 through the driest bin over cells with a non-zero lake fraction, on the climatology above, and report the spread rather than one number. The result has to be compared against the same cells' evaporable_mm, because a lake bucket deeper than the soil it sits beside is a lake that dries more slowly than the ground, which is not what a lake does.

Note the staged field is currently inert: exoplasim/inputs/t21/orogen_T21_surf_0229_provenance.json carries "lakes": null, so nothing the model is running today reads this value.

comments.author: Conor Futro
comments.text:
REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY 2026-08-31, and the inversion is now measured in the units the model runs on rather than in millimetres.

THE 2026-08-30 MEASUREMENT REPRODUCES EXACTLY, read straight off the pedology states files rather than inherited: evaporable_mm has a median of 85.9 mm on canonical-10m-carve2 over 1,639 land cells and 51.6 mm on canonical-10m-base over 1,019, with 74.1 and 82.8 per cent of cells respectively below 200 mm. canonical-10m-carve1 gives 53.6 mm and 83.3 per cent. So lake_dwmax_m = 0.2 m is deeper than the derived soil capacity on roughly three quarters of land cells and the direction argument in config/planet.yaml is inverted against the field that replaced the 0.5 m default it was written against.

WHAT IS NEW: THE SIGN, ON THE STAGED FIELD, IN W M-2. Measured on the staged surface code 0229 itself, sha-verified against its own provenance record, rather than on the states file the builder reads. lake_dwmax_m exceeds the staged soil capacity on cells holding 55.8 per cent of lake-bearing land area (328 of 457 lake-bearing cells). Evaluating the model's own wetness factor min(1, w / (0.4 C)) over the baseline climatology, staging the lake tile as configured would move the land latent heat flux by -0.048 to -0.082 W m-2 on the planet mean, NEGATIVE: the blend as configured makes lake cells DRIER, not wetter. Against config/partial_surface.yaml's 0.12 W m-2 bar that is 0.40 to 0.68 times the bar, so the defect is real and under the materiality bar at once.

The perturbation is concentrated rather than uniform: as a fraction of the cell's own soil capacity it is 0.48 per cent at the median over lake-bearing land area, 15 per cent at p90, and reaches 435 per cent, with 2.6 per cent of that area perturbed by more than 100 per cent. The worst cell reaches -16 W m-2.

STILL UNFIXED AND WHY: config/planet.yaml was outside the file scope of this session.
